# R1029 — D17.430 five-set data do not force a Hamilton P5 with the wall vertex as an endpoint

**Audit state:** PASS
**Proof provenance:** Slack `#a7c3-workspace` root `1789280602.868739`

## Statement
There is a five-vertex boundary tournament on `Z={A,C,t,b,d}` satisfying all four retained OUT star-cycle turns from D17.430,

`(d,b,t), (b,t,A), (A,t,C), (C,t,b)` tight,

but having no tight Hamilton P5 with the wall vertex `d` as an endpoint. Therefore the retained D17.430 five-set data alone do not imply an endpoint-controlled Hamilton P5 usable as a far-wall insertion port.

## Construction
For each middle vertex `v`, write `x->y` in `T_v` when `(x,v,y)` is tight. Define the five local tournaments as follows.

- `T_A`: transitive `C->b->d->t`.
- `T_C`: transitive `b->A->d->t`.
- `T_b`: transitive `A->C->d->t`.
- `T_d`: transitive `t->b->C->A`.
- `T_t`: `d` dominates `{A,C,b}`, while `A->C->b->A` is the directed triangle on the other three vertices.

These five local tournaments specify a boundary tournament on `Z`: every ordered triple with distinct vertices is decided by the tournament at its middle vertex, and complete reversal has the opposite value.

## Verification of the D17.430 packet
At middle `b`, `T_b` has `d->t`, so `(d,b,t)` is tight. At middle `t`, the directed triangle has `b->A`, `A->C`, and `C->b`, so `(b,t,A)`, `(A,t,C)`, and `(C,t,b)` are all tight. Thus the exact OUT star-cycle packet retained by D17.430 is realized.

The only cyclic local star in this construction is `T_t`; the other four local tournaments are transitive. In particular the model is compatible with the star-cycle branch rather than introducing an unrelated local defect.

## Endpoint check
Direct inspection of the local tournament tables gives exactly three tight four-vertex paths beginning at `d`:

`(d,A,t,C)`, `(d,C,t,b)`, `(d,b,t,A)`.

Their unique unused vertices are respectively `b,A,C`. Extending them to Hamilton P5s would require, respectively,

`(t,C,b)`, `(t,b,A)`, `(t,A,C)` tight.

All three are bad in the displayed local tournaments: at middle `C`, `b->...->t` places `b` before `t`; at middle `b`, `A->...->t` places `A` before `t`; and at middle `A`, `C->...->t` places `C` before `t`. Hence no Hamilton P5 starts at `d`.

Dually, direct inspection gives exactly three tight four-vertex paths ending at `d`:

`(A,b,C,d)`, `(C,A,b,d)`, `(b,C,A,d)`.

Prepending the respective unused vertex `t` would require

`(t,A,b)`, `(t,C,A)`, `(t,b,C)` tight.

Each is bad in the corresponding transitive local tournament. Hence no Hamilton P5 ends at `d`.

Therefore this boundary tournament has no tight Hamilton P5 with `d` as either endpoint.

For completeness, the model is nevertheless Hamiltonian, as D17.430/R902 predicts in the star-cycle branch. For example `(b,d,A,t,C)` is a tight Hamilton P5. The counterexample is specifically to endpoint control, not to existence of a Hamilton P5.

## Scope
This result fences only the inference from the retained five-set D17.430 data to a Hamilton P5 whose endpoint is the fixed far-wall vertex. It does not rule out endpoint control after adding source-gate ancestry, zipper data, or other information outside the five-set, and it does not invalidate the D17.430 Hamilton-5/twin-anchor-wall alternative itself.

## Applicability
Any G37 splice requiring `d` as an insertion port must use more than the four OUT star-cycle turns retained in D17.430, or use a different splice geometry. The construction is an explicit witness that a purely local strengthening of the five-set packet cannot supply that endpoint for free.

## Dependencies
- R3 / boundary antisymmetry
- D17.430 retained OUT star-cycle packet

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/INTERESTING/R1029.md -->

# R1031 — Three parallel source trimers force a Hamilton P5

## Statement
Let `a,c,p,q,r` be five distinct vertices in a Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament. If

    (a,p,c), (a,q,c), (a,r,c)

are tight, then the induced subsystem on `{a,c,p,q,r}` has a tight Hamilton path of order five.

## Scope
This uses only boundary antisymmetry R3 and distinctness. It does not use minimality, R24/R5, the old source two-cover, the spectator path, or any D17 ancestry statement.

## Proof
For distinct `x,y in {p,q,r}`, write

    x ->_a y  iff  (x,a,y) is tight,
    x ->_c y  iff  (x,c,y) is tight.

By R3, each relation is a tournament on `{p,q,r}`.

If distinct `x,y,z` satisfy `x ->_a y ->_c z`, then

    x,a,y,c,z

is a tight Hamilton P5: its middle turn `(a,y,c)` is one of the three hypotheses.

Assume for contradiction that no tight Hamilton P5 exists. Then there is no such mixed chain.

If `T_a` were transitive, relabel its vertices so

    x ->_a y,  y ->_a z,  x ->_a z.

Avoiding `x,a,y,c,z` forces `z ->_c y`, while avoiding `x,a,z,c,y` forces `y ->_c z`, contradicting that `T_c` is a tournament. Hence `T_a` is a directed 3-cycle. Relabel so

    p ->_a q ->_a r ->_a p.

Avoiding the three mixed-chain P5s then forces the opposite `c`-cycle

    r ->_c q,  p ->_c r,  q ->_c p.

Still assuming no Hamilton P5, inspect the six words

    a p c r q,
    a q c p r,
    a r c q p,
    p q a r c,
    q r a p c,
    r p a q c.

In each word the first two required turns are already tight from the source hypotheses and the two displayed cycles. Therefore the last turn must be bad; applying R3 to its complete reversal forces, respectively,

    (q,r,c), (r,p,c), (p,q,c),
    (a,q,p), (a,r,q), (a,p,r).

Now inspect

    a p r c q,
    a q p c r,
    a r q c p,
    p a q r c,
    q a r p c,
    r a p q c.

The same reasoning, using the turns just forced, yields

    (c,r,p), (c,p,q), (c,q,r),
    (r,q,a), (p,r,a), (q,p,a).

At this point only three source-only reversal bits are relevant. Write

    u = [(q,p,r) is tight],
    v = [(p,q,r) is tight],
    w = [(p,r,q) is tight].

For each of the eight values of `(u,v,w)`, the indicated pair of candidate words has every required turn already certified except one pair of complete reversals:

    000:  a c q r p   |   r p q c a
    100:  c a r q p   |   q p r a c
    010:  a c p q r   |   q r p c a
    110:  a c p q r   |   q r p c a
    001:  c a p r q   |   r q p a c
    101:  c a p r q   |   r q p a c
    011:  a c r p q   |   p q r c a
    111:  c a q p r   |   p r q a c.

For example, in the `000` row the only undecided turns are `(a,c,q)` and `(q,c,a)`, which are complete reversals. The same holds row by row. R3 therefore makes exactly one undecided turn tight in each row, so one word in the relevant pair is a tight Hamilton P5. This contradicts the assumption that no Hamilton P5 exists.

Hence `{a,c,p,q,r}` always has a tight Hamilton P5. QED.

## Live source-frame consequence
In the retained source frame, `(A,s,C)` is tight for all `s in {p,q,r}`. Therefore

    S={A,C,p,q,r}

has a Hamilton P5. Since `B union {v}` is disjoint from `S`, any Hamilton path on `H[B union {v}]`, in any order, together with this P5 would be a spanning two-cover of `H`. Thus in a hypothetical counterexample the induced subsystem `H[B union {v}]` must be nonHamiltonian.

## Audit note
Targeted out-of-order review was justified because the claim collapses the current G40 nonempty-anchor branches. The proof was checked directly against R3; the final eight-case table reduces exactly to reversal pairs. The interestingness nomination is endorsed.

# R1033 — First-flip obstruction for failed one-vertex insertion

## Statement
Let

    B=(b_1,...,b_m),  m>=2,

be a tight path in a Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament, let `x` be outside `B`, and write

    e_i={b_i,b_{i+1}}  (1<=i<=m-1),
    f_i={x,b_i}        (1<=i<=m).

Assume that inserting `x` into every one of the `m+1` slots of the displayed order of `B` fails to produce a tight path. Equivalently, `I_B(x)=empty`.

Then there is an index `1<=t<=m-1` with one of the following certificates in the R887 comparison orientation `Gamma`.

### Star-triangle
For some `2<=t<=m-1`,

    f_t -> e_{t-1} -> e_t -> f_t.

### Reverse-spoke hook

    e_t -> f_t,
    f_{t+1} -> f_t,

and additionally

    e_{t-1} -> f_t          if t>1,
    f_{t+1} -> e_{t+1}      if t<m-1,

while at `t=m-1` the failed final insertion gives

    f_m -> e_{m-1}.

Thus total failure of displayed-order one-vertex insertion always has a local obstruction on `x` and at most three consecutive vertices of `B`.

## Scope
The result uses only R3, the comparison interpretation R887, and tightness of the displayed path `B`. It does not use minimality, source-frame data, R24/R5, or D17 ancestry.

## Proof
Failure of the left endpoint insertion

    x,b_1,b_2,...,b_m

means `f_1 -> e_1` is false, so R3 gives

    e_1 -> f_1.

Failure of the right endpoint insertion means `e_{m-1} -> f_m` is false, so

    f_m -> e_{m-1}.

If some `t<=m-2` satisfies

    f_{t+1} -> e_{t+1},

choose the least such `t`; otherwise set `t=m-1`.

For `t=1`, the left endpoint failure already gives `e_t -> f_t`. For `t>1`, minimality says `f_t -> e_t` does not hold, so R3 gives

    e_t -> f_t.

Suppose first that `t>1` and

    f_t -> e_{t-1}.

Because `B` is tight,

    e_{t-1} -> e_t.

Together with `e_t -> f_t`, this gives the star-triangle

    f_t -> e_{t-1} -> e_t -> f_t.

Otherwise, whenever `t>1`, R3 gives

    e_{t-1} -> f_t.

Assume now that `t<m-1`. By the choice of `t`,

    f_{t+1} -> e_{t+1}.

If also `f_t -> f_{t+1}`, then insertion of `x` between `b_t` and `b_{t+1}` has all required comparisons forward:

    e_{t-1} -> f_t -> f_{t+1} -> e_{t+1},

with the predecessor comparison omitted when `t=1`. That would make the insertion tight, contrary to `I_B(x)=empty`. Hence

    f_{t+1} -> f_t,

and the reverse-spoke hook is obtained.

It remains to treat `t=m-1`. We already have

    e_{m-1} -> f_{m-1},
    f_m -> e_{m-1}.

If `m>2` and `f_{m-1} -> e_{m-2}`, then tightness of `B` gives the star-triangle

    f_{m-1} -> e_{m-2} -> e_{m-1} -> f_{m-1}.

Otherwise `e_{m-2} -> f_{m-1}` when that predecessor exists. Failure of insertion between `b_{m-1}` and `b_m` then forces

    f_m -> f_{m-1},

because the opposite orientation would make all required comparisons forward. For `m=2` there is no predecessor, and failed middle insertion directly gives `f_2 -> f_1`. Thus the reverse-spoke hook also holds in the terminal case. QED.

## Live source-frame consequence
By R1031, in the retained source frame a hypothetical counterexample has `H[B union {v}]` nonHamiltonian. In particular `I_B(v)=empty`, so R1033 supplies a local star-triangle or reverse-spoke-hook obstruction on `v` and a short consecutive interval of the spectator path `B`.

## Audit note
Targeted review was justified because R1031 makes this exact empty-insertion branch the current live obstruction. Every indexing and endpoint case was checked directly. The interestingness nomination is endorsed.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/INTERESTING/R1033.md -->

# R1034 — Static spectator-gate packet plus sharp source counts is insufficient

## Statement
There exists a globally edge-ordered Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament on

    {A,C,p,q,r,v,b0,b1,b2,b3}

in which all of the following hold simultaneously:

- `(A,s,C)` is tight for each `s in {p,q,r}`;
- `B=(b0,b1,b2,b3)` is a tight Hamilton spectator path;
- `X={v,p,q,r}` is P4-free and realizes the noncyclic R516 signature `11`;
- both `X union {b0}` and `X union {b3}` are P5-free;
- the universal reverse endpoint stars

      (b1,b0,x), (x,b3,b2)

  are tight for every `x in X`;
- the literal old source two-cover

      F=(b0,p,q,r,b3) | (v,b1,b2)

  is tight, has `tau(F)=3`, and contains the consecutive internal source block `p,q,r`;
- the literal three-forest

      J=(p,q,r) | (v,b3,b2) | (b0,b1)

  is tight and has `tau(J)=1`;
- `H[B union {v}]` is nonHamiltonian;
- `H[{A,C,p,q,r,v}]` is nonHamiltonian.

Therefore the displayed static conclusions of the D17.391 quiet spectator-gate frame, even when combined with the sharp physical source-frame data `tau(F)=3`, `tau(J)=1`, do not by themselves consume the one-vertex obstruction on `v`. Any successful closure must use genuinely additional information, such as dynamic/canonical ancestry that explains how the D17.421 first-loss/source-gate packet is produced, a further retained conclusion not represented here, or a stronger global smallest-counterexample consequence.

This is a fence on an abstraction. The construction is not asserted to be a smallest counterexample and does not realize the provenance assumptions that lead to the D17.391 quiet branch.

## Construction
Declare tight turns by one global strict order on ordinary edges: `(x,m,y)` is tight exactly when edge `xm` occurs before edge `my`. Use the total order

    qv < b3q < b0b1 < b0p < pr < rv < b3p < b2r < b2v < b2p
       < b3v < b2q < b1r < b1p < b1b3 < b1v < b0b2 < b1b2 < b0b3
       < b1q < b0q < b0v < b0r < Ap < pq < qr < pv < b3r < b2b3
       < Cv < Cb3 < Ar < Cr < Cp < Aq < Cq < Cb2 < Cb1 < Cb0
       < Av < Ab3 < Ab2 < Ab1 < Ab0 < AC.

Because this is a global edge order, every complete-reversal pair of turns has exactly one tight orientation, so it is an R3-compatible Strong Level-(1) realization.

## Verification
The source turns follow immediately:

    Ap < Cp,
    Aq < Cq,
    Ar < Cr.

The spectator path is tight because

    b0b1 < b1b2 < b2b3.

For `X`, take the R516 notation `(a,b,c,y)=(v,q,r,p)`. The twelve tight representatives are exactly

    vqr, vrq, qvr,
    vqp, qpv, qvp,
    prv, rpv, rvp,
    prq, rpq, pqr,

which is R516 signature `11`. Hence `X` is the noncyclic P4-free cell used by the quiet D17.391 static frame.

The universal reverse endpoint stars are immediate from

    b0b1 < b0x

and

    b3x < b2b3

for every `x in X`.

The old source rail satisfies

    b0p < pq < qr < b3r,

and the other rail satisfies

    b1v < b1b2.

Thus

    F=(b0,p,q,r,b3) | (v,b1,b2)

is a literal tight two-cover. Its selected `X|B` edges are exactly `b0p`, `b3r`, and `b1v`, so `tau(F)=3`. The source block `p,q,r` is consecutive and internal on the first rail.

Likewise `pq<qr` and `b3v<b2b3`, so

    J=(p,q,r) | (v,b3,b2) | (b0,b1)

is a literal tight three-forest. Its only selected `X|B` edge is `b3v`, so `tau(J)=1`.

Direct exact enumeration of vertex orders gives:

- zero Hamilton P4 orders on `X`;
- zero Hamilton P5 orders on `X union {b0}`;
- zero Hamilton P5 orders on `X union {b3}`;
- zero Hamilton P5 orders on `B union {v}`;
- zero Hamilton P6 orders on `{A,C,p,q,r,v}`.

The source five-set itself is Hamiltonian, for example

    A,p,q,r,C

is tight because `Ap<pq<qr<Cr`.

Hence all claimed static and sharp source-frame features coexist with the stubborn one-vertex obstruction.

## Scope and exclusions
The construction does not claim to satisfy:

- smallest-counterexample minimality;
- the historical provenance by which the D17.391 quiet branch was reached;
- absence or resolution of every R408-derived output that occurs during that derivation;
- the canonical D17.421 first-loss switch or its actual augmenter ancestry;
- the provisional D17.433-D17.439 ancestry conclusions as a generated chain.

Accordingly, the theorem does not refute those stronger dynamic routes. It isolates their necessity: static endpoint-gate geometry and sharp transition counts alone are insufficient.

## Audit note
This counterconfiguration received targeted out-of-order review because it materially determines the G41 strategy. Every displayed path inequality and transition count was checked directly from the edge order, the `X` turn table matches R516 signature `11`, and exhaustive enumeration verifies each stated P4/P5/P6 nonexistence. The interestingness nomination is endorsed.

# R1041 — Three parallel source turns do not force endpoint flexibility

## Statement
There exists a five-vertex Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament on

    {A,C,p,q,r}

such that `(A,s,C)` is tight for every `s in {p,q,r}`, but the only tight Hamilton paths of order five are

    A,r,p,C,q
    q,p,A,r,C
    q,p,r,C,A.

Consequently every Hamilton source P5 has exactly one source-spoke endpoint, that endpoint is always `q`, no Hamilton source P5 has two source-spoke endpoints, and the endpoint source spoke cannot in general be prescribed from the three parallel source turns alone.

## Construction
For each middle vertex `m`, write `u ->_m w` iff `(u,m,w)` is tight. By boundary antisymmetry R3, it suffices to specify one orientation for every pair of endpoints in each local tournament.

Use:

`m=A`:

    C->p, q->C, C->r, q->p, p->r, r->q.

`m=C`:

    A->p, A->q, r->A, p->q, r->p, q->r.

`m=p`:

    A->C, q->A, r->A, q->C, r->C, q->r.

`m=q`:

    A->C, p->A, A->r, p->C, r->C, p->r.

`m=r`:

    A->C, A->p, q->A, p->C, C->q, p->q.

Each displayed list orients all six endpoint pairs for its middle vertex, hence defines a local tournament and therefore a Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament.

The arcs `A->_p C`, `A->_q C`, and `A->_r C` give the required tight turns `(A,p,C)`, `(A,q,C)`, `(A,r,C)`.

## Exhaustive verification
For an order `w=(w0,w1,w2,w3,w4)`, tight Hamiltonicity is exactly the conjunction of

    (w0,w1,w2), (w1,w2,w3), (w2,w3,w4)

being tight. Exhaustion of all `5! = 120` vertex orders gives exactly

    A,r,p,C,q
    q,p,A,r,C
    q,p,r,C,A

and no others.

Each of these has exactly one source-spoke endpoint, namely `q`. Therefore the three parallel source turns alone force existence of a source Hamilton P5 by R1031, but do not force endpoint choice, a prescribed source endpoint, or two source-spoke endpoints.

## Scope
This construction uses only R3 and the three source turns. It does not use minimal-counterexample structure, R24, R5, the spectator path, old-F data, or D17 ancestry.

## Live consequence
Any minimality-splice argument that requires freedom to prescribe which source spoke is an endpoint of the source P5, or requires two source-spoke endpoints, needs additional global or smallest-counterexample structure. That flexibility is false at the level of the source five-set alone.

## Audit note
Audited directly from the finite certificate. Each local orientation is a tournament on the four vertices distinct from its middle vertex, the three source turns are present, and exhaustive checking of all 120 orders yields exactly the three stated Hamilton P5s. The `[INTERESTING]` nomination is endorsed because this counterexample permanently fences a natural strengthening of the live minimality-splice route.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/INTERESTING/R1041.md -->

# R1051 — The OUT-v first-loss rectangle is a literal spectator/source coordinate bridge

**Status:** PASS
**Source:** workspace root `1789345870.272209`

## Statement

Retain the sharp non-loop v-rooted literal first-loss cell of R1036, and take the OUT-`v` orientation in which the installed first-positive old edge is

`e_r=v->b_j`

with `b_j` a spectator vertex. Under the audited D17.408 sharpening R1047, the canonical D17.421 switch has the exact form

`{ b_{j-1}->b_j , v->t }  <->  { v->b_j , b_{j-1}->t }`

for a unique source spoke `t∈{p,q,r}`.

Thus the same literal four-vertex `K_{2,2}` cell simultaneously contains

- the consecutive spectator edge `b_{j-1}->b_j`,
- the `v`-spectator edge `v->b_j`,
- an actual source spoke `t`,
- the old same-side edge `v->t`, and
- the remaining cross edge `b_{j-1}->t`.

This is an exact provenance/coordinate bridge between the canonical first-loss switch and spectator order. It does not prescribe the R1033 comparison sign at this cell and does not itself give a cover or strict descent.

## Proof

R1036 gives the corrected literal first-loss switch whenever both adjacent closures exist:

`{f_r,g_{r-1}} <-> {e_r,g_r}`,

where the old pair is same-side and the new pair is crossing. In the non-source-rooted v-case, the physical `X` endpoint of `e_r` is the unique non-spoke vertex `v`.

Take the OUT-`v` orientation. Then

`e_r=a_{r-1}->b_r=v->b_j`

with `b_j∈B`. Same-sidedness of

`f_r=a_r->b_r`

forces `a_r∈B`. R1047 says every selected `B-B` edge in the canonical `J` is a consecutive edge of the displayed spectator path. Since `f_r` is oriented into `b_j`, it is exactly

`f_r=b_{j-1}->b_j`.

Now the other old same-side edge is

`g_{r-1}=a_{r-1}->b_m=v->b_m`.

Since this edge is same-side and `v∈X`, we have `b_m∈X`. The non-loop hypothesis gives `b_m≠v`. R1037 identifies

`X={v,p,q,r}`

with `p,q,r` precisely the three source spokes. Therefore

`b_m=t∈{p,q,r}`,

and

`g_{r-1}=v->t`.

The remaining new crossing edge is

`g_r=a_r->b_m=b_{j-1}->t`.

The four physical vertices are pairwise distinct: `b_{j-1}≠b_j` because they are consecutive vertices of the spectator path, `B∩X=∅`, and `t≠v` by nonloopness. Hence this is a genuine four-vertex `K_{2,2}` switch, not a collapsed or looped packet.

The source spoke is unique because it is the fixed far endpoint `b_m` of the canonical zipper switch.

## Dependencies

- `A7C3/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R1036.md`
- `A7C3/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R1037.md`
- `A7C3/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R1047.md`
- the literal D17.421 switch identity already incorporated in R1036

## Scope

The theorem records exact selected matching/support data. It does not assert that either closure is already a physical tight two-cover, does not prescribe the R1033 spoke/spectator comparison orientation, and does not consume the first-loss packet globally.

## Audit note

The `[INTERESTING]` nomination is endorsed. This is the first audited theorem that puts the dynamically generated old-`F`/augmenter first-loss coordinate, a consecutive spectator edge, and actual historical source ancestry into one literal cell. That is exactly the provenance bridge the current proof strategy seeks, even though a global consumer remains open.

# Interesting results

This directory is the curated shelf for A7C3 mathematics that is both **audited** and judged unusually important, creative, reusable, or conceptually illuminating.

A result belongs here only after a Slack `(INTERESTING)` nomination is endorsed during audit and the result receives `(PASS)` or `(PASS_ADJUSTED)`.

Typical reasons include substantial progress, repeated reuse, a strong structural principle, a creative mechanism, or a non-obvious construction/counterexample that permanently changes how a tempting route should be viewed.

Keep one canonical copy here. Do not mirror the same result under `USABLE/ACTIVE/`. If later invalidated, move it to the appropriate unusable location. If it merely becomes strategically inactive while remaining mathematically interesting, it may remain here.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/INTERESTING/README.md -->

# R2031 — INVALID: two-seam six-vertex completion

**Status:** FAIL
**Source:** Slack workspace R2031 re-audit

## Original false statement

The original R2031 claimed that distinct `A,C,s,r,t,v` with

`(A,s,C)`, `(A,r,C)`, `(s,C,t)`, `(r,A,s)`

tight must induce a tight Hamilton `P6`.

This is false.

## Error

The original proof repeatedly treated cyclic rotations of a tight ordered turn as automatically tight. R3 supplies only complete-reversal antisymmetry. Under the accepted R887 comparison model, `(x,m,y)` is an orientation of the pair of incident ordinary edges `xm,my`; cyclic rotation changes the middle vertex and is a different comparison.

## Counterexample

On vertex set `{A,C,s,t,r,v}`, globally order the ordinary edges increasingly by

`Cv < Ar < st < tv < AC < rs < rt < sv < At < Av < As < Cr < rv < Cs < Ct`.

As in R887, declare `(x,m,y)` tight exactly when edge `xm` precedes edge `my`.
This is a globally edge-ordered Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament.
The four original hypotheses hold because

`As < Cs`, `Ar < Cr`, `Cs < Ct`, `Ar < As`.

Nevertheless there is no Hamilton `P6`. The complete list of tight Hamilton `P5` orders is

- `v,t,r,C,s` (missing `A`),
- `s,t,A,v,r` (missing `C`),
- `s,r,t,A,v` (missing `C`),
- `C,v,t,A,s` (missing `r`),
- `t,v,A,s,C` (missing `r`),
- `v,A,s,C,t` (missing `r`),
- `v,t,A,s,C` (missing `r`),
- `A,r,s,C,t` (missing `v`),
- `r,A,s,C,t` (missing `v`),
- `r,t,A,s,C` (missing `v`).

For each listed `P5`, insertion of the missing vertex at either endpoint fails its newly created endpoint turn. Any Hamilton `P6` would yield a Hamilton `P5` by deleting an endpoint, so this exhausts all possible Hamilton `P6`s.

## Dependencies

Trusted dependencies: R3, R887.

Provisional dependencies: none.

## Consequence

R2031 is unusable. Any descendant whose proof invokes R2031 must be re-audited rather than inheriting its former PASS status.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/UNUSABLE/INVALID/R2031.md -->

# R2033 — INVALID: three-cap six-vertex completion

**Status:** FAIL
**Source:** Slack workspace R2033 re-audit

## Original false statement

The original R2033 claimed that distinct `A,C,s,t,r,v` with source turns

`(A,s,C)`, `(A,t,C)`, `(A,r,C)`

and additional tight turns

`(s,A,v)`, `(v,C,s)`, `(t,A,r)`

must induce a tight Hamilton `P6`.

This is false.

## Error

The proof treated cyclic rotations of tight ordered turns as automatic. R3 provides only complete-reversal antisymmetry. Under R887, changing the middle vertex changes the line-graph comparison and is not licensed by R3.

## Counterexample

On `{A,C,s,t,r,v}`, globally order the ordinary edges increasingly as

`rs < Cv < tv < rv < AC < rt < As < Cs < At < Ar < sv < Cr < st < Ct < Av`.

Declare `(x,m,y)` tight iff edge `xm` precedes edge `my` as in R887. This is a globally edge-ordered Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament. The six original hypotheses hold because

`As<Cs`, `At<Ct`, `Ar<Cr`, `As<Av`, `Cv<Cs`, `At<Ar`.

Nevertheless there is no Hamilton `P6`. The complete list of tight Hamilton `P5` orders is

- `C,v,r,t,s` (missing `A`),
- `r,v,s,t,C` (missing `A`),
- `s,r,t,A,v` (missing `C`),
- `C,v,t,A,r` (missing `s`),
- `C,v,t,r,A` (missing `s`),
- `C,v,r,t,A` (missing `s`),
- `v,t,A,r,C` (missing `s`),
- `v,C,A,s,t` (missing `r`),
- `v,C,A,t,s` (missing `r`),
- `s,A,r,C,t` (missing `v`),
- `r,s,A,t,C` (missing `v`).

For every listed `P5`, the missing vertex fails the newly created turn at either possible endpoint. Hence no `P5` extends to a Hamilton `P6`; every Hamilton `P6` would give such a `P5` after endpoint deletion.

## Dependencies

Trusted dependencies: R3, R887.

Provisional dependencies: none.

## Consequence

R2033 is unusable. Descendants whose proofs invoke it must be re-audited.

# R685 — The monotone minimum five-cell residue is exactly 43 labelled configurations, uniformly in m

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/INVALID`

## Statement
Retain the accepted crossed five-cell frame R665/R667 with D={q_2,q_{m-2}}, W=H-D, and cells G_0=Q[0,1], G_1=Q[3,m-3], G_2=Q[m-1,m], G_3={a,c}, G_4={b,z}. Let T be an exact two-cover of W with sigma_G(T)=0 and c_X(T) in {2,3}, and work in the monotone branch of accepted R671, i.e. outside the explicit R435 reverse-state, reverse-trimer/contact, or vertex-simple tight-cycle outputs. Take the contracted forest F_T WITH its cell labels, rather than up to the R670 quotient by permutation of the three Q labels and interchange of the two X labels; a configuration is by definition its labelled edge set, and a rail reading is displayed monotone in Q when the rail carries at least two Q-blocks. Then F_T is exactly one of 43 labelled configurations: 25 with c_X=2 and 18 with c_X=3, distributed over the six R670 shapes as A:6, B:4, C:12, D:3 (all c_X=2) and E:12, F:6 (all c_X=3). Writing each configuration as its two rails, the complete list is: (A) [G0 | G3-G1-G2-G4], [G0 | G4-G1-G2-G3], [G1 | G3-G0-G2-G4], [G1 | G4-G0-G2-G3], [G2 | G3-G0-G1-G4], [G2 | G4-G0-G1-G3]; (B) [G0-G1-G3-G2 | G4], [G0-G1-G4-G2 | G3], [G0-G3-G1-G2 | G4], [G0-G4-G1-G2 | G3]; (C) [G0-G1-G3 | G2-G4], [G0-G1-G4 | G2-G3], [G0-G2-G3 | G1-G4], [G0-G2-G4 | G1-G3], [G0-G3 | G1-G2-G4], [G0-G3 | G4-G1-G2], [G0-G4 | G1-G2-G3], [G0-G4 | G3-G1-G2], [G1-G3 | G4-G0-G2], [G1-G4 | G3-G0-G2], [G2-G3 | G4-G0-G1], [G2-G4 | G3-G0-G1]; (D) [G0-G1 | G3-G2-G4], [G0-G2 | G3-G1-G4], [G1-G2 | G3-G0-G4]; (E) [G0 | G1-G3-G2-G4], [G0 | G1-G4-G2-G3], [G0 | G3-G1-G4-G2], [G0 | G4-G1-G3-G2], [G0-G3-G1-G4 | G2], [G0-G3-G2-G4 | G1], [G0-G4-G1-G3 | G2], [G0-G4-G2-G3 | G1], [G1 | G3-G0-G4-G2], [G1 | G4-G0-G3-G2], [G2 | G3-G0-G4-G1], [G2 | G4-G0-G3-G1]; (F) [G0-G3 | G1-G4-G2], [G0-G3-G1 | G2-G4], [G0-G3-G2 | G1-G4], [G0-G4 | G1-G3-G2], [G0-G4-G1 | G2-G3], [G0-G4-G2 | G1-G3]. Every Q-Q adjacency occurring in this list is one of G_0G_1, G_1G_2, G_0G_2, realized respectively by the named transitions u q_3, q_{m-3} s, u s of R671, so the list is consistent with R671; in particular the shape (B) sublist is exactly the four configurations R671 derives by hand, an independent confirmation of that step. Moreover, in the monotone branch the internal order of every Q block is forced to be the original Q order, so T is completely determined by its labelled configuration together with the internal orientation of each of the two X-dimer blocks; hence the entire residue is at most 172 explicitly named ordered rail pairs. Finally, every seam-tightness condition that can distinguish these configurations involves only the twelve named vertices q_0, q_1, q_3, q_4, q_{m-4}, q_{m-3}, q_{m-1}, q_m, a, b, c, z, because interior triples of a Q block are subpath triples of Q and are automatically tight. Consequently the whole c_X in {2,3} minimum five-cell residue is one fixed finite local problem, uniformly in m>=9, with m in {6,7,8} contributing only finitely many degenerate coincidences among those twelve names.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in the crossed beyond-order-ten frame of accepted R594/R621 with X={a,b,c,z}, Q=(q_0,...,q_m), m>=6. Accepted R435, R508, R665, R667, R670, R671.

## Scope
The monotone branch of accepted R671 inside the sigma_G(T)=0 minimum five-cell setting, restricted to the genuinely new residue c_X(T) in {2,3}. Pure enumeration of contracted configurations; no realizability claim.

## Applicability
Supplies an m-uniform finite target for the entire minimum five-cell residue. Any argument that refutes or resolves each of the 43 labelled configurations closes the residue outright, without a separate lemma per R670 shape. Also usable as an audit key: any per-shape lemma should account for exactly the sublist above for its shape.

## Persistence
The count is a property of the contracted forest under the accepted R665 block/transition count, the R667(1) no-X-X rule, and the R671 monotonicity constraint. It survives any change of representative that retains those three results.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not refute or realize any configuration. Does not treat the non-monotone R435 outputs. Does not use X-dimer internal orientations, R621 endpoint gate data, or R658 rectangles to cut the count, so 43 is an upper bound on the surviving labelled residue and the true number may be smaller. Makes no claim that any configuration occurs in an actual smallest counterexample.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Retired after scoped audit failure of R685: the 43 labelled edge-set enumeration survives, but the 172 directed-candidate assertion is false. Superseded by corrected revision R1026.
- **Validity:** invalid
- **Validity note:** AUDIT 2026-09-13: scoped defect. The exact 43 labelled edge-set enumeration is correct, but the statement also claims that T is completely determined by the labelled configuration plus the two X-dimer internal orientations and therefore has at most 172 ordered rail-pair candidates. This omits a directed block-order choice for any nonsingleton component containing at most one Q-block. The full revision is therefore false as written; repair is local to the 172/completely-determined clause.
- **Review status:** needs_more_work
- **Review note:** AUDIT FAIL (SCOPED). Keep the 43-case enumeration; repair or remove the final 172 ordered-rail-pair assertion. Independent enumeration gives 22 configurations with one admissible component orientation and 21 with two, so after the four X-dimer internal orientations the corresponding directed candidate count is 256, not <=172.

## Proof
Write Q={G0,G1,G2} with the fixed order G0<G1<G2 and X={G3,G4}. By R670, after contracting the five contiguous cells, every configuration in the genuinely new minimum residue is a two-component path forest with three edges, no G3G4 edge, and one of the six typed shapes A--F. By R671, whenever a rail contains at least two Q blocks, their order along the rail is the increasing Q order. Since a configuration is its labelled edge set, reversing a displayed rail does not create a new configuration; for a canonical display, orient a rail so its Q labels increase, and if it contains at most one Q block break the remaining tie lexicographically. We now expand the six typed shapes.

(A) X-Q-Q-X plus an isolated Q. Choose the isolated Q in 3 ways. The other two Q labels then have a forced increasing order, while G3 and G4 may occupy the two path ends in 2 ways. Hence A contributes 3*2=6 configurations, exactly the six A entries displayed in R685.

(B) Q-Q-X-Q plus an isolated X. Choose the isolated X in 2 ways. On the other rail the three Q labels occur as G0,G1,G2 in increasing order, and the remaining X must occupy one of the two internal Q-gaps, giving 2 choices. Hence B contributes 2*2=4 configurations. These are exactly the four B entries, agreeing independently with the four cases already derived in R671.

(C) Q-Q-X plus Q-X. Choose the Q on the two-vertex rail in 3 ways. Choose which X label lies on that two-vertex rail in 2 ways. On the three-vertex rail the other X may be attached to either endpoint of the forced increasing pair of Q labels, giving 2 more choices. Hence C contributes 3*2*2=12 configurations, exactly the displayed C list.

(D) Q-Q plus X-Q-X. Choose the Q that is the centre of the X-Q-X component in 3 ways. The remaining two Q labels form the other edge. There is no extra factor of 2 from exchanging the two X ends: as a labelled edge set, the X-Q-X component has exactly the two edges from its centre Q to G3 and G4, and reversing its display changes no edge. Hence D contributes exactly 3 configurations.

(E) X-Q-X-Q plus an isolated Q. Choose the isolated Q in 3 ways. On the remaining four vertices there are two Q and two X labels and three Q-X edges. Such a path is exactly K_{2,2} with one edge deleted. Equivalently choose the degree-two Q in 2 ways and the degree-two X in 2 ways. Hence E contributes 3*2*2=12 configurations, precisely the twelve displayed E entries.

(F) Q-X-Q plus Q-X. Choose the Q belonging to the two-vertex component in 3 ways. Choose which X is its mate, equivalently which X is the centre of the three-vertex component, in 2 ways. The remaining two Q labels are then the endpoints of that three-vertex component. Hence F contributes 3*2=6 configurations, exactly the six displayed F entries.

Therefore the total number of labelled configurations is

    6+4+12+3+12+6 = 43.

The c_X=2 shapes are A--D, so their total is 6+4+12+3=25. The c_X=3 shapes are E,F, so their total is 12+6=18. This proves both the exhaustiveness and the stated distribution of the displayed list. It is also the same finite specification recorded independently in the project certificate M14: enumerate three-edge labelled path forests on G0,...,G4, forbid G3G4, require exactly two components, require c_X in {2,3}, and require increasing Q order on each rail. That deterministic enumeration returns the same 43 configurations and the same A6/B4/C12/D3/E12/F6 split.

For the transition claim, R671 says that in the monotone branch every Q-Q transition is oriented from the lower-index Q cell to the higher-index Q cell. There are only three possible Q-cell pairs, and R671 identifies them physically as

    G0G1 : u q3,
    G1G2 : q_{m-3} s,
    G0G2 : u s.

Thus every Q-Q adjacency appearing in the 43 configurations is one of exactly those named transitions, as claimed.

R671 also fixes the literal internal order of each Q block to the original Q orientation. Once a labelled contracted configuration is fixed, the canonical rail reading above fixes its block order for enumeration purposes. Each X cell is a physical two-vertex dimer and has at most two internal orientations. Therefore the two X dimers contribute at most 2*2=4 internal choices per labelled configuration, giving at most

    43*4 = 172

explicitly named normalized ordered rail-pair candidates. This is an upper bound only; seam constraints may remove candidates.

Finally, any tightness test wholly inside a Q block is automatic because that block is a contiguous subpath of the original tight path Q. A seam can inspect only the last two vertices of a Q block or the first two vertices of the next Q block, together with vertices of an adjacent X dimer. For G0=Q[0,1], G1=Q[3,m-3], and G2=Q[m-1,m], the only Q vertices that can occur in such seam triples are

    q0,q1,q3,q4,q_{m-4},q_{m-3},q_{m-1},q_m.

Adding the four X vertices a,b,c,z gives exactly the twelve named vertices in the statement. Hence for m>=9 every configuration-distinguishing seam condition is supported on this fixed twelve-vertex set. For m in {6,7,8}, some of those names coincide or the middle interval degenerates, leaving only finitely many exceptional coincidences. This proves the claimed m-uniform finite locality.

# R100 — Transversal branch symmetric minimum-overlap triangle

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
In the minimum-overlap-three butterfly of R98, assume the transversal alternative and choose C∈F with profile |C∩S|=2 and |C∩U|=|C∩V|=|C∩R|=1. Then |A∩C|=|B∩C|=3, so A,B,C are pairwise globally minimum-overlap supports. Their triple intersection T=A∩B∩C has size 2 and their union has size 8. Equivalently, there are uniquely determined vertices x,y,z,alpha,beta,gamma outside T and two exterior vertices delta,epsilon such that A=T∪{x,y,alpha}, B=T∪{x,z,beta}, C=T∪{y,z,gamma}, with {delta,epsilon}=V(H)\\(A∪B∪C). For each of the three minimum-overlap pairs, the third support is again a (2,1,1,1) transversal in that pair's butterfly; its private vertex is the unique non-exterior vertex in that pair's R-block.

## Hypotheses
Standing order-ten smallest-counterexample case; A,B are globally minimum-overlap with |A∩B|=3; C is a transversal supplied by alternative (i) of R98.

## Scope
Pure support-incidence normalization of the transversal branch.

## Applicability
Use to rotate the butterfly among the three supports and obtain three equivalent common-triple deletion frames.

## Persistence
All coordinates are physical support-membership coordinates and persist across representative changes.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert existence of a fourth support, overlap descent, or a spanning two-cover.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** superseded
- **Lifecycle note:** Transversal symmetric minimum-overlap triangle is a conditional normalization inside the branch eliminated by C125/R127.
- **Curation note:** Transversal symmetric minimum-overlap triangle is a conditional normalization inside the branch eliminated by C125/R127.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Verified. The (2,1,1,1) transversal gives |A∩C|=|B∩C|=3; the Venn decomposition and cyclic transversal normalization follow by direct counting.

## Proof
By R98 alternative (i), C contains exactly two vertices of S=A∩B, one vertex of U=A\\B, one vertex of V=B\\A, and one vertex of R=V(H)\\(A∪B). Hence |A∩C|=2+1=3 and |B∩C|=2+1=3. Since A,B were chosen with globally minimum support intersection 3, the three pairs A,B; A,C; B,C are all globally minimum-overlap pairs.\n\nThe triple intersection A∩B∩C is C∩S, so it has size two; call it T. Because each pairwise intersection has size three, there is exactly one vertex x in (A∩B)\\C, exactly one y in (A∩C)\\B, and exactly one z in (B∩C)\\A. Each support has size five, so after accounting for T and its two pair-only vertices, each has exactly one private vertex: alpha in A\\(B∪C), beta in B\\(A∪C), gamma in C\\(A∪B). Thus A=T∪{x,y,alpha}, B=T∪{x,z,beta}, C=T∪{y,z,gamma}. The union therefore has 2+3+3=8 vertices, leaving exactly two exterior vertices delta,epsilon.\n\nNow consider the pair A,C. Its common triple is T∪{y}; its two wings are {x,alpha} and {z,gamma}; its R-block is {beta,delta,epsilon}. The third support B=T∪{x,z,beta} contains exactly two vertices of the common triple T∪{y}, one vertex x of the first wing, one vertex z of the second wing, and the unique non-exterior R-vertex beta. Hence B is a (2,1,1,1) transversal for the A,C butterfly. The same argument cyclically shows that C is the transversal for A,B and A is the transversal for B,C. This proves the stated symmetric normalization.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED/R100.md -->

# R101 — Transversal triangle three-frame deficit kernel

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Assume the transversal alternative of R98. Then the three supports can be coordinatized as A=T∪{x,y,alpha}, B=T∪{x,z,beta}, C=T∪{y,z,gamma}, where |T|=2 and the remaining vertices are delta,epsilon. For the three minimum-overlap pairs AB, AC, BC, let S_x=T∪{x}, S_y=T∪{y}, S_z=T∪{z}. Every exact two-cover of H-S_x, H-S_y, or H-S_z has profile 4+3 and satisfies the corresponding three-block deficit identity t=1+sigma. In the x-frame, sigma=0 exactly when the three-vertex R-block {gamma,delta,epsilon} is one tight-trimer component and the other component is a tight four-path formed by concatenating the wing dimers on {y,alpha} and {z,beta} with exactly one inter-wing transition. Cyclically, the y-frame zero packet concatenates the wing dimers on {x,alpha} and {z,gamma} and has trimer {beta,delta,epsilon}; the z-frame zero packet concatenates the wing dimers on {x,beta} and {y,gamma} and has trimer {alpha,delta,epsilon}. Consequently either at least one of the three frames admits a positive-excess exact two-cover, or all three displayed zero-excess concatenated 4+3 packets exist.

## Hypotheses
Standing order-ten smallest-counterexample case; A,B are globally minimum-overlap with |A∩B|=3; C is a transversal support in R98 alternative (i).

## Scope
Finite support/deletion kernel for the transversal branch.

## Applicability
Use before reopening representative-dependent return machinery: positive excess supplies a crossing-rich frame; failure of positive excess leaves the explicit three-packet equality kernel.

## Persistence
The three physical deletion frames and their zero-excess packets are support-level; sigma remains representative-relative to the chosen exact cover.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not claim that positive excess itself gives overlap descent, nor that the simultaneous three-packet equality kernel is already impossible.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** superseded
- **Lifecycle note:** Transversal three-frame deficit kernel is conditional proof machinery under the minimum-overlap-three branch eliminated by C125/R127.
- **Curation note:** Transversal three-frame deficit kernel is conditional proof machinery under the minimum-overlap-three branch eliminated by C125/R127.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Verified after tightening each zero-excess packet: the four-component must concatenate the two frame wings with exactly one inter-wing transition, not merely have their four-vertex union as support.

## Proof
By R98, write C as two vertices of S=A∩B together with one vertex from each of U=A\B, V=B\A, and R=V(H)\(A∪B). Thus |A∩C|=|B∩C|=3. Since |A∩B|=3 is globally minimum, all three pairs A,B,C are minimum-overlap pairs. Let T=A∩B∩C, so |T|=2. Let x be the unique vertex of (A∩B)\C, y the unique vertex of (A∩C)\B, z the unique vertex of (B∩C)\A, and let alpha,beta,gamma be the private vertices of A,B,C respectively. The three supports are therefore A=T∪{x,y,alpha}, B=T∪{x,z,beta}, C=T∪{y,z,gamma}. Their union has eight vertices; denote the two exterior vertices by delta,epsilon.

Consider first the pair A,B. Its common triple is S_x=T∪{x}, its two wings are {y,alpha} and {z,beta}, and its R-block is {gamma,delta,epsilon}. By R5, H-S_x has an exact two-cover. More generally let T_x be any exact two-cover of H-S_x. R11 says its profile is 5+2 or 4+3. If it had a five-rail D, then R9 makes D a global-longest support in F. But D is disjoint from S_x and hence meets A only inside the two-vertex wing {y,alpha}, so |D∩A|≤2, contradicting global minimum overlap three. Therefore every T_x has profile 4+3.

For the physical partition {{y,alpha},{z,beta},{gamma,delta,epsilon}}, the two wings have intrinsic path-cover number one and the R-block has intrinsic path-cover number one by R8. R7 therefore gives t=1+sigma with sigma≥0. If sigma=0, each class restriction is one path and there is exactly one inter-class transition. Since the cover profile is already 4+3, the only possible grouping is the union of the two two-vertex wings versus the three-vertex R-block. More precisely, the R-block is the tight-trimer component and the four-component concatenates the tight dimer on {y,alpha} with the tight dimer on {z,beta} using exactly one inter-wing transition. Conversely, an exact cover of precisely this form has minimal class restrictions and t=1, so sigma=0 by R7.

The identical argument for the pair A,C gives common triple S_y=T∪{y}, wings {x,alpha} and {z,gamma}, R-block {beta,delta,epsilon}, and its zero packet concatenates the two wing dimers with exactly one inter-wing transition while {beta,delta,epsilon} is the trimer component. For B,C one gets S_z=T∪{z}, wings {x,beta} and {y,gamma}, R-block {alpha,delta,epsilon}, with the analogous one-transition wing concatenation and trimer component.

Finally, if any of the three frames admits an exact two-cover with sigma≥1, the first alternative of the claimed dichotomy holds. Otherwise every exact two-cover in each frame has sigma=0. By R5 at least one exact two-cover exists in each frame, so the corresponding canonical zero packet exists in all three frames. This proves the three-frame deficit kernel.

# R102 — Transversal equality-kernel four-witness shields

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Assume the transversal branch and the simultaneous zero-excess alternative of R101, with A=T∪{x,y,alpha}, B=T∪{x,z,beta}, C=T∪{y,z,gamma}. Let Q_x,Q_y,Q_z be the three zero-excess tight four-path components on W_x={y,alpha,z,beta}, W_y={x,alpha,z,gamma}, W_z={x,beta,y,gamma}. Then for every w in D_x={x,gamma,delta,epsilon}, the five-set W_x∪{w} supports no tight five-path. Cyclically, W_y∪{w} is non-Hamiltonian for every w in D_y={y,beta,delta,epsilon}, and W_z∪{w} is non-Hamiltonian for every w in D_z={z,alpha,delta,epsilon}. In particular, for any chosen ordering Q_i=(q1,q2,q3,q4) of one of the three zero-excess four-paths and every w in D_i, both direct endpoint attachments (w,q1,q2) and (q3,q4,w) are bad, hence the reverse endpoint turns (q2,q1,w) and (w,q4,q3) are tight.

## Hypotheses
Standing order-ten smallest-counterexample case; R98 transversal branch; simultaneous zero-excess alternative in R101.

## Scope
Finite equality kernel of the transversal branch.

## Applicability
Use as the labeled orientation package for attacking the simultaneous three-packet equality kernel. The two common witnesses delta,epsilon belong to all three shields.

## Persistence
Non-Hamiltonicity of the five-sets is support-level. The endpoint reverse turns are relative to the chosen zero-excess four-path ordering but are graph-intrinsic once that ordering is fixed.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not claim the shield alone is inconsistent, nor that reverse endpoint turns automatically concatenate into a five-path.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** superseded
- **Lifecycle note:** Transversal equality-kernel four-witness shields are conditional descendants of the branch eliminated by C125/R127.
- **Curation note:** Transversal equality-kernel four-witness shields are conditional descendants of the branch eliminated by C125/R127.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Verified. Minimum-overlap three makes each listed five-set non-Hamiltonian; endpoint badness and reverse tightness follow exactly from the displayed four-path and R3.

## Proof
Work in the x-frame; the y- and z-frames are cyclic. R101 supplies a tight four-path Q_x on W_x={y,alpha,z,beta}. Let w∈D_x={x,gamma,delta,epsilon}. Suppose W_x∪{w} supported a tight five-path. By R9 its order five is globally longest, so its support belongs to F. If w=x, then (W_x∪{x})∩C={y,z}; if w=gamma, then (W_x∪{gamma})∩A={y,alpha}; if w is delta or epsilon, then (W_x∪{w})∩C={y,z}. In every case this new support has intersection two with an existing longest support, contradicting that A,B,C are pairwise globally minimum-overlap supports of overlap three by R100. Thus every W_x∪{w} is non-Hamiltonian. Now choose an ordering Q_x=(q1,q2,q3,q4). If (w,q1,q2) were tight, adjoining w at the left would give a tight five-path on W_x∪{w}; similarly, if (q3,q4,w) were tight, adjoining w at the right would do so. Both are therefore bad. By boundary antisymmetry R3, their complete reversals (q2,q1,w) and (w,q4,q3) are tight. The same argument after cyclic permutation proves the y- and z-frame statements.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED/R102.md -->

# R1026 — The monotone minimum five-cell residue has exactly 43 labelled forests and at most 256 directed rail candidates

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Retain the accepted crossed five-cell frame R862/R865 with D={q_2,q_{m-2}}, W=H-D, and cells G_0=Q[0,1], G_1=Q[3,m-3], G_2=Q[m-1,m], G_3={a,c}, G_4={b,z}. Let T be an exact two-cover of W with sigma_G(T)=0 and c_X(T) in {2,3}, and work in the monotone branch of accepted R867, outside the explicit R435 reverse-state, reverse-trimer/contact, or vertex-simple tight-cycle outputs. Take the contracted forest F_T with its cell labels; a configuration is its labelled edge set, and a rail reading is displayed monotone in Q whenever that rail contains at least two Q-blocks.

Then F_T is exactly one of 43 labelled configurations: 25 with c_X=2 and 18 with c_X=3, distributed over the six R866 shapes as A:6, B:4, C:12, D:3 and E:12, F:6. The complete list is:
(A) [G0 | G3-G1-G2-G4], [G0 | G4-G1-G2-G3], [G1 | G3-G0-G2-G4], [G1 | G4-G0-G2-G3], [G2 | G3-G0-G1-G4], [G2 | G4-G0-G1-G3];
(B) [G0-G1-G3-G2 | G4], [G0-G1-G4-G2 | G3], [G0-G3-G1-G2 | G4], [G0-G4-G1-G2 | G3];
(C) [G0-G1-G3 | G2-G4], [G0-G1-G4 | G2-G3], [G0-G2-G3 | G1-G4], [G0-G2-G4 | G1-G3], [G0-G3 | G1-G2-G4], [G0-G3 | G4-G1-G2], [G0-G4 | G1-G2-G3], [G0-G4 | G3-G1-G2], [G1-G3 | G4-G0-G2], [G1-G4 | G3-G0-G2], [G2-G3 | G4-G0-G1], [G2-G4 | G3-G0-G1];
(D) [G0-G1 | G3-G2-G4], [G0-G2 | G3-G1-G4], [G1-G2 | G3-G0-G4];
(E) [G0 | G1-G3-G2-G4], [G0 | G1-G4-G2-G3], [G0 | G3-G1-G4-G2], [G0 | G4-G1-G3-G2], [G0-G3-G1-G4 | G2], [G0-G3-G2-G4 | G1], [G0-G4-G1-G3 | G2], [G0-G4-G2-G3 | G1], [G1 | G3-G0-G4-G2], [G1 | G4-G0-G3-G2], [G2 | G3-G0-G4-G1], [G2 | G4-G0-G3-G1];
(F) [G0-G3 | G1-G4-G2], [G0-G3-G1 | G2-G4], [G0-G3-G2 | G1-G4], [G0-G4 | G1-G3-G2], [G0-G4-G1 | G2-G3], [G0-G4-G2 | G1-G3].

Every Q-Q adjacency in the list is one of G_0G_1, G_1G_2, G_0G_2, realized respectively by the named R867 transitions u q_3, q_{m-3}s, u s.

For the directed rail refinement, the labelled edge set together with the two X-dimer internal orientations does not always determine T. In shapes A, B, and E, every nonsingleton rail contains at least two Q-blocks, so R867 forces its direction; these contribute 6+4+12=22 configurations with one admissible component orientation. In shapes C, D, and F, exactly one nonsingleton rail contains at most one Q-block, so that rail has two admissible directions while the other rail is Q-monotone and forced; these contribute 12+3+6=21 configurations with two admissible component orientations. Since each of the two physical X-dimer blocks has at most two internal orientations, the entire residue has at most 4(22+2*21)=256 explicitly named ordered rail-pair candidates.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in the crossed beyond-order-ten frame. Use accepted current revisions R862, R865, R866, and R867, with the R867 monotone branch as stated.

## Scope
Finite labelled classification of the sigma_G(T)=0 minimum five-cell residue with c_X(T) in {2,3}, together with the corrected directed rail-orientation upper bound.

## Applicability
Provides an exact 43-edge-set audit key and a finite directed candidate pool of size at most 256 for any later local check of this residue.

## Persistence
The 43-count depends only on the accepted five-cell block structure/no-X-X rule, the six-shape classification, and Q-monotonicity. The 256 bound additionally records the one residual component-direction bit in shapes C, D, and F.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
No realizability claim is made for any of the 43 edge sets or 256 directed candidates. In particular, this result does not claim the retired R685 bound of 172, and it does not claim that a labelled configuration plus the two X-dimer orientations uniquely determines T.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** active
- **Lifecycle note:** Corrected replacement for retired C542/R685 after the scoped audit failure of the 172-candidate assertion.
- **Review status:** pending
- **Review note:** Pending independent review. Constructed specifically to repair the scoped R685 failure while preserving its independently verified 43-case core.

## Proof
Let Q={G0,G1,G2} with fixed order G0<G1<G2 and X={G3,G4}. By R866, every contracted configuration in this residue is one of six two-component path-forest shapes A--F, with no X-X edge. By R867, on every oriented rail containing at least two Q-blocks, the Q labels must occur in increasing order. A configuration is the labelled edge set, so reversing a displayed rail does not create a second configuration.

We count each R866 shape directly.

A: X-Q-Q-X plus an isolated Q. Choose the isolated Q in 3 ways. The two labelled X vertices can occupy the two endpoint roles in 2 ways. Hence 3*2=6.

B: Q-Q-X-Q plus an isolated X. Choose which X is isolated in 2 ways. On the long rail the three Q labels are forced in increasing order, and the nonisolated X can occupy either of the two gaps between consecutive Q blocks. Hence 2*2=4.

C: Q-Q-X plus Q-X. Choose the lone Q belonging to the two-vertex component in 3 ways. Choose which labelled X belongs to that component in 2 ways. On the three-vertex component, the remaining X may attach to either endpoint of the Q-Q edge in 2 ways. Hence 3*2*2=12.

D: Q-Q plus X-Q-X. Choose the Q lying between the two X vertices in 3 ways; the other two Q vertices form the Q-Q component. Swapping the two X endpoint roles does not change the labelled edge set because both X-Q edges are present. Hence 3.

E: X-Q-X-Q plus an isolated Q. Choose the isolated Q in 3 ways. For the two remaining ordered Q vertices, choose which X lies between them in 2 ways and choose whether the other X attaches at the low-Q or high-Q outer endpoint in 2 ways. Hence 3*2*2=12.

F: Q-X-Q plus Q-X. Choose the Q on the two-vertex component in 3 ways and choose which X lies on that component in 2 ways. The remaining X is then forced between the other two Q vertices. Hence 3*2=6.

Thus there are exactly 6+4+12+3+12+6=43 labelled edge sets, with 25 in c_X=2 (A--D) and 18 in c_X=3 (E--F). The constructive choices above give exactly the displayed list in the statement, so the list is exhaustive and duplicate-free. R867 also gives the only possible Q-Q transitions: G0G1, G1G2, G0G2, realized by u q3, q_{m-3}s, and u s respectively.

It remains to count directed rail readings correctly. If a nonsingleton rail contains at least two Q-blocks, R867 fixes its direction because the Q labels must increase. Singleton rails have no directional choice. Therefore every A, B, and E configuration has a unique admissible component orientation. Their number is 6+4+12=22.

In each C configuration, the Q-X component contains only one Q-block; in each D configuration, the X-Q-X component contains only one Q-block; and in each F configuration, the Q-X component contains only one Q-block. That component is nonsingleton but R867 imposes no direction because there are not two Q labels to compare. Its reversal gives the second admissible component orientation. The other component has at least two Q-blocks and is forced. Hence every C, D, and F configuration has exactly two admissible component orientations, for 12+3+6=21 such configurations.

Finally each physical X-dimer G3 and G4 has at most two internal orientations. Thus each component-oriented configuration lifts to at most four ordered rail-pair candidates. The total is therefore at most

    4*(22 + 2*21) = 256.

This also pinpoints the error in retired R685: the extra component-direction bit in shapes C, D, and F was omitted. No realizability is asserted, so seam constraints may reduce the 256 candidates further.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED/R1026.md -->

# R103 — Transversal zero-packet paired-trimer reroot symmetry

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Assume the transversal branch and the simultaneous zero-excess alternative of R101. In the x-frame let S_x=T∪{x}, let G_x={gamma,delta,epsilon}, and let Q_x be the zero-excess tight four-path on {y,alpha,z,beta}. Choose any tight trimer orientation on S_x. Then Q_x, G_x, S_x form a spanning minimum three-cover. Consequently Q_x∪G_x is an exact two-cover of H-S_x and, in the same displayed representative, Q_x∪S_x is an exact two-cover of H-G_x. Cyclically the same holds for (S_y,G_y,Q_y) and (S_z,G_z,Q_z), where G_y={beta,delta,epsilon} and G_z={alpha,delta,epsilon}. Thus each zero-excess four-rail is literally preserved under exchanging its deleted common triple with its opposite R-trimer.

## Hypotheses
Standing order-ten smallest-counterexample case; R101 simultaneous zero-excess alternative.

## Scope
Exact representative-level reroot symmetry inside the transversal equality kernel.

## Applicability
Provides three paired deletion roots sharing the same four-rails; useful for applying deletion or return theorems from either trimer side without changing the four-path representative.

## Persistence
The preserved four-path and the two exact two-covers are representative-level facts after a trimer orientation of S_i is chosen; their physical supports are fixed.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert compatibility of the chosen S_x,S_y,S_z trimer orientations across the three different displayed covers, and does not create a spanning two-cover by itself.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Order-ten transversal zero-packet reroot symmetry. Representative-rich but zero-consumer special-case interface; preserve in historical proof architecture.
- **Curation note:** Order-ten transversal zero-packet reroot symmetry. Representative-rich but zero-consumer special-case interface; preserve in historical proof architecture.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Verified. The three disjoint tight components span all ten vertices; counterexample status makes the three-cover minimum, and R22 gives the exact paired reroots with the four-rail preserved.

## Proof
Again use the x-frame; the other two are cyclic. R101 supplies an exact two-cover Q_x∪G_x of H-S_x, where Q_x is a tight four-path and G_x is a tight trimer. By R8, S_x admits a tight trimer orientation. Hence Q_x,G_x,S_x are three pairwise disjoint tight paths covering all ten vertices. Because the standing graph is a counterexample to spanning two-cover, this displayed three-cover is minimum. Apply componentwise exact re-rooting R22. Deleting the S_x component leaves Q_x∪G_x as an exact two-cover of H-S_x, while deleting the G_x component leaves Q_x∪S_x as an exact two-cover of H-G_x, with Q_x literally unchanged in the same displayed representative. Apply the same argument to the y- and z-frame zero packets.

# R104 — Transversal core-singleton eight-support classification

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Assume the transversal branch with A=T∪{x,y,alpha}, B=T∪{x,z,beta}, C=T∪{y,z,gamma} and T={t,tprime}. Fix one core vertex t and delete it. In every exact two-cover of H-{t}, the five-vertex rail has a support D in F that necessarily contains the other core vertex tprime. Writing E=D-{tprime}, the four-set E is one of exactly eight possibilities: {x,y,z,w} for w∈{alpha,beta,gamma,delta,epsilon}, or {x,y,beta,gamma}, or {x,z,alpha,gamma}, or {y,z,alpha,beta}. In particular every prescribed-core-singleton deletion produces a new global-longest support omitting t, containing tprime, and meeting at least two of A,B,C in exactly three vertices.

## Hypotheses
Standing order-ten smallest-counterexample case; R98 transversal branch, in the symmetric coordinates of R100.

## Scope
Pure support classification for singleton deletions at the two-vertex common core of a transversal triangle.

## Applicability
Use to replace arbitrary singleton-root search at t∈T by an eight-case support family. The same list applies symmetrically after exchanging t and tprime.

## Persistence
The classification concerns the physical support of the five-rail; orientations and the complementary four-rail remain representative-dependent.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not claim every one of the eight supports occurs, nor that the supports obtained from deleting t and tprime are unique.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Eight-support classification for one order-ten transversal singleton deletion. Finite special-case enumeration with no live consumer; retire from ordinary search.
- **Curation note:** Eight-support classification for one order-ten transversal singleton deletion. Finite special-case enumeration with no live consumer; retire from ordinary search.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Verified. R46 forces the surviving core vertex into the five-rail; the three 2-of-3 overlap inequalities have exactly the eight listed four-set solutions.

## Proof
Let T={t,tprime} and delete t. By R46, every exact two-cover of H-{t} has a five-vertex rail whose support D is a global-longest support, hence D∈F. By R100, A,B,C are pairwise globally minimum-overlap supports with minimum overlap three, so |D∩A|,|D∩B|,|D∩C|≥3. Suppose tprime∉D. Since t∉D as well, meeting A=T∪{x,y,alpha} in at least three forces {x,y,alpha}⊆D; meeting B forces {x,z,beta}⊆D; meeting C forces {y,z,gamma}⊆D. Their union has six vertices {x,y,z,alpha,beta,gamma}, impossible because |D|=5. Thus tprime∈D. Put E=D-{tprime}, so |E|=4. The three overlap inequalities become |E∩{x,y,alpha}|≥2, |E∩{x,z,beta}|≥2, and |E∩{y,z,gamma}|≥2. If E contains x,y,z, its fourth vertex may be any one of alpha,beta,gamma,delta,epsilon, giving five possibilities. Otherwise E contains at most two of x,y,z. It cannot contain at most one: summing the three displayed lower bounds would require at least six incidences, while each Greek vertex alpha,beta,gamma contributes to only one inequality and each of x,y,z to two, so four vertices with at most one of x,y,z contribute at most five. Hence E contains exactly two of x,y,z. If they are x,y, the first inequality is already paid but the B and C inequalities each need one more incidence beyond x and y respectively, forcing beta and gamma; thus E={x,y,beta,gamma}. Similarly the pairs x,z and y,z force E={x,z,alpha,gamma} and E={y,z,alpha,beta}. This gives exactly the eight listed possibilities. Direct inspection shows each listed D meets at least two of A,B,C in exactly three vertices. Finally D omits t whereas A,B,C all contain t, so D is a new support distinct from A,B,C.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED/R104.md -->

# R105 — Common-triple deletion longest-path cap

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Let A,B be globally minimum-overlap longest-five supports with |A∩B|=3 and S=A∩B. Then H-S has no tight path of order five. Hence every exact two-cover of H-S has the 4+3 profile from R99, and if Q=(q1,q2,q3,q4) is its four-path and K its three-path, then for every k in K the direct endpoint triples (k,q1,q2) and (q3,q4,k) are bad, so by boundary antisymmetry the reverse triples (q2,q1,k) and (k,q4,q3) are tight.

## Hypotheses
Standing order-ten smallest-counterexample case; A,B are a globally minimum-overlap pair with overlap three.

## Scope
Minimum-overlap common-triple deletion frame.

## Applicability
Use in either zero- or positive-excess faces of R99.

## Persistence
The path-order-five obstruction is support-level; endpoint turns are relative to the chosen four-path ordering.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
No claim about internal attachments or immediate two-cover closure.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** superseded
- **Lifecycle note:** Common-triple deletion longest-path cap is branch-local minimum-overlap-three machinery and no longer needs independent canonical visibility after C125/R127.
- **Curation note:** Common-triple deletion longest-path cap is branch-local minimum-overlap-three machinery and no longer needs independent canonical visibility after C125/R127.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Verified. Any order-five path in H-S would be global-longest yet intersect A in at most two vertices, contradicting minimum overlap three; endpoint reversals follow from R3.

## Proof
Suppose H-S contained a tight path P of order five. By R9, order five is globally longest, so supp(P) belongs to the longest-five support family. Since supp(P) is disjoint from S and A=S union (A-S) with |A-S|=2, we have |supp(P)∩A| at most 2, contradicting that A belongs to a globally minimum-overlap pair of value 3. Thus H-S has no tight five-path. By R99, every exact two-cover of H-S has profile 4+3. Let Q=(q1,q2,q3,q4) be its four-path and K its three-path. For k in K, if (k,q1,q2) were tight then (k,q1,q2,q3,q4) would be a forbidden five-path in H-S; similarly if (q3,q4,k) were tight then (q1,q2,q3,q4,k) would be a forbidden five-path. Both triples are bad. Boundary antisymmetry R3 gives the tight reversals (q2,q1,k) and (k,q4,q3).

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED/R105.md -->

# R106 — Transversal triangle common-marker triple root

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
In the transversal branch coordinates A=T∪{x,y,alpha}, B=T∪{x,z,beta}, C=T∪{y,z,gamma}, with exterior pair M={delta,epsilon}, deleting M admits three exact 5+3 two-covers with long rails A,B,C respectively. Namely the complementary three-sets are K_A={z,beta,gamma}, K_B={y,alpha,gamma}, and K_C={x,alpha,beta}; each admits a tight trimer orientation, so A∪K_A, B∪K_B, and C∪K_C are exact two-covers of H-M. Thus the same physical exterior marker supports three distinct globally longest 5+3 roots forming the symmetric minimum-overlap triangle.

## Hypotheses
Standing order-ten smallest-counterexample case; R98 transversal branch in the R100 coordinates.

## Scope
Pure support-level common-marker normalization.

## Applicability
Use to apply fixed-exterior-pair or gap-two pivot theorems to A,B,C over the same physical marker without changing the deleted pair.

## Persistence
The three exact covers need not share one representative or compatible trimer orientations; only the physical marker and long-rail supports are common.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert simultaneous currentness of the three roots or any relation between their endpoint-pivot descendants.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** superseded
- **Lifecycle note:** Transversal common-marker triple root is a conditional normalization in the minimum-overlap-three branch eliminated by C125/R127.
- **Curation note:** Transversal common-marker triple root is a conditional normalization in the minimum-overlap-three branch eliminated by C125/R127.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Verified. In H-{delta,epsilon}, the complements of A,B,C are exactly the stated three-sets, each orientable as a tight trimer by R8.

## Proof
By R100, A=T∪{x,y,alpha}, B=T∪{x,z,beta}, C=T∪{y,z,gamma}, and the only vertices outside A∪B∪C are delta,epsilon. Hence M={delta,epsilon} is disjoint from A,B,C. In H-M, the complement of A is exactly {z,beta,gamma}; the complement of B is {y,alpha,gamma}; and the complement of C is {x,alpha,beta}. By R8 each of these three-sets admits a tight trimer orientation. Since A,B,C are supports of tight five-paths, pairing the corresponding five-path with the chosen complementary trimer gives an exact 5+3 two-cover of H-M in each case.

# R107 — Hub kernel radius-one-or-singleton-star compression

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Assume alternative (ii) of R98. Let X=U∪V and let W={w∈X : S∪{w,r}∈F for some r∈R}. Then W is nonempty and |W|≤3. Exactly one of the following hub-generated outcomes holds. (a) There exist a hub H=S∪{w,r}∈F, a support D∈F omitting some s∈S, and P∈{A,B} such that H=P-{p}+{x} and D=P-{q}+{y} for distinct p,q∈P and distinct x,y∉P. Thus the hub kernel itself contains an actual radius-one replacement configuration. (b) No such hub-generated pair exists; after possibly exchanging U and V, write U={w,u} with W={w}. Then every support in F omitting s∈S is the single set D_s=(S\\{s})∪{w}∪V, and for every r∈R the hub H_r=S∪{w,r} belongs to F. Equivalently, all S-omitting supports form the B-star B-{s}+{w}, while all R-touching supports form the A-star A-{u}+{r}.

## Hypotheses
Standing order-ten smallest-counterexample case; A,B are a globally minimum-overlap pair with |A∩B|=3, and the hub alternative (ii) of R98 holds.

## Scope
Pure support-incidence compression inside the R98 hub branch.

## Applicability
Use before reopening representative-dependent return or seam machinery. Outcome (a) feeds the existing radius-one common-frame machinery; outcome (b) is the only support-level hub kernel not already forcing such a configuration.

## Persistence
The conclusion is graph-intrinsic because it concerns only memberships of the global longest-five support family F.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not claim that the singleton-star kernel is impossible, nor that the radius-one outcome alone closes the order-ten case.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** superseded
- **Lifecycle note:** Hub-kernel compression is valid conditional branch mathematics, but the entire minimum-overlap-three butterfly branch is eliminated by C125/R127.
- **Curation note:** Hub-kernel compression is valid conditional branch mathematics, but the entire minimum-overlap-three butterfly branch is eliminated by C125/R127.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Verified. R13 and R98 force W nonempty; excluding the radius-one pair forces at most one hub wing per side, excludes a cross-side two-set W, hence W is singleton and uniquely forces the two stated support stars.

## Proof
Assume the hub alternative (ii) of R98. Put X=U∪V and define W as in R107. By R13, union F=V(H), so some support meets R; hence W is nonempty. Also intersection F is empty, so for each s∈S there exists at least one D∈F with s∉D. By R98 every such D is R-free, contains exactly S\\{s}, and has a three-element wing set T(D)⊆X meeting both U and V and containing every element of W. Therefore |W|≤3.

Suppose outcome (a) does not occur. Fix w∈W∩U, if this set is nonempty, and write U={w,u}. Choose a hub H=S∪{w,r}∈F witnessing w∈W. If some S-omitting support D has u∈T(D), then because |T(D)|=3 and T(D) meets V, necessarily T(D)={w,u,v} for some v∈V. Thus
H=A-{u}+{r},
D=A-{s}+{v}.
Here u and s are distinct vertices of A, while r and v are distinct vertices outside A. Hence H and D are exactly the hub-generated radius-one pair in outcome (a), contradiction. Consequently, under failure of (a), every S-omitting D excludes u. In particular W∩U cannot contain both vertices of U, because every D contains W. By symmetry |W∩V|≤1.

If |W|=2, it therefore has one element w_U∈U and one element w_V∈V. Take any S-omitting D. Its wing triple T(D) contains w_U,w_V and one further wing z. If z is the other U-vertex, the preceding argument with w_U gives outcome (a); if z is the other V-vertex, the symmetric argument with w_V gives outcome (a). Both are impossible. Hence |W|≠2. Since W is nonempty and the two-per-side cases already exclude |W|=3, we get |W|=1.

After exchanging U and V if necessary, write W={w} with U={w,u}. For every S-omitting D, the preceding no-(a) argument forces u∉T(D). Since T(D) has size three, contains w, and lies in the four-element wing set X=U∪V, it follows that T(D)={w}∪V. Thus every support omitting a given s is the same set
D_s=(S\\{s})∪{w}∪V=B-{s}+{w}.
Such a support exists for each s by intersection F=empty, so these are exactly the S-omitting supports.

Finally fix r∈R. By union F=V(H), some support C∈F contains r. In the hub alternative every R-touching support is S∪{w',r'} with w'∈W and r'∈R. Since W={w} and C contains r, C=S∪{w,r}=A-{u}+{r}. Hence H_r belongs to F for every r∈R, and every R-touching support has this form. This is outcome (b). Outcomes (a) and (b) are mutually exclusive by the opening clause of (b), completing the proof.

# R108 — Singleton-star hub kernel has an abstract support model

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
The pure five-set incidence constraints used in R13 and the hub alternative of R98 do not by themselves contradict the singleton-star outcome of R107. Concretely, on disjoint blocks S={s1,s2,s3}, U={w,u}, V={v1,v2}, R={r1,r2,r3}, the family F0={A=S∪U, B=S∪V}∪{H_i=S∪{w,r_i}:1≤i≤3}∪{D_j=(S\\{s_j})∪{w,v1,v2}:1≤j≤3} consists of eight 5-sets, has union S∪U∪V∪R, has empty total intersection, and every two members intersect in at least three vertices. Its minimum pairwise intersection is three, every R-touching member is a singleton-wing hub, and every S-omitting member is exactly the forced singleton-star support from R107.

## Hypotheses
Abstract set-system statement using the same block cardinalities as the standing overlap-three butterfly.

## Scope
Negative-space sanity check for the R98/R107 support-incidence kernel; no boundary-tournament realizability is asserted.

## Applicability
Use to rule out attempts to close the exceptional singleton-star kernel using only support sizes, pairwise intersection lower bounds, union coverage, or empty total intersection. Additional tight-path/deletion/orientation information is necessary.

## Persistence
Pure finite set-system construction.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert that F0 is realizable as the actual global-longest support family of a Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Singleton-star hub support countermodel belongs to the retired minimum-overlap-three/order-ten proof branch; preserve historically, retire canonically.
- **Curation note:** Singleton-star hub support countermodel belongs to the retired minimum-overlap-three/order-ten proof branch; preserve historically, retire canonically.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Verified finite set-system construction. All eight members have size five, union all ten vertices, empty total intersection, pairwise intersections 3 or 4, and exactly the claimed hub/star incidence pattern.

## Proof
Let F0 consist of A,B,H_1,H_2,H_3,D_1,D_2,D_3 as stated. Every member has size five. The union is all of S∪U∪V∪R: A covers S,U; B covers V; and the three hubs cover R. The total intersection is empty because A∩B=S while D_j omits s_j for j=1,2,3.

It remains to check pairwise intersections. We have |A∩B|=3. For every i,j,
|A∩H_i|=|S∪{w}|=4,
|A∩D_j|=|(S\\{s_j})∪{w}|=3,
|B∩H_i|=|S|=3,
|B∩D_j|=|(S\\{s_j})∪V|=4.
For i≠k, H_i∩H_k=S∪{w}, of size four. For every i,j, H_i∩D_j=(S\\{s_j})∪{w}, of size three. For j≠k, D_j∩D_k=(S\\{s_j,s_k})∪{w,v1,v2}, of size four. Thus every pair meets in at least three vertices, and several pairs meet in exactly three, so the minimum pairwise intersection is exactly three.

Finally, only the H_i meet R, and each is S∪{w,r_i}; hence the hub-wing set is W={w}. A member omits s_j∈S exactly when it is D_j, and D_j=(S\\{s_j})∪{w}∪V, exactly the singleton-star pattern of R107. Therefore the incidence axioms alone admit the exceptional kernel. The construction makes no claim of realizability by tight-path supports in an actual boundary tournament.
