# R110 — Transversal all-pivot four-family common-mate lift

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Assume the R106 transversal minimum-overlap triangle with common exterior marker M={delta,epsilon}, and assume that each of its three exact 5+3 roots lies in the double-transfer pivot face of R50. Then for each marker vertex m in M and each sign polarity s, there are three graph-intrinsic signed terminal-dimer supports D_A(m,s), D_B(m,s), D_C(m,s), one coming from the m-folded longest path associated to each of the roots A,B,C, such that all three have polarity s and the same witness m*=M\{m}. Moreover there exists one graph-intrinsic support E(m,s) of the opposite polarity such that E(m,s) forms a balanced pair with each of D_A(m,s), D_B(m,s), D_C(m,s). Thus the all-pivot triangle carries four three-root common-mate support families, indexed by the two physical marker vertices and the two polarities.

## Hypotheses
Standing order-ten smallest-counterexample case; R106 transversal triangle; for all three common-marker roots, the R50 reverse-four-path alternative is not used and the double-transfer pivot face holds.

## Scope
Graph-intrinsic support/sign compilation in the all-pivot transversal branch. The three members of a family need not be distinct physical dimers.

## Applicability
Use before opening separate payment descendants. It synchronizes the three common-marker roots at the signed-support level and exposes a shared opposite mate for every fixed marker/polarity family.

## Persistence
The fold-derived signed terminal-dimer systems are graph-intrinsic by R51/R52, and the R40 common opposite support is a graph-intrinsic pre-payment certificate.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
The four family actualizations may use different auxiliary marker dimers and may produce different opposite supports. No simultaneous currentness of the three folded longest paths is asserted. No coupling of later paid descendants is asserted, and the theorem does not by itself close the conjecture.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Order-ten all-pivot transversal common-mate family lift. Rich certificate production but zero-consumer and superseded strategically by later general signed-pair interaction machinery; preserve historically.
- **Curation note:** Order-ten all-pivot transversal common-mate family lift. Rich certificate production but zero-consumer and superseded strategically by later general signed-pair interaction machinery; preserve historically.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Verified as stated. For each fixed marker m and polarity s, R51/R52 provide three graph-intrinsic terminal dimer supports with common witness m*. Their union has size at most 6 and m* lies outside all three, so among 10 vertices at least 3 are simultaneously outside the supports and witness. A physical dimer on two spare vertices is therefore a nontrivial marker path disjoint from the entire family and m*. R40 applies once and yields one common opposite-polarity support paired with all three family members. The four marker/polarity instances are separate; the exclusions correctly avoid simultaneous-currentness or coupled-payment claims.

## Proof
Let the three R106 roots be indexed by i in {A,B,C}, all with common exterior pair M={delta,epsilon}, and assume all three are in the R50 double-transfer pivot face. Fix m in M and write m* for the other marker vertex. By R51, folding the i-th pivot root through m produces a globally longest folded five-path whose terminal signed-dimer system has as common witnesses the opposite three-vertex shadow together with m*. In particular m* is a named witness for that system. By R52, the two terminal physical dimers of this folded longest path have opposite polarities for every common witness. Hence, for each polarity s, choose the terminal dimer D_i(m,s) having polarity s with witness m*. R51 makes these signed systems graph-intrinsic, so for fixed (m,s) the three supports D_A(m,s),D_B(m,s),D_C(m,s) are three graph-intrinsic supports with the same polarity and the same witness m*.

Each D_i(m,s) is a physical dimer, so the union of the three supports has size at most 6. A sign witness is outside its support, hence m* is outside all three D_i(m,s). Therefore at most 7 of the 10 vertices are occupied by the three supports together with m*, leaving at least three spare vertices. Choose any two spare vertices as a physical dimer J. A physical dimer is a nontrivial marker path, and J is disjoint from every D_i(m,s) and from the common witness m*. The hypotheses of R40 now hold for the three-support family. One test of J therefore creates a single opposite-polarity support E(m,s) such that each D_i(m,s) forms a balanced pair with E(m,s).

This argument is independent for s equal to either polarity and for m equal to delta or epsilon, yielding four three-root common-mate family certificates. R40 explicitly keeps later payments of the several balanced pairs as separate descendants, so no simultaneous-payment claim is made.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED/R110.md -->

# R111 — Transversal neighboring-root symmetric-difference shield bridge

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Assume the R106 transversal triangle and the simultaneous zero-excess alternative of R101. Write K_A={z,beta,gamma}, K_B={y,alpha,gamma}, K_C={x,alpha,beta} for the three short trimers of the common-marker roots, and W_x={y,alpha,z,beta}, W_y={x,alpha,z,gamma}, W_z={x,beta,y,gamma} for the three zero-packet four-rail supports. Then K_A∩K_B={gamma} and K_A△K_B=W_x; K_A∩K_C={beta} and K_A△K_C=W_y; K_B∩K_C={alpha} and K_B△K_C=W_z. Moreover the corresponding W_i supports the R101 tight four-path Q_i and is shielded, in the sense of R102, by the shared short-trimer vertex, both common-marker vertices delta,epsilon, and the unique triangle wing vertex indexing that frame. Thus every neighboring pair of common-marker 5+3 roots has its short-trimer symmetric difference realized as exactly one shielded zero-packet four-rail.

## Hypotheses
Standing order-ten smallest-counterexample case; R106 transversal common-marker triangle; simultaneous zero-excess alternative of R101.

## Scope
Exact interface between the three R106 short trimers and the R101/R102 equality-kernel four-rails.

## Applicability
Use as the canonical coupling interface when comparing one common-marker root with either neighboring root, especially before analyzing an R50 reverse-four outcome: the relevant neighboring short trimers differ on a pre-existing tight four-rail with common-marker endpoint shields.

## Persistence
The set identities and short-trimer supports are graph-intrinsic. The displayed Q_i path orientation and its reverse endpoint turns are relative to the chosen zero-excess packet, exactly as in R102.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert that an R50 reverse-four path automatically aligns with Q_i, does not kill any status orbit by itself, and does not assert simultaneous currentness of the three R106 roots.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Order-ten symmetric-difference/shield bridge between neighboring transversal roots. Exact coordinate lemma but no live consumer; historical specialization rather than current spine.
- **Curation note:** Order-ten symmetric-difference/shield bridge between neighboring transversal roots. Exact coordinate lemma but no live consumer; historical specialization rather than current spine.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Verified exactly. The R106 trimer intersections and symmetric differences compute to the claimed singleton/W_i pairs; R101 supplies Q_x,Q_y,Q_z on those W_i in the simultaneous zero-excess face; R102 shields each W_i by precisely the shared trimer singleton, the indexing wing vertex, and delta,epsilon. Exclusions correctly avoid any reverse-four alignment or simultaneous-currentness strengthening.

## Proof
From R106, K_A={z,beta,gamma}, K_B={y,alpha,gamma}, K_C={x,alpha,beta}. Therefore K_A∩K_B={gamma} and K_A△K_B={z,beta,y,alpha}=W_x. Similarly K_A∩K_C={beta} and K_A△K_C={z,gamma,x,alpha}=W_y, while K_B∩K_C={alpha} and K_B△K_C={y,gamma,x,beta}=W_z. By R101, in the simultaneous zero-excess face these three four-sets support the tight four-paths Q_x,Q_y,Q_z. By R102, W_x is shielded by D_x={x,gamma,delta,epsilon}, W_y by D_y={y,beta,delta,epsilon}, and W_z by D_z={z,alpha,delta,epsilon}. In each case the singleton K-pair intersection is one of the shield witnesses and delta,epsilon are the two common-marker witnesses. This proves all asserted identities and the shield interface.

# R112 — Transversal zero-excess shield four-family common-mate lift

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Assume the simultaneous zero-excess transversal kernel of R102. For each i in {x,y,z}, fix an ordering Q_i=(q_{i1},q_{i2},q_{i3},q_{i4}) of its tight four-path component, and let M={delta,epsilon}. For each w in M, the three oriented left endpoint dimers L_i(w)=(q_{i2},q_{i1}) are graph-intrinsic signed supports of one common polarity with common witness w, while the three oriented right endpoint dimers R_i(w)=(q_{i4},q_{i3}) are graph-intrinsic signed supports of the opposite polarity with the same witness w. For each fixed w, there exists one graph-intrinsic opposite-polarity support E_L(w) that forms a balanced pair with every L_i(w), and separately one graph-intrinsic opposite-polarity support E_R(w) that forms a balanced pair with every R_i(w). Hence the zero-excess equality kernel carries four three-shield common-mate support families, indexed by the two common marker witnesses and the two endpoint sides.

## Hypotheses
Standing order-ten smallest-counterexample case and the R102 simultaneous zero-excess transversal kernel, with one fixed ordering chosen for each of Q_x,Q_y,Q_z.

## Scope
Graph-intrinsic signed-support compilation directly from the three R102 shields. This is a pre-payment statement and does not require the R50 pivot/reverse classification or the R51/R52 fold machinery.

## Applicability
Use before opening local return or payment descendants. It provides the common-mate fan interface directly in the zero-excess kernel and is a bridge from the common delta/epsilon endpoint shields to support-family actualization.

## Persistence
For a fixed ordering of each Q_i, the reverse endpoint turns and resulting signed dimers are graph-intrinsic by R102. The common opposite supports supplied by R40 are graph-intrinsic pre-payment certificates.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
The three Q_i need not be simultaneously current. The supports within one family need not be distinct. E_L(w) and E_R(w), and the supports for delta versus epsilon, need not coincide. No coupling of later paid descendants is asserted, and no spanning two-cover follows from this lemma alone.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** superseded
- **Lifecycle note:** Zero-excess shield four-family common-mate lift is conditional transversal machinery under a branch eliminated wholesale by C125/R127.
- **Curation note:** Zero-excess shield four-family common-mate lift is conditional transversal machinery under a branch eliminated wholesale by C125/R127.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Verified. R102 supplies, for either common marker witness w and each ordered Q_i, tight reverse endpoint trimers (q2,q1,w) and (w,q4,q3). The accepted trimer sign convention makes (q2,q1) uniformly the first-terminal polarity with witness w and (q4,q3) uniformly the opposite second-terminal polarity with witness w. Each three-support family occupies at most six vertices and excludes w, leaving at least three spare vertices in order ten; a two-vertex spare marker is simultaneously disjoint from all family supports and w, so R40 yields one common opposite support for the family. Exclusions correctly avoid simultaneous-currentness/payment claims.

## Proof
Fix w in {delta,epsilon}. For i in {x,y,z}, write the chosen R102 four-path as Q_i=(q_{i1},q_{i2},q_{i3},q_{i4}). R102 says that the direct endpoint attachments (w,q_{i1},q_{i2}) and (q_{i3},q_{i4},w) are bad and therefore, by boundary antisymmetry, the reverse turns (q_{i2},q_{i1},w) and (w,q_{i4},q_{i3}) are tight. In a tight trimer, its first terminal oriented dimer has one polarity with the third vertex as witness, while its second terminal oriented dimer has the opposite polarity with the first vertex as witness. Consequently L_i(w)=(q_{i2},q_{i1}) is a signed dimer support of the same polarity for all three i with common witness w, and R_i(w)=(q_{i4},q_{i3}) is a signed dimer support of the opposite polarity for all three i with the same witness w. These signs are graph-intrinsic once the Q_i orderings are fixed, exactly as recorded in R102.\n\nConsider first {L_x(w),L_y(w),L_z(w)}. Each support has two vertices, so their union has size at most six. Because w is the sign witness, w lies outside every support. Thus the union of the three supports together with w uses at most seven of the ten vertices. At least three vertices remain. Choose any two of those spare vertices as a physical dimer J. Then J is a nontrivial marker path disjoint from every L_i(w) and from the common witness w. R40 applies to the three graph-intrinsic supports with common polarity and common witness and yields one opposite-polarity support E_L(w) such that E_L(w) forms a balanced pair with each L_i(w). The identical counting argument applied to {R_x(w),R_y(w),R_z(w)} yields one common opposite support E_R(w). Repeating for w=delta and w=epsilon gives four three-shield common-mate families. No payment descendants are coupled, in accordance with the fence in R40.

# R113 — Transversal zero-excess canonical-core fan actualization

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Assume the simultaneous zero-excess transversal kernel in the R100 coordinates with common core T={t,tprime}, common marker M={delta,epsilon}, and the four three-support common-mate families of R112. For every witness w in M and each endpoint side s in {L,R}, the three same-polarity supports D_x(s,w), D_y(s,w), D_z(s,w) may be actualized jointly by R40 using the same physical core dimer T as the nontrivial marker path. Thus there exists a graph-intrinsic opposite-polarity support E_T(s,w), born from a single marker test on T, that forms a balanced pair with all three members of that family. Consequently all four R112 fan births can be rooted at the same physical core dimer T; only the chosen marker orientation/test and the resulting opposite support may vary with s and w.

## Hypotheses
Standing order-ten smallest-counterexample case; R102 simultaneous zero-excess transversal kernel; R112 common-mate families.

## Scope
Canonical localization of the pre-payment actualization step in the transversal equality kernel.

## Applicability
Use before any pair payment. It puts the delta/epsilon and left/right fan families through one fixed physical core marker, making cross-family collision, orientation, or central-anchor comparisons meaningful without introducing arbitrary spare vertices.

## Persistence
The physical core T and all family supports are graph-intrinsic in the R100/R102 coordinates. The common mate produced by each actualization is graph-intrinsic as in R40.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert that the four mates E_T(s,w) coincide, that the same orientation of T is used in all four tests, that later paid descendants are coupled, or that a spanning two-cover follows immediately.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Order-ten zero-excess canonical-core fan actualization. A specialized pre-payment coordination lemma with no live consumers; keep accepted history only.
- **Curation note:** Order-ten zero-excess canonical-core fan actualization. A specialized pre-payment coordination lemma with no live consumers; keep accepted history only.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Verified. The common core T is a two-vertex nontrivial tight marker path in the Level-(1) setting; it is disjoint from every W_i terminal support and from delta/epsilon, so R40 may be applied to each R112 family using the same physical core pair. The statement correctly allows marker orientation and mate to vary and does not couple payments.

## Proof
Fix w in M and one endpoint side s. By R102, the three zero-packet four-rail supports are W_x={y,alpha,z,beta}, W_y={x,alpha,z,gamma}, and W_z={x,beta,y,gamma}, while the common core is T={t,tprime} and M={delta,epsilon}. Hence T is disjoint from W_x union W_y union W_z and from w. By R112, D_x(s,w), D_y(s,w), and D_z(s,w) are the corresponding terminal dimer supports on Q_x,Q_y,Q_z, so each physical support is contained in its W_i. Thus the physical dimer T is disjoint from all three supports and from their common witness w. Choose a tight orientation of T as a nontrivial marker path. R112 gives that the three D_i(s,w) have one common polarity and witness w. Applying R40 once to this three-support family with marker T therefore produces one graph-intrinsic support E_T(s,w) of the opposite polarity, balanced with every D_i(s,w). Repeating for s=L,R and w=delta,epsilon gives the four claimed fan births, all using the same physical core dimer T. R40 does not couple later payments, and nothing here identifies the resulting mates or marker orientations across the four applications.

# R114 — Zero-excess fan forces six same-support two-witness collisions

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Assume R112. For every shield index i in {x,y,z}, the two witness-indexed left supports L_i(delta) and L_i(epsilon) are the same oriented physical dimer and have the same polarity, but carry the distinct witnesses delta and epsilon. Hence R38 places that dimer in the same-polarity two-extension collision package. Likewise R_i(delta) and R_i(epsilon) are the same oriented physical dimer of the opposite polarity with those two distinct witnesses, so R38 gives a second collision site for the same shield. Therefore the R112 zero-excess kernel contains six graph-intrinsic same-support two-witness collision sites, one on each chosen left/right endpoint dimer of Q_x,Q_y,Q_z. In particular, no abstract signed-support realization of the full R112 contract can be collision-free.

## Hypotheses
Standing hypotheses of R112, with fixed orderings Q_i=(q_{i1},q_{i2},q_{i3},q_{i4}) for i in {x,y,z}; accepted same-support interaction theorem R38.

## Scope
Immediate signed-support consequence of R112 and R38. No use of pending R113 or of later payment descendants.

## Applicability
Use before comparing the four R112 common mates. The natural next target is not existence of collisions but synchronization of the six forced collision sites, for example through common ancestry, a shared physical core/anchor, or a rule coupling the delta/epsilon descendants strongly enough to force 5+5.

## Persistence
The six collision sites are graph-intrinsic once the three Q_i orderings are fixed, because their oriented endpoint dimers and both witness certificates are graph-intrinsic under R112.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert that the six physical endpoint dimers are distinct, that their collision descendants are simultaneously current, that the four R112 mates coincide, or that any single collision forces a spanning two-cover. It only rules out a collision-free abstract model of R112.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** superseded
- **Lifecycle note:** Six collision sites in the zero-excess fan are valid conditional consequences inside the minimum-overlap-three branch, now eliminated wholesale by C125/R127.
- **Curation note:** Six collision sites in the zero-excess fan are valid conditional consequences inside the minimum-overlap-three branch, now eliminated wholesale by C125/R127.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Verified. For each fixed shield side, the delta and epsilon certificates use the same oriented endpoint dimer and the same side-determined polarity with distinct witnesses, so R38 gives the claimed same-support collision. Six is incidence-level and the non-distinctness fence is correct.

## Proof
Fix i in {x,y,z}. By R112, for each w in {delta,epsilon}, L_i(w) is the oriented dimer (q_{i2},q_{i1}); its polarity is the left-endpoint polarity and its witness is w. Therefore L_i(delta) and L_i(epsilon) have identical oriented physical support and identical polarity, while their witnesses are distinct. R38 says that two signed certificates on the same physical support with the same polarity and distinct witnesses enter the accepted two-extension collision package. Hence the left endpoint dimer of Q_i is a collision site. The same argument applies to R_i(w)=(q_{i4},q_{i3}): R_i(delta) and R_i(epsilon) have identical oriented physical support and the common right-endpoint polarity, but distinct witnesses, so R38 gives a collision site there as well. This yields two forced collision sites for each of i=x,y,z, hence six endpoint collision sites in total, counted by shield-side incidence. The conclusion is incidence-level: some of these six sites may coincide physically across different shields, but every listed shield-side carries the stated two-witness collision. Consequently any abstract model satisfying the full R112 signed-support contract and R38 necessarily contains these collisions, so a collision-free realization is impossible.

# R115 — Zero-excess terminal-dimer repetition trichotomy and odd-cycle sign defect

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
In the R102/R112 zero-excess kernel, let the two terminal physical dimers of each Q_x,Q_y,Q_z be counted by shield incidence. A physical terminal dimer can repeat across two shields only as one of e_xy={alpha,z}, e_yz={x,gamma}, e_zx={y,beta}. The number of such cross-shield repeated dimers is therefore 0, 1, or 3, never exactly 2. In the 3-repeat case the endpoint partitions are Q_x:{e_xy,e_zx}, Q_y:{e_xy,e_yz}, Q_z:{e_yz,e_zx}. Since the two terminal dimers of each Q_i have opposite R112 polarities, the three-repeat triangle cannot assign the same polarity to each repeated physical dimer in both of its shield occurrences. Hence at least one repeated physical dimer carries opposite-polarity certificates across its two shield occurrences; choosing witness delta on one occurrence and epsilon on the other gives distinct witnesses, so R38 yields the opposite-polarity same-support exclusivity/strict two-ended signed-path interaction on that dimer.

## Hypotheses
Standing R102 simultaneous zero-excess kernel, fixed orderings Q_x,Q_y,Q_z as in R112, and accepted same-support interaction theorem R38.

## Scope
Pure endpoint-incidence and sign-parity consequence of the three R102 four-sets. No use of R113 or payment descendants.

## Applicability
Use to split the zero-excess fan analysis by endpoint-support repetition count. The 3-repeat branch has an unavoidable stronger opposite-polarity same-support interaction, while the 0/1-repeat branches are the only places where such a cross-shield sign defect can be avoided.

## Persistence
The four-sets W_x,W_y,W_z are graph-intrinsic in R102. Once Q_i orderings are fixed, their terminal dimers and R112 polarities are graph-intrinsic.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert which of the three shared dimers has the sign defect, does not assert simultaneous currentness of any payment descendants, and does not claim that the strict two-ended signed path alone forces 5+5.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Order-ten zero-excess terminal-dimer repetition/parity lemma. Nontrivial combinatorics but no live consumer and tightly tied to a retired specialized kernel; preserve historically.
- **Curation note:** Order-ten zero-excess terminal-dimer repetition/parity lemma. Nontrivial combinatorics but no live consumer and tightly tied to a retired specialized kernel; preserve historically.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Verified. Pairwise W-intersections are exactly e_xy,e_yz,e_zx; two cross-shield repetitions force the third. In the three-repeat case, same polarity on each repeated dimer would 2-color an odd 3-cycle, impossible. A polarity-defective repeated dimer with delta/epsilon witnesses invokes R38 exactly as stated.

## Proof
Write W_x={y,alpha,z,beta}, W_y={x,alpha,z,gamma}, W_z={x,beta,y,gamma}. Their pairwise intersections are W_x∩W_y={alpha,z}=e_xy, W_y∩W_z={x,gamma}=e_yz, and W_z∩W_x={y,beta}=e_zx. Each Q_i=(q1,q2,q3,q4) has two disjoint terminal physical dimers {q1,q2} and {q3,q4}, whose union is W_i. Therefore any physical dimer appearing terminally in two different Q_i must lie in the corresponding two-set intersection, hence must be the unique e_ij for that shield pair. Suppose e_xy repeats. Then because e_xy is one terminal part of the partition of W_x, the other terminal part of Q_x is W_x\\e_xy=e_zx. Likewise the other terminal part of Q_y is W_y\\e_xy=e_yz. If a second repetition occurs, say e_yz also repeats, then Q_z contains e_yz and therefore its complementary terminal part is W_z\\e_yz=e_zx; since Q_x already contains e_zx, e_zx repeats as well. The same argument is cyclic, so two repetitions imply three. Thus the repetition count is 0,1,or3. In the 3-repeat case, the terminal partitions are exactly Q_x:{e_xy,e_zx}, Q_y:{e_xy,e_yz}, Q_z:{e_yz,e_zx}. By R112 the left and right terminal supports of each Q_i have opposite polarities. Assume for contradiction that every repeated physical dimer has the same polarity in its two shield occurrences. Then each e_ij has a well-defined global polarity, and each of the three displayed shield partitions requires its two incident e-dimers to have opposite global polarities. This would give a two-coloring of the 3-cycle e_xy-e_yz-e_zx-e_xy with adjacent vertices opposite, impossible. Hence some repeated physical dimer e has opposite polarities in its two shield occurrences. R112 supplies both witnesses delta and epsilon on each occurrence. Taking, for example, the delta certificate from one occurrence and the epsilon certificate from the other gives opposite polarities on the same physical support with distinct witnesses. R38 therefore invokes same-support exclusivity and the accepted strict two-ended signed-path interaction on e.

# R116 — Zero-excess canonical terminal six-cycle and private-anchor parity

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Assume the simultaneous zero-excess transversal kernel, and choose Q_x,Q_y,Q_z to be the canonical zero-packet four-path representatives supplied by R101. Then their terminal physical dimers are exactly Q_x:{y,alpha},{z,beta}; Q_y:{x,alpha},{z,gamma}; Q_z:{x,beta},{y,gamma}. These six physical dimers are pairwise distinct and form the incidence six-cycle Q_x-alpha-Q_y-gamma-Q_z-beta-Q_x, where each edge records the unique terminal dimer incident with that shield and private vertex. Under the R112 signed-terminal-dimer polarities, the two edges incident with every Q_i have opposite polarity. Consequently an odd number of the three private vertices alpha,beta,gamma have opposite-polarity incident dimers; in particular at least one private vertex p is the common physical anchor of two distinct opposite-polarity terminal dimers. By R114, each of those two dimers also carries same-polarity signed certificates with both distinct witnesses delta and epsilon. Thus the canonical equality kernel contains a doubly-witnessed opposite-polarity private-anchor pair.

## Hypotheses
Standing order-ten smallest-counterexample case; simultaneous zero-excess alternative of R101; canonical zero-packet representatives Q_x,Q_y,Q_z; accepted R112 and R114 signed-support conclusions.

## Scope
Canonical representative-level endpoint geometry and sign parity in the transversal zero-excess branch. This intentionally uses the named wing-concatenation representatives from R101, not arbitrary alternate tight four-path orderings on the same W_i supports.

## Applicability
Use before R115 repetition branching. It collapses the canonical zero packets directly to the no-repeat physical-dimer case and exposes at least one private vertex carrying two opposite-polarity, delta/epsilon-doubly-witnessed dimers. The next target is a shared-anchor interaction theorem at that private vertex.

## Persistence
The six physical terminal dimers are fixed by the canonical R101 zero-packet representatives. Their R112 polarities and R114 witness certificates are graph-intrinsic once those representative orderings are fixed.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not invalidate R115 for alternate tight four-path orderings on the same four-set supports. Does not assert that the two opposite-polarity dimers at the private anchor are terminal dimers of one tight trimer, does not couple later payment descendants, and does not by itself force a spanning two-cover.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** superseded
- **Lifecycle note:** Canonical terminal six-cycle/private-anchor parity is conditional zero-excess machinery under a branch eliminated by C125/R127. Preserve historically.
- **Curation note:** Canonical terminal six-cycle/private-anchor parity is conditional zero-excess machinery under a branch eliminated by C125/R127. Preserve historically.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Verified canonical R101 wing dimers are exactly the six terminal physical dimers; the incidence graph is the stated 6-cycle. R112 contributes one polarity flip at each shield, so closed-cycle parity forces an odd number of private-anchor flips and hence at least one opposite-polarity private-anchor pair. R114 supplies both delta and epsilon witnesses on each incident dimer. Exclusions correctly avoid a trimer or payment-coupling overclaim.

## Proof
In the x-frame, R101 says that the canonical zero-excess four-component Q_x is obtained by concatenating the tight wing dimer on {y,alpha} with the tight wing dimer on {z,beta} using exactly one inter-wing transition. Hence its two terminal physical dimers are {y,alpha} and {z,beta}. Cyclically, the terminal physical dimers of Q_y are {x,alpha} and {z,gamma}, and those of Q_z are {x,beta} and {y,gamma}. All six pairs are distinct. Regrouping them by their private vertex yields alpha incident with the Q_x dimer {y,alpha} and Q_y dimer {x,alpha}; gamma incident with the Q_y dimer {z,gamma} and Q_z dimer {y,gamma}; beta incident with the Q_z dimer {x,beta} and Q_x dimer {z,beta}. Thus the shield/private incidence graph of these six dimers is the six-cycle Q_x-alpha-Q_y-gamma-Q_z-beta-Q_x. Fix the R112 polarity labels on these six oriented terminal dimers. At every shield vertex Q_i the two incident terminal dimers have opposite polarity, so passage through each of Q_x,Q_y,Q_z flips sign. Traversing the whole six-cycle returns to the initial dimer polarity; therefore the total number of sign flips over all six vertices is even. The three shield vertices contribute exactly three flips, hence the three private vertices contribute an odd number of flips. Therefore one or three of alpha,beta,gamma have opposite-polarity incident dimers, and in particular at least one does. Finally R114 applies to every chosen terminal dimer and says that its delta-indexed and epsilon-indexed certificates are the same oriented physical support with the same polarity and distinct witnesses. Thus each of the two opposite-polarity dimers at the selected private anchor carries both witnesses delta and epsilon. This is the claimed doubly-witnessed opposite-polarity private-anchor pair.

# R117 — Zero-excess paired-anchor polarity rectangle

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Assume the canonical zero-excess terminal six-cycle of R116. Choose a private vertex p in {alpha,beta,gamma} whose two incident terminal dimers have opposite R112 polarities, as guaranteed by R116. Let Q_i,Q_j be the two shields incident with p. Then Q_i and Q_j share exactly one further wing vertex r, and the terminal dimer of Q_i incident with r and the terminal dimer of Q_j incident with r also have opposite polarities. Thus the two shields form a four-dimer rectangle consisting of two distinct opposite-polarity stars, one centered at p and one centered at r. All four dimers are pairwise distinct except for their prescribed star-center incidences, and every one carries both distinct witnesses delta and epsilon via R114. Concretely: if p=alpha then (Q_i,Q_j,r)=(Q_x,Q_y,z) and the two stars are {alpha,y},{alpha,x} and {z,beta},{z,gamma}; if p=beta then (Q_i,Q_j,r)=(Q_x,Q_z,y) and the stars are {beta,z},{beta,x} and {y,alpha},{y,gamma}; if p=gamma then (Q_i,Q_j,r)=(Q_y,Q_z,x) and the stars are {gamma,z},{gamma,y} and {x,alpha},{x,beta}.

## Hypotheses
Standing order-ten smallest-counterexample case; simultaneous zero-excess alternative; canonical R101 zero-packet representatives; accepted R116.

## Scope
Canonical signed-incidence strengthening of the R116 private-anchor output.

## Applicability
Use when attacking the shared-anchor interaction problem. Any local argument at the parity-forced private star has a parallel opposite-polarity star on the same two shields, with the same two common marker witnesses.

## Persistence
All four physical dimers, both anchors, their shield incidences, polarities, and delta/epsilon witness certificates are graph-intrinsic once the canonical R101 zero-packet representatives are fixed.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert that either opposite-polarity star already forms the terminal signed dimers of one tight trimer in the required orientations; does not couple payment descendants; does not itself force a spanning two-cover.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** superseded
- **Lifecycle note:** Zero-excess paired-anchor polarity rectangle is valid branch-local structure but lies wholly inside the minimum-overlap-three branch eliminated by C125/R127.
- **Curation note:** Zero-excess paired-anchor polarity rectangle is valid branch-local structure but lies wholly inside the minimum-overlap-three branch eliminated by C125/R127.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Verified the R116 six-cycle sign propagation: the second shared wing anchor inherits an opposite-polarity star, with four distinct rectangle dimers and both delta/epsilon witnesses.

## Proof
R116 lists the canonical terminal dimers and states that the two terminals of each shield Q_k have opposite polarity. If p=alpha, the incident shields are Q_x and Q_y. Write s for the polarity of {alpha,y} in Q_x. Then {z,beta} has polarity -s. Since {alpha,x} in Q_y has polarity -s by the choice of alpha as a sign-flip private vertex, the other Q_y terminal {z,gamma} has polarity s. Hence the z-centered pair {z,beta},{z,gamma} is also opposite-polarity. The four dimers are distinct by the R116 six-cycle list, and R116 imports from R114 both delta and epsilon as witnesses on each. The beta and gamma cases are the cyclic relabelings: for beta use Q_x,Q_z with second anchor y; for gamma use Q_y,Q_z with second anchor x. This proves the rectangle statement.

# R118 — Paired-anchor trimer lift and third-witness dichotomy

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Assume the paired-anchor polarity rectangle R117, with opposite-polarity stars {p,u},{p,v} at anchor p and {r,a},{r,b} at anchor r, all four dimers carrying the two common witnesses delta and epsilon. Boundary antisymmetry permits tight trimer orientations J_p on {u,p,v} with middle p and J_r on {a,r,b} with middle r. These trimers are vertex-disjoint and their four terminal physical dimers are exactly the four rectangle dimers. Hence R41 gives a synchronized two-anchor trimer interaction through {p,r}. Moreover, at each anchor separately there is an alignment dichotomy between the pre-existing R117 polarities and the trimer-induced terminal polarities: either both terminal dimers align, in which case each gains a third same-polarity witness (the opposite outer vertex of that trimer) in addition to delta and epsilon; or both anti-align, in which case R38 gives an opposite-polarity same-support exclusivity / strict two-ended signed-path interaction on each of the two terminal dimers. Thus each anchor produces either two three-witness same-polarity signed dimers or two strict opposite-polarity same-support interactions, while the two anchors are simultaneously linked by the R41 interaction certificate.

## Hypotheses
Standing order-ten smallest-counterexample case; canonical zero-excess kernel; pending/accepted R117 paired-anchor rectangle; boundary antisymmetry R3; same-support interaction R38; trimer central-anchor interaction R41.

## Scope
Local signed-turn amplification of the canonical zero-excess equality kernel. No payment or actualization is used.

## Applicability
Use as the next zero-excess interface. It converts the parity rectangle into actual p- and r-centered tight trimers and forces either third-witness saturation or the stronger strict same-support opposite-sign interaction at each anchor.

## Persistence
The two trimer turns are graph-intrinsic once either of the two reversal choices with prescribed middle is selected as tight by R3. R41 interactions and R38 sign interactions are historical graph-intrinsic certificates; no simultaneous paid representative is asserted.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert that the trimer-induced orientations agree with the original R112 dimer orientations. In the aligned branch it only adds a third same-polarity witness; it does not by itself close 5+5. In the anti-aligned branch the two strict interactions are graph-intrinsic, not asserted simultaneously current in one paid descendant.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Order-ten paired-anchor trimer amplification. Strong local certificate production but zero-consumer branch machinery; later general contact/pair interaction parents now carry the reusable interface.
- **Curation note:** Order-ten paired-anchor trimer amplification. Strong local certificate production but zero-consumer branch machinery; later general contact/pair interaction parents now carry the reusable interface.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Verified prescribed-middle trimers by R3, vertex-disjointness of the two rectangle stars, R41 interaction, and the align/anti-align dichotomy with third witnesses or R38 strict same-support interactions.

## Proof
Write the p-star as D_1={p,u}, D_2={p,v}, with R117 polarities s and -s, and the r-star as F_1={r,a}, F_2={r,b}, again of opposite polarity. By R3, for the ordered reversal pair (u,p,v),(v,p,u), exactly one orientation is tight; choose that tight orientation as J_p. Thus J_p is a tight trimer with middle p and terminal physical dimers D_1,D_2. Likewise one of (a,r,b),(b,r,a) is tight, giving J_r with middle r and terminal physical dimers F_1,F_2. The R117 rectangle lists six distinct vertices u,p,v,a,r,b in these two stars, so J_p and J_r are vertex-disjoint. R41 therefore supplies the synchronized two-anchor interaction through p and r. R41 also assigns opposite trimer-induced polarities t,-t to D_1,D_2. Since the old polarities are s,-s, either t=s, in which case both trimer signs align, or t=-s, in which case both anti-align. In the aligned case the trimer witness for D_1 is v and for D_2 is u; these are distinct from delta,epsilon and from the relevant support, so each support now has three distinct witnesses delta,epsilon and its trimer outer witness, all in polarity s or -s respectively. In the anti-aligned case each D_i has one trimer certificate of polarity opposite to its delta/epsilon certificate, with distinct witnesses, so R38 gives the strict two-ended same-support interaction on both D_1 and D_2. The same argument applies at r. No payment or representative transport is used.

# R119 — Transversal common-core-marker triple 3+3 cell

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
In the transversal triangle coordinates of R100, let T be the common two-vertex core and M={delta,epsilon} the common exterior marker, and put N=V(H)\\(T∪M)={x,y,z,alpha,beta,gamma}. Then the single four-vertex deletion H-(T∪M) admits three exact 3+3 covers on the same physical six-vertex cell N: (i) {x,y,alpha} ⊔ {z,beta,gamma}; (ii) {x,z,beta} ⊔ {y,alpha,gamma}; (iii) {y,z,gamma} ⊔ {x,alpha,beta}. More strongly, in any one of these three partitions and for any prescribed vertex a of the first triple and b of the second triple, the two triples can be oriented as tight trimers with middle vertices a and b respectively; hence R41 supplies a synchronized two-anchor interaction through {a,b}. Thus each of the three exact 3+3 decompositions carries a 3-by-3 middle-anchor interaction grid, all rooted in the same common deletion cell H-(T∪M).

## Hypotheses
Standing order-ten smallest-counterexample case; transversal alternative and R100 coordinates.

## Scope
Support-level/common-deletion compression valid throughout the transversal branch, not only the zero-excess face.

## Applicability
Use as a parent exact cell for private-anchor and wing-anchor interactions. In the zero-excess parity branch, choose the parity-forced private anchor and the second anchor from R117 as the two prescribed middles in the corresponding one of these exact 3+3 partitions.

## Persistence
The deletion set T∪M and the three physical 3+3 partitions are graph-intrinsic. Each prescribed-middle trimer orientation and the resulting R41 interaction is graph-intrinsic as a separate certificate; simultaneous currentness of all 27 orientations is not asserted.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
The three exact covers and their different prescribed-middle orientations are separate representatives/certificates. The lemma does not assert a spanning two-cover of H, does not couple paid descendants, and does not make all interaction-grid cells simultaneously current.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** superseded
- **Lifecycle note:** Support-level transversal 3+3 cell is valid, but the entire minimum-overlap-three branch is eliminated by parent theorem C125/R127. Preserve this exact cell historically for proof archaeology.
- **Curation note:** Support-level transversal 3+3 cell is valid, but the entire minimum-overlap-three branch is eliminated by parent theorem C125/R127. Preserve this exact cell historically for proof archaeology.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Verified the common four-vertex deletion cell, all three exact 3+3 partitions, prescribed-middle orientations via R3, and the 3x3 R41 interaction grid for each partition.

## Proof
By R100, after deleting T and M the remaining vertices are exactly N={x,y,z,alpha,beta,gamma}. The three displayed pairs of triples are complementary partitions of N. R8 gives a tight trimer orientation on every three-set, so each displayed partition is a two-path cover of H-(T∪M). Since |T∪M|=4, R5 says the path-cover number of this deletion is exactly two; hence all three displayed covers are exact 3+3 covers. For the strengthened middle-anchor statement, fix one displayed partition X⊔Y and prescribed a∈X, b∈Y. On X, choose the reversal pair of ordered triples having a as middle. By R3 exactly one member of that reversal pair is tight, so X has a tight trimer orientation with middle a. Likewise Y has a tight orientation with middle b. The two trimers are vertex-disjoint, so R41 applies and gives the synchronized two-anchor interaction through {a,b}. There are 3×3 choices per partition. Each is a separate graph-intrinsic orientation/interaction certificate, so no simultaneous-currentness claim is needed.

# R120 — Paired-anchor signs must align with the middle trimers

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Assume the paired-anchor polarity rectangle R117. At either of its two anchors c, write the opposite-polarity star as {c,u},{c,v}, with both dimers carrying the witnesses delta and epsilon. Choose the unique tight orientation J_c of the reversal pair (u,c,v),(v,c,u), so J_c is a tight trimer with middle c. Then the two R117 polarities on {c,u},{c,v} agree componentwise with the two terminal polarities induced by J_c; the anti-aligned possibility is impossible. Consequently each rectangle dimer has a third same-polarity witness, namely the opposite outer vertex of its middle trimer, in addition to delta and epsilon. This holds simultaneously as graph-intrinsic sign data at both rectangle anchors. Combined with R41, the two vertex-disjoint middle trimers therefore give a synchronized two-anchor interaction whose four terminal physical dimers are all three-witness same-polarity supports.

## Hypotheses
Standing order-ten smallest-counterexample case; R100 transversal minimum-overlap triangle; R117 paired-anchor rectangle; R3 boundary antisymmetry; R9 longest-path order five; R41 central-anchor interaction.

## Scope
Orientation-sensitive closure of the align/anti-align ambiguity in the canonical zero-excess private-anchor rectangle.

## Applicability
Use as the canonical zero-excess local interface after R117. The next step may treat the four rectangle dimers as three-witness same-polarity supports tied to one exact/common two-anchor trimer cell; no opposite-sign branch remains.

## Persistence
The forbidden-five-set argument is support-level. The chosen middle-trimer orientations and resulting third-witness certificates are graph-intrinsic. R41 interaction remains a historical interaction certificate, not simultaneous paid currentness.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert that the four three-witness supports are simultaneously actualized or paid, does not identify their later collision descendants, and does not by itself force a spanning 5+5 cover.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** superseded
- **Lifecycle note:** Paired-anchor sign alignment is valid zero-excess closure machinery, but the whole minimum-overlap-three branch is already eliminated by parent C125/R127.
- **Curation note:** Paired-anchor sign alignment is valid zero-excess closure machinery, but the whole minimum-overlap-three branch is already eliminated by parent C125/R127.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Verified the anti-alignment exclusion. Exact R112/R114 witness-order certificates extend the chosen middle trimer at both ends to a tight five-path; order five is globally maximal and each listed support violates the minimum-overlap-three geometry of R100. Alignment and third-witness saturation follow.

## Proof
Fix one rectangle anchor c with outer vertices u,v. By R3 exactly one of (u,c,v),(v,c,u) is tight; call the resulting c-middle trimer J=(u,c,v) after renaming u,v according to its tight direction. Its first terminal dimer {u,c} and second terminal dimer {c,v} have opposite trimer-induced polarities. R117 gives opposite old polarities on the same two physical dimers, so the old pair either agrees with the trimer pair componentwise or disagrees componentwise. Suppose it disagrees. Then the old sign on {u,c} is the head-facing sign relative to J, while the old sign on {c,v} is the tail-facing sign relative to J. Since both old signs have both witnesses delta and epsilon, the exact ordered turns (delta,u,c) and (c,v,epsilon) are tight (or with delta,epsilon exchanged). Together with the tight middle turn (u,c,v), this makes delta,u,c,v,epsilon a tight five-path. By R9 its support X_c={u,c,v,delta,epsilon} is globally longest. But every possible rectangle star gives X_c forbidden overlap: for the private stars, X_alpha={x,y,alpha,delta,epsilon} meets B only in x (and C only in y), X_beta={x,z,beta,delta,epsilon} meets A only in x, and X_gamma={y,z,gamma,delta,epsilon} meets A only in y; for the second-anchor stars, X_z={beta,z,gamma,delta,epsilon} is disjoint from A, X_y={alpha,y,gamma,delta,epsilon} is disjoint from B, and X_x={alpha,x,beta,delta,epsilon} is disjoint from C. Each contradicts the global minimum overlap three encoded by the R100 triangle (and in the disjoint cases already R13). Hence anti-alignment is impossible. Therefore the old polarities align with the trimer terminal polarities. The opposite outer vertex of J is then a third witness with the same polarity as delta and epsilon on each terminal dimer. Apply the same argument at the second rectangle anchor. The two middle trimers are vertex-disjoint by the R117 rectangle list, so R41 supplies the synchronized two-anchor interaction on these four three-witness supports.

# R121 — Zero-excess paired-anchor marker bridge forces overlap descent

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
In the canonical simultaneous zero-excess transversal kernel, the paired-anchor rectangle of R117 together with the alignment theorem R120 is impossible. More precisely, choose the parity-forced private anchor p and its companion anchor r from R117, and orient the two R120 middle trimers as J_p=(u,p,v) and J_r=(a,r,b). For either common marker witness w in {delta,epsilon}, R120 gives the four tight witness turns (u,p,w), (w,p,v), (a,r,w), (w,r,b). Boundary antisymmetry on the middle triple {p,w,r} then yields a tight five-path: either (u,p,w,r,b) or (a,r,w,p,v). Its support is global-longest, but according as p=alpha,beta,gamma it meets A,B,C respectively in exactly two vertices, contradicting the global minimum overlap three of R100. Hence the simultaneous zero-excess alternative cannot occur.

## Hypotheses
Standing order-ten smallest-counterexample case; R100 transversal minimum-overlap triangle; simultaneous zero-excess alternative; accepted R117 paired-anchor rectangle and R120 sign alignment.

## Scope
Direct closure of the canonical zero-excess transversal equality kernel by a support-level marker bridge. No payment, actualization, collision descent, or representative coupling is used.

## Applicability
Use after the R101 zero-packet enters simultaneous zero excess. This eliminates that branch outright, leaving the positive-excess alternative as the remaining R101 transversal branch.

## Persistence
The contradiction is support-level: the constructed order-five path is graph-intrinsic, and its overlap-two relation with the relevant one of A,B,C is physical support incidence.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not address the positive-excess branch and does not by itself prove C2. It uses one common witness only; no simultaneous use of delta and epsilon is asserted.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** superseded
- **Lifecycle note:** Zero-excess transversal branch closure is subsumed by the later parent elimination of all minimum-overlap-three configurations, C125/R127.
- **Curation note:** Zero-excess transversal branch closure is subsumed by the later parent elimination of all minimum-overlap-three configurations, C125/R127.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Verified. R120 preserves the exact witness-turn orientations needed at both rectangle anchors; R3 bridges the common witness to yield a tight five-path in either middle orientation. The resulting support has overlap exactly two with the corresponding minimum-overlap support A, B, or C in each concrete R117 case, contradicting R100.

## Proof
Choose the parity-forced private anchor p from R117 and let r be its companion anchor on the same two shields. By R120 choose tight middle-trimer orientations J_p=(u,p,v) and J_r=(a,r,b), where {u,v} are the two outer vertices of the p-star and {a,b} the two outer vertices of the r-star. Fix w=delta (the same proof works with epsilon). Because R120 says the pre-existing rectangle polarities align componentwise with the terminal polarities induced by these trimers, and because w is a same-polarity witness on every rectangle dimer, the exact ordered-turn semantics give (u,p,w) and (w,p,v) tight at p, and (a,r,w) and (w,r,b) tight at r.\n\nApply R3 to the three distinct vertices p,w,r. If (p,w,r) is tight, then u,p,w,r,b is a tight path of order five, using consecutive tight triples (u,p,w), (p,w,r), (w,r,b). If (p,w,r) is bad, R3 makes its complete reversal (r,w,p) tight, and then a,r,w,p,v is a tight path of order five, using (a,r,w), (r,w,p), (w,p,v). In either case all five vertices are distinct by the R117 rectangle geometry and because w is one of the exterior marker vertices. By R9 the resulting five-path is global-longest.\n\nNow use the concrete R117 cases together with the R100 coordinates A=T∪{x,y,alpha}, B=T∪{x,z,beta}, C=T∪{y,z,gamma}. If p=alpha then r=z, the p-outers are x,y and the r-outers are beta,gamma. Either constructed support therefore has the form {alpha,z,w,o_p,o_r} with o_p in {x,y} and o_r in {beta,gamma}; it meets A in exactly {alpha,o_p}, hence in two vertices. If p=beta then r=y, the p-outers are x,z and the r-outers are alpha,gamma, so either support meets B exactly in {beta,o_p}, again two vertices. If p=gamma then r=x, the p-outers are y,z and the r-outers are alpha,beta, so either support meets C exactly in {gamma,o_p}, again two vertices. Each contradicts R100, since A,B,C are globally minimum-overlap longest-five supports with minimum overlap three, so no global-longest five-support can meet any of them in only two vertices. Therefore the simultaneous zero-excess transversal kernel is impossible.

# R122 — Positive-excess wing-interleaving or six-exterior shield dichotomy

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Let A,B be a globally minimum-overlap pair of global-longest five-supports with |A∩B|=3, and use the R99 blocks S=A∩B, U=A\\B, V=B\\A, R=V(H)\\(A∪B). Let Q=(q1,q2,q3,q4) and K be the 4- and 3-vertex components of an exact two-cover of H-S having positive R99 excess. Then exactly one of the following structural alternatives holds. (I) supp(Q)=U∪V and supp(K)=R; the positive excess is entirely wing-interleaving, i.e. the Q ordering has at least two U/V class transitions rather than the zero-excess one-transition concatenation. (II) One wing W∈{U,V} satisfies |supp(Q)∩W|≤1. For the corresponding longest support L=S∪W, every five-set supp(Q)∪{s}, s∈S, is non-Hamiltonian, since any tight five-path on it would be global-longest and would meet L in at most two vertices. Hence for every s∈S the direct endpoint turns (s,q1,q2) and (q3,q4,s) are bad and the reverse turns (q2,q1,s) and (s,q4,q3) are tight. Combining this with R105, the same two reverse endpoint turns are tight for every k∈K. Thus every one of the six exterior vertices S∪supp(K)=V(H)\\supp(Q) is a witness for both terminal reverse-turn systems of Q.

## Hypotheses
Standing order-ten smallest-counterexample case; R99 minimum-overlap-three common-triple frame; an exact H-S two-cover with positive excess.

## Scope
Support-level and endpoint-turn compression of the positive-excess R99 branch.

## Applicability
Use as the parent split for the remaining transversal positive-excess branch. Attack the pure U/V interleaving face separately; otherwise exploit the six-exterior terminal shield without reopening arbitrary return trees.

## Persistence
The support dichotomy and non-Hamiltonicity of Q∪{s} are physical support facts. The endpoint reverse turns are graph-intrinsic relative to the displayed Q ordering.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert that the six witness certificates can be paid simultaneously, does not by itself force overlap descent, and does not classify the U/V interleaving face beyond its transition count.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** superseded
- **Lifecycle note:** Positive-excess transversal dichotomy is a branch-analysis interface under a branch now eliminated wholesale by C125/R127.
- **Curation note:** Positive-excess transversal dichotomy is a branch-analysis interface under a branch now eliminated wholesale by C125/R127.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Verified. Positive excess splits exactly into the full-wing interleaving case or a wing-deficient case; in the latter, minimum-overlap geometry plus R105 yields all six exterior endpoint witnesses.

## Proof
Let Q and K be the displayed 4+3 exact cover of H-S. If |Q∩U|=|Q∩V|=2, then |Q|=4 forces supp(Q)=U∪V, hence supp(K)=R. R99 says zero excess in this support grouping occurs exactly for a one-transition concatenation of the U and V wing dimers. Since the present cover has positive excess, its Q ordering has at least two U/V transitions. This is alternative (I).\n\nOtherwise one of U,V, call it W, satisfies |Q∩W|≤1. Put L=S∪W, so L is A or B and is a global-longest five-support. Fix s∈S. If supp(Q)∪{s} supported any tight five-path, then by the order-ten longest-path value R9 it would itself be a global-longest support. But its intersection with L is contained in (Q∩W)∪{s}, hence has size at most 2, contradicting that A,B were chosen with globally minimum longest-support overlap 3. Thus supp(Q)∪{s} is non-Hamiltonian. In particular neither displayed endpoint extension (s,q1,q2,q3,q4) nor (q1,q2,q3,q4,s) can be tight. Therefore the endpoint turns (s,q1,q2) and (q3,q4,s) are bad; boundary antisymmetry R3 yields (q2,q1,s) and (s,q4,q3) tight. This holds for every s∈S. Independently, R105 gives (q2,q1,k) and (k,q4,q3) tight for every k∈K. Since Q,K,S are disjoint and exhaust the ten vertices, S∪K is exactly the six-vertex exterior of Q. Hence both terminal reverse-turn systems of Q have all six exterior vertices as witnesses, proving (II).

# R123 — Transversal common-triple universal four-witness shield

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
In the R100 transversal coordinates, consider the x-frame S_x=T∪{x} for the pair A,B, and let Q=(q1,q2,q3,q4) and K be the 4- and 3-vertex components of any exact two-cover of H-S_x, with no assumption on R99 excess. Then for every w in {x}∪supp(K), both direct endpoint turns (w,q1,q2) and (q3,q4,w) are bad, while the reverse turns (q2,q1,w) and (w,q4,q3) are tight. Thus the two terminal reverse-turn systems of Q have the same four graph-intrinsic witnesses {x}∪supp(K). Cyclically the same statement holds in the y- and z-frames, with distinguished witnesses y and z respectively. In the simultaneous zero-excess face, K is the canonical R-block trimer and this recovers the corresponding four-witness portion of R102.

## Hypotheses
Standing order-ten smallest-counterexample case; R100 transversal minimum-overlap triangle; any exact two-cover of one of its common-triple deletion frames.

## Scope
Excess-independent endpoint shield for the transversal triangle.

## Applicability
Use as the common parent endpoint package in both positive- and zero-excess transversal analysis. In the remaining positive-excess branch, combine it with class-transition information rather than rebuilding witness turns case by case.

## Persistence
The distinguished witness and K support are physical for the displayed deletion cover; reverse turns are graph-intrinsic relative to the displayed Q ordering.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not identify K across different exact covers, does not assert simultaneous currentness across the three deletion frames, and does not by itself force a five-path or spanning two-cover.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** superseded
- **Lifecycle note:** Universal four-witness shield is a valid transversal branch lemma, but ordinary canonical retrieval should go to C125/R127, which eliminates the whole minimum-overlap-three branch.
- **Curation note:** Universal four-witness shield is a valid transversal branch lemma, but ordinary canonical retrieval should go to C125/R127, which eliminates the whole minimum-overlap-three branch.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Verified excess-independent four-witness shield. The distinguished deleted singleton cannot extend Q to a five-path by the R100 minimum-overlap triangle; R105 supplies the K witnesses.

## Proof
Work in the x-frame. By R105, for every k∈K the turns (k,q1,q2) and (q3,q4,k) are bad and (q2,q1,k),(k,q4,q3) are tight. We show the same for x. Let U_x={y,alpha} and V_x={z,beta}. If supp(Q)=U_x∪V_x, then supp(Q)∪{x} intersects C=T∪{y,z,gamma} exactly in {y,z}, since x is not in C and T is deleted. Any tight five-path on supp(Q)∪{x} would be global-longest by R9 and would therefore contradict the globally minimum overlap three of the R100 triangle. Hence this five-set is non-Hamiltonian.\n\nIf supp(Q)≠U_x∪V_x, then because |Q|=4 at least one wing W∈{U_x,V_x} satisfies |Q∩W|≤1. Let L be A when W=U_x and B when W=V_x. Since L=S_x∪W and T⊂S_x is absent from Q while x∈S_x, the five-set supp(Q)∪{x} meets L in at most {x} together with Q∩W, hence in at most two vertices. Again any tight five-path on that support would be global-longest and contradict minimum overlap three. Thus supp(Q)∪{x} is non-Hamiltonian in all cases. In particular the two endpoint extensions (x,q1,q2,q3,q4) and (q1,q2,q3,q4,x) fail, so (x,q1,q2) and (q3,q4,x) are bad. Boundary antisymmetry R3 gives (q2,q1,x) and (x,q4,q3) tight. Together with the K-witness conclusions from R105, the common witness set is {x}∪K. The y- and z-frame statements follow by the R100 cyclic symmetry.

# R124 — Transversal common-triple universal four-witness fold fan

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
In the R100 transversal x-frame, let Q=(q1,q2,q3,q4) and K be the 4- and 3-vertex components of any exact two-cover of H-S_x. For every witness w∈{x}∪supp(K), the three turns (q2,q1,w), (q4,w,q1), and (w,q4,q3) are tight, while their direct bridge orientation (q1,w,q4) is bad. Equivalently, each of the four witnesses gives the same folded three-turn pattern joining the two terminal reverse-turn systems of Q through the outer pair {q1,q4}. Cyclically the same holds in the y- and z-frames.

## Hypotheses
Standing order-ten smallest-counterexample case; R100 transversal triangle; any exact two-cover of one common-triple deletion frame.

## Scope
Excess-independent orientation package strengthening the universal four-witness shield.

## Applicability
Use as the main orientation interface for the remaining positive-excess branch. In the pure U/V interleaving face, classify the Q label pattern and combine the four folded trimers (q4,w,q1) with the wing geometry. In the non-interleaving face, combine with the larger six-witness endpoint shield.

## Persistence
All asserted turns are graph-intrinsic relative to the displayed Q ordering and witness vertex. No simultaneous exact-cover currentness beyond the original Q,K frame is asserted.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert that the four folded trimers concatenate with one another, form one current larger path, or can be paid simultaneously.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** superseded
- **Lifecycle note:** Universal four-witness fold fan is valid transversal-branch orientation machinery but lies wholly inside the minimum-overlap-three branch eliminated by C125/R127.
- **Curation note:** Universal four-witness fold fan is valid transversal-branch orientation machinery but lies wholly inside the minimum-overlap-three branch eliminated by C125/R127.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Verified fold fan. For every common witness, non-Hamiltonicity of Q union witness plus the two endpoint reverse turns forces the bridge turn q1-w-q4 bad and hence q4-w-q1 tight by R3.

## Proof
Fix the x-frame. First let w∈K. R105 gives (q2,q1,w) and (w,q4,q3) tight, and its longest-path cap says H-S_x contains no tight five-path, so Q∪{w} is non-Hamiltonian. Now let w=x. If supp(Q)=U_x∪V_x, then Q∪{x} meets the third minimum-overlap support C only in {y,z}; if not, one of the wings U_x,V_x has at most one Q-vertex and Q∪{x} meets the corresponding A or B support in at most two vertices. In either case a tight five-path on Q∪{x} would be global-longest by R9 and contradict minimum overlap three. Thus Q∪{x} is non-Hamiltonian. The two endpoint direct turns by x are therefore bad and R3 gives (q2,q1,x),(x,q4,q3) tight.\n\nHence for every w∈{x}∪K the endpoint reversals (q2,q1,w) and (w,q4,q3) are tight and the support Q∪{w} is non-Hamiltonian. If (q1,w,q4) were tight, then the three consecutive turns of (q2,q1,w,q4,q3) would all be tight, producing a forbidden tight five-path on Q∪{w}. Therefore (q1,w,q4) is bad. Boundary antisymmetry R3 gives its full reversal (q4,w,q1) tight. Rotate the R100 coordinates cyclically for the y- and z-frames.

# R125 — Universal four-witness fold cell and anchor clique

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
In any transversal common-triple exact-cover frame of R124, let Q=(q1,q2,q3,q4) be the four-path, let K be the three-path, let s be the distinguished deleted singleton for that frame, and put W={s} union supp(K). Define the six-set F={q1,q4} union W. Then for every w in W, the folded trimer J_w=(q4,w,q1) is tight and, for any tight trimer L_w on W\\{w}, J_w and L_w form an exact 3+3 two-cover of the same physical six-set F. Moreover, for every ordered pair of distinct witnesses w,r in W, L_w may be oriented with middle vertex r; hence R41 gives a central-anchor interaction with anchor pair {w,r}. Consequently the four common witnesses of R124 form a complete K4 of graph-intrinsic central-anchor interaction certificates, all rooted in one physical six-vertex fold cell F.

## Hypotheses
Standing order-ten smallest-counterexample case; any one of the R100 transversal common-triple deletion frames and any displayed exact 4+3 cover in that frame; accepted universal fold fan R124.

## Scope
Excess-independent exact-cell compression of the R124 fold fan. It applies to both positive- and zero-excess covers and does not use payment or actualization.

## Applicability
Use in the remaining positive-excess branch before opening payment descendants. In the pure interleaving face, the physical type of the outer pair {q1,q4} (whole wing versus cross-wing) becomes the only extra support-incidence datum on top of this fixed four-witness interaction cell.

## Persistence
The six-set F and the four folded trimers J_w are graph-intrinsic relative to the displayed Q ordering. The exact 3+3 covers and R41 interaction certificates may use different orientations of the complementary witness trimers and are separate representatives.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert simultaneous currentness of the four 3+3 decompositions, a common orientation of the complementary trimers, coupled payment descendants, or an immediate spanning 5+5 cover. The K4 is a family of historical graph-intrinsic interaction certificates, not one selected interaction graph in a single representative.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** superseded
- **Lifecycle note:** Four-witness fold-cell/anchor-clique structure is valid but lives entirely inside the minimum-overlap-three branch eliminated by C125/R127.
- **Curation note:** Four-witness fold-cell/anchor-clique structure is valid but lives entirely inside the minimum-overlap-three branch eliminated by C125/R127.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Verified. The common six-set F has four-vertex complement T∪{q2,q3}, so R5 makes each displayed two-trimer decomposition exact. R3 permits any prescribed complementary witness middle, and R41 realizes all six unordered witness pairs as separate central-anchor certificates.

## Proof
Fix the x-frame; the y- and z-frames are cyclic. Write S_x=T union {x}, let Q=(q1,q2,q3,q4) and K be the displayed exact 4+3 cover of H-S_x, and set W={x} union supp(K). By R124, for every w in W the ordered trimer J_w=(q4,w,q1) is tight. Fix w. The three-set W\\{w} admits a tight trimer orientation by boundary antisymmetry R3: more strongly, if r is any prescribed vertex of W\\{w} and a,b are the other two vertices, exactly one of (a,r,b) and (b,r,a) is tight, so we may choose a tight complementary trimer L_{w,r} with middle r. The two trimers J_w and L_{w,r} are vertex-disjoint and together cover F={q1,q4} union W. The complement of F in H is exactly T union {q2,q3}, a four-set. By R5, deleting that four-set leaves path-cover number exactly two. Hence the displayed two-trimer cover J_w union L_{w,r} is an exact 3+3 two-cover of that same six-set F. Since J_w has middle w and L_{w,r} has middle r, R41 applies to the two disjoint tight trimers and gives the central-anchor interaction through the unordered anchor pair {w,r}. As w and r were arbitrary distinct members of the four-set W, all six unordered witness pairs occur. Thus the R124 four-witness fan is supported on one exact six-vertex fold cell carrying a complete K4 of central-anchor interactions.

## Statement
In the standing order-ten smallest-counterexample case, the global-longest five-support family F cannot contain a globally minimum-overlap pair A,B with |A∩B|=3.

Standing order-ten smallest-counterexample case and the accepted global-longest support family F.

Parent-level elimination of the entire minimum-overlap-three butterfly branch, including both transversal and hub descendants and all zero-/positive-excess subbranches.

- **Curation note:** Overlap-three branch elimination is internal proof architecture beneath the complete order-ten closure C183.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Verified. R5 supplies an exact cover of H-S, R105 gives its 4+3 profile and forbids any P5 in H-S, while R126 forces a P5 from the disjoint P4 and P3 components. Therefore minimum longest-five support overlap three is impossible.

## Proof
Suppose A,B∈F are a globally minimum-overlap pair with |A∩B|=3, and let S=A∩B. By universal small-deletion exactness R5, H-S has an exact two-cover. By the accepted common-triple cap R105, every such exact cover has profile 4+3; write its components as a tight four-path Q and a disjoint tight trimer K. But R126 applies to Q and K and forces a tight path of order five inside V(Q)∪V(K)=V(H)\\S. This contradicts the first conclusion of R105 that H-S contains no tight path of order five. Therefore no globally minimum-overlap pair with overlap three can exist.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED/R127.md -->

# R128 — Longest-five support minimum overlap is one or two

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
In the standing order-ten smallest-counterexample case, if F is the family of supports of global-longest tight five-paths and m=min{|A∩B|: A,B∈F, A≠B}, then m∈{1,2}.

## Hypotheses
Standing order-ten smallest-counterexample case; accepted longest-five support family F.

## Scope
Parent-level frontier compression after elimination of minimum overlap three.

## Applicability
Use to replace the former minimum-overlap-three butterfly frontier. Any surviving smallest counterexample must contain a globally minimum-overlap longest-five pair of overlap one or two.

## Persistence
The conclusion concerns only graph-intrinsic support intersections.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not exclude overlap one or overlap two, and does not by itself produce a spanning two-cover.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** superseded
- **Lifecycle note:** Minimum-overlap 1-or-2 reduction is an internal staging theorem beneath the complete order-ten closure C183.
- **Curation note:** Minimum-overlap 1-or-2 reduction is an internal staging theorem beneath the complete order-ten closure C183.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Verified from R13, R14, and R127: minimum longest-five support overlap is forced into {1,2}.

## Proof
Let m be the minimum intersection size among distinct members of F. By R13 every two members of F intersect, so m>=1. By R14 there exist A,B in F with |A∩B|<=3, hence m<=3. If m=3, then A,B may be chosen as a globally minimum-overlap pair with intersection three, contradicting R127. Therefore m is neither 0 nor 3 and satisfies 1<=m<=2. Hence m∈{1,2}.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED/R128.md -->

# R129 — Minimum-overlap-two deletion gateway and disjoint-core fork

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Assume A,B are globally minimum-overlap supports of global-longest tight five-paths with |A∩B|=2. Put S=A∩B, U=A\\B, V=B\\A, and R=V(H)\\(A∪B), so |S|=|R|=2 and |U|=|V|=3. Then H-S contains a tight five-path with support D in F. Every such D has block profile (|D∩U|,|D∩V|,|D∩R|) equal to one of (2,2,1),(2,3,0),(3,2,0). Consequently at least one of A or B, call it L, has two distinct minimum-overlap partners among {A,B,D} whose two intersection cores inside L are disjoint 2-subsets.

## Hypotheses
Standing order-ten smallest-counterexample case; A,B are a globally minimum-overlap pair in the longest-five support family F with |A∩B|=2.

## Scope
Pure support/deletion geometry for the minimum-overlap-two branch.

## Applicability
Use as the parent normalization if R128 audits and the surviving minimum overlap is two. It replaces arbitrary overlap-two pairs by a longest support carrying two disjoint minimum-overlap cores.

## Persistence
All support blocks and intersections are graph-intrinsic; the constructed existence of D does not depend on retaining a particular deletion cover afterward.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not exclude minimum overlap two. Does not assert D is unique, does not force the (2,2,1) profile, and does not assert simultaneous currentness of A,B,D as paths.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** superseded
- **Lifecycle note:** Minimum-overlap-two deletion/disjoint-core gateway is internal proof architecture of the now-closed order-ten branch. Its accepted revision remains a dependency, while canonical discovery should route to the order-ten closure C183.
- **Curation note:** Minimum-overlap-two deletion/disjoint-core gateway is internal proof architecture of the now-closed order-ten branch. Its accepted revision remains a dependency, while canonical discovery should route to the order-ten closure C183.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Verified deletion gateway: exact 8-vertex two-cover is 5+3 or 4+4 under the order-five cap; R8+R126 yields a P5 in the 4+4 case; minimum-overlap-two incidence gives exactly the three listed profiles and the disjoint-core fork.

## Proof
Let S=A∩B, U=A\\B, V=B\\A, and R=V(H)\\(A∪B). Since |A|=|B|=5 and |S|=2 in an order-ten graph, |U|=|V|=3 and |R|=2. By R5, H-S has path-cover number exactly two, hence an exact two-cover. By R9 no tight path has more than five vertices, so the two component orders are either 5+3 or 4+4. In the 5+3 case, let D be the support of the five-path. In the 4+4 case, let Q be one four-path and let X be any three vertices of the other four-path. By R8, X admits a tight trimer orientation. Q and that trimer are disjoint, so R126 gives a tight five-path whose support D lies in H-S. In either case D is an order-five tight path, hence global-longest by R9, so D∈F. Because A,B are globally minimum-overlap with intersection two, |D∩A|>=2 and |D∩B|>=2. Since D is disjoint from S, these equal |D∩U| and |D∩V|. Writing u=|D∩U|, v=|D∩V|, r=|D∩R| gives u,v>=2, u,v<=3, r<=2, and u+v+r=5. Therefore (u,v,r) is exactly (2,2,1), (2,3,0), or (3,2,0). At least one of u,v equals two. If u=2, take L=A: L∩B=S and L∩D=D∩U are disjoint 2-subsets of L, and both B,D are minimum-overlap partners of L. If v=2, the symmetric choice L=B works. This proves the fork.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED/R129.md -->

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Let F be the family of supports of global-longest tight five-paths in an order-ten smallest counterexample. Then union F is V(H), intersection F is empty, and A intersect B is nonempty for every A,B in F.

## Scope
Order-ten smallest counterexample.

Support membership is graph-intrinsic; it does not make a path current in an unrelated representative.

Union: ITEM:18. Empty intersection: for every z, ITEM:14 supplies a longest P5 avoiding z. Pairwise intersection: two disjoint five-element longest supports on ten vertices are complementary; choosing corresponding tight five-paths gives a spanning two-cover, contradicting the counterexample.

# R130 — Minimum-overlap-two disjoint-core triangle normalization

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Assume the standing order-ten smallest-counterexample case and minimum longest-support overlap two. Then there exist three global-longest five-supports L,B,D such that X=L∩B and Y=L∩D are disjoint 2-subsets of L, while Z=B∩D is disjoint from L and has size 2 or 3. Hence X,Y,Z are pairwise disjoint and L,B,D have one of exactly two intersection types: (2,2,2), in which case |L∪B∪D|=9 and there is one exterior vertex; or (2,2,3), in which case |L∪B∪D|=8 and there are two exterior vertices.

## Hypotheses
Standing order-ten smallest-counterexample case; the minimum intersection among distinct global-longest five-supports equals 2; accepted R129.

## Scope
Pure support-incidence normalization of the minimum-overlap-two branch.

## Applicability
Use immediately after R129. It replaces the overlap-two branch by two finite support-triangle motifs with pairwise-disjoint intersection cores.

## Persistence
All three supports and their pairwise intersections are graph-intrinsic; the classification is purely set-theoretic once R129 supplies L,B,D.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not rule out either triangle type, does not assert simultaneous currentness of path representatives, and does not by itself force a spanning two-cover.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** superseded
- **Lifecycle note:** Minimum-overlap-two disjoint-core triangle normalization is proof-stage structure feeding the two motif impossibility theorems; the entire order-ten case is closed by C183.
- **Curation note:** Minimum-overlap-two disjoint-core triangle normalization is proof-stage structure feeding the two motif impossibility theorems; the entire order-ten case is closed by C183.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Verified pure set-theoretic normalization from R129: Z=B∩D is disjoint from L, has size 2 or 3, and inclusion-exclusion gives exactly the (2,2,2) union-9 and (2,2,3) union-8 motifs.

## Proof
By R129 choose global-longest five-supports L,B,D such that X=L∩B and Y=L∩D are disjoint and |X|=|Y|=2. Because the global minimum overlap among distinct members of F equals 2, |B∩D|≥2. Put Z=B∩D. If z∈Z∩L, then z∈B∩L=X and z∈D∩L=Y, contradicting X∩Y=∅. Hence Z∩L=∅. Since B has five vertices and |B∩L|=2, B\\L has size 3; similarly D\\L has size 3. Therefore Z⊆(B\\L)∩(D\\L), so |Z|≤3. Consequently |Z|∈{2,3}. Also X,Y⊆L while Z∩L=∅, so X,Y,Z are pairwise disjoint and L∩B∩D=∅. Inclusion-exclusion now yields |L∪B∪D|=|L|+|B|+|D|-|X|-|Y|-|Z|=15-2-2-|Z|=11-|Z|. Thus |Z|=2 gives union size 9 and one exterior vertex, while |Z|=3 gives union size 8 and two exterior vertices. This proves the normalization.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED/R130.md -->
