# R131 — Minimum-overlap-two triangle exact-root normalization

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Assume the standing order-ten smallest-counterexample case and minimum longest-support overlap two. Choose L,B,D as in R129, with X=L∩B and Y=L∩D disjoint 2-subsets of L. Put Z=B∩D. Then |Z| is 2 or 3. If |Z|=2, there are unique vertices p,b,d and one exterior vertex e such that L=X∪Y∪{p}, B=X∪Z∪{b}, D=Y∪Z∪{d}; deleting X,Y,Z respectively gives exact 5+3 covers D ⊔ {p,b,e}, B ⊔ {p,d,e}, and L ⊔ {b,d,e}, after orienting each displayed three-set as a tight trimer. If |Z|=3, there is a unique p∈L\\(X∪Y) and two exterior vertices e,f such that L=X∪Y∪{p}, B=X∪Z, D=Y∪Z; deleting X and Y respectively gives exact 5+3 covers D ⊔ {p,e,f} and B ⊔ {p,e,f}. Thus the (2,2,2) motif carries three cyclic 5+3 roots whose short trimers share one exterior vertex, while the (2,2,3) motif carries two 5+3 roots with one common physical short trimer.

## Hypotheses
Standing order-ten smallest-counterexample case; minimum longest-support overlap equals 2; accepted R129.

## Scope
Support/deletion normalization of the overlap-two disjoint-core fork.

## Applicability
Use to attack minimum overlap two through synchronized 5+3 roots. The 2-2-2 branch has a common short-trimer vertex; the 2-2-3 branch has an identical short-trimer support across two roots.

## Persistence
The support coordinates and deleted pairs are graph-intrinsic. Each short three-set can be oriented as a tight trimer by R8; the resulting exact covers are separate certificates.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert common orientations across distinct three-sets in the 2-2-2 branch, simultaneous currentness of the exact covers, or immediate 5+5 closure.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** superseded
- **Lifecycle note:** Minimum-overlap-two exact-root normalization is proof architecture for the two motif-impossibility branches, not an independent current discovery after order-ten closure C183.
- **Curation note:** Minimum-overlap-two exact-root normalization is proof architecture for the two motif-impossibility branches, not an independent current discovery after order-ten closure C183.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Statement verified. In both motifs, deleting the indicated pair-core leaves the named longest-five support plus exactly the listed complementary three-set; R8 orients that three-set as a tight trimer, and R5 supplies exactness of the pair-deletion two-cover.

## Proof
Take L,B,D from R129 and set X=L∩B, Y=L∩D. As in the direct set calculation, Z=B∩D is disjoint from L and has size 2 or 3. Suppose first |Z|=2. Since L has five vertices and X,Y are disjoint pairs, L=X∪Y∪{p} for a unique p. Similarly B=X∪Z∪{b} and D=Y∪Z∪{d} for unique b,d. These nine vertices are distinct, so let e be the unique vertex outside L∪B∪D. Delete X. The support D is disjoint from X and is a tight five-path support. The remaining three vertices of H-X outside D are exactly {p,b,e}; by R8 they admit a tight trimer orientation. Hence D and that trimer form an exact 5+3 cover of H-X. Cyclically, deleting Y gives B together with {p,d,e}, and deleting Z gives L together with {b,d,e}. Now suppose |Z|=3. Again L=X∪Y∪{p}. Since |B|=5 and B contains the disjoint sets X and Z of total size five, B=X∪Z; similarly D=Y∪Z. The union has eight vertices, so let e,f be the two exterior vertices. Deleting X leaves D intact and the remaining three vertices are {p,e,f}; orient them by R8 to obtain an exact 5+3 cover. Deleting Y gives B with the same physical short triple {p,e,f}. This proves the root normalization.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED/R131.md -->

# R14 — Low-overlap longest-support pair

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
There exist A,B in the longest-five support family F with |A intersect B| at most three.

## Scope
Order-ten smallest counterexample.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** superseded
- **Lifecycle note:** Existence of a longest-support pair with overlap at most three is strictly subsumed by C126/R128, which proves the global minimum overlap is one or two. Preserve as historical proof input.
- **Curation note:** Existence of a longest-support pair with overlap at most three is strictly subsumed by C126/R128, which proves the global minimum overlap is one or two. Preserve as historical proof input.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Legacy migration verification: this item was recorded as independently accepted in the controlling compressed A7C2 package and is being normalized into the A7C3 canonical schema.

## Proof
Assume every distinct pair in F intersects in at least four. Since supports have size five, choose A=C+{a}, B=C+{b} with |C|=4. Any further D either contains C, or omits c in C and the two intersection inequalities force D=(C-{c})+{a,b}. Thus F lies either in a common 4-star or a common 6-top. The first contradicts empty total intersection; the second contradicts full union on ten vertices.

<!-- BEGIN FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED/R140.md -->

# R140 — Type-(2,2,3) shared-trimer endpoint replacement rule

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Assume the minimum-overlap-two type-(2,2,3) motif of R130/R131: L=X∪Y∪{p}, B=X∪Z, D=Y∪Z with |X|=|Y|=2, |Z|=3, exterior vertices e,f, and common short trimer support P={p,e,f} in the exact roots D⊔P after deleting X and B⊔P after deleting Y. Fix any tight path ordering of D. For each endpoint t of that ordering there exists w∈P such that (D\\{t})∪{w} is a global-longest five-support. If t∈Y, then necessarily w=p. Symmetrically, for each endpoint t of any tight ordering of B there exists w∈P such that (B\\{t})∪{w} is a global-longest five-support, and if t∈X then necessarily w=p.

## Hypotheses
Standing order-ten smallest-counterexample case; minimum longest-support overlap equals two; accepted type-(2,2,3) support and exact-root normalization R130/R131.

## Scope
Support-level radius-one consequence inside the shared-short-trimer overlap-two motif. It is proved directly from accepted inputs and does not depend on returned R132 or pending R138.

## Applicability
Use to rotate the type-(2,2,3) motif through long-rail endpoints. A private endpoint forces replacement by p; a Z-endpoint admits a replacement by one of p,e,f.

## Persistence
The generated replacement support is a graph-intrinsic global-longest support. The chosen endpoint and path ordering belong to the displayed root representative.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not identify the replacement witness for a Z-endpoint, does not assert both endpoint replacements use distinct witnesses, and does not couple the B-root and D-root replacements in one representative.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** superseded
- **Lifecycle note:** Shared-trimer endpoint replacement rule is conditional type-(2,2,3) machinery under the motif eliminated by C131/R147.
- **Curation note:** Shared-trimer endpoint replacement rule is conditional type-(2,2,3) machinery under the motif eliminated by C131/R147.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Verified direct type-(2,2,3) endpoint-replacement rule. Every P-plus-two-D support is non-Hamiltonian by minimum-overlap-two incidence; if all Q-plus-w supports also failed, the support-tracked R126 forcing would contradict those exclusions. Hence an endpoint replacement exists, and a Y-endpoint forces witness p by overlap with L. Symmetric B-root statement is valid.

## Proof
Work first in the exact root D⊔P after deleting X, where P={p,e,f}. Choose a tight ordering D=(d1,d2,d3,d4,d5) and an orientation (x,y,z) of P that is a tight trimer. Let t=d5 and Q=(a,b,c,d)=(d1,d2,d3,d4); the other endpoint is handled by the last four-window identically.\n\nFirst, no support P∪{u,v} with u,v∈D can support a tight P5. Indeed any such P5 is global-longest by R9. Since B=X∪Z and P is disjoint from B, minimum overlap two forces u,v∈Z. But then L=X∪Y∪{p} meets P∪{u,v} only in p, giving overlap one, contradiction. Thus every P-plus-two-D support is non-Hamiltonian.\n\nSuppose for contradiction that none of Q∪{x},Q∪{y},Q∪{z} is Hamiltonian. For every w∈P, failure of (w,a,b,c,d) and (a,b,c,d,w) gives baw and wdc tight by R3; failure of (b,a,w,d,c) then gives dwa tight. Thus baw,dwa,wdc are tight for every w∈P. The three reversal pairs on the trimer have, up to relabeling, cyclic and transitive types. In the cyclic type xyz,yzx,zxy are tight. The candidates (b,a,z,x,y), (y,z,x,d,c), (d,x,z,a,y), and (x,d,y,a,z) lie respectively on P∪{a,b}, P∪{c,d}, P∪{a,d}, P∪{a,d}; all these supports were just shown non-Hamiltonian. Their successive failures force xza, dxz, yaz, ydx tight, after which (y,d,x,z,a) is a tight P5 on P∪{a,d}, contradiction. In the transitive type xyz,xzy,yxz are tight; the analogous four failed candidates force zxa, dzx, yax, zdy tight, after which (z,d,y,a,x) is a tight P5 on P∪{a,d}, contradiction. Therefore Q∪{w} supports a tight P5 for some w∈P. By R9 its support C=(D\\{t})∪{w} lies in the global-longest family F.\n\nIf t∈Y, then D\\{t} consists of the other Y vertex together with all three Z vertices. Hence C∩L has size one when w∈{e,f} and size two when w=p. Since the global minimum overlap is two, w=p is forced.\n\nThe same proof applies to the other endpoint of D. For the B-root after deleting Y, interchange X with Y and B with D. Any P-plus-two-B support meeting D twice must use two Z vertices and then meets L only at p, so the same forcing gives an endpoint replacement B\\{t}+w; if t∈X, minimum overlap with L forces w=p.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED/R140.md -->

# R141 — Type-(2,2,3) common-trimer universal shield and terminal saturation

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Assume the minimum-overlap-two type-(2,2,3) motif of R130/R131: L=X∪Y∪{p}, B=X∪Z, D=Y∪Z, with |X|=|Y|=2, |Z|=3, exterior vertices e,f, and shared short-trimer support P={p,e,f}. Put U=V(H)\\P=X∪Y∪Z. Then no five-set P∪{u,v}, for distinct u,v∈U, supports a tight five-path. Consequently, fix any tight orientation P=(a,b,c) and define E_left={u∈U:(u,a,b) is tight} and E_right={u∈U:(b,c,u) is tight}. There are no distinct x∈E_left and y∈E_right. Hence either E_left is empty, or E_right is empty, or E_left=E_right={q} for one q∈U. By boundary antisymmetry, in the first case (b,a,u) is tight for every u∈U; in the second case (u,c,b) is tight for every u∈U; and in the singleton/singleton case both families of reverse turns hold for every u∈U\\{q}. Thus every tight orientation of the common trimer has either one terminal dimer with seven common outside reverse witnesses or both terminal dimers with six common outside reverse witnesses.

## Hypotheses
Standing order-ten smallest-counterexample case; minimum longest-support overlap equals two; accepted type-(2,2,3) normalization R130/R131; boundary antisymmetry R3 and longest-path value R9.

## Scope
Support-level and ordered-turn compression of the shared-short-trimer branch. No payment, actualization, or representative coupling is used.

## Applicability
Use as the canonical fixed-trimer interface for the type-(2,2,3) motif. It upgrades the two-root shared trimer to a universal five-support shield and a near-total terminal reverse-star system before any descendant is opened.

## Persistence
The non-Hamiltonicity of all P-plus-two supports is graph-intrinsic. For each chosen tight orientation of P, the extender sets and forced reverse turns are graph-intrinsic ordered-turn facts.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert which terminal side is saturated, does not assert a common saturated side across different tight orientations of P, does not couple paid descendants, and does not itself assert a spanning 5+5 cover.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** superseded
- **Lifecycle note:** Universal shield/terminal saturation is conditional machinery inside the type-(2,2,3) motif, which is eliminated outright by C131/R147.
- **Curation note:** Universal shield/terminal saturation is conditional machinery inside the type-(2,2,3) motif, which is eliminated outright by C131/R147.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Verified the universal P-plus-two non-Hamiltonicity by minimum-overlap counting against B,D,L. The extender-set dichotomy is exact: no distinct left/right extenders can coexist, so either one side is empty or both are the same singleton; R3 then yields the stated 7-witness or 6+6 reverse-terminal saturation.

## Proof
Let U=X∪Y∪Z=V(H)\\P. Suppose for contradiction that S=P∪{u,v}, with distinct u,v∈U, supports a tight five-path. By R9, S is a global-longest five-support. Since e,f lie in none of L,B,D and P∩L={p}, P∩B=P∩D=∅, minimum overlap two with B forces both u and v to lie in B=X∪Z. Minimum overlap two with D likewise forces both u and v to lie in D=Y∪Z. Therefore u,v∈B∩D=Z. But then S∩L={p}, of size one, contradicting minimum overlap two. Hence no P∪{u,v} is Hamiltonian. Now fix a tight orientation P=(a,b,c). If there were distinct x∈E_left and y∈E_right, then (x,a,b), (a,b,c), and (b,c,y) would all be tight, so x,a,b,c,y would be a tight five-path on P∪{x,y}, contradiction. Thus every member of E_left equals every member of E_right whenever both sets are nonempty. Hence either one set is empty, or both are the same singleton {q}. If u∉E_left, then (u,a,b) is bad, so by R3 its complete reversal (b,a,u) is tight. If u∉E_right, then (b,c,u) is bad, so (u,c,b) is tight. The stated seven-witness and six-witness alternatives follow immediately.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED/R141.md -->

# R142 — Type-(2,2,3) private-endpoint motif rotation

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Assume the accepted minimum-overlap-two type-(2,2,3) motif L=X∪Y∪{p}, B=X∪Z, D=Y∪Z with |X|=|Y|=2, |Z|=3 and exterior pair {e,f}, so deleting X gives the exact root D ⊔ {p,e,f} and deleting Y gives B ⊔ {p,e,f}. Fix a tight path ordering of D and suppose an endpoint t lies in Y. Then E=(D\\{t})∪{p} is a global-longest five-support. Writing Y'=(Y\\{t})∪{p} and p'=t, the triple L,B,E is again a type-(2,2,3) motif with the same X,Z and exterior pair {e,f}: L=X∪Y'∪{p'}, B=X∪Z, E=Y'∪Z. Moreover deleting X gives the exact 5+3 root E ⊔ {p',e,f}, and deleting Y' gives B ⊔ {p',e,f}; thus the rotated motif has shared short trimer {t,e,f}. The symmetric statement holds when an endpoint t of B lies in X, rotating p with t while preserving D,Z and {e,f}.

## Hypotheses
Standing order-ten smallest-counterexample case; minimum longest-support overlap two; accepted type-(2,2,3) normalization R130/R131 and endpoint replacement rule R140.

## Scope
Support-level and exact-root symmetry of the type-(2,2,3) shared-trimer motif.

## Applicability
Use to convert any private long-rail endpoint into another shared-trimer type-(2,2,3) motif over the same exterior pair. Iterating available private endpoints creates a family of singleton states tied to {e,f} without opening payment descendants.

## Persistence
The rotated support E and all displayed support identities are graph-intrinsic. The exact roots use separate tight trimer orientations on the physical complement three-set.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert that every private vertex can be made an endpoint, that different rotations are simultaneously current path representatives, or that the shared exterior dimer {e,f} has one common sign polarity across all rotated trimers.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** superseded
- **Lifecycle note:** Private-endpoint motif rotation is a valid internal lemma of the type-(2,2,3) branch, but C131/R147 proves that motif impossible outright.
- **Curation note:** Private-endpoint motif rotation is a valid internal lemma of the type-(2,2,3) branch, but C131/R147 proves that motif impossible outright.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Private endpoint replacement genuinely rotates the type-(2,2,3) motif and its shared short trimer; exactness is supported by adjusted proof P141 with R5.

## Proof
Let t∈Y be an endpoint of the chosen tight ordering of D. By R140, because t is a private Y-endpoint, the replacement witness is forced to be p, so E=(D\\{t})∪{p} is the support of a global-longest tight five-path. Put Y'=(Y\\{t})∪{p} and p'=t. Then E=Y'∪Z and L=X∪Y∪{p}=X∪Y'∪{p'}, while B=X∪Z. The sets X,Y',Z are pairwise disjoint with sizes 2,2,3, so L∩B=X, L∩E=Y', and B∩E=Z. Hence L,B,E have type (2,2,3) with singleton p' and the same two exterior vertices e,f. Now H−X has vertex set E∪{t,e,f}; since E is a tight five-path support and {t,e,f} is a three-set, R8 supplies a tight trimer orientation on {t,e,f}, giving an exact 5+3 cover E⊔{t,e,f}. Likewise H−Y' has vertex set B∪{t,e,f}, so R8 gives the exact root B⊔{t,e,f}. Thus the new motif shares the short trimer support {t,e,f}. The argument with B and X exchanged is identical.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED/R142.md -->

# R143 — Type-(2,2,3) private rotations force exterior-dimer sign interaction

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Assume the accepted type-(2,2,3) motif L=X∪Y∪{p}, B=X∪Z, D=Y∪Z with exterior pair {e,f}. Suppose t is a private endpoint, meaning t∈Y is an endpoint of a tight ordering of D or symmetrically t∈X is an endpoint of a tight ordering of B. Then the physical exterior dimer {e,f} carries two signed certificates with distinct witnesses p and t, obtained from the original short trimer {p,e,f} and the endpoint-rotated short trimer {t,e,f}. Hence R38 forces a nontrivial same-support interaction on {e,f}: either the two certificates have the same polarity and enter the accepted two-extension collision package, or they have opposite polarities and yield the accepted strict two-ended signed-path interaction. Moreover, if two distinct private endpoints t1,t2 are available among the two long-root orderings, then {e,f} carries signed certificates with the three distinct witnesses p,t1,t2; therefore two of the three certificates have the same polarity, so a same-polarity two-extension collision on the exterior dimer {e,f} is unavoidable.

## Hypotheses
Standing order-ten smallest-counterexample case; minimum overlap two; accepted type-(2,2,3) normalization R130/R131; endpoint replacement rule R140; boundary antisymmetry and accepted sign-interaction machinery.

## Scope
Graph-intrinsic sign consequence of private endpoint rotation; no payment or simultaneous-currentness claim.

## Applicability
Use to split the type-(2,2,3) endpoint analysis. Two or more private endpoint occurrences immediately force an exterior-dimer same-polarity collision; a single private endpoint already forces a two-witness same-support interaction. The only collision-free endpoint regime can therefore have at most one private endpoint occurrence across the two long roots.

## Persistence
The physical dimer {e,f}, witness identities, and resulting R38 interaction certificates are graph-intrinsic. The two trimer orientations are separate certificates and need not be current in one representative.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not identify the polarity of an individual certificate, does not assert simultaneous payment descendants, and does not by itself turn the R38 collision or strict interaction into a spanning 5+5 cover.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** superseded
- **Lifecycle note:** Exterior-dimer sign interaction from private rotations is valid type-(2,2,3) branch machinery, but the whole motif is eliminated by C131/R147.
- **Curation note:** Exterior-dimer sign interaction from private rotations is valid type-(2,2,3) branch machinery, but the whole motif is eliminated by C131/R147.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Distinct endpoint rotations create distinct-witness signed certificates on the same physical exterior dimer; R38 gives the stated interaction/collision alternatives.

## Proof
Suppose first that t∈Y is an endpoint of D; the B/X case is symmetric. By R140, E=(D\\{t})∪{p} is a global-longest support. In the original exact root H−X, the short component has support P0={p,e,f}. In H−X after replacing D by E, the physical complement of E is P1={t,e,f}; by R3, for the prescribed middle e exactly one of (p,e,f),(f,e,p) is a tight trimer orientation on P0, and exactly one of (t,e,f),(f,e,t) is a tight trimer orientation on P1. By R41, each tight trimer supplies signed terminal dimers. In both cases the physical dimer {e,f} is terminal; its witness is the opposite outer vertex, namely p for P0 and t for P1. Thus the same physical support {e,f} has two signed certificates with distinct witnesses p and t. R38 applies: equal polarity gives the accepted two-extension collision package; opposite polarity gives same-support exclusivity and the strict two-ended signed path. If two distinct private endpoints t1,t2 are available, repeat the argument for each. The dimer {e,f} then has three certificates with witnesses p,t1,t2. There are only two polarities, so two certificates have the same polarity; their witnesses are distinct, and R38 forces a same-polarity two-extension collision.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED/R143.md -->

# R144 — Type-(2,2,3) reduces to type-(2,2,2) or an exterior-dimer collision

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Assume the accepted minimum-overlap-two type-(2,2,3) motif L=X∪Y∪{p}, B=X∪Z, D=Y∪Z with |X|=|Y|=2, |Z|=3 and exterior pair {e,f}, with exact root B ⊔ {p,e,f} after deleting Y. Fix any tight path ordering of B and let t1,t2 be its two distinct endpoints. Then either there exists a global-longest support E such that L,D,E form a type-(2,2,2) triangle with three pairwise-disjoint overlap-two cores, or the exterior physical dimer {e,f} carries a same-polarity two-extension collision with distinct witnesses among {p,t1,t2}. More precisely, apply R140 at each endpoint ti to obtain Ei=(B\\{ti})∪{wi}, wi∈{p,e,f}. If some wi∈{e,f}, then necessarily ti∈Z and L∩D=Y, D∩Ei=Z\\{ti}, L∩Ei=X, so L,D,Ei is type (2,2,2). Otherwise w1=w2=p. Then after deleting Y the complements of E1,E2 are the tight trimer supports {t1,e,f} and {t2,e,f}; together with the original short trimer {p,e,f}, these give three signed certificates on the same physical dimer {e,f} with distinct witnesses p,t1,t2. Two certificates share a polarity, so R38 forces the accepted same-polarity two-extension collision package on {e,f}.

## Hypotheses
Standing order-ten smallest-counterexample case; minimum longest-support overlap equals two; accepted type-(2,2,3) support/exact-root normalization R130/R131 and endpoint replacement rule R140.

## Scope
Parent reduction of the entire type-(2,2,3) motif. It uses one long-root ordering and no payment or representative coupling.

## Applicability
Use to remove endpoint case trees from the type-(2,2,3) branch. Subsequent work need only close the type-(2,2,2) motif and the named same-polarity exterior-dimer collision alternative.

## Persistence
All generated longest supports, pairwise core identities, and the exterior-dimer collision certificate are graph-intrinsic. The three trimer orientations are separate certificates.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert that the type-(2,2,2) branch is impossible, does not spend the exterior-dimer collision, and does not assert simultaneous currentness of the three short trimers or replacement roots.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** superseded
- **Lifecycle note:** Reduction of type-(2,2,3) to type-(2,2,2) or collision is strictly weaker than C131/R147, which directly eliminates type-(2,2,3).
- **Curation note:** Reduction of type-(2,2,3) to type-(2,2,2) or collision is strictly weaker than C131/R147, which directly eliminates type-(2,2,3).
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** One long-root ordering reduces type-(2,2,3) to either a type-(2,2,2) support triangle or an unavoidable same-polarity collision on {e,f}.

## Proof
Let B=(b1,b2,b3,b4,b5) be any tight ordering and put t1=b1,t2=b5. For each i, R140 supplies wi∈P={p,e,f} such that Ei=(B\\{ti})∪{wi} is a global-longest support. If wi is e or f, R140's private-endpoint clause shows ti cannot lie in X, hence ti∈Z. Then Ei=X∪(Z\\{ti})∪{wi}. Since wi is exterior to L∪D, we have L∩D=Y, D∩Ei=Z\\{ti}, and L∩Ei=X. These are three pairwise-disjoint 2-subsets, so L,D,Ei is a type-(2,2,2) minimum-overlap triangle. Assume therefore that neither endpoint produces this alternative. Then w1=w2=p. For each i, Ei=(B\\{ti})∪{p} is a tight five-path support. In the fixed deletion H−Y, the physical complement of Ei is exactly Ti={ti,e,f}; by R8 it supports a tight trimer. The original root has short trimer T0={p,e,f}. For each of T0,T1,T2 prescribe e as the middle. By R3 exactly one of the two complete reversals with middle e is tight, and R41 supplies signed terminal dimers. In every case {e,f} is a terminal physical dimer, with witness respectively p,t1,t2. The witnesses are distinct because t1,t2 are distinct vertices of B and B is disjoint from {p,e,f}. Thus {e,f} has three signed certificates with distinct witnesses. There are only two polarities, so two certificates have the same polarity; R38 then forces the accepted same-polarity two-extension collision package on the physical support {e,f}.

# R147 — Minimum-overlap-two type (2,2,3) shared-trimer motif is impossible

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
In the standing order-ten smallest-counterexample case with minimum longest-support overlap two, the type-(2,2,3) disjoint-core triangle of R130/R131 cannot occur. Hence every surviving minimum-overlap-two disjoint-core triangle must have type (2,2,2).

## Hypotheses
Standing order-ten smallest-counterexample case; minimum longest-support overlap two; accepted type-(2,2,3) normalization and R141 common-trimer universal shield; three-exterior pair-extension lemma R146.

## Scope
Direct support/ordered-turn closure of the shared-short-trimer overlap-two motif. No sign, payment, actualization, return, or endpoint-preserving R132 machinery.

## Applicability
Use immediately after the overlap-two triangle normalization. It removes the |Z|=3 / two-exterior branch and leaves only type (2,2,2).

## Persistence
The contradiction is graph-intrinsic on the fixed common trimer and any three of its exterior vertices.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not address the remaining type-(2,2,2) motif or minimum overlap one.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** superseded
- **Lifecycle note:** Type-(2,2,3) motif elimination is internal order-ten proof architecture beneath C183.
- **Curation note:** Type-(2,2,3) motif elimination is internal order-ten proof architecture beneath C183.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** The accepted R141 universal shield contradicts R146 on any three exterior vertices, eliminating the type-(2,2,3) motif without R132.

## Proof
In the type-(2,2,3) coordinates of R141, fix any tight orientation of the common short-trimer support P={p,e,f}. Its exterior U=X∪Y∪Z has seven vertices. R141 asserts that for every two distinct u,v∈U the five-set P∪{u,v} is non-Hamiltonian. Choose any three distinct x,y,z∈U. The local six-vertex lemma R146 applies to the fixed tight trimer P and the three exterior vertices x,y,z, and therefore at least one of P∪{x,y}, P∪{x,z}, P∪{y,z} supports a tight five-path. This directly contradicts R141. Thus the type-(2,2,3) motif is impossible. This proof does not use the returned endpoint-preserving amplification R132, R38, payment, or representative coupling.

# R15 — Radius-One Low-Overlap Localization

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
For every prescribed P in F, either there exists A in F with |A intersect P| at most three, or there are two actual one-vertex replacement supports A=P-{p_i}+{x} and B=P-{p_j}+{y} with i != j and x != y, hence |A intersect B|=3.

## Scope
Order-ten smallest counterexample; F is the actual longest-five support family.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
No generic one-vertex replacement theorem is asserted; only actual members of F are used.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Radius-one low-overlap localization is a specialized order-ten strengthening whose only downstream consumer is already retired C16. No active proof-library need remains; preserve accepted history.
- **Curation note:** Radius-one low-overlap localization is a specialized order-ten strengthening whose only downstream consumer is already retired C16. No active proof-library need remains; preserve accepted history.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Legacy migration verification: this item was recorded as independently accepted in the controlling compressed A7C2 package and is being normalized into the A7C3 canonical schema.

## Proof
Fix P and assume no F-member meets P in at most three. Every F-member differing from P and omitting p_i is then P-{p_i}+{x}. Empty total intersection gives every left p_i positive degree in the replacement graph; full union gives every exterior x positive degree. A bipartite graph with all ten vertices positive degree cannot have matching number one, since a pairwise-intersecting edge family is a star and leaves vertices on one side isolated. Two disjoint edges p_i~x and p_j~y yield actual supports A,B with intersection P-{p_i,p_j}, of size three.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED/R15.md -->

# R153 — Universal two-orientation dimer common shadow

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Let H be a smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample and let D={x,y} be any physical vertex pair. There exists one fixed exact two-cover H-D=U⊔V such that both U⊔V⊔(x,y) and U⊔V⊔(y,x) are minimum three-cover representatives of H. Thus the two opposite orientations of the same physical dimer can be compared over literally identical residual rails U,V. Relative to the four-component shadow W=U⊔V⊔(x)⊔(y), inserting either dimer has gain one and cycle debt zero.

## Hypotheses
H is a smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in the standing project sense; x,y are distinct vertices and D={x,y}.

## Scope
Universal arbitrary-pair common-shadow lemma. It is not restricted to endpoint-transfer edges, special markers, pair-deletion rigidity, or an already chosen fan. It refines R5 by retaining one chosen exact residual two-cover as a shared literal shadow for both dimer orientations.

## Applicability
Use whenever two opposite orientations of one physical pair must be tested or compared without changing the residual rails. This supplies a lawful same-shadow bridge for mirror arguments, orientation classification, sign tests, and pair-deletion consumers.

## Persistence
The residual rails U,V are literally the same in the two displayed minimum covers. The selected dimer orientation differs. Any graph-intrinsic fact about U,V remains true across the comparison; unrelated current facts are not preserved unless encoded in U or V. The common-shadow guarantee is existential in the choice of one exact H-D two-cover, not universal over every exact complement.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not imply that both dimer orientations are simultaneously selected in one cover; does not give nontriviality or size bounds for U,V beyond R5; does not supply pair-deletion rigidity; does not preserve arbitrary ancestry or roles; does not imply a progress measure, capture, protection, or spanning two-cover. Special common-shadow theorems remain nonredundant when they retain extra labels or ancestry.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Universal two-orientation dimer common shadow is an almost immediate R5/two-vertex-path convenience wrapper with no consumers; retire under the strong-or-versatile standard.
- **Curation note:** Universal two-orientation dimer common shadow is an almost immediate R5/two-vertex-path convenience wrapper with no consumers; retire under the strong-or-versatile standard.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Universal two-orientation dimer common shadow follows directly from R5 and minimum-cover restoration over one fixed residual exact two-cover.

## Proof
Recovered audited proof from CRITIC_HANDOFF_INCREMENTAL_HANDOFF_RESEARCHER_34_INCIDENT_PAIR_MIRROR_RESELECTION_CAPTURED_BOUNDARY_PACKET_2026-08-24_2026-08-24.md §3.1. The audit takes D={x,y}. Minimality gives pc(H-D)≤2; in the current bank R5 sharpens this directly to pc(H-D)=2. Choose H-D=U⊔V. The same U,V support U⊔V⊔(x,y) and U⊔V⊔(y,x). Because H has no spanning two-cover, these displayed three-covers are minimum. Relative to W=U⊔V⊔(x)⊔(y), either insertion only joins two isolated singleton components, hence gain one and zero cycle debt. The Critic explicitly PASSed both Minimality Common-Shadow Exactness for every physical pair and Universal Two-Orientation Dimer Common Shadow, and noted Pair-Deletion Rigidity is not required for bare common-shadow existence.

# R16 — Common-Frame Equality / Positive-Excess Dichotomy

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
In the radius-one arm of Radius-One Low-Overlap Localization, let S=P-{p_i,p_j}, U={p_j,x}, V={p_i,y}, and R be the vertices outside S union U union V. For any exact two-cover T of H-S and partition Pi={U,V,R}, t_Pi(T)=1+sigma with sigma>=0. If sigma=0, T is literally a tight four-path on U union V plus a tight trimer on R, and restoring any tight trimer orientation on S gives a spanning minimum 4+3+3 cover. Otherwise sigma>=1 and t_Pi(T)>=2.

## Scope
Order-ten smallest counterexample; actual radius-one replacement supports A,B sharing S.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
No stronger positive-excess classification; sigma is representative- and partition-relative; crossing conclusions do not supply orientation, ancestry, or transported currentness.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Correct order-ten radius-one scaffolding with no live downstream proof consumer; no canonical successor was found in the bounded maintenance search. Preserve the accepted theorem as historical mathematics rather than normal active retrieval.
- **Curation note:** Correct order-ten radius-one scaffolding with no live downstream proof consumer; no canonical successor was found in the bounded maintenance search. Preserve the accepted theorem as historical mathematics rather than normal active retrieval.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Legacy migration verification: this item was recorded as independently accepted in the controlling compressed A7C2 package and is being normalized into the A7C3 canonical schema.

## Proof
Delete common S. Then H-S=U sqcup V sqcup R with sizes 2,2,3, and pc(U)=pc(V)=pc(R)=1, the last by ITEM:10. ITEM:4 gives pc(H-S)=2 and ITEM:16 gives profile 5+2 or 4+3. Puncturing the actual retained longest paths A and B forces in the same exact T a transition across U|(V union R) and one across V|(U union R). ITEM:8 gives t_Pi(T)=1+sigma. If sigma=0 there is exactly one transition total, so it must be U-V; no transition touches R. Equality forces each class restriction to realize pc=1, hence one tight P4 on U union V and one tight P3 on R. Restore a tight trimer on S using ITEM:10 to obtain a spanning minimum 4+3+3 cover. If equality fails, integral sigma>=1 and t>=2.

# R168 — Small-Deletion Staircase Rail Floor

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Let H be a smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample. Let D be a deletion set of size d in {1,2,3}, and let H-D=P sqcup Q be any exact two-cover. Then |P|,|Q| >= 5-d. Thus one-vertex deletion has rail floor 4, pair deletion has rail floor 3, and arbitrary three-vertex deletion has rail floor 2.

## Hypotheses
H is a smallest counterexample; D subset V(H) with |D|=d in {1,2,3}; P sqcup Q is an exact two-cover of H-D.

## Scope
Smallest-counterexample small-deletion structure. Applies to arbitrary deletion sets of the stated sizes, not only tight-path deletion sets.

## Applicability
Parent rail-size theorem for deletion arguments. It strictly strengthens bare pair-deletion nontriviality and removes separate singleton-rail exclusions after one-, two-, and three-vertex deletion.

## Persistence
A size constraint on every exact two-cover of the fixed deletion. It is graph/deletion intrinsic at the quantified level; no specific current rail survives a representative change.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
No lower bound is asserted here for four-vertex deletion rails beyond exact two-cover status. No orientation, marker ancestry, selected state, endpoint role, or common-shadow information from specialized pair/trimer theorems is supplied.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** High-use but mathematically routine wrapper: the 4/3/2 rail floors follow immediately from R5 by adjoining a short rail to the deletion set. Retire and inline R5 conceptually in consumers.
- **Curation note:** High-use but mathematically routine wrapper: the 4/3/2 rail floors follow immediately from R5 by adjoining a short rail to the deletion set. Retire and inline R5 conceptually in consumers.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Small-Deletion Staircase Rail Floor verified.

## Proof
Suppose without loss of generality |P|<=4-d. Put E=D union V(P). Since d in {1,2,3}, E is nonempty and |E|<=4. But H-E=Q is Hamiltonian, so pc(H-E)=1. This contradicts R5, which gives pc(H-E)=2 for every nonempty deletion of at most four vertices. Therefore |P|>=5-d. The same argument gives |Q|>=5-d.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED/R168.md -->

# R169 — Proper Tight-Path Exterior Order-Five Floor

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Every proper tight path K in a smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample H leaves at least five exterior vertices: |V(H)-V(K)|>=5. Equivalently the maximum order L(H) of a proper tight path satisfies L(H)<=|H|-5.

## Hypotheses
H is a smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample and K is a proper graph-intrinsic tight path of H.

## Scope
Universal smallest-counterexample path-size theorem, independent of how K was produced or currentized.

## Applicability
Immediately upgrades any proper tight path with five exterior vertices to global-longest status and rules out oversized proper path packets. It is the clean parent behind many later five-exterior equality and order-ten longest-path normalizations.

## Persistence
Graph-intrinsic size constraint on K. It survives arbitrary representative changes because it refers only to the vertex set of the tight path.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not itself supply endpoint reverse-star orientations, selected roles, exact complement rails, source maximinity, marker ancestry, or transfer coordinates. Those require separate theorems.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** superseded
- **Lifecycle note:** Proper Tight-Path Exterior Order-Five Floor is an immediate consequence of universal small-deletion exactness R5: an oversized proper path would leave a deletion of at most four whose complement is Hamiltonian. Preserve historical citations, but make C5 the canonical theorem.
- **Curation note:** Proper Tight-Path Exterior Order-Five Floor is an immediate consequence of universal small-deletion exactness R5: an oversized proper path would leave a deletion of at most four whose complement is Hamiltonian. Preserve historical citations, but make C5 the canonical theorem.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Proper Tight-Path Exterior Order-Five Floor verified.

## Proof
Let D=V(H)-V(K). Since K is proper, D is nonempty. If |D|<=4, R5 gives pc(H-D)=2. But H-D is exactly the tight path K, so pc(H-D)=1. Contradiction. Hence |D|>=5, equivalently |K|<=|H|-5.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED/R169.md -->

# R183 — Minimum-overlap-two type (2,2,2) motif is impossible

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
In the standing order-ten smallest-counterexample case with minimum longest-support overlap two, the type-(2,2,2) disjoint-core triangle of R130/R131 cannot occur. Hence minimum longest-support overlap two is impossible.

## Hypotheses
Standing order-ten smallest-counterexample case; minimum longest-support overlap equals two; accepted type-(2,2,2) normalization R130/R131; accepted three-exterior pair-extension lemma R146; longest-path value R9.

## Scope
Direct support-level closure of the remaining minimum-overlap-two triangle motif. No sign, payment, currentization, return, or ancestry machinery is used.

## Applicability
Use after R147 has removed type (2,2,3), or directly whenever the R130/R131 type-(2,2,2) motif is present. Together with R147 this eliminates minimum overlap two.

## Persistence
The contradiction is graph-intrinsic on one fixed short trimer, two vertices of one overlap core, and one vertex of the opposite longest support.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not address minimum overlap one and does not itself produce a spanning 5+5 cover.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** superseded
- **Lifecycle note:** Type-(2,2,2) motif elimination is internal order-ten proof architecture beneath C183.
- **Curation note:** Type-(2,2,2) motif elimination is internal order-ten proof architecture beneath C183.
- **Review status:** accepted

## Proof
Let L,B,D be the type-(2,2,2) triangle from R130/R131, so L=X∪Y∪{p}, B=X∪Z∪{b}, D=Y∪Z∪{d}, where X,Y,Z are pairwise disjoint two-sets and e is the unique exterior vertex. Write X={x1,x2}. By R131, the three-set P={p,b,e} is the short side of an exact 5+3 root after deleting X; by R8 choose a tight trimer orientation on P. Observe that P is disjoint from D, because D=Y∪Z∪{d}. Choose any r∈D. The vertices x1,x2,r are distinct and lie outside P. By R146, at least one of the five-sets P∪{x1,x2}, P∪{x1,r}, P∪{x2,r} supports a tight five-vertex path. By R9 its support is a member of the global-longest support family. Yet each of these three supports meets D in at most one vertex: P∩D is empty, x1 and x2 are outside D, and among the three added exterior vertices only r belongs to D. This contradicts the assumption that the global minimum overlap between distinct longest-five supports is two. Therefore the type-(2,2,2) motif is impossible. Since R147 already eliminates type-(2,2,3), minimum overlap two is impossible.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED/R183.md -->

# R184 — Minimum-overlap-one two-hole replacement fan

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Assume the standing order-ten smallest-counterexample case and let A be a global-longest five-support with five-vertex exterior E=V(H)\\A. Suppose the global minimum overlap between distinct longest-five supports is one. Choose any tight trimer support P contained in E and write E\\P={x,y}. Then for every a in A, at least one of E\\{x}∪{a} and E\\{y}∪{a} is a global-longest five-support. Consequently one of the two four-sets E\\{x}, E\\{y} is contained in at least three distinct global-longest five-supports obtained by adjoining three distinct vertices of A.

## Hypotheses
Standing order-ten smallest-counterexample case; global minimum overlap among distinct longest-five supports equals one; accepted R8, R9, R13 and recovered three-exterior pair-extension lemma R146.

## Scope
Support-level gateway for the minimum-overlap-one branch. No sign, payment, exact-return, or representative synchronization is used.

## Applicability
Use as the first normalization once minimum overlap one is established. It turns an arbitrary overlap-one pair into a radius-one fan over one of two four-vertex exterior cores.

## Persistence
All resulting five-supports and the common four-core are graph-intrinsic. The chosen tight trimer orientation is only a proof certificate.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not identify which of the two holes is used for a given a, does not assert one common hole works for all five vertices of A, and does not itself force a spanning two-cover.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** superseded
- **Lifecycle note:** Minimum-overlap-one two-hole replacement fan is the local branch engine later eliminated outright by C182/R190.
- **Curation note:** Minimum-overlap-one two-hole replacement fan is the local branch engine later eliminated outright by C182/R190.
- **Review status:** accepted

## Proof
Let A be a global-longest five-support and E=V(H)\\A. Since H is a counterexample to a spanning two-path cover, E cannot support a tight five-path: otherwise A together with a tight path on E would be a spanning 5+5 cover. Choose a three-subset P of E and orient it as a tight trimer using R8. Write the remaining two vertices of E as x,y. Fix any a∈A. Apply R146 to P and the three distinct exterior vertices x,y,a. At least one of P∪{x,y}=E, P∪{x,a}=E\\{y}∪{a}, or P∪{y,a}=E\\{x}∪{a} supports a tight five-path. The first support E is impossible, so at least one of the two one-vertex replacement supports is Hamiltonian. By R9 it is global-longest. This holds for each of the five choices a∈A. Each a therefore chooses at least one of the two holes x,y; assigning one available hole to each a and applying pigeonhole, one hole is used for at least three distinct vertices of A. Equivalently one of E\\{x},E\\{y} lies in at least three distinct global-longest five-supports obtained by adjoining distinct A-vertices.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED/R184.md -->

# R189 — Minimum-overlap-one twenty-replacement saturation

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Assume the standing order-ten smallest-counterexample case and minimum longest-support overlap one. For every global-longest five-support A with exterior E and every a in A, at least four of the five supports (E\\{z})∪{a}, z∈E, are themselves global-longest. Consequently every A has at least twenty distinct global-longest supports meeting A in exactly one vertex.

## Hypotheses
Standing order-ten smallest-counterexample case; minimum longest-support overlap equals one; accepted R8 and R184.

## Scope
Pure support-level saturation extracted from the two-hole replacement fan. No complement counting or global extremal argument is used.

## Applicability
Use as the local lower-bound half of any global counting, clique, or support-incidence contradiction in the m=1 branch.

## Persistence
All twenty replacement supports are graph-intrinsic members of the global-longest support family.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not identify a common missing exterior vertex for different a. Does not assert all twenty-five replacements. Does not by itself yield a spanning two-cover.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** superseded
- **Lifecycle note:** Twenty-replacement saturation is a local lemma inside the minimum-overlap-one branch, which is eliminated outright by parent theorem C182/R190. Preserve historically but route ordinary retrieval to the impossibility theorem.
- **Curation note:** Twenty-replacement saturation is a local lemma inside the minimum-overlap-one branch, which is eliminated outright by parent theorem C182/R190. Preserve historically but route ordinary retrieval to the impossibility theorem.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Twenty-replacement saturation is correct and graph-intrinsic.

## Proof
Fix A in F, write E=V(H)\\A, and fix a in A. For z in E define B_z=(E\\{z})∪{a}. Suppose two distinct vertices x,y in E both gave B_x,B_y notin F. By R8 the three-set P=E\\{x,y} supports a tight trimer. Applying accepted R184 to A and this P with holes x,y says that for every a in A at least one of B_x and B_y belongs to F, contradiction. Thus at most one of the five B_z is absent, so at least four belong to F. Repeating independently for all five a in A yields at least twenty supports. They are distinct because each such support meets A in the unique adjoined vertex a, and for fixed a distinct z give distinct four-subsets of E. Each therefore meets A in exactly one vertex.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED/R189.md -->

# FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED/R190.md

<!-- BEGIN FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED/R190.md -->

# R190 — Minimum-overlap-one replacement fan is impossible

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
In the standing order-ten smallest-counterexample case, the global minimum overlap among distinct global-longest five-supports cannot equal one.

## Hypotheses
Standing order-ten smallest-counterexample case; accepted R4, R8 and R184.

## Scope
Direct support-level closure of the minimum-overlap-one branch. No sign, payment, return, spectral, or association-scheme machinery is used.

## Applicability
Use with accepted R128 and accepted elimination of minimum overlap two to close the remaining low-overlap obligation.

## Persistence
All support-family and complement-family facts are graph-intrinsic; the proof is finite support combinatorics.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not claim arbitrary radius-one replacement outside the minimum-overlap-one hypothesis. Does not use the generic four-core lemma as an input; its counting argument is repeated here.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** superseded
- **Lifecycle note:** Minimum-overlap-one elimination is internal order-ten proof architecture beneath C183.
- **Curation note:** Minimum-overlap-one elimination is internal order-ten proof architecture beneath C183.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Minimum-overlap-one replacement fan is impossible by the correct 20-versus-15 Johnson cut count.

## Proof
Assume for contradiction that the minimum overlap in the global-longest five-support family F is one. Fix A in F and put E=V(H)\\A, so |A|=|E|=5. For a in A and z in E write B(a,z)=(E\\{z}) union {a}. Let x,y be any two distinct vertices of E. By R8 the three-set P=E\\{x,y} supports a tight trimer. Accepted R184 applied to A,P,x,y says that for every a in A at least one of B(a,x),B(a,y) lies in F. Therefore for fixed a the failure set M_a={z in E:B(a,z) notin F} has size at most one. Hence at least four B(a,z) lie in F for each a. Across the five choices of a these give at least twenty distinct supports, each meeting A in exactly {a}.

Let barF={V(H)\\B:B in F}. By R4, F contains no complementary pair: complementary members would be disjoint tight five-path supports and hence a spanning two-cover, contradicting pc(H)=3. Thus F and barF are disjoint. For each replacement B(a,z) in F, its complement C(a,z)=(A\\{a}) union {z} belongs to barF and meets A in four vertices. Therefore every A in F has at least twenty neighbors in barF in J(10,5), so e_J(F,barF)>=20|F|.

For every four-set C, the six five-sets containing C form a K6 in J(10,5), and every Johnson edge belongs to exactly one such clique. Let r_C,s_C count F and barF vertices in that clique. Since F and barF are disjoint, r_C+s_C<=6, hence r_C s_C <= (r_C+s_C)^2/4 <= (3/2)(r_C+s_C). Summing over four-cores gives e_J(F,barF)<= (3/2)sum_C(r_C+s_C). Each five-set contains exactly five four-subsets, so sum_C r_C=5|F| and sum_C s_C=5|barF|=5|F|. Thus e_J(F,barF)<=15|F|, contradicting the lower bound 20|F|. Therefore minimum overlap one is impossible.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED/R190.md -->

# R2039 — QUARANTINED: consecutive-source anchor insertion packet

**Status:** CLAIMED / re-audit required
**Source:** Slack workspace R2039

## Former statement

For a literal exact two-cover rail containing consecutive internal sources

`(...,x,t,r,y,...)`,

the former result claimed that counterexample status forces at least one of `(x,t,C)` and `(A,r,y)` bad, equivalently one of `(x,C,t)` and `(r,A,y)` tight.

## Trust failure

The former proof is not valid under R3/R887.

1. It replaces `t->r` by `t->C->A->r` and claims the internal turns `(t,C,A)` and `(C,A,r)` follow by cyclic rotation from source turns `(A,t,C)` and `(A,r,C)`. R3 provides only complete-reversal antisymmetry; these rotations are independent comparisons.
2. It claims bad `(x,t,C)` yields tight `(x,C,t)`, but R3 yields the complete reverse `(C,t,x)`. Likewise bad `(A,r,y)` yields `(y,r,A)`, not automatically `(r,A,y)`.

Thus both the detour and the advertised cap conversion are unsupported. No counterexample to the theorem statement has yet been certified here, so the result is quarantined rather than marked invalid.

## Dependencies

Trusted dependencies for this trust correction: R3, R887.

Provisional dependencies: none.

Do not use R2039 until a direct repair or counterexample is audited.

# R204 — Five-exterior replacement grid has no support-only complementary-swap implication

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
The support-incidence conclusions of R169 and R192 do not by themselves imply any complementary carrier replacement. More precisely, for every integer m>=6 there is an abstract support-incidence model with disjoint sets K,E, |K|=m and |E|=5, in which K is marked as a globally-longest tight support, E is non-Hamiltonian, every carrier vertex k has exactly four successful exterior replacements (E\\{z}) union {k}, yet every complementary carrier swap (K\\{k}) union {z} is declared non-Hamiltonian. All declared proper tight supports satisfy the R169 exterior-size floor. Therefore any proof of complementary replacement synchronization must use information beyond the support-membership conclusions of R169/R192.

## Hypotheses
Only the consumer-level support-incidence conclusions of accepted R169 and R192 are being modeled. This is a logical-independence statement about those conclusions, not an assertion that the abstract model is realizable by a Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament or by a smallest counterexample.

## Scope
Contract-level negative result for the arbitrary-order five-exterior equality program.

## Applicability
Use as a proof-design fence: four-of-five replacement saturation alone cannot justify K-k+z tightness. A successful equality-face closure must add orientation, exact-cover currentness, ancestry, signed-pair synchronization, or another invariant coupling the exterior replacement to its carrier complement.

## Persistence
The model is purely combinatorial support-incidence data; no representative-relative state is asserted.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not construct an actual Strong Level-(1) tournament, does not show the equality face is realizable in a smallest counterexample, and does not refute any stronger theorem using additional hypotheses beyond R169/R192.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Historical five-exterior complementary-swap fence; the exterior grid route is no longer active.
- **Curation note:** Support-incidence countermodel showing the five-exterior replacement grid alone does not force complementary carrier swaps.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Accepted support-only complementary-swap non-implication fence in its explicit abstract-model scope.

## Proof
Fix m>=6. Let K={k_1,...,k_m} and E={e_1,...,e_5} be disjoint. Mark K as a tight globally-longest support and mark E non-Hamiltonian. Choose any function h:K->E. For each k in K and z in E with z != h(k), mark the five-set (E\\{z}) union {k} as supporting a tight P5; for z=h(k) leave that replacement non-Hamiltonian. Thus every R192 row has exactly four successful holes. Declare every complementary m-set (K\\{k}) union {z}, k in K, z in E, non-Hamiltonian. No relation in the support-membership conclusion of R192 links these declarations to the exterior-side P5 declarations. Finally, the marked support K has exactly five exterior vertices, while each marked P5 has m exterior vertices, which is at least six; hence every marked proper tight support satisfies the R169 exterior-order-five floor. The resulting incidence model satisfies the stated consumer-level conclusions while containing no complementary carrier replacement at all. Therefore such a replacement cannot follow from those support-level conclusions alone.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED/R204.md -->

# R205 — Six-exterior root fan non-descent and rail-gap fence

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Instantiate the six-exterior O3 face with a global-longest carrier K in an n-vertex hypothetical smallest counterexample. In every R196 singleton root H-{e}=K sqcup Q_e, the rail orders are n-6 and 5, so their order gap is n-11: the rails are equal only for n=11, have gap one only for n=12, gap two only for n=13, and have gap at least three for n>=14. Moreover the support/certificate conclusions of R195/R196 do not themselves imply exterior-size descent: for every m>=5 there is an abstract contract-level model with |K|=m, |E|=6, all six sets E-{e} marked as tight P5 supports, the displayed K+P5+singleton roots and puncture balanced-pair births recorded, but no tight support of order m+1 and hence no carrier with five exterior vertices. Thus an order-free slack descent requires an additional invariant coupling a singleton root or puncture pair back to a genuine carrier extension/restoration; equal-rail or small-gap arguments alone cover only the low-order specializations above.

## Hypotheses
Accepted R169, R195 and R196; for the rail-gap statement K is the global-longest carrier chosen in the O3 six-exterior slack-one face. The abstract model is a logical-independence model of the stated support/certificate conclusions, not a Strong Level-(1) realizability claim.

## Scope
Applicability and non-implication fence for arbitrary-order six-exterior slack reduction.

## Applicability
Use to prevent order-eleven 5+5 symmetry, or the gap-one/gap-two special cases, from being silently promoted to an arbitrary-order induction. A genuine descent theorem must preserve or reconstruct the global-longest carrier hypothesis after any transfer, or otherwise force an order-(|K|+1) path directly.

## Persistence
The rail-size computation is physical and order-invariant. The abstract model records only contract-level support and historical-certificate data.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not claim an actual smallest counterexample realizes the abstract model. Does not invalidate R196, R197, R198, R201, or R202. Does not say small-gap machinery is useless in orders 11-13; it only fences its order-free use.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Historical six-exterior root-fan non-descent fence; no live use remains.
- **Curation note:** Order-free non-descent/rail-gap barrier separating six-exterior root symmetry from genuine arbitrary-order descent.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Accepted six-exterior rail-gap and contract-level non-descent fence.

## Proof
Let n=|H| and suppose the carrier K has six exterior vertices, so |K|=n-6. R196 supplies roots H-{e}=K sqcup Q_e with |Q_e|=5. Hence the rail-order gap is |K|-5=n-11. The stated equal/gap-one/gap-two classification follows immediately. For the contract-level non-descent model, fix any m>=5, take disjoint K and E with |K|=m and |E|=6, mark K tight, and mark every five-set E-{e} as supporting a tight P5. For every e record both the literal spanning three-cover symbol K sqcup Q_e sqcup {e} and the exact two-cover label H-{e}=K sqcup Q_e. For every internal carrier puncture and every e, attach a fresh abstract balanced-pair certificate, independently for that frame, as permitted by the existential/non-synchronizing conclusion of R196. Declare no support of order m+1 tight. Then no path has exactly five exterior vertices relative to the m+6 vertex universe, so no slack descent has occurred, while all support, exact-root, and anonymous-certificate conclusions just listed are present. This shows those conclusions alone do not force descent. Any additional descent must therefore identify/synchronize certificates with carrier structure or force a true extension/restoration. The arithmetic gap calculation simultaneously shows that equal or gap-at-most-two root geometry is confined to n<=13.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED/R205.md -->

# R214 — Mass-two singleton floor cannot be a literal signed-pair frame

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
In a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample, any literal signed-pair frame H=K sqcup P sqcup T of the form consumed by R171 must have historical pair mass M=|P|+|T| at least five. Indeed V(P) union V(T) is exactly the exterior of the proper tight path K, so R169 gives M>=5. Consequently no balanced pair of mass two, three, or four can itself be realized as the two literal pair components in an R171 frame. In particular, mass-two floors, direct mass-four dimer pairs such as R208, and every strict paid descendant of a mass-four pair are all too small for direct R171 entry unless a later remint/rebirth first increases the literal signed-support mass to at least five.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample; H=K sqcup P sqcup T is proposed as a literal R171 signed-pair frame with K the third tight-path component.

## Scope
Sharp architecture/scope threshold for literal signed-pair-frame currentization in arbitrary-order smallest-counterexample work.

## Applicability
Use whenever a proof proposes feeding any low-mass balanced pair directly into R171. Pair mass below five is not merely hard to currentize: it is incompatible with the universal exterior floor.

## Persistence
Pure graph-intrinsic exterior-size obstruction; the prohibited low-mass literal representative cannot exist.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not prohibit historical low-mass balanced-pair ancestry, does not prohibit R171 at mass at least five, and does not prohibit a later remint/rebirth that increases the literal signed-support mass before R171 entry.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Historical mass-two literal-frame obstruction; modern bare-pair and paid-floor fences R777/R784 are the preferred warnings.
- **Curation note:** Architecture correction: a mass-two singleton floor cannot be silently treated as a literal signed-pair frame; blocks a recurrent invalid currentization move.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Accepted sharp correction: every literal R171 signed-pair frame has pair mass at least five.

## Proof
Assume the hypotheses stated in R214: H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample and H=K sqcup P sqcup T is proposed as a literal signed-pair frame of the form consumed by R171, with K the third tight-path component. No theorem-level use of R171 is needed. Because the displayed three paths are vertex-disjoint and spanning, V(P) union V(T)=V(H)\V(K), so the historical pair mass is M=|P|+|T|=|V(H)-V(K)|. The path K is proper, since P and T are nonempty signed supports. Accepted fully reconstructible R169 states that every proper tight path in a smallest counterexample has at least five exterior vertices. Therefore M>=5. Hence no literal frame satisfying these hypotheses can have pair mass two, three, or four. This proves the full R214 correction and its listed low-mass exclusions without using R171 as a premise.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED/R214.md -->

# R218 — Universal balanced-pair anchored-capacity front door

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
In every hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample H, either a spanning two-cover already occurs or one may choose an ancestry-bearing balanced pair from R198, realize it at anchored capacity, and obtain one of the following explicit productive outputs: (i) a spanning two-cover; (ii) a strict graph-intrinsic same-polarity two-witness extension/collision output or bounded reverse trimer/contact from a reservoir of size at least two; (iii) in the one-residual branch, a literal signed-pair frame and hence by R171 either a spanning two-cover, strict historical pair-mass descent, or bounded support swallow. Thus after anchored-capacity maximization no quiet anonymous residual branch remains.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample.

## Scope
Order-free universal front door. It composes the accepted adaptive mass-two pair floor with anchored-capacity maximization and the recovered literal signed-pair discharge. No exterior-slack or order-ten assumption.

## Applicability
Use as an alternative parent to O3 exterior-slack casework. It reduces every surviving smallest counterexample to explicit physical extension/contact or R171 descent/swallow outputs after one anchored-capacity maximization.

## Persistence
The initial floor and later capacity realization are lineage/representative data as in their parent theorems. Collision/contact, pair descent ancestry, and bounded swallow outputs persist only with the guarantees of R180/R171.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert that the nonclosing outputs are themselves contradictions. Does not make anchored capacity globally monotone after reset. Does not close arbitrary-order Strong Level-(1) by itself.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** superseded
- **Lifecycle note:** Universal balanced-pair anchored-capacity front door is strictly refined by C214/R222, which removes indefinite one-residual descent and classifies the only nonclosing swallow corner.
- **Curation note:** Universal balanced-pair anchored-capacity front door is strictly refined by C214/R222, which removes indefinite one-residual descent and classifies the only nonclosing swallow corner.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Verified.

## Proof
Assume no spanning two-cover initially. By R198 choose an ancestry-bearing balanced opposite-sign pair, with fixed signed anchors and witnesses. Apply the anchored-capacity construction R179 to obtain a maximizing disjoint realization (alpha;P),(T;beta), and let X be its ordinary reservoir. R180 gives three cases. If X is empty, its branch (i) already gives a spanning two-cover. If |X|>=2, branch (ii) gives a strict graph-intrinsic same-polarity two-witness extension/collision output or bounded reverse trimer/contact. It remains to treat |X|=1. Write X={x} and W=V(H)\\(V(P) union V(T)). By definition of X every vertex of W lies among x,alpha,beta, and x is in W, so 1<=|W|<=3. A one- or two-vertex set supports a tight path; if |W|=3, R8 supplies a tight trimer orientation. Hence W supports a nonempty tight path J and H=J sqcup P sqcup T is a literal spanning three-cover with P,T the historical opposite-signed pair. R171 applies, giving a spanning two-cover, strict historical pair-mass descent, or bounded support swallow. Thus every anchored-capacity branch has one of the stated productive outputs.

# R220 — Anchored-capacity one-residual branch terminates in cover or bounded swallow

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Let H be a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample and let (alpha;P),(T;beta) be an anchored-capacity realization of a balanced opposite-sign pair with ordinary reservoir of size one. Then repeated use of the literal signed-pair discharge in the one-residual frame cannot continue by strict pair-mass descent indefinitely. After finitely many literal-frame peel steps, either H has a spanning two-cover or a bounded support swallow occurs. More precisely, if the initial literal pair mass is M0, there are at most M0-5 consecutive strict-descent outputs before a non-descent R171 output is forced.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample; an anchored-capacity balanced pair has ordinary reservoir of size one.

## Scope
Order-free finite termination of the R180 one-residual branch after recovery of R171 and the universal literal-frame mass floor R214.

## Applicability
Use in the |X|=1 capacity branch to remove strict pair-mass descent as a terminal unresolved outcome. The only surviving nonclosing output is bounded support swallow.

## Persistence
The iteration is only along the literal R171 peel lineage whose successful descent steps remain in the displayed literal frame. No claim is made across unrelated recompletions or remints.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not close bounded support swallow. Does not assert global pair-mass monotonicity outside this literal peel lineage. Does not apply if a descent step abandons the R171 literal-frame continuation.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** superseded
- **Lifecycle note:** Finite termination of one-residual strict descent is an internal component of parent reduction C214/R222 and no longer needs separate canonical visibility.
- **Curation note:** Finite termination of one-residual strict descent is an internal component of parent reduction C214/R222 and no longer needs separate canonical visibility.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Verified.

## Proof
Let X={x}. Put W=V(H)\\(V(P) union V(T)). As in the direct one-residual construction, 1<=|W|<=3; choose a tight path J on W, using R8 if |W|=3. Then H=J sqcup P sqcup T is a literal R171 signed-pair frame. Let its pair mass be M0=|P|+|T|. R171 gives either a spanning two-cover, bounded support swallow, or a strict historical pair-mass descent. In the strict-descent branch, the R171 interval-peel persistence clause keeps the continuation in the displayed literal frame, so the resulting pair again satisfies the literal-frame hypotheses. By R214 every such literal frame has pair mass at least five. Hence along consecutive strict-descent outputs the integer mass forms a strictly decreasing sequence M0>M1>...>=5, of length at most M0-5. Therefore eventually a non-descent R171 output occurs, namely a spanning two-cover or bounded support swallow.

# R24 — Singleton order floor and short-complement rigidity

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED` (preserved historical quarantined revision)

## Statement

Every exact one-vertex deletion two-cover has both rails of order at least four. Therefore no proper tight path of order at most three has an exact singleton completion. The older pair-deletion and exterior-trimer completion-rigidity statements are special cases for their bare size conclusions.

## Scope
If a minimum three-cover has a singleton component and two nontrivial rails, deleting the singleton produces the exact two-rail root frame. The standard four caps, boundary collisions, and disjoint companion-collision package are available in that same representative.

After two genuine two-sided enlargements from an ancestor core, every support and witness in this transplanted singleton packet lies outside the surviving ancestor core. The core and any prescribed internal vertex survive literally. This ancestor-exterior reset is stronger than the older terminal-collision-dependent version because no pre-existing terminal collision is required.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** active
- **Lifecycle note:** Reactivated: R24 is a load-bearing foundational theorem, directly supporting R5 and a large active dependency subtree. Its current accepted proof is only a legacy compressed certificate, so modern fully reconstructible proof recovery remains an explicit research target. Retirement under the strong-or-versatile curation heuristic was premature and confused breadth with foundational importance.
- **Curation note:** Core target theorem. The statement is canonical and central; O6 remains open because its legacy proof is not yet modernly reconstructible. Canonical prominence must not be read as proof-reconstruction closure.
- **Review status:** pending
- **Review note:** Acceptance withdrawn for fresh verification on 2026-09-11. Prior acceptance was inherited from a legacy checksum-migration certificate; R24 is not currently trusted as independently verified. This is a verification quarantine, not a claim of falsity. All downstream uses must expose dependency risk until R24 is freshly audited.

## Proof
This theorem is recorded as independently accepted in A7C2_20260829_01_THEOREM_LEDGER.md. The verified compressed package preserves its controlling statement, fences, corrections, and source corridors; the full historical handoff proof transcript was intentionally not migrated. Use M1 and the relevant domain archive M2-M7 for deeper reconstruction.

# R241 — Five-exterior dense column forces widespread exact-frame carrier capture

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Assume the non-Hamiltonian five-exterior equality face. Let K=(k_1,...,k_m), m>=6, have exterior E. Then there is a hole z in E and a successful set S subseteq V(K), |S|>=ceil(4m/5), such that Q_k=(E\\{z}) union {k} supports a tight P5 for every k in S. Put F=E\\{z}. For each k in S choose a tight ordering of Q_k and choose one consecutive tight turn in that ordering in which k is an outer witness and the other two vertices form a physical dimer D(k) contained in F. There are only six possible physical dimers D(k). Every internal k in S whose physical-dimer class contains another carrier vertex has a historical same-frame capture certificate at k in the exact D(k)-deletion root K sqcup (E\\D(k)). Consequently at least max(0,ceil(4m/5)-8) distinct carrier vertices admit such exact-frame historical capture certificates.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in the five-exterior equality face; E is non-Hamiltonian; accepted R232 dense-hole column, R8 trimer existence, R5 pair-deletion exactness, and witness-adaptive capture R37.

## Scope
Arbitrary-order carrier-ancestry amplification at the five-exterior floor. This strengthens R239 by pigeonholing only the six physical dimers of the exterior four-set, using the fact that R37 is adaptive across different tested orders and polarities on the same physical support.

## Applicability
Use when replacement density must be converted into carrier-position capture. Compared with R239, the capture loss is only six singleton physical-dimer classes plus two carrier endpoints, giving the sharp contract-level bound ceil(4m/5)-8.

## Persistence
The hole z, four-core F, P5 supports Q_k, physical dimers D(k), exact D-deletion roots, selected carrier-cut crossings, and capture events have the persistence of their parent theorems. For one fixed D, all captures are sourced from the same literal exact root K sqcup (E\\D), though payment descendants are not simultaneous.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not force adjacent captured vertices, does not make different capture descendants simultaneous, does not by itself create a longer carrier or spanning two-cover, and does not feed low-mass ancestry directly into R171 contrary to R214. The strengthening does not require the two witnesses on one physical dimer to have the same tested order or polarity.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Five-exterior dense-column capture is specialized zero-consumer equality-branch machinery; retire.
- **Curation note:** Five-exterior dense-column capture is specialized zero-consumer equality-branch machinery; retire.
- **Review status:** accepted

## Proof
Fix the dense hole z supplied by R232 and put F=E-{z}. For each k in the successful set choose any tight P5 ordering of F union {k}. In every position of a five-path, k is an outer vertex of at least one consecutive tight turn, so that turn has the form (k,u,v), (u,v,k), or its head/tail-signed equivalent with u,v in F. Record only the physical dimer D(k)={u,v}. There are exactly six possible dimers in a four-set F. Now let k be internal on K and suppose k prime != k has D(k prime)=D(k)=D. Delete D. The remaining three vertices E-D form a tight trimer by R8, hence K sqcup (E-D) is a two-cover of H-D; R5 makes it exact. Relative to the retained P5 Q_k, deleting D leaves k separated from the other exterior vertices, so the two selected K states incident with k are carrier/exterior crossings for Q_k-D. The distinct witness k prime lies on at most one of those two selected states. Choose the other crossing. The P5 Q_k prime supplies an admissible signed incarnation of the same physical support D witnessed by k prime. R37 explicitly permits witness-adaptive capture across different signed incarnations of one physical support, so no equality of tested order or polarity is required. Since k prime is outside the chosen selected pair, R37 yields historical capture of carrier vertex k in this same exact D-deletion frame. Thus every internal member of every non-singleton physical-dimer class is capturable. At most six successful vertices can occupy singleton dimer classes and at most two successful vertices are carrier endpoints. With |S|>=ceil(4m/5), at least max(0,ceil(4m/5)-8) successful vertices are captured.
