# R244 — Four-core occupancy forces concentrated same-frame carrier capture

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Assume the five-exterior equality face. Let S be a physical four-core of occupancy x_S=r>=2 in the global-longest exterior family, choose one completion a with E_a=S union {a}, and let K_a=V(H)\\E_a be a retained global-longest carrier. Fix any s in S and put F_s=(S\\{s}) union {a}. Then every other completion b of S lies on K_a and F_s union {b} supports a tight P5. For each such b choose a tight P5 ordering and one consecutive turn in which b is an outer witness; let D(b) be the resulting physical dimer in F_s. Among the six possible dimers there is a dimer D for which at least ceil((r-1)/6) completion vertices share D. In the single literal exact D-deletion frame H-D=K_a sqcup (E_a\\D), every internal member of that D-class has a historical same-frame capture certificate at its own carrier position. Consequently one exact deletion frame yields captures at at least max(0,ceil((r-1)/6)-2) distinct carrier vertices, and across the at most six dimer frames at least max(0,r-9) distinct completion vertices are capturable.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in the five-exterior equality face; accepted R240 common-four-core cross-replacement saturation, R8 trimer existence, R5 pair-deletion exactness, and R37 witness-adaptive capture.

## Scope
Hybrid four-core occupancy-to-physical-progress theorem. It retains one actual global-longest carrier and converts occupancy of one physical four-core into many capture certificates, including a quantitative concentration inside one fixed exact deletion representative.

## Applicability
Use when the four-core occupancy profile x_S is nonuniform or one S is highly occupied. This is the direct bridge from structural Johnson occupancy to R239-style exact-frame carrier ancestry: occupancy r gives one same-frame capture class of size at least ceil((r-1)/6)-2.

## Persistence
S,a,s,F_s,K_a,D and the exact D-deletion frame are physical/current in the chosen root. The individual capture events are graph-intrinsic historical certificates sourced from that same frame; their paid descendants are alternative and not simultaneously current.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not force the captured positions to be adjacent, does not synchronize later capture descendants, does not itself extend K_a, and does not turn capture density into an R171 frame contrary to R214. Different physical-dimer classes use different deletion frames.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Four-core occupancy to concentrated same-frame capture is specialized equality-branch machinery with no current active consumers; retire from canonical surface.
- **Curation note:** Four-core occupancy to concentrated same-frame capture is specialized equality-branch machinery with no current active consumers; retire from canonical surface.
- **Review status:** accepted

## Proof
Let A={c:S union {c} is a global-longest exterior}; |A|=r. Fix a in A and s in S. For every b in A-{a}, R240 applied to E_a=S union {a} and E_b=S union {b} gives that Q_b=F_s union {b}, where F_s=(S-{s}) union {a}, supports a tight P5. Choose an ordering of Q_b and a consecutive tight turn having b as an outer vertex; the other two vertices form a physical dimer D(b) inside F_s. There are six possible physical dimers. Hence some D-class C has |C|>=ceil((r-1)/6). Now fix any internal b in C and choose b prime in C-{b}. Delete D. Since D is contained in E_a and |E_a|=5, E_a-D has three vertices and supports a tight trimer by R8. Thus K_a sqcup (E_a-D) is a two-cover of H-D, exact by R5. Relative to the retained P5 Q_b containing D, the two selected K_a states incident with b cross from Q_b-D to its exterior because Q_b contains no other K_a vertex. The distinct witness b prime lies on at most one of these two states; choose the other. Q_b prime supplies an admissible signed incarnation of the same physical support D witnessed by b prime, and R37 allows adaptive use of that witness regardless of tested order or polarity. Hence b is historically captured in this same exact D-deletion frame. At most two members of C are endpoints of K_a, so the chosen single frame yields at least max(0,ceil((r-1)/6)-2) captures. Summed across all six D-classes, only vertices in singleton classes and the two carrier endpoints can fail this argument; at most six plus two such vertices are lost from r-1, leaving at least max(0,r-9) capturable completion vertices.

# R250 — Repeated four-core dimer class gives bilateral same-frame carrier capture

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Assume the R244 four-core occupancy setup. Thus one fixed exact dimer-deletion frame H-D=K_a sqcup (E_a\D) retains the global-longest carrier K_a, and let B be one physical-D class of completion vertices whose successful cross-replacement P5 certificates use D with the completion vertex as an admissible outer witness. If |B|>=4, then every member b of B that is internal on K_a has two graph-intrinsic historical capture certificates sourced from this same exact D-deletion frame: one using the left K_a-edge incident with b and one using the right K_a-edge incident with b. Hence the frame yields bilateral capture at at least |B|-2 distinct carrier vertices. In particular, using the largest D-class supplied by R244, any four-core occupancy r with ceil((r-1)/6)>=4 (equivalently r>=20) yields one exact deletion frame with bilateral captures at at least ceil((r-1)/6)-2 carrier positions.

## Hypotheses
Hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in the five-exterior equality face; accepted R244 concentrated same-frame capture setup; accepted R37 witness-adaptive capture. The bilateral conclusion is invoked only for a fixed physical-D class B of size at least four.

## Scope
Order-free strengthening of R244 inside one occupied-four-core exact deletion frame.

## Applicability
Use when high four-core occupancy has produced a repeated physical dimer class. Bilateral capture exposes both carrier incidences at each internal class position and is designed to feed carrier-order consumers such as mirror reentry, insertion-obstruction, or first-loss arguments without changing the deletion frame.

## Persistence
The fixed dimer D, exact D-deletion frame, carrier K_a, class B, carrier positions, and both capture events at each internal b are retained as graph-intrinsic/historical certificates in the sense of R37/R244.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert that capture descendants for different edges or vertices are simultaneously current or paid. Does not preserve a later recompletion, does not itself create a carrier extension, and does not license direct R171 entry. Bilateral capture means two historical capture certificates sourced from the same fixed exact frame.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Repeated four-core dimer bilateral capture is specialized one-consumer high-occupancy machinery; preserve history but retire canonical identity.
- **Curation note:** Repeated four-core dimer bilateral capture is specialized one-consumer high-occupancy machinery; preserve history but retire canonical identity.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Verified exact scope and counting. At most two class vertices are carrier endpoints; ceil((r-1)/6)>=4 iff r>=20.

## Proof
Fix b internal in B. Choose b' in B\{b,k_{i-1},k_{i+1}}; this is possible because |B|>=4. R244 inherits the R239 fact that, in H-D=K_a sqcup (E_a\D), each of the two K_a-edges incident with b is a selected crossing of the retained cross-replacement support Q_b relative to D. Since b' lies on neither edge, both selected crossings avoid the admissible witness b'. Apply R37 to the left edge and choose physical endpoint b to capture; apply R37 separately to the right edge and again choose b. The two resulting capture statements are simultaneous graph-intrinsic/historical facts sourced from one unchanged exact frame, though any downstream paid descendants remain alternative. Repeat for every internal b in B. Only the two K_a endpoints can be excluded, giving at least |B|-2 bilateral positions. The occupancy corollary follows from the largest-class estimate |B|>=ceil((r-1)/6) in R244.

# R278 — The bare O4 currentizable two-trimer front door is capture-free

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Let H be a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample and let K be any proper tight path. Fix any carrier vertex b in V(K). Then there exist two vertex-disjoint tight trimers C and T such that C contains b as its middle vertex, C can be currentized as one component of a minimum three-cover, T lies wholly in the exterior of K, and R41 supplies the synchronized central-anchor interaction between C and T. Consequently the bare geometric/currentizable two-trimer conclusion underlying R273 does not require R264 punctures, capture events, crossing synchronization, or capture-reentry spokes. Any additional content of R273 must therefore reside specifically in the claimed puncture/capture ancestry on the terminal supports of C.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample; K is any proper graph-intrinsic tight path; b is any vertex of K. Accepted R3, R41, R154, and R169.

## Scope
Order-free compression of the geometric part of the recent two-puncture front door.

## Applicability
Use when evaluating R272/R273 or designing O4 descendants. Treat currentizable two-trimer geometry plus central-anchor interaction as free once a proper carrier exists; do not spend puncture machinery merely to obtain that geometry. Reserve puncture synchronization claims for ancestry that is genuinely proved.

## Persistence
The two physical trimer supports and the R41 interaction are graph-intrinsic. The minimum-cover representative currentizing C is representative-relative. No puncture or capture ancestry is asserted.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not give capture ancestry, selected-crossing ancestry, endpoint exposure, protection, or any link from the terminal dimers of C to two prescribed punctures. Does not assert C and T are simultaneously selected in one cover. Does not close H.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Valid role-consumption corollary showing currentizable two-trimer geometry is capture-free, but zero-consumer and now strategically dominated by the stronger universal role-blindness results C264/C265/C266. Exact currentization detail remains in R278 history.
- **Curation note:** Valid role-consumption corollary showing currentizable two-trimer geometry is capture-free, but zero-consumer and now strategically dominated by the stronger universal role-blindness results C264/C265/C266. Exact currentization detail remains in R278 history.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Correct: the bare two-trimer/currentization geometry follows directly from R3, R41, R154, and R169 without puncture ancestry.

## Proof
By R169, the exterior E=V(H)-V(K) has at least five vertices. Choose five distinct exterior vertices d_1,d_2,r,y,s. Boundary antisymmetry R3 gives exactly one tight orientation of the three-set {d_1,b,d_2} with middle b; call the resulting tight trimer C. Its two terminal physical supports {d_1,b} and {b,d_2} are distinct supports incident with b, so R154 currentizes their unique compatible mirror packet, equivalently C, as one component of a minimum three-cover. Independently, R3 gives a tight orientation T of {r,y,s} with prescribed middle y. The trimers C and T are vertex-disjoint because b lies on K while all five chosen vertices lie in E and the chosen exterior vertices are distinct. Therefore R41 applies directly: the two terminal dimers of C and the two terminal dimers of T supply the synchronized central-anchor interaction with middle-anchor pair {b,y}. No capture, puncture, crossing, reentry, or ancestry transport is used. Hence the currentizable two-trimer geometry and R41 interaction asserted at the bare structural level by R273 are already forced by R3/R41/R154/R169; only the extra statement that C terminal supports carry ancestry from two particular R264 punctures could constitute additional content.

Capture-free repair and strengthening of the unusable R257 fixed-trimer pair-family theorem.

The four-core coordinates, class B, fixed anchor d, common witness y, spoke signs, fixed trimer T, common mate M, balanced-pair births, and R160 interaction are graph-intrinsic/historical as specified by their parents.

The unlocalized interaction species is ubiquitous by C266. Preserve R288 as historical occupancy-indexed proof interface.

# R289 — Quiet four-core occupancy cap and O(n^4) longest-exterior ceiling

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Assume the five-exterior equality face on n vertices, with longest-exterior family Ecal and four-core occupancies x_S. Then either some four-core has x_S>=14 and the capture-free fixed-trimer nonquiet interaction of provisional R288 occurs, or x_S<=13 for every four-core S. In the latter quiet branch, 5|Ecal|=sum_S x_S<=13*binom(n,4), hence |Ecal|<=(13/5)*binom(n,4). Combining with the unconditional R231 ceiling |Ecal|<=(n/25)*binom(n,4), the quiet branch satisfies |Ecal|<=min(13/5,n/25)*binom(n,4). The two bounds agree at n=65; for n>65 the physical occupancy cap is strictly stronger and keeps the quiet exterior family on O(n^4) scale.

## Hypotheses
Hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in the five-exterior equality face; accepted R231 and provisional corrected C243/R288.

## Scope
Global extremal corollary of the repaired capture-free occupancy threshold.

## Applicability
Use as the structural/global branch complementary to the local fixed-trimer interaction route.

## Persistence
The exterior family and occupancy profile are graph-intrinsic finite-set data. The alternative nonquiet interaction is historical as in R288.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
The quiet branch means avoidance of the specific R160 nonquiet interaction forced by R288; this is not a contradiction by itself. Does not supply a lower bound on |Ecal|.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Quiet four-core occupancy O(n^4) ceiling is a derived quantitative corollary with no independent consumer; retire under the no-obvious-corollary policy.
- **Curation note:** Quiet four-core occupancy O(n^4) ceiling is a derived quantitative corollary with no independent consumer; retire under the no-obvious-corollary policy.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Valid repaired quiet occupancy ceiling: 13/5 coefficient, crossing R231 at n=65.

## Proof
Each E in Ecal contains exactly five four-subsets, so sum_S x_S=5|Ecal|. Avoidance of R288 forces x_S<=13 for all S. Therefore 5|Ecal|<=13 binom(n,4). R231 independently gives |Ecal|<=(n/25)binom(n,4). Equality of coefficients 13/5=n/25 occurs at n=65.

Then unless H has a spanning two-cover, the coordinate hierarchy is exact. If c_L<>c_R, some dimer {y,t} carries an R38 interaction with the two specified floor witnesses c_L,c_R. If c_L=c_R but b_L<>b_R, some dimer {y,t} carries an R38 interaction with the two specified captured-carrier witnesses b_L,b_R. If c_L=c_R and b_L=b_R=:b but z_L<>z_R, the actual endpoint adjacency of K incident with b carries an R38 interaction with the two specified crossing witnesses z_L,z_R via lawful R155 reentry. Therefore the only branch avoiding all three coordinate-localized R38 interactions has c_L=c_R=:c, b_L=b_R=:b, z_L=z_R=:z, and necessarily b is one of the two physical endpoints v_1,v_5 of K. In particular the R301 captured-anchor/floor-coordinate degeneracy branch is unnecessary.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample; K is a proper tight P5; accepted repaired puncture/floor inputs R294 and R299; accepted R3,R38,R41,R155. H has more than ten vertices in O4, so auxiliary vertices required below exist.

## Scope
Order-free finite normal form for the minimal two-puncture carrier. Every interaction branch is localized by the physical coordinates whose mismatch causes it; no simultaneous floor or deletion-cover currentness is asserted.

## Applicability
Use after the repaired two-puncture common-floor construction. It reduces every nonclosing branch either to an explicitly coordinate-indexed R38 certificate or to total physical coincidence of floor coordinate, captured carrier index, and crossing exterior endpoint, with the common capture at a physical endpoint of K.

## Persistence
The compared floor coordinates, captured carrier vertices, crossing endpoints, chosen R38 support and witnesses, and final coincident coordinates are graph-intrinsic historical data. Source representatives remain separate.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not claim a coordinate-localized R38 interaction itself closes H. Does not make the two floor descendants or puncture deletion covers simultaneous. Does not prescribe the common second floor coordinate c in the final residue or identify it with b or z.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Double-puncture coordinate-coincidence normal form is mathematically valid, but its first mismatch branches are fresh-triple role-blind R38 manufacture and the theorem has no consumer exploiting the exact coordinate labels. Preserve the detailed coincidence hierarchy historically.
- **Curation note:** Double-puncture coordinate-coincidence normal form is mathematically valid, but its first mismatch branches are fresh-triple role-blind R38 manufacture and the theorem has no consumer exploiting the exact coordinate labels. Preserve the detailed coincidence hierarchy historically.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Accepted repaired double-puncture coordinate hierarchy. Fresh mismatch interactions are coordinate-labeled but role-blind; the crossing mismatch is a lawful R155 old-carrier interaction.

## Proof
First suppose c_L<>c_R. Choose a physical vertex t distinct from y,c_L,c_R. By R3, orient the two triples {y,t,c_L} and {y,t,c_R} with middle t. Each gives, via the terminal-dimer sign convention R41, a signed certificate on the same physical dimer {y,t}, with distinct specified witnesses c_L,c_R. R38 gives the floor-indexed interaction. Hence in the no-such-interaction branch c_L=c_R=:c. Next suppose b_L<>b_R. Choose t distinct from y,b_L,b_R. The identical R3/R41 construction on {y,t,b_L} and {y,t,b_R} signs the same dimer {y,t} with the two specified captured-carrier witnesses, so R38 gives the capture-indexed interaction. This works even when c equals one of b_L,b_R, which removes the old R301 degeneracy. Hence without that interaction b_L=b_R=:b. Because b is a surviving carrier vertex in both puncture frames, b lies in {v_1,v_4,v_5} for D_L and in {v_1,v_2,v_5} for D_R, so b belongs their intersection {v_1,v_5}. Finally suppose z_L<>z_R. Let E_b be the genuine endpoint adjacency of the original historical carrier K incident with b: {v_1,v_2} if b=v_1 and {v_4,v_5} if b=v_5. Apply R155 separately to the lawful historical captures through {b,z_L} and {b,z_R}, using the same actual carrier adjacency E_b. Each mirror trimer signs E_b with the corresponding crossing witness z_L or z_R. Since the witnesses are distinct, R38 gives the crossing-indexed interaction. Therefore avoiding all three localized interactions forces z_L=z_R=:z, yielding the stated total coordinate-coincidence residue.

# R306 — Corrected two-puncture chain is index-coupled but not capture-ancestry-coupled

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
In the repaired R293-R296 two-puncture chain, the puncture/capture theorems contribute physical carrier indices b,bprime and retain separate historical capture events in their source frames. After those indices are obtained, the fixed-trimer packet, common-witness spokes, currentizable coupling trimer C, disjoint trimer T, and their central-anchor interaction are constructed using only the physical identities of b,bprime together with fresh exterior vertices and capture-free R3/R8/R39/R41/R154/R160/R169 machinery. The proofs are unchanged if b,bprime are replaced by arbitrary carrier vertices satisfying the same distinct/equal case split. Therefore the repaired chain currently establishes index-level co-labeling of generic geometry with two puncture histories, not a mathematical interaction or synchronization of the two capture ancestries. Any downstream claim that the capture histories themselves have synchronized must additionally invoke a theorem whose hypotheses consume the capture events or protected descendants, such as an applicable R42/R155-style ancestry transport/contact theorem.

## Hypotheses
Accepted repaired statements R293,R294,R295,R296 and their listed dependencies; accepted capture persistence scope R37 and captured-anchor protection/reentry fences R42,R155.

## Scope
Proof-architecture and provenance correction for the current two-puncture program. It does not invalidate the index-level geometric statements themselves.

## Applicability
Use when consuming R293-R296. The physical vertices b,bprime may be strategically useful because they also have historical capture certificates, but no theorem may infer interaction, simultaneous currentness, protection, or transported capture ancestry merely from their occurrence as vertices of the fresh spokes or coupling trimer. A future ancestry-sensitive consumer must make the capture event an actual premise.

## Persistence
The source capture events persist in their own historical ledgers; the fresh geometric objects are graph-intrinsic/currentizable according to their own parents. Sharing the same physical vertex does not merge those persistence classes.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not say puncture indexing is useless. A later theorem may exploit the fact that a vertex of C is historically captured. Does not invalidate R293-R296 as presently fenced. Does not prevent lawful R155 reentry when an actual historical carrier adjacency is used, nor R42 after a protected continuation is chosen.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Historical two-puncture ancestry-coupling fence; no live use remains.
- **Curation note:** Two-puncture correction separating genuine capture ancestry from fresh index-coupled geometry.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Accepted correction: repaired two-puncture geometry is index-coupled but not capture-ancestry-coupled absent an explicit ancestry-sensitive consumer.

## Proof
R293 obtains a lawful puncture-frame capture at b, but explicitly builds its later spoke/fixed-trimer packet independently by capture-free R3/R8/R39/R41/R160/R169. R294 takes two such indices b,bprime and constructs fresh spokes with a common witness y and a fixed trimer T; no capture theorem appears among the construction dependencies after the indices are named. R295 constructs C from incident physical supports through R154, using only whether b=bprime, then chooses a disjoint exterior trimer T and applies R41. R296 merely chooses the two punctures and retains the resulting indices while invoking R295. Thus, holding the same ambient vertex sets fixed, replacing the historical predicates captured(b), captured(bprime) by no predicates at all leaves every fresh geometric construction valid. The captures remain true historical facts, but they are not consumed by the derivation. By the persistence fences in R42/R155, historical capture cannot be upgraded to protection, same-representative currentness, or ancestry on a fresh support without an explicit theorem. Hence the chain is index-coupled but not capture-ancestry-coupled.

# R313 — Every proper tight path of order at least six has a puncture-forced first-contact front door

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Let H be a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample and let K=(k_1,...,k_m) be any proper tight path of order m>=6. Puncture the central adjacent dimer D={k_3,k_4}. Then either H has a spanning two-cover, or accepted R293 supplies an exact D-deletion frame with a selected crossing {b,z} from the surviving historical carrier K-D to the exterior and a valid historical capture of the carrier-side endpoint b through that crossing. The two surviving historical runs are (k_1,k_2) and (k_5,...,k_m), both nontrivial. Hence whichever run contains b, the captured vertex b has at least one genuine historical adjacency E on that same retained run. After choosing an actual capture descendant and designated quiet continuation, R312 applies: lawful R155 mirror reentry along E either reveals an earlier contact at b or is itself the first contact. Thus every proper tight path of order at least six is an order-free entry to a puncture-indexed protected first-contact event; no fresh-support ancestry transport is used.

## Hypotheses
H is a smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample; K is a proper tight path of order at least six; accepted R293 and provisional R312.

## Scope
Order-free role-sensitive puncture front door correcting the generic interaction route.

## Applicability
Use to reduce any branch possessing a proper P6-or-longer to an actual capture/contact lineage. The only residual longest-path regime not covered by this theorem has maximum proper path order at most five.

## Persistence
K,D, the two surviving historical runs, selected crossing, captured endpoint, and first-contact history are retained according to R293/R312. The exact deletion representative and protected continuation remain lineage-relative.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not claim the exposed contact closes the conjecture. Does not apply to P5 where one surviving run may be a singleton. Does not use generic fresh-spoke interactions as progress.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** superseded
- **Lifecycle note:** The P6-specific puncture first-contact front door is a narrower route to protected first contact than the universal O4 protected-first-contact front door C277; retain puncture provenance historically.
- **Curation note:** The P6-specific puncture first-contact front door is a narrower route to protected first contact than the universal O4 protected-first-contact front door C277; retain puncture provenance historically.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Accepted order-free long-path front door: every proper path of order at least six yields a puncture-indexed protected first-contact alternative using only lawful historical-carrier reentry.

## Proof
Because m>=6, deleting k_3,k_4 leaves the two historical K-runs A_L=(k_1,k_2) and A_R=(k_5,...,k_m), each of order at least two. R293 applies to this internal dimer puncture. In its nonclosing branch an exact D-deletion frame selects a carrier/exterior crossing {b,z} with b in the surviving carrier and gives a valid historical capture of b. The vertex b lies on exactly one of A_L,A_R. Since both runs are nontrivial, every vertex of either run has at least one physical adjacency inside that same historical run. Let E be such an adjacency at b. This is precisely the hypothesis needed by R312. Choose the actual capture descendant and protected quiet continuation; then lawful R155 reentry along E either encounters an already exposed earlier contact or constitutes the first contact at b.

# R315 — O4 dichotomy: protected first contact or the unique order-eleven longest-five residue

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Let H be a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in the beyond-order-ten regime. Then one of the following holds. (1) H contains a proper tight path of order at least six, in which case provisional R313 supplies an internal-dimer puncture with a lawful historical capture and, after choosing a protected continuation, a forced first-contact event via old-carrier mirror reentry. (2) Every proper tight path has order at most five. Then provisional R314 gives |H|<=11. Since R191 excludes order ten and the live regime is beyond order ten, necessarily |H|=11. Accepted R193 supplies a tight P5 in every six-set, so the maximum proper tight-path order is exactly five. Hence all contact-free survivors of O4 are confined to the single finite residue n=11, L(H)=5; every order n>=12 survivor is forced into the protected capture/contact frontier.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample of order greater than ten; accepted R191, R193; provisional R313 and R314.

## Scope
Arbitrary-order parent reduction separating genuine historical-contact progress from one finite residual order.

## Applicability
Use as the new top-level O4 split. For n>=12 work only on the protected first-contact branch; if avoiding that branch, switch entirely to order-eleven longest-five geometry.

## Persistence
The order n, maximum proper-path order L(H), and the existence of the puncture/contact event are graph/history data in their respective branches.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not claim a first-contact event itself closes the conjecture. Does not solve the order-eleven residue. Does not use generic R38 or fixed-trimer packet existence as progress.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Historical O4 top-level split into protected contact versus a unique order-eleven residue. Correct frontier staging theorem, but later arbitrary-order floor/fixed-turn reductions have replaced this strategic decomposition and its only purpose was to feed the finite order-eleven chain.
- **Curation note:** Historical O4 top-level split into protected contact versus a unique order-eleven residue. Correct frontier staging theorem, but later arbitrary-order floor/fixed-turn reductions have replaced this strategic decomposition and its only purpose was to feed the finite order-eleven chain.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Accepted new O4 parent split: beyond order ten, every survivor either enters protected first contact through a path of order at least six or is confined to n=11 with maximum proper-path order five.

## Proof
Let L be the maximum order of a proper tight path in H. If L>=6, choose such a path and apply R313 to obtain the asserted puncture-indexed capture and protected first-contact alternative, unless a spanning two-cover already occurs. Since H is hypothetical counterexample, retain the contact branch. If L<=5, R314 gives n<=2L+1<=11. The live O4 regime is beyond order ten, and R191 independently excludes order-ten smallest counterexamples, so n=11. Finally R193 applied to any six vertices gives a tight P5, so L>=5. Thus L=5. These cases exhaust all possibilities.

# R317 — Order-eleven 5+5+1 singleton roots have canonical 4+4+3 companion covers

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Assume the order-eleven longest-five residue of R315/R316. Let K=(k_1,k_2,k_3,k_4,k_5) be a global-longest P5 with six-vertex exterior E, and let e be any omission supplied by R196 for which Q=(q_1,q_2,q_3,q_4,q_5) is a tight P5 on E\\{e}. Then H=K sqcup Q sqcup {e} is a literal 5+5+1 spanning three-cover. Since both K and Q have equal global-longest order five, R44 gives both endpoint reverse-four paths. With the natural endpoint labeling these are the left cross-rail P4 on {k_1,k_2,q_1,q_2} and the right cross-rail P4 on {k_4,k_5,q_4,q_5} (with the tight orders supplied by R44). They are vertex-disjoint. The remaining vertices are exactly {k_3,q_3,e}, which support a tight trimer by R8. Hence every such singleton root has a literal companion spanning 4+4+3 cover. R196 supplies at least four distinct omissions e carrying this companion normal form.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical order-eleven smallest counterexample with maximum proper path order five; K is global-longest P5; e,Q form an R196 singleton root; accepted R44 and R8.

## Scope
Finite order-eleven equal-rail normal form.

## Applicability
Use in the unique finite residue of R315 to replace a 5+5+1 root by two cross-rail reverse P4s plus the middle trimer.

## Persistence
The two reverse P4 supports and leftover trimer support are graph-intrinsic once K,Q and their endpoint orderings are fixed. The displayed 4+4+3 cover is literal.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not sign the two P4s as an opposite historical pair. Does not by itself invoke R171 or close order eleven. Does not synchronize the companion covers for different omissions e.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Order-eleven 4+4+3 companion-cover lemma. Its downstream mixed-bridge consumer was already retired and the finite residue is no longer the active O4 architecture.
- **Curation note:** Order-eleven 4+4+3 companion-cover lemma. Its downstream mixed-bridge consumer was already retired and the finite residue is no longer the active O4 architecture.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Accepted order-eleven equal-rail normal form: each R196 5+5+1 root has a literal 4+4+3 companion cover.

## Proof
Fix one R196 root H=K sqcup Q sqcup {e}. Because the order-eleven residue has global longest-path order five, both K and Q are globally longest and have equal order. The equal-order clause of R44 therefore gives both end reverse-four paths. At one end the reverse P4 uses exactly the first two vertices of K and first two of Q; at the opposite end it uses exactly the last two vertices of K and last two of Q. For P5 rails these support sets are disjoint. Removing their eight vertices from H leaves k_3,q_3,e. Every three-set has a tight orientation by boundary antisymmetry, equivalently R8, so those three vertices form a tight trimer. The three tight paths are pairwise disjoint and cover all eleven vertices.

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Assume an order-eleven 5+5+1 singleton root H=K sqcup Q sqcup {e} in the R315/R316 residue, with ordered rails K=(k_1,k_2,k_3,k_4,k_5) and Q=(q_1,q_2,q_3,q_4,q_5). Since the global longest-path order is five, S is global-longest. Its overlap signature with the original rails and singleton is necessarily one of (|S∩K|,|S∩Q|,1_{e∈S}) in {(3,2,0),(2,3,0),(2,2,1),(3,1,1),(1,3,1)}. In particular S is distinct from K and Q, meets both rails nontrivially, and uses at most three vertices of either rail. Thus every R196 singleton root in the order-eleven residue forces a third mixed global-longest support bridging its two disjoint longest rails.

## Hypotheses
Order-eleven longest-five residue; one R196 singleton root; accepted R317 and R138.

## Scope
Finite support-exchange consequence of the equal-rail 4+4+3 normal form.

## Applicability
Use to turn a disjoint longest-support pair in the order-eleven residue into a third mixed longest support with a five-pattern overlap list.

## Persistence
K,Q,e,A,T and the resulting support S are graph-intrinsic once the root orderings are fixed. The theorem asserts existence of at least one support in the listed family, not a synchronized path representative with the root.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not identify which of the five overlap signatures occurs. Does not say the new support is disjoint from another prescribed support. Does not by itself produce a P6 or two-cover.

## Record notes

- **Curation note:** Order-eleven singleton-root mixed-longest-support bridge. Correct special-order support-exchange result with no live consumers; preserve as provenance while ordinary search emphasizes arbitrary-order carrier/exterior machinery.
- **Review status:** accepted

## Proof
R317 supplies a tight reverse P4 whose support is A={k_1,k_2,q_1,q_2} and a disjoint tight trimer on T={k_3,q_3,e}. Apply R138. Its candidates are A union {k_3}, A union {q_3}, A union {e}, T union the K-side terminal pair of A, T union the Q-side terminal pair of A, and T union the two outer endpoints of A. Their overlap signatures are respectively (3,2,0), (2,3,0), (2,2,1), (3,1,1), (1,3,1), and (2,2,1). At least one supports a tight P5. Since no proper tight path has order more than five in this residue, that P5 is global-longest. Every listed support contains vertices from both K and Q, so it is distinct from both original rails.

# R333 — First-contact mirror trimer forces dual endpoint-recompletion cut crossings

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Assume the literal first-contact mirror-trimer branch of accepted R329. Thus one minimum three-cover of H has the form H=J sqcup U sqcup V with J a tight trimer on {p,x,z}, where D={x,z} is the actual captured carrier/exterior crossing and E={p,x} is a genuine old-carrier adjacency. Then both endpoint deletions force role-sensitive exact-return crossings. For every exact two-cover of H-p, at least one selected state crosses the physical cut D | (U union V). Dually, for every exact two-cover of H-z, at least one selected state crosses E | (U union V). Hence the rooted mirror contact carries two compulsory recompletion portals over the same current residual rails: one incident with the captured-crossing vertex class and one incident with the old-carrier-edge vertex class.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample and the R329 branch-(ii) current mirror-trimer root H=J sqcup U sqcup V is given, with J on {p,x,z}, D={x,z} the captured crossing and E={p,x} the old carrier edge.

## Scope
Order-free exact-cover consequence of the role-sensitive R329 mirror root. No endpoint exposure, capture transport, or General Tight-Path Contact is used.

## Applicability
Use to classify or consume the R329 mirror-trimer branch. Any singleton-deletion recompletion must physically cross out of the surviving role-bearing boundary dimer; neither boundary role can remain an isolated two-vertex rail.

## Persistence
J,D,E and the current residual rails U,V are fixed in the source mirror-root representative. The forced-cut assertion quantifies over every exact two-cover of the corresponding singleton deletion; individual selected crossings are representative-relative.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert the two endpoint-deletion exact covers are simultaneous or share a selected crossing. Does not preserve D or E as a selected dimer in the recompleted cover. Does not imply a spanning two-cover or endpoint exposure by itself.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** First-contact mirror dual endpoint-recompletion crossings are branch-specific zero-consumer machinery; preserve accepted history but retire the claim identity.
- **Curation note:** First-contact mirror dual endpoint-recompletion crossings are branch-specific zero-consumer machinery; preserve accepted history but retire the claim identity.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Accepted. In each endpoint deletion, absence of a cut-crossing would isolate the surviving boundary dimer as two singleton components or a forbidden order-two rail.

## Proof
Write J on {p,x,z} with boundary dimers D={x,z} and E={p,x}. By R5, H-p has exact two-covers; fix any exact two-cover P sqcup Q of H-p. Suppose it selects no state crossing D | (U union V). Then the vertices x,z cannot connect in P sqcup Q to any vertex of U union V. If xz is not selected, x and z lie in two separate components, and since U union V is nonempty there are at least three components, contradiction. If xz is selected, D is an isolated two-vertex component. Because P sqcup Q has exactly two components, D is one rail of the exact two-cover, contradicting R24, which says both rails in any exact one-vertex-deletion two-cover have order at least four. Therefore every exact two-cover of H-p crosses D | (U union V). The argument for H-z and E={p,x} is identical.

Thus the R329 root cannot return after deleting its outer pair with x quiet or isolated: it must either expose x as a rail endpoint or replace the old current mirror-star {p,x},{x,z} by a selected two-edge residual star at x.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample and the accepted R329 branch-(ii) root H=J sqcup U sqcup V is given, with J on {p,x,z}.

## Scope
Order-free exact pair-deletion normal form for the rooted protected-contact mirror trimer. No General Tight-Path Contact and no capture-to-fresh-support ancestry transport.

## Applicability
Use to classify the R329 rooted mirror contact. The outer-pair deletion forces the captured anchor into either a genuine endpoint role or a new selected residual star, giving a concrete role-sensitive object for subsequent exact-cover comparison.

## Persistence
The old mirror supports D,E and capture event remain historical/source-root data. The endpoint role or new residual star is current only in the chosen exact two-cover of H-{p,z}.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not restore p,z while preserving the return rail. Does not assert endpoint exposure in a spanning cover of H. Does not synchronize the old and new stars in one representative.

- **Curation note:** The first-contact-root outer-pair endpoint/internal-star return is subsumed and strengthened by universal tight-trimer outer-pair return machine C311/R359.

By R5 choose any exact two-cover P sqcup Q of H-{p,z}. By R168, both P and Q have order at least three. The vertex x belongs to exactly one rail, say P, so |P|>=3. If x is an endpoint of P, branch (i) holds. Otherwise x is internal in the tight path ordering of P, with distinct immediate predecessor a and successor b. Since p,z are deleted, a,b lie in U union V. The consecutive turn (a,x,b) is tight and the selected supports {a,x},{x,b} form the new residual star at x. # R336 — Outer-pair endpoint return yields a literal rooted two-hole mate clause

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Assume the literal first-contact mirror-trimer branch of accepted R329, with tight current contact trimer J=(p,x,z). Choose an exact two-cover P sqcup Q of H-{p,z} in which the retained captured anchor x is an endpoint of P; by R168, |P|>=3. If P is ordered P=(x,a,b,...) from that endpoint, then the spanning two-cover proposal P*=(p,x,z,a,b,...) together with Q has exactly two uncertified turns, (x,z,a) and (z,a,b). Since H has no spanning two-cover, at least one is bad, so boundary antisymmetry gives the literal mate clause (a,z,x) tight OR (b,a,z) tight. Dually, if P=(...,b,a,x), then the proposal (...,b,a,p,x,z) together with Q has exactly the two holes (b,a,p),(a,p,x), yielding the clause (p,a,b) tight OR (x,p,a) tight. Thus every endpoint branch of the outer-pair return produces an explicit two-hole R173-admissible candidate clause anchored on one boundary side of the role-sensitive contact trimer.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample; the R329 branch-(ii) current trimer J=(p,x,z) is given; P sqcup Q is an exact two-cover of H-{p,z}; x is an endpoint of P.

## Scope
Order-free literal candidate-cover lemma inside the rooted first-contact mirror-trimer normal form.

## Applicability
Use after the endpoint branch of the outer-pair deletion return. It converts endpoint exposure of the captured anchor into a physical two-hole mate clause suitable for R173 chains or further seam classification.

## Persistence
The candidate two-cover is a proof certificate only. The forced reverse turn alternative is graph-intrinsic. J and its role-bearing boundary identities remain historical/source-root data.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert which mate is tight. Does not apply to the internal-star branch. Does not claim one clause alone forces a spanning two-cover.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** superseded
- **Lifecycle note:** The rooted two-hole mate-clause lemma is exactly the historical special case abstracted by generic tight-trimer endpoint-return theorem C310/R358.
- **Curation note:** The rooted two-hole mate-clause lemma is exactly the historical special case abstracted by generic tight-trimer endpoint-return theorem C310/R358.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Accepted. Endpoint exposure in the pair-deletion return yields a literal two-hole spanning-two-cover certificate and therefore the stated antisymmetric mate clause.

## Proof
Suppose first P=(x,a,b,...) with |P|>=3. The sequence (p,x,z,a,b,...) uses the already tight turn (p,x,z) from J, then requires only the new seam turns (x,z,a) and (z,a,b); all later turns are inherited from P starting with (a,b,...). Together with Q this would be a spanning two-cover of H if both seam turns were tight. Hence at least one is bad. R3 says the exact reverse of a bad turn is tight, giving (a,z,x) or (b,a,z). If instead P=(...,b,a,x), the candidate (...,b,a,p,x,z) inherits all earlier P turns and J, with only (b,a,p) and (a,p,x) new. Their exact reversals are (p,a,b) and (x,p,a).

H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample beyond order ten; accepted R329 mirror root and accepted R338 all-internal branch; U,V are the literal residual rails of the R329 source representative.

## Scope
Order-free role-sensitive consequence of the all-internal first-contact return cell. The endpoint floor is attached to one literal source residual rail and is not the fixed-turn target floor {p,z}.

## Applicability
Use in the all-internal branch when a concrete paid object tied to the source mirror representative is needed. It converts the four-way reverse shield into a canonical source-rail endpoint floor.

## Persistence
The source rail U, its endpoint identities u_1,u_r, the two terminal signed supports, common witness x, and the chosen refund interval are named ancestry. The paid floor {u_1},{u_r} is a descendant certificate; U and J are not asserted current at that floor.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not identify {u_1,u_r} with the fixed-turn target pair {p,z}. Does not assert the original capture event at x is a floor coordinate or survives as selected-incidence capture credit. Does not currentize the endpoint floor with the source mirror root and does not by itself close O4.

## Record notes

- **Review status:** accepted

## Proof
Let H=J sqcup U sqcup V be the source mirror-root representative in the all-internal branch, with J=(p,x,z). Since |H|>10, |U|+|V|=|H|-3>=8, so at least one of U,V has order at least four; rename it U=(u_1,...,u_r), r>=4. Accepted R338 gives the tight turns (u_2,u_1,x) and (x,u_r,u_{r-1}). Reading these in the accepted signed-dimer convention, S_L={u_1,u_2} is signed with witness x in one polarity and S_R={u_{r-1},u_r} is signed with the opposite polarity. Because r>=4 the supports are vertex-disjoint, hence they are a direct balanced pair of total mass four. Now take the contiguous tight interval C=(u_2,...,u_{r-1}) of the carrier U. It meets S_L exactly in u_2 and S_R exactly in u_{r-1}. The signed-interval rebirth mechanism used in accepted R174 therefore applies to these two supports along this explicit interval. Each touched support loses exactly its one vertex lying in C and remains nonempty; the resulting signed descendants are precisely the singleton supports {u_1} and {u_r}. Thus, outside the closing alternative of the accepted payment/refund mechanism, the lineage reaches an ancestry-bearing mass-two floor on the two physical endpoints of U. No representative/currentness beyond the stated ancestry is claimed.

# R350 — Two-witness terminal-sign protected-contact compiler

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Let H be a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample and let K=(k_0,...,k_m) be any proper tight path of order at least four. Fix either terminal physical dimer D of K and choose any two distinct exterior vertices e,f in V(H)\\V(K). No common tested orientation or polarity hypothesis is needed. For each witness separately, boundary antisymmetry on the reversal pair with the terminal carrier vertex as middle supplies a tight trimer having D as one terminal physical support, hence a valid signed incarnation of D with that witness. Delete D. R21 forces a selected crossing {x,z} from the nonempty surviving contiguous carrier A=K-D to the exterior. Since x lies on A and e,f lie outside K, at most one of e,f can equal z; therefore at least one admissible witness avoids the selected crossing. R37 captures the carrier-side endpoint x through that crossing. Because |A|>=2, x has a genuine historical adjacency on A, and after choosing an actual capture descendant and designated quiet continuation R312 forces an earlier protected contact or makes lawful R155 old-carrier mirror reentry the first contact. Consequently every terminal dimer of every proper tight path of order at least four with at least two exterior vertices is a protected-first-contact portal. In a smallest counterexample R169 supplies at least five exterior vertices automatically.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample; K is a proper tight path of order at least four; D is either terminal physical dimer; e,f are any two distinct exterior vertices.

## Scope
Order-free strengthening of R323 removing same-polarity and tested-orientation assumptions.

## Applicability
Use to enter the protected first-contact frontier from any proper tight path of order at least four. R199/global-longest endpoint shielding is unnecessary for this purpose.

## Persistence
The terminal dimer, chosen exterior witness identities, deletion crossing, capture event, surviving old carrier A, and lawful first-contact probe persist according to R21/R37/R312. The two sign incarnations need not share tested order or polarity.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert the two sign certificates are same-polarity, does not create an R38 strict-path conclusion, and does not itself close the first-contact branch. The two witnesses are used only adaptively for capture.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** R350 is a nonreconstructible protected-contact compiler with no live consumers and is explicitly fenced from O6. Preserve historically.
- **Curation note:** Generic two-witness terminal-sign protected-contact compiler for any proper path of order at least four.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Major valid strengthening: any two exterior witnesses suffice adaptively; common tested order, polarity, global-longestness, and R199 shielding are unnecessary for terminal protected contact.

## Proof
For the left terminal dimer D={k_0,k_1}, R3 makes exactly one of (e,k_0,k_1),(k_1,k_0,e) tight, and either orientation gives D as a terminal signed support with witness e; likewise for f. After deleting D, R21 selects {x,z} with x in A=K-D and z outside A. Since e,f are outside K while x is in K, the crossing can contain at most one of e,f, namely as z. The other witness is outside the selected pair, so R37 gives a valid capture of x. The terminal deletion leaves the contiguous path A of order at least two, hence x has an old adjacency. Apply R312.

## Statement
Assume the all-internal regime of provisional R359 in a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample beyond order ten. Since |H|>=11, |U|+|V|=|H|-3>=8, so at least one source residual rail, say U=(u_1,...,u_r), has r>=4. Its disjoint terminal dimers S_L={u_1,u_2} and S_R={u_{r-1},u_r} carry opposite-polarity signed certificates with the same witness x, namely (u_2,u_1,x) and (x,u_r,u_{r-1}). Hence they form a direct balanced mass-four pair. The contiguous interval (u_2,...,u_{r-1}) meets each terminal support in exactly one vertex, so the R174 signed-interval refund leaves the ancestry-bearing singleton descendants {u_1} and {u_r}; unless a spanning two-cover occurs this is a mass-two floor on the two physical endpoints of U. Since x is outside U, R3 makes exactly one of (u_1,x,u_r),(u_r,x,u_1) a tight proper turn J_U. Applying R249 to the endpoint floor enters a fixed-turn lineage on J_U with initial clock Psi=(2,0,0) and outer target pair {u_1,u_r}. Thus every all-internal outer-pair return either closes or rotates the fixed-turn target from {a,c} to a new pair {u_1,u_r} disjoint from {a,x,c}, while preserving the same physical middle x.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample beyond order ten; the all-internal branch of provisional R359 holds for a proper tight trimer J=(a,x,c).

## Scope
Order-free/beyond-order-ten recursion obtained by combining the generic return shield with the accepted endpoint-refund and fixed-turn front door.

## Applicability
Use after R359 when no endpoint return exists. It restarts the fixed-turn machinery on a new target pair tied to literal residual-rail geometry and keeps the same physical middle.

## Persistence
The source currentization and refunded floor are alternative lineage states. The source rail endpoints and middle x are graph-intrinsic identities retained in ancestry; no old capture credit is imported into the new clock.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not prove a global monotone under repeated rotations. Does not assert old and new target turns are current simultaneously. A later rotation may revisit an earlier physical target pair; such recurrence is not by itself a contradiction.

## Record notes

- **Curation note:** Universal same-middle target rotation is valid optional route geometry, but the generic fixed-turn mate-or-exit reduction C320 later consumes the recurrent rotation obstruction. Keep R360 as historical/alternate proof architecture rather than active discovery surface.

The four-way shield gives the two displayed reverse endpoint turns on U. Read their terminal dimers as opposite-polarity signed supports with common witness x, exactly as in the accepted R344 argument. They are disjoint, hence R39 gives a balanced mass-four pair. ## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample beyond order ten; the accepted R329 literal first-contact mirror-trimer branch is given.

Finite residual reduction on the contact spine. It deliberately treats repeated target rotation as a constructive cycle, not as a contradiction or global descent.

Each R18 currentization, all-internal shield, refunded floor, and fixed-turn lineage belongs to its own certified representative/ancestry. The cycle records historical certificates, not simultaneous currentness.

## Exclusions / nonclaims

- **Curation note:** First-contact-specific reduction to a same-middle target-rotation cycle is overtaken by the accepted generic fixed-turn mate-or-exit reduction C320/R387, which consumes the recurrent cycle rather than leaving it terminal.

By R373 the four terminal dimers form two cross-rail opposite-sign mass-four diagonals, and every one of the four terminal dimers belongs to one of those diagonals. Choose a terminal dimer D containing the prescribed z and its cross-rail opposite partner. The sign of D is certified by one of the named R359 shield turns with witness x, so R224 applies to the ancestry-bearing balanced-pair lineage and allows the refund orientation selecting endpoint z. Unless a spanning two-cover occurs, the lineage reaches a mass-two floor containing singleton {z}. R249 then enters a fixed-turn lineage whose outer pair is that floor pair, hence contains z.

# R376 — All-internal trimer return has at least six selectable paid-floor coordinates

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Assume the all-internal regime of R359 in a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample beyond order ten, with one source currentization H=J sqcup U sqcup V. Let Z be the union of the physical vertices lying in the four terminal dimers of U and V. Then |Z|>=6. Moreover for every z in Z, R374 gives an alternative ancestry-bearing continuation that either closes with a spanning two-cover or reaches a mass-two floor containing singleton {z}, hence a fixed-turn lineage whose outer target pair contains z. Thus every all-internal return carries at least six distinct independently selectable paid-floor coordinates.

## Hypotheses
Smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample beyond order ten; all-internal R359 return regime.

## Scope
Quantitative avoidance-reservoir corollary of the terminal-coordinate floor fan.

## Applicability
Use when a downstream floor/fixed-turn consumer needs to avoid a blocker set of size at most five.

## Persistence
The six-or-more physical terminal coordinates are graph-intrinsic relative to the chosen source rails; each selected floor lineage is alternative.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not synchronize the six floors, prescribe their second singleton coordinates, or preserve one common fixed-turn middle.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** At-least-six selectable coordinates is the immediate count of terminal vertices from R168 followed by coordinatewise C324. Useful avoidance shorthand, but low discovery value and no new persistence coordinate.
- **Curation note:** At-least-six selectable coordinates is the immediate count of terminal vertices from R168 followed by coordinatewise C324. Useful avoidance shorthand, but low discovery value and no new persistence coordinate.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Accepted after independent audit.

## Proof
R359/R168 give |U|,|V|>=2 and |U|+|V|=|H|-3>=8. A rail of order 2 contributes 2 distinct terminal-dimer vertices, order 3 contributes 3, and order at least 4 contributes 4. Under two rail orders at least 2 with sum at least 8, the minimum total contribution is attained at (2,6), giving 2+4=6. The rails are vertex-disjoint, so |Z|>=6. Apply R374 separately to every z in Z.

# R381 — Every decorated target-rotation state has at least four off-transition paid-floor escapes

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Assume one transition P_i->P_{i+1} in the decorated same-middle target-rotation cycle of R370, sourced from an all-internal R359 currentization H=J_i sqcup U_i sqcup V_i. Let Z_i be the terminal-coordinate set of that currentization. Then |Z_i|>=6 by R376, while the designated next target pair P_{i+1} consists of exactly two vertices of Z_i, namely the endpoints of the chosen long source residual rail. Hence at least four vertices z in Z_i\\P_{i+1} are available. For each such z, R374 supplies an alternative ancestry-bearing continuation that either closes or reaches a mass-two floor whose target pair contains z; therefore that alternative fixed-turn target pair is not the designated pair P_{i+1}. Thus every state of a decorated same-middle cycle has at least four independent physical coordinate choices that escape the prescribed next transition.

## Hypotheses
Smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample beyond order ten; one decorated all-internal transition in the R370 cycle.

## Scope
Quantitative branching corollary showing the same-middle cycle is not a closed deterministic state graph.

## Applicability
Use when attempting to escape or destabilize a target-rotation cycle by choosing a different paid-floor coordinate at one state.

## Persistence
Each escape lineage retains its chosen terminal coordinate and floor ancestry separately; lineages are alternative.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not guarantee the alternative target pair lies outside all other cycle pairs, does not synchronize four escapes, and does not itself force an exit or mate clause.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Four off-transition escapes is a counting corollary of C324/C326 tied to the decorated target-rotation cycle, which is no longer a canonical active route after C320. Preserve R381 historically.
- **Curation note:** Four off-transition escapes is a counting corollary of C324/C326 tied to the decorated target-rotation cycle, which is no longer a canonical active route after C320. Preserve R381 historically.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Accepted after independent audit.

## Proof
R376 gives at least six distinct selectable terminal vertices in the source all-internal currentization. R360/R370 choose P_{i+1} as the two endpoints of one source residual rail, so P_{i+1} is a two-element subset of this terminal set. At least four terminal coordinates remain outside P_{i+1}. Applying R374 to any such z gives a floor pair containing z; since z is not in P_{i+1}, that floor pair cannot equal the designated next pair.

# R392 — No-interaction regime forces universal endpoint exposure after every pair deletion

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Let H be a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample beyond order ten. Then either H contains a source-trimer-localized historical signed-support/anchor interaction or cross-generation pair interaction of the type produced by R390, or the following universal endpoint property holds: for every physical pair {a,c} subset V(H) and every vertex x outside {a,c}, there exists an exact two-cover of H-{a,c} in which x is a rail endpoint. In the universal-endpoint branch, each triple {a,x,c} also supplies an explicit R173-admissible mate clause by R358 after orienting its unique x-middle tight trimer.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample beyond order ten; accepted boundary antisymmetry R3 and provisional R390.

## Scope
Order-free global structural corollary of the universal trimer front door. It packages the absence of the historical-interaction output into an endpoint-universality property for every pair-deletion subsystem.

## Applicability
Use when attempting to consume the mate-clause side of R391. If one globally excludes source-trimer historical interactions, every pair deletion becomes endpoint-universal, a much stronger exact-cover condition that may be attacked by endpoint, graft, maximin, or mate-cycle machinery.

## Persistence
Endpoint exposure is existential separately for each triple (a,x,c); the various exact two-covers need not coincide. Each resulting mate clause is graph-intrinsic with its own literal proposal certificate.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert one exact two-cover exposes all vertices simultaneously. Does not assert endpoint universality alone closes the conjecture. Does not conjoin the many return representatives. Does not say the mate clauses are automatically linked into an R173 cycle.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** superseded
- **Lifecycle note:** No-interaction endpoint-universality statement is the intermediate branch packaged into stronger top-level reduction C322/R393. Preserve R392 as the exact branch interface and proof dependency.
- **Curation note:** No-interaction endpoint-universality statement is the intermediate branch packaged into stronger top-level reduction C322/R393. Preserve R392 as the exact branch interface and proof dependency.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Accepted after independent audit.

## Proof
Fix arbitrary distinct a,c and x outside {a,c}. Boundary antisymmetry on the physical triple {a,x,c} gives exactly one tight x-middle orientation J, either (a,x,c) or (c,x,a). Apply provisional R390 to this J. Its second output is a source-J historical signed-support/anchor or cross-generation pair interaction. If this occurs for at least one choice of a,c,x, the first alternative of the corollary holds. Otherwise it occurs for none. Hence for every choice R390 must be in its endpoint-return branch, which by construction comes from an exact two-cover of H-{a,c} placing x at a rail endpoint. Since a,c,x were arbitrary, every pair-deletion subsystem is endpoint-universal in this existential-per-vertex sense. Accepted R358 applied to each exposed x-middle trimer gives the associated literal two-hole mate clause.

# R395 — Endpoint-universal branch yields a triple-deletion three-cap fan

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Assume the endpoint-universal branch of R393 in a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample H. Fix any physical triple T={a,b,c}. Then for each t in T there exists an exact two-cover A_t sqcup B_t of the same triple-deletion residue H-T together with one designated endpoint cap for t: one of A_t,B_t has an endpoint r_t followed by a second vertex s_t such that either (t,r_t,s_t) is tight or dually (s_t,r_t,t) is tight, and reattaching t at that endpoint recovers an exact two-cover of H-(T\\{t}). Thus H-T carries three alternative exact two-cover representatives, one equipped with a lawful endpoint-restoration cap for each deleted vertex a,b,c. The three representatives need not coincide.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in the endpoint-universal branch of accepted R393; T is any three-vertex set.

## Scope
Order-free same-residue reformulation of universal pair-deletion endpoint exposure.

## Applicability
Use to replace the global quantified endpoint property by a fixed triple-deletion fiber with three vertex-labeled restoration caps. This creates a common-residue interface for transfer, overlap, component-drop, or assembly arguments.

## Persistence
For each t, the exact H-T cover A_t sqcup B_t and its t-cap are representative-relative; the deleted triple T and the fact that all three cap representatives live over H-T are graph-intrinsic. The three covers are alternative and not simultaneous.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert the three cap representatives have the same residual rails, lie in one transfer component, or can be synchronized. Does not itself produce a spanning two-cover, mate cycle, or interaction.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Endpoint-universal triple-deletion three-cap fan has no current active consumers and is branch-local staging under later endpoint-universal reductions; retire.
- **Curation note:** Endpoint-universal triple-deletion three-cap fan has no current active consumers and is branch-local staging under later endpoint-universal reductions; retire.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Accepted after audit of scope, dependencies, orientation/currentness, and persistence.

## Proof
Fix t in T. R393 gives an exact two-cover P_t sqcup Q_t of H-(T\\{t}) in which t is a rail endpoint. By R168 the rail containing t has order at least three, so deleting endpoint t leaves a tight path of order at least two. Together with the untouched opposite rail this is a two-path cover of H-T. By R5, H-T has path-cover number exactly two, so this residual cover is exact. The endpoint turn of P_t is tight and records precisely how t reattaches to that residual rail to recover the pair-deletion cover. Repeating independently for t=a,b,c yields the three cap representatives over the common residue H-T.

# R396 — Common-shadow three-cap closure-or-terminal-collision theorem

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Let H be a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample and let T={a,b,c}. Suppose one exact two-cover H-T=U sqcup V simultaneously supports endpoint-restoration caps for all three deleted vertices: for each t in T, t can be attached to one physical end of U or V by a tight endpoint turn, recovering a tight two-cover of H-(T\\{t}). Then either H has a spanning two-cover, or two distinct deleted vertices t,tprime attach at the same physical end of the same residual rail. In the latter case the terminal physical dimer at that end carries same-polarity signed certificates with the two distinct witnesses t,tprime in the same tested order, so R38 yields the accepted same-polarity two-extension collision package localized to that terminal dimer. Consequently any triple-deletion residue whose three R395 cap representatives coincide on one exact residual cover either closes or carries a literal same-end terminal collision.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample; T is a three-vertex set; H-T=U sqcup V is one exact two-cover; each t in T has an endpoint cap on this same U sqcup V.

## Scope
Order-free fixed-shadow synchronization theorem for the endpoint-universal branch.

## Applicability
Use after R395 whenever two or three restoration caps can be aligned to one exact H-T representative. In particular, if H-T has a unique exact two-cover up to swapping the two rails, all three caps align and the theorem applies.

## Persistence
The exact residual cover U sqcup V, cap target ends, and any resulting terminal collision are literal same-representative data. The collision witnesses are the named deleted vertices.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert the three R395 cap representatives always coincide. Does not classify the same-polarity collision further and does not close the conjecture in that branch.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** superseded
- **Lifecycle note:** Same-shadow three-cap closure-or-terminal-collision is an internal synchronization stage of the stronger aligned-cap consumer C345/R404, which sends any fully aligned three-cap frame to closure or role-linked interaction.
- **Curation note:** Same-shadow three-cap closure-or-terminal-collision is an internal synchronization stage of the stronger aligned-cap consumer C345/R404, which sends any fully aligned three-cap frame to closure or role-linked interaction.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Accepted after audit of scope, dependencies, orientation/currentness, and persistence.

## Proof
By R168 each rail of H-T has order at least two, so each of U,V has two well-defined physical ends with terminal dimers. Assign to each t in T one physical end e(t) at which its assumed cap attaches. If e(a),e(b),e(c) are pairwise distinct, attach all three deleted vertices simultaneously. Attachments on different rails are disjoint, and attachments at opposite ends of one rail commute because each uses only the original terminal dimer at its own end. The two resulting tight paths cover every vertex of H, contradiction. Therefore in a surviving counterexample two distinct vertices t,tprime share one end. If that end is the left end U=(u1,u2,...), the two cap turns are (t,u1,u2) and (tprime,u1,u2); dually at a right end they are (...,u_{r-1},u_r,t) and (...,u_{r-1},u_r,tprime). Thus the same oriented terminal dimer has two distinct witnesses with identical polarity and tested order. Accepted R38 gives the same-polarity two-extension collision package.

# R398 — Pair-deletion endpoint-or-persistent-middle dichotomy

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Let H be a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample beyond order ten. Fix a physical pair D={a,c} and a third vertex x outside D. Orient the unique x-middle tight trimer J on {a,x,c}. Then exactly one of the following return regimes holds. (E) Some exact two-cover of H-D places x at a rail endpoint; in that case R358 gives an explicit candidate-aware two-hole mate clause anchored on J. (I) Every exact two-cover of H-D places x internally; in that case for any chosen exact cover H-D=P sqcup Q containing x internally, the R359 all-internal return structure applies, and after currentizing J over the corresponding triple-deletion residual rails the source turn J carries the accepted R389 bilateral four-birth interaction fan localized at middle x. Thus persistent internality across one fixed pair-deletion fiber is the exact negative-space alternative to endpoint exposure, and the historical interaction output should be regarded as attached to this stronger static fiber property.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample beyond order ten; D={a,c}; x is distinct from a,c; accepted R3,R358,R359,R389.

## Scope
Order-free local negative-space reformulation of the current O4 residual.

## Applicability
Use to retain the fixed-deletion universal-internality predicate instead of collapsing immediately to anonymous historical interaction. The global no-persistent-middle branch is exactly endpoint universality.

## Persistence
The endpoint-existence statement and persistent-internality predicate are properties of the fixed deletion fiber H-D. Any chosen all-internal source cover and its R389 interaction fan are representative/historical data.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert the historical interaction closes. Does not assert a unique exact cover. Does not synchronize different all-internal source covers.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** One-consumer pair-deletion endpoint/persistent-middle helper whose consumer C340 is already superseded; retire.
- **Curation note:** One-consumer pair-deletion endpoint/persistent-middle helper whose consumer C340 is already superseded; retire.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Accepted after audit of scope, dependencies, orientation/currentness, and persistence.

## Proof
Boundary antisymmetry gives one tight x-middle orientation J on {a,x,c}. Apply R359 to J. By its quantified return classification, either some exact H-{a,c} cover has x as endpoint, in which case R358 supplies the mate clause, or every exact H-{a,c} cover has x internal. In the latter case choose any exact return and use its induced R359 source/currentization packet; accepted R389 then supplies the bilateral four-birth interaction fan at the same source turn J and middle x. The two regimes are mutually exclusive by definition and exhaustive.

# R400 — Common-shadow three-cap occupancy normal form

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Let H be a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample and let T={a,b,c}. Suppose one exact two-cover H-T=U sqcup V supports endpoint-restoration caps for all three deleted vertices. Then, unless H has a spanning two-cover, the cap-end occupancy is forced into one of two structured residues. (I) All three caps concentrate at the same physical end of U or V. (II) Exactly two deleted vertices, say a,b, cap the same physical end and the third caps a different end; then the physical deleted dimer {a,b} carries both opposite tested orientations as signed supports of the same polarity with the same witness equal to the terminal vertex of the duplicated cap end. Concretely, if U=(u_1,u_2,...) and a,b both cap the left end, then in the nonclosing branch (a,b,u_1) and (b,a,u_1) are both bad, hence (u_1,b,a) and (u_1,a,b) are tight. The right-end dual gives the opposite common polarity.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample; T is a triple; one exact H-T cover supports all three endpoint caps.

## Scope
Order-free refinement of R396 retaining the cap-end occupancy and the exact bidirectional deleted-dimer residue.

## Applicability
Use after common-shadow cap alignment. It reduces nonclosure to either three-cap concentration at one physical end or a bidirectionally signed dimer on two deleted vertices with a named terminal witness.

## Persistence
The common residual cover, cap targets, duplicated end, deleted dimer, witness, tested orientations, and signs are literal/graph-intrinsic in the displayed frame.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert the bidirectional dimer closes, that the concentrated case is impossible, or that cap representatives always align.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** superseded
- **Lifecycle note:** Three-cap occupancy 3 versus 2+1 normal form is an internal case split consumed completely by aligned-cap interaction theorem C345/R404.
- **Curation note:** Three-cap occupancy 3 versus 2+1 normal form is an internal case split consumed completely by aligned-cap interaction theorem C345/R404.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Accepted after audit of scope, dependencies, orientation/currentness, and persistence.

## Proof
There are four physical ends because R168 gives both residual rails order at least two. If the three caps target three distinct ends, the three endpoint attachments commute and give a spanning two-cover, impossible. Suppose exactly a,b target one left end U=(u1,u2,...) and c targets a different end. The cap turns (a,u1,u2) and (b,u1,u2) are tight. If (a,b,u1) is tight, then (a,b,u1,u2,...) is a tight extension of U using both a,b; attaching c at its distinct capped end commutes and closes H. Likewise if (b,a,u1) is tight. Hence in a surviving counterexample both stack turns are bad. Boundary antisymmetry gives (u1,b,a) and (u1,a,b) tight, which are same-polarity signed certificates on the two tested orientations (b,a) and (a,b) with common witness u1. The right-end case is the reversal-dual. If all three target the same end, retain that as the concentrated residue.

# R401 — Aligned three-cap dual saturation normal form

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Assume one exact triple-deletion cover H-T=U sqcup V supports restoration caps for all three deleted vertices T={a,b,c}. Unless H has a spanning two-cover, one of two dual saturation packets occurs. (R) Residual-support saturation: all three caps concentrate at one physical end, so the terminal physical dimer at that end carries three same-polarity signed certificates with the three distinct witnesses a,b,c in one tested orientation. (D) Deleted-support saturation: the cap occupancy is 2+1, and for the two deleted vertices sharing one end, their physical dimer carries both opposite tested orientations as signed supports of one common polarity with the same witness equal to the residual terminal vertex at that end. Thus common-shadow endpoint universality cannot remain diffuse without closure: it concentrates either three deleted witnesses onto one residual dimer or two orientations of one deleted dimer onto one residual witness.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample; one exact H-T cover supports all three caps; accepted/provisional R400.

## Scope
Order-free dual saturation reformulation of the aligned three-cap nonclosing residue.

## Applicability
Use as the compact local target after cap synchronization. The two branches exchange the roles of deleted and residual vertices and may admit different signed-support consumers.

## Persistence
All supports, witnesses, tested orientations and cap-end identities are graph-intrinsic/literal in the common-shadow frame.
