# R409 — Endpoint-universal pair deletion forces an internal-vertex component-drop fan

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Assume the endpoint-universal branch of accepted R393 in a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample H of order n>=11. Fix any physical pair {a,c} and any exact two-cover F=U sqcup V of H-{a,c}. By R168 both rails have order at least three, so F has exactly four physical endpoints. For every residual vertex x in V(H)\\({a,c} union End(F)), x is internal on its rail in F. Endpoint universality supplies another exact two-cover F_x of H-{a,c} in which x is a rail endpoint. Deleting x produces two literal covers of the same proper residue H-{a,c,x}: trimming x from F_x gives a cover with at most two components, while deleting internal x from F splits its rail and gives a literal three-cover. Hence R159, equivalently the endpoint-status comparison theorem R408, forces a graph-intrinsic balanced opposite-sign pair for every such x. The exact component-drop certificate is indexed by the physical puncture x and the fixed source cover F. Since H-{a,c} has n-2 vertices and F has four endpoints, there are exactly n-6 such internal vertices, at least five in the beyond-order-ten regime. Thus every fixed pair deletion in the endpoint-universal branch carries an (n-6)-vertex fan of alternative exact 3-to-2 component-drop certificates over one common source cover.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample with n>=11; accepted R168, R393, R159/R408; {a,c} is any physical pair; F is any exact two-cover of H-{a,c}.

## Scope
Order-free beyond-order-ten consequence of endpoint universality. The fan is indexed over one fixed pair-deletion source cover.

## Applicability
Use to replace vague exact-cover multiplicity in the endpoint-universal branch by at least n-6 explicit puncture-indexed component-drop certificates on triple-deletion residues.

## Persistence
The fixed source cover F and puncture identity x are retained in each component-drop certificate. The balanced pair obtained from R159/R408 is graph-intrinsic but may differ with x and is not asserted current. Different x-descendants are alternative.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert the balanced pairs for different x are distinct or simultaneous. Does not preserve x as a witness/support of the R159 pair. Does not by itself close endpoint universality.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Endpoint-universal internal-vertex component-drop fan is a coordinatewise application of C349 across one fixed pair-deletion cover. Quantitative n-6 packet count is useful shorthand but adds little discovery content and has no live consumer.
- **Curation note:** Endpoint-universal internal-vertex component-drop fan is a coordinatewise application of C349 across one fixed pair-deletion cover. Quantitative n-6 packet count is useful shorthand but adds little discovery content and has no live consumer.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Accepted after audit of scope, dependencies, orientation/currentness, and persistence.

## Proof
Let W=H-{a,c}. By R168 each rail of F has order at least three, hence End(F) consists of four distinct vertices. Fix x in W\\End(F). In F, x is internal, so F-x is a literal three-cover of W-x. By R393 endpoint universality there exists an exact two-cover F_x of W with x at a rail endpoint; deleting x from that endpoint path leaves a literal one- or two-component cover of W-x. Since W-x is proper in H, R159 applies and yields a graph-intrinsic balanced pair. This is precisely the endpoint-status disagreement mechanism of R408. The construction is available separately for every x in W\\End(F), whose cardinality is |W|-4=n-6.

# R412 — Fixed-support endpoint universality reduces to a singleton root or a collision-saturated rail

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Assume the fixed-support factorization branch of R411 for a pair deletion H-{a,c}=P sqcup Q in a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample H: every vertex of P and Q is a physical endpoint of some Hamilton tight path on its own fixed support, and endpoint choices on the two supports may be combined independently. Call a deleted vertex t attachable to a support S if some Hamilton tight path on S has an endpoint at which direct attachment of t is tight. Then either (I) at least one of a,c is attachable to at least one support; choosing such an attachment, say c to P, and any Hamilton path on Q gives a literal exact two-cover of H-a and therefore a spanning singleton-root three-cover H={a} sqcup P_c sqcup Q that retains the fixed pair-deletion support partition away from the attached c; or (II) neither a nor c is attachable to either P or Q. In case (II), both deleted vertices are blocked at every endpoint of every Hamilton path on both fixed supports. Since |P|+|Q|=|H|-2>=9, one support, say P, has order at least five. Choose any Hamilton tight path P_0=(p_1,...,p_m) on P. The two direct a-attachments at its ends are bad, so boundary antisymmetry gives opposite-polarity signed certificates with common witness a on the two disjoint reverse terminal dimers {p_1,p_2} and {p_{m-1},p_m}. They form a direct balanced mass-four pair; the interval between the inner terminal vertices invokes R174 and yields, unless a spanning two-cover occurs, an ancestry-bearing mass-two floor on the two physical endpoints {p_1},{p_m}. Hence R249 enters a floor-aligned fixed-turn lineage. Moreover both a and c are blocked at every endpoint, so every vertex x of P or Q is the endpoint of some Hamilton path whose terminal dimer carries a same-polarity R38 collision with the two witnesses a,c. Thus the no-attachment branch is simultaneously a support-wide collision saturation and a paid-floor front door.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample; R411 fixed-support factorization holds for pair {a,c} with supports P,Q; accepted R3 and R38.

## Scope
Beyond-order-ten structural reduction inside the no-cross-state fixed-support endpoint-universal branch.

## Applicability
Use after R411. Either one deleted vertex can be absorbed into one fixed rail support, producing a singleton root for the other while retaining the support partition, or both deleted vertices are globally blocked from both supports and a long-support terminal pair pays directly to an endpoint floor.

## Persistence
Attachability is existential over Hamilton paths on one fixed support. The singleton-root cover in case (I) is one chosen representative. In case (II), the collision certificate for each x may arise from a different Hamilton path P_x; the physical witness pair {a,c} and support vertex x are fixed, but the terminal neighbor may vary with x.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert the vertex-indexed collision supports are distinct, simultaneous, or closing. Does not prescribe both endpoints of a Hamilton path. The singleton-root branch does not automatically inherit maximin properties.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Fixed-support attachability/collision-saturation continuation is a branch-local consumer of C352 with no live downstream consumer. Preserve its singleton-root and support-wide collision details historically.
- **Curation note:** Fixed-support attachability/collision-saturation continuation is a branch-local consumer of C352 with no live downstream consumer. Preserve its singleton-root and support-wide collision details historically.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Accepted after audit of scope, dependencies, orientation/currentness, and persistence.

## Proof
Let B be the bipartite graph with left side {a,c}, right side {P,Q}, and tS an edge iff t is attachable to S. If B had a perfect matching, say aP and cQ, choose a Hamilton path on P with a tight a-endcap and independently a Hamilton path on Q with a tight c-endcap. Attaching a and c gives two disjoint tight paths spanning H, contradiction; the swapped matching is identical. Thus B has no perfect matching. For a 2x2 bipartite graph, either some left vertex has degree zero, or the union of the neighborhoods of both left vertices has size one. In the first case, say deg(a)=0. If deg(c)>0, choose an edge cS and its witnessing Hamilton path; attach c there and combine with any Hamilton path on the other fixed support, producing an exact two-cover of H-a and hence the singleton root. If deg(c)=0 too, either support is blocked by both witnesses. In the second Hall-failure case, both a,c have all neighbors contained in one support, so the other support is blocked by both. Now let S be a support blocked by both a,c and fix x in S. R411 supplies a Hamilton path S_x with x as a physical endpoint. The direct attachment turn for a at that endpoint is bad by nonattachability, and so is the direct attachment turn for c. Their exact reverses are tight and use the same tested orientation of the x-terminal dimer with distinct witnesses a,c, hence are same-polarity certificates. R38 gives the collision package. Repeat separately for every x in S.

# R419 — Every all-internal source-trimer vertex is selectable at the paid floor

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Assume the all-internal regime of R359 for a proper tight source trimer J=(a,x,c) in a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample H. Then for every prescribed source vertex z in {a,x,c}, there is a chosen ancestry-bearing balanced-pair continuation that either produces a spanning two-cover or reaches a mass-two balanced-pair floor in which (z) is literally one singleton signed support. The chosen lineage retains J, the physical middle x, the selected J-terminal mate containing z, the R389 pair-birth certificate through that mate, the endpoint-selective refund orientation, and the literal floor coordinate z. The three choices z=a,x,c are alternative lineages and need not coexist.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample; J=(a,x,c) is a proper tight trimer in the accepted R359 all-internal regime; accepted R389 and R224.

## Scope
Order-free source-trimer coordinate-selection theorem inside the all-internal R359 branch. It consumes the inherited-turn provenance of the R389 four-birth fan rather than merely descending an anonymous balanced pair.

## Applicability
Use when downstream work needs a mass-two floor carrying a prescribed physical coordinate of the original source trimer. In particular, it upgrades Type I ancestry from R417 to a concrete selectable floor coordinate tied to J.

## Persistence
For the chosen z-lineage retain J, x, the selected terminal signed dimer M_L or M_R of J containing z, one R389 direct pair-birth certificate using that mate, the R224 aligned refund orientation, the prescribed physical endpoint z, and the final singleton floor coordinate (z). Other source representatives and the second floor singleton need not persist.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert the three z-selective floors coexist or can be synchronized. Does not prescribe the second floor singleton. Does not claim the selected floor is target-aligned to any independently chosen vertex or closes the conjecture. Does not apply to the common-shadow Type II branch without an inherited-turn signed dimer satisfying R224.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Source-trimer vertex-selectability is used only as an internal step in the stronger fixed-turn reduction R387; inline conceptually and retire.
- **Curation note:** Source-trimer vertex-selectability is used only as an internal step in the stronger fixed-turn reduction R387; inline conceptually and retire.
- **Review status:** accepted

## Proof
Write the two terminal signed dimers of the proper tight source trimer J=(a,x,c) as M_L and M_R, so V(M_L)={a,x} and V(M_R)={x,c}. By R389, in the all-internal R359 state there are four direct mass-four balanced-pair birth certificates, with two births using M_L as the unique J-terminal mate of opposite polarity to a role-bearing residual terminal dimer and two births using M_R. Fix z in {a,x,c}. If z=a choose M_L; if z=c choose M_R; if z=x choose either terminal mate. Choose any one of the R389 direct balanced-pair births that uses the selected mate M. This produces an ancestry-bearing balanced-pair lineage containing the signed physical dimer M, and the sign of M is certified by the named inherited tight turn J itself. Therefore all hypotheses of R224 hold for M. Choose in R224 the endpoint-selective refund channel whose prescribed endpoint is z. R224 then gives either a spanning two-cover or an ancestry-bearing mass-two floor in which (z) is literally one singleton floor coordinate. Its persistence clause retains the inherited turn J, chosen refund orientation, physical endpoint z, refund certificate, and literal floor coordinate; adjoining the R389 birth certificate and source middle x to the historical ledger yields exactly the stated persistence. Since the choices of birth, terminal mate, and refund channel are made separately for each z, the three conclusions are alternative lineages and no simultaneity is claimed.

# R424 — Universal O4 reduction to localized trimer interaction or common-shadow cross-state pair

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Let H be a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample beyond order ten. Fix any two distinct prescribed vertices u,v. Unless H has a spanning two-cover, there is a chosen certificate-retaining continuation with one of the following outcomes: (1) an accepted explicit historical pair/contact exit; or (2) an ancestry-bearing both-singleton balanced-pair floor whose singleton supports are exactly {u},{v}. In outcome (2) the floor retains one of the two typed O4 provenance packages of R417: Type I source-trimer provenance, or Type II common-shadow cross-state provenance. Indeed R417 first normalizes every nonclosing O4 survivor to an ancestry-bearing both-singleton floor. Choose any b distinct from u,v; by R170 exactly one of (u,b,v),(v,b,u) is a proper tight turn J with outer pair {u,v}. Apply R423 to the R417 floor. It either closes, takes an accepted explicit historical pair/contact exit, or steers the active floor to {u,v} while preserving the incoming ancestry ledger. At that aligned checkpoint the R423 fixed-turn endpoint budget applies: at most two aligned reentries can remain quiet before later aligned reentry forces closure or an explicit historical exit. Thus no physical target pair is intrinsically inaccessible from the normalized O4 floor; the scarce information is the retained Type I/II ancestry, not floor-coordinate availability.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample beyond order ten; provisional R417 and R423; accepted R170.

## Scope
Order-free strengthening of the top-level O4 normalization. The target pair {u,v} is prescribed before the reentry continuation and is independent of the incoming both-singleton floor coordinates.

## Applicability
Use after O4 normalization when a downstream consumer needs the floor aligned to a specific physical pair, especially the original source-trimer outer pair or the original common-shadow cross-state endpoints.

## Persistence
R423 preserves the incoming R417 ancestry ledger while floor coordinates change. Hence Type I source-trimer data or Type II common-shadow/cross-state data survive target-pair alignment. The chosen target turn J and its later endpoint-capture/contact history are retained within the J-lineage.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert arbitrary same-representative synchronization; does not say an explicit historical exit closes the conjecture; does not guarantee the target-aligned floor is reached if a productive exit occurs first; does not make floor coordinates scarce or canonically determined; does not make alternative target-pair descendants simultaneous.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** R424 is a nonreconstructible target-pair O4 routing wrapper with no live consumers; preserve historically.
- **Curation note:** Target-pair O4 localization is a reusable reduction, not current spine.
- **Review status:** accepted

## Proof
Assume H does not already have a spanning two-cover. By R417 choose a certificate-retaining continuation to a both-singleton floor S carrying either Type I source-trimer provenance or Type II common-shadow cross-state provenance. Fix distinct target vertices u,v and choose b outside {u,v}; the beyond-order-ten hypothesis supplies such b. By R170 exactly one of (u,b,v) and (v,b,u) is a proper tight turn J, whose unordered outer pair is {u,v}. R423 is turn-first and floor-independent: it applies to this preselected J from the arbitrary ancestry-bearing floor S. Along its chosen continuation, either a spanning two-cover or an accepted explicit historical pair/contact exit occurs, or Complete Floor Pair Steering aligns the active floor to {u},{v}. R423 explicitly preserves the complete incoming floor ancestry ledger while the active singleton coordinates change, so the R417 Type I/II provenance survives alignment. Its selected-incidence endpoint-anchor argument further implies that at most two aligned reentries can be quiet. This proves the claimed target-pair normalization and shows that coordinate accessibility is generic once the R417 floor is available.

# R447 — Pair-deletion four-endcap matrix forces a paid floor or triple terminal collision

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Let H be a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample of order n>=11, let {a,c} be any physical pair, and let H-{a,c}=U sqcup V be any exact two-cover. The R402 endcap matrix admits the following finite consumer. Either H has a spanning two-cover; or (I) one deleted vertex, say a, is blocked at all four rail ends. Then accepted R402/R174 yields an ancestry-bearing mass-two floor on the two physical endpoints h,t of a literal long residual rail. Choose the blocked deleted vertex a as the third vertex of that floor and orient the unique a-middle tight turn J on {h,a,t}. R249 enters a lawful floor-aligned fixed-turn lineage for J, and R387 yields either an explicit R173-admissible mate clause anchored on J or an accepted historical contact/pair interaction localized to the same turn lineage; or (II) G_a=G_c={e} for one unique common good end position. At e the direct attachments of both a and c to the same source rail are tight. If e is a head endpoint p, two applications of R164 in opposite witness orders have strict-extension alternatives that would prepend both deleted vertices to the whole rail and close with the untouched other rail; hence in the nonclosing branch both (p,a,c) and (p,c,a) are forced. Thus both orientations of the deleted dimer {a,c} are head-signed with common witness p and R407 gives a fixed-trimer historical interaction localized at p. The tail-end case is dual, forcing both (c,a,q) and (a,c,q) and applying R407 at q. Consequently every exact pair-deletion endcap matrix compiles to a spanning two-cover, a literal mate clause/historical interaction through a blocked deleted vertex, or one endpoint-local R407 interaction at the unique common good end. The three bad ends are not asserted to satisfy the R407 bidirectional same-witness hypothesis.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample with n>=11; {a,c} is any physical pair; H-{a,c}=U sqcup V is any exact two-cover. Use accepted R402 for the endcap dichotomy, R174/R249/R387 for the blocked-end paid-floor branch, and R164/R407 for the common-good-end collision branch.

## Scope
Order-free beyond-order-ten strengthening of accepted R402. It consumes both nonclosing R402 branches: the blocked-end floor is routed immediately through a fixed turn whose middle is the blocked deleted vertex, while the common-good-end branch yields one certified R407 interaction at the unique end where both deleted vertices attach tightly. No endpoint-universality, capture, longest-path, or density hypothesis is used.

## Applicability
Use on any exact pair-deletion cover when one wants an actual downstream consumer rather than stopping at R402's paid floor or collision-web labels. The blocked deleted vertex is the canonical middle for case I. In case II, consume the unique common good end by double R164 and R407; do not infer the same packet at the three bad ends.

## Persistence
In case (I), retain the blocked deleted vertex a, the long-rail physical endpoints h,t, the ancestry-bearing floor, and the chosen a-middle fixed turn through the R249/R387 lineage. In case (II), retain the source deleted pair {a,c}, the unique common good end e, the two forced reverse-contact trimers at that end, the two same-polarity orientations of {a,c} with common endpoint witness, and the resulting R407 fixed-trimer interaction. Later descendants are lineage-relative and need not coexist.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert a single mate clause or historical interaction closes O4. Does not assert R407 packets at the three bad ends of case II. Does not assert later floor and interaction descendants coexist. Does not treat tight cycles as contradictions. Does not assume the source exact pair-deletion cover persists into the case-I fixed-turn lineage. Does not invoke opposite-polarity same-singleton collision.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Pair-deletion four-endcap matrix has no current consumers; retire this recent branch-specific consumer.
- **Curation note:** Pair-deletion four-endcap matrix has no current consumers; retire this recent branch-specific consumer.
- **Review status:** accepted

## Proof
Start from accepted R402. If its immediate spanning-two-cover branch occurs, stop. Suppose case (I), say a is blocked at all four rail ends. R402 gives a literal long residual rail L with physical endpoints h,t and, through its R174 refund, an ancestry-bearing mass-two floor {h},{t}. The deleted vertex a is distinct from h,t, so orient by boundary antisymmetry the unique a-middle tight turn J on {h,a,t}. Apply R249 to this specific floor and this middle a to enter a lawful pair-bearing fixed-turn lineage whose outer target pair is exactly {h,t}. Since n>=11, R387 applies: unless H closes, the lineage yields either an explicit R173-admissible two-hole mate clause anchored on J or an accepted explicit historical contact/pair exit localized to the same fixed-turn continuation. Thus the R402 paid floor is not terminal, and the original blocked deleted vertex remains the chosen middle coordinate. Now suppose case (II), so G_a=G_c={e} for one common good end position. At that one end, direct attachment of both deleted vertices a and c to the same source rail is tight. If e is a head endpoint p with next rail vertex r, then (a,p,r) and (c,p,r) are tight. Apply R164 in head form with k=a,z=c to E=(p,r). Its strict-extension alternative (c,a,p,r) would prepend c,a to the entire source rail and, together with the untouched other rail, give a spanning two-cover of H. Hence in the nonclosing branch R164 forces (p,a,c). Swap the witness order k=c,z=a; the extension (a,c,p,r) would likewise close, so (p,c,a) is forced. Therefore both orientations (a,c) and (c,a) of the deleted physical dimer are head-signed with the same common witness p. Accepted R407 now gives a fixed-trimer historical signed-support/anchor or cross-generation pair interaction localized at p. If e is instead a tail endpoint q with predecessor r, the exact tail-dual R164 argument forces both (c,a,q) and (a,c,q), so the two orientations of {a,c} are tail-signed with common witness q and R407 applies at q. Thus case (II) yields at least one genuine endpoint-local interaction packet at the unique common good end e. No claim is made that the three bad ends also satisfy the R407 bidirectional same-witness hypothesis. Combining cases I and II consumes every nonclosing R402 branch.

# R449 — Four-Support Sign-Splice Checkerboard Descent

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Retain the accepted R440 four-support theorem. In the paired specialization, suppose the four supports are grouped as two retained historical balanced opposite-sign pairs Pi_1=(H_1,T_1) and Pi_2=(H_2,T_2), with all four supports nontrivial and pairwise vertex-disjoint. Then three classes of R440 outputs are recyclable. (A) If a cell (H_i,T_j) is GG and concatenates to one tight carrier A containing both complete signed supports, R174 refunds the two touched supports. If i=j, Pi_i drops by at least two; if i!=j, Pi_i strictly descends through H_i and Pi_j strictly descends through T_j, with the untouched partners unchanged. (B) If one row i has two GB cells, choose the off-diagonal cell (H_i,T_j), j!=i, and perform its literal GB transfer; T_j loses exactly its head vertex while H_j is untouched, so Pi_j strictly descends. Dually, a column with two BG cells has an off-diagonal BG transfer strictly descending the corresponding original pair through its head support. Thus the +2-extension/reverse-trimer row/column-overcrowding subtest need not be treated as an exit. (C) If a cell is BB, write H=(...c,d), T=(a,b,...). R3 gives the tight reverse four-path (b,a,d,c). Its two turns (b,a,d) and (a,d,c) make (b,a) a tail-signed dimer with witness d and (d,c) a head-signed dimer with witness a. These two reversed terminal dimers are disjoint, oppositely signed, and have total mass four, so R39 gives a direct ancestry-bearing balanced pair and hence either a spanning two-cover or a mass-two floor. In the beyond-order-ten smallest-counterexample setting, any such BB floor enters R249 and then R387, yielding a spanning two-cover, an R173-admissible mate clause, or an accepted historical contact/pair exit. Consequently, in the paired R441/R442 use case, GG fusion, row/column overcrowding, and BB are all downstream-consumable. The only R440 residues not reduced by this theorem are the R436 witness/contact growth-cycle-reversal branch and the finite quiet checkerboard boundary; in the R442 dimer-sided specialization the quiet boundary is already consumed by R445.

## Hypotheses
The base R440 hypotheses hold. For the paired consumer statement, Pi_1=(H_1,T_1) and Pi_2=(H_2,T_2) are retained historical balanced opposite-sign pair births, with all four supports nontrivial and pairwise vertex-disjoint. Use the literal GB/BG semantics of P454, R174 for GG fusion, R3/R39 for BB. The final R249/R387 BB-floor consumer is the beyond-order-ten smallest-counterexample specialization.

## Scope
Strong Level-(1), arbitrary order for the splice/refund/direct-pair conclusions. The original pure four-support checkerboard theorem remains valid. The mate-or-exit consumption of a BB-generated floor is an O4/beyond-order-ten specialization.

## Applicability
Use inside R441/R442 after overlaps are removed. GG and row/column overcrowding pay original pair mass. BB creates a fresh direct mass-four pair from the two reversed unsigned-end dimers; in O4 send its floor through R249/R387. After this refinement, the disjoint R442 branch need only worry about R436 witness/contact-cycle geometry, since R445 separately consumes the quiet dimer boundary.

## Persistence
GG retains the fused carrier, R174 refund interval, signed descendants, and original pair identities. Overcrowding retains the chosen off-diagonal transfer and shortened original-pair support. BB retains the exact reverse P4, its two reversed signed terminal dimers with cross-witnesses a,d, the direct R39 pair ancestry, and any descendant floor/fixed-turn mate-or-exit certificate. Later lineages need not coexist with the source splice representative.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not consume the R436 witness/contact growth/cycle/reversal branch. Does not claim a proper tight cycle is contradictory. Does not make pair mass globally monotone across unrelated remints. Does not require using the +2/reverse row-sparsity test once an off-diagonal paying transfer is selected. The R249/R387 conclusion is only asserted in its smallest-counterexample beyond-order-ten scope.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** R449 is a nonreconstructible checkerboard payment-descent route with no live consumers; preserve historically.
- **Curation note:** Substantial four-support checkerboard engine with literal sign-splice transfers, paired mass descent, direct-pair birth, and contact branches.
- **Review status:** accepted

## Proof
Let Pi_1=(H_1,T_1) and Pi_2=(H_2,T_2) be the two retained historical balanced opposite-sign pairs, with all four supports nontrivial and pairwise disjoint, and use exactly the cell notation of the accepted R440 proof P454. For a cell H=(...c,d), T=(a,b,...), the tested seam turns are cda and dab.

(A) GG fusion. If both seams are tight, the literal concatenation A=(H,T) is one tight carrier containing the complete supports H_i and T_j. Apply R174 to those two disjoint nontrivial signed supports inside A. It deletes one support vertex from each while leaving nonempty signed descendants. If i=j, the historical pair Pi_i loses at least two total support vertices. If i!=j, Pi_i strictly descends through H_i while its partner T_i is untouched, and Pi_j strictly descends through T_j while H_j is untouched. Thus a GG cell is certified historical pair descent, not a terminal fusion output.

(B) Row/column overcrowding. Suppose row i contains GB in both columns. Choose the off-diagonal cell (H_i,T_j) with j!=i and perform only its literal GB transfer from P454: the head vertex a of T_j is moved to the tail of H_i. Signed-Interval Rebirth in the accepted cell analysis says T_j loses exactly that unsigned head vertex and retains a nonempty signed descendant, while H_j is untouched. Hence the original pair Pi_j strictly descends. No final +2/reverse-trimer row test is needed. Dually, if one column j contains BG in both rows, choose the off-diagonal cell (H_i,T_j), i!=j; its literal BG transfer deletes the unsigned terminal vertex d from H_i while T_i is untouched, so Pi_i strictly descends. Therefore row/column overcrowding is also certified historical pair descent.

(C) BB cell. If both cell seams are bad, R3 gives the reverse turns bad? No: precisely (b,a,d) and (a,d,c) are tight, hence A=(b,a,d,c) is a tight reverse P4 as in P454. Read its first turn as saying the reversed terminal dimer D_T=(b,a) is tail-signed by d, and its second turn as saying the reversed terminal dimer D_H=(d,c) is head-signed by a. The dimers are vertex-disjoint because H and T were disjoint; their signs have opposite polarities; and their total support mass is four. Therefore R39 forms a direct ancestry-bearing balanced pair (D_H,D_T) and gives either a spanning two-cover or a mass-two ancestry-bearing floor. In the beyond-order-ten smallest-counterexample regime, a nonclosing BB floor enters the adaptive floor-aligned fixed-turn front door R249; R387 then yields a spanning two-cover, an explicit R173-admissible mate clause, or an accepted historical contact/pair exit. Thus BB is also downstream-consumable rather than a terminal bounded object.

After removing (A)-(C), the only outputs of the R440 proof not compiled here are the R436 witness/contact branch (strict growth, proper tight cycle, or reverse-contact/reversal geometry) and the finite quiet checkerboard descent to its small boundary. In the R442 predecessor-dimer specialization, R445 already consumes the quiet boundary after at most one quiet matching. This proves the stated paired-specialization compiler.

# R453 — Three-cover six-splice mate-clause fan

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Let H be a Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament with pc(H)>2, and let H=A sqcup B sqcup C be a literal spanning three-cover in which A,B,C are nontrivial tight paths. For every ordered pair of distinct components, say A=(a_0,...,a_p) and B=(b_0,...,b_q) with p,q>=1, the literal spanning two-path proposal (a_0,...,a_p,b_0,...,b_q) sqcup C has complete hole set exactly h_1=(a_{p-1},a_p,b_0) and h_2=(a_p,b_0,b_1). Since H has no spanning two-cover, at least one hole is bad, so boundary antisymmetry yields the physically certified mate clause bar(h_1) OR bar(h_2), i.e. (b_0,a_p,a_{p-1}) tight OR (b_1,b_0,a_p) tight. Repeating over the six ordered pairs of components gives six explicit R173-admissible two-hole mate clauses attached to the same literal three-cover. In particular, if H is a smallest Strong counterexample and J is any proper tight trimer, an R18 currentization H=J sqcup U sqcup V has |U|,|V|>=2 by R168 and therefore carries the full six-splice clause fan.

## Hypotheses
Strong Level-(1); pc(H)>2; H=A sqcup B sqcup C is a literal spanning three-cover; all three components are nontrivial. For the trimer-currentization specialization, H is a smallest counterexample, J is proper, and R18/R168 are available.

## Scope
Order-free physical clause compiler. The generic six-splice statement uses only a literal nontrivial three-cover, pc(H)>2, and boundary antisymmetry. The R18/R168 specialization applies to every proper tight trimer in a smallest counterexample.

## Applicability
Use when R173-compatible physical clauses are required. It shows that clause existence is abundant at any nontrivial three-cover; downstream progress must therefore come from complement/mate linkage among clauses or from retained structural roles, not from producing one isolated clause.

## Persistence
Each clause retains its exact ordered component pair, literal spanning two-path proposal, and complete two-hole list. The six proposals are alternative proof certificates built from the same three graph-intrinsic component paths; they are not asserted simultaneously current after later representative changes.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert the six clauses contain a Physical Mate-Cycle, that any two clauses have complementary holes, or that a single clause closes H. Does not license reversal of an entire component path. Does not preserve unrelated ancestry under an R18 currentization.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Correct six-splice clause compiler, but each clause is the immediate two-seam consequence of concatenating two nontrivial components of a three-cover. Keep in proof history; isolated clause production is ubiquitous and not discovery-level.
- **Curation note:** Correct six-splice clause compiler, but each clause is the immediate two-seam consequence of concatenating two nontrivial components of a three-cover. Keep in proof history; isolated clause production is ubiquitous and not discovery-level.
- **Review status:** accepted

## Proof
Fix an ordered pair A,B and leave C untouched. Write A=(a_0,...,a_p) and B=(b_0,...,b_q), with p,q>=1. In the concatenated path A*B=(a_0,...,a_p,b_0,...,b_q), every consecutive triple lying wholly inside A or wholly inside B is tight by hypothesis. The only new consecutive triples are h_1=(a_{p-1},a_p,b_0) and h_2=(a_p,b_0,b_1). Thus (A*B) sqcup C is a literal spanning two-path proposal whose complete hole set is exactly {h_1,h_2}. If both holes were tight, it would be a spanning two-cover of H, contradicting pc(H)>2. Hence at least one h_i is bad. Boundary antisymmetry R3 says exactly the complete reversal of each bad ordered triple is tight, so bar(h_1)=(b_0,a_p,a_{p-1}) or bar(h_2)=(b_1,b_0,a_p) is tight. This is precisely a physically certified two-hole mate clause of the kind admissible to R173. There are six ordered pairs among A,B,C, and the same argument applies to each. For the proper-trimer specialization, R18 supplies H=J sqcup U sqcup V and R168 gives |U|,|V|>=2; J has order three, so all three components are nontrivial and the generic clause fan applies.

# R454 — Universal-middle mate-or-floor ubiquity fence

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Let H be a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample beyond order ten. Isolated R173-admissible mate-clause production is ubiquitous: for every proper tight trimer J, any R18 currentization H=J sqcup U sqcup V has three nontrivial components by R168, so R453 supplies six literal two-hole mate clauses before any return, payment, capture, or interaction argument. In particular, for every physical vertex x one may choose distinct a,c and orient the unique x-middle proper tight trimer J on {a,x,c}; that J already carries six physically certified mate clauses. Independently, accepted R450 gives the familiar mate-or-middle-floor continuation from J. Therefore neither the existence of a lone R173-admissible clause nor the bare existence of a mate-or-middle-floor packet with named middle x constitutes role-sensitive progress. A downstream argument must consume additional relational data: for example complementary-hole linkage among two or more literal proposals sufficient for R173, or retained ancestry/provenance tying J, x, a floor coordinate, or a clause hole to a prior capture/payment/currentness/extremal role.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample beyond order ten; accepted R3,R18,R168,R450 and provisional R453.

## Scope
Adversarial role-consumption fence. It strengthens the accepted R451 fence by showing that even an isolated physically certified R173-admissible clause, not merely the disjunctive mate-or-middle-floor packet, is universally cheap.

## Applicability
Use when evaluating proposed progress based on mate-clause generation or named-middle floor generation. Demand actual complementary-hole linkage, a forced mate cycle, a decreasing coordinate, or genuine consumption of retained structural ancestry.

## Persistence
Each ubiquitous clause retains its own literal three-cover currentization, ordered splice proposal, and exact hole pair. The fence does not erase useful provenance when a later theorem genuinely relates clauses or consumes a prior role.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not say R173 mate cycles are ubiquitous. Does not say the six splice clauses from one three-cover are complementary or mutually resolving. Does not demote role-linked clauses whose physical hole structure is consumed downstream. Does not assert every trimer produces a middle-containing floor, only that isolated mate clauses are already universal and R450 supplies its separate mate-or-floor packet.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Historical universal-middle mate/floor ubiquity fence; payment/mate production is no longer a frontier.
- **Curation note:** Role-consumption fence: mate-or-middle-floor packets are available through arbitrary physical middles, so bare existence is not progress.
- **Review status:** accepted

## Proof
Fix any proper tight trimer J. R18 supplies a literal minimum three-cover H=J sqcup U sqcup V. Since J has three vertices and H is a smallest counterexample, R168 applied to deletion V(J) gives |U|,|V|>=2. Thus the hypotheses of R453 hold, and its six ordered component splices give six literal spanning two-path proposals, each with exactly two holes and hence an R173-admissible mate clause. No historical role of J was used beyond being a proper currentizable tight path. Now fix an arbitrary physical vertex x. Choose distinct a,c; R3 orients one of (a,x,c),(c,x,a) as a proper tight trimer, so the preceding conclusion applies. Accepted R450 separately gives the mate-or-middle-floor front door from the same arbitrary J. Therefore bare production of either one isolated clause or the disjunctive mate-or-middle-floor packet cannot distinguish a role-bearing middle from an arbitrary physical vertex. Only relations among the literal clauses or retained ancestry consumed by a later theorem can do so.

# R456 — Universal fixed-turn mate-or-exit reduction

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Let H be a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample beyond order ten. Fix any proper tight turn J=(a,x,c) together with a lawful pair-bearing fixed-turn lineage in the scope of R172. Then, unless a spanning two-cover or an earlier accepted fixed-turn contact exit occurs, there is a chosen continuation to one of two explicit physical currencies: (1) an R173-admissible two-hole mate clause; or (2) a same-polarity two-witness R38 collision on a named reverse terminal dimer of one residual rail in an R359 all-internal currentization of J, with one witness the retained source middle x and the other a named endpoint of the opposite residual rail. Indeed, steer the lineage to the target floor {a,c} as before and apply R359. Endpoint return gives (1) by R358. In the all-internal branch, apply R455: the literal U-to-V or V-to-U residual-rail splice proposal forces the concrete partner-only terminal collision (2). Thus the all-internal residual no longer needs the replay-prone R160 fixed-trimer remint as its generic exit. The fixed turn J, middle x, source currentization, collided terminal dimer, second witness, and literal splice proposal remain attached to outcome (2).

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample beyond order ten; J is a proper tight turn with a lawful pair-bearing R172 lineage; accepted R358,R359 and provisional R455.

## Scope
Order-free strengthening of the fixed-turn reduction. It replaces the generic all-internal historical pair/contact exit by a concrete residual-terminal same-support collision that consumes partner-rail geometry and avoids the source-trimer replay caveat of R448. Earlier unrelated fixed-turn contact exits remain accepted outputs.

## Applicability
Use after any mechanism produces a pair-bearing fixed-turn lineage. The preferred all-internal output is now the R455 residual-terminal R38 collision, because its support and two witnesses are explicit and role-linked; use older R387/R389 routes only when their source-terminal payment ancestry is specifically needed.

## Persistence
The fixed turn J and lineage persist to target-floor entry. Endpoint-return mate clauses retain their literal proposal. In the all-internal branch the chosen R359 currentization J,U,V, source middle x, ordered residual-rail splice proposal, exact seam holes, collided reverse terminal dimer, and opposite-rail endpoint witness are retained as historical graph-intrinsic certificate data.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert a single mate clause or a single R38 collision closes H. Does not claim the two currencies are mutually exclusive across alternative continuations. Does not infer a mate cycle from isolated clauses. Does not erase richer R389 four-birth/payment ancestry when separately useful.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** R456 is a nonreconstructible fixed-turn routing wrapper with no live consumers; later physical exact-cover consumers are preferred.
- **Curation note:** Fixed-turn mate-or-exit is a reusable compiler, not current spine.
- **Review status:** accepted

## Proof
Follow the accepted R387 fixed-turn lineage until either closure/an earlier explicit contact exit occurs or the target-aligned floor {a,c} is reached. Apply R359 to the retained turn J=(a,x,c). If some exact H-{a,c} return exposes x as a rail endpoint, R358 gives the literal two-hole mate clause, proving outcome (1). Otherwise R359 is in its all-internal regime and provides a currentization H=J sqcup U sqcup V with the four x-signed reverse terminal dimers. Apply R455 to that currentization. Its literal residual-rail splice proposal U*V with J untouched, or symmetrically V*U, has exactly two seam holes; reversing whichever hole is bad gives a second same-polarity witness on a reverse terminal dimer already signed by x. R38 therefore yields outcome (2), with all support/witness/proposal data explicit. This exhausts the R359 return dichotomy.

# R462 — Deleted-neighbor restoration is fresh-witness-blind

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Let E=(e_0,...,e_m), m>=1, be a graph-intrinsic tight path and let k,z be distinct vertices outside E. In the head orientation, once (k,E) is tight, Boundary Antisymmetry R3 already forces the R164 restoration/contact dichotomy for z without using the additional hypothesis that (z,E) is tight: either (z,k,E) is tight or (e_0,k,z) is tight. Dually, once (E,k) is tight, R3 already forces either (E,k,z) tight or (z,k,e_m) tight, without using that (E,z) is tight. Thus the fresh-replacement extension in the hypotheses of R164 is logically unused by the forcing step of its dichotomy; it supplies provenance/interpretation, not extra combinatorial pressure. Consequently, applying R164 by itself to an R455 same-polarity residual-terminal collision does not consume the second R455 signed certificate: fixing the x-signed extension as the old extension, the same restoration/contact alternative is available for any distinct opposite-rail vertex z outside the retained terminal dimer, even if z did not provide the second sign. Therefore R164 alone cannot convert the two-witnessness of an R455 collision into additional physical linkage or closure. Any productive continuation must use both signed extension facts through some further consumer, or add independent ancestry/structural input.

## Hypotheses
Strong Level-(1) boundary antisymmetry R3. For the generic head/tail statement, E is a nontrivial graph-intrinsic tight path and k,z are distinct vertices outside E. The R455 consequence is in the all-internal R359 state certified by R455.

## Scope
Order-free negative/consumer-discipline lemma. It identifies the exact logical strength of the R164 routing step and fences a tempting but role-blind use of R455. It does not invalidate R164 as a role-preserving compiler.

## Applicability
Use whenever a same-support two-witness collision is proposed to be spent solely by R164. Before claiming progress, require a downstream step that genuinely consumes both signed extensions or additional retained ancestry.

## Persistence
The logical non-consumption statement is graph-independent. In the R455 specialization, the physical terminal dimer and both named witnesses remain valid historical certificates; the result only states that R164's own dichotomy does not logically use the second certificate.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not say R164 is useless: its restored extension/contact packaging may be valuable when a later theorem consumes the preserved old-neighbor role. Does not rule out closing an R455 collision by another theorem, by combining both witness facts elsewhere, or by adding a genuinely complementary proposal. Does not weaken R455 itself.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Historical deleted-neighbor fresh-witness blindness lemma; no live use remains.
- **Curation note:** R462 is a durable consumer-discipline fence: R164 restoration/contact does not logically use the fresh replacement extension, so an R455 two-witness collision spent solely through R164 has not actually consumed its second witness. Retain to prevent role-blind overcrediting of two-witnessness.
- **Review status:** accepted

## Proof
Head form. Assume only that (k,E) is tight, with E=(e_0,...,e_m), m>=1, and that z is distinct from k and outside E. Test the ordered triple (z,k,e_0). If it is tight, then (z,k,e_0,e_1,...,e_m) is a tight path: its first turn is the tested turn, while every remaining turn is already part of the tight path (k,E). Hence (z,k,E) is tight. If (z,k,e_0) is bad, Boundary Antisymmetry R3 makes its complete reversal (e_0,k,z) tight. This is exactly the head conclusion of R164. At no point was (z,E) used.

Tail form. Assume only that (E,k) is tight. Test (e_m,k,z). If it is tight, then (e_0,...,e_m,k,z) is tight because all earlier turns are already contained in (E,k). If it is bad, R3 makes the complete reversal (z,k,e_m) tight. This is exactly the tail conclusion of R164, again without using (E,z).

Therefore the extra fresh-extension hypothesis in R164 does not strengthen the logical disjunction it concludes. It records that z is itself a certified endpoint witness, which can matter to later ancestry-sensitive consumers, but R164's own forcing step is fresh-witness-blind.

Now specialize to either same-polarity residual-terminal collision supplied by R455. For example, in a head-signed collision let E be the reverse terminal dimer and let k=x be the retained R359 middle witness. R455 also supplies a second witness w from the opposite residual rail, so (w,E) is tight; however the generic argument above shows that the R164 restoration/contact alternative with z=w already follows from R3 and (x,E) alone. The same conclusion would hold for any distinct z outside E, whether or not z signed E. The tail-signed case is identical by the dual argument. Thus an R455-to-R164 step by itself does not consume the second R455 certificate and cannot be credited as additional linkage produced by two-witnessness. A genuine consumer must use both signed facts elsewhere or introduce additional structure.

# R465 — Exact-support cross-generation overlap is fresh-certificate-blind

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Assume the fixed-trimer remint configuration of R458: J=(a,x,c) is a proper tight trimer, D is a signed dimer disjoint from J carrying one signed certificate with witness x, and M is the unique terminal signed dimer of J of polarity opposite to D. Let y be any distinct witness for a second certificate of the same polarity on the same oriented support D for which the corresponding signed turn is tight. Then:

(1) The R458 remint conclusion is invariant under replacing the original opposite-rail witness w by y. Pairing M with the x-signed copy of D and with the y-signed copy of D gives two direct balanced-pair births by R39, and R160 forces the same nonquiet fixed-trimer historical interaction. This proof uses only the fixed trimer J, the physical support D, the common polarity, and witness distinctness; it does not use that y is an endpoint of the opposite residual rail or that y arose from a literal splice proposal.

(2) If these two births are then spent only through the exact-support overlap branch of R441/R436, the discharge can be made without using the y-certificate at all: on either repeated nontrivial support M or D, R436 may return the old signed extension from the first birth exactly as in the exact-replay case. Hence the composite R458 -> R441/R436 route remains valid after arbitrary replacement of the second witness by any y satisfying the same-polarity certificate condition, and it cannot by itself force any output whose novelty depends on the opposite-rail role or splice provenance of the original w. In particular it cannot by itself force a new literal sibling proposal or the simultaneous two-endpoint adjacency cuts required by R461.

Thus the current remint-plus-overlap chain is a genuine interaction certificate but is not yet a consumer of the cross-partition geometry carried specifically by the R455 opposite-rail witness.

## Hypotheses
Strong Level-(1). Accepted R39, R160, R436, R441, R458, and R461. In the abstract replacement statement, J is a proper tight trimer, D is physically disjoint from J, D has two same-polarity signed certificates with distinct witnesses x and y, and M is the opposite-polarity terminal signed dimer of J. For the R458 specialization, x is the source middle and the original second witness w comes from the R455 residual-rail splice.

## Scope
Order-free role-consumption fence for the fixed-trimer remint architecture and its exact-support R441/R436 spend. It strengthens the exact-replay fresh-certificate-blindness observation by showing that the preceding R458 remint itself is insensitive to the geometric role of the second witness.

## Applicability
Use whenever an R455/R458 collision is claimed to create cross-partition or sibling-proposal progress. Credit the opposite-rail/splice coordinate as consumed only after a later theorem uses that coordinate essentially, for example by constructing a path surgery whose validity changes under witness replacement.

## Persistence
The role-blindness is logical and survives later currentization. J, x, D, the second witness, M, and any original splice proposal may remain as historical coordinates, but this theorem records that the R39/R160 remint and exact-replay R441/R436 discharge do not use the second witness's residual-rail or splice role.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not invalidate R455 or R458, and does not say the named opposite-rail witness is useless. A different consumer may use its physical location or splice provenance essentially. Does not rule out non-exact-support R441 contact, a certificate-sensitive interaction theorem, or a genuine two-endpoint path surgery. Does not assert that every arbitrary vertex supplies the required same-polarity signed certificate on D.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Historical cross-generation certificate-blindness lemma; no live use remains.
- **Curation note:** Durable fresh-certificate/role-consumption barrier for exact-support remint-plus-overlap arguments.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Mathematically accepted; normalized literal escaped newline markers only.

## Proof
Let the first certificate on D have witness x and the second have witness y distinct from x, with the same tested orientation and polarity. Since D is disjoint from J, and M is the terminal signed dimer of J of opposite polarity, R39 applies to M together with either signed copy of D. Thus B_x=(M,D_x) and B_y=(M,D_y) are direct balanced-pair births. The hypotheses of R160 depend on the same fixed trimer J, one of its terminal signed dimers M, and a partner signed dimer D physically disjoint from J. They do not require the partner witness to lie on a designated residual rail or to come from a splice proposal. Therefore, reading B_x first and B_y second, R160 forces the same nonquiet historical signed-support/anchor or cross-generation pair interaction for every such y. This proves (1).

For (2), both births have exactly the same two nontrivial physical supports M and D. Hence any R441 comparison has cross-generation overlap. Choose either repeated oriented support P in {M,D} and view the later copy as Q=P. Apply R436 to the old signed certificate (z;P) from the first birth and Q=P. Because P is nontrivial, the singleton replay exception is irrelevant. In the at-anchor branch, the already-tight first old signed turn makes R436 return the already-known strict extension (z,P) of Q. This discharge uses only first-birth data and the equality Q=P; the second witness y and its certificate are not referenced. Thus the R441/R436 overlap route can be completed without consuming y.

Consequently the composite remint-plus-overlap argument is invariant under replacing the original R458 witness w by any y that supplies the same-polarity second certificate on D. Any conclusion whose novelty specifically requires w to be an opposite-rail endpoint, or to carry the literal R455 splice provenance, cannot follow from this chain alone. By R461, an exact complementary sibling of a native splice literal must abandon both incident source endpoint adjacencies. Nothing in the witness-substitution-invariant chain constructs such a proposal or uses both endpoint adjacencies, so that two-cut geometry requires an additional consumer.

# R469 — Native mate-sibling two-endpoint-cut barrier

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Retain R467 and R468, and expand every displayed literal three-cover by the complete physical R453 six-splice fan.

(1) Native blocked-cap fans have the wrong implication orientation. In the Unique-A blocked branch, for X={v_1,u_r,t}, every exact cover H-X=R sqcup S with R=(r_0,r_1,...) and r_0 != w has shield S_A(R)=(r_1,r_0,t) and complement bar(S_A(R))=(t,r_0,r_1). No mate literal in the complete six-splice fan of any triple-deletion cover A sqcup R' sqcup S' equals bar(S_A(R)): t is terminal in A=(v_1,u_r,t), while t is absent from R',S', and an R453 mate literal uses a right-component first/second vertex in its first coordinate. The original and shifted R467 source fans also cannot supply bar(S_A(R)); the only short-rail case in which a source-fan literal begins with t has second coordinate w, excluded by r_0 != w. Thus every S_A(R) has outdegree zero in the physical implication graph generated by the native triple-deletion fans and the source/shifted fans. Dually, in the Unique-B branch no native fan contains bar(S_B(R))=(r_1,r_0,t), so every S_B(R) is a sink in that graph. The R468 packet decorates C_A(r_0) or C_B(r_0), not the shield, so it supplies no productive length-zero shield path either.

(2) Exact replay has one sharp cross-fiber bridge, but it is not forced. In Unique-A, suppose a pair-deletion replay cover is
H-D=(t,w,p_2,...,p_m) sqcup (q_0,...,q_n),
and retain the dimer E=(v_1,u_r). The ordered Q-to-P splice in the complete R453 fan of E sqcup P sqcup Q is the physically certified clause
(t,q_n,q_{n-1}) OR (w,t,q_n).
If some exact triple-deletion cover has a rail beginning (q_n,q_{n-1},...), then its blocked shield is (q_{n-1},q_n,t), and this clause gives a length-one R463 path from that shield to (w,t,q_n). The sink is collision-decorated by O_A=(w,t,u_r), since q_n != u_r. Conversely, within this replay fan an outgoing blocked-head shield edge can occur only through exactly such a reversed terminal-dimer alignment; the other first-t replay literal has second vertex u_r, which is deleted from the triple-deletion residue. Dually, in Unique-B, from a replay cover
H-D=(p_0,...,p_{m-2},w,t) sqcup (q_0,...,q_n)
the P-to-Q splice clause is
(q_0,t,w) OR (q_1,q_0,t).
If a triple-deletion rail ends (...,q_1,q_0), its shield (t,q_0,q_1) has a length-one path to (q_0,t,w), collision-decorated by O_B=(v_1,t,w); and this reversed initial-dimer alignment is the only such exit inside that replay fan. By R168 each Q has at least three vertices, so the required reversed endpoint rail is not Q itself: R3 makes the reversed terminal/initial turn of Q bad. It is genuinely a second cross-fiber exact-cover alignment.

(3) The R467 double-winner P4 is terminal within the complete native source fan. When A and B are both tight, neither bar(A) nor bar(B) is a mate literal of any of the six native source splices, by direct component-membership and endpoint-order inspection. Hence A and B have no positive-length outgoing path in that fan. Both are already collision-decorated by the two R467 source shields, so the length-zero case of R463 returns exactly the two R467 terminal collisions and no new turn, proposal, ancestry, or downstream consumer. The tight P4 alone does not compile another physical clause.

Consequently R468 does not force any shield-to-decorated-sink path. A successful consumer must add a genuinely new physical proposal containing the exact complement of a shield, with the replay cross-fiber reversed-endpoint alignment above as the shortest presently certified route. The double-winner P4 likewise remains a terminal local packet until an external consumer uses more than its two already-decorated terminal dimers.

## Hypotheses
H is in the R467 all-internal source-trimer state; the indicated unique-winner or double-winner branch is fixed. Accepted R3, R38, R168, R453, R463, R467, and R468 are available. Every implication edge is retained with its literal spanning path-cover proposal and exact two-hole certificate.

## Scope
Order-free physical implication-orientation strengthening of the C383/R468 barrier. It analyzes the complete R453 fans of the exact source, shifted, triple-deletion, and replay covers named by R467/R468; it does not range over unconstructed external proposals.

## Applicability
Use after entering an R468 universal blocked-cap branch. Do not search the native triple-deletion six-fans for a shield exit. Instead search a replay pair-deletion cover and test whether the other rail's terminal dimer (Unique-A) or initial dimer (Unique-B) is exposed in reverse at the appropriate endpoint of a triple-deletion rail. In the R467 double-winner branch, demand a consumer of the P4 rather than re-reading its two terminal collisions.

## Persistence
Every sink/outdegree assertion retains the exact displayed component orders and the complete R453 fan formulas. A realized replay bridge retains both deletion fibers, the replay cover, the reversed endpoint alignment, the shield, the ordered splice proposal, its complete two-hole list, the old source turn, and the decorated sink. Different exact covers are alternative representatives.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert that a replay exposure cover exists, that the cross-fiber reversed-endpoint alignment exists, or that any resulting R38 collision closes H. Does not rule out an outgoing shield path created by a genuinely new physical proposal outside the R467/R468 packet or by extra accidental collision decoration. Does not claim the double-winner P4 remains terminal after a new currentization or other external construction. Does not construct a finite global smallest counterexample.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Historical native mate-sibling endpoint-cut barrier; no live use remains.
- **Curation note:** Exact native-sibling barrier separating source-neighbor replay from nonreplay endpoint exposure and reducing failure to a universal physical blocked-cap family.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** PASS: complete R453 fan orientation/enumeration checked. Native shield complements are absent; replay exit is uniquely the stated reversed endpoint-dimer alignment; double-winner A/B complements are absent from all six native splices, including short-rail edge cases.

## Proof
For an ordered splice from X=(x_0,...,x_p) to Y=(y_0,...,y_q), R453 gives mate literals M_1=(y_0,x_p,x_{p-1}) and M_2=(y_1,y_0,x_p).

Unique-A native fans. Here A=(v_1,u_r,t), and every rail of H-X omits t. Therefore, in any fan on A,R',S', M_1 cannot begin with t because no component begins with t, and M_2 cannot begin with t because no component has t as its second vertex: A has second vertex u_r and the residue rails omit t. Hence no such fan contains bar(S_A(R))=(t,r_0,r_1). In the original source fan t=u_{r-1}. A mate literal can begin with t only if t=u_2, hence r=3, and then its second coordinate is u_1=w. The same calculation applies to the shifted source fan with U^-=(u_1,...,t). Since blocked shields require r_0 != w, neither fan contains bar(S_A(R)). By the definition of G_F in R463, an arc leaves a literal L only when some clause contains bar(L). Thus every S_A(R) is a sink in the union of these physical fans. The Unique-B proof reverses the coordinate order: bar(S_B(R)) ends in t; a triple-deletion fan cannot end in t, and the sole short source/shifted possibility has penultimate coordinate w, excluded by r_0 != w.

Replay bridge, Unique-A. Let E=(v_1,u_r), P=(t,w,p_2,...,p_m), and Q=(q_0,...,q_n). R168 gives n>=2. The Q-to-P splice proposal has complete holes (q_{n-1},q_n,t) and (q_n,t,w), hence its mate clause is
L_1=(t,q_n,q_{n-1}) OR L_2=(w,t,q_n).
If a triple-deletion rail begins (q_n,q_{n-1},...), its R468 shield is S=(q_{n-1},q_n,t)=bar(L_1). The labeled arc S->L_2 is therefore physical. Since q_n lies in H-D while u_r lies in D, q_n != u_r; L_2 and O_A=(w,t,u_r) have the same tested polarity on oriented support (w,t) and distinct witnesses, so L_2 is collision-decorated. Conversely the only mate literals beginning t in the replay fan arise when P is the right component. Splicing E-to-P gives (t,u_r,v_1), which cannot equal (t,r_0,r_1) because r_0 is in H-X and u_r is deleted. Splicing Q-to-P gives L_1, so equality is exactly r_0=q_n,r_1=q_{n-1}. Finally Q itself cannot be reversed into the required rail: because n>=2, its last tight turn reverses to a bad first turn by R3.

Replay bridge, Unique-B. Write P=(p_0,...,p_{m-2},w,t) and Q=(q_0,...,q_n). The P-to-Q splice has holes (w,t,q_0) and (t,q_0,q_1), hence mate clause L_1=(q_0,t,w) OR L_2=(q_1,q_0,t). A triple-deletion rail ending (...,q_1,q_0) has shield S=(t,q_0,q_1)=bar(L_2), giving the physical arc S->L_1. Because q_0 != v_1, L_1 is collision-decorated by O_B=(v_1,t,w). Enumerating the replay fan literals ending in t gives the stated converse, and R3 plus n>=2 excludes obtaining the alignment by simply reversing Q.

Double winner. The native U-to-V clause has tight literals A=(v_1,u_r,u_{r-1}) and B=(v_2,v_1,u_r). Inspecting all six ordered source-component pairs shows no mate literal equals bar(A)=(u_{r-1},u_r,v_1) or bar(B)=(u_r,v_1,v_2): the reverse ordered pair uses the initial endpoint(s) of U and terminal endpoint(s) of V, while every pair involving J contains a J vertex. Hence no native-fan arc leaves A or B. R467 already decorates A by (x,u_r,u_{r-1}) and B by (v_2,v_1,x). R463 with length-zero paths therefore reproduces exactly those two R38 collisions. Nothing in R453 or R463 compiles the concatenated tight P4 into an additional clause. This proves all parts.

# R482 — Universal O4 interaction-or-triple-return-multiplicity reduction

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Retain R474 and R481. Its synchronized multi-internal branch I2+ also always yields explicit R435 order-change geometry. First suppose exactly two middle labels m,n are all-internal and the third label p is endpoint-return on the common literal H-T cover U sqcup V. At the literal rail end capped by p, choose one internal middle m. In the head case U=(r,s,...), the cap (p,r,s) is tight and the m-shield (s,r,m) is tight. Put C_m=(s,r,m). By R515 the good cap p has polarity opposite to the natural C_m sign on the same terminal physical dimer {r,s}; therefore R518 yields a tight P4 K on C_m plus p. Quiet R435 comparison of K with U would require r before s, while quiet comparison with C_m would require s before r, impossible. Hence an exact reversed state, tight reverse trimer, or proper tight cycle occurs. The tail case is dual. Now suppose all three middle labels a,b,c are all-internal. Choose any residual rail end, say a head U=(r,s,...), and let C_a=(s,r,a) be the a-shield trimer there. The b- and c-shields (s,r,b),(s,r,c) are same-polarity terminal signs on the same physical support. Apply R518 to C_a with b and with c. If either four-set has a P4, compare that P4 with U and C_a; the opposite r,s orders force R435. If neither four-set has a P4, R522 gives a P5 on {s,r,a,b,c}, and the same two comparisons again cannot both remain order-preserving because U has r before s while C_a has s before r. Thus R435 fires. The tail-end proof is identical after reversal. Consequently every synchronized I2+ frame is physically consumed into an explicit old-state reversal, reverse trimer, or proper tight cycle; the four-terminal collision web of R474 is not terminal.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample beyond order ten; synchronized I2+ frame of R474; accepted R435,R515,R518,R522; retain R481 as the companion I1 conclusion.

## Scope
Order-free complete elimination of the synchronized multi-internal branch by good-cap/blocked-shield or multi-shield order conflict.

## Applicability
Use after three-middle synchronization. Neither the exactly-two-internal collision web nor the all-three-internal multi-witness terminal web should be treated as a terminal output; both force explicit Reverse-Ear geometry.

## Persistence
Retain the common H-T rail, the chosen terminal dimer, the internal-middle shield trimer, the endpoint cap when present, the R518/R522 path certificate, and the exact R435 comparison/output.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not declare the resulting reverse trimer or proper cycle contradictory and does not by itself create a complementary R173/R463 proposal. The all-three-internal proof does not assert which R518 four-set first yields P4.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Stale endpoint-program O4 reduction with no current consumers; later O4 reductions now carry the live structural frontier.
- **Curation note:** Stale endpoint-program O4 reduction with no current consumers; later O4 reductions now carry the live structural frontier.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Multi-internal branch correctly reduces through R518/R522; dependency on retained R481 made explicit.

## Proof
Exactly-two-internal case. Let p be the endpoint-return label and m one internal label. At p's capped head end U=(r,s,...), (p,r,s) is tight and R359 for m gives (s,r,m) tight. Thus C_m=(s,r,m) is a tight trimer. Its natural terminal sign on {r,s} and the p-cap sign have opposite polarities by R515. R518 therefore gives a tight P4 K on {p,r,s,m}. If K has no R435 output against U, its r,s contacts occur r before s. If K has no R435 output against C_m, the same contacts occur s before r. Contradiction. Tail caps are dual. All-three-internal case. At a head end U=(r,s,...), choose one internal label a and C_a=(s,r,a). The other two internal labels b,c give the same tested shield turns (s,r,b),(s,r,c). Apply R518 to C_a with b. A P4 gives the same U-versus-C_a order contradiction. If no P4, repeat with c. Again a P4 pays. If neither yields P4, both fourth-vertex cells are in the R518 no-P4 branch, so R522 gives a tight P5 K on {s,r,a,b,c}. Quiet R435 comparison with U forces r before s, whereas quiet comparison with C_a forces s before r, contradiction. Thus some R435 output always occurs.

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Retain the hypotheses and notation of R485, including ancestral paths A=(a_0,a_1,...,a_p), B=(b_0,...,b_q), the anti-aligned spanning three-cover P sqcup A^+ sqcup B^- with P=(a_0,z_1,...,z_{m-1},b_q), and in particular its residual (P4) branch where (z_1,a_0,b_q,z_{m-1}) is tight. Put D={a_0,b_q}. Accepted R153 applied to this exact physical ancestral endpoint pair gives one exact two-cover H-D=U sqcup V such that both U sqcup V sqcup (a_0,b_q) and U sqcup V sqcup (b_q,a_0) are literal minimum three-cover representatives of H. Hence the R485(P4) bridge chord, although locally certified only in the a_0-to-b_q direction, always has a lawful cross-fiber physical proposal selecting the opposite orientation (b_q,a_0) over a fixed exact pair-deletion shadow. The identities a_0=head(A) and b_q=tail(B), and therefore the original two-cut ancestry, remain named historical coordinates in this comparison even though the new residual rails U,V need not equal or descend from A^+,B^- or the interior of P.

## Hypotheses
Accepted R485 hypotheses; H is a smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in the standing project sense; accepted R153. The displayed P4 branch is used only to identify the live wrong-direction bridge coordinate.

## Scope
Order-free cross-fiber orientation compiler for the exact ancestral bridge pair arising in R485. It does not recover the old fixed-fiber role-flip theorem and does not require the R153 shadow to coincide with the R485 residual pieces.

## Applicability
Use in the R485(P4) branch before searching for a new theorem that merely creates the reverse bridge orientation. The reverse orientation already exists as a selected dimer in a literal minimum three-cover. The remaining task is to consume/synchronize this R153 reverse-dimer shadow with the R485 bridge ancestry, for example by obtaining an exact-cover endpoint comparison to which R471 applies or by another physical clause compiler.

## Persistence
Retains the exact physical pair D={a_0,b_q}, the ancestral labels a_0=head(A), b_q=tail(B), the R485 bridge/P4 certificate, and one fixed exact H-D shadow U,V shared by both dimer orientations. The new U,V are representative-relative and carry no asserted ancestry to A,B,P.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert that U,V equal A^+,B^- or pieces of P; does not produce an exact two-cover containing (b_q,a_0); does not by itself trigger R471, R173, or R463; does not assert that selecting the reverse dimer closes H; does not preserve arbitrary R485 rail states inside U,V.

## Record notes

- **Lifecycle note:** R486 is a nonreconstructible bridge-route shadow theorem with no live consumers; preserve as historical route detail.
- **Curation note:** Cross-fiber reverse bridge-dimer shadow; preserves physical endpoint ancestry only.

## Proof
The pair a_0,b_q consists of distinct vertices because they are endpoints of the vertex-simple bridge P in R485. Therefore R153 applies to D={a_0,b_q}. It yields an exact two-cover H-D=U sqcup V and, over those same residual rails, minimum three-cover representatives U sqcup V sqcup (a_0,b_q) and U sqcup V sqcup (b_q,a_0). The latter literally selects the reverse bridge dimer (b_q,a_0). Nothing in this application changes the already certified graph identities a_0=head(A) and b_q=tail(B); those are historical coordinates attached to the same physical vertices. R153 explicitly does not preserve unrelated ancestry in U,V, so no such stronger claim is made. This proves exactly the stated cross-fiber reverse-dimer shadow and no synchronization beyond it.

# R489 — Bridge-neighbor correct-side exposure compiles to collision or exact endpoint-state reversal

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Retain the hypotheses and notation of R485 in its residual (P4) branch. Thus P=(a_0,z_1,...,z_{m-1},b_q) is a tight bridge with m>=3, C_L=(z_1,a_0,b_q) and C_R=(a_0,b_q,z_{m-1}) are tight, and D={a_0,b_q}. Put E=(a_0,b_q), let O_L=(a_0,z_1,z_2) be the original first bridge turn, and let O_R=(z_{m-2},z_{m-1},b_q) be the original last bridge turn. Let H-D=R sqcup S be any literal exact two-cover. (L) If one rail ends R=(...,y,z_1), then the literal three-cover R sqcup S sqcup E and its ordered R-to-E splice have the physical R453 mate clause (a_0,z_1,y) OR (b_q,a_0,z_1). Since C_L is tight, its exact reverse (b_q,a_0,z_1) is bad by R3, so (a_0,z_1,y) is forced tight. If y != z_2, this forced turn and O_L are same-polarity certificates on the identical oriented support (a_0,z_1) with distinct witnesses y,z_2, hence R38 gives a named source-adjacent collision. If y=z_2, the exact cover literally ends with the reversed old bridge state (z_2,z_1). (R) Dually, if one rail begins R=(z_{m-1},y,...), then the ordered E-to-R splice has mate clause (z_{m-1},b_q,a_0) OR (y,z_{m-1},b_q). Since C_R is tight, its reverse first literal is bad and (y,z_{m-1},b_q) is forced tight. If y != z_{m-2}, this and O_R give a named same-polarity source-adjacent collision on (z_{m-1},b_q); if y=z_{m-2}, the exact cover literally begins with the reversed old bridge state (z_{m-1},z_{m-2}). Consequently the cross-fiber target after R485 is only an endpoint-side bit: exposing z_1 at a rail tail or z_{m-1} at a rail head cannot terminate anonymously. It yields either a collision pinned to the original bridge boundary turn or the exact reversal of that old boundary state, with the pair-deletion cover and complete R453 clause retained.

## Hypotheses
All hypotheses of R485 including pc(H)>2 and m>=3; its P4 branch; H-D has the displayed exact two-cover; accepted R3,R38,R453.

## Scope
Order-free physical clause compiler specialized to the R485 bridge pair. It preserves the exact pair-deletion fiber, bridge-side endpoint, old bridge neighbor, and complete R453 splice certificate.

## Applicability
Use after R485/R486 when searching the exact H-{a_0,b_q} fiber. It is enough to steer z_1 to a rail tail or z_{m-1} to a rail head. A wrong predecessor/successor is productive by giving a source-adjacent collision; the only noncollision case is the exact reversed old endpoint state.

## Persistence
Retain D={a_0,b_q}; the original bridge P and old boundary turns O_L,O_R; the chosen exact H-D cover; the endpoint-side role of z_1 or z_{m-1}; the exact predecessor/successor; the literal three-cover E sqcup R sqcup S; and the complete ordered R453 splice clause. Collision or reversed-state outputs are graph-intrinsic once exhibited.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not force a correct-side endpoint exposure to exist. Does not say the resulting R38 collision or exact reversed state closes H. Does not preserve the rest of A or B inside the pair-deletion rails and does not by itself create an R173/R463 cycle.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** R489 is a nonreconstructible bridge-neighbor continuation with no live consumers; preserve historically.
- **Curation note:** Correct-side bridge-neighbor endpoint exposure compiler to collision or exact old-state reversal.
- **Review status:** accepted

## Proof
For (L), write R=(...,y,z_1). In the three-cover R sqcup S sqcup E with E=(a_0,b_q), the R453 formula for the ordered pair R-to-E gives the mate clause (a_0,z_1,y) OR (b_q,a_0,z_1). The second literal is the complete reversal of C_L=(z_1,a_0,b_q), hence bad by R3. Therefore (a_0,z_1,y) is tight. The old bridge supplies O_L=(a_0,z_1,z_2). If y is different from z_2, the two tight turns share the oriented dimer (a_0,z_1) in the same tail polarity and have distinct witnesses, so R38 gives the claimed collision. If y=z_2, the selected terminal state of R is z_2 z_1, the exact reversal of the old bridge state z_1 z_2. The right-hand statement is identical with R=(z_{m-1},y,...): the E-to-R splice gives (z_{m-1},b_q,a_0) OR (y,z_{m-1},b_q); the first is the reverse of C_R and therefore bad; the second is forced and compares with O_R=(z_{m-2},z_{m-1},b_q).
