# R490 — Endpoint-universal R485 bridge cell has no quiet side-locked residue

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Let H be a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample beyond order ten in the endpoint-universal branch of accepted R393. Retain the hypotheses and notation of R485 in its residual (P4) branch, with D={a_0,b_q}, bridge P=(a_0,z_1,...,z_{m-1},b_q), interior bridge P^o=(z_1,...,z_{m-1}), and source residual cover T=A^+ sqcup P^o sqcup B^- of W=H-D. Then at least one of the following occurs. (HT) One of the exact ancestral-neighbor bridge-chord collisions (H) or (T) of R485 occurs. (REV) Some exact two-cover of H-D contains the exact reversed old initial bridge state (z_2,z_1) or exact reversed old terminal bridge state (z_{m-1},z_{m-2}). (BP) H contains a graph-intrinsic balanced opposite-sign pair produced inside the same pair-deletion/bridge comparison, either by exact-cover endpoint/support disagreement (R408/R410) or by an R176 cross state of the named interior bridge P^o against a fixed exact H-D support partition. In addition, if neither (HT) nor (REV) occurs, R488 supplies its double ancestral-neighbor P4 fork X_A and X_B before the balanced-pair conclusion. Thus the endpoint-universal branch has no residual in which the R485 bridge remains locally reverse-chord, both source-neighbor four-cells are Hamiltonian, and the pair-deletion fiber stays quietly side-locked. Proof of the side-lock elimination: assume no (HT), (REV), or (BP). By R393 choose an exact H-D cover exposing z_1. R489 shows it cannot expose z_1 at a rail tail, so z_1 is a rail head in that cover. Similarly some exact cover exposes z_{m-1}, and R489 forces that exposure to be at a rail tail. Since no balanced pair occurs, R408 implies each of z_1,z_{m-1} is an endpoint in every exact H-D cover, and R410/R411 give one fixed unordered support partition with endpoint-Hamiltonian path families. Again by R489, z_1 is always a head and z_{m-1} always a tail. They cannot belong to the same fixed support S: then every Hamilton path on S occurring in an exact cover would have endpoints z_1,z_{m-1}; endpoint universality in R411 forces S={z_1,z_{m-1}}, but both dimer orientations are Hamilton paths on this two-vertex support, and choosing (z_{m-1},z_1) would expose z_1 at a tail, contradicting R489. Hence z_1 and z_{m-1} lie on different fixed supports. The path P^o joins them, so some selected adjacent state of P^o crosses those two supports. Apply accepted R176 to the fixed exact two-cover of W and the literal source path cover T; this yields (BP), contradiction. Therefore one of (HT),(REV),(BP) must occur.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample beyond order ten; accepted R393 endpoint-universal branch; R485(P4), R488, R489; accepted R176,R408,R410,R411.

## Scope
Order-free reduction inside the endpoint-universal global branch. It eliminates the head/tail side-lock as a terminal bridge cell while retaining the exact pair deletion D and, in the final balanced-pair branch, a named cross state of the interior bridge P^o or exact-cover endpoint/support disagreement in the same fiber.

## Applicability
Use when the R485 bridge cell is reached inside the R393 endpoint-universal regime. Do not continue searching for an abstract endpoint-side flip. Either R489 already gives a source-adjacent collision/exact reversed bridge state, or exact-cover rigidity forces a bridge-interior R176 cross-state balanced pair.

## Persistence
Retain D={a_0,b_q}; A,B,P and P^o; the R485 P4 and R488 double-P4 fork when reached; each endpoint-exposure cover used by R393/R489; and for BP either the two compared exact H-D covers or the exact fixed support partition together with the named P^o cross state used by R176.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not claim a balanced pair closes H, and does not identify a single universal pair across the alternative R408/R410/R176 births. Does not apply to the historical-interaction branch of R393 without an endpoint-universality input. Does not assert the exact reversed bridge state is already a physical mate-cycle or spanning two-cover.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** R490 is a nonreconstructible endpoint-universal bridge-cell continuation with no live consumers; preserve historically.
- **Curation note:** Endpoint-universal bridge side-lock reduction; conditional global-branch tool, not primary spine after automatic bridge-cross birth.
- **Review status:** accepted

## Proof
Assume HT, REV and BP all fail. By R393, z_1 is an endpoint in some exact cover F_L of W=H-D. If it were a tail, R489(L) would give HT or REV. Hence it is a head. Likewise z_{m-1} is an endpoint in some F_R and must be a tail by R489(R). Because BP is assumed absent, R408 applied between F_L and any other exact H-D cover shows z_1 can never become internal; similarly z_{m-1} can never become internal. R410 and then R411 place every exact H-D cover in one fixed support partition and supply endpoint-Hamiltonian flexibility on each support. The failure of HT/REV plus R489 means z_1 can never be a tail and z_{m-1} can never be a head, so they are universal oriented endpoint anchors. Suppose they lie in the same fixed support S. Since both are endpoints in every Hamilton path on S appearing in an exact cover, no third vertex of S can be an endpoint. But R411 says every vertex of S is an endpoint of some Hamilton path on S, so S has exactly the two vertices z_1,z_{m-1}. On a two-vertex support both orientations are vertex-simple tight Hamilton paths. Combining (z_{m-1},z_1) with any Hamilton path on the other fixed support, as licensed by the fixed-support factorization, gives an exact H-D cover with z_1 as a tail, contradicting R489 under the assumed failure of HT/REV. Therefore z_1,z_{m-1} occupy different fixed supports. Now T=A^+ sqcup P^o sqcup B^- is a literal path cover of W and P^o begins in one fixed support and ends in the other. Along P^o there is therefore a first adjacent state xy crossing the support partition. Taking R to be any fixed exact H-D two-cover and T as above, accepted R176 gives a graph-intrinsic balanced opposite-sign pair, which is BP. Contradiction. Finally, R488 says that under failure of HT its two ancestry-bearing four-sets are both Hamiltonian, so the DP4 packet is retained along this reduction.

# R492 — Reversed bridge endpoint shift compiles a collision-decorated R453 double fan

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Retain the hypotheses and notation of R485 in its residual (P4) branch, put D={a_0,b_q}, and assume neither ancestral-neighbor chord collision (H) nor (T) occurs. Hence R3 gives L_B=(b_{q-1},b_q,a_0) and L_A=(b_q,a_0,a_1) tight, while R488 retains its DP4 cells. Suppose one R489 exact endpoint-state reversal occurs.

(L) Left REV. Let H-D=R sqcup S with R=(r_0,...,w,z_2,z_1), put R^-=(r_0,...,w,z_2), S=(s_0,...,s_N), C_L=(z_1,a_0,b_q), and O_L=(a_0,z_1,z_2). By R168, H=R^- sqcup S sqcup C_L is a literal spanning three-cover by nontrivial paths. The S-to-C_L R453 splice certifies
T_S=(z_1,s_N,s_{N-1}) OR D_S=(a_0,z_1,s_N),
where D_S is collision-decorated by O_L because s_N!=z_2. For each Q in {R^-,S}, Q=(q_0,q_1,...), the C_L-to-Q splice certifies
D_Q=(q_0,b_q,a_0) OR H_Q=(q_1,q_0,b_q).
At least one rail Q=Q_* has q_0!=b_{q-1}; for that rail D_{Q_*} is collision-decorated by L_B.

Therefore either D_S or D_{Q_*} is tight and yields a named R38 collision, or both are bad. In the no-collision branch the physical clauses force T_S and H_{Q_*} tight, while R3 fixes the exact reverse turns (s_N,z_1,a_0) and (a_0,b_q,q_0) tight. Hence the two Hamilton P4 orders are explicit:
K_T=(s_N,z_1,a_0,b_q),
K_H=(z_1,a_0,b_q,q_0).
Thus Left REV compiles to two collision-decorated physical clauses; absent immediate collision, it produces two named shield winners together with two exact endpoint-absorbing P4s, not merely unspecified four-set Hamiltonicity.

(R) Right REV is dual. If H-D=R sqcup S with R=(z_{m-1},z_{m-2},...,r_N), put R^+=R-{z_{m-1}}, C_R=(a_0,b_q,z_{m-1}), O_R=(z_{m-2},z_{m-1},b_q). The C_R-to-S splice has decorated literal D_S=(s_0,z_{m-1},b_q), decorated by O_R; for at least one Q in {R^+,S} whose tail q_N differs from a_1, the Q-to-C_R splice has decorated literal D_Q=(b_q,a_0,q_N), decorated by L_A. If neither collision fires, the opposite clause literals are forced and R3 fixes the exact P4s
K_H=(a_0,b_q,z_{m-1},s_0),
K_T=(q_N,a_0,b_q,z_{m-1}).
All displayed clauses retain their literal two-cover proposals and complete two-hole certificates.

Consequently an R489 exact old-state reversal has a canonical physical consumption: shift the reversed bridge endpoint into the retained chord trimer, obtaining two collision-decorated R453 clauses. If their decorations do not fire, the resulting shield winners come with exact endpoint-absorbing P4 orders. The next question is whether a further surgery can cut the still-preserved chord adjacency and thereby create an outgoing R463 sibling complement.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample; all hypotheses of R485 hold in its P4 branch; neither R485 chord collision H nor T occurs; R488 and R489 may be used; accepted R3,R38,R168,R453 are available.

## Scope
Order-free physical consumer of the R489 exact endpoint-state reversal inside an R485/R488 bridge cell, strengthened to retain exact endpoint-absorbing P4 orders in the no-collision branch.

## Applicability
Use in R490(REV). Shift the reversed bridge endpoint into C_L or C_R. The two displayed R453 clauses are immediately collision-decorated. If no R38 collision occurs, continue from the forced shield and exact P4 order; do not forget that the P4 preserves one chord adjacency and therefore still needs a second cut for a sibling complement.

## Persistence
Retain D, the original bridge and R485 chord P4, the R488 DP4 cells, the exact H-D REV cover, shifted trimer, old bridge turn, reverse ancestral-neighbor turn, literal shifted three-cover, both physical R453 proposals with complete holes, any collision, and in the no-collision branch both shield winners and exact Hamilton P4 orders.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not itself produce a complement of either forced shield or close O4. The explicit P4s absorb one exact-cover endpoint but preserve the incident chord adjacency z_1->a_0 on the left or b_q->z_{m-1} on the right; further cut geometry is required for a sibling complement.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** R492 is a nonreconstructible collision-decorated R453 bridge-fan specialization with no live consumers; preserve historically.
- **Curation note:** Physical reversed-endpoint shift compiler with exact R453 proposals and endpoint-absorbing P4s.
- **Review status:** accepted

## Proof
Left REV: write a=a_0,b=b_q,l=b_{q-1}. Absence of R485(T) makes (a,b,l) bad because C_R is retained tight, hence L_B=(l,b,a) is tight by R3. Let R=(r_0,...,w,z_2,z_1) and S=(s_0,...,s_N). R168 gives |R|,|S|>=3, so R^-=R-z_1 is nontrivial; C_L=(z_1,a,b) is tight by R485(P4), hence R^- sqcup S sqcup C_L is a literal spanning three-cover.

R453 on S-to-C_L gives mate clause (z_1,s_N,s_{N-1}) OR (a,z_1,s_N). Since z_2 lies in R^- and S is disjoint, s_N!=z_2, so the second literal is collision-decorated by O_L=(a,z_1,z_2). R453 on C_L-to-Q gives (q_0,b,a) OR (q_1,q_0,b). The two heads of R^- and S are distinct, so one Q_* has q_0!=l; then (q_0,b,a) is collision-decorated by L_B. If either decorated literal is tight, R38 gives the asserted collision. Otherwise both are bad, so their clauses force T_S=(z_1,s_N,s_{N-1}) and H_{Q_*}=(q_1,q_0,b) tight. Boundary antisymmetry now gives the exact reverses (s_N,z_1,a) and (a,b,q_0) tight. Concatenating the former with C_L gives K_T=(s_N,z_1,a,b); concatenating C_L with the latter gives K_H=(z_1,a,b,q_0). These are explicit tight Hamilton P4s. R488 retains X_A,X_B independently because H,T were excluded.

Right REV is obtained by reversing head/tail roles. Absence of R485(H) gives L_A=(b,a,a_1) tight. Shift z_{m-1} from the beginning of the REV rail into C_R=(a,b,z_{m-1}). The C_R-to-S clause has decorated literal (s_0,z_{m-1},b), whose reverse (b,z_{m-1},s_0) concatenates after C_R when the decoration is bad, giving (a,b,z_{m-1},s_0). For Q with tail q_N!=a_1, the Q-to-C_R decorated literal is (b,a,q_N); if bad its reverse (q_N,a,b) concatenates before C_R, giving (q_N,a,b,z_{m-1}). The opposite literals of the two physical clauses are forced tight. This proves the strengthened claim.

# R497 — R495 one-hole fork is native-clause isolated without a second cross-arm cut

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Retain the head-fork (HF) output of R495. Thus F_H=X_H sqcup A^+ sqcup P^o is the literal spanning three-cover with X_H=(b_0,...,b_q,a_0), A^+=(a_1,...,a_p), P^o=(z_1,...,z_{m-1}), and the two candidate-aware fork mates are H_A=(a_1,a_0,b_q) and H_P=(z_1,a_0,b_q), exact complements of the bad one-hole seams s_A=(b_q,a_0,a_1) and s_P=(b_q,a_0,z_1). Then the bridge-interior prong H_P is intrinsically isolated from any native R173/R453 sibling that leaves X_H intact: in the native X_H-to-P^o R453 clause, H_P is the first mate literal, and accepted R461 says every physical two-hole sibling clause containing its exact complement s_P must break both source endpoint adjacencies b_q->a_0 in X_H and z_1->z_2 in P^o. Since m>=3, both states are defined. In particular the displayed one-hole candidates C_A and C_P of R495 preserve b_q->a_0 and therefore cannot themselves be, nor can any surgery confined to A^+ or P^o while leaving X_H intact produce, a sibling clause complementary to H_P. If p>=2, the same barrier applies to H_A: the native X_H-to-A^+ R453 clause has first mate literal H_A, so any sibling clause containing s_A must break both b_q->a_0 and a_1->a_2. Thus when both fork arms are nontrivial, consuming either head-fork mate through a physical mate cycle requires a genuine two-component cut that abandons the common live source state b_q a_0 and the corresponding arm boundary state. Dually, in the tail-fork (TF), the guaranteed bridge-interior mate T_P=(a_0,b_q,z_{m-1}) is the second mate literal of the native P^o-to-X_T splice and any sibling containing its complement t_P=(z_{m-1},b_q,a_0) must break both z_{m-2}->z_{m-1} and b_q->a_0; if q>=2 the ancestral mate T_B likewise requires breaking b_{q-2}->b_{q-1} and b_q->a_0. Therefore the R495 one-hole forks are not themselves clause progress: one-hole candidate identity is valuable, but any R173 consumer of the guaranteed bridge-interior prong must introduce a new cross-arm surgery cutting the common chord-adjacent source state b_q a_0. This strengthens R496 from a currentization incompatibility to a proposal-level two-cut fence.

## Hypotheses
Strong Level-(1); R495 head- or tail-fork output; accepted R453 and R461. For the ancestral head arm require p>=2, and for the ancestral tail arm require q>=2. The bridge-interior arms are unconditional because m>=3.

## Scope
Order-free negative-result fence on the candidate-aware R495 fork. It preserves the exact live three-cover, the common source state b_q a_0, both fork witnesses, and the physical R453 clause identities.

## Applicability
Use when attempting to turn R495(HF)/(TF) directly into an R173/R463 mate cycle. Any continuation that leaves the live X_H/X_T chord-adjacent state b_q a_0 intact cannot complement the guaranteed bridge-interior fork mate. Search instead for a surgery that simultaneously cuts b_q a_0 and the relevant P^o endpoint adjacency; when the ancestral arm is nontrivial the same two-cut requirement applies there.

## Persistence
Retain F_H or F_T, the common directed state b_q a_0, P^o endpoint adjacency, the relevant ancestral-arm adjacency when nontrivial, the exact fork mate and its antisymmetric one-hole seam, and the native R453 ordered-pair provenance. The conclusion is a necessary-condition fence on any future physical sibling proposal.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not say no cross-arm sibling exists. Does not apply R461 to a singleton ancestral arm. Does not convert a one-hole candidate into a two-hole clause. Does not claim the fork mates are useless; it identifies the additional cut any physical mate-cycle consumer must pay.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Historical R495 one-hole fork isolation fence; the R495 route is no longer live.
- **Curation note:** R495 fork mate complementation requires a genuine second cross-arm cut.
- **Review status:** accepted

## Proof
Head fork. In F_H the ordered X_H-to-P^o splice has source left endpoint states b_q a_0 and right initial state z_1 z_2. By accepted R453 its first mate literal is exactly (z_1,a_0,b_q)=H_P. The exact antisymmetric complement is (b_q,a_0,z_1)=s_P. Accepted R461 applies because X_H and P^o are nontrivial and says any literal spanning two-path proposal whose two-hole mate clause contains s_P must break both b_q a_0 and z_1 z_2. Both displayed R495 one-hole proposals C_A and C_P retain b_q a_0; moreover any surgery confined away from X_H retains it. Hence none can be such a sibling. If p>=2, apply the identical argument to the ordered X_H-to-A^+ splice: its first mate literal is H_A=(a_1,a_0,b_q), complement s_A, and R461 requires breaking b_q a_0 and a_1 a_2. Tail fork. In F_T, consider P^o-to-X_T. The second native mate literal is (a_0,b_q,z_{m-1})=T_P, whose complement is t_P=(z_{m-1},b_q,a_0). R461 requires breaking z_{m-2}z_{m-1} and b_q a_0. If q>=2, the B^--to-X_T splice has second literal T_B=(a_0,b_q,b_{q-1}), so complementing t_B requires breaking b_{q-2}b_{q-1} and b_q a_0. This is exactly the stated proposal-level cross-arm fence.

# R498 — R495 fork prongs cannot form their own physical sibling clause

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Retain either candidate-aware fork of R495. In the head fork, the two bad one-hole seams are s_A=(b_q,a_0,a_1) and s_P=(b_q,a_0,z_1), with exact mates H_A=(a_1,a_0,b_q) and H_P=(z_1,a_0,b_q) both tight. There is no literal spanning two-path proposal whose complete two-hole set is {H_A,H_P}; equivalently there is no physical two-hole mate clause having exactly the two fork complements {s_A,s_P} as its literals. Indeed if such a proposal existed, every turn outside its two displayed holes would be certified tight by definition, while both displayed holes H_A,H_P are already graph-intrinsically tight, so the proposal itself would be a spanning two-cover of H, contradicting pc(H)>2. Dually, in the tail fork there is no two-hole proposal with hole set {T_B,T_P}, hence no physical clause whose two literals are exactly {t_B,t_P}. Consequently the two one-hole prongs of R495 cannot close into a direct physical sibling edge with one another. Any R173/R463 use of a fork complement must pair it with a genuinely third clause literal. Combined with R497, the guaranteed bridge-interior prong can reach such a third literal only through a proposal that also cuts the common chord-adjacent source state b_q a_0 and the relevant P^o endpoint adjacency.

## Hypotheses
Strong Level-(1); pc(H)>2; the R495 head- or tail-fork output; literal complete-hole/mate-clause semantics. R497 is retained for the combined third-literal cut fence.

## Scope
Order-free physical-clause fence on the two-prong candidate-aware R495 fork.

## Applicability
Use when attempting to connect the two R495 fork complements directly into a mate cycle. They cannot be the two literals of one physical clause. Any implication route must leave the fork through a third literal; combine with R497 to obtain the required cross-arm cut budget on the bridge-interior exit.

## Persistence
Retains both one-hole candidate identities, both exact tight mates, both bad seams, and the live fork labels. The impossibility is graph/candidate intrinsic and independent of later currentization.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not forbid a physical clause containing one fork complement together with a third literal. Does not itself construct or rule out longer mate cycles. Does not require the two one-hole candidates to be simultaneously selected; only the graph-intrinsic tightness of their exact mates is used.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Historical R495 sibling-clause impossibility; the R495 route is no longer live.
- **Curation note:** The two R495 fork prongs cannot themselves be the literals of one physical sibling clause.
- **Review status:** accepted

## Proof
In HF, suppose a literal spanning two-path proposal Q had complete uncertified-turn set {H_A,H_P}. R495 certifies H_A and H_P tight. Every other turn of Q is certified tight by the definition of its complete hole set. Hence every turn of Q is tight, so Q is a literal spanning two-cover, contradicting pc(H)>2. The associated mate clause would have literals bar(H_A)=s_A and bar(H_P)=s_P, so no such physical clause exists. The TF proof is identical with T_B,T_P and t_B,t_P. Therefore a fork cannot directly pair its two complements; any clause route must use a third literal. R497 then supplies the extra cut requirement for the bridge-interior prong.

# R5 — Universal small-deletion exactness through four vertices

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Deleting any set of one, two, three, or four vertices from a smallest counterexample leaves a graph of path-cover number exactly two.

## Scope
Smallest counterexample.

## Applicability
Deletion set size 1 through 4.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** active
- **Curation note:** Universal small-deletion exactness is powerful legacy machinery but is explicitly excluded from independent O6 closure; toolkit is the safer navigation role.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Legacy migration verification: this item was recorded as independently accepted in the controlling compressed A7C2 package and is being normalized into the A7C3 canonical schema.

## Proof
Let H be a smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample and let D be a nonempty vertex set with 1<=|D|<=4. By R4, H-D has path-cover number at most two. We prove it cannot be Hamiltonian. Suppose H-D has a Hamilton tight path K. If |D|=1, the unique deleted vertex is a singleton tight path, so K together with it is a spanning two-cover of H, contradiction. If |D|=2, the two deleted vertices form a tight dimer, so again they together with K give a spanning two-cover. If |D|=3, R3 guarantees a tight ordering of the three deleted vertices, hence a tight trimer on D; this trimer together with K is a spanning two-cover, contradiction. It remains that |D|=4. Choose z in D and put T=D-{z}. By R3, T supports a tight trimer. Then K sqcup T is a two-path cover of H-z. This cover is exact: H-z cannot be Hamiltonian, because a Hamilton path of H-z together with singleton z would be a spanning two-cover of H. Thus K sqcup T is an exact one-vertex-deletion two-cover containing the three-vertex rail T. This contradicts R24, which says every rail in every exact one-vertex-deletion two-cover of a smallest counterexample has order at least four. Therefore H-D is not Hamiltonian in all four cases. Since R4 gives pc(H-D)<=2 and H-D is nonempty, pc(H-D)=2. This proves R5 for every deletion set of size one through four. No four-vertex orientation classification is used in the R5 proof itself; all of the hard four-vertex work is isolated in the independently audited singleton rail floor R24.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED/R5.md -->

# R500 — Beyond-order-ten R478 P5 double reversal always forces a named cross-state balanced pair

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Let H be a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample beyond order ten, and suppose the anti-aligned bridge in R495 comes specifically from the R478 P5 currentization. Hence P=(a_0,z_1,z_2,z_3,b_q) has exactly five vertices, so the literal source cover P sqcup A^+ sqcup B^- gives |H|=p+q+5 and therefore p+q>=6. If the R495 output is DR, then H contains a graph-intrinsic balanced opposite-sign pair with a four-deletion cross-state certificate retaining named bridge/ancestral residual classes. If p,q>=2 this is exactly R499. If p=1, then q>=5. Delete E_B={a_0,a_1,b_q,b_{q-2}}. The source cover restricted to H-E_B is the literal three-cover B_L sqcup (b_{q-1}) sqcup P^o, where B_L=(b_0,...,b_{q-3}) and P^o=(z_1,z_2,z_3); all three classes are nonempty. R5 gives an exact two-cover T of H-E_B, R7 forces T to select a state crossing two of these three named classes, and R176 converts that selected cross-state into a balanced opposite-sign pair. Dually, if q=1 then p>=5. Delete E_A={a_0,b_q,b_{q-1},a_2}. The restricted source cover is the literal three-cover (a_1) sqcup A_R sqcup P^o with A_R=(a_3,...,a_p), again all nonempty; R5,R7,R176 give the same conclusion. Thus in the beyond-order-ten R478 P5 application every DR output, including both short-arm cells excluded from R499, immediately births a balanced pair without currentizing the DR path or forgetting the original bridge/ancestral coordinates.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample with |H|>10; the R495 bridge is the five-vertex P5 produced in the accepted R478 application; DR occurs; accepted R5,R7,R176,R478,R495,R499.

## Scope
Primary O4 consumer of the R495 DR branch in the synchronized R478 P5 application.

## Applicability
Use immediately when R478/R485/R495 lands in DR. For p,q>=2 invoke R499. If one arm has length parameter one, the order bound forces the other arm long enough to puncture it with an alternate four-deletion, restoring a three-to-two component deficit and hence an R176 cross-state pair.

## Persistence
Retains the original five-vertex bridge P, the DR labels, and in each case the exact alternate four-deletion set plus the three named residual source classes crossed by the exact two-cover. The balanced pair is graph-intrinsic.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Specialized to the five-vertex R478 bridge and beyond-order-ten regime. Does not assert the balanced pair alone closes O4; it supplies a role-labelled entry to the accepted pair-descent machinery. Does not generalize the short-arm alternate deletion to arbitrary longer R485 bridges without a separate size argument.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired

- **Curation note:** Beyond-order-ten five-vertex bridge DR consumer including short-arm alternate deletions.

## Proof
Because the R478 bridge has five vertices, the source cover has n=|P|+|A^+|+|B^-|=5+p+q. Since n>10, p+q>=6. If p,q>=2, apply R499. Suppose p=1. Then q>=5. Delete E_B={a_0,a_1,b_q,b_{q-2}}. In the original source cover, P loses a_0,b_q and becomes P^o=(z_1,z_2,z_3); A^+=(a_1) disappears; B^-=(b_0,...,b_{q-1}) punctured at b_{q-2} becomes B_L=(b_0,...,b_{q-3}) plus singleton (b_{q-1}). These three nonempty tight paths cover H-E_B. R5 gives an exact two-cover T. Partition by their supports and apply R7: t=3-2+sigma>=1, so T has a selected state crossing two source components. R176 yields a balanced pair. If q=1, then p>=5. Delete E_A={a_0,b_q,b_{q-1},a_2}. Now B^- disappears, P becomes P^o, and A^+ punctured at a_2 becomes singleton (a_1) plus A_R=(a_3,...,a_p), again three nonempty source components. The same R5/R7/R176 argument applies. # R502 — Anti-aligned bridge forces a bridge-interior cross-state pair birth

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Let H be a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample. Let A=(a_0,a_1,...,a_p) and B=(b_0,...,b_{q-1},b_q) be vertex-simple tight paths with p,q>=1, and suppose H has the anti-aligned bridge three-cover P sqcup A^+ sqcup B^- of C388, where P=(a_0,z_1,...,z_{m-1},b_q) is tight with m>=3, A^+=(a_1,...,a_p), B^-=(b_0,...,b_{q-1}), and P^o=(z_1,...,z_{m-1}). Put D={a_0,b_q} and W=H-D. Then every exact two-cover T of W selects a directed state xy with one endpoint in V(P^o) and the other in V(A^+) union V(B^-). Consequently accepted R176 yields a graph-intrinsic balanced opposite-sign pair whose birth retains the exact pair-deletion fiber D, the selected cross state xy, and whether the nonbridge endpoint lies on A^+ or B^-. In particular a named P^o cross-state pair birth is automatic in every anti-aligned bridge cell; no endpoint-universality, R485 wrap analysis, R493 collision split, or R495 DR/HF/TF split is needed for this output.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample; p,q>=1; m>=3; P sqcup A^+ sqcup B^- is the literal anti-aligned bridge three-cover described above. Accepted R5 and R176.

## Scope
Order-free smallest-counterexample consumer for the full anti-aligned bridge configuration. It preserves the bridge-interior ancestry of the selected cross-state that births the pair.

## Applicability
Use immediately whenever an anti-aligned bridge P sqcup A^+ sqcup B^- appears in a smallest counterexample. Choose any exact two-cover of H-{a_0,b_q}; before doing endpoint-side, wrap, DR, or one-hole-fork analysis, extract a selected state crossing P^o to an ancestral residual rail and apply R176.

## Persistence
Retain D={a_0,b_q}, the literal source partition A^+ sqcup P^o sqcup B^-, the chosen exact two-cover T of W, the selected directed cross state xy, and the identity of its bridge-interior endpoint and ancestral side. The resulting balanced pair is graph-intrinsic; T and xy are the birth certificate/provenance.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert the resulting balanced pair itself closes H, is current in a common cover, or has a prescribed support size. Does not say every cross state of T touches P^o; only that at least one does. Does not provide the next physical spend of the pair. Outside smallest-counterexample scope one must separately assume an exact two-cover of H-D.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** R502 is an anti-aligned bridge cross-state birth from a retired bridge route and has no live consumer.
- **Curation note:** Bridge-specific R508 specialization retained because R176 adds a graph-intrinsic balanced pair and bridge-interior ancestry.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** PASS: Correct bridge-interior crossing proof. R508 subsumes the replacement subargument, but the R176 balanced-pair upgrade and retained bridge ancestry make this a distinct reusable consumer.

## Proof
Let D={a_0,b_q} and W=H-D. By R5, pc(W)=2, so choose any literal exact two-cover T=T_1 sqcup T_2 of W. The retained source pieces A^+, P^o, B^- are three nonempty vertex-disjoint tight paths spanning W. Suppose for contradiction that T selects no directed state with exactly one endpoint in V(P^o) and the other in V(A^+) union V(B^-). Then no T-component can contain both a P^o vertex and a vertex outside P^o, because along the ordered path from one type to the other there would be a first selected transition crossing the partition. Since P^o is nonempty, at least one T-component lies entirely in V(P^o). Because A^+ and B^- are also nonempty and T has only two components, exactly one component, say T_P, has vertex set V(P^o), while the other component T_{AB} has vertex set V(A^+) union V(B^-). Thus T_{AB} is a vertex-simple tight Hamilton path on the whole ancestral residual support A^+ union B^-. But the original bridge P=(a_0,z_1,...,z_{m-1},b_q) is a tight path on D union V(P^o), disjoint from T_{AB}; therefore P sqcup T_{AB} is a literal spanning two-cover of H, contradicting that H is a counterexample. Hence every exact two-cover T of W contains a selected cross state xy incident with P^o and one of A^+,B^-. Since W is proper in H, accepted R176 applies to the literal source cover R=A^+ sqcup P^o sqcup B^- and the exact cover T and upgrades xy to a graph-intrinsic balanced opposite-sign pair, retaining the cross-state provenance. This proves the claim.

# R504 — Bridge-cross adaptive capture is fork-witness blind

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Retain the anti-aligned bridge setup of R502, with D={a_0,b_q}, W=H-D, and a selected bridge-interior cross state xy in an exact two-cover of W. The witness-adaptive capture step used in R503 does not consume any special R495 DR/HF/TF witness packet. Indeed for every vertex w outside D, boundary antisymmetry R3 applied with middle a_0 gives exactly one of (w,a_0,b_q) and (b_q,a_0,w) tight; either turn is a valid signed incarnation of the physical support D with witness w. Since A^+,B^-,P^o are nonempty and |P^o|>=2, W has at least four vertices. For the two-vertex marker {x,y}, choose any w in W-{x,y}; its R3 sign on D avoids the marker, so accepted R37 already makes xy capture-capable and permits capture of either marker endpoint. Thus the bare conclusion of R503 that the P^o endpoint of xy can be captured through D is fork-blind and follows from R3,R37,R502 alone. Any downstream theorem claiming to consume R495 via this capture must use additional fork data after capture, such as the exact one-hole proposal/mate identities or a special witness role; the mere existence of the capture is not such a consumer.

## Hypotheses
Anti-aligned bridge setup with p,q>=1,m>=3; accepted R502 selected cross state xy in an exact H-D two-cover; accepted R3,R37.

## Scope
Order-free role-consumption fence for the R503 capture route. It distinguishes generic sign manufacture on the bridge dimer from genuine use of R495 candidate-aware fork data.

## Applicability
Use when evaluating any R495-to-capture continuation. Do not count adaptive capture of a selected D-deletion state as spending the R495 fork unless a later step explicitly uses the fork one-hole candidates, exact mates, ancestral witness identity, or another non-generic coordinate.

## Persistence
Retain D, the exact D-deletion cover, selected marker xy, and chosen generic witness w. The conclusion is logical non-consumption: the R495 witnesses may remain valid historical facts but are not needed for the capture inference.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not invalidate R503 mathematically and does not say capture is useless. It says only that the capture-existence step is available without R495. It does not rule out a later capture-based theorem that genuinely reuses the fork mate/proposal data.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Historical bridge-capture fork-witness blindness fence; bridge-capture route is no longer live.
- **Curation note:** Adaptive capture of the forced bridge cross does not by itself consume R495 fork data.
- **Review status:** accepted

## Proof
Let xy be the selected cross state from R502. Because p,q>=1 and |P^o|>=2, W=A^+ union B^- union P^o has at least four vertices, so choose w in W-{x,y}. Apply R3 to the three distinct vertices w,a_0,b_q with middle a_0. Exactly one of (w,a_0,b_q) and (b_q,a_0,w) is tight. In the first case D occurs as the terminal physical dimer (a_0,b_q); in the second it occurs as the initial physical dimer (b_q,a_0). Thus in either case D has an admissible signed incarnation with witness w. This witness is outside the selected marker xy by construction. R37 therefore applies in the exact D-deletion cover containing xy and gives a capture certificate for either chosen endpoint of xy. No R495 turn, witness, one-hole proposal, or DR/HF/TF distinction occurs in the argument. Hence adaptive capture existence is fork-witness blind.

# R505 — R495 fork mates synchronize to the forced bridge cross or expose a witness-witness state

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Retain a non-DR candidate-aware fork of R495 and the forced bridge-interior cross state supplied by R502 in an exact D-deletion cover T, D={a_0,b_q}. In the head fork HF, let M_A=H_A=(a_1,a_0,b_q) and M_P=H_P=(z_1,a_0,b_q), the exact mates of the unique bad seams of C_A and C_P. Let xy be a selected T-state with exactly one endpoint x in P^o and the other in A^+ or B^-. Then either (HH) {x,y}={a_1,z_1}, so T literally selects a directed state between the two named head-fork witnesses, the heads of the two non-X_H source components; or (MC) at least one witness w in {a_1,z_1} avoids {x,y}. Choose its corresponding exact fork mate M_w as the signed incarnation of D in R37. Then R37 captures the P^o endpoint x through the actual selected cross {x,y}, and the capture certificate is synchronized to the same graph-intrinsic turn M_w that is the exact mate of its displayed one-hole spanning proposal C_w. Choosing any genuine old P^o adjacency at x, R312 therefore yields either an earlier protected contact at x or a lawful first-contact R155 mirror reentry while the exact fork candidate C_w, its unique bad seam, its mate M_w, D, T, xy, P^o, and the capture event remain retained as historical/certificate data. In the tail fork TF the exact dual holds: with fork mates M_B=T_B=(a_0,b_q,b_{q-1}) and M_P=T_P=(a_0,b_q,z_{m-1}), either (TT) T selects the literal state on {b_{q-1},z_{m-1}}, the two named tail-fork witnesses, or one exact fork mate avoids xy and supplies the synchronized capture/first-contact route. Thus every non-DR R495 fork either exposes a direct witness-witness endpoint cross in the common D-deletion fiber or feeds one of its actual one-hole mates into the capture/first-contact lineage as the sign used for the capture.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample; accepted R495 HF or TF; accepted R502 selected P^o cross in an exact H-D two-cover; accepted R37,R312.

## Scope
Order-free role-sensitive consumer of the R495 one-hole fork. Unlike generic bridge-dimer capture, the capture witness is required to be one of the exact candidate mates unless the selected cross itself joins the two fork witnesses.

## Applicability
Use after R495+R502 in the HF/TF branch. First compare the two-vertex selected marker with the two exact fork-witness vertices. If it is not exactly their pair, choose an avoiding fork witness and use its exact mate turn as the R37 sign certificate; then probe first contact along P^o by R312.

## Persistence
In the synchronized-capture branch retain the displayed one-hole proposal C_w, its complete one-hole set, exact mate M_w, bridge dimer D, exact D-deletion cover T, selected cross xy, captured P^o endpoint x, original P^o adjacency used for R312, and the capture event. These facts may live across different representatives as historical/certificate data; no simultaneous currentness beyond the stated source frames is claimed. In HH/TT retain T and the literal selected state between the two named fork witnesses.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not say the exceptional HH/TT state closes H. Does not claim the later R312 contact preserves the original fork cover as current. Does not assert the aligned refund descendant of M_w preserves the one-hole candidate; only the identity of the sign turn used for capture with the candidate mate is synchronized. Does not apply to DR, which has separate consumers.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** R505 is a nonreconstructible R495 bridge-fork synchronization leaf with no live consumers; preserve historically.
- **Curation note:** R495 fork synchronization is bridge-route toolkit, not current spine.
- **Review status:** accepted

## Proof
Consider HF. R495 gives the exact one-hole candidates C_A,C_P with mates M_A=(a_1,a_0,b_q) and M_P=(z_1,a_0,b_q), so M_A and M_P are admissible signed incarnations of the physical bridge dimer D with distinct witnesses a_1,z_1. Hence the four-set {b,x,y,z} either supports a tight Hamilton P4 or is one of the four exact R516 no-P4 signatures. Its opposite-edge matching-block quotient is classified by R517: three signatures are vertex-uniform transitive up to block relabeling and the doubly misaligned 00 cell is vertex-uniform cyclic. The remaining vertex z is distinct from C, so corrected universal theorem R518 applies to C and z. Either {b,x,y,z} supports a Hamilton tight P4 or it is one of the exact no-P4 signatures R516 retained inside R518. In the latter case R517 gives the matching-block quotient: 11,10,01 are vertex-uniform transitive up to the stated block permutations, and 00 is vertex-uniform cyclic. # R624 — Shallow crossed covers yield only tautological X-local R358 mate clauses

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Retain the crossed phase and the four shallow singleton-deletion covers of R621. Puncturing a left-enlarged-root shallow cover at L, or a right-enlarged-root shallow cover at R, produces an exact pair-deletion two-cover in which the middle of a natural M_S gate trimer is exposed as an endpoint, so R358 applies. However the resulting four two-hole mate clauses are respectively: for root z, (z,c,a) OR (b,z,c); for root b, (b,a,c) OR (z,b,a); for root c, (b,c,a) OR (z,b,c); for root a, (z,a,c) OR (b,z,a). Under the transitive matching-height rule M_R={ab,cz}>M_S={ac,bz}>M_L={bc,az}, the first literal is already tight in the z and b clauses, while the second literal is already tight in the c and a clauses. Hence all four clauses are satisfied by pre-existing X-local mathematics and force no new turn. Therefore the direct strategy 'puncture the R621 shallow cover at the opposite Q endpoint and consume it with R358' is a sterile route unless additional non-X information is coupled to the same physical two-hole proposals.

## Hypotheses
H is in the crossed R621 frame with m>=4. Use the four shallow covers and gate polarities from R621, accepted R358, and the accepted matching-height rule of R534.

## Scope
R24 strategy fence. Crossed middle-gate phase. Rules out the most immediate shallow-cover endpoint-return mate attack as a source of new information.

## Applicability
Use whenever the R621 shallow covers suggest deleting L or R and applying R358 to the exposed gate-trimer middle. Do not spend further effort on those four isolated mate clauses: each is already discharged by the fixed X orientation. Any useful mate attack must involve an additional proposal, a clause cycle, Q-interior data, or another ancestry-bearing interaction.

## Persistence
Retain the four explicit punctured pair-deletion covers, their gate trimers, the four literal R358 clauses, and the matching-height comparison certifying which literal in each clause is already tight.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not say the punctured pair-deletion covers are useless for other comparisons. Does not rule out combining these clauses with additional physically certified clauses in an R173 cycle. Does not weaken R621, R622, or R623. Does not address deep-cover punctures or mixed pair deletions.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Historical tautological shallow R358 clause fence; current physical endpoint-star clauses and O6 R358 fence supersede its purpose.
- **Curation note:** Shows the naive shallow-cover R358 puncture route is tautological in the transitive X cell and forces no new turn without additional non-X data.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Each punctured shallow cover is exact by R5, each R358 clause is oriented correctly, and the stated X-local literal is already tight by the matching-height rule, so the isolated route is genuinely tautological.

## Proof
Write L=q_0 and R=q_m. We inspect the four roots.

Root z. R621 gives the shallow exact cover H-z=Q[0,m-1] sqcup (R,a,c,b). Delete L, an endpoint of the Q rail, to obtain the literal two-cover H-{z,L}=Q[1,m-1] sqcup (R,a,c,b). Accepted pair-deletion exactness R5 gives pc(H-{z,L})=2, so this displayed two-cover is exact. The left fully incoming M_S gate {b,z} gives the tight turn J=(z,b,L). In the displayed return the middle b is the tail endpoint of P=(R,a,c,b). Apply the tail form of R358 with outer pair {z,L}: with u=c and v=a it gives the clause (z,c,a) OR (b,z,c). By R534's matching-height rule, M(zc)=M_R>M(ca)=M_S, so (z,c,a) is already tight. The clause adds nothing.

Root b. R621 gives H-b=Q[0,m-1] sqcup (R,c,a,z). Delete L to obtain H-{b,L}=Q[1,m-1] sqcup (R,c,a,z), exact by R5. The same fully incoming gate gives J=(b,z,L), with middle z the tail endpoint of the P4. R358 gives (b,a,c) OR (z,b,a). Since M(ba)=M_R>M(ac)=M_S, (b,a,c) is already tight.

Root c. R621 gives H-c=(a,b,z,L) sqcup Q[1,m]. Delete R to obtain H-{c,R}=(a,b,z,L) sqcup Q[1,m-1], exact by R5. The right fully outgoing M_S gate {a,c} gives J=(R,a,c). Here middle a is the head endpoint of P=(a,b,z,L). The head form of R358 gives (b,c,a) OR (z,b,c). Since M(zb)=M_S>M(bc)=M_L, (z,b,c) is already tight.

Root a. R621 gives H-a=(c,z,b,L) sqcup Q[1,m]. Delete R to obtain H-{a,R}=(c,z,b,L) sqcup Q[1,m-1], exact by R5. The same outgoing gate gives J=(R,c,a), with middle c the head endpoint. R358 gives (z,a,c) OR (b,z,a). Since M(bz)=M_S>M(za)=M_L, (b,z,a) is already tight.

Thus every isolated R358 clause produced by this shallow-cover puncture is already satisfied by a known X-only turn. No new orientation is forced, proving the route fence.

Let D={q_2,q_{m-2}} and W=H-D. Retain the accepted R664 ancestry-bearing floor: singleton q_2 is tail-signed with both exact historical witnesses b and z, while singleton q_{m-2} is head-signed with both exact historical witnesses a and c. Orient every selected intercell state of T in the literal direction of its T-rail. Write these selected states as x_i y_i. A vertex of an oriented path has at most one immediate predecessor. LEFT ANCHOR. The inherited witness set {b,z} has size two, so choose one R665 transition x_L y_L with y_L not in {b,z}. If d s a were tight, Q[0,d] followed by s,a together with (c,z,b,q_m) would two-cover H; hence R3 gives a s d. The c-root gives c s d. Thus D_2=(s,d) is head-signed by a,c. Fourth, R649 says each tested orientation of G_3={a,c} is head-signed in an R542-ready reverse-boundary carrier, whereas each tested orientation of G_4={b,z} is tail-signed in an R542-ready carrier.

Now decorate each clause. In L-pre, (x_1,v,q_1) is a head sign on D_0, opposite the fixed tail signs; choosing a witness in {b,z} distinct from x_1 and applying R523 gives a labelled P4. The other literal (x_2,x_1,v) is a tail sign on the reverse E-dimer. If E=G_3 it is opposite the R649 fixed head sign and gives a P4; if E=G_4 it is a second tail witness on an R649 reverse-boundary packet, so R542 applies.

In L-post, (v,x_2,x_1) is a head sign on the reverse E-dimer: for E=G_3 it supplies a second head witness to an R649 packet and R542 applies, while for E=G_4 it is opposite the fixed tail sign and gives a P4. The literal (w,v,x_2) is a tail sign on D_L=(w,v), which already has tail witnesses b,z. Choose one distinct from x_2. Since D_L is the reverse terminal dimer of the tight carrier (q_1,v,w), R542 applies.

In R-pre, (x_1,d,r) is a head sign on D_R, which already has head witnesses a,c. Choose one distinct from x_1. D_R is the reverse terminal dimer of the old Q trimer (q_{m-4},r,d), so R542 applies. The second literal (x_2,x_1,d) is a tail sign on the reverse E-dimer and is handled exactly as the L-pre second literal: P4 for E=G_3, R542 for E=G_4.

In R-post, (d,x_2,x_1) is a head sign on the reverse E-dimer and is handled exactly as the L-post first literal: R542 for E=G_3, P4 for E=G_4. The second literal (s,d,x_2) is a tail sign on D_2=(s,d), opposite its fixed head witnesses a,c; choose one distinct from x_2 and apply R523 to obtain a labelled P4.

Finally let m=6. Then G_1 is the singleton q_3 and d=q_4. The L-post and R-pre audits remain exact two-hole audits. In L-pre the only extra turn is c_L=(x_2,q_3,q_4). If c_L is tight the same clause holds; if bad, R3 gives (q_4,q_3,x_2), a tail sign on D_R=(q_4,q_3), while R658 gives head witnesses a,c. Choose one distinct from x_2 and R523 gives a P4. In R-post the only extra turn is c_R=(q_2,q_3,x_1). If tight the same clause holds; if bad R3 gives (x_1,q_3,q_2), a head sign on D_L=(q_3,q_2), opposite the R658 tail witnesses b,z; choose one distinct from x_1 and R523 gives a P4. All shape-F cells are exhausted.

# R692 — Shape-E B-mate reflection saturates only to the pre-existing inward R542 packet

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Retain the monotone surviving shape-E cell of accepted R677. Put v=q_2, write the endpoint block X_e=G_3={a,c} in its actual T-order as (x_1,x_2), let X_i=G_4={b,z}, and suppose the B-mate (x_2,x_1,v) is tight. By the exact R677 decoration there is w in X_i such that (w,x_2,x_1,v) is a labelled tight Hamilton P4. Let w' be the other vertex of X_i. Closure-saturating the literal mate-reflection splice gives the spanning two-path proposal

(w,x_2,x_1,v,q_3,q_4,...,q_m)  sqcup  (q_1,q_0,w').

Its complete uncertified-turn set is the singleton {(x_1,v,q_3)}. Hence, in a hypothetical counterexample, that seam is bad and boundary antisymmetry forces (q_3,v,x_1) tight. This is only a third tail witness on the already-retained tested inward dimer S_L=(q_3,v): accepted R658 already tail-signs S_L by b and z, and the old Q trimer (q_1,v,q_3) already makes S_L a reverse boundary dimer of a tight short carrier. Thus the resulting R542 packet was already available from witnesses b,z before the B-mate or its labelled P4 was used. The reflection splice either closes H outright or returns witness-only reminting on the identical physical support and carrier; in the nonclosing branch it does not move a physical cut into Q.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in the accepted crossed R621/R665 sigma_G=0 frame; m>=6; the accepted R677 monotone shape-E residue occurs; X_e=G_3 and its B-mate branch is realized. Use accepted R3,R542,R621,R658,R677.

## Scope
Noncircular R24 strategy fence for one natural closure-saturation consumer of the shape-E B/P4 output. No R5,R168,R169,R224,R533 or generic R358.

## Applicability
When trying to consume the R677 B-mate by reflecting its labelled P4 into the physical Q suffix, test the displayed two-rail proposal first. A good seam closes; a bad seam is not new support geometry, because it only adds x_1 as another witness to the pre-existing R658 short-carrier packet.

## Persistence
Retain the exact R677 roles v,x_1,x_2,w,w', the displayed one-hole proposal, its sole seam, and the identity of the old carrier (q_1,v,q_3). In the bad-seam branch record that the tested support and carrier are unchanged and that witnesses b,z already suffice for R542.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not rule out a consumer of the A-mate, the X_e=G_4 same-tail B branch, the order-eleven extra-seam P4, a multi-cut proposal, or a construction using additional right-side/nonlocal data. Does not claim R542 is useless; it shows only that this particular reflection splice does not consume the B/P4 provenance or create strict cut movement.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Route-specific shape-E B-reflection saturation fence has no live dependents; preserve as historical negative information rather than maintaining a current repair branch.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** The displayed reflection proposal has exactly one uncertified seam. Its forced reverse is only an additional witness on the already R658-saturated inward dimer, so the negative result is correct and appropriately scoped.

## Proof
Let v=q_2. In the R677 B branch with X_e=G_3, write X_e=(x_1,x_2). The exact preferred proof P755 supplies a vertex w in the complementary block X_i=G_4 such that P=(w,x_2,x_1,v) is a tight P4. Write w' for the other vertex of X_i.

Consider the two vertex-disjoint sequences
C_1=(w,x_2,x_1,v,q_3,q_4,...,q_m),
C_2=(q_1,q_0,w').
They partition V(H). In C_1 the first two turns are certified by P. Every turn beginning with (v,q_3,q_4) is a consecutive old-Q turn. Therefore the only uncertified turn of C_1 is s=(x_1,v,q_3). In C_2 the unique turn is tight by the crossed-frame endpoint reverse star (q_1,q_0,y) for every y in X, retained by R621. Thus {s} is the complete hole set of C_1 sqcup C_2.

If s were tight, C_1 sqcup C_2 would be a spanning two-cover of H. Hence s is bad, and R3 gives its complete reversal (q_3,v,x_1) tight. On the tested dimer S_L=(q_3,v), this is a tail certificate with witness x_1. But R658 already gives the two tail certificates (q_3,v,b) and (q_3,v,z). The vertices b,z are distinct and lie outside the old Q trimer K_0=(q_1,v,q_3), whose reverse terminal dimer is exactly S_L. Therefore R542 was already applicable to (K_0,S_L) using b,z, before the new witness x_1 or the R677 B-mate was introduced. The bad-seam branch changes neither S_L, K_0, the pair-deletion support V(S_L), nor the physical position of the Q cut. It only enlarges an already sufficient witness set. This proves the fence.

# R704 — The two inward synchronized signed dimers amplify directly to labelled Hamilton P4s

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Retain the accepted crossed R658 frame with m>=6, put v=q_2, w=q_3, r=q_{m-3}, d=q_{m-2}, and keep the accepted sign facts that D_L=(w,v) is tail-signed by both b,z while D_R=(d,r) is head-signed by both a,c. Assuming pending R700, each inward packet already forces a labelled Hamilton P4 without invoking R542 payment. On the left apply R700 to the old-Q tight trimer K_L=(q_1,v,w) with probes b,z. If R700 gives its P4 branch, retain that labelled P4. Otherwise its DUAL-CP branch makes the reverse terminal dimer (w,v) head-signed by both b,z; combining one new head witness with the other accepted tail witness yields a literal tight Hamilton P4, for example (b,w,v,z). Dually, apply R700 to K_R=(r,d,q_{m-1}) with probes a,c. If its P4 branch occurs, retain it. Otherwise DUAL-CP makes the reverse initial dimer (d,r) tail-signed by both a,c; combining one accepted head witness with the other new tail witness yields, for example, (a,d,r,c). Hence neither inward R658 two-witness packet needs to be spent as anonymous R542 payment: each is P4-forcing in the fixed crossed frame.

## Hypotheses
H is in the accepted crossed R658 frame with m>=6. Use accepted R658 and pending R700. The probe vertices b,z (respectively a,c) lie outside the displayed old-Q trimers.

## Scope
Noncircular crossed-frame local compiler. It consumes the two inward Q-dimer R542 resources used by shape-F and related monotone arguments. No R542 descent, generic payment, R436, R5,R168,R169,R224,R533, or generic R358 is used in the conclusion.

## Applicability
Whenever a branch produces or invokes the accepted R658 left packet on (q_3,q_2) or right packet on (q_{m-2},q_{m-3}), replace anonymous R542 payment by this P4 amplification. In particular the inward-Q R542 literals in accepted R678 shape F become labelled-P4 outputs once R700 is reviewed.

## Persistence
Retain the side (left/right), the old-Q trimer used for R700, the two named X probes, and either the direct R700 P4 or the explicit mixed-polarity P4 assembled on the inward dimer, including its ordered four vertices.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert the resulting P4 alone closes H or that left and right P4 representatives coexist in one exact cover. Depends on pending R700. Does not consume X-dimer R649 packets or Reverse-Ear geometry.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Inward signed-dimer -> labelled-P4 amplification is generic local P4 production with no live dependents and no closure consumer. R829 and the modern exact-cover route make this currency non-scarce; preserve historically but do not migrate/review it as a current interface.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** PASS. On the left, R658 supplies tail signs of (q3,q2) by b,z while R700 joint no-P4 supplies head signs on that same tested dimer; mixing distinct witnesses gives (b,q3,q2,z). The right dual on (q_{m-2},q_{m-3}) is identical, giving for example (a,q_{m-2},q_{m-3},c). Thus each inward R658 packet is P4-forcing without payment.

## Proof
Left side: accepted R658 gives (w,v) tail-signed by b and by z. The old-Q triple K_L=(q_1,v,w) is tight and b,z lie outside it. Apply pending R700 with probes b,z. If its P4 branch occurs, we are done. Otherwise R700's DUAL-CP branch says the reverse terminal dimer of K_L, namely (w,v), is head-signed by both b and z. Choose the head certificate with witness b and the already accepted tail certificate with witness z. Then (b,w,v) and (w,v,z) are tight consecutive turns, so (b,w,v,z) is a tight Hamilton P4. Right side: accepted R658 gives (d,r) head-signed by a and by c. The old-Q triple K_R=(r,d,q_{m-1}) is tight, with a,c outside it. Apply R700 with probes a,c. If P4 occurs, stop. Otherwise DUAL-CP says the reverse initial dimer (d,r) is tail-signed by both a,c. Use the accepted head certificate with witness a and the new tail certificate with witness c: (a,d,r) and (d,r,c) are tight, hence (a,d,r,c) is a tight Hamilton P4. This proves both side statements.

# R714 — Every first-inward X-complement four-set is Hamiltonian in the synchronized transitive frame

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Retain the accepted R594 synchronized transitive frame with transitive P4-free four-cell X and Q=(q_0,...,q_m), m>=4. Put u=q_1 and s=q_{m-1}. Then for every x in X, both four-sets {u} union (X\{x}) and {s} union (X\{x}) support tight Hamilton P4s. Proof for u: first X union {u} is P5-free, because a Hamilton P5 on X union {u} together with the untouched tight suffix Q[2,m] would be a spanning two-cover of H. Fix x in X and choose any tight trimer C on X\{x}; such a trimer exists on every three-set by boundary antisymmetry. Since X itself is P4-free, C union {x}=X has no Hamilton P4. If C union {u} also had no Hamilton P4, accepted R522 applied to the fixed trimer C with outside vertices x,u would force a Hamilton P5 on C union {x,u}=X union {u}, contradiction. Hence C union {u} supports a Hamilton P4. The right statement is dual: X union {s} is P5-free because any P5 there together with Q[0,m-2] two-covers H, and the same R522 argument applies. Therefore all eight first-inward X-complement four-sets are graph-intrinsically Hamiltonian. In particular a LOCAL four-cell output of pending R713 is baseline Hamiltonicity already forced by R594+R522; only the DEEP selected-cut branch of R713 is new physical progress.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in accepted R594; Q=(q_0,...,q_m), m>=4; accepted R522.

## Scope
Noncircular R24 structural corollary and strategy fence. No R5,R168,R169,R224,R533, capture, payment, crossed phase, or generic R358.

## Applicability
Whenever a route produces a Hamilton P4 on q_1 plus three X vertices or q_{m-1} plus three X vertices, do not count support-Hamiltonicity alone as new progress: every such support is already Hamiltonian. A useful consumer must preserve an exact order/proposal, force a DEEP Q crossing, or couple the local P4 to nonlocal/right-side data.

## Persistence
Retain for each x the support-level existence of a Hamilton P4 on {q_1} union (X-{x}) and on {q_{m-1}} union (X-{x}). No canonical order is asserted.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not prescribe any Hamilton P4 order, synchronize the eight P4s, currentize them in one cover, or imply a spanning two-cover. Does not say a source-labelled order on one such support is useless; only bare support-Hamiltonicity is baseline.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** The only supporting proof P791 is invalid by an exact support omission, no replacement proof is known, and no live proof depends on R714. Preserve the statement and D4/broken-first-inward-hamiltonicity as a historical repair target/fence; do not present it as active mathematics until independently reproved.
- **Curation note:** Baseline support-Hamiltonicity fence: every first-inward X-complement four-set is already Hamiltonian, so producing another bare local P4 on such a support is not progress.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Durable baseline/fence: every first-inward X-complement four-set is Hamiltonian by R522, so bare LOCAL P4 support is not new progress.

## Proof
Let u=q_1. If X union {u} had a tight Hamilton P5, its support would be disjoint from the tight path Q[2,m] and the two supports partition V(H), contradicting pc(H)>2. Thus X+u is P5-free. Fix x in X and orient the three-set X-{x} as a tight trimer C, possible by R3 as included in the R594 frame. R594 says X has no Hamilton P4, so C+x has no Hamilton P4. Suppose C+u had no Hamilton P4. Accepted R522, applied to C with distinct outside vertices x,u, would then force a Hamilton P5 on C+{x,u}=X+u, contradiction. Thus C+u, equivalently {u} union (X-{x}), has a Hamilton P4. For s=q_{m-1}, a P5 on X+s together with Q[0,m-2] would two-cover H, so X+s is P5-free and the same argument gives the four right supports.

# R764 — Each X vertex in a minimum inward-anchor cover selects a unique P4 block or a unique GOOD/BAD seam

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Retain the accepted crossed beyond-order-ten inward-anchor five-cell frame with m>=6 and a minimum exact two-cover T of W=H-{q_2,q_{m-2}}, so sigma_G(T)=0. Write G_3={a,c}, G_4={b,z}, and let F_T be the contracted five-cell forest of T. Pending R763 applies. Fix an arbitrary vertex r in X={a,b,c,z}, and write S(r) for the unique contiguous T-block among {G_3,G_4} that contains r.

(P4-BLOCK) If S(r) has degree two in F_T, then S(r) is an internal X block. Pending R763(1) therefore supplies an explicit source-labelled tight Hamilton P4 whose middle physical dimer is exactly the oriented block S(r). In particular that P4 uses r.

(SEAM) If S(r) has degree one in F_T, let xi(r) be the unique selected T-state incident with S(r). Accepted R176 applied to xi(r) against the five-cell reference cover splits as follows. GOOD: both seam tests are good, and the output is a single spare-free cross-witness balanced pair whose selected state is xi(r), hence incident with S(r) and therefore with the X-layer of r. BAD: a seam test is bad, and the output is a reverse-trimer support K(r) determined by that blocked seam together with two alternative inward pins q_2 and q_{m-2}. The trimer K(r) uses at least one vertex of S(r), hence uses either r or the unique X-partner of r in S(r).

In the no-P4 source-sink residue of pending R763(2), both X blocks have degree one. Thus every r in X has a well-defined incident seam xi(r). Vertices in the same X block share that seam; vertices in opposite blocks determine the two distinguished endpoint transitions of the residue, namely the unique transition that leaves the oriented G_4 source block and the unique transition that enters the oriented G_3 sink block.

In particular, if a distinguished vertex x in X is supplied by an independent ledger (for example the mixed partner of a first-inward MIXED-SIBLING certificate), that ledger selects either a labelled P4 through x's X-block or a unique GOOD pair / BAD reverse trimer incident with x's layer, without a further shape classification and without an R436 step.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in the accepted crossed beyond-order-ten inward-anchor five-cell frame of R665/R667, m>=6, with T an exact two-cover of W=H-{q_2,q_{m-2}} in the minimum case sigma_G(T)=0. Use accepted R176 and pending R763.

## Scope
Noncircular R24 parent consumer of the R763 compression. It assigns to every X vertex a unique labelled P4 or a unique incident GOOD/BAD seam, before R436 or R312. No R5, R168, R169, R224, R533, R350, generic R358, R436, Reverse Ear, shape-specific A-F splice, or computation.

## Applicability
Use on any minimum H-{q_2,q_{m-2}} recompletion after pending R763. To consume a transported mixed-sibling ledger, instantiate r as the mixed partner x. To compare two good anchors, instantiate at both. Prefer a BAD seam at the distinguished layer: one reverse trimer, two inward pins. Do not invoke R436 or R312. Conditional on fresh review of R763.

## Persistence
Retain T, F_T, the block S(r), its degree, the labelled P4 in the P4-BLOCK branch, and in the SEAM branch the unique incident state xi(r) with its GOOD/BAD label, pair or reverse trimer, and both inward pin options. An independently supplied identity of r remains historical ledger data.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not close a labelled P4 or a BAD trimer. Does not treat sigma_G(T)>0. Does not assert that GOOD and BAD descendants coexist as current pairs. Does not require pending R759-R762 as proof dependencies; those ledgers are optional instantiators of r. Does not invoke R436, R312, or R171. Does not eliminate the Same-rail or Split-X residues, only names their distinguished seams at a chosen X vertex.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Retired by Integrator 2026-09-05: per-X minimum-seam naming was designed for transported-ledger routes that are now retired/fenced; no accepted dependents remain.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** With R763 now accepted, the degree-two/degree-one X-block split is valid. Degree two gives the labelled P4; degree one has a unique incident transition whose R176 GOOD/BAD classification gives exactly the stated seam data.

## Proof
Work in a minimum exact cover T of W=H-{q_2,q_{m-2}} as in accepted R665/R667, so each of G_3 and G_4 is one contiguous oriented dimer block of T. Pending R763 applies to T.

Fix r in X and let S(r) be its T-block. The contracted degree of S(r) in F_T is either two or one, because R763(2) records that a no-P4 residue has both X degrees equal to one, while R763(1) treats any degree-two X block as internal.

If that degree is two, R763(1) produces a labelled Hamilton P4 whose middle dimer is the oriented block S(r)=(s_0,s_1). Both vertices of S(r) lie on that P4, and r is one of those vertices.

If that degree is one, F_T has a unique edge at S(r). The corresponding selected T-state xi(r) is the unique intercell transition incident with S(r). Apply accepted R176 to the two path covers (five-cell reference, T) at this selected cross state. The persistence clause of R176 has two mechanisms. If both seam tests are good, the pair is the cross-witness pair of xi(r) and does not use an inward spare; this pair is incident with S(r) by construction. If a seam test is bad, R176 produces a reverse-trimer support from that blocked seam and uses a spare vertex outside W as the opposite singleton. The blocked seam of xi(r) is the junction of S(r) with its unique neighboring cell, so the reverse trimer uses a vertex of S(r). The available spares are q_2 and q_{m-2}. This is the BAD branch at r.

The last paragraph of the statement is only instantiation: a ledger that names a vertex of X selects the corresponding P4-block or seam. No property of that ledger is used in the case split.

# R888 — Integrable two-cover conjecture for edge-ordered complete graphs

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Conjecture. Every finite Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament whose comparison orientation Gamma(H) is acyclic has pc(H)<=2. Equivalently, for every total ordering of E(K_n), the vertex set of K_n can be partitioned into at most two vertex-disjoint increasing paths. A potentially useful strengthening is endpoint-flexibility: for every prescribed vertex v, such a two-path partition can be chosen with v exposed as an endpoint of one path.

## Hypotheses
Acyclic comparison orientation in the sense of the line-graph comparison representation, equivalently an edge-ordered complete graph. Paths are vertex-simple and increasing in the edge order; the two paths are vertex-disjoint and partition all vertices.

## Scope
New locality-escape conjecture suggested by the line-graph integrability representation. If true, any smallest counterexample to the main two-cover conjecture must have genuine comparison holonomy, so O4/O6 could restrict immediately to shortest comparison-cycle geometry.

## Applicability
Attack the acyclic/integrable branch independently of gate machinery. The globally largest edge and endpoint-flexibility are a promising induction handle, but no endpoint-flexibility theorem is currently proved.

## Persistence
Retain the equivalence with two increasing paths in an edge-ordered K_n and the stronger endpoint-flexibility candidate separately from the proved line-graph representation theorem.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Finite computation is evidence only. This revision does not claim the conjecture for n>=8, does not claim endpoint-flexibility, and does not infer anything about cyclic comparison orientations.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** active
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** PASS. Properly stated open integrable-branch conjecture; computational observations remain evidence only.

## Proof
No preferred proof was present in the authoritative Supabase record.

# R98 — Minimum-overlap three-butterfly transversal-or-hub dichotomy

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Let F be the family of supports of global-longest tight five-paths in the standing order-ten smallest counterexample. Choose A,B in F with minimum intersection size |A∩B|=3, and write S=A∩B, U=A\B, V=B\A, R=V(H)\(A∪B). Then exactly one of the following structural alternatives is available: (i) there exists C in F meeting R and omitting some vertex of S, in which case C has the exact block profile |C∩S|=2, |C∩U|=|C∩V|=|C∩R|=1; or (ii) no such C exists, every support meeting R has the form S∪{w,r} with w∈U∪V and r∈R, and for each s∈S every support D∈F with s∉D is R-free, contains exactly S\{s}, has three wing vertices meeting both U and V, and contains every wing vertex w that occurs in any R-touching support S∪{w,r}.

## Hypotheses
Standing order-ten smallest-counterexample case; A,B are a globally minimum-overlap pair in F and |A∩B|=3.

## Scope
Pure longest-support incidence statement in the minimum-overlap-three branch.

## Applicability
Use before opening representative-dependent crossing or return machinery. The first alternative is the four-block transversal branch; the second is the rigid support-incidence kernel.

## Persistence
The conclusion depends only on stable support membership and therefore persists across representative changes.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert that the transversal branch already yields overlap descent, nor that the hub kernel is impossible; it only classifies support incidences forced by minimum overlap, union F=V(H), and intersection F=empty.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** superseded
- **Lifecycle note:** Minimum-overlap-three transversal-or-hub dichotomy is conditional branch structure under a branch eliminated outright by C125/R127. Preserve as proof architecture, route canonical discovery to C125.
- **Curation note:** Minimum-overlap-three transversal-or-hub dichotomy is conditional branch structure under a branch eliminated outright by C125/R127. Preserve as proof architecture, route canonical discovery to C125.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Verified. Under minimum overlap |A∩B|=3, every support C satisfies |C∩A|,|C∩B|≥3. The four-block count forces any R-touching support omitting S to have profile (2,1,1,1). If no such support exists, R13 gives existence of R-touching supports and an S-omitting support for each s∈S; minimum-overlap comparisons then exclude two-R hubs and force every hub to be S∪{w,r}, while every s-omitting support is R-free, contains exactly S\{s}, meets both wings, and contains every hub wing. The statement accurately records this exhaustive dichotomy.

## Proof
Write a=|C∩S|, u=|C∩U|, v=|C∩V|, r=|C∩R| for C∈F. Since A,B are a minimum-overlap pair with |A∩B|=3, every C∈F satisfies |C∩A|=a+u≥3 and |C∩B|=a+v≥3. Also |S|=|R|=3, |U|=|V|=2, and a+u+v+r=5.

Suppose first that C meets R and omits some vertex of S, so r≥1 and a≤2. The inequalities exclude a=0 because u,v≤2. If a=1 then u=v=2, already using all five vertices and forcing r=0, contradiction. Hence a=2. Then u,v≥1, and because r≥1 while a+u+v+r=5, necessarily u=v=r=1. This is alternative (i).

Now assume no support meeting R omits a vertex of S. Because union F=V(H) by R13, there is at least one support meeting R, and every such support contains all three vertices of S. Any R-touching support C therefore uses its remaining two vertices outside S. It cannot use two vertices of R: if C=S∪{r1,r2}, then because intersection F is empty by R13, choose any s∈S and some D∈F with s∉D. By the no-transversal assumption D cannot meet R, since D would then meet R while omitting S. Thus D∩C⊆D∩S has size at most two, contradicting the global minimum intersection three. Hence every R-touching support has exactly one R vertex and exactly one wing vertex, i.e. C=S∪{w,r} with w∈U∪V.

Fix s∈S and any D∈F with s∉D, which exists by intersection F=empty. Again D is R-free by the no-transversal assumption. Put a_D=|D∩S|≤2. Compare D with an arbitrary hub support C=S∪{w,r}. Since D is R-free, |C∩D|=a_D+1_{w∈D}≥3. Therefore a_D cannot be at most one, so a_D=2, and necessarily w∈D. Thus D∩S=S\{s}. Since |D|=5 and D is R-free, D has exactly three vertices in U∪V. The minimum-overlap inequalities against A and B give |D∩U|≥1 and |D∩V|≥1. Finally, because the hub support C was arbitrary, D contains every wing vertex w that occurs in any R-touching support. This proves alternative (ii) and the dichotomy.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED/R98.md -->

# R99 — Minimum-overlap common-triple deletion gateway

**Record status:** `UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED`

## Statement
Let F be the family of supports of global-longest tight five-paths in the standing order-ten smallest counterexample. Choose A,B in F with globally minimum intersection |A∩B|=3, and write S=A∩B, U=A\B, V=B\A, R=V(H)\(A∪B). Then every exact two-cover T of H-S has unordered component profile 4+3. For the physical partition Pi={U,V,R}, t_Pi(T)=1+sigma with sigma>=0. Moreover sigma=0 if and only if one cover component is a tight trimer on R and the other is a tight four-path on U∪V obtained by concatenating a tight dimer on U and a tight dimer on V with exactly one inter-class transition. Otherwise sigma>=1 and hence t_Pi(T)>=2.

## Hypotheses
Standing order-ten smallest-counterexample case; A,B are a globally minimum-overlap pair in F with |A∩B|=3.

## Scope
Pure support/deletion geometry in the minimum-overlap-three butterfly branch.

## Applicability
Applies before choosing transversal versus hub in the R98 dichotomy.

## Persistence
The profile 4+3 conclusion and zero-excess classification depend only on the physical butterfly blocks and therefore are stable across representative changes; sigma itself remains cover-relative.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not classify the positive-excess case beyond t_Pi(T)>=2 and does not by itself produce a spanning two-cover.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** superseded
- **Lifecycle note:** Common-triple deletion gateway is conditional minimum-overlap-three machinery; C125/R127 eliminates the entire branch.
- **Curation note:** Common-triple deletion gateway is conditional minimum-overlap-three machinery; C125/R127 eliminates the entire branch.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Verified after tightening the zero-excess iff. A four-path merely supported on U∪V can alternate between the two wing classes and have multiple inter-class transitions; sigma=0 requires the four-component to concatenate the two wing dimers with exactly one U-V transition, while R is the trimer component.

## Proof
Let T be any exact two-cover of H-S. By R11, its component orders are 5+2 or 4+3. Suppose they are 5+2, and let D be the support of the order-five rail. By R9 every tight five-path is global-longest, so D belongs to F. But D is contained in H-S=U∪V∪R, while A=S∪U. Thus |D∩A|=|D∩U|≤2. This contradicts the hypothesis that A,B realize the globally minimum intersection size 3 among members of F. Therefore every exact two-cover T of H-S has profile 4+3.

Now use the fixed physical partition Pi={U,V,R}. Each two-vertex wing has intrinsic path-cover number one, and R has intrinsic path-cover number one by R8. Hence the sum of the three intrinsic class path-cover numbers is 3. Since T has two components, R7 gives t_Pi(T)=3-2+sigma=1+sigma with sigma≥0.

If sigma=0, R7 says each class restriction realizes its intrinsic minimum, so each of U,V,R occurs as one unbroken class-restriction path in T. Because t_Pi(T)=1, exactly one inter-class transition joins two of these three class paths, while the third class is the other cover component. The component profile has already been proved to be 4+3. The only union of two classes having size four is U∪V; the unions U∪R and V∪R have size five. Thus the R-class is a tight trimer component, while the other component is a tight four-path obtained by concatenating the U dimer and the V dimer with exactly one U-V transition. Conversely, any exact cover with precisely this structure has each class restriction at its intrinsic minimum and t_Pi(T)=1, so R7 gives sigma=0. If this canonical zero-excess cover does not occur, then sigma is a nonnegative integer different from zero, hence sigma≥1 and t_Pi(T)≥2.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/UNUSABLE/QUARANTINED/R99.md -->
