<!-- BEGIN FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R1000.md -->

# R1000 — Every physical component join is a merge, a monotone one-block transport, or a reverse-P4 rebuild

## Statement
Let G be a minimum-order counterexample to R888 and let F=A|B|C be any spanning increasing three-cover. Let t be the terminal of A and s the source of distinct component B, put e=lambda(ts), a=L_F(t) with a=-infinity when A={t}, and b=U_F(s) with b=+infinity when B={s}. Exactly one of the following strict-order regimes holds. (MERGE) a<e<b, in which case concatenating A followed by B through t->s gives a spanning increasing two-cover, impossible in G. (LOW) e<a and e<b; if A=(...,p,t), deleting p->t and adding t->s gives the increasing three-cover A^- | (t,B) | C, with the affected source and terminal boundary ranks both strictly decreased. (HIGH) a<e and b<e; if B=(s,q,...), deleting s->q and adding t->s gives the increasing three-cover (A,s) | B^+ | C, with both affected boundary ranks strictly increased. (DOUBLE) b<e<a; then A and B are nontrivial, writing A=(...,p,t), B=(s,q,...), the four-vertex path K=(q,s,t,p) is increasing. By R998, G-V(K) has an exact two-cover U|V, so K|U|V is a spanning increasing three-cover. Thus every blocked physical joining edge has an explicit completeness-specific escape operation; only the DOUBLE rebuild is not monotone in the global boundary potential.

## Hypotheses
G is a minimum-order R888 counterexample; F is a literal spanning increasing three-cover; A,B are distinct components with terminal t and source s.

## Scope
Completeness-specific physical edge-activation theorem. Pure edge order plus R888 subclass minimality through R998; no R980, threshold matching, longest-path route, or fixed seed union.

## Applicability
Use as the main fresh-edge augmentation interface. Repeated LOW/HIGH moves admit the finite boundary potential of R997; DOUBLE produces a literal reverse-endpoint P4 and discards the old complement ordering via R998.

## Persistence
Retain F,A,B,C,t,s,e,a,b and the exact regime. In LOW/HIGH retain the removed and added edges and new cover. In DOUBLE retain p,t,s,q, K=(q,s,t,p), and a fresh exact complement cover U|V.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not prove that repeated DOUBLE rebuilds terminate or that one rebuild improves any global potential. Does not assert synchronization between U|V and the discarded portions of A|B|C.

## Proof
Let F=A|B|C, with t the terminal of A and s the source of B. Put e=lambda(ts), a=L_F(t), b=U_F(s), using -infinity and +infinity at singleton boundaries. Because edge labels are distinct, e differs from every finite boundary edge incident with t or s. Therefore exactly one of the four relative-order regimes holds: a<e<b; e<a and e<b; a<e and b<e; or b<e<a. In the first regime, every inherited turn of A and B remains increasing and the only new junction is the edge t->s. At t we have a<e, and at s we have e<b, so A followed by B is increasing; with C this is a spanning two-cover, impossible in a counterexample. In the LOW regime e<a forces A nontrivial; write its last edge p->t, so lambda(pt)=a. Delete p->t and add t->s. The resulting components are the prefix A^- ending at p, the path t followed by all of B, and C. The new path begins with edge ts of label e and then, when B is nontrivial, its old first edge has label b>e; hence it is increasing. The prefix and C are inherited. Thus this is an increasing three-cover. If ordinary edge ranks are used with the singleton sentinel below all edge ranks, the new terminal boundary of A^- is the edge preceding pt, hence has rank strictly below rank(a), while the new source boundary of tB is e, strictly below b. The HIGH regime is dual: b<e forces B nontrivial; write its first edge s->q of label b. Delete s->q and add t->s. The resulting paths are A followed by s, the suffix B^+ beginning at q, and C. Since a<e, the first path is increasing; the new terminal boundary is e>a, and the new source boundary of B^+ is the next B-edge after sq, which has rank strictly above b, with the singleton sentinel above all ranks if the suffix is a singleton. Finally suppose b<e<a. Then both A and B are nontrivial. Write A=(...,p,t) and B=(s,q,...). The ordinary undirected edge labels satisfy lambda(qs)=b<e=lambda(st)<a=lambda(tp). Therefore K=(q,s,t,p) is a vertex-simple increasing P4. It is proper because C is a nonempty third component. Apply R998 to K: the induced complement G-V(K) has exact increasing path-cover number two, so choose an exact two-cover U|V. Then K|U|V is a spanning increasing three-cover containing the reverse-endpoint P4 literally. This proves the trichotomy and all stated constructions.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R1000.md -->

# R1001 — Disjoint global extreme edges force crossed endpoint shields on one shared complement cover

## Statement
Let G be a minimum-order counterexample to R888. Let m0m1 be the globally minimum edge and M0M1 the globally maximum edge, and assume these two physical edges are vertex-disjoint. Put W=V(G)-{m0,m1,M0,M1}. By R998, pc_inc(G[W])=2; fix any exact two-cover U|V of W, with sources s_U,s_V and terminals t_U,t_V. For h,k in {0,1}, the path K_{h,k}=(m_{1-h},m_h,M_k,M_{1-k}) is increasing, so K_{h,k}|U|V is a spanning three-cover. Define terminal activity T_R to mean that for some k, L_R(t_R)<lambda(t_R M_k), and source activity S_R to mean that for some h, lambda(m_h s_R)<U_R(s_R). If T_U and S_V both hold, then for suitable independent choices h,k accepted R956 applied to the middle edge m_h->M_k of K_{h,k} gives a spanning two-cover of G. Likewise T_V and S_U cannot both hold. Hence every such U|V satisfies the crossed shield clauses (not T_U or not S_V) and (not T_V or not S_U). Equivalently: either both edges from t_U to {M0,M1} lie below L_R(t_U), or both edges from {m0,m1} to s_V lie above U_R(s_V); and symmetrically with U,V exchanged.

## Hypotheses
G is a minimum-order R888 counterexample; its unique global minimum and maximum edges are vertex-disjoint; U|V is any exact two-cover of their four-vertex complement.

## Scope
Completeness-specific synchronized extreme-edge carrier lemma. Uses one common complement representative for four Hamilton P4 orientations and accepted R956 cooperative splicing.

## Applicability
Use to convert failure of all four global-extreme carrier splices into explicit pairwise endpoint shields on a fixed complement two-cover. The two endpoint choices are independent and no selected-state transport between complement representatives is used.

## Persistence
Retain the global extreme edges, W, one exact U|V, its four endpoints, the four carrier paths K_{h,k}, and which literal shield clause holds in each crossed direction.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not prove the shield clauses are contradictory. Does not prescribe which disjunct holds. Does not cover the case where the global minimum and maximum edges share a vertex.

## Proof
Let mu=lambda(m0m1) be the global minimum edge label and Omega=lambda(M0M1) the global maximum. For every h,k in {0,1}, K_{h,k}=(m_{1-h},m_h,M_k,M_{1-k}) has consecutive labels mu, lambda(m_h M_k), Omega, hence is increasing. Its vertex support X={m0,m1,M0,M1} is independent of h,k. By R998, W=V(G)-X has exact path-cover number two; fix one exact two-cover U|V once and for all. Then K_{h,k}|U|V is a spanning increasing three-cover for every h,k. Write t_U for the terminal of U and s_V for the source of V. Suppose terminal activity T_U holds and source activity S_V holds. Choose k with L_U(t_U)<lambda(t_U M_k) and choose h with lambda(m_h s_V)<U_V(s_V). Apply accepted R956 to the three components A=U, C=K_{h,k}, B=V and to the selected middle carrier edge p->v=m_h->M_k. The first R956 seam condition is L_U(t_U)<lambda(t_U M_k)<U_K(M_k). Its left inequality is the chosen terminal activity, while U_K(M_k)=Omega because M_k->M_{1-k} is the global maximum edge, so the right inequality is automatic. The second seam condition is L_K(m_h)<lambda(m_h s_V)<U_V(s_V). Its right inequality is the chosen source activity, while L_K(m_h)=mu because m_{1-h}->m_h is the global minimum edge, so the left inequality is automatic. Hence R956 gives a spanning increasing two-cover of G, contradiction. Thus not(T_U and S_V), which is the first crossed shield clause. Interchanging U and V gives not(T_V and S_U). Finally, because all edge labels are distinct, failure of T_U means both lambda(t_U M_0),lambda(t_U M_1) are strictly below L_U(t_U); failure of S_V means both lambda(m_0 s_V),lambda(m_1 s_V) are strictly above U_V(s_V), and similarly after swapping U,V. This proves the equivalent shield formulation.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R1001.md -->

# FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R1002.md

# R1002 — Pair deletion in a minimum R888 counterexample has exact two-cover number and no singleton rail

## Statement
Let G be a minimum-order counterexample to R888 and let x,y be distinct vertices. Then pc_inc(G-{x,y})=2. Moreover every exact two-path cover G-{x,y}=U|V has |U|,|V|>=2.

## Hypotheses
G is a minimum-order counterexample to R888; x,y are distinct physical vertices.

## Scope
Pure edge-ordered pair-deletion rigidity. R888-subclass analogue of the full-boundary pair-deletion theorem, proved independently from edge-order minimality.

## Applicability
Use whenever a prescribed physical pair is deleted and a nontrivial exact two-cover is required, including reverse-P4 middle-dimer recompletion.

## Persistence
Retain the deleted pair and the chosen exact pair-deletion cover; nontriviality is universal over every exact cover of that deletion.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not prescribe endpoint locations, rail supports, or a canonical representative. Does not synchronize covers of different pair deletions.

## Proof
Fix distinct x,y and put H=G-{x,y}. Since H is a smaller edge-ordered complete graph than the minimum counterexample G, pc_inc(H)<=2. If pc_inc(H)=1, let P be an increasing Hamilton path of H. The dimer (x,y) is vacuously increasing, so P|(x,y) is a spanning two-cover of G, contradiction. Hence pc_inc(H)=2. Now let U|V be any exact two-cover of H. Suppose U is a singleton {z}. Then V is an increasing Hamilton path on V(G)-{x,y,z}. The three physical vertices x,y,z induce a triangle whose three edge labels are distinct. Let e_1<e_2<e_3 be those labels. The edges carrying e_1 and e_2 share one vertex, because every two edges of a triangle do. Orient the three vertices so that the e_1 edge is traversed first and the e_2 edge second. This is an increasing Hamilton trimer Q on {x,y,z}. Then Q|V is a spanning two-cover of G, contradiction. Thus U is nontrivial; the same argument applies to V. Therefore every exact pair-deletion two-cover has both rails of order at least two.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R1002.md -->

# R1003 — A doubly extreme-shielded Hamilton rail need not absorb the global extreme four-set

## Statement
There exists an edge ordering of K8 with globally minimum edge 01 and globally maximum edge 23, disjoint, and with U=(4,5,6,7) an increasing Hamilton path on the other four vertices, such that both edges from {0,1} to the source 4 lie strictly above the first U-edge 45 and both edges from the terminal 7 to {2,3} lie strictly below the last U-edge 67, yet the full K8 has no increasing Hamilton path. One exact order is 01<03<13<46<26<45<35<27<57<17<04<37<47<36<12<02<25<14<16<05<34<56<06<24<07<67<15<23. Here rank(45)=5<rank(04)=10,rank(14)=17 and rank(27)=7,rank(37)=11<rank(67)=25. Exhaustive checking of all 8! vertex orders finds no Hamilton increasing path. Nevertheless {0}|(6,4,5,7,1,2,3) is a spanning two-cover with long-path edge ranks 3<5<8<9<14<27.

## Hypotheses
Pure finite edge-ordered K8 example.

## Scope
Exact route fence for consuming the mixed doubly-shielded branch of R1001 by Hamiltonizing the shielded rail together with the four global-extreme endpoints alone.

## Applicability
Use to reject any proposed theorem that disjoint global extreme edges plus one Hamilton rail shielded at both ends must have Hamilton union. Any R1001 consumer must use the second complement rail or additional representative exchange.

## Persistence
Retain the full 28-edge order, U=(4,5,6,7), the four shield inequalities, exhaustive 8! Hamilton check, and explicit two-cover.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not refute R888 or R1001. Does not say the full three-cover extreme-carrier configuration is trapped; the graph is explicitly two-coverable.

## Proof
Number the displayed edges from rank 0 through 27. The global minimum is 01 at rank 0 and the global maximum is 23 at rank 27. On U=(4,5,6,7), the selected ranks are rank(45)=5<rank(56)=21<rank(67)=25, so U is increasing. Its source is 4 and terminal is 7. The two minimum-pair-to-source edges have ranks rank(04)=10 and rank(14)=17, both strictly above rank(45)=5. The two terminal-to-maximum-pair edges have ranks rank(27)=7 and rank(37)=11, both strictly below rank(67)=25. Thus U has both R1001-style extreme shields. To certify non-Hamiltonicity, enumerate all 8!=40320 ordered vertex lists (v0,...,v7); for each compute the seven ranks of consecutive ordinary edges and accept only if they are strictly increasing. None is accepted. Finally the path (6,4,5,7,1,2,3) has edge ranks 3,5,8,9,14,27, strictly increasing. Together with singleton {0} it is a spanning two-cover.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R1003.md -->

# FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R1004.md

<!-- BEGIN FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R1004.md -->

# R1004 — Extreme dimers turn failed cooperative splices into two-end barrier corridors

## Statement
Let G be a finite edge-ordered complete graph with pc_inc(G)>2. MINIMUM-DIMER CORRIDOR: suppose G has a spanning increasing three-cover D|A|B where D is the dimer on vertices x,y and xy is the globally minimum edge. Orient A,B increasingly. Let p->v be any selected edge of A and let s be the source of B. If L_A(p)<lambda(ps)<U_B(s), then lambda(xv)>=U_A(v) and lambda(yv)>=U_A(v). MAXIMUM-DIMER CORRIDOR: suppose instead D is the dimer on vertices X,Y and XY is the globally maximum edge. Let p->v be any selected edge of A and t the terminal of B. If L_B(t)<lambda(tv)<U_A(v), then lambda(pX)<=L_A(p) and lambda(pY)<=L_A(p). Thus failure of all R956 cooperative splices with an extreme dimer produces simultaneous two-end successor barriers in the minimum case and simultaneous two-end predecessor barriers in the maximum case.

## Hypotheses
Pure finite edge-ordered complete graph; spanning increasing three-cover with one dimer component whose physical edge is globally minimum or globally maximum; pc_inc(G)>2.

## Scope
Pure edge-order cooperative-splice obstruction. No minimum-counterexample assumption, R980, threshold matching, longest-path hypothesis, or representative synchronization beyond the displayed literal three-cover.

## Applicability
Use after introducing a global extreme edge as a literal dimer rail. In the minimum case, every cut p->v whose prefix endpoint p is broad-compatible with the source of the third rail forces both extreme-edge endpoints to lie above the outgoing boundary at v. The maximum case is the exact dual.

## Persistence
Retain the literal dimer D, the selected cut p->v, the other rail source/terminal, the exact broad-compatibility inequality, and both forced endpoint inequalities.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert that broad-compatible cuts exist, that the resulting barriers are separated, that R949 applies automatically, or that the corridor closes G. Does not prove R888.

## Proof
MINIMUM-DIMER CORRIDOR. Let D have physical vertices x,y and globally minimum edge xy. Fix selected p->v of A and source s of B with L_A(p)<lambda(ps)<U_B(s). First orient D as (x,y), so its terminal is y and L_D(y)=lambda(xy). Since xy is globally minimum and yv is a different physical edge, lambda(xy)<lambda(yv). If lambda(yv)<U_A(v), then both R956 inequalities hold: L_D(y)<lambda(yv)<U_A(v) and L_A(p)<lambda(ps)<U_B(s). Accepted R956 would then reduce the displayed three-cover to two increasing paths, contradicting pc_inc(G)>2. Hence lambda(yv)>=U_A(v). Reverse the vacuous dimer orientation to (y,x). The same three-cover remains increasing, now with terminal x and L_D(x)=lambda(xy). Again global minimality gives lambda(xy)<lambda(xv). The same R956 application shows lambda(xv)>=U_A(v). This proves the minimum case. MAXIMUM-DIMER CORRIDOR. Let D have physical vertices X,Y and globally maximum edge XY. Fix selected p->v of A and terminal t of B with L_B(t)<lambda(tv)<U_A(v). Orient D as (X,Y), so its source is X and U_D(X)=lambda(XY). Since XY is globally maximum and pX is different, lambda(pX)<lambda(XY)=U_D(X). If L_A(p)<lambda(pX), then R956 applied with terminal t of B, source X of D, and selected edge p->v of A has both seam inequalities: L_B(t)<lambda(tv)<U_A(v) and L_A(p)<lambda(pX)<U_D(X). This would two-cover G, contradiction. Therefore lambda(pX)<=L_A(p). Reversing D to (Y,X) gives identically lambda(pY)<=L_A(p). No other property is used.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R1004.md -->

# FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R1005.md

<!-- BEGIN FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R1005.md -->

# R1005 — A minimum-side exact two-cover has no rail-shortening broad cut

## Statement
Let H be a finite edge-ordered complete graph with pc_inc(H)=2. Among all exact two-path covers of H choose A|B so that |A| is minimum among the cardinalities of all rails occurring in exact two-covers of H; orient A=(a_0,...,a_m) and B=(b_0,...,b_r) increasingly. Then for every selected edge a_i->a_{i+1} of A, neither of the following holds: (SOURCE ROTATION) L_A(a_i)<lambda(a_i b_0)<U_B(b_0); (TERMINAL ROTATION) L_B(b_r)<lambda(b_r a_{i+1})<U_A(a_{i+1}). Indeed either condition would rotate A|B into another exact two-cover having a proper prefix or suffix of A as one rail, contradicting the choice of |A|. If |A|>=2, neither endpoint a_0 nor a_m is insertable into an internal gap of B in the displayed B-order; hence accepted R895 gives canonical barriers beta_B(a_0), beta_B(a_m). More quantitatively, writing k=|A| and l=|B|: if beta_B(a_0)=j>=l-k, then lambda(b_j a_0)>=U_A(a_0); and if beta_B(a_m)=j<=k-2, then lambda(a_m b_{j+1})<=L_A(a_m).

## Hypotheses
Finite edge-ordered complete graph H with increasing path-cover number exactly two; A|B is an exact two-cover whose rail A has globally minimum rail cardinality among all exact two-covers.

## Scope
Pure edge-order representative-extremality normal form. No R888 minimality, R980, threshold matching, or longest-path hypothesis.

## Applicability
Use for a pair-deleted complement or any exact two-cover family when representative changes are allowed. It converts the no-broad-compatible-cut alternative into a canonical minimum-side normal form and supplies honest R895 barriers for the endpoints of the minimum rail.

## Persistence
Retain the exact A|B representative, k,l, all source/terminal broad-cut failures on A, and when |A|>=2 the two endpoint barriers on B with the size-sensitive high/low consequences.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not make the endpoints of B noninsertable into A. Does not assert the two endpoint barriers are distinct or force a two-cover of a larger ambient graph.

## Proof
Write A=(a_0,...,a_m), B=(b_0,...,b_r), k=|A|=m+1, l=|B|=r+1. SOURCE ROTATION ON A. Suppose for some i, 0<=i<=m-1, L_A(a_i)<lambda(a_i b_0)<U_B(b_0). Then C=(a_0,...,a_i,b_0,...,b_r) is increasing: all inherited turns are unchanged and the displayed two inequalities are exactly the new seam conditions. The suffix S=(a_{i+1},...,a_m) is increasing. Thus C|S is an exact two-cover of H and |S|=m-i<k, contradicting the choice of A. TERMINAL ROTATION ON A is dual: if L_B(b_r)<lambda(b_r a_{i+1})<U_A(a_{i+1}), then P=(a_0,...,a_i) and C=(b_0,...,b_r,a_{i+1},...,a_m) form an exact two-cover with |P|=i+1<k, contradiction. ENDPOINT NONINSERTABILITY. Assume k>=2. If a_0 were insertable into an internal gap of B in the displayed order, the resulting Hamilton path on V(B)+{a_0}, together with A-a_0=(a_1,...,a_m), would be an exact two-cover having a rail of size k-1, contradiction. The same argument applies to a_m, using A-a_m=(a_0,...,a_{m-1}). Hence R895 supplies beta_B(a_0), beta_B(a_m). SIZE-SENSITIVE SOURCE BARRIER. Put beta_B(a_0)=j and assume j>=l-k. R895 left-feasibility at the canonical barrier gives L_B(b_j)<lambda(b_j a_0). If also lambda(b_j a_0)<U_A(a_0), then cutting B after b_j and appending A gives the exact cover (b_0,...,b_j) | (b_{j+1},...,b_r,a_0,...,a_m), after choosing the equivalent source-rotation ordering A after the B prefix? More directly use C=(b_0,...,b_j,a_0,...,a_m) and S=(b_{j+1},...,b_r): the displayed inequalities make C increasing and |S|=l-j-1<=k-1, contradiction. Therefore lambda(b_j a_0)>=U_A(a_0). SIZE-SENSITIVE TERMINAL BARRIER. Put beta_B(a_m)=j and assume j<=k-2. R895 right-feasibility gives lambda(a_m b_{j+1})<U_B(b_{j+1}). If also L_A(a_m)<lambda(a_m b_{j+1}), then C=(a_0,...,a_m,b_{j+1},...,b_r) and P=(b_0,...,b_j) form an exact two-cover; |P|=j+1<=k-1, contradiction. Hence lambda(a_m b_{j+1})<=L_A(a_m). This proves all assertions.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R1005.md -->

# R1006 — A dimer rail in a pair-deletion complement lifts to a trimer singleton fiber

## Statement
Let G be a minimum-order counterexample to R888 and let x,y be distinct vertices. Suppose an exact two-cover of G-{x,y} has a dimer rail {a,b} and opposite rail B. Then G-x has an exact two-cover T|B in which T is an increasing trimer on {y,a,b}. Consequently |B|>=6. The same conclusion holds with x and y interchanged.

## Hypotheses
G is a minimum-order R888 counterexample; G-{x,y} has an exact two-cover with one rail of order two.

## Scope
Pure R888 short pair-deletion bridge into the accepted singleton trimer-fiber theory.

## Applicability
Use after R1005 or any pair-deletion argument reaches a dimer minimum rail. It converts the residue into the already-developed trimer singleton-deletion branch.

## Persistence
Retain the deleted pair x,y, the pair-deletion dimer {a,b}, an explicit increasing order T on {y,a,b}, and the same opposite rail B.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not eliminate dimer pair-deletion rails when the opposite rail has order at least six. Does not choose a canonical trimer orientation.

## Proof
Let G-{x,y}={a,b}|B with {a,b} a dimer rail. On the three vertices {y,a,b}, choose the two smallest of their three ordinary edge labels. Those two edges share a vertex, so orient the three vertices through their common endpoint in the order of the two labels; this gives an increasing trimer T on {y,a,b}. Hence G-x=T|B is an exact two-path cover: T covers y,a,b and B is inherited unchanged. Accepted R959 applies to every exact singleton-deletion two-cover in a minimum R888 counterexample, so |B|>=3. If |B|=3, this is a trimer/trimer singleton-deletion cover, excluded by accepted R978. If |B| is 4 or 5, it is excluded by accepted R975. Therefore |B|>=6. Interchanging x and y gives the symmetric assertion.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R1006.md -->

# R1007 — A trimer rail in a pair-deletion complement forces a fixed-complement four-rail singleton fiber

## Statement
Let G be a minimum-order counterexample to R888 and let x,y be distinct vertices. Suppose G-{x,y}=T|B is an exact two-cover with |T|=3. Then at least one of the four-sets V(T) union {x} and V(T) union {y} is Hamiltonian. Consequently, for at least one z in {x,y}, the singleton deletion G-z has an exact two-cover P|B in which P is a Hamilton path on V(T) union ({x,y}-{z}) and therefore has order four; the opposite rail is literally the same B as in the pair-deletion cover. If both four-sets are Hamiltonian, both singleton fibers may be chosen with the same complement rail B.

## Hypotheses
G is a minimum-order R888 counterexample; a prescribed pair deletion has an exact two-cover with a trimer rail T and opposite rail B.

## Scope
Pure R888 pair-deletion trimer bridge using the accepted local five-vertex theorem R963.

## Applicability
Use after a pair-deletion or minimum-side representative reaches a trimer rail. It upgrades to one or two singleton-deletion four-rail covers while preserving the opposite rail exactly.

## Persistence
Retain x,y, the literal trimer support V(T), the same opposite rail B, and whichever Hamilton four-set extension is obtained.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert both deleted vertices extend T. Does not classify the resulting four-vertex rail or close the singleton fiber.

## Proof
Let S=V(T), |S|=3. Suppose for contradiction that neither S union {x} nor S union {y} is Hamiltonian. Accepted R963 applies to the common triangle S and the two exterior vertices x,y, and yields an increasing Hamilton path P on S union {x,y}. Since B is disjoint from S union {x,y} and is already an increasing Hamilton path on its support, P|B is a spanning two-path cover of G, contradicting that G is a counterexample to R888. Hence at least one of S+x,S+y is Hamiltonian. If S+y is Hamiltonian, choose a Hamilton path P_y on it. Then G-x=P_y|B is an exact two-cover with a four-vertex rail and the literal unchanged complement rail B. The case S+x is symmetric. If both four-sets are Hamiltonian, both exact singleton-deletion covers exist simultaneously with the same B.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R1007.md -->

# R1008 — In a non-Hamiltonian edge-ordered K4 the mate of a minimum edge is locally second-smallest

## Statement
Let X={x,y,a,b} induce an edge-ordered K4 with no increasing Hamilton path. If xy is the smallest of the six edges of X, then the opposite edge ab is smaller than each of xa,xb,ya,yb. Hence xy and ab are the two locally smallest edges of X. In the standard transitive matching-height boundary orientation induced by the edge order, the opposite pair {xy,ab} is the top matching level M_R (because a turn is tight when its first edge is earlier).

## Hypotheses
Pure edge-ordered K4; X has no increasing Hamilton P4; xy is the minimum edge of X.

## Scope
Pure four-vertex edge-order lemma.

## Applicability
Use when a critical non-Hamiltonian four-cell contains a globally minimum physical edge. It identifies the opposite mate as the other locally low edge and fixes the matching-level normalization.

## Persistence
Retain X, the minimum edge xy, its opposite edge ab, and the four strict inequalities ab<xa,ab<xb,ab<ya,ab<yb.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not classify the order among the four cross edges and does not imply a fifth vertex Hamiltonizes X.

## Proof
Assume xy is the minimum edge of X. If ya<ab, then (x,y,a,b) has edge-label sequence xy<ya<ab and is an increasing Hamilton path, contradiction. If yb<ab, then (x,y,b,a) is increasing. If xa<ab, then (y,x,a,b) is increasing. If xb<ab, then (y,x,b,a) is increasing. Therefore ab is smaller than all four cross edges xa,xb,ya,yb. Since xy is already the minimum edge, ab is the second-smallest edge of the induced K4. For the matching-height interpretation, adjacent edges in a tight ordered triple satisfy first-edge<label second-edge. Thus the matching class whose edges are locally earliest is the top class in the convention M_R>M_S>M_L used by the accepted transitive-cell toolkit, so the opposite pair {xy,ab} is M_R.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R1008.md -->

# FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R1010.md

<!-- BEGIN FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R1010.md -->

# R1010 — A minimum-edge root requirement can fail even in a two-coverable edge-ordered complete graph

## Statement
Let H be an edge-ordered complete graph on h vertices such that (i) H has a spanning cover by two increasing paths and (ii) every increasing path of H has order at most h-2. Form G from H by adding vertices x,y, placing xy below every old H-edge, preserving the old order on E(H), and placing every xH- and yH-edge above every old H-edge. Then G has a spanning cover by two increasing paths, but no spanning two-path cover of G selects the globally minimum edge xy. Consequently the proposed Extreme-Edge Root Theorem is false. A concrete ten-vertex instance follows from accepted R823: take its n=8 matching-layer construction with parts A,B of size four, choose the internal order so that each part has an increasing Hamilton path, and then apply the two-vertex extension.

## Hypotheses
Finite edge-ordered complete graph H with a spanning two-increasing-path cover and longest increasing path order at most |H|-2; G is the displayed two-vertex extreme extension. For the concrete K10 instance use R823 at n=8 with internal edge order chosen to make both four-vertex parts Hamiltonian.

## Scope
Pure edge-ordered counterexample family, with a concrete K10 instance. It is a fence against forcing the globally minimum edge into a spanning two-cover, not against R888 itself.

## Applicability
Use to reject any proof strategy whose parent theorem requires every edge-ordered complete graph to admit a two-cover selecting its global minimum edge. The minimum edge may remain a boundary condition, but successful covers must be allowed to avoid it.

## Persistence
Retain H, its longest-path bound, one explicit two-cover of H, new vertices x,y, the block order xy < E(H) < all new spokes, and the proof that any xy-containing increasing path contains at most one old H-vertex. For the concrete instance retain the R823 A|B partition with |A|=|B|=4.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not refute R888. Does not show a minimum R888 counterexample can have this extension form. Does not reopen longest-complement research.

## Proof
Generic extension. Let H have h vertices, let P|Q be a spanning two-cover of H, and assume every increasing path in H has order at most h-2. Add x,y. Order xy first, then all old edges in their H-order, then all spokes from {x,y} to H. Because every spoke is later than every old edge, append x to the terminal of P and y to the terminal of Q. This gives a spanning two-cover of G.\n\nSuppose instead that a spanning two-cover of G selects xy. Since xy is globally minimum, it is the first edge of its rail. Once that rail next enters H through a spoke, that spoke is later than every H-edge, so no further old H-edge can follow. Hence the xy-rail contains at most one old vertex. The other rail is contained in H and must cover at least h-1 old vertices, contradicting the longest-path bound h-2. Thus no spanning two-cover selects xy.\n\nConcrete K10 instance. Apply accepted R823 with n=8, m=4. Partition H into A={0,1,2,3} and B={4,5,6,7}. Put every internal edge below every cross edge; choose the internal strict order so that 01<12<23 and 45<56<67, hence A and B themselves are increasing Hamilton paths. Decompose E(A,B) into four perfect matchings and order those matching blocks as in R823. The accepted theorem gives longest increasing path order at most m+ceil(m/2)=6=8-2. Therefore H satisfies the generic hypotheses. Add x=8,y=9 with 89 below all H-edges and all sixteen new spokes above all H-edges. Then (0,1,2,3,8)|(4,5,6,7,9) is a spanning two-cover of K10, but no spanning two-cover selects 89.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R1010.md -->

# FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R1011.md

<!-- BEGIN FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R1011.md -->

# R1011 — Minimum complement rail size alone cannot drive extreme-edge representative descent

## Statement
There exists a two-coverable edge-ordered K10 with globally minimum edge 89 such that H=G-{8,9} has exact two-cover number two and minimum possible rail size exactly two, yet no spanning two-cover of G selects 89. Concretely let H be the n=8 R823 matching-layer construction with A={0,1,2,3}, B={4,5,6,7}, internal order 01<45<12<56<23<67<02<03<13<46<47<57, and cross matching blocks (04,15,26,37)<(05,16,27,34)<(06,17,24,35)<(07,14,25,36), with the displayed within-block order. Then H has longest increasing path order at most six, and it has the exact 2+6 cover (0,1)|(5,6,7,3,4,2). Hence no exact two-cover of H has a singleton rail, so the minimum rail size is exactly two. Add 8,9 with 89 below every H-edge and every 8H,9H spoke above every H-edge. Then G is two-coverable but no two-cover selects 89, as in R1010. Therefore a representative descent theorem whose only strictly decreasing coordinate is the minimum complement rail size is false.

## Hypotheses
Explicit R823-based K8 complement H and the two-vertex extreme extension G described in the statement.

## Scope
Exact finite fence against using minimum complement rail cardinality as the sole termination potential in the minimum-edge activation program. Not a counterexample to R888.

## Applicability
Use when designing representative-descent signatures after the failure of the universal minimum-edge root theorem. Any viable potential must include additional physical obstruction data beyond minimum rail size.

## Persistence
Retain the explicit H edge order, the 2+6 cover, the R823 longest-path bound six, the absence of any singleton+Hamilton cover, and the extreme extension order 89 < E(H) < all new spokes.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not rule out lexicographic potentials beginning with rail size and then using barrier widths, extension-Hall type, or other coordinates. Does not refute R888.

## Proof
Take H on vertices 0,...,7 with A={0,1,2,3}, B={4,5,6,7}. Order the twelve internal edges by 01<45<12<56<23<67<02<03<13<46<47<57. Order the sixteen cross edges in the four perfect-matching blocks M1=(04,15,26,37), M2=(05,16,27,34), M3=(06,17,24,35), M4=(07,14,25,36), with all of M1 before M2 before M3 before M4 and with the displayed strict order within each block. This is an instance of accepted R823 at n=8,m=4, so every increasing path has order at most 4+ceil(4/2)=6.\n\nThe paths (0,1) and (5,6,7,3,4,2) form an exact two-cover: the long path uses edges 56<67<37<34<24, which lie respectively at ranks 3,5,15,19,22 in the displayed order. Thus the minimum rail size among exact two-covers is at most two. It cannot be one, because a singleton rail would require the other seven vertices to form an increasing Hamilton path of order seven, contradicting the R823 bound six. Hence the minimum rail size is exactly two.\n\nNow add vertices 8,9, place 89 below every H-edge, and place every edge from {8,9} to H above every H-edge. By R1010, the resulting K10 is two-coverable but no spanning two-cover selects 89. In particular, starting from any complement representative of minimum rail size two, there is no representative with strictly smaller minimum rail size, while the desired minimum-edge-rooted cover still does not exist. Thus minimum rail cardinality alone cannot be the strict descent coordinate.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R1011.md -->

# FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R1012.md

<!-- BEGIN FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R1012.md -->

# R1012 — Pair-deletion Hamilton-extension Hall obstruction compresses dimer and trimer short rails

## Statement
Let G be an edge-ordered complete graph with pc_inc(G)>2, let x,y be distinct vertices, and let G-{x,y}=A|B be an exact two-cover by Hamilton rail supports A,B. Form the bipartite Hamilton-extension graph E with left side {x,y}, right side {A,B}, and z~R exactly when G[V(R) union {z}] is Hamiltonian. Then nu(E)<=1. Equivalently E has a vertex cover of size at most one, so every representative has an endpoint obstruction (one deleted vertex Hamilton-extends neither rail) or a rail obstruction (one rail is Hamilton-extendable by neither deleted vertex), possibly both. If |A|=2, then x~A and y~A automatically because every three-vertex edge-ordered complete graph is Hamiltonian; hence x not~B and y not~B, so B is rail-obstructed. If |A|=3, accepted R963 forbids x not~A and y not~A simultaneously, because then A+x+y would be Hamiltonian and together with B would two-cover G. Thus for a trimer rail at least one of x,y extends A; if both extend A then B is obstructed by both, while if exactly one extends A the other deleted vertex is an endpoint obstruction.

## Hypotheses
Finite edge-ordered complete graph G with path-cover number greater than two; x,y distinct; G-{x,y} has the displayed exact Hamilton two-cover A|B. The trimer clause uses accepted R963.

## Scope
Pure support-level Hall compression for pair-deletion covers, with exact dimer/trimer short-rail consequences. No global-minimum-edge assumption, R980, threshold matching, or representative synchronization.

## Applicability
Use after choosing any pair-deletion representative in a hypothetical R888 counterexample. A perfect extension matching is immediate closure; the short-rail residuals are forced into a large-rail obstruction or a single blocked endpoint, feeding the accepted trimer/fixed-complement machinery.

## Persistence
Retain x,y, the literal rail supports A,B, the four Hamilton-extension truth values, the size-one Hall vertex cover, and in the short cases which endpoint or opposite rail is obstructed.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not prove the rank-one obstruction impossible for rails of order at least four. Does not assert the Hall obstruction type is invariant under representative change. Does not close the trimer branch by itself.

## Proof
Let E be the displayed bipartite graph. If E had a matching of size two, after possibly swapping A and B we would have Hamilton paths on A+x and B+y. Their supports are disjoint and partition V(G), so they form a spanning two-cover of G, contradicting pc_inc(G)>2. Hence nu(E)<=1. In a bipartite graph on two vertices per side, König gives a vertex cover of size at most one. If the covering vertex lies on {x,y}, that deleted endpoint is adjacent to neither rail after removing the cover vertex formulation equivalently all extension edges are incident with the other endpoint; phrased directly, one endpoint is an obstruction whenever one left vertex has degree zero. If the covering vertex lies on {A,B}, all extension edges are incident with the other rail, equivalently one rail is obstructed by both endpoints. These possibilities include the empty graph and single-edge overlaps, so the stated endpoint/rail obstruction formulation is exhaustive.\n\nIf |A|=2, then A+z has three vertices for z=x and z=y. Every edge-ordered K3 has an increasing Hamilton path: choose its two smallest incident-in-a-path edges in increasing order, or simply orient the two edges of any length-two path from smaller to larger. Thus x~A and y~A. Since nu(E)<=1, neither x~B nor y~B may hold, because either such edge together with the opposite A-edge gives a perfect matching. Hence B+x and B+y are both non-Hamiltonian.\n\nNow suppose |A|=3. If both A+x and A+y were non-Hamiltonian, accepted R963 applied to the shared triangle A would make A+x+y Hamiltonian. Together with the Hamilton rail B this would be a spanning two-cover of G, contradiction. Hence at least one deleted vertex extends A. If both extend A, then no edge to B is allowed, again because any B-extension paired with the opposite A-extension would give a perfect matching; thus B is obstructed by both x,y. If exactly one, say x, extends A, then y cannot extend B, and by assumption y does not extend A, so y is an endpoint obstruction. This proves all clauses.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R1012.md -->

# FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R1013.md

<!-- BEGIN FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R1013.md -->

# R1013 — A single pair-deletion representative can have an empty Hamilton-extension graph while another representative escapes

## Statement
There exists an edge ordering of K_8 with global minimum edge 01 such that H=G-{0,1} is non-Hamiltonian and has the literal exact two-cover (2,3,4)|(5,6,7), while none of the four supports {0,2,3,4}, {1,2,3,4}, {0,5,6,7}, {1,5,6,7} is Hamiltonian. Nevertheless G has the spanning increasing two-cover (0,1,2)|(4,6,3,5,7). One exact total edge order is 01<07<47<45<46<37<36<25<17<35<27<26<56<67<23<15<16<05<57<14<12<04<34<02<24<06<13<03. Thus the 2x2 Hamilton-extension graph attached to one exact complementary two-cover may be empty even when the complement itself is non-Hamiltonian; representative change is genuinely necessary.

## Hypotheses
Pure exact finite edge-order example on K_8; no minimum-counterexample assumption.

## Scope
Exact finite fence for representative-descent arguments based only on the Hamilton-extension graph of one fixed pair-deletion cover.

## Applicability
Use to rule out any proof claiming that every exact pair-deletion representative has a nonempty Hamilton-extension graph. It shows that progress must range over alternative exact complementary covers.

## Persistence
Retain the exact K_8 edge order, global minimum 01, the displayed dead representative 234|567, the four failed Hamilton extensions, non-Hamiltonicity of H, and the escaping rooted two-cover 012|46357.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not refute R888, the existence of a good representative, or the minimum-rail perfect-extension conjecture. It only falsifies fixed-representative nonemptiness.

## Proof
Number the displayed edges by ranks 0,...,27 in the stated order. The complement rail (2,3,4) is increasing because rank(23)=14<rank(34)=22. The rail (5,6,7) is increasing because rank(56)=12<rank(67)=13, so H=G-{0,1} has an exact two-cover. Exhaustive inspection of all 6!=720 vertex orders on H finds no increasing Hamilton path; for reference an increasing path of order five is (3,7,2,6,5), whose edge ranks are 5<10<11<12, so H is genuinely non-Hamiltonian rather than trivially short. For each of the four supports {0,2,3,4}, {1,2,3,4}, {0,5,6,7}, {1,5,6,7}, inspect all 4!=24 vertex orders; none has strictly increasing consecutive edge ranks. Thus the Hamilton-extension graph of the displayed representative (2,3,4)|(5,6,7) is empty. Finally, (0,1,2) is increasing because rank(01)=0<rank(12)=20, and (4,6,3,5,7) is increasing because rank(46)=4<rank(36)=6<rank(35)=9<rank(57)=18. These paths are vertex-disjoint and spanning, so G is two-coverable. Hence the failure is genuinely representative-specific.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R1013.md -->

# FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R1014.md

<!-- BEGIN FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R1014.md -->

# R1014 — A one-sided blocked component join transports its endpoint defects monotonically

## Statement
Let G be a finite edge-ordered complete graph and F a spanning increasing three-cover. For an ordered pair of distinct components with terminal t and source s, put a=L_F(t), b=U_F(s), e=lambda(ts). Define LOW when e<a and e<b: remove the last edge p->t of the terminal component and add t->s, producing the inherited prefix ending at p and the path t followed by the source component. Define HIGH when a<e and b<e: remove the first edge s->q of the source component and add t->s, producing the terminal component followed by s and the inherited suffix beginning at q. Both operations are legal increasing three-cover surgeries. Number the ordinary edges 0,...,M-1 by increasing rank and define Psi(F) to be the sum of the ranks of all selected edges of F. Every LOW move strictly decreases Psi, because it removes edge p t of rank a and adds t s of rank e<a. Every HIGH move strictly increases Psi, because it removes edge s q of rank b and adds t s of rank e>b. Hence every all-LOW or all-HIGH sequence terminates. If pc_inc(G)>2, LOW exhaustion yields a SOURCE-SHIELD normal form satisfying U(s)<lambda(ts) for every ordered cross-component terminal-to-source pair, while HIGH exhaustion yields a TERMINAL-SHIELD normal form satisfying lambda(ts)<L(t) for every such pair. A cover satisfying both forms has U(s)<lambda(ts)<L(t) on all six ordered cross-component joins.

## Hypotheses
Finite edge-ordered complete graph and a literal spanning increasing three-cover. For the shield-normal-form conclusions assume pc_inc(G)>2.

## Scope
Pure edge-order finite-termination theorem for physical fresh-edge transports. No R980, minimum-counterexample, threshold matching, or longest-path hypothesis.

## Applicability
Use to replace arbitrary one-sided blocker chains by two concrete extremal normal forms. The remaining local obstruction is the middle-band double block; comparing source-shield and terminal-shield forms is the next completeness-specific augmentation target.

## Persistence
Retain the initial cover, each explicit LOW/HIGH surgery if needed, the selected-edge rank-sum potential Psi, and the source/terminal shield inequalities in the terminal normal forms.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not prove source- and terminal-shield normal forms coincide, that the fully double-blocked form is impossible, or that a mixed LOW/HIGH sequence has a monotone potential. No endpoint-boundary-sum potential is asserted.

## Proof
Let F=A|B|C be a spanning increasing three-cover. Fix an ordered pair of distinct components A,B with terminal t of A and source s of B, and put a=L_F(t), b=U_F(s), e=lambda(ts), with the usual infinite endpoint conventions only for deciding whether a comparison is vacuous.

LOW. Assume e<a and e<b. Then A is nontrivial, so write its last selected edge as p->t, whose rank is exactly a. Delete p->t and add t->s. The prefix A^- ending at p is inherited. The new path obtained by placing t before B is increasing because its first selected edge has rank e and, if B is nontrivial, the next selected edge has rank b>e; every later comparison is inherited from B. Thus the result is another spanning increasing three-cover. It has the same number of selected edges as F, and differs in selected-edge rank sum only by replacing a with e. Hence Psi decreases strictly.

HIGH. Assume a<e and b<e. Then B is nontrivial, so write its first selected edge as s->q, whose rank is b. Delete s->q and add t->s. The path A followed by s is increasing because the old terminal incoming rank is a<e. The suffix B^+ beginning at q is inherited. Again the result is a spanning increasing three-cover with the same number of selected edges, and Psi changes only by replacing b with e. Hence Psi increases strictly.

Because a spanning three-cover on a fixed finite graph has exactly |V|-3 selected edges, Psi is an integer in a finite bounded set. Therefore an all-LOW sequence cannot continue indefinitely, since Psi strictly decreases at every move; likewise an all-HIGH sequence terminates because Psi strictly increases.

Assume now pc_inc(G)>2, so no direct concatenation of two components is legal. At a LOW-terminal cover, fix any ordered pair with values a,b,e. If e<b, then direct legality a<e<b is impossible, so distinctness of labels forces e<a. That is exactly the LOW condition e<a and e<b, contradicting terminality. Hence b<e for every ordered pair, giving the SOURCE-SHIELD normal form. Dually, at a HIGH-terminal cover, if a<e then direct legality a<e<b is impossible, so b<e, which is exactly HIGH; contradiction. Hence e<a for every ordered pair, giving the TERMINAL-SHIELD normal form. If a cover satisfies both, then b<e<a on all six ordered cross-component joins. This proves every clause.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R1014.md -->

# R1015 — Global-longest one-third order floor and triple-longest equality

## Statement
Let H be a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample of order n and let K be a proper global-longest tight path of order L with exterior E=V(H)\\V(K). Then 4<=|E|. Moreover E has an exact two-cover P sqcup Q, and for every such exact two-cover |P|,|Q|<=L. Consequently |E|<=2L and L>=ceil(n/3). Equality n=3L holds if and only if some exact exterior two-cover has |P|=|Q|=L; equivalently, under equality every exact exterior two-cover has both rails of order L. In that case H is literally the disjoint union of three global-longest tight paths K,P,Q of the same order L.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample; K is a proper graph-intrinsic globally longest tight path.

## Scope
R24-free size geometry of a global-longest carrier and its exact exterior two-cover. This is the clean successor to R219 with only the quarantined one-unit exterior-floor strengthening removed.

## Applicability
Use to bound exterior slack relative to a global-longest carrier, obtain L>=ceil(n/3), and isolate the extremal n=3L face as a literal three-global-longest-path frame. The only content intentionally not retained from R219 is the stronger |E|>=5 floor.

## Persistence
K and the inequalities are graph-intrinsic. Any chosen exact exterior two-cover P,Q is representative-relative, but equality forces every such cover to have both rails at the global-longest order L.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert |E|>=5. The missing upgrade 4->5 is exactly the R169/R5 four-deletion residue and remains quarantined with the R24 order-three singleton-rail core. Does not close the equality face and does not assert uniqueness of the exterior two-cover.

## Proof
Let H be a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample of order n, and let K be a proper globally longest tight path of order L. Put E=V(H)\\V(K).\n\nFirst we prove the clean lower floor |E|>=4. Since K is proper, E is nonempty. If |E|=1, the unique exterior vertex is a singleton tight path, so it together with K is a spanning two-path cover of H, contradiction. If |E|=2, the two exterior vertices form a tight dimer, again giving a spanning two-cover with K. If |E|=3, choose any ordering (a,b,c) of E. By boundary antisymmetry R3 exactly one of (a,b,c) and (c,b,a) is tight, so E supports a tight Hamilton trimer. That trimer together with K is again a spanning two-cover of H, contradiction. Hence |E|>=4.\n\nNow apply smallest-counterexample minimality R4 to the proper graph-intrinsic tight path K. It says that H[E] has path-cover number exactly two, so choose an exact two-cover E=P sqcup Q. Since K is globally longest in H and P,Q are tight paths of H, |P|<=L and |Q|<=L. Therefore |E|=|P|+|Q|<=2L. Since n=L+|E|, we obtain n<=3L, equivalently L>=ceil(n/3). The same inequalities apply to every exact exterior two-cover.\n\nSuppose n=3L. Then |E|=n-L=2L. For any exact exterior two-cover P sqcup Q we have |P|+|Q|=2L and separately |P|,|Q|<=L, forcing |P|=|Q|=L. Thus K,P,Q are three pairwise disjoint globally longest tight paths of order L whose union is V(H). Conversely, if some exact exterior two-cover has |P|=|Q|=L, then n=|K|+|P|+|Q|=3L. This proves the equality characterization.\n\nNo five-exterior floor is used. The historical R219 clause |E|>=5 is intentionally not proved here; its extra one unit is precisely the R169/R5 four-deletion residue blocked by quarantined R24. Thus this route isolates all of the one-third scale and triple-longest equality mechanism from R24 while retaining the clean universal floor |E|>=4.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R1015.md -->

# R1016 — Universal small-deletion exactness through three vertices

## Statement
Let H be a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample. For every vertex set D with 1<=|D|<=3, the induced subsystem H-D has path-cover number exactly two.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample; D is a vertex set of order one, two, or three.

## Scope
R24-free clean core of historical R5. The theorem stops exactly before the four-vertex deletion case, which is the quarantined R24-sensitive residue.

## Applicability
Use whenever a proof needs an exact two-cover after deleting at most three named vertices. This replaces historical invocations of R5 whose actual deletion set has order at most three.

## Persistence
Pure induced-subsystem exactness. Any chosen exact two-cover is representative-relative, but the equality pc(H-D)=2 is graph-intrinsic.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert exactness after deleting four vertices. In the four-deletion case the deleted four-set need not be Hamiltonian, and the missing argument is precisely the R24-sensitive content of historical R5.

## Proof
Let H be a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample and let D be a vertex set with 1<=|D|<=3. By smallest-counterexample minimality R4, the proper induced subsystem H-D has path-cover number at most two. We show it is not Hamiltonian.\n\nIf |D|=1, D itself is a singleton tight path. If H-D had a Hamilton tight path, that path together with the singleton D would be a spanning two-cover of H, contradiction.\n\nIf |D|=2, the two vertices of D form a tight dimer. Again a Hamilton path of H-D together with this dimer would two-cover H, contradiction.\n\nIf |D|=3, write D={a,b,c}. By boundary antisymmetry R3, for any ordering (a,b,c), exactly one of (a,b,c) and its complete reversal (c,b,a) is tight. Thus D supports a Hamilton tight trimer. A Hamilton path of H-D together with that trimer would again be a spanning two-cover of H, contradiction.\n\nTherefore H-D is non-Hamiltonian in every case. Since R4 already gives pc(H-D)<=2 and H-D is nonempty in the smallest-counterexample setting, we conclude pc(H-D)=2.\n\nNo statement is made for |D|=4. The proof stops exactly where the deleted set ceases to be automatically Hamiltonian under R3; that missing four-vertex case is the quarantined R24-sensitive portion of historical R5.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R1016.md -->

# R1017 — Four-deletion exactness fails only on a classified P4-free four-cell

## Statement
Let H be a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample and let D be any four-element vertex set with H-D nonempty. Then exactly one of the following holds. (EXACT) pc(H-D)=2. (CRITICAL-4) pc(H-D)=1, so H-D has a Hamilton tight path, while H[D] has no Hamilton tight P4. In the CRITICAL-4 branch, for every three-subset T of D and every tight trimer orientation C on T, writing y for the fourth vertex, the pair (C,y) lies in the no-P4 branch of R518. Hence D carries one of the four exact R516 terminal-sign alignment signatures relative to C, with the corresponding R517 matching-block quotient type (three transitive types and the uniform cyclic 00 type). Thus the only obstruction to four-deletion exactness is a graph-intrinsic P4-free four-cell with completely explicit local orientation data.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample; D is an arbitrary four-element vertex set and H-D is nonempty.

## Scope
R24-free replacement interface for the four-vertex case of historical R5. It localizes failure of exactness but does not exclude the critical four-cell.

## Applicability
Whenever a historical R5 invocation deletes four named vertices, first test whether those four vertices support a tight P4. If yes, R4 gives exact two-cover of the complement. If not, retain the exact R516/R517 critical-cell signature and handle that finite residue explicitly.

## Persistence
The deletion set D, the value pc(H-D), any chosen Hamilton path on H-D in the critical branch, P4-freeness of H[D], each chosen tight trimer C on a three-subset of D, its fourth vertex y, and the resulting R516 signature/R517 quotient are graph-intrinsic except the chosen Hamilton path representative on H-D.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not prove pc(H-D)=2 for arbitrary four-sets. Does not rule out any of the four R516 signatures. Does not prove R5 or R24. Different trimer orientations/subsets of D need not yield the same alignment bits, although all are descriptions of the same P4-free four-cell.

## Proof
Let H be a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample and let D be a four-element vertex set with W=H-D nonempty. Because W is a nonempty proper induced subsystem, accepted smallest-counterexample minimality R4 gives pc(W)<=2. Path-cover number is at least one, so pc(W) is either one or two. If pc(W)=2, the EXACT branch holds.\n\nAssume pc(W)=1. Fix a Hamilton tight path Q on W. We claim H[D] has no Hamilton tight P4. Indeed, if P were a tight Hamilton P4 on D, then P and Q would be two vertex-disjoint tight paths whose supports partition V(H), giving a spanning two-cover of H. This contradicts pc(H)=3 from R4. Hence D is P4-free.\n\nNow fix arbitrarily a three-subset T of D. By accepted R8, T admits a tight trimer orientation C=(a,b,c). Let y be the unique vertex of D-T. Apply accepted R518 to this exact trimer C and fourth vertex y. R518 gives either a Hamilton P4 on D or its explicit no-P4 double-contact branch. The first alternative is impossible because D is P4-free. Therefore (C,y) lies in the no-P4 branch of R518: the two reverse contacts are tight, one of the four exact R516 terminal-sign alignment signatures is realized, and the corresponding R517 matching-block quotient is determined, with the three transitive quotient types and the uniform cyclic 00 type exactly as stated there.\n\nThe choice of T and of its tight trimer orientation C was arbitrary, so this classification is available for every trimer presentation of D. Consequently failure of four-deletion exactness is not an unstructured residue: it is exactly the case that H-D is Hamiltonian while the deleted four-set is a graph-intrinsic P4-free critical cell carrying the full R516/R517 local orientation data. This proves the stated dichotomy. No R5, R24, R168, R169, or singleton-order-floor input is used.

# R1018 — Four-deletion exactness is equivalent to the singleton rail-order-four floor

## Statement
Let H be a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample. The following are equivalent: (A) every exact one-vertex-deletion two-cover H-z=P sqcup Q has |P|,|Q|>=4; (B) for every four-vertex set D, pc(H-D)=2. Moreover the equivalence is direct and certificate-preserving: an order-three rail P in a failed singleton-deletion cover produces the four-deletion Hamiltonian residue H-(V(P) union {z})=Q, while a four-deletion Hamiltonian residue K on H-D and any z in D produce an exact singleton-deletion cover K sqcup T where T is a tight trimer on D-{z}.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample. Use boundary antisymmetry R3 and smallest-counterexample minimality R4.

## Scope
Exact interface theorem identifying the quarantined core. This theorem does not prove either equivalent condition; it shows that repairing R5 at deletion size four and proving the operative R24 singleton rail floor are the same mathematical obligation.

## Applicability
Use to transfer a counterexample certificate or a proof between the R24 singleton-floor formulation and the R5 four-deletion formulation. In repair work, this licenses treating the unresolved |D|=4 case as exactly R24 rather than as an additional descendant obligation.

## Persistence
The deleted singleton z, the three-vertex short rail P or trimer T, the four-set D, and the Hamiltonian complementary rail Q or K are retained literally under the two translations.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not establish R24 or four-deletion exactness. Does not identify the stronger historical packaging beyond the operative rail-order floor. The already-clean deletion sizes one through three are separate and do not require this equivalence.

## Proof
Let H be a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample.\n\n(A) implies (B). Assume every exact singleton-deletion two-cover has both rails of order at least four. Let D be any four-vertex set. By R4, pc(H-D)<=2. Suppose for contradiction that H-D is Hamiltonian, with Hamilton tight path K. Choose any z in D. By R3, the three-set D-{z} has a tight trimer T. Then K sqcup T is a literal two-cover of H-z. It is exact: if H-z were Hamiltonian, that Hamilton path together with singleton z would be a spanning two-cover of H, contradiction. Thus K sqcup T is an exact singleton-deletion two-cover with a rail T of order three, contradicting (A). Therefore H-D is non-Hamiltonian. Together with R4 this gives pc(H-D)=2, proving (B).\n\n(B) implies (A). Assume pc(H-D)=2 for every four-set D. Let H-z=P sqcup Q be any exact singleton-deletion two-cover. We show both rails have order at least four. By symmetry it suffices to treat P. If |P|=1, then adjoining z to P gives a tight dimer; that dimer together with Q is a spanning two-cover of H, contradiction. If |P|=2, then V(P) union {z} is a three-set, so R3 gives a tight trimer on those three vertices; together with Q this again spans H by two tight paths, contradiction. If |P|=3, put D=V(P) union {z}. Then |D|=4 and H-D has vertex set V(Q). Since Q is already a Hamilton tight path on that residue, pc(H-D)=1, contradicting (B). Hence |P|>=4. The same argument applies to Q, so every exact singleton-deletion two-cover has both rails of order at least four, proving (A).\n\nThe translations preserve the physical certificate. In the first direction, a four-deletion Hamiltonian residue K and chosen z produce the exact short-rail singleton-deletion cover K sqcup T. In the reverse direction, a three-vertex short rail P and its deleted singleton z produce the four-set D=V(P) union {z} whose complement is literally the other Hamilton rail Q. Thus the unresolved four-deletion case of R5 and the operative singleton rail floor of R24 are exactly the same obligation, not merely adjacent consequences.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R1018.md -->

# R1019 — Every failed four-deletion exactness instance has the fixed R881 eight-core normal form

## Statement
Let H be a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample and let D be a four-vertex set such that H-D is Hamiltonian. Then D itself is exactly the four-cell X in the clean R594/R881 normal form: after choosing any z in D and a tight trimer P on D-{z}, the exact cover H-z=P sqcup Q triggers R881. Consequently D=X is a no-P4 transitive matching-height four-cell, Q=(q_0,...,q_m) with m>=6 is the Hamilton path on H-D, and with L=q_0,u=q_1,s=q_{m-1},R=q_m,N=Q[2,m-2], the eight-vertex core G_8=H[D union {L,u,s,R}] satisfies pc(G_8)=2 while H=G_8 disjoint-union N and N is a nonempty Hamilton path. Every exact two-cover G_8=A sqcup B therefore gives a literal minimum three-cover H=A sqcup B sqcup N; the aligned/crossed gate split is internal to G_8.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample; D has order four; H-D has a Hamilton tight path. Use clean R3,R4,R881.

## Scope
R24-free fallback normal form for the sole unresolved |D|=4 case of R5. It does not assert four-deletion exactness; it says any failure is forced into the already-clean bounded-core long-rail geometry with the original deleted set retained exactly as X.

## Applicability
Use whenever an argument would like R5 on a four-set D but can tolerate a structured exceptional branch. Either pc(H-D)=2, or if H-D is Hamiltonian this theorem supplies the exact R881 core decomposition with D preserved as the four-cell.

## Persistence
The original four-set D is retained literally as X. The Hamilton complement path is retained as Q up to choosing its displayed Hamilton order. The four boundary Q vertices, middle rail N, core G_8, pc(G_8)=2, and internal gate phase are retained as in R881.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not prove the exceptional branch impossible. Does not assert uniqueness of the Hamilton order Q or of an exact G_8 two-cover. Does not assume or conclude R24. It only compiles a four-deletion failure into the accepted R881 normal form.

## Proof
Let D be a four-vertex set such that H-D is Hamiltonian, and fix a Hamilton tight path Q on V(H)-D. Choose any z in D. By R3, the three-set D-{z} admits a tight trimer ordering; call the resulting path P. Then P sqcup Q is a literal two-cover of H-z. It is exact: if H-z were Hamiltonian, a Hamilton path on H-z together with singleton z would form a spanning two-cover of H, contradicting that H is a counterexample. Hence H-z=P sqcup Q is an exact singleton-deletion two-cover with |P|=3.\n\nThis is exactly the clean hypothesis of accepted R881. Apply R881 to this displayed failure certificate. Its underlying R594 normalization defines X=V(P) union {z}. But V(P)=D-{z}, so X=D literally. Therefore the original four-deletion set, not merely an isomorphic replacement, is the synchronized no-P4 transitive matching-height four-cell. R881 supplies a Hamilton ordering Q=(q_0,...,q_m) of the complementary rail with m>=6. Write L=q_0, u=q_1, s=q_{m-1}, R=q_m and N=Q[2,m-2]. Then N is nonempty and Hamiltonian, and for G_8=H[D union {L,u,s,R}] one has |V(G_8)|=8, pc(G_8)=2, and V(H)=V(G_8) disjoint-union V(N). Every exact two-cover G_8=A sqcup B consequently yields the literal minimum spanning three-cover H=A sqcup B sqcup N. R881 also states that the aligned/crossed middle-gate split is entirely internal to this same G_8.\n\nNo R24 statement is used. The proof starts from the literal failure of four-deletion exactness and feeds its own physical certificate into the accepted noncircular R881 reduction. The identity X=D is retained because R594 defines X from the three-vertex short rail and its deleted singleton, which here are exactly D-{z} and z. Thus any attempted use of R5 at deletion size four may be replaced by the structured alternative: either H-D has path-cover number two, or its Hamiltonian failure is confined to this fixed eight-core plus nonempty Hamilton middle-rail normal form.

# R1020 — A short ancestral arm in the anti-aligned DR cell forces a balanced-pair continuation without four-deletion exactness

## Statement
Let H be a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample and retain the anti-aligned bridge setup of R495 in its DR branch. Thus A=(a_0,...,a_p), B=(b_0,...,b_q), P=(a_0,z_1,...,z_{m-1},b_q) with m>=3, the source cover is P sqcup A^+ sqcup B^-, and K_D=(a_1,a_0,b_q,b_{q-1}) is a tight P4. Suppose either (L) p=1 and q>=3, or (R) q=1 and p>=3. Then there is a finite certificate-retaining continuation yielding either a spanning two-cover of H or a graph-intrinsic balanced opposite-sign pair. More precisely, in (L) put y=b_{q-2}. Apply R518 to the tight core (a_1,a_0,b_q) and y. If the four-set {a_1,a_0,b_q,y} is Hamiltonian, deleting a Hamilton P4 on it leaves the literal three-path reference cover B_L sqcup (b_{q-1}) sqcup P^o, where B_L=(b_0,...,b_{q-3}); R4 supplies an exact two-cover of the same residue, R7 forces a cross-class selected state, and R176 gives the balanced pair. If the four-set is P4-free, inspect its exact R516 signature through R518. When the right alignment bit is 1, (y,a_0,b_q) is tight and combines with the DR turn (a_0,b_q,b_{q-1}) to give the tight P4 (y,a_0,b_q,b_{q-1}); deleting it leaves the three classes (a_1), B_L, P^o and the same R4/R7/R176 argument applies. When the right alignment bit is 0, the signature gives both (y,b_q,a_0) and (a_0,b_q,a_1) tight. Hence for the tight trimer (y,b_q,a_0), its reverse terminal dimer (a_0,b_q) has two same-polarity tail witnesses a_1 and b_{q-1}, the latter from the DR turn (a_0,b_q,b_{q-1}); R542 yields the stated certificate-retaining continuation. In (R) the exact mirror is explicit: put y=a_2 and apply R518 to the tight core (a_0,b_q,b_0). If its four-set is Hamiltonian, delete that P4 and use the three classes (a_1), A_R=(a_3,...,a_p), P^o. In the P4-free branch, when the left alignment bit is 1, (a_0,b_q,y) together with the DR turn (a_1,a_0,b_q) gives the P4 (a_1,a_0,b_q,y), leaving (b_0),A_R,P^o; when the left alignment bit is 0, the signature gives (y,b_q,a_0) and (b_0,a_0,b_q), so for the tight trimer (y,b_q,a_0) the reverse terminal dimer (a_0,b_q) has two same-polarity head witnesses a_1 and b_0, and R542 applies. Thus neither short-arm DR cell needs arbitrary four-deletion exactness.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample; retain the exact R495 anti-aligned bridge coordinates and its DR output; either p=1,q>=3 or q=1,p>=3.

## Scope
R24-free consumer of the two short-arm cells excluded from historical R499. It replaces the historical R500 four-deletion use by an R518 P4-or-signature split and R542 in the no-P4 residue.

## Applicability
Use immediately when R495 lands in DR and exactly one ancestral arm has parameter one while the opposite arm has parameter at least three. Together with a clean R499 route for p,q>=2, this consumes every DR cell once the relevant size condition is met.

## Persistence
Retain A,B,P,P^o, the DR P4, the short-arm side, the probe vertex y, the exact R518 signature if P4-free, any deletion P4 and its three named residual source classes, or in the R542 branch the tested dimer (a_0,b_q) with its two exact witness turns. R4/R7/R176 cross-state provenance is retained literally in the P4 branches; R542 ancestry is retained in the collision branch.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not repair R478 or assert the R478 P5 currentization exists. Does not prove arbitrary four-deletion exactness, R5, or R24. In the R542 branch the conclusion is a finite paid continuation, not an immediate spanning two-cover. The theorem requires the opposite arm to have at least three steps so that the named residual long-arm class is nonempty.

## Proof
Retain the exact R495 coordinates and suppose its DR branch occurs, so

  K_D=(a_1,a_0,b_q,b_{q-1})

is a literal tight P4. Write P^o=(z_1,...,z_{m-1}). We treat the two short-arm cells separately.

LEFT-SHORT CELL: p=1 and q>=3.
Put

  a=a_1,  b=a_0,  c=b_q,  w=b_{q-1},  y=b_{q-2}.

The first three vertices of K_D give the tight trimer C=(a,b,c), and the second DR turn is

  (b,c,w) tight.                                           (L1)

Apply accepted R518 to C and the fourth vertex y.

L-HAMILTON branch. Suppose the four-set D_0={a,b,c,y} supports a Hamilton tight P4 J. Since P^o is nonempty, J is proper. By R4 the complement W=H-D_0 has an exact two-cover T. Restricting the original source cover P sqcup A^+ sqcup B^- to W leaves the three nonempty literal paths

  B_L=(b_0,...,b_{q-3}),   (w),   P^o.                     (L2)

Here B_L is nonempty because q>=3. Apply R7 to this three-class partition and T. L-NO-P4 branch. Suppose D_0 is P4-free. R518 therefore places (C,y) in one of the exact R516 no-P4 signatures. Let B be the right alignment bit, namely B=1 exactly when (y,b,c) is tight.

a literal tight P4. Delete V(J'). R4 gives an exact two-cover T' of its complement. The restricted source cover there is the three-path cover

Hence S carries two distinct same-polarity witnesses on one reverse boundary dimer of K. RIGHT-SHORT CELL: q=1 and p>=3.
Now put

  a=a_0,  b=b_q=b_1,  c=b_0,  w=a_1,  y=a_2.

The last three vertices of K_D are (w,a,b,c) in the displayed DR order, so in particular

# R1021 — Every quiet crossed deep gap exports to a current P4-bearing maximum three-forest

## Statement
Retain the accepted crossed R621 frame with Q=(q_0,...,q_m), m>=6, X={a,b,c,z}, and the R820 deep-gap notation. For every interior deep gap 3<=j<=m-4, at least one of the following holds: (SEAM) U_j or V_j holds; (GATE) G_AC(j) or G_BZ(j) holds; (FOREST) H has a literal minimum spanning three-cover K sqcup P sqcup Qprime in which K is a proper tight P4 crossing the old G_8|N decomposition at the physical gap q_j|q_{j+1}. More precisely, in FOREST either K is one of the four R874 probe P4s on {q_{j-1},q_j,q_{j+1},x} for x in {b,z}, or on {q_j,q_{j+1},q_{j+2},y} for y in {a,c}, or the complete central fan occurs and one may choose any K=(x,q_{j+1},q_j,y) with x in {b,z}, y in {a,c}. In every case accepted R4 gives an exact two-cover of H-V(K), so restoring K gives an actual maximum three-forest of H with the gap labels and X witnesses retained. At the terminal deep gap j=m-3, R820 already forces U_j or G_AC(j), so no terminal FOREST exception is needed.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in the accepted crossed R621 frame; m>=6. Use accepted R820, R874, and R4.

## Scope
R24 long-core export theorem. It does not close the crossed phase. It converts the joint terminal-blocker residue of R820 into current maximum-three-forest dynamics, exactly avoiding the intact-middle limitation R904.

## Applicability
At each crossed deep gap, first consume SEAM/GATE if productive. If both sides avoid those outputs, enter current maximum-three-forest space through the labelled P4 K rather than paying the two terminal packets separately. The P4 support physically uses interior Q vertices and X, so it changes the old G8|N representative.

## Persistence
Retain j, the old Q order, whichever R820 terminal packets fired, the exact R874 probe/FAN certificate, the literal P4 order K, and the exact two-cover of H-V(K) chosen by R4. The old G8|N decomposition remains historical source data, not necessarily current after the new forest is chosen.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert the new maximum three-forest has smaller largest rail, that forests from distinct gaps coexist, or that SEAM/GATE branches close. Does not claim the P4 is unique. At j=m-3 the right-terminal R820 window is absent and the theorem uses the stronger existing U_j OR G_AC(j) conclusion instead.

## Proof
Retain the accepted crossed R621 frame and fix 3<=j<=m-4. Use the exact notation of accepted R820. Its AC-side compression states\n  U_j OR G_AC(j) OR T_AC(j),\nwhere T_AC(j) means both (q_{j+2},q_{j+1},a) and (q_{j+2},q_{j+1},c) are tight. Its BZ-side compression states\n  V_j OR G_BZ(j) OR T_BZ(j),\nwhere T_BZ(j) means both (b,q_j,q_{j-1}) and (z,q_j,q_{j-1}) are tight.\n\nIf U_j or V_j holds, we are in SEAM. If G_AC(j) or G_BZ(j) holds, we are in GATE. Assume neither. Then both T_AC(j) and T_BZ(j) hold simultaneously as graph-intrinsic turn certificates in the one crossed frame.\n\nPut D_j=(q_j,q_{j-1}) and D_{j+2}=(q_{j+2},q_{j+1}). The two turns in T_BZ(j) say exactly that D_j is head-signed by the two distinct witnesses b,z. The two turns in T_AC(j) say exactly that D_{j+2} is tail-signed by the two distinct witnesses a,c. The four witnesses a,b,c,z are distinct and all lie outside Q. Thus the hypotheses of accepted R874 apply with (b_1,b_2)=(b,z) and (a_1,a_2)=(a,c).\n\nR874 gives the following exhaustive physical output. Either one of its four R518 probes already produces a Hamilton P4: a P4 on {q_{j-1},q_j,q_{j+1},x} for some x in {b,z}, or a P4 on {q_j,q_{j+1},q_{j+2},y} for some y in {a,c}; or else its FAN branch holds and all four literal paths\n  (x,q_{j+1},q_j,y),  x in {b,z}, y in {a,c},\nare tight P4s. Choose one such literal P4 and call it K.\n\nBecause m>=6 and H contains X together with all vertices of Q, K is a proper path of H. Accepted smallest-counterexample minimality R4 therefore gives an exact two-cover P sqcup Qprime of H-V(K). Restoring K gives the literal spanning three-cover\n  H = K sqcup P sqcup Qprime.\nSince H is a hypothetical smallest counterexample, pc(H)=3 by R4, so this is a minimum spanning three-cover, equivalently an actual maximum spanning three-forest.\n\nThe new rail K is not contained in either side of the old R810 decomposition H=G_8 sqcup N. In every R874 output K contains at least one vertex of X and at least the adjacent interior Q vertices q_j,q_{j+1}; for 3<=j<=m-4 these Q vertices lie in N. Thus K physically crosses the old G_8|N partition at the named gap and is a genuine representative change rather than an intact-N consumer. Retain j, the source terminal packets, the exact R874 certificate, K, and the chosen exact complement two-cover as ancestry.\n\nFinally take j=m-3. Accepted R820 explicitly states that the far-right T_AC window is absent there and its AC-side conclusion sharpens to U_j OR G_AC(j). Hence the terminal deep gap is already SEAM or GATE and no FOREST alternative is needed. This proves the theorem.
