# R1022 — Every ancestry-bearing singleton floor re-enters current maximum-three-forest space through a proper trimer

## Statement
Let H be a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample and suppose an ancestry-bearing balanced opposite-sign pair with both supports singleton is active. Then there is a finite certificate-retaining continuation yielding either a spanning two-cover of H or a literal minimum spanning three-cover J sqcup U sqcup V in which J is a named proper tight trimer arising from the paid-floor ancestry. More precisely, choose any physical pair {x,z}; an exact cover H-{x,z}=U_0 sqcup V_0 has an internal rail vertex b because |H|>10. Orient {x,b,z} as a tight turn J_0=(a,b,c) with {a,c}={x,z}, steer the floor to {a,c}, and run the fixed-turn interaction compiler R445 in this same pair-deletion frame. A first protected return may restore the aligned floor with endpoint a completed; a second predecessor-channel attempt at the same fixed turn is nonquiet by R434. Every resulting nonclosing explicit output contains a proper tight trimer J, and R4 exact-covers H-V(J), producing the asserted current maximum three-forest.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample; an ancestry-bearing both-singleton balanced floor is active. Use accepted R3,R4,R429,R432,R434,R445,R533.

## Scope
Global bridge from historical paid-floor ancestry back to current representative dynamics. It does not assert strict Morse descent after reentry and does not identify the new forest with the source representative.

## Applicability
Use whenever capture/payment, cross-state descent, or signed-support machinery reaches a genuine ancestry-bearing both-singleton floor. The floor is not terminal: it closes H or re-enters literal maximum-three-forest space through a named proper trimer after at most one protected aligned return.

## Persistence
Retain the incoming floor ancestry, chosen target pair {x,z}, fixed exact pair-deletion cover U_0|V_0, internal vertex b, fixed turn J_0, floor-steering certificates, the first R445 output/return, completed endpoint ledger A_{J_0}, the second-channel nonquiet certificate when needed, the extracted trimer J, and the final R4 complement two-cover. Source covers need not remain current.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not prove the reentered forest has smaller largest rail or lower global holonomy rank. Does not assert different output branches coexist. Does not treat a bare formal singleton pair without ancestry as productive. The only use of the order bound is to guarantee an internal vertex in the fixed pair-deletion cover.

## Proof
Let H be a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample and let F be an active ancestry-bearing both-singleton balanced floor. By accepted R533, |V(H)|=n>10. Choose any two distinct physical vertices x,z. Accepted Pair-Deletion Rigidity R429 gives an exact two-cover\n\n  H-{x,z}=U_0 sqcup V_0\n\nwith both rails nontrivial. If |U_0|=r and |V_0|=s, then r+s=n-2. The total number of rail-internal vertices is (r-2)+(s-2)=n-6>0, so choose an internal vertex b of one rail. By R3, exactly one of the two complete reversals on {x,b,z} is tight. Relabel the two outer vertices as a,c so that\n\n  J_0=(a,b,c)\n\nis a tight proper trimer and {a,c}={x,z}. The displayed pair-deletion cover is therefore also the exact frame H-{a,c}=U_0 sqcup V_0, with b internal.\n\nUse accepted Complete Floor Pair Steering R432 to steer the incoming ancestry-bearing floor to the prescribed outer pair {a,c}. Unless a spanning two-cover occurs during steering, we now have an ancestry-bearing aligned both-singleton floor (a),(c), while the fixed exact frame U_0|V_0 remains available as graph-intrinsic data. Thus all hypotheses of accepted R445 hold for J_0 and this fixed frame.\n\nRun R445, taking the predecessor channel as its first birth and protecting the endpoint a exactly as in that theorem. R445 is finite. Unless H closes by a spanning two-cover, it yields either: (i) one of its explicit non-descent geometric outputs; or (ii) a completed protected return to an aligned both-singleton floor (a),(c), with a reached as the protected singleton coordinate.\n\nSuppose first that R445 yields explicit geometry. We extract a proper tight trimer J from that certificate. For a reverse-contact/reversal output, the displayed reverse turn is already such a trimer. A signed-BB reverse four-path contains a consecutive tight trimer. A strict +2 extension, strict path growth, or fusion output contains a tight path of order at least three and hence a consecutive trimer. A vertex-simple tight cycle contains a consecutive tight trimer. Finally, an explicit historical anchor/witness-contact event in this R445 frame comes from an endpoint-anchored signed dimer birth supplied by R434; the retained sign witness together with that tight dimer is exactly a tight three-vertex turn. Since n>10, every such three-vertex support is proper in H. Thus every nonclosing explicit R445 output contains a named proper tight trimer J with its physical ancestry retained.\n\nIt remains to handle the protected-return branch. At the completion of that return, accepted R434 records endpoint a in the fixed-turn completed-endpoint set A_{J_0}. Return to the same graph-intrinsic exact pair-deletion frame U_0|V_0 and inspect the predecessor channel at b again. R434 states that when the anchored endpoint e already lies in A_{J_0}, the new nontrivial dimer containing the retained historical singleton anchor e is an explicit anchor-contact/strict-growth event and the episode is nonquiet. Taking e=a, the second predecessor attempt therefore cannot begin another quiet protected return. It immediately supplies explicit geometry of the kind just treated, in particular an endpoint-anchored signed dimer with its exact sign witness or a stricter path/cycle/reversal output. Hence after at most one protected aligned return we again obtain a named proper tight trimer J, unless H has already closed.\n\nNow apply accepted smallest-counterexample minimality R4 to J. Since J is a proper graph-intrinsic tight path, R4 gives an exact two-cover P sqcup Q of H-V(J). Restoring J gives\n\n  H = J sqcup P sqcup Q.\n\nBecause pc(H)=3 by R4, this is a literal minimum spanning three-cover, equivalently an actual maximum spanning three-forest. Retain the complete incoming floor ancestry, target pair, fixed pair-deletion frame, fixed turn J_0, R445/R434 certificates, extracted trimer J, and the chosen R4 complement cover. No claim is made that the old frame remains current after this final currentization.\n\nThus every genuine ancestry-bearing both-singleton floor has a finite route to a spanning two-cover or to current maximum-three-forest space through a named proper trimer. The proof uses no R24, R5, R168, or R169.

# R1023 — Every crossed long-phase deep gap exits to closure or current maximum-three-forest dynamics

## Statement
Retain the accepted crossed R621/R820 frame with Q=(q_0,...,q_m), m>=6. For every deep gap 3<=j<=m-3 there is a finite certificate-retaining continuation yielding either a spanning two-cover of H or an actual literal minimum spanning three-cover whose distinguished proper rail contains one of the physical gap coordinates supplied by R820. For 3<=j<=m-4: a SEAM output U_j or V_j is already a proper tight trimer and currentizes by R4; a GATE output G_AC(j) or G_BZ(j) is an inward witness on one crossed middle-gate dimer, so R682 gives either a cross-end tight trimer, which currentizes by R4, or endpoint capture/payment, which reaches a both-singleton floor by R428 and then closes or re-enters current forest space by R1022; if neither SEAM nor GATE occurs, the two R820 terminal packets coexist and R874 gives a proper labelled P4, which currentizes by R4. At j=m-3, R820 already forces U_j or G_AC(j), so only the first two mechanisms occur.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in the accepted crossed R621 frame with m>=6. Use accepted R4,R428,R682,R820,R874 and pending clean bridge R1022 once reviewed.

## Scope
Parent export theorem for the crossed R24 long phase. It removes deep-gap local taxonomy as a terminal research branch by routing every gap to closure or actual maximum-three-forest representative dynamics. It does not prove extinction of the resulting forest dynamics.

## Applicability
Use anywhere in the crossed long phase after R820. Do not separately spend terminal packets, gate witnesses, or seam literals as terminal outputs; each belongs to one of the explicit forest-entry routes in this theorem.

## Persistence
Retain j, the exact R820 disjunct and its literal turn certificates. SEAM retains its trimer order; GATE retains tested middle-gate dimer, inward witness, R682 capture/XET ancestry, any paid-floor ancestry, and final trimer/forest; terminal-packet residue retains the R874 labelled P4 and R4 complement cover.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert that forests obtained at different gaps coexist, that the resulting forest has lower largest-rail height, or that maximum-three-forest dynamics closes. The CAP route depends on R1022, which must be independently accepted before this theorem is usable. Does not claim a unique forest representative.

## Proof
Retain the accepted crossed R621 frame and the accepted deep-gap compression R820. Fix a deep gap j. We first treat 3<=j<=m-4, so every R820 window exists. Put q=q_{j+1}.\n\nAccepted R820 gives simultaneously\n\n  U_j OR G_AC(j) OR T_AC(j),\n  V_j OR G_BZ(j) OR T_BZ(j).\n\nSEAM. Suppose U_j holds. By definition, at least one of\n\n  (u,q_j,q_{j-1}),   (L,u,q_j)\n\nis tight. Either is a three-vertex tight path. Likewise, if V_j holds then at least one of\n\n  (q,s,R),   (q_{j+2},q,s)\n\nis tight. Since H has order greater than ten by accepted R533, and in any event contains X plus a long Q, each displayed trimer is proper. Accepted R4 exact-covers its complement, and restoring the trimer gives a literal minimum spanning three-cover. Thus every SEAM output already enters current maximum-three-forest space.\n\nGATE. Suppose G_AC(j) holds. Then either (q,c,a) or (q,a,c) is tight. In the first case q is a head witness on the tested crossed middle-gate dimer S=(c,a); in the second it is a head witness on S=(a,c). Because 3<=j<=m-4, the inward vertex q=q_{j+1} lies outside X union {L,R}. Thus accepted R682 applies with inward witness v=q.\n\nIf instead G_BZ(j) holds, then either (z,b,q_j) or (b,z,q_j) is tight. These are respectively tail certificates on S=(z,b) or S=(b,z), with inward witness v=q_j. Again q_j lies outside X union {L,R}, so R682 applies.\n\nIn either GATE case, R682 gives CAP or XET. In XET, one of (L,v,R),(R,v,L) is a graph-intrinsic tight trimer. It is proper, so R4 currentizes it immediately into a minimum spanning three-cover. In CAP, R682 retains an endpoint-capture/payment lineage for the middle-gate dimer S. Its R526 continuation either already gives a spanning two-cover, or reaches an ancestry-bearing balanced opposite-sign pair with a singleton support. If the opposite support is already singleton, retain the resulting both-singleton floor. Otherwise apply accepted R428 with the existing singleton fixed; unless H closes, R428 reaches an ancestry-bearing both-singleton floor. Apply R1022 to that genuine paid floor. Once R1022 is independently accepted, its finite continuation gives either a spanning two-cover or a named proper tight trimer J together with an exact R4 complement two-cover, hence a current minimum spanning three-cover. Therefore every GATE output exits to closure or current maximum-three-forest space.\n\nTERMINAL-PACKET RESIDUE. Assume now that none of U_j,V_j,G_AC(j),G_BZ(j) holds. The two R820 trichotomies force both T_AC(j) and T_BZ(j). Thus a,c tail-sign D_{j+2}=(q_{j+2},q_{j+1}) and b,z head-sign D_j=(q_j,q_{j-1}). Accepted R874 applies to these two opposite two-witness waves. It gives either one of its labelled probe Hamilton P4s or the complete central fan (x,q_{j+1},q_j,y), x in {b,z}, y in {a,c}. Choose any resulting literal tight P4 K. It is proper. By R4, H-V(K) has an exact two-cover; restoring K gives a literal minimum spanning three-cover. This is the FOREST output already isolated in R1021, now consumed as one branch of the parent theorem.\n\nFinally let j=m-3. R820 states directly that its AC-side window has no T_AC term and forces\n\n  U_j OR G_AC(j).\n\nThe SEAM and GATE arguments above apply verbatim. For G_AC the witness is q_{m-2}, which is still outside X union {L,R}, exactly within the intended R682 inward-anchor scope. Hence the terminal gap also closes or exports to current maximum-three-forest dynamics.\n\nAll branches are finite and certificate-retaining. The output forest may differ completely from the source G8|N representative; no coexistence of gapwise descendants is claimed. This proves the theorem.

Retain the accepted R594/R619 ALIGNED frame in the surviving long range m>=6. Then there is a finite certificate-retaining continuation yielding either a spanning two-cover of H or an actual literal minimum spanning three-cover. ## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in the accepted ALIGNED R594/R619 frame with m>=6. Use accepted R899,R416 and pending clean bridge R1022 once reviewed.

Parent export theorem for the complete aligned R24 long phase. It does not prove R24 or extinguish the resulting maximum-three-forest dynamics.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert the final forest has lower largest-rail height or is unique. Does not claim simultaneous currentness of payment descendants. Depends on R1022 being independently accepted before this theorem is usable.

## Proof
Retain the accepted ALIGNED R594/R619 frame with m>=6. Put W=V(H)-{b,z}. Accepted R899 supplies four simultaneous exact two-covers of H[W]. We need only the pair\n\n  T_L^a=(u,L,a,c) sqcup Q[2,m],\n  T_R^c=Q[0,m-2] sqcup (a,c,R,s).\n\nR899 computes the exact cross-state set of T_L^a relative to the support partition of T_R^c. In particular the selected state La of the literal path (u,L,a,c) has L on the Q[0,m-2] component of T_R^c and a on its {a,c,R,s} component. Thus T_L^a selects a state whose endpoints lie in two distinct components of T_R^c. Both are literal path covers of the same proper residue W.\n\nApply accepted R416 with R=T_R^c and T=T_L^a, retaining the physical cross state La and both exact cover representatives. R416 composes the R176 cross-state birth with certificate-retaining pair descent. Its chosen continuation yields either a spanning two-cover of H or an ancestry-bearing both-singleton balanced floor whose ledger retains the original same-residue cross-state provenance.\n\nIn the first case we are done. In the second case apply R1022 to that genuine paid floor. Once R1022 is independently accepted, it gives a finite certificate-retaining continuation yielding either a spanning two-cover or a named proper tight trimer J whose complement has an exact two-cover by R4, hence a literal minimum spanning three-cover H=J sqcup P sqcup Qprime. This is an actual current maximum-three-forest representative.\n\nNo other aligned cross states are needed, although R899 supplies five additional simultaneous ones. The proof therefore consumes the entire ALIGNED long phase through one fixed common-residue disagreement and does not use historical exactly-two-bad seam assumptions. No R24, R5, R168, or R169 is used beyond the standing supposition that we are analyzing the R24-failure frame.

# R1025 — Every R24 failure is absorbed into current maximum-three-forest dynamics

## Statement
Let H be a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample and suppose the operative R24 singleton rail-order-four floor fails. Then there is a finite certificate-retaining continuation yielding either a spanning two-cover of H or an actual literal minimum spanning three-cover carrying explicit ancestry from the failed singleton-deletion certificate. More precisely, accepted R881 reduces the failure to the synchronized transitive order-three frame X sqcup Q with m>=6 and the fixed order-eight core G_8 plus Hamilton middle rail N. Accepted R619 gives the exhaustive ALIGNED/CROSSED phase split. In ALIGNED, R1024 exits to closure or current maximum-three-forest dynamics through the R899 common-residue cross-state and paid-floor reentry. In CROSSED, choose the existing deep gap j=3 and apply R1023, which exits to closure or current maximum-three-forest dynamics through a seam trimer, inward-gate witness, or labelled R874 P4. Therefore the unresolved long R24 core is not an independent terminal branch: any putative R24 failure feeds the global current maximum-three-forest program with its physical source ancestry retained.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample; the operative R24 floor fails. Use accepted R881,R619 and pending phase-export theorems R1023,R1024 once independently reviewed.

## Scope
Parent routing theorem. It does not prove R24 and does not extinguish maximum-three-forest holonomy/recompletion. Its content is architectural but mathematical: the entire noncircular R24 failure normal form has a finite certificate-preserving map into the current global forest state space.

## Applicability
Use instead of maintaining R24/O6 as a standalone long-core research program. After the clean R881 normalization, dispatch ALIGNED to R1024 and CROSSED to R1023. Downstream work may then consume the resulting literal current forest with retained R24 source coordinates.

## Persistence
Retain the original failed singleton-deletion cover, normalized X,Q labels, G_8|N decomposition, gate phase, and the complete ancestry of the phase-specific export: R899 cross state and paid floor in ALIGNED; chosen deep gap, R820 disjunct, inward witness/P4 or paid floor in CROSSED; and the literal output forest.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert R24 is true, that the output forest has lower largest-rail height, or that its ancestry immediately forces closure. Does not identify forests from different gap choices. R1023 and R1024 are pending and must be accepted before this theorem is usable.

## Proof
Assume the operative R24 singleton rail-order-four floor fails in the hypothetical smallest counterexample H. Thus some singleton deletion H-z has an exact two-cover with a rail of order at most three.\n\nApply accepted R881. It is entirely R24-free as a reduction theorem and gives the unique surviving normalized failure geometry: the short rail has order three; X is the synchronized transitive matching-height four-cell; Q=(q_0,...,q_m) with m>=6; and, writing L=q_0,u=q_1,s=q_{m-1},R=q_m and N=Q[2,m-2], the fixed core G_8=H[X union {L,u,s,R}] has order eight and pc(G_8)=2, while H=G_8 disjoint-union N and N is a nonempty Hamilton path. Retain the original failed singleton-deletion certificate and all normalized physical labels.\n\nAccepted R619 gives the exhaustive middle-gate phase split of this same normalized frame. We distinguish its two cases.\n\nALIGNED. Apply R1024. Its input is exactly the accepted aligned long frame with m>=6. Once R1024 is independently accepted, its finite certificate-retaining continuation yields either a spanning two-cover of H or an actual literal minimum spanning three-cover. The latter retains the R899 common-residue pair-deletion covers, their selected cross state, the paid-floor ancestry, and the output trimer/current forest.\n\nCROSSED. Since m>=6, the deep-gap range 3<=j<=m-3 is nonempty. Choose j=3. Apply R1023 to this physical gap. Once R1023 is independently accepted, its finite continuation yields either a spanning two-cover or an actual literal minimum spanning three-cover. Its ancestry records which R820 species occurred: a seam trimer, an inward gate witness and its R682/payment lineage, or the paired-terminal R874 labelled P4, together with the final current forest.\n\nThe two phases are exhaustive, so every normalized R24 failure has one of these two finite exits. Therefore every operative R24 failure yields a spanning two-cover or enters the actual current maximum-three-forest state space with a complete certificate chain back to the failed singleton-deletion cover.\n\nBecause H is assumed to be a counterexample, the spanning-two-cover outcome is impossible in the standing hypothetical setting; thus a putative R24 failure necessarily supplies the current-forest output. This last observation does not make R24 true: it only shows that the surviving R24 obstruction has been absorbed into the global maximum-three-forest problem rather than remaining a separate long-core branch. # R1026 — Every G36 source-dimer wall collision already contains a source-visible P4

**Audit state:** PASS
**Source unit:** SV117188
**Proof provenance:** `A7C3/WORKSPACE/D17/427-g36-source-dimer-collision-always-p4.md`

## Statement
Retain the G36 source-gate wall packet of SV115482. In either orientation, the source-dimer COLLISION arm already contains a literal source-visible tight P4. Consequently the collision arm is not an independent obstruction and requires no generic R523 payment, replay, fresh witness reservoir, R24, or R5.

More precisely:

- **OUT.** The collision carrier is `K=(A,t,b)`, whose reverse terminal dimer is `D_R=(b,t)`. Choose `z` among the other two source spokes with `z != b`. Testing `(C,b,t)` and `(z,b,t)`, any bad test reverses by R3 and concatenates with `(A,t,b)` to a literal P4. If both tests are tight, `C,z` are two distinct exterior head witnesses on `D_R`, so accepted exact unit SV78488 gives a literal P4.
- **IN.** The collision carrier is `K=(b,t,C)`, whose reverse initial dimer is `D_L=(t,b)`. Choose `z` among the other two source spokes with `z != b`. Testing `(t,b,A)` and `(t,b,z)`, any bad test reverses by R3 and concatenates with `(b,t,C)` to a literal P4. If both are tight, `A,z` are two distinct exterior tail witnesses on `D_L`, so the reverse-initial case of SV78488 gives a literal P4.

Thus every persistent far wall reaching a source gate yields graph-intrinsic source-visible P4 geometry in both the original P4 arm and the collision arm of SV115482.

## Proof
Retain anchors `A,C`, source spoke `t`, the other source spokes `x,y`, and the historical tight turns

`(A,t,C), (A,x,C), (A,y,C)`.

### OUT collision
SV115482 retains `(d,b,t)` and `(A,t,b)` tight. The latter is the carrier `K=(A,t,b)` and its reverse terminal dimer is `(b,t)`. Since `b` is distinct from `A,C`, choose `z in {x,y}` with `z != b`; then `C,z` are distinct vertices outside `K`.

Test `(C,b,t)`. If it is bad, R3 gives `(t,b,C)` tight, and `(A,t,b)` followed by `(t,b,C)` is the literal P4 `(A,t,b,C)`. Otherwise `C` head-signs `(b,t)`.

Now test `(z,b,t)`. If it is bad, R3 gives `(t,b,z)` tight, producing the literal P4 `(A,t,b,z)`. If it is tight, `C,z` are two distinct exterior head witnesses on the reverse terminal dimer `(b,t)` of `K`; accepted exact unit SV78488 therefore gives a literal vertex-simple tight P4.

Hence every OUT source-dimer collision already contains a source-visible P4.

### IN collision
SV115482 retains `(t,b,d)` and `(b,t,C)` tight. Now `K=(b,t,C)` is a tight trimer with reverse initial dimer `(t,b)`. Again choose `z in {x,y}` with `z != b`, so `A,z` are distinct vertices outside `K`.

Test `(t,b,A)`. If it is bad, R3 gives `(A,b,t)` tight, and together with `(b,t,C)` this gives the literal P4 `(A,b,t,C)`. Otherwise `A` tail-signs `(t,b)`.

Test `(t,b,z)`. If it is bad, R3 gives `(z,b,t)` tight, giving the literal P4 `(z,b,t,C)`. If it is tight, `A,z` are two distinct exterior tail witnesses on the reverse initial dimer `(t,b)` of `K`; the reverse-initial case of SV78488 therefore gives a literal P4.

Hence every IN source-dimer collision also contains a source-visible P4.

## Scope fence
The fixed-wall turn and old source packet remain retained certificate data. This result does **not** itself prove that the resulting P4 yields strict old-source transition descent or a spanning two-cover of `H`; source-gate P4 absorption remains a separate obligation.

# R1027 — G36 source collision rotates to the selected far dimer; without a P4 the far rail is exactly a dimer

**Audit state:** PASS
**Source unit:** SV117618
**Proof provenance:** `A7C3/WORKSPACE/D17/429-g36-source-collision-rotation-terminal-wall-dimer.md`

## Statement
Retain the G36 source-gate wall packet after SV115482 lands in its source-dimer collision branch. In either orientation, the exact R516 signature-11 mapping rotates the anchor tests onto the actual selected far dimer. Either a labelled literal P4 occurs, or the two deleted source anchors become witnesses on that selected far dimer; any continuation of the far rail then concatenates to a P4. Hence, in the no-P4 residue, the far rail is exactly that dimer.

More precisely:

- **OUT.** The selected far boundary is `b->d`, the wall turn `(d,b,t)` and source turns `(A,t,C),(A,t,b)` are tight. Unless a P4 already appears, the four-set `{A,t,b,C}` is forced into R516 signature 11, yielding `(b,A,C)` and `(b,C,A)`. Testing `(d,b,A)` and `(d,b,C)`, any tight test gives a P4; if both are bad, R3 gives `(A,b,d)` and `(C,b,d)`, so `A,C` are head witnesses on the actual selected far dimer `(b,d)`. If the rail continued through `d->e`, then `(A,b,d,e)` is a P4. Thus the no-P4 far rail is exactly `(b,d)`.
- **IN.** Dually, the selected far boundary is `d->b`; unless a P4 already appears, R516 signature 11 and the corresponding anchor tests force `(d,b,A)` and `(d,b,C)`, so `A,C` are tail witnesses on the actual selected far dimer `(d,b)`. Any selected predecessor `e->d` produces a P4, so the no-P4 far rail is exactly `(d,b)`.

The surviving non-P4 packet is therefore an anchor-saturated wall dimer retaining the actual selected orientation and the identities of the deleted source anchors.

## Proof
### OUT orientation
Retain the selected far boundary `b->d` and tight turns

`(d,b,t), (A,t,C), (A,t,b)`.

Test `(b,t,C)`. If it is tight, `(d,b,t,C)` is a literal P4. Otherwise R3 gives `(C,t,b)` tight.

Now inspect `{A,t,b,C}` using `K=(A,t,b)`. Relative to the terminal dimers of `K`, the retained turns `(A,t,C)` and `(C,t,b)` put the fourth vertex `C` in the same tail and head polarities as the natural signs. If the four-set has a tight Hamilton P4, we are done. Otherwise R516 is forced into its exact signature-11 cell, giving

`(b,A,C), (b,C,A)` tight.

Test `(d,b,A)` and `(d,b,C)`. If the first is tight, `(d,b,A,C)` is a P4. If the second is tight, `(d,b,C,A)` is a P4. Therefore in the branch with no labelled P4 both tests are bad, and R3 gives

`(A,b,d), (C,b,d)` tight.

Thus the actual selected far dimer `(b,d)` carries `A,C` as distinct head witnesses. If the selected rail continued beyond `d` via `d->e`, then the rail turn `(b,d,e)` together with `(A,b,d)` gives the literal P4 `(A,b,d,e)`. Hence the no-P4 far component is exactly the dimer `(b,d)`.

### IN orientation
Retain the selected far boundary `d->b` and tight turns

`(A,t,C), (b,t,C), (t,b,d)`.

Test `(A,t,b)`. If it is tight, `(A,t,b,d)` is a literal P4. Otherwise R3 gives `(b,t,A)`. On the tight trimer `(b,t,C)` with fourth vertex `A`, the retained source turns force the exact R516 signature-11 cell whenever no P4 exists, yielding

`(C,A,b), (A,C,b)` tight.

Testing `(A,b,d)` and `(C,b,d)`, any tight test concatenates with these turns to a labelled P4. If both are bad, R3 gives

`(d,b,A), (d,b,C)` tight.

Thus the actual selected far dimer `(d,b)` carries `A,C` as two tail witnesses. If the rail had a predecessor `e->d`, the rail turn `(e,d,b)` together with either witness turn gives a P4. Hence the no-P4 far component is exactly `(d,b)`.

## Scope fence
This result does not invoke R542 payment/capture and does not claim closure. Its gain is packet-specific: a persistent source wall has only a P4 output or one terminal selected wall dimer saturated by both source anchors. Old gate orientation, source-anchor identities, fixed-wall provenance, and selected far-dimer orientation remain retained. R24, R5, payment, replay, and generic collision compilation are unused.

- R516

# R1028 — G35 same-rail order-two suffix is a transient reverse dimer, not an R3 seam

**Audit state:** PASS_ADJUSTED
**Proof provenance:** `A7C3/WORKSPACE/D17/424-g35-successful-pivot-far-star-persistence.md`

## Statement
Retain two consecutive successful G35 defect-pivot states `M_q,M_{q+1}` with moving terminals `a_q,a_{q+1}`, fixed far source `b_m`, fixed selected successor `c` of `b_m`, and closing shortcuts `g_i=a_i->b_m`. Assume the two closures are not singleton-loop coincidences, so `a_q,a_{q+1} != b_m`, and retain the physical successful-pivot fact `a_q != a_{q+1}`.

For either state `i`, exactly one of the following far-boundary forms occurs.

1. If `c != a_i`, then `(a_i,b_m,c)` is a genuine three-distinct-vertex seam. If that seam is bad, R3 applies legally and gives the reverse-star turn `(c,b_m,a_i)` tight.
2. If `c = a_i`, then there is no three-vertex seam at all. The already selected edge `b_m->a_i` and the shortcut `a_i->b_m` form the explicit order-two reverse dimer/backtrack `b_m->a_i->b_m`, and R3 is not invoked.

The reverse-dimer case cannot occur at both consecutive successful states, because `a_q != a_{q+1}` while `c` is fixed. Consequently any far-seam obstruction that genuinely persists across the two closures lies in the first case at both indices and yields the two reverse-star turns `(c,b_m,a_q)` and `(c,b_m,a_{q+1})`. Thus the missing same-rail order-two suffix is one-step debt and does not alter the G35 persistent-far-star conclusion or the G36 consumer of genuinely persistent fixed-wall debt.

## Hypotheses
The consecutive successful-pivot G35 setup of D17.424; `b_m` has fixed selected successor `c`; neither closure is the singleton-loop coincidence; R3 is available only for genuine three-distinct-vertex triples.

## Scope
This is the audited repair of the same-rail order-two suffix in the G35 persistence argument. It certifies the legality of every R3 use at the far boundary and separates the repeated-vertex case into an explicit reverse-dimer branch.

## Applicability
Use whenever the G35/G36 corridor argument treats the fixed far successor `c`. Before invoking R3 on `(a_i,b_m,c)`, test `c=a_i`. Equality is the transient reverse-dimer branch; inequality is the genuine seam branch. Persistent fixed-wall debt across consecutive successful pivots is therefore always represented by reverse-star turns on distinct vertices.

## Persistence
The physical vertices `a_q,a_{q+1},b_m,c`, the selected far edge `b_m->c`, and the two closing shortcuts are retained literally. No anonymous replacement of the repeated-vertex case by a trimer is permitted.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not claim that every closure fails, that every failure is a far-seam failure, or that the resulting reverse star by itself closes the proof. It repairs only the omitted same-rail order-two branch. Near-seam and ordinary shortcut-cycle transport remain governed by the surrounding G35 argument.

## Proof
Because `b_m->c` is a selected path edge, `b_m != c`. At state `i`, the closing shortcut is `g_i=a_i->b_m`, and by the nonloop hypothesis `a_i != b_m`.

First suppose `c != a_i`. Then `a_i,b_m,c` are pairwise distinct, so `(a_i,b_m,c)` is a legitimate three-vertex seam. If it is bad, boundary antisymmetry R3 applies to this actual triple and gives its exact reversal `(c,b_m,a_i)` tight. There is no repeated-vertex use of R3 in this branch.

Now suppose `c=a_i`. The selected far edge is then literally `b_m->a_i`, while the shortcut is its reverse `a_i->b_m`. Adding the shortcut therefore creates the two-edge backtrack `b_m->a_i->b_m`. The notation `(a_i,b_m,c)` would repeat `a_i` and is not a trimer, so R3 is not applicable and is not used. This is an explicit reverse-dimer branch rather than a seam branch.

The successor `c` of `b_m` is unchanged by the successful pivot: the pivot does not alter the selected outgoing edge of `b_m` in the G35 setup. The moving terminal does change, so `a_q != a_{q+1}`. Hence `c=a_q` implies `c!=a_{q+1}`, and `c=a_{q+1}` implies `c!=a_q`. The reverse-dimer branch therefore cannot persist across the two consecutive successful states.

Suppose now that the same physical far-seam obstruction is bad at both states. Since the reverse-dimer branch is not a three-vertex seam and cannot occur at both states, persistence as a far seam forces

`c!=a_q` and `c!=a_{q+1}`.

Both triples are therefore genuine and R3 yields

`(c,b_m,a_q)` tight and `(c,b_m,a_{q+1})` tight.

These are exactly two spokes of the fixed far reverse star anchored at `(c,b_m)`. Thus the only correction needed in D17.424 is the explicit order-two backtrack branch. It is transient and cannot furnish the persistent fixed-wall debt consumed by the G36 corridor. The persistent branch, when present, is unchanged and all of its R3 invocations are on distinct vertices.

## Dependencies
- R3

**Audit state:** PASS
**Proof provenance:** Slack `#a7c3-workspace` root `1789300001.841769`

## Statement
Retain the P5-free twin-wall residue of the DIRECT source-wall branch from D17.430.

- **IN.** The selected far boundary is `d->b`, and the twin wall paths give `(A,t,b)`, `(C,t,b)`, and `(t,b,d)` tight. Then both `(A,d,b)` and `(C,d,b)` are tight. Equivalently, `A,C` are distinct head witnesses on the actual selected far dimer `(d,b)`.

## Hypotheses
The exact D17.430 DIRECT twin-wall packet in either orientation; the induced five-set on `{A,C,t,b,d}` has no tight Hamilton P5; boundary antisymmetry R3.

## Scope
This is a local packet normalization. It does not by itself give a spanning two-cover, strict transition descent, or a source-gate zipper absorption theorem. Use in the P5-free DIRECT branch whenever a later consumer is sensitive to signed witnesses on the physical far dimer. In OUT the witnesses have the polarity represented by `(b,d,A)` and `(b,d,C)`; in IN the dual polarity is represented by `(A,d,b)` and `(C,d,b)`.

Retain the physical vertices `A,C,t,b,d`, the selected far-edge orientation, both twin wall P4s, and the two forced witness turns. The result does not anonymize or replace the far dimer.

## Proof
### OUT orientation
Retain the two tight wall P4s

`(d,b,t,A)` and `(d,b,t,C)`.

Equivalently, `(d,b,t)`, `(b,t,A)`, and `(b,t,C)` are tight, and the actual selected far boundary is `b->d`.

Test `(b,d,A)`. If it were bad, R3 would give its complete reversal `(A,d,b)` tight. Together with the already tight turns `(d,b,t)` and `(b,t,C)`, this would make

`(A,d,b,t,C)`

a literal tight Hamilton P5 on the five vertices `{A,C,t,b,d}`, contrary to the P5-free hypothesis. Hence `(b,d,A)` is tight.

`(A,t,b,d)` and `(C,t,b,d)`.

# R1031 — G37 first-loss zipper must be synchronized with certified source-boundary ancestry

**Audit state:** PASS_ADJUSTED
**Proof provenance:** Slack `#a7c3-workspace` root `1789300014.096059`, updated against D17.421 and D17.433–438.

## Statement
Within the G37 source-gate route, two established facts fence the remaining zipper-absorption problem.

1. The retained D17.430 five-set data do **not** imply a Hamilton P5 with the fixed far-wall vertex as an endpoint; endpoint-controlled far-wall insertion cannot be taken for free.
2. In the sharp G35 hard cell, D17.421 localizes the first numerical loss of strict old-source transition descent to one exact `K_{2,2}` two-crossing zipper rectangle, modulo the unique singleton-defect loop interruption.

The later ancestry contractions D17.433–438 sharpen how source data meet that rectangle:

- in the SINGLETON-SPOKE class, the first-loss rectangle itself is canonically source-rooted;
- in the only v-rooted X-MATED class, the cliff rectangle is not source-rooted, but the same augmenter has a canonical later terminal X-mated source boundary with transition count at most two and retained source ancestry.

Therefore the live unproved interface in this route is not a source-anonymous exact zipper and not a free endpoint-P5 splice. It is the synchronization/absorption of the exact numerical-cliff rectangle with the certified source boundary/wall packet carried by the same ancestry. A proposed relative-orientation exchange between source-anchor choices and zipper-crossing choices remains a candidate mechanism only; it is not established by these results.

## Hypotheses
The sharp G35/G37 hard-cell setup of D17.421 and D17.433–438; the D17.430 source-wall packet where relevant.

## Scope
This is a durable integration fence, not a closure theorem. It records exactly what is proved about the first-loss location and source placement, and exactly what is not available from D17.430 alone.

## Applicability
Any zipper-absorption argument in this route must:

- use the exact D17.421 `K_{2,2}` first-loss rectangle rather than an anonymous generic P4 insertion;
- retain the source-placement information from D17.433–438;
- not assume a Hamilton P5 whose endpoint is the fixed wall vertex merely from D17.430;
- explicitly justify whatever synchronization, exchange, or seam-safe pairing is used between the source packet and the numerical cliff.

## Persistence
Retain the physical first-loss rectangle and its old/new pairings, the source-root placement class, the ordered source-spoke block and X-mates in the v-rooted class, the canonical terminal source boundary when present, and the actual fixed far-wall data. Do not collapse these to an anonymous reflected `K_{2,2}`.

## Proof
R1029 supplies an explicit five-vertex boundary tournament satisfying the retained D17.430 OUT star-cycle turns while having no Hamilton P5 with the wall vertex as an endpoint. Thus endpoint control is not a consequence of the five-set packet.

Independently, D17.421 proves that consecutive normalized closures differ by a single `K_{2,2}` matching switch, with transition count changes only in `{-2,0,2}`. At the first non-loop index where the old transition floor is reached, the previous closure has transition count `tau(F)-2`, the new one has `tau(F)`, and the switch replaces two same-side edges by two `X|B` edges. This is the canonical exact two-crossing numerical cliff.

D17.433 then shows that throughout the SINGLETON-SPOKE hard cell this first-loss rectangle is source-rooted: the unique `X-X` member of its old same-side diagonal is incident with the physical source spoke responsible for the first transition rise.

D17.434 isolates the sole possible non-source-rooted cliff as the v-rooted X-MATED cell. D17.435 identifies its old source support as an ordered three-spoke block with two opposite-polarity X-mated source gates. D17.436 proves that at least one such source gate lies strictly after the v-cliff on the same augmenter. D17.438 then takes the last old F-transition on that augmenter and obtains a canonical terminal low-transition source boundary retaining the source trimer and X-mated source-block ancestry.

Hence the original Slack wording is correct in its endpoint-control fence and exact-zipper localization, but the phrase `source-anchor/P4 packet + exact K2,2 zipper` is too coarse after D17.433–438 because it can suggest that the source packet is always literally rooted at the numerical cliff. The corrected interface distinguishes source-at-cliff from source-at-terminal-boundary and identifies the missing work as synchronizing those certified objects. No relative-orientation exchange theorem is supplied by the cited results.

- `A7C3/WORKSPACE/D17/433-g37-singleton-spoke-source-rooted-first-loss-zipper.md`

# R1032 — Sharp source-frame counts do not consume the one-vertex obstruction

## Statement
There exists a globally edge-ordered Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament realizing the following data simultaneously:

- `B=(b1,b2,b3,b4)` is a tight Hamilton spectator path;
- `X={v,p,q,r}`;
- the three source turns `(A,p,C),(A,q,C),(A,r,C)` are tight;
- the source five-set `S={A,C,p,q,r}` has a Hamilton P5;
- `S union {v}` has no Hamilton P6;
- `B union {v}` has no Hamilton P5;
- on `G=H-{A,C}`, the literal old source two-cover

      F=(b1,p,q,r,b4) | (v,b2,b3)

  is tight and has `tau(F)=3`;
- the literal three-forest

      J=(p,q,r) | (v,b4,b3) | (b1,b2)

  is tight and has `tau(J)=1`.

Thus the raw source turns, Hamilton spectator, physicality of `F` and `J`, sharp transition counts, internal three-spoke old-source block, and simultaneous nonHamiltonicity of the two contracted one-vertex extensions do not by themselves force the G40/G41 closure. Any successful consumer must use further structure such as canonical D17.421 first-loss/gate ancestry, another genuine synchronization input, or a global minimal-counterexample consequence.

This is a fence on an abstraction, not a smallest counterexample.

## Construction
Use vertices

    {A,C,p,q,r,v,b1,b2,b3,b4}.

Define tight turns by a global strict order on ordinary edges: `(x,m,y)` is tight exactly when edge `xm` precedes edge `my`.

On the six-vertex nucleus `N={A,C,p,q,r,v}`, impose the edge order

    Ap < rv < Aq < Cp < Ar < AC < pr < Cv
       < pq < Av < Cq < pv < qr < qv < Cr.

Then the source turns are immediate:

    Ap < Cp,
    Aq < Cq,
    Ar < Cr.

Also

    Ap < pq < qr < Cr,

so `A,p,q,r,C` is a tight Hamilton P5 on `S`.

Direct enumeration of the `6!` vertex orders shows that no order of all six vertices has monotonically increasing consecutive edge weights. Hence `N=S union {v}` has no tight Hamilton P6.

On `{b1,b2,b3,b4,v}`, impose

    b3v < b2b4 < b2v < b1b3 < b1b4
        < b4v < b1b2 < b2b3 < b1v < b3b4.

Then

    b1b2 < b2b3 < b3b4,

so `B=(b1,b2,b3,b4)` is tight. Direct enumeration of the `5!` vertex orders shows that `B union {v}` has no tight Hamilton P5.

Finally impose the two cross inequalities

    b1p < pq,
    qr < rb4.

The two displayed total-order chains and these two additional inequalities form an acyclic partial order on ordinary edges, so extend it arbitrarily to a total edge order on the full vertex set.

## Verification of F and J
For

    F=(b1,p,q,r,b4) | (v,b2,b3),

we have

    b1p < pq < qr < rb4

and

    b2v < b2b3.

Thus both rails are tight. Relative to `X|B`, the selected crossing edges are `b1p`, `rb4`, and `vb2`, so `tau(F)=3`. The three source spokes occur consecutively and internally on the first rail.

For

    J=(p,q,r) | (v,b4,b3) | (b1,b2),

we have `pq<qr` and `vb4<b4b3`; the last component has order two. Hence `J` is a literal tight three-forest. Its only selected `X|B` edge is `vb4`, so `tau(J)=1`.

All claimed structures therefore coexist in one globally edge-ordered realization.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
The construction is not asserted to satisfy the canonical D17.421 first-loss rectangle, the later gate ancestry, the exact canonical `J` selection procedure, or smallest-counterexample minimality. It proves only that the displayed raw/sharp data are insufficient without some additional canonical or global input.

## Audit note
This explicit counterconfiguration received targeted review because it determines whether current strategy may safely abandon generic sharp-count consumers. The edge-order constraints are acyclic; the source turns and literal path/forest inequalities were checked directly; exhaustive enumeration confirms zero Hamilton P6 orders on `S union {v}` and zero Hamilton P5 orders on `B union {v}`. It remains audited and usable, but is no longer kept on the curated INTERESTING shelf because R1034 strictly strengthens the same strategic insufficiency fence.

# R1035 — G37 singleton-spoke first-loss zipper is source-rooted when both adjacent closures exist

**Audit state:** PASS_ADJUSTED
**Proof provenance:** Slack `#a7c3-workspace` root `1789311947.865839`, audited against D17.419 and D17.421.

## Statement
Assume the sharp G35/G37 hard-cell setup in the SINGLETON-SPOKE branch of D17.419. Let

\[
e_i=a_{i-1}\to b_i,\qquad f_i=a_i\to b_i,
\]

be the zipper coordinates, let `r` be the first index with `chi(e_r)=1`, and for every admissible shortcut closure `g_q=a_q->b_m` let `T_q` be the transition count of the resulting closed path.

Then:

1. `W_0=0`.
2. For every admissible `q`,
   \[
   T_q=1+S_q+(S_q\bmod 2).
   \]
   Hence the admissible closure totals are `1` before the first source transition, `3` on the plateau after the first source transition, and `3` after the second source transition.
3. If **both adjacent closures** `g_{r-1}` and `g_r` are defined, then the first numerical loss of strict old-source descent occurs at the switch from `g_{r-1}` to `g_r`: `T_{r-1}=1<2` and `T_r=3>=2`. The associated `K_{2,2}` rectangle is source-rooted. Its old same-side diagonal consists of exactly one `X-X` edge incident with the physical source `t` and one `B-B` edge.
4. If either `g_{r-1}` or `g_r` is undefined because it is the unique singleton-defect loop allowed by D17.421, no literal `K_{2,2}` switch is asserted at index `r`. The numerical staircase remains valid on all admissible closures, but the would-be first-loss rectangle is interrupted by the loop defect.

## Adjustment to D17.433
D17.433 correctly derives the staircase and the source geometry of the switch, but its stated proviso excludes only the possibility that `g_r` is the unique loop. D17.421 requires **both** `g_{r-1}` and `g_r` to exist before the adjacent closures form the literal `K_{2,2}` matching switch. The additional obstruction is real: the unique loop may occur at `g_{r-1}` while `g_r` remains admissible.

Thus the durable corrected statement is the one above. No claim is made that the literal source-rooted first-loss rectangle exists when either adjacent closure is the loop defect.

## Proof
By D17.419, in the SINGLETON-SPOKE branch the distinguished cycle `C_*` contains exactly the two F-selected transition edges, both incident with the physical source `t`, and no J-selected transition edge. Therefore `w(C_*)=2`; the prefix sum `S_q` is the `0,1,2` staircase whose rises occur at the two source-transition indices.

In the G37 hard cell,

\[
\tau(F)-\tau(J)=3-1=2=w(C_*)+W_0.
\]

Since `w(C_*)=2`, necessarily `W_0=0`.

D17.421 gives, for every admissible shortcut closure,

\[
T_q=1+S_q+W_0+\gamma_q,
\]

where

\[
\gamma_q=((S_q\bmod 2)\oplus(w(C_*)\bmod 2)).
\]

Because `w(C_*)=2` is even and `W_0=0`, this reduces to

\[
T_q=1+S_q+(S_q\bmod 2).
\]

The three staircase levels `S_q=0,1,2` therefore give transition totals `1,3,3` respectively, whenever the corresponding closure is admissible.

Let `r` be the first source-transition index. If both `g_{r-1}` and `g_r` exist, then `S_{r-1}=0` and `S_r=1`, so `T_{r-1}=1` and `T_r=3`. D17.421 identifies the passage between these adjacent closures as the exact `K_{2,2}` matching switch on the rectangle with old diagonal

\[
\{a_{r-1}b_m,\;a_rb_r\}
\]

and new diagonal

\[
\{a_{r-1}b_r,\;a_rb_m\}.
\]

Because the first transition edge `e_r=a_{r-1}b_r` is incident with physical source `t`, there are two copy-geometric cases. If `a_{r-1}=t\in X`, then `b_r,a_r\in B` and `b_m\in X`; hence `a_{r-1}b_m` is the unique old `X-X` edge and is incident with `t`, while `a_rb_r` is `B-B`. If `b_r=t\in X`, then `a_{r-1},b_m\in B` and `a_r\in X`; hence `a_rb_r` is the unique old `X-X` edge and is incident with `t`, while `a_{r-1}b_m` is `B-B`. Thus the literal first-loss rectangle, when defined, is source-rooted exactly as claimed.

Finally, D17.421 explicitly allows one unique shortcut index at which `a_q=b_m`, so `g_q` is a loop and the closure is undefined. Its `K_{2,2}` switch statement applies only when **both** adjacent closures exist. Therefore a loop at `g_{r-1}` (as well as a loop at `g_r`) prevents the literal switch at `r`, although it does not alter the formula on the remaining admissible closures. This is precisely the missing qualification in D17.433.

## Scope
This result certifies the SINGLETON-SPOKE numerical staircase and the source-rooted geometry of the first transition switch. It does not bridge across the unique loop defect and does not assert a physical first-loss rectangle when one of its two adjacent shortcut closures is undefined.

# R1036 — G37 hard-cell first positive pivot has a source/v marked corner when its adjacent switch exists

**Audit state:** PASS_ADJUSTED
**Proof provenance:** Slack `#a7c3-workspace` root `1789312109.292509`, audited against D17.419, D17.421, and corrected D17.433/R1035.

## Statement
Retain the sharp G35/G37 hard cell

`tau(F)=3`, `tau(J)=1`, `w(C_*)=2`,

with the F-normalized prefix closures of D17.421. Write

`W_0=sum_D w(D)`

for the total transition weight of the delta-zero components, let `S_q` be the zipper prefix ledger, and let `r` be the first index with `S_r>0`.

Then:

1. `W_0=0`, and every admissible normalized closure satisfies `T_q = 1 + S_q + (S_q mod 2)`.
2. For every admissible `q<r`, `S_q in {-1,0}` and hence `T_q=1`. At the first positive pivot, `S_r=1`; if `g_r` is admissible, `T_r=3=tau(F)`. Thus `r` is the first admissible numerical threshold index whenever `g_r` exists.
3. A **literal first-loss K_{2,2} rectangle at r** exists only when both adjacent closures `g_{r-1}` and `g_r` are defined. In that case its old same-side diagonal has one `X-X` edge and one `B-B` edge, and the `X-X` edge is incident with the physical X-endpoint `z` of the installed old F-transition `e_r`.
4. When that rectangle exists, exactly the intended root dichotomy holds:
   - if `z` is one of the three source spokes, the rectangle is source-rooted;
   - if it is not source-rooted, then `z=v`, the unique non-spoke X-vertex. This v-rooted case can occur only in the X-MATED SOURCE GATE ancestry class of D17.419. Since `d_F(v)=1`, every other old F transition is source-bearing.
5. If `g_{r-1}` is the unique singleton-defect loop while `g_r` exists, the numerical threshold still occurs at `r`, but there is no literal adjacent switch there. If `g_r` is the loop, the threshold closure itself is interrupted. In either loop case no source/v classification of a nonexistent first-loss rectangle is asserted.

## Adjustment to D17.434
D17.434 correctly proves the sharp-cell arithmetic, the first-positive ledger behavior, and the marked-corner geometry. It overstates the passage from the numerical threshold to a literal zipper rectangle by treating `g_r` as the only relevant loop check.

D17.421 defines the switch at index `r` by comparing the two closures `g_{r-1}` and `g_r`, so **both** must exist. The unique loop may occur at `g_{r-1}`. In that configuration `g_r` can be admissible and already have transition count three, yet the claimed `K_{2,2}` rectangle comparing the previous and current closures is absent.

Accordingly the durable dichotomy is a dichotomy of the literal first-loss rectangle **when the adjacent switch exists**. The numerical staircase itself does not need repair.

## Proof
Transition differences add over the symmetric-difference components. The sharp cell gives

`tau(F)-tau(J)=3-1=2=w(C_*)+W_0`.

Since `w(C_*)=2`, `W_0=0`. Because `w(C_*)` is even, D17.421 gives `gamma_q=S_q mod 2`, and therefore every admissible closure has

`T_q=1+S_q+(S_q mod 2)`.

For `q<r`, minimality of the first positive pivot gives `S_q<=0`. The normalized prefix matching has transition count `1+S_q`, which is a nonnegative integer, so `S_q>=-1`. Thus `S_q in {-1,0}` and the closure formula gives `T_q=1` whenever `g_q` exists. The one-step ledger changes by at most one, so `S_r=1`; if `g_r` exists then `T_r=3`. This proves the numerical threshold statement independently of whether `g_{r-1}` exists.

Now assume both `g_{r-1}` and `g_r` exist. D17.421 identifies their difference as the literal switch

`{f_r,g_{r-1}} <-> {e_r,g_r}`.

The old pair is same-side and the new pair is crossing. Let `z` be the physical X-endpoint of `e_r=a_{r-1}->b_r`. If `z=a_{r-1}`, then `g_{r-1}` is `X-X` and `f_r` is `B-B`; if `z=b_r`, then `f_r` is `X-X` and `g_{r-1}` is `B-B`. Hence the old `X-X` edge is canonically incident with `z`.

The hard-cell X-side is `{v,p,q,s}`, with `p,q,s` the three source spokes and `v` the sole non-spoke. Therefore `z` is either a source spoke or `v`. In the first case the rectangle is source-rooted. Corrected D17.433/R1035 shows that, whenever its adjacent switch exists, the SINGLETON-SPOKE branch lies in this source-rooted case. Consequently a literal non-source-rooted first-loss rectangle must be in the other D17.419 ancestry branch, X-MATED SOURCE GATE, and must have `z=v`. The old-source degree law `d_F(v)=1` then implies that every other old F transition is source-bearing.

Finally, D17.421 allows one unique index with `a_q=b_m`, making `g_q` a forbidden loop. If this index is `r-1`, then the individually admissible closure `g_r` may still realize the numerical threshold `T_r=3`, but the adjacent switch at `r` is undefined. If the loop is at `r`, the threshold closure is itself absent. This is the sole correction needed to D17.434.

## Scope
This result preserves the sharp-cell contraction but distinguishes two objects that D17.434 partially conflated: the first admissible closure at the old transition floor, and the literal adjacent `K_{2,2}` rectangle witnessing the rise. The source/v-rooted dichotomy applies to the latter only when both adjacent closures exist.

## Dependencies
- `A7C3/WORKSPACE/D17/419-g35-hard-cell-source-xx-mate-or-singleton-spoke-atom.md`
- `A7C3/WORKSPACE/D17/421-g35-normalized-shortcut-transition-frontier.md`
- `A7C3/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R1035.md`
- `A7C3/WORKSPACE/D17/434-g37-hard-cell-first-loss-root-dichotomy.md`

# R1037 — A v-rooted sharp source cover has a singleton v block and a two-ended three-spoke source block

**Audit state:** PASS
**Proof provenance:** Slack `#a7c3-workspace` root `1789312204.974029`; repaired directly from the sharp source-cover hypotheses rather than the missing historical D17.418/SV provenance.

## Statement
Let `F` be the retained exact two-path source cover of

`G = B disjoint-union X`, `X={v,p,q,r}`,

with `p,q,r` internal vertices of `F` and `tau(F)=3`. Assume the v-rooted residual cell, so the selected F-edge incident with `v` at the first-loss root is an `X|B` transition.

Then

`d_F(v)=1`, `e_XX(F)=2`, `b_X(F)=2`, `b_B(F)=3`.

Moreover the two maximal X-blocks of `F` are exactly:

- the singleton endpoint block `{v}`;
- one internal block containing all three source spokes.

Thus, up to complete reversal, the source block occurs literally as

`B_L -> s_1 -> s_2 -> s_3 -> B_R`,

where `{s_1,s_2,s_3}={p,q,r}`. Its two boundary `X|B` edges are opposite-polarity source gates, and both are X-mated by the internal edges `s_1s_2` and `s_2s_3`. The third and only non-source transition of `F` is the unique `v-B` edge.

## Proof
Because `p,q,r` are internal in the two-path cover, their selected degrees are all two. Let `d=d_F(v)` and let `e_XX` be the number of selected F-edges with both ends in X. Counting selected incidences at X gives

`6+d = 2e_XX + tau(F) = 2e_XX+3`.

The v-rooted hypothesis supplies a selected edge at `v`, so `d` is either one or two. The displayed equation makes `d` odd. Hence

`d_F(v)=1`,

and therefore `e_XX=2`.

Every maximal X-block with `m` vertices contributes exactly `m-1` selected X-X edges, so across the four X-vertices

`e_XX = |X|-b_X = 4-b_X`.

Thus `b_X=2`.

Across two nonempty directed paths, the total number of maximal monochromatic X/B blocks equals the number of X|B transitions plus the number of path components. Hence

`b_X+b_B = tau(F)+2 = 5`,

so `b_B=3`.

Now the unique selected edge incident with `v` is the displayed X|B transition. Therefore `v` cannot be adjacent in F to another X-vertex, and its maximal X-block is exactly `{v}`. Since there are exactly two X-blocks, the other one contains all of `p,q,r`.

All three source spokes are internal in F. Consequently the three-spoke X-block is itself internal on its rail: its two endpoint spokes each have one selected X-X incidence inside the block and one selected X|B incidence outside it. Writing the literal directed order as `s_1,s_2,s_3`, the rail segment is, up to reversal,

`B_L -> s_1 -> s_2 -> s_3 -> B_R`.

The two boundary transitions therefore have opposite path polarity, and each endpoint source gate is X-mated by its adjacent internal X-X edge. These two gates plus the unique v-B edge account for all three transitions because `tau(F)=3`.

No historical D17.418, SV101138, SV109219, R24, or R5 input is required.

## Scope
This is a path-cover bookkeeping theorem specialized to the retained sharp source frame. It reconstructs the quantitative and block-structure content formerly attributed to the missing D17.418 source in the v-rooted cell.

# R1038 — Every v-rooted sharp first-loss augmenter has a forward X-mated source gate

**Audit state:** PASS
**Proof provenance:** Slack `#a7c3-workspace` root `1789312289.841599`; repaired after the direct reconstruction in R1037.

## Statement
Retain the v-rooted sharp first-loss cell with

`tau(F)=3`, `tau(J)=1`, `w(C_*)=2`,

and let `r` be the first zipper index with positive prefix ledger `S_r>0`. Assume the installed F-transition at `r` is the unique v-B transition from R1037.

Let `n_F` and `n_J` be the numbers of F-selected and J-selected X|B transition edges on the unique augmenter `C_*`. Then

`(n_F,n_J)` is either `(2,0)` or `(3,1)`.

In either case at least one of the two X-mated source gates from R1037 occurs strictly after the v-transition along `C_*`. If a source gate occurs before `v`, then it is numerically neutralized by the unique J-transition before the first-positive v-pivot.

## Proof
Since `w(C_*)=2`,

`n_F-n_J=2`.

Globally `F` has exactly three transitions and `J` exactly one, so

`0<=n_F<=3`, `0<=n_J<=1`.

Therefore the only possibilities are

`(n_F,n_J)=(2,0)` or `(3,1)`.

By R1037 the three F-transitions are exactly the unique v-B transition and the two endpoint source gates of the three-spoke source block, and both source gates are X-mated.

### Case 1: `(2F,0J)`
There is no negative J contribution anywhere on `C_*`. Because `r` is the first index with positive prefix ledger and the v-transition is an F-transition at `r`, no F-transition can occur earlier. Hence the other F-transition on `C_*` lies strictly after `r`. It cannot be the v-transition again, so it is one of the two X-mated source gates.

### Case 2: `(3F,1J)`
All three F-transitions lie on `C_*`, together with the unique J-transition. Suppose both source-gate F-transitions occurred before the v-transition at `r`. Their total positive contribution would be `+2`, while the entire component contains only one J-transition contributing `-1`. After both source gates and that possible negative contribution have been encountered, some proper prefix before `r` would therefore have ledger at least `+1`, contradicting the definition of `r` as the first positive prefix.

Thus at least one source gate lies strictly after `r`.

The same prefix argument shows that any source gate occurring before `r` must be neutralized by the unique J-transition: it cannot appear alone and leave positive ledger before the designated first-positive pivot.

## Scope
The result is a numerical-ordering consequence of the sharp augmenter together with the directly reconstructed source-block structure R1037. It does not assert that transport to the forward gate is physically successful or that the gate itself closes the global two-cover problem.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R1038.md -->

# R1039 — Exact off-augmenter transition trichotomy in the v-rooted sharp cell

**Audit state:** PASS_ADJUSTED  
**Proof provenance:** D17.437, repaired against D17.421 and audited R1037/R1038.

## Statement
Assume the v-rooted sharp cell

`tau(F)=3`, `tau(J)=1`, `w(C_*)=2`,

with the remaining components of `F triangle J` neutral in matching cardinality, and retain the audited source-block and forward-gate conclusions R1037/R1038.

Then the total transition weight of the neutral symmetric-difference components is

`W_0 = sum_D w(D) = 0`.

Moreover:

1. If `C_*` carries `(3F,1J)` transition incidences, every neutral component is transition-free.
2. If `C_*` carries `(2F,0J)`, exactly one F-transition and one J-transition remain off `C_*`. The remaining F-transition is the opposite X-mated source gate from R1037. Exactly one of the following occurs:
   - **COMMON:** the F- and J-transition are the same selected edge in `F intersect J`; every neutral component is transition-free.
   - **PAIRED NEUTRAL:** they are distinct edges on one neutral component, which has exactly `(1F,1J)` transition incidences and weight `0`; every other neutral component is transition-free.
   - **SPLIT NEUTRAL:** they are distinct edges on two neutral components; the F-only component has weight `+1`, the J-only component has weight `-1`, and every other neutral component is transition-free.

Thus the first two branches exhaust the `2F/0J` case only if an independent componentwise inequality `w(D)<=0` is available for every neutral component. The aggregate normalization `W_0<=0` recorded in D17.421 does not by itself imply that inequality componentwise.

## Proof
The global transition gap is

`tau(F)-tau(J)=3-1=2`.

The distinguished augmenter contributes `w(C_*)=2`, so additivity of transition weight over the noncommon symmetric-difference edges gives

`W_0 = tau(F)-tau(J)-w(C_*) = 0`.

In the `(3F,1J)` case, `C_*` already contains all three F-transition incidences and the unique J-transition incidence. Hence no transition edge of either matching remains on a neutral component, so every neutral component is transition-free.

In the `(2F,0J)` case, exactly one of the three F-transitions and the unique J-transition remain off `C_*`. By R1037/R1038 the off-augmenter F-transition is the other X-mated boundary source gate. If the two remaining transition incidences are the same selected edge, that edge belongs to `F intersect J` and hence is absent from `F triangle J`, giving COMMON.

Otherwise the two transition edges lie in the symmetric difference. Since there is exactly one remaining F-transition and exactly one remaining J-transition, either they lie on the same neutral component or on two distinct neutral components. In the same-component case that component has local weight `1-1=0`; all other neutral components have no transition incidence. In the distinct-component case the component carrying the F-transition has weight `+1`, the component carrying the J-transition has weight `-1`, and all others have weight `0`. These weights sum to the already established `W_0=0`.

No fourth placement is possible.

## Adjustment to D17.437
D17.437 correctly identified the COMMON correction and the unchanged `(3F,1J)` branch, but it also asserted `w(D)=0` for every neutral component by citing the absent D17.416 componentwise inequality. The surviving durable D17.421 interface records only the aggregate `W_0<=0`; aggregate equality `W_0=0` does not exclude simultaneous `+1` and `-1` neutral components. The exact repair is therefore to retain the COMMON and paired-neutral branches and add the SPLIT NEUTRAL branch above.

# R1040 — Terminal X-mated source boundary in the v-rooted hard cell

**Status:** PASS_ADJUSTED
**Source:** D17.438

## Statement

In the v-rooted hard cell, let `C_*` be the unique augmenter and let `e_k` be its last old `F`-transition. Then `e_k` occurs strictly after the v-transition, is one of the two X-mated source gates, and the terminal alternating suffix beginning at `e_k` can be exchanged into `J` to produce a matching of the same cardinality as `J` with transition count at most two. The terminal gate is source-bearing, so its source spoke `t` retains the historical tight source trimer `(A,t,C)` and the adjacent old X-X mate supplied by R1037.

This result does **not** assert, without a separate theorem, that the historical D17.425 wall consumer automatically launches from this matching-level boundary or that the boundary is already a physical tight three-forest.

## Proof

R1037 identifies the three old `F` transitions in the v-rooted cell: the unique v-B transition and the two opposite-polarity X-mated source gates. R1038 shows that at least one of the source gates lies strictly after the v-transition on `C_*`. Hence the last old `F`-transition `e_k` lies strictly after the v-transition and cannot be v-bearing. It is therefore an X-mated source gate.

Write the alternating component in the indexing used for the terminal exchange, and form

`J' = J - {f_{k-1},...,f_{m-1}} + {e_k,...,e_m}`.

The alternating suffix exchange preserves matching cardinality. If `chi` is the X|B-transition indicator, then

`tau(J') = tau(J) - sum_{i=k-1}^{m-1} chi(f_i) + sum_{i=k}^{m} chi(e_i)`.

Since `k` is the last old `F`-transition on the component,

`sum_{i=k}^{m} chi(e_i)=1`.

Using `tau(J)=1` and nonnegativity of the removed-J sum gives

`tau(J') <= 1 + 1 = 2`.

Because `e_k` is source-bearing, its source endpoint `t` still carries the graph-intrinsic tight trimer `(A,t,C)`. R1037 additionally supplies the adjacent selected X-X mate and the ordered three-spoke source block.

## Audit adjustment

The original D17.438 text further said that this boundary automatically satisfies the hypotheses needed to launch D17.425's historical source-oriented wall machinery. That consumer implication was not durably reconstructed during audit and is unnecessary for the terminal-boundary theorem. It is therefore removed from the certified statement rather than treated as mathematical failure.

No R24, R5, or unrecovered D17.420 theorem is used.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R1040.md -->

# R1042 — Arbitrary insertion oscillation and the common prefix-cut backbone

**Status:** PASS
**Source:** G39 workspace barrier root; durable development `A7C3/WORKSPACE/two-vertex-extension-barrier.md`

## Statement

Let `B=(b_1,...,b_m)` be a tight displayed Hamilton path in the R3 comparison abstraction.

1. For every subset `I⊆{2,...,m-2}` there is an R3-compatible comparison orientation and an outside vertex `x` such that insertion of `x` after `b_i` preserves tightness exactly for `i∈I`. Hence no universal interval, one-crossing, or first-loss/last-gain theorem for one-vertex insertion follows from `R3 + B tight` alone.
2. Fix `B` and an outside vertex `v`, and let `s` vary over companion vertices. In the B-order-preserving prefix automaton on `B∪{v,s}`, the positive-reachability region before `s` has been consumed is independent of `s`. Consequently, whenever `H[B∪{v,s}]` is nonHamiltonian, the canonical B-ordered failure cuts for different companions share exactly the same `s`-free prefix-cut backbone; companion-specific cut behavior can begin only on a transition that consumes `s` or after `s` has already been consumed.

The first item is only an R3-level fence and does not assert realization of the full live source-frame packet. The second item is a certificate for the B-order-preserving Hamilton-word subproblem; full nonHamiltonicity implies this restricted failure, but the converse is not claimed.

## Proof

Write `e_i={b_i,b_{i+1}}`. For every internal `b_j`, prescribe

`e_{j-1} -> {b_j,x} -> e_j`.

Together with the old path comparison `e_{j-1}->e_j`, this is a consistent transitive orientation in the local comparison tournament at `b_j`. For insertion after `b_i`, all old B-turns persist and the two outer new comparisons are already positive, so the inserted word is tight exactly when

`{x,b_i} -> {x,b_{i+1}}`.

These consecutive comparisons lie in the local tournament at `x` and can be oriented independently for the chosen consecutive pairs. Thus any prescribed success set `I⊆{2,...,m-2}` occurs in an R3-compatible comparison orientation.

For the second item, form the acyclic B-ordered prefix automaton whose state records the number of B-vertices consumed, the consumed subset of `{v,s}`, and the last at most two vertices. A transition appending a new vertex is positive exactly when the new turn is tight. Let `R_s` be the positive-reachable state set.

Restrict to states in which `s` has not been consumed and to transitions that do not append `s`. This induced automaton is exactly the one-outside-vertex automaton `A(B;v)`, independent of the identity of `s`. A path ending at an `s`-free state cannot have consumed `s` earlier, because vertices are only added and never removed. Hence

`R_s ∩ A(B;v) = R_0`

for every companion `s`, where `R_0` is the positive-reachability region of `A(B;v)`. Therefore the outgoing cut restricted to transitions between `s`-free states is the same cut `δ⁺(R_0)` for every companion. Any difference must occur when appending `s` or after `s` has been consumed.

If the full induced subsystem `H[B∪{v,s}]` is nonHamiltonian, then in particular no B-ordered Hamilton word exists, so this canonical restricted cut is available.

## Scope

This result forbids using generic ordered-gap monotonicity as a theorem of R3. It replaces that nonexistent structure with an exact shared prefix-cut certificate for the B-ordered subproblem. Any stronger alignment among several companions must come from additional source-frame structure rather than from R3 and the displayed path alone.

# R1043 — Cross-distance localization for two outside insertions

**Status:** PASS_ADJUSTED
**Source:** G39 workspace localization root

## Statement

Let `B=(b_1,...,b_m)` be tight, and let `I_B(x)` be the set of gaps in the displayed B-order where one-vertex insertion of an outside vertex `x` yields a tight Hamilton word on `B∪{x}`. If `H[B∪{x,y}]` is nonHamiltonian, then

`|p-q| ≤ 1`

for every `p∈I_B(x)` and `q∈I_B(y)`.

Consequently, in the live G39 cell, if every `H[B∪{v,s}]` is nonHamiltonian and `I_B(v)≠∅`, then every companion insertion set satisfies

`I_B(s) ⊆ W_v := ⋂_{p∈I_B(v)} ({p-1,p,p+1}∩{0,...,m}).`

If the span of `I_B(v)` is `0,1,2`, then `W_v` has at most `3,2,1` gaps respectively; if the span is at least `3`, then `W_v=∅`.

The word "at most" is necessary at endpoint gaps: span zero need not produce three available gaps.

## Proof

Index the gaps of `B` by `0,...,m`, with the natural endpoint conventions. Suppose `p<q`, `p∈I_B(x)`, `q∈I_B(y)`, and `q-p≥2`.

Insert `x` into gap `p` and `y` into gap `q` simultaneously, preserving the displayed order of all B-vertices. Because the two gaps are separated by at least one untouched B-edge, no consecutive triple of the resulting Hamilton word contains both `x` and `y`. Every consecutive triple is therefore either an old tight B-triple, a triple already certified by the tight one-vertex insertion of `x`, or a triple already certified by the tight one-vertex insertion of `y`. Hence the simultaneous word is tight, contradicting nonHamiltonicity of `H[B∪{x,y}]`.

The symmetric case gives `|p-q|≤1` for all cross-pairs of legal insertion gaps.

Now fix `v`. For any companion `s`, every `q∈I_B(s)` must lie within distance one of every `p∈I_B(v)`, giving the displayed intersection formula for `W_v`.

Let `a=min I_B(v)` and `a+d=max I_B(v)`. Then

`W_v ⊆ [a+d-1,a+1]∩{0,...,m}`.

Thus `d=0,1,2` leaves at most `3,2,1` integer gaps respectively, and `d≥3` leaves none.

## Scope

This is a displayed-B-order insertion localization theorem. Full nonHamiltonicity implies the stated obstruction, but the theorem does not claim that failure of the displayed-order insertion family is sufficient for full nonHamiltonicity. No interval structure inside an individual insertion set is assumed or concluded.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R1043.md -->

# R1044 — Adjacent-slot two-vertex insertion and the diameter-two polarity wall

**Status:** PASS
**Source:** G39 workspace adjacent-gap root; durable development `A7C3/WORKSPACE/two-vertex-insertion-localization.md`

## Statement

Let `B=(b_1,...,b_m)` be tight. Suppose two outside vertices `x,y` are each individually insertible into both adjacent gaps `i` and `i+1` of the displayed B-order. Then `H[B∪{x,y}]` has a tight Hamilton path.

Consequently, under the nonHamiltonian G39 two-vertex-extension hypotheses:

1. If `I_B(v)` has span `1`, every companion insertion set `I_B(s)` has size at most one.
2. If `I_B(v)` has span `2`, say its outer gaps are `a` and `a+2`, then every nonempty companion insertion set is exactly `{a+1}`. For every such companion `s`, the two turns

`(s,b_{a+1},v)` and `(v,b_{a+2},s)`

are tight.

## Proof

Assume `i,i+1∈I_B(x)∩I_B(y)`. Consider the two B-ordered Hamilton candidates obtained by placing `x` in gap `i` and `y` in gap `i+1`, or vice versa. In the first candidate, every consecutive triple is already certified by the two one-vertex insertions except possibly

`(x,b_{i+1},y)`.

In the second, every consecutive triple is certified except possibly

`(y,b_{i+1},x)`.

These two turns are complete reversals. By R3 exactly one of them is tight. Therefore at least one candidate is a tight Hamilton path on `B∪{x,y}`. The same argument includes endpoint gaps.

For span `1`, write the two legal outer gaps of `I_B(v)` as `a,a+1`. R1043 gives `I_B(s)⊆{a,a+1}` for every nonHamiltonian companion. If both gaps belonged to `I_B(s)`, then `v` and `s` would each be insertible into both adjacent gaps, contradicting the first part. Thus `|I_B(s)|≤1`.

For span `2`, write `min I_B(v)=a`, `max I_B(v)=a+2`. R1043 gives `I_B(s)⊆{a+1}`. If nonempty, then `a+1∈I_B(s)`. Insert `v` at gap `a` and `s` at gap `a+1`. Every turn is certified except possibly `(v,b_{a+1},s)`. Since the full subsystem is nonHamiltonian, this candidate fails, so R3 forces its complete reversal `(s,b_{a+1},v)` tight.

Likewise, inserting `s` at gap `a+1` and `v` at gap `a+2` leaves only `(s,b_{a+2},v)` uncertified. Its failure forces the reverse turn `(v,b_{a+2},s)` tight.

## Scope

This is a necessary displayed-order obstruction under two-vertex nonHamiltonicity. It does not itself supply a consumer for the common polarity wall and does not claim interval structure for insertion sets beyond the stated span consequences.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R1044.md -->

# R1045 — Companion-independent obstruction certificate for the G39 B-ordered branches

**Status:** PASS
**Source:** G39 workspace certificate root

## Statement

Fix a tight displayed Hamilton path `B` and a common outside vertex `v`. For companion vertices `s`, consider the B-order-preserving extension problems on `B∪{v,s}`.

If `I_B(v)=∅`, then the one-outsider automaton `A(B;v)` has no positive terminal, and its canonical positive-reachability side `R_0` determines a negative cut

`K_0 = δ⁺(R_0)`.

This entire `s`-free cut is inherited identically inside every two-outsider automaton `A(B;v,s)`, so every companion shares the same pre-companion canonical comparison obstruction.

If `I_B(v)≠∅` and each full subsystem `H[B∪{v,s}]` is nonHamiltonian, then every companion insertion set satisfies

`I_B(s) ⊆ W_B(v) := ⋂_{p∈I_B(v)} ({p-1,p,p+1}∩{0,...,m}),`

so all companions are localized to the same window of at most three displayed gaps.

Thus, in every G39 B-ordered branch, the three companion failures are already coupled before source-specific analysis: by a common prefix cut when `I_B(v)=∅`, or by a common at-most-three-gap insertion window when `I_B(v)≠∅`.

## Proof

With only one outside vertex `v`, every B-ordered Hamilton word on `B∪{v}` is exactly the displayed path `B` with `v` inserted into one of its gaps. Hence `I_B(v)=∅` if and only if the one-outsider prefix automaton `A(B;v)` has no positive terminal.

By R1042, the positive-reachability region `R_0` then yields the canonical negative outgoing cut `K_0=δ⁺(R_0)`, and the induced `s`-free automaton inside every `A(B;v,s)` is literally the same `A(B;v)`. Therefore the `s`-free reachable side and outgoing cut are companion-independent.

In the complementary case `I_B(v)≠∅`, R1043 applies to every nonHamiltonian support `H[B∪{v,s}]`: every `q∈I_B(s)` must be within distance one of every `p∈I_B(v)`. This is exactly the displayed common window `W_B(v)`, which is contained in the radius-one neighborhood of any one `p∈I_B(v)` and therefore has at most three gaps.

## Scope

The theorem is a coupling certificate for the displayed-B-order subproblem. It does not itself consume the common cut or common window using the source-frame geometry, and it does not claim that B-ordered failure is equivalent to full nonHamiltonicity.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R1045.md -->

# R1046 — Three parallel source turns force a Hamilton P5 with some source-spoke endpoint

**Status:** PASS
**Source:** workspace source-P5 endpoint strengthening

## Statement

Let `A,C,p,q,r` be distinct vertices of a Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament and suppose

`(A,s,C)`

is tight for every `s∈{p,q,r}`. Then the induced five-set `{A,C,p,q,r}` has a tight Hamilton `P5` with at least one endpoint in `{p,q,r}`.

The source-spoke endpoint cannot in general be prescribed in advance: for each designated source label there are examples satisfying the three source turns in which that label is not an endpoint of any tight Hamilton `P5`.

## Proof

Audited R1031 gives at least one tight Hamilton `P5` on the source five-set. If one endpoint is already a source spoke, there is nothing to prove. Otherwise the endpoints are `A,C`, and after renaming the three internal source spokes as `x,y,z`, the path has one of the two orientations

`A,x,y,z,C` or `C,x,y,z,A`.

### Case 1: `A,x,y,z,C`

Write Boolean indicators

`α=[(A,y,z)]`, `β=[(z,C,x)]`, `γ=[(z,C,y)]`,
`δ=[(C,y,x)]`, `ε=[(x,A,y)]`, `η=[(x,A,z)]`.

By R3, each complete-reversal turn has the complementary value. Consider the seven source-endpoint candidates

`A,y,z,C,x`,
`A,z,C,y,x`,
`x,A,y,C,z`,
`x,A,z,C,y`,
`y,A,x,C,z`,
`z,A,x,y,C`,
`z,y,A,x,C`.

Using the source turns and the turns already certified by the original Hamilton path, their success conditions are respectively

`α∧β`, `γ∧δ`, `ε∧¬γ`, `η∧γ`, `¬ε∧¬β`, `¬η∧¬δ`, `¬α∧¬ε`.

Assume all seven fail. Failure of the last gives `α∨ε`. If `α=0`, then `ε=1`. If `α=1`, failure of the first gives `β=0`, and failure of the fifth again gives `ε=1`. Thus always `ε=1`. Failure of the third gives `γ=1`; failure of the second then gives `δ=0`; failure of the sixth gives `η=1`. But then the fourth candidate succeeds, contradiction.

### Case 2: `C,x,y,z,A`

Use

`β=[(z,C,x)]`, `γ=[(z,C,y)]`, `ε=[(x,A,y)]`, `η=[(x,A,z)]`.

The five candidates

`A,z,C,x,y`,
`x,A,z,C,y`,
`y,z,A,x,C`,
`x,A,y,C,z`,
`y,A,x,C,z`

have success conditions

`β`, `η∧γ`, `¬η`, `ε∧¬γ`, `¬ε∧¬β`.

If all fail, the first gives `β=0`, the third gives `η=1`, the second gives `γ=0`, and the fourth gives `ε=0`; the fifth then succeeds, contradiction.

Hence some tight Hamilton source `P5` has a source-spoke endpoint.

## Non-prescribability

Take the global ordinary-edge order

`pq < Ar < AC < qr < Ap < Cp < pr < Aq < Cr < Cq`.

The induced comparison orientation is a Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament and satisfies all three source turns because

`Ap<Cp`, `Aq<Cq`, `Ar<Cr`.

Its tight Hamilton `P5` orders are exactly

`A,p,r,C,q` and `r,A,p,C,q`.

Thus the designated spoke `p` is never an endpoint. Relabelling the source spokes shows that no fixed source label can be universally prescribed.

No D17 ancestry, R24, or R5 input is used.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R1046.md -->
