# R1047 — Canonical D17.408 forest uses only spectator-consecutive B-B edges

**Status:** PASS
**Source:** workspace root `1789344741.326159`

## Statement

In the canonical D17.408 bad-hole construction, the spanning tight three-path forest `J` with `tau(J)=1` may be chosen so that every selected `B-B` edge of `J` is a consecutive edge of the displayed spectator path `B`.

Consequently, at the D17.411 first-positive prefix pivot

`e_r=a_{r-1,out} b_{r,in} ∈ F\J`,  `f_r=a_{r,out} b_{r,in} ∈ J\F`,

where `chi(e_r)=1` and `chi(f_r)=0`, the deleted same-side edge `f_r` is either an `X-X` edge or a genuine consecutive spectator adjacency. More precisely, if the shared physical endpoint `b_r` lies in `B`, then `f_r` is a consecutive `B`-edge; if `b_r` lies in `X`, then `f_r` is `X-X`.

## Proof

Write the displayed spectator path as

`B=(L=b_0,b_1,...,b_m=R)`.

The original D17.408 construction uses exactly five endpoint-position patterns for its source-five-set word `K_s`. In each bad-hole branch choose the cut as follows.

### Pattern `(0,1)`

Here `K_s=(L,R,x,y,z)`. The D17.408 cut removes `sR`. The selected `B-B` edges that remain are

`L b_1, b_1 b_2, ..., b_{m-2}b_{m-1}`,

all consecutive in `B`, and D17.408 gives a tight three-forest with `tau(J)=1`.

### Pattern `(4,0)`

Here `K_s=(R,x,y,z,L)`. The D17.408 cut removes `Rx`. Its selected `B-B` edges are

`b_1b_2,...,b_{m-1}R`,

again consecutive in `B`, with `tau(J)=1`.

### Pattern `(2,1)`

Here `K_s=(x,R,L,y,z)`. The unique bad hole is

`(b_{m-1},R,L)`.

Original D17.408 explicitly permits cutting either edge of this bad hole. Choose the chord `RL`, rather than the spectator edge `b_{m-1}R`. The resulting three components are

`(x,s) | (b_1,...,b_{m-1},R) | (L,y,z)`.

The sole `X|B` transition is `Ly`, so `tau(J)=1`. Every selected `B-B` edge lies on the displayed spectator rail.

### Pattern `(3,2)`

Here `K_s=(x,y,R,L,z)`. The bad hole is

`(R,L,b_1)`.

Again original D17.408 explicitly allows either hole edge to be cut. Choose the chord `RL`. The three components may be written

`(s,z) | (x,y,R) | (L,b_1,...,b_{m-1})`.

The sole transition is `yR`, hence `tau(J)=1`, and every selected `B-B` edge is spectator-consecutive.

### Pattern `(3,4)`

Here `K_s=(x,y,z,L,R)`. The D17.408 cut removes `Ls`; the `B`-only rail is

`(b_1,...,b_{m-1},R)`.

Thus every selected `B-B` edge is again consecutive in `B`, and D17.408 gives `tau(J)=1`.

These are the five exhaustive D17.408 endpoint patterns, so in all cases

`E(J[B]) ⊆ E(B)`

for the selected path edges. The sharpening introduces no extra vertex-distinctness requirement: in the two modified cases it cuts one of the two edges of the same already-valid three-vertex bad hole used by D17.408.

For the pivot statement, D17.411 proves at the first positive proper prefix that

`chi(e_r)=1`,  `chi(f_r)=0`.

The alternating edges `e_r` and `f_r` share the physical endpoint represented by `b_r`. Since `e_r` crosses `X|B` while `f_r` is same-side, if `b_r∈B` then the other physical endpoint `a_r` of `f_r` also lies in `B`; hence `f_r` is `B-B`, and the sharpening above makes it a consecutive spectator edge. If `b_r∈X`, same-sidedness instead gives `a_r∈X`, so `f_r` is `X-X`. These cases are exhaustive.

## Audit provenance

The historical source was verified directly in Git history at migration commit `c116279447da167bf84552109b5ccd33de5e9cd8`, file `A7C3/WORKSPACE/D17/408-g33-rooted-direct-augmentation-trimer-contraction.md`. In particular, that source explicitly states that either edge of the bad hole may be cut in patterns `(2,1)` and `(3,2)`. The D17.411 first-positive-prefix ledger was independently checked in the same migration snapshot.

## Scope

This is a coordinate sharpening inside the canonical D17.408/D17.411 packet. It does not by itself assert physical realization of a later first-loss `K_{2,2}` rectangle, nor does it provide a spanning two-cover or global descent consumer.

# R1048 — A literal v-rooted first-loss pivot meets spectator order in exactly two ways

**Status:** PASS_ADJUSTED
**Source:** workspace root `1789345175.808309`

## Statement

Retain the sharp v-rooted first-loss cell of R1036, and assume the literal first-loss `K_{2,2}` switch exists, so both adjacent closures at the first-positive pivot are defined. Write

`e_r=a_{r-1}->b_r ∈ F\J`,  `f_r=a_r->b_r ∈ J\F`,

with `e_r` the installed first-positive old-`F` transition. Then exactly one of the following holds:

1. `a_{r-1}=v` and `b_r∈B`. In this case `e_r=v->b_r` is the unique old `v-B` transition, and `f_r` is a genuine consecutive spectator adjacency incident with `b_r`.
2. `b_r=v` and `a_{r-1}∈B`. In this case `f_r=a_r->v` is an `X-X` edge joining `v` to one of the source spokes `a_r∈{p,q,r}`.

Thus every literal v-rooted first-loss cell meets the spectator coordinate at its canonical pivot unless the deleted `J` edge itself is the `v`-to-source-spoke edge.

No such source/v classification is asserted at a numerical first-positive threshold whose adjacent `K_{2,2}` switch is absent because of the unique loop defect.

## Proof

R1036 gives the corrected first-loss dichotomy. Whenever the literal first-loss rectangle exists and is not source-rooted, the physical `X`-endpoint `z` of the installed old transition `e_r` is exactly the unique non-spoke vertex `v`.

R1037 gives the sharp v-rooted source-frame structure: `X={v,p,q,r}`, the three vertices `p,q,r` are the source spokes, `v` has selected old-`F` degree one, and the only non-source transition of `F` is the unique selected `v-B` edge.

D17.411's first-positive-prefix ledger gives

`chi(e_r)=1`,  `chi(f_r)=0`.

Therefore `e_r` crosses `X|B`, while `f_r` is same-side, and the two alternating edges share the physical endpoint `b_r`.

If the `X` endpoint of `e_r` is `a_{r-1}`, then R1036 makes `a_{r-1}=v` and therefore `b_r∈B`. Same-sidedness of `f_r=a_r->b_r` gives `a_r∈B`. R1047 proves that every selected `B-B` edge of the canonical `J` is a consecutive edge of the displayed spectator path. Hence `f_r` is a genuine spectator adjacency incident with `b_r`. R1037 identifies `e_r` as the unique old `v-B` transition.

If instead the `X` endpoint of `e_r` is `b_r`, then `b_r=v` and `a_{r-1}∈B`. Same-sidedness gives `a_r∈X`. Since `f_r` is a selected path edge it is not a physical loop, so `a_r≠v`; R1037 therefore gives `a_r∈{p,q,r}`. Thus `f_r=a_r->v` is exactly a source-spoke-to-`v` `X-X` edge.

The two positions of the `X` endpoint of the crossing edge `e_r` are exhaustive.

## Adjustment

The original workspace wording referred broadly to the “V-ROOTED FIRST LOSS branch of D17.434.” R1036 repaired D17.434 by separating the first numerical threshold from the literal adjacent switch: if either adjacent closure is the unique loop defect, the `K_{2,2}` rectangle does not exist and its source/v classification is unavailable. The theorem above therefore states the intended physical split only when the literal first-loss switch exists.

# R1049 — Endpoint-truncated spectator rail at the OUT-v first-positive pivot

**Status:** PASS_ADJUSTED

## Statement
In the sharpened D17.408 bad-hole construction, the canonical three-forest `J` with `tau(J)=1` may be chosen so that its selected `B-B` edges are exactly the displayed spectator path `B=(c_0=L,c_1,...,c_n=R)` with one endpoint adjacency omitted. Thus `J[B]` is either the prefix `(c_0,...,c_{n-1})` or the suffix `(c_1,...,c_n)`.

In the non-loop OUT-`v` first-positive branch, whenever the literal first-loss switch exists, write the installed pivot edge as `e_r=v->c_j`. Then the deleted edge is the oriented spectator adjacency

    f_r=c_{j-1}->c_j.

If the OUT copy of `c_j` is still on the unflipped augmenter suffix **and `c_j` is nonterminal on the endpoint-truncated `J[B]` rail**, the prefix switch creates the literal next-slot turn

    (v,c_j,c_{j+1}),

so its physicality is governed by exactly the same spoke/forward-spectator comparison variable `{v,c_j}` versus `{c_j,c_{j+1}}` that occurs in the R1033 one-vertex insertion scan. This does not identify `j` with the eventual R1033 certificate index. Terminal pivots are separate endpoint cells and do not carry this next-slot conclusion.

## Proof
R1047 audits the five D17.408 endpoint patterns and the sharpened admissible cuts. Inspecting those same five choices gives more than `E(J[B]) subset E(B)`:

- `(0,1)`: the selected B-only rail is `(c_0,...,c_{n-1})`;
- `(4,0)`: it is `(c_1,...,c_n)`;
- `(2,1)`: cutting the allowed bad-hole chord `RL` leaves `(c_1,...,c_n)`;
- `(3,2)`: cutting `RL` leaves `(c_0,...,c_{n-1})`;
- `(3,4)`: the selected B-only rail is `(c_1,...,c_n)`.

Hence every spectator adjacency is selected except exactly one of `c_0c_1` and `c_{n-1}c_n`, with no nonconsecutive `B-B` edge.

R1048 gives the audited OUT-`v` form of the first-positive literal switch: `e_r=v->c_j`, while `f_r` is a selected `B-B` edge of `J` sharing physical endpoint `c_j`. Since the chosen `J[B]` is an oriented subpath of the displayed spectator order, necessarily `f_r=c_{j-1}->c_j`.

If `c_j,out` remains on the unflipped suffix, its J-successor incidence remains in the J state. **When `c_j` is nonterminal on that truncated rail**, this successor is `c_j->c_{j+1}`. Replacing `f_r` by `e_r` therefore creates the turn `(v,c_j,c_{j+1})`. In R887 comparison notation this is exactly the comparison between the v-spoke `{v,c_j}` and the forward spectator edge `{c_j,c_{j+1}}`, one of the variables scanned in the proof of R1033. If the OUT copy has already passed behind the zipper frontier, this conclusion is not asserted; the prefix state is no longer the unflipped J successor state. If `c_j` is terminal on `J[B]`, no spectator successor exists, so the next-slot turn is likewise absent.

## Audit adjustment
The original workspace wording described the shared variable as “the R1033 first-flip comparison.” The mathematics proves equality of the comparison variable used by the two coordinate systems, but not equality of the canonical zipper pivot index with R1033's eventual certificate index.

A second scope repair is necessary at terminal pivots: being on the unflipped suffix does not create a nonexistent spectator successor. The next-slot statement therefore also requires `c_j` to be nonterminal on the endpoint-truncated `J[B]` rail. This condition was already present in the proof but was missing from the first canonical statement.

## Dependencies and scope
Uses audited R1047 for the admissible five-pattern D17.408 sharpening, audited R1048 for the OUT-`v` first-positive physical split, and audited R1033 for the spectator insertion scan. It is a coordinate bridge, not by itself a physical cover, strict old-source descent, or identification of the R1033 certificate index. R24/R5 are unused.

# R1050 — OUT-v successor regimes at the first-positive zipper pivot

## Statement
Assume the sharpened D17.408 choice and a non-loop OUT-`v` literal first-loss switch. Write the installed pivot edge as

    e_r = v->b_j

and the deleted spectator edge as

    f_r = b_{j-1}->b_j.

At the normalized first-positive state, the OUT copy of `b_j` has two relevant regimes.

1. If `b_j,out` lies behind the zipper frontier, its current selected outgoing incidence is its old `F` incidence, if one exists. Hence the newly installed old-`F` edge `v->b_j` creates an inherited `F` turn at `b_j`, or no turn if `b_j` has no old-`F` successor.
2. If `b_j,out` remains on the unflipped suffix and `b_j` is nonterminal on the endpoint-truncated `J[B]` rail, the selected successor is the spectator adjacency `b_j->b_{j+1}`. The new local turn is therefore `(v,b_j,b_{j+1})`, requiring the R887 comparison `F_j->E_j`, where `F_j={v,b_j}` and `E_j={b_j,b_{j+1}}`. For every `j<=t`, with `t` the canonical R1033 first-flip index, R1033 gives the reverse `E_j->F_j`; hence this future-suffix spectator seam is blocked. If `j=t+1` and `t<m-1`, the defining first flip instead gives `F_j->E_j`, so this one seam is tight, with all other physical and cycle obligations still separate.

No spectator-seam conclusion is asserted when `b_j` is terminal on the truncated `J[B]` rail.

## Proof
R1049 gives the endpoint-truncated spectator rail and identifies the OUT-`v` pivot as `e_r=v->b_j`, `f_r=b_{j-1}->b_j` in the literal-switch scope.

The state rule needed here does not require importing the full provisional D17.416 package. Along the alternating augmenter, the normalized prefix state is obtained from `J` by toggling the already traversed alternating prefix: each traversed `J\\F` edge is removed and its paired `F\\J` edge is installed, while the untouched suffix remains in its `J` state. Consequently a matching copy behind the frontier has its `F` incidence selected, whereas a copy on the untouched suffix retains its `J` incidence. Common incidences are unchanged and agree in both states.

Apply this to the OUT copy of physical vertex `b_j`. If it is behind the frontier, its selected outgoing incidence is exactly the old-`F` successor incidence, when present. Since `e_r=v->b_j` is itself an old-`F` edge, the resulting turn is a turn already present in the tight old forest `F`; otherwise there is no outgoing turn to check.

If `b_j,out` is still on the suffix and `b_j` is nonterminal on the chosen `J[B]` rail, R1049 says the J-successor is the displayed spectator edge `b_j->b_{j+1}`. Thus physicality at `b_j` is exactly the comparison between the v-spoke `F_j={v,b_j}` and forward spectator edge `E_j={b_j,b_{j+1}}`, namely `F_j->E_j`.

In R1033, the canonical first-flip index `t` is chosen so that `E_j->F_j` for every `1<=j<=t`: at `j=1` this is the failed left-end insertion, and for `2<=j<=t` the opposite orientation would have produced an earlier first flip. Therefore the seam is blocked for `j<=t`. When `t<m-1`, the defining flip at `j=t+1` is `F_{t+1}->E_{t+1}`, making precisely that seam tight.

## Audit adjustment
The original workspace root omitted the case in which `b_j,out` is on the unflipped suffix but `b_j` is terminal on the endpoint-truncated `J[B]` rail. In that case there is no spectator successor and hence no next-slot spectator seam to test. The audited theorem adds the necessary nonterminal hypothesis.

## Dependencies and scope
Uses audited R1049 and R1033. The behind-frontier F-state fact is reconstructed directly from alternating-prefix toggling, so no unaudited D17.416 dependency is required for this result. This is a local physicality obstruction only; it does not prove a global cover, descent, or equality of the zipper pivot with the R1033 certificate index.

# R1052 — Behind-frontier OUT-v pivots expose an earlier source-gated descent attempt

**Status:** PASS_ADJUSTED
**Source:** workspace root `1789345788.350339`

## Statement

Retain the non-loop OUT-`v` literal first-loss cell. Then the far zipper endpoint is a source spoke `t∈{p,q,r}`.

Write the first-positive pivot as

`e_r=v->b_j`,  `f_r=b_{j-1}->b_j`,

with `b_{j-1}->b_j` a consecutive spectator edge.

There are three relevant local states at `b_j,out`.

1. **Unflipped suffix, nonterminal.** The spectator successor `b_j->b_{j+1}` remains selected, and the pivot tests the R1033 next-slot comparison, as in R1050.
2. **Behind the zipper frontier.** There is a unique earlier index `q<r` with `a_q=b_j`. At that earlier normalized defect position, the canonical closing edge is exactly

   `g_q=b_j->t`.

   The edge `f_r=b_{j-1}->b_j` is still selected on the unflipped suffix, so the near seam of this closing attempt is exactly

   `(b_{j-1},b_j,t)`.

   The shortcut has two-cover matching cardinality and transition count at most two. If the normalized prefix is a literal tight three-forest, its only new physical obligations are the near seam at `b_j`, the far seam at the source spoke `t` when defined, and the possibility that both seams pass but the shortcut closes one rail into a directed cycle. The loop alternative is impossible because `b_j∈B` and `t∈X`.
3. **Unflipped suffix, terminal.** No spectator successor is selected at `b_j`, so neither the next-slot seam of (1) nor the behind-frontier construction of (2) follows merely from this local state. This endpoint-truncation residue remains separate.

Thus every behind-frontier OUT-`v` first loss carries an earlier source-gated matching-level strict-descent attempt whose near seam uses the same consecutive spectator edge later deleted at first loss. The stronger two-way claim covering every OUT-`v` first loss requires the terminal residue to be handled separately.

## Proof

R1051 identifies the exact non-loop OUT-`v` rectangle

`{ b_{j-1}->b_j , v->t } <-> { v->b_j , b_{j-1}->t }`

with `t∈{p,q,r}`. In particular the fixed far unmatched IN-copy of the zipper is `t,in`.

Assume now that `b_j,out` lies behind the first-positive frontier. Along the unique alternating augmenter, the OUT-shore labels `a_0,out,...,a_{m-1},out` are pairwise distinct. Since the physical vertex `b_j` has only one OUT copy, there is a unique earlier index `q<r` with

`a_q=b_j`.

At the normalized prefix at index `q`, the moving unmatched OUT-copy is therefore `b_j,out`, while the fixed far unmatched IN-copy remains `t,in`. Because `q<r`, the later edge

`f_r=b_{j-1}->b_j`

still lies on the unflipped suffix and remains selected. Hence the direct closure of the two free copies is the ordinary edge

`g_q=b_j->t`,

and its near endpoint uses the predecessor `b_{j-1}->b_j`, producing exactly the seam `(b_{j-1},b_j,t)`.

Before the first-positive index, the prefix transition ledger is nonpositive while `tau(J)=1`, so the unnormalized prefix has transition count at most one. Neutral normalization changes only zero-delta components to their `F` states and cannot increase the transition count. Therefore the normalized prefix also has transition count at most one. Since `g_q` crosses `B|X`, adding it raises the count by exactly one, giving transition count at most two. It also increases the matching cardinality by one, from the three-forest cardinality to the two-cover cardinality, because it joins the two free matching copies `b_j,out` and `t,in`.

If this normalized prefix is physically a tight three-path forest, `b_j` is the terminal vertex of one rail and `t` the source vertex of one rail. Adding `b_j->t` creates no new turns except the predecessor seam at `b_j` and, when `t` has a successor, the far seam at `t`. A bad seam gives its R3 complete-reversal trimer. If both seams are tight and the endpoints are on different rails, the shortcut gives a tight two-cover with transition count at most two. If both pass but the endpoints lie on the same rail, the shortcut closes exactly that rail into a directed cycle. Because `b_j∈B` and `t∈X`, `b_j=t` is impossible, so there is no loop case.

The future-suffix nonterminal alternative is exactly R1050. If instead `b_j` is terminal on the endpoint-truncated spectator rail, there is no selected spectator successor and the next-slot conclusion is unavailable. That case is therefore retained explicitly rather than silently folded into the two-way dichotomy.

## Adjustment

The workspace headline correctly identified the behind-frontier source-gated shortcut but concluded that **every** OUT-`v` first loss yields either a live R1033 next-slot comparison or that earlier seam. This omits the unflipped-suffix terminal state already isolated in R1049/R1050. The audited theorem preserves the full behind-frontier mechanism and adds the terminal endpoint residue as a third branch.

## Dependencies

- `A7C3/RESULTS/INTERESTING/R1051.md`
- `A7C3/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R1050.md`
- canonical alternating-prefix mechanics of D17.415/D17.416, reconstructed above
- R3 for the reverse-seam alternatives

## Scope

This result provides a matching-level strict-descent attempt and exact seam supports. It does not prove the normalized prefix is always a physical tight forest, consume the reverse trimers or same-rail cycle, or close the remaining terminal endpoint branch.

# R1053 — The IN-v closure-loop exception is source-pinned

**Status:** PASS
**Source:** workspace root `1789345739.325309`

## Statement

Retain the IN-`v` literal first-loss closure-loop branch. Thus the pivot has `b_r=v`, `a_r=t` for a source spoke `t`, and the loop equality is

`a_r=b_m=t`.

Then the two boundary old-`F` edges of the remaining augmenter suffix,

`e_{r+1}=t->b_{r+1}`

and

`e_m=a_{m-1}->t`,

are exactly the two selected old-`F` incidences of `t`.

Consequently either at least one of them is an old source gate across `X|B`, or both are `X-X`. In the latter case R1037 forces `t` to be the middle spoke of the ordered three-source block

`B_L -> s_1 -> s_2 -> s_3 -> B_R`,

and `e_{r+1},e_m` are exactly the two source-block edges incident with `s_2=t`.

Thus the closure-loop exception is not source-anonymous: it is either boundary-source-gated or pinned to the middle source spoke with both `X-X` mates exposed.

## Proof

R1048 gives the IN-`v` orientation of the v-rooted first-loss pivot: `b_r=v` and the deleted same-side edge is `f_r=t->v` for a source spoke `t=a_r`. In the closure-loop subcase the fixed far endpoint satisfies `b_m=a_r=t`.

The zipper coordinates give

`e_{r+1}=a_r->b_{r+1}=t->b_{r+1}`

and

`e_m=a_{m-1}->b_m=a_{m-1}->t`.

Both are selected old-`F` edges. They use the OUT and IN matching copies of the same physical source spoke `t`. They are genuine distinct incidences. If `m=r+1`, the two formulas collapse to the forbidden physical loop `t->t`, so the closure-loop branch has `m>=r+2`.

Every source spoke is internal in the old exact source cover `F`, hence has selected `F`-degree two. Therefore these two suffix-boundary edges exhaust the selected old incidences of `t`.

If either edge crosses `X|B`, it is an old source-spoke-to-spectator gate. Suppose neither crosses. Then both other endpoints lie in `X`. R1037 gives `d_F(v)=1`, and that unique old incidence of `v` is already the first-loss transition `e_r`; hence neither boundary edge can have `v` as its other endpoint. Their other endpoints are therefore source spokes.

R1037 also gives the complete source block, up to reversal,

`B_L -> s_1 -> s_2 -> s_3 -> B_R`.

The endpoint spokes `s_1,s_3` each have one source gate and one `X-X` mate, while only the middle spoke `s_2` has two selected `X-X` incidences. Thus a source spoke whose two selected incidences are both `X-X` must be `s_2`. Therefore `t=s_2`, and the two suffix-boundary edges are exactly its two source-block mates.

- `A7C3/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R1037.md`
- canonical D17.410 zipper coordinates

# R1054 — IN-v first loss exposes a source incidence on the very next augmenter edge

**Status:** PASS
**Source:** workspace root `1789345505.369599`

## Statement

In the IN-`v` first-positive branch, the deleted same-side edge is

`f_r=t->v`

for a source spoke `t∈{p,q,r}`. Since the first-positive index is proper, the next old-`F` edge on the unique augmenter exists and is

`e_{r+1}=t->b_{r+1}`.

Moreover `b_{r+1}≠v`. Hence exactly one of the following holds:

- `b_{r+1}∈B`, so `e_{r+1}` is an immediate source gate across `X|B`;
- `b_{r+1}∈X\{v}`, so `b_{r+1}` is another source spoke and `e_{r+1}` is an immediate source-source `X-X` mate.

Thus the IN-`v` first-loss branch exposes literal source ancestry one zipper edge after the pivot, with no source-anonymous interval between them.

## Proof

R1048 gives the audited IN-`v` form of the v-rooted first-positive pivot. In this orientation

`b_r=v`

and

`f_r=a_r->v`

with `a_r=t` one of the three source spokes. Hence `f_r=t->v`.

The first-positive index `r` is a proper prefix index of the augmenting path, so `r<m`. In zipper coordinates the next old edge is therefore

`e_{r+1}=a_r->b_{r+1}=t->b_{r+1}`.

R1037 gives `d_F(v)=1` in the v-rooted sharp source frame. The old transition

`e_r=a_{r-1}->v`

already uses that unique selected old-`F` incidence at `v`. Therefore the distinct selected edge `e_{r+1}` cannot also be incident with `v`, and

`b_{r+1}≠v`.

The physical partition is `G=B disjoint-union X` with `X={v,p,q,r}`. If `b_{r+1}∈B`, the edge from the source spoke `t` crosses `X|B` and is a source gate. If `b_{r+1}∈X`, then the exclusion of `v` leaves another source spoke, so the edge is source-source `X-X`. These cases are exhaustive.

# R1055 — Three-step IN-v corridor to a source gate or ledger reset

**Status:** PASS
**Source:** workspace root `1789345603.140719`

## Statement

In the genuine non-loop IN-`v` first-loss rectangle, let `r` be the first-positive zipper index. Within at most the three subsequent zipper indices `r+1,r+2,r+3`, either

1. an installed old-`F` edge is a source gate between `B` and one of `{p,q,r}`, or
2. the unique `J` transition is deleted and the prefix ledger drops from `S=1` to `S=0`.

Hence the non-loop IN-`v` first-loss cliff cannot be followed by an arbitrarily long all-same-side source-free corridor. The isolated closure-loop branch is excluded.

## Proof

At the audited IN-`v` pivot, `a_r=t_0∈{p,q,r}` and `S_r=1`. In the genuine non-loop rectangle, the same-side closure diagonal has its near endpoint in `B`, so its far endpoint `b_m` also lies in `B`.

For `k>r` before either stopping event, suppose `a_{k-1}` is a source spoke. The installed edge is `e_k=a_{k-1}->b_k∈F\J`. If `chi(e_k)=1`, it is already a source gate. Otherwise `e_k` is same-side, so `b_k∈X`. R1037 gives `d_F(v)=1`, already consumed by the first-loss edge `e_r`, so `b_k≠v`; hence `b_k` is another source spoke. If `k=m`, this same-side alternative is impossible because `b_m∈B`, so the terminal edge is necessarily a source gate.

For `k<m`, if `chi(f_k)=1` for `f_k=a_k->b_k∈J\F`, then `f_k` is the unique `J` transition. Since `e_k` is same-side, this step contributes `-1` to the prefix ledger. Earlier continuing post-`r` steps have both alternating edges same-side and contribute zero, so `S_{k-1}=1` and `S_k=0`.

If both `e_k` and `f_k` are same-side, then `a_k∈X`. It cannot equal `v`, since then the next old-`F` edge `e_{k+1}` would give a second selected `F` incidence at `v`, contradicting R1037. Thus `a_k` is again a source spoke.

The augmenter is a simple alternating path in the split matching graph, so its OUT-side vertices are distinct. Each physical vertex has one OUT copy, hence the physical labels `a_0,…,a_{m-1}` are pairwise distinct. Since `a_r` already occupies one of the three source labels, at most two subsequent all-same-side continuations can consume new source labels. Therefore by one of `k=r+1,r+2,r+3`, or earlier termination at `m`, a source gate or the unique `J` transition is forced.

## Scope

The `J`-transition alternative certifies the numerical reset `S=0`, not by itself a physical strict-descent closure. The source-gate alternative still requires its existing seam/blocker consumer. No claim is made for the isolated closure-loop branch.

## Dependencies

- R1037: `X={v,p,q,r}` and `d_F(v)=1`.
- R1048 and R1054: audited IN-`v` first-loss source-spoke coordinates and immediate source incidence.
- D17.411: first-positive prefix ledger.
- D17.415: simple augmenter coordinates; OUT-label distinctness also follows directly from path simplicity.
- D17.434 / R1036: genuine non-loop first-loss rectangle.

R24 and R5 are unused.

## Audit note

The three-step count is correct: `a_r` already uses the first of the three available source labels, so three further all-same-side continuations would require four distinct source labels. The potentially archival D17.415 distinctness claim is intrinsic to the simple split-graph alternating path, so no historical lemma is needed for that point.

# R1056 — Canonical IN-v closure diagonal is endpoint-anchored in spectator order

## Statement
Assume the sharpened D17.408 canonical forest and a non-loop IN-`v` literal first-loss switch with both adjacent closures defined. Write the displayed spectator path as

    B=(L=c_0,c_1,...,c_n=R).

If

    g_{r-1}=a_{r-1}->b_m

is the same-side closure diagonal at the first-positive pivot, then

    b_m in {L,c_1,R}.

Thus the genuine `B-B` closure diagonal is anchored at a displayed spectator endpoint or at the first spectator vertex after `L`. This does not assert that `g_{r-1}` itself is a consecutive spectator edge.

## Proof
Orient the unique F-heavy alternating component as

    e_1,f_1,e_2,f_2,...,f_{m-1},e_m,

with each `e_i in F\J` and `f_i in J\F`. Its terminal matching copy is `b_m,in`. Because the component begins and ends with F-only edges, this terminal copy is unmatched by `M_J`. Hence the physical vertex `b_m` has no selected J-incoming edge and is the initial vertex of one directed component of the three-forest `J`.

In the IN-`v` first-positive branch, `b_r=v`; because `e_r=a_{r-1}->v` crosses `X|B`, its other endpoint `a_{r-1}` lies in `B`. In the literal first-loss switch, R1036 gives the adjacent same-side closure `g_{r-1}=a_{r-1}->b_m`. In the non-loop case this is a genuine edge. Same-sidedness therefore forces `b_m in B` as well. Thus `b_m` must be a B-vertex that starts one of the canonical D17.408 J-components.

The five D17.408 bad-hole words, with the admissible sharpened cuts audited in R1047, have exactly the following B-starts:

- `(0,1)`: `(L,...,c_{n-1}) | (s) | (R,x,y,z)`, giving B-starts `L,R`;
- `(4,0)`: `(s) | (c_1,...,R) | (x,y,z,L)`, giving B-start `c_1`;
- `(2,1)`: `(x,s) | (c_1,...,R) | (L,y,z)`, giving B-starts `c_1,L`;
- `(3,2)`: `(x,y,R) | (L,...,c_{n-1}) | (s,z)`, giving B-start `L`;
- `(3,4)`: `(x,y,z,L) | (s) | (c_1,...,R)`, giving B-start `c_1`.

Their union is exactly `{L,c_1,R}`, so `b_m` lies in that set.

## Audit adjustment
The original root described this as the non-loop IN-`v` first-loss branch without explicitly inheriting R1036's closure-existence condition. The audited result requires the literal switch to exist, i.e. both adjacent closures are defined. It also states the exact set `{L,c_1,R}` rather than relying on the phrase “first interior spectator vertex,” which can be misleading in very short spectator paths.

## Dependencies and scope
Uses audited R1047 for the five admissible canonical D17.408 forests and audited R1036 for the literal first-loss closure scope. The fact that `b_m,in` is J-unmatched is reconstructed directly from the endpoint of the F-heavy alternating path, so no separate unaudited D17.410/D17.415 dependency is needed. R24/R5 are unused. This is a coordinate localization only, not a spectator-adjacency theorem, cover, or descent.

# R1057 — Terminal source-mate reduction to a three-path two-seam recompletion

**Status:** PASS
**Source:** D17.439

## Statement

Work in the v-rooted sharp hard cell. Let `t` be the source endpoint of the last old `F`-transition on the unique augmenter, as certified by R1040, and let `x` be the adjacent old `X-X` source-spoke mate supplied by R1037.

Then:

1. `t` and `x` are consecutive internal vertices of one old `F` rail, and `F-{t,x}` is exactly three nonempty literal directed paths on `G-{t,x}`.
2. The retained source turns `(A,t,C)` and `(A,x,C)` force a tight Hamilton `P4` on `{A,C,t,x}`.
3. Consequently, any legal two-seam reconnection that joins the three residual `F` paths into one tight Hamilton path yields a spanning two-path cover of `H`, with the source four-set as the other rail.

This is a conditional recompletion interface. It does **not** assert that the live first-loss `K_{2,2}` cross edges already supply the required residual-component incidence or the two required tight joins.

## Proof

By R1037, the source spokes form one internal three-vertex `X`-block on an old `F` rail, up to complete reversal,

`B_L -> s_1 -> s_2 -> s_3 -> B_R`,

with the two endpoint source spokes incident with the two old `X|B` source gates and each X-mated to the middle spoke. By R1040, the last old `F`-transition on the augmenter is one of these X-mated source gates. Hence its source endpoint `t` is one of `s_1,s_3`, and its adjacent old `X-X` mate `x` is the middle spoke `s_2`.

Thus `t,x` are consecutive internal vertices of one old `F` rail. Removing two consecutive internal vertices from a path leaves exactly two nonempty path intervals on that rail. The other rail of the exact old two-cover remains a nonempty path. Therefore

`F-{t,x} = P_1 | P_2 | P_3`

is exactly a three-path cover of `G-{t,x}`.

The retained source packet gives both `(A,t,C)` and `(A,x,C)` tight. Apply boundary antisymmetry R3 to `(t,A,x)`. If `(t,A,x)` is tight, then

`t -> A -> x -> C`

is a tight Hamilton `P4` on `{A,C,t,x}`. If `(t,A,x)` is bad, R3 gives its complete reversal `(x,A,t)` tight, so

`x -> A -> t -> C`

is a tight Hamilton `P4` using `(A,t,C)`. Call either resulting source path `Q`.

The supports of `Q` and `P_1|P_2|P_3` are disjoint and partition `V(H)`. Therefore, if two legal seams join `P_1,P_2,P_3` into one tight Hamilton path `P` on their union, then `P | Q` is a spanning two-path cover of `H`.

No R24 or R5 input is used.

## Scope

The theorem reduces the v-rooted terminal-source cell to an exact three-path recompletion problem. It certifies the residual path decomposition and the disjoint source `P4`, but not the existence of the two legal seams and not an identification of those seams with the first-loss `K_{2,2}` cross edges.

# R1058 — First-open spectator detour gives an exact two-seam interception interface

**Status:** PASS
**Source:** workspace root `1789410528.626369`

## Statement

Work in the audited v-rooted sharp cell and the non-loop OUT-`v` literal first-loss branch. Let the actual first-loss index be `r`, with

`e_r=v->b_j`,

let `s∈{p,q,r}` be the fixed far source-spoke endpoint from R1051, and let `t+1` be the first R1033-open spectator position. Put

`c=b_{t+1}`

and assume the putative first loss occurs later, `j>t+1`.

If both spectator incidences

`b_t->c`, `c->b_{t+2}`

survive in the normalized pre-loss prefix `hat M_{r-1}`, then

`K=(hat M_{r-1}-{b_t->c})+{v->c,b_t->s}`

has exact two-cover matching cardinality and

`tau(K)=tau(F)`.

There is no new seam at `v`, while the new seam at `c` is exactly the R1033 first-open turn `(v,c,b_{t+2})` and is tight. The only remaining physical obligations are the endpoint seam at `b_t`, the endpoint seam at `s` when defined, and the possibility that the reconnection closes a selected rail into a directed cycle.

If either spectator incidence at `c` fails to survive, the failure is exhausted by the endpoint-truncated / behind-frontier / off-`C_*` split-copy alternatives. If specifically `c,out` is already behind the frontier, then at its unique earlier defect prefix the direct source-gated closure `c->s` has exact two-cover matching cardinality and transition count at most two.

Thus first-open availability is reduced to an explicit physical two-seam interception candidate, an earlier matching-level strict-descent closure, or an exact split-copy support residue.

## Proof

R1037 gives `d_F(v)=1`. In the OUT-`v` branch the unique old-F incidence at `v` is the outgoing edge `v->b_j`, so F has no selected edge entering `v`. The split copy `v,in` cannot be an internal IN-copy of the alternating component `C_*`, because every such IN-copy carries its paired old-F edge; it is also not the far IN endpoint, which is `s,in` by R1051. Every off-`C_*` neutral component is placed in its F-state by the normalized-prefix convention. Hence `v,in` remains unmatched in every normalized prefix.

Immediately before the first loss, the moving free copy is `v,out` and the fixed far free copy is `s,in`. R1051 identifies the preceding closure as

`g_{r-1}=v->s`,

which is X-X and therefore same-side. D17.421 says the preceding normalized closure lies exactly two transitions below the old floor. Since `g_{r-1}` contributes zero transitions,

`tau(hat M_{r-1})=tau(F)-2`.

Assume `b_t->c` survives. Delete this B-B edge and add the disjoint edges `v->c` and `b_t->s`. Net matching cardinality increases by one, from the spanning three-forest cardinality to the spanning two-cover cardinality. The deleted edge is same-side and both added edges cross X|B, so

`tau(K)=tau(hat M_{r-1})+2=tau(F)`.

Because `v,in` is free, adding `v->c` creates no turn at `v`. If the successor edge `c->b_{t+2}` also survives, the only new turn at `c` is

`(v,c,b_{t+2})`.

By R1050 and the definition of the R1033 first-open position, its comparison is exactly

`F_{t+1}->E_{t+1}`,

so this seam is tight. No stronger physical conclusion is automatic: the seams at `b_t` and `s`, and same-rail cycle incidence, remain genuine obligations.

For the failure classification, R1049 says `J[B]` is the displayed spectator path with one endpoint adjacency omitted. Each relevant spectator incidence is therefore either absent for that endpoint-truncation reason, common in `F∩J`, a `J\F` edge on `C_*`, or a `J\F` edge on an off-`C_*` component. Common incidences survive every normalized prefix; on-`C_*` incidences survive exactly while they remain ahead of the toggled frontier; off-`C_*` `J\F` incidences disappear under F-normalization. Hence endpoint truncation, behind-frontier status, and off-component normalization exhaust support loss.

If `c,out` is behind the frontier, let `q<r` be its unique earlier alternating-component position. At `hat M_q`, the two free copies are `c,out` and `s,in`; adding `c->s` restores exact two-cover matching cardinality. Because `q` is before the first-positive frontier, the normalized prefix has transition count at most one, and the cross edge `c->s` raises it by one. Thus the closure has transition count at most two. As in R1052, this is a matching-level descent attempt until its endpoint seams and acyclicity are checked.

# R1059 — Untouched first-open spectator slot gives an off-augmenter floor-level switch

**Status:** PASS
**Source:** workspace root `1789410664.574049`

## Statement

Retain a non-loop OUT-`v` first loss at spectator `b_j` with `j>t+1`, where `t+1` is the first R1033-open spectator position. Suppose that immediately before the loss both spectator incidences at `b_{t+1}` remain in their `J` state. Then

`{b_t->b_{t+1}, v->s} <-> {v->b_{t+1}, b_t->s}`

is a well-defined literal `K_{2,2}` matching switch at exact two-cover cardinality and transition count

`tau(F)=3`,

where `s` is the fixed source-spoke far endpoint from R1051. The new forward seam

`(v,b_{t+1},b_{t+2})`

is tight by the R1033 first-open comparison, and the edge `v-b_{t+1}` lies in neither `F` nor `J`.

The result is a floor-level recompletion candidate only. Remaining endpoint seams, component incidence, and directed-cycle avoidance are separate physical obligations.

## Proof

Let `r` be the canonical first-positive index and put `M=hat M_{r-1}`. By R1051 the corresponding OUT-`v` first-loss rectangle has far endpoint `s∈{p,q,r}`. The two free split copies of `M` are `v,out` and `s,in`, and the old same-side closure

`M+{v->s}`

has transition count one.

Let `t` be the R1033 first-open index. Since `j>t+1` and both spectator incidences at `b_{t+1}` remain in their J-state, the selected edges

`d=b_t->b_{t+1}`, `u=b_{t+1}->b_{t+2}`

are present in `M`.

The detour spoke

`h=v->b_{t+1}`

is not selected by F: R1037 gives `d_F(v)=1`, and R1051 identifies the unique old v-B edge as `v->b_j`, distinct because `j>t+1`. It is not selected by J either, because both split copies of `b_{t+1}` are already occupied by the predecessor and successor spectator incidences `d,u`. Hence `h∉F∪J`, in particular `h∉F△J`.

Compare the old closure

`C=M+{v->s}`

with

`D=M-{d}+{h,b_t->s}`.

On the four distinct split copies `b_t,out`, `b_{t+1},in`, `v,out`, and `s,in`, this is exactly the switch

`{B-B, X-X} <-> {X|B, X|B}`.

Therefore D is a matching with the same cardinality as C, namely exact two-cover matching cardinality. Its transition count rises by exactly two:

`tau(D)=1+2=3=tau(F)`.

Because `u=b_{t+1}->b_{t+2}` survives, the forward new turn is precisely

`(v,b_{t+1},b_{t+2})`.

At the first R1033-open position its comparison is `F_{t+1}->E_{t+1}`, so this seam is tight.

No claim is made that D is automatically a tight acyclic two-cover: the other endpoint turns, component/backtrack incidence, and directed-cycle question remain to be checked.

# R1060 — The normalized OUT-v pre-loss state isolates v

**Status:** PASS
**Source:** workspace root `1789410744.952669`

## Statement

Immediately before any non-loop OUT-`v` literal first loss, in the F-normalized prefix `hat M_{r-1}`, both split copies `v,out` and `v,in` are unmatched. Hence the physical vertex `v` is an isolated singleton component.

Consequently, any legal off-augmenter detour edge `v->z` creates no seam at `v` and cannot by itself create a directed cycle through `v`.

## Proof

Write the OUT-`v` first-loss pivot as

`e_r=v->b_j`.

At the normalized prefix `hat M_{r-1}`, the moving unmatched OUT copy is `a_{r-1},out=v,out`, so `v,out` is free by construction.

For `v,in`, R1037 gives `d_F(v)=1`. In the OUT-`v` branch, R1048 and R1051 identify the unique selected old-F incidence at `v` as the outgoing transition `v->b_j`. Thus the F-state has no selected incidence at `v,in`.

Now consider the split symmetric difference `F△J`. The unique F-heavy alternating component `C_*` has fixed IN endpoint `s,in`, where R1051 gives `s∈{p,q,r}` and `s≠v`; therefore `v,in` is not its terminal endpoint. Nor can `v,in` be an internal IN-copy of `C_*`, because every internal alternating copy carries an incident `F\J` edge, while the F-state has no incidence at `v,in`.

Thus any noncommon J-incidence at `v,in`, if present, belongs to a delta-zero component. D17.416 neutral normalization places every such component in its F-state, deleting that J-incidence. A common `F∩J` incidence at `v,in` is impossible because F has none. Therefore `v,in` is unmatched in `hat M_{r-1}`.

Both split copies are free, so `v` is a literal singleton component. Adding a legal edge `v->z` from this singleton creates no predecessor turn at `v`; and because it attaches an isolated vertex by one outgoing edge, that edge cannot itself complete a directed cycle through `v`.

The isolation statement is for the F-normalized pre-loss prefix, not for arbitrary unnormalized J-prefixes. The detour conclusion concerns a legal selected edge leaving the isolated singleton; other endpoint seams and component interactions remain separate. R24 and R5 are unused.

**Status:** PASS
**Source:** workspace root `1789410776.990429`

## Statement

Retain the later non-loop OUT-`v` first-loss setting with `j>t+1`. Suppose the normalized pre-loss prefix `M=hat M_{r-1}` is a literal tight three-path forest and both spectator incidences at the first R1033-open slot remain selected:

`b_t->b_{t+1}`, `b_{t+1}->b_{t+2}`.

Then

`M' = M-{b_t->b_{t+1}}+{v->b_{t+1}}`

is again a literal tight three-path forest. Its free copies are `b_t,out` and the same far source copy `s,in`. Hence the entire remaining first-open interception obstruction is the single source-gated closure

`b_t->s`,

with exactly the usual predecessor seam at `b_t`, successor seam at `s` when defined, and same-rail directed-cycle alternative.

## Proof

By R1060, `v` is an isolated singleton component of the normalized pre-loss selected graph. Deleting the selected path edge

`d=b_t->b_{t+1}`

cuts one path component into two directed path pieces, one ending at `b_t` and one beginning at `b_{t+1}`. The selected graph now has four path components, including the singleton `v`.

Add

`h=v->b_{t+1}`.

Its endpoints lie on two distinct components, so this edge cannot create a directed cycle. There is no turn at `v` because both split copies of `v` were free. The successor edge `b_{t+1}->b_{t+2}` remains selected, and at the R1033 first-open position the turn

`(v,b_{t+1},b_{t+2})`

is tight. No other selected incidence changes. Therefore `M'` is literally a tight three-path forest.

The newly free OUT copy is `b_t,out`; the fixed far free IN copy remains `s,in`. Their unique direct closure is `b_t->s`. Because `b_t∈B` and `s∈X`, this edge is not a loop. Adding it has exactly four physical possibilities: a bad predecessor seam at `b_t`; a bad successor seam at `s` when a successor exists; both seams tight with endpoints on distinct rails, yielding a tight two-cover; or both seams tight with endpoints on the same rail, yielding the single directed cycle closed by the added edge.

# R146 — Three-exterior pair extension for a fixed tight trimer

## Statement
Let P be a three-vertex support carrying a tight trimer in a Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament, and let x,y,z be three distinct vertices outside P. Then at least one of the three five-sets P∪{x,y}, P∪{x,z}, P∪{y,z} supports a tight five-vertex path.

## Hypotheses
Strong Level-(1) boundary antisymmetry; P supports a tight trimer; x,y,z are distinct and outside P.

## Scope
Pure six-vertex local amplification. No smallest-counterexample, deletion, support-family, sign, payment, or representative assumptions.

## Applicability
Use whenever one fixed tight trimer has at least three named exterior vertices. It forbids a complete three-vertex pair-shield around that trimer.

## Persistence
The conclusion is graph-intrinsic on the fixed six vertices.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not identify which exterior pair extends P, and does not assert that every exterior pair extends P.

## Proof
Relabel the fixed tight trimer as P={0,1,2} with (0,1,2) tight, and the three exterior vertices as 3,4,5. Encode every complete-reversal pair {(a,b,c),(c,b,a)} of ordered triples of distinct vertices by one Boolean variable. There are 6P3/2=60 variables. For a fully deterministic numbering, take the lexicographically smaller ordered triple in each reversal pair as its canonical representative, sort the 60 canonical representatives lexicographically, and number them x_1,...,x_60 in that order. The literal for a turn t is x_i when t is the canonical representative of pair i and ¬x_i when its reverse is canonical. By R3, every Boolean assignment is exactly one Strong Level-(1) turn assignment on these six vertices. Add the unit clause asserting (0,1,2) tight.

Assume for contradiction that all three five-sets P∪{3,4}, P∪{3,5}, P∪{4,5} are non-Hamiltonian. For each of these supports and each of its 5!=120 vertex orders q=(q_1,...,q_5), add the clause saying that not all three consecutive turns q_1q_2q_3, q_2q_3q_4, q_3q_4q_5 are tight. Replacing each turn by its Boolean literal gives one three-literal clause. Thus the CNF has exactly 60 variables and 3·120+1=361 clauses.

This CNF is UNSAT by the following completely deterministic exhaustive DPLL procedure. Repeatedly perform unit propagation until no unit clause remains; when several unit clauses are present, process them in increasing variable index. If an empty clause appears, close the branch. If all clauses are satisfied, report SAT. Otherwise choose the smallest-index unassigned variable that occurs in a remaining clause and branch False before True. With the lexicographic numbering above, the exhaustive search visits 1,397 DPLL nodes, reaches maximum branch depth 22, and closes every branch by contradiction. These figures were independently regenerated from the displayed encoding and rule.

Therefore no Strong Level-(1) assignment can make all three P-plus-pair supports non-Hamiltonian. At least one of P∪{3,4}, P∪{3,5}, P∪{4,5} supports a tight P5, which is exactly R146.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R146.md -->

# R149 — Distinguished-trimer current-or-cross

## Statement
Let W admit an exact two-cover T, and let J=(j_0,j_1,j_2) be a distinguished tight trimer on three vertices of W. Among exact two-covers of W choose T maximizing the number of the two directed states j_0j_1 and j_1j_2 that are selected. Then either J occurs literally as a consecutive current trimer of T, or T contains a selected state crossing the vertex cut V(J) | (W\\V(J)).

## Hypotheses
W is the residual vertex set in a setting where exact two-covers of W exist; J=(j_0,j_1,j_2) is a certified tight trimer on V(J) subset W; T is chosen among exact two-covers of W to maximize selected overlap with the two directed states of J.

## Scope
Generic exact-residual-two-cover lemma. The historical application was the 4+3+3 residual compiler, especially the canonical-Z mate J_Z=(q_2,z,q_0), but the proof uses only the stated exact-two-cover and tight-trimer hypotheses.

## Applicability
Use when a named trimer must either be made literally current in a chosen exact residual two-cover or else converted into a physical current crossing incident with its three-vertex support. Particularly useful before capture, endpoint-role, or assembly consumers that require current rather than merely graph-intrinsic data.

## Persistence
In the first arm, J is literal selected currentness only in the chosen overlap-maximal target T. In the second arm, the crossing is a literal selected state of that same T. No historical transport is used.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not make J current in other representatives; does not say the crossing is captured, protected, a seam, or final-assembly data; does not preserve any parent candidate or parent cover; does not imply a spanning two-cover of H. The historical source explicitly retired the stronger false scratch inference that one total old-component cross forces all old internal edges to survive.

## Proof
Historical proof recovered from A7C2_MATH_EXPLORER_000006.md, Theorem 4. Suppose J is not literally current and no selected state of overlap-maximal T crosses V(J)|(W\\V(J)). Both sides are nonempty and T has exactly two components, so one component lies entirely on V(J) and the other entirely on W\\V(J). The J-side component contains all three vertices of J and hence is a tight three-vertex path on that support. Replace only that component by the certified tight path J=(j_0,j_1,j_2). The other component is unchanged, so the result remains an exact two-cover of W, now selecting both directed states of J, contradicting maximality. Therefore J is current or a selected cross touches V(J). The historical producer file carried a complete proof; later A7C2_MATH_EXPLORER_000007.md explicitly records the canonical-Z instance as accepted by A7C2_AUDIT_000007. This recovery does not claim that the entire generic producer batch had an independently located audit record, so the current Supabase proposal is correctly pending for fresh audit.

# R154 — Physical-star exact rank-two currentization

## Statement
Let H be a smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample, let x be a vertex, and let F be a family of distinct physical two-vertex supports incident with x. Then F is simultaneously currentizable as selected supports in a path-forest/minimum-three-cover representative if and only if |F|<=2. For |F|=2, say F={{p,x},{x,y}} with p,x,y distinct, exactly one of the two composable mirror packets {px,xy} and {yx,xp} is compatible; it is the two-state packet of the unique tight trimer orientation (p,x,y) or (y,x,p), and that trimer can be currentized as one component of a minimum three-cover. For |F|>=3 simultaneous currentization is impossible.

## Hypotheses
H is a smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample; F consists of distinct physical pairs all incident with the same vertex x. Currentizable means there exists one path-forest/minimum-three-cover representative selecting one orientation of every support in F.

## Scope
Exact local synchronization ceiling for physical supports incident with one vertex. This is the stronger parent of the older Incident-Pair Mirror Currentization for bare physical-support coexistence; ancestry-rich captured-crossing specializations remain separate when their historical labels are consumed.

## Applicability
Use to decide whether a requested local incident-support synchronization target is feasible at all. For two supports it supplies the unique forced mirror trimer and a minimum-cover currentization. For three or more it deletes the target as mathematically impossible rather than merely technically unresolved.

## Persistence
For |F|=2 the physical support pair and the graph-intrinsic tight mirror trimer are stable facts; the selected orientations and complement cover are representative-relative. Different pairs around x may require different mirror orientations and different complement covers. No simultaneous currentization of an entire larger star is licensed.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not preserve historical selected orientations when the forced mirror orientation is opposite; does not preserve old carrier/component identity, residual rails, capture protection, concentration, endpoint roles, or ancestry. It does not synchronize separate pairwise currentizations. The impossibility for |F|>=3 concerns simultaneous selection in a path forest, not graph-intrinsic existence of the physical supports.

## Proof
The two-support core is the independently audited Incident Physical-Pair Orientation Classification and Incident-Pair Mirror Currentization in CRITIC_HANDOFF_INCREMENTAL_HANDOFF_RESEARCHER_34_INCIDENT_PAIR_MIRROR_RESELECTION_CAPTURED_BOUNDARY_PACKET_2026-08-24_2026-08-24.md §§3.4-3.6: same-head and same-tail packets conflict; the remaining composable packets are the reverse trimers pxy and yxp; boundary antisymmetry makes exactly one tight; Universal Prescribed-Path Completion currentizes it. The later Puzzler compression explicitly records independently accepted Physical-Star Currentization Rank-Two Classification / Pair-Selective Star Currentization and identifies incident-support synchronization as exact rank two. The upper bound is elementary: a path forest has degree at most two at x, so no representative can select three distinct physical supports incident with x. Thus the family is simultaneously currentizable exactly for size at most two.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R154.md -->

# FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R156.md

<!-- BEGIN FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R156.md -->

# R156 — Universal-extension deletion rigidity

## Statement
Let H be a smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample and let X be a nonempty proper vertex set such that, for every r in V(H)\\X, the induced subsystem H[X union {r}] has a Hamilton tight path. Then pc(H-X)=2. Moreover every exact two-cover H-X=U⊔V has both U and V nontrivial; equivalently, no exact two-cover of H-X has a singleton component.

## Hypotheses
H is a smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample; X is nonempty and proper; for every r outside X, X union {r} supports a graph-intrinsic Hamilton tight path. X itself need not be Hamiltonian.

## Scope
Arbitrary-size deletion under a universal one-vertex Hamilton-extension hypothesis. This is not restricted to |X|<=4 and is therefore not subsumed by universal small-deletion exactness R5. It also adds a no-singleton rigidity conclusion for every exact residual two-cover.

## Applicability
Use in universal-extension modules to obtain a genuine exact two-rail residual frame and rule out degenerate singleton rails before maximin normalization, fixed-rail graft surgery, endpoint-role analysis, or other residual-cover consumers.

## Persistence
The universal-extension property is graph-intrinsic. The conclusion pc(H-X)=2 and the absence of singleton rails are graph-intrinsic statements about the residual subsystem. A chosen exact two-cover remains representative-relative; the theorem does not select a canonical residual cover or preserve rails across later recompletions.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert that X itself is Hamiltonian. Does not give rail-size bounds stronger than at least two vertices each. Does not provide a canonical exact two-cover, fixed-rail persistence, endpoint exposure, selected crossing states, capture/protection ancestry, or a spanning two-cover of H. Without the universal-extension hypothesis the theorem does not apply.

## Proof
Recovered from INCREMENTAL_HANDOFF_RESEARCHER_34_CYCLIC_K4_NEAR_END_GRAFT_FOUR_DELETION_RIGIDITY_2026-08-24.md, Theorem 6.1. Smallest-counterexample minimality gives pc(H-X)<=2. Suppose H-X has a Hamilton path Q and choose an endpoint r. The hypothesis supplies a Hamilton tight path K_r on X union {r}. If Q=(r), then K_r spans H, contradiction. Otherwise Q-r is a nonempty tight path disjoint from K_r and K_r⊔(Q-r) is a spanning two-cover of H, contradiction. Thus pc(H-X)=2. Now suppose an exact two-cover has a singleton component, H-X=(r)⊔Q. Again K_r exists, and K_r⊔Q is a spanning two-cover of H, contradiction. Therefore both residual rails are nontrivial. The producer file originally marked this theorem audit-pending; later same-day accepted sources explicitly list Universal-Extension Deletion Rigidity among AUDITED INPUTS CARRIED FORWARD, so the historical theorem was subsequently accepted in this scope.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R156.md -->

# FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R159.md

<!-- BEGIN FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R159.md -->

# R159 — Punctured Component-Drop Pair Theorem

## Statement
Let H be a finite Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament and let W be a proper vertex subset. Let R be a literal c-cover of H[W] and T a literal r-cover of H[W]. If r<c, then H contains a graph-intrinsic balanced opposite-sign pair.

## Hypotheses
W is a proper subset of V(H); R and T are literal path covers of exactly W; T has fewer path components than R.

## Scope
Arbitrary finite Strong Level-(1) boundary tournaments; no smallest-counterexample, extremality, endpoint, or deleted-marker hypothesis is needed beyond W being proper.

## Applicability
Generic compiler from any path-cover component drop on a proper induced subsystem to balanced-pair existence. In particular it applies whenever a fragmented complement is recompleted with fewer components.

## Persistence
The resulting balanced opposite-sign pair is graph-intrinsic historical information; it is not asserted to be selected by T or R.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not claim the pair is unique, selected, current, or immediately productive; does not claim global monotonicity of pair mass. The proper-subset/spare-vertex condition is essential to the archived proof.

## Proof
Let R be a literal c-cover and T a literal r-cover of the same proper induced subsystem H[W], with r<c. Suppose for contradiction that no selected adjacent state of T has endpoints in two distinct R-components. Then every T-component is contained wholly in the vertex set of a single R-component: along an ordered T-path, leaving one R-component for another would create a first adjacent state crossing between them. Because the T-components cover all of W, every one of the c nonempty R-components contains at least one T-component. Distinct R-components are vertex-disjoint, so these T-components are distinct. Hence r>=c, contradicting r<c. Therefore T selects a state xy whose endpoints lie in two distinct components of R. Since W is a proper subset of V(H), accepted fully reconstructible R176 applies to the literal covers R,T and this selected cross-state. It yields a graph-intrinsic balanced opposite-sign pair in H. This is exactly the R159 conclusion, with no smallest-counterexample, extremality, endpoint, or deletion-marker hypothesis beyond W being proper.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R159.md -->

# FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R163.md

<!-- BEGIN FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R163.md -->

# R163 — Complete Mate-Box Collapse

## Statement
Let H satisfy pc(H)>k. For j=1,...,r let A_j={alpha_{j,i}: i in I_j} be finite families of ordered turns. Assume that for every tuple (i_1,...,i_r) there is a literal spanning k-component path proposal C(i_1,...,i_r) whose only possibly bad turns are holes h_{j,i_j} with complete reversals alpha_{j,i_j}. Then at least one family A_j is entirely tight.

## Hypotheses
Boundary antisymmetry holds; pc(H)>k; every Cartesian-product tuple of the finite mate families has the stated literal spanning k-component proposal, with no undecided/bad turn outside the listed holes and with each listed hole's complete reversal exactly the corresponding chosen alpha.

## Scope
Finite Strong Level-(1) boundary tournaments. This is a generic propositional mate/candidate compiler independent of order ten and of any particular endcap geometry.

## Applicability
Use after constructing a full Cartesian box of literal candidate k-covers. It converts tuplewise candidate failure into an entire tight mate family, allowing one family to be treated as simultaneously available graph-intrinsic turns.

## Persistence
The conclusion that one whole mate family is graph-intrinsically tight persists across representative changes. The literal candidate proposals used in the proof are certificates only; their selected states are not asserted current afterward.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
The theorem does not manufacture the tuple family; every tuple certificate must be literal and complete. It does not apply to a partial box, proposals with additional holes, or holes whose exact antisymmetric mates are not the selected alpha turns. It does not say which family collapses.

## Proof
Fix a tuple (i_1,...,i_r). If all chosen turns alpha_{j,i_j} were bad, Boundary Antisymmetry R3 would make every reversed hole h_{j,i_j} tight. By hypothesis those are the only possible holes in C(i_1,...,i_r), so that proposal would be a literal spanning k-cover, contradicting pc(H)>k. Hence every tuple satisfies the clause alpha_{1,i_1} tight OR ... OR alpha_{r,i_r} tight. Now suppose no A_j were entirely tight. For each j choose i_j with alpha_{j,i_j} bad. The corresponding Cartesian tuple makes every literal in its clause false, contradiction. Therefore some A_j consists entirely of tight turns.

<!-- BEGIN FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R167.md -->

# R167 — Cut-Deficit Splice-or-Full-Breach Principle

## Statement
Let G be a finite Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament, C a retained tight path, Y=G-V(C), and S an exact k-cover of G. For the fixed physical partition {V(C),Y}, t_{C|Y}(S)=1+pc(G[Y])-k+rho_{C|Y}(S). Hence if k<=pc(G[Y]), S has a current C|Y crossing. At every carrier vertex used by such a crossing, either an incident historical carrier state of C is also current and together with the crossing forms a literal current tight splice turn, or no historical carrier state of C incident with that vertex is current. Thus if S has no carrier/exterior splice turn at any current C|Y crossing, every carrier vertex used by a crossing is fully breached in historical carrier incidence. In a smallest counterexample H, every proper retained tight path C has pc(H-V(C))=2, so every hypothetical spanning exact two-cover satisfies this splice-or-full-breach alternative relative to every proper retained tight path.

## Hypotheses
For the general identity: C is a retained tight path in G and S is an exact k-cover of G. For the forced-crossing conclusion assume k<=pc(G[Y]). For the final specialization H is a smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample and C is proper.

## Scope
General fixed-partition structural theorem plus smallest-counterexample specialization. Longestness is not required. The current splice/breach conclusion concerns one displayed exact cover S.

## Applicability
Use above longest-path specializations whenever a proof has a retained proper path and needs to know that an exact low-component cover must either align a carrier/exterior splice or physically breach every crossing vertex. It combines transition deficit with the local carrier-crossing lemma.

## Persistence
The partition classes and historical carrier identity are graph-intrinsic. Transition selection and splice/full-breach status are current only in S. A fully breached vertex in one representative need not remain breached after recompletion.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not identify a current splice with the exact same-final-candidate coordinate used by static assembly; does not force endpoint exposure; does not assert a global monotone; does not transfer current crossings across representatives.

## Proof
For Pi={V(C),Y}, R7 gives t_{C|Y}(S)=pc(G[C])+pc(G[Y])-k+rho. Since C is tight, pc(G[C])=1, proving t=1+pc(G[Y])-k+rho. If k<=pc(G[Y]), then t>=1, so a selected C|Y crossing exists. Fix such a crossing at v in C. If an historical carrier state incident with v is also selected, it and the crossing are the consecutive selected incidences at v on the current tight path component, hence form a literal current tight splice turn. If no such splice exists, no historical carrier state incident with v can be selected, so the crossing vertex is fully breached relative to C. For a smallest counterexample and proper C, R18 gives an exact two-cover of H-C and therefore pc(H-C)=2. Setting k=2 yields the asserted universal hypothetical-two-cover specialization.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R167.md -->

# FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R17.md

<!-- BEGIN FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R17.md -->

# R17 — Gain minus cycle debt

## Statement

For any compatible inserted family, actual path-cover improvement is raw exchange gain minus the number of physical tight-cycle components created. A physical tight cycle is constructive, not contradictory; open one selected state on each cycle.


## Hypotheses


## Scope


## Applicability


## Persistence


## Exclusions / nonclaims


## Proof
Let the initial spanning path cover have n fixed vertices and q path components. Each path component on m vertices contains exactly m-1 selected adjacent states, so the whole cover has n-q selected states. Perform any compatible inserted-family exchange in the project sense: add the inserted selected states and remove its complete blocker set, preserving the local degree/compatibility conditions so every connected component of the resulting selected-state system is either a vertex-simple path or a physical tight cycle. Let g be the raw exchange gain, namely the number of inserted selected states minus the number of removed selected states. Before cycle opening the new system therefore has n-q+g selected states. Suppose it contains exactly c cycle components. On each physical tight cycle, remove any one selected state. Removing one state opens that cycle into a vertex-simple tight path and does not alter any other component. After opening all c cycles, the resulting spanning system is a genuine path cover with n-q+g-c selected states. Since a spanning path cover with q' components has exactly n-q' selected states, we have n-q'=n-q+g-c, hence q-q'=g-c. Thus actual path-cover improvement equals raw exchange gain minus the number c of physical tight-cycle components created. In particular a physical tight cycle is constructive bookkeeping debt rather than a contradiction: one selected state pays exactly one unit to open it. This is the full R17 identity.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R17.md -->

# FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R171.md

<!-- BEGIN FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R171.md -->

# R171 — Literal Signed-Pair Frame Complete Discharge

## Statement
Let H be in the Strong smallest-counterexample program. Suppose H=K sqcup P sqcup T is a literal spanning three-cover, K is a nonempty tight path, and (a;P),(T;b) is a graph-intrinsic opposite-sign historical pair with historical pair mass M=|P|+|T|. Then at least one of the following occurs: (i) a spanning two-cover; (ii) strict historical pair-mass descent; (iii) bounded support swallow. In the swallow branch generated by the interval-peel proof, an order-three failure/contact trimer contains an entire historical support, so that support has order at most three.

## Hypotheses
Strong Level-(1); H is a hypothetical smallest counterexample to the two-cover conjecture; H is displayed literally as the three current tight-path components K,P,T; K is nonempty and proper; P,T are vertex-disjoint historical opposite-signed supports with graph-intrinsic witnesses a,b and M=|P|+|T|. The proof uses the accepted witness-order seed constructions, Signed-Interval Rebirth/Tight-Path Cut Memory, and complete historical-pair marker-contact descent.

## Scope
Strong Level-(1), no CW assumption. The interval-peel part does not require a uniform bound on |K|. Literal means the displayed current representative is exactly H=K sqcup P sqcup T and the peel consumes literal intervals of that same K without a fresh minimality completion or representative reset.

## Applicability
Use when a retained opposite-sign historical pair and a third current path exhaust the vertex set. It eliminates the full-reservoir literal-frame recurrence before fresh recompletion.

## Persistence
The historical signs are graph-intrinsic and survive as ancestry. A failed peel produces an order-three tight contact marker; Signed-Interval Rebirth may replace a deleted signed endpoint by the appropriate immediately deleted historical neighbor, so witness names need not persist. Successful peels remain in the displayed literal frame. No new completion is introduced during the peel.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not say bounded support swallow is closure; it means one historical support is completely swallowed by the bounded order-three contact marker and is therefore of order at most three. Does not make pair mass globally monotone across unrelated resets. Does not preserve original witness names after rebirth. Does not use a proper tight cycle as contradiction. Does not assert any CW-specific conclusion. The theorem is not a generic statement for arbitrary three paths lacking the historical opposite-sign pair.

## Proof
Write the literal frame as H=K sqcup P sqcup T, with K=(k_0,...,k_m), P=(p_0,...,p_r), T=(t_0,...,t_s), all nonempty, and retain the opposite signs (a;P) and (T;b). Thus a is outside P, b is outside T, (a,P) is a tight head extension, and (T,b) is a tight tail extension. Put M=|P|+|T|.

We use the following seam observation throughout. Whenever already-tight vertex-disjoint blocks are concatenated, the only uncertified turns are the one or two turns crossing each displayed block junction. In every junction used below, each uncertified turn contains one or two vertices of P or T. If such a turn h is bad, R3 makes its complete reversal C=bar(h) a tight trimer on the same three vertices. If C contains an entire contacted historical support, then that support has order at most three and R171 output (iii) holds. Otherwise apply Signed-Interval Rebirth R425 to every historical support met by C, taking its signed-side surviving interval. At least one support strictly shortens, neither surviving support is empty, and the head/tail polarities remain opposite. Hence the historical pair mass strictly decreases, giving output (ii). This is a graph-intrinsic historical descent; no fresh cover completion is invoked. Therefore in each construction below we may assume every displayed seam is tight, because the first bad seam already proves (ii) or (iii).

Step 1: eliminate cross-support witnesses. Because H is partitioned by K,P,T and a is outside P, either a lies in K or a lies in T. Suppose a lies in T. If |P|>=2, the first sign turn (a,p_0,p_1) is tight. Use this tight trimer itself as a marker. If it contains all of P (in particular |P|<=2) or all of T, output (iii). Otherwise R425 applied after deleting its three vertices leaves a nonempty head-signed descendant of P and a nonempty tail-signed descendant of T, and P loses at least p_0,p_1, so M strictly decreases: output (ii). If |P|=1, choose any two distinct vertices outside P (they exist in the displayed three-cover) and use R3 to orient a tight trimer containing the unique vertex p_0; this trimer contains all of P, giving (iii). Thus a in T is completely discharged. The exact dual argument discharges b in P: when |T|>=2 use the inherited tight terminal sign turn (t_{s-1},t_s,b), and when |T|=1 use any R3 tight trimer containing the singleton T. Consequently the only remaining case has a,b both in K.

Step 2: forward witness order. Suppose a=k_i and b=k_j with i<j. Decompose K in its old order as
K = L, a, N, b, R,
where L=(k_0,...,k_{i-1}), N=(k_{i+1},...,k_{j-1}), and R=(k_{j+1},...,k_m), omitting empty blocks. Consider the two literal vertex-disjoint spanning path proposals
A = (L,a,P,N),
B = (T,b,R).
All turns internal to L,N,R are inherited from K; (a,P) and (T,b) are the retained sign extensions. The only uncertified turns are: the single L-a-P junction turn when L is nonempty; the at-most-two P-N junction turns when N is nonempty; and the single T-b-R junction turn when R is nonempty. Every one of these junction turns meets P or T, so by the seam observation a first bad one gives (ii) or (iii). If all are tight, A and B are tight, disjoint, and cover every vertex of H. Thus they are a literal spanning two-cover, output (i).

Step 3: reverse witness order. Suppose b=k_j occurs before a=k_i, so j<i, and write
K = L, b, N, a, R
with the evident possibly empty intervals. Consider the single literal spanning order
Q = (L,T,b,N,a,P,R).
The inherited data certify every turn except those at four kinds of junction: the at-most-two L-T turns; the one turn joining the tail extension (T,b) to the next K vertex toward a when such a vertex exists; the one turn joining the last K vertex before a to the head extension (a,P) when such a predecessor exists; and the at-most-two P-R turns. (When b and a are adjacent, the two middle junction turns are simply (t_s,b,a) and (b,a,p_0).) Every uncertified turn again meets T or P. Hence any bad junction gives (ii) or (iii) by the seam observation. If all are tight, Q is a literal Hamilton tight path on H, in particular a spanning cover with at most two paths, so output (i) holds.

Step 4: coincident witnesses. Suppose a=b=k_i and write K=L,a,R. Consider
Q = (L,T,a,P,R).
The only uncertified turns are the at-most-two L-T junction turns, the central bridge turn (t_s,a,p_0), and the at-most-two P-R junction turns. The sign data already certify the turns immediately inside T,a and a,P. A bad outer junction gives (ii) or (iii) by the seam observation. If the central bridge is bad, R3 gives the tight reverse trimer (p_0,a,t_s), which meets both historical supports. If either contacted support is entirely contained in this trimer, output (iii); otherwise R425 rebirths both to nonempty opposite-signed descendants and strictly lowers M, giving (ii). If every junction is tight, Q is a literal Hamilton tight path on H, hence output (i).

These cases exhaust all possible witness locations and relative orders. Every construction uses only the original literal frame, inherited contiguous K/P/T intervals, the two original sign extensions, boundary antisymmetry, and Signed-Interval Rebirth. No minimality recompletion, unrelated representative, marker reset, or transported currentness is used. In the good branch the displayed block paths are literal paths on the original vertex partition; in the bad branch the exact reversed seam trimer is retained as the physical contact/refund certificate. Thus the reconstruction preserves precisely the historical same-frame/no-recompletion strength of R171 while proving its three stated alternatives.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R171.md -->
