# R467 — All-internal source-trimer four-birth interaction fan

## Statement
Retain every conclusion of R458. In addition, fix one directional residual seam in the all-internal R359 source state H=J sqcup U sqcup V, where J=(a,x,c), U=(u_1,...,u_r), V=(v_1,...,v_s), r,s>=2. For the native U-to-V R453 clause write A=(v_1,u_r,u_{r-1}) and B=(v_2,v_1,u_r). Then the seam has the following exhaustive source-coupled amplification.

(I) If A is tight and B is bad, then bar(B)=(u_r,v_1,v_2) is tight, so H=J sqcup U^- sqcup V^+ is a second literal minimum three-cover with U^-=(u_1,...,u_{r-1}) and V^+=(u_r,v_1,...,v_s). R168 forces both shifted residual rails nontrivial. Reapplying the all-internal R359 shield conclusion to this shifted currentization gives (v_1,u_r,x) tight. Hence the winning trimer A has same-polarity R38 collisions on both of its physical dimers: on (u_r,u_{r-1}) with head witnesses x,v_1, and on (v_1,u_r) with tail witnesses x,u_{r-1}. The second collision is itself the R455 collision of the shifted U^- to V^+ seam, with exact shifted-splice provenance.

(II) If A is bad and B is tight, then bar(A)=(u_{r-1},u_r,v_1) is tight, so H=J sqcup U^+ sqcup V^- is a second literal minimum three-cover with U^+=(u_1,...,u_r,v_1) and V^-=(v_2,...,v_s). Again R168 keeps both shifted rails nontrivial, and R359 gives the shifted shield (x,v_1,u_r) tight. Hence the winning trimer B has same-polarity R38 collisions on both physical dimers: on (v_2,v_1) with tail witnesses x,u_r, and on (v_1,u_r) with head witnesses x,v_2. The second collision is the R455 collision of the shifted U^+ to V^- seam.

(III) If both A and B are tight, then K=(v_2,v_1,u_r,u_{r-1}) is a tight four-path. The original R359 shields (v_2,v_1,x) and (x,u_r,u_{r-1}) show that both terminal dimers of K carry same-polarity R38 collisions: (v_2,v_1) with tail witnesses x,u_r, and (u_r,u_{r-1}) with head witnesses x,v_1.

Thus every directional native residual splice yields two distinct role-linked same-polarity collision supports whose x-signed polarities are opposite. In the unique-winner cases the two supports are the old residual terminal dimer and a new cross-seam terminal dimer obtained only after the exact one-vertex seam transfer; in the double-winner case they are the disjoint terminal dimers of a tight P4. The symmetric V-to-U statement also holds. In every case each collision channel may be reminted separately by R458. Unlike exact-support replay, the unique-winner amplification genuinely consumes the named opposite-rail endpoint together with its source neighbor and the exact R453 splice certificate: replacing that endpoint by an arbitrary exterior witness no longer supplies the shifted literal three-cover.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample; J=(a,x,c) is a proper tight trimer in the all-internal R359 regime; H=J sqcup U sqcup V is a fixed literal currentization with U,V nontrivial. Accepted R3,R38,R168,R359,R453,R458 are available.

## Scope
Order-free strengthening of the all-internal interaction fan. It converts each single R453 seam outcome into a two-support, polarity-controlled collision packet while preserving the exact source seam and shifted-cut provenance.

## Applicability
Use after an R455 directional splice is selected. In a unique-winner branch, shift the literal U|V cut across the unique good seam turn, reapply R359 to the same fixed trimer J, and harvest the cross-seam collision. In a double-winner branch, use the tight reversed-seam P4 and its two terminal collisions. This is a role-consuming replacement for fresh-witness-blind exact-support replay.

## Persistence
J, x, the original U,V paths, the exact R453 proposal and seam holes, the winner status, the one-vertex shifted three-cover when present, the shifted R359 shield, all named collision supports/witnesses/tested polarities, and the tight P4 in the double-winner case are graph-intrinsic or retained literal historical certificates. Original and shifted currentizations are alternative representatives; their graph-intrinsic tight turns and collision certificates persist, while later payment descendants need not coexist.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert that the two collision supports alone close H, that alternative currentizations are simultaneously current, or that generic R38/common-anchor interaction preserves these source roles. In unique-winner cases the two supports overlap and therefore do not themselves form an R39 direct balanced pair. In the double-winner case exact-support replay of later pair births still does not by itself consume fresh witnesses. No monotone iteration of seam transfers is claimed.

## Proof
Assume the hypotheses of R467 and retain the fixed physical source coordinates J=(a,x,c), U=(u_1,...,u_r), V=(v_1,...,v_s) in the stated all-internal outer-pair regime. We reconstruct the asserted source-coupled amplification directly and do not invoke the historical R359/R453/R455/R458 chain.\n\n1. Source rail floor and shields. Apply the proof mechanism of current accepted R920/P992 to this supplied source currentization. The P992 argument is representative-local and uses only the retained all-internal condition. If U were a singleton (y), then the automatic dimer (x,y), together with V, would be an exact two-cover of H-{a,c} exposing x, contradiction. If U=(y,z) were a dimer, the direct attachment (x,y,z) must be bad by all-internality, so R3 makes its reversal (z,y,x) tight; that reverse trimer together with V again gives an exact H-{a,c} cover exposing x. Hence |U|>=3. The same proof gives |V|>=3. Likewise each direct x-attachment at either end of U or V is bad, else x is exposed in an exact H-{a,c} two-cover; R3 therefore gives the four reverse shields (u_2,u_1,x), (x,u_r,u_{r-1}), (v_2,v_1,x), (x,v_s,v_{s-1}) as tight turns. These are exactly the source facts needed below.\n\n2. Literal U-to-V seam. Keep J as the third path and test the concatenation U followed by V. The only new turns are h_1=(u_{r-1},u_r,v_1) and h_2=(u_r,v_1,v_2). They cannot both be tight, because then U followed by V together with J would be a spanning two-cover of H. Define A=bar(h_1)=(v_1,u_r,u_{r-1}) and B=bar(h_2)=(v_2,v_1,u_r). By R3 at least one of A,B is tight. Retain the complete winner status.\n\n3. A-only branch. Suppose A is tight and B is bad. R3 then gives h_2=(u_r,v_1,v_2) tight. Therefore U^-=(u_1,...,u_{r-1}) and V^+=(u_r,v_1,...,v_s) are literal tight paths and H=J|U^-|V^+ is another spanning three-cover. Since |U|>=3, U^- has at least two vertices. Now test (x,u_r,v_1). If it were tight, (x,V^+)|U^- would be a two-path cover of H-{a,c} exposing x. It is exact: H-{a,c} cannot itself be Hamiltonian, because any Hamilton path there together with the automatic dimer (a,c) would two-cover H. Thus (x,u_r,v_1) would contradict the retained all-internal condition. Hence it is bad and R3 forces the shifted shield (v_1,u_r,x) tight.\n\nOn the tested oriented dimer D_1=(u_r,u_{r-1}), the original source shield (x,u_r,u_{r-1}) and A=(v_1,u_r,u_{r-1}) are two head certificates with distinct witnesses x,v_1. R523 gives the HH same-support collision packet. On D_2=(v_1,u_r), the shifted shield (v_1,u_r,x) and A=(v_1,u_r,u_{r-1}) are two tail certificates with distinct witnesses x,u_{r-1}; R523 gives the TT collision. This is exactly R467(I), including the one-vertex cut shift and the old-residual/new-cross-seam provenance.\n\n4. B-only branch. Suppose A is bad and B is tight. R3 gives h_1=(u_{r-1},u_r,v_1) tight. Put U^+=(u_1,...,u_r,v_1) and V^-=(v_2,...,v_s). Since |V|>=3, V^- has at least two vertices, and H=J|U^+|V^- is a literal spanning three-cover. If (u_r,v_1,x) were tight, then (U^+,x)|V^- would be an exact H-{a,c} two-cover exposing x, again impossible. Thus R3 forces (x,v_1,u_r) tight. The original shield (v_2,v_1,x) together with B=(v_2,v_1,u_r) gives by R523 a TT collision on D_3=(v_2,v_1), witnesses x,u_r. The shifted shield (x,v_1,u_r) together with B gives an HH collision on D_4=(v_1,u_r), witnesses x,v_2. This is exactly R467(II).\n\n5. Double-winner branch. If both A and B are tight, their literal overlap concatenates to K=(v_2,v_1,u_r,u_{r-1}), a tight P4. On its left terminal dimer (v_2,v_1), B and the source shield (v_2,v_1,x) are two tail certificates with witnesses u_r,x. On its right terminal dimer (u_r,u_{r-1}), A and the source shield (x,u_r,u_{r-1}) are two head certificates with witnesses v_1,x. R523 gives the two claimed terminal collision packets. This is R467(III). In all three cases the two collision supports have opposite x-signed polarities, exactly as stated. Exchanging U and V proves the symmetric directional assertion.\n\n6. Clean remint of every collision channel, including the historical R458 content. Fix any one of the same-polarity collision packets produced above, on tested physical dimer D, with distinct witnesses p,q; one of these is x in every R467 channel. Let M be the unique terminal signed dimer of J whose polarity is opposite to the common polarity of the two signed copies D_p,D_q. The seam supports lie outside J, so D is physically disjoint from M. Current reconstructible R514 says physically disjoint signed supports of opposite polarity form a graph-intrinsic balanced pair. Thus (D_p,M) is one historical pair birth and (D_q,M) is a second. Read the p-birth first and q-birth second before unrelated reset. They satisfy R160: both use a terminal signed dimer of the same fixed trimer J and a partner signed dimer disjoint from J. For proof-awareness, R160 is understood through accepted reconstructible P562/R441; the two generations overlap at least on M (and here also on D), so the later birth is nonquiet and yields the required historical signed-support/anchor interaction or cross-generation pair interaction. The collision witnesses, tested dimer, J-terminal mate, and exact seam/shift proposal that generated the second witness remain attached as historical coordinates.\n\nThis direct remint proves, channel by channel, every remint conclusion that R467 phrases as Retain every conclusion of R458 and each collision channel may be reminted separately by R458. Therefore R458 itself is not needed as a dependency. Sections 1-5 prove the complete source-coupled seam amplification, and Section 6 supplies the retained remint layer. The proof uses only R3,R920,R523,R514,R160. In particular it does not use R168,R359,R453,R455,R458,R5, or R24.

# R471 — Two-cover partition rigidity modulo balanced-pair birth

## Statement
Let H be a finite Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament, W a proper vertex subset, and F=P sqcup Q and F'=P' sqcup Q' two literal two-covers of H[W] with all four components nonempty. First, the representative-rigidity conclusion of R470 holds: if the unordered rail-support partitions differ, R410 yields a graph-intrinsic balanced opposite-sign pair; if the partitions agree but the literal Hamilton orders differ on some common support, R435 yields an exact reversal of an old adjacent state, a tight reverse trimer, or a vertex-simple proper tight cycle; outside these outputs the two covers are literally identical up to rail exchange. In addition, there is a sharp opposite-end refinement. Suppose Q=(q_0,...,q_n) with n>=1 and some rail K of F' exposes q_n as its head. Then either the support partitions differ and the R410 balanced-pair output occurs, or after relabelling V(K)=V(Q). Write the second vertex of K as q_j. If j=n-1, K begins with the exact reversed terminal state (q_n,q_{n-1}) of Q. If j<n-1, the consecutive K-state q_n q_j is a nonadjacent reverse-order encounter with Q, so R435 yields a tight reverse trimer or a vertex-simple proper tight cycle. Dually, if some rail of F' exposes q_0 as its tail, then either a balanced pair occurs, or that rail ends with the exact reversed initial state (q_1,q_0), or R435 yields a reverse trimer/proper cycle. Therefore forcing a terminal vertex of one exact-cover rail to the opposite end of another exact cover is sufficient to obtain either the precise terminal-state inversion or an already explicit reverse-order output; the predecessor/successor need not be steered separately.

## Hypotheses
H is a finite Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament; W is proper; F and F' are literal two-covers of H[W] with nonempty components; accepted R410 and R435. For the opposite-end refinement, the reference rail Q has at least two vertices.

## Scope
Order-free strengthening of exact-cover representative rigidity. Adds a one-coordinate endpoint-inversion criterion tailored to deletion-fiber comparisons.

## Applicability
Use when a cross-fiber argument needs the reversal of a terminal directed state. It is enough to force the old terminal vertex to the opposite rail end in another exact cover: a wrong next vertex is not failure but immediately triggers the R435 reverse-trimer/proper-cycle output. In particular this lowers the R469 cross-fiber target from a prescribed reversed endpoint dimer to opposite-end exposure of its terminal vertex.

## Persistence
The common residue and compared covers are representative-relative. Any R410 balanced pair, exact reversed directed state, reverse trimer, or proper cycle is graph-intrinsic once exhibited. The endpoint identity q_n or q_0 is retained in the special refinement.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not force opposite-end exposure to exist. Does not say a reverse trimer or proper cycle closes the conjecture. Does not localize the R435 output beyond the displayed first opposite-end state when the exact adjacent reversal fails. Does not compare different residues without an additional cross-fiber synchronization input.

## Proof
Apply R410 to F and F'. If their unordered support partitions differ, R410 gives the balanced opposite-sign pair and all conclusions follow. Hence assume the support partitions agree and relabel F' so that each rail has the same vertex support as its counterpart in F. The general representative-rigidity statement follows exactly by the index-descent argument: if a same-support rail order K differs from P=(v_0,...,v_k), the sequence of P-indices along K is a nonidentity permutation and therefore has a descent. A consecutive descent v_i v_j with i>j is a single-state reverse-order encounter in R435; when i=j+1 it is the exact reversed adjacent state, and otherwise R435 gives a reverse trimer or proper cycle. Now assume Q=(q_0,...,q_n), n>=1, and a rail K of F' has head q_n. Under the fixed support partition K must have vertex set V(Q), so K has a second vertex q_j with 0<=j<n. The consecutive K-contacts q_n,q_j are in reverse Q-order. If j=n-1, K begins with (q_n,q_{n-1}), the exact reversal of Q's terminal state. If j<n-1, the K-subpath between those consecutive contacts is the single state q_n q_j and is not the adjacent-reversal exception of R435, so R435 yields a tight reverse trimer at a seam or a vertex-simple proper tight cycle. For the dual statement, if a same-support rail K has tail q_0, write its penultimate vertex q_j. If j=1 the final state is the exact reversal (q_1,q_0) of Q's initial state; if j>1, the consecutive state q_j q_0 is a nonadjacent reverse-order encounter and R435 again yields a reverse trimer or proper cycle. Thus opposite-end exposure alone forces the advertised terminal inversion-or-output alternative.

# FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R483.md

<!-- BEGIN FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R483.md -->

# R483 — Reverse-Ear output existence is path-triple ubiquitous

## Statement
Let H be any Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament, let K be a vertex-simple tight path, and let T={a,b,c} be any three distinct vertices occurring on K. For each m in T, let J_m be the unique tight trimer on T having middle m. Then at least two of the three comparisons of K with J_m necessarily satisfy the reverse-order hypothesis of R435 and hence yield an R435 output: an exact reversal of an old state, a tight reverse trimer, or a vertex-simple proper tight cycle. Indeed K induces one linear order on the three contacts T and therefore has one unique middle vertex m_K. For the contacts of J_m to occur in increasing J_m-order along K, the literal order of J_m must equal the order induced by K, which is possible only when m=m_K. Hence at most one of J_a,J_b,J_c is order-aligned with K; for each other J_m, the sequence of its three contacts along K has an inversion, and some consecutive K-contacts form a reverse-order pair to which R435 applies. Consequently bare existence of an R435 order-change output is ubiquitous and is not by itself a progress alternative. A useful R435 descendant must retain a non-generic coordinate such as a prescribed cap edge, source adjacency, deletion-fiber role, or a downstream physical proposal that consumes the particular reversal.

## Hypotheses
Strong Level-(1); K is a vertex-simple tight path containing three distinct vertices T; accepted R3 and R435.

## Scope
Order-free proof-design fence and local theorem. It concerns bare R435-output existence, not the value of a specifically localized reversal/reverse-trimer/cycle.

## Applicability
Use when evaluating a claimed advance whose terminal output is merely some Reverse-Ear reversal, reverse trimer, or proper cycle. Require a role-specific path comparison or downstream consumer; otherwise the output is free around any tight path containing three selected vertices.

## Persistence
The chosen path K, triple T, three middle-labelled tight trimers, and each resulting R435 certificate are graph-intrinsic.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not say R435 is useless. Exact reversal of a named cap/source state, a reverse trimer carrying prescribed coordinates, or a cycle entering a specific consumer may be highly productive. Does not assert all three middle-labelled comparisons pay, only at least two.

## Proof
Read the three vertices T in their order along K, say p<q<r. Any three-vertex path whose contacts are increasing along K must have literal order (p,q,r), so its middle vertex is q. Among the three middle-labelled tight trimers J_a,J_b,J_c, only J_q has middle q. Therefore J_m for each m in T\\{q} cannot have all three contacts increasing along K. For each such J_m, list its three vertices in the order encountered along K. Since that permutation is not increasing in J_m-order, it has a descent between two consecutive entries of the K-contact sequence. Those two vertices are consecutive K-contacts with J_m and occur in reverse J_m-order, so R435 applies to the K-subpath between them. Thus at least the two m≠q comparisons produce an exact reversed state, reverse trimer, or proper cycle.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R483.md -->

# FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R484.md

<!-- BEGIN FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R484.md -->

# R484 — End-Wrap Reverse-Ear Dichotomy

## Statement
Let H be a finite Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament and let P=(v_0,v_1,...,v_n) be a vertex-simple tight path with n>=2. Put w=v_n v_0. (Head-wrap.) If v_n v_0 v_1 is tight, then either the named reverse terminal trimer v_0 v_n v_{n-1} is tight, or V(P) supports the vertex-simple proper tight cycle with cyclic order v_n,v_0,v_1,...,v_{n-1}. (Tail-wrap.) Dually, if v_{n-1} v_n v_0 is tight, then either the named reverse initial trimer v_1 v_0 v_n is tight, or V(P) supports the same proper tight cycle. Thus a one-end rotation that selects the closing state v_n v_0 never yields only an anonymous order change: it certifies either a reverse ear pinned to the opposite endpoint neighbor or a cycle on exactly the old path support.

## Hypotheses
H is a finite Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament; P is a vertex-simple tight path with at least three vertices; accepted R3 and R435.

## Scope
Pure order-free Strong Level-(1) path-interaction lemma. No completion, smallest-counterexample, fixed-fiber, overlap, role-label, or representative-synchronization hypothesis.

## Applicability
Use when a wrap/currentization moves the tail of a named tight path to its head, or the head to its tail, by selecting the closing state. In the R182 fixed-fiber notation P=C_R=(h,x_1,...,x_{r-1},t), a head-wrap t h x_1 yields either h t x_{r-1} tight or a proper tight cycle on V(C_R); the tail-wrap x_{r-1} t h yields either x_1 h t tight or that cycle.

## Persistence
The closing state, the exact opposite endpoint neighbor, the reverse trimer when obtained, and the proper cycle support/order are graph-intrinsic once exhibited. No claim is made that the input path or its rotated path remains selected in later representatives.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not recover the historical Cross-Completion Opposite-Role Collision theorem, does not define head-lost/tail-lost roles, and does not imply the deleted wrap boundary is an old residual boundary. A proper tight cycle is a constructive output, not a contradiction. The reverse trimer is localized to the named closing seam but is not by itself a spanning two-cover or physical sibling clause.

## Proof
For the head-wrap assume v_n v_0 v_1 is tight. Then K=(v_n,v_0,v_1,...,v_{n-1}) is a vertex-simple tight path. Compare K with P using R435 and take the consecutive K-contacts v_i=v_n and v_j=v_0, so i=n>0=j and the ear E is the single state v_n v_0. Since n>=2 this is the nonadjacent one-state case. R435 tests the two seam turns v_{n-1} v_n v_0 and v_n v_0 v_1. The second is tight by hypothesis. If the first is bad, R3 gives its antisymmetric reverse v_0 v_n v_{n-1} tight. If the first is also tight, R435 gives the vertex-simple proper tight cycle obtained by E followed by the old P-segment v_0,v_1,...,v_{n-1}, namely cyclic order v_n,v_0,v_1,...,v_{n-1}. For the tail-wrap assume v_{n-1} v_n v_0 is tight and use K=(v_1,v_2,...,v_n,v_0). Again the consecutive reverse-order ear is E=v_n v_0. Now the first R435 seam v_{n-1} v_n v_0 is tight by hypothesis. If the second seam v_n v_0 v_1 is bad, R3 gives v_1 v_0 v_n tight; if it is tight, the same proper cycle results.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R484.md -->

<!-- BEGIN FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R508.md -->

# R508 — Absorbable deletion blocks force recompletion crossings

## Statement
Let H be a finite boundary tournament with pc(H)>2. Let D be a nonempty proper vertex set, put W=V(H)\D, and let S be a nonempty proper subset of W. Suppose Q is a vertex-simple tight path with vertex set exactly D union S. Then every literal spanning two-path cover T=T_1 sqcup T_2 of H-D selects a directed state xy with exactly one endpoint in S and the other in W\S. Equivalently, an exact two-cover of the deletion cannot leave an absorbable remainder block S isolated from its complement. In the anti-aligned bridge setting of R502, take D={a_0,b_q}, S=V(P^o), and Q=P. In the current-trimer setting of R506, delete p and take S={x,z}, Q=J, or delete z and take S={p,x}, Q=J. Thus this single replacement principle gives the crossing core of R502 and both conclusions of R506; R5 is needed in those applications only to supply the deletion two-cover, and R24 is unnecessary.

## Hypotheses
H is finite with a well-defined tight-path cover number and pc(H)>2; D is nonempty and proper; S and W\S are both nonempty; Q is a tight path spanning exactly D union S; T is a literal two-path cover of H-D.

## Scope
Order-free combinatorial parent theorem. Boundary antisymmetry, Strong Level-(1), smallest-counterexample minimality, capture, endpoint roles, and deletion rail-size floors are not used once the two-cover T is supplied.

## Applicability
Use whenever a deletion remainder contains a named block S that can be reabsorbed together with all deleted vertices into one certified tight path Q. Any exact two-cover of the deletion must physically cross from S to the complementary remainder. R502 then uses R176 after this crossing; R506 and retired R333 are direct specializations.

## Persistence
Retain the deletion set D, absorbable block S, certified extension path Q on D union S, the particular deletion two-cover T, and at least one selected directed crossing state xy of T. The direction and location of xy are representative-relative to T; the identities of D,S,Q are fixed input coordinates.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not produce the deletion two-cover; in smallest-counterexample applications that existence comes from R5. Does not prescribe which component or endpoint realizes the crossing, does not make the crossing current in another representative, and does not itself yield a spanning two-cover. It gives no balanced-pair, capture, contact, or clause conclusion without a separate consumer.

## Proof
Assume that T=T_1 sqcup T_2 selects no directed state with one endpoint in S and the other in W\S. A path component containing vertices of both sides would, along its vertex order, have a first adjacent pair at which the side changes; that selected directed state would cross the partition. Hence each T_i is contained wholly in S or wholly in W\S. Both sides are nonempty and T has exactly two nonempty components spanning W, so after relabeling V(T_1)=S and V(T_2)=W\S. By hypothesis Q is a tight path with vertex set D union S. Therefore Q and T_2 are vertex-disjoint tight paths whose vertex sets partition V(H), so Q sqcup T_2 is a literal spanning two-cover of H. This contradicts pc(H)>2. Thus every such T selects the asserted crossing. For R502 choose (D,S,Q)=({a_0,b_q},V(P^o),P). For the two R506 conclusions choose respectively (D,S,Q)=({p},{x,z},J) and ({z},{p,x},J).

# FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R509.md

<!-- BEGIN FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R509.md -->

# R509 — Cut-indexed outward-transition recompletion exchange

## Statement
Let H be a finite Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament with pc(H)>2, and retain a fixed R508 packet. Thus D is nonempty and proper, W=V(H)\D, S is a nonempty proper subset of W, Q=(q_0,...,q_m) is a vertex-simple tight path on exactly D union S, and T=T_1 sqcup T_2 is a literal two-cover of H-D; put C=W\S and retain a selected T-state xy crossing S|C.

Decompose the two T-rails into maximal C-blocks.

(1) There are at least two C-blocks.

(2) Suppose there are exactly two C-blocks, B=(b_0,...,b_r) and K=(c_0,...,c_s). Let -1<=i<=m. Assume the outward incidences at the Q-cut after q_i exist in T in the following literal sense: if i>=0, T selects the directed state q_i b_0 immediately before B; if i<m, T selects the directed state c_s q_{i+1} immediately after K. (At i=-1 only the second condition is present, and at i=m only the first is present.) Put L_i=(q_0,...,q_i) when i>=0 and R_i=(q_{i+1},...,q_m) when i<m. Then
U_i = L_i followed by B (or just B if i=-1),
V_i = K followed by R_i (or just K if i=m)
is a literal spanning two-path proposal of H whose complete uncertified-turn set is exactly
E_i = {alpha_i=(q_{i-1},q_i,b_0) if i>=1} union {beta_i=(c_s,q_{i+1},q_{i+2}) if i<=m-2}.
Every other turn of U_i sqcup V_i is certified by Q, by the two C-blocks, or by the displayed selected T-incidences.

Consequently E_i cannot be empty. If |E_i|=1, its unique turn is bad and its exact antisymmetric reverse is tight. If |E_i|=2, at least one of alpha_i,beta_i is bad, so R3 gives the physically certified mate clause reverse(alpha_i) OR reverse(beta_i). In particular, if the retained selected crossing xy is S-to-C with S-endpoint q_i, then its Q-position chooses the cut after q_i: at i=m it alone gives the one-hole proposal, while at i<m the exact missing coordinate is a C-to-S transition from the other C-block into q_{i+1}. Dually, a retained C-to-S crossing into q_j chooses the cut before q_j: at j=0 it alone gives the one-hole proposal, while at j>0 the exact missing coordinate is an S-to-C transition from q_{j-1} into the other C-block.

## Hypotheses
H is finite Strong Level-(1) with pc(H)>2. The full fixed R508 data (D,S,Q,T,xy) are retained. For part (2), C=W\S has exactly two maximal blocks in the literal T-rails and the stated cut-indexed outward incidence or incidences occur. Empty Q-side pieces at i=-1,m are omitted.

## Scope
Order-free local/parent recompletion compiler. No smallest-counterexample minimality, capture, sign payment, endpoint universality, or source ancestry is used after the R508 packet is supplied.

## Applicability
Given the selected R508 crossing, inspect its direction and the position of its S-endpoint on Q. If that endpoint is an aligned end of Q and C has exactly two T-blocks, obtain a literal one-hole spanning proposal immediately. If it is internal, search only for the oppositely directed transition at the adjacent Q vertex and on the other C-block; finding it yields the displayed exact two-hole proposal and mate clause.

## Persistence
Retain D,S,Q, the literal two-cover T, its two named maximal C-blocks B,K, the selected crossing xy, the cut index i determined by the S-endpoint's Q-position, every required outward T-incidence, the displayed proposal U_i sqcup V_i, and the complete hole set E_i. Any forced mate turn is graph-intrinsic; the proposal and transition coordinates are representative-relative certificates.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not force a minimal-transition two-cover to have only two C-blocks. Does not force the partner outward transition at the adjacent Q vertex when the selected crossing endpoint is internal. Does not claim that a generic crossing, balanced pair, capture, or collision closes H. With three or more C-blocks, the displayed two-path proposal does not cover all of C and the theorem gives no completion.

## Proof
Let C=W\S. Each maximal C-block is a vertex-simple tight subpath of a T-rail. If there were exactly one such block B, it would contain every vertex of C. Since Q contains exactly D union S, Q and B would be disjoint tight paths partitioning V(H), contrary to pc(H)>2. This proves (1).

Assume now that B and K are the two C-blocks and fix i with the stated incidences. The supports of L_i and R_i partition V(Q)=D union S, while the supports of B and K partition C. Hence U_i and V_i are vertex-disjoint and together span H. They are vertex-simple.

Inspect their consecutive triples. Inside L_i,R_i all turns are certified by Q, and inside B,K all turns are certified by T. At the L_i-to-B splice, when both relevant triples exist, the turn (q_i,b_0,b_1) is certified because q_i b_0 is immediately before B in T; the only other splice turn is alpha_i=(q_{i-1},q_i,b_0), and it exists exactly when i>=1. If B is a singleton, the same inspection simply omits the nonexistent first turn and leaves the same alpha_i when it exists. Dually, at the K-to-R_i splice the turn (c_{s-1},c_s,q_{i+1}) is certified by T whenever it exists, and the only other splice turn is beta_i=(c_s,q_{i+1},q_{i+2}), which exists exactly when i<=m-2. Singleton and empty-side degeneracies merely omit nonexistent triples. Therefore the complete hole set is exactly E_i.

If E_i were empty, every turn of U_i and V_i would be tight, giving a literal spanning two-cover of H, impossible. If E_i has one member, it must be bad; R3 makes its complete reversal tight. If E_i={alpha_i,beta_i}, they cannot both be tight, so at least one is bad and R3 makes at least one of reverse(alpha_i),reverse(beta_i) tight. This is the asserted physical mate clause. Finally, orienting the retained xy identifies whether it supplies the left outward incidence q_i b_0 or the right outward incidence c_s q_{i+1}; its S-endpoint's index on Q identifies the cut and therefore the exact adjacent partner transition stated in the conclusion.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R509.md -->

# FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R511.md

<!-- BEGIN FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R511.md -->

# R511 — Unique-transition recompletion has a sharp three-hole obstruction

## Statement

Retain a fixed R508 packet (D,S,Q,T,xy), write C=(V(H)\D)\S, Q=(q_0,...,q_m), and let tau(T) be the number of selected T-states crossing S|C. Suppose tau(T)=1.

(1) Since R508 forces tau(T')>=1 for every exact two-cover T' of H-D, T is transition-minimal. Its component word has exactly three maximal monochromatic blocks. R509(1) forces exactly two of them to be C-blocks, so after relabelling the rails one rail is a pure C-block K=(c_0,...,c_s), and the other is A followed by B or B followed by A, where A is the unique S-block and B=(b_0,...,b_r) is the other C-block.

(2) In the SC case A B, let q_i be the last vertex of A. If i=m, R509 gives the aligned one-hole proposal. If i<m, the proposal
U=(q_0,...,q_i,b_0,...,b_r),  V=(c_0,...,c_s,q_{i+1},...,q_m)
has complete uncertified-turn set
E_SC = { (q_{i-1},q_i,b_0) if i>=1 }
       union { (c_{s-1},c_s,q_{i+1}) if s>=1 }
       union { (c_s,q_{i+1},q_{i+2}) if i<=m-2 }.

(3) In the CS case B A, let q_j be the first vertex of A. If j=0, R509 gives the aligned one-hole proposal. If j>0, the proposal
U=(q_0,...,q_{j-1},c_0,...,c_s),  V=(b_0,...,b_r,q_j,...,q_m)
has complete uncertified-turn set
E_CS = { (q_{j-2},q_{j-1},c_0) if j>=2 }
       union { (q_{j-1},c_0,c_1) if s>=1 }
       union { (b_r,q_j,q_{j+1}) if j<=m-1 }.

Each displayed set is nonempty and not all of its members are tight; therefore R3 makes the complete reversal of at least one displayed member tight. The nonaligned SC proposal has three holes exactly when s>=1 and 1<=i<=m-2. The nonaligned CS proposal has three holes exactly when s>=1 and 2<=j<=m-1. In particular j=m is an upper-end degeneracy with at most two holes, not a generic three-hole cell. The only formally zero-hole nonaligned parameter cells are m=1,i=0,s=0 in SC and m=1,j=1,s=0 in CS, and pc(H)>2 excludes their occurrence.

(4) This is a conditional normal form, not a realized countermodel. It does not assert that any Strong Level-(1), pc(H)>2 R508 packet with minimum transition count one exists. Consequently it does not by itself refute a theorem that might derive the missing R509 partner incidence for every transition-minimal cover from additional boundary-tournament structure. What it proves sharply is: if the minimum-one case occurs, the minimizing representative contains no second selected crossing, so its transition count and component word alone cannot supply the partner outward incidence. Any argument eliminating that case or forcing the partner must use additional graph-intrinsic information beyond transition minimality.


## Hypotheses

H is finite Strong Level-(1) with pc(H)>2; (D,S,Q,T,xy) is the full fixed R508 packet; tau(T)=1. Blocks are maximal in the literal T-rail orders. Empty or singleton pieces omit nonexistent triples.


## Scope

Order-free conditional obstruction and logical fence for the transition-minimization strategy. No existence of a minimum-one packet is claimed.


## Applicability

When a chosen R508 cover has tau=1, use the exact SC/CS proposal and corrected hole-count cells. Treat the result as a conditional obstruction only; a genuine refutation of a full transition-minimality implication still requires a realizable packet or a theorem showing the minimum-one branch occurs.


## Persistence

Retain D,S,Q,T, the unique crossing with its orientation and exact Q-index, the pure C-rail K, mixed C-block B, the displayed proposal, and its complete hole set. Tight reversed holes are graph-intrinsic; word, block, and proposal roles are representative-relative.


## Exclusions / nonclaims

Does not construct a boundary tournament or R508 packet with tau=1. Does not show that every transition-minimal cover has tau=1. Does not rule out an additional Strong Level-(1) theorem forcing the R509 partner incidence or excluding the minimum-one branch. Does not turn a three-hole proposal into a two-literal clause.


## Proof

R508 applies to every exact two-cover of the fixed deletion H-D and forces at least one S|C crossing, so tau=1 is the global minimum. Across two nonempty rails, the number of maximal S/C blocks is tau+2=3. R509(1) supplies at least two C-blocks. Since S and C are nonempty, the types are exactly C,C,S, giving a pure C rail K and a mixed rail AB or BA.

In SC, supports of the two displayed paths partition V(H). All internal Q-, B-, and K-turns are tight. At Q-left|B, the T-order q_i,b_0,b_1 certifies the second seam turn when it exists, leaving only (q_{i-1},q_i,b_0). At K|Q-right there is no K-to-S selected state, leaving exactly the two displayed K|Q seam turns when their vertices exist. This proves the E_SC list. The CS inspection is dual: the retained T-order b_{r-1},b_r,q_j certifies that seam turn when it exists, while the Q-left|K seam contributes its two displayed turns and B|Q-right contributes (b_r,q_j,q_{j+1}). Thus E_CS is complete.

If a displayed set were empty, or if all its members were tight, the proposal would be a literal spanning two-cover of H, contradicting pc(H)>2. R3 therefore reverses at least one bad displayed turn. Direct counting gives three SC holes iff s>=1, i>=1, and i<=m-2; it gives three CS holes iff s>=1, j>=2, and j<=m-1. This corrects the false claim that j<=m-1 follows merely from j>0. The two stated zero-hole parameter cells follow by simultaneously negating all three membership conditions and are impossible because the proposal would already be a spanning two-cover.

Finally, tau=1 says only that a hypothetical minimizing cover has a single crossing. No construction or prior dependency proves that such a packet is realizable in the full Strong Level-(1), pc(H)>2 class. Hence absence of a partner crossing inside this conditional representative is a valid data/word-level fence, but not a counterexample to any implication allowed to use additional graph structure.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R511.md -->

# FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R513.md

<!-- BEGIN FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R513.md -->

# R513 — Pure-rail seam coupling localizes the unique-transition three-hole residue

## Statement

Retain a full R512 packet and resolve outputs lexicographically by preferring R512(A) or (B) whenever either applies. Then the only unresolved P4 residue has both consecutive pure-C/Q seam holes bad. If the natural seam order is (a,b,c,d), those holes are (a,b,c) and (b,c,d), so R3 makes (d,c,b) and (c,b,a) tight. Hence the single coordinate-preserving P4 needed in the residue is the literal full reverse K*=(d,c,b,a); no enumeration of anonymous Hamilton P4 orders is needed.

CS. Put a=q_{j-2}, b=q_{j-1}, c=c_0, d=c_1. Replace the natural four-segment (a,b,c,d) in the R511 proposal by K*. This gives
U*= (q_0,...,q_{j-3}, c_1,c_0,q_{j-1},q_{j-2}, c_2,...,c_s),
V = (b_0,...,b_r,q_j,...,q_m),
with empty prefix/suffix omitted. Its complete uncertified-turn set is {g=(b_r,q_j,q_{j+1})} union L_CS(j) union R_CS(s), where
L_CS(2)=empty,
L_CS(3)={(q_0,c_1,c_0)},
L_CS(j)={(q_{j-4},q_{j-3},c_1),(q_{j-3},c_1,c_0)} for j>=4,
and
R_CS(1)=empty,
R_CS(2)={(q_{j-1},q_{j-2},c_2)},
R_CS(s)={(q_{j-1},q_{j-2},c_2),(q_{j-2},c_2,c_3)} for s>=3.
Thus (j,s)=(2,1) gives a literal one-hole spanning proposal with sole hole g; (2,2) and (3,1) give literal two-hole spanning proposals with the displayed sole outer hole together with g. Every other CS parameter cell is an exact reverse-seam irreducible cell for this coordinate-preserving substitution, with all missing outer turns displayed above: equivalently j=2,s>=3; j=3,s>=2; or j>=4,s>=1.

SC. Put a=c_{s-1}, b=c_s, c=q_{i+1}, d=q_{i+2}. Replace the natural four-segment in the other R511 rail by K*. This gives
U=(q_0,...,q_i,b_0,...,b_r),
V*=(c_0,...,c_{s-2}, q_{i+2},q_{i+1},c_s,c_{s-1}, q_{i+3},...,q_m),
again omitting empty pieces. Its complete uncertified-turn set is {h=(q_{i-1},q_i,b_0)} union L_SC(s) union R_SC(i), where
L_SC(1)=empty,
L_SC(2)={(c_0,q_{i+2},q_{i+1})},
L_SC(s)={(c_{s-3},c_{s-2},q_{i+2}),(c_{s-2},q_{i+2},q_{i+1})} for s>=3,
and
R_SC(m-2)=empty,
R_SC(m-3)={(c_s,c_{s-1},q_{i+3})},
R_SC(i)={(c_s,c_{s-1},q_{i+3}),(c_{s-1},q_{i+3},q_{i+4})} for i<=m-4.
Thus (s,i)=(1,m-2) gives a literal one-hole spanning proposal with sole hole h; (2,m-2) and (1,m-3) give literal two-hole spanning proposals. Every other SC parameter cell is exact reverse-seam irreducible for this substitution: equivalently s=1,i<=m-4; s=2,i<=m-3; or s>=3,i<=m-2.

The construction is valid whether each Q-side seam vertex lies in D or S, because it changes the spanning R511 proposal rather than the deletion cover T. If either Q-side seam vertex lies in D, K* cannot itself be a path of H-D. If both lie in S, vertex eligibility alone still does not define an alternative exact cover T' of H-D: R511/R512 retain no adjacency or neighbor relation between these two Q-consecutive vertices and their positions in the literal S-block A. Accordingly no lexicographic decrease of T is claimed without additional A-position and outer-turn certificates.


## Hypotheses

H is finite Strong Level-(1) with pc(H)>2, and the full R512(P) tau(T)=1 packet is retained. In CS, s>=1 and 2<=j<=m-1; in SC, s>=1 and 1<=i<=m-2. Outputs (A) and (B) are consumed whenever their seam-hole status permits, leaving both named seam holes bad.


## Scope

Order-free exact consumption of the pure-C/Q seam residual. It uses only boundary antisymmetry and the literal R511/R512 coordinates. The irreducibility conclusion concerns the displayed coordinate-preserving reverse-four-segment substitution, not every possible global rearrangement of T or of the spanning proposal.


## Applicability

In an R512(P) cell, first inspect the two seam holes. If zero or one is bad, use R512(A)/(B). If both are bad, use the forced literal reverse P4 and read the exact CS/SC outer-turn set above. The three listed shallow-boundary cells immediately reduce to one/two holes; all other cells expose the exact additional outer certificates still required.


## Persistence

Retain D,S,Q,T,K,B,A, the unique crossing orientation and Q cut index, the original R511 proposal and isolated mixed-seam hole, both bad seam holes, the forced ordered P4 K*, the D/S membership of both Q-side seam vertices, and every displayed outer turn. P4 tightness is graph-intrinsic; proposal, block, cut, and membership coordinates are representative-relative.


## Exclusions / nonclaims

Does not claim that both-bad P4 residue is realizable. Does not claim the forced P4 lies in H-D when a Q-side vertex lies in D. Even when both lie in S, does not infer an exact alternative deletion cover or lexicographic decrease without their literal positions in A and the needed outer turns. Does not rule out a different global splice in the listed irreducible cells. Does not use generic R435, balanced-pair, or anonymous P4 output.


## Proof

Write the natural seam order as (a,b,c,d). In the residual both (a,b,c) and (b,c,d) are bad. By R3 their complete reversals (c,b,a) and (d,c,b) are tight. These are exactly the two consecutive turns of K*=(d,c,b,a), proving K* is a literal tight Hamilton P4 with the required physical labels.

For CS, the original U rail contains the consecutive segment
(...,q_{j-4},q_{j-3},a,b,c,d,c_2,c_3,...),
with nonexistent terms omitted. Deleting (a,b,c,d) and inserting (d,c,b,a) preserves every vertex exactly once. The two internal inserted turns are certified by K*. On the left, there is no junction turn when j=2; one junction turn (q_0,d,c) when j=3; and exactly two, (q_{j-4},q_{j-3},d) and (q_{j-3},d,c), when j>=4. On the right there is none when s=1; one, (b,a,c_2), when s=2; and exactly two, (b,a,c_2) and (a,c_2,c_3), when s>=3. All turns farther from the splice remain turns of Q or K. The other proposal rail is unchanged, so its sole old uncertified turn is g. This proves completeness of the CS ledger and the hole counts.

For SC, the original V rail contains
(...,c_{s-3},c_{s-2},a,b,c,d,q_{i+3},q_{i+4},...).
The identical reverse substitution certifies its two internal turns. Its left junction contributes zero, one, or two turns according as s=1, s=2, or s>=3, exactly as displayed; its right junction contributes zero, one, or two according as i=m-2, i=m-3, or i<=m-4. Every other turn is inherited from K or Q, and U remains unchanged with sole old hole h. This proves the SC ledger.

A complete hole set of cardinality one or two is the asserted literal one-/two-hole proposal. In all other parameter cells the displayed substitution has at least the isolated old hole plus two explicitly named outer holes, so it is irreducible as a one-/two-hole output without certifying at least one of those exact outer turns. Finally, a vertex of D is absent from H-D, while membership of both Q-side vertices in S supplies no information about their locations or neighbors in A; hence the stated deletion-cover fence follows.

# R514 — Direct balanced pairs and mass-two floors

## Statement
Let H be a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample. Any two physically disjoint signed supports of opposite polarity form a graph-intrinsic balanced opposite-sign pair in the project signed-pair sense. Suppose such a pair has total support size four. Then there is a finite chosen certificate-retaining continuation yielding either a spanning two-cover of H or an ancestry-bearing balanced pair whose two supports are both singletons. If the initial support sizes are 1+3 or 3+1, apply R428 directly while preserving the singleton support. If they are 2+2, apply R427 to obtain either a spanning two-cover or a descendant pair with a singleton support; if the opposite support is already singleton we are at the floor, and otherwise apply R428. Any separately retained graph-intrinsic static configuration present at the pair birth remains valid historical/certificate data throughout the chosen continuation, but no old cover, sign witness, marker, or support is asserted to remain simultaneously current unless a cited descendant theorem says so.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample. A graph-intrinsic balanced opposite-sign pair is present with physically disjoint nonempty supports of total size four. Any additional static configuration mentioned for ancestry is already separately certified graph-intrinsically.

## Scope
Modern reconstructible replacement for the legacy Static-Core Transparent Pair Excursion wording. It isolates the exact mass-four descent actually used downstream and expresses persistence as certificate ancestry rather than as a legacy payment macro.

## Applicability
Use whenever a direct balanced pair of total support mass four is born. The only support-size profiles are 1+3, 2+2, and 3+1, and the displayed R427/R428 case split pays them to the both-singleton floor unless H is already two-covered.

## Persistence
Retain the original pair-birth certificate and the descendant certificates supplied by R427/R428. Separately certified graph-intrinsic static facts remain historical truth. The chosen singleton in R428 is preserved exactly as stated there; unrelated old current representatives and witnesses need not persist.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not claim the old Static-Core Transparent Pair Excursion proof has been historically recovered. Does not preserve simultaneous currentness of the birth frame. Does not make pair mass globally monotone across unrelated resets and does not close the both-singleton floor.

## Proof
Let the two nonempty disjoint supports have orders s,t with s+t=4. Opposite signed polarity is exactly the balanced-pair relation, so the given signed supports form a graph-intrinsic balanced opposite-sign pair. If {s,t}={1,3}, apply accepted R428 to the singleton/nontrivial pair. Its chosen certificate-retaining continuation either gives a spanning two-cover or reaches a balanced pair with both supports singleton, preserving the chosen singleton. If s=t=2, apply accepted R427 to either width-two support. Unless a spanning two-cover occurs, R427 returns a descendant balanced pair with a singleton support. If its other support is also singleton, stop. Otherwise the other support is nontrivial, so R428 applies and gives a spanning two-cover or the both-singleton floor. This exhausts all positive integer profiles with s+t=4. The continuation is certificate-retaining by R427/R428. Any separately certified graph-intrinsic static configuration remains true as historical data while representatives change; nothing here claims that its old selected states remain current. Thus the mass-four pair has exactly the stated modern floor continuation.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R514.md -->

# FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R515.md

<!-- BEGIN FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R515.md -->

# R515 — Trimer central-anchor interaction

## Statement
Let T=(a,b,c) and U=(p,q,r) be vertex-disjoint tight trimers in a Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament. Each trimer has its two natural terminal signed dimers: (a,b) is tail-signed by c and (b,c) is head-signed by a, while (p,q) is tail-signed by r and (q,r) is head-signed by p. Hence the crossed pairings Pi_1=((a,b),(q,r)) and Pi_2=((b,c),(p,q)) are two graph-intrinsic balanced opposite-sign pairs of total support mass four. Both pair births carry the same unordered pair of middle anchors {b,q}. If the two births are retained in sequence before unrelated reset, then applying R448 with fixed trimer T gives an explicit at-anchor growth/cycle/reversal interaction at b, and applying R448 with fixed trimer U gives the dual interaction at q. More generally, if a tight path is vertex-disjoint from a fixed tight trimer, every consecutive trimer window of the path gives the same two-middle-anchor construction with the fixed trimer; these are graph-intrinsic historical interaction certificates, not simultaneous paid descendants and not a closure theorem.

## Hypotheses
Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament. T and U are vertex-disjoint graph-intrinsic tight trimers. For the path version, every selected consecutive three-vertex window is a tight trimer and is disjoint from the fixed trimer.

## Scope
Modern reconstructible formulation of the legacy central-anchor interaction theorem. It removes obsolete remint/payment shorthand and states the exact crossed pair births and R448 local interaction certificate.

## Applicability
Use whenever two disjoint tight trimers, or a fixed trimer and a disjoint path window, need a role-preserving interaction at their middle vertices. The output is local historical interaction geometry, not automatic progress.

## Persistence
Retain both trimers, their middle vertices, the four natural terminal signed dimers, the two crossed balanced-pair birth certificates, and the two R448 at-anchor interaction certificates. Alternative later representatives need not coexist.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not claim the R448 growth output is fresh rather than source-trimer replay. Does not claim the two pair births are simultaneously paid, that pair mass descends, or that either interaction closes the conjecture.

## Proof
For T=(a,b,c), accepted R448 records the natural terminal signed dimers D_T^-=(a,b), tail-signed by c, and D_T^+=(b,c), head-signed by a; both contain the signed anchor b. For U=(p,q,r), the same theorem records D_U^-=(p,q), tail-signed by r, and D_U^+=(q,r), head-signed by p, both anchored at q. Because T and U are vertex-disjoint, D_T^- is physically disjoint from D_U^+ and their polarities are opposite, so by the project signed-pair definition they form a graph-intrinsic balanced opposite-sign pair Pi_1 of mass four. Likewise D_T^+ and D_U^- form Pi_2. Each birth therefore uses one terminal dimer of T and one terminal dimer of U, so both births have the same unordered middle-anchor pair {b,q}. Retain Pi_1 and Pi_2 before unrelated reset. From the T viewpoint, the earlier and later births each use one of T's terminal dimers and a partner support disjoint from T; R448 applies and gives its explicit at-anchor growth/cycle/reversal certificate at b. From the U viewpoint the same two births satisfy the dual hypotheses, so R448 gives the corresponding certificate at q. If K is a tight path disjoint from T, every consecutive three-vertex window of K is a tight trimer disjoint from T, so the identical argument applies independently to each window. Nothing asserts simultaneous current paid descendants or freshness of the returned growth branch.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R515.md -->

# R516 — Same-polarity terminal-sign no-P4 cell has exactly four alignment signatures

## Statement
Let X={a,b,c,y} be four distinct vertices in a Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament with (a,b,c) tight. Suppose the left terminal physical dimer {a,b} carries a y-sign of the same tail polarity as its natural C-sign, with arbitrary tested order, and {b,c} carries a y-sign of the same head polarity as its natural C-sign, again with arbitrary tested order. Equivalently, at least one of (a,b,y),(b,a,y) is tight and at least one of (y,b,c),(y,c,b) is tight. If X has no tight Hamilton P4, then the reverse contacts (b,a,y) and (y,c,b) are both tight. Define A=[(a,b,y) tight] and B=[(y,b,c) tight]. Then for each (A,B) there is exactly one no-P4 orientation of the twelve boundary-antisymmetry reversal pairs on X. Writing xyz for the tight ordered triple (x,y,z), complete representative sets are: 00={abc,bca,cab,yba,ayb,bay,acy,cya,yac,ycb,byc,cby}; 01={abc,acb,cab,yba,bya,bay,acy,cya,cay,ycb,byc,ybc}; 10={abc,bca,bac,aby,ayb,bay,yca,cya,yac,ycb,cyb,cby}; 11={abc,acb,bac,aby,bya,bay,yca,cya,cay,ycb,cyb,ybc}. Each displayed set contains exactly one orientation from every reversal pair and contains no tight Hamilton P4. No transitivity of the three local comparisons at a fixed middle vertex is asserted; in particular the 00 local tournaments are cyclic.

## Hypotheses
Strong Level-(1) boundary antisymmetry; a,b,c,y are distinct; (a,b,c) is tight; the two y-signs have the same polarities as the natural terminal signs but arbitrary tested dimer orders; X has no tight Hamilton P4.

## Scope
Correct reconstructible four-vertex orientation classification. Repairs the stale strict-order table in R280 while preserving its sound reverse-contact and four-alignment-cell content.

## Applicability
Use whenever a tight trimer and a fourth vertex enter the same-polarity/no-P4 terminal-sign branch. The exact 12-turn row is determined by the two alignment bits A,B.

## Persistence
All twelve tight-turn representatives, the two alignment bits, and the reverse contacts are graph-intrinsic on X.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert that every local three-way comparison at a fixed middle is transitive. Does not classify the perfect-matching-block quotient; use the corrected C262 revision for that. Does not rule out any of the four signatures.

## Proof
First force the contacts. If (b,a,y) is already the certified left same-polarity sign there is nothing to prove. Otherwise (a,b,y) is tight. If (b,a,y) were bad, R3 would make its reversal (y,a,b) tight, and together with (a,b,c) the order (y,a,b,c) would be a tight Hamilton P4, contradiction. Hence (b,a,y) is tight. Dually, if (y,c,b) is not already the certified right sign then (y,b,c) is tight; if (y,c,b) were bad, R3 would make (b,c,y) tight and (a,b,c,y) would be a tight P4. Thus both reverse contacts are forced. Now consider the twelve independent reversal pairs determined by choosing a middle vertex and an unordered pair of endpoints on X. For fixed bits A,B, the turns (a,b,c),(b,a,y),(y,c,b), the A-choice between (a,b,y) and (y,b,a), and the B-choice between (y,b,c) and (c,b,y) fix five of the twelve pairs. There remain seven binary choices. Check the 2^7=128 assignments against the exact no-P4 predicate: for every one of the 24 vertex orders (x0,x1,x2,x3), it is forbidden that both (x0,x1,x2) and (x1,x2,x3) are tight. Exactly one assignment survives for each A,B. Reading one representative from each reversal pair gives the four displayed 12-turn rows. Conversely, direct inspection of each displayed row verifies boundary antisymmetry pair-by-pair and verifies that none of the 24 Hamilton orders has both required consecutive turns. Hence the four rows are exhaustive and exact. In the 00 row, for example, at middle a the tight comparisons (c,a,b),(b,a,y),(y,a,c) form the cycle c>b>y>c, so no strict local order is claimed.

# R518 — Capture-coupling trimer amplifies to P4 or an explicit double-contact cell

## Statement
Let C=(a,b,c) be any tight trimer in a Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament and let y be any fourth vertex. Then either X={a,b,c,y} supports a tight Hamilton P4, or X is one of the exact four no-P4 alignment signatures of R516. More precisely, R3 supplies a y-sign on each terminal physical dimer {a,b} and {b,c}. Compare each with the corresponding natural terminal sign of C. If either y-sign has opposite polarity to the natural sign on that physical support, R263 yields a tight Hamilton P4 on X. Hence in the no-P4 branch both y-signs have the same terminal polarities as the natural C-signs; R516 then forces both reverse contacts (b,a,y) and (y,c,b) and determines one exact twelve-turn signature indexed by the two tested-order alignment bits. By R517, signatures 11,10,01 have vertex-uniform transitive opposite-edge matching-block quotients (with the stated block permutations), while signature 00 has the vertex-uniform cyclic quotient B_1>B_3>B_2>B_1. Thus the universal four-cell residue consists of three transitive quotient cells and one uniform cyclic cell; there is no quotient-inhomogeneous fourth cell.

## Hypotheses
Strong Level-(1) boundary antisymmetry; C=(a,b,c) is a graph-intrinsic tight trimer; y is distinct from a,b,c; accepted/provisional R263,R515,R516,R517.

## Scope
Corrected reconstructible universal four-cell theorem. Replaces R297's false R282 quotient sentence while retaining the sound P4-or-reverse-contact/signature interface.

## Applicability
Use whenever a tight trimer acquires any fourth vertex. A P4 is the opposite-polarity branch; otherwise retain the exact R516 signature and, if useful, its R517 matching-block quotient.

## Persistence
C,y,the natural terminal signs, the two y-signs and tested orders, reverse contacts, exact R516 signature, and R517 quotient type are graph-intrinsic on X.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert the four-set is current as one path-cover component. Does not attach capture ancestry. Does not rule out the cyclic 00 cell or claim any quotient type closes the conjecture.

## Proof
The tight trimer C has its two natural terminal signed dimers by R515. For the left terminal physical dimer {a,b}, boundary antisymmetry R3 on {a,b,y} with middle b supplies exactly one tight y-incidence orientation, hence one y-sign on that physical support; similarly R3 supplies a y-sign on {b,c}. If either new sign has polarity opposite to the corresponding natural C-sign, accepted R263 concatenates the two distinct sign witnesses on that same support and yields a tight Hamilton P4 on all four vertices. Therefore, if X has no tight P4, both y-signs necessarily have the same polarities as the natural terminal signs, though their tested physical-dimer orders may be aligned or reversed. These are exactly the hypotheses of R516. Hence both reverse contacts are tight and the complete Strong orientation is one of its four exact twelve-turn signatures 00,01,10,11. Applying R517 to that signature gives the corrected opposite-edge matching-block classification: 11,10,01 are vertex-uniform transitive after the stated block permutations, while 00 is vertex-uniform cyclic. This proves the complete alternative without using the false local-transitivity or quotient-inhomogeneity assertions of R280/R282/R297.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R518.md -->

# R519 — Universal common-anchor spoke-fan polarity theorem

## Statement
Let e be a vertex of a Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament and let X be a set of t>=3 distinct vertices disjoint from e. For every distinct x,y in X, boundary antisymmetry determines a unique tight e-middle trimer on {x,e,y}. Reading its terminal support incident with x gives a signed certificate on the physical spoke {e,x} with witness y, retaining the tested dimer order of that occurrence. Consequently every spoke {e,x} carries t-1 witness-indexed signed certificates. If t>=4, then among the t-1>=3 certificates on one physical spoke, at least two use the same one of the two possible tested dimer orders. Those two certificates are therefore legitimately comparable by R38 and give a graph-intrinsic same-support two-witness interaction on that tested oriented dimer. For t=3 no such interaction is forced: the two certificates may use opposite tested dimer orders, and the exact R516 doubly-misaligned 00 cell realizes this obstruction. Thus the tested-order-safe universal conclusion is complete witness coverage for t>=3 and an R38 interaction on every spoke for t>=4; no quantitative strict-versus-collision count follows without additional alignment.

## Hypotheses
Strong Level-(1) boundary antisymmetry; e is a vertex; X is a set of at least three distinct vertices disjoint from e. For the every-spoke R38 conclusion require |X|>=4.

## Scope
Reconstructible tested-order-safe common-anchor fan theorem. It corrects both the false R252 strict-count theorem and the overstrong t=3 R38 conclusion inherited by R308.

## Applicability
Use for common-anchor witness families. At any size t>=3 retain all witness-indexed certificates with their tested orders. When t>=4, pigeonhole tested order and invoke R38 on every spoke. At t=3 do not infer an R38 interaction without an explicit tested-order match.

## Persistence
The anchor, outer set, centered tight trimers, physical spoke supports, witness identities, and tested dimer orders are graph-intrinsic. For t>=4 the chosen same-tested-order witness pair and resulting R38 interaction are retained. No simultaneous currentization or payment descendant is asserted.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not force an R38 interaction on every spoke when t=3. Does not bound the number of opposite-polarity strict spokes. Does not infer a Hamilton P4 from fan size alone or transport independent witness ancestry.

## Proof
Fix x in X. For every y in X\\{x}, apply R3 to x,e,y with middle e. Exactly one of (x,e,y) and (y,e,x) is tight. Reading the terminal dimer incident with x gives a signed certificate on the physical support {e,x} witnessed by y; importantly, retain whether its tested oriented dimer is (x,e) or (e,x). Hence the spoke has t-1 distinct witness certificates. There are only two possible tested dimer orders. If t>=4, then t-1>=3, so two distinct witnesses y,z produce certificates with the same tested order. Those two are legitimate inputs to R38 on one oriented dimer; R38 gives the corresponding same-support two-witness interaction. Repeat independently for every x. For t=3 there are only two witness certificates, and no pigeonhole conclusion is available. This failure is real: in the exact R516 00 no-P4 signature, choose the common anchor b and outer set {a,c,y}. On each b-spoke the two outer-witness certificates occur in opposite tested dimer orders. If a same-tested-order R38 interaction were forced anyway, its opposite-polarity branch would contradict the exact no-P4 cell. Thus t=3 guarantees complete witness coverage but not a universal R38 interaction, while t>=4 guarantees one on every spoke. No parity comparison of polarity labels across differing tested orders is made.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R519.md -->

# R522 — Two no-P4 extensions of one tight trimer force a P5

## Statement
Let C=(a,b,c) be a tight trimer in a Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament, and let y,z be distinct vertices outside C. Suppose neither four-set C union {y} nor C union {z} supports a tight Hamilton P4. Apply the exact R516 no-P4 classification to the two fourth-vertex cells and let sigma_y,sigma_z in {00,01,10,11} be their alignment signatures. Then sigma_y=sigma_z. Indeed the shared core orientation at middle a distinguishes alignment bit A: signatures 00,01 contain (c,a,b), while 10,11 contain (b,a,c); the shared core orientation at middle c distinguishes B: signatures 00,10 contain (b,c,a), while 01,11 contain (a,c,b). Since these core turns are graph-intrinsic, both bits agree. For each common signature, one comparison of y and z now yields a literal Hamilton P5: in signatures 00 and 10, whichever of (y,a,z),(z,a,y) is tight gives respectively (c,y,a,z,b) or (c,z,a,y,b); in signature 01, whichever of (y,c,z),(z,c,y) is tight gives (b,y,c,z,a) or (b,z,c,y,a); in signature 11, whichever of (y,b,z),(z,b,y) is tight gives (c,y,b,z,a) or (c,z,b,y,a). Therefore two distinct no-P4 extensions of one tight trimer always amplify to a graph-intrinsic tight Hamilton P5 on their five-vertex union.

## Hypotheses
Strong Level-(1) boundary antisymmetry; C=(a,b,c) is tight; y,z are distinct and outside C; neither C union {y} nor C union {z} has a tight Hamilton P4; accepted R516.

## Scope
Order-free five-vertex synchronization theorem reconstructed from the valid core of rejected R477/P492. It uses the corrected exact four-signature table rather than the false legacy strict-order representation.

## Applicability
Use whenever the same tight trimer is tested against two distinct fourth vertices and both tests land in the no-P4 branch. The output is an explicit P5 on the five role-labelled vertices.

## Persistence
C,y,z, the common R516 signature, the chosen y/z comparison at the specified middle, and the resulting literal P5 are graph-intrinsic.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not currentize the P5 as a component of an unrelated path cover. Does not assert its endpoint chord is tight or that the P5 alone closes the conjecture. Does not allow mixed no-P4 signatures on the shared core.

## Proof
Apply R516 to C with y and with z. For a generic fourth vertex w, the exact R516 rows show that the orientation of the core triple with middle a is (c,a,b) in signatures 00 and 01 and (b,a,c) in signatures 10 and 11. Thus the graph-intrinsic orientation of the shared core {a,b,c} at middle a determines A, so A_y=A_z. Likewise the core orientation at middle c is (b,c,a) in signatures 00 and 10 and (a,c,b) in signatures 01 and 11, so B_y=B_z. Hence sigma_y=sigma_z. Now use R3 on the distinct triple {y,z,m} at the indicated middle m. If the common signature is 00, the row contains (c,y,a) and (a,y,b) after the substitution w=y, and likewise for z; if (y,a,z) is tight then the three turns (c,y,a),(y,a,z),(a,z,b) certify the path (c,y,a,z,b), while the reverse comparison gives (c,z,a,y,b). The same construction works in signature 10 because its row also contains (c,w,a) and (a,w,b). In signature 01, the row contains (b,w,c) and (c,w,a); compare y,z at middle c to obtain (b,y,c,z,a) or its y/z swap. In signature 11, the row contains (c,w,b) and (b,w,a); compare y,z at middle b to obtain (c,y,b,z,a) or its swap. Thus every possible common signature yields a literal tight P5 on exactly the five vertices.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R522.md -->

# FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R523.md

<!-- BEGIN FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R523.md -->

# R523 — Same-support sign interaction

## Statement
Let D=(a,b) be a fixed tested oriented physical dimer in a Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament, and let x,y be distinct witnesses outside {a,b}. A head certificate on D with witness w means the exact ordered turn (w,a,b) is tight; a tail certificate on D with witness w means the exact ordered turn (a,b,w) is tight. Then two witness-indexed certificates on this same tested orientation have the following exhaustive interaction. (HH) If (x,a,b) and (y,a,b) are tight, they are exactly the same-support two-head extension collision packet on D with distinct witnesses x,y. (TT) If (a,b,x) and (a,b,y) are tight, they are exactly the same-support two-tail extension collision packet on D. (HT) If (x,a,b) and (a,b,y) are tight, then (x,a,b,y) is a literal vertex-simple tight P4. (TH) If (y,a,b) and (a,b,x) are tight, then (y,a,b,x) is a literal vertex-simple tight P4. Thus opposite-polarity certificates on one tested oriented dimer have an explicit strict two-ended realization, while same-polarity certificates are the literal two-extension collision packet. Tested order is part of the datum: a certificate tested on (a,b) and one tested on the reverse dimer (b,a) are not licensed as a same-oriented-support interaction merely because they share the unordered physical support {a,b}. To compare reverse-tested certificates, first treat (b,a) as its own tested oriented dimer and apply this theorem there. No cyclic permutation or witness-order rearrangement of a certified turn is licensed.

## Hypotheses
a,b,x,y are distinct as required by the displayed certificates; D=(a,b) is the common tested oriented dimer; the two witnesses are distinct.

## Scope
Pure order-free unpacking of the signed-dimer convention. This is the modern reconstructible replacement for the legacy-compressed R38 interface and makes tested-order retention explicit.

## Applicability
Use whenever two signed certificates share one tested oriented dimer. Same polarity gives the named two-extension collision packet; opposite polarity gives the explicit P4. Before invoking this theorem, verify that the tested dimer order is literally the same in both certificates.

## Persistence
The tested oriented dimer, witness identities, exact ordered certificate turns, collision packet, and any resulting P4 are graph-intrinsic.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not compare certificates tested on opposite orientations of the same unordered dimer. Does not license cyclic rereading of tight turns. Does not claim a same-polarity collision or the resulting P4 by itself closes the conjecture.

## Proof
Fix D=(a,b). By definition, a head certificate witnessed by w is the tight turn (w,a,b), while a tail certificate witnessed by w is the tight turn (a,b,w), with this exact tested order retained. If x and y have the same polarity, the two displayed tight extensions with distinct witnesses are precisely the project same-support two-extension collision packet; no further inference is needed. If x is head and y tail, then the consecutive turns (x,a,b) and (a,b,y) are tight, so the vertex sequence (x,a,b,y) is a tight P4. If y is head and x tail, the same argument gives (y,a,b,x). These exhaust the two polarities for two certificates on the fixed tested orientation. A certificate on (b,a) is different ordered data; nothing in the preceding concatenations allows replacing (a,b) by (b,a) or cyclically permuting a certified turn. Hence opposite tested orders must be kept separate unless an independent theorem relates them.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R523.md -->

# FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R524.md

<!-- BEGIN FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R524.md -->

# R524 — Two-slot insertion theorem for reversal-symmetric prepend/append ternary systems

## Statement
Let V be a finite set and E a relation on ordered triples of distinct vertices. Assume (PA) for every distinct u,v,w, at least one of (u,v,w) and (w,u,v) lies in E, and (RS) reversal symmetry: (u,v,w) is in E if and only if (w,v,u) is in E. Call a vertex sequence tight when every consecutive ordered triple lies in E. Then for every tight path P=(v_0,...,v_{k-1}) and every x outside P, at least two of the k+1 literal insertion positions of x in P produce a tight path. Consequently every n-vertex system satisfying (PA)+(RS) has at least 2^(n-1) spanning tight paths. This bound is sharp: fix a total order on V and declare (a,b,c) tight exactly when b is not the maximum of {a,b,c}; then the spanning tight paths are exactly the permutations decreasing to the minimum and then increasing, hence there are exactly 2^(n-1).

## Hypotheses
Finite ordered-triple relation; distinct vertices in each tested triple; prepend/append condition (PA); reversal symmetry (RS).

## Scope
Order-free theorem for general ternary path systems. It is deliberately outside the antisymmetric Strong Level-(1) regime and serves as the exact insertion-model comparison theorem.

## Applicability
Use whenever a quotient, residual, or auxiliary ternary relation satisfies both prepend/append completeness and reversal symmetry. It gives literal insertion, not merely rerouting, and an exponential Hamilton-path count.

## Persistence
The two insertion slots are literal positions in the retained ordered path P. The Hamilton-path count is graph/relation intrinsic.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Without reversal symmetry, (PA) alone does not guarantee literal insertion into a fixed tight path; first/last-position never conditions can block two adjacent insertion slots. This theorem does not apply to boundary-antisymmetric Strong Level-(1) turns.

## Proof
Let P=(v_0,...,v_{k-1}) and x notin V(P). For each adjacent pair e_i=(v_i,v_{i+1}), consider the three possible middle vertices on the 3-set {x,v_i,v_{i+1}}. By (RS), for a fixed middle the two reverse orders have the same status. Put q_y=1 when the two orders with middle y are tight. Applying (PA) to the three cyclic choices gives q_x OR q_{v_i}, q_{v_i} OR q_{v_{i+1}}, and q_{v_{i+1}} OR q_x. Hence at most one q is zero. Thus e_i can forbid at most one insertion position: if v_i is the unique forbidden middle it blocks insertion immediately before v_i; if x is forbidden it blocks insertion between v_i and v_{i+1}; if v_{i+1} is forbidden it blocks insertion immediately after v_{i+1}; if no middle is forbidden it blocks none. Every new triple created by inserting x at a slot is associated with exactly one adjacent pair of P in this way, while all old triples not involving x remain unchanged. Therefore a bad insertion slot must be blocked by at least one adjacent pair. There are only k-1 adjacent pairs, each blocking at most one slot, but there are k+1 insertion slots, so at least two are good. For the count, fix x. Every spanning tight path of V minus {x} has at least two distinct insertions of x. Distinct parent paths and slots give distinct children because deleting x recovers both the parent order and the slot. Therefore N(V)>=2N(V minus {x}); starting from N of a one-vertex system equal to 1 gives N(V)>=2^(n-1). For sharpness, linearly order V and declare (a,b,c) tight iff b is not the largest of the three. This satisfies (PA)+(RS). A spanning permutation is tight iff it has no interior local maximum. Such a permutation is uniquely obtained by choosing which vertices other than the minimum lie to its left, placing the chosen set in decreasing order and the complement in increasing order. Thus exactly 2^(n-1) spanning tight paths occur.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R524.md -->
