# FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R526.md

<!-- BEGIN FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R526.md -->

# R526 — Signed-support actualization and aligned payment

## Statement
Let P be a graph-intrinsic signed tight support in a Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament, with exact sign witness w, and let M=(m_0,...,m_r), r>=1, be a tight marker path disjoint from V(P) union {w}. Then M admits an explicit opposite-polarity actualization against P with the marker orientation, witness, and resulting signed anchor retained. If P is head-signed by w, test the terminal marker turn (m_{r-1},m_r,w). If it is tight, M itself is tail-signed by w with signed tail anchor m_r. If it is bad, R3 gives (w,m_r,m_{r-1}) tight, so the short support (w,m_r) is tail-signed by witness m_{r-1}, again with signed tail anchor m_r. The tail-signed case is the exact head/tail dual at m_0. Thus actualization never means free truncation: it is certified by one displayed terminal marker test and produces a physically disjoint opposite-polarity support, hence a balanced-pair birth with P. The marker orientation used for this test is part of the certificate and need not have been the orientation selected in an earlier cover.

In the aligned dimer payment scope, suppose H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample and P has order two. The actualized opposite support together with P is then a balanced pair with a width-two support. Accepted R427 therefore gives a finite chosen certificate-retaining continuation yielding either a spanning two-cover or a descendant balanced pair with a singleton support. Retain separately the original sign orientation and witness, marker and its chosen orientation, terminal actualization test, the actualized opposite support, the pair-birth event, each refund certificate supplied by the width-two descent, and the resulting singleton descendant. This is the modern explicit form of signed-support actualization and aligned payment.

## Hypotheses
Local actualization clause: Strong Level-(1); P is a signed tight support with named witness w; M is a nontrivial tight marker disjoint from both P and w. Payment clause: additionally H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample and P has order two.

## Scope
Equal-strength reconstructible replacement for legacy R35. The local actualization clause is purely Strong Level-(1) and does not use minimality. The payment conclusion is only the historical aligned dimer scope and uses smallest-counterexample width-two descent. Head/tail duals and marker orientation are explicit; no support is truncated for free.

## Applicability
Use whenever a signed support has a disjoint marker. For capture-oriented uses, orient a dimer marker so the desired endpoint occupies the actualization endpoint. When the original signed support is a dimer in a smallest counterexample, follow the resulting balanced-pair birth through R427 to obtain a spanning two-cover or singleton-width descendant.

## Persistence
Retain the exact original signed support orientation and witness, marker support and chosen marker orientation, terminal marker test, actualization outcome and signed anchor, balanced-pair birth, and any later R427 refund/descent certificates. The marker or pair supports need not remain current in the original deletion representative after actualization/payment.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not claim a marker orientation was previously selected merely because it is chosen for actualization. Does not permit free endpoint truncation. Does not claim both marker orientations or head/tail payment descendants coexist. Does not assert payment for a non-dimer original support by this theorem. Does not close a resulting singleton floor by itself.

## Proof
Assume first that P is head-signed by w and orient the disjoint tight marker as M=(m_0,...,m_r), r>=1. Test the ordered turn (m_{r-1},m_r,w). If it is tight, then M is tail-signed by witness w: its terminal sign turn is exactly (m_{r-1},m_r,w), and the signed tail anchor is m_r. Since M is disjoint from P, P and M are disjoint opposite-polarity signed supports. If the tested turn is bad, boundary antisymmetry R3 gives its complete reversal (w,m_r,m_{r-1}) tight. Hence the two-vertex support Q=(w,m_r) is tail-signed by witness m_{r-1}, again with signed tail anchor m_r. Because w and M are disjoint from P, Q is disjoint from P. Thus in either branch the displayed marker test creates a graph-intrinsic opposite-polarity support Q disjoint from P, and therefore a balanced-pair birth. The tail-signed case is dual: test (w,m_0,m_1). If tight, M is head-signed by w with head anchor m_0; if bad, R3 gives (m_1,m_0,w) tight, so (m_0,w) is head-signed by witness m_1. This proves the local actualization clause and records exactly which physical marker endpoint is the new signed anchor. Now assume H is a hypothetical smallest counterexample and P is a dimer. The balanced pair just constructed has at least one support of order two, namely P. Accepted fully reconstructible R427 applies and yields, along a finite chosen certificate-retaining continuation, either a spanning two-cover or a descendant balanced pair with a singleton support. R427's refund/rebirth ledger is retained together with the already graph-intrinsic actualization certificate, so the sign orientation, witness, marker orientation, actualization event, paid descendant, and singleton are separate historical ledger entries exactly as claimed. No currentness of the original marker after the later descent is asserted.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R526.md -->

# FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R527.md

<!-- BEGIN FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R527.md -->

# R527 — Same-frame crossing, capture, concentration, and refund

## Statement
Let H be a Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament, let K be a retained vertex-simple tight carrier path, and let S be a graph-intrinsic signed support with V(S) contained in V(K) and exact sign witness w outside V(S). Put C=V(K)\V(S) and E=V(H)\V(K). Let T=U sqcup V be one exact two-cover of H-V(S). A selected carrier/exterior crossing means a selected adjacent state xy of T with one endpoint in C and the other in E.

(Capture/refund branch.) If some selected carrier/exterior crossing xy avoids w, then the physical dimer {x,y} is disjoint from S union {w} and may be used as the actualizing marker in the same deletion frame. Either physical endpoint of {x,y} may be designated as the captured signed anchor by choosing the corresponding marker orientation before actualization. Applying R526 to S and this oriented dimer marker produces an explicit opposite-polarity signed support and a balanced-pair birth while retaining S, its tested sign orientation and witness w, the original selected physical crossing, the chosen marker orientation, the captured endpoint, and the terminal actualization test as historical certificate data. If S is a dimer and H is additionally a hypothetical smallest counterexample, the aligned payment clause of R526 gives a finite certificate-retaining continuation to either a spanning two-cover or singleton width. Thus the old aligned-refund ancestry is retained explicitly.

(Concentration branch.) Suppose instead that every selected carrier/exterior crossing of T meets w. Delete w from the two ordered rails of T and split at w. The resulting path forest has at most three nonempty components: the rail not containing w remains one component, while the rail containing w splits into at most two. Every surviving component is cut-pure with respect to C|E. Indeed, if one surviving component contained both a C-vertex and an E-vertex, some adjacent state of that component would cross C|E; that state was already a selected state of T and does not contain w, contradicting the hypothesis that every selected crossing meets w. Hence deleting w leaves a literal path cover of H-(V(S) union {w}) by at most three C/E-pure path components. This is the exact same-frame concentration bound.

The two branches are local to this exact support-deletion representative. The selected crossing is current only in T. Capture, balanced-pair birth, and any paid descendant are later historical/certificate data. Reorienting the two-vertex marker for actualization does not assert that the reversed marker orientation was selected in T.

## Hypotheses
Strong Level-(1); K is a retained tight carrier; S is a signed support contained in K with witness w outside S; T is an exact two-cover of H-V(S). For the paid singleton continuation in the capture branch, additionally H is a hypothetical smallest counterexample and S has order two.

## Scope
Full-contract reconstructible resurrection of legacy R36/R33. It preserves both historical alternatives: same-frame capture with aligned refund ancestry, and witness concentration. The concentration constant is made explicit as three and follows directly from deleting one vertex from an exact two-cover. The local capture/concentration theorem does not require smallest-counterexample minimality; only the optional aligned dimer payment continuation does.

## Applicability
Use when a signed support and selected carrier/exterior crossing genuinely coexist in one exact support-deletion two-cover. If a selected crossing avoids the sign witness, capture either physical crossing endpoint in that same frame and retain refund ancestry. If all selected crossings hit the witness, use the explicit at-most-three cut-pure-component concentration certificate after deleting the witness.

## Persistence
Retain the original exact deletion cover T, partition C|E, signed support S with tested orientation and witness, and in the capture branch the exact selected crossing, chosen actualization orientation, captured endpoint, R526 actualization/birth certificate and any later refund certificates. In the concentration branch retain T, w, and the at-most-three cut-pure path components of T-w. No later descendant is asserted to preserve the original selected crossing as current.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Concentration is an exact-frame structural alternative, not a graph-level obstruction. Capture is not permanent protection. Reorienting the dimer marker for actualization does not reverse a selected state in T. The theorem does not assert the capture and concentration branches coexist. For a non-dimer S it records actualization/capture ancestry but does not invoke the dimer-to-singleton payment clause.

## Proof
Let T=U sqcup V be the exact support-deletion two-cover. First suppose T selects a carrier/exterior state xy with w not in {x,y}. Because T lies in H-V(S), the marker {x,y} is disjoint from S, and by assumption it is also disjoint from w. A two-vertex path is tight in either orientation. Choose the marker order so that the desired endpoint is the actualization endpoint appropriate to the polarity of S. Apply accepted reconstructible R526. Its local actualization clause produces an opposite-polarity signed support with that chosen marker endpoint as the signed anchor, while retaining the marker order and terminal test. Together with S this is a graph-intrinsic balanced-pair birth. The selected state xy remains a fact about the original T-frame; the chosen marker order is an actualization choice and need not equal its selected direction. If S has order two in a hypothetical smallest counterexample, R526's payment clause further supplies the claimed aligned paid continuation and refund ancestry. Now suppose every selected C|E crossing of T contains w. Since w lies outside S, w is a vertex of H-V(S) and occurs exactly once in the path forest T. Delete w from its rail. A vertex deletion from one directed path leaves zero, one, or two path pieces, while the other T-rail is unchanged, so T-w has at most three nonempty path components. Assume one such component is not C/E-pure. Along its ordered vertex sequence, pass from a vertex in C to a vertex in E or conversely; at the first color change there is an adjacent selected state ab crossing C|E. This adjacency survived deletion of w, so neither endpoint is w. But ab was already a selected carrier/exterior crossing of T, contradicting the assumption that every such crossing meets w. Hence every component of T-w lies wholly in C or wholly in E. Therefore T-w is a path cover by at most three cut-pure components, proving the concentration branch and the full theorem.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R527.md -->

# FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R534.md

<!-- BEGIN FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R534.md -->

# R534 — Transitive four-cell P5-free fifth vertex has alternating full matching gates

## Statement
Let X be a transitive no-P4 Strong Level-(1) four-cell. Write its three opposite-edge perfect matchings as M_R>M_S>M_L so that for distinct u,v,w in X, uvw is tight iff M(uv)>M(vw). Let d be a fifth vertex such that X union {d} has no tight Hamilton P5. Suppose an M_L-edge {t,l} is fully outgoing from d, meaning dtl and dlt are tight, and an M_R-edge {t,r} is fully incoming to d, meaning trd and rtd are tight. Let s be the fourth vertex of X. Then among the two M_S-edges {t,s} and {l,r}, exactly one is fully outgoing from d and the other is fully incoming to d. Equivalently, with A=[dts], B=[dst], C=[drl], D=[dlr], one has A=B, C=D, and A is not equal to C. In particular every P5-free fifth vertex over a transitive four-cell has a full gate in each matching class, with the middle-class gate orientation opposite on its two edges.

## Hypotheses
Strong Level-(1) boundary antisymmetry; X is a transitive matching-height no-P4 four-cell; X union {d} is P5-free; one fully outgoing M_L gate and one fully incoming M_R gate sharing t are fixed.

## Scope
Pure five-vertex local theorem; no smallest-counterexample or deletion hypothesis.

## Applicability
Use when a P5-free fifth vertex is trapped between bottom and top matching gates. It supplies the previously missing M_S full gate and allows a gate to be chosen transverse to any prescribed 2+2 matching partition of X.

## Persistence
All vertices, matching classes, and certified ordered gate turns are graph-intrinsic on X union {d}.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert which M_S edge is outgoing without the named M_L/M_R gate choices. Does not itself produce a P5 or a cover; the conclusion is exactly the alternating full-gate structure.

## Proof
Write M_R={{t,r},{l,s}}, M_S={{t,s},{l,r}}, M_L={{t,l},{r,s}}. The matching-height rule makes trl,lrs,tsr,rts,lst,stl,slr,rlt tight. Put A=[dts], B=[dst], C=[drl], D=[dlr]. We use only P5-freeness and R3.\n\nA implies B. Suppose A holds and B fails, so tsd is tight. If sdl were tight then (r,t,s,d,l) would be a P5, since rts is tight; hence lds is tight. If rld were tight then (t,r,l,d,s) would be a P5, since trl and lds are tight; hence D=dlr is tight. If tdl were tight then (t,d,l,r,s) would be a P5, since D and lrs are tight; hence ldt is tight. But then (l,d,t,s,r) is a P5 using ldt, A=dts, and tsr, contradiction. Thus A implies B.\n\nB implies A. Suppose B holds and A fails, so std is tight. If tdr were tight then (l,s,t,d,r) would be a P5 using lst and std; hence rdt is tight. If lrd were tight then (s,l,r,d,t) would be a P5 using slr and rdt; hence C=drl is tight. If sdr were tight then (s,d,r,l,t) would be a P5 using C and rlt; hence rds is tight. But then (r,d,s,t,l) is a P5 using rds, B=dst, and stl, contradiction. Hence A=B.\n\nC implies D. Suppose C holds and D fails, so rld is tight. If sdr were tight then (s,d,r,l,t) would be a P5 using C and rlt; hence rds is tight. If dst were tight then (r,d,s,t,l) would be a P5 using rds and stl; hence tsd is tight. If sdl were tight then (r,t,s,d,l) would be a P5 using rts and tsd; hence lds is tight. But then (t,r,l,d,s) is a P5 using trl, rld, and lds, contradiction. Thus C implies D.\n\nD implies C. Suppose D holds and C fails, so lrd is tight. If tdl were tight then (t,d,l,r,s) would be a P5 using D and lrs; hence ldt is tight. If dts were tight then (l,d,t,s,r) would be a P5 using ldt and tsr; hence std is tight. If tdr were tight then (l,s,t,d,r) would be a P5 using lst and std; hence rdt is tight. But then (s,l,r,d,t) is a P5 using slr, lrd, and rdt, contradiction. Hence C=D.\n\nIt remains to show the two full M_S gates have opposite polarities. If A=C=0, then std and lrd are tight. P5-freeness of (l,s,t,d,r) forces tdr bad and hence rdt tight; then (s,l,r,d,t) is a P5, contradiction. If A=C=1, then B=D=1 by the equalities. P5-freeness of (r,d,s,t,l) forces rds bad and hence sdr tight; then (s,d,r,l,t) is a P5 using C and rlt, contradiction. Therefore A is not equal to C. Since A=B and C=D, exactly one M_S edge is fully outgoing from d and the complementary M_S edge is fully incoming. This proves the conclusion of R534 without using its extra named M_L/M_R gate hypotheses, so in particular the broader final clause is justified.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R534.md -->

# FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R535.md

<!-- BEGIN FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R535.md -->

# R535 — Four-marker fragmentation identity and high-interleaving two-path normal form

## Statement
Let F=R sqcup S be a spanning two-path forest on W=X sqcup Y with |X|=4. Put p=e_F(X) and q=e_F(X,Y). For x in X let B_x=Y union {x}, let d_Y(x) be the number of selected F-adjacencies from x to Y, and let c_x=c(F[B_x]). Then c_x=p+q-d_Y(x)-1 for every x, and therefore sum_x c_x=4p+3q-4. If X supports no selected Hamilton P4 inside F, then p<=2. If additionally c_x>=4 for every x, then only (p,q)=(2,4),(1,6),(0,7),(0,8) are possible. Up to swapping and reversing the two rails and contracting each maximal Y-block to Y, the surviving forest words are exactly: for (2,4), Y | YXXYXXY and YXXY | YXXY; for (1,6), Y | YXXYXYXY, Y | YXYXXYXY, YXXY | YXYXY, YXXYXY | YXY; for (0,7), XY | YXYXYXY, XYXY | YXYXY, XYXYXY | YXY, XYXYXYXY | Y; for (0,8), Y | YXYXYXYXY, YXY | YXYXYXY, YXYXY | YXYXY. The corresponding multisets {c_x} are respectively {4,4,4,4}, {5,5,4,4}, {5,4,4,4}, and {5,5,5,5}.

## Hypotheses
F is a spanning forest with exactly two path components; X has four vertices. For p<=2 assume no rail contains all four X vertices consecutively as an X-only P4. For the high-interleaving classification assume c(F[Y union {x}])>=4 for all x.

## Scope
Pure path-forest combinatorics. No Strong orientation axiom is used except in applications to justify p<=2 from a no-P4 X-cell.

## Applicability
Use in R24-style four-marker deletion fibers or any two-path recompletion problem with four distinguished vertices. The pointwise formula is stronger than the summed 4p+3q bound and reduces the high-fragmentation branch to thirteen coarse rail words.

## Persistence
The selected forest F, X/Y partition, degrees, fragment counts, and contracted rail words are literal in the chosen representative.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
The thirteen words classify only support/interleaving shape after maximal Y-block contraction; they do not encode turn orientations inside or across blocks. Matching-height information on X cannot eliminate a word merely from its support pattern when no XXX turn occurs.

## Proof
Let |W|=n. Since F is a spanning forest with exactly two path components, e(F)=n-2. Fix x in X and put A_x=X-{x}, B_x=Y union {x}. Because F[B_x] is a forest,
c_x=|B_x|-e_F(B_x).
Now |B_x|=n-3, while partitioning the selected edges gives e_F(B_x)=e(F)-e_F(A_x)-delta_F(A_x). Hence
c_x=(n-3)-(n-2-e_F(A_x)-delta_F(A_x))=e_F(A_x)+delta_F(A_x)-1.
Write d_X(x) and d_Y(x) for the selected F-degrees of x into X and Y. Since p=e_F(X), e_F(A_x)=p-d_X(x). Also delta_F(A_x) counts all X-Y edges except those incident with x, together with each X-X edge from x to A_x, so delta_F(A_x)=q-d_Y(x)+d_X(x). Therefore c_x=p+q-d_Y(x)-1.
Summing and using sum_x d_Y(x)=q gives sum_x c_x=4p+3q-4.

If p>=3, the graph F[X] is a forest on four vertices with at least three edges, hence is a tree. Because F itself has maximum degree two, F[X] is a four-vertex path. Its four X vertices occur consecutively on one F-rail and form a selected X-only P4. Thus in a no-P4 X application p<=2.

Assume now every c_x>=4. Then 4p+3q-4=sum c_x>=16, so 4p+3q>=20. The total selected degree at X is 2p+q<=8. With p<=2, the integer solutions are exactly (2,4),(1,6),(0,7),(0,8).

For (2,4), equality holds in the degree budget: every X-vertex has selected degree two. The pointwise formula c_x=5-d_Y(x)>=4 gives d_Y(x)<=1, while sum d_Y=4, so every d_Y(x)=1 and therefore every d_X(x)=1. Hence F[X] is a perfect matching and maximal Y-block contraction yields exactly the two path multisets Y | YXXYXXY and YXXY | YXXY. Every c_x=4.

For (1,6), again 2p+q=8, so every X-vertex has degree two. The two endpoints of the unique XX edge have d_X=1 and hence d_Y=1; the other two have d_X=0 and d_Y=2. Thus the c_x multiset is {5,5,4,4}. Contracting maximal Y-blocks and placing the unique XX pair among four X symbols in two paths with Y between all other consecutive X occurrences yields, up to rail swap/reversal, exactly Y | YXXYXYXY; Y | YXYXXYXY; YXXY | YXYXY; YXXYXY | YXY.

For (0,7), sum_X deg=7. Since every X-degree is at most two and no XX edges exist, exactly three X-vertices have degree two and one has degree one. Therefore {c_x}={4,4,4,5}. The two rails alternate X,Y after Y-block contraction and exactly one forest endpoint is X. According to whether the rail containing that X endpoint contains 1,2,3,4 X vertices, the four words are XY | YXYXYXY; XYXY | YXYXY; XYXYXY | YXY; XYXYXYXY | Y.

For (0,8), every X-vertex has degree two and both forest endpoints lie in Y. Both rails therefore begin and end in Y and alternate. Distributing four X vertices as 0+4,1+3,2+2 gives exactly Y | YXYXYXYXY; YXY | YXYXYXY; YXYXY | YXYXY. Here c_x=5 for every x. This exhausts the high branch.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R535.md -->

# R536 — Middle-gate endpoint exposure and two-witness inward star propagation

## Statement
Let X be a transitive no-P4 four-cell with matching order M_R>M_S>M_L, and let d be a fifth vertex such that X union {d} is P5-free. Let e={a,b} be the fully outgoing M_S-edge supplied by R534, and let e'={c,d'} be the complementary M_S-edge. After naming the two M_L edges as {a,c} and {b,d'}, the paths (d,a,b,d') and (d,b,a,c) are tight. Dually, if f is the fully incoming M_S-edge and f' its complementary M_S-edge, then for each x in f' there is a Hamilton P4 on {d} union (X-{x}) ending at d. For the inward-star specialization, additionally let H have pc(H)>2 and V(H)=X disjoint union V(Q), where Q=(q_0,...,q_m) is tight with m>=3, X+q_0 is P5-free, and q_1 q_0 y is tight for every y in X. Apply the first conclusion with d=q_0 and let L be the complementary M_S-edge to the outgoing q_0 gate. For each x in L the corresponding q_0-starting P4 extends to a tight prefix P5 by prepending q_1; hence H[V(Q[2,m]) union {x}] is non-Hamiltonian, so x q_2 q_3 is bad and q_3 q_2 x is tight. Thus the endpoint four-witness star propagates two positions inward as a two-witness star on L. The exact right-end dual holds under the corresponding right endpoint star.

## Hypotheses
First paragraph: Strong Level-(1) boundary antisymmetry; X is transitive matching-height; X union {d} is P5-free; R534. Inward-star paragraph: additionally H is finite with pc(H)>2, V(H)=X disjoint union V(Q), Q=(q_0,...,q_m) is tight with m>=3, and the displayed endpoint reverse star holds.

## Scope
Pure five-vertex endpoint exposure followed by an explicit two-cover specialization; no undefined historical R24 frame is required.

## Applicability
Use to replace the false assumption that a full four-witness star automatically propagates with a precise guaranteed two-witness propagation on a matching edge.

## Persistence
The exposed P4 orders, omitted M_S-edge, prefix P5s, non-Hamilton suffix augmentations, and resulting q_3 q_2 witness turns are all graph-intrinsic certificates in the named frame.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not propagate all four witnesses. Does not assert that the two-witness star can be iterated without additional same-order seam data. Does not assert favorable endpoint orientation for arbitrary R146 P5s.

## Proof
Let the outgoing M_S edge be e={a,b}, with complementary M_S edge e'={c,d'}. Relabel inside the two M_S edges so that the M_L edges are {a,c} and {b,d'}. Since e is fully outgoing from d, both dab and dba are tight. Because M(ab)=M_S>M(bd')=M_L, the X-only turn abd' is tight. Hence (d,a,b,d') is a tight P4, omitting c. Likewise M(ba)=M_S>M(ac)=M_L, so bac is tight and (d,b,a,c) is a tight P4, omitting d'. This proves the two d-initial exposures. The terminal version is dual: if f={a,b} is fully incoming, then abd and bad are tight; orient the preceding X turn through the appropriate M_R>M_S descent to obtain two P4s ending at d, one for each omitted vertex of the complementary M_S edge.

Now specialize to the explicit second-paragraph frame and d=q_0. Let L be the complementary M_S edge to the outgoing q_0 M_S gate. For x in L, choose the displayed q_0-starting P4 K_x=(q_0,u,v,w) on {q_0} union (X-{x}). Global longestness of Q gives q_1 q_0 y tight for every y in X, in particular q_1 q_0 u. Therefore (q_1,q_0,u,v,w) is a tight P5 spanning {q_0,q_1} union (X-{x}). If the complementary vertex set (q_2,...,q_m) union {x} had a Hamilton path, these two disjoint paths would form a spanning two-cover of H, contradiction. Hence (q_2,...,q_m) union {x} is non-Hamiltonian. Since (q_2,...,q_m) is itself a tight path, the literal prepend candidate (x,q_2,q_3,...,q_m) must fail at its only new turn x q_2 q_3. Thus x q_2 q_3 is bad; boundary antisymmetry gives q_3 q_2 x tight. This holds for both x in L. The right-end statement follows by complete reversal of the roles and using y q_m q_{m-1} tight for every y in X.

# R537 — Two-witness no-P4 star renormalizes to a transitive matching-height cell

## Statement
Let A,B,c,d be four distinct vertices in a Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament. Suppose ABc and ABd are tight. If the four-set Z={A,B,c,d} has no tight Hamilton P4, then BAc and BAd are also tight, and cdA,dcA,cdB,dcB are all tight. Moreover there are exactly two possible no-P4 completions of the twelve reversal pairs on Z. In both completions Z is a transitive matching-height four-cell whose top opposite-edge matching is M_R={{A,B},{c,d}}; the remaining two cross matchings M_1={{A,c},{B,d}} and M_2={{A,d},{B,c}} occur in one of the two strict orders M_R>M_1>M_2 or M_R>M_2>M_1. Thus a same-oriented two-witness star ABc,ABd that does not already amplify to a P4 canonically renormalizes to a transitive no-P4 cell, with the star dimer and witness dimer forming the top matching.

## Hypotheses
Strong Level-(1) boundary antisymmetry; ABc and ABd tight; Z has no tight Hamilton P4.

## Scope
Pure four-vertex local theorem.

## Applicability
Use whenever a same-oriented dimer has two witnesses but the four support vertices remain P4-free. It converts the collision-like local packet into a complete matching-height cell suitable for iterative fifth-vertex gate analysis.

## Persistence
All eight forced turns and the resulting matching order are graph-intrinsic on Z.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert which of the two cross matchings is middle without one additional tested turn. Does not itself close a cover or provide currentness in another representative.

## Proof
Assume ABc and ABd are tight and Z={A,B,c,d} has no Hamilton P4.

First force the common packet. Candidate (A,B,c,d) has first turn ABc tight, so its second turn Bcd must be bad; hence by R3 dcB is tight. Candidate (A,B,d,c) similarly forces cdB tight. Candidate (A,c,d,B) has second turn cdB tight, so its first turn Acd must be bad; hence dcA is tight. Candidate (A,d,c,B) similarly forces cdA tight. Candidate (c,A,B,d) has second turn ABd tight, so cAB must be bad; hence BAc is tight. Candidate (d,A,B,c) similarly forces BAd tight. Thus
ABc,ABd,BAc,BAd,cdA,dcA,cdB,dcB
are all tight.

The only still-undetermined reversal pairs may be taken to include the cross comparison AcB versus BcA. We split on this one bit.

Case 1: AcB is tight. Candidate (d,c,A,B) already has dcA and cAB? More efficiently, repeatedly test the remaining Hamilton orders whose other consecutive turn is in the forced packet. No-P4 forces successively dBc, BdA, cAd and their reversal complements; after these forced choices every reversal pair is fixed. Reading the resulting turns by opposite-edge matchings gives
{{A,B},{c,d}} > {{A,c},{B,d}} > {{A,d},{B,c}}.
Indeed every tight triple xyz is exactly a descent from the matching containing xy to the matching containing yz.

Case 2: BcA is tight. The analogous complementary candidate chain forces dAc, AdB, cBd and the remaining reversal choices, giving
{{A,B},{c,d}} > {{A,d},{B,c}} > {{A,c},{B,d}}.

For completeness, uniqueness in either branch can be checked without any classification theorem: once the displayed eight common turns and the chosen literal AcB or BcA are fixed, each remaining reversal pair occurs as the sole uncertified turn of a Hamilton P4 candidate whose other turn is already tight, so no-P4 forces that pair's orientation. Hence there are at most two completions. The two displayed matching-height assignments realize both branches and contain no P4, since along any four-vertex path the first and third physical edges belong to the same opposite-edge matching, so a Hamilton P4 would require a strict cyclic descent M_i>M_j>M_i. Thus exactly the two stated completions occur.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R537.md -->

# R539 — Two-fragment maximal port deficit is exactly the unique-transition recompletion cell

## Statement
Retain an R508 packet with S of size three and literal deletion two-cover F. Let C be the complement of S in the deletion remainder. If F[C] has exactly two components and F[S] has two selected internal adjacencies, then the three S-vertices occur consecutively as one tight trimer block on a single F-rail, the other F-rail is a pure C-block, and F has exactly one selected S|C transition. Hence the packet is exactly an R511 tau(F)=1 SC/CS cell for the recompletion path Q on D union S. In the R24 notation, if c(F[B_x])=2 and e_F(A_x)=2, then A_x is the unique S-block and the pure-rail obstruction is an R511 cell with Q=K_x.

## Hypotheses
Full R508 packet; |S|=3; F[C] has exactly two components; e_F(S)=2.

## Scope
Order-free path-forest reduction.

## Applicability
Use when a three-vertex absorbable block has maximal internal adjacency and only two complementary fragments. It converts the apparent pure-rail obstruction into the exact R511 unique-transition normal form.

## Persistence
Retain D,S,Q,F, the consecutive S-trimer block, the pure C rail, the mixed C block, and unique crossing orientation.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not resolve the R511 three-hole residue and does not guarantee favorable positions of D inside Q.

## Proof
Because |S|=3 and e_F(S)=2 inside a two-path forest, the three S-vertices form a length-two path and hence occur consecutively as one maximal S-block A on one F-rail. For the induced C-forest, c(F[C])=e_F(S)+delta_F(S)-1. The hypotheses c(F[C])=2 and e_F(S)=2 therefore give delta_F(S)=1. Thus exactly one selected adjacency of F crosses S|C. Since F has two rails and F[C] has exactly two components, one C-component is adjacent to A across that unique transition on the mixed rail, while the other C-component is the entire other rail and is pure C. Hence the rail word is AB|K or BA|K with A the sole S-block and B,K the two C-blocks, and tau(F)=1. This is exactly the R511 SC/CS normal form for the retained R508 recompletion path Q on D union S.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R539.md -->

# R540 — Hamilton-rail plus singleton partner endpoint-cut recompletion

## Statement
Let H be a finite Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament with pc(H)>2. Let D be a nonempty proper set and suppose H-D has the literal exact two-cover R=(r_0,...,r_t) sqcup (x), with t>=2. Let K=(k_0,...,k_m) be a tight path whose support is exactly D union {r_0,r_t}. Fix an occurrence r_0=k_i. Put R^o=(r_1,...,r_{t-1}). Then U=K[0,i] followed by R^o and V=(x) followed by K[i+1,m], omitting empty pieces, form a spanning two-path proposal whose complete uncertified-turn set is { (k_{i-1},r_0,r_1) if i>=1 } union { (x,k_{i+1},k_{i+2}) if i<=m-2 }. Dually, if r_t=k_j, then U2=K[0,j-1] followed by (x) and V2=R^o followed by K[j,m] have complete uncertified-turn set { (k_{j-2},k_{j-1},x) if j>=2 } union { (r_{t-1},r_t,k_{j+1}) if j<=m-1 }. Each displayed hole set is nonempty and not all its members are tight; if it has one member that member is bad, and if it has two members at least one is bad, so R3 certifies the corresponding reverse mate clause.

## Hypotheses
H finite Strong Level-(1), pc(H)>2; H-D=R sqcup (x) literal two-cover; R has at least three vertices; K tight on exactly D plus the two physical endpoints of R.

## Scope
Order-free singleton-partner recompletion compiler.

## Applicability
Use when an R508/R509-style recompletion has exactly one nontrivial Hamilton C-rail and a singleton partner. It replaces the missing selected partner incidence by one explicit singleton seam hole and keeps the hole count at two.

## Persistence
Retain D,R,x,K, the chosen physical endpoint and its K-index, the displayed proposal, and complete hole set. Reverse mates are graph-intrinsic.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert either endpoint occupies a favorable K-position, and does not by itself improve the deletion cover.

## Proof
For the left-end construction, the supports of K[0,i], K[i+1,m], R^o, and {x} are pairwise disjoint except that r_0=k_i belongs only to the first K piece, and together they partition V(H): K spans D union {r_0,r_t}, while R^o supplies every vertex of R except its endpoints and x is the singleton rail. Thus U and V are vertex-disjoint and spanning. Inside K-pieces and inside R^o every turn is tight. At the U splice, the turn (r_0,r_1,r_2) is inherited from R whenever it exists; the only possible preceding splice turn is (k_{i-1},r_0,r_1). At the V splice from singleton x into the K-suffix, the only possible turn is (x,k_{i+1},k_{i+2}). Hence the displayed set is complete. The right-end construction is dual: K[0,j-1] followed by x has sole possible splice turn (k_{j-2},k_{j-1},x), while R^o followed by r_t=k_j and the K-suffix inherits (r_{t-2},r_{t-1},r_t) from R and has sole new turn (r_{t-1},r_t,k_{j+1}). Since pc(H)>2, neither proposal can have all displayed holes tight, and a zero-hole proposal is impossible. Therefore each nonempty hole set contains a bad turn; R3 makes its complete reverse tight, giving the stated one- or two-hole mate clause.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R540.md -->

# R541 — Two-sided middle-gate polarity compresses the transitive R24 frame to two global cases

## Statement
Let H be a finite Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament with pc(H)>2. Let X be a transitive matching-height four-cell with M_R>M_S>M_L and let Q=(q_0,...,q_m), m>=3, be a tight path with V(H)=X disjoint union V(Q). Assume X union {q_0} and X union {q_m} are P5-free and retain the endpoint reverse stars q_1 q_0 x and x q_m q_{m-1} for every x in X. By R534, at q_0 exactly one M_S-edge e_L is fully outgoing and its complementary M_S-edge f_L fully incoming; at q_m exactly one M_S-edge e_R is fully incoming and its complement f_R fully outgoing. The left gate e_L gives two tight prefix P5s, one absorbing each vertex of f_L, so for every w in f_L the induced subgraph on {w} union V(Q[2,m]) is non-Hamiltonian. Dually the right incoming gate e_R gives two tight suffix P5s, one absorbing each vertex of f_R, so for every w in f_R the induced subgraph on {w} union V(Q[0,m-2]) is non-Hamiltonian. Since M_S has exactly two edges, either e_L=e_R and f_L=f_R, or e_L and e_R are complementary and f_L and f_R are complementary. Thus the two-ended transitive frame has exactly an aligned or crossed middle-gate polarity.

## Hypotheses
H finite Strong Level-(1) with pc(H)>2; V(H)=X disjoint union V(Q); X transitive matching-height; Q=(q_0,...,q_m) tight with m>=3; both endpoint five-sets are P5-free; the displayed universal endpoint reverse stars hold; R534 and R538.

## Scope
Explicit graph-intrinsic two-ended compression; the historical phrase hard R24 frame has been replaced by its literal required data.

## Applicability
Use before any inward propagation or pair-deletion case split. It replaces independent endpoint fan choices by one binary global polarity.

## Persistence
Retain the physical M_S matching, e_L,e_R, their complementary witness edges, the four explicit absorber P5s, and the induced one-witness non-Hamiltonicity statements.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not claim either polarity is impossible and does not synchronize exact covers of the one-witness subgraphs.

## Proof
For the left endpoint, let e_L={a,b} be the fully outgoing M_S-edge at q_0, so q_0ab and q_0ba are tight. Write f_L={c,d} for the complementary M_S-edge. Relabel c,d if necessary so that bd and ac are M_L-edges. Then the matching-height rule gives abd and bac tight because M_S>M_L. Together with q_1q_0a,q_1q_0b, the two orders (q_1,q_0,a,b,d) and (q_1,q_0,b,a,c) are tight P5s. The first has complement {c} union V(Q[2,m]) and the second has complement {d} union V(Q[2,m]); R538 therefore makes both one-witness tails non-Hamiltonian. For the right endpoint, let e_R={u,v} be the fully incoming M_S-edge at q_m and f_R={r,s} its complement. Relabel r,s if necessary so that ru and sv are M_R-edges. Then ruv and svu are tight because M_R>M_S. Since uvq_m and vuq_m are tight and every xq_mq_{m-1} is tight, the orders (r,u,v,q_m,q_{m-1}) and (s,v,u,q_m,q_{m-1}) are tight P5s. Their complements are respectively {s} union V(Q[0,m-2]) and {r} union V(Q[0,m-2]), so R538 gives the two right-prefix non-Hamiltonicity conclusions. Finally M_S consists of exactly two complementary edges. Hence the selected left and right gate edges are either the same edge, in which case their complementary witness edges are the same, or they are the two distinct M_S-edges, in which case the witness edges are complementary. This is precisely the aligned/crossed dichotomy.

# R542 — Two-witness short-carrier boundary dimer forces capture or singleton-width payment

## Statement
Let H be a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample. Let K=(a,b,c) be a tight trimer and let S be either reverse boundary dimer (c,b) or (b,a), viewed as a signed support carrying two distinct same-polarity witnesses w_1,w_2 outside K on the same tested orientation. Then every exact two-cover T of H-V(S) selects a state crossing the singleton carrier remainder V(K)\\V(S) and the exterior V(H)\\V(K). For any such crossing, at least one of w_1,w_2 is not an endpoint of the crossing. Applying same-frame crossing/capture with that witness forces the capture/refund branch. Since S has order two, signed-support payment yields a finite certificate-retaining continuation to either a spanning two-cover or a descendant balanced opposite-sign pair with a singleton support. In particular the concentration branch cannot occur simultaneously for both witnesses.

## Hypotheses
H smallest Strong counterexample; K tight trimer; S one reverse terminal physical dimer of K; two distinct same-polarity signed witnesses on the same tested orientation; pair-deletion exactness for H-V(S).

## Scope
Short-carrier two-witness capture theorem; order-free beyond the trimer geometry.

## Applicability
Use when a same-polarity collision lands on a reverse terminal dimer of a 3-vertex carrier. It turns collision into an unavoidable physical capture across the complementary singleton carrier vertex.

## Persistence
Retain K,S,w_1,w_2, the chosen exact cover T, an actual selected carrier/exterior crossing, the witness avoided by that crossing, and the R527/R526 capture-payment ancestry.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not claim the singleton signed-support descendant is itself an exact singleton deletion cover or a contradiction.

## Proof
Assume S=(c,b); the head-end case S=(b,a) is dual. Put D=V(S) and W=V(H)\\D. The complementary carrier block is {a}. The original trimer K is a tight path spanning exactly D union {a}. Pair-deletion exactness supplies an exact two-cover T of H-D. Apply R508 with deletion D, absorbable block {a}, and recompletion path K. Therefore T selects at least one state crossing {a} | (V(H)\\V(K)). Such a selected state has physical support {a,y} for one exterior vertex y. Since w_1,w_2 are distinct exterior witnesses, y cannot equal both; choose w among {w_1,w_2} with y != w. The selected crossing {a,y} therefore avoids the exact sign witness w of S. The capture branch of R527 applies in this same deletion cover and actualizes a disjoint marker while retaining S and its witness. Because S has order two, the aligned payment clause built into R527 via R526 gives a finite certificate-retaining continuation to either a spanning two-cover or a descendant balanced opposite-sign pair with a singleton support. Thus the concentration alternative is impossible once both witnesses are retained: whichever crossing R508 supplies avoids at least one of them.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R542.md -->

# R544 — Aligned two-ended transitive trap forces a Hamilton P6

## Statement
Let X={a,b,c,z} be a transitive matching-height no-P4 four-cell with M(ab)=M_R, M(ac)=M_S, M(bc)=M_L. Let L,R be two exterior vertices. Suppose the following aligned gate packet is tight: caL, cbL, Lbz, Lzb, Laz, bzR, zbR, zcR, Rca, Rba, together with the intrinsic X-turn abc. Then X union {L,R} supports a Hamilton tight P6. More precisely, assuming no P6, the five candidates (c,a,L,b,z,R), (c,a,L,z,b,R), (z,b,R,c,a,L), (z,c,R,b,a,L), (z,L,a,b,c,R) successively force bLa, zLa, cRb, Lab, Rcb tight; then (R,c,b,L,a,z) is a tight P6, contradiction.

## Hypotheses
Strong Level-(1) exact reversal antisymmetry; X transitive matching-height with displayed labels; the displayed aligned gate turns are tight.

## Scope
Pure six-vertex local closure of the aligned R24 trap.

## Applicability
Use whenever two exterior vertices carry the displayed opposite middle-gate alignment around a transitive four-cell. It removes the aligned hard six-cell without any Q-interior or deletion-cover data.

## Persistence
The conclusion is graph-intrinsic. Retain the six vertices and, if used as a forcing proof, the five exact bad seams/reverse mates in order.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not address other six-cell gate polarities.

## Proof
Assume for contradiction that no Hamilton P6 exists. Candidate C1=(c,a,L,b,z,R) has turns caL, aLb, Lbz, bzR. All except aLb are tight by hypothesis, so aLb is bad and R3 gives bLa tight. Candidate C2=(c,a,L,z,b,R) similarly has sole unknown turn aLz, hence aLz is bad and zLa is tight. Candidate C3=(z,b,R,c,a,L) has turns zbR, bRc, Rca, caL, so bRc is bad and cRb tight. Candidate C4=(z,c,R,b,a,L) now has zcR, cRb, Rba tight and sole unknown baL; therefore baL is bad and Lab tight. Candidate C5=(z,L,a,b,c,R) now has zLa, Lab, abc tight and sole unknown bcR; therefore bcR is bad and Rcb tight. Finally C6=(R,c,b,L,a,z) has turns Rcb, cbL, bLa, Laz, all tight. Hence C6 is a Hamilton P6 on the six vertices, contradiction.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R544.md -->

# R546 — Wrong-polarity extreme gates force a P5 over a transitive four-cell

## Statement
Let X={a,b,c,z} be a transitive matching-height no-P4 four-cell with perfect matchings M_R>M_S>M_L, normalized by M_R={ab,cz}, M_S={ac,bz}, M_L={bc,az}. Let d be a fifth vertex and suppose X∪{d} is P5-free. Then no M_L-edge can be fully incoming to d: for every uv∈M_L, the two turns (u,v,d),(v,u,d) cannot both be tight. Dually, no M_R-edge can be fully outgoing from d: for every rs∈M_R, the two turns (d,r,s),(d,s,r) cannot both be tight. Equivalently, every bottom matching edge has at least one bad incoming orientation and every top matching edge has at least one bad outgoing orientation.

## Hypotheses
Strong Level-(1) complete-reversal antisymmetry R3; X has the transitive matching-height orientation; X+d has no Hamilton P5.

## Scope
Pure five-vertex structural lemma. No smallest-counterexample, deletion, path-cover, sign-payment, or R24 assumptions.

## Applicability
Use whenever a transitive no-P4 four-cell has a P5-free fifth vertex. It strengthens the endpoint-trap theorem by forbidding wrong-polarity full gates on every extreme matching edge, not merely asserting existence of one correctly polarized gate.

## Persistence
Retain the matching-height labels, fifth vertex d, the tested extreme matching edge, and the forced conclusion that at least one of its two wrong-polarity turns is bad. The conclusion is graph-intrinsic.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not classify middle-matching edges. Does not assert every extreme edge is fully gated in the correct polarity. Does not use or imply R24.

## Proof
In the matching-height cell the following X-turns are tight whenever used below: abc, acb, abz, zbc, zcb, zca and their matching-height equivalents.

BOTTOM. Suppose for contradiction that the bottom edge bc is fully incoming to d, so bcd and cbd are tight. Because X+d is P5-free, each displayed candidate below must fail at its sole not-yet-certified turn; R3 then certifies the complete reversal of that turn.
(1) (a,b,c,d,z) forces zdc.
(2) (a,b,z,d,c) forces dzb.
(3) (a,d,z,b,c) forces zda.
(4) (z,c,b,d,a) forces adb.
(5) (z,c,a,d,b) forces dac.
Now (z,d,a,c,b) is a tight P5, using zda,dac,acb, contradiction. Hence bcd and cbd cannot both be tight. Swapping simultaneously a↔c and b↔z preserves the matching-height structure and exchanges the two M_L edges, so the same holds for az.

TOP. Suppose for contradiction that the top edge ab is fully outgoing from d, so dab and dba are tight. Again use P5-freeness and R3:
(1) (c,d,b,a,z) forces bdc.
(2) (b,d,c,a,z) forces acd.
(3) (b,a,c,d,z) forces zdc.
(4) (a,b,z,d,c) forces dzb.
(5) (a,d,z,b,c) forces zda.
Then (z,d,a,b,c) is a tight P5, using zda,dab,abc, contradiction. Swapping the two M_R edges gives the statement for cz. Therefore no bottom edge is fully incoming and no top edge fully outgoing.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R546.md -->

# R547 — Hinged opposite-sign dimers collapse to opposite-sign singleton supports, with floor status only inside a payment lineage

## Statement
Let P and T be two graph-intrinsic signed tight dimers of opposite polarity in a Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament. Suppose their physical supports meet in exactly one hinge vertex b. Write u for the other vertex of P and v for the other vertex of T. Then deleting the hinge b from the two historical support orders and applying Signed-Interval Rebirth leaves a head-signed singleton on u from the head-signed dimer and a tail-signed singleton on v from the tail-signed dimer, regardless of which endpoint b occupied in either dimer order. Hence (u) and (v) are physically disjoint opposite-sign singleton supports and therefore form a graph-intrinsic balanced pair of total support mass two. In a hypothetical smallest-counterexample signed-payment lineage this is an ancestry-bearing both-singleton floor, with both ancestor dimers and the hinge-cut witnesses retained.

## Hypotheses
Strong Level-(1); two graph-intrinsic signed tight dimers of opposite polarity; their supports intersect in exactly one vertex b.

## Scope
Pure signed-path contact lemma. No smallest-counterexample assumption is needed for the singleton descendants themselves. The floor terminology is the usual smallest-counterexample lineage specialization.

## Applicability
Use whenever opposite-polarity dimer supports overlap in one physical vertex. It turns an overlapping pair, which is not itself balanced because it is not disjoint, into a disjoint mass-two balanced pair without any marker actualization, cover exchange, or payment descent.

## Persistence
Retain both original signed dimer orders/witnesses, the common hinge b, the two nonshared endpoints u,v, and the R425 cut ancestry. If b was the signed endpoint of a dimer, the singleton witness migrates to b exactly as prescribed by R425; otherwise the old witness persists.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not claim the two original dimers were disjoint. Does not close the resulting both-singleton floor. Does not preserve old witness names when the hinge was the signed endpoint.

## Proof
Let the head-signed dimer be P=(p_0,p_1) and the tail-signed dimer be T=(t_0,t_1), with V(P)∩V(T)={b}. Let u=V(P)\{b} and v=V(T)\{b}. Apply R425 to P with deletion set {b}. The unique surviving interval is the singleton (u). If u=p_0, it remains head-signed by P's old head witness. If u=p_1, then p_0=b was deleted immediately before it, so R425 makes (u) head-signed by witness b. Thus in either order (u) is graph-intrinsically head-signed. Dually apply R425 to T. If v=t_1 its old tail witness remains; if v=t_0 then t_1=b was deleted immediately after it, so (v) is tail-signed by witness b. Hence (v) is graph-intrinsically tail-signed. Since the two original supports met only at b, u and v are distinct, so these singleton supports are physically disjoint and have opposite polarity. By the project balanced-pair convention they form a mass-two balanced pair. The original dimer orders and the two hinge-cut events are retained as ancestry; no current representative is claimed.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R547.md -->

# R548 — Wrap selection-or-reversal for a path component

## Statement
Let a literal k-path cover contain a component P=(p_0,p_1,...,p_r), r>=1, in a Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament, and put w=(p_r,p_0). If r=1, reversing the two-vertex component gives another literal k-cover selecting w. If r>=2, then either one of the two cyclic rotations (p_r,p_0,p_1,...,p_{r-1}) or (p_1,...,p_r,p_0) is a tight path, hence another literal k-cover on the same support selecting w, or both wrap seam turns (p_r,p_0,p_1) and (p_{r-1},p_r,p_0) are bad. In the latter case R3 forces (p_1,p_0,p_r) and (p_0,p_r,p_{r-1}) tight. Thus the failed-wrap branch carries opposite-polarity signed terminal dimers; when r>=3 these turns concatenate to the tight reverse P4 (p_1,p_0,p_r,p_{r-1}).

## Hypotheses
Strong Level-(1) R3; one literal tight path component of a path cover.

## Scope
Order-free universal path-cover theorem. No smallest-counterexample, minimal-cover, deletion, sign-payment, or R24 assumptions.

## Applicability
Use whenever a named two-vertex state joins the tail of a current path component back to its head. It converts failure to select that wrap by cyclic rotation into an exact pair of reversed endpoint turns.

## Persistence
Retain the path component P, wrap state p_rp_0, which rotation succeeds if any, or in the failed-wrap branch the two exact reversed turns and reverse P4 when r>=3. All are graph-intrinsic except the selected-state role inside the displayed cover.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert the wrap-selected cover is distinct when symmetries occur. Does not turn a reverse P4 or signed-dimer packet by itself into a contradiction.

## Proof
For r=1, P=(p_0,p_1) has no triple constraints, so (p_1,p_0) is also a tight two-vertex path and selects the wrap. Assume r>=2. The head rotation P_H=(p_r,p_0,p_1,...,p_{r-1}) inherits every old turn of P except that its only new turn is (p_r,p_0,p_1). Hence if this turn is tight, P_H is tight. The tail rotation P_T=(p_1,...,p_r,p_0) likewise inherits every old turn except the new turn (p_{r-1},p_r,p_0); if that turn is tight, P_T is tight. In either case replacing P by the successful rotation preserves the number of cover components and selects the adjacent wrap state p_rp_0. If neither rotation works, both new turns are bad. R3 gives their complete reversals (p_1,p_0,p_r) and (p_0,p_r,p_{r-1}) tight. These are respectively a tail sign on the reversed head dimer (p_1,p_0) witnessed by p_r and a head sign on the reversed tail dimer (p_r,p_{r-1}) witnessed by p_0. If r>=3 then p_1 and p_{r-1} are distinct and the two turns concatenate to (p_1,p_0,p_r,p_{r-1}), a tight P4. This proves every clause.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R548.md -->

# R549 — Extreme matching gate existence over a P5-free transitive four-cell

## Statement
Let X={t,l,r,s} be a transitive matching-height no-P4 four-cell in a Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament, with opposite-edge perfect matchings M_R={{t,r},{l,s}}>M_S={{t,s},{l,r}}>M_L={{t,l},{r,s}}. Let d be a fifth vertex such that X union {d} has no tight Hamilton P5. Then at least one M_L edge is fully outgoing from d, and at least one M_R edge is fully incoming to d. Equivalently, for at least one uv in M_L both duv and dvu are tight, and for at least one xy in M_R both xyd and yxd are tight.

## Hypotheses
Strong Level-(1) boundary antisymmetry; X is a transitive matching-height four-cell; X union {d} is P5-free.

## Scope
Pure five-vertex local theorem; no smallest-counterexample, deletion-cover, or R24 hypothesis.

## Applicability
Use whenever a P5-free fifth vertex is attached to a transitive matching-height four-cell. Together with R534 it supplies a correctly polarized full gate in each of the three matching classes.

## Persistence
All five vertices, matching labels, and the existence of the correctly polarized extreme gates are graph-intrinsic.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not specify which of the two M_L edges is outgoing or which of the two M_R edges is incoming. Does not assert uniqueness of either extreme gate. Does not itself produce a P5 or a path cover.

## Proof
Write M_R={{t,r},{l,s}}, M_S={{t,s},{l,r}}, M_L={{t,l},{r,s}}. The matching-height rule supplies every X-only turn used below.\n\nBOTTOM. Suppose neither M_L edge is fully outgoing from d. Since {t,l} is not fully outgoing, at least one of dtl,dlt is bad; by R3 at least one of ltd,tld is tight. Since {r,s} is not fully outgoing, at least one of drs,dsr is bad; hence at least one of srd,rsd is tight. There are four cases.\n(1) ltd and srd tight. If rdt were tight, then (l,s,r,d,t) would be a P5 because lsr is tight; hence rdt is bad and tdr is tight. Then (s,l,t,d,r) is a P5, using slt,ltd,tdr.\n(2) ltd and rsd tight. If sdt were tight, then (l,r,s,d,t) would be a P5 because lrs is tight; hence sdt is bad and tds is tight. Then (r,l,t,d,s) is a P5, using rlt,ltd,tds.\n(3) tld and srd tight. If rdl were tight, then (t,s,r,d,l) would be a P5 because tsr is tight; hence rdl is bad and ldr is tight. Then (s,t,l,d,r) is a P5, using stl,tld,ldr.\n(4) tld and rsd tight. If sdl were tight, then (t,r,s,d,l) would be a P5 because trs is tight; hence sdl is bad and lds is tight. Then (r,t,l,d,s) is a P5, using rtl,tld,lds.\nAll four cases contradict P5-freeness, so some M_L edge is fully outgoing.\n\nTOP. Suppose neither M_R edge is fully incoming to d. Since {t,r} is not fully incoming, at least one of trd,rtd is bad; hence at least one of drt,dtr is tight. Since {l,s} is not fully incoming, at least one of lsd,sld is bad; hence at least one of dsl,dls is tight. Again there are four cases.\n(1) drt and dsl tight. If rds were tight, then (r,d,s,l,t) would be a P5 because slt is tight; hence rds is bad and sdr is tight. Then (s,d,r,t,l) is a P5, using sdr,drt,rtl.\n(2) drt and dls tight. If ldr were tight, then (l,d,r,t,s) would be a P5 because rts is tight; hence ldr is bad and rdl is tight. Then (r,d,l,s,t) is a P5, using rdl,dls,lst.\n(3) dtr and dsl tight. If tds were tight, then (t,d,s,l,r) would be a P5 because slr is tight; hence tds is bad and sdt is tight. Then (s,d,t,r,l) is a P5, using sdt,dtr,trl.\n(4) dtr and dls tight. If tdl were tight, then (t,d,l,s,r) would be a P5 because lsr is tight; hence tdl is bad and ldt is tight. Then (l,d,t,r,s) is a P5, using ldt,dtr,trs.\nThus some M_R edge is fully incoming. This proves both extreme-gate existence clauses using only R3 and the transitive matching-height orientation of X.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R549.md -->

# R552 — Equal P4 two-path covers amplify to a 5+3 cover

## Statement
Let G be an exact 2+2 ternary system (triangle-free (3,4)-tournament). Let A and B be vertex-disjoint tight paths of order 4. Then G[V(A)∪V(B)] contains a tight path of order 5, and the complementary 3-set spans a tight path of order 3. Consequently A∪B admits a spanning two-path cover whose longer component has order 5.

More generally, if two disjoint tight paths of common order t>=3 lie in an exact 2+2 system on 2t vertices, and t-1<=3 (i.e. t<=4), the same argument produces a spanning (t+1)+(t-1) two-path cover.

## Hypotheses
Exact 2+2 on every triple. The two paths are vertex-disjoint and each is tight. No maximality in a larger ambient graph is required; the intersecting-maxima lemma is applied inside the induced 8-vertex (or 2t-vertex) subsystem. No Strong Level-(1) hypothesis.

## Scope
Order-free combinatorial lemma for the isolated (3,4)-spanning / BM4 program. Outside the antisymmetric Strong Level-(1) regime.

## Applicability
Use as the d=0, t=4 two-path-cover exchange. It upgrades a balanced 4+4 cover to a 5+3 cover without SAT. Combined with a 5+3 Hamilton-merger it yields balanced 4+4 Hamilton merger.

## Persistence
The 5-path and complementary P3 are graph-intrinsic in the induced subsystem.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not by itself produce a Hamilton path. Does not amplify a 5+3 cover. The complement-is-a-path step fails for t>=5 because the leftover has order >=4 and need not be tight as a single path. Does not claim path-cover amplification for unequal lengths.

## Proof
Let H=G[V(A)∪V(B)]. Then H is itself an exact 2+2 system. By the source lemma (Devine–Milans, noDisjointMaxPaths): in any exact 2+2 system the family of maximum tight paths is pairwise intersecting. The same splice argument does not use global maximality except to reach a contradiction, and therefore any two disjoint tight paths of equal order t spawn a tight path of order at least t+1 in their union. Taking t=4, H contains a tight path P of order 5.

Let T=V(H)\\V(P); |T|=3. On T the exact 2+2 rule supplies four edges, hence at least one tight ordered triple. Thus T spans a tight P3. The pair P sqcup (that P3) is a spanning two-path cover of H whose longer rail has order 5.

The same complement arithmetic works whenever the leftover after a (t+1)-path on 2t vertices has size t-1<=3, i.e. only for t<=4.

(For completeness we recall the source splice. Align A=a1..at with B=b1..bt. An out-edge of A is a_j a_{j+1} b_j or a_j a_{j+1} b_{j+1}, and symmetrically for B. If an out-edge exists, choose one maximizing j and then j′∈{j,j+1}. The extremal choice plus exact 2+2 forces the neighboring cyclic mate needed to splice, producing a path of order at least t+1. If no out-edge exists either way, the alternating word a_t b_t a_{t-1} b_{t-1} ... a_1 b_1 is tight of order 2t, because a missing alternating turn would itself force an out-edge.)

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R552.md -->

# R553 — A bidirectionally universal bridge dimer cannot span a transitive four-cell without P5 or P6

## Statement
Let X={a,b,c,z} be a transitive matching-height no-P4 four-cell normalized by M_R={ab,cz}>M_S={ac,bz}>M_L={bc,az}. Let u,v be distinct vertices outside X. Suppose (x,u,v) and (u,v,x) are tight for every x∈X. Then at least one of the following holds: X∪{u} supports a Hamilton P5, or X∪{u,v} supports a Hamilton P6. Equivalently, if X+u is P5-free and the six-set X+u+v is P6-free, a physical dimer uv cannot carry both universal polarities X→uv and uv→X.

## Hypotheses
Strong Level-(1) complete-reversal antisymmetry R3; X is the displayed transitive matching-height cell; u,v outside X; both universal star families are tight.

## Scope
Pure six-vertex structural lemma. No smallest-counterexample, deletion, longest-path, R24, or completion assumptions.

## Applicability
Use when two independent endpoint/rotation arguments make one oriented dimer universally enterable from and universally exitable to a transitive no-P4 four-cell. It turns that bidirectional star packet into a P5/P6 alternative.

## Persistence
Retain X with its matching-height labels, u,v, the two universal star families, and the explicit candidate paths used in the proof. The conclusion is graph-intrinsic.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert which Hamilton path occurs. The proof uses the P5-free/P6-free negations to force three exact reversal turns.

## Proof
The matching-height rule gives the X-turns bac, czb, caz, bza tight. Since (c,u,v),(u,v,z) are tight, the candidate (b,a,c,u,v,z) would be a P6 if (a,c,u) were tight. Hence (a,c,u) is bad and R3 gives (u,c,a) tight. Since (b,u,v),(u,v,a) are tight, the candidate (c,z,b,u,v,a) would be a P6 if (z,b,u) were tight. Hence (z,b,u) is bad and R3 gives (u,b,z) tight. Now consider the five-set X+u. The candidate (b,u,c,a,z) has its last two turns (u,c,a) and (c,a,z) tight. P5-freeness therefore forces (b,u,c) bad, so R3 gives (c,u,b) tight. But then (c,u,b,z,a) is a Hamilton P5 on X+u: its turns are (c,u,b), (u,b,z), and the matching-height turn (b,z,a), all tight. Contradiction. Thus at least one of the claimed Hamilton paths exists.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R553.md -->

# R555 — Minimal six-seam pattern is uniquely the inward-facing double collision

## Statement
Let X={a,b,c,z} be a transitive matching-height no-P4 four-cell with M_R={ab,cz}>M_S={ac,bz}>M_L={bc,az}. Let d be a fifth vertex with X+d P5-free. Then (I) the two turns cbd and acd cannot both be tight; and (II) the two turns dba and dac cannot both be tight. Consequently, in the hard R24 order-three frame, if among the six P-side seams bcq_0, cbq_0, acq_0, q_mab, q_mac, q_mba exactly two are bad, then the bad seams are uniquely cbq_0 and q_mba. Equivalently the unique two-bad status word is (good,bad,good | good,good,bad). In that minimum cell the two forced collision dimers are the natural tested orientations (b,c) on the left and (a,b) on the right, so both collision dimers have signed anchor b.

## Hypotheses
Transitive matching-height X; the relevant fifth-vertex extension is P5-free. The R24 consequence also uses the extreme-seam forcing R546.

## Scope
Local five-cell seam classification and its R24 six-seam corollary.

## Applicability
Use to distinguish the unique exactly-two-bad residue from all higher-badness seam patterns.

## Persistence
Pure graph-intrinsic turn information.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert the exactly-two-bad pattern is realizable globally, only that it is the unique minimum status pattern if exactly two seams are bad. Does not use computation in the proof.

## Proof
Write d for the fifth vertex. We use only the matching-height turns inside X and R3.

(I) Suppose cbd and acd are both tight. Since X+d is P5-free, each displayed Hamilton candidate must fail at its only not-yet-certified turn.
1. (b,a,c,d,z): bac and acd are tight, so cdz is bad; hence zdc is tight.
2. (a,b,z,d,c): abz and zdc are tight, so bzd is bad; hence dzb is tight.
3. (a,d,z,b,c): dzb and zbc are tight, so adz is bad; hence zda is tight.
4. (z,d,a,c,b): zda and acb are tight, so dac is bad; hence cad is tight.
5. (z,c,a,d,b): zca and cad are tight, so adb is bad; hence bda is tight.
6. (z,c,b,d,a): zcb and the assumed cbd are tight, so bda must be bad, contradicting the preceding line. Thus cbd and acd cannot both be tight.

(II) Suppose dba and dac are both tight.
1. (c,d,b,a,z): dba and baz are tight, so cdb is bad; hence bdc is tight.
2. (b,d,c,a,z): bdc and caz are tight, so dca is bad; hence acd is tight.
3. (b,a,c,d,z): bac and acd are tight, so cdz is bad; hence zdc is tight.
4. (a,b,z,d,c): abz and zdc are tight, so bzd is bad; hence dzb is tight.
5. (a,d,z,b,c): dzb and zbc are tight, so adz is bad; hence zda is tight.
6. But now (z,d,a,c,b) is a Hamilton P5, using zda, the assumed dac, and acb, contradiction.

For the R24 corollary, R546 says bcq_0 and cbq_0 cannot both be good, and q_mab and q_mba cannot both be good. If exactly two of all six seams are bad, then there is exactly one bad seam in each extreme pair and the middle seams acq_0,q_mac are good. On the left, if cbq_0 were good then (I), with d=q_0, would contradict acq_0 good. Hence cbq_0 is bad and bcq_0 good. On the right, if q_mba were good then (II), with d=q_m, would contradict q_mac good. Hence q_mba is bad and q_mab good. This is the unique two-bad word. R3 then turns the two bad seams into q_0bc and abq_m, so the corresponding R543 collision orientations are (b,c) head-signed and (a,b) tail-signed; both signed anchors are b.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R555.md -->

# R560 — Absorber-complement block inequality and k-rail unique-transition normal form

## Statement
Let H be any finite directed tight-path system. Let V(H)=D disjoint-union S disjoint-union C, with S,C nonempty. Suppose A=A_1 sqcup ... sqcup A_a is a literal tight-path cover of H[D union S], and T=T_1 sqcup ... sqcup T_k is a literal tight-path cover of H-D=H[S union C]. Split every T-rail at each selected S|C transition and let b_C(T) be the total number of nonempty maximal contiguous C-blocks. Then pc(H) <= a+b_C(T). Equivalently b_C(T) >= pc(H)-a. In particular, if A is one tight path and pc(H)>k, then every k-rail cover T of H-D has b_C(T)>=k. If such a T has exactly one selected S|C transition, then it has the following canonical normal form: exactly one rail is mixed and consists of one S-block and one C-block, in either order; every other one of the k-1 rails lies wholly in C; hence all vertices of S occur in the unique S-block and there is no S-only rail. For k=2 this simultaneously recovers the crossing core of R508 and the component-word/block-count part of R511, without Strong Level-(1) or any small-order hypothesis.

## Hypotheses
Only finite tight-path combinatorics. D,S,C are pairwise disjoint and cover V(H); S,C nonempty. A covers D union S by a tight paths; T covers S union C by k tight paths.

## Scope
Order-free, deletion-size-free, and not specific to Strong Level-(1). Applicable to arbitrary path-cover thresholds k and arbitrary absorber cover size a.

## Applicability
Use whenever one has overlapping covers: an absorber cover on D union S and a deletion cover on S union C. The maximal C-block count in the deletion cover is globally constrained by pc(H).

## Persistence
Graph-intrinsic inequality plus literal block decomposition of the chosen deletion cover T.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not produce either cover A or T. Does not certify any splice between an A-rail and a C-block. Does not imply the unique-transition case exists. Does not use boundary antisymmetry, pair-deletion exactness, R24, or any order bound.

## Proof
Let T=T_1 sqcup ... sqcup T_k cover S union C. Split every T-rail at each selected S|C transition. The resulting maximal C-blocks are pairwise vertex-disjoint tight paths covering C, so there are b_C(T) of them. Together with the supplied a-path cover A of D union S, these C-blocks form a spanning path cover of H by a+b_C(T) paths. Hence pc(H)<=a+b_C(T), equivalently b_C(T)>=pc(H)-a. If a=1 and pc(H)>k, integrality gives pc(H)>=k+1, hence b_C(T)>=k.

Now assume T has exactly one selected S|C transition. Splitting all rails at that unique transition produces exactly k+1 monochromatic blocks in total. Since C is nonempty, b_C>=1; since S is nonempty, the number b_S of S-blocks is at least one. From b_C>=k and b_S+b_C=k+1 we obtain b_S<=1, hence b_S=1 and b_C=k. The unique transition lies on exactly one mixed rail, which therefore consists of the unique S-block adjacent to one C-block, in one of the two orders SC or CS. Every other rail is monochromatic. Because there is only one S-block total and it already lies on the mixed rail, every other rail lies wholly in C; in particular there is no S-only rail. This proves the full R560 contract.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R560.md -->

# FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R561.md

<!-- BEGIN FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R561.md -->

# R561 — Boundary-reversed Hamilton dimer is a universal one-vertex absorber

## Statement
Let X be a finite induced vertex set in a Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament, or more generally any exact-reversal tight-turn system. Suppose there are distinct u,v in X and two Hamilton tight paths P_start and P_end of X such that P_start begins with the ordered state (u,v) and P_end ends with the ordered state (v,u). Then every exterior vertex d notin X Hamilton-extends X. More precisely, exactly one of the reversal-pair turns (d,u,v) and (v,u,d) is tight. If (d,u,v) is tight, prepending d to P_start gives a Hamilton tight path of X union {d}; if (v,u,d) is tight, appending d to P_end gives one. Thus a single boundary-reversed Hamilton dimer makes X universally one-vertex Hamilton-extendable.

## Hypotheses
Exact complete-reversal antisymmetry on each triple. X has a Hamilton path starting with ordered dimer (u,v) and a Hamilton path ending with the reverse ordered dimer (v,u).

## Scope
Order-free and size-free. No smallest-counterexample, deletion, cover, transitive-cell, or global-longest hypothesis.

## Applicability
Provides a direct structural certificate for the universal-extension hypothesis used in later surgery theorems such as R153. Also abstracts the endpoint-gate logic behind transitive-four-cell arguments.

## Persistence
Graph-intrinsic property of X and the two Hamilton boundary states.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not claim one fixed Hamilton order of X extends every d. The extending Hamilton path may use P_start or P_end according to the antisymmetric turn at d. Does not by itself produce a spanning two-cover of a larger graph.

## Proof
Let d be exterior to X. Apply exact complete-reversal antisymmetry R3 to the ordered triple (d,u,v): exactly one of (d,u,v) and (v,u,d) is tight. If (d,u,v) is tight, prepend d to the Hamilton path P_start of X beginning with (u,v). The only new consecutive triple is (d,u,v), so the resulting path is Hamiltonian on X union {d}. If instead (v,u,d) is tight, append d to the Hamilton path P_end of X ending with (v,u); again the only new consecutive triple is the certified turn (v,u,d). Thus every exterior d Hamilton-extends X, although the extending order may depend on d.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R561.md -->

# FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R564.md

<!-- BEGIN FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R564.md -->

# R564 — Right-split order-1 dichotomy and the middle-insertion candidate

## Statement
Let G be an exact 2+2 ternary system, let P=(v0,...,v{m-1}) be a tight path with m>=3, and let x be outside P. Assume Q=(v0,...,v{m-2},x) is also tight. Then either (v0,...,v{m-1},x) is a spanning tight path, or both cyclic mates (v{m-1},x,v{m-2}) and (x,v{m-2},v{m-1}) are tight. If in the latter branch the additional turn (v{m-3},x,v{m-2}) is tight, then (v0,...,v{m-3},x,v{m-2},v{m-1}) is a spanning tight path. The only unresolved cell is the simultaneous failure of (v{m-2},v{m-1},x) and (v{m-3},x,v{m-2}).

## Hypotheses
Exact 2+2. P and Q tight as displayed. Isolated (3,4) model.

## Scope
Order-free seam lemma for BM4 split-origin caps of order 1. Outside the antisymmetric regime.

## Applicability
Use on a right split whose short rail has order 1. Does not close the residual cell.

## Persistence
The listed tight turns are graph-intrinsic.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not prove the residual cell is Hamiltonian. Does not prove global insertion. Does not revive general endpoint replacement.

## Proof
The last pair of P is (v{m-2}, v{m-1}). Exact 2+2 implies the prepend/append alternative on this triple. If (v{m-2}, v{m-1}, x) is tight, then every consecutive triple of (v0,...,v{m-1},x) is a triple of P or this last triple, so P followed by x spans. If (v{m-2}, v{m-1}, x) is missing, then among the three cyclic orders on {v{m-2},v{m-1},x} the other two, (v{m-1},x,v{m-2}) and (x,v{m-2},v{m-1}), are tight because exactly two cyclic orders are present. If in addition (v{m-3},x,v{m-2}) is tight, then (v0,...,v{m-3},x,v{m-2},v{m-1}) has exactly the two new tight turns (v{m-3},x,v{m-2}) and (x,v{m-2},v{m-1}), hence spans. The sole unresolved cell is simultaneous failure of (v{m-2},v{m-1},x) and (v{m-3},x,v{m-2}).

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R564.md -->

# FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R566.md

<!-- BEGIN FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R566.md -->

# R566 — Unique-transition crossing inherits the absorber Hamilton boundary fan

## Statement
Let H be a finite exact-reversal tight-turn system with pc(H)>k. Partition V(H)=D disjoint-union S disjoint-union C with S,C nonempty, and suppose X=H[D union S] is Hamiltonian. Let T be a literal k-path cover of H-D having exactly one selected S|C transition. By R560, T has one mixed rail and k-1 pure C-rails. (SC orientation.) Suppose the unique transition is the selected state x y with x in S and y in C. For every vertex p in (D union S)-{x} for which X has a Hamilton tight path ending with the ordered state (p,x), the turn (y,x,p) is tight. Hence the tested crossing dimer (y,x) is tail-signed by every such Hamilton predecessor p. In particular, two distinct Hamilton predecessors p_1,p_2 force a same-oriented two-tail witness collision on the actual selected crossing dimer (y,x). (CS orientation.) Dually, if the unique transition is y x with y in C and x in S, then for every p for which X has a Hamilton tight path starting with (x,p), the turn (p,x,y) is tight; thus the tested crossing dimer (x,y) is head-signed by every such Hamilton successor p, and two distinct successors force a same-oriented two-head witness collision. Therefore a unique recompletion transition converts Hamilton boundary multiplicity of the absorber into a role-sensitive witness fan on the literal selected crossing.

## Hypotheses
Finite exact-reversal tight-turn system; pc(H)>k; V(H)=D sqcup S sqcup C with S,C nonempty; H[D union S] Hamiltonian; T is a k-cover of H-D with exactly one S|C transition. Accepted/pending R560 unique-transition normal form and R3 boundary antisymmetry.

## Scope
Order-free and k-rail general. Specializes to the A7C3 k=2 smallest-counterexample recompletion setting but is not tied to any small order, transitive four-cell, or R24 rail size.

## Applicability
Use when a deletion absorber D union S has multiple Hamilton boundary states at the S-endpoint of a transition-minimal cover. The theorem converts that multiplicity into an R523 same-support witness fan on the actual crossing dimer, preserving the deletion cover and transition coordinates.

## Persistence
Retains D,S,C, the literal cover T, unique crossing orientation and endpoints x,y, and each Hamilton predecessor/successor p as the exact witness of the resulting signed crossing certificate.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert the crossing collision alone closes H. Does not apply when T has more than one S|C transition without additional block bookkeeping. Does not require the different Hamilton absorber paths to coexist as current covers; only their graph-intrinsic boundary states are used.

## Proof
Assume first that the unique selected transition is x y with x in S and y in C. By R560, after relabelling T consists of one mixed rail A B, where A is the unique S-block ending at x and B is a nonempty C-block beginning at y, together with k-1 rails lying wholly in C. Let Q be any Hamilton tight path of H[D union S] ending with ordered state (p,x). Replace A in the mixed rail by Q, keep B in its literal T-order, and keep every other T-rail unchanged. The resulting k vertex-disjoint sequences cover all of H. Every turn is certified by Q, by T inside B and the other rails, and, if B has at least two vertices, by the original T turn beginning with the selected state xy, except possibly the single splice turn (p,x,y). If (p,x,y) were tight, these sequences would form a literal k-cover of H, contrary to pc(H)>k. Hence (p,x,y) is bad. Exact reversal antisymmetry R3 gives (y,x,p) tight. Since p was arbitrary among Hamilton predecessors of x in H[D union S], every such p is a tail witness on the same tested crossing dimer (y,x); two distinct predecessors therefore give the R523 two-tail collision packet. For the dual orientation y x, R560 writes the mixed rail as B A with B ending at y and A beginning at x. Replace A by a Hamilton path Q starting (x,p). The only possible missing splice is (y,x,p), which must be bad, so R3 gives (p,x,y) tight. Thus every Hamilton successor p is a head witness on the same tested crossing dimer (x,y).

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R566.md -->
