# FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R567.md

<!-- BEGIN FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R567.md -->

# R567 — Multi-absorber transition-pressure inequality

## Statement
Let H be any finite tight-path system with p=pc(H). Let D be a proper vertex set, put W=V(H)\D, and partition W into r>=2 nonempty classes Pi={C_1,...,C_r}. Let T be a literal k-path cover of H-D, and let t_Pi(T) be the total number of selected adjacent states of T whose endpoints lie in different Pi-classes. For each i suppose H[D union (W\C_i)] has a literal path cover by a_i rails. Then t_Pi(T) >= r p - (a_1+...+a_r) - k. More precisely, pc(H[C_i])>=p-a_i for every i, and if b_i(T) is the number of maximal contiguous C_i-blocks in T then b_i(T)>=pc(H[C_i]); since sum_i b_i(T)=k+t_Pi(T), the stated inequality follows. In the two-class case W=S sqcup C, if both D union S and D union C are Hamiltonian, then every k-cover T of H-D satisfies t(T)>=2p-2-k. In particular, in a smallest two-cover counterexample p=3, every exact two-cover of such a residue has at least two S|C transitions. More generally, in the same p=3,k=2 regime, a three-class partition for which each D plus the other two classes is Hamiltonian forces at least four cross-class selected states.

## Hypotheses
Only finite tight-path combinatorics. D is proper; C_i are nonempty and partition H-D; T is a k-path cover of H-D; for each i there is an a_i-path cover of D together with all classes except C_i.

## Scope
Order-free, deletion-size-free, arbitrary path-cover threshold p, arbitrary residue cover size k, and arbitrary partition size r. No Strong Level-(1), antisymmetry, or small-order hypothesis is needed.

## Applicability
Use to rule out low-transition exact deletion covers by manufacturing cheap complementary absorbers through one common deletion set D. It converts multiple absorber certificates into a quantitative lower bound on selected cross-class states in every deletion cover.

## Persistence
Retains the common deletion D, partition Pi, each complementary absorber cover size a_i, and the literal transition count of the chosen T.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not produce the complementary absorber covers. Does not prescribe which class pairs realize the forced transitions. Does not by itself convert the forced transitions into balanced pairs, captures, or closure; those require downstream consumers.

## Proof
Fix i. Let c_i=pc(H[C_i]). By hypothesis H[D union (W\C_i)] has an a_i-path cover. Taking this cover together with a c_i-path cover of H[C_i] gives a literal spanning path cover of H with a_i+c_i rails. Therefore p=pc(H)<=a_i+c_i, so c_i>=p-a_i. Now split every rail of T at every selected transition between distinct Pi-classes. Let b_i be the number of resulting nonempty blocks whose vertices lie in C_i. These b_i blocks form a path cover of H[C_i], so b_i>=c_i>=p-a_i. If one T-rail contains m_j monochromatic blocks, it contains exactly m_j-1 cross-class selected states. Summing over the k rails gives sum_i b_i=sum_j m_j=k+t_Pi(T). Hence k+t_Pi(T)>=sum_i(p-a_i)=rp-sum_i a_i, which rearranges to t_Pi(T)>=rp-sum_i a_i-k. The stated two- and three-class corollaries are immediate substitutions.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R567.md -->

# FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R570.md

<!-- BEGIN FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R570.md -->

# R570 — Unique-transition survivors are one-sided Hamilton-boundary rigid

## Statement
Let H be a finite Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament with pc(H)>2. Partition V(H)=D disjoint-union S disjoint-union C with S,C nonempty. Assume X=H[D union S] is Hamiltonian and T is a literal exact two-cover of H-D with exactly one selected S|C transition. Then the following rigidity alternative holds. First, H[D union C] is non-Hamiltonian; otherwise R567 applied to the two Hamilton absorbers D union S and D union C forces at least two S|C transitions in T. Second, suppose the unique transition is x y with x in S and y in C. If there are two Hamilton paths of X ending at x with distinct penultimate vertices, R566 gives a same-oriented two-tail collision on the actual crossing dimer (y,x). If there are two distinct Hamilton paths of X ending at x with the same penultimate vertex, R435 applied to the two Hamilton orders on the same support gives an exact reversed old state, a tight reverse trimer, or a vertex-simple tight cycle. Hence outside those explicit interaction outputs there is AT MOST ONE Hamilton path of X ending at x. Dually, if the unique transition is y x, then outside a same-oriented two-head crossing collision or an R435 reverse-order output there is AT MOST ONE Hamilton path of X starting at x. Thus every interaction-free tau=1 recompletion cell is intrinsically one-sided: the opposite D-augmented side is non-Hamiltonian and the absorber has boundary multiplicity at most one in the literal crossing role. Endpoint accessibility is not automatic: the relevant family of Hamilton paths may be empty.

## Hypotheses
Strong Level-(1); pc(H)>2; partition D,S,C; H[D union S] Hamiltonian; T exact two-cover of H-D with exactly one S|C transition. Uses R435,R566,R567.

## Scope
Order-free. Applies to arbitrary deletion size whenever the stated exact two-cover exists; in smallest-counterexample applications D may come from any exact deletion theorem. Not tied to R24, transitive four-cells, or the eight-vertex case.

## Applicability
New low-transition target reduction. To eliminate tau=1 it suffices to produce either a Hamilton absorber on the opposite side through the same D, or two endpoint-compatible Hamilton orders of the existing absorber. A separate endpoint-accessibility theorem can strengthen the zero-or-one conclusion to exact uniqueness.

## Persistence
Retains D,S,C, the exact cover T, crossing endpoint x and exterior endpoint y, and the relevant Hamilton boundary role of X.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert existence of any Hamilton path of X ending at x in the SC orientation or starting at x in the CS orientation. Does not assert that the listed collision/reversal/cycle outputs themselves close H. Does not apply to tau>=2.

## Proof
Assume first that H[D union C] is Hamiltonian. Apply the two-class specialization of R567 to W=S sqcup C, k=2, and the two one-rail absorber covers on D union S and D union C. Since pc(H)>2, pc(H)>=3, so the number of selected S|C transitions in T is at least 2pc(H)-1-1-2>=2, contradicting tau(T)=1. Hence H[D union C] is non-Hamiltonian. Now suppose the unique transition is x y with x in S. If X has two Hamilton paths Q_1,Q_2 ending at x with distinct penultimate vertices p_1,p_2, R566 gives y x p_1 and y x p_2 tight, a same-tested-orientation two-tail collision on the actual selected crossing dimer (y,x). If instead Q_1,Q_2 are distinct but have the same penultimate vertex p, they are two different Hamilton orders on the same vertex support X. Applying R435 to one as the reference path and the other as the comparison path yields an exact reversal of an old adjacent state, a tight reverse trimer, or a vertex-simple tight cycle. Therefore, if none of these explicit outputs occurs, there cannot be two distinct Hamilton paths of X ending at x; there may be one or none. The y x orientation is the exact dual, using Hamilton paths starting at x and the head-collision half of R566.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R570.md -->

# FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R573.md

<!-- BEGIN FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R573.md -->

# R573 — Unique-crossing Hamilton ending forces a reverse tail on the selected dimer

## Statement

Let H be finite with pc(H)>2. Let D be proper, write W=V(H)\\D=S disjoint-union C with S,C nonempty, and suppose X=H[D union S] admits a tight Hamilton path. Let T be a literal exact two-cover of H-D with exactly one selected S|C transition.

(CS) Suppose the unique transition is the selected state x y with x in S and y in C. Then T has exactly one mixed rail, whose C-block starts at y, and the other rail is monochromatic. In particular C is covered by either one path starting at y or two paths, one of which starts at y.
If X has a tight Hamilton path ending with the ordered state (p,x), the turn (p,x,y) is bad. Hence (y,x,p) is tight by R3: the tested crossing dimer (y,x) is tail-signed by every such Hamilton predecessor p. If two such Hamilton paths exist with distinct penultimate vertices p_1,p_2, then R523 supplies a same-oriented two-tail witness collision on the actual selected crossing dimer (y,x).

(SC) Dually, if the unique transition is y x with y in C and x in S, and X has a tight Hamilton path starting with (x,p), then (p,x,y) is tight and the tested dimer (x,y) is head-signed by every such Hamilton successor p. Distinct successors force a same-oriented two-head R523 collision on (x,y).

No Hamilton path of X need end (resp. start) at x. The family may be empty.


## Hypotheses

H finite, pc(H)>2. D proper, S and C nonempty, X=H[D union S] Hamiltonian, T an exact two-cover of H-D with tau(T)=1. Tight/bad complementary by R3. The two-witness clause uses accepted R523.


## Scope

Order-free exact-two-cover unique-transition theorem. It does not treat k>2 covers, does not force endpoint accessibility of x on X, and does not require D union C to be Hamiltonian.


## Applicability

In any tau=1 exact two-cover cell with a certified Hamilton absorber D union S, test whether X has a Hamilton path ending (CS) or starting (SC) at the S-endpoint of the unique crossing. Each such path contributes a named reverse turn on the selected dimer. Two distinct neighbors trigger R523.


## Persistence

Retain D,S,C,T, the unique crossing state, the absorber X, every Hamilton path of X used, the displayed reverse turns, and any R523 collision. Selected-state roles remain representative-relative to T.


## Exclusions / nonclaims

Does not assert that a Hamilton path of X ends or starts at x. Does not force a second Hamilton order of X. Does not make D union C Hamiltonian. Does not treat k>2. Does not depend on pending R560 or R566-R570.


## Proof

Work first in CS: unique selected state xy, x in S, y in C. Since T has two rails and exactly one S|C adjacency, exactly one rail is mixed and the other is monochromatic. The mixed rail traverses an S-block, then y, then a (possibly trivial) C-block. Thus one C-block of T starts at y. The other rail is either pure S, in which case b_C=1 and C is a single path starting at y, or pure C, in which case b_C=2.

Let Q be a tight Hamilton path of X ending (p,x). Suppose for contradiction that (p,x,y) is tight. Concatenate Q with the C-block of T that starts at y to obtain a tight path Q+ covering D union S union that C-block.
If b_C=1 then Q+ spans V(H), contradicting pc(H)>2.
If b_C=2 then the remaining rail of T is a pure C-path disjoint from Q+, and {Q+, that rail} is a literal two-cover of H, contradicting pc(H)>2.
Hence (p,x,y) is bad, so (y,x,p) is tight by R3.
If p_1 and p_2 are distinct such predecessors, the two tight turns (y,x,p_1) and (y,x,p_2) are same-oriented two-tail certificates on the physical dimer (y,x). R523 yields the stated collision.

The SC case is symmetric: the mixed rail ends with an S-block starting at x, the relevant join is at the front of Q, and the forced tight turn is (p,x,y).
Existence of Q ending or starting at x is an extra hypothesis on each application, not a conclusion.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R573.md -->

# FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R578.md

<!-- BEGIN FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R578.md -->

# R578 — Reversed absorber dimer plus singleton mixed C-block spans H

## Statement

Let H be finite with pc(H)>2. Let D be proper, W=V(H)\\D=S disjoint-union C with S,C nonempty, and let X=H[D union S] be Hamiltonian. Let T be a literal exact two-cover of H-D with exactly one selected S|C transition. Write x for the S-endpoint and y for the C-endpoint of that transition.
By R560 the unique-transition normal form holds: one mixed rail carries every vertex of S together with one C-block B_C, and the other rail lies wholly in C. In particular b_C(T)=2.
Suppose in addition that X admits a boundary-reversed Hamilton dimer in the sense of R561, and that B_C={y}. Then R561 Hamilton-extends X by the exterior vertex y, yielding a tight Hamilton path of D union S union {y}. The remaining rail of T is a tight path on C\\{y}. Those two paths cover V(H), contradicting pc(H)>2.
Hence a tau=1 exact two-cover cell with Hamiltonian absorber and singleton mixed C-block cannot carry a boundary-reversed Hamilton dimer on X.


## Hypotheses

Finite tight-path system with pc(H)>2. X Hamiltonian. T exact two-cover of H-D with tau=1. R560 normal form. The R561 branch additionally assumes a boundary-reversed Hamilton dimer on X and B_C={y}.


## Scope

Order-free. Restricted to the singleton mixed C-block face of the R560 unique-transition form. Does not treat longer mixed C-blocks.


## Applicability

After R560, inspect the mixed C-block. If it is the singleton {y}, forbid an R561 reversed dimer on the absorber.


## Persistence

Retain D,S,C,T,x,y,B_C, the absorber, and the R561 dimer when present.


## Exclusions / nonclaims

Does not force B_C to be a singleton. Does not treat |B_C|>=2. Does not produce the reversed dimer.


## Proof

R560 applied to a Hamiltonian absorber and a k=2 unique-transition cover yields b_C=2: the mixed rail is an S-block containing all of S, followed or preceded by a C-block B_C, and the second rail R* lies wholly in C. Assume B_C={y} and that X has a boundary-reversed Hamilton dimer (u,v). R561 supplies a tight Hamilton path Q+ of X union {y}. Since B_C={y}, every remaining C-vertex lies on R*. The pair {Q+,R*} is a literal two-cover of V(H), contradicting pc(H)>2.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R578.md -->

# FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R579.md

<!-- BEGIN FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R579.md -->

# R579 — Wrap tetrachotomy for a Hamiltonian path of order at least three

## Statement
Let H be a Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament and let Q=(q_0,q_1,...,q_r) be a vertex-simple tight path with r>=2. Write alpha=(q_r,q_0,q_1) and beta=(q_{r-1},q_r,q_0) for the two wrap-seam turns, rot1=(q_r,q_0,q_1,...,q_{r-1}) and rot2=(q_1,...,q_r,q_0) for the two cyclic rotations, and w=(q_r,q_0) for the wrap state. Then exactly one of the following four exclusive branches holds.

(DW) Double wrap: alpha and beta are both tight. Equivalently both rotations are tight paths, equivalently (q_0,q_1,...,q_r,q_0) is a vertex-simple tight Hamilton cycle on V(Q).

(SW1) Single wrap, rot1: alpha is tight and beta is bad. Then rot1 is a tight Hamilton path of V(Q) starting at q_r and ending at q_{r-1}, while rot2 is not tight, and R3 supplies the reversed seam (q_0,q_r,q_{r-1}).

(SW2) Single wrap, rot2: beta is tight and alpha is bad. Then rot2 is a tight Hamilton path of V(Q) starting at q_1 and ending at q_0, while rot1 is not tight, and R3 supplies the reversed seam (q_1,q_0,q_r).

(DF) Double fail: alpha and beta are both bad. Then neither rotation is a tight path, R3 supplies both reversed seams (q_1,q_0,q_r) and (q_0,q_r,q_{r-1}), and if r>=3 those opposite-polarity certificates on the tested dimer (q_0,q_r) concatenate by R523 to the tight reverse P4 (q_1,q_0,q_r,q_{r-1}).

A single successful rotation is therefore a cyclically shifted Hamilton path, not by itself a Hamilton cycle. A Hamilton cycle on V(Q) occurs if and only if the double-wrap branch holds.

## Hypotheses
Strong Level-(1) boundary antisymmetry R3. Q is a vertex-simple tight path of order at least three. No smallest-counterexample, deletion, cover, or transition hypothesis.

## Scope
Order-free refinement of R548. Applies to any tight path component of order at least three in a Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament, whether or not it is an absorber in a deletion frame.

## Applicability
Use whenever a named Hamilton path must be classified before converting wrap data into a cycle, a second Hamilton order, an R561 reversed dimer, or an R566 boundary fan. Downstream arguments that need a Hamilton cycle on the support must invoke the double-wrap branch, not mere wrap success.

## Persistence
The four-way branch, the listed tight or bad seams, the successful rotation if any, the Hamilton cycle in DW, and the reverse P4 in DF with r>=3 are graph-intrinsic. Selected-state language is used only when Q is viewed as a cover component.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert that any branch is contradictory. Does not assert that a single successful rotation makes every vertex of V(Q) Hamilton-accessible as an endpoint. Does not produce an R561 reversed Hamilton dimer from DF or SW alone. Does not itself close a tau=1 cell.

## Proof
Let Q=(q_0,...,q_r) with r>=2 be a vertex-simple tight path in a Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament. The internal turns of Q are tight by hypothesis. The two cyclic rotations differ from Q only at a wrap seam: rot1 is tight if and only if alpha=(q_r,q_0,q_1) is tight, and rot2 is tight if and only if beta=(q_{r-1},q_r,q_0) is tight.

R548 applied to Q says that either at least one cyclic rotation is a tight path, or both wrap-seam turns alpha and beta are bad. Because each rotation is tight if and only if its seam is tight, the four truth-combinations of (alpha,beta) are exclusive and exhaustive and match the four displayed branches.

If both seams are tight, then every consecutive triple of the closed walk (q_0,q_1,...,q_r,q_0) is tight: the internal triples are those of Q and the two wrap triples are alpha and beta. The walk is vertex-simple because Q is. This is a tight Hamilton cycle on V(Q), which is (DW). Conversely, any tight Hamilton cycle through the ordered support of Q uses both wrap seams, so both rotations are tight.

If alpha is tight and beta is bad, rot1 is a tight Hamilton path and rot2 is not. R3 converts the bad seam beta into the tight reverse (q_0,q_r,q_{r-1}). This is (SW1). The symmetric argument gives (SW2).

If both seams are bad, neither rotation is tight and R3 supplies both reversed seams (q_1,q_0,q_r) and (q_0,q_r,q_{r-1}). The first is a head certificate on the tested dimer (q_0,q_r) with witness q_1; the second is a tail certificate on the same tested dimer with witness q_{r-1}. For r>=3 the four vertices q_1,q_0,q_r,q_{r-1} are distinct, so R523 opposite-polarity interaction yields the tight P4 (q_1,q_0,q_r,q_{r-1}), which is the reverse P4 already recorded by R548. This is (DF).

In particular the success language of R548 splits into (DW), (SW1), and (SW2). Only (DW) produces a Hamilton cycle. A single successful rotation changes the endpoints of Q but does not cut a cycle and does not by itself furnish two Hamilton paths with a common endpoint.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R579.md -->

# FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R581.md

<!-- BEGIN FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R581.md -->

# R581 — Reversed Hamilton dimer plus universal-extension rigidity forbids singleton residual rails

## Statement
Let H be a smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample and let X be a nonempty proper vertex set that carries a boundary-reversed Hamilton dimer in the sense of R561: there exist distinct u,v in X and Hamilton tight paths of X beginning with (u,v) and ending with (v,u). Then every exterior vertex r notin X Hamilton-extends X, so the universal-extension hypothesis of R156 holds. Consequently pc(H-X)=2, and every exact two-cover of H-X has both rails of order at least two: no exact two-cover of the complement has a singleton component.

In particular, in a tau=1 exact two-cover cell with Hamiltonian absorber X=H[D union S] that additionally carries a boundary-reversed Hamilton dimer, the R560 complement C admits the exact two-cover consisting of the mixed C-block B_C and the unique pure C-rail, and both of those C-blocks have order at least two. Thus neither C-block can be a singleton. This forbids the mixed singleton B_C={y} already ruled out order-free by R578, and additionally forbids a singleton pure C-rail, which R578 does not address.

## Hypotheses
H is a smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample. X is nonempty and proper and carries an R561 boundary-reversed Hamilton dimer. The tau=1 specialization additionally assumes a partition V(H)=D sqcup S sqcup C with X=H[D union S] Hamiltonian, and a literal exact two-cover of H-D with exactly one S|C transition, so R560 supplies b_C=2 with one mixed C-block and one pure C-rail.

## Scope
Smallest-counterexample consumer of R561+R156, with a tau=1 block-size corollary from R560. Order-free in |X| and |H| except for the standing smallest-counterexample deletion floor used by R156. Complements the order-free spanning obstruction R578, which kills only the mixed singleton and does not use minimality.

## Applicability
Use after an R561 certificate has been manufactured on an absorber or other proper set. The no-singleton residual is the correct first consumer of universal extension before any attempt to merge C-blocks or to run R567 against D union C. In tau=1 cells it gives a uniform floor |B_C|>=2 and |pure C-rail|>=2.

## Persistence
The reversed dimer on X, the universal one-vertex extensions, pc(H-X)=2, and the no-singleton residual are graph-intrinsic. In the tau=1 specialization the two C-blocks of T remain representative-relative to T.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not produce the reversed Hamilton dimer. Does not make D union C Hamiltonian. Does not force a second Hamilton order at a crossing endpoint. Does not by itself span H. Does not apply outside smallest counterexamples, except that the mixed-singleton spanning obstruction remains available from R578 without minimality.

## Proof
By R561, a boundary-reversed Hamilton dimer on X makes X a universal one-vertex absorber: for every r outside X, exactly one of the antisymmetric turns (r,u,v) and (v,u,r) is tight, and that tight turn Hamilton-extends X by prepending r to the start-path or appending r to the end-path. This is precisely the universal-extension hypothesis of R156. R156 therefore yields pc(H-X)=2, and moreover every exact two-cover of H-X has both rails nontrivial.

Now specialize to a tau=1 cell. Let V(H)=D sqcup S sqcup C with S,C nonempty, X=H[D union S] Hamiltonian, and T a literal exact two-cover of H-D with exactly one selected S|C transition. R560 gives the unique-transition normal form: exactly one rail of T is mixed and consists of one S-block covering all of S together with one C-block B_C, and the other rail is a pure C-rail. Those two C-blocks partition C and are themselves tight paths, so they form an exact two-cover of H-X=H[C]. The no-singleton clause of R156 applied to this cover forces |B_C|>=2 and forces the pure C-rail to have order at least two.

The mixed singleton B_C={y} is already impossible on order-free grounds by R578 whenever the same reversed dimer is present, because R561 would then Hamilton-extend X by y and the remaining pure C-rail would complete a spanning two-cover of H. The present theorem adds the symmetric singleton prohibition on the pure C-rail, which requires the smallest-counterexample rigidity R156 rather than a direct spanning construction.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R581.md -->

# FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R582.md

<!-- BEGIN FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R582.md -->

# R582 — Two-ended middle gates force an endpoint-favorable five-path

## Statement
Let X={a,b,c,z} be a transitive matching-height four-cell with M_R={ab,cz}>M_S={ac,bz}>M_L={bc,az}, and let L,R be distinct exterior vertices. Suppose at L one M_S edge is fully outgoing and its complementary M_S edge fully incoming, while at R one M_S edge is fully incoming and its complement fully outgoing. After an automorphism of the labelled matching-height cell, assume the L-outgoing M_S edge is {b,z}, so Lbz,Lzb,acL,caL are tight. The R-incoming M_S edge is then either {b,z} (aligned) or {a,c} (crossed). For x in X call a Hamilton tight P5 K_x on {L,R} union (X-{x}) endpoint-favorable if the position of L in K_x is not 1 or 2, or the position of R is not 2 or 3, with positions numbered 0,...,4. Then some x in X has an endpoint-favorable K_x. Equivalently, it is impossible for every Hamilton P5 on every {L,R} union (X-{x}) to place L only in positions 1,2 and R only in positions 2,3.

## Hypotheses
Strong Level-(1) exact reversal antisymmetry; X is the displayed transitive matching-height four-cell; the two exterior vertices carry the displayed full M_S gate polarities.

## Scope
Pure six-vertex gate lemma; no smallest-counterexample, deletion-cover, global-longest, R24, or computation hypothesis.

## Applicability
Use with L=q_0,R=q_m in the transitive R24 frame. Combined with R540, endpoint-favorability makes one endpoint-cut spanning proposal have exactly one uncertified turn.

## Persistence
Retain the physical six-set, aligned/crossed gate type, the explicit favorable Hamilton P5, omitted x, and its L/R positions.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not say which x is favorable. Does not say the resulting R540 one-hole mate is new information or closes H. Does not assert a Hamilton P6 on the six-set.

## Proof
Relabel within the matching-height cell so the L-outgoing M_S edge is {b,z}. Thus Lbz,Lzb,acL,caL are tight. The matching-height orientation of X supplies, among others, zbc,caz,zca,acb,bac,baz tight. Assume for contradiction that no endpoint-favorable K_x exists. Then every displayed candidate below, each of which uses {L,R} union (X-{x}) for the indicated omitted x and has L or R in a favorable position, must fail at a turn not already certified. Boundary antisymmetry R3 then supplies the complete reverse of that bad turn.

CROSSED CASE. Here the R-incoming M_S edge is {a,c}, so acR,caR,Rbz,Rzb are tight.
1. Candidate (L,R,z,b,c), omitting a, has Rzb and zbc tight. Since L is in position 0 it is favorable; therefore LRz is bad and zRL is tight.
2. Candidate (R,z,c,a,L), omitting b, has zca and caL tight. Since R is in position 0, Rzc is bad and czR is tight.
3. Candidate (c,z,R,L,a), omitting b, now has czR and zRL tight. Since L is in position 3, RLa is bad and aLR is tight.
4. But (z,c,a,L,R), omitting b, has zca, caL, aLR tight. It is endpoint-favorable (L position 3, R position 4), contradiction.

ALIGNED CASE. Here the R-incoming M_S edge is also {b,z}, so bzR,zbR,Rac,Rca are tight.
1. (L,b,z,R,c), omit a: Lbz,bzR tight, so zRc is bad and cRz tight.
2. (c,L,b,z,R), omit a: Lbz,bzR tight, so cLb is bad and bLc tight.
3. (L,R,c,a,z), omit b: Rca,caz tight, so LRc is bad and cRL tight.
4. (z,c,a,L,R), omit b: zca,caL tight, so aLR is bad and RLa tight.
5. (L,R,a,c,b), omit z: Rac,acb tight, so LRa is bad and aRL tight.
6. (b,a,c,L,R), omit z: bac,acL tight, so cLR is bad and RLc tight.
7. (c,R,L,a,z), omit b: cRL,RLa tight, so Laz is bad and zaL tight.
8. (c,R,z,a,L), omit b: cRz,zaL tight, so Rza is bad and azR tight.
9. (L,b,a,z,R), omit c: baz,azR tight, so Lba is bad and abL tight.
10. (R,a,b,L,c), omit z: abL,bLc tight, so Rab is bad and baR tight.
11. Finally (b,a,R,L,c), omitting z, has baR,aRL,RLc all tight. Since L is in position 3, this is an endpoint-favorable Hamilton P5, contradiction.

The two cases exhaust the two M_S edges available for the R-incoming gate. Thus some endpoint-favorable K_x exists. The proof is a finite explicit forcing chain and uses no computational assertion.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R582.md -->

# R583 — Four-vertex complement forces a synchronized full insertion-obstruction array

## Statement
Let H be a finite Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament with pc(H)>2. Let Q=(q_0,...,q_m), m>=1, be a vertex-simple tight path whose complement X=V(H)\\V(Q) has exactly four vertices. Then for every x in X, the induced subsystem on V(Q) union {x} is non-Hamiltonian. Consequently, for every gap i=0,...,m-1, the literal order obtained by inserting x between q_i and q_{i+1} fails. Define the present insertion turns A_i(x)=(q_{i-1},q_i,x) when i>=1, B_i(x)=(q_i,x,q_{i+1}), and C_i(x)=(x,q_{i+1},q_{i+2}) when i+2<=m. At least one present turn is bad, so by R3 at least one corresponding exact reverse turn Abar_i(x)=(x,q_i,q_{i-1}), Bbar_i(x)=(q_{i+1},x,q_i), Cbar_i(x)=(q_{i+2},q_{i+1},x) is tight. These gap clauses hold simultaneously for all four x on the same ordered Q. For every internal gap 1<=i<=m-2, at least one of the following occurs: two distinct x,y in X have both Abar_i(x),Abar_i(y) tight, giving a same-oriented two-witness packet on (q_i,q_{i-1}); two distinct x,y have both Cbar_i(x),Cbar_i(y) tight, giving such a packet on (q_{i+2},q_{i+1}); or two distinct x,y have both reverse-middle turns Bbar_i(x)=(q_{i+1},x,q_i) and Bbar_i(y)=(q_{i+1},y,q_i) tight. At the left endpoint gap i=0 with m>=2, absent a two-witness packet among the Cbar_0(x), at least three distinct x have Bbar_0(x) tight; the exact right-end dual holds. Thus an order-three singleton-deletion rail frame does not merely have endpoint reverse stars: its four-vertex complement imposes a synchronized obstruction array along every gap of the long rail.

## Hypotheses
Strong Level-(1) boundary antisymmetry; pc(H)>2; Q is a tight path; exactly four vertices lie outside Q.

## Scope
Order-free four-vertex-complement parent theorem. It does not require smallest-counterexample minimality, R24, global-longestness, a transitive/cyclic four-cell classification, or a deletion-root normalization.

## Applicability
In the live R24 restoration, if H-z=P sqcup Q is an exact singleton-deletion two-cover with |P|=3, then X=V(P) union {z} is exactly the four-vertex complement of Q, so the full four-witness gap array applies immediately. Use it as a scalable replacement for endpoint-only seam enumeration and as a source of carrier-position pressure for absorber/transition arguments.

## Persistence
The ordered path Q, the physical exterior set X, every gap index, each reverse-turn disjunction, and every realized two-witness or reverse-middle packet are graph-intrinsic in the fixed frame. No representative change is made.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not choose a unique reverse disjunct at a gap. A reverse-middle pair (q_{i+1},x,q_i),(q_{i+1},y,q_i) is not by itself an R38 same-support collision. A terminal two-witness packet is not claimed to close H. The theorem does not prove R24 or Hamiltonicity of any complementary middle. It does not assume or imply Q is globally longest.

## Proof
Fix x in X. The other three vertices X-{x} support a tight Hamilton trimer by R3. If H[V(Q) union {x}] had a Hamilton tight path K_x in any order, then K_x together with that trimer would be a spanning two-cover of H, contradicting pc(H)>2. Hence V(Q) union {x} is non-Hamiltonian. In particular, for each gap i, the literal order Q with x inserted between q_i and q_{i+1} is not tight. Every old Q-turn outside that insertion window remains certified, and the only new turns are the present members of A_i(x),B_i(x),C_i(x). Therefore at least one is bad. R3 makes its complete reversal tight, giving the displayed reverse clause. This works independently for every x and gap, so all clauses coexist as graph-intrinsic facts on one Q. For an internal gap, let L,M,R be the subsets of X for which Abar_i, Bbar_i, Cbar_i respectively are tight. The clause says L union M union R=X. If neither terminal support carries two distinct witnesses, then |L|<=1 and |R|<=1. Since |X|=4, necessarily |M|>=2, proving the trichotomy. At i=0 only M and R occur; if |R|<=1 then |M|>=3. The right endpoint is dual.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R583.md -->

# R584 — Two common reverse-middle blockers force a literal reverse P4 ear

## Statement
Let A,C,x,y be four distinct vertices in a Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament. If (A,x,C) and (A,y,C) are tight, then at least one of (A,x,C,y) and (A,y,C,x) is a tight Hamilton P4. More precisely, if (x,C,y) is tight the first path is tight; if it is bad, R3 makes (y,C,x) tight and the second path is tight. In the R583 gap notation, two reverse-middle blockers Bbar_i(x)=(q_{i+1},x,q_i) and Bbar_i(y)=(q_{i+1},y,q_i) therefore force a literal tight reverse P4 ear across the adjacent carrier state q_i q_{i+1}: either (q_{i+1},x,q_i,y) or (q_{i+1},y,q_i,x).

## Hypotheses
Strong Level-(1) exact complete-reversal antisymmetry; four displayed vertices distinct.

## Scope
Pure four-vertex local lemma, order-free and independent of smallest-counterexample or deletion assumptions.

## Applicability
Use as the direct consumer of the reverse-middle branch of R583. It converts two middle blockers into a labelled P4 with the two Q contacts in reverse carrier order.

## Persistence
Retain the two blocker turns, the tested turn xCy and its status, and the resulting labelled P4.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not by itself splice the reverse P4 into Q, currentize it in a cover, or close H.

## Proof
Assume (A,x,C) and (A,y,C) are tight. Test the turn (x,C,y). If it is tight, then (A,x,C,y) is a tight P4 because its consecutive turns are (A,x,C) and (x,C,y). If (x,C,y) is bad, exact reversal antisymmetry R3 gives (y,C,x) tight; together with the given (A,y,C), this makes (A,y,C,x) a tight P4. Thus one of the two displayed labelled Hamilton P4s always exists. Substituting A=q_{i+1}, C=q_i gives the R583 reverse-ear form.

<!-- BEGIN FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R585.md -->

# R585 — Globally longest support admits no one-vertex Hamilton extension

## Statement
Let H be a finite tight-path system and let K be a globally longest vertex-simple tight path in H. Write X=V(K) and E=V(H)\X. Then for every r in E, the induced subsystem H[X union {r}] is non-Hamiltonian. Equivalently, X admits no one-vertex Hamilton extension into the exterior of K.

Consequently X cannot carry a boundary-reversed Hamilton dimer in the sense of R561 whenever E is nonempty: R561 would Hamilton-extend X by every exterior vertex and produce a tight path of order |X|+1, contradicting global-longestness of K.

In particular, in any tau=1 exact two-cover cell whose Hamiltonian absorber X=H[D union S] coincides with the vertex set of a globally longest path of H, the R561/R578/R581 reversed-dimer branch is unavailable. Dual-absorber or second-order search in that cell cannot proceed by manufacturing an R561 dimer on X.

## Hypotheses
Finite tight-path system; K globally longest; R561 only for the second paragraph (Strong Level-(1) / exact-reversal). The first paragraph is pure length.

## Scope
Order-free. Applies to every globally longest path, independently of deletion size, cover size, or smallest-counterexample minimality.

## Applicability
Use as a negative fence before applying R561, R156, R578, or R581 to an absorber that contains a globally longest path. Forces longest-path tau=1 cells to seek a second Hamilton order or an opposite-side absorber rather than a reversed dimer on X.

## Persistence
The non-extension of X and the unavailability of R561 on X are graph-intrinsic as soon as some globally longest path spans X.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert that X is the unique maximum-order support. Does not forbid Hamilton cycles on X. Does not produce a second Hamilton order at a named crossing endpoint. Does not itself eliminate tau=1.

## Proof
Let K be globally longest of order |X|. Suppose there exists r notin X such that H[X union {r}] has a tight Hamilton path P. Then P is a tight path on |X|+1 vertices, contradicting global-longestness of K. This is independent of which Hamilton path of X is used: every Hamilton path of X union {r} has order |X|+1.

Now suppose E is nonempty and X carries a boundary-reversed Hamilton dimer in the sense of R561. Then every exterior vertex, in particular some r in E, Hamilton-extends X. The preceding paragraph yields a tight path of order |X|+1, contradiction.

If a tau=1 cell has Hamiltonian absorber X equal to the vertex set of a globally longest path, the second paragraph applies and the R561 hypothesis of R578 and R581 cannot hold on that absorber.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R585.md -->

# R589 — Aligned two-ended middle gates force a complete cross-end reverse fan

## Statement
Let H be a finite Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament with pc(H)>2. Let Q=(q_0,...,q_m), m>=2, be a tight path and let X={a,b,c,z} be its four-vertex complement. Put L=q_0 and R=q_m. Assume the aligned complementary middle-gate packet Lbz,Lzb,acL,caL,bzR,zbR,Rac,Rca is tight. Then all eight cross-end middle turns are forced tight: aRz,cRz,aRb,cRb and bLc,zLc,bLa,zLa. Equivalently, every ordered cross pair p in {b,z}, q in {a,c} satisfies p L q tight, and every q in {a,c}, p in {b,z} satisfies q R p tight. Each forced turn is the exact reverse mate of a one-hole Hamilton-P6 candidate on X union {L,R}; the corresponding candidate identity is retained. Thus the aligned two-ended gate packet rigidifies into opposite complete 2-by-2 middle rectangles at the two rail ends.

## Hypotheses
Strong Level-(1) boundary antisymmetry; pc(H)>2; V(H)=X disjoint union V(Q) with |X|=4 and Q=(q_0,...,q_m) tight, m>=2; the eight displayed aligned gate turns are tight.

## Scope
Pure aligned-gate parent theorem. No smallest-counterexample minimality, R24, transitive matching-height classification, global-longestness, capture, or computation is used once the displayed gate packet and complementary tight rail are supplied.

## Applicability
In the accepted exact-two-bad transitive R24 cell R556, the required aligned gate packet is already present with L=q_0,R=q_m. Hence the full eight-turn cross fan follows immediately for every surviving rail length, including the long m>=6 residue of R574. Use these literal endpoint rectangles before invoking R582/R540: in particular cRb and bLa are forced simultaneously, not merely as alternatives.

## Persistence
Retain X,Q,L,R, the original eight aligned gate turns, each of the eight one-hole six-vertex candidates, its unique bad turn, and the exact reversed cross-fan mate. All resulting turn signs are graph-intrinsic.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
The eight-turn fan does not itself force a Hamilton P6; the local six-vertex orientation can remain P6-free. The middle rectangles are not R38 same-support collisions. No claim is made that the fan alone closes R24, creates a second Hamilton absorber, or supplies endpoint-compatible Hamilton multiplicity for R566.

## Proof
Because m>=2, Q^o=(q_1,...,q_{m-1}) is a nonempty tight path. Any tight Hamilton P6 on X union {L,R} would therefore form a spanning two-cover with Q^o, contradicting pc(H)>2. Now test the following eight P6 orders. (1) (L,b,z,R,a,c): Lbz,bzR,Rac are tight, so zRa is bad and aRz tight. (2) (L,b,z,R,c,a): Lbz,bzR,Rca are tight, so zRc is bad and cRz tight. (3) (L,z,b,R,a,c): Lzb,zbR,Rac are tight, so bRa is bad and aRb tight. (4) (L,z,b,R,c,a): Lzb,zbR,Rca are tight, so bRc is bad and cRb tight. Dually, (5) (R,a,c,L,b,z) forces bLc from bad cLb; (6) (R,a,c,L,z,b) forces zLc from bad cLz; (7) (R,c,a,L,b,z) forces bLa from bad aLb; and (8) (R,c,a,L,z,b) forces zLa from bad aLz. These are exactly the claimed two complete middle rectangles.

# FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R593.md

<!-- BEGIN FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R593.md -->

# R593 — Every fifth vertex Hamilton-extends the cyclic no-P4 four-cell

## Statement
Let X={a,b,c,z} be the exact 00 no-Hamilton-P4 four-cell of R516; after labelling, its tight-turn representatives are abc,bca,cab,zba,azb,baz,acz,cza,zac,zcb,bzc,cbz. Then every fifth vertex d outside X lies in a Hamilton tight P5 on X∪{d}, and d can be placed one step from an end: its position is 1 or 3 in a five-vertex order numbered 0,...,4. Consequently, in an order-three singleton-deletion frame, X cannot be the cyclic 00 cell, because such a Hamilton P5 with d=q_0 together with the untouched suffix Q-q_0 would be a spanning two-cover.

## Hypotheses
Strong Level-(1) boundary antisymmetry R3; X is the exact 00 signature from R516; d is distinct from X. For the R24 consequence, Q=(q_0,...,q_m) is the disjoint long rail and m>=1.

## Scope
Universal cyclic-four-cell fifth-vertex extension with near-end placement, plus its fixed-rail singleton-deletion specialization.

## Applicability
Restores the historically cited cyclic-four-set fifth-vertex extension including the near-end placement coordinate; eliminates the cyclic branch in R24 reconstruction.

## Persistence
The Hamilton P5 is graph-intrinsic and retains the identity and near-end position class of d. In the R24 specialization it coexists with the untouched complementary Q suffix.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not guarantee both near-end positions for a fixed orientation and does not prescribe which one occurs. Does not treat transitive no-P4 cells. Does not use legacy R24.

## Proof
Write uvw when the displayed turn is tight. Every candidate below places d in position 1 or 3. Assume none is a tight P5. Each candidate has one X-only turn certified by the 00 row of R516, so its failure converts a tight antecedent mixed turn into the tight complete reversal of its other mixed turn by R3.

Starting with dab:
dab ⇒ adz (zdabc) ⇒ czd (adzcb) ⇒ bdz (aczdb) ⇒ dba (cabdz) ⇒ bdc (cdbaz) ⇒ dbz (azbdc) ⇒ bda (adbzc) ⇒ cad (bdacz) ⇒ zda (bcadz) ⇒ bad (zdabc).

Starting with bad:
bad ⇒ cda (zbadc) ⇒ dcz (bzcda) ⇒ cdb (bdcza) ⇒ abd (cdbaz) ⇒ zdb (cabdz) ⇒ cbd (zdbca) ⇒ adb (zcbda) ⇒ daz (czadb) ⇒ adc (cdazb) ⇒ dab (zbadc).

The turns dab and bad are complete reversals, so exactly one is tight by R3. Either choice forces the other, contradiction. Hence at least one of the sixteen candidate orders is a tight Hamilton P5, and inspection of the displayed candidate names shows d is always in position 1 or 3.

For the R24 specialization take d=q_0. The P5 on X∪{q_0} and the tight suffix (q_1,...,q_m) are disjoint and spanning, contradicting pc(H)>2.

# R594 — R24 failure reduces noncircularly to the synchronized transitive order-three frame

## Statement
Let H be a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample and suppose that for some vertex z an exact two-cover H-z=P⊔Q has a rail P of order at most three. Then the order-one and order-two cases close immediately. In the only surviving case, P has order three and Q has order at least five. Writing X=V(P)∪{z} and Q=(q_0,...,q_m) with m>=4, X is a no-P4 transitive matching-height four-cell. For every x∈X, Q together with any tight trimer on X-{x} is a literal exact two-cover of H-x. Both X∪{q_0} and X∪{q_m} are P5-free, and for every x∈X the endpoint reverse stars (q_1,q_0,x) and (x,q_m,q_{m-1}) are tight. After relabelling X as M(ab)=M_R>M(ac)=M_S>M(bc)=M_L, this is exactly the common transitive hard frame used by R543,R554,R576. No dependency in this reduction uses R24.

## Hypotheses
H is a smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample; H-z has a literal exact two-cover P⊔Q with |P|<=3. Accepted R3,R4,R193,R518,R590.

## Scope
Noncircular normal-form reduction for reconstruction of legacy R24.

## Applicability
Separates the fully reconstructed front half of R24 from the remaining transitive high-badness discharge and supplies all standing hypotheses of R543/R554/R576.

## Persistence
The four deletion roots are graph-intrinsic exact-cover facts on one fixed physical X,Q frame. Endpoint reverse stars and endpoint P5-free conditions hold simultaneously; no selected-state borrowing between deletion-root representatives is asserted.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not close the surviving transitive frame. Does not use R533,R169,R5,R24, or order-ten closure. Does not assert existence of a root with exactly two bad seams.

## Proof
Let H-z=P sqcup Q be the displayed exact two-cover. If |P|=1, adjoining z to P gives a tight dimer; if |P|=2, V(P) union {z} has a tight trimer by R3. Either path together with Q spans H, so |P|=3.

If |Q|=1, adjoining z to Q gives a dimer and P is the other rail. If |Q|=2, V(Q) union {z} has a tight trimer and P is the other rail. If |Q|=3 or 4, then |V(H)| is respectively 7 or 8. Choose any six vertices. R193 supplies a tight P5 on five vertices of that six-set. The remaining vertices form respectively a dimer or a three-set; the latter has a tight trimer by R3. Thus H has a spanning two-cover. Therefore |Q|>=5; write Q=(q_0,...,q_m), m>=4.

Put X=V(P) union {z}. A Hamilton P4 on X together with Q would two-cover H, so X is P4-free. For each x in X, R3 gives a tight trimer on X-{x}; with Q this is a two-cover of H-x. It is exact by R4, since a Hamilton H-x plus singleton x would two-cover H.

A Hamilton P5 on X+q_0 with Q[1,m], or on X+q_m with Q[0,m-1], would two-cover H, so both endpoint five-sets are P5-free. If (x,q_0,q_1) were tight, then (x,q_0,...,q_m) plus a trimer on X-{x} would two-cover H. R3 therefore gives (q_1,q_0,x) tight for every x. Dually (x,q_m,q_{m-1}) is tight for every x.

R518 classifies the P4-free X as transitive matching-height or cyclic 00. Accepted R590 says every fifth vertex Hamilton-extends the cyclic 00 cell. Taking q_0 would contradict the P5-freeness of X+q_0. Hence X is transitive. Relabel M(ab)=M_R>M(ac)=M_S>M(bc)=M_L. This is exactly the synchronized transitive frame used by R543,R554,R576, obtained without R24 or any theorem depending on it.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R594.md -->

# R596 — Synchronized high-side seam roots force explicit inward singleton anchors

## Statement
Retain the common transitive order-three singleton-deletion frame on X and Q=(q_0,...,q_m), m>=3, in which every re-root X-{x} is an exact trimer-plus-Q deletion cover, both endpoint five-cells are P5-free, and the endpoint reverse stars q_1 q_0 y and y q_m q_{m-1} are tight for every y in X. For a deletion root x, let ell_x and r_x be its numbers of bad left and right P-side seams among the three normalized seams. Then there exists a root x_L with ell_{x_L}=3 and a root x_R with r_{x_R}=3. More precisely, x_L is the unique intersection of a root-pair belonging to a fully-bad M_L edge at q_0 and the root-pair belonging to the fully-outgoing M_S edge at q_0; for its normalized trimer (a,b,c), (q_0,a,c,b) is a tight Hamilton P4 on {q_0} union (X-{x_L}), (q_1,q_0,a,c,b) is a tight P5, and q_3 q_2 x_L is tight. Dually, x_R is the intersection of a root-pair belonging to a fully-bad M_R edge at q_m and the root-pair belonging to the fully-incoming M_S edge at q_m; its normalized trimer has a tight P4 (b,a,c,q_m), a tight P5 (b,a,c,q_m,q_{m-1}), and x_R q_{m-2} q_{m-3} is tight. Thus the four-root seam synchronization always currentizes at least one left and one right high-side root into graph-intrinsic inward singleton anchors two positions inside Q. In the equality case of R576 with badness multiset {2,4,5,5}, these are the two distinct five-bad sibling roots.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample; X is a transitive matching-height no-P4 four-cell; Q=(q_0,...,q_m), m>=3, is the common tight rail; every re-root X-{x} with any tight trimer orientation together with Q is an exact cover of H-x; X+q_0 and X+q_m are P5-free; the common endpoint reverse stars hold. Accepted R3,R4,R534,R543,R546,R549,R576.

## Scope
R24 restoration; order-unbounded and noncircular. Converts the unavoidable side-maximal roots hidden in the R576 counting argument into explicit endpoint P5s and named inward anchor turns. No use of R24, R533, R169, R5, or the order-ten closure.

## Applicability
Use at the first and last internal Q gaps. The turns q_3 q_2 x_L and x_R q_{m-2} q_{m-3} are distinguished witnesses in the R583/R588 obstruction arrays and preserve the physical deleted-root labels.

## Persistence
The roots x_L,x_R, their selected M_L/M_S/M_R physical edges, the endpoint P4/P5 orders, and the inward turns are simultaneous graph-intrinsic certificates in the original common frame.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert x_L=x_R or x_L!=x_R outside the R576 equality-two case. Does not make the middle rail Hamiltonian and does not itself produce a spanning two-cover. A single inward anchor is not yet an R542 two-witness packet; a second witness on the same tested reverse dimer is still required for capture/payment.

## Proof
At the left endpoint put L=q_0. For each physical M_L edge e, the two roots whose trimers contain e use the two turns uvL and vuL as their bottom seams. By R546 at least one of these turns is bad for each M_L edge. By R549 some M_L edge e_L is fully outgoing from L. Boundary antisymmetry R3 then makes both incoming seam orientations on e_L bad. Let F_L be the M_S edge fully outgoing from L, supplied by R534 (with the extreme gates supplied by R549). The root-pair containing e_L and the root-pair containing F_L intersect in exactly one root x_L: the three perfect matchings of K_4 give distinct pair partitions of the four deletion roots, and a pair from two distinct partitions meets in one root. Normalize X-{x_L} as (a,b,c) so bc=e_L is its M_L edge and ac=F_L is its M_S edge. Its two bottom seams bcL,cbL are bad because e_L is fully outgoing, and its middle seam acL is bad because F_L is fully outgoing. Hence ell_{x_L}=3. Since F_L is fully outgoing, both Lac and Lca are tight. The matching-height rule gives acb tight (M(ac)=M_S>M(cb)=M_L), so K_L=(L,a,c,b) is a tight Hamilton P4 on {L} union (X-{x_L}). The standing endpoint reverse star gives q_1La tight, hence A_L=(q_1,L,a,c,b) is a tight P5. Its complementary vertex set is W_L={x_L} union {q_2,...,q_m}. If H[W_L] had a Hamilton path, that path together with A_L would be a spanning two-cover of H, contrary to pc(H)>2. Therefore W_L is non-Hamiltonian. The literal order (x_L,q_2,q_3,...,q_m) differs from the tight Q-suffix only in the first turn x_L q_2 q_3. It cannot be tight, so x_L q_2 q_3 is bad and R3 gives q_3 q_2 x_L tight.

The right endpoint is the exact dual. Put R=q_m. R549 supplies an M_R edge e_R fully incoming to R, so R3 makes both outgoing seam orientations on e_R bad. Let F_R be the M_S edge fully incoming to R. The two associated root-pairs meet in a unique root x_R. Normalize X-{x_R} so ab=e_R and ac=F_R. Then its two top seams Rab,Rba and its middle seam Rac are bad, hence r_{x_R}=3. Full incoming polarity of F_R gives acR tight, and the matching-height turn bac is tight, so K_R=(b,a,c,R) is a tight P4. The endpoint reverse star cRq_{m-1} extends it to A_R=(b,a,c,R,q_{m-1}). If W_R={x_R} union {q_0,...,q_{m-2}} were Hamiltonian, W_R together with A_R would two-cover H. Hence the literal order (q_0,...,q_{m-2},x_R) fails at its only new turn q_{m-3}q_{m-2}x_R; R3 yields x_R q_{m-2} q_{m-3} tight.

Finally consider the equality-two configuration in R576. If r is the unique two-bad root, its selected one-bad M_L pair, common good M_S pair, and selected one-bad M_R pair are the three pairs through r. The root sharing only its M_R pair is the left-side three-bad root x_L, while the root sharing only its M_L pair is the right-side three-bad root x_R. These are two different members of the other three roots and are exactly the two five-bad siblings in the {2,4,5,5} law.

# R597 — Endpoint-local synchronized five-badness does not discharge the R24 frame

## Statement
There exists a Strong Level-(1) orientation on six vertices X union {L,R}, with X={a,b,c,z} the transitive matching-height four-cell M_R={ab,cz}>M_S={ac,bz}>M_L={bc,az}, such that both endpoint five-cells X union {L} and X union {R} are Hamilton-P5-free, the full six-cell is Hamilton-P6-free, and, for every root x in X, exactly five of the six normalized R24 seams formed from the three tight trimer orders on X-{x} are bad. Hence neither one five-bad root nor any endpoint-local synchronization of two or all four five-bad roots forces a local Hamilton P6. In particular the R576 total-badness information (even strengthened from total at least 16 to the realized total 20 with badness multiset {5,5,5,5}) cannot by itself discharge R24.

## Hypotheses
Strong Level-(1) exact reversal antisymmetry only; X is the displayed transitive matching-height four-cell. The P5-free and P6-free properties and seam counts are part of the explicit finite certificate.

## Scope
Finite endpoint-local obstruction for the transitive R24 hard frame.

## Applicability
Use as a route fence when attempting to consume R576 or any high-badness sibling-root statement. A successful R24 discharge must add information involving an interior vertex/gap of Q, or a theorem that makes paid descendants/certificates simultaneously current.

## Persistence
Graph-intrinsic finite orientation certificate; independent of descendant currentness.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not construct a global smallest counterexample and does not satisfy or refute the full gapwise R583 array on a long Q. Does not show that Q-interior strengthened discharge is impossible. Does not deny that individual bad seams trigger R542 capture/payment; it shows only that endpoint badness and endpoint Hamilton forcing alone cannot finish.

## Proof
Write uvw for the tight turn (u,v,w). Exactly one tight representative from each reversal pair is:

middle a: Laz, RaL, baL, baR, bac, baz, caL, caR, caz, zaR.
middle b: Lba, Lbc, Lbz, RbL, Rbc, Rbz, abR, abc, abz, zbc.
middle c: LcR, Lcb, Rcb, acL, acR, acb, zcL, zcR, zca, zcb.
middle z: LzR, Lza, Lzb, Rza, Rzb, bza, czL, czR, cza, czb.
middle L: aLR, bLR, bLa, bLc, bLz, cLR, cLa, zLR, zLa, zLc.
middle R: aRL, bRL, bRa, bRc, bRz, cRL, cRa, zRL, zRa, zRc.

Each middle has ten unordered endpoint pairs, so these 60 words define a Strong orientation. Its X-only representatives are precisely the matching-height orientation. Direct lookup over the 120 orders of X+L and 120 orders of X+R finds a missing consecutive turn in every order; direct lookup over all 720 six-orders does likewise. Thus the endpoint cells are P5-free and the six-cell P6-free.

The six normalized seams, with + tight and - bad, are:
root a: zbL-, bcL-, cbL-, Rcz-, Rzb+, Rzc-;
root b: azL-, zaL-, caL+, Rca-, Rcz-, Rzc-;
root c: bzL-, azL-, zaL-, Rab-, Rba-, Rbz+;
root z: bcL-, cbL-, acL+, Rab-, Rac-, Rba-.
Every root therefore has exactly five bad seams. All checks are literal finite lookups in the displayed complete orientation table, and no circular result is used.

# R598 — High-side R24 roots absorb two rail vertices into exact enlarged deletion covers

## Statement
In the synchronized transitive R24 frame of R596, the unavoidable side-maximal roots x_L and x_R give literal exact two-covers
H-x_L = (q_1,q_0,a,c,b) sqcup (q_2,...,q_m)
and
H-x_R = (q_0,...,q_{m-2}) sqcup (b,a,c,q_m,q_{m-1}),
where (a,b,c) denotes the corresponding normalized trimer in each root. Thus a three-seam side-maximal root is not merely a collision or inward-star certificate: it re-roots the deleted singleton and absorbs exactly two named physical vertices from that end of Q into a tight rail of order five, while preserving the remaining Q interval literally. Both enlarged roots coexist as graph-intrinsic cover certificates in the original H.

## Hypotheses
Accepted common transitive R24 hard frame and pending R596 with m>=3.

## Scope
Noncircular R24 restoration corollary. Exact literal cover and shortened-Q coordinates; no maximin normalization is asserted.

## Applicability
Provides the two one-sided enlarged roots that must be compared or iterated in the remaining long-middle branch.

## Persistence
The deleted labels x_L,x_R, absorbed endpoint pairs {q_0,q_1},{q_{m-1},q_m}, complete P5 orders, and untouched Q suffix/prefix remain literal.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert x_L=x_R. Does not say the order-five rail is globally longest or maximin. The two exact covers generally delete different vertices and therefore are not automatically simultaneous current covers of one deletion.

## Proof
R596 gives the tight path A_L=(q_1,q_0,a,c,b) on {q_0,q_1} union (X-{x_L}). The untouched suffix B_L=(q_2,...,q_m) is tight because it is an interval of Q. Their supports are disjoint and their union is V(H)-{x_L}; hence A_L sqcup B_L is a literal two-cover of H-x_L. It is exact: if H-x_L had a Hamilton tight path, that path together with the singleton (x_L) would be a spanning two-cover of H, contradicting pc(H)>2. This proves the left formula and records that precisely q_0,q_1 were absorbed from Q.

Dually, R596 gives A_R=(b,a,c,q_m,q_{m-1}) and the untouched prefix B_R=(q_0,...,q_{m-2}). They partition H-x_R and are tight. A Hamilton path of H-x_R would again pair with singleton x_R to two-cover H, so this displayed cover is exact. Both are literal facts of the same H, although their deleted labels may differ.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R598.md -->

# R613 — One-sided gap-1 EAR data do not force the first R24 zipper switch

## Statement
There exists a Strong Level-(1) orientation F on V=X∪{L,u,v,w}, where X={a,b,c,z}, with all of the following simultaneous properties.

(1) X is the transitive matching-height four-cell M_R={ab,cz}>M_S={ac,bz}>M_L={bc,az}.

(2) (L,u,v,w) is tight; (u,L,x) is tight for every x∈X; Lbc,Lcb,Lac,Lca are tight; and wvz is tight. In particular z has exactly the left high-side R596/R598 seed order (u,L,a,c,b) and the inward anchor wvz, with L=q_0,u=q_1,v=q_2,w=q_3.

(3) X∪{L} is Hamilton-P5-free.

(4) At the gap u|v, with original insertion turns A_x=(L,u,x), B_x=(u,x,v), C_x=(x,v,w), the tightness rows are (T,F,T) for x=a,b,c and (T,T,F) for x=z. Thus there are no reverse-A witnesses, the only reverse-C witness is the distinguished anchor z, and the three reverse-middle turns vau,vbu,vcu are tight. The R583/R588 outcome is therefore genuinely the EAR branch, not a hidden terminal two-witness branch; indeed for every x<y in {a,b,c}, (v,y,u,x) is a literal tight P4 ear.

(5) More strongly, every tight path in F ending with v,w has order at most four. The only such paths of order four are (c,u,v,w),(z,u,v,w),(L,u,v,w). Consequently, for every nonempty Y⊆X there is no Hamilton path on {L,u,v,w}∪Y ending in v,w. This realizes the full one-sided prefix-subset obstruction through q_3 that would follow in the R24 frame by concatenation to Q[4,m].

(6) For every root r∈X there is no Hamilton path on (X−{r})∪{L,u,v} beginning at v. Hence none of the four proposed advanced states L(2,r) exists.

Therefore the left seed R598, its distinguished R596 anchor, the complete gap-1 R583 clause, even a literal R588 EAR, and all one-sided prefix-compatible nonextension information through q_3 do not by themselves compile to a first root-switched zipper state. Any valid zipper theorem must use additional retained data—such as a nonlocal/right-root coordinate, a payment descendant with an explicit cover interpretation, or a stronger state invariant—not merely the one-sided local packet.

## Hypotheses
Only Strong Level-(1) boundary antisymmetry. The construction is a finite eight-vertex orientation and does not assume a smallest counterexample.

## Scope
Durable R24 strategy fence. It refutes the proposed local inference from the one-sided R596/R598 seed plus the gap-1 R583/R588 EAR data, even after adding every prefix-subset obstruction visible on X∪Q[0,3].

## Applicability
Use when designing the carrier-indexed zipper. A sound first transition must retain and consume data absent from this model, most plausibly the synchronized right root or an explicitly currentized R542 descendant. Do not spend further effort trying to derive L(2,r) solely from the left eight-vertex packet.

## Persistence
Retain the physical labels X,L,u,v,w; root z; seed order (u,L,a,c,b); gap index u|v; exact A/B/C tightness rows; the three reverse-middle witnesses and literal EARs; and the two obstruction families in (5),(6).

## Exclusions / nonclaims
This is not a counterexample to R24, does not have pc(F)>2, and does not claim the local orientation extends to a hypothetical smallest counterexample. It does not refute a nonlocal exchange using the simultaneous right root, exact pair-deletion covers, or the full internal structure of an R542 payment continuation. It refutes only conclusions whose used hypotheses are contained in the explicitly realized one-sided packet.

## Proof
Order the vertices
a<b<c<z<L<u<v<w.
For a middle vertex y and endpoints p<q, the following table lists exactly those canonical turns pyq that are tight. Every unlisted canonical turn pyq is bad, and its complete reversal qyp is tight. Thus the table defines a Strong Level-(1) orientation by construction.

middle a: bac, baz, baL, bau, caz, Lau.
middle b: abc, abz, abL, abu, zbL, zbu.
middle c: acb.
middle z: azv, bzL, bzv, czL, czv, Lzv, uzv.
middle L: aLb, aLz, aLv, bLv, cLz, cLv, zLv, uLv.
middle u: cuv, zuv, Luv.
middle v: avw, bvw, cvw, uvw.
middle w: none.

Restricting the table to X gives exactly the matching-height rule M_R>M_S>M_L. It also gives Luv,uvw; uLx for all x∈X; Lbc,Lcb,Lac,Lca; and wvz. Hence (u,L,a,c,b) is tight: its turns are uLa,Lac,acb.

We first verify X+L is P5-free without an oracle. The complete list of tight P4s in this five-set is
abzL, aLbc, baLz, czbL, czLb, cLaz, cLza, zLbc, Lacb, Lcaz, Lcza, Lczb.
For these twelve orders, respectively, the unused vertex would require the final turn
zLc, bcz, Lzc, bLa, Lba, azb, zab, bca, cbz, azb, zab, zba.
Every displayed required turn is bad in the table. Any Hamilton P5 has a tight P4 prefix, so none exists.

At gap u|v, direct table lookup gives
(A_x,B_x,C_x)=(T,F,T) for x=a,b,c,
and (A_z,B_z,C_z)=(T,T,F).
Reversal therefore gives vau,vbu,vcu and wvz tight, with every x u L bad and wav,wbv,wcv bad. There are no two reverse-terminal witnesses. For x<y in {a,b,c}, vyu is one of the three reverse-middle turns and yux is the reversal of the unlisted canonical turn xuy; hence (v,y,u,x) is a tight P4 ear.

The prefix-subset obstruction is also read off completely. The tight paths ending v,w of order three are
avw,bvw,cvw,uvw,
and the tight ones of order four are
cuvw,zuvw,Luvw.
There is no order-five continuation: a predecessor of cuvw would require pcu, a predecessor of zuvw would require pzu, and a predecessor of Luvw would require pLu; every such turn with a still-unused p is bad in the table. The only listed path containing both L and u is Luvw, and it contains no X-vertex. This proves (5).

Finally fix a deleted root r and inspect tight paths on S_r=(X−{r})∪{L,u,v} that begin at v. The complete lists of order-five prefixes are as follows; after the slash is the unused sixth vertex and the required final turn, which is bad:

r=a:
vczbL / u, bLu;
vczbu / L, buL;
vczLb / u, Lbu;
vcubL / z, bLz.

r=b:
vcLaz / u, azu;
vcLau / z, auz;
vcLza / u, zau;
vcuaz / L, azL.

r=c:
vabzL / u, zLu;
vbaLz / u, Lzu;
vbuaz / L, azL.

r=z:
vaLbc / u, bcu;
vbuac / L, acL;
vcLau / b, aub;
vcubL / a, bLa;
vuacb / L, cbL.

Successive extension using the middle-tournament table gives exactly these prefixes. Since every Hamilton P6 beginning at v would have one of them as its first five vertices, and every listed final turn is bad, no such P6 exists for any r. This proves (6) and the claimed insufficiency fence.

# R619 — Middle-gate polarity partitions all four R24 roots into synchronized enlarged-cover pairs

## Statement
Retain the synchronized transitive order-three R24 frame with X={a,b,c,z}, M_R={ab,cz}>M_S={ac,bz}>M_L={bc,az}, Q=(q_0,...,q_m), m>=4, and write L=q_0, u=q_1, R=q_m, s=q_{m-1}. Normalize the left fully outgoing M_S gate to e_L={a,c}; hence its complementary M_S edge is f_L={b,z}. Then both roots in f_L, not only the distinguished high-side root, have literal exact left-enlarged singleton-deletion covers: H-z=(u,L,a,c,b) sqcup Q[2,m] and H-b=(u,L,c,a,z) sqcup Q[2,m]. Let e_R be the fully incoming M_S edge at R and f_R its complement. Both roots in f_R have literal exact right-enlarged covers obtained by the right dual of R536. Consequently the two-ended geometry has exactly two phases. (A) Aligned phase e_R=e_L={a,c}: f_R=f_L={b,z}, and both H-z and H-b carry simultaneous opposite-end enlarged covers. Explicitly, H-z also equals Q[0,m-2] sqcup (b,a,c,R,s), while H-b also equals Q[0,m-2] sqcup (z,c,a,R,s). For r=z the left/right pair of covers has cross states L a, q_{m-2}s, u q_2, cR; for r=b it has cross states Lc, q_{m-2}s, u q_2, aR. Each selected state crosses the two components of the opposite cover, so R176 gives a balanced opposite-sign pair birth from each state, with the same deleted root and both physical Q cuts retained. (B) Crossed phase e_R={b,z}: f_R={a,c}. Then the right enlarged covers are H-c=Q[0,m-2] sqcup (a,b,z,R,s) and H-a=Q[0,m-2] sqcup (c,z,b,R,s). Thus the four roots split cleanly into the left-enlarged pair {b,z} and the right-enlarged pair {a,c}. In particular the residual branch previously phrased as x_R in {a,c} is exactly the crossed middle-gate phase, not a one-root exception.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in the accepted synchronized transitive R24 frame of R594; X={a,b,c,z} has the displayed matching-height orientation; Q=(q_0,...,q_m) with m>=4 is the common tight rail; both endpoint five-cells are P5-free with the common endpoint reverse stars. # R621 — Crossed middle gates force four asymmetric opposite-end singleton-deletion weaves

## Statement
Retain the crossed middle-gate phase of R619 with X={a,b,c,z}, M_R={ab,cz}>M_S={ac,bz}>M_L={bc,az}, Q=(q_0,...,q_m), m>=4, and write L=q_0, u=q_1, R=q_m, s=q_{m-1}. Thus the left M_S gate {a,c} is fully outgoing from L and its complement {b,z} fully incoming to L, while at the right endpoint {b,z} is fully incoming to R and {a,c} fully outgoing from R. R619 gives the deep enlarged covers
H-z=(u,L,a,c,b) sqcup Q[2,m],
H-b=(u,L,c,a,z) sqcup Q[2,m],
H-c=Q[0,m-2] sqcup (a,b,z,R,s),
H-a=Q[0,m-2] sqcup (c,z,b,R,s).

Then every one of the four roots also has a literal exact opposite-end shallow cover:
H-z=Q[0,m-1] sqcup (R,a,c,b),
H-b=Q[0,m-1] sqcup (R,c,a,z),
H-c=(a,b,z,L) sqcup Q[1,m],
H-a=(c,z,b,L) sqcup Q[1,m].

Consequently every singleton deletion H-r in the crossed phase carries two distinct exact two-covers with opposite-end absorption. For the left-enlarged roots z,b the native cover absorbs {L,u} and the shallow opposite cover absorbs {R}; their four selected cross states, comparing the two covers in both directions, are respectively
r=z: L a, s R, u q_2, R a;
r=b: L c, s R, u q_2, R c.
For the right-enlarged roots c,a the shallow opposite cover absorbs {L} and the native cover absorbs {s,R}; their four selected cross states are respectively
r=c: z L, q_{m-2}s, L u, z R;
r=a: b L, q_{m-2}s, L u, b R.
Each displayed state joins the two components of the opposite exact cover, so R176 yields a graph-intrinsic balanced opposite-sign pair birth from every one of the sixteen root-labelled cross states. Thus the crossed phase is not a no-weave residue: it contains four asymmetric 2-versus-1 endpoint-absorption singleton-deletion weaves. The asymmetry is only that each root retains the deep physical Q cut on its native enlarged side and the outermost Q cut on the opposite side.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in the crossed phase of pending R619; Q=(q_0,...,q_m) with m>=4. Use the exact deep covers and the complementary M_S gate polarities supplied by R619/R534, singleton-deletion exactness from R4, and R176 for the cross-state pair births.

## Scope
Noncircular R24 restoration. Fixed crossed-polarity frame; exact singleton-deletion covers and cross-state weave structure. No pair-deletion staircase, generic payment descendant, or order-ten closure is used.

## Applicability
Use before entering the mixed pair-deletion staircase. In the crossed phase there is already a same-root opposite-end weave for every deletion root. Downstream work should first test consumers of these four asymmetric weaves, especially consumers sensitive to the native deep cut plus opposite shallow cut, rather than assuming that nonlocal coupling first appears only after deleting a mixed root pair.

## Persistence
Retain the four root labels, both M_S gate edges and polarities, all eight exact singleton-deletion covers, the absorbed Q endpoint sets, and the sixteen root-labelled selected cross states. These are simultaneous graph-intrinsic cover certificates in the original H, although R176 descendants are alternative historical births rather than simultaneously paid representatives.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert that any R176 pair birth closes H, that the sixteen pair births are simultaneously paid/current, or that the shallow cover can be extended one further Q vertex. Does not by itself discharge the crossed phase. Does not invalidate R620; it shows only that the pair-deletion staircase is not the earliest available nonlocal weave.

## Proof
By R619, in the crossed phase {a,c} is the left fully outgoing M_S edge and {b,z} its fully incoming complement; at the right endpoint {b,z} is fully incoming and {a,c} its fully outgoing complement. The four displayed deep covers are exactly those of R619.

For root z, the deep left P5 contains the tight turn (a,c,b). Since {a,c} is fully outgoing from R, (R,a,c) is tight. Hence (R,a,c,b) is a tight P4. Together with the untouched Q[0,m-1] it covers H-z. Exactness follows from R4: if H-z were Hamiltonian, that Hamilton path plus singleton z would two-cover H. Thus H-z=Q[0,m-1] sqcup (R,a,c,b). The same argument with the deep H-b P5 turn (c,a,z) and the tight gate turn (R,c,a) gives H-b=Q[0,m-1] sqcup (R,c,a,z).

Dually, for root c the deep right P5 contains the tight turn (a,b,z). Since {b,z} is fully incoming to L, (b,z,L) is tight. Hence (a,b,z,L) is a tight P4, and with Q[1,m] it gives an exact cover of H-c. For root a, (c,z,b) is a turn of the deep right P5 and (z,b,L) is tight from the same fully incoming left gate, giving the exact cover H-a=(c,z,b,L) sqcup Q[1,m].

Now compare each shallow cover with its deep cover. For H-z, the shallow cover selects L a and s R across the two deep components, while the deep cover selects u q_2 and R a across the two shallow components. For H-b the identical check gives L c, s R, u q_2, R c. For H-c, the shallow cover selects z L and q_{m-2}s across the deep components, while the deep cover selects L u and z R across the shallow components. For H-a the corresponding states are b L, q_{m-2}s, L u, b R. Every comparison is literal from the displayed path orders. Since H-r is proper, R176 applies independently to each selected cross state and gives the stated graph-intrinsic balanced-pair birth. No payment or simultaneous-currentness inference is used.

# R626 — Synchronized two-root left packet still does not force a cover-valued first inward switch

## Statement
There exists a Strong Level-(1) orientation F on V=X union {L,u,v,w}, X={a,b,c,z}, which simultaneously realizes the full local left high-side data of the synchronized two-root packet while avoiding every cover-valued first inward switch visible on this prefix. Specifically: (1) X is the transitive matching-height no-P4 four-cell M_R={ab,cz}>M_S={ac,bz}>M_L={bc,az}; (L,u,v,w) is tight; X union {L} is Hamilton-P5-free; (u,L,x) is tight for every x in X; and the full left gate turns Lbc,Lcb,Lac,Lca,bzL,zbL,czL,zcL are tight. (2) F-z has the two literal exact two-covers (u,L,a,c,b) sqcup (v,w) and (L,a,c,b) sqcup (u,v,w), while F-b has the two literal exact two-covers (u,L,c,a,z) sqcup (v,w) and (L,c,a,z) sqcup (u,v,w). Thus the two enlarged roots share the same local suffix and the same physical frame. (3) Every immediate one-turn left reinsertion proposal from those four covers is blocked in the counterexample direction: Luz,vuz,wvz,aLz,Lub,vub,wvb,cLb are tight; the terminal short-rail mates zbc and bza are also tight in X. Hence the packet contains both R614-type seed-concatenation blockers and the full 2-by-2 witness rectangle on (L,u) and (w,v). (4) Nevertheless neither six-set {L,u,v,a,b,c} nor {L,u,v,a,c,z} has a Hamilton P6. Thus neither synchronized root produces the desired advanced local rail on (X-{r}) union {L,u,v}. (5) More strongly, the only tight paths in F ending with the ordered suffix (v,w) are (v,w), (u,v,w), (c,v,w), (L,u,v,w), and (z,c,v,w); in each case the complementary vertices have no Hamilton path. Hence no pair of disjoint tight paths covering F has one rail ending in (v,w), so no prefix configuration visible on this eight-vertex packet can concatenate with an external continuation of Q after w to give a spanning two-cover. Therefore the synchronized two-root left packet, even after closure-saturating all immediate one-hole proposals, does not by itself compile to a spanning two-cover or an advanced H-r cover A_2 sqcup Q[3,m]. Any valid consumer must import information not contained in this local packet, such as a nonlocal/right-root coordinate or a stronger cross-frame invariant.

## Hypotheses
Only Strong Level-(1) boundary antisymmetry is used for the finite countermodel. The displayed packet reproduces the accepted transitive X geometry, endpoint P5-freeness, left gate data, both synchronized enlarged-root truncations, and all immediate left one-turn reinsertion blockers corresponding to the live R598/R614/R616 frame.

## Scope
Durable R24 strategy fence strengthening R613 after the synchronized two-root refinement. It tests the entire left prefix X union Q[0,3], not a standalone one-sided EAR table.

## Applicability
Use to rule out purely local exact-cover exchange/currentization arguments that consume only the two synchronized left roots and their q0..q3 one-hole blockers. A successful next step must retain an additional nonlocal/right-side coordinate or a stronger invariant tying this packet to another frame.

## Persistence
Retain the eight physical labels L,u,v,w,a,b,c,z; roots b,z; the four local deletion covers; the blocker/mate turns; the complete orientation certificate; the two P6-free advanced six-sets; and the complete list of paths ending v,w with non-Hamilton complements.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not show that the full R24 frame is realizable, does not contradict R616, and does not rule out consumers using right-end/root synchronization, global pair-deletion structure, or other nonlocal information. The countermodel is local and is intended only as an implication fence.

## Proof
Fix the vertex order L<u<v<w<a<b<c<z. For every 3-set {x<y<z}, encode the three reversal pairs by bits eps_1 eps_2 eps_3, where eps_1=1 means xyz is tight (else zyx is tight), eps_2=1 means xzy is tight (else yzx is tight), and eps_3=1 means yxz is tight (else zxy is tight). Every omitted 3-set has code 000. Use the following nonzero codes:

Luv 101; Luw 111; Lua 111; Lub 101; Luc 111; Luz 101; Lva 010; Lwa 110; Lwb 001; Lwz 001; Lab 001; Lac 111; Laz 101; Lbc 110; Lbz 001; Lcz 001; uvw 101; uva 101; uvb 001; uvc 001; uvz 001; uwa 001; uaz 010; ubc 011; vwa 111; vwb 111; vwc 100; vwz 001; vac 010; vaz 010; vbc 110; vcz 001; waz 010; abc 111; abz 101; acz 001.

This assigns exactly one tight orientation in every complete-reversal pair, so F is Strong Level-(1). Direct evaluation gives the matching-height rule on X, the tight rail (L,u,v,w), the endpoint star (u,L,x) for all x in X, and the full left gate packet Lbc,Lcb,Lac,Lca,bzL,zbL,czL,zcL. The paths (u,L,a,c,b), (L,a,c,b), (u,v,w), (u,L,c,a,z), and (L,c,a,z) are tight, so the four displayed deletion two-covers are literal. Exhaustive enumeration of all 7! orders shows that F-z and F-b each have zero Hamilton paths. Hence those displayed two-covers are exact.

The same certificate gives Luz,vuz,wvz,aLz,Lub,vub,wvb,cLb,zbc,bza tight. Exhaustive enumeration of the 5! orders on X union {L} gives zero Hamilton P5s. Enumeration of the 6! orders on {L,u,v,a,b,c} and {L,u,v,a,c,z} gives zero Hamilton P6s.

Finally enumerate every vertex-simple tight path ending with ordered dimer (v,w). There are exactly five: (v,w), (u,v,w), (c,v,w), (L,u,v,w), and (z,c,v,w). For the complementary vertex sets of these five paths, exhaustive Hamilton-path counts are respectively 0,0,0,0,0. Therefore no two-path cover of F can have one rail ending (v,w). All conclusions follow from this finite complete-reversal certificate. The certificate was located by a 0-1 feasibility search, but the proof is the explicit orientation table plus exhaustive finite verification; no solver assumption enters the mathematical conclusion.
