# R654 — Every vertex of a smallest counterexample is a universal preserved floor coordinate

## Statement
Let H be a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample. Fix any vertex p and any prescribed target x!=p. Then there is a finite chosen certificate-retaining continuation yielding either a spanning two-cover of H or an ancestry-bearing mass-two balanced-pair floor whose singleton supports are exactly {p,x}, with p preserved as a literal singleton coordinate during the final target-steering step. In fact choose any auxiliary vertex t distinct from p (and arbitrary relative to x). Pair-Deletion Rigidity gives an exact two-cover H-{p,t}=U sqcup V with both rails nontrivial. Split U at any selected adjacent state yz into two nonempty contiguous tight subpaths A and B. Then R=A sqcup B sqcup V is a literal three-cover of the same proper residue W=H-{p,t}, while T=U sqcup V is a literal two-cover selecting yz across the distinct R-components A and B. Apply the fully reconstructed R176 proof to this explicit cross state and choose the arbitrary spare vertex d=p. The resulting balanced opposite-sign pair has one signed support literally singleton (p) and the other support of order at most two. If the opposite support is a singleton, a p-containing floor is already present; otherwise accepted R428 pays that support to singleton width while preserving (p). Finally accepted R432 preserves p and replaces only the other singleton by the prescribed x. Thus every physical vertex is universally steerable to a floor with every chosen partner. Different choices of p,x,t and split state are alternative lineages.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample. Use accepted Pair-Deletion Rigidity R429, fully reconstructible cross-state upgrade R176, fixed-singleton descent R428, and complete floor steering R432.

## Scope
Order-free global Strong Level-(1) theorem. No R24 frame, transitive four-cell, endpoint, capture, middle-gate, longest-path, or beyond-order-ten hypothesis is used.

## Applicability
Whenever a downstream consumer needs a floor containing a prescribed physical vertex p and any chosen second coordinate x, there is no need for a specialized source packet merely to obtain those coordinates. Delete p with any auxiliary t, split one rail of an exact pair-deletion two-cover, use the split edge as the R176 cross state with spare p, pay while preserving p, then steer the other singleton to x. Specialized floor constructions remain valuable only for the extra ancestry they retain.

## Persistence
Retain p,t; exact pair-deletion cover U sqcup V; chosen split state yz of U; split reference cover A sqcup B sqcup V; R176 birth with literal singleton p; any R428 refund certificates preserving p; and the R432 replacement ledger to target x.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not make different target floors simultaneous or current in one representative. Does not make floor coordinates rare, canonical, or contradictory. Does not preserve arbitrary source geometry beyond the split-cover ancestry. Does not imply specialized floor constructions are redundant when their physical provenance is needed downstream. Does not by itself close H.

## Proof
Fix p and choose any auxiliary t!=p. Accepted Pair-Deletion Rigidity R429 gives an exact two-cover T=U sqcup V of W=H-{p,t}, with both U and V nontrivial. Orient U=(u_0,...,u_k), k>=1, and choose any selected state y z=(u_i,u_{i+1}). Let A=(u_0,...,u_i) and B=(u_{i+1},...,u_k). Both are nonempty contiguous tight subpaths of U. Therefore R=A sqcup B sqcup V is a literal three-component path cover of exactly W. The original T is a literal two-cover of W and selects the directed state yz whose endpoints lie in the distinct R-components A and B.\n\nApply accepted fully reconstructed R176 directly to R,T,yz. Its spare vertex d may be chosen arbitrarily outside W. Since p is outside W, choose d=p. In the nontrivial-source-component case, the P540 construction signs a dimer inside W with common witness z and gives the opposite singleton sign on (p) using the automatic p-z tight dimer; in the singleton-source-component case it signs the source singleton and again gives the opposite singleton (p). Thus in every case the R176 birth has one signed support literally (p), and its opposite support has order at most two.\n\nIf the opposite support is already singleton, retain the resulting ancestry-bearing both-singleton floor {p,v}. If it has order two, apply accepted R428 with (p) as the fixed singleton side. Along its chosen nonclosing continuation p is unchanged and the opposite support strictly descends to singleton width, so closure occurs or a floor {p,v} results.\n\nNow fix the originally prescribed x!=p. Apply accepted R432 with target pair {p,x}. The current floor already shares p with the target, so use the one-coordinate replacement macro preserving p. It yields either a spanning two-cover or the exact ancestry-bearing floor {p,x}. This proves the theorem.

H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in accepted crossed R621; m>=4. Use accepted R621 shallow covers, accepted R594 endpoint reverse stars, R429 pair-deletion exactness, and R3.

## Scope
Noncircular R24 restoration. Crossed phase only. Direct two-hole certificates; removes both R5 and the hidden R358->R168 dependency from earlier routes.

## Applicability
Use as the explicit inward endpoint-star clause packet. Search for sibling clauses/reversals or collision decorations involving u or s; do not treat these as X-local tautologies.

## Persistence
Retain the four shallow covers, the four R594 endpoint-star turns, four pair-deletion covers, four explicit spanning proposals, exact two-hole sets, and eight reverse literals.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert any clause closes H or that the clauses form a cycle. Supersedes R662 for reconstructible noncircular use; no R358,R168,R5,R169,R224,R533.

## Proof
Write L=q_0,u=q_1,R=q_m,s=q_{m-1}.

Root z. R621 gives H-z=Q[0,m-1] sqcup (R,a,c,b). Delete s, leaving Q[0,m-2] sqcup (R,a,c,b), a literal two-cover of H-{z,s}; R429 makes it exact. Accepted R594 gives the endpoint-star turn (z,R,s). Consider P_z=(z,R,s,a,c,b). The turns (z,R,s), (a,c,b), and (R,a,c) are certified; the only uncertified consecutive turns are (R,s,a) and (s,a,c). If both were tight, P_z together with Q[0,m-2] would two-cover H. Hence at least one is bad, so R3 gives (a,s,R) or (c,a,s) tight.

Root b. R621 gives H-b=Q[0,m-1] sqcup (R,c,a,z). Delete s and use R429. R594 gives (b,R,s). The proposal P_b=(b,R,s,c,a,z) has only holes (R,s,c) and (s,c,a), so R3 gives (c,s,R) or (a,c,s).

Root c. R621 gives H-c=(a,b,z,L) sqcup Q[1,m]. Delete u to obtain the exact R429 cover (a,b,z,L) sqcup Q[2,m] of H-{c,u}. R594 gives (u,L,c). The proposal P_c=(a,b,z,u,L,c) inherits (a,b,z) and (u,L,c); its only holes are (b,z,u) and (z,u,L). Thus R3 gives (u,z,b) or (L,u,z).

Root a. From H-a=(c,z,b,L) sqcup Q[1,m], delete u and use R429. R594 gives (u,L,a). The proposal P_a=(c,z,b,u,L,a) has only holes (z,b,u) and (b,u,L), so R3 gives (u,b,z) or (L,u,b).

These are literal physical two-hole certificates. No generic R358 or rail-size theorem is used. Every reverse literal contains u or s, so the clauses are not decided solely by the X matching-height orientation. This proves R668.

# R682 — An inward witness on a crossed middle-gate dimer forces endpoint capture or a cross-end tight trimer

## Statement
Retain the accepted crossed R621/R649 frame with X={a,b,c,z}, endpoints L=q_0 and R=q_m, and let S be any one of the four oriented middle-gate dimers (a,c),(c,a),(b,z),(z,b). Suppose a vertex v outside X union {L,R} is a sign witness on the tested orientation S, with the polarity appropriate to the displayed tight turn. Then every exact two-cover T of H-V(S) has the following nonlocal dichotomy.

(CAP) For at least one endpoint e in {L,R}, T selects a carrier/exterior state on {e,y} with y outside the R649 short carrier K_e=S union {e} and y!=v. Using S with witness v and this same-frame selected crossing, accepted R527 may be oriented to capture e itself. Since S is a dimer, the R526 payment continuation then yields either a spanning two-cover or a certificate-retaining singleton-width descendant, while preserving S, the inward witness v, the physical endpoint e, and the actual selected crossing as source ancestry.

(XET) Otherwise T contains selected states on both physical supports {L,v} and {R,v}. Since v occurs on exactly one T rail and has both L and R as its two selected neighbors, that rail contains either the consecutive order (L,v,R) or (R,v,L); hence one of these is a graph-intrinsic tight trimer. Thus failure of inward-witness capture at both endpoint carriers forces an explicit tight trimer joining the two opposite Q endpoints through v.

The two endpoint crossings needed for the dichotomy are unconditional: R649 supplies for every tested S both a tight trimer carrier K_L with V(K_L)=V(S) union {L} and a tight trimer carrier K_R with V(K_R)=V(S) union {R}. Applying accepted R508 separately to K_L and K_R in the same exact support-deletion cover T forces a selected crossing out of singleton L and a selected crossing out of singleton R. Consequently, for the anchor witnesses v=q_2 or v=q_{m-2} produced by the new five-cell exchange packets, a same-polarity X-dimer collision can no longer be paid anonymously: it either carries that inward anchor into an endpoint-capture lineage or creates the literal cross-end trimer L-v-R / R-v-L.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in accepted crossed R621; S is one oriented middle-gate dimer among (a,c),(c,a),(b,z),(z,b); v is outside X union {L,R} and is an exact sign witness on S. Use accepted R649,R508,R527,R526.

## Scope
Noncircular R24 consumer. Fixed crossed middle-gate X dimers with a new exterior witness. Same exact H-V(S) two-cover is used for both endpoint crossings. No R5,R168,R169,R224,R533,generic R358, or R436.

## Applicability
Use immediately when an anchor-exchange clause adds q_2 or q_{m-2} as a same-polarity witness on an oriented G_3 or G_4 dimer. Choose any exact H-V(S) two-cover and run both endpoint R508 carriers simultaneously. If either endpoint crossing avoids the inward witness, capture that endpoint using the inward witness itself; only if both endpoint crossings are forced through the inward witness does the exact cover contain a cross-end tight trimer.

## Persistence
Retain S and its tested orientation/polarity, inward witness v, the chosen exact H-V(S) cover T, both R649 endpoint carriers K_L,K_R, one selected L-exterior state and one selected R-exterior state. In CAP retain the avoiding crossing, captured endpoint, R527/R526 actualization and later payment ancestry. In XET retain the literal T-rail order L-v-R or R-v-L.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert a singleton-width paid descendant closes H or preserves T as current. Does not assert CAP descendants from L and R coexist; only the source endpoint crossings coexist in T. Does not apply when the additional sign witness lies in X union {L,R}. Does not by itself consume the cross-end trimer.

## Proof
Fix an exact two-cover T of H-V(S). Accepted R649 lists, for each of the four tested orientations S, a tight trimer K_L whose support is V(S) union {L}, and another tight trimer K_R whose support is V(S) union {R}. Concretely, for S=(a,c) these may be (L,c,a) and (R,c,a); for S=(c,a), (L,a,c) and (R,a,c); for S=(b,z), (z,b,L) and (z,b,R); for S=(z,b), (b,z,L) and (b,z,R). Only their supports and tightness matter here.

Apply R508 to the deletion D=V(S), absorbable singleton {L}, recompletion path K_L, and the exact cover T. It forces at least one selected T-state crossing {L} | (V(H)\V(K_L)); write one such physical state as {L,y_L}. Apply R508 again to the same T, now with K_R. It forces a selected state {R,y_R} crossing {R} | (V(H)\V(K_R)). These are simultaneous current facts of the one exact cover T.

If some endpoint crossing avoids v, say y_e!=v for e=L or R, then its physical marker {e,y_e} is disjoint from V(S) union {v}: e is outside S, y_e lies outside K_e and hence outside S and e, and by assumption y_e!=v. Use S as the signed support with exact witness v and apply accepted R527 to the same selected crossing. R527 permits either physical marker endpoint to be designated as the captured signed anchor by orienting the marker accordingly, so designate e. This gives the CAP certificate while retaining S, v, the exact T-state {e,y_e}, marker orientation, and captured endpoint e. Because S has order two, R527 invokes the aligned dimer payment of R526, yielding either a spanning two-cover or a certificate-retaining singleton-width descendant. No later currentness of T is claimed.

Suppose no endpoint crossing avoids v. Then every selected L-exterior crossing is incident with v and every selected R-exterior crossing is incident with v. In particular the two states supplied above have supports {L,v} and {R,v}. The vertex v appears exactly once in the path cover T. Both selected states therefore lie on the same T rail and are the two rail adjacencies incident with v. Since L and R are distinct, v is internal on that rail, with consecutive order either L,v,R or R,v,L. A T rail is a tight path, so its consecutive three-vertex segment is a tight trimer in the corresponding order. This is XET and completes the dichotomy.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R682.md -->

# FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R684.md

<!-- BEGIN FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R684.md -->

# R684 — The R682 cross-end alternative is an entire exact deletion rail

## Statement
Retain the XET branch of pending R682 for an oriented crossed middle-gate dimer S and exterior witness v. Let T be the exact two-cover of H-V(S) used there. Then, after orienting one component, T has the literal form
T = (L,v,R) sqcup P  or  T=(R,v,L) sqcup P,
where the displayed cross-end trimer is an entire T rail and P is a tight Hamilton path on V(H)\(V(S) union {L,v,R}).

Indeed XET arises precisely because no selected carrier/exterior crossing from singleton L in the R649 carrier K_L avoids v, and no such crossing from singleton R in K_R avoids v. The selected states {L,v} and {R,v} lie on one T rail. If L had any second rail-neighbor p, then p lies outside K_L (T omits S and p is distinct from L,v), so {L,p} would be a selected L-exterior crossing avoiding v, contradiction. Hence L is a rail endpoint. The identical argument makes R a rail endpoint. A path rail containing consecutive L-v-R with both L and R endpoints has exactly those three vertices. The other rail therefore spans every remaining vertex of H-V(S).

## Hypotheses
Pending R682 XET branch, with its exact H-V(S) cover T and the two R649 singleton-carrier crossing conditions.

## Scope
Source-frame sharpening of R682. No additional minimality, payment, R358, R436, or small-deletion theorem.

## Applicability
Whenever R682 falls into XET, replace the phrase “cross-end tight trimer” by the stronger exact-cover normal form: the cross-end trimer is one entire rail of H-S and the other rail is Hamiltonian on its complement. Consume this exact two-rail representative before invoking generic trimer machinery.

## Persistence
Retain S,v,T, the orientation L-v-R or R-v-L, the fact that L and R are T-rail endpoints, and the complementary Hamilton rail P.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not itself splice S back into T or produce a spanning two-cover of H. Depends on pending R682.

## Proof
In the XET proof of R682, the same exact cover T selects states on physical supports {L,v} and {R,v}, and no selected carrier/exterior crossing out of L or R avoids v. Both selected states lie on one T rail and give consecutive order L,v,R or R,v,L. Suppose L had a second neighbor p on that rail. Since T is a cover of H-V(S), p is not in S; and p is distinct from L and v. The R649 L-carrier K_L has vertex set V(S) union {L}, so p lies in V(H)\V(K_L). Therefore the selected adjacency {L,p} is a carrier/exterior crossing for K_L that avoids v, contradicting the defining XET assumption. Hence L has no second neighbor and is a rail endpoint. The same argument using K_R makes R a rail endpoint. A vertex-simple path rail containing both endpoints L,R with v as their common consecutive neighbor can contain no additional vertex, so it is exactly (L,v,R) or (R,v,L). Since T has exactly two rails and spans H-V(S), the other rail P contains every vertex outside V(S) union {L,v,R} and is tight. This proves the claim.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R684.md -->

# R686 — Carrier-witness saturation: capture fails only for a single witness with at most two carriers

## Statement
Let H be a Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament with pc(H)>2. Let S be a graph-intrinsic signed tight support with a fixed tested orientation, and let T be one exact two-cover of H-V(S). Let K_1,...,K_k with k>=1 be retained vertex-simple tight carriers with V(K_i)=V(S) union {c_i}, the complementary singletons c_1,...,c_k pairwise distinct. Let W be a nonempty set of exact same-polarity sign witnesses on the tested orientation of S, with W disjoint from V(S) union {c_1,...,c_k}.

Applying accepted R508 once per carrier to the same T, with deletion D=V(S), absorbable block {c_i}, and recompletion path K_i, yields for each i a selected T-state {c_i,y_i} with y_i outside V(K_i)=V(S) union {c_i}. Call these k simultaneous states the forced crossing family of T.

Then the accepted R527 capture/refund branch applies to some crossing/witness pair of this family unless W={v} is a singleton and y_i=v for every i. Since v lies on exactly one rail of the two-path cover T it has at most two selected neighbours, and c_1,...,c_k are distinct, so that exceptional configuration forces k<=2. Consequently:

(i) If |W|>=2, capture is unconditional for every k>=1.
(ii) If |W|=1 and k>=3, capture is unconditional.
(iii) If |W|=1 with W={v} and k=2, then either capture holds, or v is internal on its T rail with selected neighbours c_1 and c_2, so T contains a graph-intrinsic tight trimer of consecutive order (c_1,v,c_2) or (c_2,v,c_1).
(iv) If |W|=1 and k=1, nothing is concluded beyond the R527 dichotomy for that single carrier.

Whenever capture holds, S has order two, and H is a hypothetical smallest counterexample, accepted R526 aligned dimer payment gives a finite certificate-retaining continuation to either a spanning two-cover or a descendant balanced pair with singleton support, retaining S, its tested orientation, the used witness, the exact selected crossing, the chosen marker orientation, and the captured vertex.

The escape in (iii) is the only one, and it is sharp: capture fails exactly when a single available witness is selected-adjacent to every complementary singleton. Accepted R542 is the corner k=1, |W|=2 of clause (i). The CAP/XET dichotomy of pending R682 is the corner k=2, |W|=1 of clause (iii) with c_1,c_2 the two physical endpoints. Clause (ii) is the previously unused corner: three or more carriers with distinct complementary singletons defeat any single witness outright, independently of frame, order, and witness identity.

## Hypotheses
Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament H with pc(H)>2. S is a graph-intrinsic signed tight support with a fixed tested orientation. An exact two-cover T of H-V(S) is supplied, not produced. K_1,...,K_k are retained vertex-simple tight carriers with V(K_i)=V(S) union {c_i} and c_1,...,c_k pairwise distinct. W is a nonempty set of exact same-polarity sign witnesses on the tested orientation, disjoint from V(S) union {c_1,...,c_k}. Uses accepted R508 and R527. The payment clause additionally requires S of order two and H a hypothetical smallest counterexample, via accepted R526.

## Scope
Order-free combinatorial parent theorem for carrier/witness counting. No crossed frame, five-cell residue, order bound, or occupancy normalization. No R5,R168,R169,R224,R533,R24, generic R358, or R436. Does not supply the exact deletion two-cover.

## Applicability
Use whenever a tested signed dimer carries several tight carriers whose supports exceed V(S) by distinct single vertices. Count carriers k and available same-polarity witnesses j: capture is unconditional if j>=2 or k>=3, and only j=1 with k<=2 can escape, the k=2 escape being exactly a c_1-v-c_2 tight trimer. When a frame supplies a third carrier, prefer enlarging the carrier list over hunting for a second witness.

## Persistence
Retain S with tested orientation and polarity, the carrier list and its complementary singletons, the witness set, the chosen exact H-V(S) cover T, the forced crossing family, and in the capture branch the avoiding crossing, the used witness, the marker orientation, the captured vertex, and R527/R526 ancestry. In the k=2 escape retain the literal rail order (c_1,v,c_2).

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not produce the exact deletion two-cover. Does not assert that captures at different complementary singletons coexist as paid descendants, nor that any paid descendant is current in T. Does not assert that the k=2 escape and a capture coexist under its own hypotheses; that requires a third carrier. Does not apply when a witness coincides with a complementary singleton or lies in V(S). Gives no conclusion for k=1 with a single witness beyond R527. Does not by itself consume a cross-end trimer or close H.

## Proof
Fix the exact two-cover T of H-V(S). By definition T is a literal spanning two-path cover T_1 sqcup T_2 of H-V(S).

Step 1 (forced crossing family). Fix i in {1,...,k}. Apply accepted R508 with deletion D=V(S), absorbable block {c_i}, recompletion path Q=K_i, and the cover T. Its hypotheses hold: D is nonempty and proper; {c_i} is a nonempty proper subset of V(H)\D, since c_i is not in V(S) and H has further vertices; K_i is a vertex-simple tight path with vertex set exactly D union {c_i}; T is a literal spanning two-path cover of H-D; and pc(H)>2. R508 therefore forces a selected T-state with exactly one endpoint in {c_i} and the other in (V(H)\V(S))\{c_i}. Write one such physical state as {c_i,y_i}. Because y_i lies outside V(S) union {c_i}=V(K_i), this state is a selected carrier/exterior crossing for the R527 partition C_i=V(K_i)\V(S)={c_i} and E_i=V(H)\V(K_i). All k such states are simultaneous current facts of the single cover T, since only T and the fixed deletion D=V(S) are shared.

Step 2 (when capture applies). Let w be an element of W. Since W is disjoint from V(S) union {c_1,...,c_k}, w is neither in V(S) nor equal to any c_i. Hence the crossing {c_i,y_i} avoids w if and only if y_i is not equal to w. Suppose some pair (i,w) satisfies y_i not equal to w. Apply accepted R527 with retained tight carrier K_i, signed support S with V(S) contained in V(K_i), exact sign witness w outside V(S), the cover T, and this selected carrier/exterior crossing. The physical dimer {c_i,y_i} is disjoint from V(S) union {w}, so the capture/refund branch of R527 applies, and either physical endpoint may be designated as the captured signed anchor by choosing the corresponding marker orientation before actualization; in particular c_i may be designated. This is the capture conclusion.

Step 3 (isolating the escape). Capture therefore fails only when y_i=w for every i and every w in W. If W contained two distinct elements w and w prime, then y_1 would have to equal both, which is impossible. Hence W={v} is a singleton and y_i=v for every i.

Step 4 (the counting step). In that case the states {c_1,v},...,{c_k,v} are all selected in T, and they are pairwise distinct because c_1,...,c_k are pairwise distinct. Each is a rail adjacency incident with v. The vertex v lies in H-V(S) because W is disjoint from V(S), so v occupies exactly one position on exactly one rail of T, and a vertex of a path has at most two adjacencies on that path. Hence k<=2. This establishes clause (i) via Step 3, clause (ii) via this bound, and the dichotomy asserted in clause (iii).

Step 5 (the k=2 escape is a trimer). Suppose k=2 and capture fails. By Steps 3 and 4 the two selected states {c_1,v} and {c_2,v} are exactly the two rail adjacencies at v, so v is internal on its rail with neighbours c_1 and c_2, and that rail contains the consecutive order (c_1,v,c_2) or (c_2,v,c_1). A T rail is a tight path, so this three-vertex segment is a graph-intrinsic tight trimer in the corresponding order.

Step 6 (payment). Suppose capture holds, S has order two, and H is a hypothetical smallest counterexample. Then R527 invokes the aligned dimer payment clause of accepted R526 on S and the oriented marker {c_i,y_i}, which is a tight dimer disjoint from V(S) union {w}, giving a finite certificate-retaining continuation to either a spanning two-cover or a descendant balanced pair with singleton support, while retaining the coordinates listed in the persistence contract. No later currentness of T is claimed.

Step 7 (the two known corners). With k=1 and |W|=2 the single crossing {c_1,y_1} can equal at most one of the two witnesses, so the other witness avoids it and Step 2 gives capture; this is exactly accepted R542. With k=2, |W|=1, and c_1,c_2 the two physical endpoints of the crossed frame, Steps 3 to 5 give the CAP/XET dichotomy of pending R682. The present theorem is therefore a common parent of both, and clause (ii) is the corner neither of them uses.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R686.md -->

# R693 — Short-carrier deletion covers reduce to a physical mate clause or an internal singleton

## Statement
Let H be a finite Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament with pc(H)>2, let K=(k_0,k_1,k_2) be a tight trimer, and take one boundary decomposition D={k_1,k_2}, S={k_0}; the exact dual D={k_0,k_1}, S={k_2} also holds. Let T be any exact two-cover of H-D. Since K is a tight path on exactly D union S, accepted R508 forces at least one selected S|(V(H)\V(K)) transition. Because S is the singleton {k_0}, its transition count tau(T) is exactly its degree in its T-rail and is therefore either one or two. If tau(T)=2, k_0 is internal on its T-rail and both incident selected states are explicit carrier/exterior crossings. If tau(T)=1, k_0 is a T-rail endpoint and T already certifies a physical spanning proposal with at most two holes. More precisely, if the mixed rail has form C-S, the aligned endpoint case of R509/R511 gives a one-hole proposal. If it has form S-C, write the other pure exterior rail as C'=(c_0,...,c_s). Specializing the R511 SC normal form to Q=K, m=2 and i=0 gives the complete hole set {(c_{s-1},c_s,k_1) when s>=1} union {(c_s,k_1,k_2)}, of size one or two. Boundary antisymmetry therefore forces the reverse of the unique hole, or yields the physically certified two-hole mate clause formed by the two reversals. The terminal decomposition D={k_0,k_1}, S={k_2} is the exact reverse dual. Consequently every R542 short-carrier source cover refines before payment to exactly one of two concrete geometries: a degree-one complementary singleton carrying a physical one/two-hole proposal, or a degree-two internal singleton carrying two actual exterior crossings.

## Hypotheses
H is finite Strong Level-(1) with pc(H)>2; K=(k_0,k_1,k_2) is a tight trimer; D is one boundary dimer of K and S is the opposite singleton; T is an exact two-cover of H-D. Use accepted R508, R509, R511, and R3.

## Scope
Order-free short-carrier recompletion reduction. No smallest-counterexample payment, capture, R5, R168, R169, R224, R533, generic R358, or R436.

## Applicability
Apply immediately to the exact boundary-dimer deletion cover in any R542-ready packet. If the complementary singleton is a rail endpoint, retain the exact one/two-hole proposal instead of spending the packet anonymously. Only the internal-singleton degree-two branch still needs a new consumer or endpointization argument.

## Persistence
Retain K,D,S,T, the singleton degree and literal rail position. In the degree-one branch retain the pure exterior rail, displayed spanning proposal, complete hole set, and forced reverse literal or mate clause. In the degree-two branch retain both selected crossings incident with the internal singleton.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not close a physical mate clause, does not consume the internal-singleton branch, and does not assert an exact cover can be chosen with singleton degree one. It does not use capture or payment and does not claim alternative deletion covers coexist.

## Proof
Take D={k_1,k_2}, S={k_0}; the other end is dual. R508 applies with Q=K and forces tau(T)>=1. Since k_0 is a singleton in a path cover, tau(T)=deg_T(k_0) is 1 or 2. Degree two is exactly the stated internal branch. Suppose tau=1. R511(1) gives one pure exterior rail and one mixed rail with the unique S-block at an end. In the C-S orientation, the S block begins at q_0=k_0, so R511(3), j=0, invokes the aligned one-hole case of R509. In the S-C orientation, R511(2) has i=0 for Q=(k_0,k_1,k_2). Its first possible hole is absent because i<1; its other two holes are exactly (c_{s-1},c_s,k_1) when the pure exterior rail has at least two vertices, and (c_s,k_1,k_2). Hence the complete hole set has size one or two, never three. Since pc(H)>2, not all holes can be tight; R3 forces the reverse of the unique hole or gives the two reversed literals as a certified mate clause. Reversing all orders proves the k_2 endpoint case.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R693.md -->

# R696 — Two-witness short-carrier deletion covers refine to mate geometry, dual-witness capture, or a witness sandwich

## Statement
Let H be a finite Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament with pc(H)>2. Let K=(k_0,k_1,k_2) be a tight trimer, let S be one reverse boundary dimer of K, and let e be the complementary singleton V(K)\V(S). Assume S, in its tested orientation, has two distinct same-polarity witnesses w_1,w_2 outside K. Let T be any exact two-cover of H-V(S). Then e has T-degree one or two, and exactly one of the following geometric branches holds. (END) deg_T(e)=1. Then the R511 unique-transition normal form specialized to the trimer K gives a literal spanning two-path proposal of H with complete uncertified-turn set of size one or two; hence boundary antisymmetry gives either one forced reverse turn or a physically certified two-hole mate clause. The unique selected e-exterior state also avoids at least one of w_1,w_2, so R527 captures e in the same frame. (FREE) deg_T(e)=2 and at least one T-neighbor x of e lies outside {w_1,w_2}. Then {e,x} is a selected carrier/exterior state avoiding both witnesses. The same physical crossing can therefore be fed to R527 twice, once with witness w_1 and once with witness w_2, producing two alternative same-frame capture certificates that both designate e while retaining different exact witnesses. No coexistence of the two descendants is asserted. (SANDWICH) deg_T(e)=2 and the two T-neighbors of e are exactly w_1,w_2. Then one T-rail contains the literal consecutive order (w_1,e,w_2) or (w_2,e,w_1), so that ordered triple is a graph-intrinsic tight trimer. Each of its two selected boundary states still captures e using the other witness. Thus every two-witness short-carrier packet has, before anonymous payment, either endpoint mate geometry, a crossing simultaneously usable with either witness, or a literal tight trimer joining the two witnesses through the complementary singleton. In a hypothetical smallest counterexample, every capture branch may additionally be followed by the accepted aligned-dimer payment continuation.

## Hypotheses
Finite Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament H with pc(H)>2; K is a tight trimer; S is a reverse boundary dimer of K with two distinct same-polarity witnesses w_1,w_2 outside K; e is the complementary singleton; T is an exact two-cover of H-V(S). Smallest-counterexample minimality is needed only for the optional aligned payment sentence.

## Scope
Order-free geometric refinement of the accepted R542 short-carrier theorem. It uses only the literal exact deletion cover, singleton degree in a path cover, the accepted R508/R511 recompletion normal form, boundary antisymmetry, and same-frame R527 capture. It does not assume any crossed-frame, five-cell, order bound, protected-contact, or generic growth machinery.

## Applicability
Use whenever an R542-ready two-witness trimer packet appears. Inspect the complementary singleton in an exact support-deletion cover before spending the packet. Degree one exposes a one/two-hole proposal; degree two either gives a selected crossing avoiding both witnesses, allowing witness-selectable capture on one physical state, or forces the two witnesses to be the literal rail-neighbors of the singleton and hence gives a witness-sandwich tight trimer.

## Persistence
Durable parent refinement of two-witness short-carrier capture. The witness-sandwich branch is intended to be reusable when the two witnesses are distinguished physical coordinates such as opposite long-rail endpoints.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not claim the two R527 capture descendants coexist. Does not claim the END mate clause necessarily moves support rather than reminting a witness. Does not claim the witness-sandwich trimer alone closes H.

## Proof
Put D=V(S), W=V(H)-D, and S_0={e}. Since K spans exactly D union S_0, accepted R508 applies to every exact two-cover T of H-D and forces a selected state crossing S_0 | (W-S_0). Because S_0 is the singleton {e}, every selected state incident with e is such a crossing, and the number of such states is deg_T(e). A vertex in a path cover has degree at most two, so deg_T(e) is 1 or 2. If deg_T(e)=1, then tau(T)=1 in the R508 packet (D,S_0,K,T). Accepted R511 applies. Since K has order three, its explicit SC/CS normal forms have at most two uncertified turns: this is the m=2 specialization of the displayed R511 hole sets. Therefore there is a literal spanning two-path proposal with one or two holes. As pc(H)>2, not all holes are tight; R3 yields the reverse of the unique hole, or, in the two-hole case, the certified disjunction of their reversals. The unique selected state {e,x} contains at most one of the distinct witnesses w_1,w_2 and therefore avoids the other, so R527 also captures e in this same cover. Now suppose deg_T(e)=2, and write the two distinct rail-neighbors of e as y,z. If {y,z}={w_1,w_2}, then e is internal on its T-rail and the consecutive rail segment is either (w_1,e,w_2) or (w_2,e,w_1). Every consecutive triple of a T-rail is tight, giving SANDWICH. Moreover {e,w_1} avoids w_2 and {e,w_2} avoids w_1, so either state gives an R527 capture of e using the opposite witness. Finally suppose {y,z}!={w_1,w_2}. Because both sets have size two, at least one neighbor, say x, is not in {w_1,w_2}. Then {e,x} is a selected carrier/exterior crossing and is disjoint from both witnesses. The support S is signed with the same tested polarity by each w_i. Thus the hypotheses of R527 hold separately with the same T, S, and physical selected state {e,x}, first using w_1 and then using w_2. Orient the marker in each application so that e is the designated captured anchor. This produces two alternative valid capture certificates on the same physical crossing, with different retained witnesses. These alternatives need not coexist after actualization. The three branches exhaust deg_T(e)=1,2 and prove the theorem.

# R698 — Paired crossed middle-gate orientations cannot both collapse to cross-end witness sandwiches

## Statement
Retain the accepted crossed R621/R649 frame with endpoints L=q_0 and R=q_m. Fix any exact two-cover T of H-{a,c}. Apply R696 simultaneously to the two R649 X-complementary packets S=(a,c), K=(z,c,a), e=z, witnesses {L,R}, and S=(c,a), K=(b,a,c), e=b, witnesses {L,R}. The SANDWICH branch cannot occur for both packets in the same T. Indeed it would require T to contain both L-z-R (or its reverse) and L-b-R (or its reverse) as consecutive tight rail trimers, equivalently both distinct vertices z and b would have T-neighbor set {L,R}; no disjoint union of paths can contain that configuration. Consequently, in every exact H-{a,c} two-cover, at least one of z,b lies in the R696 END or FREE branch: either that complementary X singleton is a rail endpoint and supplies a literal one/two-hole spanning proposal plus capture, or it has a selected exterior crossing that avoids both L and R and hence can be used to capture the singleton with either endpoint as the retained sign witness. Dually, in every exact two-cover of H-{b,z}, applying R696 to S=(b,z), e=c and S=(z,b), e=a shows that at least one of c,a lies in END or FREE. Thus each crossed middle-gate deletion pair has an unavoidable non-sandwich X-complementary packet: a physical mate geometry or a selected X-exterior crossing simultaneously avoiding both physical Q endpoints.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in the accepted crossed R621/R649 frame. T is any exact two-cover of H-{a,c} or H-{b,z}. Use the two X-complementary R649 packets on the two orientations of the deleted middle-gate dimer and pending R696.

## Scope
Crossed-frame simultaneous-cover consequence of the order-free R696 trichotomy. It uses only the two opposite tested orientations that delete the same physical X pair and the fact that a two-path cover is a path forest. No five-cell, order bound, reverse-ear, protected-contact, or generic growth machinery is used.

## Applicability
When working in an exact deletion cover of one crossed middle-gate pair, inspect both oriented R649 packets together rather than spending one orientation in isolation. At least one complementary X vertex gives either endpoint mate geometry or a crossing avoiding both L and R. The two cross-end-sandwich residues cannot coexist.

## Persistence
Durable simultaneous-orientation refinement of R649. It converts the shared witness pair {L,R} into a non-sandwich guarantee on at least one of the two complementary X coordinates for each middle-gate deletion.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert which complementary X vertex is non-sandwich. Does not assert END is impossible. Does not assert the resulting mate clause or dual-endpoint-free crossing alone closes H.

## Proof
Consider T, an exact two-cover of H-{a,c}. Accepted R649 gives two X-complementary two-witness short-carrier packets on this same deletion: for tested S=(a,c), the tight carrier (z,c,a) has complementary singleton z and witnesses L,R; for tested S=(c,a), the tight carrier (b,a,c) has complementary singleton b and witnesses L,R. Apply R696 to both packets using the same T. Suppose for contradiction that both are in SANDWICH. Then z has exactly the two T-neighbors L,R, and b also has exactly the two T-neighbors L,R. Hence the selected-state graph of T contains the four distinct edges Lz,zR,Rb,bL. These form a cycle on L,z,R,b. But the selected-state graph of a two-path cover is a disjoint union of paths and is therefore acyclic. Contradiction. Thus at least one of the two packets is not SANDWICH. By the exhaustive R696 trichotomy it is END or FREE, with exactly the stated mate/capture or dual-witness-free crossing conclusion. The proof for H-{b,z} is identical using the R649 packets (b,z) with carrier (z,b,c), complementary c, witnesses L,R, and (z,b) with carrier (b,z,a), complementary a, witnesses L,R.

# R7 — Intrinsic Partition-Cover Deficit Identity

## Statement
For a fixed partition into physical classes, the number t_Pi(T) of selected transitions between classes in a current exact cover T equals the sum of the intrinsic path-cover numbers of the classes minus the number of current cover components, plus a nonnegative representative-relative excess sigma. Equality sigma=0 means every class restriction realizes its intrinsic minimum path-cover number.

## Hypotheses


## Scope
A fixed physical partition and one displayed exact cover.

## Applicability


## Persistence


## Exclusions / nonclaims
The excess is not a global monotone or literal exchange credit.

## Proof
Restrict each current rail to the partition classes. If t transitions join different classes, cutting those transitions produces the number of current rails plus t monochromatic path blocks. Each class contributes at least its intrinsic path-cover number; the nonnegative difference is sigma. Rearranging gives the identity, and equality is exactly simultaneous intrinsic minimality of all class restrictions.

# R700 — Two-probe trimer amplification gives a P4 or dual reverse-boundary R542 packets

## Statement
Let H be a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample, let K=(a,b,c) be any tight trimer, and let y_1,y_2 be two distinct vertices outside V(K). Then at least one of the following holds. (P4) For some i in {1,2}, the four-set V(K) union {y_i} supports a tight Hamilton P4. (DUAL-CP) Both reverse boundary dimers of K are simultaneously two-witness R542-ready packets: the reverse initial dimer D_L=(b,a) is tail-signed by both y_1,y_2, and the reverse terminal dimer D_R=(c,b) is head-signed by both y_1,y_2. Consequently accepted R542 applies independently to D_L with carrier K and complementary singleton c, and to D_R with carrier K and complementary singleton a. The two packet facts coexist graph-intrinsically, although their capture/payment descendants are alternative continuations. Indeed, apply accepted R518 to K with fourth vertex y_i for i=1,2. If either application yields its P4 branch, stop. Otherwise the no-P4 branch of R518 gives, for each i, both reverse contacts (b,a,y_i) and (y_i,c,b). The first pair of turns is exactly same-tail two-witness polarity on tested D_L=(b,a), while the second is same-head two-witness polarity on tested D_R=(c,b); both witnesses lie outside K, so R542 applies at both boundaries. In particular, a two-witness short-carrier SANDWICH output from pending R696 never has to be paid on its old inward-Q support: regarding the witness sandwich itself as K and choosing any two distinguished outside probes converts it either to a labelled P4 or to two new short-carrier packets supported on the cross dimers joining the sandwich middle to its two exterior witnesses.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample; K=(a,b,c) is tight; y_1,y_2 are distinct and outside K. Use accepted R518 and R542.

## Scope
Order-free local compiler. Pure four-cell amplification plus short-carrier typing. No crossed-frame, deletion-root, R5,R168,R169,R224,R533,generic R358, R436, or R24 input.

## Applicability
Whenever a tight trimer is the current geometric residue and at least two named outside vertices matter, probe the trimer with both before invoking generic payment. A P4 is immediate progress. If neither probe gives a P4, retain both reverse boundary dimers as simultaneous two-witness R542 packets with the SAME named probe pair. For an R696 witness sandwich at q_1, choose one X vertex and the opposite Q endpoint R; this moves the packet from the inward-Q dimer to X-q_1 cross supports while retaining a nonlocal endpoint witness. Use the exact dual at q_{m-1} with L.

## Persistence
Retain K, the two probe identities y_1,y_2, both R518 four-cell tests, and in the no-P4 branch all four reverse-contact turns. Retain both tested reverse boundary dimers, their common two-witness set, carrier K, and complementary singleton identities. Later R542 descendants are alternative and need not coexist.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert either R542 descendant closes H or that the two paid descendants coexist. Does not claim repeated application is a globally monotone process. Does not by itself consume the END/FREE branches of pending R696. Does not assert a P4 is spanning.

## Proof
Fix K=(a,b,c) and y_i outside K. Accepted R518 says that either K union {y_i} has a Hamilton P4, or its no-P4 branch forces the exact reverse contacts (b,a,y_i) and (y_i,c,b). If the P4 branch occurs for i=1 or 2, outcome P4 holds. Otherwise, for i=1,2 both displayed contacts hold. Thus on the fixed tested dimer D_L=(b,a), the turns (b,a,y_1) and (b,a,y_2) are two distinct tail certificates, so D_L is same-tail two-witness signed. Since K begins with boundary state (a,b), D_L=(b,a) is exactly its reverse initial boundary dimer; y_1,y_2 are outside K. Accepted R542 applies, with complementary carrier singleton c. Likewise on D_R=(c,b), the turns (y_1,c,b) and (y_2,c,b) are two distinct head certificates. Because K ends in boundary state (b,c), D_R is exactly the reverse terminal boundary dimer of K; R542 applies with complementary singleton a. All four turns are graph-intrinsic facts of the same H, so the two packet certificates coexist even though R542 continuations are alternative. This proves the corollary.

# R702 — Every crossed middle-gate deletion cover gives mate geometry or an inward X-Q transition

## Statement
Retain the accepted crossed R621/R649 frame with X={a,b,c,z}, Q=(q_0,...,q_m), L=q_0 and R=q_m. Let D be either crossed middle-gate pair {a,c} or {b,z}, let X_D=X\D be the complementary middle-gate pair, and let T be any exact two-cover of H-D. Apply R696 to the two R649 packets on the two tested orientations of D whose complementary singleton runs through the two vertices of X_D and whose same-polarity witness pair is {L,R}. Then at least one of the following holds. (MATE) One of those packets is in the R696 END branch, hence supplies its literal spanning two-path proposal with one or two uncertified turns and the corresponding forced reverse turn / physical two-hole mate clause. (INWARD) T contains a selected adjacent state between a vertex x in X_D and an interior Q vertex q_i with 1<=i<=m-1. Thus, outside the concrete END mate geometry, every exact crossed middle-gate deletion cover already moves a physical selected cut from X into the interior of Q; no balanced-pair payment or second deletion cover is needed for this transition.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in the accepted crossed R621/R649 frame. D is one of {a,c},{b,z}; T is any exact two-cover of H-D. Use pending R696 on the two X-complementary packets with witness pair {L,R}. Smallest-counterexample minimality is used only through the existence/exactness already present in the frame and R696 context; the path-forest and gate-polarity step is local.

## Scope
Noncircular crossed-frame local consumer. It uses the physical middle-gate deletion cover itself and crossed endpoint gate polarity. No five-cell classification, Reverse Ear, R39 floor descent, generic payment, R436, R450, R5, R168, R169, R224, R533, or generic R358 is used.

## Applicability
Whenever a crossed middle-gate pair is deleted, inspect the two complementary-X R696 packets together. If neither complementary singleton is an END, an actual selected X-Q state reaches q_1,...,q_{m-1}. In particular a FREE state equal to the other complementary X vertex is not a residue: the resulting internal X-dimer block must have an inward Q neighbor.

## Persistence
Retain D, the exact deletion cover T, the two complementary X labels, and either the exact R696 END proposal/hole data or the literal selected inward X-Q state with its q_i coordinate and T orientation.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert that every inward X-Q selected state itself closes H, that it is unique, or that its R527 descendants remain current. Does not claim a specific interior index i. Does not use anonymous balanced-pair descent as progress. Review of this result requires review/acceptance of R696 or a simultaneous review of the dependency chain.

## Proof
Fix D and T. First take D={a,c}, so X_D={b,z}; the other deletion is the exact dual. R649 supplies two R696-ready packets on the two tested orientations of D, one with complementary singleton b and one with complementary singleton z, both with witness pair {L,R}. Apply R696 to both in the same T. They cannot both be SANDWICH: that would make both b and z have T-neighbor set {L,R}, impossible in a disjoint union of paths. Therefore at least one packet is END or FREE. If one is END, MATE holds. Assume no packet is END and choose a FREE complementary singleton e in {b,z}. By R696, e has T-degree two and has a selected neighbor x outside {L,R}. The R621 exact-frame identities span H by X union V(Q), while a,c are deleted. Hence x is either an interior Q vertex q_i, 1<=i<=m-1, or the other complementary X vertex e'. In the first case INWARD holds. Suppose x=e'. Since no packet is END, e' also has T-degree two. Thus e,e' occur as a consecutive internal two-vertex block on one T-rail, with distinct outside neighbors p,q. No vertices besides b,z and Q remain in H-{a,c}, so p,q lie on Q. If either is q_i with 1<=i<=m-1, INWARD holds. Suppose instead {p,q}={L,R}. Then that T-rail contains the b,z block between L and R. But R621 says {b,z} is fully incoming to both physical endpoints: (b,z,L),(z,b,L),(b,z,R),(z,b,R) are tight. Whichever endpoint precedes the ordered b,z block on the T-rail therefore creates the exact reverse of one of these certified tight turns. For example L,b,z reverses z,b,L and L,z,b reverses b,z,L; the R-first cases are identical at R. By boundary antisymmetry that preceding endpoint turn is bad, contradicting T tightness. Hence {p,q}!={L,R}, so one is an interior Q vertex and INWARD follows. Now take D={b,z}, X_D={a,c}. The same argument applies. If the a,c block were internal with outside neighbors exactly L,R, R621 says both endpoints are fully outgoing to {a,c}: (L,a,c),(L,c,a),(R,a,c),(R,c,a) are tight. Whichever endpoint follows the ordered a,c block on the T-rail produces the reverse of one of these tight turns, again contradicting T tightness. Thus an interior Q neighbor is forced. This proves the dichotomy for both crossed middle-gate deletions.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R702.md -->

# R703 — One-step inward reverse-star lift forces a P4 or Reverse-Ear geometry

## Statement
Let Q=(q_0,...,q_m) be any vertex-simple tight path in a Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament and let x be a vertex outside Q. There are two dual local forms. (L) Suppose 1<=i<=m-1 and the reverse-boundary witness trimer J_L=(q_{i+1},q_i,x) is tight. Then either the four-set {q_{i-1},q_i,q_{i+1},x} supports a tight Hamilton P4, or explicit Reverse-Ear geometry occurs relative to Q. More precisely, apply R518 to J_L with fourth vertex q_{i-1}. In the no-P4 branch R518 forces the all-Q trimer K_L=(q_i,q_{i+1},q_{i-1}) tight. Along K_L the consecutive Q contacts q_{i+1},q_{i-1} occur in decreasing Q-order and are not adjacent on Q, so R435 applied to Q and K_L yields a tight reverse trimer/reversal cell or a vertex-simple tight cycle. (R) Suppose 0<=i<=m-2 and J_R=(x,q_{i+1},q_i) is tight. Then either {x,q_i,q_{i+1},q_{i+2}} supports a tight Hamilton P4, or explicit Reverse-Ear geometry occurs. Indeed R518 with fourth vertex q_{i+2} forces in its no-P4 branch K_R=(q_{i+2},q_i,q_{i+1}) tight; the consecutive contacts q_{i+2},q_i occur in reverse nonadjacent Q-order, so R435 fires. Thus a new exterior witness on either inward reverse-boundary orientation of an internal Q dimer can never remain only same-support witness reminting: one old neighboring Q vertex lifts it immediately to a labelled P4 or to the Reverse-Ear/cycle queue.

## Hypotheses
Q is a vertex-simple tight path in a finite Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament; x lies outside Q. In form (L), J_L=(q_{i+1},q_i,x) is tight with i>=1 so q_{i-1} exists. In form (R), J_R=(x,q_{i+1},q_i) is tight with i+2<=m so q_{i+2} exists. Use accepted R518 and R435.

## Scope
Pure order-free local path interaction. No smallest-counterexample, deletion exactness, crossed frame, payment, R5,R168,R169,R224,R533,R358, or R436.

## Applicability
Use immediately whenever a same-polarity packet or failed splice adds a new exterior witness to an inward Q dimer in one of the displayed reverse-boundary orientations. Do not report it as a third witness on an already-payable R542 support. Probe by the next old Q vertex outside the carrier. This directly consumes the shape-F L-post inward packet (q_3,q_2,x) with q_1 and the R-pre right packet (x,q_{m-2},q_{m-3}) with q_{m-1}, as well as the R692 shape-E remint.

## Persistence
Retain Q and its physical index order, x, the source trimer J_L or J_R, the chosen neighboring Q probe, the R518 four-cell test, and either the exact labelled P4 or the all-Q nonmonotone trimer K_L/K_R plus the R435 reverse-trimer/reversal/cycle certificate.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not consume the resulting P4 or R435 cycle/reverse cell. Does not apply at a path endpoint where the required outside Q probe does not exist. Does not say an old two-witness packet without a newly exhibited exterior witness has already entered this lemma; the displayed witness trimer must be retained.

## Proof
For (L), set a=q_{i+1}, b=q_i, c=x and y=q_{i-1} in accepted R518. If its P4 branch occurs, the first conclusion holds. Otherwise R518 forces (b,a,y)=(q_i,q_{i+1},q_{i-1}) and (y,c,b)=(q_{i-1},x,q_i) tight. Retain K_L=(q_i,q_{i+1},q_{i-1}). Compare K_L with Q. The consecutive K_L contacts q_{i+1} and q_{i-1} have Q indices i+1>i-1, and the K_L subpath between them is the single state q_{i+1}q_{i-1}. Its interior is empty. Since the two endpoints are distance two on Q, this is not R435's special adjacent old-state reversal case. Therefore R435's nonadjacent branch gives a reverse trimer/reversal cell or a vertex-simple tight cycle. For (R), set a=x, b=q_{i+1}, c=q_i and y=q_{i+2}. Again a P4 settles the first outcome. In the no-P4 branch R518 forces (y,c,b)=(q_{i+2},q_i,q_{i+1}) tight (and also (q_{i+1},x,q_{i+2}) tight). Retain K_R=(q_{i+2},q_i,q_{i+1}). Its consecutive Q contacts q_{i+2},q_i occur in reverse order with gap two, so the identical R435 argument yields explicit Reverse-Ear/cycle geometry. This proves both forms.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R703.md -->

# R718 — The endpoint-star six-cell does not propagate the middle-gate bit one step inward

## Statement
Let X={a,b,c,z} be the transitive matching-height P4-free four-cell with M_R={ab,cz}>M_S={ac,bz}>M_L={bc,az}. There exist Strong Level-(1) orientations on X union {L,u} satisfying simultaneously: (i) X+L is Hamilton-P5-free; (ii) X+u is Hamilton-P5-free; (iii) X+{L,u} is Hamilton-P6-free; and (iv) (u,L,x) is tight for every x in X, in which the outgoing M_S gate at u is the SAME physical M_S edge as the outgoing M_S gate at L. There also exist such orientations in which the outgoing M_S gate at u is the COMPLEMENTARY M_S edge to the outgoing gate at L. Hence the natural local packet consisting of transitive X, the two P5-free fifth-vertex cells, P6-freeness of the six-cell, and the full endpoint reverse star uLx does not determine whether the middle-gate bit is preserved or flipped from L to u. By the automorphism of the matching-height cell interchanging the two M_S edges, all four ordered gate-bit pairs occur. Therefore no R24 route may infer a deterministic one-step middle-gate propagation law from this local packet alone.

## Hypotheses
Only Strong Level-(1) complete-reversal antisymmetry is used. The finite models are on six vertices X union {L,u}; X has the displayed matching-height orientation.

## Scope
Finite local R24 strategy fence. No smallest-counterexample minimality, deletion exactness, capture, payment, R5,R168,R169,R224,R533,R358, or computation-dependent hidden assumption beyond the explicit certificate verification.

## Applicability
Use when considering propagation of the alternating middle-gate polarity from q_0 to q_1 (or dually q_m to q_{m-1}) using only the endpoint-star six-cell. A successful inward propagation or zipper invariant must consume additional information absent here, such as the opposite end, a high-side root/inward-star coordinate, or an exact deletion-cover crossing.

## Persistence
Retain the two explicit six-vertex certificate words and the distinction SAME versus OPPOSITE middle-gate relation.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert either six-vertex model extends to a smallest counterexample or to the full long-Q R24 frame. Does not refute nonlocal gate synchronization using q_{m-1},q_m or exact cover data. Does not say the first-inward gate is useless; only that its bit is not determined by the endpoint-local packet.

## Proof
Fix vertex order a<b<c<z<L<u. For each middle vertex m, list the unordered endpoint pairs from the other five vertices in lexicographic order induced by this vertex order. A 10-bit word records the complete Strong orientation at middle m: bit 1 means the canonical ordered turn (p,m,q) with p<q is tight; bit 0 means its complete reversal (q,m,p) is tight. Thus six 10-bit words define all 60 reversal pairs.

MODEL S (same M_S gate; {a,c} outgoing and {b,z} incoming at both L and u):
a: 1111100000
b: 1111000110
c: 1000000000
z: 0000011111
L: 1010000100
u: 1010010100

MODEL O (opposite M_S gate; {a,c} outgoing at L while {b,z} is outgoing at u):
a: 1111101001
b: 1111000100
c: 1001000011
z: 0000010100
L: 1010000100
u: 0000100000

For clarity, the endpoint-pair orders used by these words are: at a: bc,bz,bL,bu,cz,cL,cu,zL,zu,Lu; at b: ac,az,aL,au,cz,cL,cu,zL,zu,Lu; at c: ab,az,aL,au,bz,bL,bu,zL,zu,Lu; at z: ab,ac,aL,au,bc,bL,bu,cL,cu,Lu; at L: ab,ac,az,au,bc,bz,bu,cz,cu,zu; at u: ab,ac,az,aL,bc,bz,bL,cz,cL,zL.

Direct reconstruction gives in BOTH models: the restriction to X is exactly the matching-height P4-free cell; every uLx (x in X) is tight; no one of the 120 orders on X+L is a Hamilton P5; no one of the 120 orders on X+u is a Hamilton P5; and no one of the 720 orders on X+{L,u} is a Hamilton P6. In Model S the full M_S turns at L are Lac,Lca,bzL,zbL and at u are uac,uca,bzu,zbu, so the outgoing edge is {a,c} at both. In Model O the L gate is unchanged while at u the full M_S turns are ubz,uzb,acu,cau, so the outgoing edge is {b,z}, the complementary edge. The matching-height automorphism exchanging the two M_S edges converts (same 0,0) to (same 1,1) and (opposite 0,1) to (opposite 1,0). This proves the fence.

# R719 — A cross-end trimer R-x-L feeds R435 only into the pre-existing endpoint stars

## Statement
Retain the accepted R594 synchronized transitive frame with X disjoint from Q=(L=q_0,u=q_1,...,s=q_{m-1},R=q_m), m>=4, and the universal endpoint reverse stars (u,L,x) and (x,R,s) tight for every x in X. Fix x in X and suppose the cross-end trimer K=(R,x,L) is tight. Compare K with Q by accepted Reverse Ear R435 using consecutive Q-contacts R=q_m then L=q_0. The two seam turns required to close the R435 cycle are exactly (s,R,x) and (x,L,u). Both are automatically bad: their complete reversals (x,R,s) and (u,L,x) are the already accepted R594 endpoint-star turns. Therefore the vertex-simple cycle branch of R435 is impossible for this ear. Moreover the two possible R435 reverse-trimer outputs are exactly the already-known endpoint-star turns (x,R,s) and (u,L,x). Consequently applying R435 to a cross-end trimer (R,x,L) creates no fresh turn geometry beyond the cross-end trimer itself; its seam output is certificate-stationary endpoint-star replay. Any useful consumer of (R,x,L) must use the trimer by another mechanism rather than crediting generic Reverse-Ear/cycle progress.

## Hypotheses
Accepted R594 synchronized transitive frame; x in X; cross-end trimer (R,x,L) tight; accepted R3 and R435.

## Scope
Pure R594/R435 specialization and strategy fence. No crossed phase, deletion cover, payment, capture, R5,R168,R169,R224,R533,R358, or R436.

## Applicability
Whenever a route produces a tight trimer (q_m,x,q_0), retain that trimer as new cross-end geometry but do not report the subsequent R435 call as a new Reverse-Ear/cycle output. Search instead for a direct cross-end recompletion, a four/five-cell amplification using x, or a deletion-cover consumer of the physical chord through x.

## Persistence
Retain x, cross-end trimer (R,x,L), the two failed seam turns, and their identification with the accepted endpoint stars.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not say the cross-end trimer itself is useless or stationary; only its generic R435 seam consumption is stationary. Does not treat the opposite orientation (L,x,R), whose seam pattern is different. Does not assert any cross-end trimer exists.

## Proof
Let P=Q=(L,u,...,s,R) and E=K=(R,x,L). The consecutive K-contacts with P are v_i=R=q_m and v_j=L=q_0, with i=m>0=j and internal ear vertex x outside Q. In the nonadjacent R435 case the cycle candidate follows the old Q segment from L through ... through s,R and then the ear R,x,L. The only two seam turns not already certified by Q or K are (s,R,x) at the R seam and (x,L,u) at the L seam. Accepted R594 gives (x,R,s) tight and (u,L,x) tight for every x in X. By boundary antisymmetry R3, (s,R,x) and (x,L,u) are therefore bad. Thus the cycle case requiring both seams tight is impossible. The exact R3 reversals of the two failed seams are (x,R,s) and (u,L,x), which are exactly the same pre-existing R594 endpoint-star turns. This exhausts the R435 alternatives for E and proves the claim.

## Statement
There exists a Strong Level-(1) orientation F on V=X union {L,u,v,w}, X={a,b,c,z}, satisfying simultaneously: (1) X is the transitive matching-height four-cell M_R={ab,cz}>M_S={ac,bz}>M_L={bc,az}; (2) (L,u,v,w) is tight; (3) every endpoint-star turn (u,L,x), x in X, is tight; (4) the full left crossed/high-side gate packet Lbc,Lcb,Lac,Lca,bzL,zbL,czL,zcL is tight; (5) the R658 left rectangle turns Lub,Luz,wvb,wvz are tight; and (6) the explicit R704 labelled Hamilton P4 (b,w,v,z) is tight. Nevertheless F has no Hamilton tight P8. Consequently the accepted R704 inward P4, even together with all of these one-sided crossed/high-side prefix coordinates, does not force X union Q[0,3] to be Hamiltonian. In particular it cannot by itself supply the missing one-rail complementary absorber that would strengthen the natural three-class R567 puncture count from one transition to two. Any such amplification must use a genuinely nonlocal/right-side coordinate or additional cross-frame information.

## Hypotheses
Only Strong Level-(1) complete-reversal antisymmetry. The theorem is witnessed by the explicit eight-vertex orientation certificate in the proof.

## Scope
Finite local R24 strategy fence strengthening the one-sided limitation behind R626 by adding the explicit R704 P4. No smallest-counterexample, deletion-cover, payment, R5,R168,R169,R224,R533, generic R358, or R436.

## Applicability
Do not try to consume the R704 left P4 merely by proving the eight-vertex prefix X union Q[0,3] Hamiltonian from the one-sided crossed/high-side packet. A successful R567 or splice consumer must import opposite-end or other nonlocal data.

## Persistence
Retain the eight labels L,u,v,w,a,b,c,z, all displayed required turns, the complete orientation code table, the explicit P4 (b,w,v,z), and the verified zero Hamilton-P8 count.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not show the full global crossed R24 frame is realizable. Does not refute consumers using right-end data, both R704 P4s, the R621 opposite-end weaves, or additional exact-cover coordinates. It only refutes the stated local implication.

## Proof
Fix the vertex order L<u<v<w<a<b<c<z. For each three-set {x<y<z}, encode the three complete-reversal pairs by bits eps_1 eps_2 eps_3, where eps_1=1 means xyz is tight (otherwise zyx), eps_2=1 means xzy is tight (otherwise yzx), and eps_3=1 means yxz is tight (otherwise zxy). Every omitted three-set has code 000. The nonzero codes are: Luv 101; Luw 101; Lua 101; Lub 101; Luc 111; Luz 101; Lvb 001; Lvz 010; Lwb 001; Lwc 001; Lab 001; Lac 110; Laz 010; Lbc 110; uvw 101; uva 101; uvb 101; uvc 111; uvz 111; uwa 001; uwb 001; uwc 101; uab 001; uac 110; uaz 110; ubc 110; ubz 010; vwa 100; vwb 001; vwc 101; vwz 001; vab 100; vac 111; vaz 110; vbc 110; vbz 010; wab 010; wac 110; waz 110; wbc 111; wbz 111; abc 111; abz 101; acz 001. This assigns exactly one tight orientation in every complete-reversal pair, hence is Strong Level-(1). Direct evaluation verifies the matching-height X rule, the tight path (L,u,v,w), all four turns (u,L,x), the eight displayed left gate turns, Lub,Luz,wvb,wvz, and the P4 turns bwv,wvz. Exhaustive evaluation of all 8!=40320 vertex orders gives zero Hamilton tight P8s. The certificate was found by a 0-1 feasibility search; the mathematical proof is the explicit orientation table and finite exhaustive verification.

# R723 — Crossed deep/shallow covers symmetrize to four-root first-inward reverse stars

## Statement
Retain the accepted crossed R621 frame with X={a,b,c,z}, Q=(q_0,...,q_m), m>=4, L=q_0, u=q_1, R=q_m, s=q_{m-1}, v=q_2 and d=q_{m-2}. Then every root x in X has two literal exact singleton-deletion covers of the symmetric shallow form H-x=A_x^L sqcup Q[1,m] and H-x=Q[0,m-1] sqcup A_x^R, where the short P4s are: x=z: A_z^L=(L,a,c,b), A_z^R=(R,a,c,b); x=b: A_b^L=(L,c,a,z), A_b^R=(R,c,a,z); x=c: A_c^L=(a,b,z,L), A_c^R=(a,b,z,R); x=a: A_a^L=(c,z,b,L), A_a^R=(c,z,b,R). Consequently the first inward reverse boundary dimers of Q are universally signed by the entire four-cell: for every x in X, (v,u,x)=(q_2,q_1,x) is tight and (x,s,d)=(x,q_{m-1},q_{m-2}) is tight. Equivalently the tested dimer (q_2,q_1) is tail-signed by all four vertices of X and the tested dimer (q_{m-1},q_{m-2}) is head-signed by all four vertices of X. These four-witness stars coexist graph-intrinsically in the original crossed frame.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in the accepted crossed R621 frame; Q=(q_0,...,q_m), m>=4. Use only the literal R621 deep/shallow singleton-deletion covers and boundary antisymmetry R3.

## Scope
Noncircular crossed-frame strengthening. It symmetrizes the R621 deletion covers by moving the already-selected q_1 or q_{m-1} vertex back onto its original Q subpath, and then uses only the impossibility of a spanning two-cover to force the first-inward reverse stars. No R5,R168,R169,R224,R533,five-cell classification,generic payment,R436,or computation is used.

## Applicability
Use whenever the crossed R621 frame is available. It upgrades the previously pair-specific inward witness information to all four X vertices on the one-step-in reverse dimers (q_2,q_1) and (q_{m-1},q_{m-2}), while retaining four explicit root-labelled exact covers at each side.

## Persistence


## Exclusions / nonclaims


## Proof
For roots z and b, accepted R621 gives the deep exact covers H-z=(u,L,a,c,b) sqcup Q[2,m] and H-b=(u,L,c,a,z) sqcup Q[2,m]. Removing the initial vertex u from the displayed short P5 and placing it back on its original Q suffix does not require a new seam: (L,a,c,b) and (L,c,a,z) are literal tight subpaths of the displayed P5s, while Q[1,m]=(u,q_2,...,R) is a literal tight subpath of Q. Hence H-z=(L,a,c,b) sqcup Q[1,m] and H-b=(L,c,a,z) sqcup Q[1,m] are literal two-covers. For roots c and a, R621 already gives the left shallow covers H-c=(a,b,z,L) sqcup Q[1,m] and H-a=(c,z,b,L) sqcup Q[1,m]. Thus the asserted A_x^L cover exists for every x in X. Dually, R621 already gives the right shallow covers for z,b: H-z=Q[0,m-1] sqcup (R,a,c,b) and H-b=Q[0,m-1] sqcup (R,c,a,z). Its right-deep covers H-c=Q[0,m-2] sqcup (a,b,z,R,s) and H-a=Q[0,m-2] sqcup (c,z,b,R,s) may be truncated at their terminal vertex s and s returned to its original Q prefix, yielding H-c=Q[0,m-1] sqcup (a,b,z,R) and H-a=Q[0,m-1] sqcup (c,z,b,R). Therefore the asserted A_x^R cover exists for every x. Each displayed two-cover of H-x is exact: if H-x were Hamiltonian then its Hamilton path together with singleton (x) would be a spanning two-cover of H. Now fix x in X and use the left shallow cover A_x^L sqcup Q[1,m]. If (x,u,v) were tight, then (x,u,v,q_3,...,R) together with A_x^L would be a spanning two-cover of H. Hence (x,u,v) is bad, and R3 forces its exact reversal (v,u,x) tight. Since x was arbitrary, (v,u,x) is tight for all x in X. Likewise use the right shallow cover Q[0,m-1] sqcup A_x^R. If (d,s,x) were tight, appending x to Q[0,m-1] and retaining A_x^R would two-cover H. Thus (d,s,x) is bad and R3 forces (x,s,d) tight for every x. This proves both universal inward stars and the full statement.

## Statement
There exists a seven-vertex Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament F on X union {L,u,v}, with X={a,b,c,z}, having all of the following properties simultaneously. (4) The full R723 first-inward star holds: (v,u,x) is tight for every x in X. (5) The R725 left saturation turns (b,a,u) and (z,c,u) are tight. (6) Both R727 candidate four-sets are genuinely Hamiltonian: {a,b,c,u} contains the tight P4 (a,c,u,b), while {c,z,a,u} contains the tight P4 (c,z,a,u). Any consumer of the R727 P4 branch must use something other than bare Hamilton extension on the seven-coordinate end gadget, such as same-residue cover comparison, nonlocal/right-end data, or provenance-bearing pair interaction.

## Hypotheses
Explicit finite Strong Level-(1) orientation. No smallest-counterexample assumption is used; the result is a local obstruction to an inference from the listed crossed-frame turn data.

Strategy fence for the first-step zipper program. It does not say that R727 P4s are useless; pending R733 gives a nonlocal-in-the-cover-space pair consumer. It only rules out deducing a Hamilton P6 on any root support from the seven-coordinate local turn packet itself.

## Persistence


## Exclusions / nonclaims

# R773 — A reverse terminal contact either makes a local P4 or steps inward into the nonreplay R703 lift

## Statement
Let H be a finite Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament and let K=(k_0,k_1,...,k_r) be a vertex-simple tight path with r>=3. Let h lie outside K. HEAD. Suppose the reverse head-contact trimer (k_1,k_0,h) is tight. Test the turn tau_H=(k_1,k_2,h). If tau_H is tight, then (k_0,k_1,k_2,h) is a literal tight P4. If tau_H is bad, boundary antisymmetry forces (h,k_2,k_1) tight. This is exactly the internal right-form reverse-star hypothesis of accepted R703 on the old path K at i=1. Hence R703 yields either a tight Hamilton P4 on {h,k_1,k_2,k_3} or explicit Reverse-Ear geometry relative to K: a reverse state/reverse trimer or a vertex-simple tight cycle. TAIL. Suppose (h,k_r,k_{r-1}) is tight. Test tau_T=(h,k_{r-2},k_{r-1}). If tau_T is tight, then (h,k_{r-2},k_{r-1},k_r) is a literal tight P4. If tau_T is bad, antisymmetry forces (k_{r-1},k_{r-2},h) tight, exactly the internal left-form R703 hypothesis on K at i=r-2. Hence R703 yields either a tight Hamilton P4 on {k_{r-3},k_{r-2},k_{r-1},h} or explicit Reverse-Ear geometry relative to K. Thus every reverse terminal contact on a path of order at least four either produces an adjacent local P4 immediately or moves one step inward to an R703 event whose reverse-ear branch cannot merely replay the original endpoint contact.

## Hypotheses
Finite Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament; K=(k_0,...,k_r) tight with r>=3; h outside K; one displayed reverse terminal-contact trimer is tight. Uses accepted R3 and R703.

## Scope
Pure order-free local terminal-contact consumer. No smallest-counterexample minimality, deletion exactness, crossed frame, R5,R168,R169,R224,R533,generic R358,R436,R312,or computation.

## Applicability
Preferred consumer after pending R770 produces a reverse terminal contact on a retained path of order at least four. Unlike the raw R435 endpoint-ear specialization in pending R771, this theorem first tests the opposite seam and, in the bad branch, shifts the witness one dimer inward before invoking R703. Use this route when replay of the original endpoint contact would not count as progress.

## Persistence
Retain K,h,the original endpoint contact,the tested inward seam,and either the explicit adjacent P4 or the shifted internal reverse-star plus the full R703 P4/Reverse-Ear certificate. Any role-labelled subpath embedded in K remains historical geometry.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not consume the resulting P4 or R703 reverse-ear/cycle output. Does not assert a P4 extends all of K or that the resulting geometry closes H. Requires at least four vertices on K so the R703 inward probe k_3 or k_{r-3} exists. Does not invalidate pending R771; it is the preferred nonreplay refinement.

## Proof
Head case. The old path K certifies (k_0,k_1,k_2). Test tau_H=(k_1,k_2,h). If tight, the two consecutive turns (k_0,k_1,k_2) and (k_1,k_2,h) certify the tight P4 (k_0,k_1,k_2,h). If tau_H is bad, accepted boundary antisymmetry R3 gives its complete reverse (h,k_2,k_1) tight. With Q=K, x=h and i=1 this is exactly the right-form hypothesis J_R=(x,q_{i+1},q_i) of accepted R703; r>=3 supplies q_{i+2}=k_3. Therefore R703 yields either a Hamilton P4 on {h,k_1,k_2,k_3} or its explicit Reverse-Ear/reversal/cycle output. Tail case. The old path certifies (k_{r-2},k_{r-1},k_r). Test tau_T=(h,k_{r-2},k_{r-1}). If tight, together they certify (h,k_{r-2},k_{r-1},k_r). If bad, R3 gives (k_{r-1},k_{r-2},h) tight. With Q=K, x=h and i=r-2 this is the left-form hypothesis J_L=(q_{i+1},q_i,x) of R703; r>=3 supplies q_{i-1}=k_{r-3}. Apply R703. In either shifted branch, the R703 reverse-ear construction is based on a new internal reverse-star and an all-K nonmonotone trimer, so it is not merely the original terminal-contact certificate. This proves the dual alternatives.

# FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R776.md

<!-- BEGIN FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R776.md -->

# R776 — Internal-trimer puncture of a P5 exposes both endpoints or selects the endpoint chord

## Statement
Let H be a finite boundary tournament with pc(H)>2, and let J=(j_0,j_1,j_2,j_3,j_4) be a proper vertex-simple tight P5. Put D={j_1,j_2,j_3}, E=V(H)\\V(J), and let T be any literal exact two-cover of H-D. Then exactly one of the following structural regimes holds. (DUAL-EXTERIOR) The endpoint chord {j_0,j_4} is not selected in T. Then T contains a selected state {j_0,a} with a in E and a selected state {j_4,b} with b in E; thus both P5 endpoints simultaneously have current exterior crossings in the same exact cover T. (ENDPOINT-CHORD) The state {j_0,j_4} is selected in T. Then at least one of j_0,j_4 also participates in a selected state to E. More precisely, the three R508 applications giving this are: apply R508 with deletion D, absorbable singleton S={j_0}, and tight recompletion path J_L=(j_0,j_1,j_2,j_3), forcing a selected state from j_0 to either j_4 or E; apply R508 with S={j_4} and J_R=(j_1,j_2,j_3,j_4), forcing a selected state from j_4 to either j_0 or E; and apply R508 with S={j_0,j_4} and recompletion path J itself, forcing a selected state from the endpoint pair to E. Consequently the only way either endpoint can avoid a true exterior neighbor is for the two P5 endpoints themselves to be selected adjacent, and even then the other R508 obligation forces a true exterior crossing at one endpoint. In a hypothetical smallest counterexample, accepted R4 supplies such an exact two-cover T because the deleted internal trimer D is a proper tight path.

## Hypotheses
Finite boundary tournament H with pc(H)>2; J is a proper vertex-simple tight P5; T is a supplied exact two-cover of H-{j_1,j_2,j_3}. For the unconditional smallest-counterexample corollary, use accepted R4. Uses accepted R508.

## Scope
Order-free generic P5 recompletion theorem. No crossed frame, sign machinery, R5,R168,R169,R224,R533,R350,generic R358,R176,R436,R312,capture,payment,Reverse Ear,or computation.

## Applicability
Use whenever a role-labelled P5 has important physical endpoints. It strengthens pending R769 before any R3 classification: first inspect whether the endpoint chord is selected. If not, both endpoints have simultaneous exterior crossings in one exact middle-trimer-deletion cover. If yes, retain the selected endpoint chord plus the forced exterior crossing. In the R775 depth-two P5 J=(q_2,q_1,x,q_{m-1},q_{m-2}), the ENDPOINT-CHORD branch is the selected long inward state {q_2,q_{m-2}}, while DUAL-EXTERIOR gives simultaneous current crossings at both inward anchors in H-{q_1,x,q_{m-1}}.

## Persistence
Retain J,D,the exact cover T, the endpoint chord selected/not-selected bit, both singleton R508 crossing certificates, and the endpoint-pair R508 exterior crossing certificate. In DUAL-EXTERIOR retain one exterior neighbor at each endpoint. In ENDPOINT-CHORD retain the selected chord and at least one endpoint-exterior selected state. All selected states are T-relative.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not classify the directions or polarities of the selected endpoint crossings. Does not assert both endpoint-exterior crossings are distinct, lie on different rails, or by themselves close H. In the ENDPOINT-CHORD branch it does not assert which endpoint has the additional exterior neighbor. Does not turn the selected endpoint chord into a spanning path. Does not require both rails of T to remain nontrivial after deleting an endpoint.

## Proof
Let W=V(H)\\D. Since J is proper, E=V(H)\\V(J) is nonempty. First apply accepted R508 with deletion D, S={j_0}, and Q=J_L=(j_0,j_1,j_2,j_3). The path Q is tight and has vertex set exactly D union {j_0}; hence T selects a state from j_0 to W\\{j_0}. The only surviving J-vertex besides j_0 is j_4, so this neighbor is either j_4 or a vertex of E. Dually, applying R508 with S={j_4} and Q=J_R=(j_1,j_2,j_3,j_4) forces a selected state from j_4 to either j_0 or E. Third, apply R508 with S={j_0,j_4} and Q=J itself. Since V(J)=D union S and E=W\\S is nonempty, T contains a selected state joining one endpoint in {j_0,j_4} to E. If the endpoint chord {j_0,j_4} is not selected, the first singleton obligation cannot terminate at j_4 and therefore gives j_0-E, while the second cannot terminate at j_0 and gives j_4-E. This is DUAL-EXTERIOR. If the endpoint chord is selected, the third application independently forces an endpoint-E state, giving ENDPOINT-CHORD. The two regimes are exhaustive. In a smallest counterexample, accepted R4 supplies an exact two-cover of H-D because D is a proper tight trimer. This proves the theorem.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R776.md -->
