# R777 — The first-inward star and Q path satisfy raw R547 hinge geometry; the resulting bare mass-two pair is free

## Statement
STRUCTURAL CONTENT (retained from revision 1). At the hinge q_1 the frame already supplies signed tight dimers of both polarities whose supports meet in exactly one vertex: the Q turn (q_1,q_2,q_3) makes D_Q=(q_1,q_2) tail-signed by q_3; accepted R594 makes D_L=(q_1,q_0) tail-signed by any x in X; accepted R723 makes D_x=(q_1,x) head-signed by q_2 for every x in X. Since X is disjoint from V(Q), any two of these meet exactly in q_1, so the hypothesis of accepted R547 is satisfied by raw accepted tight turns, with no exact cover, deletion fiber, capture, contact, actualization, payment, or minimality. R547 then returns, for each x in X, the disjoint opposite-polarity singleton supports (q_2) tail-signed and (x) head-signed, and likewise (q_0) and (x). Dually at s=q_{m-1}, with E_Q=(d,s) head-signed by rho, E_R=(R,s) head-signed by x, E_x=(x,s) tail-signed by d, R547 returns (q_{m-2}) head-signed with (x) tail-signed, and (R) with (x).

RETRACTION. Revision 1 presented the resulting balanced pairs as a mass-two floor at depth two reached without payment, and described this as making the capture/contact production line unnecessary in this frame. That framing is withdrawn as unsupported. By the canonical dictionary, a signed support is a tight support with an exact outside sign witness, a singleton (v) is head-signed by w exactly when (w,v) is tight, and a balanced opposite-sign pair is any two physically disjoint graph-intrinsic signed supports of opposite polarity. A two-vertex path is automatically tight, so in a tournament every vertex with an in-neighbour is head-signed and every vertex with an out-neighbour is tail-signed. Graph-intrinsic mass-two balanced pairs are therefore generically free, and exhibiting one is not evidence of support descent, cut movement, or any other progress against the standing R24 criterion. The correct reading of accepted R547 is that its scarce output is the RETAINED ANCESTRY - both ancestor dimers, their witnesses, and the R425 hinge cut, carried inside a signed-payment lineage - and not the balanced pair itself.

WHAT SURVIVES. The claim is now exactly this: the q_1-pencil and its dual at q_{m-1} satisfy the R547 hinge hypothesis on accepted tight turns alone. This is a statement about where R547 is applicable in the frame. It becomes mathematically valuable only if the two ancestor dimers are already carried by a payment lineage, in which case R547 supplies an ancestry-bearing both-singleton floor; establishing such lineage membership is not done here and is the actual open step.

## Hypotheses
H is a Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament in the accepted crossed R621/R723 frame, X={a,b,c,z} disjoint from V(Q), Q=(q_0,...,q_m), m>=4. Uses accepted R723, R594, R547 (and R425 inside it).

## Scope
Revision 2 of C624. Retains the structural hinge observation of R772 and RETRACTS its progress framing. Same dependencies; no cover, capture, contact, payment, or minimality.

## Applicability
Use as an applicability map for R547 in this frame, not as a progress result. Before writing a deletion-cover argument, check whether the frame already hands you two opposite-polarity dimers meeting in one vertex; if the ancestor dimers are lineage-carried, R547 gives an ancestry-bearing floor for free. If they are not lineage-carried, the output is a generic balanced pair and should not be counted.

## Persistence
Retain the hinge vertex, the two ancestor signed dimers with their historical support orders and exact witnesses, the nonhinge endpoints and their polarities, and the R425 hinge-cut ancestry. Retain also the retraction: do not cite this claim as evidence of floor descent or cut movement.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not close H. Does not claim strict physical cut movement, support descent, or any progress against the standing R24 criterion; revision 1's contrary framing is explicitly retracted. Does not claim the balanced pairs are scarce, novel, or hard to obtain - by the canonical definitions they are generically free. Does not establish that the ancestor dimers D_Q,D_L,D_x,E_Q,E_R,E_x lie in any signed-payment lineage, which is the step that would make R547's ancestry output meaningful. Does not assert lineage simultaneity across x or across the two ends. Does not assert any relation to the R744, R755, R756, or R757 capture fibers. Does not use or validate pending R753, R755, R756, R757.

## Proof
PART A, structural (unchanged from revision 1). (1) Q is a tight path, so (q_1,q_2,q_3) is tight and D_Q=(q_1,q_2) is tail-signed with exact witness q_3. (2) Accepted R723 gives the tight trimer (q_2,q_1,x) for every x in X, so D_x=(q_1,x) is head-signed with exact witness q_2. (3) Accepted R594 gives (q_1,q_0,x) tight, so D_L=(q_1,q_0) is tail-signed with witness any x in X. (4) X is disjoint from V(Q) in the R621 frame, so V(D_Q) cap V(D_x) = V(D_L) cap V(D_x) = {q_1} exactly. (5) The polarities are opposite, so each of (D_Q,D_x) and (D_L,D_x) satisfies the hypothesis of accepted R547 with hinge b=q_1, and R547 returns the stated disjoint opposite-sign singletons on the nonhinge endpoints, with both ancestor dimers, their witnesses, and the R425 hinge-cut ancestry retained. The dual at s=q_{m-1} is verbatim with E_Q=(d,s) head-signed by rho=q_{m-3}, E_R=(R,s) head-signed by x via accepted R594, and E_x=(x,s) tail-signed by d via accepted R723; supports meet exactly in s. No exact cover, deletion fiber, R508 crossing, R527/R542 capture, R312 contact, actualization, payment descent, or minimality hypothesis is used.

PART B, the retraction. By the canonical dictionary entry for signed support, a path P=(v_0,...,v_k) is head-signed by w when (w,v_0,...,v_k) is tight and tail-signed by z when (v_0,...,v_k,z) is tight. Specialize to k=0. A singleton (v) is head-signed by w exactly when (w,v) is tight, and tail-signed by z exactly when (v,z) is tight. A two-vertex path in a tournament is automatically tight. Hence in any Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament, every vertex possessing an in-neighbour is a head-signed graph-intrinsic singleton support, and every vertex possessing an out-neighbour is a tail-signed one. By the canonical dictionary entry for balanced opposite-sign pair, such a pair is precisely two physically disjoint graph-intrinsic signed supports of opposite polarity, retained together as one pair certificate. Therefore any two distinct vertices u,v such that u has an in-neighbour and v has an out-neighbour already furnish a graph-intrinsic balanced pair of total support mass two, with no hypothesis on the frame whatsoever. Consequently the mass-two balanced pairs produced in Part A are not scarce objects, and their existence cannot witness support descent, floor movement, or progress against the standing criterion of strict physical cut movement into Q. Revision 1 asserted the contrary and is corrected here. The scarce content of accepted R547 is not its pair conclusion but its ancestry conclusion: within a hypothetical smallest-counterexample signed-payment lineage it yields an ancestry-bearing both-singleton floor carrying both ancestor dimers and the hinge-cut witnesses. Part A does not place D_Q,D_L,D_x,E_Q,E_R,E_x in any such lineage, so it does not deliver that conclusion. This proves the corrected statement.

# R778 — P5 internal-trimer recompletion forces a P6 or same-cover nonreplay endpoint packets

## Statement
Let H be a finite Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament with pc(H)>2, let J=(j_0,j_1,j_2,j_3,j_4) be a proper vertex-simple tight P5, put D={j_1,j_2,j_3}, E=V(H)\V(J), and let T be any literal exact two-cover of H-D. Then either H contains a tight P6 obtained by adjoining to one endpoint of J a T-selected vertex of E, or, in the no-P6 branch, the R776 endpoint-chord dichotomy upgrades as follows. (CHORD-NONREPLAY) If {j_0,j_4} is selected in T, then at least one endpoint has a T-selected exterior neighbor h in E; for that endpoint the only boundary-antisymmetric orientation compatible with no P6 is the reverse terminal-contact orientation, so accepted R773 yields either an adjacent local P4 or its one-step-inward R703 Reverse-Ear/reversal/cycle geometry. Retain the selected endpoint chord simultaneously in T. (DUAL-NONREPLAY) If {j_0,j_4} is not selected in T, then T has selected exterior states {j_0,a} and {j_4,b} with a,b in E. In the no-P6 branch boundary antisymmetry forces both reverse terminal contacts (j_1,j_0,a) and (b,j_4,j_3) tight. Accepted R773 therefore yields, independently at both ends, an adjacent local P4 or a one-step-inward R703 Reverse-Ear/reversal/cycle packet. The two source exterior states coexist in the same exact cover T. Thus internal-trimer recompletion of a proper P5 cannot leave a bare endpoint-crossing residue: absent immediate path extension, it produces a chorded nonreplay packet or simultaneous two-ended nonreplay geometry.

## Hypotheses
H is finite Strong Level-(1) with pc(H)>2; J is a proper vertex-simple tight P5; T is a literal exact two-cover of H-{j_1,j_2,j_3}. Use accepted R776, boundary antisymmetry R3, and accepted R773.

## Scope
Order-free generic consumer of the accepted R776 P5 recompletion theorem. No crossed frame, smallest-counterexample minimality beyond supplied T, R5,R168,R169,R224,R533,R350,generic R358,R176,R312,R436,capture,payment,or computation.

## Applicability
Use immediately after R776. First test the forced T-selected endpoint-exterior states against the terminal turns of J. Any forward orientation is a literal P6 extension. If no such extension exists, use R773 on the forced reverse terminal contacts. In the DUAL-EXTERIOR branch this yields two source-labelled nonreplay packets tied to one common exact recompletion; in the ENDPOINT-CHORD branch retain the selected endpoint chord while consuming the forced exterior state.

## Persistence
Retain J,D,T,the endpoint-chord selected/not-selected bit, every R776 source endpoint-exterior selected state used, the exact R3 orientation at each endpoint, and either the resulting literal P6 or the full R773 certificate (adjacent P4 or shifted R703 Reverse-Ear/reversal/cycle geometry). In DUAL-NONREPLAY retain that both endpoint source states coexist in the same T; later R773 outputs are graph-intrinsic certificates and are not asserted to coexist as selected states.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not consume the resulting P6, local P4, Reverse-Ear, reversal, or cycle. Does not assert the two exterior neighbors a,b are distinct, lie on different rails, or survive as selected states after any later continuation. In CHORD-NONREPLAY does not prescribe which endpoint has the exterior neighbor. Does not say the endpoint chord alone carries sign information or forms a cycle. Does not close H by itself.

## Proof
Apply accepted R776 to the fixed exact cover T of H-D. First consider any T-selected exterior state {j_0,a} at the left endpoint, with a in E. Boundary antisymmetry R3 on the three distinct vertices {a,j_0,j_1} gives exactly one of (a,j_0,j_1) and (j_1,j_0,a) tight. In the first case, the old P5 turns (j_0,j_1,j_2),(j_1,j_2,j_3),(j_2,j_3,j_4) concatenate with (a,j_0,j_1), so (a,j_0,j_1,j_2,j_3,j_4) is a vertex-simple tight P6. In the second case, (j_1,j_0,a) is exactly the reverse head-contact hypothesis of accepted R773 on K=J with h=a. Hence R773 yields either the adjacent local P4 or the shifted one-step-inward R703 Reverse-Ear/reversal/cycle geometry. Dually, for any T-selected exterior state {j_4,b}, R3 on {j_3,j_4,b} gives either (j_3,j_4,b) tight, yielding the P6 (j_0,j_1,j_2,j_3,j_4,b), or (b,j_4,j_3) tight, exactly the reverse tail-contact hypothesis of R773. Now suppose no such P6 exists. If R776 is in ENDPOINT-CHORD, the chord {j_0,j_4} is selected and R776 supplies at least one endpoint-exterior state; by the preceding classification its forward orientation is impossible, so it yields an R773 nonreplay packet while the chord remains selected in the same T. If R776 is in DUAL-EXTERIOR, it supplies both {j_0,a} and {j_4,b} in the same T. No-P6 excludes both forward orientations, so both reverse terminal contacts are forced and R773 applies at both ends. This proves the stated alternatives.

# R784 — A raw first-inward R547 hinge does not license Complete Floor Pair Steering

## Statement
Retain the accepted crossed R621/R723 frame and fix x in X. The raw tight turns (q_1,q_2,q_3) and (q_2,q_1,x) make D_Q=(q_1,q_2) tail-signed and D_x=(q_1,x) head-signed, with supports meeting exactly at q_1. Accepted R547 therefore applies at the graph-intrinsic signed-support level and yields disjoint opposite-sign singleton supports (q_2) and (x), together with the two ancestor dimers and hinge-cut witnesses.

This output does NOT by itself satisfy the hypothesis of accepted Complete Floor Pair Steering R432. R547's theorem contract distinguishes the graph-intrinsic balanced pair from the ancestry-bearing floor specialization: the latter is asserted only inside a hypothetical smallest-counterexample signed-payment lineage. R432 in turn requires an active ancestry-bearing both-singleton floor whose historical singleton signs and pair ancestry are available, and its persistence contract explicitly consumes the incoming paid-floor ledger, including original pair birth/refund-contact data and actualizing replacement certificates. The raw D_Q,D_x construction supplies no pair-deletion cover, pair birth, capture, actualization, payment, or earlier refund/contact ledger.

Consequently one may not infer from the raw hinge alone that R432 can preserve q_2 and replace x by q_{m-2}. Any such steering requires a separate theorem establishing that the R547 hinge descendants belong to an active signed-payment lineage with the ledger required by R432, or a new steering theorem whose hypothesis is only a graph-intrinsic balanced pair.

In particular the conclusion of superseded R774 is not established by dependencies R547,R723,R432 alone.

## Hypotheses
Use accepted R547,R432,R723 and the canonical signed-support/floor distinction in their exact contracts. No additional payment-lineage hypothesis is assumed for the raw first-inward dimers.

## Scope
Canonical correction/fence for superseded R774. It separates graph-intrinsic hinge collapse from lineage-qualified paid-floor steering. No new positive route is asserted.

## Applicability
Before invoking R432 on a both-singleton pair obtained from raw signed turns or an R547 hinge, verify an actual signed-payment lineage and its retained pair-birth/actualization/refund ledger. If that ledger is absent, stop at the graph-intrinsic balanced pair; do not steer its coordinates.

## Persistence
Retain D_Q,D_x,their exact witnesses,the hinge q_1,the R547 singleton descendants,and the negative provenance fact that no paid-floor ledger has been established. If later mathematics establishes lineage membership, retain that new certificate separately before invoking R432.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not deny the graph-intrinsic R547 singleton pair, and does not claim no payment lineage can ever be constructed. Does not weaken R432 for genuine ancestry-bearing paid floors. Does not invalidate accepted R723 or R547. It only blocks the unlicensed raw-hinge-to-R432 composition used by R774.

## Proof
The turns (q_1,q_2,q_3) and (q_2,q_1,x) establish the two signed dimers and the one-vertex hinge, so R547 applies exactly as a pure signed-path contact lemma. Its statement first concludes a graph-intrinsic balanced pair of total mass two. Only afterward does it add: in a hypothetical smallest-counterexample signed-payment lineage this is an ancestry-bearing both-singleton floor. Thus lineage membership is an additional specialization, not a consequence of the raw hinge hypotheses.

R432 assumes an ancestry-bearing both-singleton balanced-pair floor is active and says the historical singleton signs and pair ancestry are available to the replacement macro. Its persistence clause is stronger still: the continuation retains the full physical ancestry ledger of the incoming paid floor, including original pair birth/refund-contact certificates and actualizing replacement data, and its exclusions forbid bare formal relabeling without those physical certificates.

The raw D_Q,D_x construction used by R774 has only graph-intrinsic tight turns plus R547 hinge-cut ancestry. It explicitly uses no deletion cover, capture, actualization, payment, or refund/contact step. Therefore the hypotheses required by R432 are not established. The claimed coordinate steering is consequently unlicensed unless additional lineage-producing mathematics is supplied. This proves the fence.

# R785 — Every two-witness short-carrier END branch is a selected-state reversal or a P4

## Statement
Let H be a finite Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament with pc(H)>2. Let K be a tight trimer, let S be one reverse boundary dimer of K in a fixed tested orientation, let e be the complementary singleton, and assume S has two distinct same-polarity witnesses w_1,w_2 outside K on that same tested orientation. Let T be any exact two-cover of H-V(S), and suppose accepted R696 is in its END branch, so deg_T(e)=1. Then the exact R511 trimer-endpoint normal form forces one of two graph-intrinsic outputs. (REV) Some physical state pq selected in T has the reverse state qp occurring inside the forced reverse trimer from the END hole certificate. (P4) The END hole certificate supplies an opposite-polarity sign on the exact tested orientation S; choosing one of w_1,w_2 distinct from the new witness and applying accepted R523 gives a literal tight Hamilton P4. Thus no two-witness R696 END branch needs to terminate as an anonymous one/two-hole mate clause: it always compiles to selected-state reversal geometry or a P4. The reverse-initial/tail-signed case is the exact order dual of the reverse-terminal/head-signed case.

## Hypotheses
H is finite Strong Level-(1) with pc(H)>2; K is a tight trimer; S is a reverse boundary dimer of K with a fixed tested orientation and two distinct same-polarity witnesses w_1,w_2 outside K; e is the complementary singleton; T is an exact two-cover of H-V(S); R696 is in END, equivalently deg_T(e)=1.

## Scope
Order-free parent generalization of accepted R720. No crossed frame, smallest-counterexample minimality, R5,R168,R169,R224,R533,R350,generic R358,R176,R312,R436,capture,payment,or computation.

## Applicability
Use immediately whenever an R696 two-witness short-carrier packet lands in END. Read the exact R511 degree-one trimer specialization before preserving a mate clause. In the cross-depth R781 packet this removes END as anonymous residue and yields an actual current-state reversal or a role-labelled P4.

## Persistence
Retain K,S,e,T,the exact tested orientation of S,the two same-polarity witness certificates,the literal END rail orientation and complete R511 hole set. In REV retain the selected T-state pq and its tight reverse qp. In P4 retain the opposite-polarity certificate on the exact tested S,the chosen old witness distinct from the new witness,and the resulting ordered P4.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not say REV or P4 alone closes H. Does not compare certificates on opposite tested orientations of one unordered dimer. Does not consume R696 FREE or SANDWICH. Does not assert a degree-one exact cover can always be chosen. Does not use the optional R696 capture/payment continuation.

## Proof
Write first K=(e,k_1,k_2), with reverse terminal tested dimer S=(k_2,k_1) head-signed by distinct witnesses w_1,w_2. Since R696 is in END, e has degree one in T. If e is the terminal vertex of its mixed T-rail, the aligned endpoint case of the exact R511/R509 trimer specialization has one hole, and the forced reverse trimer contains the reverse of the unique selected state incident with e. This is REV. Otherwise e begins the mixed rail. Write the other pure exterior rail C=(c_0,...,c_s). The exact m=2,i=0 R511 formula gives complete hole set {(c_{s-1},c_s,k_1) if s>=1} union {(c_s,k_1,k_2)}. Since pc(H)>2, not all holes are tight. If the first hole is bad, R3 gives (k_1,c_s,c_{s-1}) tight; its terminal state c_sc_{s-1} reverses the selected T-state c_{s-1}c_s, giving REV. If the second hole is bad, R3 gives (k_2,k_1,c_s) tight. This is a tail certificate on the exact tested dimer S=(k_2,k_1), opposite the fixed head polarity supplied by w_1,w_2. The new witness c_s can equal at most one of the two distinct old witnesses, so choose w_i distinct from c_s. Accepted R523 on that exact tested orientation gives the literal P4 (w_i,k_2,k_1,c_s). These alternatives exhaust END. For the reverse-initial case K=(k_0,k_1,e), where S=(k_1,k_0) is tail-signed by w_1,w_2, reverse all orders. The aligned one-hole branch again yields REV; in the nonaligned branch one bad hole reverses a selected pure-rail state and the other yields a head certificate (c_0,k_1,k_0) on the exact tested S, which combines by R523 with a distinct fixed tail witness to give P4. Hence every two-witness END branch is REV or P4.

# R801 — The SHORTCUT-CUT P4 and P6 are X-blocked at both ends: no X vertex can seam onto K or J-sharp

## Statement
In the SHORTCUT-CUT branch of accepted R789, neither of the two distinguished tight paths can be extended by a vertex of X at either end. Precisely: (K-BLOCK) For every x in X, the turn (x,u,v) is bad and the turn (d,s,x) is bad. Hence no x in X prepends to K=(u,v,d,s) and no x in X appends to it. (J-BLOCK) For every x in X, the turn (x,L,u) is bad and the turn (s,R,x) is bad. Hence no x in X prepends to J#=(L,u,v,d,s,R) and no x in X appends to it. Both blocks are immediate from accepted universal star geometry together with boundary antisymmetry: accepted R723 gives (v,u,x) and (x,s,d) tight for every x in X, and accepted R594 gives (u,L,x) and (x,R,s) tight for every x in X, so R3 makes each displayed complete reversal bad. CONSEQUENCE for the X-ENDPOINT-CROSSING residue. In the SHORTCUT-CUT branch the natural spanning proposals are K together with the two rails of the exact cover T# of H-{u,v,d,s}, and J# together with a path on X union Q[3,m-3]. Neither proposal can be improved by seaming an X vertex onto an end of K or of J#. Therefore any spanning-two-cover splice in this branch must attach at a deep interval vertex of Q[3,m-3], or at the physical endpoints L,R in a manner not consisting of an X vertex adjacent to an end of J#, or must proceed by an interior rail exchange rather than an end seam. In particular the X-ENDPOINT-CROSSING alternative of R789, in which the selected {L,R}-to-X crossing lands in X rather than in deep Q, cannot be consumed by end-seaming that crossing partner onto either distinguished path.

## Hypotheses
Accepted crossed R621/R723 frame, m>=6, in the SHORTCUT-CUT branch of accepted R789: A=(u,v,d) and B=(v,d,s) are both tight, K=(u,v,d,s) is the tight P4, and J#=(L,u,v,d,s,R) is the tight endpoint-preserving P6, with L=q_0,u=q_1,v=q_2,d=q_{m-2},s=q_{m-1},R=q_m. Uses accepted R723, R594, R3.

## Scope
Cheap reusable blocking fact for the accepted R789 SHORTCUT-CUT branch. Uses only accepted R789, R723, R594 and boundary antisymmetry R3. No cover, capture, contact, payment, floor steering, R436, R508 recount, or computation.

## Applicability
Apply as a closure-saturation filter before attempting any end-seam construction in the SHORTCUT-CUT branch. It removes the whole family of X-end-attachment proposals in one step, and it says the two ends of J# are X-inert in exactly the same way at both physical endpoints, which is a two-ended symmetric fact rather than one-sided information. Use it to direct effort at deep Q[3,m-3] attachment or at interior exchange.

## Persistence
Retain the SHORTCUT-CUT branch data of R789 (A,B tight, K, J#), the four families of accepted star turns (v,u,x),(x,s,d),(u,L,x),(x,R,s), and the four displayed bad reversals (x,u,v),(d,s,x),(x,L,u),(s,R,x). All outputs are graph-intrinsic and cover-free.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not close H and is not progress by the standing strict-cut criterion; it is a blocking fact only. Does not block attachment of a deep Q[3,m-3] vertex to K or J#, which is untested here. Does not block interior splices, rail exchanges, or non-end seams. Does not claim T# has any particular rail endpoint structure, nor which of L,R carries the R508 crossing. Does not assert the X-ENDPOINT-CROSSING alternative is impossible; it only removes end-seam consumers of it. Does not apply outside the SHORTCUT-CUT branch, since REV-L and REV-R supply different P4s.

## Proof
Work in the SHORTCUT-CUT branch of accepted R789, so A=(u,v,d) and B=(v,d,s) are tight, K=(u,v,d,s) is a tight P4, and J#=(L,u,v,d,s,R) is a tight P6.

K-BLOCK. Extending K at its initial end by a vertex y means asserting the tight path (y,u,v,d,s), whose initial turn is (y,u,v). Accepted R723 gives the tight trimer (v,u,x) for every x in X. By boundary antisymmetry R3, the ordered turn (a,b,c) is tight exactly when its complete reversal (c,b,a) is bad; applying this to (v,u,x) shows (x,u,v) is bad. Hence for y=x in X the required initial turn is bad and no such extension exists. Extending K at its terminal end by y means asserting (u,v,d,s,y), whose terminal turn is (d,s,y). Accepted R723 gives (x,s,d) tight for every x in X, so by R3 its complete reversal (d,s,x) is bad. Hence no x in X appends. This proves K-BLOCK.

J-BLOCK. Extending J# at its initial end by y requires the initial turn (y,L,u). Accepted R594 gives (u,L,x) tight for every x in X, so by R3 the complete reversal (x,L,u) is bad, and no x in X prepends. Extending J# at its terminal end by y requires the terminal turn (s,R,y). Accepted R594 gives (x,R,s) tight for every x in X, so by R3 the complete reversal (s,R,x) is bad, and no x in X appends. This proves J-BLOCK.

CONSEQUENCE. In this branch accepted R4 supplies an exact two-cover T# of H-{u,v,d,s}, and R789 forces a selected state crossing {L,R} against X union Q[3,m-3]. Suppose that crossing lands in X, which is the X-ENDPOINT-CROSSING residue named as the current frontier. The obvious closure-saturation move is to seam the X partner of that crossing onto an end of one of the two distinguished tight paths, producing a spanning proposal with fewer components. K-BLOCK and J-BLOCK show every such end seam is bad, for every vertex of X and at every one of the four ends. Hence no end-seam consumer of the X-ENDPOINT-CROSSING residue exists, and a successful splice in this branch must use a deep Q[3,m-3] attachment or an interior exchange. Note the blocks are symmetric across the two physical ends, so this is two-ended information and is not subject to the one-sided fences of accepted R626 and R721. This proves the negative result.

# R803 — A long-rail deep crossing is multiple, reverse-ear geometric, or pinned to the first/last deep vertex

## Statement
Let H be a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample and let Q=(q_0,...,q_m) be a vertex-simple tight path with m>=6. Put L=q_0,u=q_1,v=q_2, M=Q[3,m-3], rho=q_{m-3}, d=q_{m-2},s=q_{m-1},R=q_m. Test A=(u,v,d) and B=(v,d,s), and choose one bounded tight deletion path D as follows: if A is bad, boundary antisymmetry gives C_L=(d,v,u) tight and take D={d,v,u}; if A is tight and B is bad, take C_R=(s,d,v) and D={s,d,v}; if A and B are tight, take C_#=(u,v,d,s) and D={u,v,d,s}. For every exact two-cover T of H-D let tau_M(T) be the number of selected T-states with one endpoint in M and the other in C=V(H)-(D union M). Then tau_M(T)>=1. Moreover, for every such T exactly one of the following holds: (MULTI) tau_M(T)>=2; (EAR) comparing the M-subpath(s) of T with the original path Q via R435 yields an explicit reversal of an old Q-state, a tight reverse trimer, or a vertex-simple tight cycle; (PINNED-ONE) tau_M(T)=1, one T rail is a pure C-path, the other consists of the entire M-block followed by one C-block or vice versa, the M-block is literally (q_3,q_4,...,q_{m-3}), and the unique selected M|C state is therefore exactly (rho,y) or (y,q_3) for some y in C. Thus a unique quiet deep crossing can occur only at the first or last vertex of the untouched deep interval.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample; Q is a vertex-simple tight path of order at least seven (m>=6). Uses accepted boundary antisymmetry R3, smallest-counterexample complement exactness R4, Reverse Ear R435, and absorber-complement unique-transition normal form R560.

## Scope
Order-free long-rail refinement. No R24 frame, four-cell classification, endpoint gates, R5,R168,R169,R224,R533,R350,generic R358,R508,capture,payment,R436,or computation.

## Applicability
Apply whenever a smallest counterexample contains a tight path Q of order at least seven. First choose the bounded trimer/P4 deletion by the two cross-depth tests. In any exact complement two-cover count selected states across M=Q[3,m-3]. Two or more crossings are retained directly. If there is exactly one, use R560 and R435; outside explicit reverse-ear geometry the crossing is forced to be incident with q_3 or q_{m-3}. Downstream arguments may therefore treat the tau=1 cell as a nearest-deep boundary event rather than an anonymous interior crossing.

## Persistence
Retain Q, the chosen branch and deletion path D, the exact cover T, M and C, tau_M(T), and all selected M|C states. In EAR retain the exact R435 reversal/reverse-trimer/cycle. In PINNED-ONE retain the pure C rail, mixed rail orientation, literal M-block order, outside endpoint y, and whether the unique state is (rho,y) or (y,q_3).

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert tau_M(T)>=2. Does not treat an R435 cycle as a contradiction. Does not identify the outside vertex y in PINNED-ONE or claim the pinned crossing alone closes H. Does not assert different deletion-branch covers coexist. When m=6, q_3=rho and the two pinned physical deep vertices coincide, though the crossing orientation remains distinguished.

## Proof
Write E=V(H)-V(Q), M=Q[3,m-3], and choose D by the displayed tests. In the LEFT case A=(u,v,d) is bad, so R3 gives (d,v,u) tight. In the RIGHT case A is tight and B=(v,d,s) is bad, so R3 gives (s,d,v) tight. In the FOUR case A and B are tight and concatenate to the tight P4 (u,v,d,s). In each case D is therefore the support of a proper graph-intrinsic tight path, so accepted R4 supplies an exact two-cover T of H-D. Put C=V(H)-(D union M). Both M and C are nonempty: m>=6 makes M nonempty, while C contains at least the physical outer vertices not deleted. Suppose T selected no state crossing M|C. Then each T rail lies wholly in one side of the partition. Since T has exactly two nonempty rails and both sides are nonempty, one rail is a Hamilton tight path on all of C and the other lies on M. But the original Q supplies a tight Hamilton path on D union M: in LEFT use Q[1,m-2]=(u,v,q_3,...,rho,d); in RIGHT use Q[2,m-1]=(v,q_3,...,rho,d,s); in FOUR use Q[1,m-1]=(u,v,q_3,...,rho,d,s). This old-Q path and the Hamilton C rail are disjoint and span H, contradicting pc(H)=3. Hence tau_M(T)>=1. If tau_M(T)>=2 we are in MULTI. Assume tau_M(T)=1. Apply accepted R560 to the partition D,M,C, using the displayed old-Q Hamilton path as a one-path cover of H[D union M] and T as the two-cover of H-D. R560 says exactly one T rail is mixed and consists of one M-block and one C-block in one of the two orders, every vertex of M lies in that unique M-block, and the other T rail is wholly in C. Let K_M be the tight M-block. Compare K_M with the original tight path P_M=(q_3,q_4,...,rho) using accepted Reverse Ear R435. If K_M encounters two P_M vertices in decreasing P_M order, R435 gives an old-state reversal, tight reverse trimer, or vertex-simple tight cycle, which is EAR. Otherwise all P_M contacts on K_M occur in increasing order. Since V(K_M)=V(P_M)=M and every M vertex occurs exactly once, K_M must literally be (q_3,q_4,...,rho). If the mixed rail has order K_M followed by a C-block, its unique M|C state is (rho,y), where y is the first C vertex. If the mixed rail has a C-block followed by K_M, its unique crossing is (y,q_3), where y is the last C vertex. This is PINNED-ONE and exhausts the possibilities.

# R804 — The R803 unique pinned deep crossing always forces an old-Q state reversal

## Statement
Retain accepted R803 with L=q_0,u=q_1,v=q_2,M=Q[3,m-3],rho=q_{m-3},d=q_{m-2},s=q_{m-1},R=q_m, and suppose an exact complement two-cover T is in PINNED-ONE. Thus the sole M|C selected state is either (rho,y) or (y,q_3). Then H already contains a tight path containing the reversal of an old consecutive Q-state. Consequently PINNED-ONE is not a genuine quiet residue: every exact cover in the R803 construction satisfies either (MULTI) tau_M(T)>=2 or (EAR+) an explicit old-Q state reversal, tight reverse trimer/contact, or vertex-simple tight cycle. More explicitly, the pinned branch always yields one of the reversed states v u, q_3 v, s d, q_4 q_3, or rho p where p is the old Q-predecessor of rho (p=q_{m-4} when m>=7 and p=v when m=6), embedded in a displayed tight trimer supplied by R579 or R573.

## Hypotheses
Retain accepted R803 and its PINNED-ONE branch for a tight path Q=(q_0,...,q_m), m>=6. Use accepted wrap tetrachotomy R579 and accepted unique-crossing Hamilton-ending lemma R573.

## Scope
Order-free consumer of the only quiet unique-transition cell in accepted R803. No R24 frame, four-cell structure, capture, payment, R436, R508, or computation.

## Applicability
Use immediately after accepted R803. Do not split PINNED-ONE by the identity of y: wrap the branch-specific Hamilton absorber. A failed needed wrap seam already gives a reversed old-Q state by R579; a successful wrap moves q_3 or rho to an absorber endpoint, where R573 applied to the unique selected crossing gives a tight trimer containing q_4 q_3 or rho p. Thus only MULTI remains as a non-EAR current-cover residue.

## Persistence
Retain Q, the R803 branch-specific deletion path and absorber, T, the unique selected crossing, the R579 wrap branch, and the exact tight trimer/P4 or R573 reverse-sign trimer exhibiting the old-Q reversal.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not claim an old-state reversal, reverse trimer, or cycle is itself a contradiction or spanning two-cover. Does not consume the MULTI branch. Does not assert the R573 sign trimer is selected in T; it is graph-intrinsic. When m=6 the deep interval is the singleton {q_3}, and the predecessor/successor formulas specialize as stated.

## Proof
Let the three branch-specific Hamilton absorbers on D union M from accepted R803 be P_L=(u,v,q_3,...,rho,d) in LEFT, P_R=(v,q_3,...,rho,d,s) in RIGHT, and P_F=(u,v,q_3,...,rho,d,s) in FOUR. We treat the two possible PINNED-ONE orientations.

LEFT, crossing (rho,y). For P_L the first wrap seam in R579 is alpha_L=(d,u,v). If alpha_L is bad, R579 is in SW2 or DF and supplies the tight reversed seam (v,u,d), which contains the reversed old Q-state vu. If alpha_L is tight, R579 gives the tight rotation (d,u,v,q_3,...,rho), a Hamilton path on D union M ending at rho. Apply accepted R573 in its CS form to the unique selected state rho y. If p is the penultimate vertex of that rotation, R573 forces (y,rho,p) tight. Here p=q_{m-4} for m>=7, while for m=6 we have p=v; in either case rho p is the reversal of the old consecutive Q-state p rho.

LEFT, crossing (y,q_3). Apply the full R579 tetrachotomy to P_L. In every non-DW branch R579 supplies one of the tight reversed seams (u,d,rho) or (v,u,d), containing respectively the reversed old state d rho or v u. In DW the absorber is a tight Hamilton cycle. Rotate that cycle to start at q_3; its successor is q_4 (equal to d when m=6). R573 in SC form applied to y q_3 then forces (q_4,q_3,y) tight, containing the reversed old state q_4 q_3.

RIGHT, crossing (y,q_3). For P_R the second wrap seam is beta_R=(d,s,v). If beta_R is bad, R579 is in SW1 or DF and supplies (v,s,d) tight, containing the reversed old state s d. If beta_R is tight, R579 gives rot2=(q_3,...,rho,d,s,v), beginning at q_3 with successor q_4; R573 SC gives (q_4,q_3,y) tight.

RIGHT, crossing (rho,y). Apply the full R579 tetrachotomy to P_R. Every non-DW branch supplies either (v,s,d) or (q_3,v,s), containing respectively the reversed old state s d or q_3 v. In DW rotate the tight Hamilton cycle to (d,s,v,q_3,...,rho), which ends at rho. R573 CS gives (y,rho,p) tight with p the old predecessor of rho, hence the reversed old state rho p.

FOUR. Apply the full R579 tetrachotomy to P_F. Every non-DW branch supplies either (u,s,d) or (v,u,s), containing the reversed old state s d or v u. In DW the absorber is a Hamilton cycle. For crossing rho y rotate it to (d,s,u,v,q_3,...,rho) and apply R573 CS, obtaining (y,rho,p) with reversed old state rho p. For crossing y q_3 rotate it to start q_3 and apply R573 SC, obtaining (q_4,q_3,y).

Thus every PINNED-ONE case contains an explicit reversal of an old consecutive Q-state. Combining with the MULTI/EAR/PINNED-ONE trichotomy of accepted R803 eliminates PINNED-ONE as a separate quiet branch and yields the stated MULTI versus EAR+ dichotomy.

# R806 — The crossed arbitrary-order frame renormalizes to one fixed order-ten exact-two-cover core plus the middle rail

## Statement
Retain the accepted crossed R621 frame in the beyond-order-ten range m>=6, with X={a,b,c,z}, Q=(q_0,...,q_m), L=q_0, u=q_1, v=q_2, M=Q[3,m-3], d=q_{m-2}, s=q_{m-1}, and R=q_m. Put G=H[X union {L,u,v,d,s,R}]. Then |V(G)|=10, V(H)=V(G) disjoint-union V(M), M is a tight Hamilton path on its support, and pc(G)=2. Consequently every exact two-cover G=A sqcup B gives a literal minimum spanning three-cover H=A sqcup B sqcup M. Moreover the three bounded deletion supports appearing in accepted R803, D_L={d,v,u}, D_R={s,d,v}, and D_F={u,v,d,s}, all lie in this same fixed core G. Thus every R803 exact complement cover is a recompletion of one bounded puncture of G coupled to the unchanged middle rail M; in particular the R803/R804 MULTI branch is intrinsically a same-cover coupling between M and G-D, not an arbitrary-order outer residue.

## Hypotheses
Accepted crossed R621 frame with m>=6 and smallest-counterexample minimality R4. The final interpretation of the three named bounded punctures uses accepted R803.

## Scope
Elevator renormalization of the crossed beyond-ten R24 frame. No R5,R168,R169,R224,R533,R350,generic R358,capture,payment,R436,or computation.

## Applicability
Use before classifying MULTI crossings. Replace the variable-size outer world by the fixed induced ten-vertex core G. Choose and retain an exact two-cover A sqcup B of G; then M sqcup A sqcup B is a canonical minimum three-cover of H. Analyze R803 MULTI by comparing its exact cover of H-D against the punctured geometry of this fixed core, rather than by treating its M-crossings independently.

## Persistence
Retain the physical ten-set X union {L,u,v,d,s,R}, the middle interval M, the exact equality pc(G)=2, one chosen exact two-cover A sqcup B of G, and the fact that D_L,D_R,D_F are all subsets of G while M is untouched.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert G is a smallest counterexample or permit use of the order-ten counterexample theorem R191 on G. Does not classify the exact two-covers of G, force endpoint universality in G, or by itself consume MULTI. Does not claim different R803 deletion-cover representatives coexist. The conclusion is a representation/renormalization theorem: fixed order-ten pc=2 core plus one long tight rail.

## Proof
Because m>=6, the six Q-coordinates L=q_0,u=q_1,v=q_2,d=q_{m-2},s=q_{m-1},R=q_m are pairwise distinct. The four-set X is disjoint from V(Q), so G has exactly ten vertices. The remaining Q vertices are exactly M=Q[3,m-3]; hence V(H)=V(G) disjoint-union V(M). Since Q is tight, its interval M is a tight Hamilton path on V(M), including the singleton case m=6. In particular M is nonempty, so G is a proper induced subsystem of H. Accepted smallest-counterexample minimality R4 therefore gives pc(G)<=2. Suppose pc(G)=1. Then G has a Hamilton tight path P_G. The two disjoint tight paths P_G and M cover all vertices of H, giving pc(H)<=2, contradicting the R4 conclusion pc(H)=3. Therefore pc(G)=2. Choose any exact two-cover G=A sqcup B. Then A,B,M are three disjoint tight paths covering H. Since pc(H)=3, this is a literal minimum three-cover. Finally, accepted R803 uses only D_L={d,v,u}, D_R={s,d,v}, or D_F={u,v,d,s}; each is visibly contained in V(G), while M is disjoint from all three. Hence every R803 recompletion deletes a bounded subset of the same fixed ten-core and leaves the same middle rail untouched. This proves the stated renormalization and the interpretation of MULTI as M-to-(G-D) coupling.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R806.md -->

# R807 — Each crossed seven-vertex puncture core exposes its exceptional outer endpoint in an exact two-cover

## Statement
Retain the accepted crossed R621 frame with X={a,b,c,z}, endpoints L=q_0,R=q_m, first inward vertices u=q_1,s=q_{m-1}, and crossed middle gate M_S={{a,c},{b,z}}. Put C_L=X union {L,s,R} and C_R=X union {L,u,R}. Then C_L has a literal exact two-cover by two nonempty tight paths in which R is an endpoint of one rail, and C_R has a literal exact two-cover in which L is an endpoint of one rail. More precisely, LEFT: apply R518 to the tight trimer (L,c,a) with fourth vertex s. If {L,c,a,s} supports a Hamilton P4 P, then P sqcup (b,z,R) is an exact two-cover of C_L exposing R. Otherwise R518 forces the reverse contact (c,L,s) tight, and (c,L,s) sqcup (a,b,z,R) is an exact two-cover of C_L exposing R. RIGHT: apply R518 to the tight trimer (b,z,R) with fourth vertex u. If {b,z,R,u} supports a Hamilton P4 P, then (L,a,c) sqcup P is an exact two-cover of C_R exposing L. Otherwise R518 forces the reverse contact (u,R,z) tight, and (L,a,c,b) sqcup (u,R,z) is an exact two-cover of C_R exposing L.

## Hypotheses
Accepted crossed R621 frame; accepted universal four-cell theorem R518.

## Scope
Fixed seven-vertex local endpoint-exposure lemma. No minimality, R803/R806, R5,R168,R169,R224,R533,R350,generic R358,capture,payment,R436,or computation.

## Applicability
Use in the R803/R806 LEFT and RIGHT puncture cores whenever a two-rail bracketing argument needs the exceptional physical endpoint R (left core) or L (right core) to be available as a rail endpoint. Together with the previously explicit core covers, this removes the sole endpoint exception in the contiguous-middle minimum-MULTI bracketing analysis.

## Persistence
Retain the physical core C_L or C_R, the R518 branch, and the displayed exact endpoint-exposing two-cover with its literal rail orders.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert a unique endpoint-exposing cover, Hamiltonicity of the seven-vertex core, or closure of H. Does not use or imply R572 by itself.

## Proof
LEFT. Accepted R621 gives the tight trimer (L,c,a), the tight trimer (b,z,R), and the tight P4 (a,b,z,R) as a prefix of (a,b,z,R,s). Apply accepted R518 to C=(L,c,a) with fourth vertex s. If the four-set {L,c,a,s} is Hamilton-P4, choose any Hamilton tight path P on it. Its support is disjoint from {b,z,R}, so P and (b,z,R) are two disjoint nonempty tight paths covering C_L, with R an endpoint of the second rail. If the four-set is P4-free, R518 forces the reverse contact (c,L,s) tight. The two tight paths (c,L,s) and (a,b,z,R) are disjoint, nonempty, and their supports partition C_L; R is an endpoint of the second rail. Thus C_L has the required endpoint-exposing exact two-cover. RIGHT. Accepted R621 gives the tight trimer (b,z,R), the tight trimer (L,a,c), and the tight P4 (L,a,c,b). Apply R518 to C=(b,z,R) with fourth vertex u. In the Hamilton-P4 branch, a Hamilton path P on {b,z,R,u} together with (L,a,c) exactly two-covers C_R and exposes L. In the no-P4 branch, R518 forces the reverse contact (u,R,z) tight. Then (L,a,c,b) and (u,R,z) are disjoint nonempty tight paths covering C_R, with L an endpoint of the first rail. This proves both assertions.

# R808 — Every four-exterior long rail has a branch-independent ten-vertex pc=2 core

## Statement
Let H be a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample and let Q=(q_0,...,q_m), m>=6, be a vertex-simple tight path with exactly four exterior vertices X=V(H)-V(Q). Put M=Q[3,m-3] and G=H[X union {q_0,q_1,q_2,q_{m-2},q_{m-1},q_m}]. Then |V(G)|=10, V(H)=V(G) disjoint-union V(M), M is a tight Hamilton path on its support, and pc(G)=2. Consequently every exact two-cover G=A sqcup B gives a literal minimum spanning three-cover H=A sqcup B sqcup M. This conclusion is independent of every endpoint-gate, matching-height, aligned/crossed, seam-badness, capture, payment, and reverse-ear choice.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample; Q is a proper vertex-simple tight path with exactly four exterior vertices; m>=6. Uses accepted smallest-counterexample minimality R4 only.

## Scope
Order-free branch-independent core renormalization for the four-exterior long-rail regime. No R5,R168,R169,R224,R533,R350,generic R358, gate classification, capture, payment, R436, Reverse Ear, or computation.

## Applicability
Apply upstream of the aligned/crossed R541 split. Replace the variable-length four-exterior frame by one fixed ten-vertex pc=2 core G plus the untouched Hamilton middle interval M. Downstream branch-specific arguments should be phrased as attempts to splice M onto an exact two-cover rail of G, or to prove that such a splice is impossible and exploit the resulting bad seam.

## Persistence
Retain X,Q,M,G, the exact equality pc(G)=2, and one chosen exact two-cover A sqcup B of G. No claim is made that a particular core cover is canonical.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not close H. Does not say G is a smallest counterexample or permit R191 on G. Does not expose any prescribed endpoint in a core two-cover and does not certify a seam between M and G. It is a representation theorem only.

## Proof
Because Q has exactly four exterior vertices and m>=6, the six named Q vertices q_0,q_1,q_2,q_{m-2},q_{m-1},q_m are pairwise distinct and disjoint from X, so G has order ten. The remaining vertices of Q are exactly M=Q[3,m-3], hence V(H)=V(G) disjoint-union V(M). Since Q is tight, M is a tight Hamilton path on its support; when m=6 it is a singleton path. Thus M is nonempty and G is a proper induced subsystem of H. Accepted R4 gives pc(G)<=2. If pc(G)=1, let P_G be a Hamilton tight path of G. Then P_G and M are two vertex-disjoint tight paths whose supports partition V(H), yielding pc(H)<=2, contradicting the R4 conclusion pc(H)=3. Therefore pc(G)=2. Any exact two-cover G=A sqcup B then gives the literal minimum three-cover A sqcup B sqcup M of H.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R808.md -->

# R810 — The synchronized transitive frame renormalizes before the gate split to one order-eight exact-two-cover core plus the middle rail

## Statement
Retain the accepted synchronized transitive frame R594 in the beyond-order-ten range, with X the transitive matching-height four-cell and Q=(q_0,...,q_m), m>=6. Write L=q_0, u=q_1, s=q_{m-1}, R=q_m, put N=Q[2,m-2], and let G_8=H[X union {L,u,s,R}]. Then |V(G_8)|=8, V(H)=V(G_8) disjoint-union V(N), N is a tight Hamilton path on its support, and pc(G_8)=2. Consequently every exact two-cover G_8=A sqcup B gives a literal minimum spanning three-cover H=A sqcup B sqcup N. Moreover the complete aligned/crossed middle-gate split of accepted R541 is internal to this same eight-vertex core: the endpoint stars (u,L,x) and (x,R,s) for x in X and all L/R-to-M_S gate orientations involve only vertices of G_8. Thus ALIGNED and CROSSED are two internal orientations of one fixed bounded core coupled to the identical long middle rail N; the arbitrary-order part does not participate in the gate split.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in the accepted synchronized transitive R594 frame; beyond order ten gives m>=6. Use accepted R4 for complement exactness and accepted R541 for the aligned/crossed gate split.

## Scope
Global O4-v2 Elevator renormalization upstream of ALIGNED/CROSSED. No R5,R168,R169,R224,R533,R350,generic R358,capture,payment,R436,Reverse Ear,or computation.

## Applicability
Use before branching into aligned or crossed analyses. Any global closure theorem may work with the fixed order-eight core G_8 and the middle rail N, treating ALIGNED/CROSSED only as different internal gate orientations of G_8. This is the preferred common representation; crossed R806 remains a deeper branch-specific refinement when q_2 and q_{m-2} must be moved into the bounded core.

## Persistence
Retain the physical decomposition H=G_8 disjoint-union N, the exact pc(G_8)=2 fact, the labels X,L,u,s,R, the endpoint reverse stars from R594, and the R541 gate classification as data internal to G_8. Exact two-cover representatives of G_8 are not canonical.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not close either ALIGNED or CROSSED. Does not assert G_8 is Hamiltonian, prescribe endpoints in an exact two-cover of G_8, or imply an R572 splice. Does not identify the exact support partition of an arbitrary G_8 two-cover. Does not replace branch-specific deeper geometry such as R574 or R806 when that geometry is needed.

## Proof
Put N=Q[2,m-2]=(q_2,...,q_{m-2}). Since m>=6, N is nonempty, and as a contiguous subpath of Q it is tight. Its complement is exactly V(G_8)=X union {L,u,s,R}, so |V(G_8)|=4+4=8 and V(H)=V(G_8) disjoint-union V(N). Because G_8 is a proper induced subsystem of the hypothetical smallest counterexample H, accepted R4 gives pc(G_8)<=2. If pc(G_8)=1, let P be a Hamilton tight path of G_8. Then P and the tight path N are disjoint and together span H, giving pc(H)<=2, contradiction. Therefore pc(G_8)=2. Any exact two-cover A sqcup B of G_8 consequently yields the literal minimum spanning three-cover A sqcup B sqcup N of H. Finally, the synchronized endpoint stars retained by R594 are (u,L,x) and (x,R,s) for x in X, all supported inside G_8. The accepted R541 ALIGNED/CROSSED split compares the left and right M_S gate edges at L and R, hence likewise depends only on turns inside X union {L,R}, a subset of G_8. Thus the entire gate split is an internal orientation distinction of one fixed eight-vertex pc=2 core, while the arbitrary-length middle rail N is identical in both branches.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R810.md -->

# R815 — Two repeated reverse-middle blockers on adjacent gaps force a reverse zigzag P5

## Statement
Then exactly one of the two displayed reverse zigzags is a tight P5: (q_{i+2},x,q_{i+1},y,q_i) or (q_{i+2},y,q_{i+1},x,q_i). Equivalently, if two distinct exterior vertices are reverse-middle blockers at each of two adjacent gaps of Q, those repeated blocker identities stitch into a literal tight P5 whose three Q contacts occur in descending old-Q order q_{i+2},q_{i+1},q_i. In the R583 four-complement obstruction array, if the reverse-middle blocker sets at adjacent gaps have intersection of size at least two, this P5 occurs immediately without spending either gap through R542/R588.

## Hypotheses
Let Q=(q_0,...,q_m) be a vertex-simple tight path in a Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament, let 0<=i<=m-2, and let x,y be distinct vertices outside V(Q). Assume the four reverse-middle blocker turns (q_{i+1},x,q_i), (q_{i+1},y,q_i), (q_{i+2},x,q_{i+1}), and (q_{i+2},y,q_{i+1}) are tight.

## Scope
Pure order-free adjacent-gap lemma. No smallest-counterexample minimality, deletion cover, R24/R5, matching-height structure, payment, capture, or computation.

## Applicability
Use on simultaneous gap-obstruction arrays before consuming individual two-witness packets or P4 ears. It upgrades repeated blocker identities across neighboring cuts to one five-vertex role-labelled object. In an R24 frame, absence of this zigzag forces every pair of adjacent reverse-middle blocker sets to intersect in at most one vertex.

## Persistence
Retain the adjacent gap index i, the two exterior identities x,y, all four blocker turns, the tested central turn between x and y through q_{i+1}, and the resulting literal P5 orientation.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert the P5 is selected in any deletion cover, does not by itself give a spanning two-cover, and does not claim that reverse-middle blocker sets at adjacent gaps must overlap twice.

## Proof
Test T=(x,q_{i+1},y). If T is tight, then (q_{i+2},x,q_{i+1},y,q_i) is a tight P5: its consecutive turns are (q_{i+2},x,q_{i+1}), T, and (q_{i+1},y,q_i), all tight by hypothesis. If T is bad, accepted boundary antisymmetry R3 makes its complete reversal (y,q_{i+1},x) tight. Then (q_{i+2},y,q_{i+1},x,q_i) is a tight P5 using the other two blocker turns. The two cases are exclusive by R3. The R583 application is immediate by choosing any two vertices in the intersection of the adjacent reverse-middle blocker sets.

# R817 — Crossed gates give four canonical 4+4 covers of the order-eight core

## Statement
Retain the accepted crossed R621 frame with X={a,b,c,z}, Q=(q_0,...,q_m), m>=4, L=q_0, u=q_1, s=q_{m-1}, R=q_m, left middle gate {a,c} fully outgoing from L, and right middle gate {b,z} fully incoming to R. Put G_8=H[X union {L,u,s,R}]. Then all four pairs obtained by choosing one left rail from A_1=(u,L,a,c), A_2=(u,L,c,a) and one right rail from B_1=(b,z,R,s), B_2=(z,b,R,s) are literal exact two-covers of G_8. Thus the crossed order-eight core has one fixed support partition {u,L,a,c} sqcup {b,z,R,s} carrying four simultaneous P4-by-P4 representatives. Moreover N=Q[2,m-2] is a nonempty tight path, so each of the four core covers together with N is a literal spanning three-cover of H; in a hypothetical smallest counterexample it is therefore a minimum three-cover.

## Hypotheses
H is in the accepted crossed R621 frame; m>=4; notation X={a,b,c,z}, L=q_0, u=q_1, s=q_{m-1}, R=q_m. Uses only the crossed gate polarities and universal endpoint reverse stars already present in accepted R621.

## Scope
Noncircular crossed-frame bounded-core theorem, valid already for m>=4. It strengthens the generic order-eight-core viewpoint by giving an explicit support partition and four literal P4-by-P4 representatives in the crossed branch.

## Applicability
Use as the preferred crossed bounded-core interface before deeper pair-deletion, capture, or five-cell machinery. The four simultaneous core representatives can be fed independently into block-insertion or rail-rotation arguments against the common middle path Q[2,m-2].

## Persistence
Retain the physical support partition {u,L,a,c}|{b,z,R,s}, the four oriented P4 rails A_1,A_2,B_1,B_2, and the common middle path N=Q[2,m-2]. These are simultaneous graph-intrinsic path facts in the original crossed frame.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not close the crossed phase. Does not assert that the middle path N attaches to either core rail, that one of the four core covers is preferred, or that an analogous fixed 4+4 support partition exists in the aligned phase.

## Proof
In the crossed R621 frame, the left middle gate {a,c} is fully outgoing from L, so (L,a,c) and (L,c,a) are tight. The universal endpoint reverse stars retained in the same frame give (u,L,a) and (u,L,c) tight. Hence A_1=(u,L,a,c) and A_2=(u,L,c,a) are both tight P4s on the same support {u,L,a,c}. Dually, the right middle gate {b,z} is fully incoming to R, so (b,z,R) and (z,b,R) are tight, while the endpoint reverse stars give (b,R,s) and (z,R,s) tight. Hence B_1=(b,z,R,s) and B_2=(z,b,R,s) are both tight P4s on support {b,z,R,s}. The two supports are disjoint and partition V(G_8)=X union {L,u,s,R}. Therefore each of A_1 sqcup B_1, A_1 sqcup B_2, A_2 sqcup B_1, A_2 sqcup B_2 is a literal exact two-cover of G_8. Since m>=4, N=Q[2,m-2] is nonempty (a singleton when m=4 is allowed) and is a tight subpath of Q. Its support is disjoint from G_8 and together they partition V(H), so adjoining N to any of the four core covers gives a literal spanning three-cover of H. In a hypothetical smallest counterexample pc(H)>2, so each displayed three-cover is minimum.

# R818 — Corrected deep-cut split-splice clauses couple both R583 terminal blockers to two core seams

## Statement
Retain accepted R594 and R619 with X={a,b,c,z}, M_R={ab,cz}>M_S={ac,bz}>M_L={bc,az}, Q=(q_0,...,q_m), m>=6, L=q_0,u=q_1,s=q_{m-1},R=q_m, and normalize the left outgoing M_S gate to {a,c}. For a deep cut 3<=j<=m-3 put q=q_{j+1}, define A_j(x)=(x,q_j,q_{j-1}), and when j<=m-4 define C_j(x)=(q_{j+2},q,x). Then literal split-splice proposals from the synchronized enlarged-root covers give the following complete physical hole clauses. LEFT, in both phases: for root z, A_j(z) OR (R,z,q_j) OR (q,b,c) OR C_j(b); for root b, A_j(b) OR (R,b,q_j) OR (q,z,a) OR C_j(z). CROSSED right pair: A_j(a) OR (b,a,q_j) OR (q,c,L) OR C_j(c); and A_j(c) OR (z,c,q_j) OR (q,a,L) OR C_j(a). ALIGNED right pair: A_j(b) OR (a,b,q_j) OR (q,z,L) OR C_j(z); and A_j(z) OR (c,z,q_j) OR (q,b,L) OR C_j(b). At the terminal deep cut j=m-3 the C_j literal is absent from each clause because the Q suffix has only the singleton q_{m-2}; the remaining three literals are exhaustive. Each displayed disjunction means at least one listed turn is tight. These are the corrected full seam-window replacements for the invalid R816 two-hole clauses.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in accepted R594; accepted R619 supplies the phase-labelled enlarged singleton-deletion covers; R594 supplies the endpoint-star trimers used to restore the deleted root inside G8; m>=6. Boundary antisymmetry R3 converts a bad seam turn to the displayed reverse literal.

## Scope
R24/O6 exact array-intersection theorem. Corrects and supersedes pending R816; does not depend on pending R812. No R5,R168,R169,R224,R533,R350,generic R358,R542,capture,payment,R436,Reverse Ear,or computation.

## Applicability
Use as the exact deep-cut interface between accepted R583 and the synchronized enlarged-root covers. Unlike R816, every physical junction window is retained. The outer literals A_j and C_j are precisely the two R583 terminal blocker families; the two middle literals are matching-labelled core/cross-end turns. Compare these complete clauses across roots and adjacent cuts before invoking any payment machinery.

## Persistence
Retain j, phase, root label, the exact two candidate spanning rails, every present junction turn before reversal, and the corresponding displayed reverse literals. At j=m-3 retain the three-hole boundary specialization.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
R812 and R816 are not licensed by this theorem and should remain fenced. No clause may be shortened by dropping a companion junction turn without a separate proof that the dropped turn is tight. The theorem does not choose a disjunct, close H, or imply a binary 2-SAT system. It does not assert any selected-state currentness.

## Proof
Fix 3<=j<=m-3 and q=q_{j+1}. LEFT ROOT z. Accepted R619 plus the R594 star gives the G8 cover (u,L,a,c,b) sqcup (z,R,s). Consider P=(q_2,...,q_j,z,R,s) and S=(u,L,a,c,b,q,q_{j+2},...,q_{m-2}), omitting the tail after q when j=m-3. The only new turns of P are h1=(q_{j-1},q_j,z) and h2=(q_j,z,R). The only new turns of S are h3=(c,b,q) and, when j<=m-4, h4=(b,q,q_{j+2}). If all present h_k were tight, P sqcup S would be a spanning two-cover of H. Thus some h_k is bad. Their complete reversals are respectively A_j(z)=(z,q_j,q_{j-1}), (R,z,q_j), (q,b,c), and C_j(b)=(q_{j+2},q,b), proving the first clause. LEFT ROOT b uses G8=(u,L,c,a,z) sqcup (b,R,s). The four hole turns are (q_{j-1},q_j,b),(q_j,b,R),(a,z,q),(z,q,q_{j+2}); reversing yields A_j(b),(R,b,q_j),(q,z,a),C_j(z). CROSSED RIGHT ROOT c uses G8=(u,L,c) sqcup (a,b,z,R,s). The prefix candidate (q_2,...,q_j,a,b,z,R,s) has new turns (q_{j-1},q_j,a),(q_j,a,b); the suffix (u,L,c,q,q_{j+2},...) has new turns (L,c,q) and, when present, (c,q,q_{j+2}). Reversing a bad hole gives A_j(a),(b,a,q_j),(q,c,L),C_j(c). Crossed root a similarly uses (u,L,a) sqcup (c,z,b,R,s) and yields A_j(c),(z,c,q_j),(q,a,L),C_j(a). In the aligned phase the right G8 covers are (u,L,z) sqcup (b,a,c,R,s) and (u,L,b) sqcup (z,c,a,R,s). Their four hole reversals are respectively A_j(b),(a,b,q_j),(q,z,L),C_j(z), and A_j(z),(c,z,q_j),(q,b,L),C_j(b). At j=m-3 the second Q-side turn after q does not exist, so h4 is absent and the corresponding C_j literal is simply omitted. This proves every displayed clause with the complete seam window retained.

# R820 — Crossed 4+4 core orientations compress every deep gap to endpoint seam, middle-gate witness, or paired terminal blockers

## Statement
Retain the accepted crossed R621 frame with X={a,b,c,z}, Q=(q_0,...,q_m), m>=6, L=q_0,u=q_1,s=q_{m-1},R=q_m, and N=Q[2,m-2]. The crossed gates give the four graph-intrinsic core P4s A_1=(u,L,a,c), A_2=(u,L,c,a), B_1=(b,z,R,s), B_2=(z,b,R,s), with every A_i disjoint from every B_k and together spanning the order-eight core. Fix a deep gap 3<=j<=m-3 and put q=q_{j+1}. Define U_j to mean at least one of (u,q_j,q_{j-1}) and (L,u,q_j) is tight. Define G_AC(j) to mean at least one of (q,c,a),(q,a,c) is tight, equivalently q is a head witness on one tested orientation of the crossed middle-gate edge {a,c}. When j<=m-4 define T_AC(j) to mean both (q_{j+2},q,a) and (q_{j+2},q,c) are tight. Then U_j OR G_AC(j) OR T_AC(j) holds; at the terminal deep gap j=m-3 the T_AC term is absent, so U_j OR G_AC(j) holds. Dually define V_j to mean (q,s,R) is tight or, when j<=m-4, (q_{j+2},q,s) is tight. Define G_BZ(j) to mean at least one of (z,b,q_j),(b,z,q_j) is tight, equivalently q_j is a tail witness on one tested orientation of {b,z}. Define T_BZ(j) to mean both (b,q_j,q_{j-1}) and (z,q_j,q_{j-1}) are tight. Then V_j OR G_BZ(j) OR T_BZ(j) holds. Thus every crossed deep gap has two simultaneous three-way compressions: on the {a,c} side, endpoint/deep-Q seam or middle-gate witness or a paired right-terminal R583 packet; on the {b,z} side, the exact dual with a paired left-terminal R583 packet.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in accepted crossed R621; m>=6. Uses accepted R811 block-insertion obstruction and only the four crossed gate/endpoint-star P4s already graph-intrinsic in R621.

## Scope
Crossed-phase O6/R24 finite-state compression. Accepted-input theorem; does not depend on pending R817,R818,R812,R816. No R5,R168,R169,R224,R533,R350,generic R358,R542,capture,payment,R436,or Reverse Ear.

## Applicability
Use at each deep gap before consuming individual R583 packets. G_AC or G_BZ is immediately admissible to accepted R682 because q or q_j lies outside X union {L,R}. T_AC and T_BZ are exact two-witness terminal-blocker packets of the accepted R583 type and may be retained simultaneously rather than paid. The quiet residue therefore consists only of the two endpoint/deep-Q seam states U_j and V_j plus explicit paired terminal packets.

## Persistence
Retain j,q,the four fixed P4 rails A_1,A_2,B_1,B_2,the exact R811 seam-window alternatives for each orientation,and whichever U/G/T disjuncts occur. GATE witnesses and paired terminal blockers are graph-intrinsic in the common crossed frame.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert the same trichotomy branch occurs at adjacent gaps, that a GATE/R682 descendant closes H, or that paired terminal blockers are contradictions. U_j and V_j are disjunctions of two exact turns and must not be collapsed to one representative. At j=m-3 the absent q_{j+2} windows are not to be invented.

## Proof
The crossed R621 turns give A_1=(u,L,a,c), A_2=(u,L,c,a), B_1=(b,z,R,s), B_2=(z,b,R,s) as tight P4s, and any A_i together with any B_k is an exact two-cover of the fixed order-eight core. Fix a deep gap 3<=j<=m-3 and put q=q_{j+1}. Insert A_1 between q_j and q in N=Q[2,m-2]. Every old turn of A_1 and N remains tight; the only new consecutive triples are (q_{j-1},q_j,u), (q_j,u,L), (a,c,q), and, when j<=m-4, (c,q,q_{j+2}). If all present new turns were tight, the inserted path together with any disjoint B_k would be a spanning two-cover of H, impossible. Therefore at least one new turn is bad, and R3 yields one of the reversals (u,q_j,q_{j-1}), (L,u,q_j), (q,c,a), and, when present, (q_{j+2},q,c). The same insertion of A_2 yields one of (u,q_j,q_{j-1}), (L,u,q_j), (q,a,c), and, when present, (q_{j+2},q,a). If neither U_j nor G_AC(j) holds, the shared first two alternatives and the respective middle-gate alternatives are false, so both far-right reversals are tight, giving T_AC(j). At j=m-3 those far-right triples are absent, so U_j OR G_AC(j). Dually insert B_1 and B_2 at the same gap. Their new triples are respectively the two left boundary triples meeting q_j, the middle-gate triples through b,z, and the two right boundary triples meeting q; reversing at least one bad new turn gives the clauses A_j(b) OR (z,b,q_j) OR V_j and A_j(z) OR (b,z,q_j) OR V_j, with the far-side term omitted exactly at the terminal gap. If neither V_j nor G_BZ(j) holds, both A_j(b) and A_j(z) are forced, giving T_BZ(j). Thus the two stated trichotomies hold using only the graph-intrinsic crossed core paths, the old Q order, pc(H)>2 from the R621 frame, and R3.

# R823 — Matching-layer edge orders give an explicit 3/4 spanning-path fence

## Statement
Let n=2m be even. Take the complete graph K_n with an equipartition V=A disjoint-union B, |A|=|B|=m. Totally order its edges so that every edge internal to A or B precedes every A-B edge. Decompose the complete bipartite edge set E(A,B) into perfect matchings M_1,...,M_m, and order the cross edges in matching blocks M_1<...<M_m, with arbitrary order inside each block. Define the associated exact-reversal boundary tournament H by declaring an ordered triple (u,v,w) tight exactly when the graph edge {u,v} precedes {v,w} in the edge order. Then tight paths in H are exactly increasing paths in the edge-ordered K_n, and every such path has at most m+ceil(m/2)=ceil(3n/4) vertices. In particular this edge-order-induced boundary tournament has no spanning tight path for n>=4. The obstruction is a two-resource budget: once an increasing path uses its first cross edge it can never return to an internal edge; its remaining suffix alternates across A|B, uses at most one edge from each perfect-matching block, and every two cross edges consume a fresh vertex on the side containing the initial internal prefix.

## Hypotheses
n=2m is even; K_n is edge ordered with all within-part edges below all cross edges and with the cross edges grouped in the ordered perfect-matching blocks of a 1-factorization of K_{m,m}. The induced ternary relation is tight(u,v,w) iff uv<vw.

## Scope
Elementary explicit fence against spanning-path or near-spanning-path conjectures for boundary tournaments arising from edge-ordered complete graphs. The point is the transferable resource-budget mechanism, not the numerically strongest known monotone-path upper bound.

## Applicability
Use when a proposed general spanning-tight-path principle relies only on exact reversal, local abundance, or complete underlying support and therefore must survive edge-order-induced boundary tournaments. The construction suggests testing path-growth arguments against layered transition resources and vertex-consumption budgets. It may also motivate multipartite, hierarchical, or recursively layered variants.

## Persistence
Retain the partition A|B, the low internal/high cross edge split, the ordered matching blocks M_i, the first-cross position of any tested path, the number c of cross edges used, and the resulting vertex-budget inequality.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
This is not claimed to be the sharpest upper bound for increasing paths in edge-ordered complete graphs; substantially stronger asymptotic constructions are known. It does not show that every Strong Level-(1) structural hypothesis used elsewhere in A7C3 is realized by this subclass unless separately checked. It does not claim the ceil(3n/4) bound is always attained by this ordering, nor that simple recursion inside A and B improves the constant.

## Proof
Let P be an increasing vertex-simple path in the prescribed edge ordering. If P uses no cross edge, then it lies entirely in A or entirely in B and has at most m vertices. Otherwise consider its first cross edge. Before that edge, every used edge is internal, and since no cross edge has yet occurred all vertices of the initial segment lie in one part; by symmetry call it A. After the first cross edge no internal edge can occur, because every internal edge precedes every cross edge in the total order. Hence the remainder of P consists entirely of cross edges and alternates between A and B. Let c be the number of cross edges used. Because the cross edges are ordered in blocks M_1<...<M_m, their matching indices along P are nondecreasing. Two consecutive cross edges cannot lie in the same M_i, since a perfect matching has no two incident edges. All cross edges after the first are consecutive path edges, so P uses at most one edge from each matching block. Therefore c<=m. Let p be the number of vertices in the initial A-segment, including the A-endpoint of the first cross edge. The c-edge alternating cross suffix introduces floor(c/2) additional A-vertices, all distinct because P is vertex-simple. Thus p+floor(c/2)<=m. The total number of vertices of P is p+c, so |P|<=m-floor(c/2)+c=m+ceil(c/2)<=m+ceil(m/2)=ceil(3m/2)=ceil(3n/4). Finally, under the translation tight(u,v,w) iff uv<vw, an ordered vertex sequence is a tight path exactly when its consecutive graph edges are strictly increasing, so the same bound holds for tight paths in H.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R823.md -->

# R825 — Four cross-pair cut obligations have a middle-edge, complementary-pair, or three-star normal form

## Statement
Let T be a vertex-disjoint path cover (in particular, any exact two-cover) on a vertex set W containing four distinguished vertices X={a,b,c,z}. Consider the four cuts S_ab={a,b}, S_az={a,z}, S_cb={c,b}, S_cz={c,z}, each against W minus that two-set. Assume that for each of these four cuts T selects at least one adjacent state crossing the cut. Partition the six physical X-edges into M_R={ab,cz}, M_S={ac,bz}, M_L={az,bc}. Then T contains one of the following seven source-visible configurations. (MS) A selected M_S state ac or bz. (AC-EXT) selected X-exterior states incident with a and c. (BZ-EXT) selected X-exterior states incident with b and z. (RL) one selected M_R state and one selected M_L state. (STAR-ab) selected X-exterior states incident with a and b, together with a selected M_L state. (STAR-az) selected X-exterior states incident with a and z, together with a selected M_R state. (STAR-cb) selected X-exterior states incident with c and b, together with a selected M_R state. (STAR-cz) selected X-exterior states incident with c and z, together with a selected M_L state. Here an X-exterior state means a selected state with exactly one endpoint in X. Moreover, in (RL) the selected M_R and M_L states share exactly one X vertex, hence they are consecutive adjacencies of one T rail and form a selected three-vertex X segment. If T is a tight path cover and X is the transitive matching-height cell with M_R>M_S>M_L, that segment is oriented from its M_R edge through the common pivot to its M_L edge and is a tight X-trimer.

## Hypotheses
T is a vertex-disjoint path cover on W containing X={a,b,c,z}; each of the four displayed two-vertex cuts has at least one selected T-state crossing it. The final orientation sentence additionally assumes T is tight and X is the transitive matching-height cell M_R>M_S>M_L.

## Scope
Pure finite cut-incidence lemma. No smallest-counterexample minimality, Strong Level-(1) antisymmetry, R24, R508, payment, capture, Reverse Ear, or computation is needed for the seven-shape classification. It is designed to consume four simultaneous R508 obligations once they have been established elsewhere.

## Applicability
Use whenever four recompletion carriers on the same deleted support force crossings of the four cross-pair cuts ab,az,cb,cz in one fixed exact cover. First harvest an M_S selected state if present. Otherwise extract an inclusion-minimal family of selected states covering the four cut obligations; it is either one of three complementary pairs or one of four three-stars, with the physical translations listed in the statement.

## Persistence
Retain the fixed path cover T, the labelled X-set and matching partition M_R,M_S,M_L, the four cut obligations, the actual selected states chosen for an inclusion-minimal covering family, and its one of seven physical shape labels. In RL retain the common X pivot and the literal three-vertex rail segment.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert any of the seven shapes closes H. Does not assert the selected exterior states have distinct exterior endpoints. Does not assert a star is the entire incidence pattern of T, only that the displayed subconfiguration is selected. Does not infer capture, payment, protected contact, or a spanning path. The seven labels are alternatives for a retained inclusion-minimal obligation cover and need not be mutually exclusive in the full T.

## Proof
Number the cuts 1=S_ab, 2=S_az, 3=S_cb, 4=S_cz. A selected state with no X endpoint crosses none of them. A selected state with exactly one X endpoint has signature 12 at a, 13 at b, 34 at c, or 24 at z. For an X-X state, direct separation gives signature 23 for either M_R edge ab or cz, signature 14 for either M_L edge az or bc, and signature 1234 for either M_S edge ac or bz. Thus if a selected M_S state exists we are in (MS). Otherwise every selected state relevant to the four obligations has one of the six 2-subset signatures 12,13,14,23,24,34. Because all four obligations are met, choose an inclusion-minimal selected subfamily F whose signature union is {1,2,3,4}. If |F|=2, its two 2-subsets must be disjoint complements. The three complementary pairs are 12+34, 13+24, and 14+23, translating respectively to AC-EXT, BZ-EXT, and RL. Now suppose |F|>=3. Inclusion-minimality means every member of F contains a cut-index not contained in the union of the other members. Since there are only four indices and every signature has size two, |F| cannot exceed three: four members would each require a distinct private index, forcing four pairwise distinct private indices while each 2-subset also contains a second index belonging to another member, which would destroy privacy for at least one member; equivalently an inclusion-minimal edge cover of four labelled vertices by 2-edges has at most three edges. Hence |F|=3. Regard the three signatures as edges of K_4 on vertices {1,2,3,4}. They cover all four vertices and every edge has a private endpoint. A three-edge graph on four vertices with this property is necessarily K_1,3: a path P4 has a middle edge with no private endpoint, and any graph containing two disjoint edges already contains a complementary two-edge cover, contradicting minimality. The four possible centers give signature sets {12,13,14}, {12,24,23}, {13,34,23}, {24,34,14}, translating to STAR-ab, STAR-az, STAR-cb, STAR-cz respectively. Finally, in RL one selected edge belongs to M_R and one to M_L. Any edges from two distinct perfect matchings of K_4 meet in exactly one vertex. Since both are selected states of a path forest, at their common vertex they are the two consecutive rail adjacencies, giving a literal three-vertex X segment. If the rail is tight and X has matching heights M_R>M_S>M_L, the rail direction must traverse the M_R edge first and the M_L edge second, so the segment is a tight matching-height trimer. This proves the classification.

# FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R829.md

<!-- BEGIN FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R829.md -->

# R829 — Calderbank–Chung–Sturtevant GF(2)^k ordering gives an asymptotic one-half monotone-path fence

## Statement
For n=2^k, identify V(K_n) with GF(2)^k. For each nonzero d, the edges {x,y} with x+y=d form a perfect matching M_d. Totally order the edge set by placing the matching classes M_d in lexicographic order of d, with arbitrary order inside each class. If P=(v_0,...,v_t) is a simple increasing path, then the edge-difference sequence d_i=v_{i-1}+v_i is strictly lexicographically increasing and every nonempty consecutive block has nonzero sum. Hence t is at most f(k), where f(k) is the maximum length of a lexicographically increasing sequence in GF(2)^k having no zero-sum consecutive block. Calderbank, Chung and Sturtevant (Discrete Math. 50 (1984), 15–28) prove f(k) <= (1/2+o(1))2^k. Therefore this edge ordering has no increasing path longer than (1/2+o(1))n. Under the standard translation declaring an ordered triple (u,v,w) tight iff edge {u,v} precedes edge {v,w}, this yields Strong Level-(1) boundary tournaments with no tight path longer than (1/2+o(1))n.

## Hypotheses
n=2^k. The asymptotic f(k) bound is imported from Calderbank–Chung–Sturtevant 1984; the edge-ordering-to-vector-sequence reduction is proved here.

## Scope
Literature fence against spanning or near-spanning tight-path conjectures in arbitrary Strong Level-(1) boundary tournaments. Infinite power-of-two family suffices for the fence.

## Applicability
Use to reject any proposed theorem asserting that boundary antisymmetry alone forces a tight path on more than (1/2+o(1))n vertices. More strategically, remember the mechanism: encode transition classes by an abelian-group difference so path simplicity becomes a no-zero-consecutive-block condition.

## Persistence
Durable fence and construction template.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Not a claim about smallest counterexamples satisfying the project cover-minimality hypotheses. Not a new proof of the Calderbank–Chung–Sturtevant sequence bound. Does not supersede the elementary 3/4 resource-budget fence R823; the two constructions expose different mechanisms.

## Proof
Let V=GF(2)^k. For each d != 0 put M_d={{x,x+d}:x in V}; after identifying duplicate unordered pairs, M_d is a perfect matching. The M_d partition E(K_n), since every edge {x,y} has unique nonzero difference d=x+y. Order the classes lexicographically by d and order edges arbitrarily inside a class. Let P=(v_0,...,v_t) be an increasing simple path and put d_i=v_{i-1}+v_i. Because each M_d is a matching, P cannot traverse two consecutive edges from the same class. Since all edges of one class form one contiguous block in the global ordering, once an increasing path leaves M_d it cannot return; consequently d_1<...<d_t lexicographically. For any 1<=a<=b<=t, sum_{i=a}^b d_i=(v_{a-1}+v_a)+...+(v_{b-1}+v_b)=v_{a-1}+v_b in characteristic two. The path is vertex-simple, so v_{a-1} != v_b and this sum is nonzero. Thus (d_1,...,d_t) is a lex-increasing sequence with every consecutive block sum nonzero. By Calderbank, Chung and Sturtevant, 'Increasing sequences with nonzero block sums and increasing paths in edge-ordered graphs', Discrete Mathematics 50 (1984), 15–28, the maximum possible length f(k) of such a sequence satisfies f(k)<=(1/2+o(1))2^k. Hence t<=(1/2+o(1))n. Finally, declaring (u,v,w) tight iff {u,v}<{v,w} gives exact reversal antisymmetry because reversing the ordered triple reverses the comparison of the same two distinct edges; increasing graph paths are exactly tight paths in this induced boundary tournament.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R829.md -->
