# FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R833.md

<!-- BEGIN FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R833.md -->

# R833 — Two-block middle-dimer puncture of a P4 is a reverse seam, reverse endpoint chord, or anti-aligned endpoints

## Statement
Let H be a finite Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament with pc(H)>2, let K=(x,p,q,y) be a vertex-simple tight P4, put D={p,q} and C=V(H)\V(K), and let T=T_1 sqcup T_2 be a literal exact two-cover of H-D whose two rails are nontrivial. Let b_T(x,y) be the number of maximal nonempty C-blocks obtained from the two T-rails after deleting x and y. Then b_T(x,y)>=2. If b_T(x,y)=2, at least one of the following source-visible alternatives holds. (X-REVERSE) T selects a directed state c x with c in C, and the reverse seam (p,x,c) is tight. (Y-REVERSE) T selects a directed state y c with c in C, and the reverse seam (c,y,q) is tight. (REVERSE-CHORD) T selects the directed endpoint chord y x. (ANTI-ENDS) x and y are nonadjacent T-vertices of degree one, x is the first vertex of its T-rail, and y is the last vertex of its T-rail (the two endpoints may lie on the same or different rails). More precisely, writing epsilon=1 if {x,y} is a selected T-state and 0 otherwise, the exact block-count identity is b_T(x,y)=deg_T(x)+deg_T(y)-epsilon. Thus in the two-block case either epsilon=0 and both endpoints have degree one, or epsilon=1 and their degrees are {1,2}. In the latter case the only orientation avoiding X-REVERSE and Y-REVERSE is y x; in the former case the only orientation avoiding both reverse seams is ANTI-ENDS.

## Hypotheses
Strong Level-(1); pc(H)>2; K=(x,p,q,y) is a tight P4; T is a literal exact two-cover of H-{p,q} with both rails nontrivial.

## Scope
Order-free exact-cover refinement of middle-dimer P4 recompletion. No smallest-counterexample minimality is used after the nontrivial two-cover is supplied. In a smallest counterexample R429 supplies the required cover/nontriviality for every physical middle dimer.

## Applicability
Apply to any P4 K=(x,p,q,y) after deleting its middle dimer. It is especially useful when several P4s share the same deleted dimer and exact two-cover: any carrier whose endpoint-pair deletion leaves only two complementary blocks is reduced to a named reverse seam, a selected reverse endpoint chord, or a rigid anti-aligned endpoint placement.

## Persistence
Retain K,D,C,the literal cover T,the block count b_T(x,y),the T-degrees and adjacency bit of x,y,and whichever selected state/reverse seam/endpoint placement is obtained. Reverse seams are graph-intrinsic; selected states and endpoint roles are source-cover-relative.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert that some endpoint pair has b_T=2. Does not assert the reverse seam, reverse chord, or anti-aligned endpoint placement closes H. Does not identify different exact two-covers or transport selected states between representatives. Does not infer capture, payment, protected contact, or long-path growth.

## Proof
Put W=V(H)\D and S={x,y}. The P4 K is a tight path on exactly D union S, so accepted R508 makes (D,S,K,T) a recompletion packet, and accepted R509(1) gives b_T(x,y)>=2. For the exact count, T is a forest with two components, hence |E(T)|=|V(T)|-2. Let epsilon be 1 when xy is a T-edge and 0 otherwise. Deleting x,y removes deg_T(x)+deg_T(y)-epsilon edges. The remaining graph is exactly the disjoint union of the maximal C-blocks, so b_T(x,y)=(|V(T)|-2)-(|E(T)|-deg_T(x)-deg_T(y)+epsilon)=deg_T(x)+deg_T(y)-epsilon. Because both T-rails are nontrivial, each of x,y has degree one or two. Assume b_T=2. If epsilon=0, then deg_T(x)=deg_T(y)=1. If the unique incidence at x is c->x with c in C, use the C-to-S endpoint case j=0 of R509: its literal spanning two-path proposal has unique uncertified turn (c,x,p), so pc(H)>2 makes that turn bad and R3, as already packaged by R509, gives (p,x,c) tight. Dually, if the unique incidence at y is y->c, the S-to-C endpoint case i=m has unique hole (q,y,c), forcing (c,y,q). If neither incidence occurs, the unique edge at x is directed x->C and the unique edge at y is directed C->y; therefore x is the initial endpoint of its T-rail and y the terminal endpoint of its T-rail. Since epsilon=0 they are nonadjacent, giving ANTI-ENDS. If epsilon=1, the degree sum is three, so one of x,y has degree one and the other degree two. If the selected chord is y->x, retain REVERSE-CHORD. If it is x->y and x is the degree-two vertex, its other path incidence is necessarily c->x, so the preceding X-REVERSE argument applies. If instead y is degree two, its other incidence is y->c and Y-REVERSE applies. This exhausts the two-block case.

# R834 — A signed dimer in a three-cover forces reverse seams at polarity-misaligned rail endpoints

## Statement
Let H be a finite Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament with pc(H)>2. Suppose H=D sqcup U sqcup V is a literal spanning three-cover by nontrivial tight paths, with D=(p,q) a dimer. (TAIL-START.) If the first vertex y=u_0 of U is a tail witness on the tested orientation D, so (p,q,y) is tight, then the reverse outer seam (u_1,y,q) is tight. (HEAD-END.) If the last vertex x=u_r of U is a head witness on D, so (x,p,q) is tight, then the reverse outer seam (p,x,u_{r-1}) is tight. The same conclusions hold with U and V interchanged. Consequently, if A is any set of tail witnesses on D and B any set of head witnesses on D, then in a source three-cover with no such forced terminal reverse seam, every rail endpoint lying in A can occur only as a rail end, and every rail endpoint lying in B can occur only as a rail start.

## Hypotheses
Strong Level-(1); pc(H)>2; H=D sqcup U sqcup V is a literal spanning three-cover by nontrivial tight paths; D=(p,q) has order two. Tail/head witness assertions use the exact displayed tested orientation.

## Scope
Order-free physical-splice lemma. It uses the complete R453 two-hole certificate and boundary antisymmetry, so it is safe under the R812/R816 seam correction. No smallest-counterexample minimality, capture, payment, Reverse Ear, or path-length growth.

## Applicability
Use whenever a signed dimer itself is one component of a literal spanning three-cover and a sign witness appears at an endpoint of one of the other rails. In the central R822 collision fan, D is head-signed by B={b,z} and tail-signed by A={a,c}, while any exact cover T of H-D gives H=D sqcup T_1 sqcup T_2. Therefore every A-start or B-end in T immediately creates a named reverse outer seam; a seam-quiet source cover must orient X-endpoints B-at-start and A-at-end.

## Persistence
Retain the literal three-cover D,U,V, the tested orientation (p,q), the named endpoint witness, its adjacent rail vertex, the exact R453 ordered-pair proposal and hole pair, and the forced reverse outer seam. The reverse seam is graph-intrinsic; endpoint roles are source-cover-relative.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert that every rail has an endpoint in A union B, that the forced reverse seam closes H, or that a seam-quiet cover exists. Does not permit insertion of D using only one checked seam. Does not infer capture, payment, or a long path.

## Proof
TAIL-START. Write U=(y,u_1,...,u_r). Apply R879 to the literal nontrivial spanning three-cover H=D sqcup U sqcup V and the ordered component pair D=(p,q),U. Its exact physical splice clause is (y,q,p) OR (u_1,y,q), the reversals of the two complete seam holes (p,q,y) and (q,y,u_1). By hypothesis (p,q,y) is tight, so boundary antisymmetry R3 makes its complete reversal (y,q,p) bad. Therefore the R879 clause forces (u_1,y,q) tight. HEAD-END. Write U=(u_0,...,u_{r-1},x). Apply R879 to the ordered pair U,D. Its splice clause is (p,x,u_{r-1}) OR (q,p,x), reversing the complete seam holes (u_{r-1},x,p) and (x,p,q). The head-witness hypothesis makes (x,p,q) tight, so R3 makes (q,p,x) bad; hence (p,x,u_{r-1}) is tight. Interchanging U and V is identical. The seam-quiet endpoint-orientation consequence is the direct contrapositive of these two statements. This proves exactly R834 without the optional smallest-counterexample specialization bundled into retired R453.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R834.md -->

# R835 — The two inward stars of the R574 middle do not force Hamiltonicity at the first live order

## Statement
There exists a five-vertex Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament F on {a,c,v,w,d} such that N=(v,w,d) is tight and the four inward-star turns (w,v,a),(w,v,c),(a,d,w),(c,d,w) are all tight, but F has no tight Hamilton P5. Thus the local middle data retained by accepted R574 at m=6, namely Q[2,4]=(v,w,d) together with the two left witnesses a,c on the reverse dimer (w,v) and the two right witnesses a,c on the reverse dimer (d,w), do not by themselves force the complementary middle support {a,c,v,w,d} to be Hamiltonian. This remains true even with the stronger property that, for every fixed middle vertex y, the induced tournament on the other four vertices defined by x ->_y z iff (x,y,z) is tight is transitive. One explicit certificate is given by the following five local orders, declaring (x,y,z) tight exactly when x precedes z in the order attached to middle y: middle a: c>d>v>w; middle c: a>w>d>v; middle v: w>d>a>c; middle w: v>c>d>a; middle d: v>a>c>w.

## Hypotheses
Pure five-vertex Strong Level-(1) exact-reversal setting. The displayed local-order construction completely defines the ternary orientation.

## Scope
Finite local strategy fence for the aligned/exactly-two-bad R574 middle at the first surviving length m=6. It does not claim the full R574/R556 frame extends to this five-vertex certificate.

## Applicability
Use to reject any proof step that tries to close the m>=6 R574 residue solely from the facts that Q[2,m-2] is tight and a,c sign the first and last inward reverse dimers. Additional global shell, deletion-cover, gate-fan, or recompletion information is genuinely required.

## Persistence
Retain the explicit five local transitive orders and the five required R574 turns as a regression certificate.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not construct a full order-eleven R24 counterexample or even extend to the entire X union Q frame. Does not show the aligned branch survives globally. It only disproves the local Hamilton-middle implication from the R574 retained middle data. No asymptotic claim is made.

## Proof
For each middle y, orient every reversal pair (x,y,z)/(z,y,x) by the displayed transitive order at y. This defines a Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament. The required turns are immediate: at middle w the order v>c>d>a gives (v,w,d); at middle v the order w>d>a>c gives (w,v,a),(w,v,c); at middle d the order v>a>c>w gives (a,d,w),(c,d,w). Direct inspection from the five local orders gives exactly the following tight P4s: (a,c,w,d), (a,c,d,w), (a,d,c,v), (c,a,d,w), (c,d,w,a), (v,w,c,d), (v,d,a,w), (v,d,w,a), (w,v,d,a), (w,v,d,c), (d,a,v,c), (d,v,a,w). Their respective missing vertices are v,v,w,v,v,a,c,c,c,a,w,c. Appending that missing vertex would require respectively the turns (w,d,v),(d,w,v),(c,v,w),(d,w,v),(w,a,v),(c,d,a),(a,w,c),(w,a,c),(d,a,c),(d,c,a),(v,c,w),(a,w,c), and each of these is bad by the displayed middle orders. Every Hamilton P5 would have a tight first four-vertex prefix and then append the unique missing vertex, so no Hamilton P5 exists.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R835.md -->

# R837 — Crossed middle-gate dimers are one-way path endcaps unless they force a labelled P4

## Statement
Retain the accepted crossed R621/R649 frame with X={a,b,c,z}, middle-gate dimers G_3={a,c} and G_4={b,z}. Let K be any vertex-simple tight path in H. (G3 endcap.) Suppose K contains the two vertices of G_3 consecutively in either order S=(s_0,s_1). If S is not the terminal block of K, let y be the vertex immediately following s_1. Then H contains a tight Hamilton P4 on {s_0,s_1,y,w} for some fixed-frame R649 witness w distinct from y. Consequently, in the absence of this labelled P4, every contiguous occurrence of G_3 on any tight path is terminal. (G4 endcap.) Suppose K contains the two vertices of G_4 consecutively in either order S=(s_0,s_1). If S is not the initial block of K, let y be the vertex immediately preceding s_0. Then H contains a tight Hamilton P4 on {y,s_0,s_1,w} for some fixed-frame R649 witness w distinct from y. Consequently, in the absence of this labelled P4, every contiguous occurrence of G_4 on any tight path is initial. In particular, for any exact two-cover T of W=H-{q_2,q_{m-2}} in the crossed beyond-ten inward-anchor frame, if neither X dimer is fragmented and no such labelled P4 occurs, the G_4 block is the initial block of its T-rail and the G_3 block is the terminal block of its T-rail. Hence any positive excess sigma_G(T)>0 in that no-P4, unfragmented-X branch is paid entirely by fragmentation of the three Q-cells; it cannot come from an internal or wrongly oriented contiguous X block.

## Hypotheses
Accepted crossed R621/R649 frame and accepted universal four-cell theorem R518. For the final sigma corollary, T is an exact two-cover of the inward-anchor deletion residue W=H-{q_2,q_{m-2}} and both physical X dimers each occur as one contiguous T-block.

## Scope
Noncircular crossed-frame path-level theorem, valid independently of sigma_G(T), five-cell quotient shape, monotonicity, or order beyond the existence of the named frame. The final corollary specializes to the beyond-ten inward-anchor deletion cover.

## Applicability
Use before any sigma=0/sigma>0 split. First inspect whether either crossed X dimer is contiguous on a current path. A nonterminal G_3 or noninitial G_4 immediately yields source-labelled P4 geometry. If both X dimers are contiguous and no P4 occurs, pin G_4 to a rail start and G_3 to a rail end; all excess transition complexity must then live in Q-cell fragmentation.

## Persistence
Retain the actual orientation of the contiguous X dimer, its immediate path neighbor, a distinct fixed R649 same-polarity witness, and the resulting four-vertex P4 certificate. In the no-P4 branch retain the forced rail-end role of each contiguous X dimer.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not rule out fragmentation of G_3 or G_4 into singleton blocks. Does not close sigma>0 when excess lies only in Q-cell fragmentation. Does not assert the labelled P4 itself closes H. Does not require or consume R763.

## Proof
For G_3, let S=(s_0,s_1) be its actual consecutive order on K and suppose y follows s_1. Tightness of K gives (s_0,s_1,y) tight, so y is a tail witness on S. By accepted R649, for either orientation S=(a,c) or (c,a), the same tested dimer has fixed head polarity witnessed by at least three named vertices in the crossed frame; equivalently there exists a fixed w distinct from S with (w,s_0,s_1) tight, and because there are at least three choices we may choose w != y. Apply accepted R518 to the tight trimer (w,s_0,s_1) with fourth vertex y. The y-sign on the terminal physical dimer S has polarity opposite the natural head sign from w, so R518 is in its Hamilton-P4 branch. Hence {w,s_0,s_1,y} supports a tight P4. Therefore if no such P4 is retained, a contiguous G_3 block cannot have a successor and must terminate its path. The G_4 proof is dual. Let S=(s_0,s_1) be its actual consecutive order and suppose y precedes s_0. Tightness gives (y,s_0,s_1), a head sign on S. R649 supplies at least three fixed tail witnesses w with (s_0,s_1,w) tight for either orientation of G_4; choose w != y. Applying R518 to (s_0,s_1,w) with fourth vertex y gives a Hamilton P4 because the y-sign is opposite in polarity to the natural tail sign. Thus absent P4, contiguous G_4 must be initial. For an inward-anchor exact two-cover T with both X dimers unfragmented, apply the two path-level conclusions to their T-rails. Since sigma counts extra source-cell blocks beyond the five reference cells, and neither X cell contributes an extra block in this branch, every positive sigma contribution comes from splitting one or more Q-cells.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R837.md -->

# R840 — Safe crossed X endcaps can touch a monotone Q rail only at the physical endpoints

## Statement
Retain the accepted crossed R621/R649 frame with Q=(q_0,...,q_m), L=q_0, R=q_m, and let K be any vertex-simple tight path. Suppose G_4={b,z} occurs as one contiguous initial block of K in either order S_4, and G_3={a,c} occurs as one contiguous terminal block of K in either order S_3 whenever that endcap is present. Then for each present endcap one of the following holds. (NONLOCAL) Its adjacent Q vertex is interior, i.e. lies in V(Q)-{L,R}; that vertex is a sign witness on the tested X dimer, so accepted R682 yields either an endpoint-capture lineage or a graph-intrinsic tight cross-end trimer L-v-R or R-v-L. (ENDPOINT) Its adjacent Q vertex is L or R. Consequently, if neither R682 nonlocal output is retained and K is also outside the Reverse-Ear outputs of R435 relative to Q, every Q-contacting crossed X endcap is attached directly to a physical endpoint. If both endcaps lie on the same K rail, writing E for the Q vertex immediately after G_4 and F for the Q vertex immediately before G_3, the only endpoint pairs compatible with increasing Q-order are (E,F)=(L,L),(L,R),(R,R); the reversed pair (R,L) forces an R435 output. Thus an intact no-P4/no-RE/no-R682 crossed rail has X attachment geometry drawn from a bounded three-state endpoint list, independent of m.

## Hypotheses
Accepted crossed R621/R649 frame; accepted R682 and R435. The path K contains whichever X dimers are under discussion as contiguous endcaps, with its remaining contacts drawn from Q.

## Scope
Crossed-frame endpoint normalization. No deletion-cover choice, sigma assumption, five-cell quotient classification, capture payment, or order bound beyond the named Q endpoints is used.

## Applicability
After R837 pins intact G_4 to a rail start and intact G_3 to a rail end, inspect their immediate Q neighbors. Any interior neighbor is already an R682 nonlocal event. Otherwise replace arbitrary long-rail attachment positions by endpoint labels L/R; on a common rail only LL, LR, RR survive outside Reverse Ear.

## Persistence
Retain the tested X-dimer orientation, its actual adjacent Q vertex, the R682 inward-witness packet when interior, or the endpoint label when safe; for a common rail retain the ordered endpoint pair.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not say endpoint attachments themselves close H. Does not exclude G_4-R-G_3 or G_4-L-G_3 short rails. Does not treat fragmented X dimers. Does not claim CAP and XET outputs coexist.

## Proof
Let S_4=(s_0,s_1) be the actual orientation of a contiguous initial G_4 block and let v be the next K vertex, assumed to lie in Q. Tightness gives (s_0,s_1,v), so v is a sign witness on the tested orientation S_4. If v is interior to Q then v lies outside X union {L,R}, and accepted R682 applies directly, yielding CAP or XET. Therefore outside that nonlocal output v is one of L,R. Dually, let S_3=(t_0,t_1) be the actual orientation of a contiguous terminal G_3 block and let v be the preceding Q vertex. Tightness gives (v,t_0,t_1), again a sign witness on the tested orientation S_3; if v is interior, R682 applies, so outside its output v lies in {L,R}. Finally suppose both endcaps occur on one rail and neither R682 output occurs. Let E follow G_4 and F precede G_3. Both are in {L,R}. Outside R435 outputs, Q contacts along K occur in increasing Q-index order. Since L=q_0 precedes R=q_m, the ordered endpoint pair cannot be (R,L). The remaining possibilities are (L,L),(L,R),(R,R), where equality means the same sole endpoint contact lies between the two endcaps. This proves the bounded endpoint normalization.

# R841 — Crossed m=6 one-hole cap closure forces a twenty-turn outer fan

## Statement
Retain the accepted crossed R621 frame at m=6, Q=(L,u,v,w,d,s,R), X={a,b,c,z}, M_R={ab,cz}>M_S={ac,bz}>M_L={bc,az}. Then the following twenty turns are forced tight by literal one-hole spanning two-path proposals. FIRST LAYER (12): c s R, a s R, L u b, L u z, c R z, c R b, a R z, a R b, c L z, c L b, a L z, a L b. SECOND LAYER (8): c z R, R c b, a b R, R a z, c z L, L c b, a b L, L a z. Each first-layer turn is the exact reversal of the sole uncertified turn in a spanning two-path proposal using a consecutive Q prefix/suffix and a five/six-vertex outer path whose other turns are accepted crossed-gate, endpoint-star, or matching-height turns. Each second-layer turn is obtained by an analogous one-hole proposal using one first-layer turn plus accepted matching-height/gate turns.

## Hypotheses
Accepted crossed R621 frame at m=6, accepted R594 endpoint stars/matching-height four-cell, boundary antisymmetry R3, and pc(H)>2.

## Scope
Finite crossed m=6 R24/O6 cap-saturation lemma. Pure literal one-hole spanning-cover forcing; no R5,R168,R169,R224,R533,R350,generic R358,capture,payment,R436,Reverse Ear,or computation.

## Applicability
Use before resolving the paired R583/R818 terminal-gap clauses. The twenty turns are simultaneous graph-intrinsic cap data and may serve as exact companion literals in Mate-Fork or R833/R834 endpoint arguments.

## Persistence
Retain Q labels, X matching labels, all twenty displayed turns, and for each turn the one-hole spanning proposal listed in the proof.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not by itself close the crossed m=6 frame. Does not claim the twenty turns exhaust all one-hole consequences. Does not infer generic path growth or balanced-pair progress.

## Proof
Write Q=(L,u,v,w,d,s,R). We list each spanning two-path proposal and its sole uncertified turn; every unlisted consecutive turn is accepted from Q, the matching-height orientation on X, the crossed M_S gates, or the universal endpoint stars of R594/R621. Since pc(H)>2, the unique hole is bad, so R3 forces its complete reversal.\n\nFIRST LAYER.\n(1) (L,u,v,w,d) together with (a,b,z,R,s,c) has sole hole (R,s,c); hence (c,s,R).\n(2) (L,u,v,w,d) together with (c,z,b,R,s,a) has sole hole (R,s,a); hence (a,s,R).\n(3) (v,w,d,s,R) together with (b,u,L,c,a,z) has sole hole (b,u,L); hence (L,u,b).\n(4) (v,w,d,s,R) together with (z,u,L,a,c,b) has sole hole (z,u,L); hence (L,u,z).\n(5) (L,u,v,w,d,s) together with (a,b,z,R,c) has sole hole (z,R,c); hence (c,R,z).\n(6) (L,u,v,w,d,s) together with (b,R,c,a,z) has sole hole (b,R,c); hence (c,R,b).\n(7) (L,u,v,w,d,s) together with (b,z,R,a,c) has sole hole (z,R,a); hence (a,R,z).\n(8) (L,u,v,w,d,s) together with (c,z,b,R,a) has sole hole (b,R,a); hence (a,R,b).\n(9) (u,v,w,d,s,R) together with (a,b,z,L,c) has sole hole (z,L,c); hence (c,L,z).\n(10) (u,v,w,d,s,R) together with (b,L,c,a,z) has sole hole (b,L,c); hence (c,L,b).\n(11) (u,v,w,d,s,R) together with (b,z,L,a,c) has sole hole (z,L,a); hence (a,L,z).\n(12) (u,v,w,d,s,R) together with (c,z,b,L,a) has sole hole (b,L,a); hence (a,L,b).\n\nFor completeness, the outer matching-height turns used above include abz, czb, caz, bac and their displayed relabellings; the gate/star turns include bzR,zbR,bzL,zbL,Lac,Lca,Rac,Rca,uLx,xRs.\n\nSECOND LAYER. Use the first-layer turns just obtained.\n(13) (L,u,v,w,d,s) together with (a,R,z,c,b) has sole hole (R,z,c): aRz is first-layer and zcb is matching-height. Hence (c,z,R).\n(14) (L,u,v,w,d,s) together with (a,b,c,R,z) has sole hole (b,c,R): abc is matching-height and cRz is first-layer. Hence (R,c,b).\n(15) (L,u,v,w,d,s) together with (c,R,b,a,z) has sole hole (R,b,a): cRb is first-layer and baz is matching-height. Hence (a,b,R).\n(16) (L,u,v,w,d,s) together with (c,z,a,R,b) has sole hole (z,a,R): cza is matching-height and aRb is first-layer. Hence (R,a,z).\n(17) (u,v,w,d,s,R) together with (a,L,z,c,b) has sole hole (L,z,c): aLz is first-layer and zcb is matching-height. Hence (c,z,L).\n(18) (u,v,w,d,s,R) together with (a,b,c,L,z) has sole hole (b,c,L): abc is matching-height and cLz is first-layer. Hence (L,c,b).\n(19) (u,v,w,d,s,R) together with (c,L,b,a,z) has sole hole (L,b,a): cLb is first-layer and baz is matching-height. Hence (a,b,L).\n(20) (u,v,w,d,s,R) together with (c,z,a,L,b) has sole hole (z,a,L): cza is matching-height and aLb is first-layer. Hence (L,a,z).\n\nEvery displayed proposal consists of two disjoint paths whose supports partition V(H), and each complete hole ledger has size one exactly as stated. This proves all twenty forced turns.

# FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R843.md

<!-- BEGIN FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R843.md -->

# R843 — A bidirectional same-dimer P4 pair eliminates the R833 chord and anti-end residues

## Statement
Let H be a finite Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament with pc(H)>2. Let p,q,x,y be four distinct vertices such that both K=(x,p,q,y) and K^*=(y,p,q,x) are tight P4s. Put D={p,q}, C=V(H)\\{x,p,q,y}, and let T=T_1 sqcup T_2 be a literal exact two-cover of H-D with both rails nontrivial. Then either b_T(x,y)>2, or T forces a source-visible reverse seam at x or y. More explicitly, if b_T(x,y)=2, at least one of the following occurs for some c in C: T selects c x and (p,x,c) is tight; T selects y c and (c,y,q) is tight; T selects c y and (p,y,c) is tight; or T selects x c and (c,x,q) is tight. Thus the REVERSE-CHORD and ANTI-ENDS residues of R833 cannot jointly survive the two opposite endpoint orders on the same middle dimer.

## Hypotheses
Strong Level-(1), pc(H)>2; K=(x,p,q,y) and K^*=(y,p,q,x) are both tight; T is one exact two-cover of H-{p,q} with both rails nontrivial.

## Scope
Order-free fixed-cover strengthening of accepted R833. No smallest-counterexample minimality is needed once T is supplied. No capture, payment, Reverse Ear, path growth, or computation.

## Applicability
Use whenever a signed dimer has two distinct witnesses x,y in both endpoint roles, producing both P4 orders x-D-y and y-D-x. In the crossed m=6 R583 terminal-gap analysis, any two right-terminal blockers (s,d,x),(s,d,y), together with accepted R723 head signs (x,s,d),(y,s,d), give exactly this bidirectional pair on D=(s,d); hence the entire right-terminal two-witness branch becomes HIGH-BLOCK or a physical reverse seam in one exact H-{s,d} cover. The left terminal branch has the same consequence when its two witnesses are b,z, using accepted R658 tail signs on (w,v).

## Persistence
Retain both P4 orders, the common physical middle dimer D, the single exact cover T, b_T(x,y), and the selected state plus reverse seam if the two-block case occurs.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not claim b_T(x,y)>2 is contradictory or that the forced reverse seam closes H. Does not identify which of the four reverse-seam forms occurs. Does not compare different exact covers.

## Proof
The quantity b_T(x,y) depends only on the physical endpoint pair {x,y} and the fixed cover T, so it is identical for K=(x,p,q,y) and K^*=(y,p,q,x). If b_T(x,y)>2 we are done. Assume b_T(x,y)=2 and apply accepted R833 first to K. If X-REVERSE or Y-REVERSE occurs, one of the first two displayed reverse seams is obtained. Hence suppose neither occurs. R833 then leaves only REVERSE-CHORD, in which T selects the directed state y x, or ANTI-ENDS, in which x,y are nonadjacent degree-one T-vertices with x first on its rail and y last on its rail. Apply R833 again to K^*. If one of its reverse-seam alternatives occurs, we obtain one of the last two displayed forms. Otherwise K^* leaves only its REVERSE-CHORD, the directed state x y, or its ANTI-ENDS, with y first and x last. These residual choices cannot coexist. T is a literal path cover with fixed rail orientations, so it cannot simultaneously select both directed states y x and x y. A chord residue from one application cannot coexist with ANTI-ENDS from the other, because ANTI-ENDS explicitly makes x and y nonadjacent. Finally, if both applications take ANTI-ENDS, the first makes x a first endpoint and y a last endpoint, while the second makes y a first endpoint and x a last endpoint. If x,y lie on the same rail this reverses the two fixed endpoint roles and is impossible. If they lie on different rails, each of x and y would have to be both the first and last vertex of its own rail; since both T rails are nontrivial by hypothesis, that is impossible as well. Therefore at least one R833 application must produce a reverse seam whenever b_T(x,y)=2. This proves the lemma.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R843.md -->

# R844 — Exact-core rails force a full block-insertion obstruction array along a Hamilton complement

## Statement
Let H be a finite Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament with pc(H)>2. Suppose V(H)=V(G) disjoint-union V(M), where M=(m_0,...,m_t) is a nonempty tight path and G has a literal exact two-cover A sqcup B by nonempty tight paths. Fix A=(a_0,...,a_r). For every insertion slot of A as one contiguous block into the displayed order of M, the complete seam window contains a bad turn. INTERNAL GAP: for 0<=i<t, if r=0, at least one of the present turns (m_{i-1},m_i,a_0) [i>=1], (m_i,a_0,m_{i+1}), (a_0,m_{i+1},m_{i+2}) [i+2<=t] is bad; if r>=1, at least one of the present turns (m_{i-1},m_i,a_0) [i>=1], (m_i,a_0,a_1), (a_{r-1},a_r,m_{i+1}), (a_r,m_{i+1},m_{i+2}) [i+2<=t] is bad. BEFORE M: if r=t=0 then H is already two-coverable; otherwise at least one of the present turns (a_{r-1},a_r,m_0) [r>=1] and (a_r,m_0,m_1) [t>=1] is bad. AFTER M: if r=t=0 then H is already two-coverable; otherwise at least one of the present turns (m_{t-1},m_t,a_0) [t>=1] and (m_t,a_0,a_1) [r>=1] is bad. In every slot, boundary antisymmetry makes the complete reversal of at least one bad displayed turn tight. The same conclusions hold with B in place of A. Thus one exact core cover supplies a synchronized, complete physical seam-window obstruction at every internal and exterior insertion position of the Hamilton complement.

## Hypotheses
Finite Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament H with pc(H)>2; a vertex partition into a nonempty tight path M and an induced remainder G carrying a literal exact two-cover A sqcup B by nonempty tight paths. Uses boundary antisymmetry R3 only.

## Scope
Order-free corrected parent theorem for block insertion. Repairs accepted R811 by replacing its incorrect exterior one-turn endpoint assertion with the complete two-turn boundary windows. No smallest-counterexample minimality or frame-specific machinery.

## Applicability
Use as the canonical block-insertion compiler once freshly accepted. Internal-gap applications recover the sound body of R811. Exterior applications keep both junction turns when both concatenated paths are nontrivial and directly specialize to finite core-middle concatenation clauses such as R839.

## Persistence
Retain the chosen exact core cover, the Hamilton complement rail, the insertion slot, the complete list of present seam-window turns, and whichever reversed bad turn is certified. Never drop a present junction turn merely because the insertion occurs at an exterior slot.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert which seam-window turn is bad. Does not permit shortening a two-turn exterior window to a single blocker when both concatenated paths are nontrivial. Does not by itself close H.

## Proof
Fix A=(a_0,...,a_r), the untouched rail B, and M=(m_0,...,m_t). At an internal gap insert A between m_i and m_{i+1}. Every consecutive triple wholly inside A or M is already tight. The only new consecutive triples are exactly the turns listed in the statement: three when r=0, subject to boundary omissions, and four when r>=1, again subject to boundary omissions. If all present new turns were tight, the inserted sequence would be a tight Hamilton path on V(A) union V(M); together with B this would be a spanning two-cover of H, contradicting pc(H)>2. Hence some present turn is bad, and R3 makes its complete reversal tight. Before M, the candidate sequence is (a_0,...,a_r,m_0,...,m_t). Its only new consecutive triples are (a_{r-1},a_r,m_0) when r>=1 and (a_r,m_0,m_1) when t>=1. If both are absent then r=t=0 and A union M is an automatic tight dimer, so with B it two-covers H. Otherwise if all present boundary turns were tight the same concatenation plus B would two-cover H, so at least one present turn is bad and R3 reverses it. After M the candidate is (m_0,...,m_t,a_0,...,a_r), whose only new triples are (m_{t-1},m_t,a_0) when t>=1 and (m_t,a_0,a_1) when r>=1; the identical argument applies, with r=t=0 again already impossible. Repeating with B proves the complete array.

# R846 — A 2x2 signed-dimer rectangle forces reverse seam, high block count, closure, or a pure head-to-tail exterior weave

## Statement
Let H be a finite Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament with pc(H)>2. Let D=(p,q) be an oriented dimer and let A={a,c}, B={b,z} be four distinct vertices disjoint from D. Suppose D is head-signed by every vertex of A and tail-signed by every vertex of B: (a,p,q),(c,p,q),(p,q,b),(p,q,z) are tight. Let T=T_1 sqcup T_2 be a literal exact two-cover of H-V(D) with both rails nontrivial. Then at least one of the following holds. (HIGH) For some h in A,t in B, the R833 block count b_T(h,t)>2. (SEAM) T forces an R833/R834 source-visible reverse seam at one of a,c,b,z. (CLOSE) H has a spanning two-cover. (WEAVE) The two T-rail starts are exactly a,c, the two T-rail ends are exactly b,z, T selects no X-X state on X=A union B, and consequently each of a,c,b,z has its unique endpoint adjacency to a vertex of V(H)\\(V(D) union X). Thus in WEAVE the two rails each have the form A-start -> nonempty exterior block -> B-end, with the four X-exterior endpoint states simultaneous in one fixed cover.

## Hypotheses
Strong Level-(1), pc(H)>2; D=(p,q) is disjoint from X={a,b,c,z}; A={a,c} are head witnesses and B={b,z} tail witnesses on the identical tested orientation D; T is one exact two-cover of H-D with both rails nontrivial.

## Scope
Order-free fixed-cover strengthening of the 2x2 opposite-polarity dimer rectangle. No smallest-counterexample minimality once T is supplied. No R508,R825,capture,payment,protected contact,Reverse Ear,path growth,or computation.

## Applicability
Preferred consumer of a full 2x2 same-dimer sign rectangle. In crossed m=6, an LT-AC R583 packet on D=(w,v) combines with accepted R658 tail witnesses b,z and enters this theorem immediately. The quiet residue is a rigid four-endpoint exterior weave rather than an anonymous P4 fan or R825 shape.

## Persistence
Retain D and tested orientation, witness bipartition A|B, the fixed exact cover T, all four cross-pair P4s h-D-t, every relevant R833 block count, and in WEAVE the exact start/end assignment plus the four selected X-exterior endpoint states.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not claim HIGH or SEAM alone closes H. Does not prescribe which B-end pairs with which A-start in WEAVE, nor the exterior block orders. Does not transport endpoint roles to another exact cover.

## Proof
For every h in A={a,c} and t in B={b,z}, the certified turns (h,p,q) and (p,q,t) concatenate to a tight P4 K_{h,t}=(h,p,q,t). Fix the exact cover T. If b_T(h,t)>2 for some cross pair, retain HIGH. Hence assume b_T(h,t)=2 for all four cross pairs. If any application below yields a reverse seam, retain SEAM. Fix h,t and apply accepted R833 to K_{h,t}. At block count two, outside a reverse seam the only alternatives are REVERSE-CHORD, in which T selects the directed state t h, or ANTI-ENDS, in which h and t are nonadjacent degree-one endpoints with h first and t last. We show REVERSE-CHORD cannot occur without a reverse seam. R833 gives b_T(h,t)=deg_T(h)+deg_T(t)-1=2 in the chord case, so {deg_T(h),deg_T(t)}={1,2}. If deg_T(t)=1, then because the selected chord is directed t h, the tail witness t is the first vertex of its T rail. But H=D sqcup T_1 sqcup T_2 is a literal spanning three-cover and t is a tail witness on D; accepted R834 TAIL-START forces a reverse outer seam, contrary to the seam-quiet supposition. If deg_T(h)=1, then the directed chord t h makes the head witness h the last vertex of its rail; accepted R834 HEAD-END again forces a reverse seam. Thus in the absence of SEAM every cross-pair R833 application is ANTI-ENDS. Therefore for each h in A and each t in B, h is a T-rail start and t is a T-rail end. Since T has exactly two rails and a,c are distinct, its two starts are exactly a,c. Likewise its two ends are exactly b,z. Now suppose T selects an X-X state. A state ac would join the two distinct rail starts and is impossible; similarly bz cannot join the two distinct rail ends. Every other X-X edge is a cross pair h t with h in A,t in B. Because h is a rail start and t a rail end, if they are adjacent on one T rail then that rail contains exactly the two vertices h,t. Its orientation must be h t: the reverse t h would make t a start and h an end, contradicting the established endpoint roles. But K_{h,t}=(h,p,q,t) is tight. Replacing the two-vertex T rail (h,t) by K_{h,t} and leaving the other T rail unchanged inserts exactly the deleted dimer D and gives two vertex-disjoint tight paths spanning H. This is CLOSE. Hence outside CLOSE no X-X state is selected. Finally each of a,c,b,z is a degree-one endpoint of a nontrivial T rail. Since it has no selected X-X neighbor, its unique selected neighbor lies in V(H)\\(V(D) union X). Thus the rails begin at a,c, end at b,z, and have nonempty exterior blocks between their X endpoints. This is WEAVE and proves the theorem.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R846.md -->

# R848 — The universal first-inward rectangle cuts to a four-witness outer-inward singleton pair

## Statement
Retain the accepted crossed R621/R723 frame. Put u=q_1, v=q_2, d=q_{m-2}, s=q_{m-1}. Then the frame contains a graph-intrinsic balanced opposite-sign singleton pair on exactly {u,s}={q_1,q_{m-1}}, and each singleton has all four X vertices available as inherited witnesses of its polarity. For m>=5, for each x in X the R723 dimer (v,u) is tail-signed by x and (s,d) is head-signed by x. Deleting the contiguous interval Q[2,m-2] and applying R425 separately leaves tail-signed singleton (u) and head-signed singleton (s), both still witnessed by x. Since the four source sign certificates coexist, the same physical singleton pair carries all four witness certificates. For m=4, the two source dimers meet exactly at q_2 and R547 hinge reduction leaves the same opposite-sign singleton supports {q_1,q_3}, again with the four witness-indexed hinge certificates. This theorem asserts the signed singleton-pair geometry only. It does not assert that the pair is a payment-lineage floor.

## Hypotheses
H is in the accepted crossed R621/R723 frame with m>=4. Use accepted R425 and R547 only for signed-support rebirth/hinge geometry.

## Scope
Corrected structural form of the former outer-inward floor theorem. No payment-lineage membership, pair descent, capture, actualization, or floor steering is assumed or concluded.

## Applicability
Use as a static signed-support and witness-ledger fact at the first inward Q coordinates. It can support later arguments that need the physical singleton signs or the deletion pair {q_1,q_{m-1}}, but a separate certified pair-lineage theorem is required before invoking any floor-only steering or payment consumer.

## Persistence
Retain the physical singleton supports q_1 and q_{m-1}, their opposite polarities, all four X witness certificates, and the exact R425 cut or R547 hinge certificate used to obtain them.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not claim an ancestry-bearing floor, signed-payment lineage membership, support descent, cut progress, or permission to invoke R432. Does not claim the four witness-indexed constructions are four different lineages; they are coexisting graph-intrinsic certificates on the same physical singleton pair.

## Proof
Fix x in X. For m>=5, accepted R723 gives (v,u,x) and (x,s,d) tight. Thus D_L=(v,u) is tail-signed by x and D_R=(s,d) is head-signed by x. Delete C=Q[2,m-2]. In D_L the deleted vertex is v and the surviving terminal interval is singleton u, so the tail form of R425 keeps x as a tail witness on u. In D_R the deleted vertex is d and the surviving initial interval is singleton s, so the head form of R425 keeps x as a head witness on s. The supports {u} and {s} are disjoint and have opposite polarity. Because the R723 sign turns hold for every x in X in the same frame, all four witness certificates are graph-intrinsically available on this same physical pair. If m=4, D_L=(q_2,q_1) and D_R=(q_3,q_2) meet exactly at hinge q_2. R547 applied to these opposite-polarity dimers leaves singleton q_1 on the tail side and q_3 on the head side; applying the same hinge calculation to each of the four witness-indexed sign certificates gives the four-witness ledger. No step places these supports into a signed-payment lineage, so the conclusion is exactly the graph-intrinsic balanced singleton pair and no stronger.

# R849 — Crossed high-side rectangles yield an inward Q signed pair, with certified payment only from m>=7

## Statement
Retain the accepted crossed R621 frame with X={a,b,c,z}, Q=(q_0,...,q_m), m>=6, L=q_0, u=q_1, R=q_m, s=q_{m-1}. The same fixed graph contains two synchronized signed-dimer rectangles. On the left, (L,u) and S_L=(q_3,q_2) are tail-signed by each of b,z. On the right, (s,R) and S_R=(q_{m-2},q_{m-3}) are head-signed by each of a,c. Thus S_L and S_R are opposite-polarity inward Q dimers with fully named endpoint-root witnesses. If m=6, their supports meet exactly in hinge q_3, so R547 yields the graph-intrinsic opposite-sign singleton pair {(q_2),(q_4)} together with the two ancestor dimers and hinge-cut witnesses; no payment-lineage floor is asserted. If m>=7, the two dimer supports are disjoint and form a direct mass-four balanced pair, so accepted R514 yields a finite certificate-retaining continuation to either a spanning two-cover or an ancestry-bearing both-singleton floor. Hence the frame always has the two-ended signed rectangle; certified payment descent follows automatically from it only in the disjoint range m>=7.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in the accepted crossed R621 frame with m>=6. Use accepted R3, R536, R547, R514, and the crossed gate/endpoint-star data retained by R621.

## Scope
Corrected form of the inward-rectangle theorem. Separates raw hinged singletonization at m=6 from genuine mass-four pair descent at m>=7.

## Applicability
Use the signed rectangle itself uniformly for m>=6. Use its automatic certified pair-payment conclusion only for m>=7. At m=6 any floor-only consumer needs an additional theorem placing the R547 hinge descendants into a signed-payment lineage.

## Persistence
Retain the four inward/endpoint signed dimers, witnesses {b,z} on the left and {a,c} on the right, and the exact m=6 hinge or m>=7 disjoint-pair certificate.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
At m=6 does not claim an ancestry-bearing floor or permission to invoke R432. At m>=7 does not claim the paid floor has prescribed singleton coordinates or preserves Q as current. Does not assert simultaneous currentness with branch-specific descendants.

## Proof
Accepted R536 gives q_3q_2b and q_3q_2z tight. To sign (L,u), suppose buL were tight. Then (b,u,L,c,a,z) is a tight path using the endpoint star uLc, the outgoing crossed gate Lca, and matching-height turn caz; together with Q[2,m] it would span H by two paths. Thus buL is bad and R3 gives Lub tight. The same argument with (z,u,L,a,c,b) gives Luz. Hence (L,u) and S_L=(q_3,q_2) are tail-signed by both b,z. Dually, if Rsa were tight then (c,z,b,R,s,a) together with Q[0,m-2] would two-cover H, so R3 gives asR; similarly csR is tight. The right dual of R536 gives a q_{m-2} q_{m-3} and c q_{m-2} q_{m-3}. Hence (s,R) and S_R=(q_{m-2},q_{m-3}) are head-signed by both a,c. If m=6 then S_L=(q_3,q_2) and S_R=(q_4,q_3) meet exactly at q_3. R547 therefore leaves opposite-sign singleton supports q_2 and q_4 with the ancestor-dimer and hinge certificates; by the exact R547/R777 contract this is only a graph-intrinsic balanced pair unless those ancestors are separately shown to lie in a payment lineage. If m>=7 the supports are disjoint. They are then a direct balanced pair of total mass four, so accepted R514 applies and yields either a spanning two-cover or an ancestry-bearing both-singleton floor. This proves the corrected split conclusion.

# R850 — A common long-rail cut exposes the simultaneous depth-two four-witness singleton pair

## Statement
Retain the accepted crossed R621 frame in the beyond-order-ten range m>=6. Put u=q_1, v=q_2, d=q_{m-2}, s=q_{m-1}. Then one fixed contiguous cut of the physical long rail Q exposes a graph-intrinsic balanced opposite-sign singleton pair exactly on {q_2,q_{m-2}} with a simultaneous four-witness ledger: q_2 is tail-signed by both b,z and q_{m-2} is head-signed by both a,c. More precisely, the crossed frame forces S_L=(q_3,q_2) tail-signed by b,z and S_R=(q_{m-2},q_{m-3}) head-signed by a,c. Cutting C=Q[3,m-3] and applying R425 separately to S_L and S_R leaves the two named singleton supports with those inherited witnesses. The two supports are distinct for m>=6 and have opposite polarity, so they form a graph-intrinsic mass-two balanced pair. The retained static ledger contains the four sign turns and the one common Q-cut interval. No ancestry-bearing floor or payment-lineage membership is asserted.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in the accepted crossed R621 frame, m>=6. Use accepted R3,R536,R425 and the crossed gate/endpoint-star data of R621.

## Scope
Corrected coordinate theorem. It preserves the simultaneous two-ended signed singleton geometry while retracting the unsupported floor/payment-lineage upgrade.

Use when an argument needs the exact physical pair {q_2,q_{m-2}}, its opposite singleton signs, or the common-cut four-witness ledger. Before invoking R432 or any other floor-only consumer, separately establish a certified signed-payment lineage for this pair.

## Persistence

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not claim an ancestry-bearing floor, pair descent, strict payment progress, or R432 eligibility. Does not claim the four witness turns are contradictory or that the original long rail remains current in later continuations.

## Proof
Accepted R536 and the crossed endpoint/gate data give the left and right inward sign rectangles exactly as follows. R536 gives q_3q_2b and q_3q_2z. If buL were tight, then (b,u,L,c,a,z) together with Q[2,m] would two-cover H, so R3 gives Lub; similarly Luz. Thus S_L=(q_3,q_2) is tail-signed by b,z. Dually the crossed right gate and endpoint stars imply that Rsa and Rsc are bad by the analogous spanning-cover proposals, so R3 gives asR and csR; the right-end R536 clause gives a q_{m-2} q_{m-3} and c q_{m-2} q_{m-3}. Thus S_R=(q_{m-2},q_{m-3}) is head-signed by a,c. Now delete C=Q[3,m-3]. In S_L the deleted q_3 leaves the terminal singleton q_2, and R425 preserves each old tail witness b,z. In S_R the deleted q_{m-3} leaves the initial singleton q_{m-2}, and R425 preserves each head witness a,c. Since m>=6, q_2 and q_{m-2} are distinct. Their singleton supports are physically disjoint and oppositely signed, hence form a graph-intrinsic balanced pair of total mass two. Because the two R425 applications are separate signed-support rebirths rather than a certified pair descent, the proof concludes only this static pair and its witness/cut ledger, not floor status.

## Statement

If m>=7, every physical choice {i,j}={0,1},{0,2},{1,2} restores immediately to a spanning two-cover of H. For {0,1}, replace the selected G_0-G_1 transition by the original Q segment through q_2 and extend the isolated G_2 leftward by q_{m-2}. For {1,2}, restore q_{m-2} between G_1,G_2 and extend isolated G_0 rightward by q_2. For {0,2}, leave the X-G_0-G_2-X rail untouched and extend isolated G_1 on both sides to Q[2,m-2].

At m=6, the nonadjacent {0,2} placement still closes exactly. In the {0,1} placement, the same restoration has only one possibly uncertified turn, (q_2,q_3,x), where x is the first vertex of the terminal X block after singleton G_1={q_3}; if it is tight H is two-covered, while if bad R3 gives (x,q_3,q_2), which has head polarity opposite the R849 tail-signed dimer (q_3,q_2), hence R523 yields a labelled Hamilton P4 after choosing a distinct witness from {b,z}. Dually, in the {1,2} placement the sole possible seam is (x,q_3,q_4), where x is the last vertex of the initial X block before G_1; if tight H is two-covered, while if bad R3 gives (q_4,q_3,x), opposite the R849 head-signed dimer (q_4,q_3), and R523 yields a labelled Hamilton P4 using a distinct witness from {a,c}. Therefore shape A has no quiet monotone residue: for m>=7 it is impossible in a counterexample, and at m=6 it either closes or produces an explicit source-labelled inward P4.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in accepted crossed R862 sigma=0 frame; m>=6; R866 shape A; accepted R867,R849,R3,R523.

## Scope
Noncircular R24 restoration. c_X=2 shape A only. Pure literal Q restoration plus the order-eleven R849 seam check; no R5,R168,R169,R224,R533,generic R358, or R436.

After R866/R867 identifies shape A, restore the deleted anchors directly rather than analyzing its Q-X transitions. For m>=7 discard the shape by an explicit spanning two-cover. At m=6 retain only the displayed inward-P4 seam branch if the restoration seam is bad.

## Exclusions / nonclaims

## Proof
Let G_0=(q_0,q_1), G_1=(q_3,...,q_{m-3}), G_2=(q_{m-1},q_m), v=q_2 and d=q_{m-2}. By R867, outside explicit Reverse-Ear geometry the shape-A rail is literally E_L-G_i-G_j-E_R with i<j, where E_L,E_R are the two X dimers, and G_k is the isolated second rail.

If {i,j}={0,1}, replace the selected transition from G_0 to G_1 by the old Q segment G_0,v,G_1. Keep both endpoint-X splices inherited from T. Make the second rail d,G_2, which is the old Q interval Q[m-2,m]. For m>=7, G_1 has at least two vertices, so inserting v at its left boundary does not alter the inherited G_1-E_R terminal splice; every turn of both restored rails is certified. They span H, contradiction.

If {i,j}={1,2}, use the exact dual: restore d between G_1 and G_2 on the mixed rail and take G_0,v as the second rail. For m>=7 the inherited E_L-G_1 splice is unaffected, and the two restored rails span H.

If {i,j}={0,2}, do not alter the mixed rail E_L-G_0-G_2-E_R at all. Replace the isolated rail G_1 by v,G_1,d=Q[2,m-2]. This is tight for every m>=6 and gives a spanning two-cover immediately.

Now m=6. Then G_1=(q_3), v=q_2 and d=q_4. The nonadjacent case is still immediate because (q_2,q_3,q_4) is an old Q trimer. In the {0,1} case, the restored first rail has the form E_L,G_0,q_2,q_3,E_R. All its turns are certified except possibly (q_2,q_3,x), where x is the first vertex of E_R. If that turn is tight, the displayed two-cover closes H. If it is bad, R3 gives (x,q_3,q_2) tight. R849 says D_L=(q_3,q_2) is tail-signed by both b,z. Choose r in {b,z} with r!=x. Then (x,q_3,q_2) is a head certificate and (q_3,q_2,r) a tail certificate on the same tested dimer with distinct witnesses, so R523 gives the tight P4 (x,q_3,q_2,r).

In the {1,2} case the restored mixed rail has the form E_L,q_3,q_4,G_2,E_R. The only possible new turn is (x,q_3,q_4), with x the last vertex of E_L. If tight, closure follows. If bad, R3 gives (q_4,q_3,x) tight. R849 says D_R=(q_4,q_3) is head-signed by both a,c. Choose r in {a,c} distinct from x. # R856 — c_X=2 split-X shape C reduces to closure, facing-anchor clauses, or one-hole X forcing

## Statement
Retain the accepted crossed R862 sigma_G(T)=0 five-cell frame with m>=6 and suppose the R866 forest is c_X=2 shape C: one T rail has two Q blocks and one endpoint X block, and the other rail has the remaining Q block and the other endpoint X block. Outside explicit Reverse-Ear geometry, write the two Q blocks on the first rail as G_i,G_j with i<j; the endpoint X block may lie before or after them, and the second rail may have either Q-X or X-Q orientation.

For m>=7 the monotone physical configurations have the following complete normal form. If {i,j}={0,1}, every configuration closes by restoring q_2 and q_{m-2} except the inward-facing orientation G_0-G_1-X_A together with X_B-G_2. In that sole residue, after restoring q_2 on the first rail, the second-rail proposal X_B,q_{m-2},G_2 has exactly two holes and yields the clause
(q_{m-2},y_2,y_1) OR (q_{m-1},q_{m-2},y_2),
where X_B=(y_1,y_2). The second literal always gives a labelled P4 against the fixed head signs a,c on (q_{m-1},q_{m-2}); the first gives R542 if X_B=G_3={a,c} and a labelled P4 if X_B=G_4={b,z}.

If {i,j}={1,2}, every configuration closes except the inward-facing orientation X_A-G_1-G_2 together with G_0-X_B. In that sole residue, after restoring q_{m-2} on the first rail, the second-rail proposal G_0,q_2,X_B has exactly two holes and yields the clause
(y_1,q_2,q_1) OR (y_2,y_1,q_2).
The first literal always gives a labelled P4 against the fixed tail signs b,z on (q_2,q_1); the second gives a labelled P4 if X_B=G_3 and R542 if X_B=G_4.

If {i,j}={0,2}, the first rail may be left in its original T form. The single-G_1 rail absorbs both deleted anchors. If it is X_B-G_1, then K=(q_2,X_B,G_1,q_{m-2}) is, for m>=7, a spanning proposal with exactly one hole (q_2,y_1,y_2); hence that hole is bad and (y_2,y_1,q_2) is forced tight, giving a labelled P4 when X_B=G_3 and an R542-ready packet when X_B=G_4. If it is G_1-X_B, then K=(q_2,G_1,X_B,q_{m-2}) has exactly one hole (y_1,y_2,q_{m-2}); hence (q_{m-2},y_2,y_1) is forced tight, giving R542 when X_B=G_3 and a labelled P4 when X_B=G_4. Thus the nonadjacent Q-pair is stronger than a mate clause: it forces a single source-decorated reverse X literal.

At m=6, G_1={q_3}. Every preceding closure/clause/one-hole construction remains valid unless it exposes one additional singleton-middle seam. There are only four such seam types: (q_2,q_3,x) when a restored left anchor precedes a terminal X block; (x,q_3,q_4) when an initial X block precedes a restored right anchor; and the same two forms on the single-G_1 rail in the nonadjacent case. If the extra seam is tight, the corresponding m>=7 conclusion goes through unchanged. If it is bad, R3 reverses it to (x,q_3,q_2) or (q_4,q_3,x), and R849 plus R523 gives a labelled Hamilton P4 using respectively a distinct witness from {b,z} or {a,c}. Hence shape C has no quiet monotone residue for any m>=6: it either closes, gives an inward-facing two-hole anchor clause whose realized literal is P4- or R542-ready, forces a one-hole reverse-X literal with the same consumer-ready typing, or at order eleven yields a labelled inward P4.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in accepted crossed R862 sigma=0 frame; m>=6; R866 shape C; accepted R867,R616,R621,R649,R849,R3,R523,R542.

## Scope
Noncircular R24 restoration. Complete monotone consumer of c_X=2 Split-X shape C. Uses literal anchor restoration, physical one/two-hole proposals, and fixed-frame sign packets; no R5,R168,R169,R224,R533,generic R358, or generic R436.

## Applicability
After R866/R867 identifies shape C, first record which physical Q pair lies on the two-Q rail and whether its endpoint X block faces inward or outward. Adjacent Q pairs close except the unique inward-facing configuration, which gives the displayed anchor clause. A nonadjacent G_0-G_2 pair should be treated by the stronger one-hole insertion on the single-G_1 rail. At m=6 test the unique singleton-middle seam first; badness is already a labelled inward P4.

## Persistence
Retain the physical Q-pair, directions and identities of X_A and X_B, the exact restored rails, the one/two-hole proposal and complete hole set, and the fixed source sign used to type the realized reverse X or inward-Q literal. For R542 outputs retain its short carrier; for P4 outputs retain the literal order.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not claim a labelled P4 or R542 continuation closes H. Does not consume R867 Reverse-Ear outputs. Does not address Internal-X shape B or sigma>0. Alternative clause/payment branches are not asserted to coexist.

## Proof
Put v=q_2, w=q_3, d=q_{m-2}, r=q_{m-3}, s=q_{m-1}. Outside R867 Reverse-Ear geometry, the two Q blocks on the three-block rail occur in increasing Q order. Call its endpoint X block X_A and the X block on the other rail X_B=(y_1,y_2) in actual T order when needed.

We first record two boundary sign resources exactly as in the fixed crossed frame. R616 gives the enlarged roots H-z=(q_1,q_0,a,c,b) sqcup Q[2,m] and H-b=(q_1,q_0,c,a,z) sqcup Q[2,m]. If z q_1 v were tight, then (z,q_1,v,...,q_m) together with (q_0,a,c,b) would two-cover H, so R3 gives v q_1 z; similarly v q_1 b is tight. Thus D_0=(v,q_1) is tail-signed by b,z. On the right, R621 gives H-a=Q[0,d] sqcup (c,z,b,q_m,s) and H-c=Q[0,d] sqcup (a,b,z,q_m,s). If d s a were tight, Q[0,d],s,a together with (c,z,b,q_m) would two-cover H, hence a s d is tight; similarly c s d is tight. Thus D_2=(s,d) is head-signed by a,c. R649 supplies R542-ready fixed head polarity on every orientation of G_3={a,c} and fixed tail polarity on every orientation of G_4={b,z}.

CASE {G_i,G_j}={G_0,G_1}. If the first rail is X_A-G_0-G_1, restore v between G_0,G_1 and append d after G_1. For m>=7 this gives a tight rail X_A,G_0,v,G_1,d; the second source rail is untouched, so the two rails span H. If instead the first rail is G_0-G_1-X_A, restore v there. When the second rail is G_2-X_B, prepend d to it, giving d,G_2-X_B; both rails are tight and span H. Thus only G_0-G_1-X_A together with X_B-G_2 remains. The first restored rail is tight for m>=7. On the second rail consider X_B,d,G_2. Its only holes are (y_1,y_2,d) and (y_2,d,s), so R3 gives A=(d,y_2,y_1) OR B=(s,d,y_2). B is a tail sign on D_2 opposite the fixed head witnesses a,c, hence choose one distinct from y_2 and use R523 to obtain a labelled P4. A is a head sign on the reverse X_B dimer: if X_B=G_3 it is same-head on an R649 reverse-boundary packet, so R542 applies; if X_B=G_4 it is opposite the fixed tail sign and R523 gives a P4.

CASE {G_i,G_j}={G_1,G_2}. If the first rail is G_1-G_2-X_A, prepend v and restore d between G_1,G_2; this gives a tight rail v,G_1,d,G_2-X_A for m>=7, so closure follows with the untouched second rail. If instead it is X_A-G_1-G_2, restore d. When the second rail is X_B-G_0, append v to it, giving X_B-G_0,v and closure. Thus only X_A-G_1-G_2 together with G_0-X_B remains. Consider G_0,v,X_B on the second rail. Its holes are (q_1,v,y_1) and (v,y_1,y_2), giving clause A=(y_1,v,q_1) OR B=(y_2,y_1,v). A is a head sign on D_0 opposite its tail witnesses b,z, hence R523 gives a labelled P4. B is a tail sign on the reverse X_B dimer: P4 for X_B=G_3, R542 for X_B=G_4 by R649.

CASE {G_i,G_j}={G_0,G_2}. Leave the entire three-block source rail, including its selected G_0-G_2 transition and endpoint X_A, untouched. All missing vertices v,d must be absorbed by the single-G_1 rail. If that rail is X_B-G_1, use K=(v,y_1,y_2,G_1,d). For m>=7 the source X_B-G_1 splice and the old Q extension G_1,d are unaffected, so the unique hole is h=(v,y_1,y_2). If h were tight, K with the untouched first rail would two-cover H. Thus h is bad and R3 forces (y_2,y_1,v), a tail sign on the reverse X_B dimer. R649/R523 gives a P4 for X_B=G_3, while for X_B=G_4 the same-tail sign with new witness v makes an R542-ready two-witness packet. If the single-G_1 rail is G_1-X_B, use K=(v,G_1,y_1,y_2,d). Its unique hole for m>=7 is (y_1,y_2,d), so R3 forces (d,y_2,y_1), a head sign on the reverse X_B dimer. R649 gives R542 for X_B=G_3 and a P4 for X_B=G_4.

Finally m=6, so G_1=(q_3), v=q_2,d=q_4. Review the preceding constructions. Whenever a restored anchor meets G_1 on the side opposite an inherited X splice, the lost second G_1 vertex leaves exactly one extra seam. In the {0,1} cells with first rail G_0-G_1-X_A this seam is (v,q_3,x); in the {1,2} cells with X_A-G_1-G_2 it is (x,q_3,d). In the nonadjacent case X_B-G_1 the extra seam is (y_2,q_3,d), and in G_1-X_B it is (v,q_3,y_1). No other new seams occur. If the relevant extra seam is tight, the m>=7 closure, two-hole clause, or one-hole forcing proceeds unchanged. If (v,q_3,x) is bad, R3 gives (x,q_3,v), a head sign on D_L=(q_3,v), while R849 tail-signs D_L by b,z; choose a distinct witness and R523 gives a P4. If (x,q_3,d) is bad, R3 gives (d,q_3,x), a tail sign on D_R=(d,q_3), while R849 head-signs D_R by a,c; again R523 gives a P4. The two nonadjacent extra seams are the same two forms. Hence every m=6 exception is already a labelled inward P4. This exhausts shape C.

# R862 — Simultaneous inward-anchor deletion forces an R24-safe five-cell triple-transition fan

## Statement
Retain the crossed beyond-order-ten R621 frame, put D={q_2,q_{m-2}}, m>=6, and W=H-D. Then W has the literal five-component reference cover G_0=Q[0,1], G_1=Q[3,m-3], G_2=Q[m-1,m], G_3=(a,c), G_4=(b,z). All five components are nonempty pairwise vertex-disjoint tight paths. For every exact two-cover T of W, the number t_G(T) of selected T-states joining distinct G_i is t_G(T)=3+sigma(T)>=3, with equality exactly when every G_i occurs in one contiguous T-block. Thus one common exact pair-deletion recompletion contains at least three simultaneous source-labelled cross states. Every such cross state is individually R176-admissible, and because q_2,q_{m-2} are precisely the two vertices outside W, either one may be chosen as the spare singleton coordinate in the explicit R176 construction. The conclusion is exact transition geometry tied to one common deleted inward-anchor pair; no signed-floor or payment-lineage hypothesis is used or asserted.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in accepted crossed R621, m>=6. Use R429 Pair-Deletion Rigidity, R7 Intrinsic Partition-Cover Deficit Identity, and R176 Spare-Vertex Cross-State Pair Upgrade.

## Scope
Noncircular R24 restoration. Crossed phase, beyond order ten. Exact pair-deletion transition geometry at the two inward Q anchors. No R5,R168,R169,R224,R533,R620,generic R358,R436, or floor lineage is used.

## Applicability
Choose one exact two-cover of H-{q_2,q_{m-2}} and retain all intercell transitions simultaneously. Attack sigma>0 or revisited-cell patterns first; at transition minimum three classify only the finite two-rail arrangements of the five physical blocks.

## Persistence
Retain D={q_2,q_{m-2}}, the five source cells, the exact R429 cover T, every selected intercell state, t_G and sigma, and any separately chosen R176 spare-anchor certificate. No signed-floor ancestry is part of this theorem.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert three independent closing pairs, simultaneous currentness of R176 descendants, t_G=3 always, or any signed-payment floor. Its gain is one R24-safe common recompletion with at least three source-labelled crossings.

## Proof
Put D={q_2,q_{m-2}} and W=H-D. No signed-floor input is needed for the cover count below. Since m>=6, the three Q pieces G_0=Q[0,1], G_1=Q[3,m-3], and G_2=Q[m-1,m] are all nonempty contiguous subpaths of the tight rail Q. The two remaining sets G_3={a,c} and G_4={b,z} are two-vertex paths and hence automatically tight. The five vertex sets are pairwise disjoint and their union is exactly W, so R_G=G_0 sqcup G_1 sqcup G_2 sqcup G_3 sqcup G_4 is a literal five-path cover of W. Each induced class H[G_i] has path-cover number one, witnessed by its displayed path. Accepted Pair-Deletion Rigidity R429 gives an exact two-cover T=T_1 sqcup T_2 of W. Apply the accepted Intrinsic Partition-Cover Deficit Identity R7 to the fixed partition Pi={V(G_0),...,V(G_4)} and T. Since the sum of the five intrinsic class path-cover numbers is 5 and T has 2 rails, R7 gives t_Pi(T)=5-2+sigma(T)=3+sigma(T)>=3, where sigma(T)>=0. The equality characterization in R7 says sigma(T)=0 exactly when every class occurs in one contiguous T-block. Every counted transition is a selected adjacent state xy of T whose endpoints lie in two distinct components of the literal reference cover R_G. Since W is proper, accepted R176 applies to each such selected state. In the explicit R176 proof the spare vertex d may be chosen arbitrarily in V(H)-W=D; hence for each selected cross state one may choose d=q_2 or d=q_{m-2}, retaining that inward anchor as the spare singleton coordinate of the resulting balanced-pair certificate. All counted transitions belong to the same exact T and therefore coexist as selected source-labelled states before any separate R176 continuation is chosen. This proves the lemma.

# R865 — Minimum five-cell inward-anchor recompletion splits by Q-X transition count, with the one-cross branch already dimer-localized

## Statement
Retain the accepted crossed beyond-ten five-cell packet R862, with D={q_2,q_{m-2}}, W=H-D, and cells G_0=Q[0,1], G_1=Q[3,m-3], G_2=Q[m-1,m], G_3={a,c}, G_4={b,z}. Let T be an exact two-cover of W in the minimum case sigma_G(T)=0, so each G_i occurs as one contiguous T-block and T has exactly three intercell selected transitions. Then: (1) T has no selected transition directly between G_3 and G_4. Indeed such an adjacency would make the four consecutive vertices of the two dimer blocks a tight Hamilton P4 on X={a,b,c,z}, contradicting the P4-free transitive frame of R594. (2) Let c_X(T) be the number of selected transitions with one endpoint in a Q-cell G_0,G_1,G_2 and the other in an X-dimer cell G_3,G_4. Then c_X(T) is one of 1,2,3. It is at least one because accepted R508 applied with deletion set D, surviving carrier S=V(Q)-D, and absorber Q forces every exact H-D two-cover to cross S|X; it is at most three because T has exactly three intercell transitions. Since G_3G_4 is impossible, the remaining 3-c_X(T) transitions are Q-cell to Q-cell. (3) If c_X(T)=1, then the three Q-cells are joined by the other two transitions into one Q-cell path, exactly one X-dimer is attached to that path, and the other X-dimer is an isolated T-rail. Equivalently the contracted five-cell forest is P4 disjoint union P1. Relative to the R508 partition S=V(Q)-D and C=X, T has tau(T)=1 and exactly two maximal C-blocks, namely the two physical dimers G_3 and G_4. Hence T is exactly an accepted R511 unique-transition recompletion packet with one pure C rail equal to one X-dimer and the other X-dimer the C-block of the mixed rail. After the accepted R512/R513 seam reduction, any surviving both-bad pure-seam residue has dimer pure-C rail and therefore lies directly in accepted R550 in the CS orientation or accepted R568 in the SC orientation. Thus the c_X=1 minimum branch is not a new five-cell species: it is a source-labelled specialization of the existing dimer unique-transition cell. The only genuinely new minimum five-cell transition patterns have c_X=2 or c_X=3.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in the accepted crossed R621 frame, in the beyond-ten range m>=6. Accepted R862 supplies the five-cell exact-cover packet and sigma=0 minimum case. Use accepted R594 P4-freeness of X, accepted R508/R511/R512/R513 recompletion machinery, and accepted dimer refinements R550,R568.

## Scope
Noncircular R24 restoration. Beyond-ten crossed phase, sigma=0 specialization of the accepted R862 five-cell fan. No R5,R168,R169,R224,R533,generic R358, or R24 is used.

## Applicability
When analyzing a minimum R862 recompletion, first count Q-X transitions. Discard c_X=1 as an already localized R511/R550/R568 branch and focus new work on c_X=2 or 3, where at least two source-labelled Q-X incidences coexist in the same exact pair-deletion frame.

## Persistence
Retain D; all five physical cells; the exact cover T; its three selected intercell transitions; the contracted two-path forest; the Q-X transition count c_X. In c_X=1 retain the identity and orientation of the pure X dimer, the mixed X dimer, the unique Q-X crossing and its Q cut index, and the full R511/R512/R513/R550-or-R568 seam certificates.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not close the c_X=1 R550/R568 residuals; it only proves they are old localized cells rather than new five-cell geometry. Does not classify c_X=2 or c_X=3 beyond their transition counts. Does not assert the three source transitions yield simultaneous R176 descendants. Does not use the R664 witness families yet.

## Proof
Let D={q_2,q_{m-2}} and retain an exact two-cover T of W=H-D with sigma_G(T)=0 in the R862 partition. By R862, each of G_0,...,G_4 occurs as exactly one contiguous T-block and the total number of intercell selected transitions is t_G(T)=3. Contract each block to its cell label. Since T consists of two vertex-simple path rails, the contracted transition graph F_T is a two-component path forest on the five vertices G_0,...,G_4 with exactly three edges.

First exclude the edge G_3G_4. If a selected T-state joins the G_3 block to the G_4 block, then because sigma_G(T)=0 both blocks are complete contiguous dimers. The four consecutive vertices obtained by traversing the first dimer block, the selected interblock state, and the second dimer block form a tight P4 using exactly X={a,b,c,z}. This contradicts the P4-free conclusion of accepted R594. Hence no G_3-G_4 transition occurs.

Now apply accepted R508 with the same deletion set D and with S=V(Q)-D=G_0 union G_1 union G_2. The original path Q is a tight path on exactly D union S. Its complement in W is C=X=G_3 union G_4. Therefore every exact two-cover T of H-D selects at least one state crossing S|C. In the sigma=0 cell language, this is exactly a Q-cell to X-cell transition. Let c_X(T) denote their number. Since T has exactly three intercell transitions and none is G_3-G_4, 1<=c_X(T)<=3 and every remaining intercell edge is between two Q-cells.

Assume c_X(T)=1. Then the other two edges of F_T are Q-Q edges. There are three Q-cell vertices G_0,G_1,G_2. Because F_T is a forest, two Q-Q edges on these three vertices must form the unique three-vertex path, so all three Q cells lie in one connected component. The unique Q-X edge attaches exactly one of G_3,G_4 to that component; the other X-cell has no incident edge, because G_3G_4 is forbidden and there is only one Q-X edge. Thus F_T has shape P_4 disjoint union P_1. In particular one rail of T is exactly one complete X-dimer block and the other rail contains all three Q blocks and the other complete X-dimer block.

Return to the R508 partition S=V(Q)-D and C=X. The number tau(T) of selected S|C states is exactly c_X(T)=1. Because sigma_G(T)=0 and G_3G_4 is absent, the two maximal C-blocks in the literal T rails are precisely the two full physical dimers G_3 and G_4: one is the pure rail and the other is the unique C-block of the mixed rail. Hence the hypotheses and exact block word of accepted R511 are satisfied, with the pure C-block K having order two. Accepted R512/R513 give the complete unique-transition seam reduction. If an easy R512 output occurs, retain it. Otherwise the only hard residue is the R513 both-bad pure C/Q seam cell. Since the pure C rail K is a dimer, its parameter is s=1. If the mixed rail has C after S (CS), accepted R550 is exactly the dimer pure-C refinement of that R513 residue; if it has S after C (SC), accepted R568 is the exact dual refinement. Thus every c_X=1 sigma=0 recompletion is already governed by the accepted unique-transition/dimer seam machinery.

Consequently the only sigma=0 R862 transition counts not already reduced to that old cell are c_X=2 and c_X=3. No payment descendant or representative transfer is used anywhere in the classification.

# R866 — Minimum inward-anchor five-cell residue has only six typed forest shapes and three structural regimes

## Statement
Retain the sigma_G(T)=0 minimum five-cell setting of accepted R865. Contract each complete contiguous cell block G_0,G_1,G_2,G_3,G_4 in the exact two-cover T to a vertex, writing Q for any of G_0,G_1,G_2 and X for either of G_3,G_4. The contracted graph F_T is a two-component path forest on three Q-vertices and two X-vertices with exactly three edges, no X-X edge, and c_X(T) in {2,3} in the genuinely new residue. Up to permutation of the three Q labels and interchange of the two X labels, exactly six typed forest shapes occur. For c_X=2: (A) X-Q-Q-X plus an isolated Q; (B) Q-Q-X-Q plus an isolated X; (C) Q-Q-X plus Q-X; (D) Q-Q plus X-Q-X. For c_X=3: (E) X-Q-X-Q plus an isolated Q; (F) Q-X-Q plus Q-X. Consequently the entire c_X=2,3 minimum residue falls into only three structural regimes. (I) Internal-X regime: some X-dimer cell has degree two in F_T; this is every c_X=3 cover and c_X=2 shape (B). (II) Same-rail endpoint-X regime: both X-dimer cells have degree one and lie on the same T-rail; these are c_X=2 shapes (A) and (D). (III) Split-X regime: both X-dimer cells have degree one and lie on different T-rails; this is only c_X=2 shape (C). In regime (I), the degree-two X block is literally preceded and followed by Q blocks on one oriented T-rail. In regime (II), orienting the common rail makes one X block its first endpoint and the other its last endpoint. No other minimum c_X=2 or 3 topology exists.

## Hypotheses
Accepted R865 sigma=0 five-cell packet, with c_X(T) in {2,3}.

## Scope
Pure finite path-forest classification inside the noncircular crossed R24 five-cell frame. No sign/payment theorem is used.

## Applicability
Replace ad hoc enumeration of c_X=2/3 block arrangements by the three regimes Internal-X, Same-rail endpoint-X, and Split-X. Combine only afterward with transition-direction/source-decoration data.

## Persistence
Retain the exact cover T, physical identities of G_0,...,G_4, all three selected intercell transitions, and the contracted two-component path forest. The six shapes are quotient types; physical Q/X labels and rail directions remain retained separately.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not classify orientations of the T rails, Hamilton orders inside Q-cell blocks, or the collision/P4 decorations of Q-X transitions. Does not claim any shape closes H. Q-cell permutations and X-cell swaps are only quotient symmetries for listing shapes; physical cell identities remain distinct downstream.

## Proof
By accepted R865, in the sigma_G(T)=0 case each of the five cells is one complete contiguous T-block and T has exactly three intercell transitions. Contracting the blocks gives a graph F_T with five vertices and three edges. Each T rail contracts to a path, so F_T is a forest with exactly two path components and maximum degree at most two. R865 also excludes the X-X edge G_3G_4. We work only in the new c_X=2,3 residue.

CASE c_X=2. Exactly one of the three edges is Q-Q and two are Q-X. Let e be the unique Q-Q edge. Because maximum degree is two, the two Q-X edges can be placed relative to e in only the following quotient-distinct ways.
(1) Attach one X to each endpoint of e. This gives the four-vertex path X-Q-Q-X and leaves the third Q isolated: shape A.
(2) Attach one X to an endpoint of e and attach the second Q-X edge from that same X to the third Q. This gives Q-Q-X-Q and leaves the other X isolated: shape B. Equivalently this is the unique c_X=2 shape with an X vertex of degree two.
(3) Attach one X to one endpoint of e and use the other Q-X edge between the third Q and the other X. This gives Q-Q-X plus Q-X: shape C.
(4) Use both Q-X edges at the third Q, joining it to both X vertices. Then e is a separate Q-Q component and the other component is X-Q-X: shape D.
These exhaust the possibilities. To see this formally, each Q-X edge either meets an endpoint of e or the third Q. If neither meets the third Q, maximum degree forces them to hit different endpoints, giving A. If exactly one meets the third Q, then the other either meets the same X, giving B, or the other X, giving C after quotient relabelling. If both meet the third Q, they must use the two distinct X vertices, giving D.

CASE c_X=3. There is no Q-Q edge. Thus F_T is a bipartite path forest with three Q vertices, two X vertices, three edges. Since the sum of X-degrees is three, one X has degree two and the other has degree one. The degree-two X is joined to two Q vertices. The remaining Q-X edge either attaches the degree-one X to one of those two Q vertices, producing the four-vertex path X-Q-X-Q and leaving the third Q isolated (shape E), or attaches it to the third Q, producing Q-X-Q plus Q-X (shape F). These are quotient-distinct and exhaustive.

The structural regimes now follow immediately. Shapes B,E,F contain an X vertex of degree two, and no other shape does; E,F are exactly all c_X=3 shapes. Shapes A,D have both X vertices degree one in the same nontrivial path component, hence on the same T rail, with one at each end after orienting that rail. Shape C has its two degree-one X vertices in the two different path components, hence on different T rails. This proves R670.
