# R867 — Reverse-ear normalization makes every minimum five-cell Q block literal and ordered

## Statement
Retain the accepted sigma_G(T)=0 five-cell packet of R865, with original tight rail Q=(q_0,...,q_m), cells G_0=Q[0,1], G_1=Q[3,m-3], G_2=Q[m-1,m], and exact two-cover T of W=H-{q_2,q_{m-2}}. Apply accepted Reverse Ear R435 separately to each T-rail K against the original graph-intrinsic path Q. Then either a T-rail yields an explicit Q-relative reverse selected state, reverse trimer/contact, or vertex-simple tight cycle as in R435, or every Q vertex met along that T-rail occurs in strictly increasing Q-index order. In the latter monotone branch, because sigma_G(T)=0 makes each G_i one complete contiguous T-block containing all vertices of that Q interval, the literal T-order inside every Q-cell block is exactly the original Q orientation: G_0=(L,u), G_1=(q_3,...,q_{m-3}), G_2=(s,R). Consequently every intercell transition endpoint on a Q block is physically named. A Q-X transition leaving G_0,G_1,G_2 uses respectively u,q_{m-3},R; one entering those blocks uses respectively L,q_3,s. Every Q-Q transition is oriented from lower-index cell to higher-index cell and is exactly one of u q_3 (G_0->G_1), q_{m-3}s (G_1->G_2), or u s (G_0->G_2). In particular, in the c_X=2 Internal-X shape of R670, where all three Q cells lie on one T-rail and the degree-two X block separates two Q blocks, monotonicity forces the X block to replace one actual deleted-anchor gap: the rail order is either G_0-X-G_1-G_2 or G_0-G_1-X-G_2. Thus its two Q-X transition endpoints are exactly {u,q_3} in the left-gap case or {q_{m-3},s} in the right-gap case. The alternative in which that X block joins nonadjacent G_0 and G_2 is impossible outside the explicit R435 reverse/cycle output.

## Hypotheses
Accepted R865 minimum sigma=0 five-cell frame and accepted R435 Reverse Ear Lemma. The Internal-X addendum uses the finite c_X=2 forest shape classified in R670, but its path-shape fact may be read directly from the contracted T forest.

## Scope
Noncircular R24 restoration. Pure path-order normalization of one exact inward-anchor deletion cover. No payment, R5,R168,R169,R224,R533, or generic R358 is used.

## Applicability
Before analyzing c_X=2/3 forest orientations, compare each T rail with Q. Treat any reverse-ear output as an explicit source-localized geometric branch. Otherwise replace every Q-cell block by its literal original Q interval and use only the named boundary vertices for all transition-splice calculations.

## Persistence
Retain Q, T, the five cell identities, literal T rail directions, all Q contacts, and any R435 reverse state/trimer/cycle certificate. In the monotone branch retain the exact original-Q order of every Q block and the named endpoints of every intercell selected state.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not close an R435 reverse/cycle branch. Does not constrain the Hamilton order of the X-dimer blocks beyond their two possible orientations. Does not assert a Q-Q skip turn is itself contradictory. The Internal-X conclusion applies only to the c_X=2 degree-two-X shape with all three Q cells on one rail.

## Proof
Let Q=(q_0,...,q_m), L=q_0,u=q_1,s=q_{m-1},R=q_m, and let T=T_1 sqcup T_2 be an exact cover in the accepted R865 sigma_G(T)=0 case. Fix one oriented T rail K. Both Q and K are vertex-simple tight paths. List the vertices of Q encountered along K in K-order. Accepted R435 says that if two consecutive K-contacts with Q occur in reverse Q-index order, then K already yields one of the explicit Reverse-Ear outputs: an exact reversed old state, a reverse trimer/contact at a seam, or a vertex-simple tight cycle. Therefore, unless such an output is retained, the Q vertices encountered along K occur in strictly increasing Q-index order. Apply this independently to both T rails.

Assume the monotone branch. By sigma_G(T)=0, each physical cell G_i occurs in exactly one contiguous T-block. For i=0,1,2, every vertex of G_i is a Q vertex, and the block contains all vertices of that interval. Since their K-order is increasing in Q-index, the block order is forced literally: G_0=(q_0,q_1)=(L,u), G_1=(q_3,...,q_{m-3}), and G_2=(q_{m-1},q_m)=(s,R). This also covers m=6, when G_1 is the singleton q_3.

Now read an intercell selected state incident with a Q block. If a rail leaves G_0,G_1,G_2 toward the next block, the Q endpoint is respectively the last displayed vertex u,q_{m-3},R. If it enters those blocks, the endpoint is respectively the first displayed vertex L,q_3,s. If two Q blocks are adjacent on one rail, monotonicity forces the lower-index block first. Thus G_0->G_1 selects exactly u q_3, G_1->G_2 selects q_{m-3}s, and G_0->G_2 selects u s. No reverse Q-Q orientation occurs without the already separated R435 output.

For the final c_X=2 Internal-X claim, suppose the contracted forest has one X vertex of degree two. Since c_X=2, both Q-X edges are incident with that X vertex and the third edge is Q-Q. The other X vertex is isolated. The nonisolated component therefore contains the degree-two X and all three Q vertices and is a four-vertex path. Along its actual T orientation the three Q contacts must appear G_0,G_1,G_2 in this order. The X vertex occupies one of the two gaps between consecutive Q contacts. Hence the only possible rail orders are G_0-X-G_1-G_2 or G_0-G_1-X-G_2. A purported G_0-X-G_2 adjacency would leave G_1 attached by the sole Q-Q edge to either G_0 or G_2; either orientation of the resulting four-vertex path encounters two Q cells out of increasing index order, contrary to the monotone branch. Finally the named Q-X endpoints follow from the block endpoint calculation: {u,q_3} for G_0-X-G_1 and {q_{m-3},s} for G_1-X-G_2. This proves R671.

# R868 — Internal X blocks force a labelled P4; the minimum five-cell P4-free residue is source-sink oriented

## Statement
Retain the accepted crossed beyond-order-ten inward-anchor five-cell frame of R862/R865 with m>=6, and let T be an exact two-cover of W=H-{q_2,q_{m-2}} in the minimum case sigma_G(T)=0. Thus each X cell G_3={a,c} and G_4={b,z} occurs as one complete contiguous oriented dimer block of T. Then the following hold.

(1) INTERNAL-X P4. If either X-dimer block has degree two in the contracted five-cell forest F_T, then H contains an explicit source-labelled tight Hamilton P4. More precisely, write the degree-two block in its literal T-order as S=(s_0,s_1), with Q vertices y_- immediately before S and y_+ immediately after S on that T rail. If S=G_3, accepted R649 supplies fixed head polarity on S with at least three named source witnesses. The outgoing triple (s_0,s_1,y_+) is a tail sign on S, opposite to that fixed head polarity; choosing a fixed head witness w distinct from y_+, accepted R518 forces a Hamilton P4 on {w,s_0,s_1,y_+}. If S=G_4, accepted R649 supplies fixed tail polarity on S; the incoming triple (y_-,s_0,s_1) is an opposite head sign, and choosing a fixed tail witness w distinct from y_- makes R518 force a Hamilton P4 on {y_-,s_0,s_1,w}.

Consequently every R866 Internal-X minimum configuration has a labelled P4: this includes all c_X(T)=3 shapes E and F and the c_X(T)=2 internal-X shape B.

(2) SOURCE-SINK ORIENTATION OF THE NO-P4 RESIDUE. Suppose no Q-X transition of T yields the opposite-polarity R518 P4 described above. Then neither X block has degree two, so both have degree one. Moreover the unique transition incident with G_3 must ENTER the oriented G_3 block, while the unique transition incident with G_4 must LEAVE the oriented G_4 block. Hence G_4 is an initial block of its T rail and G_3 is a terminal block of its T rail. Therefore the only surviving R866 structural regimes are Same-rail endpoint-X and Split-X. In the same-rail regime the common oriented rail runs G_4 -> ... -> G_3. In the split-X regime the rail containing G_4 begins at G_4 and the rail containing G_3 ends at G_3.

Thus the six-shape minimum taxonomy collapses, before any R176 payment or generic contact, to a labelled-P4 branch or a canonically source-sink-oriented endpoint-X residue.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in the accepted crossed R621 frame, m>=6. Use accepted R862/R865 in the minimum case sigma_G(T)=0, accepted fixed-polarity source packets R649, the opposite-polarity four-cell amplifier R518, and the accepted forest-regime classification R866.

## Scope
Noncircular R24 compression of the sigma=0 inward-anchor five-cell fan. It eliminates the entire Internal-X regime to labelled P4 geometry and canonically orients the remaining endpoint-X residue. No R5,R168,R169,R224,R533,R350,generic R358,R176 payment,R436,Reverse Ear,shape-specific A-F splice theorem,or computation.

## Applicability
Apply immediately to any minimum exact H-{q_2,q_{m-2}} recompletion before shape-by-shape analysis. If an X block is internal, retain the labelled P4 and stop classifying that forest. Otherwise orient the surviving endpoint-X geometry with G_4={b,z} as a rail source and G_3={a,c} as a rail sink. In particular, when used after pending R761, this compression acts on the same exact recompletion while leaving the transported mixed-sibling ancestry ledger untouched as historical data.

## Persistence
Retain the exact cover T, the five physical cells and their literal T orientations, the contracted forest, the degree and incident Q endpoint(s) of each X block, the chosen fixed R649 witness, and any resulting labelled R518 P4. In the no-P4 branch retain the forced source/sink orientation G_4 -> Q and Q -> G_3 together with all original source labels. Any independent ancestry ledger, including the pending R761 mixed-sibling ledger, remains historical certificate data but is not asserted to constrain T unless separately consumed.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not close a labelled P4 branch. Does not treat sigma_G(T)>0, where an X dimer may be fragmented and the contiguous-block argument is unavailable. Does not consume same-polarity R38 collisions, does not move a physical cut by itself, and does not assert the transported R761 sibling-fiber ancestry changes the local transition proof. Does not eliminate the Same-rail endpoint-X or Split-X residues. Does not supersede shape-specific theorems outside this compressed branch, although it makes their Internal-X entry unnecessary whenever this theorem is used.

## Proof
Let T be a minimum sigma_G(T)=0 exact two-cover in the accepted R862/R865 frame. Every physical cell G_i is one contiguous T-block. In particular G_3={a,c} and G_4={b,z} each appear as a literal oriented two-vertex block.

First suppose an X block has degree two in the contracted forest. It lies internally on one oriented T rail, hence has one selected Q-X state entering it and one selected Q-X state leaving it.

Take S=G_3 in its literal T-order S=(s_0,s_1). Accepted R649 gives fixed head polarity on either possible orientation of this physical dimer. Concretely, in orientation (a,c) it gives the distinct head witnesses L,R,b, and in orientation (c,a) it gives L,R,z. Let y_+ be the Q vertex immediately after S on the T rail. Tightness of T makes (s_0,s_1,y_+) tight, so y_+ is a tail witness on the same oriented dimer S, opposite to the fixed R649 head polarity. Choose one fixed R649 head witness w distinct from y_+; this is always possible because at least three are available. The fixed source trimer (w,s_0,s_1) is tight, while (s_0,s_1,y_+) is an opposite-polarity sign on its terminal physical dimer. Accepted R518 therefore forces a tight Hamilton P4 on {w,s_0,s_1,y_+}.

Now take S=G_4 in its literal T-order. Accepted R649 gives fixed tail polarity on either possible orientation, with at least three named source witnesses. Let y_- be the Q vertex immediately before S. Tightness of T makes (y_-,s_0,s_1) tight, so y_- is a head witness on S, opposite to the fixed tail polarity. Choose a fixed R649 tail witness w distinct from y_-. The fixed source trimer (s_0,s_1,w) is tight and the y_- sign has the opposite polarity on its initial physical dimer, so R518 forces a tight Hamilton P4 on {y_-,s_0,s_1,w}. This proves the Internal-X P4 assertion.

Accepted R866 says every c_X=3 minimum forest and c_X=2 shape B contains an internal degree-two X block, so all of those configurations lie in the P4 branch.

For the second assertion, suppose no Q-X incidence produces the opposite-polarity P4 above. Then no X block can have degree two, hence both X blocks have degree one. Let the unique incidence of G_3 be considered in its literal T direction. If it left G_3, it would be a tail sign opposite to R649's fixed head polarity and the preceding argument would force a P4. Therefore it must enter G_3, so G_3 is the terminal block of its rail. Dually, if the unique incidence of G_4 entered G_4, it would be a head sign opposite to R649's fixed tail polarity and would force a P4. Therefore it must leave G_4, so G_4 is the initial block of its rail.

R866 now leaves only Same-rail endpoint-X and Split-X. If the two X blocks lie on one rail, its orientation necessarily begins at G_4 and ends at G_3. If they lie on different rails, the G_4 rail begins at G_4 and the G_3 rail ends at G_3. No R176 birth, payment descent, or shape-specific splice is used. This proves the theorem.

# R869 — BAD inward-anchor seams avoid both deleted anchors and amplify to an inward P4 or dual two-witness boundary packets

## Statement
Retain the accepted crossed beyond-order-ten inward-anchor five-cell frame of R862. Put v=q_2, d=q_{m-2}, W=H-{v,d}, and let G be the literal five-component reference cover of W from R862. Fix any exact two-cover T of W and any selected intercell transition xi of T relative to G. Suppose the preferred accepted R176 proof for xi lies in its BAD seam branch, so it exposes a tight reverse trimer K=(k_0,k_1,k_2) whose signed nontrivial support is cut from one old G-component at an endpoint of xi. Then V(K) is contained in W. In particular v and d are distinct vertices outside K.

Consequently accepted R700 applies to K with probes v,d. Exactly one of the following useful alternatives is available.

(P4-INWARD) At least one of V(K) union {v} and V(K) union {d} supports a tight Hamilton P4.

(DUAL-CP) Neither probe gives a P4. Then both reverse boundary dimers of K are simultaneously two-witness R542-ready packets with the SAME distinguished witness pair {v,d}: if K=(k_0,k_1,k_2), the reverse initial dimer (k_1,k_0) is tail-signed by both v,d and the reverse terminal dimer (k_2,k_1) is head-signed by both v,d. Thus R542, and if desired its accepted geometric refinement R696, applies independently at both boundaries without generic R436 or protected first contact.

The containment V(K) subset W is literal: in the preferred R176 proof every reverse-trimer vertex is either an endpoint of the selected transition xi or an old neighbor of such an endpoint inside one reference component of G, and all those vertices belong to W. Therefore no BAD reverse trimer produced from an R862 transition can contain either deleted inward anchor. In particular the MEETS-q_{m-2} subbranch stated in pending R765 is empty; every such BAD trimer necessarily avoids both q_2 and q_{m-2}. 

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in the accepted crossed R621 frame, m>=6. Use accepted R862, the preferred full proof P540 of accepted R176, and accepted R700. T is any exact two-cover of W=H-{q_2,q_{m-2}}, and xi is any R862 intercell transition whose R176 analysis takes a BAD seam branch. 

## Scope
Noncircular accepted-input parent theorem for BAD seams in the simultaneous inward-anchor five-cell frame. No pending mixed-sibling theorem is needed. No R5,R168,R169,R224,R533,R350,generic R358,R436,R312,Reverse Ear,shape taxonomy,or computation. It also records a correction to the pending R765 branch split. 

## Applicability
Whenever an R862/R761 analysis encounters a BAD R176 seam, first record that its reverse trimer lies wholly in W and hence avoids both deleted inward anchors. Probe that trimer immediately with q_2 and q_{m-2} via R700. Prefer the P4-INWARD output; otherwise retain both reverse boundary dimers as simultaneous two-witness packets with the same inward witness pair. Do not pursue an R765 MEETS-d branch: it is impossible. 

## Persistence
Retain W, the reference cover G, exact cover T, selected transition xi, the exact R176 BAD reverse trimer K and old-neighbor provenance, the two deleted inward anchors v,d as outside probes, both R700 four-cell tests, and in DUAL-CP both tested reverse boundary dimers with the common witness pair {v,d}. Selectedness of xi is T-relative; the trimer, P4s, and sign packets are graph-intrinsic certificate data. 

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert that either R542/R696 descendant closes H, that the two packet descendants coexist, or that a Hamilton P4 is spanning. Does not consume GOOD R176 transitions. Does not treat sigma>0 differently from sigma=0: the theorem applies to any supplied R862 intercell BAD transition. Does not canonically reject or repair pending R765; it proves that R765's MEETS-d alternative is mathematically empty. 

## Proof
Let xi be the selected intercell state. In the preferred full proof P540 of R176, a BAD seam is produced as follows. Both endpoints of xi lie in W, in distinct components of the reference cover G. Choose the endpoint k_1 on the reference component being tested and an old G-neighbor k_0 of k_1. Boundary antisymmetry on the other selected endpoint k_2, k_1, k_0 gives the displayed reverse trimer, in one of the two dual orientations. Every one of k_0,k_1,k_2 lies in W. Therefore K is disjoint from {v,d}=V(H)-W at these two distinguished deleted coordinates.

Now v and d are distinct vertices outside the tight trimer K. Apply accepted R700 with y_1=v and y_2=d. If either R518 probe in R700 yields a Hamilton P4, this is P4-INWARD. Otherwise R700's joint no-P4 branch gives both reverse contacts for each probe and therefore makes the reverse initial boundary dimer of K tail-signed by both v,d and the reverse terminal boundary dimer head-signed by both v,d, on the exact tested orientations stated by R700. These are simultaneous two-witness R542-ready packets. This proves the dichotomy. Since d is outside K in every BAD branch, the MEETS-d alternative of pending R765 has no realizations.

# R870 — Crossed excess recompletions reduce to three binary Q-cell splits outside P4 or Reverse-Ear geometry

## Statement
Retain the accepted crossed beyond-ten inward-anchor five-cell frame R862 with W=H-{q_2,q_{m-2}}, source cells G_0=Q[0,1], G_1=Q[3,m-3], G_2=Q[m-1,m], G_3={a,c}, G_4={b,z}, and let T be any exact two-cover of W. Suppose both X cells G_3,G_4 are unfragmented, i.e. each occurs as one contiguous two-vertex T-block. Then at least one of the following holds. (P4) H contains a source-labelled tight Hamilton P4 obtained from an incorrectly placed contiguous X block by the R649/R518 polarity argument. (RE) Comparing a T-rail with the original Q by R435 yields an explicit reversed old Q-state, reverse trimer/contact, or vertex-simple tight cycle. (BINARY-SPLIT) Neither geometric output occurs. Then G_4 is the initial block of its T-rail, G_3 is the terminal block of its T-rail, and after deleting these possible endcaps each T-rail consists only of Q vertices encountered in strictly increasing Q-index order. Consequently, for each i in {0,1,2}, the vertices of G_i occur in at most one T-block on each rail. Hence G_i contributes either one source-cell block total, if all of G_i lies on one rail, or exactly two source-cell blocks, if G_i is split nontrivially between the two rails. Therefore sigma_G(T) is exactly the number of Q-cells G_i that are split between the two rails. In particular sigma_G(T) is in {0,1,2,3}; if sigma_G(T)>0, all excess is encoded by at most three binary split decisions and t_G(T)=3+sigma_G(T)<=6.

## Hypotheses
Accepted crossed R621/R649 frame; accepted inward-anchor five-cell frame R862; accepted R518 and Reverse Ear R435; T is any exact two-cover of W and both physical X dimers are contiguous T-blocks.

## Scope
Noncircular crossed beyond-ten sigma compression. It treats every sigma_G(T), not only sigma=0, under the explicit unfragmented-X hypothesis. No payment, capture, floor steering, or finite forest enumeration is used.

## Applicability
Use at the start of sigma>0 analysis. If an X block is wrongly placed, retain the labelled P4. If Q order reverses, retain the R435 output. Otherwise replace the arbitrary excess block word by a 3-bit record indicating which of G_0,G_1,G_2 are split across the two rails.

## Persistence
Retain T, the actual X-dimer orientations and rail-end roles, any R435 output, and in BINARY-SPLIT the three split bits together with the two increasing Q-subsequences carried by the T-rails.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not treat fragmentation of G_3 or G_4 into singleton blocks. Does not claim a split pattern closes H. Does not require the Q vertices assigned to one rail to be consecutive in Q, only increasing. Does not consume P4 or Reverse-Ear outputs.

## Proof
Let the two X dimers be contiguous. For G_3 in its actual T-order S=(s_0,s_1), if a T vertex y follows S then (s_0,s_1,y) is tight. Accepted R649 supplies fixed head polarity on either orientation of G_3 with at least three named witnesses; choose w distinct from y with (w,s_0,s_1) tight. The y-sign is opposite in polarity on the terminal dimer, so R518 gives a Hamilton P4. Hence outside P4, G_3 is terminal. Dually, if a vertex y precedes contiguous G_4, then (y,s_0,s_1) is a head sign opposite the fixed R649 tail polarity; choosing a distinct fixed tail witness and applying R518 gives a Hamilton P4. Hence outside P4, G_4 is initial. Now compare each T-rail K with the original tight path Q by R435. If Q contacts occur in reverse index order, retain the corresponding R435 reversed-state/reverse-trimer/cycle output. Otherwise Q vertices along K occur in strictly increasing Q-index order. Since any G_4 block can occur only at the beginning and any G_3 block only at the end, the portion of K between those endcaps contains only Q vertices. Fix a Q cell G_i, which is an interval in the Q index order. Once K leaves that interval for a higher-index Q cell, increasing order forbids returning to G_i; and there is no internal X block available to separate two occurrences of G_i. Thus all G_i vertices assigned to K form one maximal G_i block, though they need not be consecutive indices in Q. Therefore each G_i contributes at most one block on each of the two T-rails: one total block if it lies wholly on one rail, exactly two if both rails meet it. The two X cells contribute exactly one block each by hypothesis. Relative to the five reference cells, sigma_G(T) is the number of extra blocks, hence precisely the number of Q cells represented on both rails. This number lies in {0,1,2,3}, and R862 gives t_G(T)=3+sigma_G(T).

# R872 — Opposite-polarity dimer certificates force a two-endpoint recompletion crossing

## Statement
Let H be a finite Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament with pc(H)>2. Let D=(a,b) be a tested oriented physical dimer, and let x,y be distinct vertices outside {a,b} such that (x,a,b) and (a,b,y) are tight. Accepted R523(HT) supplies the vertex-simple tight P4 K=(x,a,b,y). Put Delta={a,b}, S={x,y}, and E=V(H)\(Delta union S), and assume E is nonempty. Let T be any supplied literal exact two-cover of H-Delta. Then accepted R508, applied to deletion Delta, absorbable block S, recompletion path K, and T, forces T to select a directed state with exactly one endpoint in S and the other in E. Equivalently, the two opposite-polarity witnesses on D cannot remain T-isolated from the exterior of K. The same conclusion holds with x,y exchanged under R523(TH), via the P4 (y,a,b,x).

## Hypotheses
Finite Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament H with pc(H)>2; D=(a,b) tested oriented dimer; x,y are distinct opposite-polarity witnesses on that same tested orientation; E=V(H)\{a,b,x,y} nonempty; T is a supplied exact two-cover of H-{a,b}. Uses accepted R523 and R508 only.

## Scope
Order-free parent compilation of R523(HT/TH) with R508. No smallest-counterexample minimality, R5, crossed frame, first-inward geometry, capture, protected contact, R312, R527, R429, or rail-nontriviality hypothesis.

## Applicability
Use whenever two opposite-polarity certificates share one tested oriented dimer and an exact two-cover of the deleted dimer is independently available. Prefer this parent over manually forming the P4 and then quoting R508. Capture/payment/first-contact are later consumers.

## Persistence
Retain the tested oriented dimer D, witness identities and polarities, R523 P4 K, deletion Delta, block S, supplied cover T, and at least one selected S|E crossing of T. The P4/signs are graph-intrinsic; the crossing is T-relative.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not produce the deletion two-cover, does not invoke R5, does not claim both T rails nontrivial, does not determine which witness is the S-endpoint, and does not capture/pay/contact or produce closure. Opposite tested orientations remain distinct data.

## Proof
Write D=(a,b), with (x,a,b) and (a,b,y) tight. By accepted R523(HT), K=(x,a,b,y) is a vertex-simple tight P4. Let Delta={a,b}, S={x,y}, and W=V(H)\Delta. Then V(K)=Delta union S and E=W\S is nonempty by hypothesis. Because pc(H)>2 and T is a supplied exact two-cover of H-Delta, accepted R508 applies to (Delta,S,K,T) and forces a selected T-state with exactly one endpoint in S and the other in W\S=E. The TH orientation is identical after exchanging x and y and using the R523 P4 (y,a,b,x). No existence theorem for T is used.

# R873 — Two-probe reverse-dimer packets propagate as directed witness waves along a tight path

## Statement
Let Q=(q_0,...,q_m) be a vertex-simple tight path in a Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament and let x,y be distinct vertices outside Q. For 1<=i<=m-1 write D_i=(q_i,q_{i-1}). Let H_i(x,y) mean that D_i is head-signed by both probes, and T_i(x,y) that D_i is tail-signed by both. For each i with q_{i+1} present, apply accepted R518 separately to K_i=(q_{i-1},q_i,q_{i+1}) with fourth vertex x and with fourth vertex y. Either one of the two four-sets K_i union {x}, K_i union {y} supports a Hamilton P4, or simultaneously T_i(x,y) and H_{i+1}(x,y) hold. Consequently a pre-existing H_i packet either meets a probe P4 or becomes bidirectionally saturated while the HEAD packet propagates to D_{i+1}; dually a pre-existing T_{i+1} packet propagates left to D_i. Iterating, a P4-free run propagates the same two probes one dimer at a time and leaves every traversed dimer bidirectionally saturated.

## Hypotheses
Q tight; x,y distinct outside Q; accepted order-free R518. No smallest-counterexample, deletion cover, matching-height frame, payment, or minimality.

## Scope
Pure order-free propagation lemma for same-pair two-probe packets. No R700,R5,R168,R169,R224,R533,R350,generic R358,R542,payment,capture,R436,or computation.

## Applicability
In the crossed frame use accepted R849 for the inward signed seeds and accepted R820 for paired terminal packets. Absent labelled probe P4s, packets move one Q dimer at a time. Retain the wave only as exact sign geometry; R829 forbids treating propagation length itself as closure progress.

## Persistence
Retain Q, index, probe identities, source packet, and at each step either the exact labelled P4 support or the newly propagated packet plus bidirectional saturation of the source dimer. All sign turns coexist along a P4-free run.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert a propagation run is P4-free, that a P4 closes H, or that different witness-pair waves interact automatically. Does not spend saturated dimers. Path-length growth is not claimed.

## Proof
Fix i and K_i=(q_{i-1},q_i,q_{i+1}). Apply accepted R518 to K_i with fourth vertex x. If its P4 branch occurs, stop. Otherwise R518 gives the two reverse contacts (q_i,q_{i-1},x) and (x,q_{i+1},q_i). Apply R518 independently with fourth vertex y. Again either a probe P4 occurs or it gives (q_i,q_{i-1},y) and (y,q_{i+1},q_i). Thus in the joint no-P4 branch D_i=(q_i,q_{i-1}) is tail-signed by both x,y and D_{i+1}=(q_{i+1},q_i) is head-signed by both x,y. If H_i was already known, D_i is now bidirectionally saturated and H_{i+1} is new; if T_{i+1} was already known, the dual leftward statement holds. Repeating the same two R518 probes at consecutive trimers proves the iterated wave statement.

# R874 — Oppositely directed two-witness waves at distance two collide into a four-P4 central fan

## Statement
Let Q=(q_0,...,q_m) be a vertex-simple tight path in a Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament. Fix 1<=j<=m-2 and four distinct vertices a_1,a_2,b_1,b_2 outside Q. Suppose D_j=(q_j,q_{j-1}) is head-signed by both b_1,b_2 and D_{j+2}=(q_{j+2},q_{j+1}) is tail-signed by both a_1,a_2. Apply accepted R518 separately to K_j=(q_{j-1},q_j,q_{j+1}) with probes b_1,b_2 and to K_{j+1}=(q_j,q_{j+1},q_{j+2}) with probes a_1,a_2. Then either one of those four probe four-sets supports a Hamilton P4, or the central reverse dimer D_{j+1}=(q_{j+1},q_j) is head-signed by both b probes and tail-signed by both a probes. In the latter FAN branch, accepted R523 gives all four literal tight P4s (b_r,q_{j+1},q_j,a_s), r,s in {1,2}. Thus opposite two-witness waves separated by one Q dimer cannot pass quietly: absent a probe P4 they meet in a complete 2-by-2 central P4 fan.

## Hypotheses
Q tight; a_1,a_2,b_1,b_2 four distinct vertices outside Q; D_j head-signed by b_1,b_2; D_{j+2} tail-signed by a_1,a_2. Uses accepted R518 and R523 only.

## Scope
Pure order-free two-wave collision lemma. No R700, smallest-counterexample, R24 frame, deletion cover, payment, capture, R5,R168,R169,R224,R533,R350,generic R358,R436,Reverse Ear,or computation.

## Applicability
In the crossed R24 frame take {b_1,b_2}={b,z} and {a_1,a_2}={a,c}. Accepted R820 paired terminal packets can provide the source hypotheses. Retain the FAN as one simultaneous graph-intrinsic object; use exact-cover seam consumers such as R833/R834 rather than generic path-growth optimism.

## Persistence
Retain Q,j,the ordered witness pairs,the two source packets, all four R518 probe tests, and in FAN all four central sign certificates and all four mixed P4 orders.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert any P4 closes H, that FAN extends to a long path, or that source packets arose in one cover. Does not spend or actualize the central dimer.

## Proof
Apply R518 to K_j=(q_{j-1},q_j,q_{j+1}) with b_1 and b_2 separately. If either P4 branch occurs, P4-LEFT holds. Otherwise the two no-P4 outputs give (b_r,q_{j+1},q_j) tight for r=1,2, so D_{j+1} is head-signed by both b probes. Independently apply R518 to K_{j+1}=(q_j,q_{j+1},q_{j+2}) with a_1,a_2. Outside a probe P4, its no-P4 outputs give (q_{j+1},q_j,a_s) tight for s=1,2, so the same tested D_{j+1} is tail-signed by both a probes. In the joint no-P4 branch, each b_r head certificate and a_s tail certificate share the identical tested orientation and have distinct witnesses. Accepted R523(HT) therefore gives the tight P4 (b_r,q_{j+1},q_j,a_s). All four choices coexist graph-intrinsically.

# R875 — At the crossed m=6 gap, every R583 packet reduces to reverse-middle P4, fixed-cover seam/high-block, signed-rectangle weave, or core seam

## Statement
Retain the accepted crossed m=6 frame Q=(L,u,v,w,d,s,R), X={a,b,c,z}, with corrected inward signed rectangles from accepted R849. Apply accepted R583 at the unique internal gap w|d. Then one of the following source-visible outcomes occurs.

(RM) A reverse-middle two-witness packet occurs, and accepted R584 gives a labelled Hamilton P4.

(RT) A right-terminal packet occurs: distinct x,y in X satisfy (s,d,x),(s,d,y). Accepted R723 also gives (x,s,d),(y,s,d), so both P4 orders (x,s,d,y) and (y,s,d,x) are tight. For any exact two-cover T of H-{s,d}, both rails are necessarily nontrivial; hence accepted R843 gives either b_T(x,y)>2 or an R833 source-visible reverse seam.

(LT-AC) The left-terminal witness pair is {a,c}. Then D=(w,v) is head-signed by a,c from R583 and tail-signed by b,z from accepted R849. For any exact two-cover T of H-D, both rails are nontrivial and accepted R846 gives HIGH, SEAM, CLOSE, or WEAVE. In WEAVE, accepted R847 further gives either explicit R435 reverse/cycle geometry or, up to interchanging rails, exactly one of the two monotone Q-contact partitions {L,d,R}|{u,s} or {u,d,R}|{L,s}.

(LT-BZ) The left-terminal witness pair is {b,z}. Accepted R849 tail-signs D=(w,v) by b,z, while R583 head-signs it by b,z, so both P4 orders (b,w,v,z),(z,w,v,b) are tight. Every exact H-D two-cover therefore gives HIGH or an R843 reverse seam.

(LT-MIX) The left-terminal witness pair is {h,k}, with h in {a,c} and k in {b,z}. If h=a, accepted R839(A2) gives either the literal core seam (v,a,c) or the additional tail sign (w,v,a); in the latter branch, R849 tail-signs k and the two opposite endpoint orders (a,w,v,k),(k,w,v,a) are both tight, so R843 gives HIGH or a reverse seam. If h=c, accepted R839(A1) gives either core seam (v,c,a) or tail sign (w,v,c), with the identical R843 conclusion.

Thus the unique crossed m=6 R583 packet has no anonymous terminal residue: it is a labelled P4, fixed-cover HIGH/SEAM geometry, the rigid R846/R847 rectangle WEAVE, or one of the two literal core seams (v,a,c),(v,c,a).

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in accepted crossed R621 at m=6. Uses accepted R3,R4,R583,R584,R723,R839,R843,R846,R847,R849. No R5,R24,R825,R508,capture,payment,protected contact,or path-growth theorem.

## Scope
Finite crossed m=6 terminal-gap compression with corrected provenance and complete fixed-cover hypotheses. Replaces old R845 dependence on the brittle R825 seven/eight-shape route.

## Applicability
Use first on the unique m=6 R583 packet. Reverse-middle and bidirectional terminal packets go directly to R584/R843. A full {a,c} head by {b,z} tail rectangle goes through R846 then R847. Mixed packets use the exact R839 A1/A2 core-seam clause before R843. Preserve all fixed-cover endpoint/block data.

## Persistence
Retain packet type, witness identities, tested central dimer, and for any fixed-cover branch the chosen exact deletion cover, its nontrivial rails, block count, selected reverse seam or WEAVE endpoint roles/Q-contact partition. In LT-MIX retain the exact R839 literal realized.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not claim a labelled P4, HIGH block count, reverse seam, R435 cycle/reversal, surviving WEAVE partition, or core seam closes H. Does not identify a canonical exact deletion cover. Does not use R825 or any seven-shape terminology.

## Proof

Retain the crossed m=6 frame Q=(L,u,v,w,d,s,R), X={a,b,c,z}. We use the R583 obstruction array at the unique internal gap w|d. The proof is organized by the packet R583 produces.

[cover-nontriviality]
We first record a local cover fact. Let D be any tight physical dimer and let T=T_1 sqcup T_2 be an exact two-cover of H-D supplied by R4. The deletion system H-D is not Hamiltonian, since a Hamilton path of H-D together with D would two-cover H. Neither T rail is singleton: if T_1={r}, then on V(D) union {r}, R3 supplies a tight trimer; that trimer together with T_2 would span H by two paths. Thus every exact dimer-deletion cover used below has two nontrivial rails.

[reverse-middle]
If R583 yields two reverse-middle blockers across w|d, R584 applies directly and produces a labelled tight reverse P4. This is outcome RM.

[right-terminal]
Suppose R583 yields distinct x,y with (s,d,x),(s,d,y). R723 supplies (x,s,d),(y,s,d), hence both P4s (x,s,d,y) and (y,s,d,x) are tight on common middle dimer (s,d). Choose any exact H-{s,d} two-cover T. By cover-nontriviality both rails are nontrivial, so R843 gives either b_T(x,y)>2 or a source-visible reverse seam. This is RT.

[core-middle-six-clauses]
We now prove locally the six m=6 core-middle clauses formerly isolated as R839. Put N=(v,w,d). R817 gives four core P4 rails A_1=(u,L,a,c), A_2=(u,L,c,a), B_1=(b,z,R,s), B_2=(z,b,R,s), with every A_i disjoint from every B_k and A_i sqcup B_k an exact two-cover of the order-eight core. Hence N together with any chosen A_i,B_k partitions V(H).

Concatenate N with these core rails. Every internal turn remains certified and exactly the two seam turns at the concatenation are new. If both seam turns were tight, the concatenated rail plus the untouched complementary core rail would two-cover H; therefore at least one seam turn is bad and R3 makes its reversal tight.

1. Append A_i after N. The only new turns are (w,d,u),(d,u,L), so we obtain (u,d,w) OR (L,u,d). Call this E_A.
2. Prepend A_1 before N: (u,L,a,c,v,w,d). The new turns are (a,c,v),(c,v,w), giving (v,c,a) OR (w,v,c). Call this A_1.
3. Prepend A_2 before N: (u,L,c,a,v,w,d). The new turns are (c,a,v),(a,v,w), giving (v,a,c) OR (w,v,a). Call this A_2.
4. Append B_1 after N: (v,w,d,b,z,R,s). The new turns are (w,d,b),(d,b,z), giving (b,d,w) OR (z,b,d). Call this B_1.
5. Append B_2 after N: (v,w,d,z,b,R,s). The new turns are (w,d,z),(d,z,b), giving (z,d,w) OR (b,z,d). Call this B_2.
6. Prepend B_k before N. The final seam window is (...,R,s,v,w,d), with new turns (R,s,v),(s,v,w), giving (v,s,R) OR (w,v,s). Call this E_B.

The hole lists are complete because the supports are literal disjoint spanning partitions. These six clauses are simultaneous physical facts in the fixed m=6 frame.

[left-terminal]
Now suppose R583 gives distinct head witnesses x,y on D_L=(w,v): (x,w,v),(y,w,v).

If {x,y}={b,z}, R849 tail-signs the same D_L by b,z. Thus both (b,w,v,z) and (z,w,v,b) are tight P4s. Any exact H-D_L cover has nontrivial rails, so R843 gives HIGH or a reverse seam. This is LT-BZ.

If {x,y}={a,c}, R849 tail-signs D_L by b,z, giving the full head/tail 2x2 signed rectangle. For any exact H-D_L cover T, cover-nontriviality applies and R846 yields HIGH, SEAM, CLOSE, or WEAVE. The quiet WEAVE branch is normalized below.

If {x,y} is mixed, write {h,k} with h in {a,c}, k in {b,z}. If h=a, local clause A_2 above says (v,a,c) OR (w,v,a). In the first case retain the literal core seam (v,a,c). In the second, a is also a tail witness on D_L. R849 already tail-signs k, while both a,k are head witnesses from R583, so both (a,w,v,k) and (k,w,v,a) are tight; R843 gives HIGH or reverse seam. If h=c, use local clause A_1: (v,c,a) OR (w,v,c), and the same argument gives either core seam (v,c,a) or a bidirectional same-dimer P4 pair followed by R843. This is LT-MIX.

[weave-normalization]
It remains to justify the precise quiet WEAVE alternative formerly isolated as R847. Let T=T_1 sqcup T_2 be a WEAVE cover of H-{w,v} from R846. Thus its two rail starts are exactly a,c, its two rail ends exactly b,z, it selects no X-X state, and each rail has the form h -> E_h -> t with a nonempty exterior block E_h drawn from E={L,u,d,s,R}; the two E-blocks partition E.

Compare each T rail with the old path Q using R435. If either comparison produces an old-state reversal, reverse trimer/contact, or vertex-simple tight cycle, retain that explicit R435 output. Otherwise the Q contacts along each T rail occur in increasing Q-index order.

Under this monotonicity there are three forbidden same-rail patterns. For every start h in {a,c}, R594 gives (u,L,h), so R3 makes (h,L,u) bad; hence L and u cannot lie on the same weave rail. For every end t in {b,z}, R594 gives (t,R,s), so (s,R,t) is bad; hence s and R cannot lie on one rail. R723 gives (t,s,d), so (d,s,t) is bad; hence d and s cannot lie together either. Each rail has a nonempty E-block and the blocks partition five vertices. A 1+4 split is impossible: whichever vertex is isolated, the four-block contains at least one forbidden pair L,u or s,R (and in the relevant cases d,s). Therefore the sizes are 2 and 3. Among d,s,R, two must share a rail; d,s and s,R are forbidden, so the shared pair is exactly {d,R}, while s is on the other rail. Finally L and u must split. Thus, up to interchanging rails, the only possible contact partitions are {L,d,R}|{u,s} and {u,d,R}|{L,s}, each in increasing Q order. This proves the full quiet WEAVE normalization.

[conclusion]
The R583 packet possibilities are exhausted. Reverse-middle gives a labelled P4 via R584. Right-terminal and LT-BZ give fixed-cover HIGH/SEAM via R843. LT-AC gives R846 HIGH/SEAM/CLOSE, or WEAVE followed by either explicit R435 geometry or one of the two monotone contact partitions just proved. LT-MIX gives either one of the literal core seams (v,a,c),(v,c,a) or HIGH/SEAM via R843. This is exactly R875.

# R876 — The aligned order-ten R24 frame has an immediate 6+4 spanning cover

## Statement
Retain the aligned m=5 R594/R619 frame with Q=(L,u,v,d,s,R), X={a,b,c,z}, and aligned middle-gate edge {a,c}. Then H has the literal spanning two-cover P_6 sqcup P_4 where P_6=(u,L,a,c,R,s) and P_4=(b,d,v,z). Hence no aligned m=5 order-three R24 frame exists.

## Hypotheses
Hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in the aligned R619/R594 frame with m=5. Use accepted R594 endpoint stars, aligned gate turns from R619, and aligned inward turns from R536.

## Scope
Finite aligned m=5 closure. Literal 6+4 two-cover; no payment, capture, R5,R24, Mate-Fork, computation, or path-growth theorem.

## Applicability
Use as the complete aligned m=5 finite base once freshly reviewed.

## Persistence
Retain Q,X and the two literal path orders P_6=(u,L,a,c,R,s), P_4=(b,d,v,z).

## Exclusions / nonclaims
No additional phase or residue remains.

## Proof
Write Q=(L,u,v,d,s,R). Accepted R594 gives the universal endpoint-star turns (u,L,x) and (x,R,s) for every x in X, hence in particular (u,L,a) and (c,R,s). In the aligned R619 gate, {a,c} is the same middle-gate edge at both ends, so (L,a,c) and (a,c,R) are tight. Therefore the order P_6=(u,L,a,c,R,s) is a tight path, with consecutive turns (u,L,a),(L,a,c),(a,c,R),(c,R,s).

Accepted R536 in the aligned phase says the complementary middle-gate edge {b,z} gives the right inward turns (b,q_{m-2},q_{m-3}) and (z,q_{m-2},q_{m-3}); at m=5 these are (b,d,v) and (z,d,v). The left inward packet gives (d,v,z) on the same complement. In particular (b,d,v) and (d,v,z) are tight, so P_4=(b,d,v,z) is tight.

The supports of P_6 and P_4 are disjoint and together are {L,u,v,d,s,R} union {a,b,c,z}=V(H). Thus P_6 sqcup P_4 is a spanning two-cover of H, contradicting pc(H)>2. Hence the aligned m=5 frame is impossible.

# R877 — The order-nine R24 frame closes in both gate phases by one-hole cap collisions

## Statement
Retain the m=4 synchronized transitive R594 frame Q=(L,u,v,s,R), X={a,b,c,z}. In the aligned phase, two literal one-hole spanning proposals force both reverse orientations (b,u,v) and (v,u,b) tight, contradicting R3. In the crossed phase, six literal one-hole proposals force Rbu=(R,b,u), aLz=(a,L,z), cRb=(c,R,b), saL=(s,a,L), then both Lzv=(L,z,v) and vzL=(v,z,L) tight, again contradicting R3. Hence no m=4 order-three R24 frame exists in either gate phase.

## Hypotheses
Hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in accepted R594 with m=4, in either aligned or crossed R619 phase. Use accepted R3,R536,R594,R619 and, in the crossed phase, R723.

## Scope
Finite m=4 closure by explicit one-hole spanning proposals only. No R5,R24,payment,capture,Mate-Fork,or computation.

## Applicability
Use as the complete m=4 finite base once freshly reviewed.

## Persistence
Retain every displayed two-path proposal and its unique uncertified hole. Each forced reverse literal is graph-intrinsic; the final contradiction is a literal reversal pair.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
No residual branch remains in either gate phase.

## Proof
We repeatedly use the following literal one-hole principle. If two vertex-disjoint proposed paths have supports partitioning V(H), and every required turn except one ordered triple tau is already tight, then tau must be bad because otherwise the two paths would be a spanning two-cover of H. Boundary antisymmetry R3 therefore makes rev(tau) tight.

ALIGNED. Let Q=(L,u,v,s,R). Consider
(1) (z,v,u,b) sqcup (L,a,c,R,s). The only uncertified turn is (v,u,b). Indeed (z,v,u) is the aligned right-inward turn from R536 at m=4; (L,a,c),(a,c,R) are the aligned gates and (c,R,s) is an R594 endpoint star. Hence the cap forces the reverse (b,u,v) tight.
(2) (L,c,a,z) sqcup (b,u,v,s,R). The only uncertified turn is (b,u,v): (L,c,a) is the aligned gate, (c,a,z) is a tight X-turn in the R594 matching-height four-cell, and (u,v,s),(v,s,R) are Q turns. Hence (v,u,b) is tight.
The two forced turns (b,u,v) and (v,u,b) are exact complete reversals, contradicting R3.

CROSSED. Retain accepted R723, which at m=4 gives (v,u,x) and (x,s,v) tight for every x in X, and R536, which gives the relevant inward complement turns.
(1) (L,c,a,z) sqcup (v,u,b,R,s) has sole hole (u,b,R): (L,c,a) is a left gate, (c,a,z) an X-turn, (v,u,b) comes from R723, and (b,R,s) is an endpoint star. Thus (R,b,u)=:Rbu is tight.
(2) (u,v,s,R) sqcup (b,z,L,a,c) has sole hole (z,L,a): Q certifies the first rail, while (b,z,L) and (L,a,c) are crossed left gates. Thus (a,L,z)=:aLz is tight.
(3) (L,u,v,s) sqcup (b,R,c,a,z) has sole hole (b,R,c): the first rail is Q, (R,c,a) is a crossed right gate, and (c,a,z) is an X-turn. Thus (c,R,b)=:cRb is tight.
(4) (c,z,b,R) sqcup (u,L,a,s,v) has sole hole (L,a,s): (c,z,b) is an X-turn, (z,b,R) a crossed right gate, (u,L,a) an endpoint star, and (a,s,v) comes from R723. Thus (s,a,L)=:saL is tight.
(5) (c,R,b,u) sqcup (a,s,v,z,L) has sole hole (v,z,L): the first rail uses cRb and Rbu; the second uses (a,s,v) from R723 and (s,v,z) from R536. Thus (L,z,v)=:Lzv is tight.
(6) (c,R,b,u) sqcup (s,a,L,z,v) has sole hole (L,z,v): the first rail again uses cRb,Rbu; the second uses saL,aLz. Thus (v,z,L)=:vzL is tight.
The final forced turns Lzv=(L,z,v) and vzL=(v,z,L) are complete reversals, contradicting R3. Therefore the crossed phase is impossible as well.

# R878 — The crossed order-ten R24 frame closes by a six-Mate-Fork companion certificate

## Statement
Retain the crossed m=5 frame Q=(L,u,v,d,s,R), X={a,b,c,z}. Ten explicit one-hole spanning caps force the graph-intrinsic turns Rbv=(R,b,v), Rzv=(R,z,v), aLb=(a,L,b), aLz=(a,L,z), aRb=(a,R,b), cLz=(c,L,z), cRb=(c,R,b), cRz=(c,R,z), daL=(d,a,L), dcL=(d,c,L). Six applications of the accepted physical Mate-Fork rule R173 then force, in order, Rbu=(R,b,u), saL=(s,a,L), Ras=(R,a,s), asu=(a,s,u), sub=(s,u,b), and ubL=(u,b,L). Consequently P_6=(R,a,s,u,b,L) and P_4=(c,d,v,z) are disjoint tight paths spanning H. Hence no crossed m=5 order-three R24 frame exists.

## Hypotheses
Hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in accepted crossed R621/R594 with m=5. Use accepted R3,R173,R536,R594,R621,R723 and the matching-height X-turn table encoded in R594.

## Scope
Finite crossed m=5 closure by a literal ten-cap plus six-Mate-Fork companion certificate. No R5,R24,R824,R350,payment,capture,Hamilton-growth theorem,or computation.

## Applicability
Use as the complete crossed m=5 finite base once freshly reviewed. Preserve the literal proposals and hole pairs; do not compress this proof to anonymous Mate-Fork existence.

## Persistence
Retain all ten one-hole proposals, their unique holes and forced reversals; then retain each of the twelve two-hole Mate-Fork proposals, the mate pair and shared hole, and each forced shared-hole reversal. The final P6 and P4 are literal graph-intrinsic paths.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not use the intermediate R824 half-crossed gate theorem, any paid-floor lineage, or generic path growth. The certificate is finite and source-turn exact.

## Proof
Write Q=(L,u,v,d,s,R). We use the same one-hole principle as usual: a spanning two-path proposal with one uncertified turn tau forces rev(tau) by pc(H)>2 and R3. Every non-hole turn below is one of: a Q turn; an R594 endpoint star; a crossed R621 gate turn; an R723 first-inward star; an R536 inward turn; an R594 matching-height X turn; or a literal previously forced in the proof.

TEN ONE-HOLE CAPS.
1. (u,L,c,a,z) sqcup (d,v,b,R,s), hole (v,b,R), forces Rbv=(R,b,v). The certified turns are uLc,Lca,caz and dvb,bRs.
2. (u,L,a,c,b) sqcup (d,v,z,R,s), hole (v,z,R), forces Rzv=(R,z,v). Certified: uLa,Lac,acb and dvz,zRs.
3. (u,v,d,s,R) sqcup (c,z,b,L,a), hole (b,L,a), forces aLb=(a,L,b). Certified: Q and czb,zbL.
4. (u,v,d,s,R) sqcup (b,z,L,a,c), hole (z,L,a), forces aLz=(a,L,z). Certified: Q and bzL,Lac.
5. (L,u,v,d,s) sqcup (c,z,b,R,a), hole (b,R,a), forces aRb=(a,R,b). Certified: Q and czb,zbR.
6. (u,v,d,s,R) sqcup (a,b,z,L,c), hole (z,L,c), forces cLz=(c,L,z). Certified: Q and abz,bzL.
7. (L,u,v,d,s) sqcup (b,R,c,a,z), hole (b,R,c), forces cRb=(c,R,b). Certified: Q and Rca,caz.
8. (L,u,v,d,s) sqcup (a,b,z,R,c), hole (z,R,c), forces cRz=(c,R,z). Certified: Q and abz,bzR.
9. (u,L,a,d,v) sqcup (c,z,b,R,s), hole (L,a,d), forces daL=(d,a,L). Certified: uLa,adv and czb,zbR,bRs.
10. (u,L,c,d,v) sqcup (a,b,z,R,s), hole (L,c,d), forces dcL=(d,c,L). Certified: uLc,cdv and abz,bzR,zRs.
Here adv,cdv,dvb,dvz are the accepted m=5 R536 inward turns.

We now apply accepted physical Mate-Fork rule R173 six times. In each pair below all unlisted turns are certified, and the two hole sets are {h,t} and {h,rev(t)}; therefore R173 forces rev(h).

F1. Proposals
(a,d,c,L,z) sqcup (v,u,b,R,s), holes {adc, ubR},
(c,d,a,L,z) sqcup (v,u,b,R,s), holes {cda, ubR}.
The mate holes adc/cda are reversals. Nonholes use dcL,cLz in the first rails and vub,bRs in the second. Hence R173 forces Rbu=(R,b,u).

F2. Proposals
(u,L,a,s,d) sqcup (c,R,b,v,z), holes {Las, bvz},
(u,L,a,s,d) sqcup (c,R,z,v,b), holes {Las, zvb}.
The mate holes bvz/zvb are reversals. Nonholes use uLa,asd and cRb,Rbv in the first proposal, cRz,Rzv in the second. Hence R173 forces saL=(s,a,L).

F3. Proposals
(c,d,v,z,L) sqcup (s,a,R,b,u), holes {vzL, saR},
(d,c,L,z,v) sqcup (s,a,R,b,u), holes {Lzv, saR}.
The mate holes vzL/Lzv are reversals. Nonholes use cdv,dvz and dcL,cLz, while the common second rail uses aRb,Rbu. Hence R173 forces Ras=(R,a,s).

F4. Proposals
(u,s,a,L,b) sqcup (R,c,d,v,z), holes {usa, Rcd},
(u,s,a,L,b) sqcup (d,c,R,z,v), holes {usa, dcR}.
The mate holes Rcd/dcR are reversals. The first rail uses saL,aLb; the second rails use cdv,dvz or cRz,Rzv. Hence R173 forces asu=(a,s,u).

F5. Proposals
(a,d,v,z,L) sqcup (c,R,b,u,s), holes {vzL, bus},
(d,a,L,z,v) sqcup (c,R,b,u,s), holes {Lzv, bus}.
The mate holes vzL/Lzv are reversals. Nonholes use adv,dvz or daL,aLz, while the second rail uses cRb,Rbu. Hence R173 forces sub=(s,u,b).

F6. Proposals
(s,a,L,b,u) sqcup (d,c,R,z,v), holes {Lbu, dcR},
(s,a,L,b,u) sqcup (R,c,d,v,z), holes {Lbu, Rcd}.
The mate holes dcR/Rcd are reversals. The first rail uses saL,aLb; the second rails use cRz,Rzv or cdv,dvz. Hence R173 forces ubL=(u,b,L).

FINAL COVER. The six forced turns concatenate as
P_6=(R,a,s,u,b,L),
whose consecutive turns are Ras, asu, sub, ubL. Accepted R536 gives cdv and dvz, so
P_4=(c,d,v,z)
is tight. Their supports are disjoint and together equal V(H)=X union {L,u,v,d,s,R}. Thus P_6 sqcup P_4 is a spanning two-cover, contradiction.

# R879 — Every nontrivial spanning three-cover carries a six-clause physical splice fan

## Statement
Let H be a finite Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament with pc(H)>2, and let H=A sqcup B sqcup C be a literal spanning three-cover in which A,B,C are nontrivial tight paths. For every ordered pair of distinct components, say A=(a_0,...,a_p) and B=(b_0,...,b_q) with p,q>=1, the literal spanning two-path proposal (a_0,...,a_p,b_0,...,b_q) sqcup C has complete uncertified-turn set exactly h_1=(a_{p-1},a_p,b_0) and h_2=(a_p,b_0,b_1). Hence at least one of h_1,h_2 is bad, and boundary antisymmetry forces the physical mate clause (b_0,a_p,a_{p-1}) tight OR (b_1,b_0,a_p) tight. Repeating this for all six ordered pairs among A,B,C gives six explicit two-hole physical mate clauses attached to the same literal three-cover.

## Hypotheses
H is finite Strong Level-(1) with pc(H)>2. H=A sqcup B sqcup C is a literal spanning three-cover and all three component paths have order at least two. Only boundary antisymmetry R3 is used.

## Scope
Order-free generic physical seam compiler. This is the R3-only core extracted from retired R453, with its optional smallest-counterexample/R168 specialization deliberately removed.

## Applicability
Use whenever a literal nontrivial spanning three-cover is already present and a complete physical two-hole splice clause is needed. In particular this is the intended reconstructible parent for the R834 signed-dimer three-cover seam theorem.

## Persistence
Retain the three literal component paths, each ordered component pair, the exact concatenated spanning proposal, and its complete two-hole set. The six proposals are alternative certificates built from the same graph-intrinsic component paths.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert that the six clauses contain a Mate-Cycle/Mate-Fork pair, that any two holes are complementary, or that one clause closes H. Does not currentize an arbitrary prescribed path and makes no smallest-counterexample rail-size claim.

## Proof
Fix an ordered pair A,B and leave C unchanged. Write A=(a_0,...,a_p), B=(b_0,...,b_q) with p,q>=1. In the concatenated path A*B=(a_0,...,a_p,b_0,...,b_q), every consecutive triple lying wholly in A or wholly in B is tight. The only new consecutive triples are h_1=(a_{p-1},a_p,b_0) and h_2=(a_p,b_0,b_1). Therefore (A*B) sqcup C is a spanning two-path proposal with complete hole set {h_1,h_2}. If both were tight, H would have a spanning two-cover, contradicting pc(H)>2. So at least one h_i is bad. By R3 the complete reversal of a bad ordered triple is tight, giving (b_0,a_p,a_{p-1}) OR (b_1,b_0,a_p). The same argument applies independently to each of the six ordered pairs A,B; A,C; B,A; B,C; C,A; C,B.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R879.md -->

# R880 — Every surviving synchronized order-three R24 frame has long rail parameter m at least six

## Statement
Retain the accepted synchronized transitive order-three frame R594 with Q=(q_0,...,q_m), m>=4, and the exhaustive aligned/crossed gate split R619. Then m>=6. Indeed m=4 is impossible in both gate phases by accepted R877. If m=5, the aligned phase is impossible by accepted R876 and the crossed phase is impossible by accepted R878. Therefore no synchronized transitive R24 frame exists for m in {4,5}; every surviving frame lies in the common long-core regime m>=6.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in the accepted R594 synchronized transitive order-three frame. Use accepted exhaustive gate split R619 and accepted finite-base closures R876,R877,R878.

## Scope
Noncircular finite-base parent theorem for O6/R24 reconstruction. It does not prove the m>=6 case and uses no R24,R5,R168,R169,R224,R533,R350,or generic R358.

## Applicability
Use immediately after R594. It eliminates all finite base branching from subsequent reasoning: the surviving order-three frame may be assumed m>=6 before introducing R810/R806, inward-anchor five-cell structure, or the crossed m=6 packet.

## Persistence
Retain the original R594 frame labels and the conclusion m>=6. The individual m=4 and m=5 phase certificates remain available as proof leaves but need not be carried as separate frontier cases.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not close any m>=6 frame. Does not assert the aligned phase is impossible for m>=6. Does not replace the detailed R876/R877/R878 certificates when their literal path orders or Mate-Fork ancestry are needed.

## Proof
By R594 the surviving order-three frame has m>=4. If m=4, accepted R877 gives a contradiction in both the aligned and crossed gate phases, so m is not 4. Suppose m=5. Accepted R619 gives the exhaustive dichotomy ALIGNED or CROSSED. In the aligned phase, accepted R876 exhibits an immediate literal spanning 6+4 two-cover, contradiction. In the crossed phase, accepted R878 derives ten one-hole cap turns, six physical Mate-Fork companions, and a final literal 6+4 two-cover, contradiction. Thus m is not 5. Therefore every surviving R594 frame has m>=6.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R880.md -->

# R881 — Every R24 failure reduces to one fixed order-eight pc=2 core coupled to a nonempty Hamilton middle rail

## Statement
Let H be a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample and suppose R24 fails: for some vertex z an exact two-cover H-z=P sqcup Q has a rail P of order at most three. Then, after the noncircular normalization of R594 and the finite-base exclusion R880, the unique surviving case has an order-three short rail, a transitive matching-height four-cell X, and Q=(q_0,...,q_m) with m>=6. Writing L=q_0, u=q_1, s=q_{m-1}, R=q_m, N=Q[2,m-2], and G_8=H[X union {L,u,s,R}], one has V(H)=V(G_8) disjoint-union V(N), N is a nonempty tight Hamilton path on its support, |V(G_8)|=8, and pc(G_8)=2. Every exact two-cover G_8=A sqcup B therefore gives a literal minimum spanning three-cover H=A sqcup B sqcup N. Moreover the aligned/crossed middle-gate split is entirely internal to G_8. Thus the whole unresolved content of R24 is a bounded eight-vertex exact-two-cover core coupled to one Hamilton middle rail of arbitrary positive order.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample and R24 fails through some singleton-deletion exact two-cover with a rail of order at most three. Use accepted R594, pending finite-base parent R880 once reviewed, and accepted R810.

## Scope
Noncircular O6 long-case entrance theorem. It packages the reconstructed front half, finite-base closure, and common bounded-core renormalization. No R24,R5,R168,R169,R224,R533,R350,or generic R358 is used.

## Applicability
Preferred startup theorem for the remaining O6 long case after fresh review. Work directly with the fixed order-eight pc=2 core G_8 and Hamilton middle rail N; ALIGNED/CROSSED is only an internal orientation choice in G_8. Use deeper R806 only when q_2,q_{m-2} must be moved into a ten-vertex bounded core.

## Persistence
Retain the original failed singleton-deletion certificate, normalized X,Q labels, m>=6, the physical decomposition H=G_8 disjoint-union N, pc(G_8)=2, the endpoint reverse stars, and the internal aligned/crossed gate classification. Exact G_8 two-cover representatives are not canonical.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not close the m>=6 case, assert G_8 Hamiltonian, prescribe endpoints of an exact G_8 two-cover, or make the middle rail N interact with the core automatically. Does not replace R594/R810 when their detailed certificates are needed.

## Proof
Apply R594 to the assumed R24 failure. The order-one and order-two short rails close immediately, so the surviving short rail has order three and yields the synchronized transitive matching-height frame X,Q with m>=4. Apply R880 to exclude m=4 and m=5; hence m>=6. Now apply R810 to this same R594 frame. With L=q_0,u=q_1,s=q_{m-1},R=q_m, N=Q[2,m-2], and G_8=H[X union {L,u,s,R}], R810 gives |G_8|=8, V(H)=V(G_8) disjoint-union V(N), N a nonempty tight Hamilton path, and pc(G_8)=2. It also records that every exact G_8 two-cover extends with N to a literal spanning three-cover and that the aligned/crossed gate split uses only vertices of G_8. These are exactly the claimed conclusions.

# R882 — c_X=2 shape D closes adjacent placements or forces a typed two-end mate clause

## Statement
Retain the accepted crossed R862 sigma_G(T)=0 inward-anchor five-cell frame with m>=6 and suppose the accepted R866 forest is c_X=2 shape D: one T rail consists of two Q blocks G_i-G_j with i<j, while the other has type X_L-G_k-X_R on the remaining Q block. Apply accepted R867. Outside its explicit Reverse-Ear outputs, adjacent Q-pair placements {i,j}={0,1} or {1,2} restore q_2,q_{m-2} to a literal spanning two-cover and are impossible in a counterexample. Hence the sole monotone residue is the nonadjacent skip G_0-G_2 together with X_L-G_1-X_R. Writing X_L=(x_1,x_2), X_R=(y_1,y_2) in their actual T orders, the untouched G_0-G_2 rail together with K=(q_2,x_1,x_2,G_1,y_1,y_2,q_{m-2}) is a literal spanning two-path proposal whose complete hole set is exactly {(q_2,x_1,x_2),(y_1,y_2,q_{m-2})}. Therefore the reverse literals A=(x_2,x_1,q_2) or B=(q_{m-2},y_2,y_1) form a physical mate clause. If X_L=G_3={a,c} and X_R=G_4={b,z}, accepted R649 and R523 make either realized branch a labelled Hamilton P4. If X_L=G_4 and X_R=G_3, accepted R649 and R542 make either realized branch an explicit two-witness R542-ready packet. Thus shape D has no quiet monotone residue: adjacent Q pairs close, while the unique skip placement forces a two-end clause whose realized branch is uniformly P4-type or uniformly R542-type according to the left/right X identity.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in the accepted crossed R862 sigma=0 frame; m>=6; accepted R866 shape D; accepted R867,R649,R3,R523,R542.

## Scope
Current-interface rebase of the accepted historical shape-D theorem R680. Noncircular crossed R24 restoration; pure literal restoration plus one physical two-hole clause. No R5,R168,R169,R224,R533,generic R358, payment, capture, or R436.

## Applicability
After R866 identifies shape D, discard adjacent Q-pair placements by literal Q restoration. In the unique G_0-G_2 skip placement, preserve the actual X_L-G_1-X_R order and use the two deleted inward anchors to obtain the displayed physical mate clause. The identity of X_L determines whether both branches are P4-type or R542-ready.

## Persistence
Retain the exact T rails, the physical Q-cell identities, actual orientations of X_L and X_R, the untouched G_0-G_2 rail, the two deleted anchors q_2,q_{m-2}, and the complete two-hole proposal K with both reverse clause literals.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert that shape D itself closes in the nonadjacent skip placement. Does not choose which mate-clause literal is tight. Does not infer payment, protected contact, long-path growth, or any consequence beyond the stated P4/R542 typing.

## Proof
Let v=q_2 and d=q_{m-2}. By accepted R867, outside its explicit Reverse-Ear outputs the Q-Q rail occurs in physical increasing order G_i-G_j. If (i,j)=(0,1), replace its selected G_0-G_1 transition by the old Q segment G_0,v,G_1 and then append d. The resulting path is exactly Q[0,m-2], hence tight for every m>=6. The other T rail X_L-G_2-X_R is untouched and tight. These two paths span H, contradiction. If (i,j)=(1,2), prepend v and restore d between G_1,G_2; the resulting path is Q[2,m], while X_L-G_0-X_R is untouched. Again H is two-covered. Thus only (i,j)=(0,2) can remain. Write the surviving source rails as G_0-G_2 and X_L-G_1-X_R, with X_L=(x_1,x_2) and X_R=(y_1,y_2) in their actual T orders. Consider K=(v,x_1,x_2,G_1,y_1,y_2,d). Inside X_L-G_1-X_R every turn is inherited from T. Prepending v creates exactly the endpoint turn h_L=(v,x_1,x_2), and appending d creates exactly h_R=(y_1,y_2,d); there are no other new turns, even when m=6 and G_1 is the singleton q_3, because the entire source subrail X_L-G_1-X_R remains untouched internally. The support of K together with the untouched G_0-G_2 rail is all of V(H). If h_L and h_R were both tight, these two paths would two-cover H. Hence by R3 at least one reverse A=(x_2,x_1,v) or B=(d,y_2,y_1) is tight. The tested dimers in A and B are exactly the reverse orientations of the two X blocks. R649 supplies an R542-ready fixed head polarity on either orientation of G_3={a,c} and fixed tail polarity on either orientation of G_4={b,z}. Suppose X_L=G_3 and X_R=G_4. Then A is a tail certificate on a reverse G_3 dimer, opposite its fixed head certificate, so R523 gives a labelled tight P4. Likewise B is a head certificate on a reverse G_4 dimer, opposite its fixed tail certificate, and R523 gives a labelled P4. Thus either clause branch is P4-type. If instead X_L=G_4 and X_R=G_3, then A has the same tail polarity as the fixed G_4 packet, with new witness v outside the R649 short carrier; it therefore supplies a two-witness R542 packet. Similarly B is same-head on the reverse G_3 dimer with new witness d outside its R649 carrier, so R542 applies. Thus either clause branch is R542-type. This exhausts shape D.

# R883 — Minimum inward-anchor five-cell recompletions introduce no new quiet species

## Statement
Retain the accepted crossed beyond-ten inward-anchor five-cell setting and let T be an exact two-cover of W=H-{q_2,q_{m-2}} in the minimum case sigma_G(T)=0. Then every such T compiles into one of the following already-named interfaces. (UT) If c_X(T)=1, T is exactly the accepted R865 specialization of the R511 unique-transition cell, with its dimer pure-C hard residue localized by the R550/R568 seam refinements. (P4/CLOSE) If c_X(T) is 2 or 3 and some X block is internal, accepted R868 gives a source-labelled Hamilton P4. In the remaining endpoint-X regimes, accepted R855 consumes shape A by literal closure or, only at m=6, a labelled inward P4. Accepted R856 consumes split-X shape C by literal closure, a labelled P4, or a physical one/two-hole reverse-X or facing-anchor clause whose realized branch is P4- or R542-ready. Pending-current-interface shape-D theorem R882 consumes the final same-rail endpoint-X shape D by literal closure for adjacent Q pairs or a physical two-end mate clause whose realized branch is uniformly P4-type or R542-ready. Consequently, once R882 is accepted, the sigma_G(T)=0 five-cell layer has no unnamed quiet combinatorial residue: every minimum recompletion is either an established unique-transition packet, already closes H, produces a labelled P4, or lands in an explicit source-decorated R542/mate-clause interface.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in the accepted crossed R862 frame with m>=6; T is an exact two-cover of W in the minimum case sigma_G(T)=0. Use accepted R865,R866,R868,R855,R856 and the current-interface shape-D rebase R882.

## Scope
Noncircular structural parent for the complete minimum five-cell layer. It is a classification/compilation theorem, not a new closure theorem. It packages existing accepted consumers and the current-interface shape-D rebase without adding payment, protected-contact, or path-growth claims.

## Applicability
Use immediately after detecting sigma_G(T)=0. Do not enumerate five-cell forests again. First apply R865. If c_X=1, enter the existing unique-transition machinery. Otherwise apply R868; only endpoint-X residues remain, and shapes A,C,D are consumed by R855,R856,R882 respectively.

## Persistence
Retain the exact deletion pair, T, the five source cells, sigma_G(T)=0, c_X(T), the R866 shape/regime label, and whichever named downstream packet is produced.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert that every minimum recompletion immediately two-covers H. Does not consume the resulting P4, R542 packet, or mate clause. Does not treat sigma_G(T)>0 or fragmented-X excess covers.

## Proof
Let T be a minimum inward-anchor five-cell recompletion, so sigma_G(T)=0. By accepted R865, c_X(T) is 1,2,or3. If c_X(T)=1, R865 itself proves that the contracted forest is P4 disjoint union P1 relative to the five source cells and that, relative to the full-Q R508 partition, T is exactly an R511 unique-transition packet with two physical X-dimer C-blocks. After R512/R513, the surviving both-bad dimer pure-C residues lie in the accepted R550/R568 refinements. This is the UT output and introduces no new five-cell species. Now suppose c_X(T) is 2 or3. Accepted R866 classifies the contracted two-rail forest into shapes A-F and the three regimes Internal-X, Same-rail endpoint-X, and Split-X. Accepted R868 proves that every Internal-X configuration, namely every c_X=3 shape and c_X=2 shape B, yields a source-labelled Hamilton P4. Outside that P4 branch, both X blocks are degree-one source/sink endcaps, so only shape A or D in the same-rail regime and shape C in the split-X regime remain. Accepted R855 consumes shape A: for m>=7 literal restoration gives a spanning two-cover, while at m=6 the only failed restoration seam reverses against the inward signed dimer to a labelled P4. Accepted R856 consumes shape C: every monotone configuration either closes, yields a labelled P4, or produces an explicit one/two-hole facing-anchor or reverse-X literal whose realized branch is P4- or R542-ready. Finally R882 consumes shape D: adjacent Q pairs restore to a spanning two-cover, and the unique G_0-G_2 skip gives a physical two-end mate clause whose realized literal is uniformly P4-type or uniformly R542-ready according to the left/right X identity. These cases exhaust c_X=1,2,3 and all six R866 shapes. Therefore no unnamed quiet minimum five-cell residue remains.

# R884 — A tight cross-end turn compiles directly to a two-ended deep seam packet

## Statement
Retain the accepted synchronized transitive R594 frame in the surviving long regime m>=6. Write L=q_0,u=q_1,v=q_2,d=q_{m-2},s=q_{m-1},R=q_m. Fix e in X such that (L,e,R) is tight. Let gamma be the M_R-partner of e and let {alpha,beta} be the other M_R edge, so X-{e}={alpha,beta,gamma}. Then J=(u,L,e,R,s) is a tight P5, and with T_1=(beta,alpha,gamma), T_2=(alpha,beta,gamma), each T_i together with Q[2,m-2] is a literal exact two-cover of the residue W=H-V(J). The residue is non-Hamiltonian. Moreover the following graph-intrinsic seam packet holds simultaneously. (LEFT) Either (L,u,gamma) is tight, or both (v,u,gamma,alpha) and (v,u,gamma,beta) are labelled tight P4s. (RIGHT) Either {alpha,beta,s,d} supports one of the labelled P4s (alpha,beta,s,d),(beta,alpha,s,d), or both (alpha,s,R) and (beta,s,R) are tight. (Q-LEFT) Either (L,u,d) is tight or (u,d,q_{m-3}) is tight. (Q-RIGHT) Either (v,s,R) is tight or (q_3,v,s) is tight. Thus every surviving tight cross-end orientation (L,e,R) directly yields a fixed two-ended role-sensitive packet: endpoint witness enrichment, labelled P4, or cross-depth inward witness. No intermediate residue theorem is needed as a consumer interface.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in accepted R594, with m>=6, and (L,e,R) tight for e in X. Use accepted R3,R4,R537,R594,R723,R849.

## Scope
Noncircular current-O6 parent theorem. It composes the accepted mathematics formerly split between retired R749 and active R859, but is proved directly from current active inputs and does not depend on either route theorem.

## Applicability
Whenever the synchronized transitive frame exposes a tight cross-end turn (q_0,e,q_m), use this theorem directly. Do not first route through retired R749. The output preserves the exact e,gamma,alpha,beta labels, both residue trimers, both endpoint dimers, and the inward coordinates v,d.

## Persistence
Retain e, its M_R partner gamma, the other M_R edge {alpha,beta}, the P5 J, the two literal residue covers T_1 plus Q[2,m-2] and T_2 plus Q[2,m-2], and all four seam alternatives simultaneously.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert which seam alternative occurs, does not itself consume the resulting P4 or witness packet, and makes no payment, capture, protected-contact, Reverse-Ear, or path-growth claim.

## Proof
Write X-{e}={alpha,beta,gamma}, where gamma is the M_R-partner of e and {alpha,beta} is the other M_R edge. Since X is the accepted transitive matching-height cell of R594, accepted R537 gives both T_1=(beta,alpha,gamma) and T_2=(alpha,beta,gamma) as tight trimers. Also R594 gives (u,L,e) and (e,R,s) tight, while (L,e,R) is tight by hypothesis, so J=(u,L,e,R,s) is a tight P5. Its complementary vertex set is W=(X-{e}) union Q[2,m-2]. For each i, T_i and Q[2,m-2] are vertex-disjoint tight paths spanning W, so they form a literal exact two-cover of W. If W had a tight Hamilton path P, then P together with J would be a spanning two-cover of H, contrary to the smallest-counterexample property R4. Hence W is non-Hamiltonian.

Fix i and write T_i=(p_0,p_1,p_2), so p_2=gamma. T_i cannot be concatenated immediately before J. If both seam turns (p_1,p_2,u) and (p_2,u,L) were tight, then T_i followed by J would be one tight path and Q[2,m-2] the other, spanning H. Therefore at least one seam is bad, and R3 gives at least one reverse (u,p_2,p_1) or (L,u,p_2) tight. For T_1 this is (u,gamma,alpha) or (L,u,gamma); for T_2 it is (u,gamma,beta) or (L,u,gamma). Thus either (L,u,gamma) is tight, or both (u,gamma,alpha) and (u,gamma,beta) are tight. Accepted R723 gives (v,u,gamma) tight, so in the latter case both (v,u,gamma,alpha) and (v,u,gamma,beta) are labelled tight P4s. This proves LEFT.

Likewise T_i cannot be concatenated immediately after J. If both (R,s,p_0) and (s,p_0,p_1) were tight, then J followed by T_i together with Q[2,m-2] would two-cover H. Hence R3 gives at least one of (p_0,s,R) and (p_1,p_0,s). For T_1 this is (beta,s,R) or (alpha,beta,s); for T_2 it is (alpha,s,R) or (beta,alpha,s). If (beta,s,R) is absent, then (alpha,beta,s) is tight, and R723 gives (beta,s,d), so (alpha,beta,s,d) is a labelled P4. If (alpha,s,R) is absent, then (beta,alpha,s) is tight, and R723 gives (alpha,s,d), so (beta,alpha,s,d) is a labelled P4. Therefore either one of those P4s exists or both (alpha,s,R) and (beta,s,R) are tight. This proves RIGHT.

Finally use the other residue rail A=Q[2,m-2]=(v,q_3,...,d), which is nontrivial because m>=6. A cannot precede J. If both (q_{m-3},d,u) and (d,u,L) were tight, A followed by J together with T_i would two-cover H. Hence R3 gives (u,d,q_{m-3}) or (L,u,d). A also cannot follow J. If both (R,s,v) and (s,v,q_3) were tight, J followed by A together with T_i would two-cover H, so R3 gives (v,s,R) or (q_3,v,s). These conclusions are independent of i and coexist with LEFT and RIGHT. Accepted R849 identifies the second alternatives as cross-depth witness enrichments on the inward signed dimers. No intermediate R749 or R859 theorem has been used.
