# R885 — Fragmented-X five-cell excess has a bounded separator budget

## Statement
Retain the accepted crossed beyond-ten inward-anchor five-cell frame R862 with W=H-{q_2,q_{m-2}}, source cells G_0=Q[0,1], G_1=Q[3,m-3], G_2=Q[m-1,m], G_3={a,c}, G_4={b,z}, and let T be any exact two-cover of W. Let f(T) be the number of X cells among G_3,G_4 that are fragmented in T, meaning that their two vertices do not form one contiguous T-block; thus f(T) is in {0,1,2}. Let b_i(T) be the number of maximal nonempty T-blocks lying in G_i. Then at least one of the following holds. (P4) An unfragmented X cell is placed away from its forced path end and accepted R837 yields a source-labelled tight Hamilton P4. (RE) Comparing a T-rail with Q by accepted R435 yields an explicit reversed old Q-state, reverse trimer/contact, or vertex-simple tight cycle. (BOUNDED) Neither geometric output occurs. Then every unfragmented G_4 block is initial on its T-rail, every unfragmented G_3 block is terminal, and the Q vertices encountered on each T-rail occur in strictly increasing Q-index order. Moreover b_3+b_4=2+f(T) and b_0+b_1+b_2<=6+2f(T). Consequently sum_i b_i<=8+3f(T). Since R862 gives t_G(T)=3+sigma_G(T), equivalently sum_i b_i=5+sigma_G(T), one has sigma_G(T)<=3+3f(T) and t_G(T)<=6+3f(T). In particular the contracted five-cell block forest has at most 8 blocks when f=0, at most 11 when f=1, and at most 14 when f=2. If Y=G_0 union G_1 union G_2 and r_Y is the number of maximal Y-blocks of T, then r_Y<=2+2f(T). Writing p=e_T(X) and q=e_T(X,Y) as in accepted R535, one has r_Y=p+q-2, hence p+q<=4+2f(T), and c_x=r_Y+1-d_Y(x)<=3+2f(T) for every x in X. In the exactly-one-fragmented case f(T)=1 there is a sharp dichotomy: either some x in X has c_x<=3, or (p,q)=(2,4) and c_x=4 for all four x. Thus the missing R535 high-interleaving floor is completely localized on f=1: if c_x>=4 for every x, the unique coarse parameter type is (2,4). Fragmented-X excess is therefore an m-independent bounded separator problem, with the one-fragmented and two-fragmented regimes having sharply different finite budgets, while f=0 recovers the numerical bound of R870.

## Hypotheses
Accepted crossed R862 inward-anchor five-cell frame and one exact two-cover T of W. Use accepted R837 for endcap placement of any contiguous X dimer, accepted Reverse Ear R435 for Q-contact monotonicity outside its explicit outputs, and accepted R535 for the optional X/Y fragmentation corollary.

## Scope
Noncircular crossed R24/O6 five-cell compression for arbitrary sigma_G(T), including fragmented X dimers. No payment, capture, floor steering, R436, R5, R168, R169, R224, R533, R350, generic R358, finite m-enumeration, or computation.

## Applicability
Use at the start of the previously unnamed fragmented-X excess branch. Split first by f=1 versus f=2. For f=1, either retain a named marker x with c_x<=3, or enter the unique extremal coarse type (p,q)=(2,4) with all c_x=4; also sigma<=6, t_G<=9 and there are at most 11 cell blocks. For f=2, sigma<=9, t_G<=12 and there are at most 14 cell blocks. Do not assume c_x>=4: on f=1 this theorem turns its failure into an explicit low-fragment marker and its validity into one unique R535 parameter type.

## Persistence
Retain T, the five physical source cells, f(T), all cell-block counts b_i, any R837 P4 or R435 output, and in the bounded branch the increasing Q-contact order together with the X/Y counts p,q,r_Y and d_Y(x),c_x when used.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not classify or close the f=1 or f=2 block forests. Does not prove c_x>=4. Does not assert that the 13 R535 high-interleaving words apply without their stated hypothesis. In f=1 it proves only the low-marker versus unique extremal-parameter dichotomy, not closure of either side. Does not turn a labelled P4 or Reverse-Ear output into closure by itself. The block bounds are upper bounds and do not claim every pattern is realizable.

## Proof
Let f=f(T). First suppose an unfragmented G_3 or G_4 occurs away from the path end prescribed by accepted R837. Then R837 gives the stated labelled P4, so assume this does not happen. Thus every intact G_4 block is initial and every intact G_3 block is terminal. Apply accepted Reverse Ear R435 to each T-rail K against the original path Q. If some pair of consecutive Q-contacts on K occurs in reverse Q-order, retain the corresponding R435 reversed state, reverse trimer/contact, or cycle. Hence in the remaining branch all Q contacts on each T-rail occur in increasing Q-index order.

For i=0,1,2, G_i is a Q-index interval. On a fixed T-rail, after deleting the fragmented-X singleton vertices, the Q contacts belonging to G_i form at most one contiguous G_i block: a lower-index Q cell cannot occur between two G_i contacts and a higher-index Q cell cannot be followed by a return to G_i because Q-contact order is increasing. Thus, across two rails, there are at most six baseline Q-cell blocks. Exactly 2f X vertices belong to fragmented X cells, and each such singleton occurrence can split at most one existing Q-cell block into two. Intact X dimers are endcaps in the present no-P4 branch and split none. Therefore b_0+b_1+b_2<=6+2f.

Each X cell has two vertices. If it is intact it contributes one cell block; if fragmented its two vertices contribute two singleton cell blocks. Hence b_3+b_4=2+f, and B:=sum_{i=0}^4 b_i<=8+3f. Along two nonempty T-rails, the number t_G(T) of selected transitions between distinct source cells is exactly B-2. Accepted R862 gives t_G(T)=3+sigma_G(T), so B=5+sigma_G(T). Therefore sigma_G(T)<=3+3f and t_G(T)<=6+3f. The displayed bounds 8,11,14 on the contracted block forest are immediate for f=0,1,2.

Now put Y=G_0 union G_1 union G_2. In the same monotone/endcap branch, deleting X from each T-rail leaves at most one Y-run, except that each of the 2f fragmented-X singleton occurrences can separate one additional Y-run. Hence r_Y:=c(T[Y])<=2+2f. Let p=e_T(X) and q=e_T(X,Y). Since T is a spanning two-path forest on X union Y with |X|=4, it has |X|+|Y|-2 edges, of which p+q are incident with X and the rest lie in Y. Therefore r_Y=|Y|-e_T(Y)=p+q-2. Thus p+q<=4+2f. Accepted R535 says c_x=p+q-d_Y(x)-1=r_Y+1-d_Y(x), so c_x<=3+2f for every x.

Finally take f=1. The crossed frame has X P4-free, so accepted R535 gives p<=2. Also p+q<=6 as just proved. Hence the R535 sum identity gives sum_x c_x=4p+3q-4=3(p+q)+p-4<=16. If some c_x<4, integrality gives a named x with c_x<=3. Otherwise all four c_x>=4, so their sum is at least 16. Equality must then hold throughout: sum_x c_x=16, p+q=6 and p=2. Thus q=4, and equality in the four lower bounds forces c_x=4 for every x. This is exactly the claimed f=1 dichotomy.

# R886 — A single fragmented X dimer is a double low-component marker pair

## Statement
Retain the accepted crossed beyond-ten inward-anchor five-cell frame and the BOUNDED branch of accepted R885. Suppose exactly one middle-gate X cell is fragmented, f(T)=1. Let F={x,x'} be that fragmented X cell and I the other, contiguous X cell. Then BOTH fragmented markers satisfy c_x=c(T[Y union {x}])<=3 and c_{x'}<=3, where Y=G_0 union G_1 union G_2. Moreover there is an exact binary refinement. (LOW2) At least one of x,x' has c<=2; equivalently r_Y<=3. (MAX3) Otherwise c_x=c_{x'}=3; equivalently r_Y=4. In MAX3 necessarily p=e_T(X)=1, q=e_T(X,Y)=5, both fragmented markers have d_Y=2, and the two intact-cell vertices have Y-degrees 1 and 0 in some order. Hence the full degree/c-value multisets are d_Y={2,2,1,0} and c={3,3,4,5}, with the two 3s exactly on the fragmented cell. Furthermore MAX3 has only three contracted X/Y rail skeletons. Contract each of the four maximal Y-runs to a symbol Y, keep the two vertices of I as the consecutive endcap block II, and keep the two fragmented markers individually as F. Up to swapping the two rails, reversing either displayed rail, interchanging the two fragmented labels, and reversing the internal order of I, the skeleton is exactly one of: (M0) II-Y | Y-F-Y-F-Y; (M1) II-Y-F-Y | Y-F-Y; (M2) II-Y-F-Y-F-Y | Y. Equivalently, the rail containing the intact endcap contains t=0,1,2 fragmented markers, and this integer t completely determines the coarse skeleton. In particular the all-high hypothesis c_y>=4 for every y in X is impossible for f=1, so the R535 13-word high-interleaving classification never applies in the exactly-one-fragmented regime. Also, if p=2 then necessarily q<=3 and r_Y<=3, hence p=2 lies in LOW2.

## Hypotheses
Accepted R885 BOUNDED branch with f(T)=1 in the crossed R594/R862 frame; accepted R837 endcap placement for the unique contiguous middle-gate X cell; accepted R535 notation and P4-free bound p<=2.

## Scope
Noncircular crossed R24/O6 sharpening of the exactly-one-fragmented five-cell excess branch. Pure path-forest/endcap geometry after R885; no payment, capture, R436, R5, R168, R169, R224, R533, R350, generic R358, or computation.

## Applicability
Use immediately after R885 when f=1. Split only into LOW2, equivalently r_Y<=3, and MAX3, equivalently r_Y=4 with p=1,q=5 and both fragmented markers c=3. MAX3 is already completely coarse-normalized to M0/M1/M2 according to how many fragmented markers lie on the intact-endcap rail. Do not use the R535 all-high 13-word classification in f=1. A second X-X edge p=2 is automatically confined to LOW2.

## Persistence
Retain T, F={x,x'}, the intact R837 endcap I, the residual forest T-I, both c-values, and the LOW2/MAX3 label. In MAX3 retain p=1,q=5,r_Y=4, d_Y=2 on both fragmented markers, {1,0} on I, and the M0/M1/M2 contracted skeleton with actual rail assignment and marker labels before quotienting symmetries.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not close LOW2 or any of M0/M1/M2, identify which source Q-cell contributes each Y-run, or assert every coarse MAX3 skeleton is realizable in the Strong frame. Does not strengthen f=2.

## Proof
Let F={x,x'} be the fragmented middle-gate cell and I the unique intact middle-gate cell. In the BOUNDED branch of accepted R885 no R837 labelled-P4 output occurs, so accepted R837 places I as an actual endcap block of its T-rail: G_4 is initial when intact, and G_3 is terminal when intact. Put T'=T-I and let k=c(T') be its number of nonempty path components. Endcap deletion cannot split a rail, so k is either 1 or 2.

Fix x in F. Since B_x=Y union {x}=W-(I union {x'}), one has T[B_x]=T'-x'. For any vertex w of a path forest, deleting w changes the number of nonempty components by deg(w)-1: an isolated singleton removes one component, an endpoint leaves the count unchanged, and an internal degree-two vertex splits one component into two. Therefore

  c_x = k + deg_{T'}(x') - 1,
  c_{x'} = k + deg_{T'}(x) - 1.

Because k<=2 and every path-forest degree is at most two, both c_x and c_{x'} are at most three. This immediately kills the all-high R535 hypothesis in f=1.

Suppose neither fragmented marker is LOW2. Then c_x=c_{x'}=3. The displayed identities force k=2 and deg_{T'}(x)=deg_{T'}(x')=2. In particular neither fragmented marker is adjacent in T to the deleted endcap I, because such an adjacency would disappear in T' and leave its T'-degree at most one. The fragmented markers are not adjacent to each other by definition of fragmentation. Hence both of their two T-neighbors lie in Y, so d_Y(x)=d_Y(x')=2. Also there is no cross-cell X-X edge. Thus the only selected X-X edge is the intact-cell edge, giving p=1. Since k=2, the intact endcap rail was nontrivial before deletion, so its unique boundary edge leaving I exists. That edge cannot go to F, as just shown, and therefore goes to Y. Hence the two intact-cell vertices have total Y-degree exactly one, with degrees {1,0}. Consequently q=sum_{y in X} d_Y(y)=2+2+1=5, and accepted R535 gives r_Y=p+q-2=1+5-2=4. The pointwise identity c_y=r_Y+1-d_Y(y)=5-d_Y(y) gives c-multiset {3,3,4,5}, with the two 3s exactly on F. This is MAX3.

Conversely suppose r_Y=4. The intact cell contributes an X-X edge, so p>=1; accepted R594/R535 gives p<=2. If p=2, the second X-X edge must be cross-cell, incident with some fragmented marker f. Then d_Y(f)<=1. But the first part gives c_f<=3, while r_Y=q in the p=2 case, so q+1-d_Y(f)=c_f<=3 and hence q<=3, contradicting r_Y=q=4. Therefore p=1, so q=5. Since both fragmented c-values are at most three, c=5-d_Y forces d_Y=2 on each fragmented marker. The intact vertices then contribute the remaining one Y-degree, giving {1,0}; hence both fragmented c-values are exactly three. Thus r_Y=4 implies MAX3.

It follows immediately that MAX3 is equivalent to r_Y=4. Since R885 gives r_Y<=4, failure of MAX3 is equivalent to r_Y<=3; and because both fragmented c-values are at most three, failure of MAX3 is also equivalent to at least one of them being at most two. This proves the LOW2 equivalence. The preceding p=2 argument also proves directly that p=2 forces q<=3 and r_Y=q<=3.

It remains to classify the coarse MAX3 skeleton. Contract each maximal Y-run to one vertex labelled Y, while keeping the four X vertices. By maximality of the Y-runs there are no Y-Y edges in this contracted forest. In MAX3 the only X-X edge is the intact dimer I, exactly one vertex of I has one Y-neighbor and the other has none, and each fragmented marker has degree two with both neighbors in Y. Therefore the component containing I begins, up to reversal, with the endcap segment II-Y. Thereafter every fragmented marker that lies on this component is an internal separator Y-F-Y. The other component contains the remaining fragmented markers, each likewise internal, and therefore begins and ends in Y (or is a single isolated Y if it contains no fragmented marker). If t is the number of fragmented markers on the I-component, then t is 0,1,or2. The I-component uses exactly t+1 of the four Y-runs, while the other component uses the remaining 3-t Y-runs and 2-t fragmented markers. Hence, up to rail swapping, rail reversal, interchange of fragmented labels, and reversal of the two vertices of I, the three and only three skeletons are

  M0: II-Y | Y-F-Y-F-Y,
  M1: II-Y-F-Y | Y-F-Y,
  M2: II-Y-F-Y-F-Y | Y.

Conversely each possible t gives exactly the displayed path-forest skeleton. This is only a coarse X/Y classification and does not assert source-Q-cell realizability.

Therefore the exactly-one-fragmented branch has the exact LOW2/MAX3 dichotomy, and the sole MAX3 face has only the three displayed contracted rail skeletons.

# R887 — Boundary tournaments are line-graph comparison orientations; edge-orderability is exactly acyclicity

## Statement
Let H be a finite Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament on vertex set V and use boundary antisymmetry. Define the comparison orientation Gamma(H) on the vertex set E(K_V) as follows: whenever e={u,v} and f={v,w} are distinct incident edges of K_V, orient the line-graph edge e->f exactly when the ordered turn (u,v,w) is tight. Then: (1) Gamma(H) is a well-defined orientation of the full line graph L(K_V). (2) A vertex-simple sequence P=(v_0,...,v_k) is a tight path in H iff its consecutive ordinary edges e_i={v_{i-1},v_i} satisfy e_1->e_2->...->e_k in Gamma(H). Thus tight paths are precisely the directed line-graph edge chains whose underlying K_V walk is vertex-simple. (3) H is representable by a global total order < on E(K_V), with (u,v,w) tight iff {u,v}<{v,w}, iff Gamma(H) is acyclic. In the acyclic case any topological ordering of Gamma(H) is such an edge order. (4) If Gamma(H) is cyclic, let C be a shortest directed cycle. C is chordless in L(K_V). If |C|=3, its three ordinary edges are either a star {va,vb,vc}, giving a directed 3-cycle a->_{T_v}b->_{T_v}c->_{T_v}a in the local middle-v tournament, or the three edges of an ordinary triangle, giving all three cyclic turns tight. If |C|=r>=4, the edges of C are exactly the edges of a simple ordinary r-cycle (v_0v_1,v_1v_2,...,v_{r-1}v_0), and the directed cycle orientation says every cyclic consecutive turn (v_i,v_{i+1},v_{i+2}) is tight (indices mod r). Hence every failure of edge-orderability has a minimal holonomy certificate of star-triangle type or vertex-simple cyclic-turn type.

## Hypotheses
H is finite and satisfies accepted exact complete-reversal antisymmetry R3. No smallest-counterexample, path-cover, R24, deletion, gate, capture, payment, or order assumption is used.

## Scope
Order-free representation and integrability theorem. It identifies the ternary tight-turn relation with an orientation of L(K_V), characterizes the edge-ordered subclass by acyclicity, and classifies shortest comparison cycles.

## Applicability
Use as a new front door for global arguments. The acyclic branch is exactly ordinary edge-ordered complete-graph mathematics. In the cyclic branch, choose a shortest comparison cycle and retain either a local star directed triangle or a vertex-simple cyclic tight-turn certificate. This gives a decomposition orthogonal to aligned/crossed gate analysis.

## Persistence
Retain Gamma(H), the ordinary-edge vertex corresponding to each line-graph vertex, the exact arc/turn dictionary, and for a shortest directed cycle its ordered edge list and induced star/ordinary-cycle support.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not prove the acyclic/edge-ordered class has path-cover number at most two. Does not claim a local star directed triangle or a tight cycle by itself closes a smallest counterexample. A directed path in Gamma(H) may correspond to an ordinary trail with repeated original vertices; tight-path equivalence requires the stated vertex-simplicity condition.

## Proof
For each unordered ordinary edge e={u,v} of K_V create one vertex of Gamma. Two such vertices are adjacent exactly when the ordinary edges meet, so the underlying graph is L(K_V). If e={u,v} and f={v,w}, the two possible directions e->f and f->e correspond respectively to (u,v,w) and (w,v,u). Accepted R3 says exactly one of this complete-reversal pair is tight, so exactly one line-graph direction is present. This proves (1).

For P=(v_0,...,v_k), put e_i={v_{i-1},v_i}. The line-graph arc e_i->e_{i+1} is, by definition, equivalent to tightness of (v_{i-1},v_i,v_{i+1}). Therefore every consecutive triple of P is tight iff every consecutive comparison arc is directed forward. Adding the stipulated vertex-simplicity of P gives (2).

If a total edge order < realizes H, every arc e->f of Gamma points from the earlier edge to the later edge, so Gamma has no directed cycle. Conversely, suppose Gamma is acyclic. Take any topological total ordering < of its vertices E(K_V). For every distinct u,v,w, the incident edges e={u,v}, f={v,w} are adjacent in Gamma, and e->f iff (u,v,w) is tight. A topological order places e<f exactly in that case. Hence < reproduces every tight turn of H. This proves (3).

Now suppose Gamma has a directed cycle and choose one C=e_0->e_1->...->e_{r-1}->e_0 of minimum length. If two nonconsecutive vertices e_i,e_j of C were adjacent in L(K_V), their line-graph edge has one orientation. If e_i->e_j, that chord together with the directed segment from e_j forward to e_i gives a shorter directed cycle; if e_j->e_i, the complementary directed segment from e_i forward to e_j plus the chord does. Thus C is chordless.

For r=3, three pairwise incident 2-subsets are either the three edges of one ordinary triangle or three edges sharing one common ordinary vertex v. In the star case, writing them va,vb,vc in cyclic line-graph order gives (a,v,b),(b,v,c),(c,v,a) tight. In the ordinary-triangle case, cyclically label the original vertices a,b,c so the comparison edges are ab->bc->ca->ab; then (a,b,c),(b,c,a),(c,a,b) are tight.

For r>=4, chordlessness means nonconsecutive ordinary edges e_i,e_j are disjoint, while consecutive ones meet. Put v_i=e_{i-1} cap e_i (indices mod r). Nonconsecutive-disjointness forces the v_i to be distinct and e_i={v_i,v_{i+1}}. Hence the e_i are exactly the edges of the simple ordinary cycle v_0v_1...v_{r-1}v_0. Finally e_i->e_{i+1} is equivalent to (v_i,v_{i+1},v_{i+2}) tight for every i. This proves (4).

# R893 — Foundational fully directed hypergraph and boundary-tournament vocabulary

## Statement
A fully directed hypergraph has edges that are ordered lists of distinct vertices. An r-graph is an r-uniform hypergraph, and an r-digraph is an r-uniform fully directed hypergraph. For k<=r!, a k-orientation of an r-graph G is an r-digraph G' on the same vertex set such that each edge e of G has exactly k orderings appearing as edges of G'. An (r,k)-tournament is a k-orientation of the complete r-graph. An interval in a list is a consecutive sublist; an r-interval has size r. A directed tight path is an r-digraph whose vertices admit a linear ordering in which every r-interval is an edge; a directed tight cycle is defined analogously using a cyclic ordering. An r-uniform fully directed hypergraph G is a boundary tournament if for every ordered (r-2)-tuple (v_1,...,v_{r-2}) of distinct vertices and distinct u,w outside it, exactly one of (u,v_1,...,v_{r-2},w) and (w,v_1,...,v_{r-2},u) is an edge. Hence every r-uniform boundary tournament is an (r,r!/2)-tournament. An edge-ordered hypergraph is a hypergraph whose edge set is linearly ordered. A monotone path in an edge-ordered r-uniform hypergraph is a tight-style vertex sequence v_1...v_k whose consecutive r-edges occur in increasing order in the edge ordering. The altitude alt(H) is the maximum number of vertices in a monotone path of H.

## Hypotheses
Definitions transcribed and normalized from the attached manuscript sources.

## Scope
General directed-hypergraph terminology and the boundary-tournament terminology motivating this project.

## Applicability
Canonical vocabulary layer for the project. In the present problem r=3.

## Persistence
Durable foundational terminology.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Historical Level nomenclature is not part of these source definitions.

## Proof
The first clauses of R893 are definitions, so the only derived assertion needing proof is: every r-uniform boundary tournament is an (r,r!/2)-tournament.

Fix an underlying r-element vertex set e. It has exactly r! linear orderings. For any ordering

    (u,v1,...,v_{r-2},w),

define its mate by swapping the first and last entries while leaving the ordered middle tuple fixed:

    (w,v1,...,v_{r-2},u).

This operation is an involution and has no fixed point because u and w are distinct. Hence the r! orderings of e split into exactly r!/2 disjoint two-element pairs.

By the defining boundary-tournament condition, for every ordered middle tuple (v1,...,v_{r-2}) and the two remaining distinct endpoints u,w, exactly one member of the corresponding pair is an edge. Therefore exactly one ordering is selected from each of the r!/2 pairs. Thus e has exactly r!/2 directed orderings as edges.

Since e was arbitrary, the fully directed hypergraph is a k-orientation of the complete r-graph with k=r!/2, i.e. an (r,r!/2)-tournament. The remaining terminology in R893 is definitional and requires no further derivation.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R893.md -->

# R894 — Both fragmented X dimers force a low marker or a three-skeleton fully alternating face

## Statement
Retain the accepted crossed beyond-ten inward-anchor five-cell frame and the BOUNDED branch of accepted R885. Suppose both middle-gate X cells are fragmented, f(T)=2. Put Y=G_0 union G_1 union G_2, p=e_T(X), q=e_T(X,Y), r_Y=c(T[Y]), and c_x=c(T[Y union {x}]) as in R535. Then exactly one of the following two regimes holds. (LOW4) Some x in X has c_x<=4; equivalently r_Y<=5. (MAX5) r_Y=6; equivalently (p,q)=(0,8); equivalently c_x=5 for every x in X. In MAX5 every X vertex has d_Y(x)=2, there is no selected X-X edge, and every X vertex is an internal separator between two Y-runs. After contracting each maximal Y-run to Y and retaining the four X vertices individually, the two T-rails have, up to swapping the rails, reversing either rail, and relabelling X vertices, exactly one of three coarse skeletons: (N0) Y | Y-X-Y-X-Y-X-Y-X-Y; (N1) Y-X-Y | Y-X-Y-X-Y-X-Y; (N2) Y-X-Y-X-Y | Y-X-Y-X-Y. Thus the fully fragmented branch has no diffuse all-high region: outside a named c<=4 marker it collapses to one extremal parameter point and three alternating X/Y skeletons.

## Hypotheses
Accepted R885 BOUNDED branch with f(T)=2 in the crossed R594/R862 frame. Use accepted R535 notation/identities and the fact that T is a spanning two-path forest, hence every X vertex has selected degree at most two.

## Scope
Noncircular crossed R24/O6 sharpening of the both-fragmented five-cell excess branch. Pure two-path-forest arithmetic and maximal-run geometry; no payment, capture, R436, R5, R168, R169, R224, R533, R350, generic R358, or computation.

## Applicability
Use immediately after R885 when f=2. Split only into LOW4, where a concrete marker x has c(T[Y union {x}])<=4, and MAX5, where p=0,q=8,r_Y=6 and the entire coarse forest is one of N0,N1,N2. In MAX5 there are no X-X selected adjacencies at all, so all four distinguished vertices are pure Y-separators.

## Persistence
Retain T, all four X labels and physical cell memberships, p,q,r_Y,d_Y,c_x, the LOW4 witness when present, and in MAX5 the actual rail assignment and order of the four X labels before quotienting to N0/N1/N2.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not close LOW4 or any MAX5 skeleton, assign the six Y-runs to the source Q-cells G_0,G_1,G_2, or assert every coarse MAX5 skeleton is realizable in the Strong frame. The N0/N1/N2 quotient forgets X labels and source-Q-cell labels. Does not consume any labelled P4 or Reverse-Ear output excluded by the R885 BOUNDED branch.

## Proof
Work in the BOUNDED branch of accepted R885 with f(T)=2. Put X={a,b,c,z} and Y=G_0 union G_1 union G_2. Accepted R885 gives r_Y<=2+2f=6 and the exact identity r_Y=p+q-2. Because T is a two-path forest, every vertex of X has selected T-degree at most two. Summing those four degrees gives the elementary budget 2p+q=sum_{x in X}deg_T(x)<=8.

First suppose r_Y=6. Then p+q=8. Combining this with 2p+q<=8 gives p=0 and q=8. Since q=sum_x d_Y(x)=8 and every d_Y(x)<=deg_T(x)<=2, every x in X has d_Y(x)=2. The R535 pointwise identity gives c_x=r_Y+1-d_Y(x)=7-2=5 for all four x. Thus r_Y=6 implies the claimed MAX5 parameter point. Conversely (p,q)=(0,8) gives r_Y=6 immediately, and the same degree sum forces d_Y(x)=2 and hence c_x=5 for every x.

Now suppose instead that no marker is LOW4, so c_x>=5 for every x. Accepted R535 gives sum_x c_x=4p+3q-4. The degree budget implies q<=8-2p, hence sum_x c_x<=4p+3(8-2p)-4=20-2p<=20. But four values each at least five have sum at least twenty. Equality is therefore forced throughout: p=0, q=8, and sum_x c_x=20, so every c_x=5. By the first paragraph this is exactly r_Y=6. Therefore failure of MAX5 is equivalent to r_Y<=5 and forces at least one x with c_x<=4. Conversely a marker with c_x<=4 cannot occur when r_Y=6, because the r_Y=6 face has all c_x=5. This proves the exact LOW4/MAX5 dichotomy and the stated equivalences.

It remains to classify the coarse MAX5 forest. There p=0 and every x in X has d_Y(x)=deg_T(x)=2. Hence no two X vertices are adjacent in T, every X vertex is internal on its rail, and both of its neighbors lie in Y. Contract each maximal Y-run to one symbol Y. Each rail therefore alternates Y-X-Y-X-...-Y and starts and ends in Y. There are four X symbols total and r_Y=6 Y-runs total. If one rail contains t X symbols, it contains t+1 Y symbols, while the other contains 4-t X symbols and 5-t Y symbols. Up to swapping rails we may take t=0,1,2. These give exactly N0: Y | Y-X-Y-X-Y-X-Y-X-Y; N1: Y-X-Y | Y-X-Y-X-Y-X-Y; and N2: Y-X-Y-X-Y | Y-X-Y-X-Y. Reversal and X-label permutations create no further coarse species. This classification does not assert realizability after restoring the physical X and Q-cell labels.

# R895 — Noninsertable vertices in an edge-ordered path have canonical pure reverse-middle barrier gaps

## Statement
Let G be an edge-ordered graph and let Q=(q_0,...,q_m), m>=1, be an increasing path. Let x be a vertex outside Q adjacent to every q_i. For 0<=i<=m-1, call the gap i right-feasible if either i=m-1 or the edge xq_{i+1} precedes q_{i+1}q_{i+2}; call it left-feasible if either i=0 or q_{i-1}q_i precedes q_i x. Assume that inserting x between q_i and q_{i+1} never gives an increasing path, for any i. Then some gap is simultaneously left- and right-feasible, and at every such gap the middle spoke pair is reversed: xq_{i+1} precedes xq_i. In particular, if beta(x) is the least right-feasible gap, then beta(x) is also left-feasible and xq_{beta(x)+1}<xq_{beta(x)}. Moreover, for two such noninsertable vertices x,y, if beta(x)<beta(y), then at the rail vertex q_{beta(x)+1} one has xq_{beta(x)+1}<q_{beta(x)+1}q_{beta(x)+2}<yq_{beta(x)+1}; consequently the ordered turn (x,q_{beta(x)+1},y) is tight in the boundary tournament induced by the edge order. Thus any family of noninsertable exterior vertices carries a canonical barrier preorder, with strict barrier separation witnessed by a graph-intrinsic cross turn.

## Hypotheses
A total order on the edges; Q is an increasing path; x (and y for the comparison clause) is adjacent to every Q vertex; no literal insertion of the vertex into an internal gap of the displayed Q order is increasing. The final tight-turn interpretation uses the standard edge-order boundary relation (u,v,w) tight iff uv precedes vw.

## Scope
Pure edge-ordered path insertion lemma. No smallest-counterexample minimality, R24 frame, four-cell structure, deletion cover, capture, payment, or computation. In an edge-orderable boundary tournament it applies directly to any retained tight path.

## Applicability
In an edge-orderable R24-failure frame, inserting any x in the four-vertex exterior X into the common long rail Q would leave the other three X vertices as a tight trimer and hence produce a spanning two-cover. Therefore every x in X is noninsertable and receives a canonical beta(x). Each beta(x) supplies the pure reverse-middle blocker (q_{beta+1},x,q_beta), with both outer seams already compatible; if beta(x)<beta(y), the barrier-order witness (x,q_{beta(x)+1},y) is simultaneously tight. This replaces a generic multi-blocker insertion array by one scalar crossing-time object in the integrable branch.

## Persistence
Retain the displayed edge order, Q, each exterior vertex, its least right-feasible gap beta, the two outer feasibility inequalities, the strict reversed spoke inequality at beta, and for separated beta-values the witnessed cross turn at q_{beta(x)+1}.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert that beta-values are distinct, concentrated, or unique among all simultaneously feasible gaps. Does not by itself give a spanning two-cover or close the integrable R24 branch. Does not apply to arbitrary non-edge-orderable boundary tournaments. Does not claim spoke weights are monotone along Q after the first barrier.

## Proof
Write e_i=q_iq_{i+1} for the Q-edges, so e_0<e_1<...<e_{m-1}. For a fixed exterior x define L_0=true and, for i>=1, L_i to mean e_{i-1}<q_i x. Define R_{m-1}=true and, for i<=m-2, R_i to mean xq_{i+1}<e_{i+1}. Suppose for contradiction that no i has both L_i and R_i. Since L_0 holds, R_0 fails. If i<m-1 and L_i holds while R_i fails, then e_{i+1}<xq_{i+1}; because e_i<e_{i+1}, we get e_i<xq_{i+1}, which is exactly L_{i+1}. Inductively L_{m-1} holds, but R_{m-1} is true by definition, contradiction. Hence some gap i has both outer seam inequalities. At such a gap, inserting x between q_i and q_{i+1} would be increasing unless the middle comparison q_i x < xq_{i+1} fails: the preceding turn is certified by L_i when present and the following turn by R_i when present. By hypothesis the insertion is not increasing, so totality of the edge order gives xq_{i+1}<q_i x. Now let beta(x) be the least right-feasible gap. For every j<beta(x), R_j fails. Starting from L_0 and using the same propagation shows L_{beta(x)}; the preceding argument then gives xq_{beta(x)+1}<q_{beta(x)}x. Finally suppose beta(x)<beta(y). Then beta(x)<=m-2. At i=beta(x), R_i(x) gives xq_{i+1}<e_{i+1}, while minimality of beta(y) makes R_i(y) false and hence e_{i+1}<yq_{i+1}. Therefore xq_{i+1}<e_{i+1}<yq_{i+1}, so in the edge-order boundary relation (x,q_{i+1},y) is tight. This proves all claims.

# R896 — MAX3 intact crossed endcaps are physically endpoint-anchored outside the R840 nonlocal event

## Statement
Retain the accepted crossed R885 BOUNDED branch with f(T)=1 and the accepted R886 MAX3 regime. Let I be the unique unfragmented middle-gate X cell, and orient the actual T-rail containing I in its forced R885 direction: if I=G_4={b,z}, then I is the initial block of that rail; if I=G_3={a,c}, then I is the terminal block. Apply accepted R840 to the Q vertex adjacent to I. Then exactly one of the following occurs. (NONLOCAL) That adjacent Q vertex is interior to Q, and R840 yields the accepted R682 nonlocal output: an endpoint-capture lineage or a graph-intrinsic tight cross-end trimer through that interior witness. (ENDPOINT) The adjacent Q vertex is one of the physical endpoints L=q_0 or R=q_m. Moreover, in the MAX3 skeletons M1 and M2, where the intact-endcap rail also contains at least one fragmented marker and hence at least one additional Y-run beyond the Y-run touching I, the endpoint is forced: if I=G_4 at the rail start, its adjacent Q vertex is L; if I=G_3 at the rail end, its adjacent Q vertex is R. Only M0, whose intact-endcap rail contains no fragmented marker, retains the two endpoint possibilities L or R. Thus outside the named R840/R682 nonlocal event the anonymous MAX3 skeletons acquire a physical endpoint label, and M1/M2 have a unique natural end attachment.

## Hypotheses
Accepted crossed R594/R862 frame; accepted R885 BOUNDED branch with f(T)=1; accepted R886 MAX3; accepted R840 endpoint normalization.

## Scope
Noncircular source-label sharpening of the accepted MAX3 branch. No payment, capture execution, R5, R168, R169, R224, R533, generic R358, R436, or computation.

## Applicability
Use immediately after R886 enters MAX3. First discharge the R840 NONLOCAL output if it occurs. Otherwise orient the intact X cell in its forced R885 endcap role. In M1/M2 the intact G_4 endcap is attached to L and the intact G_3 endcap to R; only M0 keeps an L/R choice. This is the preferred physical labeling before any per-skeleton seam analysis.

## Persistence


## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not close M0/M1/M2. Does not determine which source Q-cell supplies every other Y-run. Does not assert that the R682 nonlocal branch is contradictory.

## Proof
Work in accepted R886 MAX3 inside the accepted R885 BOUNDED branch. Let I denote the unique intact X cell. By R885, if I=G_4={b,z}, the whole two-vertex block I occurs initially on its T-rail; if I=G_3={a,c}, it occurs terminally. Also by R885, outside its already-separated Reverse-Ear branch, Q vertices encountered along either T-rail occur in strictly increasing Q-index order.\n\nApply accepted R840 to the Q vertex adjacent to I. If that Q vertex is interior to Q, R840 gives its NONLOCAL alternative, namely the retained R682 output. This is exactly the stated NONLOCAL branch. Hence suppose not. Then R840 says the adjacent Q vertex is L=q_0 or R=q_m.\n\nNow suppose the MAX3 skeleton is M1 or M2. By the R886 classification, the rail containing I also contains at least one fragmented marker. Consequently, besides the Y-run immediately adjacent to I, that rail contains at least one additional Y-run separated from it by a fragmented X marker.\n\nIf I=G_4, orient the rail in its actual R885 direction, starting with I. If the adjacent Q vertex were R=q_m, then every later Q vertex on that same rail would have to have Q-index strictly larger than m, impossible. But M1/M2 requires a later Y-run containing a Q vertex. Therefore the adjacent endpoint is L.\n\nDually, if I=G_3, orient the rail in its actual R885 direction ending with I. If the adjacent Q vertex were L=q_0, then every earlier Q vertex on that rail would have to have Q-index strictly smaller than 0, impossible. But M1/M2 requires an earlier Y-run. Therefore the adjacent endpoint is R.\n\nFor M0, R886 says the intact-endcap rail contains no fragmented marker and hence no second Y-run. The above monotonicity contradiction is unavailable, so R840 leaves exactly the two endpoint possibilities L or R. This proves every asserted branch and no stronger endpoint claim is made.

# R897 — A LOW2 fragmented marker exposes a five-vertex inward absorber or an inward-anchor P4

## Statement
Retain the accepted crossed R885 BOUNDED branch with f(T)=1 and the accepted R886 LOW2 regime. Choose a fragmented marker x with c_x=c(T[Y union {x}])<=2. Put v=q_2, d=q_{m-2}, D_x={v,d} union (X-{x}), and R_x=Y union {x}=V(H)-D_x. Choose any tight trimer C on X-{x}. Then the induced path forest T[R_x] covers R_x with exactly c_x tight path components. Applying accepted R522 to the common tight trimer C with the two probes v,d gives one of two source-visible alternatives. (P4) At least one of C union {v} or C union {d} supports a tight Hamilton P4. (ABSORBER) D_x=C union {v,d} supports a tight Hamilton P5. In the ABSORBER branch, if c_x=1 then T[R_x] is a Hamilton path and H is immediately the literal spanning two-cover D_x sqcup R_x, impossible in a counterexample. Hence every surviving ABSORBER branch has c_x=2 and yields the literal spanning three-cover H=P_x sqcup U sqcup V, where P_x is a Hamilton P5 on D_x and U,V are exactly the two components of T[R_x]. Therefore LOW2 reduces to an inward-anchor P4 or to one exact five-vertex-absorber three-cover; the only extra distinction needed before generic three-cover splice machinery is whether U or V is a singleton.

## Hypotheses
Accepted crossed R594/R862 frame; accepted R886 LOW2; accepted R522; x is a LOW2 fragmented marker with c_x<=2.

## Scope
Noncircular consumer translation for the LOW2 branch. Pure induced-path-forest bookkeeping plus the accepted two-probe P5 synchronization theorem. No payment, capture, R5, R168, R169, R224, R533, generic R358, R436, or computation.

## Applicability
Use immediately after R886 enters LOW2. The c_x=1 absorber branch closes. For c_x=2 retain the exact source-labeled P5 P_x on {q_2,q_{m-2}} union (X-{x}) together with the two literal residue rails U,V. If both U,V are nontrivial, the packet is exactly the kind of spanning three-cover targeted by the pending clean splice parent R879; if one is a singleton, isolate that singleton-residue face rather than returning to coarse fragmentation counting.

## Persistence


## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert that the P4 alternative closes H. Does not invoke pending R879 as a proved theorem. Does not claim the c_x=2 three-cover closes when a residue rail is singleton or nontrivial.

## Proof
Retain accepted R886 LOW2 and choose a fragmented marker x with c_x=c(T[Y union {x}])<=2. Let v=q_2 and d=q_{m-2}. Set D_x={v,d} union (X-{x}) and R_x=Y union {x}. Since W=Y union X and T is a two-path forest on W, deleting the three vertices X-{x} from the literal T-rails leaves the induced forest T[R_x]. By the definition of c_x in R886, this forest has exactly c_x connected path components. Each component is a contiguous subpath of a T-rail and hence is tight. It covers all of R_x.\n\nBy accepted R594, every three-subset X-{x} supports a tight trimer; choose one orientation C on those three vertices. Apply accepted R522 to the tight trimer C with the two distinct outside probes v and d. R522 says: if either C union {v} or C union {d} has a Hamilton P4, retain that P4; otherwise C union {v,d}=D_x has a Hamilton P5. This gives the stated P4/ABSORBER alternative.\n\nAssume the ABSORBER branch, and let P_x be a Hamilton P5 on D_x. If c_x=1, then T[R_x] consists of one Hamilton tight path on all of R_x. Since D_x and R_x partition V(H), P_x together with that Hamilton path is a literal spanning two-cover of H, contradicting the standing counterexample hypothesis. Therefore every surviving ABSORBER branch has c_x=2.\n\nWhen c_x=2, write U and V for the two components of T[R_x]. They are vertex-disjoint tight paths covering R_x. Thus H=P_x sqcup U sqcup V is a literal spanning three-cover with the exact source-labelled five-vertex component P_x on {q_2,q_{m-2}} union (X-{x}). No claim is made that U,V are both nontrivial; if they are, the packet has exactly the form targeted by the separately pending generic splice theorem R879, while a singleton component must be treated separately. This proves the stated reduction without using R879.

# R898 — The MAX5 alternating face is a labelled P4 or four simultaneous neighbor-witness middle-gate packets

## Statement
Retain the accepted crossed R885 BOUNDED branch with f(T)=2 and the accepted R894 MAX5 regime. Thus p=0,q=8, every x in X has exactly two selected T-neighbors, both in Y, and there is no selected X-X edge. For x in X write N_T(x) for its two Y-neighbors. Then at least one of the following holds. (P4-END) H contains a source-labelled tight Hamilton P4 using one physical endpoint L and one selected X-Y incidence of T. (FOUR-PACKETS) All eight selected X-Y incidences have forced middle-gate polarity simultaneously: for every y in N_T(a), (y,a,c) is tight; for every y in N_T(c), (y,c,a) is tight; for every y in N_T(b), (z,b,y) is tight; and for every y in N_T(z), (b,z,y) is tight. Consequently the four tested oriented middle-gate dimers (a,c),(c,a),(z,b),(b,z) are respectively two-head, two-head, two-tail, two-tail witness packets whose witness pairs are exactly N_T(a),N_T(c),N_T(b),N_T(z). Using the fixed all-X carriers already present in accepted R649, all four are simultaneously R542-ready: (a,c) with carrier (z,c,a), (c,a) with carrier (b,a,c), (z,b) with carrier (b,z,a), and (b,z) with carrier (z,b,c). Thus the MAX5 branch no longer needs to split by N0/N1/N2 before its next consumer: outside a labelled endpoint P4 it canonically yields four physical two-witness packets tied to the actual T-neighbor pairs.

## Hypotheses
Accepted crossed R621/R649 frame; accepted R894 MAX5 in one exact two-cover T of W=H-{q_2,q_{m-2}}; accepted boundary antisymmetry R3 and R542.

## Scope
Noncircular consumer theorem for the fully fragmented MAX5 face. It converts the current-cover X-Y incidence pattern into simultaneous physical signed-dimer packets. No payment execution, capture, R5, R168, R169, R224, R533, generic R358, R436, or computation.

## Applicability
Use immediately after R894 enters MAX5. Test the eight X-Y incidences against the fixed crossed endpoint signs. Any polarity mismatch gives the displayed endpoint-labelled P4. Otherwise discard the coarse N0/N1/N2 distinction for the next step and retain four simultaneous R542-ready packets with exact current witness pairs N_T(a),N_T(c),N_T(b),N_T(z). Future consumers should exploit coexistence of these four packets rather than enumerate alternating skeletons.

## Persistence


## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert that an R542 payment descendant closes H. Does not identify the source Q-cell of every neighbor in N_T(x). Does not claim N0,N1,N2 are impossible or isomorphic as source-labelled covers; it only shows they share the same stronger packet interface.

## Proof
Work in accepted R894 MAX5. Since p=0 and q=8, every x in X has T-degree two and both of its selected neighbors lie in Y. Because T is a path forest, the two neighbors of each x are distinct. Write N_T(x) for this two-element neighbor set.\n\nWe use the fixed crossed endpoint signs from accepted R649. Its preferred proof records: (a,c) is head-signed by L, so (L,a,c) is tight; (c,a) is head-signed by L, so (L,c,a) is tight; (b,z) is tail-signed by L, so (b,z,L) is tight; and (z,b) is tail-signed by L, so (z,b,L) is tight.\n\nFix y in N_T(a). Boundary antisymmetry R3 at middle a says exactly one of (y,a,c) and (c,a,y) is tight. If (c,a,y) is tight, then tested dimer (c,a) is tail-signed by y while R649 head-signs the same tested orientation by L through (L,c,a). Accepted R523, or direct concatenation, gives the literal tight P4 (L,c,a,y). Hence outside P4-END we must have (y,a,c) tight for every y in N_T(a). Thus (a,c) is head-signed by both members of N_T(a).\n\nFix y in N_T(c). R3 says exactly one of (y,c,a) and (a,c,y) is tight. If (a,c,y) is tight, then (a,c) is tail-signed by y while R649 head-signs (a,c) by L through (L,a,c), giving the literal P4 (L,a,c,y). Hence outside P4-END, (y,c,a) is tight for every y in N_T(c), so (c,a) is head-signed by both members of N_T(c).\n\nFix y in N_T(b). R3 says exactly one of (y,b,z) and (z,b,y) is tight. If (y,b,z) is tight, tested dimer (b,z) is head-signed by y while R649 tail-signs (b,z) by L through (b,z,L), giving the literal P4 (y,b,z,L). Hence outside P4-END, (z,b,y) is tight for every y in N_T(b), so (z,b) is tail-signed by both members of N_T(b).\n\nFinally fix y in N_T(z). R3 says exactly one of (y,z,b) and (b,z,y) is tight. If (y,z,b) is tight, tested dimer (z,b) is head-signed by y while R649 tail-signs (z,b) by L through (z,b,L), giving the literal P4 (y,z,b,L). Hence outside P4-END, (b,z,y) is tight for every y in N_T(z), so (b,z) is tail-signed by both members of N_T(z).\n\nThese four conclusions coexist because they were derived from the same fixed exact cover T and graph-intrinsic R649 endpoint signs. R649 also supplies tight all-X carriers whose reverse boundary dimers are exactly these tested orientations: (z,c,a) for S=(a,c), (b,a,c) for S=(c,a), (b,z,a) for S=(z,b), and (z,b,c) for S=(b,z). Each witness pair N_T(x) lies in Y and is therefore disjoint from its all-X carrier. Accepted R542 therefore applies independently to all four packets. This proves FOUR-PACKETS. No use was made of whether the coarse alternating skeleton was N0,N1,or N2, so the conclusion is common to all three.

# R899 — The aligned long phase has four canonical exact covers of one common pair-deletion residue

## Statement
Retain the accepted R594/R619 frame in the ALIGNED phase and the surviving long range m>=6. Write L=q_0,u=q_1,v=q_2,d=q_{m-2},s=q_{m-1},R=q_m, with X={a,b,c,z} and common aligned complementary root pair {b,z}. Then the single pair-deletion residue H-{b,z} has four simultaneous literal exact two-covers: T_L^a=(u,L,a,c) sqcup Q[2,m], T_L^c=(u,L,c,a) sqcup Q[2,m], T_R^c=Q[0,m-2] sqcup (a,c,R,s), and T_R^a=Q[0,m-2] sqcup (c,a,R,s). The two left representatives have the same rail-support partition and differ only by the order of {a,c}; the two right representatives likewise. Comparing a left representative with a right representative gives a fixed same-residue four-cross-state rectangle. Relative to the right support partition, T_L^a has exactly the two selected cross states L a and d s, while T_L^c has exactly L c and d s. Relative to the left support partition, T_R^c has exactly u v and c R, while T_R^a has exactly u v and a R. Thus the ALIGNED long phase can be entered through one common exact H-{b,z} fiber carrying four representatives and the simultaneous physical cross-state set {L a,L c,d s,u v,c R,a R}, with the variable end contacts forming the 2-by-2 choices {L a,L c} and {c R,a R}. No exactly-two-bad seam hypothesis is needed.

## Hypotheses
Accepted synchronized transitive R594 frame; accepted R619 ALIGNED phase; m>=6.

## Scope
Noncircular aligned-phase parent interface. Pure literal deletion of the common endpoint root from the four R619 enlarged singleton-deletion covers and exact same-residue cross-state bookkeeping. No R556 exactly-two-bad assumption, R5, R168, R169, R224, R533, capture, payment, R436, or computation.

## Applicability
Use as the default ALIGNED long-case entrance after R619. Work in the single common pair-deletion fiber H-{b,z} and compare its four canonical representatives rather than reverting to one-sided seam counts or the historical exactly-two-bad cell. Consumers should exploit same-residue representative rigidity, the fixed inward cross states d s and u v, and the two endpoint-contact choices L{a,c} and {a,c}R.

## Persistence


## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert that the four cross states force a spanning two-cover, a paid floor, or a contradiction. Does not imply the historical exactly-two-bad R556 seam pattern. Does not identify a unique preferred representative among the four covers.

## Proof
Retain accepted R619 in the ALIGNED phase. Its four enlarged singleton-deletion covers are: H-z=(u,L,a,c,b) sqcup Q[2,m] and H-z=Q[0,m-2] sqcup (b,a,c,R,s); H-b=(u,L,c,a,z) sqcup Q[2,m] and H-b=Q[0,m-2] sqcup (z,c,a,R,s).\n\nIn the first H-z cover, b is the terminal vertex of the short rail. Deleting b therefore leaves the tight P4 (u,L,a,c), while Q[2,m] is unchanged; together they cover exactly H-{b,z}. This is T_L^a. In the first H-b cover, z is terminal, giving T_L^c=(u,L,c,a) sqcup Q[2,m]. In the second H-z cover, b is initial on the short rail, so deleting b leaves (a,c,R,s), giving T_R^c=Q[0,m-2] sqcup (a,c,R,s). In the second H-b cover, deleting initial z leaves (c,a,R,s), giving T_R^a=Q[0,m-2] sqcup (c,a,R,s). Thus all four are literal exact two-covers of the same residue H-{b,z}.\n\nNow compare support partitions. Every right representative has support partition Q[0,m-2] | {a,c,R,s}. In T_L^a=(u,L,a,c) | Q[2,m], the selected states on the short rail are uL,La,ac. Here u,L lie in Q[0,m-2] while a,c lie in the right short support, so La is the unique short-rail cross state. On Q[2,m], all adjacent Q states through d=q_{m-2} remain inside Q[0,m-2] until the state ds, after which s,R lie in the right short support; hence ds is the unique Q-rail cross state. Therefore the complete selected cross-state set of T_L^a relative to the right support partition is {La,ds}. The same argument for T_L^c gives {Lc,ds}.\n\nDually, every left representative has support partition {u,L,a,c} | Q[2,m]. In T_R^c=Q[0,m-2] | (a,c,R,s), the Q-prefix crosses this partition exactly at uv=(u,q_2), and the right short rail crosses it exactly at cR; thus its selected cross-state set is {uv,cR}. For T_R^a the corresponding set is {uv,aR}. These facts are simultaneous because all four covers are graph-intrinsic literal representatives supplied by the same R619 aligned frame. This proves the stated common-pair four-cover interface.

# R900 — Every fragmented crossed X marker is X-pure or yields an endpoint-augmented two-witness packet modulo a labelled P4

## Statement
Retain the accepted crossed inward-anchor frame R862 with W=H-{q_2,q_{m-2}}, Y=G_0 union G_1 union G_2, and let T be any exact two-cover of W. Let x be one vertex of a fragmented middle-gate X cell, meaning that x is not T-adjacent to its physical mate in the same cell G_3={a,c} or G_4={b,z}. Then at least one of the following holds. (X-PURE) x has no selected T-neighbor in Y. Pair-Deletion Rigidity R429 then implies deg_T(x) is one or two, and every selected neighbor of x lies in the other middle-gate X cell. Hence either x is a rail endpoint adjacent to exactly one vertex of the other X cell, or x is internal and its two T-neighbors are exactly the two vertices of the other X cell, giving a literal three-vertex X-only rail segment through x. (P4-END) For some selected Y-neighbor y of x and some endpoint e in {L,R} distinct from y, H contains one of the source-labelled tight P4s (e,c,a,y), (e,a,c,y), (y,b,z,e), or (y,z,b,e), chosen according as x=a,c,b,z. (TWO-WITNESS) For some selected Y-neighbor y of x and some endpoint e in {L,R} distinct from y, the appropriate tested middle-gate dimer has y and e as two distinct same-polarity witnesses: if x=a, (a,c) is head-signed by y,e; if x=c, (c,a) is head-signed by y,e; if x=b, (z,b) is tail-signed by y,e; if x=z, (b,z) is tail-signed by y,e. Using the fixed all-X carriers from accepted R649, the packet is R542-ready. Therefore every fragmented marker that has even one current Y-neighbor immediately yields P4-END or TWO-WITNESS; the only residue is X-PURE. In addition, in the f=2 LOW4 branch of R894, if x is chosen with c_x<=4 and X-PURE holds, then d_Y(x)=0 and the R535 identity c_x=r_Y+1-d_Y(x) gives r_Y<=3. Thus the useful-output-free LOW4 residue is an X-pure low marker together with at most three maximal Y-runs. FULLY FRAGMENTED COROLLARY. If f(T)=2, so both X cells are fragmented, then X-PURE cannot occur for all four X vertices simultaneously. Hence H necessarily has a P4-END output or at least one TWO-WITNESS packet. Indeed, if every x in X were X-PURE, T would select no X-Y state. Since X and Y are both nonempty and T has exactly two rails, one rail would cover all four vertices of X and the other all of Y, contradicting the accepted fact that the transitive matching-height four-cell X has no tight Hamilton P4. Therefore the entire f=2 branch, including both LOW4 and MAX5, reduces to a labelled endpoint P4 or a physical current-witness two-witness middle-gate packet. Pending R898 is a stronger MAX5 refinement because it gives four simultaneous such packets in its no-P4 branch.

## Hypotheses
Accepted crossed R594/R621/R649 frame and accepted inward-anchor pair-deletion frame R862; T is any exact two-cover of W=H-{q_2,q_{m-2}}; x belongs to a fragmented X cell. Use accepted R3,R429,R535,R542,R594,R649. The r_Y<=3 sentence additionally assumes R894 LOW4. The fully fragmented corollary assumes f(T)=2.

## Scope
Noncircular local consumer for fragmented middle-gate markers, independent of R885 BOUNDED monotonicity and of the LOW/MAX classification until the final LOW4 corollary. No payment execution, capture, R5,R168,R169,R224,R533,generic R358,R436, or computation.

## Applicability
Use before detailed fragmented-X casework. If a fragmented marker touches Y at all, immediately obtain a labelled P4 or an R542-ready two-witness packet using one physical endpoint as the second witness. In f=2, not all four markers can be X-pure, so the entire fully fragmented branch already has one of these useful outputs; LOW4 needs no independent X-pure endgame after this parent is accepted. MAX5 may still use pending R898 when four simultaneous packets are materially stronger. Outside f=2, an X-pure marker remains the only local residue. If a LOW4 marker itself is X-pure, then r_Y<=3.

## Persistence


## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not say the X-PURE residue is contradictory. Does not assert that the R542-ready packet closes H. Does not determine the source Q-cell of y. The LOW4 r_Y<=3 conclusion applies only when the chosen low marker is X-PURE.

## Proof
Let v=q_2 and d=q_{m-2}. Let x be a fragmented X marker. Suppose first that x has a selected T-neighbor y in Y. Choose e from {L,R} with e!=y; this is always possible because L and R are distinct. Accepted R649 supplies both L and R as same-polarity witnesses on each of the four tested middle-gate orientations used below, together with the fixed all-X short carriers. We compare y with the physical mate of x using R3.\n\nCase x=a. R3 at middle a gives exactly one of (y,a,c) and (c,a,y). If (c,a,y) is tight, R649 gives (e,c,a) tight, so (e,c,a,y) is a literal tight P4. Otherwise (y,a,c) is tight. R649 also gives (e,a,c) tight, so y and e are distinct head witnesses on tested dimer (a,c). The R649 carrier (z,c,a) has reverse terminal dimer (a,c), hence R542 applies.\n\nCase x=c. R3 gives exactly one of (y,c,a) and (a,c,y). If (a,c,y) is tight, R649 gives (e,a,c), so (e,a,c,y) is a P4. Otherwise (y,c,a) is tight, and with fixed head witness e on (c,a) the pair {y,e} is a two-head-witness packet; carrier (b,a,c) makes it R542-ready.\n\nCase x=b. R3 gives exactly one of (y,b,z) and (z,b,y). If (y,b,z) is tight, R649 gives (b,z,e), so (y,b,z,e) is a P4. Otherwise (z,b,y) is tight. R649 gives (z,b,e), so y,e are distinct tail witnesses on tested dimer (z,b); carrier (b,z,a) makes it R542-ready.\n\nCase x=z. R3 gives exactly one of (y,z,b) and (b,z,y). If (y,z,b) is tight, R649 gives (z,b,e), so (y,z,b,e) is a P4. Otherwise (b,z,y) is tight. R649 gives (b,z,e), so y,e are distinct tail witnesses on tested dimer (b,z); carrier (z,b,c) makes it R542-ready.\n\nThus if x has any Y-neighbor, P4-END or TWO-WITNESS holds. Suppose neither holds. Then x has no Y-neighbor. Because T is an exact two-cover of the physical pair deletion H-{v,d}, accepted R429 says both rails are nontrivial, so deg_T(x) is one or two. Fragmentation says x is not adjacent to its same-cell mate. Since x has no Y-neighbor, every selected neighbor lies in the other middle-gate X cell. If deg_T(x)=1, x is a rail endpoint joined to one vertex of that other cell. If deg_T(x)=2, the other X cell has exactly two vertices and these must be the two neighbors, so T contains the literal X-only length-two segment through x. This proves X-PURE.\n\nFinally suppose we are in accepted R894 LOW4 and x is a chosen low marker with c_x<=4. In X-PURE, d_Y(x)=0. Accepted R535 gives c_x=r_Y+1-d_Y(x), hence c_x=r_Y+1. Therefore r_Y<=3. This proves the stated LOW4 corollary.

For the fully fragmented corollary, assume f(T)=2 and suppose for contradiction that neither P4-END nor TWO-WITNESS occurs for any x in X. Both physical X cells are fragmented, so the local conclusion applies to all four vertices and forces X-PURE for every x. Thus no selected T-state joins X to Y. Both X and Y are nonempty in the R862 frame. Since T has exactly two connected rails and no rail can contain both an X vertex and a Y vertex without an X-Y adjacent state, the two rails must consist of one X-only rail and one Y-only rail. The X-only rail contains all four vertices of X and is therefore a tight Hamilton P4 on X. This contradicts the accepted R594 transitive matching-height property that X is P4-free. Hence some x yields P4-END or TWO-WITNESS. This argument does not distinguish LOW4 from MAX5, proving the stated f=2 collapse.

# R901 — The five-cell separator budget is one conservation identity r_Y + p + delta_X = 6

## Statement
Retain the accepted crossed beyond-ten inward-anchor five-cell frame R862 with W=H-{q_2,q_{m-2}}, source cells G_0=Q[0,1], G_1=Q[3,m-3], G_2=Q[m-1,m], G_3={a,c}, G_4={b,z}, X=G_3 union G_4, Y=G_0 union G_1 union G_2, and let T be any exact two-cover of W. Use the accepted R535/R885 notation p=e_T(X), q=e_T(X,Y), r_Y=c(T[Y]), d_Y(x), c_x=c(T[Y union {x}]), and f=f(T). Define the X endpoint deficiency delta_X(T)=sum_{x in X}(2-d_T(x)), where d_T is selected degree in T.

(1) CONSERVATION. Unconditionally, with no BOUNDED hypothesis, sum_{v in W}(2-d_T(v))=4 exactly, so delta_X is precisely the number of the four rail-end slots of T occupied by X vertices, an isolated vertex occupying two slots, and 0<=delta_X<=4. Moreover
    r_Y + p + delta_X = 6.
This contains the accepted R885 identity r_Y=p+q-2 as the special substitution q=8-delta_X-2p.

(2) BOUNDED SLACK. In the BOUNDED branch of accepted R885 each unfragmented X cell contributes at least one unit to p, namely its own internal selected edge, and at least one unit to delta_X, namely the outer vertex of its forced initial/terminal block. Hence p>=2-f and delta_X>=2-f. Defining the slack s(T)=(p-(2-f))+(delta_X-(2-f))>=0, one has the identity
    r_Y = 2 + 2f - s(T).
Thus the accepted R885 bound r_Y<=2+2f is not an inequality chain but a conservation law with an explicit nonnegative defect, and the defect is physical: it counts extra X-X selected edges and extra X rail-end occupancy beyond what the unfragmented cells already force.

(3) UNIFORM MAX FACE. The MAX face at fragmentation level f is exactly the zero-slack face s(T)=0, equivalently p=2-f and delta_X=2-f. On it every coarse parameter is determined by f alone:
    r_Y=2+2f, q=2+3f;
    every fragmented marker has d_Y=2 and c=1+2f;
    each unfragmented cell has outer vertex with d_Y=0 and c=3+2f, inner vertex with d_Y=1 and c=2+2f.
Specializing: f=0 gives (p,q,r_Y)=(2,2,2) with c multiset {2,2,3,3}; f=1 gives (1,5,4) with d_Y multiset {2,2,1,0} and c multiset {3,3,4,5}, which is exactly the accepted R886 MAX3 parameter point; f=2 gives (0,8,6) with c_x=5 for all x and no selected X-X edge, which is exactly the accepted R894 MAX5 parameter point. Hence the three separately established extremal parameter points are one face read at three values of f.

(4) UNIFORM LOW FACE, PHYSICALLY. The LOW face at level f is exactly s(T)>=1, equivalently: T selects an X-X edge other than the internal edges of the unfragmented cells, OR some X vertex occupies a rail-end slot other than the outer vertices of the unfragmented cells. Combined with the accepted equivalences of R886 and R894, the parameter conditions 'some marker has c<=2' (LOW2, f=1) and 'some x has c_x<=4' (LOW4, f=2) are each equivalent to this single physical excess condition.

(5) LOW4 PHYSICAL NORMAL FORM. When f=2 there is no unfragmented cell, so 2-f=0 and s(T)=p+delta_X with no forced contribution. Therefore LOW4 holds if and only if at least one of the following occurs, and the two are not mutually exclusive:
    (LOW4-EDGE) T selects an X-X edge; since both middle-gate cells are fragmented, neither {a,c} nor {b,z} is a T-edge, so any such edge is necessarily a CROSS-CELL middle-gate edge, one of ab, az, cb, cz joining G_3 to G_4;
    (LOW4-END) some x in X has d_T(x)<=1, that is, some X vertex occupies a rail-end slot of T.
Moreover the LOW4 depth satisfies 5-r_Y = p+delta_X-1, so the coarse parameter c-value deficit is exactly the total physical excess. This replaces the parameter condition c_x<=4 by two named source-labelled physical objects, a G_3-G_4 middle-gate adjacency or an X rail endpoint, both of which retain their crossed-frame cell labels.

## Hypotheses
Accepted crossed R862 inward-anchor five-cell frame and one exact two-cover T of W. Part (1) uses only that T is a spanning two-path forest on W. Parts (2)-(5) additionally use the BOUNDED branch of accepted R885 for the unfragmented-cell endcap rule and the identity r_Y=p+q-2, and accepted R535 for the pointwise formula c_x=r_Y+1-d_Y(x). Parts (4)-(5) cite the accepted low-marker equivalences of R886 and R894. No payment, capture, floor steering, R436, R5, R168, R169, R224, R533, R350, generic R358, finite m-enumeration, or computation.

## Scope
Noncircular crossed R24/O6 parent compression of the numerical layer of the R885 fragmentation family. Order-free and m-independent; a pure conservation identity for the five-cell separator budget together with its zero-slack face and a physical reading of the low faces.

## Applicability
Use as the arithmetic front door to the entire sigma>0 five-cell excess branch, in place of recomputing coarse parameters separately at each fragmentation level. Given f, read the MAX parameter point directly off (3) rather than deriving it; given a configuration, compute the slack s=6-r_Y-... equivalently s=p+delta_X-2(2-f) to place it. For consumers, prefer (4) and (5): the low faces are not a parameter condition but the presence of a physically named excess object, an extra X-X selected edge or an extra X rail-end slot. In particular (5) supplies the previously missing source-labelled normal form for the LOW4 leaf: attack LOW4-EDGE through crossed middle-gate G_3-G_4 adjacency geometry and LOW4-END through X-endpoint role machinery.

## Persistence
Retain T, f, the five physical source cells and all X labels, p, q, r_Y, delta_X, d_Y, c_x, the slack s(T), the identity of which X vertices occupy rail-end slots, and in LOW4-EDGE the exact cross-cell pair among ab, az, cb, cz.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not close any MAX or LOW face and does not close LOW4. Does not assert that any coarse parameter point or skeleton is realizable in the Strong frame. Does not assign the Y-runs to the source cells G_0,G_1,G_2. Does not imply the geometric content of R870, R886, or R894: the endcap placement rule, the M0/M1/M2 skeletons, and the N0/N1/N2 skeletons are NOT consequences of this identity, which explains only the numerical layer of that family; accordingly this result is not a ground for retiring or superseding those theorems. The LOW4-EDGE and LOW4-END alternatives are not exclusive. Does not extend the frame to fragmentation counts outside {0,1,2} and makes no claim about sigma=0. Does not consume the labelled P4 or Reverse-Ear outputs excluded by the R885 BOUNDED branch.

## Proof
SETUP. T is an exact two-cover of W, that is two vertex-disjoint tight paths spanning W. As a graph T is a forest of exactly two paths, hence has |W|-2 edges and maximum degree 2.

PART (1). Partition the edges of T by type: e(T)=p+q+e_T(Y). The induced subgraph T[Y] is a disjoint union of paths on |Y| vertices with r_Y components, so e_T(Y)=|Y|-r_Y. Since X has four vertices, |W|=|Y|+4, and therefore p+q+|Y|-r_Y=|W|-2=|Y|+2, giving p+q=r_Y+2. This is the accepted R885 identity r_Y=p+q-2.
Next count degrees. Each X-X edge contributes 2 and each X-Y edge contributes 1 to sum_{x in X} d_T(x), so sum_{x in X} d_T(x)=2p+q and delta_X=8-(2p+q). Eliminating q via p+q=r_Y+2 gives delta_X=8-p-(p+q)=8-p-(r_Y+2)=6-p-r_Y, that is r_Y+p+delta_X=6.
Finally sum_{v in W}(2-d_T(v))=2|W|-2e(T)=2|W|-2(|W|-2)=4. Every vertex has d_T in {0,1,2}, so this total of 4 is distributed over the rail-end slots: each of the two rails has two ends, and a rail of order one is a single vertex of degree 0 occupying both of its own slots. Hence delta_X is exactly the number of those four slots occupied by X vertices, and 0<=delta_X<=4.

PART (2). Work in the BOUNDED branch of accepted R885. If a cell G_i, i in {3,4}, is unfragmented then b_i(T)=1, so its two vertices lie in one contiguous T-block and are T-adjacent; that edge lies inside X and the edges arising from the two distinct cells are distinct. Hence p>=2-f. By the BOUNDED endcap rule an unfragmented G_4 block is initial on its T-rail and an unfragmented G_3 block is terminal on its T-rail; in either case the outer vertex of the block has d_T<=1 and so contributes at least one unit to delta_X. The two cells are disjoint, so delta_X>=2-f. Substituting both bounds into part (1),
  r_Y = 6 - p - delta_X = 6 - (2-f) - (2-f) - s(T) = 2 + 2f - s(T),
where s(T)=(p-(2-f))+(delta_X-(2-f))>=0. In particular r_Y<=2+2f, which is the accepted R885 bound, now with an explicit defect.

PART (3). Suppose s(T)=0, so p=2-f and delta_X=2-f exactly. Then r_Y=2+2f and q=r_Y+2-p=(2+2f)+2-(2-f)=2+3f.
Since p=2-f is already accounted for by the internal edges of the unfragmented cells, T selects no other X-X edge; in particular every fragmented marker has no X-neighbour. Since delta_X=2-f is already accounted for by the outer vertices of the unfragmented blocks, every other X vertex has d_T=2. Hence every fragmented marker has d_T=2 with both neighbours in Y, so d_Y=2, and by the accepted R535 formula c=r_Y+1-d_Y=(2+2f)+1-2=1+2f.
For an unfragmented cell, its outer vertex has d_T=1 and its unique edge is the internal cell edge, so d_Y=0 and c=r_Y+1=3+2f. Its inner vertex has d_T=2 with one edge inside the cell, hence exactly one Y-neighbour, so d_Y=1 and c=r_Y=2+2f.
Specializing f=0 gives (p,q,r_Y)=(2,2,2) and c multiset {2,2,3,3}. Specializing f=1 gives (p,q,r_Y)=(1,5,4), d_Y multiset {2,2,1,0} with the two 2s on the fragmented cell, and c multiset {3,3,4,5}: this is verbatim the accepted R886 MAX3 parameter point. Specializing f=2 gives (p,q,r_Y)=(0,8,6), no selected X-X edge, d_Y=2 and c_x=5 for every x: this is verbatim the accepted R894 MAX5 parameter point.

PART (4). By part (2), s(T)>=1 is equivalent to r_Y<=1+2f, and by definition s(T)>=1 holds exactly when p>2-f or delta_X>2-f, that is when T selects an X-X edge beyond the internal edges of the unfragmented cells, or some X vertex occupies a rail-end slot beyond the outer vertices of the unfragmented blocks. Accepted R886 states that for f=1 the condition r_Y<=3 is equivalent to some marker having c<=2, and accepted R894 states that for f=2 the condition r_Y<=5 is equivalent to some x having c_x<=4. Combining gives the stated equivalence of the parameter conditions with the physical excess condition.

PART (5). Let f=2. Then 2-f=0, so parts (2) and (4) give s(T)=p+delta_X and LOW4 is equivalent to p+delta_X>=1. If p>=1 then T selects an X-X edge; because both cells are fragmented, b_3(T)=b_4(T)=2, so a and c are not T-adjacent and b and z are not T-adjacent, whence any selected X-X edge joins a vertex of G_3 to a vertex of G_4 and is therefore one of ab, az, cb, cz. If instead p=0 then delta_X>=1, so some x in X has d_T(x)<=1 and occupies a rail-end slot. The two cases may overlap. Finally r_Y=6-p-delta_X gives 5-r_Y=p+delta_X-1 as claimed.

# R902 — Every nonHamilton five-vertex boundary tournament is edge-orderable

## Statement
Let H be a boundary 3-tournament on exactly five vertices. If H has no directed tight Hamilton path, its line-graph comparison orientation Gamma(H) is acyclic. Equivalently there is a total order on E(K_5) realizing every tight turn as an increasing consecutive-edge comparison. In contrapositive form, any nonintegrable five-vertex boundary tournament is Hamiltonian. Consequently, in any boundary tournament with pc(H)>2, the five-vertex complement of any proper tight path is edge-orderable.

## Hypotheses
Boundary antisymmetry R3; comparison orientation and shortest-cycle classification R887. The complement consequence assumes only pc(H)>2 and a tight path whose complement has exactly five vertices.

## Scope
A single finite integrability parent with an order-free critical-complement consequence.

## Applicability
Replaces case-specific cycle exclusion on any five-vertex Hamilton obstruction by one global acyclicity certificate; applies to both endpoint five-cells of the synchronized frame. Does not discharge a remaining O6 branch.

## Persistence


## Exclusions / nonclaims
Acyclicity is necessary, not sufficient, for a five-set to be nonHamilton. No integrability assertion for arbitrary larger nonHamilton induced systems. No global two-cover or R24 closure. This is a computer-assisted proof proposal, pending independent review.

## Proof
Define one Boolean variable for each reversal pair of ordered triples on {0,1,2,3,4}; the positive representative has first vertex smaller than last. For every permutation p, the clause OR_i NOT tight(p_i,p_{i+1},p_{i+2}), i=0,1,2, asserts p is not Hamilton. The 120 clauses are therefore exactly the absence of a Hamilton P5, with no extra orientation assumptions.

By R887 a shortest directed comparison cycle is a star triangle, an ordinary triangle, or a vertex-simple ordinary cycle. On five vertices, an ordinary cycle has length at most five. A length-five cycle itself gives a Hamilton P5. Up to relabelling, the three other possibilities are the roots triangle, square, star in the code below. Each corresponding CNF is refuted by the embedded binary case-split/unit-propagation certificate. The verifier checks every propagation from its indexed original clause, checks a false original clause at every leaf, and checks both values of every split variable. Consequently it verifies an exhaustive propositional proof, not merely an optimization solver status. The recorded (split nodes, contradiction leaves, unit steps) counts are respectively (29,30,331), (3,4,41), (15,16,189). The certificates were produced and verified using the Python standard library. Run Python normally, without disabling assertions.

Thus Gamma has no directed cycle. R887 supplies a global edge order by topological sorting. For the critical-complement consequence, a Hamilton five-vertex complement together with the displayed proper tight path would be a spanning two-cover, contradicting pc(H)>2. Therefore that complement is nonHamilton and the theorem applies.

Self-contained certificate generator, verifier, and recorded proof trees:
```python
from itertools import permutations
import json

N=5
keys=[t for t in permutations(range(N),3) if t[0]<t[2]]
ids={t:i+1 for i,t in enumerate(keys)}
def lit(t): return ids[t] if t[0]<t[2] else -ids[t[::-1]]
base=[tuple(-lit(p[i:i+3]) for i in range(3)) for p in permutations(range(N))]
roots={'triangle':[(0,1,2),(1,2,0),(2,0,1)],
       'square':[(0,1,2),(1,2,3),(2,3,0),(3,0,1)],
       'star':[(1,0,2),(2,0,3),(3,0,1)]}
def solve(cs,ass):
    ass=set(ass)
    steps=[]
    while True:
        residual=[]
        unit=None
        for i,c in enumerate(cs):
            if any(l in ass for l in c): continue
            r=[l for l in c if -l not in ass]
            if not r: return {'units':steps,'conflict':i}
            if len(r)==1:
                unit=(i,r[0]); break
            residual.append(r)
        if unit is None: break
        steps.append(unit); ass.add(unit[1])
    if not residual: raise RuntimeError('SAT')
    freq={}
    for c in residual:
        for l in c: freq[abs(l)]=freq.get(abs(l),0)+2**(-len(c))
    v=max(freq,key=freq.get)
    return {'units':steps,'split':v,'positive':solve(cs,ass|{v}), 'negative':solve(cs,ass|{-v})}
def stats(t):
    if 'conflict' in t: return (0,1,len(t['units']))
    a,b=stats(t['positive']),stats(t['negative'])
    return (1+a[0]+b[0],a[1]+b[1],len(t['units'])+a[2]+b[2])
def verify(cs,t,ass):
    ass=set(ass)
    for i,l in t['units']:
        c=cs[i]
        assert not any(x in ass for x in c)
        assert [x for x in c if -x not in ass]==[l]
        ass.add(l)
    if 'conflict' in t:
        assert all(-x in ass for x in cs[t['conflict']]); return
    v=t['split']; assert v not in ass and -v not in ass
    verify(cs,t['positive'],ass|{v}); verify(cs,t['negative'],ass|{-v})
```

# FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R903.md

<!-- BEGIN FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R903.md -->

# R903 — Edge-orderability has arbitrarily large vertex-minimal obstructions, even with transitive middle tournaments

## Statement
For every integer n>=4 there is a boundary 3-tournament H_n on n vertices such that (i) its comparison orientation Gamma(H_n) has exactly one directed simple cycle, of length n; (ii) every proper induced subsystem is edge-orderable; (iii) every local middle-vertex tournament is transitive; and (iv) H_n has a cyclic tight Hamilton ordering, hence pc(H_n)=1. Consequently edge-orderability of boundary tournaments has no characterization by forbidden induced subsystems of bounded vertex order: for every fixed k, some non-edge-orderable boundary tournament has every induced subsystem of order at most k edge-orderable.

## Hypotheses
n>=4. Boundary means exactly one of (u,v,w) and (w,v,u) is tight for each ordered triple of distinct vertices. Edge-orderability means a total order on E(K_V) realizes tightness by uv<vw.

## Scope
Order-free obstruction family for local-to-global integrability. Independent of smallest-counterexample, R24/R5, gate phases, and pending five-vertex R902.

## Applicability
Rules out inferring global edge-orderability from bounded-size induced edge-orderability, even when all local middle tournaments are transitive. In particular, accepting the proposed five-vertex nonHamilton-implies-edge-orderable result would not supply this missing local-to-global inference. Hamiltonicity is explicit, so the family itself cannot occur as a smallest two-cover counterexample.

## Persistence
Retain the labelled ordinary Hamilton cycle e_i={v_i,v_{i+1}}, its cyclic comparison orientation, and the common total ordering of all noncycle ordinary edges.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not refute the two-cover conjecture: each constructed H_n is Hamiltonian. Does not rule out an integrability theorem with extra smallest-counterexample or exact-cover hypotheses. Does not establish or use R902. No canonical promotion or acceptance is requested by the producer.

## Proof
Let V={v_0,...,v_{n-1}}, with indices modulo n, and let e_i={v_i,v_{i+1}}. For n>=4, the vertices e_i induce a chordless n-cycle in L(K_V). Let D=E(K_V)\{e_0,...,e_{n-1}} and choose any total order on D. Orient every adjacency between members of D from earlier to later. Orient every adjacency between d in D and e_i from d to e_i. Finally orient e_i -> e_{i+1} for all i modulo n. These rules orient every edge of L(K_V) exactly once. Define (u,v,w) tight iff {u,v}->{v,w}; opposite reversals are complementary, so this defines a boundary tournament, with the comparison dictionary of accepted R887.

A directed cycle cannot use both D and its complement because there is no arc from a cycle-edge vertex back into D. The orientation on D is acyclic because it follows one total order. The orientation induced by {e_i} is exactly the directed n-cycle. It follows that this is the unique directed simple cycle in Gamma(H_n).

If U is a proper subset of V, an omitted original vertex removes its two incident cycle edges from E(K_U). The restriction Gamma(H_n)[E(K_U)] therefore cannot contain the unique directed cycle and is acyclic. By R887, H_n[U] is edge-orderable. This also covers the trivial small U cases.

For a fixed original vertex v_i, the incident ordinary edges form a clique of L(K_V). All incident members of D precede both cycle edges in their common total order, and the last two edges satisfy e_{i-1}->e_i. Thus this clique is transitively oriented, proving transitivity of each local middle tournament directly.

Finally e_i->e_{i+1} means (v_i,v_{i+1},v_{i+2}) is tight for every cyclic index. Hence (v_0,...,v_{n-1}) is a tight Hamilton path, and every rotation is as well. The full H_n is not edge-orderable because its comparison orientation is cyclic. Given any fixed k, take n>max(k,3). All subsystems on at most k vertices are proper and edge-orderable, but H_n is not. Any supposed bounded-order forbidden-induced characterization would therefore fail on H_n.
