# R904 — Hamiltonian crossed local frames of every order can forbid all two-covers preserving the eight-core middle rail

## Statement
For every n>=11 there is a Hamiltonian boundary 3-tournament H on n vertices with V(H)=X disjoint-union V(Q), X={a,b,c,z}, Q=(L,u,v,w_1,...,w_k,d,s,R), k=n-10>=1, and N=(v,w_1,...,w_k,d), satisfying: X is the transitive P4-free matching-height four-cell {ab,cz}>{ac,bz}>{bc,az}; X+L and X+R are P5-free; the universal reverse endpoint stars and the crossed middle gates hold; G=H[X union {L,u,s,R}] has pc(G)=2 and all four literal 4+4 covers from {(u,L,a,c),(u,L,c,a)} times {(b,z,R,s),(z,b,R,s)}; nevertheless no cover of H by at most two tight paths contains N as a contiguous block in its given order. An explicit Hamilton path is (c,v,a,b,z,d,w_1,...,w_k,L,u,s,R). Moreover the fixed core has the exact support criterion: for E subset {L,u,s,R}, G[X union E] is Hamiltonian iff (u in E and L not in E) or (s in E and R not in E).

## Hypotheses
Existence theorem for finite boundary 3-tournaments; exact complete-reversal antisymmetry and vertex-simple paths. These are graph-intrinsic crossed local data, NOT the full smallest-counterexample assumptions of R594/R619.

## Scope
Order-free limitation of the intact-middle consumer of the eight-core decomposition. One fixed eight-vertex computational certificate and a symbolic all-order completion.

## Applicability
Shows that the local eight-core partition, exact crossed 4+4 representatives, endpoint five-set obstructions, and reverse stars alone cannot imply an intact-N spanning two-cover. A consumer must exploit additional hypotheses or allow splitting/rearranging N or selected deeper cuts. The fixed core support criterion exposes the precise endpoint-pair obstruction.

## Persistence
Full 168-bit core orientation, exact bit ordering, standard-library exhaustive verifier, symbolic completion for all k>=1, Hamilton path P, and proof of the intact-N exclusion are embedded in the proof text.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Not a counterexample to the two-cover conjecture or to R24: H is Hamiltonian. Does not satisfy or assert smallest-counterexample minimality or exactness of all singleton-deletion covers. Does not rule out a proof using those extra constraints, insertion into the middle, or deeper cuts. The witness itself keeps W intact after removing v,d, so it does not establish an obstruction for every fixed cut depth. Not canonically accepted or promoted by its producer.

## Proof
This is a computer-assisted finite-certificate proof for one fixed eight-vertex core, followed by a symbolic construction for every order. No solver is needed to verify the certificate.

1. THE FIXED CORE.
Use labels (a,b,c,z,L,u,s,R)=(0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7). The 168-bit certificate in the verifier below lists the tightness of (x,y,t) for x<t, in the exact loop order y=0..7, x=0..7, t=x+1..7, excluding y in {x,t}. Reverse triples have complementary tightness. Thus the certificate defines a boundary tournament G unambiguously.

Direct exhaustive checking on this fixed core establishes:
(i) X={a,b,c,z} has matching heights {ab,cz}>{ac,bz}>{bc,az}, tight turns being descending comparisons.
(ii) For EVERY E subset of {L,u,s,R}, G[X union E] is Hamiltonian if and only if
       (u in E and L not in E) OR (s in E and R not in E).
(iii) For every x in G minus {L,u}, (x,L,u) is bad; for every x in G minus {s,R}, (s,R,x) is bad.
(iv) The eight gate turns (L,a,c),(L,c,a),(b,z,L),(z,b,L),(b,z,R),(z,b,R),(R,a,c),(R,c,a) are tight. The four enlarged paths (u,L,a,c,b), (u,L,c,a,z), (a,b,z,R,s), (c,z,b,R,s) are tight. All four pairs choosing A from {(u,L,a,c),(u,L,c,a)} and B from {(b,z,R,s),(z,b,R,s)} are tight 4+4 covers.

In particular pc(G)=2 by (ii) with E all four caps and (iv); X+L and X+R are nonHamiltonian by (ii). The endpoint reverse stars follow from (iii) by antisymmetry. The verifier checks (ii) by testing all permutations of each of sixteen sets of size at most eight, not by relying on a MILP UNSAT answer.

2. PARAMETRIC COMPLETION.
For any k>=1 introduce new vertices v,d,w_1,...,w_k. Put W=(w_1,...,w_k),
N=(v,W,d), Q=(L,u,v,W,d,s,R), and P=(c,v,a,b,z,d,W,L,u,s,R).
The resulting order is n=k+10 and the rail convention Q=(q_0,...,q_m) has m=k+5>=6.

Retain every core turn and prescribe the following comparisons:
  (x,v,w_1) tight iff x=u, for x in G;
  (w_k,d,x) tight iff x=s, for x in G;
  (x,u,v) tight iff x=L, for x in G minus {u};
  (d,s,x) tight iff x=R, for x in G minus {s}.
Require every consecutive triple of Q and of P to be tight. Complete every as-yet-unset reversal pair arbitrarily (the verifier uses the increasing outer-index orientation).

These prescriptions are consistent for every k. The four comparison families have different middle vertices v,d,u,s and involve a new vertex, so neither conflict with each other nor with the core. The four exterior Q seam turns are the specified true choices x=L,u,s,R. Internal W turns are shared by Q and P in the same direction; at entry Q uses v and P uses d, while at exit Q uses d and P uses L. These comparisons do not reverse one another. For k=1, the additional P turn (z,d,w_1) is the reversal of the prescribed bad turn (w_1,d,z), so is consistent. For k>=2 that P turn is unset by the four families. All other P turns either use a new comparison pair or are core turns (a,b,z),(L,u,s),(u,s,R), verified tight in the certificate. Thus the completion exists symbolically for all k. P is visibly vertex-simple and spanning, so H is Hamiltonian.

The core and all listed local geometry remain literally unchanged; Q is tight by construction. Thus the R810-type physical partition into this exact two-cover core and middle rail, and the crossed core representatives of R817, hold as graph-intrinsic data. This statement does NOT import the smallest-counterexample hypothesis of those results.

3. NO TWO-COVER CAN KEEP N INTACT.
Suppose a cover by at most two paths keeps N as one contiguous block in its given order. Write its component containing N as A N C and its other component as B; A,B,C consist only of core vertices and B may initially be allowed empty.

If A is nonempty its last vertex must be u by the first comparison family. If |A|>=2 its penultimate vertex must be L by the third family. If |A|>=3, the third-last vertex would make a tight (x,L,u), forbidden by core property (iii). Consequently A is empty, (u), or (L,u).
Dually C is empty, (s), or (s,R).

It follows that B contains all of X, and its cap set E satisfies u in E => L in E and s in E => R in E. By (ii), B's support is nonHamiltonian. This contradicts B being the remaining path. In particular B cannot be omitted, since it contains X. This proves the claimed exclusion.

4. SCOPE.
These examples are Hamiltonian, not smallest counterexamples. They refute an intact-N normalization inferred solely from the enumerated local frame/core data, even at arbitrary rail length. They do not refute a normalization using additional smallest-counterexample/deletion-cover constraints; they do not exclude inserting core blocks into N, splitting N, or choosing deeper cuts. In fact the displayed Hamilton path retains W intact after the selected cut that removes v and d from N. Therefore no conclusion about failure of EVERY fixed-depth end modification is justified.

5. SELF-CONTAINED VERIFIER.
The following uses only Python's standard library. It checks the finite certificate exhaustively, verifies the core paths/barriers, and implements the symbolic completion with consistency assertions. The sample k values are implementation checks only; the preceding argument proves the all-k assertion.

```python
"""Self-contained finite certificate and parametric construction; stdlib only."""
from itertools import permutations
CORE_BITS='111011100000000100000111111000001111000001100000000001100000000000001010011001001011101000000001000000111010000000000000000100100001000010001001011101001010011101001011'
a,b,c,z,L,u,s,R=range(8)
keys=[(x,y,t) for y in range(8) for x in range(8) for t in range(x+1,8) if y not in (x,t)]
assert len(CORE_BITS)==len(keys)==168
core=dict(zip(keys,map(int,CORE_BITS)))
def turn(table,t):
 x,y,q=t
 return bool(table[(x,y,q)]) if x<q else not table[(q,y,x)]
def path(table,p):return all(turn(table,t) for t in zip(p,p[1:],p[2:]))
def force(table,t,value=True):
 x,y,q=t; key=(min(x,q),y,max(x,q));bit=int(value if x<q else not value)
 assert key not in table or table[key]==bit,(t,value)
 table[key]=bit
height={frozenset(e):h for h,es in [(3,[(a,b),(c,z)]),(2,[(a,c),(b,z)]),(1,[(b,c),(a,z)])] for e in es}
for t in permutations(range(4),3):
 assert turn(core,t)==(height[frozenset(t[:2])]>height[frozenset(t[1:])])
for mask in range(16):
 E=[x for i,x in enumerate((L,u,s,R)) if mask>>i&1]
 has=any(path(core,p) for p in permutations([a,b,c,z]+E))
 assert has==((u in E and L not in E) or (s in E and R not in E))
for x in range(4):assert turn(core,(u,L,x)) and turn(core,(x,R,s))
for x in range(8):
 if x not in (L,u):assert not turn(core,(x,L,u))
 if x not in (s,R):assert not turn(core,(s,R,x))
for t in [(L,a,c),(L,c,a),(b,z,L),(z,b,L),(b,z,R),(z,b,R),(R,a,c),(R,c,a)]:assert turn(core,t)
for p in [(u,L,a,c,b),(u,L,c,a,z),(a,b,z,R,s),(c,z,b,R,s)]:assert path(core,p)
for A in [(u,L,a,c),(u,L,c,a)]:
 for B in [(b,z,R,s),(z,b,R,s)]:assert path(core,A) and path(core,B)

def construct(k):
 assert k>=1
 v,d=8,9;W=list(range(10,10+k));first,last=W[0],W[-1];T=core.copy()
 for x in range(8):
  force(T,(x,v,first),x==u)
  force(T,(last,d,x),x==s)
  if x!=u:force(T,(x,u,v),x==L)
  if x!=s:force(T,(d,s,x),x==R)
 Q=[L,u,v]+W+[d,s,R]
 P=[c,v,a,b,z,d]+W+[L,u,s,R]
 for p in [Q,P]:
  for t in zip(p,p[1:],p[2:]):force(T,t)
 n=10+k
 for y in range(n):
  for x in range(n):
   for q in range(x+1,n):
    if y not in (x,q):T.setdefault((x,y,q),1)
 assert path(T,Q) and path(T,P) and set(P)==set(range(n)) and len(P)==n
 return T,Q,P
for k in [1,2,3,4,20]:construct(k)
print('PASS: core support equivalence, crossed paths, stars, and parametric construction checks.')
print('The proof for every k is symbolic; these parameter checks are consistency checks, not an exhaustive proof over k.')

```

# R905 — Crossed singleton-deletion endpoint rotations force deep-coupled two-witness packets at both ends

## Statement
Retain the accepted crossed R621 frame with X={a,b,c,z}, Q=(q_0,...,q_m), m>=6, L=q_0,u=q_1,v=q_2,d=q_{m-2},s=q_{m-1},R=q_m. Put t=q_3, h=q_4, r=q_{m-3}, and ell=q_{m-4}. Then the first deep cut at each end forces a graph-intrinsic short-carrier two-witness packet that genuinely uses a deep rail coordinate. LEFT: at least one of the following four packets exists, where S is the displayed tested reverse boundary dimer of tight trimer K, e is the complementary singleton, and W is a same-polarity witness pair outside K: (L0) K=(d,s,R), S=(R,s), e=d, W={v,z}; (L1) K=(z,c,b), S=(b,c), e=z, W={a,t}; (L2) K=(c,a,z), S=(z,a), e=c, W={b,t}; (L3) K=(v,t,h), S=(h,t), e=v, W={b,z}. RIGHT: at least one of the following four packets exists: (R0) K=(L,u,v), S=(u,L), e=v, W={d,a}; (R1) K=(ell,r,d), S=(r,ell), e=d, W={a,c}; (R2) K=(a,b,z), S=(b,a), e=z, W={c,r}; (R3) K=(c,z,b), S=(z,c), e=b, W={a,r}. Thus the crossed long frame cannot realize the R904-style endpoint-rotation freedom at either side: singleton-deletion non-Hamiltonicity forces a two-witness packet reaching q_3/q_4 or q_{m-4}/q_{m-3}, or a cross-end packet using v or d.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest boundary-tournament counterexample in the accepted crossed R621 frame; m>=6. Uses only the literal R621 singleton-deletion covers and tight turns, plus boundary antisymmetry R3.

## Scope
Noncircular crossed long phase. Selected-depth endpoint-rotation consumer; no R5,R168,R169,R224,R533,five-cell classification,capture,payment,R436,or computation.

## Applicability
Use immediately after R621/R723 when an intact-middle-only consumer stalls. Each forced packet is an exact input type for the accepted two-witness short-carrier consumer R696, but unlike the core-only R649 packet family, every packet here contains a first-deep rail coordinate or a cross-end witness. This supplies a concrete smallest-counterexample constraint violated by the pending R904 witness family.

## Persistence
Retain the two root-coupled three-hole clauses used in the proof at each side and whichever packet is realized. Left clauses: (t,b,c) OR (h,t,b) OR (v,R,s), and (t,z,a) OR (h,t,z) OR (v,R,s). Right clauses: (u,L,d) OR (a,r,ell) OR (b,a,r), and (u,L,d) OR (c,r,ell) OR (z,c,r). These clauses and the resulting packet are graph-intrinsic in the fixed crossed frame.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not close the crossed phase, choose which packet occurs, or assert that an R696 descendant closes H. Does not preserve the whole middle rail intact. Does not claim R904 is false; R904 is a pending local-frame witness outside smallest-counterexample minimality. The result is a selected-depth consequence of genuine singleton-deletion non-Hamiltonicity, not a bounded-state normalization of all cover interactions.

## Proof
Let t=q_3 and h=q_4. R621 gives the exact deletion covers H-z=(u,L,a,c,b) sqcup Q[2,m] and H-b=(u,L,c,a,z) sqcup Q[2,m], where Q[2,m]=(v,t,h,...,s,R). Consider the spanning orders of the two deletion residues obtained by rotating the first vertex v of the long rail to its end:
P_z=(u,L,a,c,b,t,h,...,s,R,v),
P_b=(u,L,c,a,z,t,h,...,s,R,v).
All consecutive triples in P_z are already tight except possibly (c,b,t), (b,t,h), and (s,R,v). All consecutive triples in P_b are already tight except possibly (a,z,t), (z,t,h), and (s,R,v). If all three holes in either order were tight, that order would be a Hamilton path of H-z or H-b; adding the deleted vertex as a singleton would give a spanning two-cover of H, impossible in a smallest counterexample. Hence each order has a bad hole. By boundary antisymmetry R3, the exact reversals give the simultaneous clauses
(1) (t,b,c) OR (h,t,b) OR (v,R,s),
(2) (t,z,a) OR (h,t,z) OR (v,R,s).
If (v,R,s) is tight, then K=(d,s,R) is a tight Q trimer, S=(R,s) is its reverse boundary dimer, and v together with z are same-polarity witnesses because R621 contains the tight turn (z,R,s). This is L0. Suppose instead (v,R,s) is bad. Then the first two literals of each clause remain. If (t,b,c) is tight, K=(z,c,b) is tight from the transitive matching-height orientation of X, S=(b,c) is its reverse boundary dimer, and a,t are same-polarity witnesses because (a,b,c) is tight; this is L1. If (t,z,a) is tight, similarly K=(c,a,z), S=(z,a), and b,t are witnesses because (b,z,a) is tight; this is L2. If neither first literal is tight, clauses (1),(2) force both (h,t,b) and (h,t,z). Since K=(v,t,h) is a tight Q trimer and S=(h,t) is its reverse boundary dimer, b,z are same-polarity witnesses, giving L3. Thus one left packet always exists.

For the right side put r=q_{m-3}, ell=q_{m-4}. R621 gives H-c=Q[0,m-2] sqcup (a,b,z,R,s) and H-a=Q[0,m-2] sqcup (c,z,b,R,s), with Q[0,m-2]=(L,u,...,ell,r,d). Rotate the final vertex d of the long rail to its front and concatenate:
P_c=(d,L,u,...,ell,r,a,b,z,R,s),
P_a=(d,L,u,...,ell,r,c,z,b,R,s).
The only uncertified turns are respectively (d,L,u),(ell,r,a),(r,a,b) and (d,L,u),(ell,r,c),(r,c,z). Non-Hamiltonicity of H-c and H-a plus R3 therefore gives
(3) (u,L,d) OR (a,r,ell) OR (b,a,r),
(4) (u,L,d) OR (c,r,ell) OR (z,c,r).
If (u,L,d) is tight, K=(L,u,v) is tight, S=(u,L) is its reverse boundary dimer, and d,a are witnesses because R621 contains (u,L,a); this is R0. Otherwise, if (b,a,r) is tight then K=(a,b,z) is tight, S=(b,a), and c,r are witnesses because (b,a,c) is tight, giving R2. If (z,c,r) is tight then K=(c,z,b), S=(z,c), and a,r are witnesses because (z,c,a) is tight, giving R3. If neither of those literals is tight, (3),(4) force both (a,r,ell) and (c,r,ell). Since K=(ell,r,d) is a tight Q trimer and S=(r,ell) is its reverse boundary dimer, a,c are witnesses, giving R1. Thus one right packet always exists. The two arguments are simultaneous in the same crossed frame.

# R910 — Every crossed middle-gate pair-deletion cover is Reverse-Ear active

## Statement
Retain the accepted crossed R621/R649 frame with X={a,b,c,z}, Q=(q_0,...,q_m), L=q_0, R=q_m, and crossed middle-gate pairs G_3={a,c}, G_4={b,z}. Fix either tested orientation S=(s_0,s_1) of G_3 and let T=T_1 sqcup T_2 be any exact two-cover of H-V(S). Then T together with the fixed crossed frame always yields an accepted R435 Reverse-Ear output: a reversed selected/old state, a tight reverse trimer/contact, or a vertex-simple tight cycle. Dually the same holds for either tested orientation of G_4. More precisely, for G_3, accepted R649 makes R a head witness on S. Let K be the T-rail containing R. If R is terminal on K, accepted R834 gives a tight reverse outer seam (s_0,R,y), where y is the T-predecessor of R; this trimer contains the reversed selected state R y of the T-state y R, so R435 applies relative to K. If R is not terminal, let y be its T-successor. Since V(H)-V(S)=V(Q) union G_4, either y=q_i is a Q vertex or y is one vertex x of G_4. In the Q case K encounters the consecutive Q-contacts R=q_m then q_i with i<m, so R435 applies relative to Q. In the G_4 case, writing x' for the other G_4 vertex, the crossed right gate gives the tight trimer (x',x,R); it contains the reversed state x R of the selected T-state R x, so R435 applies relative to K. These cases exhaust T. For G_4, accepted R649 makes L a tail witness on S. On the T-rail containing L, if L is initial, R834 gives a reverse outer seam containing the reverse of its selected successor state; if L has a predecessor q_i in Q then q_i,L are decreasing Q-contacts; if its predecessor is x in G_3 then the crossed left gate trimer (L,x,x') contains the reverse of the selected state x L. Hence R435 applies in every case. Therefore no exact crossed middle-gate pair-deletion cover is Reverse-Ear quiet.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in the accepted crossed R621 frame. S is either orientation of one crossed middle-gate pair G_3 or G_4. T is any exact two-cover of H-V(S). Use accepted R649 for endpoint polarity, R429 for nontriviality of both T rails, R834 for the endpoint case, the literal crossed gate trimers from R621, and R435 Reverse Ear.

## Scope
Accepted-input crossed-frame parent theorem. No R905/R906, selected-depth witness, capture, payment, five-cell taxonomy, generic growth, R5,R168,R169,R224,R533, or computation.

## Applicability
Whenever an argument reaches an exact deletion cover of either crossed middle-gate pair, do not branch into CAP/XET/payment merely to exploit endpoint carriers. Apply this theorem first: the source cover already carries explicit R435 reversal/reverse-trimer/cycle geometry. In particular, once reviewed, it consumes the entire middle-gate alternative of pending R906, including both R682 CAP and XET.

## Persistence
Retain the tested middle-gate orientation S, exact cover T, the distinguished endpoint R for G_3 or L for G_4, its actual rail role/neighbor, and the exact R435 trigger: R834 reverse seam, decreasing Q-contact pair, or crossed-gate reverse selected state. Retain the resulting R435 geometric output.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not claim an R435 output alone closes H or that every exact cover has the same output type. Does not transport selected states between covers. Does not claim middle-gate deletion itself is impossible. The theorem only says every such exact cover is Reverse-Ear active.

## Proof
Fix S=(s_0,s_1) an orientation of G_3={a,c}. By accepted R649/P728, the tested orientation S is head-signed by both physical endpoints L,R; in particular (R,s_0,s_1) is tight. Let T=T_1 sqcup T_2 be any exact cover of H-S. R429 makes both rails nontrivial. Let K be the oriented T-rail containing R. If R is the terminal vertex of K, write y for its predecessor. In the literal spanning three-cover H=S sqcup T_1 sqcup T_2, R is a head witness on S, so accepted R834 HEAD-END gives the tight reverse outer seam (s_0,R,y). Compare this trimer with K: its consecutive K-contacts are R then y, while K selects y then R. Thus accepted R435 is in its adjacent-state reversal output. Suppose instead R is not terminal and let y be its successor on K. The deleted vertices are exactly G_3, so y lies in Q or in G_4. If y=q_i is in Q, then K has consecutive Q-contacts R=q_m then q_i with i<m, strictly decreasing in Q-order; accepted R435 applies to K relative to Q. If y=x lies in G_4, let x' be its mate. The accepted crossed right gate in R621 gives (x',x,R) tight: explicitly (b,z,R) and (z,b,R) are both tight, so whichever x occurs, choose the other as x'. This tight trimer contains the state x R, the reverse of the selected T-state R x. Comparing it with K, R435 again gives the adjacent-state reversal output. These cases exhaust the G_3 deletion cover. For G_4 the proof is the exact dual. R649/P728 says either tested orientation of G_4 is tail-signed by L,R, in particular by L. Let K be the T-rail containing L. If L is initial, with successor y, R834 TAIL-START gives a tight reverse outer seam whose first state reverses the selected L y state, so R435 applies. If L is not initial, let y be its predecessor. If y=q_i lies in Q, K encounters q_i then L=q_0 in decreasing Q-order, so R435 applies relative to Q. If y=x lies in G_3, let x' be its mate; the crossed left gate gives both (L,a,c) and (L,c,a) tight, hence (L,x,x') is tight and contains the reverse state L x of selected x L. R435 applies relative to K. Therefore every exact deletion cover of either crossed middle-gate pair is Reverse-Ear active.

# R911 — Crossed common pair-deletion concatenations force first-depth gate witness or bidirectional inward-dimer rigidity

## Statement
Retain the accepted crossed R621 frame with X={a,b,c,z}, Q=(q_0,...,q_m), m>=6, L=q_0,u=q_1,v=q_2,t=q_3,r=q_{m-3},d=q_{m-2},s=q_{m-1},R=q_m. Then the two crossed middle-gate pair-deletion residues give two simultaneous accepted-input two-hole systems. LEFT, on H-{b,z}, the exact covers (u,L,a,c) sqcup Q[2,m] and (u,L,c,a) sqcup Q[2,m] imply the graph-intrinsic clauses (v,c,a) OR (t,v,c), and (v,a,c) OR (t,v,a). Consequently either v=q_2 is a head witness on one tested orientation of G_3={a,c}, or the reverse Q dimer D_L=(t,v)=(q_3,q_2) is tail-signed by both a and c. In the latter case accepted R873, applied one step to the left, gives either a labelled probe P4 or also makes D_L head-signed by a,c; hence both P4s (a,t,v,c) and (c,t,v,a) are tight and accepted R843 applies to every exact H-{t,v} two-cover, forcing block count >2 or a source-visible reverse seam. RIGHT, on H-{a,c}, the exact covers Q[0,m-2] sqcup (b,z,R,s) and Q[0,m-2] sqcup (z,b,R,s) imply (b,d,r) OR (z,b,d), and (z,d,r) OR (b,z,d). Consequently either d=q_{m-2} is a tail witness on one tested orientation of G_4={b,z}, or D_R=(d,r)=(q_{m-2},q_{m-3}) is head-signed by both b,z. In the latter case R873 gives either a labelled probe P4 or also tail-signs D_R by b,z, yielding both P4s (b,d,r,z) and (z,d,r,b), so R843 gives fixed-cover block/seam rigidity on every exact H-{d,r} two-cover. Thus at each side the common pair-deletion residue forces a first-depth middle-gate witness or a named bidirectional inward-Q dimer, modulo a labelled P4; no singleton-deletion endpoint rotation or generic payment is needed.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in the accepted crossed R621 frame; m>=6. Use accepted Pair-Deletion Rigidity R429 to exclude Hamiltonicity of H-{b,z} and H-{a,c}, boundary antisymmetry R3, propagation R873, same-support interaction R523, and fixed-cover bidirectional P4 consumer R843.

## Scope
Crossed long phase, accepted-input first-depth theorem. No R905/R906, singleton-deletion endpoint rotation, capture, payment, five-cell taxonomy, R5,R168,R169,R224,R533, generic R358, Reverse Ear, or computation.

## Applicability
Preferred first-depth consequence in the crossed phase. Before using pending R905, inspect these two common pair-deletion clauses. A gate-witness output feeds any middle-gate witness consumer while preserving the physical depth-two coordinate v or d; the complementary branch gives a bidirectionally signed first-depth reverse Q dimer and a fixed exact pair-deletion cover interface through R843. This is strictly shorter and dependency-cleaner than the three-hole endpoint-rotation route for obtaining selected-depth structure.

## Persistence
Retain both exact pair-deletion covers at each side, the two literal Hamilton path proposals and their complete two-hole sets, the four reverse clauses, and whichever side output occurs. In the dimer branch retain the tested reverse Q dimer, witness pair, R873 probe tests, both P4 orders in the no-P4 branch, and the exact R843 cover/block-count or reverse-seam certificate.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not close H, choose which disjunct occurs, or claim a gate witness is itself contradictory. Does not claim the R843 HIGH branch closes. Left and right outputs coexist only as graph-intrinsic alternatives supplied by their separate pair-deletion arguments; no common exact cover is asserted.

## Proof
LEFT. Delete the common crossed complementary pair {b,z}. From accepted R621, deleting b from H-z=(u,L,a,c,b) sqcup Q[2,m] gives the literal exact cover (u,L,a,c) sqcup Q[2,m] of H-{b,z}; deleting z from H-b=(u,L,c,a,z) sqcup Q[2,m] gives (u,L,c,a) sqcup Q[2,m]. Concatenate the two rails of the first cover in the displayed order P_1=(u,L,a,c,v,t,q_4,...,R). Every turn is certified except alpha=(a,c,v) and beta=(c,v,t). If both were tight, P_1 would be a Hamilton tight path of H-{b,z}, contradicting accepted R429, which says pc(H-{b,z})=2. Hence at least one is bad; R3 gives reverse(alpha)=(v,c,a) or reverse(beta)=(t,v,c) tight. The second exact cover similarly gives P_2=(u,L,c,a,v,t,q_4,...,R), with only holes (c,a,v),(a,v,t), hence (v,a,c) OR (t,v,a). If either first literal occurs, v is a head witness on tested orientation (c,a) or (a,c) of G_3. If neither occurs, both (t,v,c) and (t,v,a) are tight, so D_L=(t,v)=D_3 is tail-signed by probes a,c. Apply accepted R873 in its right-to-left form using K_2=(u,v,t): either one of the two probe four-sets is Hamiltonian, giving the labelled P4 branch, or D_3 also becomes head-signed by both probes. In the latter case R523 gives both P4 orders (a,t,v,c) and (c,t,v,a). Pair-Deletion Rigidity supplies nontrivial exact covers of H-{t,v}, and accepted R843 applies to each such cover, giving b_T(a,c)>2 or a source-visible reverse seam. RIGHT. Delete {a,c}. R621 gives exact covers Q[0,m-2] sqcup (b,z,R,s) and Q[0,m-2] sqcup (z,b,R,s). Concatenating the first gives P_3=(L,u,...,r,d,b,z,R,s), whose only holes are (r,d,b),(d,b,z). R429 excludes Hamiltonicity, so R3 gives (b,d,r) OR (z,b,d). The second gives (z,d,r) OR (b,z,d). If either second literal occurs, d is a tail witness on tested orientation (z,b) or (b,z) of G_4. If neither occurs, D_R=(d,r)=D_{m-2} is head-signed by b,z. Apply R873 at i=m-2: either a probe P4 occurs, or D_R also becomes tail-signed by b,z. Then R523 gives (b,d,r,z) and (z,d,r,b), and R843 gives block-count >2 or a source-visible reverse seam in every exact H-{d,r} cover. This proves both side compressions.

# R914 — Crossed first-depth pair deletions force bi-oriented anchors, a labelled P4, or Reverse-Ear geometry

## Statement
Retain the accepted crossed R621 frame with X={a,b,c,z}, Q=(q_0,...,q_m), m>=6, and L=q_0,u=q_1,v=q_2,t=q_3,r=q_{m-3},d=q_{m-2},s=q_{m-1},R=q_m. Then at least one of the following occurs. (BI-ANCHORS) All four first-depth anchor turns are simultaneously tight: (v,a,c), (v,c,a), (b,z,d), and (z,b,d). Equivalently v head-signs both tested orientations of G_3={a,c}, while d tail-signs both tested orientations of G_4={b,z}. (P4) One of the source-labelled first-depth four-sets produced below supports a tight Hamilton P4. (REVERSE-EAR) Accepted R435 Reverse-Ear geometry occurs relative to the original Q: a reversed old state, a tight reverse trimer/reversal cell, or a vertex-simple tight cycle. Thus, outside P4/Reverse-Ear geometry, there is no packet tree, witness-wave corridor, or one-orientation anchor residue: the crossed long phase is forced into the single bi-oriented two-ended anchor state.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest boundary-tournament counterexample in the accepted crossed R621 frame, m>=6. Uses accepted R3,R429,R621,R703 only.

## Scope
Accepted-input crossed-long parent compression. Directly strengthens earlier C724 revisions and removes their R849/R873/R516 propagation layer. No R905/R906, capture, payment, five-cell classification, generic path growth, or computation.

## Applicability
Preferred first-depth crossed front door after review. Derive the two left and two right pair-deletion clauses. Any dimer literal immediately enters accepted R703 and therefore gives P4 or Reverse-Ear geometry. Hence the only branch requiring further producer analysis is BI-ANCHORS, with all four exact anchor turns retained. Do not open the R905 endpoint-rotation tree or propagate a witness wave first.

## Persistence
In BI-ANCHORS retain v,d, both tested orientations of G_3 and G_4, and all four anchor turns. In P4 retain the exact first-depth dimer literal, R703 probe, and labelled four-set. In REVERSE-EAR retain the source dimer literal, Q order, R703 forced nonmonotone Q trimer, and exact R435 output.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert BI-ANCHORS, a P4, or a Reverse-Ear output closes H. Does not declare a tight cycle contradictory. Does not claim bare Reverse-Ear existence is rare or progress; R483 remains a fence. The value is the elimination of every other first-depth producer state.

## Proof
From accepted R621, delete b from H-b=(u,L,c,a,z) sqcup Q[2,m] and z from H-z=(u,L,a,c,b) sqcup Q[2,m]. By accepted Pair-Deletion Rigidity R429 these are exact two-covers (u,L,c,a) sqcup Q[2,m] and (u,L,a,c) sqcup Q[2,m] of H-{b,z}. Concatenating each short rail into the front of Q[2,m], the first proposal has exactly two uncertified turns (c,a,v),(a,v,t), so because H has no spanning two-cover at least one is bad and R3 gives (v,a,c) OR (t,v,a). The second gives (v,c,a) OR (t,v,c). Now consider either dimer literal (t,v,x) with x=a or c. Since t=q_3 and v=q_2, this is exactly R703 form (L), J_L=(q_{i+1},q_i,x), at i=2. Accepted R703 therefore gives either a Hamilton P4 on {u,v,t,x} or explicit R435 Reverse-Ear geometry relative to Q. Hence outside P4/RE both left clauses must choose their anchor literals, so (v,a,c) and (v,c,a) are simultaneously tight. Dually, delete c and a from the two right R621 singleton-deletion covers to obtain exact covers of H-{a,c}. Concatenating Q[0,m-2] into the short right rails gives the clauses (b,d,r) OR (z,b,d) and (z,d,r) OR (b,z,d). Each dimer literal has the form (x,q_{i+1},q_i) with q_{i+1}=d=q_{m-2}, q_i=r=q_{m-3}, namely R703 form (R) at i=m-3. Thus any such literal gives a labelled P4 or R435 geometry. Outside those outputs both right clauses must choose (z,b,d) and (b,z,d). Therefore outside P4/RE all four anchor turns coexist: (v,a,c),(v,c,a),(b,z,d),(z,b,d). This proves the trichotomy directly from accepted inputs.

# R915 — A signed cross-end trimer rail forces the opposite reverse seam

## Statement
Let H be a finite boundary tournament with pc(H)>2. Let S=(p,q) be a tested oriented dimer, and let x,y,v be distinct vertices outside S. Let T be an exact two-cover of H-V(S) whose two rails are nontrivial, with one rail exactly (x,v,y) (the other orientation is handled by swapping x,y). If x and y are head witnesses on S, so (x,p,q) and (y,p,q) are tight, while v is a tail witness, so (p,q,v) is tight, then the opposite-end reverse seam (y,v,q) is tight. Dually, if x and y are tail witnesses on S while v is a head witness, then (p,v,x) is tight. For a cross rail (y,v,x), the corresponding conclusions are (x,v,q) in the head-endpoint/tail-middle case and (p,v,y) in the tail-endpoint/head-middle case. Thus a three-vertex exact-cover rail whose endpoints have one sign polarity on S and whose middle vertex has the opposite polarity deterministically emits a reverse seam at the opposite physical endpoint.

## Hypotheses
H is finite with pc(H)>2; S=(p,q) is a tested oriented dimer; x,y,v are distinct outside S; T is an exact two-cover of H-V(S) with both rails nontrivial and with one rail exactly (x,v,y) or (y,v,x); the displayed head/tail sign turns hold on the same tested orientation S.

## Scope
Order-free exact-cover parent lemma. No smallest-counterexample minimality, crossed frame, selected depth, R621, R649, R682, R684, R906, payment, or computation is needed once the signed dimer and exact cross-end trimer rail are supplied.

## Applicability
Use whenever an exact deletion cover contains a three-vertex rail x-v-y and the two physical endpoints have one sign polarity on the deleted tested dimer while v has the opposite polarity. In the crossed middle-gate XET setting, R649 supplies the endpoint polarity and any producer supplying the opposite inward-witness polarity may invoke this theorem directly, yielding the R908 seam without depending on that producer's identity.

## Persistence
Retain S with tested orientation, the exact sign turns for x,y,v, the exact two-cover T and cross-rail orientation, the R523 P4 used in the proof, the exact b_T=2 calculation, and the forced R833 reverse seam. The seam is graph-intrinsic; T states and block count remain source-cover-relative.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert the reverse seam closes H. Does not require or preserve any particular long rail outside the exact cover T. Does not transport selected states to other representatives. If the second T rail is trivial, R833 is not licensed by this theorem.

## Proof
Assume first that x,y are head witnesses on S=(p,q) and v is a tail witness, and orient the cross rail as (x,v,y). Then (x,p,q) and (p,q,v) are tight, so R523 gives the tight P4 K=(x,p,q,v). Apply R833 to K with middle dimer {p,q} and the actual exact cover T of H-{p,q}. Put C=V(H)\V(K). Deleting the P4 endpoints x and v from the rail (x,v,y) leaves exactly the singleton C-block {y}; the other nontrivial T rail is disjoint from K and remains one C-block. Hence b_T(x,v)=2. R833 X-REVERSE is impossible because x has no selected exterior neighbor: its only T-neighbor is v, which is the other P4 endpoint. REVERSE-CHORD is impossible because it would require the selected state v x, while T selects x v. ANTI-ENDS is impossible because v has T-degree two in (x,v,y). Therefore R833 Y-REVERSE must hold. Its selected exterior neighbor of v is uniquely y, so the forced seam is (y,v,q), as claimed. If the rail is (y,v,x), use the head witness y instead and obtain (x,v,q). For the dual polarity, suppose x,y are tail witnesses and v is a head witness. With rail (x,v,y), R523 gives K=(v,p,q,y). Again deleting endpoints v,y leaves exactly {x} plus the other T rail, so b_T(v,y)=2. Y-REVERSE is impossible because y is terminal, REVERSE-CHORD would require y v while T selects v y, and ANTI-ENDS is impossible because v has degree two. Thus X-REVERSE holds, with unique exterior predecessor x of v, forcing (p,v,x). The rail (y,v,x) gives (p,v,y) identically.

# R917 — BI-ANCHORS saturate across the opposite middle gate unless the inward five-set is Hamiltonian

## Statement
Retain the accepted crossed R914 BI-ANCHOR branch with X={a,b,c,z}, matching heights {ab,cz}>{ac,bz}>{bc,az}, v=q_2 and d=q_{m-2}. Then independently at the two inward anchors: (LEFT) either H[X union {v}] has a tight Hamilton P5, or both cross-depth turns (b,z,v) and (z,b,v) are tight; equivalently v tail-signs both tested orientations of G_4={b,z}, while R914 already head-signs both orientations of G_3={a,c} by v. (RIGHT) either H[X union {d}] has a tight Hamilton P5, or both cross-depth turns (d,a,c) and (d,c,a) are tight; equivalently d head-signs both tested orientations of G_3, while R914 already tail-signs both orientations of G_4 by d. Consequently, if neither inward five-set X+v nor X+d is Hamiltonian, the full symmetric inward sign matrix holds simultaneously: v and d head-sign both orientations of G_3 and tail-sign both orientations of G_4. The proof is finite and computer-free once accepted R902 supplies edge-orderability of a nonHamilton five-set.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest boundary-tournament counterexample in the accepted crossed R914 BI-ANCHOR branch. X is the accepted R594 transitive matching-height four-cell. Uses accepted R902: every nonHamilton five-vertex boundary tournament is edge-orderable.

## Scope
Crossed long phase, BI-ANCHOR consumer. Accepted-input, computer-free proof. No R905/R906, capture, payment, five-cell taxonomy, Reverse Ear, R5,R168,R169,R224,R533, generic R358, or computation.

## Applicability
After R914 enters BI-ANCHORS, test the two induced five-sets X+v and X+d. A nonHamilton side immediately supplies both missing opposite-gate cross-depth sign bits. If both are nonHamilton, retain the full 2-by-2 inward sign matrix. If a side is Hamiltonian, retain its literal Hamilton P5 as a role-sensitive absorber candidate rather than converting it to generic P5 currency.

## Persistence
Retain X with its matching-height labels, v,d, the four R914 anchor turns, for each nonHamilton five-set the R902 edge order and the exact two-case Hamilton-path contradiction, and the resulting cross-depth sign turns. In a Hamilton branch retain an explicit Hamilton P5 order when later chosen. All sign conclusions are graph-intrinsic.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert X+v or X+d is nonHamiltonian, does not assert the two Hamilton/nonHamilton branches synchronize any exact deletion covers, and does not close H. A Hamilton P5 on X+v or X+d is only an absorber support until a cover-valued consumer is supplied. The full sign matrix is not claimed by itself to force a Hamilton P6 or a spanning two-cover.

## Proof
LEFT. Assume H[X union {v}] is nonHamiltonian. By accepted R902 it is edge-orderable; fix a total edge order < realizing tight turns. The matching-height orientation of X gives the incident-edge inequalities ab<ac<az, ab<bz<bc, cz<ac<bc, and cz<bz<az. The R914 anchors (v,a,c) and (v,c,a) give av<ac and cv<ac. We prove bz<bv. Suppose instead bv<bz. Compare bv and cv. If bv<cv, then the ordinary-edge sequence of the vertex order (b,v,c,a,z) is bv<cv<ac<az, so (b,v,c,a,z) is a tight Hamilton P5 by the edge-order dictionary. If cv<bv, then (c,v,b,z,a) has edge sequence cv<bv<bz<az and is a tight Hamilton P5. Both contradict nonHamiltonicity. Hence bz<bv, which is exactly the tight turn (z,b,v). Next prove bz<vz. Suppose instead vz<bz. Compare vz and av. If vz<av, then (z,v,a,c,b) has vz<av<ac<bc; if av<vz, then (a,v,z,b,c) has av<vz<bz<bc. Either is a tight Hamilton P5, contradiction. Therefore bz<vz, exactly (b,z,v) tight. Thus v tail-signs both orientations of G_4.

RIGHT. Assume H[X union {d}] is nonHamiltonian and fix its R902 edge order. R914 gives (b,z,d) and (z,b,d), hence bz<zd and bz<bd. We prove ad<ac, i.e. (d,a,c) tight. Suppose ac<ad. Compare bd and ad. If bd<ad, then (c,z,b,d,a) has cz<bz<bd<ad; if ad<bd, then (z,c,a,d,b) has cz<ac<ad<bd. Either is a Hamilton P5, contradiction. Hence ad<ac. Similarly prove cd<ac. Suppose ac<cd. Compare zd and cd. If zd<cd, then (a,b,z,d,c) has ab<bz<zd<cd; if cd<zd, then (b,a,c,d,z) has ab<ac<cd<zd. Again either is Hamilton, contradiction. Thus cd<ac, exactly (d,c,a) tight. Therefore d head-signs both orientations of G_3. The two side arguments use only graph-intrinsic turns in the common R914 frame, so when both five-sets are nonHamiltonian all eight inward gate-sign turns coexist. This proves the theorem.

# R919 — Generic tight-trimer outer-pair endpoint return yields a two-hole mate clause

## Statement
Let H be a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample and let J=(a,x,c) be any graph-intrinsic tight trimer. Choose an exact two-cover P sqcup Q of H-{a,c} in which x is an endpoint of P. Then P is not a singleton, and endpoint exposure yields an explicit one-hole or two-hole mate certificate without any rail-floor hypothesis. If P begins (x,u), then when P has order two the spanning proposal (a,x,c,u) sqcup Q has the unique uncertified turn (x,c,u), which must be bad, so (u,c,x) is tight. If P begins (x,u,v,...) with order at least three, the proposal (a,x,c,u,v,...) sqcup Q has exactly two uncertified turns (x,c,u) and (c,u,v); at least one is bad, so (u,c,x) is tight OR (v,u,c) is tight. The right-end case is the exact dual: for P=(u,x) one forces (x,a,u), while for P=(...,v,u,x) one gets (a,u,v) tight OR (x,a,u) tight. Thus every outer-pair endpoint return of the middle vertex of a tight trimer gives an explicit R173-admissible mate clause, with the order-two case degenerating to a forced one-hole mate.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample; J=(a,x,c) is a tight trimer; P sqcup Q is an exact two-cover of H-{a,c}; x is an endpoint of P.

## Scope
Order-free endpoint-return compiler. Replaces the R168-dependent formulation by an exact order-two/order-at-least-three seam split.

## Applicability
Use whenever an exact outer-pair deletion cover exposes the middle of a known tight trimer. No small-deletion rail floor is needed.

## Persistence
Retain the literal spanning proposal and its one- or two-hole seam ledger; the forced reverse mate or mate disjunction is graph-intrinsic.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert which mate wins in the two-hole case; one mate clause alone does not close H; does not claim an endpoint rail has order at least three.

## Proof
Proof of R919. Let J=(a,x,c) be tight and P sqcup Q an exact two-cover of H-{a,c} with x an endpoint of P. If P=(x) is singleton, then J sqcup Q is already a spanning two-cover of H, impossible. Thus P has order at least two. Suppose x is the first vertex. If P=(x,u), consider (a,x,c,u) sqcup Q. The turn (a,x,c) is certified by J and the unique new turn is h=(x,c,u). If h were tight, the proposal would two-cover H; hence h is bad, and R3 gives (u,c,x) tight. If P=(x,u,v,...) has order at least three, the proposal (a,x,c,u,v,...) sqcup Q has exactly the two new turns h1=(x,c,u), h2=(c,u,v). Every later turn is inherited from P and the first turn is inherited from J. They cannot both be tight, so at least one is bad; R3 gives (u,c,x) tight or (v,u,c) tight. If x is the last vertex, reverse the construction: for P=(u,x), the proposal (u,a,x,c) sqcup Q has unique hole (u,a,x), forcing (x,a,u); for P=(...,v,u,x), the proposal (...,v,u,a,x,c) sqcup Q has exactly the holes (v,u,a),(u,a,x), forcing (a,u,v) or (x,a,u). This proves R919 without a rail-floor theorem.

Proof of R920. Let J=(a,x,c) be proper. By R4, H-J has an exact two-cover U sqcup V; restoring J gives the named minimum three-cover. For the outer pair {a,c}, either some exact H-{a,c} cover exposes x or every such cover keeps x internal. In the first case apply the just-proved endpoint seam argument of R919.

Assume the all-internal case. Fix any exact return P sqcup Q of H-{a,c}; it exists by R4 applied to the pair deletion, and x is internal, say P=(...,ell,x,r,...). Deleting x splits P into two nonempty tight subpaths P_L,P_R, so P_L sqcup P_R sqcup Q is a literal three-cover of W=H-J. The source U sqcup V is a literal two-cover of the same proper W. R159 therefore gives a graph-intrinsic balanced opposite-sign pair.

It remains to prove the source-rail and shield assertions without R168. Neither U nor V can be singleton. If U=(y), then (x,y) is a valid two-vertex tight path and (x,y) sqcup V is an exact two-cover of H-{a,c} exposing x, contrary to all-internality. Thus both rails have order at least two. Write U=(u0,...,ur) with r>=1. The direct attachment at its left end is bad: if r>=1 and (x,u0,u1) were tight, then (x,u0,...,ur) sqcup V would be an exact H-{a,c} cover exposing x. Hence R3 forces (u1,u0,x) tight. If r=1, this reverse trimer itself uses exactly x and all vertices of U, so (u1,u0,x) sqcup V is an exact H-{a,c} cover exposing x, again impossible. Therefore r>=2 and |U|>=3. The same argument gives |V|>=3.

With both rails of order at least three, the two direct x-attachments at each end of each rail are defined. Each is bad for the same endpoint-exposure reason. Applying R3 to their complete reversals gives the four reverse terminal shields: for U, (u1,u0,x) and (x,ur,u_{r-1}); for V the analogous two turns. Together with the R159 pair this is exactly the asserted all-internal normal form. No R168, R24, R5, capture, or first-contact theorem is used.

# R920 — Universal tight-trimer outer-pair return machine

## Statement
Let H be a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample and let J=(a,x,c) be any proper graph-intrinsic tight trimer. By smallest-counterexample minimality choose an exact two-cover U sqcup V of H-J, so H=J sqcup U sqcup V is a minimum three-cover. Exactly one of the following outer-pair return regimes holds. (I) Some exact two-cover of H-{a,c} places x at a rail endpoint; then the endpoint-return compiler gives an explicit one-hole or two-hole R173-admissible mate certificate. (II) Every exact two-cover of H-{a,c} places x internally. In regime (II), for any chosen return P=(...,ell,x,r,...) sqcup Q, deleting x gives a literal three-cover of H-J while U sqcup V is a literal two-cover of the same proper residue, so R159 supplies a graph-intrinsic balanced opposite-sign pair. Moreover each of U,V has order at least three. A singleton source rail (y) would make (x,y) together with the other rail an exact H-{a,c} cover exposing x. If a source rail were a dimer (y,z), the direct attachment (x,y,z) is bad by all-internality, so R3 makes its reverse (z,y,x) tight, again giving an exact H-{a,c} cover exposing x. Finally all four direct attachments of x to the two ends of U,V are bad, and R3 forces the four reverse terminal shield turns. Hence every proper tight trimer has a noncircular endpoint-mate or all-internal component-drop/three-vertex-rail-floor/four-shield normal form.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample; J=(a,x,c) is any proper tight trimer.

## Scope
Order-free universal tight-trimer return machine, reconstructed without R168, R24, R5, capture, or first-contact ancestry.

## Applicability
Use after any graph-intrinsic trimer construction or fixed-turn target return. In the all-internal branch the source rails are automatically of order at least three, so terminal-trimer collision consumers are available.

## Persistence
The chosen source currentization and any outer-pair return are alternative representatives. The R159 pair, source rail-order conclusion, and forced reverse shields are graph-intrinsic/historical certificates relative to the named source paths.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not preserve unrelated ancestry when currentizing J; does not assert endpoint and all-internal regimes coexist; the R159 pair is anonymous and not automatically productive; does not by itself close the all-internal branch.

## Proof
Proof of R919. Let J=(a,x,c) be tight and P sqcup Q an exact two-cover of H-{a,c} with x an endpoint of P. If P=(x) is singleton, then J sqcup Q is already a spanning two-cover of H, impossible. If h were tight, the proposal would two-cover H; hence h is bad, and R3 gives (u,c,x) tight. If P=(x,u,v,...) has order at least three, the proposal (a,x,c,u,v,...) sqcup Q has exactly the two new turns h1=(x,c,u), h2=(c,u,v). Every later turn is inherited from P and the first turn is inherited from J. They cannot both be tight, so at least one is bad; R3 gives (u,c,x) tight or (v,u,c) tight. If x is the last vertex, reverse the construction: for P=(u,x), the proposal (u,a,x,c) sqcup Q has unique hole (u,a,x), forcing (x,a,u); for P=(...,v,u,x), the proposal (...,v,u,a,x,c) sqcup Q has exactly the holes (v,u,a),(u,a,x), forcing (a,u,v) or (x,a,u). This proves R919 without a rail-floor theorem.

Proof of R920. Let J=(a,x,c) be proper. By R4, H-J has an exact two-cover U sqcup V; restoring J gives the named minimum three-cover. For the outer pair {a,c}, either some exact H-{a,c} cover exposes x or every such cover keeps x internal. In the first case apply the just-proved endpoint seam argument of R919.

Assume the all-internal case. Fix any exact return P sqcup Q of H-{a,c}; it exists by R4 applied to the pair deletion, and x is internal, say P=(...,ell,x,r,...). Deleting x splits P into two nonempty tight subpaths P_L,P_R, so P_L sqcup P_R sqcup Q is a literal three-cover of W=H-J. The source U sqcup V is a literal two-cover of the same proper W. R159 therefore gives a graph-intrinsic balanced opposite-sign pair.

It remains to prove the source-rail and shield assertions without R168. Neither U nor V can be singleton. If U=(y), then (x,y) is a valid two-vertex tight path and (x,y) sqcup V is an exact two-cover of H-{a,c} exposing x, contrary to all-internality. Thus both rails have order at least two. Write U=(u0,...,ur) with r>=1. The direct attachment at its left end is bad: if r>=1 and (x,u0,u1) were tight, then (x,u0,...,ur) sqcup V would be an exact H-{a,c} cover exposing x. Hence R3 forces (u1,u0,x) tight. If r=1, this reverse trimer itself uses exactly x and all vertices of U, so (u1,u0,x) sqcup V is an exact H-{a,c} cover exposing x, again impossible. Therefore r>=2 and |U|>=3. The same argument gives |V|>=3.

# R921 — Fully internal crossed recompletion forces dual inward gate anchors and a deep endpoint-capture/Reverse-Ear packet

## Statement
Retain the accepted crossed beyond-ten inward-anchor frame with X={a,b,c,z}, Q=(q_0,...,q_m), m>=6, L=q_0, u=q_1, s=q_{m-1}, R=q_m, D={q_2,q_{m-2}}, W=H-D, Y=Q[0,1] union Q[3,m-3] union Q[m-1,m], and physical middle gates G_3={a,c}, G_4={b,z}. Let T be any exact two-cover of W such that every x in X is internal in T and no selected T-edge has both ends in X; equivalently e_T(X)=0 and delta_T(X)=0.

Then H necessarily has source-labelled GEOM: either a labelled tight Hamilton P4 arising from the crossed/four-cell packet, or an accepted R435 Reverse-Ear output (a reversed old Q-state, tight reverse trimer, or vertex-simple tight cycle) whose Q coordinates are retained.

More precisely, outside an immediate R885/R898 GEOM output, T is the fully fragmented MAX5 face. There exist selected X-Y incidences x_3 y_3 and x_4 y_4 with x_3 in G_3, x_4 in G_4, y_3,y_4 outside {L,R}, such that the associated R898 tested orientations make y_3 a head witness on G_3 and y_4 a tail witness on G_4; at least one of y_3,y_4 lies in the genuine middle Q-cell G_1=Q[3,m-3]. Call such a deep witness y=q_i and its tested gate orientation S.

Apply accepted R682 to S,y in any exact H-V(S) two-cover. In its XET branch the cover contains (R,y,L) or (L,y,R). The first is immediately R435-active against Q. For (L,y,R), probe by q_{i-1} with R518. Either a labelled P4 occurs, or the no-P4 signature forces (y,L,q_{i-1}) tight, whose consecutive Q contacts y=q_i then L=q_0 occur in strict reverse Q-order; R435 gives GEOM.

In the CAP branch R682 supplies a physical endpoint e in {L,R}, an actual selected crossing D_e={e,t} avoiding y, and a lawful R527 capture of e using y. Open the retained R526 actualization certificate. Because the marker is the dimer {e,t} oriented to capture e with witness y, exactly one of the complete reversals (t,e,y) and (y,e,t) is the certified tight terminal actualization turn. If e=L and (y,L,t) is tight, its consecutive Q contacts y then L are already in reverse order, so R435 fires. If instead (t,L,y) is tight, choose z from {q_{i-1},q_{i+1}} distinct from t; such z exists because 3<=i<=m-3. Apply R518 to (t,L,y) with fourth vertex z. Either a labelled P4 occurs, or R518 forces (z,y,L) tight, whose consecutive contacts y then L are reverse-Q, so R435 fires. The e=R case is dual: (t,R,y) is immediately reverse-Q, while from (y,R,t), probing by a neighbor z of y distinct from t yields in the no-P4 branch (R,y,z), whose contacts R then y are reverse-Q. Thus CAP also gives GEOM.

Therefore the fully internal separated/MAX5 face has no protected-contact, payment, or fixed-turn residue: the guaranteed genuinely deep gate witness is consumed locally into a labelled P4 or explicit Reverse-Ear/reversal/cycle geometry. No selected state of T is transported into a gate-deletion cover; only the graph-intrinsic R898 witness turn is reused.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in the accepted crossed R621/R862 frame, m>=6. T is an exact two-cover of W=H-{q_2,q_{m-2}} with e_T(X)=delta_T(X)=0. Uses accepted R885,R894,R898,R682,R526,R527,R518,R435.

## Scope
Noncircular crossed-phase consumer of the fully internal separated face. No R5,R168,R169,R224,R533,generic R358,payment execution,R436,fixed-turn machinery,or computation. Fresh middle-gate deletion covers are used only through accepted R682; selected states are never transported from the source MAX5 cover.

## Applicability
Use when extremal recompletion enters PERSISTENT, or whenever one inward-anchor exact cover has all four X vertices internal and no X-X selected edge. Harvest immediate R885/R898 geometry; otherwise choose the guaranteed deep R898 gate witness and apply R682. Both R682 branches are now locally consumed: XET by R435/R518, CAP by opening the R526 actualization turn and probing it against the old Q path. Thus this face terminates entirely in labelled P4/Reverse-Ear geometry.

## Persistence
Retain T, all eight selected X-Y incidences, the two gate witnesses and tested orientations, the identity of a deep witness y=q_i in G_1, the chosen exact H-V(S) cover used by R682, and the exact geometric output. In CAP also retain endpoint e, selected crossing {e,t}, marker orientation, R527 capture certificate, and the R526 tight actualization turn before its R518/R435 consumption. Gate-deletion covers remain separate representatives from T.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not claim a labelled P4, reverse trimer, reversal, or vertex-simple tight cycle by itself closes H. Does not identify in advance which middle gate carries the deep witness. Does not transport selected states between residues or assert alternative R682 descendants coexist. The theorem eliminates the former protected-first-contact residue only because the retained deep witness and old Q order consume the exact capture actualization turn locally.

## Proof
Fix the accepted crossed inward-anchor frame and an exact two-cover T of W=H-{q_2,q_{m-2}} satisfying e_T(X)=0 and delta_T(X)=0.

1. MAX5 outside existing geometry.
Since delta_T(X)=0, each x in X has selected degree two. Since e_T(X)=0, all its selected neighbours lie in Y, so q=e_T(X,Y)=8. Neither physical middle-gate pair is selected, hence f(T)=2. Apply accepted R885. Its P4 or Reverse-Ear branch is GEOM. Otherwise T is BOUNDED, and accepted R894 identifies p=0,q=8 as MAX5. Apply accepted R898. Its P4-END branch is GEOM. Otherwise retain FOUR-PACKETS: every selected neighbour y of a certifies (y,a,c), every neighbour of c certifies (y,c,a), every neighbour of b certifies (z,b,y), and every neighbour of z certifies (b,z,y).

2. One inward witness on each physical gate.
If both a and c had only L,R as selected neighbours, degree two would force N_T(a)=N_T(c)={L,R}, giving the selected 4-cycle a-L-c-R-a, impossible in a path forest. Choose x_3 in {a,c} with y_3 in N_T(x_3) outside {L,R}; R898 makes y_3 a head witness on S_3=(a,c) or (c,a) according to x_3. The identical argument on {b,z} gives x_4,y_4 outside {L,R}, with y_4 a tail witness on S_4=(z,b) or (b,z).

3. At least one witness is genuinely deep.
Let B={L,u,s,R}. If all eight selected X-Y incidences ended in B, their degree contribution to B would be eight. Each B-vertex has selected degree at most two, so all four would have degree exactly two, both neighbours in X. The four X vertices already have degree two into B. Hence the selected subgraph on X union B would be 2-regular and contain a cycle, impossible. Thus some selected X-Y incidence ends in Y-B=G_1=Q[3,m-3]. Choose the witness on that physical gate to be this incidence. Write it y=q_i, 3<=i<=m-3, and let S be the corresponding tested orientation of G_3 or G_4.

4. Apply the deep-witness endpoint dichotomy.
Apply accepted R682 to S,y in any exact two-cover T' of H-V(S). No selected state of the original T is used in T'; only the graph-intrinsic witness turn on S is reused.

4A. XET.
Suppose R682 gives XET. Then T' contains a tight cross-end trimer K=(R,y,L) or K=(L,y,R). If K=(R,y,L), the consecutive Q contacts R=q_m then y=q_i occur in reverse Q-order m>i, so accepted R435 gives a reversed old state, tight reverse trimer, or vertex-simple tight cycle.

It remains K=(L,y,R). Apply accepted R518 to K with fourth vertex q_{i-1}, distinct from K because i>=3. If the four-set supports a tight Hamilton P4, GEOM holds. Otherwise the no-P4 branch of R518 forces the reverse contact trimer (y,L,q_{i-1}) tight. Along that trimer the consecutive Q contacts y=q_i then L=q_0 occur in strict reverse Q-order and are nonadjacent. R435 therefore gives GEOM.

4B. CAP.
Suppose R682 gives CAP. Then for some e in {L,R}, T' selects a physical carrier/exterior crossing D_e={e,t} with t distinct from y, and R527 may be oriented to capture e using the exact sign witness y. Retain the R526 actualization certificate inside this capture. Because the marker is the dimer {e,t} oriented so that e is the actualization endpoint, the terminal marker test and its R3 reversal are the complete reversal pair (t,e,y) and (y,e,t); exactly one is tight. Call this certified tight trimer J_e.

First let e=L. If J_e=(y,L,t), its consecutive Q contacts y=q_i then L=q_0 are already in reverse order, so R435 gives GEOM. Otherwise J_e=(t,L,y). The two old-Q neighbours q_{i-1},q_{i+1} both exist because 3<=i<=m-3, and at most one equals t. Choose z in {q_{i-1},q_{i+1}} with z!=t. Apply R518 to the tight trimer (t,L,y) with fourth vertex z. If a Hamilton P4 occurs, GEOM holds. Otherwise the no-P4 signature forces the reverse contact (z,y,L) tight. Its consecutive Q contacts y=q_i then L=q_0 occur in strict reverse Q-order, so R435 gives GEOM.

Now let e=R. If J_e=(t,R,y), its consecutive Q contacts R=q_m then y=q_i are reverse-Q, so R435 gives GEOM. Otherwise J_e=(y,R,t). Choose z in {q_{i-1},q_{i+1}} with z!=t. R518 on (y,R,t) with fourth vertex z gives either a Hamilton P4 or, in the no-P4 branch, the reverse contact (R,y,z) tight. The consecutive Q contacts R=q_m then y=q_i are reverse-Q, so R435 gives GEOM.

Thus both R682 branches are completely consumed into labelled P4 or explicit R435 geometry. Therefore every fully internal separated/MAX5 recompletion lies in GEOM. No protected-contact, payment, or fixed-turn residue remains. This proves the theorem.

# R924 — The CCS F(6) difference-class edge ordering has a spanning two-increasing-path cover

## Statement
Let V=GF(2)^6, identified with integers 0,...,63. Order the ordinary edges of K_V by their nonzero XOR-difference class: every edge {x,y} has class d=x xor y, and all edges of class d precede all edges of class e whenever d<e; order inside each class arbitrarily. Then V is partitioned by the two increasing paths P=(1,5,3,4,13,7,11,6,9,25,8,26,14,23,10,21,48,22,49,24,50,30,51,28,44,29,47,27,34,31) and Q=(32,33,37,35,36,45,39,43,38,41,57,40,58,46,55,42,52,20,53,16,54,17,56,18,62,19,60,12,61,15,59,2,63,0). Consequently this 64-vertex Calderbank–Chung–Sturtevant difference-class ordering has increasing path-cover number at most two.

## Hypotheses
Only the explicit GF(2)^6 difference-class ordering is assumed. No asymptotic CCS bound, smallest-counterexample hypothesis, R24 machinery, deletion cover, or within-class edge ordering is used.

## Scope
Exact finite resolution of the classical 64-vertex CCS F(6) candidate. The statement is invariant under arbitrary ordering inside each fixed difference class because consecutive edges of a vertex-simple path have distinct XOR differences.

## Applicability
Use as a certified guardrail against treating the k=6 CCS half-length construction as a counterexample to the two-cover conjecture. The proof exposes a cooperative two-vertex bridge plus endpoint-transfer mechanism that succeeds although neither omitted vertex is singly insertable into the translated f*-rails.

## Persistence
Retain the two explicit vertex lists and their XOR-difference lists as the certificate. Primary exposition is D5/DR5.11 section ccs-f6-two-cover.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not prove the general edge-ordered two-cover conjecture R888, does not prove all CCS F(k) are two-coverable, and does not assert that the translated f*-pair itself spans. The result is only for this explicit F(6) difference-class order, though all within-class tie orders are covered.

## Proof
Identify GF(2)^6 with integers 0,...,63 using bitwise xor as vector addition. In the stated edge order, a vertex-simple path is increasing exactly when its consecutive XOR differences are strictly increasing, since difference classes are ordered 1<...<63 and consecutive path edges have distinct differences.\n\nFor P=(1,5,3,4,13,7,11,6,9,25,8,26,14,23,10,21,48,22,49,24,50,30,51,28,44,29,47,27,34,31), direct xor of consecutive vertices gives\n4,6,7,9,10,12,13,15,16,17,18,20,25,29,31,37,38,39,41,42,44,45,47,48,49,50,52,57,61.\nThis list is strictly increasing, so P is increasing.\n\nFor Q=(32,33,37,35,36,45,39,43,38,41,57,40,58,46,55,42,52,20,53,16,54,17,56,18,62,19,60,12,61,15,59,2,63,0), direct xor of consecutive vertices gives\n1,4,6,7,9,10,12,13,15,16,17,18,20,25,29,30,32,33,37,38,39,41,42,44,45,47,48,49,50,52,57,61,63.\nThis list is strictly increasing, so Q is increasing.\n\nThe P-list has 30 distinct vertices and the Q-list has 34 distinct vertices. Their sets are disjoint. Sorting their union gives every integer 0,1,...,63 exactly once. Thus P and Q are vertex-disjoint and span V, proving path-cover number at most two.\n\nFor mechanism/provenance, start from the CCS recursive translated pair documented in D5/DR5.11: its missing vertices are 20 and 52. Neither is singly insertable into either translated rail. The successful modification deletes initial vertex 0 from the first rail; on the second rail it replaces edge 42-53 of difference31 by 42-52-20-53 of differences30,32,33, which fits between neighboring differences29 and37; finally it appends transferred 0 after63 using difference63>61. This provenance is not needed for validity of the explicit certificate above.

# R925 — Every recursive CCS XOR difference-class ordering has a spanning two-increasing-path cover

## Statement
For every integer k>=5, let F(k) be the edge-ordered complete graph on V=GF(2)^k in which every edge {x,y} has difference class d=x xor y, all edges of class d precede all edges of class e whenever d<e in lexicographic/integer order, and edges inside a fixed class are ordered arbitrarily. Then V(F(k)) can be partitioned into two vertex-disjoint increasing paths. Hence pc_inc(F(k))<=2 for every k>=5. In particular, the entire Calderbank–Chung–Sturtevant difference-class family that gives the classical asymptotic one-half upper fence for the longest single monotone path is nevertheless two-coverable.

## Hypotheses
k>=5. The only edge-order structure used is the GF(2)^k XOR difference-class order. No assumption on the ordering inside one difference class is needed, because consecutive edges of a vertex-simple path have distinct XOR differences.

## Scope
Infinite-family theorem for the classical Calderbank–Chung–Sturtevant obstruction family. The proof is constructive and recursive: it builds two canonical prefix-XOR rails, describes their exact hole recursion, forms an even-cycle multigraph of safe two-hole bridges, chooses a perfect matching of bridges, and inserts every hole.

## Applicability
Use as a guardrail against treating the CCS asymptotic half-length construction as a possible counterexample to the two-cover conjecture. More importantly, the proof supplies a reusable cooperative bridge identity r -> (r-1,r+1,r+2) and an even-cycle matching mechanism for recursively structured holes.

## Persistence
Primary audited exposition: D5/DR5.16 section ccs-all-k-two-cover. Retain the recursive sequences A_k, prefix rails P_k,Q_k, hole recursion H_{k+1}, bridge multigraph Gamma_k, its 2-lift recursion, rail-by-rail bridge-window separation, and the perfect-matching insertion argument.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not prove R888 for arbitrary edge orders, does not prove every edge-ordered complete graph admits such a bridge graph, and does not imply a single monotone path longer than the known CCS bound. The result concerns this explicit XOR difference-class family only.

## Proof
We prove that the entire recursive Calderbank–Chung–Sturtevant difference-class family is two-coverable, even though it is the classical source of the asymptotic one-half longest-monotone-path fence.

1. Difference-class order and the recursive sequences.

For k>=1 identify GF(2)^k with the integers 0,...,2^k-1 in binary. Give every ordinary edge {x,y} the nonzero difference label x xor y, and order the difference classes by their integer (equivalently lexicographic binary) order. Consecutive edges of a vertex-simple path cannot have the same difference because x xor y=y xor z would imply x=z. Therefore within-class tie order is irrelevant: a vertex sequence is increasing exactly when its consecutive XOR differences are strictly increasing.

The k=5 CCS sequence is

A_5=(1,4,6,7,9,10,12,13,15,16,17,18,20,25,29,31).

Its prefix-XOR path and its translate by the total XOR 21 are

P_5=(0,1,5,3,4,13,7,11,6,9,25,8,26,14,23,10),
Q_5=(21,20,16,22,17,24,18,30,19,28,12,29,15,27,2,31).

They are disjoint and together contain all 32 vertices, so F(5) is already two-covered.

For the induction it is convenient to start from the explicit k=6 sequence

A_6=(1,4,6,7,9,10,12,13,15,16,17,18,20,25,29,31,37,38,39,41,42,44,45,47,48,49,50,52,57,61,63).

For k>=6, write A_k=(a_1,...,a_t) and N=2^k. Define A_{k+1} by the CCS recursion

- if t is odd, A_{k+1}=(A_k, N+A_k);
- if t is even, put A_k^-=(a_1 xor a_2,a_3,...,a_t) and set A_{k+1}=(A_k,N+A_k^-).

Here N+A means add the new leading binary 1, so numerically each term is N+a. The first three terms remain 1,4,6, hence a_1 xor a_2=5<6 and A_k^- is increasing whenever it is used. Thus every A_k is strictly increasing. Also A_k ends in N-1 and its penultimate term is at most N-3; these facts hold at k=6 and are preserved by either lift.

Let t_k=|A_k|. Let

s_0=0,
 s_i=a_1 xor ... xor a_i  (1<=i<=t_k),
 c_k=s_{t_k}.

Define the canonical prefix rail

P_k=(s_0,s_1,...,s_{t_k-1})

and the translated rail Q_k=c_k+P_k, where + denotes XOR. Their consecutive difference labels are a_1,...,a_{t_k-1}, so whenever the vertex lists are simple and disjoint they are increasing paths.

At k=6, c_6=32. If c_k=2^{k-1}, then in either recursive branch the low-bit XOR of the two blocks cancels, while the second block has odd length (t_k in the odd branch, t_k-1 in the even branch), so its new leading bit survives. Hence

c_{k+1}=2^k.

Therefore for every k>=6,

c_k=2^{k-1}.

2. Exact hole recursion.

Let S_k={s_0,...,s_{t_k-1}} be the vertex set of P_k, let C_k=S_k union (c_k+S_k), and let

H_k=GF(2)^k \ C_k.

At k=6 the displayed rails are simple and disjoint and

H_6={20,52}.

We now derive H_{k+1} exactly and at the same time prove inductively that P_{k+1},Q_{k+1} remain simple and disjoint.

Fix k>=6, put N=2^k and c=c_k=N/2, and assume P_k,Q_k are disjoint. View GF(2)^{k+1} as two N-vertex layers according to the new leading bit.

If t=t_k is odd, the second block of A_{k+1} is N+A_k. Ignoring the new leading bit, its prefix states are c+S_k. Since Q_{k+1}=N+P_{k+1}, taking the union of the two new rails supplies both leading-bit copies of every low-bit state in

S_k union (c+S_k)=C_k.

Thus

H_{k+1}=H_k union (N+H_k).                                      (2.1)

If t is even, the prefix set of A_k^- is

S_k^-={0,s_2,s_3,...,s_{t-1}}=S_k\{s_1}.

Because s_1=a_1=1, the low-bit projections covered by the two new rails are

S_k union (c+S_k^-)
 = C_k \ {c+1}.

Hence

H_{k+1}=H_k union (N+H_k) union {c+1,N+c+1}.                    (2.2)

In the odd case the new covered set has 2|C_k| elements, exactly the total number of entries in P_{k+1},Q_{k+1}. In the even case it has 2(|C_k|-1) elements, again exactly the total number of entries in the two new rails. Therefore no repetitions or intersections are hidden in the set calculation: the new rails are simple and disjoint.

3. The universal odd-label two-hole bridge.

Suppose an increasing XOR rail contains an edge

x -> z=x xor r

with r odd. Define

u=x xor (r-1),
 v=u xor (r+1).

Then

x xor u=r-1,
 u xor v=r+1,
 v xor z=(r-1) xor (r+1) xor r=r+2,

where the last identity holds for every odd r. Therefore, if the preceding rail label is below r-1, the following rail label is above r+2, and u,v are unused, the one edge of label r may be replaced by

x -> u -> v -> z

with increasing labels

r-1 < r+1 < r+2.

We call this a safe r-bridge. It absorbs exactly two holes without changing the order of any old rail vertex.

4. A bridge graph on all holes.

We construct, for every k>=6, a multigraph Gamma_k whose vertex set is H_k. Every edge of Gamma_k is attached to one safe bridge position on P_k or Q_k, and its two endpoints are exactly the two holes absorbed by that bridge.

Base k=6. The P_6 edge 10-21 has label 31. Its bridge vertices are

10 xor 30=20,
20 xor 32=52.

The neighboring rail labels are 29 and 37, so this is safe. The translated Q_6 edge gives the same unordered hole pair. Thus Gamma_6 consists of two parallel edges on {20,52}, one P-edge and one Q-edge. It is a 2-regular even-cycle multigraph.

For bookkeeping, let R_k be the set of bridge labels used by Gamma_k. Initially R_6={31}. The induction below gives

R_{k+1}=R_k union (N+R_k)                         if t_k is odd,
R_{k+1}=R_k union {N-1} union (N+R_k)             if t_k is even.       (4.1)

Consequently every bridge label is odd, at least 31, distinct bridge labels differ by at least 32, and every r in R_k is at most 2^k-33. These properties are immediate at k=6 and preserved by (4.1). In particular no old bridge label is a_1 or a_2, and no bridge label is the final term of A_k.

Inductive lift of Gamma_k. Again put N=2^k and c=N/2. Write h^0=h and h^1=N+h for the two copies of an old hole h.

Take a P-colored bridge of Gamma_k at label r, with hole pair {u,v}. In A_{k+1}, the first-block occurrence of the same label r has the same old prefix state. Hence the corresponding P_{k+1} bridge is {u^0,v^0}, while translating the rail by the new total XOR N gives the Q_{k+1} bridge {u^1,v^1}. Thus a P-colored old bridge lifts to the two horizontal copies of that edge.

Now take a Q-colored old bridge at label r. If the old P-prefix immediately before r is x, then its Q-hole pair has the form

{c+u,c+v},

where u=x xor (r-1) and v=u xor (r+1). The second block of A_{k+1} contains the label N+r: in the odd branch this is immediate, and in the even branch r survives in A_k^- because r is neither a_1 nor a_2. Immediately before that high label, the low-bit part of the new prefix state is c+x; only its new leading bit depends on parity. Therefore the two bridge vertices for N+r are

(c+u)^{epsilon}, (c+v)^{1-epsilon}

for some epsilon in {0,1}. The Q_{k+1} translate supplies the complementary pair

(c+u)^{1-epsilon}, (c+v)^{epsilon}.

Thus a Q-colored old bridge lifts to the two crossed copies of that edge.

Ignoring the P/Q colors, these two rules say exactly that the old 2-regular multigraph Gamma_k is replaced by a 2-lift on the two copies of H_k. A cycle of length m in a 2-lift becomes either two m-cycles or one 2m-cycle. Since every old cycle is even, every lifted cycle is even.

There is one additional feature in the even-length branch. Formula (2.2) creates the two new holes

z=c+1,
 z^1=N+c+1.

The last first-block edge has label r=N-1. Its initial vertex is s_{t-1}=c xor (N-1), so its bridge vertices are

(c xor (N-1)) xor (N-2)=c+1=z

and

z xor N=N+c+1=z^1.

The translated rail gives the same unordered pair, so these two new holes form an additional two-cycle of parallel P/Q bridge edges. The bridge is safe: the preceding label is at most N-3<N-2, while the next used label is N+(a_1 xor a_2)=N+5>N+1.

Hence, in either parity branch,

Gamma_{k+1} is a disjoint union of even cycles.                 (4.2)

The bridge positions inherited from old edges remain safe because their local neighboring labels are unchanged in the first block and are shifted uniformly by N in the second block. In the even branch the only altered beginning of A_k^- is 5, while every inherited bridge label is at least 31. The special bridge was checked above. Finally, on each fixed rail, distinct bridge labels have disjoint ordered windows [r-1,r+2], because distinct labels in R_k differ by at least 32. The same bridge label may occur once on each of the two rails; those replacements are on disjoint vertex sequences and do not interact. Hence any collection of safe bridges selected on either rail may be performed simultaneously.

5. Perfect matching and spanning two-cover.

Every finite even cycle has a perfect matching; the same is true for a two-cycle of parallel edges. By (4.2), Gamma_k therefore has a perfect matching M_k.

For every matched edge of Gamma_k, perform the associated safe bridge replacement on its designated rail P_k or Q_k. Distinct matched bridge edges use disjoint hole pairs, so every hole is inserted exactly once and no inserted vertex is repeated. The original rails already partition GF(2)^k\H_k. Thus the two modified rails are vertex-disjoint and together contain every vertex of GF(2)^k.

Each modified rail remains increasing: every individual replacement substitutes r by r-1,r+1,r+2 inside its certified seam; on each rail the windows for distinct selected bridge labels are separated, while equal-label replacements can only occur on the two different rails and therefore do not interact. Therefore the two modified rails form a spanning cover by two increasing paths.

This proves that for every k>=6 the CCS difference-class ordering F(k) has increasing path-cover number at most two. Together with the explicit k=5 pair above, the conclusion holds for every k>=5.

The theorem is specific to the CCS XOR difference-class family. It does not prove R888 for arbitrary edge orders. Its significance is that the entire classical family giving the asymptotic (1/2+o(1)) upper fence for the longest single monotone path nevertheless has a spanning two-path cover, by a recursive cooperative-absorption mechanism rather than by one long path.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R925.md -->
