# R927 — Global absence of universal source crossings saturates one middle layer and forces the odd uniform residue

## Statement
Let H be a hypothetical smallest counterexample to the boundary-tournament two-path-cover conjecture. Call a literal exact singleton-deletion source C_x=A|B of H-x universally crossed at z in A if every literal exact two-nonempty-path cover of H-z selects an adjacency with one endpoint in A-{z} and the other in B; define the dual notion for z in B.

Then at least one of the following holds.

(U) There exist a physical source cover C_x=A|B and a vertex z on one source rail which is universally crossed relative to that source.

(M) There is an integer k>=2 with |V(H)|=2k+1 such that every k-subset of V(H) supports a Hamilton tight path and no (k+1)-subset supports one.

More strongly, if (U) fails globally, fix ANY exact source C_x=A|B and write |A|=k, |B|=l. Then for every deletion label y and every partition V(H)-{y}=S disjoint-union T with |S|=k and |T|=l, there is a literal exact H-y two-cover whose rail supports are exactly S|T. Hence every k-set and every l-set of H is Hamiltonian. The no-two-cover condition then forces k=l, giving (M).

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest counterexample, so accepted R4 supplies pc(H)=3 and pc(H[W])<=2 for every nonempty proper W. Tight paths are vertex-simple and contiguous subpaths are tight; singletons and dimers are vacuously tight.

## Scope
Global O4 parent reduction. The proof uses smallest-counterexample minimality plus literal singleton-deletion cover manipulation. It does not use R24, payment, capture, compatibility graphs, rail-incidence roots, extremal cover families, Reverse Ear, or boundary antisymmetry beyond the ambient tight-path conventions.

## Applicability
Use before splitting into the two current D17 research arms. If a universal source crossing is found, enter Universal Source-Crossing Absorption. If none exists anywhere, the theorem immediately gives the odd uniform middle-layer residue. The stronger partition-saturation conclusion may be reused inside the uniform arm whenever actual k|k support partitions are needed.

## Persistence
In branch U retain the exact source C_x=A|B, offending vertex z, and the universal quantifier over actual exact H-z covers. In the quiet proof retain each literal singleton source used in the three-substitution exchange; no Hamilton order is transported between distinct covers. In branch M retain only support-level Hamiltonicity of every k-set and non-Hamiltonicity of every (k+1)-set; no canonical Hamilton order is asserted.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not absorb the universal-crossing branch and does not prove the uniform middle-layer residue impossible. Does not synchronize Hamilton orders across different supports or deletion fibers. Does not infer Hamiltonicity of subsets smaller than k by arbitrary restriction. Does not use or imply a monotone compatibility potential.

## Proof
Let H be a smallest counterexample. By R4, pc(H)=3 and every proper induced subsystem has path-cover number at most two.

1. Exact singleton sources and the rail floor. Since any set of at most four vertices is covered by two vacuous paths of order at most two, |V(H)|>=5. For each x, H-x has path-cover number at most two. If it is Hamiltonian, split a Hamilton order into two contiguous subpaths of orders at least two; if its cover number is two, take a minimum two-cover. Thus exact two-nonempty-path singleton sources exist. Moreover no exact H-x two-cover can contain a singleton rail (y): the other rail together with the vacuous dimer (x,y) would two-cover H. Hence every source rail has at least two vertices.

2. Quiet deleted-label substitution. Fix ANY exact source
  C_x=A|B
of H-x and z in A. Put S=A-{z}; S and B are nonempty. Suppose z is not universally crossed relative to this source. Choose an exact two-cover T of H-z having no selected adjacency between S and B.

Let R be the T-rail containing x. If all vertices of R other than x lie in only one of the classes S,B, then the other T-rail cannot mix S and B either. Since both classes are nonempty and the two rails cover S union B union {x}, the rail R must contain all of one class together with x and the other rail all of the opposite class. Hence either S union {x} or B union {x} is Hamiltonian.

Otherwise R-x meets both S and B. Because no selected S-B adjacency exists, x is internal on R and separates one contiguous S-side from one contiguous B-side. The other T-rail is monochromatic. If it is an S-rail, then the B-side of R contains all of B and that side together with x is a Hamilton path on B union {x}. If the other rail is a B-rail, then the S-side of R contains all of S and together with x is a Hamilton path on S union {x}. Again one of the two augmented supports S+x or B+x is Hamiltonian.

The B+x possibility is impossible: the original source rail A is Hamiltonian, disjoint from B+x, and A union (B+x)=V(H), so those two paths would two-cover H. Therefore S+x is Hamiltonian. Pair an actual Hamilton path on S+x with the untouched original B-rail. This gives a literal exact H-z cover with support partition
  (A-{z}+{x}) | B.
The dual statement holds for z in B. No Hamilton order has been transported from one fiber to another; only a newly certified support path and the untouched opposite source rail are used.

3. Three quiet substitutions perform one support exchange. Assume now that alternative (U) fails globally, meaning no vertex is universally crossed relative to any exact singleton source. Fix an exact source C_x=A|B and choose a in A, b in B. Apply the quiet substitution three times.

First, from source C_x and deleted vertex a obtain the exact H-a cover
  (A-{a}+{x}) | B.
Second, regard that literal cover as the source at a and delete b. Since b lies on its B-rail, obtain the exact H-b cover
  (A-{a}+{x}) | (B-{b}+{a}).
Third, regard this cover as the source at b and delete x, which lies on its first rail. Obtain the exact H-x cover
  (A-{a}+{b}) | (B-{b}+{a}).
Thus any one-for-one exchange a<->b between the two support classes of a fixed H-x source is realizable by actual singleton covers. The intermediate covers are alternatives, used sequentially; no simultaneous currentness is asserted.

4. Saturation of one fiber. Write |A|=k and |B|=l. The graph of k-subsets of V(H)-{x}, joined when they differ by one exchange, is connected. Repeatedly applying the preceding three-substitution move therefore shows: for EVERY k-subset S of V(H)-{x}, there is an exact H-x two-cover with supports
  S | ((V(H)-{x})-S).
Hence every k|l support partition of H-x is realized by actual Hamilton rails.

5. The same side sizes occur at every deletion label. Let y be any vertex. If y=x use the original source. If y lies in A, one quiet substitution from C_x gives the exact H-y source
  (A-{y}+{x}) | B,
whose rail sizes are k,l. If y lies in B, use the dual source
  A | (B-{y}+{x}).
Starting from this size-k|l source at y and repeating the exchange argument of step 4 saturates EVERY k|l partition of H-y.

Consequently every k-subset of V(H) is Hamiltonian: given such a set S, choose y outside S and realize S as the k-rail of an H-y cover. Likewise every l-subset is Hamiltonian.

6. The side sizes must be equal. We have
  |V(H)|=k+l+1.
Suppose k<l. Choose any Hamilton l-set and one Hamilton order on it. Because l>=k+1, a contiguous subpath of that order on exactly k+1 vertices is tight. Its complement in H has
  k+l+1-(k+1)=l
vertices, hence is Hamiltonian by the preceding saturation. These two disjoint tight paths span H, contradiction. The case l<k is dual. Therefore k=l, so |V(H)|=2k+1.

Every k-set is Hamiltonian. No (k+1)-set can be Hamiltonian, because its k-vertex complement is Hamiltonian and the two Hamilton paths would span H. This is alternative (M).

Thus if (U) does not occur, (M) must occur, proving the dichotomy and the stronger fiberwise partition-saturation statement.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R927.md -->

# R933 — Two-ended Hamilton absorber gives a two-hole spanning splice

## Statement
Let H be a finite exact-reversal tight-turn system with pc(H)>1. Let X and Y partition V(H), and let Y have a literal two-path cover U sqcup V with both rails nonempty. Choose an endpoint x of U and an endpoint y of V. In one displayed orientation write U=(x,u_1,...,u_r), V=(v_0,...,v_{s-1},y), and suppose X union {x,y} has a Hamilton tight path Q=(y,q_1,...,q_t,x); the other three endpoint-role choices are exact duals.

Then concatenating V-y, Q, and U-x gives a vertex-simple spanning word K whose complete uncertified-turn set consists of at most the two attachment turns alpha=(v_{s-1},y,q_1) when the left residual seam exists and beta=(q_t,x,u_1) when the right residual seam exists. Every other consecutive turn of K is certified. Hence if pc(H)>1 at least one existing attachment turn is bad, and exact reversal gives reverse(alpha) OR reverse(beta), omitting nonexistent holes.

Stronger pc(H)>2 seam clause: if pc(H)>2, then BOTH residual seams must exist and BOTH alpha and beta are bad. Indeed if at most one bad attachment turn existed, cutting the vertex-simple spanning word K at one edge of that bad triple would delete the only bad consecutive turn and leave two contiguous tight paths spanning H. Therefore a one-hole configuration, or a two-hole configuration with exactly one bad hole, is impossible when pc(H)>2. By exact reversal, both reverse(alpha) and reverse(beta) are then tight simultaneously.

## Hypotheses
Finite exact-reversal tight-turn system; X,Y partition V(H); U,V are vertex-disjoint nonempty tight paths covering Y; x,y are endpoints on different rails in the required opposite roles; X+x+y has a Hamilton tight path exposing y,x as displayed. The simultaneous-two-hole conclusion additionally assumes pc(H)>2.

## Scope
Order-free and size-free absorber splice theorem. The new clause strengthens the existing complete two-hole ledger specifically in the pc>2 regime and handles all residual-seam degeneracies.

## Applicability
Use R572 as before for a mate disjunction under pc>1. In a hypothetical smallest counterexample or any pc>2 system, use the stronger clause: both attachment holes must physically exist and both are bad, so both exact reversed turns are simultaneously certified. This is a seam/window fact, not a standalone absorber hierarchy.

## Persistence
Retain X,Y, literal rails U,V, chosen endpoint roles x,y, exact Hamilton absorber order Q, the vertex-simple spanning word K, both possible attachment turns, and whether each seam exists. In the pc>2 clause retain both reversed bad turns simultaneously.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert existence of the endpoint-role Hamilton absorber. Does not apply when x,y lie on the same residue rail. The pc>2 clause does not by itself close H; it supplies simultaneous exact reversed seam turns only after the complete bad-turn ledger is verified.

## Proof
In the displayed endpoint orientation form
  K=(v_0,...,v_{s-1},y,q_1,...,q_t,x,u_1,...,u_r),
omitting an empty residual piece when U-x or V-y is empty. Because X,Y partition V(H), Q spans X union {x,y}, and Q meets U sqcup V only at x,y, K is vertex-simple and spans H.

Every consecutive triple wholly inside the surviving V segment is tight, every triple wholly inside Q is tight, and every triple wholly inside the surviving U segment is tight. At the left attachment the only possibly uncertified consecutive turn is alpha=(v_{s-1},y,q_1), when all three displayed vertices exist. At the right attachment the only possibly uncertified turn is beta=(q_t,x,u_1), when all three exist. Thus the complete uncertified-turn set of K is a subset of {alpha,beta}, with absent seams omitted.

If every existing attachment turn were tight, K itself would be a Hamilton tight path, contradicting pc(H)>1. Hence at least one existing hole is bad. Exact reversal antisymmetry gives the usual mate disjunction reverse(alpha) OR reverse(beta).

Now assume pc(H)>2. We prove that both seams exist and both holes are bad. Suppose instead that the complete bad-turn list of K has size at most one. It cannot have size zero, by the preceding paragraph, so let gamma be its unique bad consecutive turn. Since gamma is a consecutive triple of the vertex-simple spanning word K, choose either of the two word edges lying inside gamma and cut K at that edge. The two resulting contiguous subwords are vertex-disjoint, cover V(H), and may be singletons or dimers. Any consecutive triple lying wholly inside either subword is also a consecutive triple of K distinct from gamma, hence tight: the cut destroys gamma and creates no new turns. Therefore the two subwords are tight paths spanning H, contradicting pc(H)>2.

Thus K has at least two bad turns. Its complete uncertified-turn set has at most the two holes alpha,beta, while every other turn is certified tight. Hence both alpha and beta must exist and both must be bad. Exact reversal gives both reverse(alpha) and reverse(beta) tight simultaneously. In particular either residual seam being absent would leave at most one possible bad turn and is impossible under pc(H)>2.

The other three endpoint-role choices are obtained by forming the corresponding role-correct concatenation and repeating the same complete-window argument; no tight path is silently reversed. This proves the strengthened theorem.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R933.md -->

# R936 — Threshold matching duality and exact one-sided rotations for increasing path covers

## Statement
Let G=K_V be a complete graph with a strict total edge order represented by distinct real labels lambda(uv), and let n=|V|. For any real threshold vector tau=(tau_v), form a balanced bipartite graph B_tau with copies V_out,V_in and edge u_out v_in exactly when tau_u<lambda(uv)<tau_v. Then
  pc_inc(G)=n-max_tau nu(B_tau)
           =min_tau max_{X subseteq V} (|X|-|N_{B_tau}(X)|).

Moreover fix any spanning increasing k-path cover F and orient its components increasingly. Let L(v) be the label of the incoming F-edge, with L(v)=-infinity at a source, and U(v) the outgoing label, with U(v)=+infinity at a terminal. Define
  u_out v_in in B^- iff L(u)<lambda(uv)<=L(v),
  u_out v_in in B^+ iff U(u)<=lambda(uv)<U(v).
Then the F-edges form a matching of size n-k in both graphs. Every size-(n-k) matching in B^- compiles to a spanning increasing k-path cover with exactly the same source set as F; every size-(n-k) matching in B^+ compiles to one with exactly the same terminal set. Thus B^- and B^+ are exact collision-free one-sided rotation systems.

ORDERED-1-FACTORIZATION BRIDGE. Suppose in addition that the edge order is by perfect-matching rounds M_1<...<M_{n-1}; write c(uv)=t for uv in M_t, and use the discrete conventions L(source)=0, U(terminal)=n. Call an oriented round-t edge u->v interval-compatible when L(u)<t<U(v). Every interval-compatible oriented edge lies in exactly one of the following PRIORITY classes:
(LOWER) t<=L(v), so u_out v_in belongs to B^-;
(UPPER) t>L(v) and U(u)<=t, so u_out v_in belongs to B^+;
(ACTIVE-ACTIVE) L(v)<t<U(u), so both u and v are active at round t, meaning L(w)<t<U(w), and they lie on distinct current path components.
Thus the wider interval-compatible edge reservoir decomposes into two safe one-sided rotation classes plus a genuinely two-sided cross-component remainder. Combined with any round-abundance count, this classification is only a localization of where the compulsory compatible edges live; it is not itself an augmentation theorem.

## Hypotheses
General threshold statements: finite complete graph with distinct edge labels and a spanning increasing k-path cover F where used. Ordered-factorization bridge: n even, edges partitioned into perfect matching rounds with all M_i before M_j for i<j; L,U are round indices with source/terminal conventions 0,n.

## Scope
Pure edge-ordered graph parent combining movable-threshold Hall duality, exact one-sided rotations, and the Independent-safe lower/upper/active-active classification for ordered 1-factorizations.

## Applicability
Use the threshold identity for R888/Hall reformulations. Use B^- or B^+ for legitimate one-sided rotations. In ordered 1-factorizations, classify every interval-compatible round edge by the priority split before combining compatible-edge abundance with rotation arguments: only LOWER/UPPER are automatically safe matching moves; ACTIVE-ACTIVE is the genuinely two-sided cross-component residue.

## Persistence
Retain the threshold vector and matched arcs. For rotations retain F, source/terminal sets, L,U, and which one-sided graph is used. For the ordered-factorization bridge retain round t, orientation u->v, its priority class, and if active-active the two distinct current components containing u,v.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not prove deficiency <=2, R888, or the ordered-1-factorization two-cover theorem. Does not say all interval-compatible edges lie in one safe matching graph. ACTIVE-ACTIVE edges are not automatically legal simultaneous rotations. Does not preserve both source and terminal sets or all endpoint labels simultaneously.

## Proof
The general threshold-matching identity and the exact B^-/B^+ source-/terminal-preserving rotation conclusions are precisely the accepted theorem R932. It remains only to prove the ordered-1-factorization bridge.

Assume E(K_n)=M_1 disjoint-union ... disjoint-union M_{n-1}, ordered by rounds, and let F be a spanning increasing path cover. Write c(uv)=t when uv lies in M_t. Use L(source)=0 and U(terminal)=n. Let u->v be interval-compatible at round t, so
  L(u)<t<U(v).                                      (1)

Apply the following priority rule.

If t<=L(v), then together with (1) we have
  L(u)<t<=L(v),
which is exactly the discrete lower-cut condition for u_out v_in to belong to B^-.

Otherwise t>L(v). If U(u)<=t, then together with (1) we have
  U(u)<=t<U(v),
which is exactly the upper-cut condition for u_out v_in to belong to B^+.

Finally suppose neither of the preceding cases holds. Then t>L(v) and t<U(u). Combining these inequalities with (1) gives
  L(u)<t<U(u),
  L(v)<t<U(v).
Thus both u and v are active at round t.

It remains to show that active u and v cannot lie on the same current path component. Along any oriented increasing path of F, the selected edge colors strictly increase. Relative to a fixed round t, there is at most one vertex w whose incoming selected color is below t and whose outgoing selected color is above t: it is the unique vertex lying between the last selected edge color below t and the first selected edge color above t, with the source/terminal conventions covering the ends. If the component itself uses an edge of color t, then no vertex of that component is active because the tail has U=t and the head has L=t. Therefore every current component contains at most one active vertex at round t. Since u and v are distinct endpoints of an ordinary edge, if both are active they lie on distinct components.

The three priority classes are exhaustive and disjoint by construction: LOWER is tested first; among the remaining edges UPPER is tested second; if both tests fail the displayed active-active inequalities hold. LOWER and UPPER inherit the safe one-sided matching interpretation from R932. The ACTIVE-ACTIVE class is only a cross-component location statement; no simultaneous splice legality follows. This proves the strengthening R936.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R936.md -->

# R942 — A minimum-side disconnected interaction reduces to fixed-complement-size recurrence

## Statement
Let H be a hypothetical smallest boundary-tournament counterexample. Among all literal singleton-deletion source covers C_p=A|B and all universally crossing vertices z on either source rail, choose one with offending rail size |A| minimum, with z in A. Assume A-z is non-Hamiltonian and retain the actual source order A=L-z-R with L,R nonempty. Put W=H-{p,z}. For any exact two-cover F of W define the class-interaction graph J(F) on {L,R,B} by joining two source classes when F selects an adjacency between them.

DISCONNECTED INTERACTION. If some exact W-cover F has disconnected J(F), then the accepted R931 alternatives hold: H has a spanning two-cover, H lies in the odd uniform middle-layer residue, or there is an actual singleton-deletion universal-crossing source whose offending rail size equals the Hamilton support obtained by joining the two nonisolated classes. The recurrence may be equal or larger than the original minimum size and must be retained.

CONNECTED-INTERACTION SUPPORT FORM. Suppose instead that J(F) is connected for EVERY exact W two-cover F. Then
  pc(L union R)=pc(L union B)=pc(R union B)=2.
Conversely these three equalities imply that J(F) is connected for every exact W two-cover. Thus the hard residue is equivalently three nonempty Hamilton atoms L,R,B such that every two-atom union is non-Hamiltonian but exactly two-coverable, while W itself has exact path-cover number two.

PAIR-RESTRICTION LEDGER. For any chosen exact W-cover F, let b_L,b_R,b_B be the numbers of maximal source-class blocks in its two literal rails, let e_LR,e_LB,e_RB count selected transitions of the three pair types, and put theta=e_LR+e_LB+e_RB. For distinct X,Y let c_XY(F) be the number of path components of the restriction F[X union Y]. Then
  c_XY=b_X+b_Y-e_XY,
  c_LR+c_LB+c_RB=4+theta.
In the hard residue c_XY>=2 for every pair. Hence with sigma_XY=c_XY-2,
  sigma_LR+sigma_LB+sigma_RB=theta-2.

RAINBOW-HINGE / SPLIT-STAR DICHOTOMY. Contract each maximal L-,R-,B-block along the two F rails to its class label. Exactly one of the following structural forms occurs.

(RAINBOW HINGE) Some rail contains three consecutive maximal blocks X-K-Y with X,K,Y all distinct. The two literal selected block-boundary states are differently typed transitions sharing the same actual middle F-block K.

(SPLIT-STAR WEAVE) No rail has such a rainbow triple. Then both rails are nontrivial and each alternates between exactly two source classes. Their two class-pairs are distinct and share a unique center K; after naming the leaves X,Y, one rail has support X union K_1 and alternates only X/K, the other has support K_2 union Y and alternates only K/Y, where K=K_1 disjoint-union K_2 with K_1,K_2 nonempty. The retained literal source order on K necessarily contains at least one consecutive source state with one endpoint in K_1 and the other in K_2, hence a graph-intrinsic source adjacency crossing the two F rails.

No identification is made between F-block internal orders and the original source orders. This dichotomy is the canonical arbitrary-fragmentation entrance for the connected branch: the remaining absorption theorem must consume the two current seam types of a rainbow hinge or the split-star weave, or else return to the disconnected/recurrent alternatives above.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest counterexample. Universal crossing is the physical selected-adjacency notion. The chosen (p,A|B,z) globally minimizes the offending universal-crossing rail size. A-z is non-Hamiltonian, so z is internal in A=L-z-R with L,R nonempty. W=H-{p,z}. Every cover mentioned is a literal exact two-nonempty-path cover. The connected-interaction clauses apply only after the disconnected R931 alternatives are excluded.

## Scope
Canonical Arm-A parent strengthening accepted R931. It is independent of transition multiplicity and replaces theta-shape taxonomy by a support-only pairwise non-Hamiltonicity characterization plus one exact two-rail block-word dichotomy.

## Applicability
Use before any detailed fragmentation case analysis. If a disconnected J-cover exists, invoke the R931 closure/uniform/recurrence alternatives with recurrence retained. Otherwise choose any exact W-cover and work only with its rainbow hinge or split-star weave. The pair-restriction slack identity is bookkeeping, not a monotone potential.

## Persistence
Retain the literal source order L-z-R and B, the exact W-cover F, all maximal source-class blocks and selected interblock states. In a rainbow hinge retain both boundary states and the entire middle block. In a split-star weave retain the actual partition K=K_1 union K_2, both rail words, and at least one literal source-order K_1|K_2 crossing state. No source-order/current-cover order synchronization is assumed.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not consume the rainbow hinge or split-star weave into a spanning two-cover. Does not make theta or the sigma ledger a global descent. Does not eliminate the equal/larger R931 recurrence. Does not assert F-blocks are intervals of the original source orders. Does not license inserting the omitted label p or z without complete seam verification.

## Proof
The disconnected-interaction alternatives are exactly accepted R931, so assume they have been excluded and prove the new connected-branch structure.

1. W and the pair unions. The common residue W=H-{p,z} is a proper induced subsystem, so smallest-counterexample minimality gives pc(W)<=2. If W were Hamiltonian, a Hamilton path on W together with the vacuous tight dimer (p,z) would be a spanning two-cover of H. Thus pc(W)=2.

Each of L,R,B is a nonempty literal tight source path. Hence each pair union, such as L union B, has path-cover number at most two. Suppose L union B were Hamiltonian. A Hamilton path on L union B together with the literal source path R would be an exact two-cover of W whose class-interaction graph isolates R, contradicting the hard assumption that every exact W-cover has connected J. Thus pc(L union B)=2. The same argument gives pc(R union B)=2. Also pc(L union R)=2; this is already A-z and is non-Hamiltonian by hypothesis. Therefore all three pair unions have path-cover number exactly two.

Conversely suppose all three pair unions are non-Hamiltonian. If some exact W-cover F had disconnected J(F), accepted R931's elementary isolation argument says one source class is a pure F-rail and the union of the other two classes is Hamiltonian in the other F-rail. This contradicts one of the three pairwise non-Hamiltonicity statements. Hence every exact W-cover has connected J. This proves the equivalence.

2. Pair-restriction ledger. Fix any exact W-cover F. Split its two literal rails into maximal L-,R-,B-blocks. Let b_X be the number of X-blocks and e_XY the number of selected F-adjacencies between an X-block and a Y-block. The quotient obtained by contracting blocks is a disjoint union of two paths, so
  b_L+b_R+b_B=2+theta,
where theta=e_LR+e_LB+e_RB.

Now restrict F to X union Y. Its quotient is obtained by deleting all Z-block vertices and incident edges from the two-path block forest. Therefore it remains a forest with b_X+b_Y vertices and exactly e_XY edges. The number of path components of F[X union Y] is consequently
  c_XY=b_X+b_Y-e_XY.
Summing over LR,LB,RB counts every b_X twice and every transition count once:
  c_LR+c_LB+c_RB
   =2(b_L+b_R+b_B)-theta
   =2(2+theta)-theta
   =4+theta.
In the hard residue each pair support has path-cover number two, so every restriction F[X union Y] has at least two components. Put sigma_XY=c_XY-2>=0. Subtracting six from the preceding identity gives
  sigma_LR+sigma_LB+sigma_RB=theta-2.
No monotonicity claim is used.

3. Rainbow-hinge/split-star dichotomy. Replace each maximal source-class block along each F-rail by its label. Adjacent labels in a rail word are distinct. If some rail contains three consecutive labels X,K,Y which are pairwise distinct, retain the corresponding three actual maximal blocks. The two literal selected adjacencies at the block boundaries have types XK and KY, hence are differently typed transitions sharing the same actual middle block K. This is the RAINBOW-HINGE alternative.

Assume no rainbow triple occurs. In any rail word of length at least three, if consecutive labels are a_i,a_{i+1},a_{i+2}, then a_i!=a_{i+1} and a_{i+1}!=a_{i+2}; absence of a three-distinct window forces a_{i+2}=a_i. Inductively every rail word alternates between at most two fixed labels.

Neither rail can contribute no interaction edge. If one rail consisted of a single block, the other rail could realize at most one source-class pair under the preceding two-label conclusion, so J(F) would have at most one edge and be disconnected. Hence both rails have at least two blocks and each realizes exactly one unordered class pair. These two pairs cannot be equal, again because J(F) is connected. On the three labels L,R,B, two distinct pair edges which form a connected graph share a unique center K. Name the other endpoints X and Y. Thus one rail alternates only between X and K and the other only between K and Y.

The leaf X occurs only on the first rail and Y only on the second. The center K occurs on both rails, because each rail realizes its center-leaf interaction. Let K_1 and K_2 be the subsets of K lying on the first and second rails. They are nonempty, disjoint, and cover K, giving
  V(P)=X union K_1,
  V(Q)=K_2 union Y.
This is the SPLIT-STAR WEAVE support form. Finally retain the original literal Hamilton source order on K. Since K_1 and K_2 are both nonempty, scanning that linear order from one end to the other must encounter two consecutive source vertices lying in different parts at the first change of part. That literal source adjacency has one endpoint on each F-rail. Its tightness is inherited from the source path K and is graph-intrinsic; no relation between the internal F-block orders and the source order has been asserted.

The two alternatives are mutually exclusive by construction and exhaustive. Together with accepted R931 they give precisely the claimed canonical arbitrary-fragmentation entrance. This proves R942.

# R945 — Role-correct endpoint-return Hall cycles reduce to R435 geometry or a directed triangle

## Statement
Let Omega be a finite boundary tournament with |Omega|>=4 such that Omega is non-Hamiltonian but every one-vertex deletion Omega-y is Hamiltonian. Build the complete endpoint-core incidence graph with left vertices y in Omega and right vertices Omega-{y,r}; join y to Omega-{y,r} when some actual Hamilton path on Omega-y has r as a physical endpoint.

(1) This bipartite graph satisfies Hall, so there exists a matching saturating all left labels. Writing the matched right core as Omega-{y,f(y)} gives a functional digraph y->f(y). Matched 2-cycles are impossible, so every directed cycle has length at least three.

(2) Choose, among all left-saturating endpoint-core matchings, one whose shortest directed cycle has minimum possible length, and choose one such shortest cycle C=(y_0,...,y_{t-1}). For each matched edge choose an ACTUAL Hamilton path P_i on Omega-y_i realizing endpoint y_{i+1}=f(y_i), and retain whether that endpoint is the HEAD or TAIL of the certified path. Compare each consecutive pair P_i,P_{i+1} by accepted R435.

Then either some adjacent comparison yields an explicit R435 reversal, reverse-trimer, or proper tight cycle, OR t=3. In particular, outside explicit R435 geometry an extremal endpoint-return matching has a directed triangle as its shortest cycle.

More precisely, for t>=4 and R435-quiet adjacent comparisons, any change of endpoint role HEAD<->TAIL would make P_i have endpoints {y_{i+1},y_{i+2}}, yielding an unused skip-one endpoint core Omega-{y_i,y_{i+2}} and a rematching that shortens C. Hence all matched roles around C are equal. In the all-HEAD case P_i begins y_{i+1},y_{i+2},y_{i+3}; non-Hamiltonicity says (y_{i+1},y_{i+2},y_{i+3}) is bad, contradiction. The all-TAIL case is the exact certified-direction dual. No reversal of a tight path is used.

## Hypotheses
Finite Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament Omega, |Omega|>=4, Omega non-Hamiltonian, and Omega-y Hamiltonian for every y. R435 is used only in its contact-monotonicity alternative after retaining explicit path orientations.

## Scope
Role-correct repair of the endpoint-return matching argument in D17/DR17.42. Pure hypohamiltonian-block theorem; no smallest-counterexample or source-recurrence hypotheses are needed.

## Applicability
Use inside a saturated deletion-Hamiltonian block. First choose an extremal left-saturating endpoint-core matching and preserve actual HEAD/TAIL roles of matched endpoints. Then either retain explicit R435 geometry or a shortest directed triangle. Do not orient an arbitrary puncture path from a matched endpoint and do not infer that every cycle of an arbitrary matching is triangular.

## Persistence
Retain the matched right cores, functional map f, shortest cycle, actual Hamilton puncture paths P_i, each matched endpoint role HEAD/TAIL, and any rematched skip-one core used in the shortening argument. Triangle output is unoriented beyond the actual recorded roles unless further certified.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not say every endpoint-return cycle is a triangle. Does not say a matched endpoint can be chosen as a path head. Does not make the three forward cyclic turns uniformly bad in a triangle with mixed roles. Does not consume R435 output or the triangle into a spanning two-cover.

## Proof
Build the endpoint-core incidence graph B. For each y in Omega, any Hamilton path on Omega-y has two distinct physical endpoints r,s, so y has at least two distinct right neighbors Omega-{y,r} and Omega-{y,s}. A right core R=Omega-{a,b} can be adjacent only to left labels a or b, because an incidence y-R means R=Omega-{y,r} for some endpoint r. Hence every right vertex has degree at most two. For every left subset S,
  2|S| <= e(S,N(S)) <= 2|N(S)|,
so Hall holds and a matching saturating all left labels exists.

Write the matched core of y as Omega-{y,f(y)}. Then f(y)!=y. If y->r and r->y were both matched, both left labels would be matched to the same right core Omega-{y,r}, impossible. Thus the functional digraph f has no directed 2-cycle; every directed cycle has length at least three.

Among all left-saturating matchings choose one for which the length of a shortest directed cycle is minimum. Let
  C: y_0 -> y_1 -> ... -> y_{t-1} -> y_0
be such a shortest cycle. For each i choose an actual Hamilton path P_i on Omega-y_i which exposes the matched endpoint y_{i+1}. Record epsilon_i=H if y_{i+1} is the first vertex of P_i and epsilon_i=T if it is the last vertex. No path is reversed.

Compare P_i with P_{i+1}. Their common vertex set is Omega-{y_i,y_{i+1}}. If R435 produces a reversal, reverse trimer, or proper tight cycle, retain that output and the theorem is proved. Hence assume every adjacent comparison is R435-quiet, so the common vertices occur in increasing P_i-order along P_{i+1}.

We first determine the position of y_{i+2} in P_i. It is a common vertex. If epsilon_{i+1}=H, then y_{i+2} is the first vertex of P_{i+1}, hence the first common contact along P_{i+1}; monotonicity makes it the first common vertex of P_i. If epsilon_i=H, the only initial noncommon vertex of P_i is its head y_{i+1}, so P_i begins (y_{i+1},y_{i+2},...). If epsilon_i=T, its terminal noncommon vertex is y_{i+1}, so the first common vertex is the actual head and P_i begins (y_{i+2},...). Dually, if epsilon_{i+1}=T, then y_{i+2} is the last common contact along P_{i+1}; monotonicity makes it the last common vertex of P_i. Thus if epsilon_i=H, P_i ends (...,y_{i+2}), while if epsilon_i=T, P_i ends (...,y_{i+2},y_{i+1}).

Consequently, whenever epsilon_i != epsilon_{i+1}, the actual path P_i has endpoint set exactly {y_{i+1},y_{i+2}}. Therefore y_i is incident to the additional endpoint core
  R'=Omega-{y_i,y_{i+2}}.
Assume t>=4. The right core R' is unused by the chosen matching. Indeed only left labels y_i and y_{i+2} can be adjacent to R'. The first is currently matched to Omega-{y_i,y_{i+1}}. The second is currently matched to Omega-{y_{i+2},y_{i+3}}, which is different because t>=4 gives y_{i+3}!=y_i. No other left label can use R'. Rematch y_i from its old core to R'. All other matched cores stay unchanged, so this is again a left-saturating matching. Its functional digraph has the directed cycle
  y_i -> y_{i+2} -> y_{i+3} -> ... -> y_{i-1} -> y_i,
of length t-1. This contradicts the extremal choice of the original matching. Hence for t>=4 all epsilon_i are equal around C.

Suppose first every epsilon_i=H. From the positional argument above, P_i begins y_{i+1},y_{i+2}. Since P_i spans Omega-y_i and Omega is non-Hamiltonian, prepending the omitted y_i cannot be tight. Therefore
  (y_i,y_{i+1},y_{i+2})
is bad, and R3 gives its complete reversal tight.

Now t>=4 implies y_{i+3} is distinct from y_i,y_{i+1}. The next path P_{i+1} begins y_{i+2},y_{i+3}. These are consecutive common contacts with P_i. R435-quiet monotonicity therefore makes them consecutive in P_i as well: after the initial noncommon head y_{i+1}, every remaining P_i vertex is common with P_{i+1}, so no third common vertex can lie between y_{i+2} and y_{i+3} in P_i without also occurring between those consecutive contacts in P_{i+1}. Hence P_i begins
  y_{i+1},y_{i+2},y_{i+3},
so (y_{i+1},y_{i+2},y_{i+3}) is tight. But applying the preceding non-Hamiltonicity statement with index i+1 says the same turn is bad. Contradiction.

The all-TAIL case is symmetric without reversing any path. The positional argument gives
  P_i=(...,y_{i+2},y_{i+1}).
Appending omitted y_i would Hamiltonize Omega, so (y_{i+2},y_{i+1},y_i) is bad. Since P_{i+1} ends (...,y_{i+3},y_{i+2}), the last two common contacts y_{i+3},y_{i+2} are consecutive; monotonicity forces P_i to end
  (...,y_{i+3},y_{i+2},y_{i+1}).
Thus (y_{i+3},y_{i+2},y_{i+1}) is tight, while the same turn is bad by the append obstruction for P_{i+1}. Contradiction.

Therefore an R435-quiet extremal shortest cycle cannot have t>=4. Since matched 2-cycles are impossible, t=3. This proves the role-correct theorem. Note that a triangle may have mixed HEAD/TAIL roles, so no uniform cyclic bad/tight orientation class is asserted.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R945.md -->

# R946 — A minimal endpoint-Hall obstruction is factor-critical and splits into port-switch, pair-switch, or a rigid common-core bicycle

## Statement
Retain every accepted conclusion of R939: inclusion-minimal endpoint-Hall structure, the exact arbitrary rooted replacement ledger, the proper rigid fresh-core compression bound, and the switch-free common-core component normal form.

ROOTED ENDPOINT-FAN CURRENTIZATION. Let F be an inclusion-minimal Hall-deficient left family with N=N(F), and let S be any support in F. Let R_1,...,R_q be distinct endpoint-deletion cores of S arising from actual Hamilton endpoint realizations. Choose one perfect matching M from F-{S} onto N, whose existence is guaranteed by Hall minimality. For each i let T_i be the unique support matched by M to R_i. Then the T_i are distinct. Define
  M_i = M - {T_i R_i} + {S R_i}.
Then M_i is a matching of F-{T_i} onto all of N: every right core remains saturated, S becomes matched, and T_i is the unique unmatched left support. Thus every actual endpoint incidence S-R_i can be currentized into a near-perfect matching using one COMMON base matching M.

For i!=j, the symmetric difference M_i triangle M_j is exactly the four-edge alternating path
  T_i - R_i - S - R_j - T_j.
All other matching edges are identical. Therefore q endpoint realizations on one support give a q-way common-base exchange fan, not q unrelated Hall representations.

In particular, in the k=5 clean PAIR-SWITCH branch of accepted R944, the switched support has exactly four distinct endpoint-deletion cores coming from its two disjoint endpoint pairs. These four incidences admit four simultaneous rooted near-perfect matchings with the common-base length-four exchange geometry above.

## Hypotheses
Complete all-endpoint incidence graph. F is inclusion-minimal Hall-deficient. S belongs to F. R_i are distinct actual endpoint-deletion neighbors of S. The final four-way specialization assumes k=5, no PORT-SWITCH, and a clean PAIR-SWITCH support as in accepted R944.

## Scope
Strengthening of the canonical Hall parent by the exact simultaneous matching interface needed for in-circuit switch consumption. Pure matching theory once the physical endpoint incidences are supplied.

## Applicability
For a clean in-circuit pair-switch, root the Hall circuit at the switched support S, choose one common perfect matching of F-{S}, and retain all four currentized matchings M_i simultaneously. Any proposed path-order consumer may compare these representations, but their Hamilton path orders are not synchronized merely because the matching skeleton is. Use the full R939 neighborhood ledger for any support replacement.

## Persistence
Retain F,N,S, all actual endpoint-deletion cores R_i, one common root matching M, the distinct matched supports T_i, every M_i, and the exact alternating path T_i-R_i-S-R_j-T_j for each pair i,j. Do not replace the complete endpoint neighborhood by a selected endpoint pair.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not produce P_{k+1}, R561, or a Hall improvement by itself. Does not synchronize Hamilton orders attached to different incidences. Does not eliminate PORT-SWITCH. Does not say abstract matching currentization licenses arbitrary switched-edge path surgery.

## Proof
All pre-existing structural and replacement-ledger conclusions are exactly accepted R939, so only the endpoint-fan assertion needs proof.

Let F be inclusion-minimal Hall-deficient and N=N(F). Accepted R939 includes the factor-critical property: for every chosen root support S in F, the balanced bipartite graph between F-{S} and N has a perfect matching M.

Let R_1,...,R_q be distinct actual endpoint-deletion neighbors of S. Because M saturates every right core in N, each R_i is matched by M to a unique support T_i in F-{S}. Distinct R_i have distinct T_i, since M is a matching and one left support cannot be used on two matching edges.

For each i remove the matching edge T_i-R_i and add the actual incidence S-R_i. The result
  M_i=M-{T_iR_i}+{SR_i}
uses each right core exactly once: R_i remains matched, now to S, and all other right cores keep their M-edge. On the left, every support of F except T_i is used exactly once. Therefore M_i is a perfect matching from F-{T_i} onto N, equivalently a near-perfect matching of F which leaves exactly T_i unmatched. This proves simultaneous currentization of every endpoint incidence S-R_i from one common base matching M.

For i!=j, M_i and M_j agree on every base edge of M except T_iR_i and T_jR_j, and respectively contain SR_i and SR_j. Thus their symmetric difference is exactly
  {T_iR_i, R_iS, SR_j, R_jT_j},
which is the alternating path
  T_i-R_i-S-R_j-T_j.
No other edge differs. Hence all currentizations form a q-way common-base exchange fan.

Finally specialize to k=5 and a clean PAIR-SWITCH support S under no PORT-SWITCH. Accepted R944 places such S inside the minimum Hall obstruction. Under unique ports, distinct endpoint pairs on one support cannot share an endpoint: otherwise the common endpoint-deletion core would realize two different ports. On five vertices there can therefore be at most two distinct endpoint pairs, and PAIR-SWITCH means exactly two disjoint pairs. Their four endpoint deletions are distinct, so q=4 and the preceding construction yields the claimed four rooted near-perfect matchings. This proves R946.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R946.md -->

# R947 — A longest increasing path can have non-Hamiltonian complement even when another one-vertex-swapped longest path has Hamiltonian complement

## Statement
There exists an edge ordering of K_16 with a globally longest increasing path P on 12 vertices such that the induced edge-ordered K_4 on V\\V(P) has no increasing Hamilton path. In the same ordering there is another globally longest increasing path P' whose support differs from P by exchanging one vertex and whose four-vertex complement does have an increasing Hamilton path. Hence the strengthening that EVERY globally longest increasing path has Hamiltonian complement is false, while this example does not refute the existential longest-complement conjecture.

## Hypotheses
Explicit matching-layer edge order on K_16 described in the proof: A={0,...,7}, B={8,...,15}; all internal edges precede all cross edges; cross edges are in cyclic perfect-matching blocks M_0<...<M_7.

## Scope
Exact finite fence for the longest-path-complement research direction inside the edge-ordered subclass.

## Applicability
Use to distinguish the false universal-longest-support statement from the still-open existential statement. It is also a reproducible model of the desired extremal support exchange: a bad longest support is repaired by one vertex swap.

## Persistence
Retain the exact internal-edge order, the paths P and P', the two four-vertex complements, and the R823 12-vertex global upper bound.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not refute the existential claim that SOME globally longest path has Hamiltonian complement; indeed this construction explicitly supplies such a good longest path. Does not prove that one-vertex support exchange always suffices.

## Proof
Let A={0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7} and B={8,9,10,11,12,13,14,15}. Put every edge internal to A or B before every A-B edge. Order the 56 internal edges, from least to greatest, as

27, 11-12, 15, 04, 36, 8-13, 47, 45, 57, 12, 35, 23, 07, 89, 16, 9-11, 14-15, 12-15, 11-13, 8-12, 02, 34, 06, 03, 37, 10-14, 12-14, 9-14, 10-12, 8-10, 67, 8-14, 11-14, 14, 56, 10-15, 10-11, 13-14, 10-13, 17, 24, 9-10, 26, 11-15, 01, 12-13, 05, 13-15, 9-15, 8-11, 9-13, 46, 13, 8-15, 9-12, 25.

(Here ij denotes the unordered edge {i,j}; hyphens are used only when a vertex has two digits.) For k=0,...,7 let M_k be the perfect matching of A to B consisting of {a, 8+((a+k) mod 8)} for a in A. Put all edges of M_k before all edges of M_l whenever k<l. The order inside one M_k is arbitrary.

This is exactly an R823 matching-layer ordering with m=8. Therefore every increasing path has at most 8+ceil(8/2)=12 vertices.

Consider
P=(12,14,13,15,8,0,9,7,10,5,11,4).
Its first four edges 12-14,14-13,13-15,15-8 occur in the displayed internal order at positions 27,38,48,54 respectively. Its remaining seven edges lie successively in cross blocks M_0,M_1,M_2,M_3,M_5,M_6,M_7. Hence P is increasing and has 12 vertices. By the R823 upper bound it is globally longest.

Its complement is X={1,2,3,6}. Restricted to X, the six edges occur in the order
36 < 12 < 23 < 16 < 26 < 13.
There is no increasing Hamilton path on X. To see this without computation, in any monotone Hamilton path on four vertices the middle of its three path-edges must have one smaller outer edge incident at one endpoint and one larger outer edge incident at the other, with the two outer endpoints distinct. The least edge 36 and greatest edge 13 cannot be the middle. If 12 is the middle, its only smaller edge is 36, which touches neither 1 nor 2. If 23 is the middle, choosing smaller outer edge 36 forces the remaining outer edge to be 12, also smaller; choosing smaller outer edge 12 forces the remaining outer edge to be 36. If 16 is the middle, the only possible smaller outer edges touching it are 36 and 12, and they force the opposite outer edge to be respectively 12 and 36, again smaller. If 26 is the middle, its only larger edge is 13, which touches neither 2 nor 6. Thus no middle edge works.

Now exchange 7 in the support of P with 6 and take
P'=(12,14,13,15,8,0,9,6,10,5,11,4).
The internal prefix is unchanged. The cross-block sequence is now M_0,M_1,M_3,M_4,M_5,M_6,M_7, so P' is again increasing on 12 vertices and hence globally longest. Its complement is X'={1,2,3,7}, and
1,2,3,7
is increasing because 12<23<37 in the displayed internal-edge order. Therefore X' has an increasing Hamilton path.

So P is a globally longest increasing path with non-Hamiltonian complement, while the one-vertex-swapped globally longest path P' has Hamiltonian complement. This disproves only the universal-longest-support strengthening and explicitly preserves the existential possibility.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R947.md -->

# R949 — Separated insertion barriers carry an increasing rail corridor and an exact detour inequality

## Statement
Let P=(p_0,...,p_m) be an increasing path in an edge-ordered complete graph and let x,y be vertices outside P that are not insertable into any internal gap of P in the displayed order. If their canonical R895 barriers satisfy beta(x)=i<j=beta(y), then (x,p_{i+1},p_{i+2},...,p_j,y) is an increasing path. Consequently, if an increasing path Q disjoint from P contains x,y consecutively and its adjacent outer path edges (when present) lie respectively below the first corridor edge and above the last corridor edge, replacing xy by this corridor gives an increasing path of order |Q|+(j-i). If P is globally longest, every such valid detour satisfies |Q|+(j-i)<=|P|. In particular, beta(x)=0 and beta(y)=m-1 force (x,p_1,...,p_{m-1},y) to be another path of order |P|.

## Hypotheses
Pure edge-ordered complete graph setting; P increasing; x,y outside P and noninsertable into P; beta is the accepted R895 least-right-feasible barrier.

## Scope
Pure support-exchange lemma for longest-path complement investigations.

## Applicability
Use to turn strict barrier separation into a whole increasing corridor through P, rather than only the one-witness cross turn. The detour form supplies exact obstructions to cooperative exchanges with complementary paths.

## Persistence
Retain the adjacent-barrier case separately from the wider-gap chain, the exact corridor vertex list, and the detour length increment j-i.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Corridors cannot in general be concatenated through an intermediate exterior vertex: the canonical barrier inequality there is reversed. This lemma does not imply that sorting exterior vertices by beta is itself an increasing path, and does not prove the longest-complement conjecture.

## Proof
Write e_k=p_kp_{k+1}, so e_0<...<e_{m-1}. Put i=beta(x)<j=beta(y).

If j=i+1, accepted R895 says that strict barrier separation is witnessed at p_{i+1} by
x p_{i+1} < p_{i+1} y.
Hence (x,p_{i+1},y) is increasing.

Assume j>=i+2. Right-feasibility at gap i gives
x p_{i+1} < e_{i+1}.
The displayed rail is increasing, so
e_{i+1}<e_{i+2}<...<e_{j-1}.
The R895 propagation argument gives left-feasibility at the canonical gap j of y, hence
e_{j-1}<p_j y.
Combining these inequalities gives
x p_{i+1}<e_{i+1}<...<e_{j-1}<p_j y,
which is exactly the edge-label sequence of
(x,p_{i+1},p_{i+2},...,p_j,y).
Thus the corridor is increasing in all cases.

Now let Q be an increasing path disjoint from P containing the consecutive edge x->y. If x has a predecessor on Q, let a be that preceding Q-edge label; if y has a successor, let b be the following Q-edge label. Suppose every present outer seam is favorable, namely a<x p_{i+1} on the left and p_j y<b on the right. Replace the single edge xy of Q by the corridor. The old Q inequalities, the two assumed outer inequalities, and the corridor inequalities just proved show that the resulting path is increasing. It is vertex-simple because Q is disjoint from P, and it gains exactly j-i vertices of P, so its order is |Q|+(j-i).

If P is globally longest, no increasing path has order exceeding |P|, hence every valid detour satisfies |Q|+(j-i)<=|P|.

Finally, if i=0 and j=m-1, the corridor is
(x,p_1,...,p_{m-1},y),
which has 2+(m-1)=m+1=|P| vertices. It is therefore another path of the same order as P, and if P is globally longest then so is this corridor path.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R949.md -->

# R950 — Failure of every one-vertex longest-rail substitution creates two parity replacement barriers

## Statement
Let P=(p_0,...,p_m), m>=2, be an increasing path in an edge-ordered complete graph, with e_i=p_ip_{i+1}. Let x be outside P. If replacing no single p_i by x in the displayed order gives an increasing path, then on each parity class of positions i there is a canonical internal position rho_r(x) with the following properties. Writing A_i=p_{i-1}x and B_i=xp_{i+1}, the outer substitution inequalities hold at i, but the middle one is forced to reverse: B_i<A_i. More precisely rho_r(x) is the least position i of parity r for which the right outer condition is feasible; propagation by steps of two makes the left outer condition feasible there. Moreover, if rho_r(x)<rho_r(y) for two nonreplaceable exterior vertices on the same parity, then x,p_{rho_r(x)+1},y is an increasing three-vertex path.

## Hypotheses
Pure edge-ordered complete graph setting; P increasing of order at least three; x outside P and no literal one-position substitution p_i->x preserves the displayed increasing order.

## Scope
Second-order analogue of the R895 insertion barrier, designed for longest-support exchange rather than insertion.

## Applicability
Use when a longest-support extremal argument needs to consume failure of every one-vertex support substitution. It turns that failure into two parity-indexed canonical obstruction coordinates and cross-turn witnesses.

## Persistence
Retain the definitions of left/right outer substitution feasibility, the two-step propagation L_i and not R_i implies L_{i+2}, and the same-parity strict-separation witness.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not say that every exterior vertex has a replacement slot. Does not by itself imply a Hamilton complement, and the parity barrier witnesses cannot in general be concatenated through one exterior vertex because its middle substitution inequality is reversed.

## Proof
Write e_i=p_ip_{i+1}, so e_0<...<e_{m-1}. For a proposed substitution of x for p_i define

L_i(x): true if i=0 or i=1, and e_{i-2}<p_{i-1}x if i>=2;
R_i(x): true if i=m or i=m-1, and xp_{i+1}<e_{i+1} if i<=m-2.

For 1<=i<=m-1, the displayed path with p_i replaced by x is increasing exactly when L_i(x), p_{i-1}x<xp_{i+1}, and R_i(x) all hold. At i=0 substitution works exactly when R_0(x) holds; at i=m it works exactly when L_m(x) holds.

The key propagation is by two positions. Suppose L_i(x) holds and R_i(x) fails, with i<=m-2. Failure of R_i gives e_{i+1}<xp_{i+1}. Since e_i<e_{i+1}, we have e_i<p_{i+1}x, which is precisely L_{i+2}(x). Thus
L_i and not R_i imply L_{i+2}.

Fix a parity r in {0,1} that occurs among the positions 0,...,m. The first position of that parity, r, has L_r automatically. Along that parity class there is eventually a right-feasible position, because the last one or two positions m-1,m have R automatically. Let rho_r(x) be the least position of parity r with R true. Repeated two-step propagation shows L_{rho_r(x)} true. If rho_r(x)=0, then R_0 holds and x replaces p_0, contrary to hypothesis. If rho_r(x)=m, then L_m holds and x replaces p_m, again contrary to hypothesis. Hence rho_r(x) is internal. Since both outer conditions hold there but substitution is impossible, the middle comparison must fail, and strict totality gives
xp_{rho_r(x)+1}<p_{rho_r(x)-1}x.
This proves the two parity replacement barriers.

Finally let x,y be two nonreplaceable exterior vertices and suppose on parity r that i=rho_r(x)<j=rho_r(y). Since the positions have the same parity, i<=j-2, hence i<=m-2. Right feasibility of x at i gives
xp_{i+1}<e_{i+1}.
Because i is an earlier position of the same parity than the least right-feasible position j for y, R_i(y) fails, so
e_{i+1}<yp_{i+1}.
Therefore
xp_{i+1}<yp_{i+1},
and (x,p_{i+1},y) is increasing.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R950.md -->

# R951 — A minimum counterexample to the existential longest-complement property has a hierarchical three-rail cover

## Statement
Define property E for a finite edge-ordered complete graph G: some globally longest increasing path P has an induced complement G-V(P) with an increasing Hamilton path, allowing the empty complement. Suppose E is false for some graph and choose a counterexample G of minimum order.

Then for EVERY globally longest increasing path P of G, the complement H=G-V(P) is non-Hamiltonian and has increasing path-cover number exactly two. More precisely, because H has smaller order, H satisfies E. Hence H has a globally longest increasing path A such that H-V(A) has an increasing Hamilton path B. Since H is non-Hamiltonian, B is nonempty. Thus
  V(G)=V(P) disjoint-union V(A) disjoint-union V(B)
is a literal partition into three nonempty increasing paths, with P globally longest in G, A globally longest in H, and B Hamilton on H-A. Consequently
  |P| >= |A| >= |B| >= 1.

Therefore the existential longest-complement property reduces, by minimum-counterexample induction, to excluding this hierarchical three-rail configuration for every choice of globally longest P in the minimum counterexample.

## Hypotheses
Pure finite edge-ordered complete-graph setting. Property E is as defined in the statement. G is chosen of minimum order among counterexamples to E.

## Scope
Independent-safe extremal reduction for the proposed existential longest-path-complement theorem. No ordered-1-factorization or boundary-tournament shared strategy is used.

## Applicability
Use as the parent entrance for the existential longest-complement direction. In a hypothetical minimum counterexample, retain an arbitrary globally longest P, then choose A globally longest in its complement with Hamilton complementary rail B. Any exchange theorem need only contradict or improve this hierarchical P|A|B configuration. R947 shows why one must quantify over all globally longest P rather than fix an arbitrary bad support.

## Persistence
Retain the minimum counterexample G, the arbitrary globally longest path P, H=G-P, a globally longest A in H, the Hamilton complement B=H-A, and the inequalities |P|>=|A|>=|B|>=1. Preserve literal edge orders and path orders.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not prove property E or R888. Does not say every longest path in an arbitrary graph has path-cover-two complement. Does not assert A or B is globally longest in G. Does not imply a one-vertex exchange exists.

## Proof
Let G be a minimum-order counterexample to property E, and let P be any globally longest increasing path of G. Put H=G-V(P).

Because G fails E, H cannot have an increasing Hamilton path: if it did, this particular globally longest P would witness E in G. Thus H is non-Hamiltonian.

The graph H has strictly fewer vertices than G because P is nonempty. By minimality of G, H satisfies property E. Therefore there exists a globally longest increasing path A of H such that the induced complement H-V(A) has an increasing Hamilton path; call that path B, with the convention that it could initially be empty.

It cannot be empty. If H-V(A) were empty, then A would be a Hamilton increasing path of H, contradicting that H is non-Hamiltonian. Thus A and B are both nonempty and form an exact two-path cover of H. Since H itself is not Hamiltonian, its increasing path-cover number is exactly two.

Combining with P gives the literal disjoint partition
  V(G)=V(P) union V(A) union V(B)
into three nonempty increasing paths. Since P is globally longest in G and A is itself an increasing path in the induced subgraph H, |P|>=|A|. Since A is globally longest in H and B is an increasing path in H, |A|>=|B|. Therefore |P|>=|A|>=|B|>=1.

The choice of P was arbitrary among globally longest paths of G, so the same conclusion holds for every such P. This proves R951.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R951.md -->

# R952 — A minimum longest-complement counterexample has support-swap persistence or two parity barriers at every exterior vertex

## Statement
Retain the setting of accepted R951: G is a minimum-order counterexample to the existential longest-complement property E, P=(p_0,...,p_m) is any globally longest increasing path, and H=G-V(P) is non-Hamiltonian with increasing path-cover number exactly two.

Fix any exterior vertex x in H. Exactly one of the following two interfaces is available.

(SUPPORT-SWAP.) There exists a position i such that replacing p_i by x in the displayed P order gives an increasing path
  P'=(p_0,...,p_{i-1},x,p_{i+1},...,p_m).
Then P' has the same order as P and is therefore globally longest in G. Its complement is
  H'=(H-{x}) union {p_i},
and H' is non-Hamiltonian. By R951 applied to P', pc_inc(H')=2 and H' admits its own hierarchical two-rail complement A'|B'. Thus every valid one-position longest-support swap remains inside the minimum-counterexample state; if any such H' were Hamiltonian, G would satisfy E.

(PARITY BARRIER.) No one-position substitution p_i->x preserves the displayed increasing order. Then accepted R950 applies and x has two canonical parity replacement barriers rho_0(x),rho_1(x), with both outer substitution inequalities feasible at each barrier and the middle comparison reversed. For two exterior vertices x,y in this barrier branch, strict separation rho_r(x)<rho_r(y) on one parity supplies the actual increasing turn (x,p_{rho_r(x)+1},y).

Hence the local support-exchange problem in a minimum counterexample has no third state: a vertex either generates another globally longest support with another exact path-cover-two complement, or it carries the full two-parity replacement obstruction.

## Hypotheses
Pure finite edge-ordered complete graph. G is a minimum counterexample to property E from R951. P is any globally longest increasing path. x lies outside P. The barrier clause uses accepted R950 when all literal one-position substitutions fail.

## Scope
Independent-safe synthesis of accepted R951 and R950. It is a support-exchange interface for the existential longest-complement program, not a proof of the conjecture.

## Applicability
Use after the R951 three-rail reduction. Support swaps may be iterated only as actual globally longest displayed-order substitutions; after every swap reselect the R951 complement rails for the new support. If a chosen exterior vertex admits no swap, retain both parity barriers instead of treating nonreplacement as featureless failure. A future proof needs an extremal objective on the longest-support exchange graph or a consumer of the parity-barrier population.

## Persistence
Retain G, the actual order P, x, every successful replacement position and resulting support/complement, or both rho parity barriers and their outer/middle inequalities. After a swap retain a fresh R951 hierarchical cover of the new complement; do not transport the old A|B orders automatically.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not say a support swap improves any monotone objective. Does not say every exterior vertex is replaceable. Does not synchronize the path-cover-two complements of different longest supports. Does not prove property E or R888.

## Proof
Retain G,P,H and x as in the statement.

If there exists i such that replacing p_i by x in the displayed P order is increasing, call the resulting path P'. It has exactly |P| vertices. Since P is globally longest, no increasing path has more than |P| vertices, so P' is also globally longest. Its vertex complement is exactly H'=(H-{x}) union {p_i}. Because G is a counterexample to property E, the complement of every globally longest path is non-Hamiltonian. Hence H' is non-Hamiltonian. Accepted R951 applies to the arbitrary globally longest path P': its complement H' has increasing path-cover number exactly two and admits a hierarchical decomposition A'|B' with A' globally longest in H' and B' Hamilton on the remainder. This is SUPPORT-SWAP.

If no such i exists, x satisfies exactly the hypothesis of accepted R950 with respect to the displayed increasing path P. Therefore both parity-indexed canonical barriers rho_0(x),rho_1(x) exist, are internal, have both outer substitution conditions feasible, and have the middle edge inequality reversed. For two such nonreplaceable vertices x,y, accepted R950 also gives the stated same-parity cross turn whenever rho_r(x)<rho_r(y). This is PARITY BARRIER.

The two cases are exhaustive by whether at least one displayed-order one-position substitution exists. This proves R952.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R952.md -->

# R953 — Critical equal recurrence yields a common-core saturated two-ear fork

## Statement
Retain every conclusion and hypothesis of accepted R948 in the critical equal-recurrence case with R isolated: the actual source order A=L-z-R, equal petals |B|=|Z|=k<a with Z={z} union R, mixed Hamilton support M=L union B, the two literal exact H-p covers (L union Z)|B and (L union B)|Z, and the saturated non-Hamiltonian deletion-Hamiltonian universe Omega=Z union {p}. The L-isolated case is dual.

ARBITRARY-DELETION UNIQUE-TRANSITION PACKET. Since Omega-z=R union {p} is Hamiltonian, choose an actual Hamilton path K on R+p. Deleting the entire old petal B gives the literal exact two-cover of H-B
  (L followed by z) | K.
With deletion set D=B, absorbable block S=L, complement C=Omega, and absorber Q=M on B union L, this is an actual R508 packet with exactly ONE selected S|C transition, namely the literal old-source boundary from the final vertex of L to z. Thus the critical two-ear fork itself realizes tau=1 for an arbitrary non-singleton deletion, without assuming transition minimization. All accepted R511/R512/R513 consumers may be invoked only with the resulting actual orders and their complete seam windows.

COMMON-CORE DELETION FORCES DIRECT CROSS-PETAL CONTACT. The proper residue H-L has path-cover number exactly two. For EVERY exact two-cover T of H-L, applying R508 to absorber M=L union B forces a B|(Z+p) selected adjacency, while applying R508 to absorber A=L union Z forces a Z|(B+p) selected adjacency in the SAME T. In fact T must contain a direct physical B-Z selected adjacency. If no B-Z state were selected, the two forced crossings would be B-p and Z-p, making p internal with exactly two interclass incidences. The block identity then gives b_B+b_Z=3, so one of B or Z is a single whole maximal block adjacent to p; that would Hamiltonize B+p or Z+p, both non-Hamiltonian. Contradiction.

CROSS-PETAL SPLIT. If B union Z is non-Hamiltonian, then each of B+Z, B+p, Z+p has path-cover number exactly two, every exact H-L two-cover has connected interaction on classes {B,Z,{p}}, and every such cover is either a rainbow hinge or a split-star weave by the R942 block-word argument. In a split-star the singleton {p} cannot be the center, so the center is B or Z. Every exact cover still contains a current B-Z state.

If B union Z is Hamiltonian, retain an actual Hamilton path P_BZ. Then P_BZ|L is an exact H-p source. Since |L|=a-k<a, global minimality makes every L-side vertex quiet; therefore Gamma=L union {p} is non-Hamiltonian and deletion-Hamiltonian and (B union Z)+y is non-Hamiltonian for every y in Gamma. Running the same quiet PORT-CROSS / COMPLETE-EXCHANGE saturation used in R931 yields exactly: a spanning two-cover, the uniform middle-layer residue, or a universal recurrence only on the B union Z side, of size 2k. Hence 2k<a forbids recurrence; 2k=a is the same-size fixed case; 2k>a is a larger recurrence with a strictly smaller saturated opposite rail L of size a-k<k.

THREE-PETAL FIXED POINT. In the same-size subcase 2k=a, if the incoming critical source was already normalized so that B+p is deletion-Hamiltonian, then |L|=|B|=|Z|=k and all three blocks L+p, B+p, Z+p are non-Hamiltonian deletion-Hamiltonian, meeting pairwise exactly in p. Simultaneously all three pair unions L+B, L+Z, B+Z are Hamiltonian. This three-petal saturated fixed point is the only same-size p-isolated recurrence residue asserted here.

## Hypotheses
Accepted R948 critical equal-recurrence hypotheses. H is a smallest counterexample, the original offending rail size a is globally minimum, R is isolated in the disconnected R942 event, and |M|=|A|=a. The final three-petal clause additionally assumes the incoming source is normalized with B+p deletion-Hamiltonian.

## Scope
Canonical strengthening of the Arm-A critical recurrence premise. It converts the same-fiber two-ear fork into two legal arbitrary-deletion R508 constraints on one common residue, forces direct cross-petal current state, and gives the exact Hamilton-vs-non-Hamilton cross-petal recurrence split.

## Applicability
Use before inventing any new recurrence packet. The critical fork already supplies a real tau=1 arbitrary-deletion packet and, after deleting L, a simultaneous two-absorber constraint on EVERY exact target cover. If B+Z is non-Hamiltonian, work only with the cross-petal rainbow/split-star form while retaining both absorbers. If B+Z is Hamiltonian, retain the new saturated Gamma port and the recurrence size 2k honestly. At 2k=a and normalized input, target the full three-petal saturated fixed point rather than separate local saturation lemmas.

## Persistence
Retain p,z,L,R,B,Z,M; both H-p covers; an actual puncture path K on R+p; the exact H-B tau=1 cover; for each H-L cover both forced R508 crossings and at least one direct B-Z state; in the B+Z-Hamiltonian branch retain P_BZ, Gamma=L+p, all its puncture Hamilton paths, and the recurrence support. In the fixed point retain all three saturated petals and all three Hamilton pair unions. Never synchronize unrelated Hamilton orders.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not close the cross-petal rainbow/split-star branch. Does not consume the three-petal fixed point. Does not make 2k>a a global descent. Does not assert the R511/R513 mate outputs close H without a complete seam consumer. Does not use the role-sensitive puncture normal form of DR17.44 section 29.

## Proof
Retain all accepted R948 data, with R isolated. Thus A=L-z-R is the actual old source order, Z={z} union R, M=L union B is an actual Hamilton support, |B|=|Z|=k<a, and H-p has the two literal exact covers
  (L union Z) | B,
  (L union B) | Z.
Also Omega=Z union {p} is non-Hamiltonian and Omega-y is Hamiltonian for every y in Omega. The old source universe B union {p} is non-Hamiltonian as well: if it were Hamiltonian, it would be disjoint from the old Hamilton rail A=L union Z and those two paths would span H.

1. Arbitrary-deletion tau=1 packet. Since z belongs to Omega and Omega-z=R union {p} is Hamiltonian, choose an actual Hamilton path K on R+p. Delete the whole old petal B. The vertices of H-B are L, z, R, p. The literal old-source prefix L followed by z is tight, and K spans R+p, so
  T_B=(L followed by z) | K
is a literal two-cover of H-B. It is exact: if H-B were Hamiltonian, that Hamilton path together with the old Hamilton path B would two-cover H.

Put D=B and S=L. In H-D the complementary remainder is C=Omega=Z+p. The actual path Q=M spans exactly D union S=B union L. Hence accepted R508 applies. In the displayed cover T_B the L-block is followed by z, giving exactly one selected S|C adjacency, namely the old source boundary ell-z where ell is the final vertex of L. The other rail K lies wholly in C. Thus tau(T_B)=1. This establishes the claimed legal arbitrary-deletion unique-transition packet. Any later R511/R513 use must retain these actual path orders and seam coordinates.

2. Delete the common core. Since L is a nonempty tight path, H-L cannot be Hamiltonian: otherwise L together with a Hamilton path on H-L would two-cover H. Smallest-counterexample minimality gives pc(H-L)<=2, so pc(H-L)=2.

Let T be any exact two-cover of H-L. Apply R508 first with deletion set D=L, absorbable block S=B, and absorber Q=M=L union B. The complementary remainder is Z+p, so T selects a B|(Z+p) adjacency. Apply R508 again to the SAME T with D=L, S=Z, and absorber Q=A=L union Z. The complementary remainder is B+p, so T selects a Z|(B+p) adjacency.

We prove T has a direct B-Z selected adjacency. Suppose not. Then the first forced crossing must be B-p and the second Z-p. Since p is one vertex in a two-path cover and is incident to both required interclass states, it has selected degree two and is internal on one T-rail, with one B-neighbor and one Z-neighbor. There are no other interclass transitions because B-Z is absent and p has no further selected incidence. Let b_B,b_Z be the numbers of maximal B- and Z-blocks. Contracting maximal class blocks in the two T-rails gives a two-component forest with b_B+b_Z+1 vertices and exactly two interclass edges. Hence
  b_B+b_Z+1=2+2,
so b_B+b_Z=3. One of B,Z therefore occurs as exactly one whole maximal block. If Z is whole, its required p-adjacency makes p followed by that actual Z-block, or the reverse, a tight Hamilton path on Z+p=Omega, contradicting non-Hamiltonicity of Omega. If B is whole, its p-adjacency Hamiltonizes B+p, contradicting the old source-universe non-Hamiltonicity proved above. Thus every exact T has a direct physical B-Z selected state.

3. Non-Hamiltonian B+Z branch. Suppose B union Z is non-Hamiltonian. Each pair union B+Z, B+p, Z+p is nevertheless coverable by two tight paths, using its two displayed source classes. Hence each has path-cover number exactly two. If an exact H-L cover had disconnected interaction on the three classes B,Z,{p}, one class would be isolated and the union of the other two classes would be Hamiltonian, exactly as in the elementary isolation argument of R942. This contradicts pairwise non-Hamiltonicity. Thus every exact cover has connected interaction.

The R942 block-word proof is purely combinatorial once three nonempty Hamilton classes and a connected two-rail interaction are supplied. Applying it to B,Z,{p}, every exact H-L cover is a rainbow hinge or split-star weave. In the split-star alternative the center class is split nontrivially between both rails; the singleton {p} cannot be split, so the center is B or Z. The direct B-Z state proved in step 2 remains current in every representative. No absorption is claimed.

4. Hamiltonian B+Z branch. Suppose instead B union Z is Hamiltonian and fix an actual Hamilton path P_BZ. Then
  P_BZ | L
is an exact H-p source. Write l=|L|=a-k<a. A universal crossing on the literal L rail of this source would have offending rail size l<a, contradicting global minimality of a. Hence every y in L is quiet on the L-side.

We verify the resulting saturation rather than transport it. Put Gamma=L union {p}. For y in L choose an exact H-y two-cover with no selected adjacency between L-y and B+Z. The source classes are L and B+Z and p is the only exchanged label. The standard seam-free quiet substitution used in the accepted R931 proof gives L-y+p Hamiltonian unless B+Z+p were Hamiltonian. The latter would be disjoint from the old Hamilton source rail L and would two-cover H, so it is impossible. Hence Gamma-y=L-y+p is Hamiltonian for every y in L; Gamma-p=L is already Hamiltonian. Thus Gamma is deletion-Hamiltonian. Gamma itself is non-Hamiltonian, since Gamma together with the disjoint Hamilton support B+Z would otherwise two-cover H. For every y in Gamma, (B+Z)+y is non-Hamiltonian because its complementary support Gamma-y is Hamiltonian.

We are therefore in exactly the saturated-port situation used in accepted R931/P1003, with small rail size l<a and fixed complementary rail size 2k. For each y in Gamma the source (Gamma-y)|(B+Z) is actual. If for some m in B+Z the replacement (B+Z)-m+y is non-Hamiltonian, that m is a universal crossing on the 2k-side, giving the stated recurrence. If every such replacement is Hamiltonian, the complete-exchange/quiet two-pivot argument of R931 saturates all l|2k support partitions unless a universal crossing occurs. A crossing on the l-side is impossible by l<a; hence the only recurrence size is 2k. If no recurrence occurs, unequal sizes close H by the R931 contiguous-subpath argument, and equal sizes give the uniform middle-layer residue. Thus the exact alternatives are spanning two-cover, uniform middle layer, or a universal recurrence only on the 2k-side.

If 2k<a, the recurrence is forbidden by the definition of a. If 2k=a, it is same-size. If 2k>a, then l=a-k<k, so the recurring source comes with a strictly smaller saturated opposite rail; no global monotonicity beyond this numerical fact is asserted.

5. Three-petal fixed point. Assume 2k=a and the incoming critical source was already normalized so that B+p is deletion-Hamiltonian. Then l=a-k=k. The new Gamma=L+p is deletion-Hamiltonian by step 4 and Omega=Z+p is deletion-Hamiltonian by R948. All three are non-Hamiltonian source universes. Their pair unions are Hamiltonian: L+Z=A is the old source rail, L+B=M is the mixed ear, and B+Z is Hamiltonian by the present branch assumption. Therefore L+p, B+p, Z+p are three equal saturated (k+1)-vertex blocks meeting pairwise exactly in p, with all three pairwise petal unions Hamiltonian. This is the claimed fixed point.

The L-isolated case is obtained by exact left-right duality. This proves R953.
