# R954 — An ordered XOR 1-factorization of K16 has no longest path with Hamilton complement but has a spanning two-path cover

## Statement
Let V=GF(2)^4 identified with 0,...,15. For every nonzero difference d, let M_d be the perfect matching of edges {x,x xor d}. Order the fifteen matching blocks by 1<7<6<2<4<3<5<10<12<13<14<9<8<11<15, with arbitrary order inside each block. Then every globally longest increasing path has exactly 12 vertices, and the complement of every globally longest increasing path is a four-vertex induced edge order with no increasing Hamilton path. Nevertheless V has a spanning cover by two vertex-disjoint increasing paths. Hence the existential strengthening of R888 asserting that some globally longest increasing path always has Hamiltonian complement is false even inside ordered 1-factorizations.

## Hypotheses
Explicit ordered 1-factorization of K16 by XOR difference classes in the displayed block order. Within-block tie order is irrelevant for vertex-simple increasing paths.

## Scope
Exact finite fence against longest-first strategies for R888 and the ordered-1-factorization theorem.

## Applicability
Use to reject any proof strategy that first insists one rail be globally longest and then Hamilton-covers its complement. The example remains positively two-coverable, so it is also a laboratory for genuinely cooperative two-rail constructions.

## Persistence
Retain the block order; the R823 equality classification; the normalized eight-case omitted-cross table; the base longest path (4,5,7,3,0,10,6,8,1,9,2,13); the base bad complement {11,12,14,15}; and the explicit two-cover (0,1,3,7,4,14,2,13) plus its xor-8 translate.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not refute R888 or the ordinary ordered-1-factorization two-cover theorem. Does not assert that all longest-complement failures have this XOR form. The conclusion concerns the displayed block order only.

## Proof
Write V=GF(2)^4 as the integers 0,...,15 under bitwise xor. For each nonzero d, the edges {x,x xor d} form a perfect matching M_d. The displayed order of the fifteen difference classes is\n\n1<7<6<2<4<3<5<10<12<13<14<9<8<11<15.\n\nConsecutive edges of a vertex-simple path cannot have the same xor difference, so within-block order is irrelevant. Put A={0,...,7} and B={8,...,15}. Differences below 8 are internal to A or B and are exactly the first seven blocks; differences at least 8 are cross edges and are exactly the final eight blocks. Thus accepted R823 applies with m=8 and every increasing path has at most 8+ceil(8/2)=12 vertices.\n\nWe classify the equality case. Let P be an increasing path on 12 vertices. In the notation of the R823 proof, let c be its number of cross edges and let p be the number of vertices in the initial one-part segment, including the endpoint of the first cross edge. Then p+c=12, c<=8, and p+floor(c/2)<=8. Hence c is 7 or 8. If c=8, P uses all eight cross blocks in their displayed order 10,12,13,14,9,8,11,15. Their xor is 0, so the forced consecutive cross walk returns after eight cross edges to its starting vertex, contradicting vertex simplicity. Therefore c=7 and p=5.\n\nThe seven cross edges use seven of the eight cross blocks. XOR translation preserves every difference class, so translate P by its first-cross starting vertex and, if necessary, thereby swap A and B; we may normalize that starting vertex to 0 in A. For each possible omitted cross difference delta, the consecutive cross part is forced because at each used matching block the current vertex has a unique mate. The following table gives the cross-walk states beginning at 0. When the walk is simple, the last column gives the five A-vertices that the initial internal prefix would have to occupy and the number of increasing Hamilton orders of that five-set ending at 0 under the internal block order 1<7<6<2<4<3<5. The latter counts are the direct check of the 4!=24 possible orders before 0.\n\nomit 10: 0,12,1,15,6,14,5,10 ; required {0,2,3,4,7}; count 0.\nomit 12: 0,10,7,9,0,8,3,12 ; repeats 0.\nomit 13: 0,10,6,8,1,9,2,13 ; required {0,3,4,5,7}; count 1, uniquely (4,5,7,3,0), with differences 1,2,4,3.\nomit 14: 0,10,6,11,2,10,1,14 ; repeats 10.\nomit 9: 0,10,6,11,5,13,6,9 ; repeats 6.\nomit 8: 0,10,6,11,5,12,7,8 ; required {0,1,2,3,4}; count 0.\nomit 11: 0,10,6,11,5,12,4,11 ; repeats 11.\nomit 15: 0,10,6,11,5,12,4,15 ; required {0,1,2,3,7}; count 0.\n\nThus every 12-vertex increasing path is an xor translate of\n\nP0=(4,5,7,3,0,10,6,8,1,9,2,13),\n\nwhose difference sequence is\n\n1,2,4,3,10,12,14,9,8,11,15.\n\nIts complement is C0={11,12,14,15}. Hence every globally longest path complement is an xor translate of C0. We show C0 has no increasing Hamilton path. Its three opposite-edge perfect matchings are\n\n{{14,15},{11,12}}, with differences 1,7 and block ranks 1,2;\n{{12,14},{11,15}}, with differences 2,4 and block ranks 4,5;\n{{12,15},{11,14}}, with differences 3,5 and block ranks 6,7.\n\nThus every edge of the first opposite matching precedes every edge of the second, and every edge of the second precedes every edge of the third. In any Hamilton path on four vertices, the first and third edges are disjoint and therefore form one of the three opposite perfect matchings, while the middle edge belongs to another. If the middle edge comes from a higher matching band than the two outer edges, then middle>third; if it comes from a lower band, then first>middle. Either way the three path edges cannot be strictly increasing. Hence C0 is non-Hamiltonian, and the same holds for every xor translate. Therefore no globally longest path has Hamiltonian complement.\n\nNevertheless the graph has a spanning two-path cover. Let\n\nR=(0,1,3,7,4,14,2,13)\nand\nR+8=(8,9,11,15,12,6,10,5).\n\nThese two vertex lists are disjoint and together contain all sixteen vertices. Both have the same consecutive xor-difference sequence\n\n1,2,4,3,10,12,15,\n\nwhose block ranks are 1,4,5,6,8,9,15, strictly increasing. Hence both are increasing paths. This proves all assertions.

# R955 — Minimum rigid endpoint-Hall circuits force nonrigid chords; at k=5 the K4-e exception is impossible

## Statement
Retain accepted R944 in the k=5 uniform middle-layer residue on eleven vertices and choose F to be a minimum-cardinality Hall-deficient left family in the COMPLETE all-endpoint incidence graph. Then F necessarily contains a PORT-SWITCH. The clean PAIR-SWITCH alternative of R944 is impossible.

Indeed, suppose all endpoint cores of F have unique ports and S in F is a clean PAIR-SWITCH support. Write S={a,b,c,d,e} with its two disjoint realized endpoint pairs {a,b} and {c,d}. Root the factor-critical Hall family at S and choose one perfect matching M from F-{S} onto N(F). Let R_a=S-a, R_b=S-b, R_c=S-c, R_d=S-d, and let T_a,T_b,T_c,T_d be their distinct M-matched supports. Write x_a=T_a-R_a, ..., x_d=T_d-R_d. Unique ports force actual Hamilton endpoint pairs {x_a,b},{x_b,a},{x_c,d},{x_d,c} on the four matched supports. Moreover the endpoint-pair graph of every displayed support is a matching: two realized endpoint pairs sharing exactly one vertex would create a PORT-SWITCH at their common endpoint-deletion core.

For every possible equality pattern among x_a,x_b,x_c,x_d, these five support conditions are incompatible with the absence of a tight P6. Up to relabeling the exterior completion labels there are exactly the 15 restricted-growth patterns
0000,0001,0010,0011,0012,0100,0101,0102,0110,0111,0112,0120,0121,0122,0123.
Each corresponding exact boundary-SAT instance is UNSAT. Therefore clean PAIR-SWITCH cannot occur in F, leaving PORT-SWITCH as the only R944 alternative.

## Hypotheses
Uniform middle-layer residue with k=5, |V(H)|=11: every five-set is Hamiltonian and no six-set supports a tight P6. Complete all-endpoint incidence graph. F is a minimum-cardinality Hall-deficient left family. Use accepted R944 for the in-circuit PORT/clean-PAIR dichotomy and accepted R946 for common-base rooted currentization.

## Scope
Order-eleven strengthening of R944. It eliminates the clean PAIR-SWITCH alternative by the full four-way rooted matching fan. This is not a general-k theorem.

## Applicability
Use as the preferred k=5 Arm-B entrance. Start directly with a minimum-cardinality Hall obstruction containing a physical PORT-SWITCH. Clean PAIR-SWITCH is no longer a live order-eleven branch, though R946 remains a valid historical/simultaneous matching theorem. The next closure theorem must consume the in-circuit PORT-SWITCH into P6, R561, or a fully accounted Hall improvement.

## Persistence
Retain F and its complete endpoint neighborhood, the physical PORT-SWITCH core and its competing actual endpoint realizations. For the eliminated pair-switch branch retain S, R_a,R_b,R_c,R_d, one common root matching M, T_a,T_b,T_c,T_d, completion labels x_a,...,x_d, all 15 equality patterns, exact CNF encodings, and independent UNSAT certificates.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not consume PORT-SWITCH. Does not prove Uniform Middle-Layer Growth for k>5. Does not synchronize Hamilton orders across different supports. Does not say the four-way fan theorem holds without the no-PORT cleanliness condition. Does not alter the historical validity of R943, R944, or R946.

## Proof
Retain the k=5 order-eleven uniform residue and choose F to be a minimum-cardinality Hall-deficient left family in the complete all-endpoint incidence graph. Accepted R944 says that F contains either a PORT-SWITCH or, if every endpoint core has a unique port, a clean PAIR-SWITCH support. Suppose for contradiction that there is no PORT-SWITCH and that S in F is a clean PAIR-SWITCH.

Relabel the five vertices of S as {a,b,c,d,e} so that two actual Hamilton paths on S have disjoint endpoint pairs {a,b} and {c,d}. Under unique ports the endpoint-pair graph of any support is a matching: if two realized endpoint pairs {u,v} and {u,w} shared exactly one endpoint u, then the common endpoint-deletion core S-u would realize two distinct ports v,w. Thus S has no endpoint pair sharing one endpoint with either displayed pair; on five vertices there is no third pair disjoint from both, so these are exactly its two endpoint pairs.

Root the factor-critical Hall family at S. By accepted R946 choose one perfect matching M from F-{S} onto N(F). Put
  R_a=S-a, R_b=S-b, R_c=S-c, R_d=S-d.
These are four distinct endpoint neighbors of S. Let T_a,T_b,T_c,T_d be their distinct M-matched supports and write
  x_a=T_a-R_a, x_b=T_b-R_b, x_c=T_c-R_c, x_d=T_d-R_d.
Each x_u lies outside S. The incidence T_a-R_a is realized by an actual Hamilton path on T_a exposing completion x_a. Since R_a has the unique port b, that path has endpoint pair {x_a,b}. Similarly the four matched supports have required realized endpoint pairs
  T_a: {x_a,b},
  T_b: {x_b,a},
  T_c: {x_c,d},
  T_d: {x_d,c}.
Again, because there is no PORT-SWITCH, the complete endpoint-pair graph of each T_u is a matching.

It remains to show that these five support conditions force a P6 regardless of coincidences among x_a,x_b,x_c,x_d. Up to relabeling the exterior completion labels, their equality type is one of the Bell-number B_4=15 restricted-growth strings
  0000, 0001, 0010, 0011, 0012,
  0100, 0101, 0102, 0110, 0111,
  0112, 0120, 0121, 0122, 0123.
For a pattern with r distinct exterior labels use n=5+r vertices, with a,b,c,d,e=0,1,2,3,4 and the r exterior labels 5,...,4+r. The five supports are
  S={a,b,c,d,e},
  T_a={b,c,d,e,x_a},
  T_b={a,c,d,e,x_b},
  T_c={a,b,d,e,x_c},
  T_d={a,b,c,e,x_d}.
They remain pairwise distinct for every equality pattern.

Exact CNF encoding. Introduce one Boolean turn variable for every complete-reversal pair of ordered triples, with the lexicographically smaller orientation positive. For every ordered six-tuple forbid simultaneous tightness of its four consecutive turns. For each of the five displayed supports introduce one endpoint-pair indicator E_Q for each unordered pair Q of its vertices. For every one of the 120 orders O of that support, with endpoint pair Q and three consecutive turn literals t_1,t_2,t_3, add
  not t_1 OR not t_2 OR not t_3 OR E_Q.
Thus every actual Hamilton order activates its physical endpoint-pair indicator. For every two endpoint pairs Q,Q' sharing exactly one vertex add
  not E_Q OR not E_Q',
which is exactly the no-PORT matching condition on the endpoint-pair graph. Finally require actual existence of each named endpoint pair, not merely its indicator: for each required pair use the 12 vertex orders with those endpoints, introduce one witness variable per order, make each witness imply its three turn literals, and require at least one of the 12 witnesses. There are six such existence requirements: two on S and one on each T_u. No Hamiltonicity or endpoint restriction is imposed on any unrelated five-set.

The resulting instances have, according to r, 182 to 374 variables and 1,692 to 61,452 clauses. The Integrator independently generated all fifteen CNFs from the preceding definition and solved them with a standalone watched-literal DPLL implementation, separate from the DR17.45 solver and proof trees. The solver uses exact unit propagation, chooses an unassigned variable of maximum static sum of 2^{-|C|} over its incident clauses, breaks ties by variable index, and branches false before true. It was cross-checked against exhaustive truth-table search on 100 random CNFs with up to seven variables, with no disagreement. Every one of the fifteen pair-switch instances is UNSAT. The independent search-node counts, in the pattern order above, are
  21387,14915,15115,14641,13447,
  16947,13385,13379,13385,18107,
  13373,13377,13371,14645,13981,
with maximum decision depth at most 27.

Therefore the assumed clean PAIR-SWITCH packet cannot exist in any P6-free boundary tournament. R944 leaves only PORT-SWITCH. Hence every minimum-cardinality Hall obstruction in the k=5 uniform residue contains a physical PORT-SWITCH, proving R955.

# R956 — A three-component broad-interval augment reduces an increasing path cover by one component

## Statement
Let F be a spanning cover of an edge-ordered complete graph by c>=3 vertex-disjoint increasing paths, oriented increasingly, with incoming/outgoing boundary labels L,U. Let p->v be a selected F-edge on one component C. Let t be the terminal of a second component A and s the source of a third component B, with A,B,C pairwise distinct. If L(t)<lambda(tv)<U(v) and L(p)<lambda(ps)<U(s), then deleting p->v and adding t->v and p->s produces a spanning cover by c-1 vertex-disjoint increasing paths. The conclusion remains valid when A or B is a singleton under the usual L(source)=-infinity and U(terminal)=+infinity conventions.

## Hypotheses
Pure edge-ordered complete graph; F is a literal spanning increasing path cover; the three named components are distinct.

## Scope
Order-free cooperative augmentation lemma. It is the collision-free length-three case of the broad interval relation and does not require a common threshold vector.

## Applicability
Use as the augmentation consumer for endpoint-rotation closures or active-active residuals. In a minimum-component cover, every such triple must violate at least one of the two broad seam inequalities.

## Persistence
Retain the exact component roles A|C|B, the removed edge p->v, the two new edges t->v and p->s, and both full seam inequalities.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not justify arbitrary alternating paths or matchings in the broad interval graph. Longer alternations can change both incidences of one original vertex and fail increasingness. Does not by itself prove R888 or the ordered-1-factorization theorem.

## Proof
Write the three distinct components as A=(a_0,...,a_r=t), C=(c_0,...,c_i=p,c_{i+1}=v,...,c_m), and B=(s=b_0,b_1,...,b_q), allowing A or B to be a singleton. Delete the selected edge p->v of C. Form\n\nA'=(a_0,...,t,v,c_{i+2},...,c_m)\n\nand\n\nB'=(c_0,...,p,s,b_1,...,b_q).\n\nTogether with every untouched component of F, these sequences partition every vertex exactly once, and the number of components changes from c to c-1 because the three components A,C,B are replaced by two.\n\nAll consecutive edge comparisons internal to the inherited pieces are unchanged. At the new seam t->v, the incoming edge at t has label L(t) when A is nontrivial and is absent when A is a singleton; the outgoing edge from v has label U(v) when v is nonterminal and is absent when v was terminal. Hence the hypothesis L(t)<lambda(tv)<U(v), with the infinite endpoint conventions, is exactly what is needed for A' to remain increasing. Likewise at the seam p->s, the incoming edge at p has label L(p) when p is nonsource and is absent otherwise, while the outgoing edge from s has label U(s) when B is nontrivial and is absent when B is a singleton. Thus L(p)<lambda(ps)<U(s) is exactly the complete seam condition for B'. No original vertex receives two new incoming or two new outgoing edges: p loses p->v and gains p->s, while v loses its old incoming edge and gains t->v. Therefore the two resulting components are vertex-simple directed paths. This proves the lemma.

# R957 — Seven-vertex port rigidity eliminates the order-eleven uniform middle layer

## Statement
LOCAL PORT-RIGIDITY THEOREM. Let G be a boundary tournament on seven vertices such that every five-vertex subset supports a Hamilton tight P5 and G contains no tight P6. Fix any four-set R. Across ALL Hamilton endpoint completions of R, the physical port is unique: there do not exist Hamilton paths on R+x and R+y, with x,y outside R (possibly x=y), exposing x and y as endpoints and having distinct opposite endpoints p,q in R.

Equivalently, for every four-core R the complete endpoint-core port set Pi(R) has size at most one.

ORDER-ELEVEN COROLLARY. Hence the k=5, |V(H)|=11 uniform middle-layer residue is impossible. Indeed every seven-vertex induced subsystem of such an H satisfies the local hypotheses, so every four-core of H has a unique port. But accepted R955 says that in the order-eleven uniform residue a minimum-cardinality Hall obstruction necessarily contains a PORT-SWITCH, i.e. some four-core with at least two ports. Contradiction.

## Hypotheses
Local theorem: seven-vertex Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament, every five-set Hamiltonian, no tight P6. Global corollary: k=5 order-eleven uniform residue from R927, together with accepted R955.

## Scope
Exact finite theorem plus the complete elimination of the k=5/order-eleven uniform middle-layer arm. This does not address uniform residues with k>5.

## Applicability
Use to delete the entire order-eleven uniform middle-layer branch. Any hypothetical k=5 uniform residue would give seven-vertex port uniqueness, contradicting the PORT-SWITCH forced by R955. For general k, retain the existing Hall machinery; no large-k port-rigidity statement is claimed.

## Persistence
For the local theorem retain R, the two completion labels x,y, distinct ports p,q, the distinction x=y versus x!=y, one actual first Hamilton order, the second required endpoint-pair existence, the every-five-set Hamilton witnesses, and all no-P6 clauses. For the global corollary retain the R955 minimum Hall family and its forced port-switch core.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not prove the full Uniform Middle-Layer Growth theorem for k>5. Does not say a six-vertex uniform packet has unique ports; an exact six-vertex cross-support PORT-SWITCH fence exists. Does not use or imply path-order synchronization. Does not eliminate the Universal Source-Crossing arm.

## Proof
We first prove the local seven-vertex theorem. Let G have seven vertices, every five-set Hamiltonian, and no tight P6. Fix a four-core R and suppose two physical ports p!=q are realized at R. Thus there are completion labels x,y outside R and actual Hamilton paths on R+x and R+y exposing the completion labels as endpoints, with opposite endpoints p and q respectively. There are two cases.

CASE I: x=y. Then one five-support S=R+x has two Hamilton endpoint pairs {x,p} and {x,q} sharing the completion vertex x. Relabel the seven vertices so
  R={0,1,2,3}, x=4, p=0, q=1,
with the two remaining vertices 5,6. Choose one actual Hamilton order O of S with endpoint pair {4,0}. There are exactly 2*3!=12 such orders. It is enough to refute each possible choice of O separately. For each choice impose the three turn literals certifying O and require, in addition, an actual Hamilton order of S with endpoint pair {4,1}.

CASE II: x!=y. Relabel
  R={0,1,2,3}, x=4, y=5, p=0, q=1,
with the seventh vertex 6. Put S=R+4 and T=R+5. Choose one actual Hamilton order O of S with endpoint pair {4,0}; again there are exactly 12 possibilities. Fix its three turn literals and require an actual Hamilton order of T with endpoint pair {5,1}.

For either case and each of the twelve choices of O use the following exact CNF.

BOUNDARY VARIABLES. On seven vertices there are 7*6*5/2=105 complete-reversal pairs of ordered triples. Introduce one Boolean variable for each pair, with the lexicographically smaller orientation as the positive literal.

NO P6. For each ordered six-tuple of distinct vertices, forbid simultaneous tightness of its four consecutive turns. There are 7P6=5040 such four-literal clauses.

UNIFORM FIVE-SET HAMILTONICITY. There are C(7,5)=21 five-subsets. For each five-subset U introduce one witness variable for each of its 5!=120 vertex orders. A witness implies the three consecutive turn literals of that order, giving 21*120*3=7560 binary implication clauses. Add one 120-literal existence clause for each U. Thus every five-set has an actual Hamilton P5 and no endpoint restriction is imposed.

FIRST PORT REALIZATION. The chosen first Hamilton order O is imposed by its three turn literals as unit clauses. Branching over all 12 endpoint-preserving choices is exhaustive because the hypothesized first port realization supplies at least one such actual order.

SECOND PORT REALIZATION. In Case I, introduce 12 witness variables for the orders of S whose endpoint pair is {4,1}. In Case II, introduce 12 witnesses for the orders of T whose endpoint pair is {5,1}. Each witness implies its three turn literals, and one 12-literal clause requires one witness.

Therefore every normalized case has
  105 + 21*120 + 12 = 2637 variables
and
  5040 + 21*120*3 + 21 + 3 + 12*3 + 1 = 12661 clauses.
No endpoint-pair cleanliness, Hall incidence, or Hamiltonicity beyond the 21 five-sets is assumed.

EXHAUSTIVE VERIFICATION. The Integrator generated all 24 CNFs directly from this definition: twelve Case-I instances and twelve Case-II instances. A standalone watched-literal DPLL solver with exact unit propagation, static weighted occurrence choice sum_C 2^{-|C|}, variable-index tie breaking, and false-before-true branching proves every instance UNSAT. The solver was independently sanity-checked against exhaustive truth-table evaluation on 100 random CNFs with at most seven variables, with no disagreement.

For Case I the twelve searches close between 180,092 and 306,967 nodes, maximum decision depth 43. For Case II they close between 95,490 and 113,962 nodes, maximum depth 44. Hence neither same-support nor different-support two-port realization can occur. Every four-core in G has at most one physical port.

Now suppose H is in the k=5, |H|=11 uniform middle-layer residue. Every seven-vertex induced subsystem of H satisfies the local hypotheses because every five-set of H is Hamiltonian and H has no P6. If any four-core R of H had two ports, retain the involved completion supports and enlarge their union, if necessary, to any seven vertices. The local theorem would forbid those two port realizations. Thus every four-core in H has a unique port.

But accepted R955 says that in exactly this order-eleven uniform residue, a minimum-cardinality Hall-deficient family in the complete all-endpoint incidence graph necessarily contains a PORT-SWITCH, i.e. a four-core with at least two distinct physical ports. Contradiction. Therefore the k=5 order-eleven uniform middle-layer residue does not exist. This proves R957.

# R958 — A two-cut singleton cross-swap reduces a three-cover to two increasing paths

## Statement
Let an edge-ordered complete graph have a spanning three-path cover A sqcup B sqcup {z}, with A and B nontrivial increasing paths. Orient A,B increasingly. Choose selected edges q->w of A and p->v of B. Let L(x) denote the incoming selected-edge label, with L(source)=-infinity, and U(x) the outgoing selected-edge label, with U(terminal)=+infinity. If L(q)<lambda(qz)<lambda(zv)<U(v) and L(p)<lambda(pw)<U(w), then deleting q->w and p->v and adding q->z, z->v, and p->w yields a spanning cover by two vertex-disjoint increasing paths. Explicitly the new paths are A_prefix_through_q followed by z followed by B_suffix_from_v, and B_prefix_through_p followed by A_suffix_from_w.

## Hypotheses
Pure finite edge-ordered complete graph; literal spanning cover A|B|{z}; A,B nontrivial increasing; q->w and p->v are selected edges on distinct rails.

## Scope
Order-free two-cut cooperative singleton absorption lemma; no 1-factorization hypothesis.

## Applicability
Use after one-cut R956 fails, or as a length-five threshold augment rooted at the singleton. It supplies a concrete consumer for simultaneous two-rail rotations.

## Persistence
Retain the two cut edges q->w,p->v, the three added edges qz,zv,pw, and the two full inequalities L(q)<qz<zv<U(v) and L(p)<pw<U(w).

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not prove every singleton three-cover admits such a pair of cuts. Does not justify arbitrary broad-interval alternating paths.

## Proof
Write A=A^- q,w A^+ where A^- ends immediately before q if nonempty and A^+ begins immediately after w if nonempty; equivalently let A_q be the prefix of A ending at q and A_w the suffix beginning at w. Likewise write B_p for the prefix of B ending at p and B_v for the suffix beginning at v. Delete the selected edges q->w and p->v. This splits A into A_q and A_w and B into B_p and B_v. Now form P1=A_q,z,B_v and P2=B_p,A_w. These two sequences are vertex-disjoint and together use every vertex exactly once. Every consecutive edge internal to A_q,A_w,B_p,B_v is inherited from the original increasing rails. At the new junctions of P1, the edge entering q (when present) has label L(q), followed by qz and then zv, followed by the old outgoing edge from v (when present) of label U(v). The hypothesis L(q)<lambda(qz)<lambda(zv)<U(v), interpreted with -infinity/+infinity endpoint conventions, therefore makes every new turn at q,z,v increasing. At the unique new junction of P2, the edge entering p (when present) has label L(p), then pw, then the old outgoing edge from w (when present) has label U(w); the hypothesis L(p)<lambda(pw)<U(w) makes these turns increasing. Hence P1 and P2 are increasing paths. Since two old edges were removed and three cross edges added, the component count drops from three to two, but the explicit path construction already proves the claimed spanning two-cover.

# R959 — A minimum counterexample to R888 has exact singleton-deletion two-covers with rail order at least three

## Statement
Let G be a finite edge-ordered complete graph that is a counterexample to R888 of minimum vertex order. Then pc_inc(G)=3. For every vertex z, pc_inc(G-z)=2, and in every exact two-path cover A|B of G-z both rails have at least three vertices. Hence any choice of one exact two-cover for each singleton deletion satisfies the hypotheses of the accepted singleton-cover compatibility theorem R926.

## Hypotheses
G is a minimum-order counterexample to the conjecture R888 that every edge-ordered complete graph has increasing path-cover number at most two.

## Scope
Pure edge-ordered minimal-counterexample reduction.

## Applicability
Use as the universal entrance for singleton absorption, deletion-fiber compatibility, or threshold exchange arguments for R888.

## Persistence
Retain minimum-order choice, exact two-cover of each G-z, and the singleton/dimer rail absorption arguments.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not prove R888 or any stronger rail floor. Does not assert a chosen deletion cover has unique supports or synchronized orders.

## Proof
Fix z in V(G). By minimum order, G-z satisfies R888, so pc_inc(G-z)<=2. If pc_inc(G-z)=1, let P be a Hamilton increasing path of G-z. Then P together with the singleton {z} is a spanning two-path cover of G, contradicting that G is a counterexample. Hence pc_inc(G-z)=2 for every z. Adding z as a singleton to any exact two-cover of G-z gives a spanning three-path cover of G, so pc_inc(G)<=3. Since G is a counterexample to pc_inc<=2, pc_inc(G)=3. Now let A|B be any exact two-path cover of G-z. If A is a singleton {a}, then B together with the dimer (z,a) is a spanning two-cover of G, contradiction. If A is a dimer on vertices a,b, consider the three ordinary edge labels on {z,a,b}. Let e_min and e_max be the smallest and largest of those three edges. In a triangle any two distinct edges share a common vertex; write e_min=uv and e_max=vw at their common endpoint v. Then (u,v,w) is an increasing Hamilton path of the three-set because lambda(uv)<lambda(vw). Replacing the dimer A and singleton z by this trimer, while retaining B, gives a spanning two-cover of G, contradiction. Thus |A|>=3, and symmetrically |B|>=3. The last statement follows because accepted R926 only requires chosen exact singleton-deletion two-covers with both rails of size at least two.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R959.md -->

# R961 — Role-correct endpoint-return Hall cycles reduce to R435 geometry or a constant-role directed triangle

## Statement
Retain all accepted conclusions of R945. In addition, choose the left-saturating endpoint-core matching and shortest directed cycle as in R945, and assume every adjacent puncture-path comparison is R435-quiet. Then the resulting shortest directed cycle is a triangle and its three matched endpoint roles are all the same: either all three matched endpoints are HEADs of their certified Hamilton puncture paths or all three are TAILs.

Write the triangle labels cyclically as A,B,C and put M=Omega-{A,B,C}. R435-quiet monotonicity gives one common literal order M=(m_1,...,m_r) in all three puncture paths. For each i, y_0=A,y_1=B,y_2=C, the path form is determined by (epsilon_i,epsilon_{i+1}): HH=(y_{i+1},y_{i+2},M), HT=(y_{i+1},M,y_{i+2}), TH=(y_{i+2},M,y_{i+1}), TT=(M,y_{i+2},y_{i+1}). Up to cyclic rotation the mixed patterns are HHT and HTT. In HHT, (B,C,M),(C,M,A),(B,M,A) occur, and the final turn of (C,M,A) appends A to (B,C,M), Hamiltonizing Omega. In HTT, (B,M,C),(M,A,C),(B,M,A) occur, and the final two turns of (M,A,C) insert A before C in (B,M,C), Hamiltonizing Omega. Hence only HHH or TTT survives outside explicit R435 output.

## Hypotheses
Finite boundary tournament Omega, |Omega|>=5, Omega non-Hamiltonian, every one-vertex deletion Hamiltonian. Use the R945 extremal left-saturating endpoint-core matching and assume adjacent comparisons on its shortest cycle are R435-quiet.

## Scope
All-order strengthening of accepted R945 for non-Hamiltonian deletion-Hamiltonian blocks. It removes the mixed-role triangle residual by literal puncture-path seam surgery. This redeposits the mathematics after a procedural review-write error on R960.

## Applicability
Inside a deletion-Hamiltonian non-Hamiltonian block, use R945 and then this theorem: either retain explicit R435 geometry, or work with one directed endpoint-return triangle whose three certified puncture paths have a common HEAD role or a common TAIL role.

## Persistence
Retain the matching, triangle labels A,B,C, actual puncture paths, certified HEAD/TAIL roles, common literal M order, and the exact mixed-role surgery.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not consume the surviving HHH/TTT triangle. Does not reverse any puncture path or synchronize unrelated puncture paths.

## Proof
Apply accepted R945. If an adjacent puncture-path comparison yields an R435 reversal, reverse trimer, or proper tight cycle, retain that output. Otherwise the extremal shortest functional cycle is a directed triangle. Write y_0=A,y_1=B,y_2=C cyclically, and let P_i be the actual Hamilton path on Omega-y_i whose matched endpoint is y_{i+1}; epsilon_i=H or T records whether that endpoint is the certified head or tail. No path is reversed.

Put M=Omega-{A,B,C}. Quiet adjacent comparisons preserve the literal order of their common vertices, so all three puncture paths induce one common order M=(m_1,...,m_r), r>=2. The common vertex y_{i+2} is the matched endpoint of P_{i+1}; if epsilon_{i+1}=H it is the first common contact in both P_{i+1} and P_i, and if epsilon_{i+1}=T it is the last common contact in both. Together with the location of the noncommon matched label y_{i+1} in P_i, this gives exactly:
HH: P_i=(y_{i+1},y_{i+2},M);
HT: P_i=(y_{i+1},M,y_{i+2});
TH: P_i=(y_{i+2},M,y_{i+1});
TT: P_i=(M,y_{i+2},y_{i+1}).

If roles are mixed, cyclic rotation reduces to HHT or HTT.

For HHT, epsilon_0=H,epsilon_1=H,epsilon_2=T, so
P_0=(B,C,M), P_1=(C,M,A), P_2=(B,M,A).
All turns of (B,C,M) are certified by P_0. The sole new turn required to append A is (m_{r-1},m_r,A), which is the final turn of P_1. Thus (B,C,M,A) is Hamiltonian on Omega, contradiction.

For HTT, epsilon_0=H,epsilon_1=T,epsilon_2=T, so
P_0=(B,M,C), P_1=(M,A,C), P_2=(B,M,A).
Insert A immediately before C in P_0. The only new turns are (m_{r-1},m_r,A) and (m_r,A,C), both consecutive turns of P_1. Hence (B,M,A,C) is Hamiltonian on Omega, contradiction.

Thus every quiet triangle has constant role HHH or TTT. This proves R961.

# R962 — A trimer deletion rail in a minimum R888 counterexample forces a four-vertex compatibility star with four blocked Hamilton extensions

## Statement
Let G be a minimum-order counterexample to R888. Suppose for some z there is an exact two-path cover G-z=A|B with |A|=3. Put X=A union {z}. Then X is non-Hamiltonian. For every x in X, the three-set X-{x} has an increasing Hamilton path and G-x has an exact two-cover (X-{x})|B. Hence the singleton-deletion cover family may be chosen so that the four physical vertices in X form one compatibility clique in the sense of R926; in the canonical rail-incidence root they are four edges incident with one root port P and Omega_P=X. Moreover B union {x} is non-Hamiltonian for every x in X.

## Hypotheses
G is a minimum-order edge-ordered complete-graph counterexample to R888; G-z has an exact two-cover with one rail of order three.

## Scope
Pure edge-order singleton-fiber reduction plus accepted R926 support-root interpretation.

## Applicability
Use to attack the first possible short deletion rail. It reduces the case to four simultaneous blocked one-vertex Hamilton extensions of one fixed Hamilton rail B, with a four-vertex non-Hamiltonian port universe X.

## Persistence
Retain z, the literal trimer support A, fixed opposite Hamilton rail B, X=A+z, the four exact covers (X-x)|B, and the common R926 root port universe Omega_P=X.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not prove that trimer rails are impossible, does not synchronize the Hamilton orders on X-x, and does not classify X beyond non-Hamiltonicity.

## Proof
Let G be a minimum-order counterexample to R888 and suppose G-z=A|B is an exact two-path cover with |A|=3. Put X=A∪{z}. By R959 both A and B are nonempty, indeed of order at least three. First X is non-Hamiltonian: if X had an increasing Hamilton path, that path together with the literal increasing Hamilton path on B from the displayed cover would be a spanning two-path cover of G, contradiction.\n\nFix x∈X. The induced graph on X-{x} has three vertices. Every edge-ordered triangle has an increasing Hamilton path: among its three edge labels, the minimum and maximum edges share one vertex, and traversing the minimum edge into that common vertex and then the maximum edge gives a two-edge increasing path. Hence X-{x} is Hamiltonian. Since B is disjoint from X and is Hamiltonian in the original cover, G-x has the exact two-cover (X-{x})|B. We may therefore choose these four covers for the four singleton deletions x∈X.\n\nFor distinct x,y∈X, the chosen support partitions for G-x and G-y restrict on V(G)-{x,y} to the same unordered partition (X-{x,y})|B. Thus x and y are compatible in the sense of R926. Hence the four physical vertices of X form a K4 in the compatibility graph, which R926 identifies with the line graph L(R) of a simple triangle-free root R. In a simple triangle-free graph, four pairwise incident edges must have a common endpoint: choose two meeting at P; any third edge incident with both either also contains P or completes a triangle, so it contains P; the same applies to the fourth. Let P be this common root port.\n\nUsing the cover C_z, the P-side rail support is X-{z}; therefore the R926 port universe is Omega_P=(X-{z})∪{z}=X. There can be no further physical edge incident with P, because every edge incident with P belongs to Omega_P by the definition of a port universe, while Omega_P=X. Thus the four vertices of X are exactly the four physical root edges incident with P.\n\nFinally fix x∈X. If B∪{x} had an increasing Hamilton path, then together with the already established Hamilton path on X-{x} it would form a spanning two-path cover of G, contradiction. Hence B∪{x} is non-Hamiltonian for every x∈X. This proves all assertions.

# R963 — Two P4-free edge-ordered four-sets sharing a triangle force a Hamilton five-path

## Statement
Let G be an edge-ordered complete graph and let T={u0,u1,u2} be a three-vertex set. Let x,y be distinct vertices outside T. If both induced edge orders on T∪{x} and T∪{y} have no increasing Hamilton path, then G[T∪{x,y}] has an increasing Hamilton path.

## Hypotheses
Pure edge-ordered complete graph; two four-vertex induced subgraphs sharing exactly the triangle T are non-Hamiltonian.

## Scope
Pure local edge-order theorem; no minimality or singleton-fiber assumptions.

## Applicability
Use when two critical four-vertex port universes differ by exchanging one completion vertex. It converts simultaneous P4-free constraints under the same numerical edge order into a Hamilton P5.

## Persistence
Retain the shared-triangle normalization, the elementary K4 matching-height classification, and the two candidate Hamilton paths selected by comparing the two middle spoke edges.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert either four-set is unique or that a Hamilton P5 by itself extends to a global two-cover.

## Proof
First note the elementary K4 classification. Let the six edges of an edge-ordered K4 be e1<e2<...<e6. If e1 and e2 shared a vertex, say e1=ab and e2=bc, then with d the fourth vertex the edge cd occurs after e2, so a-b-c-d would be an increasing Hamilton path. Hence e1,e2 are disjoint. Dually e5,e6 are disjoint: if e5=bc and e6=cd, then the remaining edge ab occurs before e5, so a-b-c-d is increasing. Therefore {e1,e2} and {e5,e6} are two opposite perfect matchings, and the remaining {e3,e4} is the third opposite perfect matching. Thus every non-Hamiltonian edge-ordered K4 has its three opposite matchings in strict height blocks. Conversely such a matching-block order is visibly P4-free because the first and third edges of any Hamilton path are opposite and hence lie in the same matching block, so they cannot straddle the middle path edge increasingly.\n\nNow suppose T={u0,u1,u2} and both T+x and T+y are non-Hamiltonian. Relabel T so u1u2<u0u2<u0u1. In the K4 T+r, r∈{x,y}, the opposite matching containing u1u2 is {u1u2,ru0}, the one containing u0u2 is {u0u2,ru1}, and the one containing u0u1 is {u0u1,ru2}. Since the three internal T edges occur in the displayed low/middle/high order, the matching-height classification forces all edges of the first matching below all edges of the second, and all edges of the second below all edges of the third. In particular ru0<ru1<ru2 for r=x,y. Compare xu1 and yu1. If xu1<yu1, then the path u0,x,u1,y,u2 has edge labels u0x<xu1<yu1<yu2 and is increasing. If yu1<xu1, then u0,y,u1,x,u2 is increasing. Thus T∪{x,y} has an increasing Hamilton path.

# R965 — Singleton-cover compatibility has a canonical rail-incidence root which is a forest or one spanning odd cycle

## Statement
Retain every conclusion of accepted R926. Let Q be a root vertex whose port universe Omega_Q is SATURATED in the sense that the physical edge labels incident with Q are exactly the vertices of Omega_Q, and suppose |Omega_Q|=deg_R(Q)>=3. Then the connected component of the R926 root containing Q is a depth-two star-of-stars.

More precisely, R is in its forest alternative. For every incident edge x=Q R_x,
  Omega_{R_x}=(V(H)-Omega_Q) union {x}.
Every physical edge p outside Omega_Q that lies in the Q-component has root-edge depth exactly two from Q, so it has the unique form p=R_x S_p for one x in Omega_Q. The far endpoint S_p is a leaf and
  Omega_{S_p}=(Omega_Q-{x}) union {p}.
There are no root edges at depth three or greater in this component.

Consequently, whenever a critical block Omega is realized by the compatible singleton fibers P | (Omega-x) for all x in Omega and these spokes saturate one R926 port Q, every outside physical label that lies in that root component is a literal one-for-one exchanged leaf Omega-x+p. The theorem is support/universe geometry only; it does not assert that all outside labels lie in this component or synchronize Hamilton orders.

## Hypotheses
Accepted R926 setup. A root vertex Q has saturated universe Omega_Q: its incident physical edge labels equal Omega_Q. Degree at least three.

## Scope
Pure strengthening of accepted R926. No boundary antisymmetry or Hamilton-order synchronization is used beyond the R926 rail-incidence root and its one-defect universe colorings.

## Applicability
Use around any saturated critical port universe. It generalizes the root-depth part of R964 and identifies every same-component outside label with one exact one-for-one universe exchange. In the balanced uniform middle layer a deliberate choice of singleton covers can place every complementary label into this depth-two component, recovering the spanning double-star support shell.

## Persistence
Retain Q, Omega_Q, each spoke x=Q R_x, every depth-two physical edge p=R_x S_p, and the exact port universes Omega_{R_x} and Omega_{S_p}. No path-order relation is inherited.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not say every physical label outside Omega_Q belongs to the Q-component. Does not prove a critical block is absorbable. Does not assert Hamiltonicity of the exchanged universe Omega_Q-x+p unless supplied separately. Does not synchronize any Hamilton orders.

## Proof
Retain the accepted R926 root R and port universes. Let Q have saturated universe Omega=Omega_Q, so the physical edges incident with Q are exactly the labels in Omega, and deg(Q)=|Omega|>=3.

Because accepted R926 says the root is either a forest or one spanning odd cycle, and every vertex of the spanning-cycle alternative has degree two, Q of degree at least three forces the FOREST alternative.

Fix one incident physical edge x=Q R_x. R926 gives
  Omega_Q union Omega_{R_x}=V(H),
  Omega_Q intersect Omega_{R_x}={x}.
Since Omega_Q=Omega, this determines
  Omega_{R_x}=(V(H)-Omega) union {x}.                       (1)

Now let p be a physical label outside Omega whose root edge belongs to the connected component of Q. Use the accepted R926 one-defect coloring
  epsilon_p(S)=1 iff p in Omega_S.
Since p notin Omega_Q, epsilon_p(Q)=0. For every spoke x=Q R_x, equation (1) gives p in Omega_{R_x}, so epsilon_p(R_x)=1. More generally, every root edge other than the physical edge p is bichromatic under epsilon_p, while the two endpoints of edge p both have color 1.

Define the depth of a root edge e in the Q-component to be one plus the distance from Q to its nearer endpoint. Let the physical edge p have depth d. Along the unique forest path from Q to the nearer endpoint of p there are d-1 root edges, none equal to p, so the one-defect coloring alternates across all of them. Starting from epsilon_p(Q)=0, the nearer endpoint therefore has color congruent to d-1 mod 2. But it is an endpoint of the p-edge, so its color is 1. Hence d is even.                              (2)

By saturation, every depth-one edge is labelled by a vertex of Omega, and conversely no physical label outside Omega can occur at depth one. Thus every root edge at depth at least two has a physical label outside Omega and itself satisfies the even-depth conclusion (2). If some edge had depth at least three, take the first edge at depth three along its Q-path. That edge is outside Omega but has odd depth, contradicting (2). Hence the component has no edge of depth three or greater. Every outside physical edge in the component has depth exactly two.

So each such p has a unique form
  p=R_x S_p
for one spoke x=Q R_x. Since no depth-three edge exists, S_p is a leaf. Apply R926's union/intersection identities to the p-edge. From (1), Omega_{R_x}=(V-Omega) union {x}. Therefore V-Omega_{R_x}=Omega-{x}. The opposite universe Omega_{S_p} must contain every vertex outside Omega_{R_x}, must contain p, and can contain no other vertex of Omega_{R_x} because the intersection across edge p is exactly {p}. Consequently
  Omega_{S_p}=(Omega-{x}) union {p}.                        (3)

Equations (1)-(3) prove the claimed depth-two star-of-stars normal form and exact one-for-one exchange universes. No Hamilton-order synchronization or boundary antisymmetry beyond the already accepted R926 structure was used.

# R966 — Two-ended replacement by one exterior vertex forces Reverse-Ear geometry or a Hamilton extension

## Statement
Let Q=(q_0,q_1,...,q_r) be a vertex-simple Hamilton tight path on a support X with r>=2, and let y be a vertex outside X. Assume X union {y} is non-Hamiltonian. Suppose there is a Hamilton tight path L on (X-{q_0}) union {y} and a Hamilton tight path R on (X-{q_r}) union {y}.

Then at least one of the three path comparisons (Q,L), (Q,R), or (L,R) has an explicit R435 Reverse-Ear output: a reversed old state, a tight reverse trimer at a seam, or a vertex-simple proper tight cycle. Equivalently, outside explicit R435 geometry one exterior vertex cannot simultaneously Hamilton-replace both endpoints of one Hamilton path while the full one-vertex extension remains non-Hamiltonian.

More precisely, if (Q,L) is R435-quiet then L is exactly one of
  (y,q_1,q_2,...,q_r),
  (q_1,y,q_2,...,q_r).
If (Q,R) is R435-quiet then R is exactly one of
  (q_0,...,q_{r-1},y),
  (q_0,...,q_{r-2},y,q_{r-1}).
If (L,R) is also R435-quiet, the common-vertex orders can agree only in the boundary-overlap cases r=2 or r=3, and in each such case the two certified path segments concatenate to a Hamilton path of X union {y}, contradiction.

## Hypotheses
Finite Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament; Q is a tight path of order at least three; y is exterior; X+y is non-Hamiltonian; both endpoint-replacement supports admit actual Hamilton tight paths L and R.

## Scope
Pure all-order path-interaction theorem. No smallest-counterexample, cover, uniformity, critical-block, payment, or global-longest hypothesis.

## Applicability
Critical-block endpoint-exchange capacity. In Arm A it proves the working claim that one y cannot realize both left- and right-end exchange in an R435-quiet cell. In Arm B uniformity supplies both endpoint-replacement supports for every y outside a Hamilton k-rail, so every such y forces explicit R435 geometry unless the forbidden k+1 extension already exists.

## Persistence
Retain Q with its literal orientation, y, actual replacement paths L and R, and whichever exact R435 comparison fires. If all comparisons are provisionally quiet, retain the forced near-end insertion forms and the literal Hamilton-extension splice.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not consume the resulting R435 output. Does not say which of the three comparisons fires. Does not imply a spanning two-cover without an additional consumer. Does not reverse any input path.

## Proof
Let Q=(q_0,q_1,...,q_r), r>=2, be a tight Hamilton path on X, let y be outside X, and assume X union {y} is non-Hamiltonian. Let L be Hamilton on (X-{q_0}) union {y} and R Hamilton on (X-{q_r}) union {y}. Suppose, toward contradiction, that all three comparisons (Q,L), (Q,R), and (L,R) are R435-quiet.\n\nFirst compare Q with L. The Q-contacts appearing in L are exactly q_1,...,q_r. By the concluding monotonicity clause of R435, because the comparison is quiet these contacts occur in increasing Q-order. Hence L is obtained by inserting y into the literal sequence (q_1,...,q_r). If y were not in one of the first two positions of L, then L would begin (q_1,q_2). Since (q_0,q_1,q_2) is tight on Q, prepending q_0 to L would give a tight Hamilton path on X union {y}, contradiction. Therefore\n  L=(y,q_1,q_2,...,q_r)\nor\n  L=(q_1,y,q_2,...,q_r).                                             (1)\n\nDually compare Q with R. Quietness forces the Q-contacts q_0,...,q_{r-1} to occur in increasing Q-order, so R is obtained by inserting y into (q_0,...,q_{r-1}). If y were not in one of the last two positions, R would end (q_{r-2},q_{r-1}); appending q_r using the tight Q-turn (q_{r-2},q_{r-1},q_r) would Hamiltonize X union {y}. Thus\n  R=(q_0,...,q_{r-1},y)\nor\n  R=(q_0,...,q_{r-2},y,q_{r-1}).                                     (2)\n\nNow compare L with R. Their common vertices are y,q_1,...,q_{r-1}. Write L_1=(y,q_1,...,q_r), L_2=(q_1,y,q_2,...,q_r), R_1=(q_0,...,q_{r-1},y), and R_2=(q_0,...,q_{r-2},y,q_{r-1}).\n\nFor (L_1,R_1), the common order has y before q_1 in L_1 but q_1 before y in R_1, so R435 fires. For (L_1,R_2), the same reversal occurs whenever r>=3; the only quiet possibility is r=2. For (L_2,R_1), y precedes q_2 in L_2 but follows q_2 in R_1 whenever r>=3; the only quiet possibility is r=2. For (L_2,R_2), the same reversal with q_2 occurs whenever r>=4; for r=2 the common pair q_1,y is reversed, so R435 fires; the only quiet possibility is r=3. Thus all three comparisons can be quiet only in the following three boundary-overlap cases.\n\nIf r=2, L=L_1=(y,q_1,q_2) and R=R_2=(q_0,y,q_1). The consecutive tight turns from R and L concatenate to the Hamilton path (q_0,y,q_1,q_2) on X union {y}, contradiction.\n\nIf r=2, L=L_2=(q_1,y,q_2) and R=R_1=(q_0,q_1,y). They concatenate to (q_0,q_1,y,q_2), again Hamilton on X union {y}.\n\nIf r=3, L=L_2=(q_1,y,q_2,q_3) and R=R_2=(q_0,q_1,y,q_2). Their overlapping certified turns concatenate to the Hamilton path (q_0,q_1,y,q_2,q_3).\n\nEvery quiet possibility therefore contradicts non-Hamiltonicity of X union {y}. Hence at least one of (Q,L), (Q,R), or (L,R) has an explicit R435 output. No reversal of an input path is used.

# R971 — Every edge-ordered K7 has a spanning cover by at most two increasing paths

## Statement
Let K_7 have any strict total order on its 21 ordinary edges. Then its seven vertices can be partitioned into at most two vertex-disjoint increasing paths. Equivalently, no edge ordering of K_7 has increasing path-cover number at least three.

## Hypotheses
Pure edge-ordered complete graph K7 with a strict total order on all 21 edges.

## Scope
Exact finite edge-order theorem. Computational certificate is complete and self-contained at the CNF level; no boundary-tournament shared strategy or minimum-counterexample hypothesis is used.

## Applicability
Finite base for R888. In particular, a minimum R888 counterexample has order at least eight; hence in the R962/R969 trimer-fiber setup the fixed opposite rail B cannot also have order three, and the R969 long-rail reduction applies to every trimer deletion rail once this finite theorem is canonically accepted.

## Persistence
Retain the 21 lexicographically indexed ordinary edges, 210 pairwise edge-order variables, 2660 transitivity clauses, 12600 deduplicated two-path-cover-forbidding clauses, canonical CNF hash, and the independent DPLL/MILP infeasibility checks.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not prove R888 for order eight or larger. Does not classify extremal K7 edge orders or produce a canonical two-cover algorithm. Pending canonical review must remain distinct from the checked computational evidence.

## Proof
Index the 21 ordinary edges of K_7 lexicographically as e_0,...,e_20. For each 0<=i<j<=20 introduce one Boolean variable X_{ij}, interpreted as “e_i precedes e_j in the edge order”. Since exactly one of e_i<e_j and e_j<e_i holds, one bit per unordered edge-pair is enough; there are C(21,2)=210 variables.

TOTAL-ORDER CLAUSES. For every i<j<k add
  (not X_{ij}) OR (not X_{jk}) OR X_{ik},
  X_{ij} OR X_{jk} OR (not X_{ik}).
These are exactly the two clauses excluding the two directed 3-cycles on {e_i,e_j,e_k}. There are 2*C(21,3)=2660 such clauses. A tournament on the 21 edge-objects with no directed triangle is transitive, so these clauses are equivalent to the existence of one strict total edge order realizing all X_{ij}.

TWO-PATH-COVER CLAUSES. Take every ordered vertex permutation pi=(v_0,...,v_6) and every cut c in {1,...,6}. This represents the two oriented vertex paths
  P=(v_0,...,v_{c-1}),
  Q=(v_c,...,v_6).
For a path W=(w_0,...,w_s), write f_t={w_t,w_{t+1}}. The path is increasing exactly when every consecutive comparison f_t<f_{t+1} holds, t=0,...,s-2; a singleton or dimer contributes no comparison. For each (pi,c), collect all comparison literals required simultaneously by P and Q and add the single clause which is the disjunction of their negations. Thus the clause says that this particular ordered two-path cover is not increasing on both rails.

Every spanning cover by two increasing paths occurs among these permutation/cut representations after orienting each rail increasingly and ordering the two rails. A Hamilton increasing path also yields one of these two-path covers by splitting off its first vertex as a singleton, so forbidding all represented two-path covers forbids covers by at most two paths. Conversely, a satisfying assignment of all cover-forbidding clauses represents a strict edge order with no spanning increasing two-path cover.

After exact deduplication, the cover family contributes 12,600 distinct clauses: 7,560 clauses of length three and 5,040 clauses of length four. Together with the 2,660 transitivity clauses, the final CNF has
  210 variables,
  15,260 clauses,
  10,220 clauses of length three,
  5,040 clauses of length four.
Sorting literals in each clause by variable and sorting clauses lexicographically, the DIMACS-style text “lit ... lit 0” joined by newlines has SHA-256
  625270abc73035479584b613d96049c50cf10f22eb8e4bf565928f96e246c9eb.

EXHAUSTIVE CHECK 1: DPLL. A deterministic watched-literal DPLL verifier performs unit propagation to closure, then branches on the unassigned variable of highest total literal occurrence (ties by lowest variable index); it tries the majority-occurrence polarity first, with positive chosen on a tie, then the opposite polarity. On the full unsymmetrized CNF above it terminates UNSAT after 355 recursive search nodes, maximum branch depth 24, with no satisfying leaf. The watched-literal implementation was separately compared against brute-force truth-table satisfiability on 300 randomly generated CNFs with at most eight variables and agreed in every case. No vertex or edge-order symmetry assumption is used in this 355-node run.

EXHAUSTIVE CHECK 2: INDEPENDENT BINARY MILP. Independently encode the same 210 comparison bits as binary variables. Each of the two transitivity clauses per edge triple is written as its equivalent linear 0-1 inequality, and each forbidden two-path conjunction is written as “sum of its required comparison indicators <= number of requirements minus 1”. This gives 15,260 linear constraints before solver presolve. SciPy 1.17 scipy.optimize.milp with bundled HiGHS reports the model infeasible. This model was generated independently of the watched-literal propagation code.

Therefore the CNF has no satisfying assignment. Hence no strict edge ordering of K_7 can avoid every spanning cover by at most two increasing paths. Every edge-ordered K_7 has increasing path-cover number at most two, proving R971.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R971.md -->

# R972 — A trimer port forces a depth-two critical-cell component and expels Hamilton endpoints of the opposite rail

## Statement
Retain every conclusion of accepted R969 in the minimum-order R888 trimer-fiber setup G=X disjoint-union B. Then the following additional conclusions hold.

(1) CRITICAL FIVE-CELL DUALITY. For every Hamilton-deletable b in B and every x in X, X+b is non-Hamiltonian, X-x+b is Hamiltonian, and B-b+x is non-Hamiltonian. Thus every Hamilton-deletable b simultaneously gives four small-side Hamilton replacements and four complementary blocked large-side exchanges.

(2) INTERIOR BARRIER CONFINEMENT. Fix any increasing Hamilton order B=(b_0,...,b_m). For every x in X let beta_B(x) be the accepted R895 canonical insertion barrier against this displayed order. Then
  1 <= beta_B(x) <= m-2.
In particular every canonical barrier lies strictly away from both ends of every Hamilton order on B.

(3) OPPOSITE-RAIL FLOOR. Necessarily |B|>=5. Order three is impossible because the interval [1,m-2] is empty. Order four is impossible because, for distinct x,y in X, the blocked four-sets (B-b_0)+x and (B-b_0)+y share the Hamilton triangle B-b_0; accepted R963 Hamiltonizes their five-vertex union, while the complementary three-set is automatically Hamiltonian, yielding a spanning two-cover.

Consequently the accepted R969 long-rail reduction is universal in the trimer-fiber branch: every Hamilton order on B enters the R541 ALIGNED/CROSSED gate state, R582 supplies an endpoint-favorable P5, and R540 yields a one-hole spanning proposal with the exact normalized seam coordinates already retained by R969/D5. The current trimer problem therefore has no |B|=3 or |B|=4 residual.

## Hypotheses
G is a minimum-order counterexample to R888 in the accepted R969 trimer-fiber setup. B=(b_0,...,b_m) is any increasing Hamilton order on the fixed opposite rail. Uses accepted R895,R963,R967,R969.

## Scope
Independent-safe monotone merge of accepted R969 with the mathematically verified P1041 barrier/five-cell strengthening. It preserves the current gate/one-hole interface while adding interior barrier confinement and the |B|>=5 floor.

## Applicability
Use as the next trimer parent once reviewed. Do not restart small-order or endpoint-gate classification: every trimer branch has |B|>=5, four interior R895 barriers on every Hamilton order, R969 aligned/crossed one-hole data, and critical five-cell duality at every Hamilton-deletable rail vertex.

## Persistence
Retain all R969 coordinates. Additionally retain each Hamilton-deletable b, each x, the Hamilton small support X-x+b, blocked support B-b+x, the chosen Hamilton order B, beta_B(x), and the endpoint inequalities xb_1>e_1 and b_{m-1}x<e_{m-2}.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not close either ALIGNED or CROSSED one-hole branch. Does not assert beta-values are distinct or ordered, every interior vertex of B is Hamilton-deletable, or R958 applies. Does not use pending R971.

## Proof
Retain every conclusion of accepted R969.

Let b in B be Hamilton-deletable and fix x in X. Since B-b is Hamiltonian, X+b cannot be Hamiltonian, otherwise (X+b)|(B-b) is a spanning two-cover. Suppose X-x+b were non-Hamiltonian. Then X and X-x+b are two non-Hamiltonian four-sets sharing the triangle X-x, so accepted R963 gives a Hamilton path on X+b. Together with Hamilton B-b this again two-covers G, contradiction. Hence X-x+b is Hamiltonian. Accepted R967 gives the complementary statement that B-b+x is non-Hamiltonian. This proves the critical five-cell duality.

Now fix any Hamilton order B=(b_0,...,b_m), write e_i=b_i b_{i+1}, and fix x in X. Since B+x is non-Hamiltonian, x is noninsertable into every gap of this displayed order, so accepted R895 defines beta_B(x). Endpoint b_0 is Hamilton-deletable, and R967 makes B-b_0+x non-Hamiltonian. If xb_1<e_1 then (x,b_1,...,b_m) is Hamiltonian on B-b_0+x, contradiction. Thus xb_1>e_1, so gap 0 is not right-feasible and beta_B(x) is not 0.

Dually b_m is Hamilton-deletable and R967 makes B-b_m+x non-Hamiltonian. If b_{m-1}x>e_{m-2}, then (b_0,...,b_{m-1},x) is Hamiltonian on B-b_m+x, contradiction. Hence b_{m-1}x<e_{m-2}. If beta_B(x)=m-1, the R895 canonical gap is left-feasible and would require e_{m-2}<b_{m-1}x, contradiction. Therefore beta_B(x) is not m-1. Consequently 1<=beta_B(x)<=m-2 for every x.

This interval is empty when |B|=3, so order three is impossible. If |B|=4, choose distinct x,y in X. The endpoint b_0 is Hamilton-deletable, so R967 makes S_x=(B-b_0)+x and S_y=(B-b_0)+y two non-Hamiltonian four-sets sharing the triangle B-b_0. R963 Hamiltonizes their five-vertex union (B-b_0)+x+y. Its complement is {b_0} union (X-{x,y}), a three-set and hence Hamiltonian in every edge-ordered complete graph. The two Hamilton paths form a spanning two-cover, contradiction. Thus |B|>=5.

Since |B|>=5, the size hypothesis of accepted R969 always holds. Therefore every Hamilton order on B has the retained R969 R541 ALIGNED/CROSSED polarity, R582 endpoint-favorable P5, R540 one-hole proposal, and normalized exact seam coordinates, in addition to the new critical-five-cell and interior-barrier conclusions. This proves R972.

# R974 — Universal first-inward stars compile to two-ended path geometry and same-frame capture portals

## Statement
Let H be a finite Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament with pc(H)>2. Let Q=(q_0,...,q_m), m>=4, be a tight path and let X be a four-vertex set disjoint from Q. Write u=q_1, v=q_2, d=q_{m-2}, s=q_{m-1}, w=q_3, and rho=q_{m-3}. Assume the UNIVERSAL FIRST-INWARD STARS
  (v,u,x) tight and (x,s,d) tight for every x in X.
Then:

(1) TWO-ENDED PATH GEOMETRY. Either for some x in X the forward middle turn (u,x,s) is tight, in which case (v,u,x,s) is a tight P4 and, when m>=5, it extends to the vertex-simple tight P5 (v,u,x,s,d); or else every forward middle turn is bad, so (s,x,u) is tight for every x and every unordered pair {x,y} in X supports one of the tight cross-depth P4s (s,x,u,y),(s,y,u,x). Thus the m=4 hinge case is explicitly P4-valued, while the P5 conclusion is restricted to m>=5.

(2) STATIC FOUR-WITNESS SINGLETON PAIR. The first-inward reverse dimers carry opposite polarities with any chosen common witness x: (v,u) is tail-signed by x and (s,d) is head-signed by x. Cutting the intervening Q interval when m>=5, or applying the one-hinge reduction when m=4, gives opposite-sign singleton supports {u} and {s}; the same physical singleton pair retains all four X witness certificates. This is static signed-support geometry, not payment-lineage floor status.

(3) LEFT SAME-FRAME CAPTURE PORTALS. Suppose T_L is any exact two-cover of H-{u,v}. Regard S_L=(u,v) as tail-signed by w via the old Q turn (u,v,w). For each x in X, K_x=(v,u,x) is a tight trimer spanning {u,v,x}. R508 applied to the same T_L forces a selected state C_x={x,y_x} with y_x outside K_x. At most two distinct x can have y_x=w because the selected-state graph of T_L is a union of two paths and deg_{T_L}(w)<=2. Therefore at least two distinct x in X have witness-avoiding selected crossings. For each such x, R527 can orient the crossing marker so that x itself is the captured signed anchor in this same deletion frame.

(4) RIGHT SAME-FRAME CAPTURE PORTALS. Dually, if T_R is any exact two-cover of H-{d,s}, regard S_R=(d,s) as head-signed by rho via (rho,d,s). For every x, K_x=(x,s,d) is a tight trimer. R508 in the same T_R gives four x-labelled crossings; at most two use rho as exterior endpoint, so at least two distinct X vertices are witness-avoiding and may each be captured by R527 in that same right deletion frame.

In a minimum-order counterexample to R888, accepted R967 supplies the displayed universal first-inward stars for every Hamilton order of the fixed opposite rail B in the trimer-fiber setup, and minimum-order induction supplies the required pair-deletion two-covers. Thus this theorem gives an Independent-safe bridge from the D5 trimer shell into the mature first-inward path/capture machinery without assuming the crossed R24 frame.

## Hypotheses
H finite Strong Level-(1) with pc(H)>2; Q tight with m>=4; X a four-set disjoint from Q; displayed universal first-inward star families. Parts (3),(4) additionally assume literal exact two-covers of the displayed pair deletions.

## Scope
Corrected pure literal-star compiler plus exact-cover capture portal theorem. Generalizes transferable cores of R775/R848/R744 but repairs the m=4 repeated-vertex defect in the old R775 P5 wording. No gate phase, R24, R5, payment lineage, Reverse Ear, or computation is used.

## Applicability
Use whenever two four-witness first-inward stars occur around one tight rail. In the minimum R888 trimer branch they arise directly from R967 endpoint-exchange blocking. At m=4 retain the P4/hinge outputs, not a P5.

## Persistence
Retain Q,u,v,d,s,w,rho,X; all star turns; exact P4/P5 or pair-indexed P4 certificates; singleton signs and four witness certificates; for each portal side the one fixed deletion cover, four R508 crossings, and at least two witness-avoiding captured X anchors.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert a P5 at m=4. Does not assert the same two X anchors are captured on both sides, coexistence of multiple actualized descendants, R312 first-contact ancestry, payment-lineage floor status, or closure.

## Proof
Put u=q_1, v=q_2, d=q_{m-2}, s=q_{m-1}. For every x in X, (v,u,x) and (x,s,d) are tight.

For the path geometry, apply R3 to {u,x,s}. If (u,x,s) is tight for some x, then the consecutive turns (v,u,x),(u,x,s) make (v,u,x,s) a tight P4. If m>=5 then q_2=v and q_{m-2}=d are distinct, so appending the tight turn (x,s,d) gives the vertex-simple tight P5 (v,u,x,s,d). When m=4, v=d=q_2, so no P5 is claimed; the P4 is the exact forward-middle output. If no x has (u,x,s) tight, then R3 gives (s,x,u) for every x. For distinct x,y, R3 on {x,u,y} gives exactly one of (x,u,y),(y,u,x), yielding respectively the tight P4 (s,x,u,y) or (s,y,u,x). This proves (1) with the m=4 correction.

For (2), (v,u,x) makes (v,u) tail-signed by x and (x,s,d) makes (s,d) head-signed by x. If m>=5, apply R425 to the intervening Q interval exactly as in the standard cut-memory argument: the left surviving singleton u keeps x as tail witness and the right singleton s keeps x as head witness. If m=4, the source dimers meet exactly at v=d=q_2 and R547 hinge reduction leaves opposite-sign singletons u=q_1 and s=q_3. Since x was arbitrary and all star certificates coexist, the same singleton pair carries all four X witness ledgers.

For (3), let T_L cover H-{u,v}. The Q turn (u,v,w), w=q_3, makes S_L=(u,v) tail-signed by w. For each x, K_x=(v,u,x) is tight and spans {u,v,x}. R508 with deletion {u,v}, absorbable singleton {x}, K_x, and the same T_L gives a selected crossing C_x={x,y_x}, y_x outside K_x. Distinct x give distinct selected edges. If y_x=w call x blocked. Since T_L is a two-path forest, w has selected degree at most two, so at most two x are blocked. At least two crossings avoid w; R527 applied in this same frame may orient each marker to designate its X endpoint x as captured. No coexistence of later actualizations is asserted.

For (4), let T_R cover H-{d,s}. The old Q turn (rho,d,s), rho=q_{m-3}, makes S_R=(d,s) head-signed by rho. For each x, K_x=(x,s,d) is tight. R508 gives C_x={x,y_x}; at most two selected crossings can have y_x=rho because deg_{T_R}(rho)<=2. Each other crossing avoids the witness, so R527 captures its X endpoint. Hence at least two distinct right portals exist.

Finally specialize to the minimum R888 trimer setup. Accepted R967 says endpoint deletion/replacement supports are non-Hamiltonian. For the left endpoint q_0, if xq_1<q_1q_2 then (x,q_1,...,q_m) Hamiltonizes (B-q_0)+x, contradiction; hence q_1q_2<q_1x, i.e. (v,u,x). At the right endpoint, if q_{m-2}q_{m-1}<q_{m-1}x then (q_0,...,q_{m-1},x) Hamiltonizes (B-q_m)+x; therefore xq_{m-1}<q_{m-2}q_{m-1}, i.e. (x,s,d). Minimum-order induction gives pc<=2 on each proper pair deletion; if a pair deletion is Hamiltonian, split one Hamilton path into two nonempty tight paths to obtain the exact two-cover needed above. This proves the R888 specialization and R974.

# R975 — A trimer deletion rail in a minimum R888 counterexample cannot face a Hamilton rail of order four or five

## Statement
Let G be a minimum-order counterexample to R888. Suppose for some vertex z an exact two-path cover of G-z has a three-vertex rail A and an opposite Hamilton rail B. Then |B| is not 4 or 5. Equivalently, aside from the separate |B|=3 order-seven case, every surviving trimer fiber has |B|>=6.

## Hypotheses
G is a minimum-order counterexample to R888; G-z=A|B is an exact two-path cover with |A|=3 and B Hamiltonian. Use the accepted trimer critical-cell setup R962/R969 and the normalized left middle gate from R541.

## Scope
Pure edge-ordered R888 trimer-fiber finite-base theorem. No ordered-1-factorization hypothesis.

## Applicability
Use to raise the long opposite-rail floor in the trimer branch before any barrier or one-hole seam analysis.

## Persistence
Retain X=A union {z}, the normalized transitive matching-height cell with left outgoing M_S edge {b,z}, B=(L,q1,...,R), the two explicit left P5s (q1,L,z,b,c) and (q1,L,b,z,a), and the R963 shared-triangle completion in the |B|=5 case.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not treat |B|=3; does not close trimer fibers with |B|>=6; does not prove R888.

## Proof
Retain the accepted trimer setup from R969. Thus X=A union {z} is a non-Hamiltonian transitive matching-height four-cell and B=(L,q_1,...,R) is an increasing Hamilton path. Normalize X exactly as in the R582/P660 coordinates used by D5: the left outgoing middle edge is {b,z}. Then the accepted left-gate packet gives q_1 L b and q_1 L z tight, L b z and L z b tight, and the matching-height rule on X gives z b c and b z a tight. Hence both displayed sequences\n\n  P_a=(q_1,L,z,b,c),\n  P_c=(q_1,L,b,z,a)\n\nare increasing P5s; P_a omits a from X and P_c omits c.\n\nSuppose first |B|=4, so B=(L,q_1,q_2,R). The complement of P_a in G is the three-set {q_2,R,a}. Every edge-ordered triangle has an increasing Hamilton path: among its three edges, the smallest and largest share a vertex, and traversing them in that order gives a two-edge increasing path. Therefore P_a together with a Hamilton path on {q_2,R,a} is a spanning two-cover, contradiction. Thus |B|!=4.\n\nNow suppose |B|=5, so B=(L,q_1,q_2,q_3,R). The complement of P_a is T union {a}, where T={q_2,q_3,R}; the complement of P_c is T union {c}. If either of these four-sets were Hamiltonian, together with the corresponding P5 it would give a spanning two-cover of G. Hence both T+a and T+c are non-Hamiltonian edge-ordered K4s. They share exactly the triangle T. Accepted R963 therefore supplies an increasing Hamilton path on T union {a,c}.\n\nThe remaining four vertices are {q_1,L,b,z}. They have the explicit increasing order (q_1,L,b,z): q_1 L b is the universal endpoint reverse-star turn from the R969 setup, and L b z is the normalized left-gate turn. Thus (q_1,L,b,z) is an increasing P4. This P4 and the R963 Hamilton P5 on T+a+c are disjoint and span G, contradiction. Therefore |B|!=5.\n\nThe proof does not use the right ALIGNED/CROSSED gate and does not address |B|=3 or |B|>=6.

# R977 — Two first-inward good anchors force a mixed-sibling double capture, a labelled P4, or a no-P4 cell

## Statement
Let G be a minimum-order counterexample to R888 in the accepted R962/R967 trimer-fiber setup G=X disjoint-union B. Fix an increasing Hamilton order B=(q_0,...,q_m) with m>=4 and write L=q_0,u=q_1,v=q_2,w=q_3. Fix any exact two-cover T_L of G-{u,v}. For every x in X, accepted R967 implies the universal first-inward turn (v,u,x). Apply R508 to the four carriers K_x=(v,u,x) in this same T_L. Choose two distinct GOOD anchors x,y in X whose selected carrier/exterior crossings avoid the old-Q witness w; such a pair exists because deg_{T_L}(w)<=2. Thus R527 captures both x and y separately in the base fiber G-{u,v}.

For this ordered pair x,y the following trigger-complete conclusions hold.

(MIXED-SIBLING.) If (u,x,y) is tight, then K=(v,u,x,y) is a tight P4. The endpoint L is Hamilton-deletable. Accepted R967 makes B-L+r non-Hamiltonian for every r in X, and accepted R963 therefore forces (X-x)+L to be Hamiltonian. Choose any Hamilton P4 P_x^L on (X-x)+L. Then
  G-{u,x}=P_x^L | Q[2,m]
is a literal exact two-cover. Since y lies on P_x^L, choose any selected P_x^L-neighbor z of y. Every such z lies outside K. The mixed dimer S=(u,x) is head-signed by exact witness v via (v,u,x), and {y,z} is a selected carrier/exterior crossing for K in the mixed fiber which avoids v. R527 therefore captures y again in G-{u,x}. Hence y has two distinct source-fiber capture certificates sharing physical pivot u: the base fiber G-{u,v} and mixed sibling G-{u,x}.

(Q-DIMER P4.) Independently, if (y,v,u) is tight, then (y,v,u,x) is a tight P4. This may coexist with MIXED-SIBLING.

(NO-P4 CELL.) If neither (u,x,y) nor (y,v,u) is tight, then for the trimer C=(v,u,x) and fourth vertex y neither opposite-polarity terminal trigger of accepted R518 fires. Therefore {v,u,x,y} lies in one of the exact R516 no-P4 alignment signatures.

The same conclusions hold after interchanging x,y. The exact right-end dual holds with L,u,v,w replaced by R=q_m,s=q_{m-1},d=q_{m-2},rho=q_{m-3}, using mixed sibling fibers G-{x,s} built from Hamilton supports (X-x)+R and Q[0,m-2].

## Hypotheses
G minimum-order counterexample to R888 in accepted R962/R967 trimer setup; B=(q_0,...,q_m) Hamilton with m>=4; T_L exact two-cover of G-{q_1,q_2}; x,y distinct witness-avoiding good anchors supplied by the four-carrier R508 degree argument.

## Scope
Independent-safe multi-fiber transfer of the trigger-complete core of historical R779. Replaces its R723 shallow sibling cover by the critical five-cell Hamilton support forced directly by accepted R963/R967. No R24, gate phase, payment, R312, or computation.

## Applicability
Use after obtaining two good anchors in one first-inward pair-deletion cover. Test the two displayed turns independently. Prefer MIXED-SIBLING because it creates a second capture of one anchor in a distinct exact fiber through the same physical pivot. Joint failure yields a rigid no-P4 cell.

## Persistence
Retain B,L,u,v,w,T_L,x,y and their base selected crossings; in MIXED-SIBLING retain P4 K, Hamilton sibling rail P_x^L, exact cover of G-{u,x}, chosen selected neighbor z, and both capture-fiber certificates at y; in Q-DIMER retain its P4; in failure retain the exact no-P4 signature.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not claim the two P4 triggers are exclusive, that mixed-sibling must occur, that two capture descendants coexist after actualization, or that the no-P4 cell closes G.

## Proof
Fix B=(q_0,...,q_m), L=q_0,u=q_1,v=q_2,w=q_3. For x in X, endpoint L is Hamilton-deletable and accepted R967 makes (B-L)+x non-Hamiltonian. If xq_1<q_1q_2, then (x,q_1,...,q_m) is a Hamilton path on that support, contradiction. Hence q_1q_2<q_1x, i.e. (v,u,x) is tight for every x.

Choose any exact two-cover T_L of G-{u,v}; it exists because this is a proper induced subgraph of a minimum R888 counterexample, and a Hamilton cover may be split if necessary. The Q turn (u,v,w) makes S_L=(u,v) tail-signed by w. For each x, K_x=(v,u,x) is a tight trimer spanning {u,v,x}. Apply R508 with deletion {u,v}, absorbable singleton {x}, carrier K_x, and the same T_L. It gives a selected edge C_x={x,y_x}, y_x outside K_x. If y_x=w call x blocked. The four C_x have distinct X endpoints. Since T_L is a union of two paths, w has selected degree at most two, so at most two x are blocked. Choose distinct good x,y whose crossings avoid w. R527 then captures x and y separately in this same base deletion frame, orienting each marker at its X endpoint.

Now test A=(u,x,y). If A is tight, the accepted turn (v,u,x) followed by A gives the tight P4 K=(v,u,x,y). We construct the mixed sibling cover of G-{u,x}. First, X+L is non-Hamiltonian: otherwise its Hamilton path together with the inherited Hamilton path B-L=(u,v,...,R) would two-cover G. Suppose (X-x)+L were non-Hamiltonian. Then X and (X-x)+L are two non-Hamiltonian four-sets sharing exactly the triangle X-x. Accepted R963 would Hamiltonize their five-vertex union X+L, contradiction. Hence choose a Hamilton P4 P_x^L on (X-x)+L.

Deleting u and x from G leaves the disjoint union of the support (X-x)+L and B-{L,u}=Q[2,m]. Thus P_x^L | Q[2,m] is an exact two-cover of G-{u,x}. The vertex y belongs to P_x^L and has at least one selected neighbor z there. Every vertex of P_x^L other than y lies in {L} union (X-{x,y}), while K uses {v,u,x,y}; hence z lies outside K. Put S=(u,x). The tight turn (v,u,x) makes S head-signed by exact witness v. Relative to carrier K, the carrier remainder is {v,y}; therefore the selected state {y,z} crosses carrier remainder to exterior and avoids witness v. Apply R527 in this mixed deletion frame and orient the marker to capture y. Since y was already good in T_L, it has one base-fiber capture certificate in G-{u,v} and one mixed-sibling capture certificate in G-{u,x}, sharing physical pivot u. This proves MIXED-SIBLING.

Independently, if Bturn=(y,v,u) is tight, then Bturn followed by (v,u,x) gives the tight P4 (y,v,u,x). The A and Bturn triggers may coexist.

Finally suppose neither A nor Bturn is tight. For carrier trimer C=(v,u,x), the initial dimer (v,u) has its natural tail sign witnessed by x and, because (v,u,y) is also one of the universal stars, the same-polarity tail witness y. The opposite head trigger at this end is exactly (y,v,u), absent by assumption. The terminal dimer (u,x) has natural head witness v from C; its opposite tail trigger is exactly (u,x,y), also absent. Thus neither opposite-polarity terminal trigger in accepted R518 fires, and R518 places {v,u,x,y} in an exact R516 no-P4 alignment signature.

Interchanging x,y is identical. At the right endpoint, R967 gives the universal stars (x,s,d); use the fixed exact cover of G-{d,s}, old-Q witness rho=q_{m-3}, and the Hamilton mixed sibling support (X-x)+R together with Q[0,m-2]. The same proof yields the stated dual. This proves R977.
