# R978 — The order-seven trimer/trimer residue cannot occur in a minimum R888 counterexample

## Statement
Let G be a minimum-order counterexample to R888 in the trimer-fiber setup G=X disjoint-union B, where |X|=4, X is non-Hamiltonian, B is Hamiltonian, and B+x is non-Hamiltonian for every x in X. Then |B| is not 3. Indeed if |B|=3, for any distinct x,y in X the two non-Hamiltonian four-sets B union {x} and B union {y} share the triangle B, so accepted R963 gives an increasing Hamilton path on B union {x,y}; the remaining two vertices X-{x,y} form a dimer, yielding a spanning two-path cover of G.

## Hypotheses
Minimum-order R888 counterexample in the accepted trimer-fiber setup; |B|=3 for contradiction.

## Scope
Pure edge-ordered trimer-fiber closure of the order-seven residual left outside R969.

## Applicability
Use with R969 to eliminate its explicit |B|=3 exception; every surviving trimer fiber has |B|>=4 and therefore enters the R969 gate/one-hole reduction.

## Persistence
Retain X, B, two chosen x,y, the two P4-free four-sets B+x and B+y, the R963 Hamilton P5 on their union, and the complementary X-dimer.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not close the |B|>=4 one-hole R969 branch.

## Proof
Assume |B|=3 and choose distinct x,y in X. By the trimer-fiber hypotheses, both induced four-sets B union {x} and B union {y} are non-Hamiltonian. They share exactly the triangle B. Accepted R963 therefore gives an increasing Hamilton path K on B union {x,y}. The remaining vertex set is X minus {x,y}, which has exactly two vertices and hence forms a vacuously increasing dimer path D. The paths K and D are vertex-disjoint and span G, contradicting that G is a counterexample to R888. Thus |B| cannot equal 3.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R978.md -->

# R979 — Every singleton deletion in a minimum R888 counterexample admits a four-by-four exact cover

## Statement
Let G be a minimum-order counterexample to R888. Then for every vertex z there exists an exact two-path cover G-z=P|Q in which |P|>=4 and |Q|>=4. Proof: minimality gives some exact two-cover of G-z; accepted R959 makes both rails have order at least 3. If both are at least 4, stop. Otherwise one rail A has order 3 and the opposite rail B is Hamilton. Put X=A union {z}. Accepted R972 applies to this trimer fiber, gives |B|>=5, and for every Hamilton-deletable b in B gives Hamiltonicity of X-z+b=A+b. Choose b as an endpoint of any Hamilton order of B; then B-b is Hamiltonian as well. Hence (A+b)|(B-b) is an exact cover of G-z with rail orders 4 and |B|-1>=4.

## Hypotheses
G is a minimum-order counterexample to R888. Uses accepted R959 and R972.

## Scope
Pure edge-ordered minimum-counterexample rail-floor strengthening. It is existential per deletion fiber: some exact cover has both rails at least four.

## Applicability
Use when choosing singleton-deletion cover families for R926/R965: representatives may always be chosen with rail floor four, so no selected trimer port is necessary.

## Persistence
For each z retain an initial exact cover, and if it has trimer A retain X=A+z, a Hamilton order of B, one endpoint b, the R972 Hamilton support A+b, and the repaired cover (A+b)|(B-b).

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not say every exact cover of G-z has both rails at least four; accepted R959 only gives the universal floor three. Does not eliminate trimer covers as alternative representatives.

## Proof
Fix z. Minimum-order counterexample minimality gives an exact two-path cover G-z=A|B. By accepted R959 both rails have order at least three. If both have order at least four there is nothing to prove. Otherwise, relabel so |A|=3. Put X=A union {z}. Then this is exactly the accepted R972 trimer-fiber setup. R972 gives |B|>=5 and its critical five-cell duality: for every Hamilton-deletable b in B and every x in X, the support X-x+b is Hamiltonian. Choose any increasing Hamilton order of B and let b be one of its endpoints. Then b is Hamilton-deletable because B-b is the inherited Hamilton suffix or prefix. Apply the critical five-cell conclusion with x=z. The support X-z+b=A+b is Hamiltonian. The two supports A+b and B-b are disjoint and partition V(G)-{z}. Hence they form an exact two-path cover of G-z. Their orders are 4 and |B|-1, respectively, and |B|-1>=4. Thus every deletion fiber has some exact cover with both rails of order at least four.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R979.md -->

# R980 — Symmetric-difference path-cover exchanges form a weighted collision poset

## Statement
Let G be a finite edge-ordered graph on vertex set V, with distinct real edge labels lambda, and let F_0,F_1 be two spanning increasing path covers having the same number k of components. Orient every rail increasingly and let M_0,M_1 be the corresponding matchings in the bipartite graph V_out sqcup V_in: u_out v_in is selected exactly when u->v is a consecutive rail edge. Thus |M_0|=|M_1|=|V|-k.

Let C be the set of connected components of the bipartite symmetric difference M_0 triangle M_1. For C in C put delta(C)=|M_1 cap C|-|M_0 cap C|. Every delta(C) lies in {-1,0,1} and sum_C delta(C)=0.

For i=0,1 and v in V, let L_i(v) be the label of the incoming F_i edge, with L_i(v)=-infinity at an F_i source, and let U_i(v) be the label of the outgoing F_i edge, with U_i(v)=+infinity at an F_i terminal. Then L_i(v)<U_i(v).

Whenever v_in and v_out are incident with changed edges belonging to two distinct symmetric-difference components C_in(v),C_out(v), impose the following directed collision constraints on component flip bits 0<1:
(1) if L_1(v)>=U_0(v), impose C_in(v) <= C_out(v);
(2) if L_0(v)>=U_1(v), impose C_out(v) <= C_in(v).
The two inequalities (1),(2) can never both occur at one vertex. Let preceq be the preorder generated by all these constraints.

For any subset W of symmetric-difference components, form M_W by using the M_1 edges on components in W and the M_0 edges on components outside W, while retaining all common edges. Then M_W is the directed matching of a spanning increasing path cover if and only if W is an upper set of the preorder preceq. In that case
  |M_W|=|M_0|+sum_{C in W} delta(C),
so the resulting cover has
  k-sum_{C in W} delta(C)
components.

Consequently, if some upper set W has positive total delta-weight, F_0 and F_1 have a globally cooperative componentwise recombination with strictly fewer than k paths. In particular, for k=3 any positive upper set yields a spanning cover by at most two increasing paths.

Dually, if no upper set has positive total delta-weight, collapse the preorder to its strongly connected component DAG. There exists an integral nonnegative flow on its directed arcs whose net outflow minus inflow at each DAG node equals the total delta-weight of that node. Equivalently every positive gain unit is transported upward through physical collision constraints to negative loss units. Thus failure of every globally cooperative componentwise recombination has an exact collision-transport certificate.

## Hypotheses
Finite edge-ordered graph; F_0,F_1 are spanning increasing path covers with the same number of components. No completeness, smallest-counterexample, boundary-tournament, local-surgery, or fixed-threshold hypothesis is needed.

## Scope
Pure edge-ordered matching/path-cover theorem. It permits simultaneous rewriting on arbitrarily many symmetric-difference components and gives an exact max-closure/min-cut dual obstruction.

## Applicability
Compare two singleton-deletion three-covers of a hypothetical R888 counterexample, after adjoining the deleted vertex as a singleton. Any positive upper set closes R888. Otherwise retain the integral collision flow as a global obstruction certificate. For compatible singleton fibers with a synchronized common rail, the theorem localizes to the exchanged port universe.

## Persistence
Retain F_0,F_1, M_0,M_1, every alternating component and delta-weight, each physical vertex producing a directed collision constraint, the resulting preorder/SCC DAG, and either an explicit positive upper set or the integral collision flow.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert that every pair of three-covers has a positive upper set. Does not by itself prove R888. Does not say arbitrary broad-interval alternating paths compile. Does not synchronize Hamilton orders on equal supports unless they are explicitly chosen equal. The flow certificate is a structural obstruction, not a contradiction.

## Proof
Orient every rail of F_i in its increasing direction. For each consecutive rail pair u->v select the bipartite edge u_out v_in. Because every physical vertex has at most one predecessor and one successor, M_i is a matching. A k-path cover on n vertices has exactly n-k selected adjacencies, hence |M_0|=|M_1|=n-k.

1. SYMMETRIC-DIFFERENCE COMPONENTS AND WEIGHTS.
The graph M_0 triangle M_1 has maximum degree two and alternates between M_0 and M_1 edges. Hence each connected component is an alternating cycle or alternating path. On a cycle the two matchings contribute equally many edges. On a path their contributions differ by at most one. Therefore delta(C)=|M_1 cap C|-|M_0 cap C| belongs to {-1,0,1}. Summing over components gives sum delta=|M_1|-|M_0|=0.

For any set W of components, choosing M_1 on W and M_0 off W produces a bipartite matching M_W: distinct symmetric-difference components are vertex-disjoint in the bipartite graph, and common edges are disjoint from every changed edge at their copies. Its cardinality is
  |M_W|=|M_0|+sum_{C in W} delta(C).
The only issue is whether this directed matching is an increasing path cover in the physical graph.

2. THE ONLY POSSIBLE PHYSICAL COLLISIONS.
At a physical vertex v write L_i(v) for its F_i incoming label, with -infinity if absent, and U_i(v) for its F_i outgoing label, with +infinity if absent. Since F_i is increasing, L_i(v)<U_i(v).

If the choice of incoming edge at v is fixed between M_0 and M_1, then L_0(v)=L_1(v) as a selected label/convention and both possible outgoing choices are compatible with it because F_0 and F_1 are individually increasing. The same holds if the outgoing choice is fixed. If both copies change but v_in and v_out lie in the same symmetric-difference component, they receive the same flip bit, so the local pair is exactly the F_0 pair or exactly the F_1 pair and is safe.

Thus a new local condition arises only when v_in and v_out belong to two distinct changed components C_in and C_out. There are four bit choices. The equal choices 00 and 11 are safe because they reproduce F_0 and F_1. The mixed choice 10 (incoming from F_1, outgoing from F_0) is safe exactly when
  L_1(v)<U_0(v).
The mixed choice 01 is safe exactly when
  L_0(v)<U_1(v).
These two mixed inequalities cannot both fail. Indeed failure of both would give
  L_1(v)>=U_0(v)>L_0(v)>=U_1(v)>L_1(v),
a contradiction. Therefore each physical vertex forbids at most one mixed orientation.

If L_1(v)>=U_0(v), the forbidden state is C_in=1,C_out=0, so impose the implication C_in<=C_out. If L_0(v)>=U_1(v), impose C_out<=C_in. The two generating implications cannot both be produced at v. Let preceq be their transitive closure.

3. FEASIBLE FLIPS ARE EXACTLY UPPER SETS.
Suppose W is an upper set for preceq. At every collision vertex, W cannot realize a forbidden mixed state, because every generating implication c<=d has the property c in W => d in W. All other local states were shown safe. Hence every physical vertex with both a selected incoming and outgoing edge in M_W has incoming label strictly below outgoing label.

Conversely, if W is not an upper set, then some generating implication c<=d has c in W and d not in W. At its witnessing physical vertex the corresponding forbidden mixed state occurs, so the selected incoming label is at least the selected outgoing label. Therefore M_W is not an increasing path cover.

It remains only to verify that a locally increasing directed matching gives a path cover rather than directed cycles. Each physical vertex has indegree and outdegree at most one. If a directed cycle existed, writing its selected edge labels in cyclic order would give a strict increase at every vertex and hence
  a_0<a_1<...<a_r<a_0,
impossible. Thus every component is a directed path or singleton. Therefore M_W is exactly the matching of a spanning increasing path cover if and only if W is upper.

Combining this with the cardinality formula, the cover represented by an upper set W has
  n-|M_W|=k-sum_{C in W} delta(C)
components. Any upper set of positive weight therefore strictly improves F_0; for k=3 it gives at most two paths.

4. COLLISION-TRANSPORT DUAL.
Assume no upper set has positive total delta-weight. Collapse strongly connected components of preceq. A flip must be constant on each such class, so this loses no feasible assignments. Give each DAG node D weight
  w(D)=sum_{C in D} delta(C).
The total weight is zero, and every upper set of DAG nodes has weight at most zero.

Build a flow network by adjoining source s and sink t. For each node D with w(D)>0 add s->D of capacity w(D). For w(D)<0 add D->t of capacity -w(D). Give every DAG arc infinite capacity. Let P be the total positive weight, equal to total negative absolute weight.

A finite s-t cut is determined by an upper set U of DAG nodes on the source side: if a DAG arc left U the cut would have infinite capacity. Its finite capacity is
  P - sum_{D in U,w(D)>0} w(D) + sum_{D in U,w(D)<0} (-w(D))
  = P-w(U).
By hypothesis w(U)<=0, so every cut has capacity at least P. The trivial cut has capacity P. Max-flow/min-cut therefore gives a flow of value P saturating every source-supply and sink-demand edge. All capacities are integral, so an integral maximum flow exists.

Discard s,t. At each DAG node D, flow conservation becomes
  outflow(D)-inflow(D)=w(D).
Thus every positive gain unit is transported along directed collision implications to negative loss units. Conversely, existence of such a flow immediately gives w(U)<=0 for every upper set U, since no DAG arc leaves an upper set and summing the divergence over U gives w(U)=-inflow_from_outside(U)<=0.

This proves the exact upper-set/improvement alternative and its collision-transport dual.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R980.md -->

# R982 — Maximum increasing-path covers are connected by indecomposable collision exchanges

## Statement
Let G be a finite edge-ordered graph and suppose its minimum increasing path-cover number is k. Let F and F' be two spanning increasing k-path covers, encoded by their directed bipartite matchings M,M' of size |V(G)|-k. Apply the collision-poset construction of R980 to any such pair. Because k is minimum, every feasible upper-set recombination has collision weight at most zero.

(1) ZERO-WEIGHT LATTICE. The zero-weight upper sets form a distributive lattice under union and intersection. Every such upper set gives another spanning increasing k-path cover.

(2) INDECOMPOSABLE EXCHANGE CHAIN. Call a pair R980-indecomposable when its only zero-weight upper sets are the empty set and the whole symmetric-difference component set. Then any two spanning increasing k-path covers can be joined by a finite chain F=F_0,F_1,...,F_m=F' of spanning increasing k-path covers such that each adjacent pair is R980-indecomposable. Moreover the chain may be obtained recursively so that each decomposition step strictly decreases the number of selected edges in the relevant symmetric difference.

(3) STRICT GAIN-LOSS EXPANSION. For an R980-indecomposable adjacent pair, let P be its +1 alternating components and N its -1 alternating components. Then |P|=|N|. If P is nonempty, define a bipartite reachability graph from P to N by p~n iff p is below n in the collision preorder. This graph satisfies strict Hall expansion: for every nonempty proper S subset P, |N(S)|>=|S|+1, and N(P)=N. Hence it has a perfect matching from gains to reachable losses. In particular, for k=3 one has |P|<=3; if |P|=2 then each gain reaches both losses, and if |P|=3 then each gain reaches at least two losses and every pair of gains collectively reaches all three losses.

(4) SAME-SINGLETON SPECIALIZATION. If k=3 and both covers contain the same physical singleton z, then z_out and z_in are common unmatched copies, so |P|=|N|<=2. Every zero-weight recombination also retains z as a singleton. Thus any two exact two-covers of G-z, after adjoining z, can be connected through R980-indecomposable exact two-covers of the same deletion fiber; every nonzero elementary same-fiber transition has either one gain reaching its loss or two gains each reaching both losses.

All statements are conditional on the validity of R980 and do not assert that an improving positive upper set exists.

## Hypotheses
Finite edge-ordered graph. R980 collision-poset theorem. For the same-singleton clause, both spanning k=3 covers have the same singleton z.

## Scope
Pure family-level consequence of R980. Converts pairwise nonimprovement into a connected elementary exchange theory and strict gain-loss reachability.

## Applicability
Use in a hypothetical R888 counterexample after adjoining omitted vertices to singleton-deletion two-covers. Replace arbitrary pairwise collision flows by chains of indecomposable maximum-cover moves. In one deletion fiber, elementary moves have at most two gains, with the two-gain case fully cross-linked to both losses.

## Persistence
Retain the two endpoint covers, the zero-weight upper-set lattice, each recursively produced intermediate maximum cover, and for each indecomposable adjacent pair its collision preorder, gain/loss component sets, and reachability graph. For same-fiber use retain the common singleton.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not prove R888, does not force any positive-weight upper set, and does not assert compatibility of gain-loss routings across different indecomposable moves. Does not promote R980; this theorem remains pending while R980 is pending.

## Proof
Let F_0,F_1 be spanning increasing k-path covers in a graph whose minimum increasing path-cover number is k. Let C be the R980 symmetric-difference component set, let delta:C->{-1,0,1} be the component weights, and let <= be the R980 collision preorder. For an upper set W put w(W)=sum_{C in W}delta(C). By R980, W compiles to a spanning increasing cover with k-w(W) components. Since k is minimum, w(W)<=0 for every upper set W. Also w(empty)=w(C)=0.

1. ZERO-WEIGHT LATTICE.
Let U,V be zero-weight upper sets. Upper sets are closed under union and intersection. Weight is modular:
  w(U union V)+w(U intersect V)=w(U)+w(V)=0.
Both terms on the left are <=0 by minimum-cover nonimprovement. Hence both are zero. Thus the zero-weight upper sets are closed under union/intersection and form a distributive lattice. R980 gives a spanning increasing k-cover for every member.

2. RECURSIVE INDECOMPOSABLE CHAIN.
If the pair F_0,F_1 has no proper nonempty zero-weight upper set, it is indecomposable and there is nothing to do. Otherwise choose such a W and let H be its R980 recombination. Then H is another k-cover. Moreover M(F_0) triangle M(H) consists exactly of the changed edges in symmetric-difference components belonging to W, while M(H) triangle M(F_1) consists exactly of those in the complementary components. Since W is nonempty and proper, both symmetric differences have strictly fewer selected edges than M(F_0) triangle M(F_1). Apply induction on symmetric-difference size to F_0,H and H,F_1 and concatenate the resulting chains. This terminates and proves the indecomposable exchange-chain statement.

3. STRICT HALL EXPANSION IN AN INDECOMPOSABLE PAIR.
Now assume F_0,F_1 is indecomposable. If a proper nonempty upper set U existed with w(U)=0 it would contradict indecomposability, while positive weight is impossible. Therefore every proper nonempty upper set has w(U)<0.

Let P be the +1 components and N the -1 components. Since total weight is zero, |P|=|N|=:g. For S subseteq P let Up(S) be its upward closure and let N(S)=N intersect Up(S). Every positive component lying in Up(S) contributes +1, every negative component there belongs to N(S), and zero components contribute nothing.

First take nonempty proper S subset P. If Up(S) is the whole component set, then N(S)=N and |N(S)|=g>|S|. If Up(S) is proper, indecomposability gives
  0>w(Up(S))=|P intersect Up(S)|-|N(S)|.
Since S subseteq P intersect Up(S),
  |N(S)|>|P intersect Up(S)|>=|S|,
so |N(S)|>=|S|+1.

For S=P, if Up(P) were proper then the same inequality would give |N(P)|>|P|=g, impossible because N has only g members. Hence Up(P) is the whole component set and N(P)=N. This proves strict Hall expansion and in particular ordinary Hall, so a perfect matching from P to reachable N exists.

For k=3, each directed matching has exactly six unmatched bipartite copies. A +1 alternating path consumes two copies unmatched in F_0 but matched in F_1, so g<=3. If g=2, strict expansion for a one-element S forces both losses into its neighborhood; hence each gain reaches both losses. If g=3, each singleton gain reaches at least two losses, and each two-gain set reaches all three.

4. SAME SINGLETON.
Suppose k=3 and both covers contain the same singleton z. Then z_out and z_in are unmatched in both matchings and are not incident with the symmetric difference. Thus among the six unmatched copies of each matching, at least two are common. Therefore at most four unmatched copies can be exclusive to either matching. Each +1 component uses two F_0-exclusive unmatched copies, so g<=2 (and similarly for losses).

Any R980 recombination changes only symmetric-difference edges. Since neither copy of z is incident with such an edge, both remain unmatched and z remains a singleton. A zero-weight recombination is therefore a spanning three-cover retaining z singleton; deleting z leaves an exact two-cover of G-z. Applying the recursive construction entirely within this pair preserves z at every intermediate step. The strict Hall conclusions then specialize to the one-gain or fully cross-linked two-gain alternatives.

This proves all clauses of R982, conditional on R980.

# R983 — Two non-Hamiltonian endpoint extensions of one increasing rail need not Hamiltonize the two-rail union

## Statement
There exists an edge ordering of K_8 with two disjoint increasing paths A=(0,1,2,3) and B=(4,5,6,7) such that both induced five-vertex graphs on A union {4} and A union {7} are non-Hamiltonian in the increasing-path sense, while the full eight-vertex graph is also non-Hamiltonian. One exact edge order is 57<46<47<45<56<37<26<67<34<36<25<35<27<24<01<16<13<02<12<07<17<05<03<23<15<14<06<04. Thus the proposed rail-coupled endpoint lemma 'if both A+b_0 and A+b_m are non-Hamiltonian for the endpoints of a common increasing opposite rail B, then A union B is Hamiltonian' is false even for |A|=|B|=4.

## Hypotheses
Pure finite edge-ordered complete graph; no minimum-counterexample assumption.

## Scope
Exact finite negative result for a tempting R979 maximal-rail endpoint-extension route.

## Applicability
Use as a fence against trying to close R888 solely from a maximal singleton-deletion rail A and non-Hamiltonicity of A plus the two endpoints of the opposite rail. Additional multi-fiber or order-valued information is necessary.

## Persistence
Retain the exact K8 edge order, displayed rails A,B, and exact non-Hamiltonicity checks on A+4, A+7, and all eight vertices.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not refute R888 and does not assert the displayed K8 has path-cover number three. It only refutes the stated rail-coupled Hamiltonization shortcut.

## Proof
Assign ranks 0,...,27 to the displayed edges in order: 57,46,47,45,56,37,26,67,34,36,25,35,27,24,01,16,13,02,12,07,17,05,03,23,15,14,06,04. The rail A=(0,1,2,3) uses ranks 14,18,23 and is increasing. The rail B=(4,5,6,7) uses ranks 3,4,7 and is increasing. For a vertex sequence (v_0,...,v_{r-1}), it is an increasing Hamilton path exactly when rank(v_0v_1)<rank(v_1v_2)<...<rank(v_{r-2}v_{r-1}). A deterministic exhaustive check over all 5!=120 sequences on {0,1,2,3,4} finds none satisfying the inequalities; the same check over all 120 sequences on {0,1,2,3,7} finds none; and the check over all 8!=40320 sequences on {0,...,7} finds none. A reproducing checker is: edges='57 46 47 45 56 37 26 67 34 36 25 35 27 24 01 16 13 02 12 07 17 05 03 23 15 14 06 04'.split(); rank={tuple(sorted(map(int,e))):i for i,e in enumerate(edges)}; def inc(p): return all(rank[tuple(sorted((p[i],p[i+1])))]<rank[tuple(sorted((p[i+1],p[i+2])))] for i in range(len(p)-2)); then assert not any(inc(p) for p in permutations((0,1,2,3,4))); assert not any(inc(p) for p in permutations((0,1,2,3,7))); assert not any(inc(p) for p in permutations(range(8))). Therefore both endpoint extensions A+4 and A+7 are non-Hamiltonian and A union B is non-Hamiltonian, proving the exact negative statement.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R983.md -->

<!-- BEGIN FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R986.md -->

# R986 — A singleton-rich family of equal matchings forces a larger matching in their union

## Statement
Let V be a finite set of size n and let L={v_out:v in V}, R={v_in:v in V}. For every z in V let M_z be a bipartite matching on L sqcup R of one common positive size r, with z_out and z_in both unmatched by M_z. Let U be the union graph of all M_z. Then nu(U)>=r+1. More strongly, fix ANY size-r matching M contained in U, not necessarily one of the family matchings. There is an M-augmenting path P in U of one of two forms. (PAIR-GAIN) For some x, P is a connected component of M triangle M_x having one more M_x edge than M edge. (ZERO-TRANSFER-PLUS-EDGE) Otherwise, there are physical labels ell,y and an M-unmatched right copy rho such that P consists of an even zero-weight alternating path Q from an M-unmatched left copy to ell_out, followed by one edge ell_out rho belonging to M_y; Q is either trivial or is the component of M triangle M_ell containing ell_out. Hence every non-M edge of P belongs to at most two singleton-family matchings. In particular, after any zero-weight recombination that remains a size-r matching inside U, the same at-most-three-family augmentation theorem can be applied again from the recombined matching.

## Hypotheses
Finite balanced bipartite copy set; one size-r matching M_z for every physical label z, simultaneously exposing z_out and z_in; r>0; the chosen base M is any size-r matching contained in the union U.

## Scope
Pure family-level bipartite matching theorem with an iterative at-most-three-family augmentation. No edge-order inequalities, R980, R982, or threshold vector is used in the theorem itself.

## Applicability
In a minimum R888 counterexample, the union of one singleton three-cover per vertex contains ordinary cardinality augmentation from every selected-edge-union three-cover, including covers produced by zero-weight R980 recombination. Thus iterative zero-recombine-and-compare work never leaves the domain where an at-most-three-cover ordinary augmentation certificate exists.

## Persistence
Retain the singleton family {M_z}, union U, arbitrary current size-r base M subset U, and either a pair-gain component or a zero-transfer path from M triangle M_ell plus one final edge supplied by M_y.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert that the ordinary augmenting path is locally increasing. Does not assert that every zero recombination is available without R980. Physical collision/order compatibility is the remaining obstruction.

## Proof
Let M be any size-r matching contained in U, and let X_L,X_R be its unmatched left and right copies. If for some x a component of M triangle M_x contains one more M_x edge than M edge, it is an M-augmenting path and we are in PAIR-GAIN. Assume no such component exists for any x. Since |M_x|=|M|=r, the component weights of M triangle M_x sum to zero, so absence of positive components forces every component to have weight zero. Thus every left copy ell_out is reachable from X_L by an M-alternating zero path using only M and M_ell: if ell_out is unmatched in M take the trivial path; otherwise ell_out is unmatched in M_ell and the balanced component containing it is an even alternating path whose other endpoint is an M-unmatched left copy. Some rho in X_R has a neighbor ell_out in U. If every rho in X_R were isolated, then every family matching M_z would leave all |X_R|=n-r of them unmatched. Because r>0 choose z with z_in outside X_R. The matching M_z additionally leaves z_in unmatched, so has size at most r-1, contradiction. Choose ell_out rho in U and a family matching M_y containing it. Append that edge to the zero path Q from X_L to ell_out. Since rho is M-unmatched, it cannot occur internally on Q, and ell_out rho is not an M-edge. Hence Q+(ell_out rho) is an M-augmenting path. Its non-M edges lie in M_ell except for the last edge, which lies in M_y. This proves the arbitrary-base constructive clause and therefore nu(U)>=r+1. Reapplying the same argument after any size-r recombination inside U is immediate because the hypotheses on the fixed singleton family and union U are unchanged.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R986.md -->

# R987 — A four-by-four singleton three-cover can require leaving every selected-edge-preserving threshold box

## Statement
Retain the exact K9 edge order of R981:
07<24<45<03<01<28<68<36<12<27<37<14<16<38<58<78<17<47<57<26<48<15<23<56<04<34<13<05<46<02<35<18<25<06<67<08.
In addition to the R981 threshold-box fence and explicit two-cover, this same edge order admits the following nine increasing 4+4+singleton covers F_z, one isolating each z:
F_0=(4,5,1,3)|(8,2,7,6)|{0};
F_1=(6,5,0,8)|(4,2,7,3)|{1};
F_2=(0,3,7,1)|(8,5,6,4)|{2};
F_3=(2,1,4,0)|(6,8,7,5)|{3};
F_4=(3,8,5,0)|(1,2,6,7)|{4};
F_5=(0,1,4,3)|(8,2,7,6)|{5};
F_6=(4,1,8,0)|(3,7,5,2)|{6};
F_7=(4,0,5,2)|(8,6,1,3)|{7};
F_8=(3,0,1,5)|(2,4,6,7)|{8}.
For every unordered pair F_x,F_y, exhaustive symmetric-difference component flipping shows that no locally increasing recombination has more than six selected edges; equivalently no pair has a positive R980 upper-set recombination.
Nevertheless F_0 and F_2 have a legal neutral recombination obtained by flipping the zero-weight alternating 4-cycle
{7->6,5->1} <-> {7->1,5->6}.
The resulting three-cover is
H={0}|(4,5,6)|(8,2,7,1,3).
Comparing H with F_1, the component flip using the zero components
{8->2,4->5}<->{4->2,6->5},
{5->6}<->{5->0},
and the +1 component empty<->{0->8}, while retaining the -1 component {1->3,7->1}<->{7->3}, gives the size-seven increasing matching corresponding to
(4,2,7,1,3)|(6,5,0,8).
Thus an initially pairwise nonimproving singleton seed family can escape after one neutral recombination, and that escape necessarily leaves the original 4+4+singleton seed class. This is an exact finite proof-of-mechanism for neutral collision recombination; it is not a universal escape theorem.

## Hypotheses
Pure finite edge-ordered K9 example. R980 terminology is used only for interpretation; the finite verification enumerates all symmetric-difference component flips and checks the matching and local increasing inequalities directly.

## Scope
Exact finite strengthening of the R981 fence. It tests the neutral-recombination mechanism on the same K9 edge order and exhibits pairwise nonimproving seeds whose neutral closure immediately unlocks a two-cover.

## Applicability
Use as a regression test for any proposed neutral-recombination escape theorem. A theorem must allow intermediate three-covers with arbitrary component sizes; restricting every iterate to the original 4+4+singleton seed class misses the displayed escape.

## Persistence
Retain the full R981 edge order, all nine listed singleton seeds, the pairwise nonimprovement certificate, the neutral F0/F2 4-cycle flip, H, and the positive H/F1 recombination producing the explicit two-cover.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not prove that every pairwise nonimproving seed family escapes. Does not prove termination of neutral closure. Does not show that a trapped neutral family is impossible. Does not refute R888 or R980.

## Proof
Represent each unordered edge by its zero-based rank in the displayed 36-edge order. For a directed matching M, let in[v] and out[v] be the selected predecessor/successor when present. Call M increasing iff every vertex with both selected sides satisfies rank(in[v],v)<rank(v,out[v]). Such a directed matching cannot contain a directed cycle, because labels would strictly increase around the cycle; hence it is exactly an increasing path cover.

1. Seed verification. For each listed F_z, compute the three consecutive edge ranks on each four-vertex rail. They are strictly increasing, so each F_z is an increasing 4+4+singleton cover and its matching has six edges.

2. Exhaustive pairwise recombination check. For a pair M0,M1, form the connected components of the bipartite symmetric difference on copies v_out,v_in. Each component C stores its M0-edge set E0(C) and M1-edge set E1(C). Enumerate all 2^c subsets W of the c components. Form M_W from common edges, M1 component edges on W, and M0 component edges off W. Reject M_W unless it is a bipartite matching and satisfies the physical local increasing test above. For all 36 unordered pairs among F_0,...,F_8, every accepted M_W has at most six edges.

3. Neutral escape. The F0 matching is {4->5,5->1,1->3,8->2,2->7,7->6}. The F2 matching is {0->3,3->7,7->1,8->5,5->6,6->4}. Their symmetric difference contains the zero-weight alternating 4-cycle {7->6,5->1} versus {7->1,5->6}. Flipping only this component in F0 gives H={4->5,5->6,8->2,2->7,7->1,1->3}, namely {0}|(4,5,6)|(8,2,7,1,3). Its edge ranks are 2<23 and 5<9<16<26, so H is increasing and still has six selected edges.

4. Positive comparison with F1. The F1 matching is {6->5,5->0,0->8,4->2,2->7,7->3}. Relative to H, the symmetric-difference components are: C0: {1->3,7->1} versus {7->3}, weight -1; C1: {8->2,4->5} versus {4->2,6->5}, weight 0; C2: {5->6} versus {5->0}, weight 0; C3: empty versus {0->8}, weight +1; plus common edge 2->7. Choose C1,C2,C3 from F1 and C0 from H. The resulting matching is {4->2,2->7,7->1,1->3,6->5,5->0,0->8}. Its two directed paths are (4,2,7,1,3) and (6,5,0,8), with edge ranks 1<9<16<26 and 23<27<35. Hence it is an increasing spanning two-cover.

Thus the initial nine singleton seeds are pairwise nonimproving under every componentwise recombination, but one legal neutral recombination outside the 4+4+singleton seed class unlocks a positive comparison with a third seed.

# FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R988.md

<!-- BEGIN FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R988.md -->

# R988 — A zero-transfer augmentation either exposes its donor gain or collision-transports the opposite defect

## Statement
Let G be an edge-ordered graph and let {M_z:z in V} be a singleton-rich family of equal-size increasing-cover matchings as in accepted R986, with union U. Let M subset U be any increasing matching of the same size r. Assume the R986 augmentation from M is in its ZERO-TRANSFER-PLUS-EDGE branch: there are labels ell,y, an M-unmatched right copy rho_in, a zero-weight alternating component Q of M triangle M_ell, and a donor edge e=ell_out rho_in in M_y, where Q has ell_out as the endpoint that is unmatched in M_ell. Assume also that the pair (M,M_ell) has no M_ell-heavy component; equivalently, since |M|=|M_ell|, every component of M triangle M_ell has weight zero.

Apply the accepted R980 collision preorder to (M,M_ell), and let W be the upper closure of Q. Then W has total weight zero, so flipping W gives another increasing size-r cover matching H. The copy ell_out is unmatched in H.

Let D_rho be the symmetric-difference component containing rho_in, if M and M_ell differ at rho_in. Exactly one of the following occurs.

(DONOR-EXPOSED) D_rho is absent or D_rho is not in W. Then rho_in remains unmatched in H. Consequently the component of H triangle M_y containing e is exactly the singleton edge {e}, with weight +1. Thus the ordinary final donor edge of R986 has been converted into a literal R980 gain component.

(FORCED-COUPLING) D_rho belongs to W. Then Q<=D_rho in the collision preorder, so there is an explicit directed chain of physical collision constraints from the terminal-defect transfer Q to the right-side component D_rho. Since rho_in is unmatched in M but changed on D_rho, D_rho is a zero alternating path whose flip matches rho_in and exposes one other right copy sigma_in. Thus the neutral currentization that exposes ell_out necessarily transports the source defect rho_in to sigma_in, and the complete collision chain witnessing that coupling is retained.

The dual statement holds with left/right and incoming/outgoing interchanged. The lemma is conditional on accepted R980 and R986 and is not a termination theorem.

## Hypotheses
Accepted R986 zero-transfer setup from an increasing size-r base matching M inside the singleton-family union; accepted R980 collision preorder for M versus M_ell; no pair-gain component in M triangle M_ell, so all its components have weight zero.

## Scope
Family-level neutral-recombination consumer. Converts the R986 zero-transfer certificate into either a literal singleton +1 donor component or an explicit forced collision chain that transports the opposite-side unmatched defect.

## Applicability
Use inside the neutral closure demanded by the Independent guidance. Iterating the dichotomy yields either a positive upper-set opportunity or a directed dependency network coupling terminal and source defect transfers. Any claimed saturation theorem should consume that network rather than only pairwise min-cut flows.

## Persistence
Retain M,M_ell,M_y,Q,e,rho_in, the R980 upper closure W, H, and either the singleton gain {e} or D_rho together with the full directed collision chain Q<=...<=D_rho and the new exposed right copy sigma_in.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not say the singleton gain itself is an upper set. Does not force a positive R980 upper set. Does not prove that repeated defect transport terminates or that collision chains from different comparisons are coherent.

## Proof
Let Q be the R986 zero-weight component of M triangle M_ell with endpoint ell_out unmatched in M_ell. By the no-pair-gain hypothesis, no component of M triangle M_ell has positive weight. Since the total weight over all components is |M_ell|-|M|=0, no component has negative weight either. Hence every component has weight zero.

Let W be the upper closure of Q in the R980 collision preorder. Because every component has weight zero, W has total weight zero. Accepted R980 therefore says that flipping exactly W gives an increasing matching H of the same size r.

The bipartite copy ell_out belongs only to Q among the symmetric-difference components. On Q, H uses the M_ell state. Since ell_out is unmatched in M_ell, ell_out is unmatched in H. Components added to the upper closure are bipartite-copy disjoint from Q and cannot change this conclusion.

Now inspect rho_in. It is unmatched in M by the R986 certificate. If M and M_ell agree at rho_in, then it is also unmatched in M_ell and no symmetric-difference component contains it; therefore rho_in remains unmatched in H. If they differ there, let D_rho be the unique symmetric-difference component containing rho_in.

If D_rho is not in W, H retains the M state at rho_in, hence rho_in is unmatched in H. Thus both ell_out and rho_in are unmatched in H. The donor matching M_y contains e=ell_out rho_in. Because M_y is a matching, e is the only M_y edge incident with either of those two bipartite copies. Because H has no edge incident with either copy, the connected component of H triangle M_y containing e consists of e alone. Relative to H it therefore has one M_y edge and no H edge, so its weight is +1. This is DONOR-EXPOSED.

Suppose instead D_rho belongs to W. By definition W is the upper closure of Q, so Q preceq D_rho. Hence the transitive closure contains a directed path from Q to D_rho, each arc witnessed by one physical R980 collision inequality; retain those witnessing vertices and inequalities.

Because rho_in is unmatched in M but M and M_ell differ at rho_in, M_ell matches rho_in. The component D_rho has weight zero. A zero-weight alternating component containing an endpoint unmatched in exactly one of the two matchings cannot be a cycle. It is an even alternating path. Since rho_in lies on the right bipartition and is unmatched in M but matched in M_ell, its other endpoint also lies on the right bipartition and is unmatched in M_ell but matched in M. Call that endpoint sigma_in. Flipping D_rho from the M state to the M_ell state therefore matches rho_in and exposes sigma_in. Since D_rho is included in W, H realizes exactly that transfer. This is FORCED-COUPLING.

The two cases are exhaustive. Interchanging out/in, left/right, and reversing the roles of source and terminal copies gives the dual statement.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R988.md -->

<!-- BEGIN FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R989.md -->

# R989 — A singleton-rich neutral-recombination family can be permanently trapped inside its selected-edge union

## Statement
There exists an edge ordering of K9 and nine increasing 4+4+singleton three-covers F_z, one isolating each physical vertex z, such that if U is the union of all directed selected edges appearing in the F_z, then: (i) U has ordinary bipartite matching number at least 7=n-2; (ii) every order-compatible directed matching contained in U has size at most 6=n-3; hence no finite sequence of R980-style neutral recombinations among covers whose selected edges remain in U can ever expose a positive recombination; but (iii) the ambient edge-ordered K9 is Hamiltonian by an explicit increasing Hamilton path using fresh directed edges outside U. Concretely the edge order is 37<15<58<17<67<07<12<24<36<27<48<28<68<56<01<18<47<08<25<34<04<57<14<06<26<35<02<38<03<23<16<05<46<13<78<45. The seed covers are F0=(4,8,6,1)|(7,2,5,3)|{0}; F1=(7,3,5,0)|(4,8,6,2)|{1}; F2=(7,3,5,0)|(4,8,6,1)|{2}; F3=(7,2,5,0)|(4,8,6,1)|{3}; F4=(5,8,0,3)|(7,2,6,1)|{4}; F5=(4,8,0,3)|(7,2,6,1)|{5}; F6=(7,1,8,0)|(4,2,5,3)|{6}; F7=(5,8,0,3)|(4,2,6,1)|{7}; F8=(7,3,5,0)|(4,2,6,1)|{8}. Their selected-edge union is U={0->3,1->8,2->5,2->6,3->5,4->2,4->8,5->0,5->3,5->8,6->1,6->2,7->1,7->2,7->3,8->0,8->6}. An ordinary size-seven matching in U is {6->1,1->8,0->3,4->2,5->0,2->6,3->5}. Exhaustive inspection of all C(17,7)=19448 seven-edge subsets shows that none is simultaneously a bipartite matching and locally increasing at every physical vertex. Nevertheless (7,1,2,4,8,6,5,3,0) is an increasing Hamilton path, with edge ranks 3<6<7<10<12<13<25<28.

## Hypotheses
Pure finite edge-ordered K9 example; no minimum-counterexample hypothesis. Order-compatible means distinct selected tails and heads and, at every physical vertex with both a selected incoming and outgoing edge, incoming edge rank is strictly smaller than outgoing edge rank.

## Scope
Exact finite fence against any universal theorem asserting that neutral R980 recombination inside one fixed singleton-seed selected-edge union must eventually yield a two-cover.

## Applicability
Use as a regression test for neutral-recombination escape theorems. Any universal R888 proof based on a fixed chosen singleton seed family must permit introduction of fresh complete-graph edges, replacement of seed representatives, or another operation that enlarges the selected-edge universe.

## Persistence
Retain the exact 36-edge order, all nine seed covers, the 17-edge directed union U, the explicit ordinary size-seven matching, the exhaustive 19448-subset order-compatibility check, and the explicit ambient Hamilton path.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not refute R888; the ambient graph is explicitly Hamiltonian. Does not refute R980 or R986. Does not say every singleton seed family is trapped. Does not rule out escape after changing seed representatives or introducing fresh complete-graph edges.

## Proof
Give the 36 unordered edges zero-based ranks in the displayed order. The consecutive rank triples on the two rails of F0,...,F8 are respectively: F0: 10<12<30 and 9<18<25; F1: 0<25<31 and 10<12<24; F2: 0<25<31 and 10<12<30; F3: 9<18<31 and 10<12<30; F4: 2<17<28 and 9<24<30; F5: 10<17<28 and 9<24<30; F6: 3<15<17 and 7<18<25; F7: 2<17<28 and 7<24<30; F8: 0<25<31 and 7<24<30. Hence all nine displayed objects are increasing 4+4+singleton three-covers. Their directed selected-edge union is exactly U={0->3,1->8,2->5,2->6,3->5,4->2,4->8,5->0,5->3,5->8,6->1,6->2,7->1,7->2,7->3,8->0,8->6}. The seven edges {6->1,1->8,0->3,4->2,5->0,2->6,3->5} have distinct tails and distinct heads, so the ordinary bipartite matching number of U is at least seven. For order compatibility, enumerate all 7-edge subsets S of the 17-edge set U. Reject S if two edges have the same tail or the same head. For every surviving S and every physical vertex v carrying both u->v and v->w, reject S when rank(uv)>=rank(vw). There are exactly binom(17,7)=19448 subsets; none survives both tests. This finite check is deterministic and may be reproduced by the literal loop over combinations(U,7) followed by the two stated tests. Therefore U has no order-compatible matching of size seven. Since order-compatible matchings are hereditary under deleting selected edges, it has none of any larger size either, so its order-compatible rank is exactly six because each seed supplies six. Every R980 componentwise recombination uses only selected edges from its two input covers. Starting from the nine seeds, all neutral recombinations therefore remain inside U. Inductively every cover in their neutral closure has all selected edges in U. A positive recombination from any two closure members would be an order-compatible matching of size seven contained in U, impossible. Thus the fixed selected-edge neutral closure is permanently trapped. Finally the physical Hamilton order (7,1,2,4,8,6,5,3,0) has consecutive edge ranks 3<6<7<10<12<13<25<28, so it is an increasing Hamilton path in the ambient K9. Hence the trap is purely a restriction of the chosen selected-edge universe and not an R888 obstruction.

# R991 — A global minimum edge forces mutual source exclusion and canonical fresh-edge three-covers

## Statement
Let G be a minimum-order counterexample to R888, with distinct edge labels, and let uv be the globally minimum ordinary edge. Then pc_inc(G-u)=pc_inc(G-v)=2. In every exact two-path cover of G-u, the vertex v is not the source of either rail; symmetrically, in every exact two-path cover of G-v, u is not a rail source. Indeed, any source exposure would let the omitted endpoint be prepended through uv and would give a spanning two-cover of G.

More precisely, let G-u=A|B be any exact increasing two-cover, orient both rails increasingly, and suppose v lies on A=(a_0,...,a_i=v,...,a_r). Then i>=1. Writing p=a_{i-1}, delete the selected edge p->v and add the fresh edge u->v. The resulting selected-edge set is the spanning increasing three-cover
  (a_0,...,p) | (u,v,a_{i+1},...,a_r) | B,
with the obvious dimer interpretation if i=r. The construction is always legal because uv is globally minimum, hence lambda(uv)<lambda(v a_{i+1}) whenever the latter edge exists. It preserves matching cardinality n-3 while introducing the complete-graph edge uv. The symmetric construction holds from every exact two-cover of G-v, producing a three-cover whose corresponding rail begins v,u.

Consequently, any general theorem asserting that every prescribed vertex of every edge-ordered complete graph with increasing path-cover number at most two can be exposed as a rail source would imply R888 immediately.

## Hypotheses
G is a minimum-order counterexample to R888; uv is its globally minimum edge. Uses accepted singleton-deletion exactness/minimality R959.

## Scope
Pure edge-ordered minimum-counterexample reduction and completeness-specific fresh-edge construction.

## Applicability
Use the global minimum edge as a fresh edge outside a restricted neutral selected-edge family. Every deletion-fiber cover yields a canonical three-cover using uv. Source exposure of the opposite endpoint closes R888 immediately.

## Persistence
Retain uv, the chosen exact cover of G-u or G-v, the position of the opposite endpoint on its rail, the deleted predecessor edge, and the canonical fresh-edge three-cover.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not prove prescribed-source exposure. Does not prove R888. Does not assert the fresh-edge three-cover has a positive R980 recombination with any particular seed. Does not reopen the longest-path-complement route.

## Proof
Accepted R959 gives pc_inc(G)=3 and, for every vertex x, pc_inc(G-x)=2 with every exact two-cover having two nonempty rails. Fix the globally minimum edge uv.

Take any exact cover G-u=A|B and orient both rails increasingly. If v were the source of its rail, write that rail as (v,a_1,...,a_r). If r=0, then adjoining u gives the dimer (u,v), which together with the other rail two-covers G. If r>=1, global minimality of uv gives lambda(uv)<lambda(v a_1), so (u,v,a_1,...,a_r) is increasing. Again the untouched other rail gives a spanning two-cover of G. Both contradict that G is a counterexample. Hence v is not a source in any exact cover of G-u. Interchanging u and v proves the symmetric assertion for G-v.

Now retain G-u=A|B and suppose v lies on A=(a_0,...,a_i=v,...,a_r). We have i>=1. Let p=a_{i-1}. Delete the selected adjacency p->v. This splits A into the nonempty prefix (a_0,...,p) and the suffix (v,a_{i+1},...,a_r), with the suffix possibly the singleton {v}. Add the fresh directed edge u->v. If i<r, then uv is globally smaller than v a_{i+1}, so (u,v,a_{i+1},...,a_r) is increasing; if i=r, (u,v) is a dimer and is vacuously increasing. Every other selected adjacency is inherited from A or B. Therefore
  (a_0,...,p) | (u,v,a_{i+1},...,a_r) | B
is a spanning increasing three-cover of G. The selected matching lost one edge and gained one edge relative to the size-(n-3) matching of G-u, so it still has n-3 edges, exactly as a three-cover should. The construction from G-v is identical after swapping u and v.

Finally, if a general prescribed-source theorem held for every edge-ordered complete graph of path-cover number at most two, apply it to G-u with prescribed vertex v. The first paragraph would then produce a spanning two-cover of G. Thus that theorem implies R888.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R991.md -->

# R992 — A singleton endpoint transfer either closes two paths or forces an extreme carrier-triangle edge

## Statement
Let G be a finite edge-ordered complete graph with pc_inc(G)>2. A SOURCE TRANSFER for singleton pair {x,y} at carrier neighbor v means there are literal spanning three-covers A | (y,v,b_2,...,b_m) | {x} and A | (x,v,b_2,...,b_m) | {y}, with the obvious order-two interpretation when no b_2 exists. Then lambda(vx)<lambda(xy) and lambda(vy)<lambda(xy), so xy is the unique maximum edge of triangle {x,y,v}. Dually, a TERMINAL TRANSFER at carrier neighbor w means there are literal spanning three-covers A | (...,w,y) | {x} and A | (...,w,x) | {y}; then lambda(xy)<lambda(wx) and lambda(xy)<lambda(wy), so xy is the unique minimum edge of {x,y,w}. If the same unordered singleton pair {x,y} occurs in both a source transfer with carrier v and a terminal transfer with carrier w, where v,w are distinct from x,y, then lambda(vx),lambda(vy) < lambda(xy) < lambda(wx),lambda(wy). Consequently both (v,x,y,w) and (v,y,x,w) are increasing Hamilton P4 orders.

## Hypotheses
Finite edge-ordered complete graph with pc_inc(G)>2. The source and terminal transfer configurations are the literal cover pairs displayed in the statement. For the mixed clause, the same singleton pair occurs once at each polarity.

## Scope
Pure local edge-order transfer theorem and mixed-polarity P4 compiler; no R980/R986/minimum-counterexample assumption.

## Applicability
Use after neutral/fresh-edge endpoint transport. A repeated singleton pair at opposite polarities converts two failed fresh-edge escapes into explicit increasing P4 geometry.

## Persistence
Retain x,y, source carrier v, terminal carrier w, all four strict spoke comparisons around xy, and both P4 orders.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert that a mixed-polarity repetition must occur. Does not by itself absorb the P4 complement or prove R888. Does not assert global coherence of transfer certificates.

## Proof
For the source transfer, retain literal covers A | (y,v,b_2,...,b_m) | {x} and A | (x,v,b_2,...,b_m) | {y}. Since the second rail in each cover is increasing, lambda(yv)<lambda(vb_2) and lambda(xv)<lambda(vb_2) when b_2 exists; only the first edge matters below. If lambda(xy)<lambda(yv), then (x,y,v,b_2,...,b_m) is increasing, and together with A it two-covers G. If lambda(xy)<lambda(xv), then (y,x,v,b_2,...,b_m) is increasing and again A gives a two-cover. In a graph with pc_inc(G)>2 both conclusions are impossible. Hence lambda(xy)>lambda(yv) and lambda(xy)>lambda(xv), so xy is the unique maximum edge of {x,y,v}. The order-two carrier case is identical with the tail after v absent.

For the terminal transfer, retain A | (...,v,y) | {x} and A | (...,v,x) | {y}. If lambda(vy)<lambda(xy), appending x to the first rail gives (...,v,y,x), while if lambda(vx)<lambda(xy), appending y to the second gives (...,v,x,y). Either would two-cover G with A. Therefore pc_inc(G)>2 forces lambda(xy)<lambda(vy) and lambda(xy)<lambda(vx), making xy the unique minimum edge of the carrier triangle.

Now suppose the same singleton pair {x,y} appears in a source transfer with carrier v and a terminal transfer with carrier w. The source conclusion gives lambda(vx)<lambda(xy) and lambda(vy)<lambda(xy). The terminal conclusion gives lambda(xy)<lambda(wx) and lambda(xy)<lambda(wy). Hence
  lambda(vx)<lambda(xy)<lambda(yw),
so (v,x,y,w) is increasing; and
  lambda(vy)<lambda(xy)<lambda(xw),
so (v,y,x,w) is increasing. These are two explicit Hamilton P4 orders on {v,x,y,w}. No synchronization of the underlying transfer covers is needed beyond the graph-intrinsic edge inequalities.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R992.md -->

# R995 — An isolated dimer gain is blocked only by the two physical endpoint windows

## Statement
Assume accepted R980 and let G be a minimum-order counterexample to R888. Let F be a spanning increasing three-cover, let t be a terminal of one F-component and s the source of a different F-component, and put e=lambda(ts). By accepted R999 choose a spanning three-cover D containing the dimer rail (t,s). In the symmetric difference M_F triangle M_D, E={t_out s_in} is a singleton component of weight +1. Let a=L_F(t), with a=-infinity if t is a singleton, and b=U_F(s), with b=+infinity if s is a singleton. Then every generating R980 collision implication having E as its lower/source component occurs at one of the two physical vertices t,s, and exactly the following are possible: (T-BLOCK) if a>=e, then E<=C_t, where C_t is the symmetric-difference component containing the F-selected incoming edge at t; (S-BLOCK) if e>=b, then E<=C_s, where C_s is the component containing the F-selected outgoing edge at s. No T-BLOCK exists when t has no incoming edge and no S-BLOCK exists when s has no outgoing edge. There are no other outgoing generating implications from E. Moreover every existing first blocker C_t or C_s has weight 0 or -1, never +1. Hence if a<e<b, E has no successors, {E} is a positive upper set, and flipping E is exactly the direct component merge through t->s. In a counterexample at least one of a>=e or e>=b must therefore hold; the upper closure of the fresh gain begins by transporting precisely the failed endpoint window(s).

## Hypotheses
Accepted R980 collision-preorder theorem; minimum R888 counterexample G; spanning increasing three-cover F; t terminal and s source on different F-components; dimer cover D supplied by accepted R999.

## Scope
Completeness-specific physical edge-activation lemma. It localizes the obstruction to a fresh terminal-to-source edge to the actual incoming threshold at its terminal and outgoing threshold at its source.

## Applicability
Use after selecting a desired joining edge t->s. If it is not immediately legal, retain the exact blocker component(s) C_t,C_s and their witnessing inequalities. Neutral exchange may then be used only to transport those endpoint defects; no abstract gain-loss graph without the physical inequalities is sufficient.

## Persistence
Retain F,D,t,s,e,a,b,E and every existing blocker C_t,C_s, including the selected F edge at the blocked physical copy and the inequality a>=e or e>=b.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not prove the blocker upper closure has weight zero, that transporting one blocker activates e, or that repeated transport terminates. Does not assert coherence across different dimer comparisons.

## Proof
Let F be cover 0 and D be cover 1 in the notation of R980. By accepted R999, E={t_out s_in} is a singleton symmetric-difference component with delta(E)=+1. Because E contains only t_out and s_in, a physical collision constraint involving E can occur only at t or s. At t, F has no outgoing selected edge, so U_0(t)=+infinity, while D has outgoing edge ts of label e and no incoming dimer edge, so U_1(t)=e and L_1(t)=-infinity. The incoming choice at t is changed exactly when t has an F-predecessor; let its symmetric-difference component be C_t and write L_0(t)=a. The only mixed state in which E=1 and C_t=0 uses the F incoming edge and D outgoing edge, and is increasing exactly when a<e. If a>=e, R980 imposes C_out(t)<=C_in(t), namely E<=C_t. The opposite possible implication would require L_1(t)>=U_0(t), i.e. -infinity>=+infinity, impossible. If t has no F incoming edge then a=-infinity and no t-blocker exists. At s, F has no incoming selected edge, so L_0(s)=-infinity, while D has incoming edge ts of label e and no outgoing dimer edge, so L_1(s)=e and U_1(s)=+infinity. If s has F-successor, let C_s be the component containing that outgoing edge and put U_0(s)=b. The mixed state E=1,C_s=0 uses the D incoming edge and F outgoing edge and is increasing exactly when e<b. If e>=b, R980 imposes C_in(s)<=C_out(s), namely E<=C_s. The opposite possible implication would require L_0(s)>=U_1(s), impossible. If s has no F outgoing edge then b=+infinity and no s-blocker exists. There is no third physical vertex at which E participates, so these are all generating outgoing implications from E. Finally, C_t, when it exists, contains the F-only selected edge incident with t_in, while t_in is unmatched in D. Therefore its alternating path has an F-only endpoint, so its D-minus-F weight is either 0 or -1, never +1. The same argument at s_out shows delta(C_s) is 0 or -1. If a<e<b neither outgoing implication exists, so E has no successor in the generated preorder. Hence {E} is an upper set of weight +1. R980 then gives a cover with one fewer component; concretely flipping E simply joins the F-path ending at t to the F-path starting at s, and the inequalities a<e<b are exactly the two new seam conditions. In a counterexample this cannot occur, so at least one endpoint inequality fails.

# R998 — Every proper increasing path in a minimum R888 counterexample has an exact two-covered complement

## Statement
Let G be a minimum-order counterexample to R888, and let K be any nonempty proper vertex-simple increasing path of G. Put H=G-V(K). Then pc_inc(H)=2. Consequently H has an exact two-path cover U|V, and K|U|V is a spanning increasing three-path cover of G containing K literally as one rail. In particular every oriented physical edge, every increasing trimer, and every increasing P4 can be restored literally as one component of a spanning three-cover.

## Hypotheses
G is a minimum-order counterexample to R888; K is a nonempty proper increasing path in G.

## Scope
Pure edge-ordered minimum-counterexample restoration theorem. No boundary-tournament minimality, R980, threshold matching, longest-path hypothesis, or singleton-family structure.

## Applicability
Use whenever completeness or a local edge-order inequality produces a new increasing path K whose old complement ordering should be discarded. It supplies a fresh exact two-cover of the complement while retaining K literally. In particular it is the parent for arbitrary dimer donors and double-block reverse-P4 rebuilds.

## Persistence
Retain G, the literal increasing path K, its vertex complement H, and one exact two-cover U|V of H.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert any relation between U|V and a previous cover of the same vertices. Does not prescribe endpoints or support sizes of U,V beyond nonemptiness forced by pc_inc(H)=2. Does not prove that repeated restorations terminate.

## Proof
Let G be a minimum-order counterexample to R888 and let K be a nonempty proper increasing path. Put H=G-V(K). Since K is proper, H is nonempty and has strictly fewer vertices than G. Being an induced subgraph of an edge-ordered complete graph, H is itself an edge-ordered complete graph. By minimum-order choice of G, H is not a counterexample to R888, so pc_inc(H)<=2. If pc_inc(H)=1, H has an increasing Hamilton path P. Then K|P is a spanning cover of G by at most two increasing paths, contradicting that G is a counterexample. Hence pc_inc(H)=2. Choose an exact two-path cover H=U|V. Since K,U,V are disjoint increasing paths whose vertex sets partition V(G), K|U|V is a spanning increasing three-cover containing K literally. The final dimer, trimer, and P4 specializations are immediate because every such object is a nonempty proper increasing path whenever G itself is a counterexample.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R998.md -->

# R999 — Every directed edge of a minimum R888 counterexample is a literal dimer rail of a spanning three-cover

## Statement
Let G be a minimum-order counterexample to R888. For every ordered pair of distinct vertices (x,y), there exists a spanning increasing three-cover D=A|B|(x,y) in which x->y is literally a dimer rail. More generally this is the dimer specialization of R998. If F is any spanning increasing three-cover in which x is a terminal and y is a source of different components, then relative to any such D the directed matching edge x_out y_in is an isolated D-only component of M_F triangle M_D, with weight +1.

## Hypotheses
G is a minimum-order counterexample to R888; x,y are distinct. For the isolated-gain clause F is any spanning increasing three-cover with x terminal and y source on different components.

## Scope
Pure edge-ordered minimum-counterexample completeness lemma, now explicitly based on the R888-specific prescribed-path restoration parent R998. No full boundary-tournament minimality is used.

## Applicability
Use to introduce any chosen fresh complete-graph edge as a literal dimer rail, and to realize a desired terminal-to-source joining edge as an isolated +1 symmetric-difference component before collision analysis.

## Persistence
Retain x,y, the literal dimer cover D, the current cover F when present, and the isolated component {x_out y_in}.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert that the isolated gain is collision-free or an upper set. Does not by itself reduce the number of paths. R980 is not needed for existence of the isolated component.

## Proof
By R998 applied to the proper increasing path K=(x,y), the complement G-{x,y} has an exact two-cover A|B. Therefore D=A|B|(x,y) is a spanning increasing three-cover containing x->y literally as a dimer rail. Now let F be any spanning increasing three-cover in which x is a terminal of one component and y is the source of a different component. In the directed matching M_F, x_out is unmatched because x is terminal, and y_in is unmatched because y is a source. In M_D, the dimer contributes the selected edge x_out y_in. Since a bipartite matching has degree at most one at each copy, no other edge of M_D triangle M_F can share x_out or y_in with x_out y_in. Hence {x_out y_in} is by itself a connected symmetric-difference component. It contains one M_D edge and no M_F edge, so its weight relative to F->D is +1. No collision-poset theorem is needed for this component-level fact.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/ACTIVE/R999.md -->

# R126 — Disjoint four-path plus trimer forces a five-path

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Let Q=(a,b,c,d) be a tight four-vertex path in a Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament, and let {x,y,z} be disjoint from Q and support a tight trimer. Then the seven-vertex set V(Q)∪{x,y,z} contains a tight path of order five.

## Hypotheses
Strong Level-(1) boundary antisymmetry; Q is a tight four-path; the disjoint three-set supports a tight trimer.

## Scope
Pure local path-amplification lemma. No order-ten minimality, deletion exactness, payment, or support-family assumptions are used.

## Applicability
Use whenever a displayed tight P4 has a disjoint tight trimer. In particular, any exact 4+3 cover supplies the hypotheses.

## Persistence
All asserted paths and forced turns are graph-intrinsic on the fixed seven vertices.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert a Hamilton path on all seven vertices, does not prescribe which five vertices support the resulting path, and does not claim an analogous P4 plus arbitrary three-set statement without first orienting that three-set as a tight trimer.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Narrow two-consumer local amplification helper; retain immutable proof history but inline conceptually into consumers.
- **Curation note:** Narrow two-consumer local amplification helper; retain immutable proof history but inline conceptually into consumers.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Verified independently at the ordered-turn level. Assuming no P5 forces the universal packet baw,dwa,wdc for each trimer vertex. The remaining local trimer orientations reduce, up to relabeling, to cyclic and transitive types; the stated reversal chains in both cases correctly force an explicit tight P5.

## Proof
Write Q=(a,b,c,d), so abc and bcd are tight. Orient the disjoint trimer as (x,y,z), so xyz is tight, and suppose for contradiction that V(Q)∪{x,y,z} contains no tight five-path.\n\nFirst obtain a universal three-turn packet for every w∈{x,y,z}. The candidate (w,a,b,c,d) cannot be a five-path, while abc and bcd are tight, so wab is bad and hence baw is tight by boundary antisymmetry. Likewise (a,b,c,d,w) cannot be a five-path, so cdw is bad and hence wdc is tight. Now (b,a,w,d,c) cannot be a five-path; since baw and wdc are tight, awd is bad and hence dwa is tight. Therefore, for every w∈{x,y,z},\n\n    baw,  dwa,  wdc\n\nare tight.\n\nIt remains only to use the local orientation type on {x,y,z}. Boundary antisymmetry chooses exactly one order from each reversal pair, so the eight possible local patterns form two isomorphism types under relabeling of x,y,z. Representatives are:\n\n(C) cyclic: xyz, yzx, zxy are tight;\n(T) transitive: xyz, xzy, yxz are tight.\n\nCase (C). Since baz and zxy are tight, the candidate (b,a,z,x,y) forces azx bad, hence xza tight. Since yzx and xdc are tight, (y,z,x,d,c) forces zxd bad, hence dxz tight. Since dxz and xza are tight, (d,x,z,a,y) forces zay bad, hence yaz tight. Since dya and yaz are tight, (x,d,y,a,z) forces xdy bad, hence ydx tight. But then\n\n    (y,d,x,z,a)\n\nis a tight five-path, because ydx, dxz, and xza are tight, contradiction.\n\nCase (T). Since bax and xzy are tight, (b,a,x,z,y) forces axz bad, hence zxa tight. Since yxz and zdc are tight, (y,x,z,d,c) forces xzd bad, hence dzx tight. Since dzx and zxa are tight, (d,z,x,a,y) forces xay bad, hence yax tight. Since dzx and zxa are tight, (y,d,z,x,a) forces ydz bad, hence zdy tight. But then\n\n    (z,d,y,a,x)\n\nis a tight five-path, because zdy, dya, and yax are tight, contradiction.\n\nThus a disjoint tight four-path and tight trimer always force a tight five-path.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/LEGACY/R126.md -->

# R138 — Endpoint-preserving P4-plus-trimer amplification

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Let Q=(a,b,c,d) be a tight four-vertex path and let K={x,y,z} be disjoint from Q and support a tight trimer. Then some tight five-path has support in the six-support family {Q∪{x}, Q∪{y}, Q∪{z}, K∪{a,b}, K∪{c,d}, K∪{a,d}}.

## Hypotheses
Strong Level-(1) boundary antisymmetry; Q is a tight four-path; K is a disjoint three-set supporting a tight trimer.

## Scope
Local support-controlled repair of the failed endpoint-preserving R132 formulation. No order-ten minimality or support-family assumptions are used.

## Applicability
Use when R126 alone gives too little support control. In a constrained support family, eliminate impossible members of the displayed six-support list to force one of the survivors.

## Persistence
The conclusion is graph-intrinsic on the fixed seven vertices and names only physical supports.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert that K∪{a,d} is always Hamiltonian. In particular it does not recover the rejected endpoint-preserving R132 statement; the successful support may instead be Q∪{w}, K∪{a,b}, or K∪{c,d}.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** One-consumer support-controlled amplification helper; retain immutable proof history but remove first-class canonical visibility.
- **Curation note:** One-consumer support-controlled amplification helper; retain immutable proof history but remove first-class canonical visibility.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Verified repaired local support-control lemma. Assuming all six named supports non-Hamiltonian yields the same forced turn packet as P125, but now every subsequent candidate is blocked by one of those explicitly assumed supports; cyclic and transitive trimer types both end in a contradiction P5 on K union {a,d}. The conclusion correctly retains the full six-support alternative and does not overclaim endpoint preservation.

## Proof
Orient K as (x,y,z), so xyz is tight, and suppose for contradiction that none of Q∪{x}, Q∪{y}, Q∪{z}, K∪{a,b}, K∪{c,d}, K∪{a,d} supports a tight five-path. For every w∈K, Q∪{w} is non-Hamiltonian. Since Q=(a,b,c,d) is tight, the failed candidates (w,a,b,c,d) and (a,b,c,d,w) force wab and cdw bad, hence baw and wdc tight by R3. The failed candidate (b,a,w,d,c), whose first and last turns are now tight, forces awd bad and hence dwa tight. Thus for every w∈K the packet baw, dwa, wdc is tight.\n\nThe three reversal pairs on K give eight local patterns, with two types up to relabeling. In the cyclic type take xyz, yzx, zxy tight. Since K∪{a,b} is non-Hamiltonian, (b,a,z,x,y) forces azx bad, hence xza tight. Since K∪{c,d} is non-Hamiltonian, (y,z,x,d,c) forces zxd bad, hence dxz tight. Since K∪{a,d} is non-Hamiltonian, (d,x,z,a,y) forces zay bad, hence yaz tight; then (x,d,y,a,z) forces xdy bad, hence ydx tight. But (y,d,x,z,a) is now a tight five-path on K∪{a,d}, contradiction.\n\nIn the transitive type take xyz, xzy, yxz tight. Non-Hamiltonicity of K∪{a,b} makes (b,a,x,z,y) force axz bad, hence zxa tight. Non-Hamiltonicity of K∪{c,d} makes (y,x,z,d,c) force xzd bad, hence dzx tight. Non-Hamiltonicity of K∪{a,d} makes (d,z,x,a,y) force xay bad, hence yax tight; then (y,d,z,x,a) forces ydz bad, hence zdy tight. But (z,d,y,a,x) is now a tight five-path on K∪{a,d}, contradiction. Therefore at least one of the six named supports is Hamiltonian.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/LEGACY/R138.md -->

# R139 — Endpoint-preserving P4-plus-trimer amplification is not locally valid

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Boundary antisymmetry together with a tight four-path Q=(a,b,c,d) and a disjoint tight trimer K={x,y,z} does not force the endpoint five-set {a,d,x,y,z} to support a tight five-path. There is an explicit boundary-antisymmetric turn assignment with abc, bcd, and xyz tight but with {a,d,x,y,z} non-Hamiltonian.

## Hypotheses
Only the local Strong Level-(1) boundary antisymmetry relation R3 and the displayed tight-path/trimer hypotheses.

## Scope
Finite counterexample to the returned R132 endpoint-preserving strengthening. It does not contradict accepted R126, which only guarantees some P5 somewhere on the seven vertices.

## Applicability
Use to prevent future arguments from extracting K∪{a,d} as a guaranteed P5 support from R126/P125. Support control must retain the full alternative family, as in corrected C130/R138.

## Persistence
The counterexample is an explicit graph-intrinsic finite turn assignment; all unspecified reversal pairs can be extended arbitrarily subject to R3.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not refute the controlled-support replacement R138 and does not rule out endpoint completion under additional hypotheses not present in the local R132 statement.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Historical local counterexample to endpoint-preserving P4+trimer amplification; superseded strategically by broader modern path/exact-cover fences.
- **Curation note:** Explicit finite counterexample to the false endpoint-preserving P4-plus-trimer amplification.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Explicit local counterexample independently verified. On E={a,d,x,y,z} the stated R3 assignment has exactly 12 tight P4 orderings and no tight P5; adjoining b,c with abc and bcd tight preserves the induced non-Hamiltonicity of E. Thus the rejected endpoint-preserving R132 statement is genuinely false under only its local hypotheses.

## Proof
On E={a,d,x,y,z}, for each unordered triple declare exactly the following three ordered triples tight, and declare their complete reversals bad:\n{a,d,x}: adx, axd, dax.\n{a,d,y}: ady, ayd, day.\n{a,d,z}: daz, dza, zda.\n{a,x,y}: xay, xya, yxa.\n{a,x,z}: axz, azx, xaz.\n{a,y,z}: yza, zay, zya.\n{d,x,y}: xdy, xyd, yxd.\n{d,x,z}: dxz, dzx, zdx.\n{d,y,z}: dzy, zdy, zyd.\n{x,y,z}: xyz, yxz, yzx.\nThis satisfies R3 and in particular xyz is tight. Direct inspection gives exactly the following tight four-paths on E: adxz, axdy, daxz, dazx, dzay, dzya, xayd, xyza, yxaz, zayd, zdax, zday. Their respective missing vertices and blocked right-extension turns are: y with xzy bad; z with dyz bad; y with xzy bad; y with zxy bad; x with ayx bad; x with yax bad; z with ydz bad; d with zad bad; d with azd bad; x with ydx bad; y with axy bad; x with ayx bad. Hence none of the twelve tight four-paths extends to a tight five-path, and every tight five-path would have a tight first four-path, so E supports no tight P5. Now adjoin b,c. Declare abc and bcd tight, making Q=(a,b,c,d) a tight P4; retain xyz tight; orient every other new reversal pair arbitrarily subject to R3. The endpoint set E is unchanged and remains non-Hamiltonian. This is the required counterexample.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/LEGACY/R139.md -->

# R148 — Three prescribed-middle trimers do not force a core four-path

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Boundary antisymmetry alone does not imply that three tight trimers on {p,b,e}, {p,d,e}, and {b,d,e}, each chosen with e as the middle vertex, force a tight four-vertex path on {p,b,d,e}. There is an explicit Strong Level-(1) local orientation on these four vertices satisfying all three prescribed-middle trimers but admitting no tight P4 on the four-set.

## Hypotheses
Only Strong Level-(1) boundary antisymmetry on four distinct vertices p,b,d,e.

## Scope
Local negative result for the type-(2,2,2) common-exterior spoke motif. It addresses only what follows from the three e-centered short-trimer orientations themselves.

## Applicability
Use to rule out attempts to close type-(2,2,2) from the three common-e short trimers alone. Any successful closure must additionally consume information from the long roots, support minimality, sign interaction, or another cross-root invariant.

## Persistence
The countermodel is a complete assignment of the twelve reversal pairs on the four fixed vertices.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not show the full type-(2,2,2) motif is realizable, and does not rule out a Hamilton path forced after adding the long-root constraints.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Historical prescribed-middle local counterexample with no live use; preserve historically.
- **Curation note:** Explicit four-vertex countermodel showing three prescribed-middle trimers do not force a core P4.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** The explicit local countermodel shows the three e-centered trimers alone do not force a P4; this is a valid negative-space result.

## Proof
On the four vertices {p,b,d,e}, declare the following twelve ordered triples tight, one from each complete-reversal pair: dbp, bdp, dpb; ebp, peb, epb; pde, ped, epd; bde, bed, dbe. Their complete reversals are bad. This is therefore a valid local R3 assignment. In particular the three prescribed-middle trimers peb, ped, and bed are all tight, corresponding to the three type-(2,2,2) short supports with common middle e. Now inspect the 24 possible orderings (v1,v2,v3,v4) of the four vertices. A tight P4 would require both v1v2v3 and v2v3v4 to belong to the displayed tight list. Direct enumeration of the 24 orderings gives no such ordering. Hence the three e-centered trimers alone do not force a tight P4 on their union. Since they contain no information involving vertices outside this four-set, they also cannot by themselves force a larger Hamilton complement without additional cross-root input.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/LEGACY/R148.md -->
