# R150 — Current-trimer endpoint/incidence role trichotomy

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Let T be an exact two-cover of an eight-vertex residual set whose component-size profile is 5+3 or 4+4. If a distinguished trimer J=(j_0,j_1,j_2) occurs literally as three consecutive vertices of one selected component of T, then one of the following holds: (i) both outer vertices j_0,j_2 are current component endpoints; (ii) exactly one of j_0,j_2 is a current component endpoint; or (iii) both j_0,j_2 are internal and each has a selected external incidence on that component.

## Hypotheses
T is an exact two-cover of eight vertices with component orders 5+3 or 4+4; J=(j_0,j_1,j_2) is literally selected consecutively in one target component with the stated orientation.

## Scope
Pure path-position consequence for the residual 5+3/4+4 profiles. Historically stated as Corollary 5 of the 4+3+3 residual compiler, and especially used for the canonical candidate mate J_Z.

## Applicability
Use after a named trimer has been currentized in an exact eight-vertex residual two-cover, when downstream consumers need endpoint exposure or current external incidence on the trimer outer vertices.

## Persistence
All endpoint and incidence roles are literal selected roles in the same target T in which J is current. No role is transported to another representative.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not make the parent candidate current; does not identify the external incidences with any prescribed historical edges; does not imply capture, protection, a seam, or final assembly; does not assert simultaneous endpoint exposure and internal incidence.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Eight-vertex current-trimer endpoint/incidence trichotomy is essentially path-position bookkeeping once the trimer is literally consecutive. Zero-consumer convenience lemma with low independent discovery value.
- **Curation note:** Eight-vertex current-trimer endpoint/incidence trichotomy is essentially path-position bookkeeping once the trimer is literally consecutive. Zero-consumer convenience lemma with low independent discovery value.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Current-trimer endpoint/incidence role trichotomy is the exact exhaustive position classification in 5+3/4+4 residual profiles.

## Proof
Recovered from A7C2_MATH_EXPLORER_000006.md, Corollary 5. If the target rail containing J has order 3, J is the entire component and both outer vertices are endpoints. If it has order 4, a consecutive trimer occupies positions 1-3 or 2-4, so exactly one outer vertex is an endpoint. If it has order 5, J occupies positions 1-3, 2-4, or 3-5. In the first and last positions one outer vertex is an endpoint; in positions 2-4 both outer vertices are internal and each is incident with the adjacent selected path state outside J. These exhaust the possibilities.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/LEGACY/R150.md -->

# R151 — Five-vertex Hamilton-4 Reverse-Wrap root fan

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
In the order-ten minimum-three-cover counterexample setting, let X be a tight five-path and let its five-vertex exterior be S={y_0,y_1,y_2,y_3,a}. If (y_0,y_1,y_2,y_3) is a tight Hamilton four-path on S\\{a}, then the five exterior trimers (y_1,y_0,a), (y_0,y_1,y_2), (y_1,y_2,y_3), (a,y_3,y_2), and (y_3,a,y_0) are simultaneously graph-intrinsically tight. More strongly, they occur as five literal minimum 5+3+2 covers with the same fixed five-path X: X⊔(y_1,y_0,a)⊔(y_2,y_3); X⊔(y_0,y_1,y_2)⊔(y_3,a); X⊔(y_1,y_2,y_3)⊔(a,y_0); X⊔(a,y_3,y_2)⊔(y_0,y_1); and X⊔(y_3,a,y_0)⊔(y_1,y_2). Equivalently, deleting the displayed marker dimer in each cover gives an exact 5+3 pair-deletion root with X retained literally.

## Hypotheses
Order-ten standing counterexample with minimum path-cover number three; X is a tight five-path on five vertices; its exterior has exactly five vertices S={y_0,y_1,y_2,y_3,a}; (y_0,y_1,y_2,y_3) is tight in the displayed orientation. Historical sources call this the audited Five-Vertex Hamilton-4 Reverse-Wrap / five-root compiler.

## Scope
Generic order-ten five-exterior compiler. It applies whenever a globally-longest five-path has a five-vertex exterior containing a tight Hamilton four-path. Later A7C2 work repeatedly used the generic fan and concrete theta specialization as accepted shared input.

## Applicability
Use when one needs several exact pair-deletion roots on the same physical exterior five-set while retaining the same five-path X literally. The five roots expose all five cycle marker supports {y_0,y_1},{y_1,y_2},{y_2,y_3},{y_3,a},{a,y_0} together with the corresponding complementary fixed trimer.

## Persistence
The same five-path X is literal in all five displayed minimum covers. Each trimer and marker dimer is literal only in its displayed root. The five trimer tightness statements are graph-intrinsic and may be reused across representatives. Marker-dimer orientation is not globally fixed by this contract.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert that one chosen orientation of every marker dimer persists around the entire physical five-root cell; later producer-local orientation-holonomy/coherent-dimer claims are not imported here. Does not transport arbitrary selected states between roots, does not imply capture/protection, and does not imply a spanning two-cover. The physical-support fan is stronger than bare five-exterior reverse-star equality because it retains one common X and five exact pair-deletion roots.

## Record notes

- **Curation note:** Order-ten five-exterior Hamilton-4 reverse-wrap root fan. Rich exact-root packet but zero-consumer special-order infrastructure; preserve historically rather than as a current spine theorem.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Accepted as usable legacy-certified Reverse-Wrap five-root infrastructure; proof route remains intentionally dependency-incomplete rather than falsely reconstructed.

## Proof
Historical acceptance/provenance certificate. A7C2_MATH_PUZZLER_000002 states that its producer parent A7C2_MATH_PUZZLER_000001 was independently accepted by A7C2_AUDIT_000001 with an orientation fence, and names as accepted input the Reverse-Wrap five-root fan and exact theta specialization. A7C2_MATH_EXPLORER_000006 independently names A7C2_AUDIT_000001 as the audited Five-Vertex Hamilton-4 Reverse-Wrap / five-root compiler, and applies it whenever a globally-longest five-path has a five-vertex exterior containing a tight Hamilton four-path. This proposal imports only that repeatedly attested audited base mathematics, not the later unaudited orientation-coherence theorems. Exact original proof dependencies were not recovered.

# R155 — Captured crossing / carrier-edge mirror reentry

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Let A be a graph-intrinsic historical carrier path, let D={x,y} be a physical crossing support with x in A and y outside A, and retain the historical fact that x was captured using that physical crossing. For any historical carrier adjacency E={p,x} incident with x, there exists a later minimum three-cover in which E and D are the two boundary physical supports of their unique tight mirror trimer through x. The historical capture event at x remains valid event ancestry in that later certificate.

## Hypotheses
Smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample; A is a previously certified graph-intrinsic carrier path; D={x,y} is a previously certified physical crossing of A with x on A and y outside A; x has a valid historical capture certificate using D; E={p,x} is any physical adjacency of x on the historical carrier A.

## Scope
Ancestry-bearing specialization of incident-pair mirror currentization. Its bare two-support coexistence is subsumed by Physical-Star Exact Rank-Two Currentization, but the named historical capture event and carrier-edge identity are retained because later capture/fixed-turn consumers use them.

## Applicability
Use after a capture event when a downstream argument needs a proper current mirror trimer whose middle is the captured physical vertex and whose two boundary supports are the captured crossing and a chosen old carrier adjacency. The terminal-carrier-edge specialization gives a later trimer with the old terminal physical support and captured crossing as boundaries.

## Persistence
Physical support identities D,E and the fact of the historical capture event are graph-intrinsic/historical and remain valid. The later mirror trimer is current in a newly chosen minimum three-cover. The original selected crossing orientation, carrier-edge orientation, old carrier component, residual rails, and any current protection do not persist unless separately proved.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Capture is not upgraded to protection. The theorem does not preserve the original selected crossing orientation, marker orientation, carrier-edge orientation, old carrier as a current component, old residual rails, R33 same-frame concentration, endpoint exposure, or any unrelated selected state. It is not a same-representative transport theorem and does not by itself yield a final seam or two-cover.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Integrator cleanup: route-specific capture/payment/capacity machinery with no live consumers, relations, or guidance references; accepted mathematics preserved historically.
- **Curation note:** Ancestry-bearing captured-crossing mirror reentry retaining the named capture event and chosen old carrier adjacency.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Captured crossing/carrier-edge mirror reentry is valid with ancestry-only persistence and appropriately excludes old selected roles and protection.

## Proof
Recovered verbatim in substance from the independently audited CRITIC_HANDOFF_INCREMENTAL_HANDOFF_RESEARCHER_34_INCIDENT_PAIR_MIRROR_RESELECTION_CAPTURED_BOUNDARY_PACKET_2026-08-24_2026-08-24.md §3.7. # R157 — Non-Hamilton universal-extension fixed-rail endpoint surgery

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Let H be a smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample, let X be a nonempty proper non-Hamilton vertex set, put Y=V(H)\\X, and assume every r in Y Hamilton-extends X. Fix any exact two-cover Y=U⊔V. For every endpoint r of U, choose any Hamilton tight path P_r on X union {r}. Then r is internal in P_r and P_r⊔(U-r)⊔V is a spanning minimum three-cover of H. Dually the same holds for every endpoint of V. Thus the opposite residual rail survives literally, while every selected state of the touched rail survives except its unique terminal state incident with r, which is exactly the unique blocker paid by the graft.

## Hypotheses
H is a smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample; X is nonempty, proper, and non-Hamilton; Y=H-X; every r in Y extends X to a Hamilton tight path; Y=U⊔V is one fixed exact two-cover; r is an endpoint of one chosen residual rail.

## Scope
Fixed-representative specialization of the universal internal-vertex graft in the non-Hamilton universal-extension setting. It applies to any chosen exact residual two-cover, not only cyclic-K4 instances. The point is literal residual-rail retention, not a new graft mechanism.

## Applicability
Use when universal-extension arguments need to currentize X union {r} without discarding the residual frame. It gives an endpoint-indexed minimum cover in which one whole old rail survives and the touched rail loses exactly one terminal selected state, enabling same-rail boundary packets, role tracking, and fixed-frame comparisons.

## Persistence
Within each endpoint-indexed output, the untouched residual rail is literally unchanged and all selected states of the touched rail except its terminal state at r survive literally. The Hamilton path P_r is current in that output. Different choices of r or P_r generally give different representatives and are not synchronized. No unrelated older rails or ancestry are inherited.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not expose the paid endpoint as a useful endpoint in the output; does not steer which side of P_r contains r; does not select any prescribed crossing support; does not preserve old carriers, R33/R28/R29 ancestry, capture/protection, or rails from frames other than the fixed U⊔V; does not synchronize different endpoint graft covers; does not imply Two-Seam/One-Hole assembly or a spanning two-cover.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Universal-extension fixed-rail endpoint surgery is technically useful but too specialized and currently unused to justify first-class canonical visibility.
- **Curation note:** Universal-extension fixed-rail endpoint surgery is technically useful but too specialized and currently unused to justify first-class canonical visibility.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Fixed-rail endpoint surgery is a valid R19 specialization preserving the untouched rail and all touched-rail states except the paid terminal state.

## Proof
Recovered as the accepted Non-Hamilton Universal-Extension Fixed-Rail Surgery / Cyclic-K4 Fixed-Rail Near-End Graft interface from the Aug. 24 Researcher/Critic/Puzzler chain. Fix an exact residual two-cover Y=U⊔V and endpoint r of U. The universal-extension hypothesis gives P_r Hamiltonian on X union {r}. Since X is non-Hamilton, r is internal in P_r; otherwise deleting endpoint r would Hamiltonize X. Universal Internal-Vertex Graft applied to P_r and U⊔V has blocker set equal to the selected incidence at r. At a rail endpoint this is exactly the one terminal state of U, so gain is one and cycle debt zero. The output is literally P_r⊔(U-r)⊔V. Universal-Extension Deletion Rigidity ensures U has at least two vertices, so U-r is nonempty. Hence the output is a spanning three-cover and therefore minimum. The opposite rail V survives intact and every U-state other than the terminal state at r survives. The later maximin handoff explicitly lists Non-Hamilton Universal-Extension Fixed-Rail Surgery among audited inputs, and the Puzzler consolidation carries the fixed-representative rail-retention scope as accepted.

# R158 — Carrier-Crossing Splice-or-Full-Breach Lemma

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Let C be a retained tight path in a finite Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament, and let S be a literal current path cover containing V(C). If S selects a state crossing V(C) | (V(S)-V(C)) at a carrier vertex v, then either S also selects an historical carrier state of C incident with v, in which case that state and the crossing are consecutive selected states and form a literal current tight splice turn in S, or S selects no historical carrier state of C incident with v. Hence in the no-splice branch an internal crossing vertex loses both historical carrier incidences, while a terminal crossing vertex loses its unique historical carrier incidence.

## Hypotheses
C is a graph-intrinsic retained tight path; S is one displayed literal path cover on a vertex set containing V(C); a current selected state of S crosses the physical cut V(C) | outside at v in V(C).

## Scope
Universal Strong Level-(1) local path-cover statement; no smallest-counterexample or extremality hypothesis is required.

## Applicability
Diagnoses any current carrier/exterior crossing as same-representative splice alignment or complete local historical breach. Useful before invoking assembly or fragmentation machinery.

## Persistence
The splice/breach conclusion is current only in the displayed representative S. Historical carrier identities remain graph-intrinsic after later representative changes, but selection does not.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not identify the splice with a final-candidate assembly coordinate; does not transfer selected states across representatives; does not assert endpoint exposure; does not create a two-cover.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** superseded
- **Lifecycle note:** Carrier-Crossing Splice-or-Full-Breach is the local ingredient explicitly subsumed by the more general Cut-Deficit Splice-or-Full-Breach Principle C163, which adds the transition identity and forced-crossing criterion.
- **Curation note:** Carrier-Crossing Splice-or-Full-Breach is the local ingredient explicitly subsumed by the more general Cut-Deficit Splice-or-Full-Breach Principle C163, which adds the transition identity and forced-crossing criterion.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Carrier-crossing splice/full-breach lemma verified.

## Proof
Let e be the selected crossing state incident with v. If a historical carrier state f of C incident with v is also selected in S, path-forest incidence forces e and f to be the two consecutive selected incidences at v on one current path component (with the obvious endpoint simplification). Since S is a tight path cover, their ordered triple is tight, so e and f form a literal current carrier/exterior splice turn. Therefore if no such splice turn occurs at the crossing vertex, no historical carrier state incident with v can be selected. If v is internal in C this excludes both old adjacent states; if v is terminal it excludes the unique old adjacent state.

# R161 — Root Boundary-Anchored Collision Normal Form

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Let H be a smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample and F=P0 sqcup P1 sqcup P2 any actual spanning three-cover. After finitely many actual rank-preserving owner switches there is an actual spanning three-cover F*=P0* sqcup P1* sqcup P2* in one of two dual forms. Tail form: P0* ends (...,u,v), x,y are the current heads of P1*,P2*, uv is the current last boundary state, uvx and uvy are bad, hence xvu and yvu are tight; thus reverse support (v,u) has two distinct same-polarity witnesses in current endpoint roles. Head form: P0* begins (u,v,...), x,y are the current tails of P1*,P2*, uv is the current first boundary state, xuv and yuv are bad, hence vux and vuy are tight. All boundary and witness roles occur in the same displayed final representative.

## Hypotheses
H is a smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample; F is any actual spanning three-cover.

## Scope
Strong-safe owner-descent / three-cover fan scope. No nontriviality assumption is needed on the two witness components beyond being distinct nonempty cover components.

## Applicability
Transforms a specified ancestry-bearing spanning three-cover into a live boundary-anchored same-polarity collision frame. Its value is transformation of a chosen representative, not anonymous root collision existence.

## Persistence
Only the final F* representative and graph-intrinsic collision turns are guaranteed. Pre-switch selected states, roles, reserve labels, envelope data, or other ancestry do not survive unless separately preserved.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Same-polarity collision is not itself a contradiction or spanning two-cover. The theorem does not preserve arbitrary pre-descent history and does not assert a final assembly coordinate.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** R161 is an old owner-descent boundary-collision normal form with no live O4/O6 route. Preserve as historical representative machinery.
- **Curation note:** Reusable boundary-anchored collision normal form; no longer a current project spine node.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Root boundary-anchored collision normal form accepted with same-representative fences.

## Proof
Start from the given actual spanning three-cover F=P_0 sqcup P_1 sqcup P_2. Because H has no spanning two-cover, not all three components can be singletons: if they were, any two vertices form a tight dimer and together with the third singleton would give a spanning two-cover. Relabel so P_0 is nontrivial. Maintain P_0 as the owner component.

Suppose the current owner ends (...,u,v), and let x be the current head of one of the other components, say P_1=(x,x_1,...). Test the literal seam turn (u,v,x). If it is bad, do nothing for this donor. If it is tight and P_1 has order at least two, replace the current three-cover by
P_0'=(P_0,x),  P_1'=(x_1,...),  P_2'=P_2.
Every inherited turn remains tight and the only new owner turn is exactly (u,v,x), so this is an actual spanning three-cover with the same number of nonempty components. This is a literal rank-three owner switch. If instead P_1 is the singleton (x), then a tight (u,v,x) would make P_0'=(P_0,x) together with P_2 a spanning two-cover, impossible in H. Hence for a singleton donor the seam is necessarily bad.

Repeat the same test for the current heads of both non-owner components, performing an absorption whenever a seam is tight and the donor remains nonempty. Every performed switch increases |P_0| by one while the two donor components remain nonempty. Therefore at most |V(H)|-3 switches can occur, so the process terminates at an actual spanning three-cover F*=P_0* sqcup P_1* sqcup P_2*. Write the final owner tail as (...,u,v) and the two other current heads as x,y. By termination, neither head can be absorbed. If a donor has order at least two, this means the corresponding seam uvx or uvy is bad; if it is a singleton, the same seam is bad because otherwise H would be two-covered. Thus both uvx and uvy are bad in this one displayed final representative.

Boundary antisymmetry R3 now gives the complete reversals xvu and yvu tight. Hence the reverse tested support (v,u) carries two distinct same-polarity witnesses x,y, while uv is literally the current last boundary state of P_0*. All boundary and witness roles are simultaneous in F*. This is exactly the R161 tail form. Applying the identical argument after reversing the choice of owner end gives the stated head-dual form if desired, but the theorem only requires one of the two dual forms. No historical currentness or representative is transported through the switches; only the final actual representative and graph-intrinsic tight turns are retained, matching the R161 persistence clause.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/LEGACY/R161.md -->

# R164 — Deleted-Neighbor Restoration Collision

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Let E=(e_0,...,e_m) be a graph-intrinsic tight path and let k,z be distinct vertices outside E representing an old deleted endpoint neighbor and a fresh replacement endpoint witness. Head form: if m>=1 and both (k,E) and (z,E) are tight, then either (z,k,E) is tight or (e_0,k,z) is a tight reverse-contact trimer. Tail form: if both (E,k) and (E,z) are tight, then either (E,k,z) is tight or (z,k,e_m) is a tight reverse-contact trimer. If E is a singleton, the two distinct endpoint witnesses already force one of the two three-vertex contact orders by boundary antisymmetry.

## Hypotheses
E is a retained graph-intrinsic tight path; k and z are distinct and outside E. In the nontrivial head form the turns k e_0 e_1 and z e_0 e_1 are tight; in the nontrivial tail form e_{m-1} e_m k and e_{m-1} e_m z are tight.

## Scope
Universal Strong Level-(1) graph-intrinsic restoration lemma. No smallest-counterexample, exact-cover, or current-selection hypothesis is required once the two old/fresh extensions are certified.

## Applicability
Consumes endpoint-role loss when a residual path has both an historical deleted neighbor and a fresh replacement witness. Outside bounded reverse contact, it restores the deleted neighbor into a strictly longer one-ended extension, preserving the identity of the old neighbor.

## Persistence
Both alternatives are graph-intrinsic path/turn certificates and therefore persist historically after representative changes. Any current role of k,z,E that produced them does not persist unless separately protected.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
The bounded reverse trimer/contact is not itself a spanning two-cover or contradiction. The theorem does not assert the restoration alternative always occurs, and does not preserve the source comparison representative or selected role-loss state.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Deleted-neighbor restoration collision is a narrow two-consumer local helper; conceptually inline its one-step antisymmetry argument into consumers and retire the claim identity.
- **Curation note:** Deleted-neighbor restoration collision is a narrow two-consumer local helper; conceptually inline its one-step antisymmetry argument into consumers and retire the claim identity.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Deleted-Neighbor Restoration Collision verified.

## Proof
Head form: because (k,E) is tight, k e_0 e_1 is tight and all later turns of E are tight. Test z k e_0. If tight, then z,k,e_0,e_1,...,e_m is a tight path, proving the strict restoration extension through the old deleted neighbor k. If z k e_0 is bad, Boundary Antisymmetry R3 gives e_0 k z tight, a bounded reverse-contact trimer. Tail form: test e_m k z. If it is tight, append k,z to E using the already tight old turn e_{m-1} e_m k; if it is bad, R3 gives z k e_m tight. If E is the singleton (e), test z e k; either it is tight or its complete reversal k e z is tight, so bounded contact is immediate.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/LEGACY/R164.md -->

# R165 — Arbitrary Prescribed-Head Two-Cover Is False

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
There exists an eight-vertex Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament H and a vertex r such that H has a spanning cover by two tight paths, but no spanning two-path cover has r as the head of either path. In fact the archived example is CW-free, has r=0, every tight path beginning at 0 has order at most three, and H contains a tight path of order seven.

## Hypotheses
None; this is an explicit existential counterexample. The vertex set is {0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7}. Tightness is defined by local tournaments T_v via u v w tight iff u beats w in T_v.

## Scope
Negative result for Strong Level-(1), already inside the CW-free subclass. Therefore no Strong proof may invoke arbitrary prescribed-head two-cover completion or arbitrary prescribed-head Hamilton/two-path induction.

## Applicability
Regression barrier for rooted variants and proof designs that try to keep an arbitrarily chosen vertex as a current path head through minimum two-cover completion.

## Persistence
Graph-intrinsic explicit counterexample. Independent of representatives in the current A7C3 proof.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not refute the unrooted Strong Level-(1) Two-Cover Conjecture. Does not say every root can fail; in the archived example only root 0 fails and an unrooted two-cover exists.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Historical counterexample to arbitrary prescribed-head two-cover; no live use remains.
- **Curation note:** Explicit CW-free counterexample to arbitrary prescribed-head two-cover completion.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Arbitrary prescribed-head two-cover counterexample accepted as explicit legacy finite certificate.

## Proof
Use the seven transitive local orders and the cyclic-top T_2 written in the accepted P164 certificate. For every middle vertex v, define u v w tight iff u beats w in T_v. Each T_v is a tournament, so for every distinct u,v,w exactly one of u v w and w v u is tight; hence this is a Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament.

The advertised unrooted cover is literal: (2,4,3,7,0,5,6) is tight by direct lookup in T_4,T_3,T_7,T_0,T_5, and singleton (1) is a tight path, so these two paths span V.

Now enumerate tight simple paths beginning at 0 from the retained local tournaments. There are exactly ten such paths in total and their maximum order is three. The only order-three rooted paths are (0,5,6) and (0,6,5). For every tight rooted path P beginning at 0, enumerate all permutations of its complement V\V(P) and test consecutive triples by the same local-tournament rule. No complement has a Hamilton tight ordering. Therefore no spanning two-path cover can have 0 as the head of either path. This is exhaustive because any such rooted two-cover consists of one tight simple path beginning at 0 together with a Hamilton tight path on its complement.

The claimed long path is also literal: (2,4,3,7,0,5,6) is a tight path of order seven.

Finally verify CW-freeness directly without the lost historical rank table. Form the ordered-state digraph on the 56 states (u,v), u!=v, with an arc (u,v)->(v,w) exactly when u v w is tight. Kahn topological elimination removes all 56 states, so this state digraph is acyclic. A closed tight walk would give a directed cycle in this state digraph, therefore none exists. Thus the explicit example is CW-free. All checks use only the local tournaments retained in the accepted certificate; no external historical dependency is required.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/LEGACY/R165.md -->

# R166 — Two-Sided Middle-Incidence Seam Test

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Let a,b,c,r,s be distinct vertices with abc tight. Then either rab and bcs are both tight, in which case (r,a,b,c,s) is a tight five-path, or bar is tight, or scb is tight. Equivalently, failure of the left seam rab produces the reverse trimer (b,a,r), and failure of the right seam bcs produces the reverse trimer (s,c,b).

## Hypotheses
The five vertices are distinct and abc is tight.

## Scope
Universal Strong Level-(1) local turn lemma. No deletion frame, pair payment, smallest-counterexample hypothesis, or current representative is required.

## Applicability
Use whenever a retained/fixed turn abc sits between proposed predecessor r and successor s. It reduces the two-seam test to either literal five-path assembly or one of two exact reverse-trimer certificates. The archived Two-Sided Middle-Incidence Discharge is the fixed pair-deletion/payment specialization.

## Persistence
All conclusions are graph-intrinsic tight-path/turn facts and persist historically. Any current roles that supplied r,s in an application are separate.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
The reverse trimers are certificates, not contradictions or spanning covers. No refund/payment conclusion is included unless the application separately satisfies the signed-support payment hypotheses. The theorem does not say which seam fails.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Universal two-sided seam test is an almost immediate boundary-antisymmetry convenience lemma: both seams give the concatenated P5, otherwise the failing seam reverses. Zero consumers and low discovery value.
- **Curation note:** Universal two-sided seam test is an almost immediate boundary-antisymmetry convenience lemma: both seams give the concatenated P5, otherwise the failing seam reverses. Zero consumers and low discovery value.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Two-Sided Middle-Incidence Seam Test verified.

## Proof
If rab and bcs are tight, then the three consecutive turns of (r,a,b,c,s) are rab, abc, bcs, all tight, so the five-path is tight. If rab is bad, Boundary Antisymmetry R3 gives bar tight. If bcs is bad, R3 gives scb tight. These alternatives exhaust the two tests.

# R170 — Universal Proper-Turn Front Door

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Every hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample H contains a proper graph-intrinsic tight turn J=(a,b,c). More strongly, for any three distinct vertices a,b,c, exactly one of (a,b,c) and (c,b,a) is tight; since |H|>3, either orientation is a proper tight path whenever it is the tight one.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest counterexample to the Strong Level-(1) Two-Cover Conjecture.

## Scope
Global entry lemma for the Strong smallest-counterexample setting.

## Applicability
Allows any argument whose only entry requirement is a chosen proper tight turn to start immediately, without first producing a longest-path portal, fan, pivot, marker, collision, or paid pair. It is the upstream entry theorem referenced by the historical fixed-turn lineage.

## Persistence
The chosen turn is graph-intrinsic and remains a valid tight path after representative changes. Any fixed-turn lineage built on it must keep the same physical turn identity if its own theorem requires that.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not itself produce a balanced pair, descent, endpoint exposure, exact deletion frame, or two-cover. It does not say the fixed-turn lex clock controls arbitrary representative resets.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Universal Proper-Turn Front Door is essentially boundary antisymmetry plus the standing size>3 fact: any chosen triple has exactly one tight reversal orientation and is proper. Useful shorthand with three consumers, but negligible independent discovery content.
- **Curation note:** Universal Proper-Turn Front Door is essentially boundary antisymmetry plus the standing size>3 fact: any chosen triple has exactly one tight reversal orientation and is proper. Useful shorthand with three consumers, but negligible independent discovery content.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Universal Proper-Turn Front Door verified.

## Proof
Take any three distinct vertices a,b,c. By Boundary Antisymmetry R3, exactly one of abc and cba is tight, so H contains a tight trimer J on those vertices. It remains only to see that J is proper. A graph with at most two vertices has a spanning cover by at most two one- or two-vertex tight paths. A graph on exactly three vertices has a spanning tight trimer by the same antisymmetry argument. Therefore a counterexample has more than three vertices, and J is a proper tight path.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/LEGACY/R170.md -->

# R174 — Multi-Support Adjacent-Color Refund

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Let S_1,...,S_r, r>=2, be pairwise vertex-disjoint nontrivial graph-intrinsic signed tight supports of arbitrary sign polarities. Suppose one tight path A contains the union of all V(S_i). Then there exist distinct i,j and a contiguous tight interval C of A such that C meets S_i in exactly one vertex, meets S_j in exactly one vertex, and meets every other S_k in no vertex. After Signed-Interval Rebirth on the two touched supports, total support mass sum |S_i| decreases by at least two. In particular any two disjoint nontrivial signed supports lying in one tight carrier admit an order-free two-support refund, independent of their relative sign polarities or historical order.

## Hypotheses
Strong Level-(1); S_i are pairwise disjoint, nontrivial graph-intrinsic signed tight supports; A is one tight carrier containing all support vertices; Signed-Interval Rebirth / Tight-Path Cut Memory is available for deleting a proper interval meeting a signed support partially.

## Scope
Order-free, arbitrary sign polarities, arbitrary number r>=2 of disjoint nontrivial signed supports. No smallest-counterexample assumption is needed for the adjacent-color combinatorics itself beyond whatever scope is required by the imported signed-support rebirth theorem.

## Applicability
Use whenever several historical signed supports have all been swallowed into one tight carrier. It pays support mass immediately without first aligning historical support order, running Reverse Ear, or classifying anchor order.

## Persistence
Untouched supports persist unchanged. Each touched support retains a nonempty signed descendant because the chosen interval meets it in exactly one vertex and the support is nontrivial. Tight-Path Cut Memory may shift the active witness to the appropriate surviving historical boundary; witness names are not fixed forever.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Requires every touched support to be nontrivial; do not apply the two-support refund when one support is singleton. Does not require opposite signs or a balanced pair. Does not itself close the support-mass floor. Does not make total pair/support mass globally monotone across unrelated new births or representative resets. Does not erase richer Reverse-Ear/contact ancestry when such geometry is independently useful.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** R174 is a multi-support historical payment/refund theorem with no live route or obligation reference. Preserve historically.
- **Curation note:** Order-free multi-support adjacent-color refund parent with untouched-support persistence and cut-memory ancestry.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Multi-Support Adjacent-Color Refund accepted; adjacent-color interval argument verified.

## Proof
Let A be the tight carrier containing the pairwise disjoint nontrivial signed supports S_1,...,S_r, r>=2. Traverse A in its path order and retain only those vertices lying in the union of the support sets. Label each retained vertex by the unique support index i for which it belongs to S_i. Since every support is nonempty and r>=2, this finite color word uses at least two colors, hence contains two consecutive retained positions of different colors, say x in S_i followed by y in S_j with i!=j. Let C be the contiguous interval of A from x through y. By consecutivity in the retained support-encounter sequence, the interior of C contains no support vertex at all. Therefore C meets S_i exactly in {x}, meets S_j exactly in {y}, and misses every other S_k. Because S_i and S_j are nontrivial, each has at least one vertex outside C, so neither is swallowed. Apply fully reconstructible Signed-Interval Rebirth/Tight-Path Cut Memory R425 to each of the two signed supports after deleting C. Each touched support has a nonempty signed descendant obtained from a surviving old-path interval, with size at most |S_i|-1 and |S_j|-1 respectively; witness names may migrate to the appropriate cut neighbors exactly as R425 allows. Every untouched S_k persists unchanged. Hence the total support mass decreases by at least two. This proves the multi-support theorem. The r=2 statement is the same argument with only two colors and does not use relative sign polarity or historical support order.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/LEGACY/R174.md -->

# R177 — Crossed-Deletion Port-Preservation Regression

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
There exists a seven-vertex Level-(3) boundary tournament on vertices x,c,d,z,a,b,e satisfying the crossed deletion-window conditions xcd tight, abe tight, cdz bad, zab bad, and dza bad, for which no spanning two-path cover simultaneously preserves the literal exterior ports x,c at the beginning of one path and b,e at the end of the other. Nevertheless the same system has a Hamilton tight path. Hence crossed local deletion data alone does not force a bounded port-preserving two-path reroute.

## Hypotheses
Explicit Level-(3) edge-order witness: ab < xa < be < zb < db < ae < za < cz < xz < cb < xd < dz < da < ze < xc < ce < xe < cd < de < ca < xb. Tightness is interpreted by the standard Level-(3) increasing-edge-order representation.

## Scope
Strong Level-(1) negative result. It refutes only a purely local port-preserving reroute theorem under the displayed crossed-window hypotheses. It is not a counterexample to the Strong Two-Cover Conjecture.

## Applicability
Guardrail against arguments that insist a crossed five-vertex deletion core must reconnect to both original exterior rails without additional global retention/extremality hypotheses.

## Persistence
The counterexample is a fixed graph-intrinsic finite witness. Its Hamilton tight path a,b,z,x,c,d,e shows that the obstruction is port preservation rather than path-coverability.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not say port preservation is impossible under stronger global smallest-counterexample or extremal hypotheses. Does not invalidate explicit retention/restoration theorems. Does not contradict Universal Prescribed-Path Completion, which deliberately allows the complement rails to change.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Historical crossed-deletion port-preservation regression; no live use remains.
- **Curation note:** Explicit crossed-deletion counterexample showing two exterior ports cannot be assumed preserved.

# R178 — Single-Relocation Plus Segment-Reversal Hamilton Descent Is Incomplete

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
There exists an eight-vertex Level-(3) boundary tournament and a Hamilton cyclic order C with raw cyclic defect cut number kappa_0(C)=3 such that every distinct single-vertex relocation of C and every proper cyclic contiguous-segment reversal of C still has kappa_0 at least three, while a genuine two-block transposition produces a cyclic order with kappa_0=2. Therefore single-vertex relocation plus arbitrary proper segment reversal is not a complete universal Hamilton-defect descent system.

## Hypotheses
Explicit Level-(3) edge-order witness on K8: 06 < 15 < 37 < 05 < 46 < 26 < 13 < 07 < 45 < 34 < 67 < 12 < 25 < 16 < 14 < 27 < 56 < 57 < 04 < 01 < 23 < 35 < 47 < 03 < 36 < 02 < 17 < 24. For a Hamilton cyclic order C, D(C) is the set of defective turn centers and kappa_0(C)=min{|F|: F subseteq E(C), D(C) subseteq V(F)}.

## Scope
Strong Level-(1) negative result, witnessed already in Level-(3). It refutes completeness of the specified local Hamilton move set, not the existence of some other descent operation.

## Applicability
Guardrail for Hamilton-order approaches: any universal descent architecture must permit genuine two-block/internal rerouting or an equivalent nonlocal operation.

## Persistence
The explicit edge-order witness is graph-intrinsic. The negative conclusion concerns the entire enumerated move neighborhood of the displayed cyclic order.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not say single relocations or segment reversals are never useful. Does not refute the Universal Linear Defect Formula or Two-Short-Run Normal Form. Does not claim the exhibited system is a counterexample to the Strong Two-Cover Conjecture.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Historical failure of single-relocation/segment-reversal descent; no live use remains.
- **Curation note:** Explicit counterexample showing relocation plus segment reversal is not a complete Hamilton-defect descent system.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Hamilton local-move incompleteness regression accepted as explicit finite guardrail.

## Proof
Use the displayed K8 total edge order 06<15<37<05<46<26<13<07<45<34<67<12<25<16<14<27<56<57<04<01<23<35<47<03<36<02<17<24 and define u v w tight iff edge uv precedes edge vw. As in every such edge-order representation, complete reversal swaps the two adjacent edges, so exactly one of u v w and w v u is tight.

For the cyclic order C=(0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7), inspect each cyclic turn (v_{i-1},v_i,v_{i+1}). The resulting defect word is G D G D D G D D, so the defective centers are {1,3,4,6,7}. The minimum number of cycle edges whose incident vertices cover those defective centers is kappa_0(C)=3.

Enumerate every distinct single-vertex relocation of the displayed linear representative C: remove one of the eight vertices and reinsert it in any of the eight positions, discard the unchanged order, and deduplicate. This gives exactly 49 distinct orders. Recompute the cyclic defect centers and kappa_0 for each; every value is 3 or 4, hence none decreases below 3.

Next enumerate every proper cyclic contiguous segment, of lengths 2 through 7 and all eight cyclic starting positions, reverse that segment in place, discard the unchanged order, and deduplicate. This gives exactly 44 distinct proper cyclic segment reversals. Again every resulting kappa_0 is 3 or 4.

Finally take C'=(0,4,3,1,2,5,6,7). Its defect word is G D D G G G D D, with defective centers {1,2,6,7}, and kappa_0(C')=2. C' is obtained by the stated genuine two-block transposition, moving block (4) across block (1,2) with the indicated internal rearrangement. Therefore single-vertex relocation plus arbitrary proper cyclic segment reversal is not a complete universal defect-descent move set. All counts and defect values are reconstructed directly from the retained edge order and the definition of kappa_0.

# R179 — Anchored-Capacity Unsigned-End Reverse-Star Saturation

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Let (alpha;P),(T;beta) be a balanced opposite-sign pair and fix the signed head h of P, the signed tail t of T, and witnesses alpha,beta. Among all vertex-disjoint tight path pairs (P',T') with head(P')=h and (alpha,P') tight, tail(T')=t and (T',beta) tight, choose one maximizing |P'|+|T'|. Write this anchored-capacity realization again as (P,T), and put X=V(H)\(V(P) union V(T) union {alpha,beta}). Then every x in X has the following forced reverse-star signs. If P=(...,c,d) is nontrivial, x d c is tight; if P=(p) is singleton, x p alpha is tight. Dually, if T=(a,b,...) is nontrivial, b a x is tight; if T=(t) is singleton, beta t x is tight.

## Hypotheses
H is a finite Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament. (alpha;P) is a head-signed tight path and (T;beta) is a tail-signed tight path; P,T are vertex-disjoint and the witnesses lie outside their own supports. The four anchored data (alpha,h;t,beta) are fixed while maximizing |P'|+|T'| over disjoint realizations satisfying the same signed head/tail conditions.

## Scope
Graph-intrinsic, Strong Level-(1)-safe, and representative-relative. The conclusion concerns every ordinary reservoir vertex outside the chosen capacity supports and their two fixed witnesses. It applies equally to nontrivial and singleton supports through the displayed formulas.

## Applicability
Use to turn a static anchored-capacity maximum into full same-polarity witness families on the reverse dimer at each unsigned support end. It is the input for reservoir collision, balanced-cut visibility, and later fixed-frame capacity collisions.

## Persistence
The tight reverse-star turns are graph-intrinsic once proved. The anchored-capacity realization itself is only an auxiliary extremal representative. Historical supports, birth frame, pivots, theta ports/shadows, payment/capture ancestry, and other labels are not replaced by the capacity representative and must be retained separately when needed.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
No claim that anchored capacity is a global monotone, remains maximal after support truncation/refund, or is preserved by recompletion. No claim that the reverse-star trimers are selected in one current cover before a separate currentization. No CW-freeness, state-DAG, scalarization, or cycle-contradiction inference is used.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Integrator cleanup: route-specific capture/payment/capacity machinery with no live consumers, relations, or guidance references; accepted mathematics preserved historically.
- **Curation note:** Anchored-capacity extremal primitive forcing full reverse-star witness saturation at unsigned support ends.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Anchored-Capacity Unsigned-End Reverse-Star Saturation verified.

## Proof
Fix an anchored-capacity realization (P,T) with the four anchored data held fixed. Let x lie in the ordinary reservoir X, so x is outside P,T,alpha,beta. Suppose first that the head-signed support P=(p_0,...,c,d) is nontrivial. If the turn (c,d,x) were tight, then P^+=(p_0,...,c,d,x) would be a tight path with the same head h=p_0 and the same head-sign witness alpha, because (alpha,P) remains a tight prefix of (alpha,P^+). It remains vertex-disjoint from T, and its size is one larger, contradicting maximality of |P|+|T|. Thus (c,d,x) is bad. Boundary antisymmetry R3 on the distinct triple {c,d,x} forces (x,d,c) tight. If P=(p) is singleton, tightness of (alpha,p,x) would similarly extend the head-signed support while preserving h=p, witness alpha, and disjointness, so (alpha,p,x) is bad and R3 forces (x,p,alpha) tight.

The tail side is dual. If T=(a,b,...,t) is nontrivial and (x,a,b) were tight, then (x,T) would be a larger tight path with the same tail t and the same tail-sign witness beta, remaining disjoint from P, contradicting capacity maximality. Hence (x,a,b) is bad and R3 gives (b,a,x) tight. If T=(t) is singleton, an extension (x,t,beta) would contradict maximality, so its reverse (beta,t,x) is tight. These are exactly the four R179 reverse-star formulas. The conclusions are graph-intrinsic tight turns; only the maximizing realization is representative-relative. No further dependency is used.

# R180 — Anchored-Capacity Reservoir Collision-or-One-Residual

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Let (alpha;P),(T;beta) be an anchored-capacity realization for fixed signed anchors and witnesses, and let X=V(H)\(V(P) union V(T) union {alpha,beta}) be the ordinary reservoir. Define the head-side capacity reverse dimer D_P=(d,c) when P=(...,c,d) is nontrivial and D_P=(p,alpha) when P=(p) is singleton; define the tail-side capacity reverse dimer D_T=(b,a) when T=(a,b,...) is nontrivial and D_T=(beta,t) when T=(t) is singleton. Then exactly the following trichotomy is available: (i) if X is empty, H has a spanning two-cover; (ii) if |X|>=2, any two distinct x,y in X are same-polarity witnesses on the fixed dimer D_P (and dually D_T), so Same-Support Sign Interaction yields a strict graph-intrinsic two-witness extension or a bounded reverse trimer/contact; (iii) if |X|=1, the two capacity supports together with their two fixed witnesses cover all but one vertex. Thus the only anchored-capacity maximum avoiding closure and the accepted same-polarity collision output is a one-residual near-spanning anchored carrier.

## Hypotheses
H is a finite Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament. (alpha;P),(T;beta) form a balanced opposite-sign pair and (P,T) is an anchored-capacity maximum for the fixed witnesses and signed head/tail anchors in the sense of Anchored-Capacity Unsigned-End Reverse-Star Saturation.

## Scope
Strong-safe, graph-intrinsic collision theorem in one fixed anchored-capacity representation. No smallest-counterexample hypothesis is needed for the collision part; the empty-reservoir conclusion is the literal two-cover consequence of the signed paths themselves.

## Applicability
Use capacity statically before further payment/recompletion: a reservoir of size at least two cannot remain quiet, while the only collision-free nonclosed capacity face has one ordinary residual vertex. The theorem is the parent of the capacity-flat synchronized-floor collision.

## Persistence
The fixed reverse-dimer signs and any strict extension/reverse-contact output are graph-intrinsic. The capacity realization remains representative-relative. Original historical supports and their ancestry are retained separately and are not replaced by the capacity pair.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
The one-residual case is not closed: no claim is made that its last vertex inserts into either support. No claim that capacity is monotone under later support truncation or recompletion. No claim that the collision output is a spanning two-cover. No CW-specific inference is used.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** R180 is an anchored-capacity route theorem with no live route or obligation reference. Preserve the accepted result historically.
- **Curation note:** Reusable anchored-capacity collision theorem; optional route, not current spine.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Anchored-Capacity Reservoir Collision-or-One-Residual accepted in fixed-capacity scope.

## Proof
Let (alpha;P),(T;beta) be the anchored-capacity realization and X its ordinary reservoir. Define D_P,D_T exactly as in R180. By fully reconstructible R179, every x in X gives the same tested orientation and same polarity on D_P: when P=(...,c,d), the tight turn (x,d,c) makes the fixed oriented dimer D_P=(d,c) head-signed by x; when P=(p) is singleton, (x,p,alpha) makes D_P=(p,alpha) head-signed by x. Dually every x in X gives the same tested oriented dimer D_T its tail polarity. Therefore if |X|>=2 and x,y are distinct reservoir vertices, R523 is licensed on the identical tested orientation, with distinct same-polarity witnesses x,y. Its HH or TT branch is exactly the historical same-polarity two-extension collision packet: the fixed oriented dimer has two distinct graph-intrinsic witness extensions. Hence the first collision alternative stated in R180, a strict graph-intrinsic two-witness extension, already holds. No unordered-support comparison and no additional opaque collision theorem are used.

If X is empty, every vertex of H lies in V(P) union V(T) union {alpha,beta}. We construct a spanning cover by at most two tight paths using the signed extensions themselves. The head sign means (alpha,P) is tight whenever alpha is outside P; the tail sign means (T,beta) is tight whenever beta is outside T. Because P and T are vertex-disjoint, each witness is either outside both supports or lies on the opposite support. If alpha and beta are distinct and both outside P union T, then (alpha,P) and (T,beta) are disjoint tight paths spanning H. If exactly one witness, say alpha, lies on the opposite support T, then P and T already contain alpha; append only the other outside witness beta to T when beta is outside T, so P and (T,beta) span, or if beta also lies on P then P and T already span. The head/tail dual is identical. If alpha=beta=w and w is outside both supports, then w can be absorbed into either signed path, e.g. (w,P) together with T, giving a spanning two-cover. Thus X=empty forces a spanning cover by at most two tight paths.

The only remaining cardinality is |X|=1. By definition, the anchored-capacity supports together with their two fixed witnesses then cover all vertices except that one ordinary reservoir vertex. No insertion or closure claim is made. These three cases are exhaustive and give exactly the R180 collision-or-one-residual trichotomy. The capacity realization is representative-relative, while the R179 signs and R523 collision packet are graph-intrinsic.

# R181 — Capacity-Flat Synchronized Floor Collision

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
In the synchronized ancestry-bearing floor, suppose the anchored-capacity-flat balanced pair has mass M=2, hence singleton supports (p),(t) with fixed witnesses alpha,beta. Suppose simultaneously that the retained parent envelope A* has at least three vertices and the fixed reserve trimer T_q=(q0,q1,q2) is disjoint from A*. Then the ordinary reservoir of the fixed anchored-capacity representation contains at least two vertices. Consequently the general Anchored-Capacity Reservoir Collision theorem fires in that same representation: before any ordinary-vertex M=4 lift, floor steering, or choice of puncture frame, one has a strict same-polarity extension or a bounded reverse trimer/contact. The one-residual exception of the general capacity theorem is impossible in this synchronized floor.

## Hypotheses
Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament. A synchronized ancestry-bearing M=2 floor with singleton balanced supports (p),(t), fixed witnesses alpha,beta, a retained parent envelope A* with |A*|>=3, and a fixed tight reserve trimer T_q=(q0,q1,q2) vertex-disjoint from A*. The anchored capacity for the fixed singleton anchors/witnesses is flat at this floor.

## Scope
Specialized synchronized floor corollary. The extra A*/T_q ancestry is essential to the reservoir cardinality argument. The collision occurs in one fixed capacity representation; separately steered puncture descendants are not combined.

## Applicability
Use to eliminate the one-residual near-spanning exception and force first physical collision at the ancestry-bearing M=2 floor without lifting back to M=4 or choosing left/right puncture frames.

## Persistence
The retained A*, T_q/q1, singleton anchors, fixed witnesses, and preexisting synchronized ancestry remain historical labels. The collision output is graph-intrinsic. The theorem does not discard the stronger common-frame ancestry merely because first progress is forced earlier.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
This is not a theorem about every abstract mass-two balanced pair or every capacity floor. It requires the synchronized package with disjoint A* and T_q and |A*|>=3. It does not close the strict-extension or bounded-contact outputs. It does not combine left/right puncture frames or assert capacity monotonicity.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Capacity-flat synchronized floor collision is a specialized zero-consumer corollary; preserve it in history but not as a peer canonical theorem.
- **Curation note:** Capacity-flat synchronized floor collision is a specialized zero-consumer corollary; preserve it in history but not as a peer canonical theorem.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Capacity-Flat Synchronized Floor Collision verified from reservoir cardinality and R180.

## Proof
At the synchronized floor the anchored-capacity supports are the singletons (p) and (t), with fixed witnesses alpha,beta. Thus S={p,t,alpha,beta} has at most four vertices. The retained parent envelope satisfies |A*|>=3. The fixed reserve trimer T_q=(q0,q1,q2) has three vertices and V(A*) is disjoint from V(T_q), so |V(A*) union V(T_q)|>=6. At most four of these six or more vertices lie in S. Hence at least two distinct vertices lie outside the two supports and their fixed witnesses, i.e. in the ordinary reservoir X. Apply R180. The X-empty and |X|=1 faces are impossible; the |X|>=2 face gives a same-polarity two-witness collision on a fixed capacity reverse dimer, hence the accepted strict extension or bounded reverse trimer/contact output. All data are taken in one fixed capacity representation.

In the surviving quiet/no-R12-exit branch, x_{r-1}t is exactly the literal old last boundary r t of R_H. Dually, if x_{r-1} t h is tight, T_T=T-{h x_1}+{th} is an exact two-cover selecting th with zero cycle debt and, in the surviving quiet/no-R12-exit branch, h x_1 is exactly the literal old first boundary h s of R_T. The synchronized hard fixed-fiber package is in force: old residual cover O=A* disjoint_union R_H disjoint_union R_T of H-T_q; a quiet overlap-maximal exact two-cover T with fixed endpoint sets and straight pairing; completion-independent role labels R_H=head-lost and R_T=tail-lost; and the historical Cross-Completion Opposite-Role Collision package is available. The stated old-boundary conclusion is conditional on remaining in the quiet branch and excluding that package's already-productive outputs.

## Scope
Strong Level-(1)-safe, representative-relative exact-two-cover theorem in the synchronized fixed-endpoint fiber. It identifies the literal selected state removed by the successful wrap rotation and preserves all other selected states of that exact target.

## Applicability
Use when a residual splice th is selected by an intracomponent wrap in the quiet fixed fiber and downstream assembly needs the exact old boundary sacrificed rather than merely existence of a selected th. The head and tail versions are exact duals.

## Persistence
In the rotated exact target, th is literally selected, the identified old residual boundary is literally absent, and every other selected state of T survives. The original target T, its literal C_R order, and any previously certified same-cover internal A* excursion remain simultaneously known as historical/current-frame certificates. However the rotated target is not guaranteed to retain both original A* ingress/egress states if one coincides with the deleted terminal boundary.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
No claim that selecting th fuses the literal old residual paths R_H and R_T. No claim that every exact two-cover lies in the quiet overlap-maximal fiber. No use of role-polarity rigidity on a nonquiet rotated cover: leaving the quiet branch is an accepted physical exit instead. No claim that matching-cycle variation is a physical move. No CW-specific argument. No one-seam final assembly conclusion.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Fixed-fiber selected-wrap old-boundary alignment is a narrow representative-specific zero-consumer theorem; preserve as proof history.
- **Curation note:** Fixed-fiber selected-wrap old-boundary alignment is a narrow representative-specific zero-consumer theorem; preserve as proof history.

## Proof
Write C_R=(h,x_1,...,x_{r-1},t). If t h x_1 is tight, then (t,h,x_1,...,x_{r-1}) is a tight path, so T_H=T-{x_{r-1}t}+{th} is an exact two-cover of H-T_q. It changes one selected state, preserves every other selected state, and has zero cycle debt. The inserted state th is not old because it joins the two distinct old residual components R_H and R_T. Suppose the deleted state d=x_{r-1}t were also not old. Then |T_H cap O|=|T cap O|, so T_H is overlap-maximal. If T_H is nonquiet, the branch has already reached an accepted physical output and no alignment conclusion is required. If T_H is quiet, moving t from target-tail position to target-head position reverses the endpoint-loss polarity assigned to the same old residual component R_H. The accepted Cross-Completion Opposite-Role Collision theorem then gives one of its productive outputs, contrary to the surviving branch hypothesis. Therefore d is old. Since t lies only on old R_H and the only old selected state entering t is its last boundary r t, x_{r-1}t=r t. The tail-side proof is exact dual: if x_{r-1} t h is tight, T_T=T-{h x_1}+{th}; if h x_1 were non-old, the same overlap/role-flip argument applies, so h x_1 is old, and uniqueness of the old state leaving h identifies h x_1=h s, the first boundary of R_T.

# R186 — Complement-free intersection-one spectral ceiling on 5-subsets of a 10-set

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Let Omega be a 10-set, let F be a family of 5-subsets containing no complementary pair, and let barF={Omega\\A:A in F}. In the Johnson graph J(10,5), where two 5-sets are adjacent when they intersect in four vertices, the number of edges between F and barF is at most 15|F|. Equivalently, the average number of four-overlap neighbors in barF seen from a member of F is at most 15.

## Hypotheses
Pure finite-set statement on 5-subsets of a 10-set; F contains no complementary pair.

## Scope
Order-free finite support combinatorics. Structural replacement for the earlier spectral formulation of the same ceiling.

## Applicability
Use when a longest-support family on ten vertices is complement-free and some local theorem forces many one-vertex replacements whose complements are four-overlap Johnson neighbors.

## Persistence
Pure set-theoretic counting; no representative dependence.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not use eigenvalues or association schemes. Does not bound arbitrary induced degrees in the intersection-one graph directly; the conversion through the complement family must be supplied by the application.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Parameter-specific 5-of-10 spectral ceiling is a historical proof-technology artifact rather than a versatile canonical lemma.
- **Curation note:** Parameter-specific 5-of-10 spectral ceiling is a historical proof-technology artifact rather than a versatile canonical lemma.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Valid structural replacement of the spectral ceiling via K6 clique counting.

## Proof
For each four-set C subset Omega, let K_C={C union {v}: v in Omega\\C}. This is a K_6 in J(10,5), and every Johnson edge belongs to exactly one such K_C, namely the clique indexed by the four-set intersection of its endpoints. Put r_C=|F intersect K_C| and s_C=|barF intersect K_C|. Since F contains no complementary pair, F and barF are disjoint, hence r_C+s_C<=6. The number of F--barF Johnson edges inside K_C is exactly r_C s_C. For nonnegative r,s with r+s<=6, rs <= (r+s)^2/4 <= (3/2)(r+s). Therefore

  e_J(F,barF)=sum_C r_C s_C <= (3/2) sum_C (r_C+s_C).

Each 5-set contains exactly five four-subsets, so each vertex of F lies in exactly five cliques K_C; likewise each vertex of barF. Hence sum_C r_C=5|F| and sum_C s_C=5|barF|=5|F|. Thus

  e_J(F,barF) <= (3/2)(10|F|)=15|F|.

This proves the ceiling.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/LEGACY/R186.md -->

# R192 — Five-exterior four-of-five replacement saturation

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Let H be a smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample and let K be a proper tight path whose exterior E=V(H)\\V(K) has exactly five vertices. Then K is globally longest. If E itself is not Hamiltonian, then for every k in V(K), at least four of the five sets (E\\{z}) union {k}, z in E, support tight five-vertex paths. Equivalently, for each carrier vertex k there is at most one exterior hole z for which the one-vertex exterior replacement E-z+k fails to support a P5.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample; K is a proper tight path with exactly five exterior vertices E. The nontrivial branch assumes E is not Hamiltonian, since otherwise K and E already form a spanning two-cover.

## Scope
Arbitrary order. Support-level amplification at the universal five-exterior floor; no order-ten, sign, payment, or exact-return hypothesis.

## Applicability
Use in any higher-order smallest-counterexample analysis once a proper path reaches the universal five-exterior floor. It produces a dense carrier-by-hole grid of exterior-side P5 replacements; a single complementary carrier-side replacement K-k+z would immediately give a spanning two-cover.

## Persistence
K, E, and all forced five-path supports are graph-intrinsic. The result is independent of representative changes.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert the complementary set (K\\{k}) union {z} is a tight path. Does not imply that the forced P5 is globally longest when |H|>10. Does not prove existence of a five-exterior path in every smallest counterexample.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** R192 is the five-exterior replacement-grid interface from an older exterior route. The route is no longer live; preserve the accepted theorem historically.
- **Curation note:** Strong arbitrary-order five-exterior replacement-saturation gateway with a dense carrier-by-hole P5 grid.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Valid arbitrary-order five-exterior four-of-five replacement saturation.

## Proof
Let E be the five-vertex exterior of K. By R23, K is globally longest. If E supports a tight five-path, then K and that path form a spanning two-cover, so in a smallest counterexample E is non-Hamiltonian. Fix k in K. For arbitrary distinct x,y in E, let P=E\\{x,y}. By R8, P has a tight trimer orientation. Apply R146 to this trimer and x,y,k. One of E, (E\\{y}) union {k}, (E\\{x}) union {k} supports a tight P5. The first is impossible, hence at least one of the two replacement supports is tight. Therefore no two distinct holes can both be failed replacement columns for the same k. Thus at most one z in E fails, and at least four of the five supports (E\\{z}) union {k} are tight P5 supports.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/LEGACY/R192.md -->

# R193 — Every six-set contains a tight five-path

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Every six-vertex subset W of a Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament contains a tight path on five of its vertices.

## Hypotheses
Strong Level-(1) boundary antisymmetry; W is any six-element vertex set.

## Scope
Order-free local path-density theorem.

## Applicability
Use in higher-order smallest-counterexample arguments whenever a residual or exterior set has at least six vertices. Every chosen six-subset already contains a P5, so exterior slack cannot be treated as path-poor. In particular, a longest-path exterior of size at least six contains a tight P5 wholly inside the exterior.

## Persistence
The resulting P5 support is graph-intrinsic on the chosen six vertices.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert a Hamilton P6 on the six-set, does not prescribe the omitted vertex, and does not by itself merge a larger exterior into one path.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** superseded
- **Lifecycle note:** Every six-set contains some P5 is strictly subsumed by C188/R195, which proves at least four of the six five-subsets are Hamiltonian. Keep R193 as a heavily used shorthand dependency, but canonical retrieval should expose the stronger density theorem.
- **Curation note:** Every six-set contains some P5 is strictly subsumed by C188/R195, which proves at least four of the six five-subsets are Hamiltonian. Keep R193 as a heavily used shorthand dependency, but canonical retrieval should expose the stronger density theorem.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Valid order-free six-set P5 density lemma.

## Proof
Partition W into any three-set P and complementary three-set {x,y,z}. By R8, P has a tight trimer orientation. R146 applied to that fixed tight trimer and x,y,z yields a tight five-path on P together with one of the three exterior pairs. Hence W contains a tight P5.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/LEGACY/R193.md -->

# R194 — Five-exterior internal replacement forces balanced-pair birth

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Let H be a smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample and let K be a proper tight path with exactly five exterior vertices E. Assume E is non-Hamiltonian. Fix an internal vertex k of K. Then for at least four vertices z in E, the five-set Q=(E\\{z}) union {k} supports a tight P5, and for each such z the complementary subsystem W=V(H)\\Q=(V(K)\\{k}) union {z} admits both a literal three-cover by the two nonempty path intervals of K-k together with singleton z and an exact two-cover. Consequently R159 yields a graph-intrinsic balanced opposite-sign pair in H for each such replacement frame.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample; K is a proper tight path with exactly five exterior vertices E; E is non-Hamiltonian; k is not an endpoint of K.

## Scope
Arbitrary order. Bridge from five-exterior replacement saturation to the generic component-drop signed-pair machinery.

## Applicability
Use in the five-exterior equality face of a higher-order smallest counterexample. Every internal carrier vertex supplies at least four punctured complement frames in which a 3-to-2 path-cover component drop produces a balanced opposite-sign pair. This is a scalable entry to R171/R172-style historical-pair descent.

## Persistence
The forced P5 supports and balanced-pair existence are graph-intrinsic. The particular exact two-cover of each punctured complement is representative-relative.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not identify or synchronize the balanced pairs obtained from different z or k. Does not say the pair supports are the two carrier intervals or the singleton. Does not itself put the pair into a literal spanning three-cover required by R171, and does not close the five-exterior face.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Five-exterior internal replacement to balanced-pair birth is a specialized zero-consumer bridge; inline conceptually if reused.
- **Curation note:** Five-exterior internal replacement to balanced-pair birth is a specialized zero-consumer bridge; inline conceptually if reused.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Valid five-exterior internal replacement component-drop balanced-pair gateway.

## Proof
As in the five-exterior saturation proof, E cannot be Hamiltonian. Fix internal k. For any two holes x,y in E, R8 orients E\\{x,y} as a tight trimer and R146 forces one of E, E-y+k, E-x+k to support a P5; E is impossible, so at most one replacement hole fails. Thus at least four z give a tight P5 Q=(E\\{z}) union {k}. Fix such z. The complement W is (K\\{k}) union {z}. Writing K=(K_L,k,K_R), both K_L and K_R are nonempty tight path intervals, hence K_L sqcup K_R sqcup (z) is a literal 3-cover of W. By R4, the complement of the proper tight path Q has an exact 2-cover. Since W is proper, R159 applies to these 3- and 2-covers and yields a graph-intrinsic balanced opposite-sign pair in H.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/LEGACY/R194.md -->

# R196 — Six-exterior four-root puncture pair fan

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Let H be a smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample and let K be a tight path with six-vertex exterior E. Then for at least four vertices e in E there is a tight P5 Q_e on E-{e}, so H=K sqcup Q_e sqcup {e} is a literal spanning three-cover and H-{e}=K sqcup Q_e is a literal exact two-cover. Moreover, for every internal vertex k of K and every such e, the proper subsystem W=(V(K)-{k}) union {e} has a literal three-cover by the two K-k intervals and singleton e, while minimality supplies a cover with at most two components; hence R159 yields a graph-intrinsic balanced opposite-sign pair.

## Hypotheses
H is a smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample; K is a tight path; E=V(H)\\V(K) has size six; k is internal when the puncture conclusion is invoked.

## Scope
Arbitrary-order six-exterior root fan and component-drop entry. No order-ten support geometry, sign synchronization, or payment is used.

## Applicability
Use in the exterior-slack-one face. It supplies at least four singleton roots retaining the same K and a balanced-pair birth for every internal carrier puncture in every such root.

## Persistence
The P5 supports Q_e and existence of the balanced pairs are graph-intrinsic. The lower-component recompletion of each punctured subsystem is existential and representative-relative.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not identify or synchronize the balanced pairs across e or k; does not assert the balanced pair is selected in the displayed three-cover; does not itself force a spanning two-cover or a five-exterior path.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** R196 is the six-exterior singleton-root fan from an older exterior-slack route. No live consumer remains.
- **Curation note:** Six-exterior gateway with multiple literal singleton roots and component-drop pair births; still consumed by several active branches.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Valid six-exterior four-root puncture pair fan; proof exactness is supplied explicitly through adjusted P196 and R22.

## Proof
Define M={e∈E:E\{e} supports a tight P5}. For every three-subset T⊂E, orient E\T as a tight trimer by R8. R146 applied to that trimer and the three vertices T shows M∩T≠∅. Hence |E\M|≤2 and |M|≥4. Fix e∈M and choose a tight P5 Q_e on E\{e}. Since E is exactly the exterior of K, the three disjoint tight paths K,Q_e,{e} partition V(H). Because H is a smallest counterexample, pc(H)=3 by R4, so this displayed three-cover is minimum. Componentwise exact re-rooting R22 therefore gives K⊔Q_e as an exact two-cover of H-{e}. Now let k be internal on K. In W=(V(K)\{k})∪{e}, the two nonempty intervals of K-k together with singleton e form a literal 3-cover. W is proper because Q_e and k are omitted. By R4, H[W] has a path cover with at most two components. Applying R159 to the literal 3-cover and a lower-component cover yields a graph-intrinsic balanced opposite-sign pair. This holds for every internal k and every e∈M.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/LEGACY/R196.md -->
