# R197 — Global-longest terminal-dimer universal adaptive-capture gateway

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Let H be a smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample and let K=(k0,...,km), m>=2, be a proper global-longest tight path with exterior E=V(H)\\V(K). For the left terminal physical dimer D_L={k0,k1}, the orientation (k1,k0) is tail-signed by every e in E; for the right terminal dimer D_R={k_{m-1},k_m}, the orientation (k_m,k_{m-1}) is head-signed by every e in E. Fix either terminal dimer D. In every exact two-cover of H-D, the Puncture Crossing Parent supplies a selected crossing from the nonempty surviving carrier K-D to E. Every such selected crossing is witness-adaptively capture-capable: one may choose an exterior sign witness avoiding the crossing and then choose either physical endpoint of the crossing to capture. The same-frame capture carries aligned refund ancestry, so the chosen channel enters the accepted aligned-dimer payment lineage, yielding either a spanning two-cover or a singleton-width paid descendant with the capture/refund ancestry retained.

## Hypotheses
H is a smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample; K is a proper globally longest tight path of order at least three.

## Scope
Order-free longest-path terminal gateway. No order-ten, five-exterior equality, six-exterior density, payment synchronization, or CW-freeness is used.

## Applicability
Use at either end of any globally longest path before opening specialized exterior-slack casework. It removes the capture/concentration alternative from terminal-dimer puncture frames and provides an aligned paid lineage tied to an actual selected carrier/exterior crossing.

## Persistence
The reverse terminal signs are graph-intrinsic. The crossing is current only in its chosen exact D-deletion cover. Capture, refund, and paid descendants belong to the chosen lineage and retain historical ancestry, not simultaneous currentness across different choices.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not prescribe which carrier/exterior crossing occurs, does not make all crossing choices simultaneous, does not prescribe which singleton survives the generic aligned payment, does not assert exterior-size descent, and does not itself close the conjecture.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** R197 is a nonreconstructible global-longest adaptive-capture gateway with no live consumers; capture production is no longer a frontier.
- **Curation note:** Strong order-free global-longest terminal gateway: every terminal puncture yields witness-adaptive capture and an aligned paid lineage tied to an actual selected crossing.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Valid global-longest terminal-dimer adaptive-capture gateway within the stated lineage-relative exclusions.

## Proof
Fix a terminal dimer D of the proper globally longest tight path K=(k_0,...,k_m), m>=2. Accepted R199 gives the required graph-intrinsic reverse sign on D from every exterior vertex e in E=V(H)-V(K): at the left end (k_1,k_0,e) is tight for every e, and at the right end (e,k_m,k_{m-1}) is tight for every e.\n\nFirst note that |E|>=2 without R169. Since K is proper, E is nonempty. If E={e} were a singleton, then K together with the singleton path (e) would be a spanning two-path cover of H, contradicting pc(H)>2. Thus E contains at least two vertices.\n\nBy accepted Pair-Deletion Rigidity R429, H-V(D) has an exact two-cover T=U sqcup V with both rails nontrivial. Put S=V(K)-V(D). Because m>=2, S is nonempty; because E is nonempty, S is a proper subset of W=V(H)-V(D). The original path K is a tight path spanning exactly V(D) union S. Therefore accepted R508, with deletion V(D), absorbable block S, carrier K, and the fixed cover T, forces a selected T-state xy crossing S | E. Exactly one endpoint of xy lies in E; call it e_xy.\n\nChoose w in E-{e_xy}, possible because |E|>=2. The R199 reverse terminal turn with witness w signs D in the required tested orientation, and the selected carrier/exterior crossing xy avoids w. Apply accepted R527 to the retained carrier K, signed support D, witness w, and the same exact deletion cover T. Its capture/refund branch applies to xy. By choosing the marker orientation, either physical endpoint of xy may be designated as the captured signed anchor, exactly as required in R197. R527 retains the original selected crossing, chosen marker orientation, capture event, and refund ancestry as historical certificate data.\n\nFinally D has order two and H is a hypothetical smallest counterexample, so the dimer payment clause of R527 applies: along the chosen certificate-retaining continuation, either H acquires a spanning two-cover or the lineage reaches singleton width, with the capture/refund ancestry retained. This proves every clause of R197. The only cardinality used is |E|>=2, derived directly from pc(H)>2; the quarantined five-exterior floor R169, and hence R5/R24, never enter.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/LEGACY/R197.md -->

# R199 — Global-longest universal exterior endpoint shield

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Let K=(k_1,...,k_m) be a globally longest tight path in a Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament. For every vertex w outside K, the direct endpoint attachment turns (w,k_1,k_2) and (k_{m-1},k_m,w) are bad. Hence by boundary antisymmetry the reverse endpoint turns (k_2,k_1,w) and (w,k_m,k_{m-1}) are tight. Thus every exterior vertex simultaneously witnesses both terminal reverse systems of K as graph-intrinsic facts.

## Hypotheses
Strong Level-(1) boundary antisymmetry; K is a globally longest tight path; w is exterior to K.

## Scope
Order-free graph-intrinsic endpoint shielding for globally longest paths.

## Applicability
Use whenever several exact roots or exterior cells retain one globally longest path K. All exterior vertices can be treated as common witnesses to both terminal reverse systems without any representative synchronization.

## Persistence
The bad direct attachments and tight reverse turns are graph-intrinsic relative to the fixed ordering of K and survive representative changes.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert any exterior vertex attaches internally, does not join two exterior witnesses, and does not by itself produce a longer path, exact cover, sign currentization, or payment descendant.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Global-longest exterior endpoint shielding is an immediate maximality-plus-boundary-antisymmetry observation. Despite several consumers, it is proof shorthand rather than independent mathematics; inline the two-line argument conceptually.
- **Curation note:** Global-longest exterior endpoint shielding is an immediate maximality-plus-boundary-antisymmetry observation. Despite several consumers, it is proof shorthand rather than independent mathematics; inline the two-line argument conceptually.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Valid global-longest universal exterior endpoint shield.

## Proof
Fix w outside K=(k_1,...,k_m). If (w,k_1,k_2) were tight, then (w,k_1,...,k_m) would be a tight path of order m+1, contradicting global longestness of K. Therefore (w,k_1,k_2) is bad, and R3 makes its complete reversal (k_2,k_1,w) tight. Likewise, if (k_{m-1},k_m,w) were tight then (k_1,...,k_m,w) would extend K, so this direct turn is bad and R3 makes (w,k_m,k_{m-1}) tight. The argument is independent for every exterior w, so all asserted reverse turns hold simultaneously as graph-intrinsic facts.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/LEGACY/R199.md -->

# R201 — Six-exterior singleton-root maximin applicability fence

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
In the six-exterior four-root setting, the literal singleton roots K sqcup Q_e obtained by componentwise exact re-rooting are not presently licensed as maximin singleton-root source frames. Therefore the accepted Canonical splice sign trichotomy R26 cannot be applied to those literal roots merely from exactness, common retention of K, or short-rail order five. An additional theorem preserving the prescribed rail K under maximin singleton-root normalization, or another direct consumer of the literal roots, is required.

## Hypotheses
Accepted contracts R22 and R26; six-exterior investigation in which literal exact singleton roots retain one prescribed rail K.

## Scope
Applicability fence for the arbitrary-order six-exterior program.

## Applicability
Use to prevent importing the order-five forced-both-bad face of R26 into an arbitrary literal singleton root without proving the maximin hypothesis. The natural archive task is to locate or reconstruct a prescribed-rail maximinization theorem.

## Persistence
Methodological scope fence; no representative-relative mathematical state is asserted.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert that no such prescribed-rail maximin theorem exists; only that none is currently accepted/indexed under the searched contracts and R22 does not supply it.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Historical six-exterior maximin applicability fence; the exterior route is no longer active.
- **Curation note:** Applicability correction preventing maximin splice machinery from being used on arbitrary singleton roots.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Valid scope correction preventing illicit use of maximin singleton-root machinery on arbitrary literal six-exterior roots.

## Proof
R22 states that deleting the singleton from a displayed minimum three-cover leaves the other two paths as an exact two-cover in the same representative. R26, by contrast, is explicitly scoped to an imbalanced maximin singleton-root frame. No clause of R22 promotes an arbitrary exact singleton root to maximin, and no accepted claim located in the targeted theorem-bank search supplies maximinization while retaining a prescribed rail K literally. Hence R26 is not a lawful consumer of the six-exterior literal roots without an additional bridge theorem.

# R202 — Global-longest carrier endpoint balanced-pair refund

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Let H be a smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample and let K=(k_1,...,k_m), m>=4, be a proper globally longest tight path with nonempty exterior E. For every w in E, the left terminal physical dimer D_L={k_1,k_2}, oriented (k_2,k_1), and the right terminal physical dimer D_R={k_{m-1},k_m}, oriented (k_m,k_{m-1}), are disjoint signed supports of opposite polarity with the same exterior witness w. Hence they form a direct mass-four balanced pair. Moreover, because both supports lie in the single tight carrier K, the Multi-Support Adjacent-Color Refund may be realized using the contiguous middle interval of K from k_2 through k_{m-1}; this interval meets D_L and D_R in exactly one vertex each. Signed-Interval Rebirth therefore leaves two nonempty signed descendants supported exactly on the outer endpoint singletons {k_1} and {k_m}. These descendants retain the respective opposite polarities, so K canonically carries an endpoint-aligned mass-two balanced-pair ancestry on its two physical endpoints before any unrelated representative reset.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample; K is a proper globally longest tight path of order at least four; E=V(H)\\V(K) is nonempty.

## Scope
Order-free carrier-specific composition of the universal exterior endpoint shield with direct balanced-pair and adjacent-color refund machinery.

## Applicability
Use in the five- or six-exterior O3 faces to obtain a balanced-pair ancestry tied to the physical endpoints of the chosen longest carrier K, rather than an anonymous pair born in a punctured recompletion. This may be combined with later capture/currentization or fixed-turn machinery, subject to their representative hypotheses.

## Persistence
K, its terminal physical dimers, the exterior reverse-sign certificates, and the identity of the outer endpoint singleton descendants are graph-intrinsic/historical. Witness names may change under Signed-Interval Rebirth. No later current selection is asserted.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert that the endpoint singleton pair is simultaneously current with K or with any exterior P5/singleton root; does not produce a literal R171 three-cover; does not preserve the original common witness w after rebirth; does not by itself force exterior-slack descent or a spanning two-cover.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Global-longest carrier endpoint balanced-pair refund is a zero-consumer carrier-specific composition of endpoint signs, direct pair birth, and adjacent-color refund; preserve historically but remove from canonical surface.
- **Curation note:** Global-longest carrier endpoint balanced-pair refund is a zero-consumer carrier-specific composition of endpoint signs, direct pair birth, and adjacent-color refund; preserve historically but remove from canonical surface.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Verified in exact historical scope. Any proper globally longest carrier of order at least four with nonempty exterior canonically yields an endpoint-aligned mass-two balanced-pair ancestry on its two physical endpoints. No simultaneous currentness or exterior-slack descent is inferred.

## Proof
Fix w in E. By R199, (k_2,k_1,w) is tight and gives the left terminal dimer D_L={k_1,k_2} its tail-facing sign, while (w,k_m,k_{m-1}) is tight and gives the right terminal dimer D_R={k_{m-1},k_m} its head-facing sign. These polarities are opposite. Since m>=4, D_L and D_R are vertex-disjoint and have total support size four, so R39 makes them a direct balanced pair. Both nontrivial signed supports lie in the one tight carrier K. Apply R174 to this two-support family. Along K, the support-colored vertices occur first in D_L and later in D_R. Taking the contiguous interval C=(k_2,...,k_{m-1}) meets D_L only in k_2 and D_R only in k_{m-1}. R174/Signed-Interval Rebirth therefore deletes one support vertex from each without swallowing either support. Because each original support has order two, the surviving signed descendants are exactly the singletons {k_1} and {k_m}. Rebirth retains each support as a signed descendant (though its witness name may change), so the two descendants retain the opposite polarities inherited from D_L and D_R. Thus the resulting historical pair has total mass two and is canonically aligned with the two physical endpoints of K. No claim of simultaneous currentness with K or any exterior root is made.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/LEGACY/R202.md -->

# R203 — Five-exterior common-hole synchronization

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Assume the five-exterior non-Hamiltonian equality face of R192. For any t distinct carrier vertices k_1,...,k_t in V(K), with 1 <= t <= 4, there are at least 5-t exterior vertices z in E such that every one of the t five-sets (E\\{z}) union {k_i} supports a tight P5. In particular, any four prescribed carrier vertices have a common exterior omission z for which the same exterior four-set E\\{z} completes to a tight P5 with each of the four carrier vertices. Hence every consecutive four-window of K admits such a common omission.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample; K is a proper tight path with exactly five exterior vertices E; E is non-Hamiltonian; accepted R192.

## Scope
Arbitrary order. Pure support-incidence corollary of the R192 four-of-five row saturation.

## Applicability
Use to synchronize several carrier rows before invoking orientation-sensitive or ancestry-sensitive machinery. The four-window specialization gives one fixed exterior four-set with four separate carrier completions.

## Persistence
The successful replacement supports are graph-intrinsic. The common omission z is a physical exterior vertex chosen from the fixed E.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not synchronize the P5 orderings on the common five-supports, does not assert any complementary carrier replacement K-k_i+z is tight, and does not itself give a spanning two-cover.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Common-hole synchronization is an immediate support-incidence counting corollary of the four-of-five row saturation. Zero consumers and no orientation/ancestry synchronization; keep inside proof text/history rather than active surface.
- **Curation note:** Common-hole synchronization is an immediate support-incidence counting corollary of the four-of-five row saturation. Zero consumers and no orientation/ancestry synchronization; keep inside proof text/history rather than active surface.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Accepted common-hole synchronization corollary of R192.

## Proof
For a carrier vertex k let F_k be the set of exterior holes z in E for which (E\\{z}) union {k} does not support a tight P5. R192 gives |F_k|<=1. For distinct k_1,...,k_t, a hole z is simultaneously successful for all t rows exactly when z lies in E\\(F_{k_1} union ... union F_{k_t}). The union of the t failure sets has size at most t, so the common success set has size at least |E|-t=5-t. For t=4 this is nonempty. Choosing the four vertices to be any consecutive four-window of K gives the final specialization.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/LEGACY/R203.md -->

# R206 — Four-row common-hole synchronization does not force the local carrier replacement

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
There exists a nine-vertex Level-(1) boundary-antisymmetric turn system with a tight four-path Q=(q0,q1,q2,q3), a five-set E=F union {z} with |F|=4, such that E is non-Hamiltonian, every five-set F union {q_i} supports a tight P5 for i=0,1,2,3, but Q union {z} is non-Hamiltonian. Hence even perfect four-row synchronization on one common exterior four-set, together with a literal tight carrier P4, does not by itself force the most local omitted-vertex carrier-side P5.

## Hypotheses
Only Level-(1) boundary antisymmetry is used. This is a local turn-system countermodel, not a smallest-counterexample model and not a model of the full five-exterior equality face.

## Scope
Local negative result for the five-exterior common-hole strategy.

## Applicability
Use as a proof-design fence after four-row common-hole synchronization: a closure must exploit additional information such as the actual orderings/ancestry of the exterior-side P5s, exact-cover incidence, signs, or longer-carrier context. Bare support Hamiltonicity of the four completions is insufficient.

## Persistence
The countermodel is a fixed graph-intrinsic turn table on nine labeled vertices.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not show that the full R192 equality-face hypotheses are realizable without a complementary replacement. Does not refute a theorem using the entire carrier K, smallest-counterexample minimality, or synchronized P5 orderings.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Historical common-hole local synchronization countermodel; no live use remains.
- **Curation note:** Explicit local countermodel: four-row common-hole synchronization plus a carrier P4 does not force the omitted-vertex carrier P5.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Accepted local countermodel showing four-row common-hole support synchronization alone does not force Q+z Hamiltonian.

## Proof
Use vertices Q={0,1,2,3}, F={4,5,6,7}, z=8. For each unordered triple i<j<k, use the three reversal pairs A: (i,j,k)/(k,j,i), B: (i,k,j)/(j,k,i), C: (j,i,k)/(k,i,j). By default declare the canonical A/B/C order bad and its complete reversal tight. Reverse that choice, declaring the canonical order tight, exactly for the following 31 canonical orders: 012,021,031,108,023,032,203,028,208,038,308,123,132,182,138,183,283,275,527,546,457,547,458,485,486,567,657,568,658,758,768. This specifies exactly one tight member of every reversal pair and therefore satisfies boundary antisymmetry. In this table Q=(0,1,2,3) is tight. The four supports F+q_i have respectively the following explicit tight P5 orderings: for q0, (5,7,4,6,0); for q1, (6,5,7,1,4); for q2, (6,7,5,2,4); for q3, (6,5,7,4,3). A direct finite check of all 120 vertex orders on E={4,5,6,7,8} finds no tight P5, and the same check on Q+z={0,1,2,3,8} finds no tight P5. For a compact independent encoding, listing the A,B,C truth bits in lexicographic order of unordered triples gives the 252-bit hexadecimal signature c8000f000a00140000000c0008003000000000008000300000000000dc10b49, with 1 meaning the canonical order is tight. Thus all asserted positive and negative Hamiltonicity claims are exactly reconstructible from the displayed turn table.

# R207 — Five-exterior replacement grid forces an exterior-dimer two-witness interaction

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Assume the non-Hamiltonian five-exterior equality face of R192 and suppose the carrier K has at least six vertices. Then some physical dimer D contained in E carries signed certificates with two distinct carrier witnesses k,kprime in V(K), arising from two of the R192 replacement P5s. Consequently R38 forces a genuine same-support two-witness interaction on D: either the two certificates have the same polarity and enter the accepted two-extension collision package, or they have opposite polarities and enter same-support exclusivity, yielding the accepted strict two-ended signed-path interaction. In particular, after R191 excludes order ten, every surviving O3 five-exterior equality face has such an interaction.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample; K is a proper tight path with five-vertex exterior E; E is non-Hamiltonian; accepted R192; |K|>=6. Signed terminal dimers of tight trimers are interpreted as in accepted R41/R38.

## Scope
Arbitrary-order cross-side coupling theorem for the five-exterior replacement grid. It uses one unit of ordering information from each successful P5, beyond bare support incidence.

## Applicability
Use as the canonical next consumer of R192 in the equality face. It replaces the unsupported hope of complementary carrier replacement by a forced graph-intrinsic exterior-dimer interaction with two distinct carrier witnesses. Downstream work may feed that interaction into capture, restoration, or fixed-turn machinery.

## Persistence
The physical exterior dimer D, the two distinct carrier witnesses, and their tested signed orders are graph-intrinsic historical certificates. The several replacement P5 representatives need not be simultaneously current.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not identify D or the two witnesses in advance; does not prescribe whether their polarities agree; does not itself produce K-k+z, exterior-size descent, or a spanning two-cover; does not assert simultaneous currentness of the two replacement P5s.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Five-exterior replacement-grid interaction lemma is a specialized zero-consumer consumer; preserve historical proof but retire claim identity.
- **Curation note:** Five-exterior replacement-grid interaction lemma is a specialized zero-consumer consumer; preserve historical proof but retire claim identity.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Accepted forced exterior-dimer two-witness interaction in every post-R191 five-exterior equality face.

## Proof
Fix k in K. By R192 there are at least four distinct holes z in E for which S_{k,z}=(E\\{z}) union {k} supports a tight P5. For each such z choose one tight ordering of S_{k,z}. In any five-vertex ordering containing exactly one special vertex k and four vertices of E\\{z}, at least one consecutive tight trimer has k at one end and two vertices of E\\{z} in the other two positions: if k is in position 1 use turn 1-3; in position 2 use turn 2-4; in position 3 use turn 1-3 or 3-5; in position 4 use turn 2-4; in position 5 use turn 3-5. By the tight-trimer signed-terminal convention recorded in R41, the physical dimer formed by those two exterior vertices carries a signed certificate with witness k. Choose one such dimer D_{k,z} subset E\\{z}. For a fixed physical dimer D subset E, D can equal D_{k,z} only when z is not in D. Since |E|=5 and |D|=2, there are only three holes z outside D. Therefore one physical dimer can account for at most three of the at least four successful holes in a fixed k-row. Hence the set A_k={D_{k,z}: z successful} contains at least two distinct physical dimers. Suppose for contradiction that no physical exterior dimer carries certificates with two distinct carrier witnesses. Then the sets A_k are pairwise disjoint as k varies. If |K|>=6 this would require at least 2|K|>=12 distinct physical dimers inside E, but E has only C(5,2)=10. Contradiction. Thus some D lies in A_k intersect A_kprime for distinct k,kprime. The two signed certificates on the same physical support have distinct witnesses, so R38 gives exactly the stated same-polarity collision or opposite-polarity strict interaction. Finally, in the post-R191 O3 equality face H has order greater than ten and |E|=5, so |K|=|H|-5>=6.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/LEGACY/R207.md -->

# R208 — Six-exterior singleton-root common-witness terminal-dimer rectangle

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Let H be a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample, let K=(k_1,...,k_m), m>=5, be a proper global-longest tight path with six-vertex exterior E, and let e be any R196 omission for which Q_e=(q_1,...,q_5) is a tight P5 on E\\{e}. Then the four reverse terminal dimers D_K^L=(k_2,k_1), D_K^R=(k_m,k_{m-1}), D_Q^L=(q_2,q_1), D_Q^R=(q_5,q_4) are all signed by the same physical witness e. The two left dimers have one common polarity and the two right dimers the opposite polarity. Hence every left dimer forms a direct mass-four balanced pair with every right dimer, giving a 2-by-2 common-witness rectangle of pair births that includes both cross-rail pairs D_K^L with D_Q^R and D_Q^L with D_K^R. R196 supplies at least four distinct singleton roots carrying such a rectangle.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest counterexample; K is proper and global-longest with |E|=6; e is one of the at least four omissions supplied by accepted R196; Q_e is a chosen tight ordering of E\\{e}. Boundary antisymmetry R3, signed terminal-dimer convention R41, and direct balanced-pair theorem R39 are available.

## Scope
Order-free, root-specific coupling in the six-exterior slack-one face. No maximin singleton-root normalization, payment synchronization, or order-ten geometry is used.

## Applicability
Use instead of anonymous puncture-pair births when a literal R196 root is available. It ties graph-intrinsic signed supports simultaneously to the terminal geometry of the retained global-longest carrier and the exterior P5, providing cross-rail pair choices for capture/refund/fixed-turn descendants.

## Persistence
The four physical terminal dimers, common witness e, tested reverse turns, and polarity rectangle are graph-intrinsic. The literal root K sqcup Q_e sqcup {e} is a separate current representative for the chosen e.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not say any of the four dimer supports are separate current cover components, does not put a cross pair directly into the literal three-component form required by R171, does not synchronize rectangles for different e in one representative, and does not itself force exterior-size descent or a spanning two-cover.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Six-exterior common-witness terminal-dimer rectangle is a specialized root corollary; its only downstream payment specialization has already been retired. Preserve the rectangle historically rather than as an active peer to general pair machinery.
- **Curation note:** Six-exterior common-witness terminal-dimer rectangle is a specialized root corollary; its only downstream payment specialization has already been retired. Preserve the rectangle historically rather than as an active peer to general pair machinery.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Accepted six-exterior singleton-root common-witness terminal-dimer rectangle.

## Proof
Fix an R196 root H=K sqcup Q_e sqcup {e}. Since K is global-longest, neither (e,k_1,k_2) nor (k_{m-1},k_m,e) can be tight, because either would extend K to a longer tight path. R3 therefore gives (k_2,k_1,e) and (e,k_m,k_{m-1}) tight. Thus D_K^L and D_K^R are signed by witness e with opposite terminal polarities. Next E itself cannot support a tight P6: if it did, that P6 together with the disjoint tight path K would be a spanning two-cover of H. Therefore, in the chosen ordering Q_e=(q_1,...,q_5), neither (e,q_1,q_2) nor (q_4,q_5,e) can be tight, since either would extend Q_e to a tight P6 on all of E. R3 gives (q_2,q_1,e) and (e,q_5,q_4) tight. Hence D_Q^L and D_Q^R are likewise signed by e with opposite terminal polarities. The left reverse turns have the same witness placement pattern, as do the right reverse turns, so D_K^L and D_Q^L have the same polarity, while D_K^R and D_Q^R have the opposite polarity. All carrier dimers are disjoint from all exterior dimers; m>=5 makes D_K^L,D_K^R disjoint, and the order-five Q_e makes D_Q^L,D_Q^R disjoint. By R39 every left/right choice is therefore a direct balanced pair of total support size four. R196 provides at least four choices of e with Q_e, yielding at least four such root-specific rectangles.

# R209 — Six-exterior singleton roots carry double endpoint-floor ancestry

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
In the O3 six-exterior slack-one face, fix any R196 singleton root H=K sqcup Q_e sqcup {e}, with K=(k_1,...,k_m) global-longest and Q_e=(q_1,...,q_5) a tight exterior P5. Then the root carries two separate graph-intrinsic ancestry-bearing mass-two balanced-pair certificates: one supported on the carrier endpoint singletons {k_1},{k_m}, supplied by R202, and one supported on the exterior-P5 endpoint singletons {q_1},{q_5}. Thus every such root has a canonical four-physical-endpoint double-floor ancestry on the two rail endpoint pairs.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample; K is proper global-longest with six-vertex exterior E; e is an R196 Hamiltonian omission; Q_e is a chosen tight P5 ordering on E\\{e}; accepted R202 and Multi-Support Adjacent-Color Refund R174.

## Scope
Historical ancestry compression of one literal six-exterior singleton root. The two mass-two floors are separate descendants/certificates, not asserted simultaneously current.

## Applicability
Use to reduce six-exterior root analysis to interactions among the four physical rail endpoints. Any future synchronization theorem need only couple the two endpoint-floor ancestries or couple one of them to the retained singleton witness e.

## Persistence
The four physical rail endpoints and the existence/polarities of their signed singleton descendants are historical graph-intrinsic ancestry data. Witness names may change under rebirth.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert the two floor pairs occur in one representative, does not give a literal R171 frame containing both pairs, does not identify reborn witnesses across the two rails, and does not itself force a two-cover or exterior-size descent.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Six-exterior singleton-root double endpoint-floor ancestry is a clean but specialized corollary with no live consumers. Preserve the four-endpoint ancestry result historically; ordinary search should emphasize broader pair/floor parents.
- **Curation note:** Six-exterior singleton-root double endpoint-floor ancestry is a clean but specialized corollary with no live consumers. Preserve the four-endpoint ancestry result historically; ordinary search should emphasize broader pair/floor parents.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Accepted double endpoint-floor ancestry for each six-exterior singleton root; the two floor descendants are historical and not asserted simultaneously current.

## Proof
The carrier endpoint-floor ancestry on {k_1},{k_m} is exactly R202. For Q_e, first note that E cannot support a tight P6, since K is disjoint from E and K sqcup E would then be a spanning two-cover. Hence in Q_e=(q_1,...,q_5) both direct attachments (e,q_1,q_2) and (q_4,q_5,e) are bad. Boundary antisymmetry gives (q_2,q_1,e) and (e,q_5,q_4) tight, so the disjoint terminal physical dimers {q_1,q_2} and {q_4,q_5} are signed by e with opposite polarities and form a direct balanced pair by R39. Both signed supports lie in the single tight carrier Q_e. The contiguous middle interval C=(q_2,q_3,q_4) meets the left terminal dimer in exactly q_2 and the right terminal dimer in exactly q_4. Applying the adjacent-color refund / Signed-Interval Rebirth mechanism R174 to this interval leaves nonempty signed descendants supported exactly on the untouched outer endpoint singletons {q_1} and {q_5}; their opposite polarities are retained. Thus Q_e has an endpoint-aligned mass-two pair ancestry. Together with the independent R202 ancestry on the endpoints of K, the chosen singleton root carries the stated double endpoint-floor ancestry. The two refund descendants need not be current simultaneously.

# R210 — Global-longest terminal capture-to-interaction funnel

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Let H be a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample and K a proper globally longest tight path of order at least three. Fix either terminal physical dimer D of K. Then, unless a spanning two-cover already occurs, one may choose an exact two-cover of H-D, obtain a selected surviving-carrier/exterior crossing, choose a fresh exterior sign witness avoiding that crossing, and capture either physical endpoint of the crossing in the same frame. The captured-middle mirror-turn mechanism then produces a proper tight turn J whose middle is that freshly captured vertex and enters a chosen fixed-turn lineage. Along that lineage only finitely many quiet fixed-turn episodes can occur before a graph-intrinsic historical pair/contact interaction is forced.

## Hypotheses
H is a smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample; K is a proper globally longest tight path of order at least three; one terminal dimer is chosen.

## Scope
Order-free compression from a global-longest terminal dimer to the historical-interaction frontier. No exterior-slack, order-ten, five-exterior, six-exterior, or simultaneous-currentness hypothesis.

## Applicability
Use before specialized exterior-slack casework when it is enough to reduce the problem to an explicit historical pair/contact interaction. It shows that terminal adaptive capture is not a dead-end local resource: it has a lawful fixed-turn continuation to interaction.

## Persistence
The terminal signs and resulting proper turn are graph-intrinsic; capture and the fixed-turn continuation are lineage-relative. The eventual interaction is historical. The original exact deletion cover and crossing need not remain current.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert that the eventual interaction is itself a spanning two-cover, does not localize the first interaction at the captured middle, does not preserve the original crossing or complement rails, does not give exterior-size descent, and does not close O3 by itself.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** R210 is a global-longest capture-to-interaction funnel whose terminal currency is the now-saturated contact/interaction frontier; no live consumers remain.
- **Curation note:** Global-longest capture-to-interaction funnel remains reusable but is not on the current canonical proof backbone.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Accepted terminal capture-to-interaction funnel in stated lineage-relative scope.

## Proof
Fix the chosen terminal dimer of the globally longest path K and assume no spanning two-cover occurs. Accepted R197 supplies an exact deletion two-cover with a selected crossing between the surviving carrier K-D and the exterior, an exterior sign witness avoiding that crossing, and capture capability for either physical endpoint. Choose the carrier endpoint x of the crossing and capture x. The other crossing endpoint y lies outside K. Because x lies on the historical path K of order at least three, it has a genuine historical carrier adjacency {p,x} in K. Apply R155 to the historical carrier K, crossing {x,y}, capture event at x, and adjacency {p,x}. R155 gives a later minimum three-cover containing the unique tight mirror trimer J on {p,x,y}, with x as its middle and with the capture retained as ancestry. This J is proper because K itself is proper and leaves at least the exterior vertices. Meanwhile the nonclosing R197 payment lineage supplies an ancestry-bearing balanced pair with one singleton support. If the opposite support is nontrivial, apply R428 to reach a both-singleton floor while preserving the existing capture/refund ancestry; if it is already singleton, we are already at such a floor. Apply R432 to steer this same ancestry-bearing floor to the unordered outer pair of J, retaining the incoming capture/refund ledger. We may now enter the R172 pair-bearing lineage for this fixed graph-intrinsic turn J. R172 gives a strictly decreasing nonnegative lexicographic rank on every quiet nonclosing nonexit macro step, so only finitely many such quiet episodes can occur. Since the standing branch excludes a spanning two-cover, eventual failure of quiet continuation is one of R172s explicit historical pair/contact exits. Thus the terminal crossing, fresh capture at its carrier endpoint, captured-middle mirror turn, and finite fixed-turn continuation to historical interaction all follow with exactly the lineage-relative persistence and no same-representative transport claimed by R210.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/LEGACY/R210.md -->

# R211 — Six-exterior carrier-by-exterior central-anchor interaction grid

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Let H be a smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample and let K be a tight path with six-vertex exterior E. Then there exists a subset U of E with |U| at least four such that for every internal vertex b of K and every q in U, H carries a graph-intrinsic synchronized central-anchor interaction with anchor pair {b,q} in the sense of R41. More concretely, for each q in U there is a good omission e and a tight P5 order Q_e on E-{e} in which q is an internal vertex; the consecutive trimer window of K centered at b and the consecutive trimer window of Q_e centered at q are disjoint tight trimers, hence R41 supplies two direct mass-four pair births with the same unordered middle-anchor pair {b,q}.

## Hypotheses
H is a smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample; K is a tight path; E=V(H)\\V(K) has size six. The interaction conclusion is asserted for internal vertices of K.

## Scope
Arbitrary-order six-exterior interaction localization. No order-ten support geometry, maximin singleton-root hypothesis, pair currentization, or payment synchronization is used.

## Applicability
Use in the exterior-slack-one face to replace the anonymous R196 puncture-pair fan by a named bipartite interaction grid between every internal carrier vertex and at least four exterior anchors.

## Persistence
The tight trimer windows and R41 central-anchor interactions are graph-intrinsic/historical. The particular P5 order chosen for each good omission is a proof certificate; no simultaneous current three-cover or paid descendant is asserted.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert that the interactions close, are simultaneously current, or share one exterior P5 root. Does not identify all six exterior vertices as anchors. Does not give an interaction-capacity contradiction or exterior-size descent.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Six-exterior carrier/exterior interaction grid is a slack-one specialization with no current consumers; preserve historical mathematics but retire canonical identity.
- **Curation note:** Six-exterior carrier/exterior interaction grid is a slack-one specialization with no current consumers; preserve historical mathematics but retire canonical identity.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Accepted six-exterior carrier-by-exterior central-anchor interaction grid.

## Proof
By R196 there are at least four distinct omitted vertices e in E for which E-{e} has a tight P5 Q_e. Fix one tight order for each such Q_e and let I_e be the set of its three internal vertices. Put U=union I_e. If |U| were at most three, then because each I_e has size three we would have one fixed 3-set U=I_e for every good omission e. But I_e is contained in E-{e}, so every good omitted vertex e would lie in E-U. Since |E-U|=3, this is impossible for at least four distinct good omissions. Hence |U|>=4. Now fix an internal vertex b of K and q in U. Choose a good omission e with q in I_e. The consecutive trimer window of K centered at b is tight, and the consecutive trimer window of Q_e centered at q is tight; their supports are disjoint because Q_e is contained in E. R41 applied to these two disjoint trimers supplies the synchronized two-anchor interaction with middle-anchor pair {b,q}. Since b and q were arbitrary, the full stated grid follows.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/LEGACY/R211.md -->

# R213 — Six-exterior cross-rail terminal-payment double channel

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
In the six-exterior slack-one face, fix any accepted R208 singleton root H=K sqcup Q_e sqcup {e}. The two cross-rail diagonal balanced pairs D_K^L with D_Q^R and D_Q^L with D_K^R each satisfy the Historical-Support Terminal-Reversal Payment hypotheses: one signed dimer is a historical signed support, the opposite-polarity partner is a terminal dimer of the entire disjoint opposite rail. Therefore, before any unrelated recompletion, either diagonal may be chosen to launch a lawful payment continuation yielding either a spanning two-cover or strict decrease of its initial mass-four signed-support mass. Thus every R208 root carries two distinct branch-free cross-rail payment channels tied to its four physical rail-end dimers.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in the six-exterior face; an R208 singleton root H=K sqcup Q_e sqcup {e} is fixed.

## Scope
Order-free payment corollary of the six-exterior common-witness terminal-dimer rectangle. No maximin root, order-ten, or simultaneous-floor synchronization hypothesis.

## Applicability
Use when converting the static R208 cross-rail rectangle into actual signed-pair motion. Each diagonal can be paid immediately, without first steering to a floor or classifying a return corridor.

## Persistence
The chosen diagonal signed supports and the terminal-reversal/extension certificate produced by R162 persist as historical ancestry. The original literal singleton root or opposite rail is not asserted current after payment unless separately retained.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert that both payment descendants coexist, that the two strict descents interact, that either descendant reaches mass two in one step, or that a strict payment gives exterior-size descent or closure.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Six-exterior cross-rail double payment channel is a specialized corollary of the root rectangle plus generic terminal payment, with no live consumers. Useful proof interface historically, low discovery value now.
- **Curation note:** Six-exterior cross-rail double payment channel is a specialized corollary of the root rectangle plus generic terminal payment, with no live consumers. Useful proof interface historically, low discovery value now.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Accepted six-exterior cross-rail terminal-payment double channel.

## Proof
Fix the R208 root and its four signed terminal dimers. R208 states that D_K^L and D_Q^R have opposite polarity, as do D_Q^L and D_K^R, and that K and Q_e are vertex-disjoint tight paths. For the first diagonal take the historical signed support S=D_K^L and the disjoint tight path T=Q_e with terminal dimer D_T=D_Q^R. These are exactly the R162 hypotheses, so before unrelated reset the terminal-reversal payment gives either a spanning two-cover or strict decrease from the initial mass four. For the second diagonal take S=D_Q^L and T=K with terminal dimer D_T=D_K^R and apply R162 identically. The two applications are separate lawful choices; no simultaneous descendant is claimed.

# R215 — Global-longest terminal complete exterior-witness collision web

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Let K be a proper globally longest tight path in a Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament, with exterior E of size r. Fix either terminal physical dimer D of K in the reverse orientation supplied by R199. Then every e in E gives a signed certificate on the same oriented physical support D with the same polarity. Consequently every unordered pair of distinct exterior witnesses {e,f} enters the accepted same-polarity two-extension collision package of R38 on D. Thus each terminal dimer carries a complete collision web indexed by the binomial(r,2) witness pairs. In particular, in the six-exterior O3 face each terminal dimer carries fifteen such two-witness collision certificates.

## Hypotheses
K is a proper globally longest tight path; E is its exterior; one terminal physical dimer is fixed.

## Scope
Order-free terminal multi-witness interaction corollary. No smallest-counterexample minimality beyond any downstream use of the collision package, and no exterior-slack specialization is needed for the general statement.

## Applicability
Use whenever terminal adaptive-capture or collision machinery needs two distinct exterior witnesses. Any two may be chosen on either terminal dimer, so witness avoidance constraints can be satisfied without rebuilding signs.

## Persistence
The physical terminal dimer, all exterior witness identities, tested sign orders, and pairwise collision certificates are graph-intrinsic.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert simultaneous current collision descendants, does not say different witness-pair collision packages are independent or compatible, and does not itself force capture, payment, exterior descent, or a spanning two-cover.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Complete exterior-witness collision web is a convenience wrapper around global-longest endpoint shielding plus pairwise R38; inline into its consumer.
- **Curation note:** Complete exterior-witness collision web is a convenience wrapper around global-longest endpoint shielding plus pairwise R38; inline into its consumer.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Accepted complete exterior-witness collision web on each terminal dimer.

## Proof
Fix the left terminal dimer; the right end is identical. R199 states that for every e in E the same reverse-oriented terminal dimer is signed with the same polarity by e. Let e and f be distinct exterior vertices. These are therefore two signed certificates on the same physical support, with distinct witnesses and equal polarity. By the same-polarity branch of R38, they enter the accepted two-extension collision package. Since e,f were arbitrary, this holds for every unordered pair of exterior witnesses, giving a complete collision web of size binomial(r,2).

# R216 — Two-thirds Hamilton-five density in every vertex set

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Let W be any r-vertex subset, r>=6, of a Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament. Let h_5(W) be the number of five-subsets of W that support a tight five-vertex path. Then h_5(W) >= (2/3) binom(r,5). Equivalently, at least two-thirds of all physical five-subsets of W are Hamiltonian P5 supports.

## Hypotheses
Strong Level-(1) boundary antisymmetry; W is any finite vertex subset of order r>=6; accepted four-of-six Hamilton-five density R195.

## Scope
Order-free local density amplification by pure double counting.

## Applicability
Use for arbitrary exterior slack. Any exterior or residual vertex set of size at least six is not merely guaranteed to contain one P5: a uniform two-thirds fraction of all its five-subsets are P5 supports. This gives a scalable combinatorial reservoir for synchronized-root and replacement arguments.

## Persistence
The Hamiltonian five-support count is graph-intrinsic on W.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert a P6 or longer path, does not prescribe compatible P5 orderings, does not imply a common omitted vertex, and does not by itself yield exterior-size descent or a spanning two-cover.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** superseded
- **Lifecycle note:** The two-thirds Hamilton-five density theorem is an immediate double-counting corollary of R195 and is strictly subsumed by the stronger conditional Johnson hierarchy C281.
- **Curation note:** The two-thirds Hamilton-five density theorem is an immediate double-counting corollary of R195 and is strictly subsumed by the stronger conditional Johnson hierarchy C281.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Accepted two-thirds Hamilton-five density theorem.

## Proof
Let I be the set of pairs (S,F) with F subset S subset W, |S|=6, |F|=5, and F supporting a tight P5. By R195, each six-set S contains at least four Hamiltonian five-subsets, so |I|>=4 binom(r,6). On the other hand, each Hamiltonian five-subset F of W is contained in exactly r-5 six-subsets S=F union {x}, x in W-F. Hence |I|=(r-5) h_5(W). Therefore (r-5)h_5(W)>=4 binom(r,6). Using binom(r,6)=binom(r,5)(r-5)/6 and r>=6, divide by r-5 to obtain h_5(W)>= (4/6)binom(r,5)=(2/3)binom(r,5).

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/LEGACY/R216.md -->

# R217 — Anchored-capacity one-residual branch enters literal signed-pair discharge

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Let H be a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample and let (alpha;P),(T;beta) be an anchored-capacity realization of a balanced opposite-sign pair in the sense of R179/R180. If the ordinary reservoir X=V(H)\\(V(P) union V(T) union {alpha,beta}) has exactly one vertex x, then W=V(H)\\(V(P) union V(T)) has order between one and three and supports a tight path J. Hence H=J sqcup P sqcup T is a literal spanning three-cover whose P,T components are the historical opposite-signed pair, so R171 applies. Therefore the one-residual branch yields either a spanning two-cover, strict historical pair-mass descent, or bounded support swallow; it is not an inert capacity exception.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample; (alpha;P),(T;beta) is a balanced opposite-sign pair realized at anchored capacity; the ordinary reservoir X of R180 has size one.

## Scope
Order-free composition of anchored-capacity one-residual geometry with literal signed-pair discharge. Witnesses may coincide or lie in the opposite support; no disjoint-witness assumption is needed.

## Applicability
Use in the |X|=1 branch of R180. It removes the former near-spanning dead end by converting the at-most-three vertices outside the two capacity supports into the literal third path required by R171.

## Persistence
The capacity supports and their historical signs are the R180 data. The third path J is a proof/current frame on the physical leftover vertices. R171 outputs retain only the ancestry guaranteed by that theorem.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not claim the R171 outputs individually close the conjecture. Does not make pair mass globally monotone after unrelated resets. Does not require alpha and beta distinct or outside the opposite support.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** superseded
- **Lifecycle note:** One-residual capacity entry into literal R171 discharge is an internal stage of the stronger parent reduction C214/R222, which carries the branch through finite descent to its terminal tiny corner.
- **Curation note:** One-residual capacity entry into literal R171 discharge is an internal stage of the stronger parent reduction C214/R222, which carries the branch through finite descent to its terminal tiny corner.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Verified.

## Proof
Let X={x}. Put W=V(H)\\(V(P) union V(T)). By the definition X=V(H)\\(V(P) union V(T) union {alpha,beta}), every vertex of W belongs to {x,alpha,beta}; moreover x belongs to W, so 1<=|W|<=3. If |W|=1, the singleton is a tight path. If |W|=2, either ordering is a tight two-vertex path because there is no three-turn constraint. If |W|=3, R8 supplies a tight trimer order on W. Thus in all cases W supports a nonempty tight path J. Since P,T are vertex-disjoint tight supports and W is exactly their physical complement, H=J sqcup P sqcup T is a literal spanning three-cover. The historical balanced pair gives opposite signs (alpha;P),(T;beta), so all hypotheses of R171 are met. R171 yields a spanning two-cover, strict historical pair-mass descent, or bounded support swallow. Therefore R180 branch (iii) is not inert once R171 is available.

# R221 — One-residual terminal swallow reduces to the 2+3 / 3+(2-or-3) corner

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
In the anchored-capacity one-residual branch of a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample, follow the literal R171 peel lineage until its first non-descent output. If that output is bounded support swallow rather than a spanning two-cover, then the swallowed literal signed support S has order two or three. If |S|=2, the surviving third literal rail J has order exactly three. If |S|=3, J has order two or three. Thus the entire nonclosing one-residual branch terminates in the finite local size corner 2+3 or 3+(2 or 3).

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample; an anchored-capacity balanced pair has ordinary reservoir of size one; the literal R171 peel continuation is followed until its first non-descent output.

## Scope
Order-free size compression of the only nonclosing one-residual anchored-capacity output.

## Applicability
Use after the one-residual capacity branch has been converted to a literal R171 frame. It replaces arbitrary bounded swallow by two explicit small-size cases suitable for local trimer/dimer analysis.

## Persistence
The size conclusion concerns the terminal literal peel frame. No claim is made that the original capacity supports or witnesses remain current after intermediate peel steps.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not close either size corner. Does not assert the swallowed support is the original pre-peel capacity support. Does not apply to bounded contacts arising outside the one-residual literal R171 lineage.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** superseded
- **Lifecycle note:** Tiny-swallow 2+3 / 3+(2-or-3) classification is now incorporated into the statement of parent reduction C214/R222. Preserve as proof-stage history.
- **Curation note:** Tiny-swallow 2+3 / 3+(2-or-3) classification is now incorporated into the statement of parent reduction C214/R222. Preserve as proof-stage history.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Verified.

## Proof
Start in the anchored-capacity one-residual branch of R221. Accepted R217 supplies a literal spanning three-cover

  H = J_0 sqcup P_0 sqcup T_0

in the scope of R171, where 1<=|J_0|<=3 and P_0,T_0 are the historical opposite-signed supports.

Follow the literal R171/P597 peel lineage through consecutive strict pair-mass descents. The mechanism of P597 is important here. A bad displayed seam is reversed by R3 to a tight contact trimer. If that trimer swallows an entire historical support, R171 is already in its bounded-swallow output. Otherwise R425 rebirths nonempty signed surviving intervals of the contacted supports and strictly lowers the integer pair mass M, with no fresh completion or representative reset. The good geometry remains in the same literal frame; the third rail is a surviving literal interval of the previous third rail. Thus successive strict descents may be iterated inside one literal no-recompletion lineage. Since both historical supports remain nonempty, M is a positive integer bounded below by two; indeed in any nonclosing literal frame M>=4, because if the union of the two support vertex sets had order at most three, those vertices would themselves admit one Hamilton tight path (dimer at order two, or an R3 trimer at order three), which together with the third rail would two-cover H. Therefore strict descent cannot continue indefinitely. A first non-descent output occurs after finitely many steps.

If that output is a spanning two-cover, we are done. Assume it is bounded support swallow. Write the terminal literal frame as

  H = J sqcup S sqcup T,

where S is the completely swallowed historical signed support and T is the untouched opposite-signed support. By the literal interval persistence just described, J is a surviving interval of J_0, so

  1 <= |J| <= 3.                                           (1)

By the bounded-swallow clause of R171, the failure/contact trimer contains all of S, hence

  1 <= |S| <= 3.                                           (2)

Also X:=V(S) union V(J) is exactly the physical complement of T. If |X|<=3, then X supports one Hamilton tight path: the order-one/two cases are vacuous singleton/dimer paths and the order-three case has a tight trimer orientation by R3. That Hamilton path together with T is a spanning two-cover of H, contradiction. Thus

  |S|+|J| >= 4.                                            (3)

It remains to exclude equality in (3). Assume |X|=4. The R171 lineage retains the graph-intrinsic historical sign of the untouched support T. Let beta be its retained sign witness. By definition beta lies outside V(T); because H=J sqcup S sqcup T, we have beta in X.

We construct an exact singleton-deletion cover H-z=P sqcup T with |P|=3 and V(P) union {z}=X.

If (|S|,|J|)=(1,3), let S={z} and take P=J.

If (|S|,|J|)=(2,2), write S={z,w}. The three-set V(J) union {w} admits a tight trimer order P by R3.

If (|S|,|J|)=(3,1), write S={z,w_1,w_2}; the three-set V(J) union {w_1,w_2} admits a tight trimer order P by R3.

In every case P sqcup T is a literal two-cover of H-z. It is exact: if H-z were Hamiltonian, that Hamilton path together with singleton z would be a spanning two-cover of H.

Apply accepted R594 to this exact singleton-deletion row, using the same literal order

  T=(t_0,...,t_m)

from the terminal R171 frame as its long rail. R594 closes its small opposite-rail cases; since H is a counterexample, we are in its surviving normalization, where m>=4 and for every x in X the simultaneous endpoint reverse stars

  (t_1,t_0,x) tight,      (x,t_m,t_{m-1}) tight             (4)

hold.

Set x=beta. If T is head-signed by beta, then the retained historical sign extension gives

  (beta,t_0,t_1) tight,

while (4) gives its complete reversal (t_1,t_0,beta) tight, contradicting R3. If T is tail-signed by beta, the retained sign gives

  (t_{m-1},t_m,beta) tight,

while (4) gives its complete reversal (beta,t_m,t_{m-1}) tight, again contradicting R3. Therefore |X| cannot equal four.

Combining (1),(2),(3) with the exclusion of total four gives |S|+|J|>=5 while each coordinate is at most three. The only possibilities are

  (|S|,|J|)=(2,3),(3,2),(3,3).

This is exactly the conclusion of R221. No R24, R5, R168, R169, or R214 is used.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/LEGACY/R221.md -->

# R222 — Universal anchored-capacity reduction to contact or tiny swallow corner

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Every hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample H admits the following order-free reduction. Either a spanning two-cover occurs, or there is an anchored-capacity balanced-pair realization with reservoir of size at least two whose fixed capacity reverse dimer yields the R180 strict same-polarity two-witness extension/collision output or bounded reverse trimer/contact, or a one-residual capacity lineage terminates in bounded support swallow in one of exactly the small size corners: swallowed support order two with surviving third literal rail order three, or swallowed support order three with surviving third literal rail order two or three. Thus, modulo immediate closure, the arbitrary-order problem reduces to capacity-specific bounded contact/extension geometry or the finite 2+3 / 3+(2-or-3) swallow corner; no anonymous pair floor, exterior-slack case split, or indefinite pair-mass descent remains.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample.

## Scope
Order-free parent reduction of the arbitrary-order Strong Level-(1) program. It bypasses the five-exterior/six-exterior split and uses only accepted balanced-pair, anchored-capacity, literal-discharge, and small-deletion structure.

## Applicability
Use as a candidate replacement frontier for O3 after audit. Future work need only consume the capacity-specific R180 contact/extension branch and the explicit tiny swallow corner.

## Persistence
The anchored-capacity branch is representative-relative as in R179/R180; its collision/contact output is graph-intrinsic. The tiny swallow corner concerns the terminal literal R171 peel frame. No simultaneous currentness between the two branches is asserted.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not close either residual branch. Does not claim anonymous same-polarity collision is progress without using its capacity anchors. Does not assert global pair-mass monotonicity or preserve the initial floor representative through capacity maximization.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** superseded
- **Lifecycle note:** The anchored-capacity contact-or-tiny-swallow reduction is strictly refined by C218/R227, which carries the same one-residual lineage through the tiny corner and recycles it into the established five/six-exterior gateways. No live consumer requires the intermediate tiny-corner stopping point.
- **Curation note:** The anchored-capacity contact-or-tiny-swallow reduction is strictly refined by C218/R227, which carries the same one-residual lineage through the tiny corner and recycles it into the established five/six-exterior gateways. No live consumer requires the intermediate tiny-corner stopping point.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Verified.

## Proof
Let H be a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample. We reconstruct the R222 reduction using only the modern clean pair machinery and the noncircular synchronized short-rail normalization.

INITIAL BALANCED PAIR. Fix any two distinct vertices p,x. Accepted R654 gives a finite certificate-retaining continuation with one of two outcomes: either H already has a spanning two-cover, in which case R222 is finished, or there is an ancestry-bearing mass-two balanced opposite-sign floor whose singleton supports are exactly {p,x}. Retain one such pair. This replaces the historical use of R198 entirely.

ANCHORED CAPACITY. Apply accepted R179 to the retained balanced pair and choose an anchored-capacity realization (alpha;P),(T;beta), maximizing |P|+|T| for the fixed signed anchors and witnesses. Let

  X = V(H) \ (V(P) union V(T) union {alpha,beta})

be its ordinary reservoir. Apply accepted R180.

If X is empty, R180 gives a spanning two-cover.

If |X|>=2, R180 gives exactly the capacity-specific branch stated in R222: the fixed capacity reverse dimer carries two same-polarity reservoir witnesses in one tested orientation, hence the strict two-witness extension/collision or bounded reverse-trimer/contact output of the accepted same-support interaction. This is the non-one-residual branch of R222.

It remains to treat |X|=1.

ONE-RESIDUAL LITERAL ENTRANCE. Accepted R217 converts this anchored-capacity one-residual realization into a literal spanning three-cover

  H = J_0 sqcup P_0 sqcup T_0

in the scope of R171, where P_0,T_0 are the historical opposite-signed supports and

  1 <= |J_0| <= 3.                                         (1)

Follow the actual literal peel mechanism of the fully reconstructible preferred proof P597 of R171. At each application, a good branch closes H by a spanning two-cover. A bad seam is reversed by R3 to a tight contact trimer. If that trimer contains an entire historical support, bounded support swallow occurs. Otherwise Signed-Interval Rebirth inside R171 leaves nonempty opposite-signed surviving intervals and strictly lowers the integer historical pair mass M, with no fresh completion or representative reset. The third rail remains a surviving literal interval of the previous third rail. Thus consecutive strict-descents stay inside one literal no-recompletion lineage.

Strict descent cannot continue indefinitely. Both historical supports remain nonempty, so M is a positive integer. More sharply, in any nonclosing literal frame M>=4: if the union of the two support vertex sets had order at most three, those vertices would support one Hamilton tight path, and together with the third rail would two-cover H. Therefore after finitely many strict descents there is a first non-descent R171 output.

If it is a spanning two-cover, stop. Assume it is bounded support swallow and write the terminal literal frame as

  H = J sqcup S sqcup T,

where S is the completely swallowed historical support and T is the untouched opposite-signed support. P597 interval persistence and (1) give

  1 <= |J| <= 3.                                           (2)

The R171 swallow clause itself gives

  1 <= |S| <= 3.                                           (3)

The set Y=V(S) union V(J) is exactly the physical complement of T. If |Y|<=3, then Y supports one Hamilton tight path: singleton/dimer trivially, and an order-three tight path by R3. That path together with T would be a spanning two-cover. Hence every nonclosing terminal swallow satisfies

  |S|+|J| >= 4.                                            (4)

MASS-FOUR EXTINCTION. Assume equality in (4). Because the R171 lineage retains graph-intrinsic sign ancestry, the untouched support T retains an exact sign witness beta outside V(T). Since H=J sqcup S sqcup T, beta lies in

  Y=V(S) union V(J),   |Y|=4.                              (5)

We construct an exact singleton-deletion cover H-z=Q sqcup T with |Q|=3 and V(Q) union {z}=Y.

If (|S|,|J|)=(1,3), let S={z} and Q=J.

If (|S|,|J|)=(2,2), write S={z,w}; by R3 the three-set V(J) union {w} has a tight trimer order Q.

If (|S|,|J|)=(3,1), write S={z,w_1,w_2}; by R3 the three-set V(J) union {w_1,w_2} has a tight trimer order Q.

In every case Q sqcup T is a literal two-cover of H-z. It is exact, since a Hamilton path on H-z together with singleton z would two-cover H.

Apply accepted R594 to this exact singleton-deletion row, keeping the literal terminal order T=(t_0,...,t_m) as the long rail. Its small opposite-rail cases close; therefore in the surviving counterexample normalization m>=4 and for every y in Y,

  (t_1,t_0,y) tight,       (y,t_m,t_{m-1}) tight.           (6)

Take y=beta from (5). If T is head-signed by beta, its retained sign gives (beta,t_0,t_1) tight, whose complete reversal (t_1,t_0,beta) is tight by (6), contradicting R3. If T is tail-signed by beta, its retained sign gives (t_{m-1},t_m,beta) tight, whose complete reversal (beta,t_m,t_{m-1}) is tight by (6), again contradicting R3. Hence |S|+|J| cannot equal four.

By (2),(3),(4) and the mass-four exclusion, the only possible nonclosing terminal swallow profiles are

  (|S|,|J|)=(2,3),(3,2),(3,3).

These are exactly the tiny swallow corners stated in R222. Combining them with the earlier R180 reservoir>=2 branch proves every alternative in R222. No R24, R5, R168, R169, R198, or R214 is used.

# R223 — R171 dimer swallow creates a bidirectional endpoint-refund fork

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
In a literal signed-pair frame consumed by R171, suppose the bounded-swallow output completely swallows one historical signed support S of order two. Then the same physical dimer S carries both opposite orientations as signed supports of the same historical polarity, with distinct witnesses: the incoming pair witness signs the original orientation, while the order-three peel-contact marker signs the reverse orientation. Consequently accepted aligned dimer payment R35 applies independently to the two orientations. Unless a spanning two-cover occurs on one route, the two routes produce physically certified singleton descendants supported at the two different physical endpoints of S. Thus an R171 width-two swallow is not a terminal bounded object; it canonically opens an endpoint-separated two-route refund fork.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample; H=K sqcup P sqcup T is a literal R171 signed-pair frame; an R171 peel terminates in complete swallow of one pair support S with |S|=2.

## Scope
Order-free refinement of the width-two bounded-swallow output in the accepted literal signed-pair discharge proof. The two paid routes are separate descendants and are not asserted simultaneously current.

## Applicability
Use whenever R171 returns bounded swallow at support order two. It replaces the bare dimer terminal by two endpoint-specific paid continuations, one for each orientation of the swallowed physical dimer.

## Persistence
The physical dimer S, the incoming historical sign, the peel-contact trimer, its marker witness, and the identities of the two physical singleton endpoints are graph-intrinsic/historical. Each R35 paid descendant is lineage-relative; the two singleton descendants need not coexist in one representative and the old literal R171 frame need not survive payment.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not itself contradict the singleton-deletion rail floor because R35 does not keep the old literal third rail current. Does not assert the two endpoint singleton descendants are simultaneously current, form one balanced pair, or close the conjecture.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** R171 dimer-swallow bidirectional refund fork is a specialized zero-consumer refinement; preserve in proof history.
- **Curation note:** R171 dimer-swallow bidirectional refund fork is a specialized zero-consumer refinement; preserve in proof history.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Verified.

## Proof
Consider first a swallowed head-signed support S=(s0,s1) with historical witness alpha, so (alpha,s0,s1) is tight. The accepted proof P170 of R171 peels a marker vertex nu from the literal third path. Complete swallow at this width-two support means the support-to-marker seam (s0,s1,nu) is bad. Boundary antisymmetry R3 therefore makes (nu,s1,s0) tight. Hence the reverse ordered support (s1,s0) is itself head-signed, now by witness nu. Moreover nu cannot equal alpha: if nu=alpha, then (alpha,s0,s1) and its complete reversal (alpha,s1,s0) would both be tight, contradicting R3. Thus S carries two genuine signed orientations with distinct witnesses. Apply accepted Signed-support actualization and aligned payment R35 to the historical orientation (s0,s1). Its aligned width-two payment gives either a spanning two-cover or a physically certified singleton descendant on s1. Apply R35 separately to the reverse signed orientation (s1,s0); it gives either a spanning two-cover or a physically certified singleton descendant on s0. These are separate paid lineages, so no simultaneous currentness is asserted. The tail-signed case is obtained by reversing the head/tail roles in the accepted R171 peel and R35 payment; again the two opposite dimer orientations lower to the two opposite physical singleton endpoints. Therefore every width-two R171 swallow canonically carries the asserted endpoint-separated refund fork.

# R224 — Inherited-turn endpoint-selective paid-floor continuation

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Let H be a smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample and suppose an ancestry-bearing balanced-pair lineage contains a signed physical dimer D whose sign is certified by a named inherited tight turn. Choose the aligned dimer refund orientation so that one prescribed physical endpoint z of D is the singleton surviving the width-two payment. Then along the accepted inherited-turn paid continuation, either a spanning two-cover occurs or the lineage reaches an ancestry-bearing mass-two floor in which (z) is literally one singleton floor coordinate. The other floor singleton is not prescribed. The head/tail dual and the two possible endpoint choices are separate alternative lineages.

## Hypotheses
H is a smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample; D is an aligned signed dimer inside an ancestry-bearing balanced-pair/payment lineage; its sign comes from a named inherited tight turn; one of the two orientation-compatible endpoint-selective refund channels is chosen.

## Scope
Historical Strong signed-payment theorem recovered from the audited archive. This is a lineage/persistence theorem, not simultaneous currentization of two endpoint choices.

## Applicability
Use when a signed dimer arises from a named physical turn and later arguments need one chosen physical endpoint to survive not merely the first dimer refund but all the way to the mass-two floor.

## Persistence
The named inherited turn, chosen refund orientation, physical endpoint z, refund certificate, and literal floor coordinate (z) are retained in the chosen ancestry ledger. The old marker, source cover, opposite support, and second floor singleton need not remain current or retain their old identities.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not prescribe the second floor singleton. Does not assert both endpoint-selective floors coexist or can be synchronized. Does not preserve an arbitrary old literal three-cover through payment. Does not imply a target-aligned floor for any independently chosen second vertex, and does not close the conjecture.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Integrator cleanup: route-specific capture/payment/capacity machinery with no live consumers, relations, or guidance references; accepted mathematics preserved historically.
- **Curation note:** Widely reusable endpoint-selective payment theorem preserving a chosen physical endpoint to the mass-two floor.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Verified historical endpoint-selective paid-floor theorem.

## Proof
Let the ancestry-bearing balanced pair contain a signed physical dimer D=(d_0,d_1) and a physically disjoint opposite-polarity signed support T. Fix the prescribed endpoint z in V(D), and let d be the other endpoint. The named inherited tight turn certifying the sign of D is retained in the ancestry ledger.

Apply R425 to the historical signed path D with deletion set {d}. The unique surviving interval is the singleton (z). R425 says that (z) is graph-intrinsically signed with the same polarity as D. If z lies at the historically signed end, the old witness remains; otherwise the cut neighbor d is the new exact witness. In either case the original inherited turn, the chosen endpoint z, and the one-vertex cut from D to (z) remain exact ancestry data. The opposite support T is untouched, so (z) and T are physically disjoint signed supports of opposite polarity.

By the first clause of R514, these two supports therefore form a new graph-intrinsic balanced opposite-sign pair, with its birth certificate explicitly descended from the original D-side certificate. If T is already a singleton, this is the required ancestry-bearing mass-two floor containing the literal coordinate (z). If T is nontrivial, apply R428 to this singleton/nontrivial balanced pair with p=z. Its chosen certificate-retaining continuation preserves the singleton support (z) exactly and yields either a spanning two-cover of H or a balanced pair whose two supports are both singletons. In the latter case (z) is literally one floor coordinate and the second coordinate is uncontrolled, exactly as R224 asserts.

The opposite choice of endpoint of D is obtained by deleting the other endpoint in the first R425 step; head/tail duality is built into R425 and R428. The two endpoint choices are alternative lineages, not simultaneous states. No old cover or unrelated witness is transported. Thus the named inherited turn and original dimer remain historical ancestry, while current pair status after clipping is supplied afresh by R514. This proves R224 without R169, R35, or any exterior-cardinality assumption.
