# R226 — R171 dimer-swallow 2+3 corner re-enters the five-exterior equality face

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Let H be a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample and let H=J sqcup S sqcup T be a terminal literal R171 frame in which S is the completely swallowed historical pair support. Suppose the local sizes are one of (|S|,|J|)=(2,3),(3,2),(3,3). Then the untouched opposite support T canonically re-enters the accepted exterior gateway program. In the first two cases T has exactly five exterior vertices E=S union J, hence is globally longest by R23; if E is Hamiltonian there is a spanning two-cover, and otherwise R192 gives four-of-five replacement saturation for every carrier vertex of T. In the (3,3) case T has exactly six exterior vertices E=S union J, and accepted R196 supplies at least four omissions e for which E-{e} is a tight P5 and H=T sqcup Q_e sqcup {e} is a literal singleton-root three-cover, together with the R196 puncture-pair consequences. Thus none of the 2+3, 3+2, or 3+3 bounded-swallow size corners is a new isolated terminal species.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample; H=J sqcup S sqcup T is a literal terminal R171 frame after complete swallow of pair support S; the ordered size pair (|S|,|J|) is one of (2,3),(3,2),(3,3).

## Scope
Order-free recycling theorem from the finite R171 small-swallow corner back to accepted five- and six-exterior machinery. No anchored-capacity parent is assumed.

## Applicability
Use whenever bounded swallow has already been compressed to the 2+3 / 3+(2-or-3) corner. The theorem sends every such case back to R192 or R196 rather than opening bespoke small-support cleanup.

## Persistence
The literal terminal supports J,S,T and E=S union J are physical in the R171 frame. Five-exterior global-longestness and R192 replacement supports are graph-intrinsic. In the six-exterior case the R196 singleton roots are separate literal representatives for each good omission.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not close the non-Hamiltonian five-exterior equality face or the six-exterior four-root fan. Does not assert complementary carrier swaps, exterior-size descent, or simultaneous currentness across different R196 roots.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** superseded
- **Lifecycle note:** The terminal 2+3 / 3+2 / 3+3 recycle lemma is incorporated directly into parent reduction C218/R227. Preserve as proof-stage history, not a peer active theorem.
- **Curation note:** The terminal 2+3 / 3+2 / 3+3 recycle lemma is incorporated directly into parent reduction C218/R227. Preserve as proof-stage history, not a peer active theorem.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Verified.

## Proof
Because H=J sqcup S sqcup T is a literal vertex-disjoint spanning frame, E:=V(H)\\V(T)=V(J) union V(S). If (|S|,|J|) is (2,3) or (3,2), then |E|=5. The path T is proper and has exactly five exterior vertices, so accepted R23 makes T globally longest. If E supports a tight P5 Q, then T sqcup Q is a spanning two-cover. Otherwise E is non-Hamiltonian and accepted R192 applies to the carrier T and exterior E, giving for every t in V(T) at least four successful five-set replacements (E-{z}) union {t}. If instead (|S|,|J|)=(3,3), then |E|=6. Accepted R196 applies to the tight path T with six-vertex exterior E: at least four e in E have a tight P5 Q_e on E-{e}, giving literal spanning three-covers H=T sqcup Q_e sqcup {e} and the associated puncture balanced-pair fan. These exhaust the listed tiny corners.

# R227 — Universal anchored-capacity reduction to contact or five/six-exterior recycle

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Every hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample H satisfies the following order-free alternative. Either a spanning two-cover occurs; or an anchored-capacity balanced-pair realization has ordinary reservoir of size at least two and yields the capacity-specific R180 strict same-polarity two-witness extension/collision output or bounded reverse trimer/contact; or, after a one-residual anchored-capacity lineage and finite literal R171 discharge, the untouched opposite pair support T re-enters one of the accepted exterior gateways: a five-exterior non-Hamiltonian R192 replacement-saturation frame, or a six-exterior R196 four-root singleton fan. Thus outside immediate closure the arbitrary-order problem reduces to the capacity-specific |X|>=2 contact/extension branch or the already-developed five/six-exterior gateway programs.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample.

## Scope
Order-free parent reduction built only from accepted live revisions. It bypasses the stale O3 split as an initial normalization while returning its one-residual terminal cases to the same five/six-exterior gateway machinery.

## Applicability
Use as a candidate replacement parent for arbitrary-order work after audit. Future work may focus on consuming the capacity-specific R180 collision/contact branch and the accepted R192/R196 gateway outputs.

## Persistence
The anchored-capacity realization and R171 peel lineage are representative/lineage-relative as in their parents. The final five- or six-vertex exterior set and its carrier T are literal in the terminal peel frame; R192/R196 outputs then have their usual graph-intrinsic or separate-root persistence.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not close the R180 |X|>=2 contact/extension branch, the non-Hamiltonian five-exterior replacement grid, or the six-exterior four-root fan. Does not assert complementary carrier swaps, exterior-size descent, or that anonymous collision production is progress by itself.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** superseded
- **Lifecycle note:** R227 is preserved as a valid historical anchored-capacity theorem, but it no longer belongs in the active canonical spine. Its stated canonical function was to serve as a candidate arbitrary-order front door. Accepted R533 now proves every surviving hypothetical smallest counterexample is beyond order ten, and active reconstructible R352 is explicitly the preferred universal protected-contact front door in that regime. The pair R533+R352 therefore preserves the global normalization function without relying on R227's unreconstructed extra literal-peel iteration coordinate or its retired R22/R23/R24 leaves. This supersession does not assert that R352 reproduces every five/six-exterior output of R227; those historical outputs remain recorded in R227/P227.
- **Curation note:** R227 is preserved as a valid historical anchored-capacity theorem, but it no longer belongs in the active canonical spine. Its stated canonical function was to serve as a candidate arbitrary-order front door. Accepted R533 now proves every surviving hypothetical smallest counterexample is beyond order ten, and active reconstructible R352 is explicitly the preferred universal protected-contact front door in that regime. The pair R533+R352 therefore preserves the global normalization function without relying on R227's unreconstructed extra literal-peel iteration coordinate or its retired R22/R23/R24 leaves. This supersession does not assert that R352 reproduces every five/six-exterior output of R227; those historical outputs remain recorded in R227/P227.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Verified.

## Proof
Let H be a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample.

CLEAN UNIVERSAL ENTRANCE. Fix any two distinct vertices. Accepted R654 yields either a spanning two-cover of H or an ancestry-bearing mass-two balanced opposite-sign floor. In the latter case apply accepted R179 and choose an anchored-capacity realization (alpha;P),(T;beta). Let X be its ordinary reservoir and apply accepted R180.

If X is empty, H is two-covered. If |X|>=2, R180 gives exactly the first nonclosing output species of R227: the fixed capacity reverse dimer has two same-polarity reservoir witnesses and therefore yields the capacity-specific strict two-witness extension/collision output or bounded reverse trimer/contact. Hence only |X|=1 remains.

ONE-RESIDUAL LITERAL LINEAGE. Accepted R217 converts |X|=1 into a literal R171 frame

  H = J_0 sqcup P_0 sqcup T_0,

where 1<=|J_0|<=3 and P_0,T_0 are opposite-signed historical supports. Follow the fully reconstructible literal peel of R171/P597. Every strict-descent output stays in the same no-recompletion lineage, leaves the third rail as a surviving interval, keeps both historical supports nonempty, and strictly lowers their integer total mass. Therefore strict descent cannot continue indefinitely. A first non-descent output is either a spanning two-cover or bounded support swallow.

Assume swallow and write the terminal frame

  H = J sqcup S sqcup T,

with S the swallowed historical signed support and T the untouched opposite support. Literal interval persistence gives |J|<=3, while R171 gives |S|<=3. Both are nonempty. If |S|+|J|<=3, the whole exterior E:=V(S) union V(J) of T is Hamiltonian (singleton/dimer, or an R3 trimer), so E together with T is a spanning two-cover. Thus |E|>=4.

We exclude |E|=4. The untouched support T retains a historical sign witness beta, and beta lies in E because beta is outside T and the terminal frame partitions H. Construct an exact singleton-deletion cover H-z=Q sqcup T with |Q|=3 and V(Q) union {z}=E as follows. For profile (1,3), delete the singleton S and take Q=J. For profile (2,2), delete one vertex z of S and orient the other S vertex together with the dimer J as a tight trimer Q by R3. For profile (3,1), delete one vertex z of S and orient the remaining two S vertices together with the singleton J as a tight trimer Q by R3. The displayed cover is exact because Hamiltonicity of H-z together with singleton z would two-cover H.

Apply accepted R594 to Q sqcup T, keeping the literal terminal order T=(t_0,...,t_m) as its long rail. In the surviving counterexample normalization it gives, for every e in E,

  (t_1,t_0,e) tight,     (e,t_m,t_{m-1}) tight.

Taking e=beta contradicts the retained sign of T by R3: for a head sign it reverses (beta,t_0,t_1), and for a tail sign it reverses (t_{m-1},t_m,beta). Therefore |E| cannot be four.

Thus every nonclosing terminal swallow has |S|,|J|<=3 and |E|>=5, so exactly

  (|S|,|J|)=(2,3),(3,2),(3,3).                             (1)

FIVE/SIX-EXTERIOR REENTRY. In the first two profiles of (1), E has exactly five vertices. If E supports a Hamilton tight P5, that P5 together with T is a spanning two-cover. Otherwise T is a proper tight path with exactly five exterior vertices E and E is non-Hamiltonian, so accepted R192 applies directly and supplies the five-exterior four-of-five replacement-saturation frame required by R227.

In the final profile (3,3), E has exactly six vertices. Accepted R196 applies to the tight path T with six-vertex exterior E and supplies at least four singleton roots H=T sqcup Q_e sqcup {e}, together with its puncture balanced-pair fan. This is exactly the six-exterior gateway stated in R227.

Hence every smallest counterexample satisfies the R227 alternative: closure, the R180 reservoir>=2 capacity contact/extension branch, the R192 five-exterior replacement gateway, or the R196 six-exterior four-root gateway. No R24, R5, R168, R169, R198, or R214 is used.

# R228 — Hamilton-five density hierarchy through every fixed triple

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Let W be an r-vertex subset, r>=6, of a Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament, and let S subset W have size s in {0,1,2,3}. Let h_5(W;S) be the number of five-subsets F of W containing S that support a tight P5. Then h_5(W;S) >= ((4-s)/(6-s)) * binom(r-s,5-s). Explicitly: at least two-thirds of all five-subsets of W are Hamilton-five supports; every fixed vertex lies in at least three-fifths of its possible five-set supersets that are P5 supports; every fixed pair lies in at least one-half; and every fixed triple lies in at least one-third. In particular every physical triple in any six-or-larger vertex set has many Hamilton-five extensions.

## Hypotheses
Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament; W is any r-set with r>=6; S subset W and 0<=|S|<=3.

## Scope
Pure order-free set-density consequence of accepted four-of-six Hamilton-five density R195.

## Applicability
Use when a fixed physical vertex, dimer, or trimer must be embedded into a P5 while retaining its support identity. The s=3 case globalizes the local trimer pair-extension phenomenon into a quantitative extension reservoir.

## Persistence
Pure graph-intrinsic support counting. No ordering of the P5s is synchronized, and no representative-relative data is involved.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not prescribe the P5 ordering on a successful support, does not preserve a chosen orientation of S inside that P5, and does not extend to fixed four-sets by this argument. Density counts do not imply simultaneous currentness or a spanning two-cover.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** superseded
- **Lifecycle note:** The older fixed-subset Hamilton-five density hierarchy is strictly improved by C281/R327 for every subset size it covers; keep the stronger Johnson-degree theorem canonical.
- **Curation note:** The older fixed-subset Hamilton-five density hierarchy is strictly improved by C281/R327 for every subset size it covers; keep the stronger Johnson-degree theorem canonical.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Verified.

## Proof
Fix S with |S|=s<=3. Consider all six-subsets U of W containing S. There are binom(r-s,6-s) of them. For any such U, accepted R195 says at least four of the six five-subsets U-{u} support tight P5s. A five-subset U-{u} fails to contain all of S only when the omitted vertex u lies in S; there are exactly s such omissions. Hence among the at least four Hamilton five-subsets, at least 4-s contain S. Therefore the number N of incident pairs (U,F), where S subset F subset U, |F|=5, |U|=6 and F supports a P5, satisfies N >= (4-s) binom(r-s,6-s). On the other hand, each Hamilton five-subset F of W containing S lies in exactly r-5 six-subsets U of W, obtained by adjoining one vertex of W-F. Hence N=(r-5) h_5(W;S). Dividing and using binom(r-s,6-s)/(r-5)=binom(r-s,5-s)/(6-s) gives h_5(W;S) >= ((4-s)/(6-s)) binom(r-s,5-s). Substituting s=0,1,2,3 yields the stated fractions 2/3, 3/5, 1/2, 1/3.

# R229 — Small-complement balanced pairs recycle to the five/six-exterior gateways

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Let H be a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample and let (alpha;P),(T;beta) be any balanced opposite-sign pair with vertex-disjoint tight supports. Put W=V(H)\\(V(P) union V(T)). If 1<=|W|<=3, then there is a finite chosen continuation with the following outcome: either a spanning two-cover occurs, or the terminal literal pair frame has an untouched opposite support whose exterior has size five or six and therefore enters the accepted R192 five-exterior replacement-saturation gateway or the accepted R196 six-exterior four-root gateway. More precisely, after finite R171 descent any nonclosing bounded swallow has size pattern (swallowed support, surviving third rail) equal to (2,3),(3,2), or (3,3); the first two give a five-exterior carrier, while the last gives a six-exterior carrier.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample; P,T are vertex-disjoint historical opposite-signed tight supports; their physical complement W has order one, two, or three.

## Scope
Order-free balanced-pair small-complement theorem. No anchored-capacity, exterior-slack, order-ten, or prescribed-root hypothesis.

## Applicability
Use whenever pair growth/capacity leaves at most three ordinary physical vertices outside the two signed supports. It converts near-spanning pair geometry directly into the existing five/six-exterior gateway programs.

## Persistence
The initial signs are historical. A tight path on W makes the initial R171 frame literal. Strict peel descendants stay within that chosen literal lineage. The final five/six-exterior carrier and its exterior are literal in the terminal frame; R192/R196 then have their standard persistence.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not close R192 or R196. Does not apply when the physical complement has four or more vertices. Does not make pair mass globally monotone outside the chosen R171 peel lineage.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Small-complement balanced-pair recycle is a zero-consumer finite gateway reduction. It is useful proof architecture but not sufficiently broad for the lean canonical toolkit.
- **Curation note:** Small-complement balanced-pair recycle is a zero-consumer finite gateway reduction. It is useful proof architecture but not sufficiently broad for the lean canonical toolkit.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Verified.

## Proof
Retain the hypotheses of R229: H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample, (alpha;P),(T;beta) is a balanced opposite-sign historical pair with vertex-disjoint nonempty tight supports, and

  W = V(H) \ (V(P) union V(T))

has order between one and three.

INITIAL LITERAL FRAME. Choose one tight path J_0 spanning W. For |W|=1 this is the singleton, for |W|=2 the dimer, and for |W|=3 an appropriate tight trimer orientation exists by R3. Hence

  H = J_0 sqcup P sqcup T

is a literal spanning three-cover in the scope of accepted R171, and |J_0|<=3.

FINITE LITERAL DESCENT. Follow the fully reconstructible preferred R171/P597 peel lineage. A spanning-two-cover output closes. Every strict-descent output is generated by an exact reversed seam/contact trimer and Signed-Interval Rebirth inside the same literal no-recompletion lineage; it keeps both historical opposite-signed supports nonempty, leaves the third rail as a surviving interval of the previous third rail, and strictly lowers the integer pair mass. Consequently strict descent cannot continue indefinitely. There is a first non-descent output.

Assume this output is bounded support swallow rather than a spanning two-cover. Write the terminal literal frame

  H = J sqcup S sqcup T,

where S is the completely swallowed historical signed support and T is the untouched opposite support. Literal interval persistence gives

  1 <= |J| <= |J_0| <= 3,                                 (1)

and the R171 swallow clause gives

  1 <= |S| <= 3.                                           (2)

Put E=V(S) union V(J), the exact physical exterior of T. If |E|<=3, then E supports a Hamilton tight path, by trivial singleton/dimer structure or R3 in order three. That path together with T would be a spanning two-cover. Hence every nonclosing terminal swallow has |E|>=4.

EXCLUDE |E|=4. The R171 lineage preserves the graph-intrinsic historical sign ancestry of the untouched support T. Let beta' be its retained exact sign witness. Since beta' lies outside T and H=J sqcup S sqcup T, we have beta' in E.

If |E|=4, construct an exact singleton-deletion two-cover H-z=Q sqcup T with |Q|=3 and V(Q) union {z}=E. For profile (1,3), take z to be the singleton S and Q=J. For (2,2), delete one S-vertex z and orient the other S-vertex together with the dimer J as a tight trimer Q by R3. For (3,1), delete one S-vertex z and orient the other two S-vertices together with singleton J as a tight trimer Q by R3. In each case Q sqcup T is exact because Hamiltonicity of H-z together with singleton z would two-cover H.

Apply accepted R594 to Q sqcup T, retaining the literal terminal order T=(t_0,...,t_m) as the long rail. In the surviving counterexample normalization R594 gives for every e in E

  (t_1,t_0,e) tight,      (e,t_m,t_{m-1}) tight.            (3)

Set e=beta'. If T is head-signed by beta', its retained sign contains (beta',t_0,t_1), while (3) contains the complete reversal (t_1,t_0,beta'), contradicting R3. If T is tail-signed by beta', its retained sign contains (t_{m-1},t_m,beta'), while (3) contains the complete reversal (beta',t_m,t_{m-1}), again contradicting R3. Therefore |E| is not four.

By (1),(2), every nonclosing terminal exterior E has order exactly five or six. If |E|=5 and E itself supports a Hamilton P5, that P5 together with T two-covers H. Otherwise accepted R192 applies to the proper tight carrier T with non-Hamiltonian five-vertex exterior E and yields the five-exterior four-of-five replacement-saturation gateway. If |E|=6, accepted R196 applies to T and E and yields the six-exterior four-root singleton fan.

Thus the finite chosen R171 continuation from the original small-complement balanced pair ends either in a spanning two-cover or in exactly the accepted R192/R196 five/six-exterior gateways, proving R229. No R24, R5, R168, R169, or R214 is used.

# R232 — Five-exterior dense-hole column bound

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Assume the non-Hamiltonian five-exterior equality face of R192, and put m=|V(K)|. Then there exists an exterior vertex z in E such that (E\\{z}) union {k} supports a tight P5 for at least ceil(4m/5) distinct carrier vertices k in V(K). Equivalently, one fixed exterior four-set F=E\\{z} has at least ceil(4m/5) distinct one-vertex carrier completions to tight P5 supports. In the post-R191 O3 equality face m>=6, so one common exterior four-set has at least five distinct carrier completions.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample; K is a proper tight path with five-vertex exterior E; E is non-Hamiltonian; accepted R192.

## Scope
Arbitrary-order support-incidence corollary of the R192 replacement grid.

## Applicability
Use when a single fixed exterior four-set is preferable to the row-wise R192 formulation. It gives a large common carrier-witness family over one physical four-set, suitable for sign/dimer pigeonhole or restoration tests.

## Persistence
The exterior hole z, fixed four-set F=E\\{z}, and all successful P5 supports F union {k} are graph-intrinsic.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert which z is dense, does not improve the 4/5 density fraction, does not synchronize P5 orderings, and does not imply any complementary carrier replacement.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Dense-hole column bound is the direct carrier-hole pigeonhole consequence of C185/R192: row density at least four-fifths implies some fixed hole succeeds on at least four-fifths of carrier vertices. Preserve R232 as a useful proof interface, but low independent discovery value.
- **Curation note:** Dense-hole column bound is the direct carrier-hole pigeonhole consequence of C185/R192: row density at least four-fifths implies some fixed hole succeeds on at least four-fifths of carrier vertices. Preserve R232 as a useful proof interface, but low independent discovery value.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Verified.

## Proof
For k in V(K) and z in E, call (k,z) successful when (E\\{z}) union {k} supports a tight P5. R192 gives at least four successful incidences in every carrier row, so the total number I of successful incidences satisfies I>=4m. There are exactly five exterior-hole columns. Hence some z has at least ceil(I/5)>=ceil(4m/5) successful carrier vertices. Taking F=E\\{z} gives the claimed fixed four-set. After R191, every surviving five-exterior equality face has |H|>10 and m=|H|-5>=6, so ceil(4m/5)>=5.

# R233 — Sharp five-exterior grid countermodel survives collision and restoration contact

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
There exists an eleven-vertex Level-(1) boundary-antisymmetric turn system with a tight carrier P6 K on vertices {0,1,2,3,4,5} and exterior E={6,7,8,9,10} such that: (i) E is non-Hamiltonian; (ii) for each carrier k exactly four of the five replacement supports (E\\{z}) union {k} are Hamiltonian, with failed holes f(0)=6, f(1)=7, f(2)=8, f(3)=9, f(4)=10, f(5)=10; hence the five hole-column sizes are 5,5,5,5,4 and the averaging bound ceil(4|K|/5)=5 is attained; (iii) every one of the thirty complementary carrier supports (K\\{k}) union {z} is non-Hamiltonian as a P6; (iv) the repeated exterior dimer (7,8) has same-side tight witness turns (7,8,1) and (7,8,2), arising inside successful replacement P5s, so it realizes the local same-polarity/two-witness pattern behind R207; and (v) applying the tail form of R164 to E0=(7,8) and witnesses 1,2 takes the reverse-contact alternative (2,1,8) tight, while the local restoration P4 (7,8,1,2) is blocked because (8,1,2) is bad. Thus the R192 replacement grid, an R207-type repeated signed exterior dimer, and the R164 restoration/contact dichotomy do not locally force any complementary carrier replacement. Any such global composition must use additional smallest-counterexample, carrier-position, ancestry, or representative information.

## Hypotheses
Only Level-(1) boundary antisymmetry is assumed for the explicit turn model. The claim is a local regression fence, not a smallest-counterexample model and not a refutation of a theorem that uses the full global hypotheses of R192/R207.

## Scope
Actual local countermodel for naive carrier-restoration compositions in the five-exterior program; simultaneously shows local sharpness of the R192 4/5 row density and the R232 column averaging bound at carrier order six.

## Applicability
Use to reject proof steps of the form replacement-grid plus repeated exterior-dimer collision plus bare R164 contact implies K-k+z Hamiltonian. A valid composition must retain extra structure not present in the local contracts, such as the positions of the two carrier witnesses along K, selected exact-cover incidence, ancestry, or a global extremality/minimality argument.

## Persistence
The countermodel is one fixed graph-intrinsic turn table. All positive and negative Hamiltonicity statements can be reconstructed by finite enumeration from the signature below.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not show a genuine smallest counterexample exists. Does not enforce absence of P7s or the universal exterior floor. Does not refute a carrier-restoration theorem using global-longestness plus additional carrier-order information. Does not claim the averaging bound is globally sharp for every carrier order.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Historical five-exterior grid countermodel; no live route depends on it.
- **Curation note:** Sharp countermodel: replacement-grid saturation plus collision/restoration contact still does not force carrier replacement.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Verified explicit regression countermodel.

## Proof
Let K={0,1,2,3,4,5}, E={6,7,8,9,10}. Encode the Level-(1) turn table as follows. For each unordered triple i<j<k, take the three reversal pairs A:(i,j,k)/(k,j,i), B:(i,k,j)/(j,k,i), C:(j,i,k)/(k,i,j). In lexicographic order of unordered triples and then A,B,C, let a bit 1 mean the displayed canonical order is tight and bit 0 mean its complete reversal is tight. The resulting 495-bit string, interpreted as an unsigned binary integer and left-padded to 124 hexadecimal digits, is 6b4ffffb4ffff3800050000924800bdbe9b6db6d58924e24936db401801f098924e24936db68bc0400a004124902351820924824b01c029040703dbe9c08. This chooses exactly one tight order in every reversal pair, hence satisfies boundary antisymmetry. Direct verification gives K=(0,1,2,3,4,5) tight and finds no tight P5 ordering on E. Exhausting all 120 orders of each replacement five-set gives exactly the successful-hole rows: k=0 succeeds for z=7,8,9,10; k=1 for z=6,8,9,10; k=2 for z=6,7,9,10; k=3 for z=6,7,8,10; k=4 for z=6,7,8,9; k=5 for z=6,7,8,9. Therefore every row has size four and the column sizes for z=6,7,8,9,10 are 5,5,5,5,4. Example certified P5s include (10,7,8,1,9) on (E\\{6}) union {1} and (10,9,7,8,2) on (E\\{6}) union {2}; these contain the tight turns (7,8,1) and (7,8,2), respectively, putting the same oriented exterior dimer (7,8) under two distinct same-side carrier witnesses. In the same table (8,1,2) is bad and its reverse (2,1,8) is tight. Thus R164 applied in tail form to retained dimer path (7,8) and witnesses 1,2 takes the reverse-contact branch, not the P4 restoration branch. Finally, exhaustive enumeration of all 720 orders on each of the thirty six-sets (K\\{k}) union {z}, k in K, z in E, finds no tight P6. Hence the local replacement/collision/restoration data coexist with total complementary carrier-swap failure, as claimed.

# R234 — Five-exterior replacement family may have a universal failed hole locally

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
There exists an eleven-vertex Level-(1) boundary-antisymmetric turn system with a tight carrier P6 K={0,1,2,3,4,5} and exterior E={6,7,8,9,10} such that E is non-Hamiltonian, and for every carrier vertex k the four replacement supports (E\\{z}) union {k} are Hamiltonian exactly for z in {7,8,9,10}, while the replacement support (E\\{6}) union {k} is non-Hamiltonian for every k. Thus one exterior vertex can be a universal failed hole across the entire carrier even while every R192 row has exactly four successes. The same model can simultaneously have every complementary carrier six-set (K\\{k}) union {z} non-Hamiltonian. Therefore neither Level-(1) boundary antisymmetry nor the row-wise four-of-five replacement pattern forces global coverage of all five exterior holes.

## Hypotheses
Only Level-(1) boundary antisymmetry is assumed for the explicit local turn model. This is not asserted to be a genuine smallest-counterexample equality frame.

## Scope
Local sharpness fence for coverage conjectures about the five-exterior replacement family.

## Applicability
Use to reject arguments that infer every exterior hole is successful for at least one carrier vertex merely from R192-type row density or local turn constraints. Any theorem forcing the fifth hole to appear must use additional global-smallest-counterexample, longest-carrier, ancestry, or exact-cover structure.

## Persistence
The countermodel is one fixed graph-intrinsic turn table; all Hamiltonicity statements are finitely reconstructible from the displayed signature.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not refute the possibility that full smallest-counterexample hypotheses force all five holes globally. Does not assert a universal failed hole exists in every R192 frame. Does not improve or weaken the accepted R232 dense-column lower bound.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Historical five-exterior universal-hole countermodel; no live route depends on it.
- **Curation note:** Sharp countermodel showing a universal failed exterior hole can persist across all replacement rows.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Verified explicit universal-failed-hole countermodel.

## Proof
Let K={0,1,2,3,4,5}, E={6,7,8,9,10}. Encode the turn table by the same convention used in R233: for each unordered triple i<j<k, the three canonical reversal-pair representatives are A=(i,j,k), B=(i,k,j), C=(j,i,k); list bits in lexicographic unordered-triple order and then A,B,C, with 1 meaning the canonical order is tight and 0 meaning its complete reversal is tight. The 495-bit table, interpreted as an unsigned binary integer and left-padded to 124 hexadecimal digits, is 5fbdb6d400000c0924fb6da49264137278a6ffffc0000000000001200e016c0924fb6da49240235278c92480000100406c00001042436600390582037395. This defines exactly one tight order in every reversal pair. Direct finite enumeration verifies K=(0,1,2,3,4,5) is tight and E has no tight P5. For each k=0,...,5, exhaustive enumeration of the five replacement supports shows success exactly for holes z=7,8,9,10 and failure for z=6. Hence the hole-column counts are 0,6,6,6,6. The same exhaustive check of all 720 orders on each six-set (K\\{k}) union {z}, for all thirty pairs (k,z), finds no tight P6. Thus one exterior hole can be absent from the entire local replacement family despite exact four-of-five row saturation, as claimed.

# R235 — Reverse-terminal restoration cannot be silently spliced into the forward carrier

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Let K=(k0,k1,...,km) be a proper globally longest path and apply the R215 collision web on its left terminal physical dimer in the reverse orientation D=(k1,k0). For two exterior witnesses e,f, R164 may be applied to the tight extensions (D,e) and (D,f), yielding either the local restored P4 (k1,k0,e,f) up to witness order, or the corresponding bounded reverse-contact trimer. Neither R164 alternative is a forward-carrier extension merely from these hypotheses: the retained dimer is oriented k1,k0, whereas the forward carrier seam is k0,k1. Strong Level-(1) tightness does not license reversing the carrier or cyclically rereading turns. Therefore any R215+R164 composition that grafts the restoration output back onto K requires an additional orientation/bridge theorem; physical equality of the terminal dimer is insufficient. The right-end statement is dual.

## Hypotheses
Accepted R164 and R215; K is read in its displayed forward orientation. No additional carrier-reversal or seam-bridge theorem is assumed.

## Scope
Applicability/orientation fence for proposed carrier-restoration compositions in the arbitrary-order program.

## Applicability
Use whenever R164 is invoked on an R215 reverse terminal dimer. The local restoration/contact output is valid, but downstream arguments must separately prove compatibility with the forward carrier before calling it a carrier extension, carrier replacement, or exterior descent.

## Persistence
The physical terminal dimer and both orientations are graph-intrinsic labels. The distinction between the reverse signed orientation and the forward carrier order must be retained across historical use.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not say the R164 output is useless, does not forbid a separate bridge from converting it into carrier progress, and does not invalidate R164 or R215. It only forbids an unproved direct splice based on physical-support identity.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Historical reverse-terminal restoration warning; modern complete-seam rules provide the active guardrail.
- **Curation note:** Orientation correction: reverse terminal support equality does not license silent forward-carrier splicing.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Verified.

## Proof
At the left end of K=(k0,k1,k2,...), R215 fixes the reverse-oriented physical terminal dimer D=(k1,k0). For any exterior witnesses e,f the corresponding same-polarity signed turns are of the tail-extension form (k1,k0,e) and (k1,k0,f), after naming the polarity consistently with R215. R164 applied to the retained path E=D therefore tests the turn e f k0 (equivalently after the theorem naming, one gets either a four-path beginning with the ordered dimer k1,k0 and then the two witnesses, or the exact antisymmetric reverse-contact trimer). In the P4 branch the first two vertices remain k1,k0. The displayed forward carrier K begins k0,k1 and its next certified turn is k0 k1 k2; there is no accepted rule allowing the ordered pair k1,k0 to be substituted for k0,k1, nor does boundary antisymmetry permit cyclic rereading. In the contact branch the output is only the bounded three-vertex contact recorded by R164. Hence neither branch alone produces a literal forward extension or replacement of K. The right endpoint is identical after reversing left/right notation.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/LEGACY/R235.md -->

# R236 — Global-longest full carrier insertion-obstruction clauses

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Let K=(v_0,...,v_m) be a globally longest tight path in a Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament and let w be exterior to K. For each gap i between v_i and v_{i+1}, inserting w into that gap cannot yield a tight path of order |K|+1. Hence among the newly required turns A_i=(v_{i-1},v_i,w) when i>=1, B_i=(v_i,w,v_{i+1}), and C_i=(w,v_{i+1},v_{i+2}) when i+2<=m, at least one present turn is bad. Equivalently, by boundary antisymmetry, at least one of the exact reverse turns (w,v_i,v_{i-1}), (v_{i+1},w,v_i), (v_{i+2},v_{i+1},w), with the same boundary omissions, is tight. Thus every exterior vertex carries a complete gap-indexed family of two-way endpoint clauses and three-way internal reverse-turn clauses along the full ordered carrier.

## Hypotheses
Strong Level-(1) boundary antisymmetry; K is globally longest; w is outside K.

## Scope
Order-free global-longestness lemma. It extends terminal endpoint shielding from the two ends to every insertion gap of the retained carrier, but records clauses rather than choosing one tight mate in each gap.

## Applicability
Use when a proof needs carrier-position information missing from endpoint-only collision webs. The gap clauses can be combined with fixed exterior replacement supports, exact-cover crossings, or literal mate/candidate certificates to seek a carrier-aware forcing chain.

## Persistence
The ordered carrier K, exterior vertex w, and each finite disjunction of reverse-turn certificates are graph-intrinsic. A particular disjunct is not selected unless separately forced.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert which reverse turn is tight at any gap; does not by itself produce a longer carrier, a replacement path, a path-cover clause admissible to R173, or simultaneous selected turns. Physical Mate-Cycle forcing still requires its own literal candidate-cover hypotheses.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** The full carrier insertion-obstruction clauses are a mechanically repeated longestness-plus-R3 observation at each gap. Inline the gap test when needed rather than keep a first-class lemma.
- **Curation note:** The full carrier insertion-obstruction clauses are a mechanically repeated longestness-plus-R3 observation at each gap. Inline the gap test when needed rather than keep a first-class lemma.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Valid global-longest insertion-obstruction clause family.

## Proof
Fix i. The proposed inserted ordering is (v_0,...,v_i,w,v_{i+1},...,v_m). Every old consecutive triple of K remains unchanged except those meeting the insertion site. These are exactly A_i when i>=1, B_i always, and C_i when i+2<=m. If all present changed turns were tight, the inserted ordering would be a tight path on |K|+1 vertices, contradicting global longestness. Therefore at least one present changed turn is bad. Strong Level-(1) boundary antisymmetry makes its complete reversal tight, giving the displayed reverse-turn disjunction. The endpoint gaps have two changed turns; internal gaps have three.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/LEGACY/R236.md -->

# R237 — Five-exterior dense column contains a consecutive triple

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Assume the non-Hamiltonian five-exterior equality face and let K=(k_1,...,k_m), m>=6, have exterior E. Then there is a hole z in E and three consecutive carrier vertices k_i,k_{i+1},k_{i+2} such that each of the three five-sets (E\\{z}) union {k_i}, (E\\{z}) union {k_{i+1}}, and (E\\{z}) union {k_{i+2}} supports a tight P5.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in the five-exterior equality face; E is non-Hamiltonian; accepted dense-hole column bound R232.

## Scope
Pure carrier-order refinement of R232. No sign, payment, currentization, or P5-order synchronization is used.

## Applicability
Use when downstream arguments need the fixed exterior four-core completions to meet actual consecutive positions of the globally-longest carrier, rather than an unordered carrier subset.

## Persistence
The hole z, the three physical carrier vertices, their carrier adjacency/turn, and the three P5 supports are graph-intrinsic.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not synchronize the three P5 orderings, does not imply a P6 on their union, does not force a complementary carrier replacement, and does not by itself defeat the R233/R234 local countermodels without additional global-longest or exact-cover structure.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Consecutive-triple dense-column lemma is a useful positional corollary of the five-exterior column bound but has no live consumers and does not synchronize P5 orderings. Keep as proof history rather than a first-class discovery.
- **Curation note:** Consecutive-triple dense-column lemma is a useful positional corollary of the five-exterior column bound but has no live consumers and does not synchronize P5 orderings. Keep as proof history rather than a first-class discovery.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Valid consecutive-triple consequence of R232.

## Proof
Let t be the number of failures in the dense column. Then t<=floor(m/5). If no three consecutive positions succeed, every block of three carrier positions contains a failure, so t>=floor(m/3) for the disjoint blocks (1,2,3),(4,5,6),.... For m>=6, floor(m/3)>floor(m/5), contradiction. Therefore some three consecutive positions all succeed, yielding the displayed three P5 supports over the same four-set E-{z}.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/LEGACY/R237.md -->

# R240 — Five-exterior common-four-core cross-replacement saturation

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Let H be a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in the five-exterior equality face. Let S be a four-vertex set and let a,b be distinct vertices outside S such that E_a=S∪{a} and E_b=S∪{b} are both exteriors of global-longest tight paths. Then for every s∈S the five-set Q_s=(S\\{s})∪{a,b} supports a tight P5. Equivalently, in the R192 replacement row for carrier vertex b relative to exterior E_a, the unique failed hole is a; symmetrically, in the row for carrier vertex a relative to E_b, the unique failed hole is b. The complementary sets V(H)\\Q_s=(V(H)\\E_a\\{b})∪{s} are therefore non-Hamiltonian as single tight paths, since otherwise Q_s together with its complement would span H by two tight paths. More generally, if x_S=r longest-carrier exteriors contain S, then every unordered pair of their completion vertices produces four distinct cross-replacement P5 supports, for a total of 4*binom(r,2) distinct P5 supports localized on the same physical four-core.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in the five-exterior equality face; accepted five-exterior four-of-five replacement saturation R192; S is a physical four-set; E_a=S∪{a} and E_b=S∪{b} are exteriors of global-longest tight paths.

## Scope
Arbitrary-order structural localization of high four-core occupancy in the five-exterior equality face. It uses actual longest-carrier exteriors, not merely local Hamiltonian five-sets.

## Applicability
Use when a physical four-core has occupancy at least two in the longest-carrier exterior family. It converts each pair of completions into four explicit P5 supports and identifies the exact failed-hole relation in both neighboring R192 rows. This is compatible with R231 occupancy counting and supplies concrete support packets for R239-style exact-frame capture or further carrier-coupling arguments.

## Persistence
The four-core S, completion vertices, longest-carrier exterior memberships, failed-hole identities, P5 supports Q_s, and complementary non-Hamiltonicity are graph-intrinsic. No simultaneous currentness of the corresponding global-longest carrier representatives is asserted.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not synchronize P5 orderings, does not assert a P6, does not force the complementary carrier replacements to be tight, does not currentize captures across different roots, and does not by itself close the five-exterior equality face.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Five-exterior common-four-core cross-replacement saturation now has no current active consumer and is specialized branch geometry; preserve proof history, retire canonical identity.
- **Curation note:** Five-exterior common-four-core cross-replacement saturation now has no current active consumer and is specialized branch geometry; preserve proof history, retire canonical identity.
- **Review status:** accepted

## Proof
Fix S and distinct completion vertices a,b with E_a=S∪{a} and E_b=S∪{b} both exteriors of global-longest tight paths. Since H is a counterexample, neither E_a nor E_b can itself support a tight P5: if E_b did, then by definition its complement K_b=V(H)\\E_b is a global-longest tight path, and K_b together with the P5 on E_b would be a spanning two-cover. Let K_a=V(H)\\E_a. Because b∉E_a, the vertex b lies on K_a. Apply R192 to the five-exterior frame (K_a,E_a) and the carrier vertex b. Among the five replacement supports (E_a\\{z})∪{b}, z∈E_a, at least four support tight P5s. For z=a this replacement is exactly S∪{b}=E_b, which is non-Hamiltonian by the preceding paragraph. Therefore z=a is the unique failed hole in this row, and for every s∈S the replacement (E_a\\{s})∪{b}=(S\\{s})∪{a,b} supports a tight P5. Interchanging a and b gives the symmetric failed-hole statement. For any s∈S, if the complementary set V(H)\\Q_s supported one tight path, that path together with the tight P5 on Q_s would be a spanning two-cover, impossible; hence the complement is non-Hamiltonian as one path. Finally, if A_S={x:S∪{x} is a longest-carrier exterior} has size r, the supports (S\\{s})∪{a,b} are distinct for distinct choices of s∈S and unordered {a,b}⊂A_S, yielding exactly 4*binom(r,2) distinct localized P5 supports.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/LEGACY/R240.md -->

# R242 — Occupied four-core produces a common-substitute global-longest carrier fiber

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Assume the five-exterior equality face and let S be a physical four-set with occupancy x_S=r in the family Ecal of exteriors of global-longest carriers. Let A={a outside S : S union {a} is in Ecal} and U=V(H)\\S, so |A|=r. For every a in A, the complement K_a=U\\{a} supports a global-longest tight path. Moreover U itself is non-Hamiltonian and K_a sqcup {a} is therefore an exact two-cover of H[U]. For any distinct a,b in A one has the literal support identity K_b=(K_a\\{b}) union {a}; hence, relative to the retained carrier K_a, every b in A\\{a} is a genuine common-substitute swap position: replacing b by the single fixed vertex a yields another global-longest carrier support. In addition, R240 gives that in the R192 row of b relative to exterior S union {a}, the failed hole is exactly a and all four holes s in S succeed.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in the five-exterior equality face; S is a four-set with occupancy r in the global-longest exterior family; accepted R240.

## Scope
Arbitrary-order structural bridge from four-core occupancy to physical carrier geometry. It converts one occupied Johnson clique into a common-substitute family of actual global-longest carrier supports and exact Hamilton-plus-singleton covers of one fixed subsystem.

## Applicability
Use when an occupancy argument identifies a four-core S with many completions. Fixing one completion a turns all other completion vertices into physical positions of one retained carrier K_a that can each be swapped for the same substitute a while preserving global-longest support. The exact subsystem U=V(H)\\S is common to the whole fiber.

## Persistence
S, A, U, all carrier supports K_a, their global-longest status, and all support identities are graph-intrinsic. A chosen tight ordering of each K_a is representative data; no synchronization of those orderings is asserted.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert compatible orientations of the different global-longest carriers, does not make their path representatives simultaneous, does not force U itself to be Hamiltonian, and does not by itself yield a spanning two-cover or carrier extension. The Hamilton-plus-singleton covers are exact covers of the proper subsystem U, not of H.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Occupied-four-core common-substitute carrier fiber is a specialized equality-program parent with no current consumers; not broad enough for the tightened canonical surface.
- **Curation note:** Occupied-four-core common-substitute carrier fiber is a specialized equality-program parent with no current consumers; not broad enough for the tightened canonical surface.
- **Review status:** accepted

## Proof
Put A={a:S union {a} in Ecal} and U=V(H)-S. For each a in A, by definition of Ecal there is a global-longest tight path whose exterior is E_a=S union {a}. Its support is the set-theoretic complement K_a=V(H)-E_a=U-{a}. In the equality face every global-longest path has order |H|-5=|U|-1. If U itself were Hamiltonian, H would contain a tight path of order |U|=|H|-4, contradicting global longestness. Hence the displayed cover U=K_a sqcup {a} has path-cover number exactly two. Now fix distinct a,b in A. Since K_a=U-{a} contains b and K_b=U-{b}, set algebra gives K_b=(K_a-{b}) union {a}. Thus one and the same exterior completion vertex a is a valid one-for-one substitute for every other completion b on K_a, always producing another global-longest carrier support. Finally, R240 applied to E_a and E_b says that relative to E_a the R192 replacement row indexed by carrier vertex b fails exactly at hole a and succeeds at every s in S.

# R243 — Five-exterior longest-carrier Johnson sparsity and spectral ceiling

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Let H be a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample of order n in the five-exterior equality face, and let Ecal be the family of five-sets occurring as exteriors of global-longest tight paths. For every physical four-set S put x_S=|{E in Ecal:S subset E}|. Then (i) sum_S x_S=5|Ecal|; (ii) the Johnson-edge count inside Ecal is sum_S binom(x_S,2), because every pair of five-sets with intersection four has a unique common four-core; (iii) R192 local sparsity gives sum_S x_S(x_S-1)<= (n-5)|Ecal|, hence sum_S x_S^2<=n|Ecal|. Consequently Cauchy gives |Ecal| <= [n/(5(n-4))] binom(n,5). Equivalently, the same global ceiling previously obtained spectrally follows from the edge-disjoint clique decomposition J(n,5)=union_S K_{n-4}.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in the five-exterior equality face; accepted R192 local four-of-five replacement saturation, hence the accepted Johnson local-degree bound for Ecal.

## Scope
Arbitrary-order structural extremal theorem at the five-exterior floor. This is a four-core occupancy reformulation and proof of the R231 ceiling; no Johnson eigenvalues or association-scheme calculation is needed.

## Applicability
Use when global counting must remain physically localized. The variables x_S identify concrete overloaded four-cores and can be combined directly with R240 cross-replacement packets or R239/R241 capture machinery.

## Persistence
Ecal and every occupancy x_S are graph-intrinsic finite-set data. The identities and inequalities are purely combinatorial.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not supply a lower bound on |Ecal| or on any individual x_S, does not assert occupancy uniformity, and does not by itself close the equality face. It strengthens the proof architecture, not the numerical ceiling.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Five-exterior Johnson sparsity/spectral ceiling is specialized zero-consumer proof technology; preserve historical route, not first-class canonical visibility.
- **Curation note:** Five-exterior Johnson sparsity/spectral ceiling is specialized zero-consumer proof technology; preserve historical route, not first-class canonical visibility.
- **Review status:** accepted

## Proof
Write N=|Ecal|. Each exterior E contains exactly five four-subsets, so summing incidences (S,E) gives sum_S x_S=5N. Two distinct five-sets are adjacent in J(n,5) exactly when they share four vertices, and that common four-set is unique. Therefore the induced Johnson-edge count on Ecal is e(Ecal)=sum_S binom(x_S,2). Accepted R192 local sparsity says every E in Ecal has at most n-5 neighbors in Ecal, so 2e(Ecal)<= (n-5)N. Hence sum_S x_S(x_S-1)<= (n-5)N. Adding sum_S x_S=5N gives sum_S x_S^2<=nN. There are binom(n,4) physical four-sets. By Cauchy, 25N^2=(sum_S x_S)^2<=binom(n,4) sum_S x_S^2<=binom(n,4)nN. Since N>0, N<=n binom(n,4)/25. Using binom(n,5)=binom(n,4)(n-4)/5 yields N<=[n/(5(n-4))]binom(n,5). This is exactly the former spectral ceiling, now with the occupancy profile retained.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/LEGACY/R243.md -->

# R245 — Occupied four-core Hamilton-five support cascade

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Assume the five-exterior equality face and let S be a four-core with completion set A={a:S union {a} is a global-longest exterior}, |A|=r. Then: (1) for every distinct a,b in A, the six-set S union {a,b} has exactly four Hamiltonian five-subsets, namely (S\\{s}) union {a,b} for s in S; the two remaining five-subsets S union {a} and S union {b} are non-Hamiltonian. Equivalently, for every s and every tight trimer orientation of S\\{s}, R146 applied with exterior triple {a,b,s} is forced to exit through the unique cross-support (S\\{s}) union {a,b}. (2) For every three distinct completions a,b,c in A there are at least two distinct physical pairs R subset S such that R union {a,b,c} supports a tight P5. Consequently S union A contains at least 4*binom(r,2) distinct Hamilton five-supports of type 3-core+2-completion and at least 2*binom(r,3) distinct Hamilton five-supports of type 2-core+3-completion.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in the five-exterior equality face; accepted R240 cross-replacement saturation, R195 four-of-six Hamilton-five density, R146 disjoint-trimer three-extension forcing, and R8 trimer existence.

## Scope
Pure graph-intrinsic support cascade localized on one occupied physical four-core. No carrier-order synchronization, exact-cover currentization, sign payment, or spectral argument is used.

## Applicability
Use when a high-occupancy four-core must be converted into a richer local Hamilton-support packet. The second layer supplies supports containing three completion vertices, which may be used for carrier-carrier signed-dimer or insertion-obstruction arguments unavailable from pairwise R240 cells alone.

## Persistence
S, A and every listed five-support are graph-intrinsic. The P5 orderings witnessing Hamiltonicity need not be synchronized.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not force a P6, does not make any listed support a longest-carrier exterior, does not synchronize P5 orderings, and does not imply type 1-core+4-completion supports are Hamiltonian.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Derived Hamilton-five support cascade inside one occupied four-core. The counting layers follow from R240/R195/R146 and have no live consumers; retain inside proof history while C232 remains the structural active interface.
- **Curation note:** Derived Hamilton-five support cascade inside one occupied four-core. The counting layers follow from R240/R195/R146 and have no live consumers; retain inside proof history while C232 remains the structural active interface.
- **Review status:** accepted

## Proof
Fix a!=b in A. R240 says Q_s=(S-{s}) union {a,b} is Hamiltonian for every s in S. The other two five-subsets of W=S union {a,b} are E_a=S union {a} and E_b=S union {b}; each is the exterior of a global-longest carrier, hence cannot be Hamiltonian, since otherwise that exterior path together with its complementary carrier would be a spanning two-cover. Thus W has exactly the four cross Hamiltonian five-subsets. Now fix s. By R8 orient S-{s} as a tight trimer and apply R146 with the three exterior vertices a,b,s. Its three candidate P5 supports are E_a,E_b,Q_s. Since the first two are non-Hamiltonian, the R146 conclusion is forced to Q_s. For part (2), fix distinct a,b,c in A and a three-subset T of S. In W_T=T union {a,b,c}, the three five-subsets T union {b,c}, T union {a,c}, T union {a,b} are Hamiltonian by part (1), because T=S-{s} for the unique s outside T. Accepted R195 says W_T has at least four Hamiltonian five-subsets. Therefore at least one of the other three five-subsets, obtained by omitting a vertex t of T, is Hamiltonian; it has the form (T-{t}) union {a,b,c}=R union {a,b,c} for a pair R subset T. This holds for each of the four triples T subset S. One fixed pair R subset S is contained in exactly two of those four triples, so a single successful R cannot serve all four T; at least two distinct successful core pairs are required for the fixed completion triple. Counting over completion pairs/triples gives the stated distinct-support totals.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/LEGACY/R245.md -->

# R246 — Common-substitute aligned-swap obstruction clauses

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Assume the five-exterior equality face. Let S be a four-core with two completions a,b, let E_a=S union {a}, and choose a tight ordering K=(k_0,...,k_{m-1}) of the complementary global-longest carrier K_a. Suppose b=k_i. The neighboring exterior E_b=S union {b} has complementary global-longest support (K_a\\{b}) union {a}. Form the order-preserving swap candidate K[i:a]=(k_0,...,k_{i-1},a,k_{i+1},...,k_{m-1}). Then either K[i:a] is tight, hence is an explicitly orientation-synchronized global-longest realization of the E_b-complement, or at least one present reverse-turn blocker is tight: (a,k_{i-1},k_{i-2}) when i>=2; (k_{i+1},a,k_{i-1}) when 1<=i<=m-2; (k_{i+2},k_{i+1},a) when i<=m-3. At endpoints the clause has the corresponding single new turn, and one step from an endpoint it has the corresponding two turns. Thus every common-substitute swap position carries either an aligned longest-carrier swap or a localized one-of-at-most-three reverse-turn certificate.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in the five-exterior equality face; E_a and E_b are two global-longest exteriors sharing the physical four-core S; accepted boundary antisymmetry R3 and R240 support identity.

## Scope
Order-free carrier-order refinement of four-core occupancy. This is the one-for-one replacement analogue of R236 insertion obstruction and keeps the original carrier order explicit.

## Applicability
Use on the common-substitute carrier fiber generated by an occupied four-core. Aligned outcomes synchronize actual neighboring global-longest carriers with the retained K order; failed outcomes produce exact reverse turns at the deleted position that can be combined with R236 gap clauses, capture ancestry, or restoration tests.

## Persistence
K and its displayed order are the chosen retained carrier; S,a,b and the support identity of the neighboring carrier are graph-intrinsic. Each reverse-turn alternative is graph-intrinsic. The disjunction does not select one blocker unless further information is supplied.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert the order-preserving swap is always tight, does not identify which reverse blocker occurs when it fails, and does not by itself produce a longer carrier. Tightness of some other ordering on the swapped support is already known but is not used to infer the displayed ordering.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Common-substitute aligned-swap obstruction clauses are a narrow zero-consumer carrier-order refinement; retire.
- **Curation note:** Common-substitute aligned-swap obstruction clauses are a narrow zero-consumer carrier-order refinement; retire.
- **Review status:** accepted

## Proof
Write b=k_i. The path K[i:a] has the same ordered vertices as K except at position i. Every consecutive triple not meeting position i is therefore already tight. The only new triples are L_i=(k_{i-2},k_{i-1},a) when i>=2, M_i=(k_{i-1},a,k_{i+1}) when 1<=i<=m-2, and R_i=(a,k_{i+1},k_{i+2}) when i<=m-3, with the evident boundary omissions. If all present triples are tight, K[i:a] is a tight Hamilton ordering of the support (K_a-{b}) union {a}; R240 identifies this support as the complement of E_b, so it is global-longest. Otherwise some present new triple is bad. Boundary antisymmetry R3 turns its complete reversal tight, giving respectively (a,k_{i-1},k_{i-2}), (k_{i+1},a,k_{i-1}), or (k_{i+2},k_{i+1},a). No other turns are needed or claimed.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/LEGACY/R246.md -->

# R247 — Aligned common-substitute swap yields a bidirectional signed-dimer floor fork

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Assume the five-exterior equality face. Let E_a=S union {a} and E_b=S union {b} be two global-longest exteriors sharing the four-core S, let K=(...,u,b,v,...) be a tight ordering of the E_a-complement with b internal, and suppose the order-preserving swap K[b:a] obtained by replacing b with a is tight. Then the physical swap dimer {a,b} is signed in both orientations by named inherited turns with witnesses among u,v: global longestness of K forces one of (b,a,u) or (v,b,a) tight, and independently one of (a,b,u) or (v,a,b) tight. Consequently, choosing any tight trimer T inside S, one may pair either signed orientation of {a,b} with an opposite-polarity terminal signed dimer of T to obtain a direct mass-four balanced pair. Applying the accepted inherited-turn endpoint-selective paid-floor continuation gives two separate lawful alternatives: either a spanning two-cover occurs or an ancestry-bearing mass-two floor is reached with singleton (a) as one literal floor coordinate; and, in a separate lineage, either a spanning two-cover occurs or such a floor is reached with singleton (b) as one literal floor coordinate.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in the five-exterior equality face; E_a and E_b share a four-core S; K is a globally-longest carrier complementary to E_a; b is internal on the chosen K order; the order-preserving swap b->a is tight; accepted R3, R8, R39, and R224.

## Scope
Carrier-order/signed-payment consequence of an orientation-aligned common-substitute swap. The two endpoint-selective paid floors are alternative lineages, not simultaneous current states.

## Applicability
Use after an aligned outcome of the common-substitute swap obstruction. It converts a purely carrier-order synchronization into a named bidirectional signed dimer and controlled floor ancestry preserving either the substitute vertex or the replaced carrier vertex.

## Persistence
The physical vertices a,b,u,v, the two inherited sign turns on {a,b}, and the chosen endpoint identity in each R224 continuation persist as historical ancestry. The direct balanced-pair realization and resulting floors belong to separate chosen descendants; simultaneous currentness is not asserted.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not synchronize the two endpoint-selective floors, does not prescribe the second floor singleton, does not feed the mass-two floor directly into R171 contrary to R214, and does not by itself close the equality face.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Aligned common-substitute signed-dimer floor fork is a narrow zero-consumer specialization; preserve as history.
- **Curation note:** Aligned common-substitute signed-dimer floor fork is a narrow zero-consumer specialization; preserve as history.
- **Review status:** accepted

## Proof
Write the local carrier segment as (...,u,b,v,...), with the evident endpoint truncations outside u,v. The aligned swap hypothesis says (...,u,a,v,...) is a tight path on the neighboring global-longest support. Consider first the path obtained from K by inserting a immediately before b, so its local segment is (...,u,a,b,v,...). Every turn away from this local segment is inherited from K; the outer seam on the u side is inherited from the aligned swap and the outer seam on the v side is inherited from K. Thus the only uncertified local turns are uab and abv. If both were tight, the resulting path would contain all vertices of K plus a, contradicting global longestness. Hence uab is bad or abv is bad. By R3, respectively bau or vba is tight. Either turn signs the physical orientation (b,a), with named witness u or v. Now insert a immediately after b, giving (...,u,b,a,v,...). The only uncertified turns are uba and bav, because the u-side outer seam is inherited from K and the v-side outer seam from the aligned swap. Global longestness forces one bad; R3 gives respectively abu or vab tight, signing the opposite physical orientation (a,b). Thus {a,b} is bidirectionally signed by named inherited turns. Choose any three vertices of S and orient them as a tight trimer by R8. Its two terminal dimers have opposite polarities. For either chosen sign on {a,b}, select the disjoint terminal dimer of opposite polarity; R39 gives a direct mass-four balanced pair. Since the {a,b} sign comes from a named inherited turn, R224 applies. Using the endpoint-selective channel preserving a gives either a two-cover or a mass-two floor with (a) literal; choosing the separate endpoint-selective channel preserving b gives the analogous alternative with (b) literal. The two continuations are not combined.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/LEGACY/R247.md -->

# R248 — Every longest-carrier exterior vertex is selectable at the paid floor

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Let H be a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample and let K=(k_1,...,k_m), m>=2, be a proper globally longest tight path with exterior E. Fix any prescribed exterior vertex a in E. Then either H already has a spanning two-cover, or there is an ancestry-bearing mass-two balanced-pair floor in which singleton (a) is literally one floor coordinate. The construction is endpoint-local: R199 gives the tight reverse endpoint turn (k_2,k_1,a), whose terminal dimer (k_1,a) is head-signed by k_2. Choose any three vertices of E\\{a} and orient them as a tight trimer by R8; its tail-signed terminal dimer is disjoint from {k_1,a}. R39 gives a direct mass-four balanced pair, and R224 applied to the named inherited turn selects the endpoint a through payment to the mass-two floor. The right endpoint gives the dual construction.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample; K is proper and globally longest of order at least two; a lies outside K; accepted R199, R8, R39, and R224.

## Scope
Order-free prescribed-exterior-vertex floor-selection theorem. No five-exterior equality, four-core occupancy, order-ten geometry, or simultaneous-currentness assumption is used.

## Applicability
Use whenever downstream fixed-turn, capture, or ancestry machinery needs a chosen physical exterior vertex to survive all the way to the mass-two floor. In a five-exterior equality frame, every one of the five exterior vertices is separately selectable.

## Persistence
The prescribed physical vertex a, the endpoint reverse turn, the selected endpoint-refund channel, and the literal floor coordinate (a) persist in the chosen lineage. The opposite floor singleton and the source carrier representative need not persist.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Different choices of a produce separate alternative lineages and are not simultaneous. Does not prescribe the second floor singleton, does not currentize the floor into R171 contrary to R214, and does not by itself close the conjecture.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** R248 is a longest-carrier paid-floor coordinate specialization with no live consumers; broader preserved-coordinate machinery now supplies coordinate access without this route.
- **Curation note:** Prescribed exterior floor-selection is reusable payment machinery, not current spine.
- **Review status:** accepted

## Proof
Fix a in E. R199 gives (k_2,k_1,a) tight at the left end of K. The terminal physical dimer D=(k_1,a) is therefore head-signed by the named witness k_2. Since every proper tight path in a smallest counterexample leaves at least five exterior vertices, E-{a} has at least four vertices; choose any three of them and orient that triple T=(t_0,t_1,t_2) as a tight trimer by R8. Its left terminal dimer (t_0,t_1) is tail-signed by t_2 and is vertex-disjoint from D. Thus D and (t_0,t_1) are disjoint opposite-polarity signed supports of total mass four, so R39 gives a direct balanced-pair lineage unless a spanning two-cover has already occurred. The sign on D comes from the named inherited turn (k_2,k_1,a). Apply R224 and choose the endpoint-selective refund channel whose surviving endpoint is a. R224 yields either a spanning two-cover or an ancestry-bearing mass-two floor in which (a) is literally one singleton coordinate. No claim is made about the identity of the other singleton or about simultaneous floors for different exterior vertices.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/LEGACY/R248.md -->

# R249 — Adaptive floor-aligned fixed-turn universal front door

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Let H be a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample. More strongly than the original existential formulation: given any ancestry-bearing mass-two balanced-pair floor whose two singleton supports are {a} and {c}, choose any vertex b distinct from a,c. Exactly one of (a,b,c) and (c,b,a) is a tight proper turn J by boundary antisymmetry. Its unordered outer pair is exactly the floor pair {a,c}. Entering the R172 pair-bearing fixed-turn lineage at this floor with no pre-entry capture credit gives Psi_J=(2,0,0). Hence every first quiet, nonclosing, non-exit macro step retaining J must strictly lower epsilon_J and therefore acquire at least one of the two floor vertices a,c as a captured outer endpoint before pair-mass remint or target-distance debt can be charged. In particular, the original R198 existential front door follows by first producing any mass-two floor.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample; an ancestry-bearing mass-two floor with singleton supports {a},{c} is given; accepted R3 and R172. The standard smallest-counterexample size floor guarantees a third vertex b and properness of the chosen turn.

## Scope
Order-free universal conditional strengthening of R198. The floor-to-turn step works for every ancestry-bearing mass-two floor, not merely the specific floor produced in the original proof.

## Applicability
Use after any endpoint-selective or prescribed-coordinate floor construction, including R224/R248. A chosen floor vertex automatically becomes one outer target of a fixed-turn lineage; the first quiet step must capture one of the two floor coordinates.

## Persistence
The given floor pair, chosen proper turn J, and its outer target pair are retained in the chosen lineage. No pre-entry capture is credited. Later conclusions remain lineage-relative as in R172.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not guarantee which of the two floor vertices is captured first, does not preserve an earlier source representative, does not make Psi global across turn changes, and does not assert explicit R172 exits close the conjecture.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** R249 is an old floor-aligned fixed-turn front door with no live consumer; payment/fixed-turn routing is no longer a current frontier.
- **Curation note:** Versatile floor-to-fixed-turn interface with exact initial clock and first-quiet-capture behavior.
- **Review status:** accepted

## Proof
Let the given ancestry-bearing mass-two floor have singleton supports {a} and {c}. First observe directly, without any deletion-floor theorem, that a counterexample H must have at least five vertices. Indeed every vertex set of size at most four can be partitioned into at most two parts of size at most two, and every singleton or ordered dimer is vacuously a tight path; hence pc(H)<=2 for |H|<=4. Thus choose b distinct from a,c. Since |H|>=5, the three-set {a,b,c} is a proper subset of V(H). By R3 exactly one of (a,b,c) and (c,b,a) is tight; retain that orientation as the proper turn J. Its unordered outer pair is exactly {a,c}, the given floor pair. Enter the R172 pair-bearing fixed-turn lineage at this floor with no pre-entry capture credit. Then A_J is empty, so epsilon_J=2; the current balanced-pair mass is M=2, so M-2=0; and the current floor S={a,c} equals the target outer pair, so delta_J=2-|S intersect {a,c}|=0. Hence Psi_J=(2,0,0). By R172 every first quiet, nonclosing, non-exit macro retaining J must strictly decrease Psi_J. Since its second and third coordinates are already zero, that first decrease must lower epsilon_J, i.e. acquire at least one of a,c as a captured historical signed anchor before any quiet remint or target-distance debt can be charged. This proves the full R249 contract from R3 and R172 alone.

# R26 — Canonical splice sign trichotomy

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement

In an imbalanced maximin singleton-root frame, test the two canonical splice turns that attach the two ends of the short rail to the long rail.

## Scope
- If both are bad, the source frame retains the two reverse short-boundary states. This face is forced when the short rail has order four or five.
- If exactly one is good, the short rail has order at least six. A two-unit singleton reset and the witness-order normal form preserve the good splice, the opposite reverse boundary state, and either a current mate subpath or one of the explicit cross-end trimers.
- If both are good, the short rail has order at least eight. There are two useful descendants with different resources:
  - moving only the two outer short-rail endpoints onto the long rail gives a two-unit reset that keeps both canonical splices and the prescribed singleton current;
  - moving two boundary vertices at each end gives the deeper central residue and selects both reverse source short-boundary states as well.

The order-eight threshold follows already in the source frame: the deepest path and the middle rail form a literal exact cover after deleting the prescribed singleton, so the one-vertex deletion rail floor rules out short-rail orders four through seven. It does not require re-rooting the deeper descendant.

These three faces live in separate representatives. No selected state is imported between them.

# R263 — Opposite-polarity same-dimer witnesses concatenate to a literal tight P4

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Let D=(a,b) be an oriented physical dimer carrying two signed certificates with distinct witnesses x and y of opposite polarities. Orient the polarity labels so that x is the head witness and y is the tail witness. Then the certified turns are (x,a,b) tight and (a,b,y) tight, hence (x,a,b,y) is a literal tight four-vertex path. Equivalently, every opposite-polarity distinct-witness same-support interaction in R38 has an explicit strict two-ended realization as a P4 whose middle physical dimer is the signed support and whose endpoints are exactly the two witnesses.

## Hypotheses
Accepted Strong signed-dimer head/tail convention and accepted same-support interaction theorem R38; the two witnesses are distinct and lie outside the dimer support.

## Scope
Order-free graph-intrinsic unpacking of the strict two-ended signed-path output already referenced by R38. It promotes the previously compressed geometry into an explicit canonical path statement.

## Applicability
Use whenever R38 lands in the opposite-polarity branch and a downstream argument needs the actual vertex sequence rather than an interaction label. The strict path is obtained with no currentization or payment.

## Persistence
The oriented dimer, witness identities, certified turns, and resulting P4 are graph-intrinsic. Later representative changes do not erase the path fact.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert anything in the same-polarity collision branch, does not allow cyclic rereading of the P4, does not currentize the path as a selected component in an unrelated cover, and does not by itself force a two-cover.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Opposite-polarity same-dimer-to-P4 is a direct unpacking of the R38 branch used by only two active consumers; inline conceptually and retire.
- **Curation note:** Opposite-polarity same-dimer-to-P4 is a direct unpacking of the R38 branch used by only two active consumers; inline conceptually and retire.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Valid explicit P4 geometry for the R38 opposite-polarity same-dimer branch.

## Proof
A head-signed certificate on the oriented dimer (a,b) with witness x is precisely the tight turn (x,a,b). A tail-signed certificate on the same oriented dimer with witness y is precisely the tight turn (a,b,y). When the two certificates have opposite polarities and x!=y, choose the orientation of D so that x is the head witness and y is the tail witness. The two consecutive tight turns share the ordered dimer (a,b), so by the definition of a tight path their concatenation (x,a,b,y) is a tight P4. This is exactly the strict two-ended signed-path interaction named but not expanded in R38.
