# FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/LEGACY/R37.md

<!-- BEGIN FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/LEGACY/R37.md -->

# R37 — Witness-adaptive capture

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement

Suppose one physical support has several admissible signed incarnations with different witnesses. In one exact support-deletion cover, any selected state disjoint from the support is capture-capable whenever at least one admissible witness is outside that selected pair. Choose such a witness, choose either physical marker endpoint to capture, and apply the same-frame theorem. This bypasses concentration for that selected state.

## Scope
For an internal adjacent dimer of a retained path, the two neighboring path vertices are opposite natural sign witnesses. Every selected carrier/exterior crossing meets at most one of them. Hence every such crossing is individually capture-capable in the same deletion frame. If its carrier-side endpoint is neither witness, both polarities give separate capture certificates through the same selected physical crossing.

The different certificates are simultaneous graph-intrinsic/historical facts, not simultaneous payment descendants.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Integrator cleanup: route-specific capture/payment/capacity machinery with no live consumers, relations, or guidance references; accepted mathematics preserved historically.
- **Curation note:** Canonical witness-adaptive same-frame capture theorem preserving exact deletion-frame/crossing/witness roles.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Legacy migration verification: inherited independently accepted status from the controlling checksum-verified A7C2 theorem ledger.

## Proof
Let S be the physical signed support and let xy be the selected state in the exact S-deletion cover. By hypothesis there is at least one admissible signed incarnation of S whose witness w lies outside {x,y}. Choose that incarnation. The selected state xy is disjoint from S because it lies in the S-deletion cover, and it avoids w by choice. Therefore the capture/refund branch of accepted R527 applies in this exact frame. Use the physical dimer {x,y} as the actualizing marker. Since a two-vertex path is tight in either order, choose the marker orientation so that whichever of x or y is prescribed occupies the marker endpoint recorded as the new signed anchor. R527 then gives a valid historical capture certificate for that chosen physical endpoint, while retaining the selected crossing support, chosen witness and actualization orientation as ancestry. This proves witness-adaptive capture for the selected state. If several witnesses are admissible, the choice can be made separately for each selected state; no simultaneous payment descendants are asserted. For an internal adjacent dimer of a retained path, its two natural neighboring witnesses are distinct, and a two-vertex selected carrier/exterior crossing can meet at most one of them, so one is always available and the same argument applies crossing by crossing.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/LEGACY/R37.md -->

# R375 — Johnson t=2 equality has a universal paired-design normal form

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Let B be a family of k-subsets of an r-element ground set, with r>=k+1, such that every (k+1)-set contains at most two members of B. Suppose equality holds in the R326 density ceiling, so |B|/binom(r,k)=r/[k(r-k+1)]. Then k divides r. Every (k-1)-subset S lies in exactly r/k members of B, so B is a (k-1)-(r,k,r/k) design at the core-incidence level. Every (k+1)-set containing at least one member of B contains exactly two. Equivalently, for every F in B and every x outside F there is a unique f in F such that (F\\{f}) union {x} also lies in B. Hence the selected family is locally paired in every occupied union clique and has induced Johnson degree exactly r-k at every selected vertex.

## Hypotheses
Finite k-uniform family; local (k+1)-occupancy at most two; equality in R326.

## Scope
Pure finite-set equality theorem, generalizing the R331 paired four-design structure.

## Applicability
Use when equality or near-equality in a higher-k Johnson local-degree bound is reached.

## Persistence
The design incidences, unique swaps, and Johnson adjacencies are intrinsic finite-set data.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert such equality families exist for arbitrary k,r and does not classify them globally.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** superseded
- **Lifecycle note:** The t=2 paired-design normal form is a direct specialization/unpacking of the equality conditions already contained in the Johnson local-clique degree density theorem C283. Preserve the useful formulation historically, but keep the general parent canonical.
- **Curation note:** The t=2 paired-design normal form is a direct specialization/unpacking of the equality conditions already contained in the Johnson local-clique degree density theorem C283. Preserve the useful formulation historically, but keep the general parent canonical.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Accepted after independent audit.

## Proof
At equality in R326 with t=2, every (k-1)-core occupancy is constant and every selected k-set F has the maximum possible induced Johnson degree r-k, because each of its r-k containing (k+1)-union cliques contributes at most one selected neighbor. The constant core occupancy is mu=k|B|/binom(r,k-1). Substituting |B|=[r/(k(r-k+1))]binom(r,k) and binom(r,k)/binom(r,k-1)=(r-k+1)/k gives mu=r/k, so k divides r and B is a (k-1)-(r,k,r/k) design at the incidence level. For any F in B and x outside F, U=F union {x} contains F. Maximal degree forces the union clique on U to contain one further selected k-set, and the local cap two makes it unique; it must be F-f+x for a unique f in F. Therefore every occupied (k+1)-set has exactly two selected members and every F has induced Johnson degree r-k.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/LEGACY/R375.md -->

# R377 — Johnson paired-design equality has a full lower-incidence divisibility tower

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Assume the t=2 equality setting of R375: B is a k-uniform family on an r-element ground set attaining the R326 ceiling, hence a (k-1)-(r,k,r/k) design. Then for every s with 0<=s<=k-1, every fixed s-subset S lies in the same number lambda_s of members of B, namely lambda_s=(r/k)*binom(r-s,k-1-s)/(k-s). In particular every displayed lambda_s must be an integer. Thus equality imposes a nested arithmetic divisibility tower at all lower incidence levels, not merely k|r. The k=5 arithmetic fences R346/R353/R355 arise as special integrality consequences of this tower together with additional local pairing/parity information.

## Hypotheses
Finite k-uniform family in the equality case of R375.

## Scope
Pure finite-design corollary.

## Applicability
Use to rule out equality arithmetically at higher k or to compute exact link sizes before applying local structural consumers.

## Persistence
All incidence counts are intrinsic finite-set data.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert the integrality conditions are sufficient for existence and does not incorporate extra parity constraints coming from local pairing beyond the design axioms.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Lower-incidence divisibility tower is an immediate design-counting corollary of the paired-design normal form C325; keep it historical, not first-class.
- **Curation note:** Lower-incidence divisibility tower is an immediate design-counting corollary of the paired-design normal form C325; keep it historical, not first-class.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Accepted after independent audit.

## Proof
R375 makes B a (k-1)-(r,k,r/k) design. Fix an s-set S, 0<=s<=k-1. Count pairs (F,T) where F in B contains S and T is a (k-1)-subset with S subseteq T subseteq F. Each block F containing S contributes binom(k-s,k-1-s)=k-s choices of T. On the other hand there are binom(r-s,k-1-s) choices of T, each lying in exactly r/k blocks. Hence lambda_s(k-s)=(r/k)binom(r-s,k-1-s), giving the formula. Integrality follows because lambda_s counts blocks.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/LEGACY/R377.md -->

# R378 — Johnson paired-design equality has balanced reversible swap routing

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Assume the t=2 equality setting of R375 and write r=kq. For every selected block F in B and every f in F define A_f(F)={x outside F : (F\\{f}) union {x} lies in B}. Then the k classes A_f(F), f in F, partition V\\F and each has cardinality q-1. Moreover the routing is reversible: if x belongs to A_f(F) and G=(F\\{f}) union {x}, then f belongs to A_x(G), where A_x(G) is the replacement class indexed by the element x of G. Thus every equality block carries a canonical balanced k-way routing of all outside vertices into equal swap classes, with every selected Johnson edge paired by the reverse swap.

## Hypotheses
Finite k-uniform family in the t=2 equality case of R375; r=kq.

## Scope
Pure finite-set local routing theorem.

## Applicability
Use to convert abstract equality designs into explicit local replacement coordinates. This generalizes the balanced five-way routing phenomena seen in the k=5 Hamilton-five equality analysis.

## Persistence
The routing classes and reversible Johnson swaps are intrinsic finite-set data.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not classify the global compatibility of the local routing partitions and does not assert a group or algebraic structure.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Balanced reversible swap routing is a one-consumer direct consequence of the unique-swap/regularity content already present in C325; retire.
- **Curation note:** Balanced reversible swap routing is a one-consumer direct consequence of the unique-swap/regularity content already present in C325; retire.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Accepted after independent audit.

## Proof
R375 gives r=kq, unique swap pairing in every occupied (k+1)-set, and constant (k-1)-core occupancy q. Fix F in B. For every outside x, the occupied union F union {x} contains exactly one selected neighbor of F, necessarily F-f+x for a unique f in F; hence the A_f(F) partition V\\F. For fixed f, the core S=F\\{f} lies in exactly q selected blocks. One is F itself; the other q-1 are precisely S union {x} with x in A_f(F). Thus |A_f(F)|=q-1. If x in A_f(F) and G=F-f+x, then F and G are the two selected members of the union clique F union {x}=G union {f}; uniqueness from G therefore routes f back through the element x, i.e. f in A_x(G).

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/LEGACY/R378.md -->

# R379 — Johnson paired-design equality induces a regular linear clique geometry

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Assume the t=2 equality setting of R375 and write r=kq. Let G be the induced Johnson graph J(r,k)[B] on the selected k-sets. For every physical (k-1)-core S, the selected blocks containing S form a clique L_S of order q. Every vertex F in B lies on exactly k such core-cliques L_{F\\{f}}, f in F. Every edge of G lies in exactly one core-clique, namely the clique indexed by the intersection of its endpoints. Consequently G is k(q-1)-regular and the open neighborhood of every vertex is the disjoint union of k cliques K_{q-1}. Equivalently, the incidence structure with points B and lines {L_S: |S|=k-1} is a regular partial linear space with line size q and point degree k, and G is its point graph.

## Hypotheses
Finite k-uniform family in the t=2 equality case of R375; r=kq.

## Scope
Pure finite-set/graph structural theorem.

## Applicability
Use to study equality families via local graph geometry, clique incidence, spectral methods, or partial-linear-space classification rather than only block-design counts.

## Persistence
The Johnson graph, core-cliques, and incidence structure are intrinsic finite combinatorial data.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert the core-cliques are maximal in every degenerate q=1 case and does not classify all such partial linear spaces globally.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** superseded
- **Lifecycle note:** The regular linear clique geometry is contained in the stronger biregular girth-eight Levi geometry; retain the latter as the canonical incidence-geometric theorem.
- **Curation note:** The regular linear clique geometry is contained in the stronger biregular girth-eight Levi geometry; retain the latter as the canonical incidence-geometric theorem.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Accepted after independent audit.

## Proof
R375 gives exactly q selected blocks through every (k-1)-core S, so they form a clique L_S of order q in J(r,k). A selected block F contains exactly k different (k-1)-cores F\\{f}, hence lies on exactly k such cliques. If two selected blocks are adjacent in J(r,k), their intersection has size k-1 and is their unique common core, so every edge lies on exactly one L_S. By R378, for each f in F there are exactly q-1 neighbors obtained by replacing f, and neighbors arising from distinct f differ from F in different deleted elements and therefore intersect each other in only k-2 elements; they are not adjacent. Thus N_G(F) is the disjoint union of k cliques K_{q-1}, giving degree k(q-1). The line-intersection property follows because two distinct (k-1)-cores can lie together in at most one k-set.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/LEGACY/R379.md -->

# R394 — One-hole mate finish

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Let C be a fixed displayed spanning two-component path-forest candidate in a Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament whose complete uncertified turn set consists of one ordered turn h. If h is tight, C is already a spanning two-cover. If h is bad, boundary antisymmetry gives the exact reverse mate bar(h) tight, and the candidate retains the identity of h and its exact mate as candidate-aware local data. This one-hole mate packet does not by itself produce a spanning two-cover or contradiction; any further assembly conclusion requires an additional theorem consuming the same candidate identity, orientation, endpoint/seam roles, or ancestry.

## Hypotheses
A fixed displayed spanning two-component candidate with exactly one uncertified turn h; Strong Level-(1) boundary antisymmetry.

## Scope
Correction/modernization of legacy R64. It records only the source-supported one-hole mate output and explicitly removes the misleading automatic-finish reading.

## Applicability
Use whenever a final candidate has exactly one hole. It licenses the exact mate of that hole as graph-intrinsic candidate-aware data, but no more.

## Persistence
The displayed candidate identity, physical hole h, and exact reverse mate are retained as graph-intrinsic/candidate-relative data. No current representative containing both candidate seam and mate is asserted.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert the mate closes the conjecture, restores the missing turn, currentizes compatibly with the candidate, or supplies capture/protection. Same-end mate/splice incompatibility remains a fence.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** One-hole mate finish has very low discovery depth and no current consumers; preserve exact mate bookkeeping in proof history rather than canonical search.
- **Curation note:** One-hole mate finish has very low discovery depth and no current consumers; preserve exact mate bookkeeping in proof history rather than canonical search.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Accepted correction: a one-hole candidate gives closure if the hole is tight, otherwise only the exact reverse mate with candidate identity; no automatic finish.

## Proof
The candidate has one uncertified turn h. If h is tight the displayed two-path forest is a spanning two-cover. Otherwise h is bad and Strong boundary antisymmetry makes the exact reverse turn bar(h) tight. Historical source review explicitly corrects the old finish language: the one-hole theorem supplies the exact mate/canonicality information but not automatic closure.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/LEGACY/R394.md -->

# R40 — Support-family actualization

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement

Let several graph-intrinsic supports have the same polarity and same witness. One disjoint nontrivial marker path can be tested once to create a single common opposite-polarity support. Every original support then forms a balanced pair with that same opposite support. The head/tail dual is exact.

## Scope
This is a joint pre-payment certificate. Payments from the several pairs remain separate descendants.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Integrator cleanup: route-specific capture/payment/capacity machinery with no live consumers, relations, or guidance references; accepted mathematics preserved historically.
- **Curation note:** Versatile support-family actualization theorem producing one common opposite support and a family of balanced births from same-witness supports.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Legacy migration verification: inherited independently accepted status from the controlling checksum-verified A7C2 theorem ledger.

## Proof
Let S_1,...,S_r be the graph-intrinsic signed supports, all with the same polarity and the same sign witness w, and let M=(m_0,...,m_k), k>=1, be a tight marker path disjoint from the union of all V(S_i) and from w. Assume first that the family supports are head-signed by w. Perform the single terminal marker test from fully reconstructed R526: test (m_{k-1},m_k,w). If it is tight, the whole marker M is tail-signed by w, so set Q=M. If it is bad, R526/R3 gives (w,m_k,m_{k-1}) tight, so set Q=(w,m_k), tail-signed by witness m_{k-1}. This construction uses only M,w and the common family polarity; it does not depend on i. Hence the same physical signed support Q is produced for every S_i. Because M and w are disjoint from every S_i, Q is physically disjoint from every S_i in either branch. Each S_i has polarity opposite Q, so fully reconstructible direct balanced-pair theorem R514 gives a balanced opposite-sign pair (S_i,Q) for every i. All these pair births share the same Q certificate, but their later payment descendants are separate historical lineages. The tail-signed family case is the exact head/tail dual using R526's initial marker-end test at m_0. This proves the full support-family actualization theorem: one marker test creates one common opposite support and every original family member pairs with it.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/LEGACY/R40.md -->

# R407 — Bidirectional same-witness dimer interaction compiler

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Let H be a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample of order at least six. Let D={a,b} be a physical dimer such that both tested orientations (a,b) and (b,a) carry signed certificates of the same polarity with one common witness u outside D. Then H carries an accepted fixed-trimer historical signed-support/anchor or cross-generation pair interaction at the same physical anchor u. Choose two fresh vertices r,s outside {a,b,u} and orient the unique tight u-middle trimer T on {r,u,s}. Its two terminal signed dimers have opposite polarities and common anchor u. Choose the terminal mate M of polarity opposite to the two D-incarnations. R39 forms two direct balanced-pair births, pairing M separately with (a,b) and (b,a). After either birth is historical first, R160 forces the other to be nonquiet before unrelated reset, yielding the interaction at u.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample with at least six vertices; D={a,b}; both tested orientations of D have one common polarity and common witness u; accepted R3,R39,R41,R160.

## Scope
Order-free local signed-support compiler; cap geometry, payment ancestry and deletion frames are unnecessary.

## Applicability
Use whenever bidirectional same-witness dimer saturation appears, including R400/R401 2+1 cap residues and R171-like orientation forks when the common-witness hypothesis is met.

## Persistence
D, its two tested orientations, common witness u, chosen u-middle trimer and fixed-anchor interaction are graph-intrinsic/historical. Pair payments are alternative descendants.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not close the resulting interaction and does not apply when the two dimer orientations have different polarities or different witnesses.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Bidirectional same-witness dimer interaction compiler is a narrow zero-consumer local composition of existing pair/trimer interaction primitives; inline if revived.
- **Curation note:** Bidirectional same-witness dimer interaction compiler is a narrow zero-consumer local composition of existing pair/trimer interaction primitives; inline if revived.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Accepted after audit of scope, dependencies, orientation/currentness, and persistence.

## Proof
Choose r,s distinct from a,b,u. Boundary antisymmetry gives a tight u-middle trimer T. R41 gives its two terminal signed dimers opposite polarities with common anchor u. Select the terminal dimer M opposite to the common polarity of the two signed orientations of D. Since M is disjoint from D, R39 gives a balanced pair for each orientation. These are two pair births through the same fixed trimer T. By R160, after one is historical the other cannot be a quiet independent epoch and forces the accepted historical interaction at u.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/LEGACY/R407.md -->

# R408 — Endpoint-status disagreement between two exact covers forces a balanced pair

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Let H be a finite Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament and let W be a proper vertex subset. Suppose H[W] admits two literal exact two-covers F=P sqcup Q and Fprime=Pprime sqcup Qprime. If some physical vertex x in W is an endpoint of its path component in F and is internal on its path component in Fprime, then H contains a graph-intrinsic balanced opposite-sign pair. Indeed delete x. Trimming the endpoint occurrence of x from F leaves a literal cover of W-{x} with at most two components, while deleting the internal occurrence of x from Fprime splits its path component into two nonempty paths and leaves the other component unchanged, giving a literal three-cover of W-{x}. Since W-{x} is proper, R159 applies to this component drop. Thus any family of exact two-covers of one proper residue that contains no balanced-pair-producing endpoint/internal disagreement must have the same endpoint set in every member.

## Hypotheses
H is a finite Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament; W is a proper vertex subset; F and Fprime are literal exact two-covers of H[W]; x is an endpoint in F and internal in Fprime; accepted R159.

## Scope
Order-free cover-comparison theorem. No smallest-counterexample, capture, payment, or path-extremality hypothesis.

## Applicability
Use when several exact two-cover representatives of the same deletion residue are available. Any change in endpoint status across representatives immediately yields a balanced pair; therefore a genuinely quiet multiplicity branch is confined to a fixed endpoint-set fiber.

## Persistence
The two source covers are representative-relative. The balanced pair produced by R159 is graph-intrinsic historical information. No source rail or endpoint role is asserted to persist after the component-drop comparison.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not say distinct covers with the same endpoint set are equal or productive. Does not make the balanced pair current or immediately closing. If x is an endpoint in both covers or internal in both, the theorem gives no conclusion.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Endpoint-status disagreement to balanced pair is a one-step application of the general component-drop theorem R159 after deleting the disagreeing vertex; inline this move and retire the wrapper.
- **Curation note:** Endpoint-status disagreement to balanced pair is a one-step application of the general component-drop theorem R159 after deleting the disagreeing vertex; inline this move and retire the wrapper.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Accepted after audit of scope, dependencies, orientation/currentness, and persistence.

## Proof
Let F=P sqcup Q and assume x is an endpoint of P. Removing x from P leaves either a nonempty tight path or nothing; together with Q this is a literal cover T of W-{x} with one or two components. In Fprime, x lies internally on one path, say Pprime=(...,l,x,r,...). Removing x splits Pprime into two nonempty tight subpaths Pprime_L,Pprime_R, while Qprime remains a tight path, so R=Pprime_L sqcup Pprime_R sqcup Qprime is a literal three-cover of exactly W-{x}. Because W is proper in H, so is W-{x}. Hence R159 applies with c=3 and r=|T|<=2, producing a graph-intrinsic balanced opposite-sign pair in H. The final endpoint-set statement is the contrapositive: if no such balanced-pair-producing disagreement occurs among a family of exact two-covers, every vertex has the same endpoint/internal status in every cover, so all covers have the same endpoint set.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/LEGACY/R408.md -->

# R411 — Endpoint-universal pair deletion factorizes into endpoint-Hamiltonian rail supports modulo balanced pairs

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Assume the endpoint-universal branch of accepted R393 in a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample H. Fix any physical pair {a,c} and one exact two-cover F=P sqcup Q of W=H-{a,c}. Then either H contains a graph-intrinsic balanced opposite-sign pair arising from a cross-state comparison with another exact cover of W, or the following fixed-support factorization holds. Every exact two-cover of W has the same unordered rail-support partition {V(P),V(Q)}. Moreover for every x in V(P) there exists a Hamilton tight path P_x on exactly V(P) having x as a physical endpoint, and for every y in V(Q) there exists a Hamilton tight path Q_y on exactly V(Q) having y as a physical endpoint. Consequently for every prescribed pair x in V(P), y in V(Q), the disjoint union P_x sqcup Q_y is an exact two-cover of W exposing x and y simultaneously. Thus the quiet endpoint-universal branch over one pair deletion is not an arbitrary family of covers: it is a product of two endpoint-Hamiltonian path families on fixed disjoint supports.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample; accepted R393 and R410; {a,c} is any physical pair; F=P sqcup Q is any exact two-cover of H-{a,c}.

## Scope
Beyond-order-ten structural factorization of endpoint universality. No capture, first-contact, longest-path, or density hypothesis.

## Applicability
Use to replace endpoint-universal cover multiplicity by fixed-support Hamilton-path flexibility unless a balanced pair is already produced. Simultaneous cross-rail endpoint steering is then free by independent choice of the two supportwise Hamilton paths.

## Persistence
The fixed support partition is graph/deletion-relative in the no-balanced-pair branch. Each chosen Hamilton path P_x or Q_y is representative-relative. Different endpoint choices are alternative and may be combined only across the two disjoint fixed supports, where tightness is independent.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not prescribe the opposite endpoint or terminal neighbor of P_x or Q_y. Does not assert Hamilton-connectedness, path reversal, or simultaneous realization of two prescribed endpoints on the same support. Does not by itself close the endpoint-universal branch.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** One-consumer endpoint-universal factorization whose consumer C353 is already retired; retire.
- **Curation note:** One-consumer endpoint-universal factorization whose consumer C353 is already retired; retire.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Accepted after audit of scope, dependencies, orientation/currentness, and persistence.

## Proof
Let W=H-{a,c} and fix F=P sqcup Q. Assume no balanced pair arises from cross-state comparison with another exact two-cover of W. By R410 every exact two-cover of W then has unordered support partition {V(P),V(Q)}. Fix x in V(P). Endpoint universality R393 gives an exact two-cover F_x of W in which x is a rail endpoint. Since the support partition of F_x equals that of F, the path of F_x containing x is supported on V(P), hence is a Hamilton tight path P_x on H[V(P)] with endpoint x. The same argument gives Q_y for every y in V(Q). Finally P_x and Q_y are tight paths on disjoint fixed supports whose union is W, so for any prescribed x,y their disjoint union is itself a literal exact two-cover of W exposing both endpoints simultaneously. If any exposing cover changes support partition, R410 gives the alternative balanced pair.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/LEGACY/R411.md -->

# R421 — Common-shadow cross-state pair has a certificate-paid both-singleton checkpoint

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Let H be a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample of order n>=11, let W be a proper vertex subset, and let R,T be literal path covers of W such that T selects a state crossing two components of R. Apply R176 and then the certificate-retaining descent R416. Unless H already has a spanning two-cover, this yields an ancestry-bearing mass-two balanced-pair floor F0 with singleton supports (p),(t), named sign witnesses alpha,beta, and the full R176 common-shadow birth provenance retained. Put B0={p,t,alpha,beta}. Then for every prescribed z in V(H)\B0 there is a separate chosen continuation which either closes by a spanning two-cover or reaches another ancestry-bearing mass-two floor F_z in which (z) is literally one singleton support, while the entire common-shadow/R176 ancestry of F0 remains historical data. Hence every nonclosing common-shadow cross-state branch has at least n-|B0|>=n-4>=7 independently selectable fresh paid-floor coordinates. Each such continuation is supplied by R420: choose one auxiliary u outside B0 union {z}, actualize a signed dimer containing z from one singleton support, and use inherited-turn endpoint-selective payment to retain z at the descendant floor. The bad-seam branches retain the positive support-mass payment already guaranteed by R416; in the good/good branch no positive net payment from the original R176 birth is asserted, but its previously opaque support orders no longer obstruct coordinate-rich floor continuation.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample with n>=11; W is proper; R,T are literal covers of W with a selected T-state crossing R-components; accepted R176,R416; provisional R420.

## Scope
Order-free common-shadow ancestry theorem in the beyond-order-ten regime. It strengthens R416 by adding a large prescribed fresh-coordinate floor fan after the first certificate-retaining mass-two checkpoint.

## Applicability
Use on the Type II/common-shadow branch of the top-level O4 normalization. It removes good/good support-order opacity as a reason to split the frontier: after the first R176-ancestry floor, at least seven fresh physical coordinates are separately selectable. Downstream work should therefore consume cross-state ancestry or compare role-bearing coordinates, not merely ask for another floor or another arbitrary selectable vertex.

## Persistence
The common residue W, compared covers, selected cross state, exact R176 good/good cross-witness or bad-seam reverse-trimer/spare-vertex birth data, the first floor ancestry, chosen fresh coordinate z, auxiliary marker, actualization turn, endpoint-selective refund, and literal descendant singleton (z) are retained as historical ledger data within each chosen lineage. Different z-lineages are alternative and need not coexist.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not prescribe the second singleton of F_z. Does not claim floors for different z coexist. Does not assert that z is an original cross-state endpoint or witness. Does not assert positive net support-mass descent in the original good/good R176 birth. Does not make arbitrary coordinate selectability itself progress or close the conjecture.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Common-shadow branch-specific fresh-coordinate fan was an important stepping stone, but the modern reconstructed floor-steering machinery C369/C368 and universal O4 target-pair reduction preserve ancestry without this separate coordinate-count theorem. No live consumer remains.
- **Curation note:** Common-shadow branch-specific fresh-coordinate fan was an important stepping stone, but the modern reconstructed floor-steering machinery C369/C368 and universal O4 target-pair reduction preserve ancestry without this separate coordinate-count theorem. No live consumer remains.
- **Review status:** accepted

## Proof
Apply accepted R416. If it closes, stop. Otherwise obtain a mass-two floor F0 whose singleton supports are (p),(t), with named sign witnesses alpha,beta, and whose historical ledger contains the complete R176 common-shadow provenance. Let B0={p,t,alpha,beta}; |B0|<=4. Fix z outside B0. Since n>=11 there exists u outside B0 union {z}. The hypotheses of provisional R420 hold for F0 and z, so R420 yields either a spanning two-cover or a descendant ancestry-bearing mass-two floor F_z containing literal singleton (z). By the persistence clause of R420 the complete prior floor ancestry is retained, hence so is the R176 common-shadow birth certificate retained by R416. There are at least n-|B0|>=n-4>=7 possible choices of z. These are alternative lineages. In R176 bad-seam branches, R416 already guarantees at least one unit of support-mass descent from the dimer-plus-singleton birth. In the good/good branch the direct birth support orders remain unspecified, but this is irrelevant to the coordinate-fan conclusion because R420 begins from the R416 mass-two checkpoint.

# R422 — Fresh-coordinate paid-floor steering from any ancestry-bearing mass-two pair

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Let H be a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample with |V(H)|>=6 and let F be any ancestry-bearing mass-two balanced opposite-sign pair whose singleton supports are (p),(t), with named sign witnesses alpha,beta. Then for every prescribed physical vertex z in V(H) there is a chosen ancestry-retaining continuation which either gives a spanning two-cover or reaches an ancestry-bearing mass-two balanced-pair floor in which (z) is literally one singleton support. If z is p or t, use F itself. If z lies outside B={p,t,alpha,beta}, apply R420. If z is a sign witness not already equal to p or t, choose two auxiliary vertices u,v outside B. For z=alpha, use R3 on the z-middle triple {u,z,v}; whichever orientation is tight makes either (u,z) or (v,z) a tail-signed dimer by R41, opposite to the retained head-signed singleton (p). For z=beta use the exact dual to obtain a head-signed dimer containing z opposite to the retained tail-signed singleton (t). In either witness case the dimer sign comes from the displayed named tight turn, so R224 preserves z literally to a descendant mass-two floor. The complete ancestry ledger of F remains historical data. Different z-lineages are alternative. Thus single-coordinate floor selectability is universal once a mass-two ancestry-bearing pair is available; what remains nontrivial is simultaneous control of the second floor coordinate or consumption of the retained ancestry.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample with |V(H)|>=6; F is an ancestry-bearing mass-two balanced pair with singleton supports (p),(t) and named witnesses alpha,beta; accepted R3,R41,R224 and provisional R420.

## Scope
Order-free one-coordinate floor-steering parent. In O4 the order hypothesis is automatic. This theorem reconstructs a precise ancestry-preserving quantifier that was only compressedly remembered in historical Complete Floor Steering summaries.

## Applicability
Use after any ancestry-bearing mass-two checkpoint, including R415/R416/R417. Any desired graph vertex may be chosen as one literal floor coordinate without sacrificing the prior ancestry ledger. Therefore downstream work should not count one-coordinate floor access itself as progress; the meaningful targets are prescribed-pair synchronization, protected-role transfer, or an ancestry-sensitive interaction.

## Persistence
Retain the complete incoming floor ancestry. In nontrivial steering cases also retain the prescribed vertex z, chosen auxiliary vertices, the named tight turn certifying the dimer containing z, the R224 refund orientation, and literal singleton (z) at the descendant floor. The old second singleton and old active representative need not remain current.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not prescribe or control the second descendant floor singleton. Does not claim floors for different z coexist. Does not preserve an independently chosen capture/protection role unless already guaranteed by another theorem. Does not imply an arbitrary prescribed floor pair can be reached. Does not make repeated floor reminting progress or close the conjecture.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** superseded
- **Lifecycle note:** Fresh-coordinate steering to some floor containing z is strictly weaker than reconstructed prescribed one-coordinate replacement C369/R433 and complete pair steering C368/R432, which allow arbitrary targets while retaining the chosen singleton/ancestry.
- **Curation note:** Fresh-coordinate steering to some floor containing z is strictly weaker than reconstructed prescribed one-coordinate replacement C369/R433 and complete pair steering C368/R432, which allow arbitrary targets while retaining the chosen singleton/ancestry.
- **Review status:** accepted

## Proof
Write the incoming floor, after taking the exact head/tail dual if necessary, as (alpha;(p)) together with ((t);beta). Let B={p,t,alpha,beta}; |B|<=4. Fix z in V(H). If z=p or z=t, the incoming floor already has the required coordinate. Suppose z lies outside B. Since |V(H)|>=6, there exists u outside B union {z}; apply provisional R420 to obtain closure or a mass-two floor with literal singleton (z), retaining the incoming ancestry. It remains to treat a sign witness not already equal to a support. Suppose z=alpha and alpha not in {p,t}. Because |V(H)|>=6 choose distinct u,v outside B. Apply boundary antisymmetry R3 to the triple {u,alpha,v} with alpha in the middle. Exactly one of (u,alpha,v) and (v,alpha,u) is tight. In the first case D=(u,alpha) is tail-signed by witness v; in the second D=(v,alpha) is tail-signed by witness u. By R41 this is a signed physical dimer containing alpha, disjoint from (p), with polarity opposite the retained head-signed singleton (p). Hence they form an ancestry-bearing balanced pair, and the sign on D is certified by the displayed named tight turn. Apply R224 and choose endpoint alpha; it yields closure or a mass-two floor containing literal singleton (alpha). The incoming floor ancestry remains historical data in the chosen ledger. The case z=beta is the exact dual: place beta in the middle of a triple on two fresh auxiliaries; whichever orientation is tight gives a head-signed dimer containing beta, opposite to the retained tail-signed singleton (t), and R224 preserves beta. Coincident witnesses cause no problem: if alpha=beta is not already a support coordinate, either witness construction applies. This exhausts all z.

# R426 — Pair-Complement Sandwich and Fixed-Witness Descent to Width Two

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Let H be a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample and let (alpha;P),(T;beta) be a historical balanced opposite-sign pair. Local sandwich: when |P|,|T|>=3 and U is any nonempty tight path disjoint from both supports, testing the at-most-four new seam turns in the literal concatenation (P,U,T) gives exactly either (i) (P,U,T) tight, or (ii) an explicit reverse tight trimer meeting only unsigned support-end vertices and a descendant balanced pair with the same signed endpoints and witnesses alpha,beta and mass drop 1 or 2. Global fixed-witness descent: cover the outside reservoir H-(V(P) union V(T)) by at most two paths U sqcup V and apply the local sandwich to a nonempty component U. Hence before any unrelated marker reset one gets a spanning two-cover or a strict descendant balanced pair. Iterating while both supports have order at least three preserves the two original signed endpoints/witnesses and an ordered reverse-shell certificate stack, and terminates at a spanning two-cover or min{|P|,|T|}<=2.

## Hypotheses
H is a smallest Strong counterexample for the global/iterated statement. The pair supports P,T are vertex-disjoint tight paths carrying opposite graph-intrinsic signs (alpha;P) and (T;beta). The local sandwich part requires |P|,|T|>=3 and a nonempty tight path U disjoint from both supports.

## Scope
Strong Level-(1), arbitrary order. The local sandwich itself is purely physical and does not use minimality; minimality is used only to obtain an at-most-two-path cover of the outside reservoir for the global descent.

## Applicability
Primary non-small balanced-pair payment engine. It converts complement-cover seams into literal reverse-trimer refund certificates and gives a chosen finite continuation to width at most two while retaining fixed witnesses and the reverse-shell ancestry ledger.

## Persistence
During the non-small phase the active head support is a prefix of its historical support, the active tail support a suffix, the original signed endpoints and witnesses alpha,beta remain fixed, and every paid deletion is recorded by an explicit reverse trimer in an ordered shell stack. The markers need not be simultaneously selected later.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Not a global scalar monotone under arbitrary proof operations; the chosen continuation is meaningful only with its certificate stack. Does not close support order one or two. Does not claim old refund markers stay current. Does not treat tight cycles as contradictions.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Fixed-witness descent-to-width-two is a one-consumer lower-level step internal to the stronger width-two dimension-lowering theorem C363; retire and inline conceptually.
- **Curation note:** Fixed-witness descent-to-width-two is a one-consumer lower-level step internal to the stronger width-two dimension-lowering theorem C363; retire and inline conceptually.
- **Review status:** accepted

## Proof
Historical R12 certificate. Write P=(p_0,...,p_r), T=(t_0,...,t_s). For a singleton U=(u), the only new turns are p_{r-1}p_ru, p_rut_0, and ut_0t_1. A failed turn reverses to a tight trimer clipping respectively two vertices from P, one vertex from each support, or two vertices from T; Signed-Interval Rebirth gives the corresponding descendant pair, and the singleton-U drops are two units. For nontrivial U=(u_0,...,u_k), the only new seams are p_{r-1}p_ru_0, p_ru_0u_1, u_{k-1}u_kt_0, u_kt_0t_1. Failure gives respectively reverse trimers (u_0,p_r,p_{r-1}), (u_1,u_0,p_r), (t_0,u_k,u_{k-1}), or (t_1,t_0,u_k), and drops pair mass by 2,1,1,2. Because |P|,|T|>=3, these contacts do not swallow a support, and the surviving prefix/suffix retains alpha,beta exactly. If all seams are good, (P,U,T) is tight. In the smallest-counterexample setting take O=H-(P union T)=U sqcup V from minimality. If the sandwich succeeds, (P,U,T) sqcup V is a spanning two-cover; otherwise the reverse trimer pays the pair. Iteration strictly reduces mass and accumulates the physical shell certificates until one support has order at most two. Researcher 13 independently audited the sandwich, seam tables, exact refunds, fixed-witness descent, shell ledger, and width-two stopping theorem PASS.

<!-- BEGIN FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/LEGACY/R429.md -->

# R429 — Pair-Deletion Rigidity

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Let H be a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample and let p,t be any two distinct vertices. Then pc(H-{p,t})=2. Moreover every exact two-cover H-{p,t}=U sqcup V has both rails nontrivial: |U|,|V|>=2.

## Hypotheses
H is a smallest counterexample to the Strong Level-(1) Two-Cover Conjecture; p,t are distinct vertices.

## Scope
Strong Level-(1), arbitrary order and arbitrary deleted physical pair. No sign, witness, orientation, or order-ten hypothesis.

## Applicability
Use whenever a proof deletes a prescribed physical pair and needs an exact two-cover with two selected nontrivial rails, especially for marker actualization and fixed-turn floor steering.

## Persistence
The conclusion is universal over every exact two-cover of the same pair-deleted graph. It supplies nontriviality of both current rails but no identity or orientation persistence across different exact covers.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not prescribe heads/tails or rail membership of other vertices; does not identify a canonical two-cover; does not preserve an earlier representative.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Proof-library convenience theorem whose pc=2 conclusion is already R5 and whose nontrivial-rail conclusion follows from the same small-deletion/exterior-size mechanism. Four existing proof dependencies remain valid on accepted R429, but ordinary search should not present C365 as a separate structural discovery.
- **Curation note:** Proof-library convenience theorem whose pc=2 conclusion is already R5 and whose nontrivial-rail conclusion follows from the same small-deletion/exterior-size mechanism. Four existing proof dependencies remain valid on accepted R429, but ordinary search should not present C365 as a separate structural discovery.
- **Review status:** accepted

## Proof
By smallest-counterexample minimality, pc(H-{p,t})<=2. Suppose first that H-{p,t} has a Hamilton tight path W. If W=(w) has one vertex, boundary antisymmetry on p,w,t gives one of (p,w,t),(t,w,p) tight, yielding a spanning tight path on H, impossible. Otherwise write W=(w_0,w_1,...). Boundary antisymmetry on p,w_0,t gives a tight trimer K on {p,w_0,t}. The suffix (w_1,...) is tight and disjoint from K, so K together with that suffix gives a spanning two-cover of H, contradiction. Hence pc(H-{p,t})=2. Now let U sqcup V be any exact two-cover. If U=(u) is singleton, antisymmetry on p,u,t gives a tight trimer on {p,u,t}; together with V this is a spanning two-cover of H, contradiction. The same applies to V. Thus both rails are nontrivial. This is the historical Pair-Deletion Rigidity proof, later repeatedly audited and used.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/LEGACY/R429.md -->

# R430 — Marker Endpoint Anchor Capture

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Let M=(m_0,...,m_r), r>=1, be a tight marker path disjoint from a graph-intrinsic signed support. In head-to-tail Signed-Support Marker Actualization of a head-signed support (a;P) using M, the produced opposite-polarity tail-signed support has signed tail anchor exactly m_r. Dually, in tail-to-head actualization of a tail-signed support (P;b) using M, the produced head-signed support has signed head anchor exactly m_0. In the head-to-tail case, if m_{r-1}m_ra is tight the whole marker M is tail-signed by a; if it is bad, boundary antisymmetry gives a m_r m_{r-1} tight and the short support (a,m_r) is tail-signed with tail anchor m_r. The dual endpoint statement is exact.

## Hypotheses
A graph-intrinsic signed support and a disjoint nontrivial tight marker M are given, and the accepted Signed-Support Marker Actualization test is performed in the indicated polarity direction.

## Scope
Strong Level-(1), arbitrary marker length. This identifies the physical endpoint captured by marker actualization; it is stronger than merely asserting that an opposite support exists.

## Applicability
Use when later arguments need the identity of the signed/captured physical anchor supplied by an actualizing marker, especially orientation-selective dimer capture and fixed-turn endpoint budgets.

## Persistence
The captured marker endpoint is a graph-intrinsic signed anchor in the produced support and remains historical ancestry after representative changes. Current protection or selected status requires a separate theorem.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Capture is not protection. Does not assert the marker orientation was selected in the source cover; does not preserve the entire marker as current in the bad-test branch; does not localize later first contact without a protected continuation.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Marker Endpoint Anchor Capture is a two-consumer one-test helper; conceptually inline its local antisymmetry argument into the stronger floor-steering machinery and retire the claim identity.
- **Curation note:** Marker Endpoint Anchor Capture is a two-consumer one-test helper; conceptually inline its local antisymmetry argument into the stronger floor-steering machinery and retire the claim identity.
- **Review status:** accepted

## Proof
Let (alpha;P) be head-signed and let M=(m_0,...,m_r), r>=1, be a disjoint tight marker used in the head-to-tail actualization direction. Test the terminal turn m_{r-1} m_r alpha. If it is tight, then (M;alpha) is a tail-signed support and its signed tail anchor is exactly m_r. If it is bad, Boundary Antisymmetry R3 gives alpha m_r m_{r-1} tight. Hence the two-vertex support (alpha,m_r) is tail-signed by witness m_{r-1}, again with signed tail anchor exactly m_r. Thus either actualization outcome records the physical endpoint m_r as the new signed anchor. The exact tail-to-head dual tests alpha m_0 m_1 and records m_0 as the head anchor. This is precisely the historical Marker Endpoint Anchor Capture calculation; no generic actualization theorem is needed once the terminal marker turn is displayed.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/LEGACY/R430.md -->

# R431 — Orientation-Selective Dimer Capture

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Let {x,y} be a physical dimer used as a disjoint actualizing marker for a graph-intrinsic signed support. Either physical endpoint may be designated as the captured signed anchor: orient the marker as (x,y) or (y,x) before actualization, and apply Marker Endpoint Anchor Capture in the appropriate polarity direction. Thus in head-to-tail actualization one may choose x or y to be the resulting tail anchor by choosing it as marker tail; dually in tail-to-head actualization one may choose either endpoint as the resulting head anchor by choosing it as marker head.

## Hypotheses
A signed support and a disjoint physical dimer {x,y} are given. The dimer is used as a marker for Signed-Support Marker Actualization. A two-vertex path has no internal turn, so both orders are legitimate tight marker orientations.

## Scope
Strong Level-(1). Special to a two-vertex marker. This is an actualization-orientation choice, not a statement about which orientation was selected in an earlier cover.

## Applicability
Use when a proof needs to actualize a signed support while forcing a prescribed physical endpoint of a dimer marker to become the new captured/signed anchor. This is the endpoint-choice step in arbitrary target floor steering.

## Persistence
The chosen physical endpoint becomes a graph-intrinsic historical signed anchor of the produced support. The chosen marker orientation is part of the actualization certificate.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not reverse a currently selected dimer state; does not claim both orientations are simultaneously current; does not extend freely to markers of order >=3, whose reversed order need not be tight; does not itself provide later anchor protection.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Orientation-Selective Dimer Capture is the tiny orientation-selection wrapper around C366/R430: orient the marker so the desired physical endpoint is the signed anchor. Preserve R431 as proof shorthand for C369; low independent discovery value.
- **Curation note:** Orientation-Selective Dimer Capture is the tiny orientation-selection wrapper around C366/R430: orient the marker so the desired physical endpoint is the signed anchor. Preserve R431 as proof shorthand for C369; low independent discovery value.
- **Review status:** accepted

## Proof
Let D={x,y} be a physical dimer marker. Both ordered paths (x,y) and (y,x) are tight, since a two-vertex path has no turn condition. In head-to-tail actualization, R430 records the marker terminal vertex as the signed/captured endpoint. Therefore orient the marker with the desired endpoint last. In the tail-to-head dual, R430 records the marker initial vertex, so orient the desired endpoint first. This marker-orientation choice does not alter or reverse any previously selected orientation of D in another representative.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/LEGACY/R431.md -->

# R433 — Prescribed Opposite-Singleton Replacement

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Let H be a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample at an ancestry-bearing both-singleton floor with active supports (p),(t). For every prescribed vertex x not in {p,t}, there is a finite chosen certificate-retaining continuation yielding a spanning two-cover or another ancestry-bearing both-singleton floor (p),(x). The singleton p is retained as the fixed singleton throughout the replacement macro. The exact head/tail dual replaces p by an arbitrary prescribed x while retaining t. No freshness, capture-history, protected-anchor, or order-ten hypothesis is required.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample; (p),(t) is an active ancestry-bearing mass-two balanced floor; x is distinct from p,t; Pair-Deletion Rigidity R429, reconstructed Marker Endpoint Anchor Capture R430 / Orientation-Selective Dimer Capture R431, and the one-rail unsigned-end refund R175 are available.

## Scope
Strong Level-(1), arbitrary order. This is the exact historical Universal Both-Singleton Singleton-Replacement / prescribed opposite-singleton macro audited before Complete Floor Pair Steering.

## Applicability
Use to change exactly one coordinate of an active ancestry-bearing floor to any prescribed vertex while retaining the other singleton coordinate. It is the atomic steering macro consumed by Complete Floor Pair Steering.

## Persistence
Retain the fixed singleton p; the incoming floor ancestry; the exact pair-deletion rails of H-{p,t}; the selected rail dimer containing x; the marker orientation chosen to make x the signed endpoint; the actualization outcome; the nontrivial opposite rail used for the one-rail refund; and the final literal singleton x. Earlier protected/capture roles remain historical only unless their own persistence theorem applies.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not preserve the old floor representative state-for-state; does not preserve an additional protected/current role on p beyond keeping p as the floor singleton; does not claim different target-x continuations coexist; marker orientation does not reverse an old selected dimer orientation; does not close the both-singleton layer.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** superseded
- **Lifecycle note:** Prescribed opposite-singleton replacement is a narrow atomic steering step used inside the stronger Complete Floor Pair Steering theorem; retire the helper identity under the parent.
- **Curation note:** Prescribed opposite-singleton replacement is a narrow atomic steering step used inside the stronger Complete Floor Pair Steering theorem; retire the helper identity under the parent.
- **Review status:** accepted

## Proof
Pair-Deletion Rigidity R429 gives an exact two-cover H-{p,t}=U sqcup V with both rails nontrivial. The prescribed vertex x lies on one rail, say U, and therefore lies on at least one selected adjacency dimer D of U. Regard the current singleton (p) as a formal head-signed singleton with witness t. Because D has two possible marker orders, R431 permits choosing its orientation so x is the marker endpoint identified by R430 in head-to-tail actualization. Run the explicit R430 terminal-turn test. In the tight branch the oriented dimer D itself is an opposite tail-signed support whose signed endpoint is x; in the bad branch antisymmetry produces the short opposite support (t,x), again with signed endpoint x. In either branch the fixed singleton (p) is untouched, so we have a singleton/nontrivial balanced pair with opposite support of order two and signed endpoint x. The other old deletion rail, say V, is nontrivial, selected in the literal pair-deletion frame, and disjoint from p and from the new order-two support (including t in the bad branch). Use its selected boundary as the outside boundary in the one-rail unsigned-end refund R175. R175 clips exactly the unsigned endpoint of the order-two support and, by Signed-Interval Rebirth in its reconstructed proof, leaves its signed endpoint x while leaving (p) untouched. Thus the nonclosing descendant floor is exactly (p),(x). The head/tail dual gives replacement of p while retaining t. This is the historical R17 prescribed singleton-replacement macro, independently audited PASS by the subsequent R18 handoff.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/LEGACY/R433.md -->

# R439 — Historical pair-birth anchors force immediate nonquiet fixed-turn reentry

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Let H be a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample of order at least seven. Suppose an ancestry-bearing both-singleton floor is retained together with the full birth certificate of an earlier balanced opposite-sign pair (alpha;P),(T;beta), and let h,t be the distinct signed anchors of the two disjoint birth supports. Then there is a chosen ancestry-retaining continuation which yields either a spanning two-cover during floor steering or an aligned floor on {h,t} with the following bilateral property. In some exact two-cover H-{h,t}=U sqcup V, one rail has an internal vertex b. Orient the unique tight turn on {h,b,t}; at b both a selected predecessor and a selected successor exist in the same aligned frame. The two R434 endpoint-incidence channels are therefore both available, one anchored at h and the other at t. Each channel separately yields either a spanning two-cover during actualization or a nontrivial signed dimer whose signed endpoint is the corresponding old birth anchor. By R436 that later dimer forces an explicit strict-growth, tight-cycle, or reverse-contact/reversal output. Thus from one aligned frame there are two alternative immediate nonquiet historical-anchor channels, one touching each original pair-birth anchor; neither channel can complete a quiet endpoint-budget episode.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample with |V(H)|>=7; an ancestry-bearing both-singleton floor is active; its ledger retains an earlier balanced-pair birth with disjoint signed supports and signed anchors h,t.

## Scope
Order-free for smallest counterexamples of order at least seven; bilateral ancestry-sensitive strengthening of fixed-turn reentry. In O4 the size hypothesis is automatic.

## Applicability
Use after certificate-retaining pair descent, especially R417. Steer to the two original birth anchors, choose an internal middle of one pair-deletion rail, and obtain two alternative nonquiet channels from one aligned frame.

## Persistence
Retain the original birth supports/anchors, the R432 steering ledger, one exact H-{h,t} cover, the chosen internal middle b and its predecessor/successor, the two endpoint-anchored dimer certificates, and each corresponding R436 output separately. The two actualization descendants are alternative and need not coexist.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert the two R436 descendants coexist. Does not identify the stronger historical internal-middle simultaneous two-pair collision theorem mentioned in R434. Does not claim any one growth/cycle/reversal output closes the conjecture. Does not require the old birth supports to remain current.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Historical pair-birth-anchor nonquiet reentry has no current consumers; preserve as historical ancestry-specific theorem, not canonical shelf item.
- **Curation note:** Historical pair-birth-anchor nonquiet reentry has no current consumers; preserve as historical ancestry-specific theorem, not canonical shelf item.
- **Review status:** accepted

## Proof
Apply R432 to steer the active both-singleton floor to {h,t}, retaining the original birth ledger, unless a spanning two-cover occurs. By R429, H-{h,t} has an exact two-cover by two nontrivial rails. Since |H|-2>=5, one rail has order at least three; choose an internal vertex b on that rail. By R170 exactly one orientation of the turn on {h,b,t} is tight; label its outer endpoints a,c so {a,c}={h,t}. Because b is internal in the displayed rail, it has both a selected predecessor and a selected successor. R434 applied to the predecessor gives either closure or a nontrivial signed dimer anchored at a; applied separately to the successor gives either closure or a nontrivial signed dimer anchored at c. The vertices a and c are exactly the two historical signed anchors h,t of the retained pair-birth supports. Each newly produced dimer is a genuinely later proper tight path containing an old historical anchor and is not the vacuous replay of an old singleton certificate. Therefore R436 forces an explicit at-anchor growth/cycle/reversal/contact output in each nonclosing channel. Hence neither endpoint incidence can be a quiet completed episode, and the aligned frame carries a bilateral alternative fork of nonquiet outputs.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/LEGACY/R439.md -->

# R441 — Cross-Generation Two-Pair Collision / Descent

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Let Pi_1=(H_1,T_1) and Pi_2=(H_2,T_2) be two historical balanced opposite-sign pair births retained before an unrelated reset, where all four signed supports H_1,T_1,H_2,T_2 are nontrivial tight paths. Then the second pair cannot become an independent quiet historical package. If a support of Pi_2 meets a support of Pi_1, General Tight-Path Contact / Historical Anchor Protection R436 already yields an explicit anchor-contact/growth/cycle/reversal output or a strict signed-side descendant of the older support, hence strict historical support descent. If no cross-generation overlap occurs, then because the two supports inside each balanced pair are disjoint, the four supports are pairwise vertex-disjoint and Four-Support Sign-Splice Checkerboard Descent R440 applies directly. Thus before any unrelated reset one obtains strict historical support descent/contact, fused or strict signed growth, a vertex-simple tight cycle, a bounded reverse/contact or signed-BB core, or bounded-small output. No common birth frame, marker, exact cover, or simultaneous current paid descendants are required.

## Hypotheses
Two historical balanced opposite-sign pair-birth certificates are retained before an unrelated reset. Each of their four signed supports is nontrivial at the time the two births are compared. The two supports within each pair are vertex-disjoint. Across the two births, supports may overlap.

## Scope
Strong Level-(1), arbitrary order. Corrected nontrivial-support cross-generation interaction theorem. This is the scope actually needed by the internal-middle consumer. The broader historical R14 wording that passed through arbitrary overlap normalization is not asserted at exact singleton coincidence.

## Applicability
Use when two retained historical balanced-pair births each still have two nontrivial supports. Any cross-generation overlap is already a paying R436 contact/descent; only the completely disjoint case reaches R440.

## Persistence
The two birth certificates remain historical data. If an overlap occurs, retain the exact old/new supports and the R436 contact or strict signed descendant. If no overlap occurs, retain the four original nontrivial supports and the R440 checkerboard/descent certificate. No simultaneous current paid descendants are asserted.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not cover arbitrary width-one coincidence after supports have been paid to singletons. In particular, two later certificates on the same singleton are not declared productive merely because the certificates are distinct. Same-polarity same-singleton certificates with distinct witnesses may have additional local structure, but no general opposite-polarity singleton collision is claimed here. Does not assert interaction is closure or that pair mass is globally monotone.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Cross-generation two-pair collision/descent currently feeds only a historical superseded revision; retire canonical identity while preserving the accepted proof.
- **Curation note:** Cross-generation two-pair collision/descent currently feeds only a historical superseded revision; retire canonical identity while preserving the accepted proof.
- **Review status:** accepted

## Proof
Write Pi_1=(H_1,T_1) and Pi_2=(H_2,T_2), with all four supports nontrivial. The two supports inside each pair are disjoint by the balanced-pair hypothesis. Suppose first that some support Q of Pi_2 meets some support P of Pi_1. Apply R436 to the older signed support P and the later proper tight path Q. If Q contains the signed anchor of P, R436 gives strict path growth, a vertex-simple tight cycle, or a reverse contact/reversal cell. If Q avoids the signed anchor, R436 gives a nonempty strictly shorter signed-side descendant of P disjoint from Q. This strict historical support descent is already a nonquiet output, so stop; there is no need to continue truncating P toward singleton width. Suppose instead that there is no cross-generation overlap at all. Since H_1 and T_1 are disjoint and H_2 and T_2 are disjoint, all four supports are then pairwise vertex-disjoint. They are nontrivial by hypothesis, so R440 applies directly and its finite checkerboard continuation yields fused/grown path, vertex-simple tight cycle, bounded contact/reversal or signed-BB core, strict signed growth, or bounded-small output. Thus two nontrivial historical balanced pair births cannot form independent quiet epochs before an unrelated reset. The proof deliberately makes no assertion about exact singleton coincidence after later payment; that is the corrected historical fence.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/LEGACY/R441.md -->

# R443 — Linear Internal-Middle Interaction Reservoir

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Let H be a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample of order n, fix distinct outer vertices x,z, and fix one exact two-cover H-{x,z}=U sqcup V with both rails nontrivial. Suppose an ancestry-bearing both-singleton floor is available. Then the fixed frame U sqcup V has exactly n-6 internal rail vertices. For every internal vertex b, boundary antisymmetry uniquely orients the outer pair to a proper turn J_b=(a,b,c) with {a,c}={x,z}. There is an alternative chosen continuation which aligns the floor to {a,c} and then applies Internal Middle Immediate Pair Interaction in the same fixed U sqcup V frame, yielding a spanning two-cover or a zero-quiet historical pair-interaction packet I_b. Thus one fixed pair-deletion frame supports exactly n-6 internal-middle interaction packets indexed by its internal vertices. The turn orientation may vary with b.

## Hypotheses
H is a smallest Strong counterexample; x,z are distinct; H-{x,z}=U sqcup V is one fixed exact two-cover with two nontrivial rails; an ancestry-bearing mass-two floor is available. Each b considered is internal on U or V.

## Scope
Strong Level-(1), arbitrary order. Same-frame packet-family corollary. The packets are alternative chosen continuations indexed by internal vertices of one fixed deletion cover; current descendants for different b are not asserted to coexist.

## Applicability
Use when one wants to exploit many internal middles without changing the deleted outer pair or the base rails. In the historical beyond-order-nine setting n>=10, the reservoir has at least four indices.

## Persistence
The unordered deleted pair {x,z}, the fixed rails U,V, each packet index b, its turn orientation, selected predecessor/successor, endpoint-dimer birth certificates, and its R442 interaction output are retained as packet-specific historical data. Different packet continuations need not share later representatives.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert all n-6 paid descendants or pair births are simultaneously current. Does not assert turn orientation is uniform across b. Does not turn a finite family of interaction certificates into a contradiction. Does not prove the historical interaction-saturated frame has a no-replay property; same-frame historical replay remains a separate issue.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Linear Internal-Middle Interaction Reservoir is the direct n-6 counting corollary of C376/R442 plus the four rail endpoints in one fixed pair-deletion cover. Useful packet-count shorthand, but little independent discovery content and no live consumer.
- **Curation note:** Linear Internal-Middle Interaction Reservoir is the direct n-6 counting corollary of C376/R442 plus the four rail endpoints in one fixed pair-deletion cover. Useful packet-count shorthand, but little independent discovery content and no live consumer.
- **Review status:** accepted

## Proof
Because U,V are nontrivial paths, each has exactly two rail endpoints. Among the n-2 vertices of H-{x,z}, exactly four are rail endpoints, so exactly n-6 are internal. Fix one internal b. Boundary antisymmetry uniquely orients x,b,z into a proper turn J_b=(a,b,c) with {a,c}={x,z}. R432 either gives a spanning two-cover or aligns the available ancestry-bearing floor to (a),(c). The displayed U sqcup V remains the same exact cover of H-{x,z}, and b remains internal with its same selected predecessor/successor. Corrected R442 now applies at the nontrivial pair-birth stage and yields its zero-quiet historical interaction output without invoking any same-singleton collision. Repeat independently for each internal b. The n-6 packets are alternative continuations over one common fixed deletion frame; later descendants are not synchronized.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/LEGACY/R443.md -->

# R448 — Fixed-Trimer Central-Anchor No-Quiet Remint

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Fix a graph-intrinsic tight trimer T=(q0,q1,q2). Its terminal signed dimers D^-=(q0,q1), tail-signed by q2, and D^+=(q1,q2), head-signed by q0, are nontrivial and have the same signed anchor q1. Suppose one historical balanced pair has been born using one of D^-,D^+ and a partner signed support disjoint from T, and a later balanced-pair birth before unrelated reset uses either terminal dimer of the same fixed T and another partner signed support disjoint from T. Then the two fixed-trimer terminal supports admit an explicit graph-intrinsic R436 at-anchor normalization: taking the earlier terminal dimer as the older signed support P and the later terminal dimer as Q, Q contains the signed anchor q1 of P, and because P,Q are dimers the singleton exact-replay exception does not apply. Hence R436 yields strict full-P growth, strict Q growth, a vertex-simple tight cycle, or a three-vertex reverse-contact/reversal cell. This replaces a completely opaque interaction label by a concrete local certificate at q1, but the growth alternative may reproduce the already-known source trimer T and therefore is not, by itself, a proof of new progress or a consumer of the R160 interaction obstruction. Any stronger use must show that the returned certificate is not merely source-trimer replay or must combine it with additional partner/provenance data.

## Hypotheses
T=(q0,q1,q2) is a graph-intrinsic tight trimer. Two historical balanced-pair births are retained before unrelated reset. Each birth uses one terminal signed dimer of this same T and a partner signed support physically disjoint from T. The terminal dimer used by each birth may be the same or different. Accepted R436 is available.

## Scope
Strong Level-(1), graph-intrinsic normalization of the historical fixed-trimer interaction engine. No smallest-counterexample, payment, current-cover, or pair-mass hypothesis is needed beyond the existence of the two historical births. This is a certificate refinement, not a closure theorem.

## Applicability
Use when an R160-style interaction needs to be unpacked into literal local path geometry at the fixed trimer middle. Do not count the R436 growth branch as progress without checking whether it is only the original source trimer T.

## Persistence
Retain the fixed trimer T, its middle q1, the identities of the earlier and later terminal supports, and the exact R436 growth/cycle/reversal certificate. If the certificate is the old source trimer replay, record that explicitly rather than treating it as a fresh event. Partner supports and payment descendants need not coexist.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not claim the R160 interaction obstruction is solved. Does not claim the R436 growth output is new relative to the source data; it may be exactly the already-known trimer T. Does not claim any one growth/cycle/reversal certificate closes the conjecture. Does not treat a proper tight cycle as contradictory. Does not assert partner supports interact or coexist. Does not invoke singleton collision.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Current fixed-trimer remint normalization is a direct application of R436 to two terminal dimers sharing the source middle, and explicitly may return only the already-known source trimer. Valid certificate refinement but no independent consumer/discovery value.
- **Curation note:** Current fixed-trimer remint normalization is a direct application of R436 to two terminal dimers sharing the source middle, and explicitly may return only the already-known source trimer. Valid certificate refinement but no independent consumer/discovery value.
- **Review status:** accepted

## Proof
Let T=(q0,q1,q2) be tight. The terminal dimers D^-=(q0,q1), tail-signed by q2, and D^+=(q1,q2), head-signed by q0, are both proper tight paths of order two and both have signed anchor q1. Consider two historical balanced-pair births through T before unrelated reset. Let P be the terminal dimer used in the earlier birth, with its graph-intrinsic sign, and Q the terminal dimer used in the later birth. Whether P and Q are the same terminal dimer or the two opposite terminal dimers, Q contains q1. Thus Q meets P at the signed anchor of P. Apply accepted R436. The away-anchor truncation branch is impossible. Its only stationary-replay exclusion concerns an exact singleton support, whereas P and Q have order two. Therefore R436 supplies an at-anchor certificate: strict growth of P, strict growth of Q, a vertex-simple tight cycle, or a three-vertex reverse-contact/reversal cell. This certificate is graph-intrinsic and can be retained beside the two historical birth certificates. However, when P and Q are terminal pieces of the already-known source trimer, a strict-growth certificate can be exactly the original trimer T (for example by adjoining the original sign witness). Accordingly this argument refines the opaque R160 interaction label into literal local geometry but does not prove that the geometry is fresh or that the R160 obstruction has been consumed. Any later theorem using this normalization as progress must separately exclude source-trimer replay or exploit additional partner/provenance information.
