# R450 — Universal tight-trimer mate-or-interaction front door

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Let H be a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample beyond order ten and let J=(a,x,c) be any proper graph-intrinsic tight trimer. Then, unless H has a spanning two-cover, there is a finite chosen continuation yielding either (1) an explicit R173-admissible two-hole mate clause anchored on J, or (2) an ancestry-bearing mass-two balanced opposite-sign floor having the source middle (x) literally as one singleton coordinate. In fact, in the all-internal branch there are four alternative such middle-containing paid-floor lineages, one from each R389 source-trimer pair birth. Apply R359. Endpoint return gives (1) by R358. Otherwise R389 supplies four direct mass-four balanced-pair births, each consisting of one role-bearing residual terminal dimer and the unique opposite-polarity terminal signed dimer M of J. The sign on M is certified by the named inherited source turn J and M contains x. Apply R224 to M in that birth and choose x as the surviving endpoint. Unless a two-cover occurs, R224 carries the same ancestry-bearing pair lineage all the way to a mass-two floor containing the literal singleton (x). Thus the all-internal R390/R389 historical-interaction output is not terminal: it canonically admits four alternative actual paid checkpoints preserving the source middle as a floor coordinate.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample beyond order ten; J is a proper tight trimer; accepted R358, R359, R389, and R224.

## Scope
Strong Level-(1), beyond order ten. Order-free source-trimer consumer. It replaces the all-internal historical-interaction label by endpoint-selective paid floors retaining the trimer middle.

## Applicability
Use from any proper tight trimer when downstream work needs actual source-localized descent. Endpoint return gives a mate clause; persistent internality gives four alternative ancestry-bearing mass-two floors each containing the source middle x.

## Persistence
Endpoint branch retains the literal R358 proposal. In the all-internal branch retain J,x,U,V, the R359 four terminal shields, the chosen R389 pair-birth certificate, its specific J-terminal mate, the R224 endpoint-selective refund orientation, and literal singleton (x) at the descendant floor. Different birth/floor lineages are alternative.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert a single mate clause closes the conjecture. Does not prescribe the second singleton coordinate of any middle-containing floor. Does not assert the four paid floors coexist or have distinct second coordinates. Does not make the source currentization current at the floor.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** R450 is an older source-trimer mate/interaction front door with no live consumer and nonreconstructible ancestry route. Preserve historically.
- **Curation note:** Generic tight-trimer consumer converting endpoint/all-internal return geometry into a mate clause or ancestry-bearing middle-containing paid floor; ubiquity is separately fenced by C379.
- **Review status:** accepted

## Proof
Let J=(a,x,c) be the given proper tight trimer in the hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample H. Apply accepted fully reconstructible R920.

In regime (I), some exact two-cover of H-{a,c} exposes x at a rail endpoint. The endpoint-return compiler included in R920 gives an explicit one-hole or two-hole R173-admissible mate certificate anchored on J. This is conclusion (1) of R450.

Assume regime (II), so every exact outer-pair return keeps x internal. R920 supplies a source currentization H=J sqcup U sqcup V with |U|,|V|>=3 and the four graph-intrinsic reverse terminal shields. Write U=(u_0,...,u_r), V=(v_0,...,v_s). The left shields (u_1,u_0,x) and (v_1,v_0,x) make the oriented terminal dimers D_UL=(u_1,u_0) and D_VL=(v_1,v_0) tail-signed by x. The right shields (x,u_r,u_{r-1}) and (x,v_s,v_{s-1}) make D_UR=(u_r,u_{r-1}) and D_VR=(v_s,v_{s-1}) head-signed by x.

The source trimer J supplies exactly the complementary terminal signs needed for these births: M_H=(x,c) is head-signed by witness a because (a,x,c) is tight, while M_T=(a,x) is tail-signed by witness c. Thus for each left source dimer D in {D_UL,D_VL}, D and M_H are physically disjoint signed supports of opposite polarity; for each right source dimer D in {D_UR,D_VR}, D and M_T are physically disjoint signed supports of opposite polarity. By the direct-pair clause of R514, these are four graph-intrinsic balanced-pair births. They are exactly the four source-terminal/J-terminal births described historically in the R389 branch, now reconstructed directly from the R920 shields.

Fix any one of these four births and denote its J-terminal mate by M. The support M is a signed dimer containing x, and its sign is certified by the named source turn J. Apply R425 to M deleting its other endpoint. For M_H=(x,c), delete c; the surviving singleton (x) remains head-signed by the original witness a. For M_T=(a,x), delete a; the surviving singleton (x) remains tail-signed by the original witness c. Hence in both orientations the named turn J itself continues to certify the sign on the literal singleton x; no witness migration is needed. The chosen source dimer D is untouched and has the opposite polarity. By R514, (x) and D therefore form a graph-intrinsic balanced opposite-sign pair whose ancestry records the chosen one of the four source births and the cut M -> (x).

Now D is nontrivial (indeed a dimer). Apply R428 to this singleton/nontrivial balanced pair with the singleton p=x fixed. The chosen certificate-retaining continuation yields either a spanning two-cover or a both-singleton balanced floor while preserving (x) literally throughout. In the nonclosing case the resulting mass-two floor therefore has x as one singleton coordinate. The second singleton is not prescribed. Repeating this argument separately for D_UL,D_VL,D_UR,D_VR gives four alternative ancestry-bearing middle-containing floor lineages, with the corresponding source endpoint/shield provenance retained. They are alternative descendants; simultaneous currentness is not asserted.

This proves R450 using only the clean R920 return machine, R425 cut memory, R514 direct pair birth, and R428 fixed-singleton descent. No R358, R359, R389, R224, R24, R5, or exterior-size floor is used.

# R488 — Reverse-chord bridge cell forces an ancestral-neighbor P4 fork

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Retain the hypotheses and notation of R485 and suppose its residual (P4) branch occurs, so (z_1,a_0,b_q,z_{m-1}) is a tight P4. Put l=b_{q-1}, r=a_1, X_B={z_1,a_0,b_q,l}, and X_A={a_0,b_q,z_{m-1},r}. Then at least one of the following occurs: (H) the exact R485 head collision on the oriented bridge chord (a_0,b_q), namely both (z_1,a_0,b_q) and (r,a_0,b_q) are tight; (T) the exact R485 tail collision on the same chord, namely both (a_0,b_q,z_{m-1}) and (a_0,b_q,l) are tight; or (DP4) both X_B and X_A support tight Hamilton P4s. In particular, a single ancestry-bearing four-cell failure already upgrades the original reverse-chord P4 to one of R485's source-neighbor collision outputs. Proof: apply R518 to C_B=(z_1,a_0,b_q) with fourth vertex l. If X_B has no P4, R518 forces (l,b_q,a_0) tight. If (b_q,a_0,r) were also tight, then (b_0,...,l,b_q,a_0,r,...,a_p) together with P^o=(z_1,...,z_{m-1}) would be a spanning two-cover, contradicting pc(H)>2. Hence (b_q,a_0,r) is bad, so R3 forces its reverse (r,a_0,b_q) tight, giving (H) with the retained trimer (z_1,a_0,b_q). Dually, if X_A has no P4, R518 forces (b_q,a_0,r) tight; then (l,b_q,a_0) must be bad, so R3 forces (a_0,b_q,l) tight, giving (T) with the retained trimer (a_0,b_q,z_{m-1}). Therefore if neither collision occurs, neither four-cell may be no-P4, and both X_B and X_A support tight Hamilton P4s.

## Hypotheses
All hypotheses of R485, including pc(H)>2, p,q>=1 and m>=3; the R485(P4) branch; accepted R3,R38,R518.

## Scope
Order-free ancestry-preserving amplification of the sole local residual in R485. It keeps both old source neighbors and both bridge-side witnesses and replaces a lone reverse-chord P4 by an exact collision-or-double-P4 trichotomy.

## Applicability
Use immediately in the R485(P4) branch. Test the two exact four-sets obtained by adjoining b_{q-1} to (z_1,a_0,b_q) and a_1 to (a_0,b_q,z_{m-1}). If either cell has no P4, recover the corresponding R485 chord collision; only the double-P4 branch survives without an ancestral-neighbor collision.

## Persistence
Retain A,B,P; a_0=head(A), b_q=tail(B); source neighbors a_1,b_{q-1}; bridge neighbors z_1,z_{m-1}; the original R485 P4; and in DP4 both exact four-set supports X_A,X_B. In H/T retain the exact collision witness pair from R485. Hamilton orders inside X_A,X_B are not fixed.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not specify either Hamilton order in DP4, does not itself produce a complementary R173/R463 sibling clause, does not force any pair-deletion endpoint-side flip, and does not claim the double-P4 residual is contradictory. It does not validate ancestry-free use of R486 or generic R435 outputs.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** R488 is an R485 reverse-chord bridge refinement; the R485 bridge route is no longer live.
- **Curation note:** Conditional reverse-chord P4 fork compiler; valid but lower-priority after stronger full-ancestry bridge reductions.
- **Review status:** accepted

## Proof
Let l=b_{q-1} and r=a_1. The R485(P4) branch gives C_B=(z_1,a_0,b_q) tight and C_A=(a_0,b_q,z_{m-1}) tight. Apply R518 to C_B with l. If X_B has no tight Hamilton P4, its no-P4 reverse contact gives s_B=(l,b_q,a_0) tight. Suppose also s_A=(b_q,a_0,r) were tight. Because B=(b_0,...,l,b_q) and A=(a_0,r,...,a_p) are ancestral tight paths, L=(b_0,...,l,b_q,a_0,r,...,a_p) is then a vertex-simple tight path: its only cross-source turns are s_B and s_A. The source cover P sqcup A^+ sqcup B^- is literal, so the complementary vertices are exactly P^o=(z_1,...,z_{m-1}), a nonempty tight contiguous subpath of P. Hence L sqcup P^o is a spanning two-cover, contradicting pc(H)>2. Therefore s_A is bad. R3 gives its reverse (r,a_0,b_q) tight, which together with retained (z_1,a_0,b_q) is the exact R485(H) witness pair. The dual argument starts from X_A no-P4: R518 gives s_A tight, closure forbids s_B, R3 yields (a_0,b_q,l) tight, and retained (a_0,b_q,z_{m-1}) gives R485(T). Consequently, if neither H nor T occurs, both X_B and X_A must support tight Hamilton P4s.

# FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/LEGACY/R496.md

<!-- BEGIN FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/LEGACY/R496.md -->

# R496 — R495 same-end fork mates cannot preserve either source exit under currentization

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Retain the head-fork (HF) output of R495. Thus X_H=(b_0,...,b_q,a_0), A^+=(a_1,...,a_p), and P^o=(z_1,...,z_{m-1}) form the displayed spanning three-cover, while the two one-hole candidates have bad seams s_A=(b_q,a_0,a_1) and s_P=(b_q,a_0,z_1) with tight exact mates H_A=(a_1,a_0,b_q) and H_P=(z_1,a_0,b_q). Then no vertex-disjoint path forest can simultaneously select either mate H_A or H_P and either of the two old directed exit states a_0a_1 or a_0z_1. Indeed each mate places a_0 internally with unique successor b_q; selecting a_0a_1 or a_0z_1 in any path component would give a_0 a second successor, while placing that state in another component would reuse a_0. Moreover H_A and H_P cannot be simultaneously selected in one path forest because both use the same internal state a_0b_q with distinct predecessors a_1,z_1. Dually, in the tail-fork (TF) output no path forest selecting either mate T_B=(a_0,b_q,b_{q-1}) or T_P=(a_0,b_q,z_{m-1}) can retain either old incoming state b_{q-1}b_q or z_{m-1}b_q, and the two tail mates cannot be simultaneously selected. Consequently bare R18 currentization, R19 grafting, or any argument that first makes an R495 fork mate current and only afterwards asks to retain the original two-prong ancestry cannot consume the fork. A valid consumer must instead use the literal one-hole proposal/hole certificate before mate currentization, or perform a genuinely cross-arm reroute that recreates the lost source exit/entry on another component.

## Hypotheses
The R495 head-fork HF or tail-fork TF packet is retained, with the displayed physical vertices distinct as inherited from its literal three-cover. A path forest means vertex-disjoint directed paths, so each internal vertex has one predecessor and one successor.

## Scope
Pure path-forest simultaneous-currentness obstruction attached to the R495 HF/TF fork. No smallest-counterexample, antisymmetry, payment, or completion theorem is used beyond the existence of the displayed fork states.

## Applicability
Fence the live R495 HF/TF residue before trying generic prescribed-path currentization or internal grafting. The result identifies exactly which coordinates are structurally incompatible with a current mate and therefore which data must be consumed at candidate level.

## Persistence
Retain the exact R495 mate trimers and old source exit/entry states as physical directed-state coordinates. The conclusion is a simultaneous-currentness incompatibility; the historical truth of all source/fork certificates remains available after representative changes.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
This does not say a fork mate is useless, does not forbid a later surgery from recreating an ancestral state elsewhere, and does not rule out a cross-arm or opposite-end reroute. It is only a simultaneous-currentness obstruction for the displayed physical states.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** R496 is an R495 same-end fork fence; the R495 bridge-fork program is no longer live, so preserve this only as historical negative evidence.
- **Curation note:** Currentizing an R495 fork mate necessarily destroys the displayed same-side source exits/entries.
- **Review status:** accepted

## Proof
Assume the R495 head fork HF. If a vertex-disjoint path forest selects H_A=(a_1,a_0,b_q), then a_0 occurs internally in one path component with predecessor a_1 and successor b_q. Selecting either old directed exit a_0a_1 or a_0z_1 in that same component would require a_0 to have a successor different from b_q; placing such a state in another component would reuse a_0. Hence neither old exit can coexist with H_A. The identical argument applies to H_P=(z_1,a_0,b_q): again a_0 is internal with unique successor b_q, so neither a_0a_1 nor a_0z_1 can coexist with it. Finally H_A and H_P cannot both be selected in one path forest. If placed in one component, a_0 would have the two distinct predecessors a_1 and z_1; if placed in different components, they reuse a_0 and b_q. Thus the two head mates are mutually incompatible as current states. The tail fork TF is dual. Selecting T_B=(a_0,b_q,b_{q-1}) or T_P=(a_0,b_q,z_{m-1}) makes b_q internal with unique predecessor a_0. Either old incoming state b_{q-1}b_q or z_{m-1}b_q would require a second predecessor if placed in the same component and would reuse b_q if placed elsewhere. The two tail mates cannot coexist because they require distinct successors b_{q-1},z_{m-1} from the same internal b_q (or else reuse vertices across components). Therefore currentizing a fork mate necessarily destroys the displayed same-side source exits/entries; any consumer preserving their ancestry must act at candidate level or recreate the lost state by a separate reroute.

# R499 — Long-arm R495 double reversal forces a named-residue cross-state balanced pair

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Let H be a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample and retain the DR output of R495 in the R485 notation. Thus K_D=(a_1,a_0,b_q,b_{q-1}) is a tight P4, while the original source three-cover is P sqcup A^+ sqcup B^- with A=(a_0,a_1,...,a_p), B=(b_0,...,b_q), P=(a_0,z_1,...,z_{m-1},b_q), m>=3. Assume p>=2 and q>=2. Delete the four DR vertices E={a_1,a_0,b_q,b_{q-1}} and put W=H-E. Then the three named paths A^{++}=(a_2,...,a_p), B^{--}=(b_0,...,b_{q-2}), and P^o=(z_1,...,z_{m-1}) are nonempty, vertex-disjoint, tight, and form a literal three-component path cover R of W. By accepted four-deletion exactness R5, W has a literal exact two-cover T=U sqcup V. Apply the partition-cover deficit identity R7 to the fixed physical partition Pi={V(A^{++}),V(B^{--}),V(P^o)} and the current cover T. Each class has intrinsic path-cover number one, while T has two components, so the number t_Pi(T) of selected transitions between distinct named classes is 3-2+sigma=1+sigma>=1. Hence T selects some directed state xy whose endpoints lie in two distinct components of the named source cover R. Since W is proper, accepted R176 applies to the literal path covers R and T and yields a graph-intrinsic balanced opposite-sign pair. Therefore the R495 double ancestral-end reversal is immediately consumable whenever both ancestral arms continue beyond the reversed endpoint pair: it forces a balanced-pair birth whose cross-state provenance retains exactly which two of A^{++},B^{--},P^o were joined by the four-deletion exact cover. The only DR cases not covered are the short-arm cells p=1 or q=1, where one named residual class is empty and the three-to-two transition deficit disappears.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample; accepted R495 DR output; p,q>=2; accepted R5,R7,R176.

## Scope
Order-free smallest-counterexample consumer of the R495 DR branch. It converts a simultaneous two-end reversal into a balanced pair without currentizing DR and without losing the named two-cut ancestry.

## Applicability
Use immediately on R495(DR) when both ancestral rails extend at least one vertex beyond a_1 and b_{q-1}. Delete the four DR vertices, keep the three literal residual source pieces as the reference cover, choose any exact four-deletion two-cover, and take its forced cross-class state through R176. Only p=1 or q=1 requires separate analysis.

## Persistence
Retains the DR support, the four-deletion set, all three named residual classes A^{++},B^{--},P^o, the exact two-cover T, and the particular selected cross-class state witnessing the R176 balanced-pair birth. The resulting balanced pair is graph-intrinsic.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not handle p=1 or q=1. Does not assert which pair of the three named residual classes is crossed. Does not claim the balanced pair itself closes O4; it feeds the accepted pair-payment/descent machinery. Does not require the DR path to be currentized.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** R499 is a nonreconstructible R495 long-arm branch theorem with no live consumers; preserve historically.
- **Curation note:** Long-arm DR consumer via four-deletion three-class cross-state balanced-pair birth.
- **Review status:** accepted

## Proof
Retain the hypotheses and exact coordinates of R499. Thus the R495 DR output gives the literal tight P4 K_D=(a_1,a_0,b_q,b_{q-1}), and p,q>=2. Put E={a_1,a_0,b_q,b_{q-1}}=V(K_D) and W=H-E. Because P^o=(z_1,...,z_{m-1}) is nonempty, E is a proper subset of V(H).\n\nThe historical proof invoked R5 to obtain an exact two-cover of W. This is unnecessary. K_D is itself a proper graph-intrinsic tight path, so accepted smallest-counterexample minimality R4 applies directly to K_D and gives an exact two-cover T=U sqcup V of its complement W. This preserves exactly the same physical four-deletion residue used by the historical proof, but with no four-deletion exactness theorem.\n\nAfter deleting E, the original source geometry restricts to the three literal paths A^{++}=(a_2,...,a_p), B^{--}=(b_0,...,b_{q-2}), and P^o=(z_1,...,z_{m-1}). The assumptions p,q>=2 and m>=3 make all three nonempty. They are pairwise vertex-disjoint and cover W, so R=A^{++} sqcup B^{--} sqcup P^o is a literal three-path cover of W. Each of the three physical classes has intrinsic path-cover number one.\n\nApply the accepted partition-cover deficit identity R7 to the fixed partition Pi={V(A^{++}),V(B^{--}),V(P^o)} and the current exact two-cover T. Since the three class path-cover numbers sum to three while T has two components, R7 gives t_Pi(T)=3-2+sigma=1+sigma>=1. Hence T selects a directed state xy whose endpoints lie in two distinct components of the source cover R.\n\nThe residue W is proper because E is nonempty. Accepted R176 therefore applies to the literal path covers R and T and this actual selected cross-state xy, producing a graph-intrinsic balanced opposite-sign pair. Retain the exact crossed pair of named residual classes and the selected state as the cross-state provenance.\n\nThis is exactly the conclusion of R499. The proof uses R4 only through the prescribed-path complement clause on the already-retained DR path K_D. No R5, R24, R168, R169, or arbitrary four-deletion exactness is used.

# R501 — Anti-aligned two-cut bridge side compiler

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Retain the hypotheses and notation of R495. Then at least one of the following occurs.

(DR) The R495 double ancestral-end reversal K_D=(a_1,a_0,b_q,b_{q-1}) is tight.

(HP4) In the head-fork branch HF, the four-set X_H={a_1,z_1,a_0,b_q} supports a tight Hamilton P4.

(HR) In the head-fork branch HF, both tested orientations of the bridge chord {a_0,b_q} are head-signed by both named witnesses a_1 and z_1, and both tested orientations of the cross-arm head dimer {a_1,z_1} are head-signed by the common witness a_0. Explicitly, in addition to the retained R495 turns (a_1,a_0,b_q) and (z_1,a_0,b_q), the turns (a_1,b_q,a_0), (z_1,b_q,a_0), (a_0,a_1,z_1), and (a_0,z_1,a_1) are tight. Hence accepted R407 applies to the bidirectional dimer {a_1,z_1} with common witness a_0 and yields a fixed-trimer historical signed-support/anchor or cross-generation pair interaction localized at the exact deleted bridge endpoint a_0.

(TP4) In the tail-fork branch TF, the four-set X_T={b_{q-1},z_{m-1},a_0,b_q} supports a tight Hamilton P4.

(TR) In the tail-fork branch TF, both tested orientations of the bridge chord {a_0,b_q} are tail-signed by both named witnesses b_{q-1} and z_{m-1}, and both tested orientations of the cross-arm tail dimer {b_{q-1},z_{m-1}} are tail-signed by the common witness b_q. Explicitly, in addition to the retained R495 turns (a_0,b_q,b_{q-1}) and (a_0,b_q,z_{m-1}), the turns (b_q,a_0,b_{q-1}), (b_q,a_0,z_{m-1}), (z_{m-1},b_{q-1},b_q), and (b_{q-1},z_{m-1},b_q) are tight. Hence R407 applies to {b_{q-1},z_{m-1}} with common witness b_q and yields the corresponding historical interaction localized at the exact deleted bridge endpoint b_q.

Thus an R495 candidate-aware fork never stops at a bare same-support collision: it either creates a role-labelled four-vertex Hamilton path joining the two fork witnesses to the bridge chord, or creates a bidirectional cross-arm signed dimer whose common witness is one of the original deleted bridge endpoints.

## Hypotheses
All hypotheses of accepted R495; accepted R407 and R518. For the R407 conclusion H is a hypothetical smallest counterexample of order at least six, automatically satisfied in O4.

## Scope
Order-free local amplification of the R495 fork, with the final R407 localization interpreted in the smallest-counterexample setting. The result preserves the exact ancestral/bridge witness identities and deleted endpoint anchor.

## Applicability
Use immediately after R495 HF/TF. If no role-labelled P4 appears on the four fork vertices, the fork compiles to a bidirectional cross-arm dimer anchored at the deleted bridge endpoint; do not report only the original R38 collision.

## Persistence
The R495 fork witnesses, bridge chord, four-set, all six displayed turns in HR/TR, and the cross-arm bidirectional dimer are graph-intrinsic. The R407 interaction is historical and anchored at the named deleted endpoint; paid descendants need not coexist.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not say the role-labelled P4 is itself a spanning two-cover or sibling clause. Does not say the R407 interaction closes O4. Does not currentize the mate trimers or preserve the R495 one-hole proposals through the R407 payment descendants. The two fork branches remain alternative representatives.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** R501 is an R495 anti-aligned bridge side compiler; the R495 bridge route is no longer live.
- **Curation note:** Anti-aligned two-cut bridge side compiler is branch-local toolkit.
- **Review status:** accepted

## Proof
Assume first the head fork HF of R495 and abbreviate x=a_1, y=z_1, a=a_0, b=b_q. The retained fork gives the two tight trimers C_x=(x,a,b) and C_y=(y,a,b). Apply accepted R518 to C_x with fourth vertex y. If the four-set {x,y,a,b} has a tight Hamilton P4, output HP4. Otherwise the corrected no-P4 branch forces the reverse contacts (a,x,y) and (y,b,a) tight. Now apply R518 to C_y with fourth vertex x. Again a P4 gives HP4; otherwise the no-P4 branch forces (a,y,x) and (x,b,a) tight. In the joint no-P4 branch we therefore have (x,a,b),(y,a,b),(x,b,a),(y,b,a),(a,x,y),(a,y,x) all tight. The first four say that both tested orientations (a,b) and (b,a) of the bridge chord are head-signed by both witnesses x,y. The last two say that both tested orientations (x,y) and (y,x) of the physical cross-arm dimer are head-signed by the common witness a. Accepted R407 therefore applies to D={x,y} with common witness a and produces the stated historical fixed-trimer/anchor or cross-generation pair interaction localized at a=a_0. This proves HR. The tail fork is dual, but write it explicitly to preserve tested order. Put x=b_{q-1}, y=z_{m-1}, a=a_0, b=b_q. R495 gives C_x=(a,b,x) and C_y=(a,b,y) tight. Apply R518 to C_x with fourth vertex y. Outside TP4, the no-P4 branch forces (b,a,y) and (y,x,b) tight. Apply R518 to C_y with fourth vertex x. Outside TP4, it forces (b,a,x) and (x,y,b) tight. Hence both orientations (a,b),(b,a) of the bridge chord are tail-signed by x,y, while both orientations (x,y),(y,x) of the cross-arm tail dimer are tail-signed by the common witness b=b_q. R407 applies at b_q and gives TR. Together with the DR alternative already present in R495, these exhaust the fork.

# R506 — Every current trimer component forces dual recompletion cut crossings

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Let H be a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample and let H=J sqcup U sqcup V be any literal spanning three-cover in which J=(p,x,z) is a tight trimer and U,V are nonempty tight paths. Put D={x,z} and E={p,x}. Then every exact two-cover of H-p contains a selected state crossing the physical cut D | (U union V), and every exact two-cover of H-z contains a selected state crossing the cut E | (U union V). Equivalently, after deleting either outer endpoint of a current trimer component, the surviving boundary dimer cannot remain isolated from the other two source components in any exact recompletion. This conclusion depends only on the literal trimer three-cover and smallest-counterexample deletion floors; capture, first-contact, mirror ancestry, and endpoint-universality are unnecessary.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample; H=J sqcup U sqcup V is a literal spanning three-cover; J=(p,x,z) is tight; U,V are nonempty. Accepted R5 and R24.

## Scope
Order-free generic parent of historical R333. It isolates the exact recompletion-crossing content of a current trimer component.

## Applicability
Use whenever a proper tight trimer is current as one component of a minimum three-cover and downstream work needs a selected crossing tied to one of its two boundary dimers after deleting the opposite outer endpoint.

## Persistence
Retain the source current trimer J, its physical boundary dimers D,E, and source residual rails U,V. The forced crossing statement quantifies over every exact two-cover of H-p or H-z; individual crossings remain representative-relative.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert the two singleton-deletion covers coexist, share a crossing, or preserve J as current. Does not itself capture or protect the forced crossing and does not imply a spanning two-cover. The theorem requires both residual source components U,V to be nonempty.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** superseded
- **Lifecycle note:** R506 is mathematically correct but all of its crossing content is the two current-trimer substitutions into R508, with R5 only supplying the exact deletion cover and R24 unnecessary. Preserve R506/P521 as historical specialization evidence; direct attention to C405.
- **Curation note:** R506 is mathematically correct but all of its crossing content is the two current-trimer substitutions into R508, with R5 only supplying the exact deletion cover and R24 unnecessary. Preserve R506/P521 as historical specialization evidence; direct attention to C405.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** PASS: Correct dual trimer crossing specialization. The proof via R24 is valid, although R508 gives a strictly leaner parent route and makes R24 unnecessary.

## Proof
Retain the hypotheses of R506. Thus H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample and

  H = J sqcup U sqcup V,
  J=(p,x,z)

is a literal spanning three-cover with U,V nonempty tight paths.

DELETE p. The subsystem H-p is nonempty and proper, so accepted smallest-counterexample minimality R4 gives pc(H-p)<=2. It cannot be Hamiltonian: if Q_p were a Hamilton tight path on H-p, then Q_p together with the singleton path (p) would be a spanning two-path cover of H, contradicting pc(H)=3. Therefore

  pc(H-p)=2.                                               (1)

Let T be any exact two-cover of H-p. In the notation of accepted R508 take deletion set D={p}, absorbable block S={x,z}, and certified recompletion path Q=J=(p,x,z). Then Q spans exactly D union S. Moreover S is nonempty and proper inside V(H-p), because U and V are both nonempty. R508 therefore forces T to select a directed state crossing

  {x,z} | (V(U) union V(V)).                               (2)

Since T was arbitrary, every exact two-cover of H-p has the required crossing.

DELETE z. The same argument gives pc(H-z)=2: R4 gives at most two, and Hamiltonicity of H-z together with singleton z would two-cover H. Let T' be any exact two-cover of H-z. Apply R508 with deletion D'={z}, absorbable block S'={p,x}, and the same certified trimer Q=J. Again S' is nonempty and proper because U,V are nonempty. Hence T' selects a state crossing

  {p,x} | (V(U) union V(V)).                               (3)

Equations (2) and (3) are exactly the two conclusions of R506. No R5, R24, rail-size floor, capture, or endpoint-universality input is used.

# R507 — Current-trimer recompletion crossings compile to boundary collision, P4, or reverse contact

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Let H be a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample and H=J sqcup U sqcup V a literal spanning three-cover with J=(p,x,z) a tight trimer and U,V nonempty. Retain the dual forced recompletion crossings of R506. (P-deletion.) Put D=(x,z). In any exact two-cover of H-p choose a selected state crossing the physical cut {x,z} | (U union V), and let y outside {x,z} be its non-D endpoint. If the D-endpoint of the crossing is x, then either (y,x,z) is tight, in which case D carries a same-polarity two-witness interaction with the natural J-witness p and the recompletion witness y, or the exact reverse-contact trimer (z,x,y) is tight. If the D-endpoint is z, then either (x,z,y) is tight, in which case K=(p,x,z,y) is a literal tight P4 extending J through the recompletion vertex y, or the reverse-contact trimer (y,z,x) is tight. (Z-deletion.) Put E=(p,x). In any exact two-cover of H-z choose a selected crossing from {p,x} to y outside. If the E-endpoint is p, then either (y,p,x) is tight, in which case K=(y,p,x,z) is a literal tight P4 extending J at its head, or the reverse-contact trimer (x,p,y) is tight. If the E-endpoint is x, then either (p,x,y) is tight, in which case E carries a same-polarity two-witness interaction with natural J-witness z and recompletion witness y, or the reverse-contact trimer (y,x,p) is tight. Thus each compulsory singleton-deletion crossing of a current trimer has an explicit boundary-dimer consumer pinned to which trimer endpoint was touched.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample; H=J sqcup U sqcup V with J=(p,x,z) tight and U,V nonempty; accepted R506; accepted R3,R38.

## Scope
Order-free graph-intrinsic local compiler for the forced recompletion crossings of a current trimer. The outputs remain pinned to the exact surviving boundary dimer and touched endpoint.

## Applicability
Use immediately after R506 or historical R333. Inspect which vertex of the surviving boundary dimer participates in the selected recompletion crossing, then apply the corresponding R3 reversal pair. Do not stop at an anonymous cross state.

## Persistence
Retain J, the chosen outer deletion, surviving oriented boundary dimer D or E, the exact recompletion cover, selected physical crossing, touched dimer endpoint, outside vertex y, and the resulting collision/P4/reverse-trimer certificate. Collision witnesses are the named deleted outer J-vertex and y.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert any one P4, collision, or reverse trimer closes H. Does not assert the two outer-deletion recompletion covers coexist. The selected crossing direction in the exact cover is irrelevant to the local R3 classification; only the physical endpoint of the surviving dimer that it touches is used.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** R507 is a nonreconstructible current-trimer crossing continuation with no live consumers; newer exact physical consumers cover the active use cases.
- **Curation note:** Generic current-trimer recompletion crossing compiler pinned to touched boundary endpoint.
- **Review status:** accepted

## Proof
For H-p the surviving boundary dimer is D=(x,z), and J=(p,x,z) gives the natural tight head-sign turn (p,x,z) on D with witness p. Let y be the outside endpoint of a selected recompletion crossing from the physical set {x,z}. If the crossing touches x, apply R3 with middle x to {y,x,z}: exactly one of (y,x,z) and (z,x,y) is tight. In the first case (y,x,z) is another head-sign certificate on the identical oriented support D=(x,z), with witness y distinct from p, so R38 gives the same-polarity two-witness collision package on D. In the second case retain the explicit reverse-contact trimer (z,x,y). If the crossing touches z, apply R3 with middle z: exactly one of (x,z,y) and (y,z,x) is tight. In the first case it concatenates literally with J to the tight P4 (p,x,z,y); in the second retain (y,z,x). For H-z the surviving oriented dimer is E=(p,x), and J gives its natural tail-sign turn (p,x,z) with witness z. If a forced crossing touches p, R3 at middle p gives either (y,p,x), which concatenates with J to (y,p,x,z), or (x,p,y), the reverse contact. If it touches x, R3 at middle x gives either (p,x,y), a second tail-sign on E with witness y and hence an R38 same-polarity collision with natural witness z, or (y,x,p), the reverse contact. These are exactly the four asserted cases.

## Statement

# R517 — Four-signature contact family has one quotient-inhomogeneous cell

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Retain the four exact no-P4 signatures of R516 on X={a,b,c,y}. Partition the six physical dimers into opposite-edge perfect matchings B_1={{a,b},{c,y}}, B_2={{a,c},{b,y}}, B_3={{a,y},{b,c}}. At a fixed middle vertex, compare the three matching blocks through the orientations of the three incident physical dimers. The induced block tournament is vertex-uniform in every signature. For (A,B)=(1,1) it is the transitive order B_1>B_2>B_3; for (1,0), B_1>B_3>B_2; for (0,1), B_2>B_1>B_3. For the doubly misaligned signature (0,0), the induced tournament is the same directed 3-cycle at every middle vertex: B_1>B_3>B_2>B_1. Thus tested-order ambiguity creates three transitive quotient cells up to block relabeling and one genuinely cyclic quotient cell; the 00 cell is uniform cyclic, not quotient-inhomogeneous.

## Hypotheses
The exact four no-P4 signatures of accepted/provisional R516 on X={a,b,c,y}.

## Scope
Correct matching-block quotient classification for the four terminal-sign no-P4 cells. Repairs the erroneous inhomogeneous 00 classification in R282 and recovers the sound quotient content of the abandoned R283 formulation.

## Applicability
Use after identifying an R516 signature when downstream geometry depends only on the opposite-edge matching-block tournament. Three cells are transitive up to block relabeling; 00 is the unique cyclic cell.

## Persistence
The perfect-matching partition, alignment bits, and induced three-block tournament at each middle vertex are graph-intrinsic on X.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not claim any quotient type is impossible or closing. Does not assert consumers of one transitive block order are invariant under relabeling. Does not identify the cyclic 00 cell with any specialized historical closure theorem.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** superseded
- **Lifecycle note:** Matching-block calculation for the four R280 signatures is incorporated into the corrected canonical quotient summary C263/R298. Preserve R282 as the proof dependency underlying that summary.
- **Curation note:** Matching-block calculation for the four R280 signatures is incorporated into the corrected canonical quotient summary C263/R298. Preserve R282 as the proof dependency underlying that summary.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** PASS: corrected opposite-edge matching-block quotient. Direct reading of R516 gives three vertex-uniform transitive cells and a vertex-uniform cyclic 00 cell B1>B3>B2>B1.

## Proof
Use the opposite-edge blocks B_1={{a,b},{c,y}}, B_2={{a,c},{b,y}}, B_3={{a,y},{b,c}}. At middle a the incident dimers {a,b},{a,c},{a,y} represent B_1,B_2,B_3; similarly each other middle is incident with exactly one edge from each block. Read the three local comparisons from the exact R516 row. In signature 11, at middle a the turns (b,a,c),(b,a,y),(c,a,y) give B_1>B_2>B_3, and the corresponding three comparisons at b,c,y give the same order. The same direct read gives B_1>B_3>B_2 at every middle in signature 10 and B_2>B_1>B_3 at every middle in signature 01. In signature 00, the middle-a turns (c,a,b),(b,a,y),(y,a,c) give B_2>B_1, B_1>B_3, and B_3>B_2, i.e. B_1>B_3>B_2>B_1. Reading the remaining three middles from the same 00 row gives exactly the same directed block edges. Hence the quotient is vertex-uniform cyclic in 00 and vertex-uniform transitive in the other three signatures.

# R520 — Common-anchor strict-spoke count fails without tested-order alignment

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
The quantitative strict-spoke conclusion of historical R252 is false without tested-order alignment. Already for t=3, the exact R516 doubly-misaligned 00 no-P4 signature gives a Strong four-vertex common-anchor cell in which every spoke receives the two expected outer-witness certificates but the two certificates on each spoke use opposite tested dimer orders. Hence no R38 interaction on that spoke is forced from those two certificates alone. In particular R252's claimed lower bound of at least t-2=1 opposite-polarity strict spoke would imply, via R263 on a common tested order, a Hamilton P4 on the same four vertices, contradicting the exact no-P4 cell. The defect is the parity comparison across repeated occurrences of one physical spoke while allowing tested dimer order to change. The tested-order-safe replacement is R519: every common-anchor spoke has certificates from all other outer witnesses for t>=3; when t>=4, pigeonhole among the two tested dimer orders guarantees an R38 interaction on every spoke; when t=3 even that interaction need not be forced. No uniform lower bound on strict opposite-polarity spokes follows without extra alignment hypotheses.

## Hypotheses
Strong Level-(1) boundary antisymmetry. Historical R252 is the object under correction. Accepted R263 and corrected R516/R519 are available.

## Scope
Reconstructible correction fence for the invalid strict-count theorem and for the overstrong t=3 interaction residue that survived into R307/R308.

## Applicability
Use to block any descendant that imports R252's strict-spoke count or assumes every t=3 spoke has a comparable witness pair. Use R519 for the exact tested-order-safe replacement.

## Persistence
The R516 00 cell is a graph-intrinsic counterexample. The corrected R519 witness certificates retain their tested orders; for t>=4 the chosen same-order witness pair and R38 output are graph-intrinsic.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not rule out strict-spoke counts under stronger geometry or explicit tested-order alignment. Does not deny the individual witness certificates. For t>=4 it does not deny, and R519 proves, an R38 interaction on every spoke.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Historical tested-order alignment counterexample; no live use remains.
- **Curation note:** Essential tested-order correction withdrawing the false common-anchor strict-spoke count.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** PASS: exact correction of R252 and the overstrong t=3 residue. R516 00 refutes the strict-spoke parity claim; R519 gives the complete replacement.

## Proof
Take the exact R516 signature 00 on {a,b,c,y} and choose common anchor b with outer set {a,c,y}. The three centered b-middle trimers are exactly the common-anchor fan data. Inspect the explicit 00 row. On each physical b-spoke, its two outer-witness certificates use opposite tested dimer orders. Thus no pair of certificates on that spoke is automatically a same-oriented-dimer input to R38. This already shows why the historical parity multiplication is ill-posed. Moreover historical R252 claims that for t=3 at least one spoke is forced into the strict opposite-polarity branch. Such a strict same-oriented-dimer pair would satisfy R263 and produce a Hamilton tight P4 on these four vertices, contradicting the exact no-P4 property of R516. Hence the quantitative strict-count theorem is false. The correct general theorem is R519. Every spoke always receives all t-1 outer witnesses with tested orders retained. At t=3 no interaction need be forced, as the 00 cell demonstrates. At t>=4, at least three certificates lie on each physical spoke, so two share one of the two tested orders and R38 applies. No strict-versus-collision count follows without additional alignment.

# R525 — Nine-never-condition normalization and literal-insertion barrier

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Let E be any relation on ordered triples of distinct vertices satisfying (PA): for every distinct u,v,w, (u,v,w) is in E or (w,u,v) is in E. On each unordered 3-set T, E contains a four-order subrelation still satisfying (PA), and every minimal four-order pattern is exactly one of nine never conditions xNp: one designated vertex x in T is forbidden from one designated position p in {1,2,3}, while the other four orders are retained. Equivalently, the two omitted orders are one from each cyclic class and necessarily place the same vertex in the same position. The p=2 patterns are reversal-symmetric middle blockers and obstruct at most one literal insertion slot relative to a fixed adjacent pair. The p=1 and p=3 patterns can obstruct two adjacent insertion slots. In particular (PA) alone does not imply that an outside vertex can be literally inserted into a fixed tight path. There is a four-vertex example with tight path (a,b,c) and outside vertex w for which all four insertion positions fail: on {w,a,b} take the never condition bN3, so (w,a,b) and (a,w,b) are bad; on {b,c,w} take bN1, so (b,w,c) and (b,c,w) are bad; choose either of the remaining two triple rules so that (a,b,c) is tight and choose any lawful rule on {a,c,w}. Then wabc, awbc, abwc, and abcw each contain a displayed bad turn. Thus any proof of the unrestricted spanning-path conjecture must allow rerouting/reordering or exploit more than fixed-order insertion.

## Hypotheses
Finite ordered-triple relation satisfying (PA). For the explicit barrier, four distinct vertices a,b,c,w.

## Scope
Order-free normalization/fence for the special prepend/append ternary condition. It precisely separates the easy reversal-symmetric insertion theorem from the unrestricted nine-pattern problem.

## Applicability
Use before attempting a Redei-style fixed-order insertion proof under (PA) alone. Normalize each 3-set to a never condition and track first/last-position double blockers explicitly.

## Persistence
The nine local rule types and the explicit four-vertex noninsertable path are intrinsic finite certificates.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not give a counterexample to existence of a spanning tight path under (PA), nor to the conjectured 2^(n-1) lower bound. It rules out only literal insertion into an arbitrarily fixed tight path.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Historical nine-never-condition insertion barrier; no live use remains.
- **Curation note:** Durable PA-only obstruction to Redei-style literal insertion; preserves the nine never-condition normalization and explicit four-vertex blocker.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Correct nine-pattern normalization under PA alone and valid four-vertex literal-insertion barrier. It is only a fixed-order insertion obstruction, not a spanning-path counterexample.

## Proof
Fix an unordered triple {a,b,c}. The orders split into cyclic classes C+=(abc,bca,cab) and C-=(acb,cba,bac). Applying (PA) cyclically within either class says no two members of that class can both be bad, so at least two members of each class are tight. Deleting surplus tight orders if necessary leaves exactly two tight orders in each class, equivalently one omitted order from C+ and one from C-. There are 3*3=9 choices of omitted pair. Direct inspection shows that each pair has a unique common vertex occurring in the same position in both omitted permutations; conversely fixing a vertex x and position p omits exactly the two orders with x in position p, one from each cyclic class. Hence the nine minimal patterns are exactly xNp. For a fixed oriented adjacent pair (a,b) and outside w, the three literal placements relevant to preserving a before b are (w,a,b),(a,w,b),(a,b,w). A middle-never rule removes at most one of these, while aN1 removes the latter two and bN3 removes the former two, producing adjacent double blockers. For the explicit barrier, make bN3 the rule on {w,a,b}; then wab and awb are bad. Make bN1 the rule on {b,c,w}; then bwc and bcw are bad. Choose a lawful rule on {a,b,c} that leaves abc tight, and any lawful rule on {a,c,w}. The path abc is tight. Prepending w fails at wab; inserting between a,b fails at awb; inserting between b,c fails at bwc; appending w fails at bcw. Every local rule is one of the nine minimal (PA) patterns, so the full relation satisfies (PA).

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/LEGACY/R525.md -->

# R528 — Captured-crossing mirror reentry does not transport ancestry to fresh exterior spokes

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Let x have a valid historical capture certificate through a physical crossing D={x,y}. Accepted R155 may be invoked with any graph-intrinsic historical tight carrier A that is certified before the R155 application, satisfies x in V(A) and y notin V(A), and has a genuine carrier adjacency E={p,x} at x. The carrier A need not be the carrier that was current, selected, or even already certified in the original capture representative; a later-certified tight path through x is admissible provided D genuinely crosses it and E is one of its physical adjacencies. What the capture contributes is historical event ancestry attached to the physical captured vertex x and crossing D. R155 then currentizes the incident supports D and E through their unique tight mirror trimer while retaining that capture event as ancestry.

The lawful fence is therefore narrower than legacy R277. Merely inventing an arbitrary fresh support incident with x does not make it an R155 carrier adjacency: one must first have a genuinely certified graph-intrinsic carrier A containing that support and crossed by D. R155 also does not transport the original selected orientation of D, the original carrier/component identity, old residual rails, endpoint roles, same-frame concentration, or capture protection. Thus later-certified carriers are allowed, but unrelated fresh supports and selected-role/currentness transport remain forbidden.

## Hypotheses
Accepted fully reconstructible R155; a valid historical capture of x through D={x,y}; a graph-intrinsic tight carrier A certified by the time of R155 application with x in A, y outside A, and a genuine adjacency E={p,x} on A.

## Scope
Correction of overstrong R277. It resolves the contradiction between R277's statement and its own validity note by reading the exact reconstructed R155 contract literally. The capture carrier need not be original-frame-identical; the required invariant is a certified carrier crossed by the same captured physical pair D.

## Applicability
When auditing capture-to-mirror arguments, ask whether the proposed second support is an actual adjacency of some certified historical carrier A that D crosses. If yes, R155 may be used even if A was certified after capture. If not, incident-support existence alone is insufficient for the ancestry-bearing R155 conclusion.

## Persistence
Retain the physical captured pair D, vertex x, historical capture event, chosen certified carrier A, genuine carrier adjacency E, and later mirror-trimer certificate. No original representative roles or protection are transported unless separately proved.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not say every fresh support through x is lawful. Does not transport capture ancestry to a support that is not an adjacency on a certified carrier crossed by D. Does not preserve original selected orientations, old cover components, residual rails, endpoint exposure, same-frame concentration, or protection. Does not by itself revalidate any historically invalidated downstream proof; those require independent re-audit on their exact geometry.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** R528 is a route-specific captured-crossing ancestry-blindness fence from a contact program that is no longer live; preserve historically.
- **Curation note:** Permanent correction: captured-crossing mirror reentry cannot transport ancestry onto a fresh exterior spoke.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Corrected literal scope of R155: the carrier need only be certified by application time and crossed by the captured pair; original-frame carrier identity is not required. Arbitrary incident supports still are not carrier adjacencies for purposes of citing exact R155.

## Proof
Accepted R155 states: let A be a graph-intrinsic historical carrier path, let D={x,y} be a physical crossing with x in A and y outside A, retain the historical fact that x was captured using D, and choose any carrier adjacency E={p,x}; then a later minimum three-cover currentizes D and E as the boundary supports of their unique tight mirror trimer, while the capture event remains ancestry. None of these hypotheses says A must have been current in, or identical to a carrier from, the original capture frame. Historical capture is attached to the physical event (x,D), and R155 explicitly refuses to transport selected orientations or old carrier currentness. Hence if a path A is certified later but before the R155 application, and D crosses A at x, it satisfies the theorem exactly. Conversely, an arbitrary fresh support E incident with x is not enough: unless E is an adjacency of some certified carrier A with y outside A, the R155 carrier-adjacency hypothesis has not been met. This proves the corrected fence and shows that the stronger prohibition asserted in R277 was not a consequence of R155.

<!-- END FILE: A7C3/ARCHAEOLOGY/RESULTS/USABLE/LEGACY/R528.md -->

# R530 — Internal captured crossing mirror-orientation normal form

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Let A=(...,l,x,r,...) be a graph-intrinsic historical tight carrier path in a smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample, let D={x,z} be a physical crossing of A with z outside A, and suppose x has a valid historical capture certificate through D. Assume x is internal on A, with distinct historical carrier neighbors l,r. Apply R155 separately to the genuine carrier adjacencies {l,x} and {x,r}. The left mirror is exactly one of (l,x,z) or (z,x,l), and the right mirror is exactly one of (r,x,z) or (z,x,r). Together with the inherited carrier turn (l,x,r), exactly one of the following four cells occurs.

(HH) (l,x,z) and (r,x,z) are tight. Then the identical tested oriented dimer (x,z) is head-signed by the distinct witnesses l,r, giving the R523 same-head collision packet on the actual captured support D.

(TT) (z,x,l) and (z,x,r) are tight. Then the identical tested oriented dimer (z,x) is tail-signed by l,r, giving the R523 same-tail collision packet on D.

(RC) (l,x,z) and (z,x,r) are tight. Since the inherited carrier turn (l,x,r) is also tight, the identical tested oriented carrier dimer (x,r) is head-signed by the distinct witnesses l,z, giving an R523 same-head collision packet on the genuine old carrier adjacency {x,r}.

(CY) (z,x,l) and (r,x,z) are tight. Then the three x-middle turns (z,x,l),(l,x,r),(r,x,z) form the cyclic middle-x residue. Apply corrected universal four-cell theorem R518 to the tight trimer (z,x,l) with fourth vertex r. Either {z,x,l,r} supports a tight Hamilton P4, or it is the exact corresponding R516 no-P4 signature; in the latter case the additional reverse contacts (x,z,r) and (r,l,x) are tight. Thus the only internal-capture residue not already an R523 collision is a role-labelled P4 or one explicit corrected no-P4 four-cell on the two carrier neighbors, captured vertex, and crossing vertex.

Every output retains the historical capture event through D and the identities of l,x,r,z. The two R155 mirror trimers may live in separate later representatives; only their graph-intrinsic tight-turn certificates and capture ancestry are combined.

## Hypotheses
Smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample; A is a certified historical tight carrier; D={x,z} crosses A at internal x; x has a valid historical capture through D; l,r are the two distinct genuine carrier neighbors of x. Accepted R155,R523,R518.

## Scope
Exact tested-order normal form for an internal historical capture. It replaces the false interaction-only R311 interface and keeps the cyclic mirror-orientation residue explicit.

## Applicability
Use whenever a captured vertex is internal on a retained historical carrier. Read the two lawful R155 mirror orientations literally. Three orientation cells immediately give a same-tested-order collision; the cyclic fourth cell gives P4 or an exact R516 no-P4 signature.

## Persistence
Retain A,D,x,l,r,z, the historical capture event, both graph-intrinsic R155 mirror-turn certificates, and whichever collision/P4/no-P4-cell output occurs. The two mirror currentizations need not coexist in one representative.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not compare reverse-tested certificates on D. Does not claim every internal capture yields an R523 interaction on the captured support. Does not claim the two mirror trimers are simultaneously current. Does not close the P4 or no-P4 residue by itself.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** R530 is a captured-crossing mirror normal form from the retired capture route; no live consumer remains.
- **Curation note:** Exact tested-order internal-capture mirror-orientation normal form; reusable local compiler and correction of false R311, but not a top-level spine theorem.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Exact four-case tested-order normal form verified. HH/TT collide on the captured dimer, RC collides on the genuine carrier dimer, and CY is exactly P4-or-R516-cell via R518.

## Proof
Because A is tight and x is internal, the inherited carrier turn (l,x,r) is tight. Apply R155 with E_L={l,x}. The unique tight mirror trimer on {l,x,z} has x as middle, hence is exactly one of (l,x,z) and (z,x,l). Apply R155 with E_R={x,r}; its mirror is exactly one of (r,x,z) and (z,x,r). These choices give four cells. If the mirrors are (l,x,z),(r,x,z), both are head certificates on the identical tested oriented dimer (x,z), witnessed by l,r, so R523 gives HH. If they are (z,x,l),(z,x,r), both are tail certificates on (z,x), so R523 gives TT. If they are (l,x,z),(z,x,r), compare the latter with the inherited carrier turn (l,x,r): both are head certificates on the identical tested oriented dimer (x,r), with distinct witnesses z,l, so R523 gives RC. The only remaining choice is (z,x,l),(r,x,z). Together with (l,x,r), the x-middle orientations are z->l->r->z. Apply R518 to C=(z,x,l) with fourth vertex r. Either the four-set has a Hamilton P4, or the no-P4 branch forces exactly (x,z,r) and (r,l,x), placing the four vertices in the corresponding exact R516 signature. These alternatives are exhaustive. Each mirror certificate was produced by R155 from the same historical capture event, so that ancestry remains attached to the role-labelled output without any simultaneous-currentness claim.

# R532 — Historical-Support Terminal-Reversal Payment

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Let H be a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample. Let S be a graph-intrinsic signed tight support and let T=(t_0,...,t_m), m>=1, be a tight path vertex-disjoint from S. Let D be either terminal physical dimer of T and suppose a signed incarnation of D has polarity opposite to S, so (S,D) is an ancestry-bearing balanced opposite-sign pair of initial mass M=|S|+2. Then there is a chosen certificate-retaining continuation yielding either a spanning two-cover or a strict descendant balanced pair of mass M'<M. In addition, the named terminal position of D in T supplies an explicit terminal extension/reversal certificate before the descent: for any chosen vertex nu in S, testing the literal T-side attachment of nu at D gives either a tight one-vertex terminal extension of T at that end or, by boundary antisymmetry, the exact reverse terminal trimer. This terminal certificate, the original signed-pair birth, and the physical terminal dimer D remain retained as historical ancestry of the chosen descent. The strict width decrease may be chosen so that either prescribed physical endpoint of D is the singleton surviving the first refund step. The head/tail and left/right terminal cases are exact duals.

## Hypotheses
H is a smallest Strong counterexample; S and T are vertex-disjoint tight paths; D is a terminal physical dimer of T carrying a graph-intrinsic sign opposite in polarity to S.

## Scope
Modern explicit replacement for the legacy terminal-reversal payment packet; order-free and certificate-retaining.

## Applicability
Use when a historical signed support is paired with an oppositely signed terminal dimer of a named tight path and a strict paid descendant is needed while retaining the terminal position/reversal certificate.

## Persistence
Retains the original pair birth, terminal path T and physical terminal dimer D as historical coordinates, the displayed terminal extension/reversal turn, the chosen endpoint-survival refund marker, and the resulting descendant pair. No old cover is asserted current after the refund.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not preserve the whole path T as current after payment; does not assert both endpoint-selective descendants simultaneously; does not by itself close the both-singleton floor.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** R532 is an ancestry-specific terminal-reversal payment compiler with no live consumer. Generic signed-support and exact-cover tools remain active.
- **Curation note:** Generic order-free terminal-reversal payment primitive: opposite-signed terminal dimer plus historical support yields closure or strict paid-mass descent before reset.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** The replacement statement is mathematically sound and preserves the legacy terminal-position function. The terminal extension/reversal certificate is an explicit R3 dichotomy, and the endpoint-selective strict descent is available from reconstructed R224. Acceptance of the revision does not by itself certify reconstructibility; a full proof route will be attached next.

## Proof
Let D be the stated signed terminal dimer of T and name the inherited tight turn witnessing its sign. First record the terminal-position certificate independently of payment. If D is the right terminal dimer (t_{m-1},t_m), choose any nu in V(S) and test (t_{m-1},t_m,nu). If tight, (t_0,...,t_m,nu) is a one-vertex tight terminal extension of T. If bad, R3 gives the exact reversal (nu,t_m,t_{m-1}) tight. For the left terminal dimer, test (nu,t_0,t_1); if tight then (nu,t_0,...,t_m) extends T, and if bad R3 gives (t_1,t_0,nu) tight. Thus in all four left/right polarity cases an explicit terminal extension-or-reversal turn is retained. Now ignore currentness of T and use the graph-intrinsic balanced pair (S,D). Its initial mass is M=|S|+2, with |S|>=1. Accepted R224 applies to the signed physical dimer D and the opposite-polarity support S. Prescribe either physical endpoint z of D. R224 gives a chosen ancestry-retaining continuation that either produces a spanning two-cover or first refunds D to the signed singleton (z) and then reaches a mass-two both-singleton floor while preserving z. In the nonclosing branch the resulting mass Mprime=2 is strictly smaller than M. Because the terminal extension/reversal turn, T, D, the original pair birth, and the chosen endpoint are graph-intrinsic historical certificate data, they remain retained while the R224 continuation changes representatives. This proves the full R532 contract, including endpoint selectivity and all left/right head/tail duals.

# R533 — Every hypothetical smallest counterexample is beyond order ten

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Every hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample H has |V(H)|>10.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample.

## Scope
Global order gate for the smallest-counterexample program. It converts every theorem stated in the beyond-order-ten regime into a theorem covering every surviving hypothetical smallest counterexample.

## Applicability
Use before the modern O4 spine whenever a theorem is phrased for counterexamples beyond order ten.

## Persistence
Pure order statement; no representative-relative coordinates are involved.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not itself produce a two-cover or specify any O4 provenance.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** R533 is a redundant beyond-order-ten wrapper around the accepted order-ten closure. O4 already pins R191 directly, and O6 explicitly forbids R533 as a closing input. Preserve historically.
- **Curation note:** Global order gate: every hypothetical smallest counterexample is beyond order ten. This is canonical because it makes the modern beyond-order-ten spine globally applicable and replaces the old need for an arbitrary-order front door.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** The global order-gate statement is correct: the smallest-counterexample program forces at least a proper trimer, six-set P5 density then forces order at least ten, and R191 excludes ten.

## Proof
Let H be a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample of order n. We prove n>10 without using the exterior-five floor R169.\n\nFirst suppose n<=8. By R4, pc(H)=3 and every nonempty proper induced subsystem has path-cover number at most two. Fix any vertex z. The subsystem H-z cannot be Hamiltonian: a Hamilton tight path on H-z together with the singleton path (z) would be a spanning two-path cover of H, contradicting pc(H)=3. Hence H-z has an exact two-cover A sqcup B. Since |A|+|B|=n-1<=7, one rail has order at most three. Therefore H satisfies the failure hypothesis of accepted R881: some exact singleton-deletion two-cover has a rail of order at most three. The conclusion of R881 places every such surviving failure in a synchronized order-three frame H=X sqcup Q with |X|=4 and Q=(q_0,...,q_m), m>=6. Thus n=4+(m+1)=m+5>=11, contradiction. Hence n>=9.\n\nNow suppose n=9. Choose any six-vertex subset W of H. Accepted R193 supplies a tight path K on five vertices of W. Its exterior E=V(H)-V(K) has exactly four vertices. Choose any z in E. The remaining three-set E-{z} supports a tight trimer T by R3: for any ordering of its three distinct vertices, exactly one of that ordering and its complete reversal is tight. Thus K sqcup T is a literal spanning two-cover of H-z. Again H-z cannot be Hamiltonian, since a Hamilton path of H-z together with singleton z would two-cover H. Hence K sqcup T is an exact singleton-deletion two-cover with the rail T of order three. Accepted R881 therefore forces n>=11, contradicting n=9. Consequently n>=10.\n\nFinally n=10 is impossible by R191, the order-ten closure theorem. Therefore every hypothetical smallest counterexample has n>10, exactly the conclusion of R533.\n\nThe route uses R881 only through its clean noncircular implication from an actual short-rail singleton-deletion exact cover to the surviving m>=6 frame. It does not assume R24. The historical dependency R169 is completely absent. At present R191 has the clean pending alternate proof P1096; thus this repair isolates the only remaining review dependency of the order-ten endpoint in R191 rather than the quarantined R24/R169 artery.

# R538 — Complementary prefix absorbers force dual one-witness tail non-Hamiltonicity

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Let H be a finite boundary tournament with pc(H)>2. Let T be a vertex set, let c,d be distinct vertices outside T, and suppose there are tight paths L_c and L_d such that V(L_c)=V(H)\\(T union {d}) and V(L_d)=V(H)\\(T union {c}). Then neither H[T union {c}] nor H[T union {d}] has a Hamilton tight path. In the R24 left-end packet, the two certified prefix P5s q1,q0,a,b,d and q1,q0,b,a,c give this with T=V(Q[2,m]): hence both one-witness tails c+Q[2,m] and d+Q[2,m] are non-Hamiltonian.

## Hypotheses
Finite H with pc(H)>2; disjoint named T,c,d; the two complementary absorber paths exist literally.

## Scope
Order-free replacement lemma; specialized R24 consequence packages the left endpoint gate into two graph-intrinsic non-Hamiltonian tail statements.

## Applicability
Use whenever two alternative path absorbers cover the complement of one of two witnesses. It converts local alternative absorbers into global induced-subgraph Hamiltonicity obstructions.

## Persistence
Persist T,c,d and the two absorber paths. The non-Hamiltonicity conclusions are graph-intrinsic.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert anything about literal insertion positions or orientations of Hamilton paths on larger sets.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** R538 is a proof-level prefix-absorber helper whose sole live consumer is the canonical gate compressor R541. Preserve historically.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Accepted order-free complementary-absorber non-Hamiltonicity lemma.

## Proof
Assume H[T union {c}] has a Hamilton tight path K_c. By hypothesis L_d is a tight path with vertex set V(H)\\(T union {c}). Thus K_c and L_d are vertex-disjoint tight paths whose supports partition V(H), contradicting pc(H)>2. Therefore H[T union {c}] is non-Hamiltonian. The argument for H[T union {d}] using L_c is identical. In the R24 packet, L_c=(q1,q0,a,b,d) has complement {c} union V(Q[2,m]) and L_d=(q1,q0,b,a,c) has complement {d} union V(Q[2,m]), so both displayed tails are non-Hamiltonian.

# R543 — Order-three rail dichotomy: paid boundary collision or aligned two-ended trap

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Let H be a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample. Let X={a,b,c,z} be a transitive matching-height four-cell with M(ab)=M_R, M(ac)=M_S, M(bc)=M_L. Let Q=(q_0,...,q_m), m>=3, be a tight path such that H-z has the literal two-cover on supports {a,b,c} and V(Q), and assume X union {q_0} and X union {q_m} are P5-free with endpoint reverse stars q_1 q_0 x and x q_m q_{m-1} tight for every x in X. The three tight trimer orders on {a,b,c} are (a,b,c),(a,c,b),(b,a,c). For any such order (u,v,w), test the junctions (v,w,q_0) and (q_m,u,v). If either is bad, its R3 reverse together with the forced z-extension reverse contact gives a same-polarity two-witness collision on the corresponding reverse terminal dimer, so R542 forces capture/payment. If all six junctions are tight, then bcq_0, cbq_0, acq_0, q_mab, q_mac, q_mba are tight. Accepted R549 and R534 then force the aligned gate packet: M_L edge az is fully outgoing at q_0; M_S edge bz is fully outgoing at q_0 while ac is fully incoming; M_R edge cz is fully incoming at q_m; M_S edge bz is fully incoming at q_m while ac is fully outgoing. Consequently (q_1,q_0,b,z,q_m,q_{m-1}) is a literal tight P6. Thus the frame lies in the paid-boundary-collision branch or this explicit aligned two-ended trap branch.

## Hypotheses
H hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample; X={a,b,c,z} transitive matching-height with the displayed matching labels; Q=(q_0,...,q_m), m>=3, tight and disjoint from X; H-z has the literal exact two-cover with trimer support {a,b,c} and Q; X+q_0 and X+q_m are P5-free; the displayed endpoint reverse stars hold; R3, R534, R542, and R549.

## Scope
Explicit smallest-counterexample reduction. The unrecovered historical endpoint-trap hypothesis is replaced by accepted R549, and the former hard-frame shorthand is expanded into literal data.

## Applicability
Use before R146 witness selection or pair-deletion fragmentation. The second branch is a fixed aligned gate normal form, not an anonymous hard six-cell.

## Persistence
Retain matching labels, the tested tight trimer order if collision occurs, exact bad seam and two witnesses; or in aligned branch all displayed gate turns and the P6 q_1,q_0,b,z,q_m,q_{m-1}.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Payment may end at a singleton signed-support descendant rather than immediate closure. The aligned P6 alone is not a spanning two-cover.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Historical order-three paid-collision/aligned-trap reduction. Its accepted revision remains a reconstructible premise of R596, but the modern active interface is R594/R596/R619 and physical exact-cover geometry rather than payment/trap branching.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Accepted after replacing the unrecovered endpoint-trap reference by R549 and spelling out the former hard-frame data, including m>=3.

## Proof
In the transitive matching-height four-cell, the triangle on {a,b,c} has edge heights M(ab)=M_R, M(ac)=M_S, M(bc)=M_L. Hence exactly the three orders abc, acb, bac are tight. Fix any tight order (u,v,w). Since H-z=(u,v,w) sqcup Q is still the same literal exact deletion cover, the tail extension (u,v,w,z) cannot be tight together with Q; therefore (v,w,z) is bad and R3 gives (z,w,v) tight. Similarly (z,u,v,w) cannot be tight together with Q, so (z,u,v) is bad and R3 gives (v,u,z) tight. Now if the P-to-Q side seam (v,w,q_0) is bad, R3 gives (q_0,w,v) tight; together with (z,w,v) this is a same-polarity two-witness collision on tested dimer (w,v), with witnesses q_0,z, so R542 applies. If the Q-to-P side seam (q_m,u,v) is bad, R3 gives (v,u,q_m) tight; together with (v,u,z) this is the dual collision on (v,u), with witnesses q_m,z. This proves the first branch. Assume therefore that both P-side seams are tight for all three tight orders. Reading the three orders gives bcq_0, cbq_0, acq_0 and q_mab, q_mac, q_mba tight. At q_0, bcq_0 and cbq_0 imply by R3 that q_0cb and q_0bc are bad, so the M_L edge bc cannot be the fully outgoing bottom gate supplied by the R549 extreme matching gate existence theorem. Hence the complementary M_L edge az is fully outgoing: q_0az and q_0za are tight. Also acq_0 makes q_0ca bad, so the M_S edge ac cannot be the fully outgoing middle gate. By R534 exactly one M_S edge is fully outgoing and the complementary one fully incoming; therefore bz is fully outgoing at q_0 and ac fully incoming. At q_m, q_mab and q_mba make the M_R edge ab fully outgoing, hence it cannot be the fully incoming top gate; the complementary M_R edge cz is therefore fully incoming. Since q_mac is tight, its reversal caq_m is bad, so ac cannot be the fully incoming M_S edge. R534 therefore makes ac fully outgoing and bz fully incoming at q_m. In particular q_0bz and bzq_m are tight. The standing endpoint reverse stars give q_1q_0b and zq_mq_{m-1} tight. Thus the consecutive turns of (q_1,q_0,b,z,q_m,q_{m-1}) are q_1q_0b, q_0bz, bzq_m, zq_mq_{m-1}, all tight, proving the explicit aligned P6 and the dichotomy.

# R550 — Dimer pure-C rail seam refinement in the both-bad CS cell

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Retain a full R513 both-bad CS packet with s=1. Thus the pure C-rail is the dimer K=(c_0,c_1), the cut satisfies 2<=j<=m-1, the seam four-set is F={a,b,c,d} with a=q_{j-2}, b=q_{j-1}, c=c_0, d=c_1, and both seam holes (a,b,c) and (b,c,d) are bad. Write g=(b_r,q_j,q_{j+1}) for the isolated mixed-seam hole. Then the unique Hamilton P4 on F retaining the oriented Q-boundary dimer (a,b) as prefix is P_L=(a,b,d,c). If P_L is tight, replacing the seam by P_L yields a spanning proposal with sole uncertified turn g, so g is bad and its reverse is tight. If (a,b,d) is bad, then (d,b,a) is tight and together with the already forced (c,b,a) gives an R523 same-head collision on tested dimer (b,a) with witnesses c,d. If (b,d,c) is bad, then (c,d,b) is tight.

## Hypotheses
H is finite Strong Level-(1) with pc(H)>2; the full accepted R513 both-bad CS packet is retained with s=1 and 2<=j<=m-1.

## Scope
Order-free coordinate-preserving refinement of the accepted R513 CS residue restricted to a dimer pure C-rail.

## Applicability
Use inside an R513 both-bad CS cell when s=1. Test the two turns of P_L=(q_{j-2},q_{j-1},c_1,c_0): if both are tight reduce to the sole mixed hole g; if the first is bad retain the R523 collision on the reversed Q-seam dimer; if the second is bad retain its R3 reverse.

## Persistence
Retain the full R513 packet, cut index j, dimer pure rail K, both bad natural seam holes, the two P_L turn statuses, the sole-hole proposal when certified, and the collision packet when the first P_L turn is bad.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not replace or narrow R513. Does not treat s>=2, the SC side, or assert that P_L is always tight. Does not claim an alternative deletion cover or lexicographic decrease.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** R550 is a narrow both-bad CS seam implementation lemma now encapsulated by canonical five-cell parent R865.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Accepted as an independent refinement claim so the broader canonical R513/C408 contract is not narrowed.

## Proof
Retain the R513 both-bad CS packet with s=1. Put a=q_{j-2}, b=q_{j-1}, c=c_0, d=c_1. The natural seam turns abc and bcd are bad, so R3 gives cba and dcb tight. The inherited isolated mixed hole is g=(b_r,q_j,q_{j+1}).\n\nAny Hamilton P4 on {a,b,c,d} with prefix (a,b) has form (a,b,x,y) with {x,y}={c,d}. The order (a,b,c,d) fails at abc, so the unique possible prefix-preserving order is P_L=(a,b,d,c), and it is tight exactly when abd and bdc are tight.\n\nIf P_L is tight, set U_L=(q_0,...,q_{j-1},d,c) and keep the inherited mixed rail V=(b_0,...,b_r,q_j,...,q_m). Every turn of U_L is either an old Q-turn or one of abd,bdc; because s=1 there is no further C suffix. Every turn of V is inherited except g. Thus {g} is the complete uncertified-turn set. Since pc(H)>2, g cannot be tight; R3 gives (q_{j+1},q_j,b_r) tight.\n\nIf abd is bad, R3 gives dba tight. Together with inherited cba, this gives two head certificates on the same tested oriented dimer (b,a), with distinct witnesses d and c; R523 identifies the exact same-head collision packet. If bdc is bad, R3 gives cdb tight. These alternatives exhaust the possible failure of P_L. The construction rewrites only the spanning proposal and makes no claim about changing the deletion cover.
