# R554 — Transitive order-three rail forces a hinged opposite-polarity double collision

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Retain the full accepted R543 transitive order-three rail frame, normalized by X={a,b,c,z} with M_R={ab,cz}>M_S={ac,bz}>M_L={bc,az} and Q=(q_0,...,q_m). Among the six P-side seams from the three tight orders (a,b,c),(a,c,b),(b,a,c), at least one of bcq_0 and cbq_0 is bad, and at least one of q_mab and q_mba is bad. Hence at least two P-side seams are bad on the distinct physical rail edges {b,c} and {a,b}. By the R543 collision clause, a bad left seam gives a same-head two-witness collision on one tested orientation of {b,c}, with witnesses q_0,z, while a bad right seam gives a same-tail two-witness collision on one tested orientation of {a,b}, with witnesses q_m,z. Thus the frame carries opposite-polarity graph-intrinsic collision packets on dimers overlapping exactly in hinge b and sharing z as a collision witness. Applying R547 at b yields an ancestry-bearing both-singleton floor whose physical singleton supports are c on the head side and a on the tail side, retaining both ancestor collision dimers, tested orientations, witnesses, and hinge-cut certificates.

## Hypotheses
Full accepted R543 frame; in particular X+q_0 and X+q_m are P5-free with the displayed matching-height normalization. Accepted R546 and R547.

## Scope
Explicit consequence of the accepted R543 frame; no undefined historical hard-frame shorthand or global-longest assumption is needed beyond data already retained by R543.

## Applicability
Use before any capture/payment descent when the physical identities of both short-rail boundary collisions are needed simultaneously.

## Persistence
The two collision certificates and the hinge-cut floor are graph-intrinsic/historical certificate data. No claim is made that two later capture descendants are simultaneously current.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert a spanning two-cover. Does not treat the both-singleton floor as contradictory. Does not use four-deletion exactness or cyclic-K4 rigidity.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Valid hinged opposite-polarity collision/floor consequence of historical R543, but zero-dependent and terminates in old paid-floor currency. Preserve historically; modern provenance and exact-cover interfaces are preferred.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Accepted after replacing historical hard-frame shorthand by the full accepted R543 frame.

## Proof
Because {b,c} is an M_L edge of the transitive matching-height cell X and X+q_0 is P5-free, R546 says {b,c} cannot be fully incoming to q_0. Full incoming would mean exactly that both bcq_0 and cbq_0 are tight. Therefore at least one of these two seams is bad. Likewise {a,b} is an M_R edge and X+q_m is P5-free. R546 says an M_R edge cannot be fully outgoing from q_m, i.e. q_mab and q_mba cannot both be tight. Hence at least one of those two right seams is bad. The two forced bad seams lie on the distinct physical edges {b,c} and {a,b}, proving the oracle claim without enumeration and without using the aligned all-seams-good branch.

For a bad left seam, the bad-seam clause already proved in R543 applies to the corresponding tight order of the physical rail: R3 supplies the exact reverse turn at q_0 and the failed z-extension supplies the same tested reverse dimer with witness z. Thus one tested orientation of {b,c} carries two head certificates, with witnesses q_0,z. Dually a bad right seam gives one tested orientation of {a,b} carrying two tail certificates, with witnesses q_m,z. These physical dimers overlap exactly in b and have opposite polarities. R547 therefore applies directly: delete the hinge b from the two historical support orders and use Signed-Interval Rebirth. The nonhinge vertex c survives as the head-signed singleton and a survives as the tail-signed singleton. All collision and hinge-cut certificates remain in the ancestry ledger. No simultaneous descendant-currentness is asserted.

# R556 — Unique two-bad seam cell forces the aligned gate packet minus its two bad turns

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
In the hard transitive R24 order-three frame, assume exactly two of the six P-side seams are bad. By R555 these are cbq_0 and q_mba. Then the endpoint five-cells have the following full gate polarities. At q_0: the M_L edge az is fully outgoing, the M_S edge bz is fully outgoing, and the complementary M_S edge ac is fully incoming. At q_m: the M_R edge cz is fully incoming, the M_S edge bz is fully incoming, and the complementary M_S edge ac is fully outgoing. Thus the exact two-bad cell contains the aligned R543/R544 gate packet except precisely for the two seam turns cbq_0 and q_mba. In particular q_0az,q_0za,z b? are certified as appropriate, and czq_m,zcq_m are certified on the right.

## Hypotheses
Hard transitive R24 frame and exactly two bad P-side seams.

## Scope
The unique minimum two-bad six-seam residue.

## Applicability
Use to actualize the two forced collision packets with the short az and cz crossing markers while retaining exact endpoint roles.

## Exclusions / nonclaims

## Record notes

- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Gate polarities follow exactly from R555 plus R3,R534,R549.

## Proof
By R555 the unique two-bad word is bcq_0 good, cbq_0 bad, acq_0 good on the left and q_mab good, q_mac good, q_mba bad on the right.

At d=q_0, the tight turn acq_0 has complete reverse q_0ca bad by R3. Hence the M_S edge ac cannot be fully outgoing from q_0. R534 says the two M_S edges have opposite full polarities, so ac is fully incoming and its complementary M_S edge bz is fully outgoing. Next bcq_0 is tight, so its reverse q_0cb is bad. Thus the M_L edge bc cannot be fully outgoing from q_0. R549 guarantees that some M_L edge is fully outgoing, and the only other M_L edge is az. Hence az is fully outgoing.

At d=q_m, q_mac is tight, so its reverse caq_m is bad. Thus ac cannot be fully incoming to q_m. By R534, ac is fully outgoing and bz is fully incoming. Also q_mab is tight, so its reverse baq_m is bad. Therefore the M_R edge ab cannot be fully incoming to q_m. R549 guarantees a fully incoming M_R edge, hence the complementary top edge cz is fully incoming.

These are exactly the asserted gate polarities.

## Statement
Assume the unique exactly-two-bad transitive R24 seam cell of R555/R556. Then the two forced collision packets admit explicit same-frame capture/actualization certificates using only the original deletion frame. On the left, the collision support (b,c) is head-signed by q_0 (and also by z). Pair-delete {b,c}. Dually, pair-delete {a,b}; H-{a,b}=(c,z) sqcup Q is exact. The crossing cz avoids q_m. With marker M_R=(c,z), R556 gives zcq_m tight, so the tail-to-head test q_mcz is bad and actualization yields exactly (c,q_m), head-signed by z with captured/signed anchor c. Hence Pi_R=((c,q_m),(a,b)) is a direct balanced pair birth retaining the right collision, q_m witness, physical crossing cz, captured endpoint c, and z as actualization witness. The four nontrivial supports have cross-birth intersections H_L∩H_R={c}, H_L∩T_R={b}, T_L∩T_R={a}, and T_L∩H_R=empty. The two births are simultaneous graph-intrinsic certificate options; no claim is made that two paid descendants are simultaneously current.

- **Lifecycle note:** Historical minimum-seam capture branch; contact/capture production is saturated and this result has no current external consumer.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** The two pair-deletion frames and R526/R527 actualizations are legitimate and R24-free; currentness fences are respected.

## Proof
R555 gives the left same-head collision on tested support (b,c), in particular q_0bc tight, and the right same-tail collision on (a,b), in particular abq_m tight. Pair-Deletion Rigidity R429 says pc(H-{b,c})=pc(H-{a,b})=2. The displayed decompositions (z,a) sqcup Q and (c,z) sqcup Q are literal two-path covers, hence exact.

For {b,c}, the surviving short carrier vertex is a and the selected dimer az is a carrier/exterior crossing. It avoids the admissible collision witness q_0. Apply R527/R526 with support (b,c) head-signed by q_0 and marker orientation M=(z,a), designating a as captured endpoint. The relevant marker test is zaq_0. By R556, az is fully outgoing from q_0, so q_0az is tight; R3 therefore makes zaq_0 bad. The bad-test branch of signed-support actualization gives the exact short tail support (q_0,a), witnessed by z, with tail anchor a. This is disjoint from (b,c), so it is the promised balanced pair birth Pi_L.

For {a,b}, the surviving short carrier vertex is c and cz is the selected carrier/exterior crossing in (c,z) sqcup Q, avoiding q_m. Apply the tail-to-head dual with support (a,b) tail-signed by q_m and marker M=(c,z), capturing c. R556 says cz is fully incoming to q_m, hence zcq_m is tight and the reverse test q_mcz is bad. The bad-test branch gives the short head support (c,q_m), witnessed by z, with head anchor c. Pair it with (a,b) to obtain Pi_R.

All four supports are dimers. Their stated intersections follow directly from the vertex sets and q_0,q_m outside X and distinct in the hard frame.

# R56 — Root-marker exact returns

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement

Fix one adjacent dimer of the root five-path and consider any exact cover of its complement. The remaining vertices split into the old exterior marker, the surviving three vertices of the old five-path, and the fixed trimer.

## Scope
Every such return has a precise physical-marker role:

- if the old marker state is selected, it is either a terminal or internal dimer block of one current rail;
- if the marker state is absent, both marker vertices are current rail endpoints or at least one is internal in a literal current turn crossing from the marker class to the rest.

In all cases a current turn crosses the marker cut. This is the order-ten specialization of the accepted two-singleton marker-role classification parent.

# R563 — Trimer pure-rail both-bad CS cell at j=2 admits a suffix-preserving one-hole splice

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement

Retain a full R513 both-bad CS packet with (j,s)=(2,2). Thus the pure C-rail is the trimer K=(c_0,c_1,c_2), the Q-prefix of the seam is the dimer (q_0,q_1), the seam four-set is F={a,b,c,d} with a=q_0, b=q_1, c=c_0, d=c_1, both seam holes (a,b,c) and (b,c,d) are bad, and g=(b_r,q_2,q_3) exists as the isolated mixed-seam hole of the parent R511 proposal (since 2=j<=m-1 forces m>=3). R3 supplies the forced tight reverses (c,b,a) and (d,c,b), hence K*=(d,c,b,a)=(c_1,c_0,q_1,q_0) is tight. Write rho=(b,a,c_2)=(q_1,q_0,c_2) for the unique R513 right outer turn at s=2.

(1) The R513 reverse-four-segment proposal
U*=(c_1,c_0,q_1,q_0,c_2),\nV=(b_0,...,b_r,q_2,...,q_m)
has complete uncertified-turn set {g,rho}. If rho is tight, this is a literal one-hole proposal with sole hole g, so g is bad and reverse(g)=(q_3,q_2,b_r) is tight. If rho is bad, reverse(rho)=(c_2,q_0,q_1) is tight.

(2) The unique Hamilton P4 on F that retains the oriented K-boundary dimer (c,d)=(c_0,c_1) as its suffix is P_R=(b,a,c,d)=(q_1,q_0,c_0,c_1). It is tight if and only if (q_1,q_0,c_0) and (q_0,c_0,c_1) are tight.

(3) If P_R is tight, the spanning proposal
U_R=(q_1,q_0,c_0,c_1,c_2),\nV=(b_0,...,b_r,q_2,...,q_m)
has complete uncertified-turn set {g}: the two P_R turns are tight by hypothesis and (c_0,c_1,c_2) is a K-turn. Hence this is a literal one-hole proposal, g is bad, and reverse(g) is tight.

(4) If (q_1,q_0,c_0) is bad, then (c_0,q_0,q_1) is tight. If (q_0,c_0,c_1) is bad, then (c_1,c_0,q_0) is tight.

Therefore the R513 (2,2) cell reduces to a one-hole proposal with unchanged V and sole hole g unless both rho and P_R fail, in which case the exact missing turns are rho together with at least one P_R turn, each with its displayed R3 reverse. The construction rewrites only the spanning proposal and does not require D/S membership of q_0 or q_1.

## Hypotheses

H is finite Strong Level-(1) with pc(H)>2. The full accepted R513 both-bad CS packet is retained with the additional parameter restriction (j,s)=(2,2). Tight/bad are complementary by R3.

## Scope

Order-free coordinate-preserving refinement of the accepted R513 CS residue at the unique shallow cell where the pure C-rail is a trimer and the Q-seam prefix is a dimer. It does not treat j>=3 or s>=3, and it does not claim an SC dual beyond the R513 (s,i)=(2,m-2) cell.

## Applicability

In an R513 both-bad CS cell, read (j,s). If (j,s)=(2,2), first test rho=(q_1,q_0,c_2) on the R513 reverse splice; if it is tight, keep U* sqcup V as a one-hole proposal. Independently test the two P_R turns; if both are tight, use U_R sqcup V as a one-hole proposal. If both tests fail, retain the displayed reverse mates as the exact irreducible certificate. If (j,s) is not (2,2), this theorem does not apply.

## Persistence

Retain D,S,Q,T,K,B,A, the unique crossing orientation, cut index j=2, both bad seam holes, g, rho with its tight/bad status, the two P_R turns with their statuses, and the chosen one-hole proposal when certified. Forced reverses are graph-intrinsic; proposal coordinates are representative-relative.

## Exclusions / nonclaims

Does not assert that rho or P_R is always tight, that the both-bad residue is realizable, or that T decreases. Does not splice leftover vertices when j>=3 or s>=3. Does not enumerate anonymous P4 orders other than K* and the unique (c_0,c_1)-preserving order. Does not treat the SC side. Does not use R435, balanced-pair birth, or an unlabeled reverse trimer as an output.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Narrow R513 (j,s)=(2,2) splice refinement with no live consumers. Preserve historically; generic R511/R513 and later short-carrier/block interfaces are the maintained abstraction.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Exact (j,s)=(2,2) CS refinement of R513; hole ledger and suffix-preserving one-hole branch are correct and properly fenced.

## Proof

Work in the retained R513 both-bad CS packet with j=2 and s=2. Then a=q_0, b=q_1, K=(c_0,c_1,c_2), F={q_0,q_1,c_0,c_1}, the turns (q_0,q_1,c_0) and (q_1,c_0,c_1) are bad, and R3 gives (c_0,q_1,q_0) and (c_1,c_0,q_1) tight. In particular K*=(c_1,c_0,q_1,q_0) is a tight Hamilton P4 on F. The genuine three-hole CS range forces j<=m-1, so m>=3 and g=(b_r,q_2,q_3) is a defined mixed attachment on the unchanged rail V=(B followed by Q[2,m]).

(1) The R513 substitution at these parameters is U*=(c_1,c_0,q_1,q_0,c_2). Its consecutive triples are (c_1,c_0,q_1) (a K* turn), (c_0,q_1,q_0) (a K* turn), and rho=(q_1,q_0,c_2). Every consecutive triple of V is a B-turn, a Q-turn, or g. Thus the complete uncertified-turn set is {g,rho}. If rho is tight, the set reduces to {g}. A one-hole spanning proposal in this packet cannot have its unique hole tight: otherwise U* sqcup V would be a spanning two-cover, contradicting pc(H)>2. Hence g is bad and R3 gives reverse(g)=(q_3,q_2,b_r) tight. If instead rho is bad, R3 gives reverse(rho)=(c_2,q_0,q_1) tight.

(2) Any Hamilton P4 on F with suffix (c_0,c_1) has the form (x,y,c_0,c_1) with {x,y}={q_0,q_1}. The choice (q_0,q_1,c_0,c_1) begins with the bad seam hole (q_0,q_1,c_0). The remaining choice is P_R=(q_1,q_0,c_0,c_1), tight exactly when (q_1,q_0,c_0) and (q_0,c_0,c_1) are tight.

(3) Assume P_R is tight. Form U_R=(q_1,q_0,c_0,c_1,c_2). Its first two triples are the turns of P_R, hence tight. Its last triple is (c_0,c_1,c_2), a K-turn. The rail V is unchanged, with sole mixed attachment g. There is no omitted vertex: V(U_R)= {q_0,q_1} union V(K) and V(V)=V(B) union V(Q[2,m]), which together exhaust V(H) because {q_0,q_1}=Q[0,j-1] at j=2. Therefore the complete uncertified-turn set is {g}, g is bad, and reverse(g) is tight.

(4) If (q_1,q_0,c_0) is bad, R3 gives (c_0,q_0,q_1) tight. If (q_0,c_0,c_1) is bad, R3 gives (c_1,c_0,q_0) tight.

No vertex of T is moved, and the D/S membership of q_0,q_1 is unused, because both displayed proposals rewrite the spanning R511/R513 rails rather than exchanging blocks of H-D.

# R565 — Trimer pure-rail both-bad CS cell at j=3 has a three-splice hole menu

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement

Retain a full R513 both-bad CS packet with (j,s)=(3,2). Thus K=(c_0,c_1,c_2), the seam four-set is F={a,b,c,d} with a=q_1, b=q_2, c=c_0, d=c_1, both seam holes (a,b,c) and (b,c,d) are bad, and g=(b_r,q_3,q_4) exists because j=3<=m-1 forces m>=4. R3 supplies (c,b,a) and (d,c,b) tight, so K*=(d,c,b,a)=(c_1,c_0,q_2,q_1) is tight. Write lambda*=(q_0,c_1,c_0), rho=(q_2,q_1,c_2), lambda=(q_0,q_2,q_1), and sigma=(c_1,c_0,c_2).

(1) The R513 reverse-four-segment proposal
U*=(q_0,c_1,c_0,q_2,q_1,c_2),\nV=(b_0,...,b_r,q_3,...,q_m)
has complete uncertified-turn set {g,lambda*,rho}. If both lambda* and rho are tight, this is a literal one-hole proposal with sole hole g. If exactly one of lambda*,rho is tight, it is a literal two-hole proposal.

(2) The unique Hamilton P4 on F retaining suffix (c_0,c_1) is P_R=(q_2,q_1,c_0,c_1). If P_R is tight, the proposal
U_R=(q_0,q_2,q_1,c_0,c_1,c_2),\nV as above
has complete uncertified-turn set {g,lambda}, since (c_0,c_1,c_2) is a K-turn. If additionally lambda is tight, this is a one-hole proposal with sole hole g.

(3) The unique Hamilton P4 on F retaining prefix (q_1,q_2) is P_L=(q_1,q_2,c_1,c_0). If P_L is tight, the proposal
U_L=(q_0,q_1,q_2,c_1,c_0,c_2),\nV as above
has complete uncertified-turn set {g,sigma}, since (q_0,q_1,q_2) is a Q-turn.

(4) If any displayed outer turn is bad, R3 supplies its reverse. In particular if lambda* is bad then (c_0,c_1,q_0) is tight; if rho is bad then (c_2,q_1,q_2) is tight; if lambda is bad then (q_1,q_2,q_0) is tight; if sigma is bad then (c_2,c_0,c_1) is tight.

Thus the cell is a one-hole proposal with unchanged V and sole hole g whenever any one of the three splices has all of its listed outer turns tight. Otherwise it is a two-hole proposal from that splice, or an irreducible cell whose missing outer turns are among {lambda*,rho,lambda,sigma}, each with its displayed reverse. No D/S membership of q_1,q_2 is used.

## Hypotheses

H is finite Strong Level-(1) with pc(H)>2. The full accepted R513 both-bad CS packet is retained with (j,s)=(3,2). Tight/bad are complementary by R3.

## Scope

Order-free coordinate-preserving refinement of the R513 CS residue at the unique cell where the Q-seam prefix has length three and the pure C-rail is a trimer. It does not treat j>=4 or s>=3.

## Applicability

In an R513 both-bad CS cell with (j,s)=(3,2), test the outer turns of U*, U_R, and U_L in that order. Stop at the first splice whose listed outer turns are all tight and keep that one-/two-hole proposal. If none succeeds, retain the four named missing turns and their R3 reverses.

## Persistence

Retain D,S,Q,T,K,B,A, crossing orientation, cut index j=3, both bad seam holes, g, the four named outer turns with tight/bad status, and the chosen proposal when certified. Forced reverses are graph-intrinsic; proposal coordinates are representative-relative.

## Exclusions / nonclaims

Does not assert that any splice is always tight, that the both-bad residue is realizable, or that T decreases. Does not treat j>=4 or s>=3. Does not enumerate anonymous P4 orders beyond K*, P_R, and P_L. Does not treat the SC side. Does not use R435, balanced-pair birth, or an unlabeled reverse trimer as an output.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Narrow R513 (j,s)=(3,2) three-splice menu with no live consumers. Preserve historically; generic unique-transition seam machinery is the maintained interface.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Valid (j,s)=(3,2) three-splice menu; states only exact one/two-hole or named residual certificates.

## Proof

Work in the retained R513 both-bad CS packet with j=3 and s=2. Then a=q_1, b=q_2, K=(c_0,c_1,c_2), F={q_1,q_2,c_0,c_1}, the turns (q_1,q_2,c_0) and (q_2,c_0,c_1) are bad, and R3 gives (c_0,q_2,q_1) and (c_1,c_0,q_2) tight. Hence K*=(c_1,c_0,q_2,q_1) is tight. The range j<=m-1 forces m>=4, so g=(b_r,q_3,q_4) is a defined mixed attachment on the unchanged rail V=(B followed by Q[3,m]).

(1) The R513 substitution is U*=(q_0,c_1,c_0,q_2,q_1,c_2). Its consecutive triples are lambda*=(q_0,c_1,c_0), the two K* turns, and rho=(q_2,q_1,c_2). Every consecutive triple of V is a B-turn, a Q-turn, or g. Thus the complete uncertified-turn set is {g,lambda*,rho}. If both lambda* and rho are tight the set reduces to {g}, so g is bad by pc(H)>2 and reverse(g) is tight. If exactly one of lambda*,rho is tight the set has size two.

(2) The only Hamilton P4 on F with suffix (c_0,c_1) other than the forbidden natural order is P_R=(q_2,q_1,c_0,c_1). If it is tight, U_R=(q_0,q_2,q_1,c_0,c_1,c_2) has consecutive triples lambda=(q_0,q_2,q_1), the two P_R turns, and the K-turn (c_0,c_1,c_2). With V unchanged the uncertified set is {g,lambda}. If lambda is also tight this is a one-hole proposal with sole hole g.

(3) The only Hamilton P4 on F with prefix (q_1,q_2) other than the forbidden natural order is P_L=(q_1,q_2,c_1,c_0). If it is tight, U_L=(q_0,q_1,q_2,c_1,c_0,c_2) has consecutive triples the Q-turn (q_0,q_1,q_2), the two P_L turns, and sigma=(c_1,c_0,c_2). The uncertified set is {g,sigma}.

(4) Each bad outer turn has its R3 reverse as displayed. No vertex of T is moved.

# R568 — Dimer pure-C rail seam refinement in the both-bad SC cell

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement

Retain a full R513 both-bad SC packet with s=1. Thus the pure C-rail is the dimer K=(c_0,c_1), the cut satisfies 1<=i<=m-2, the seam four-set is F={a,b,c,d} with a=c_0, b=c_1, c=q_{i+1}, d=q_{i+2}, and both seam holes (a,b,c) and (b,c,d) are bad. Write h=(q_{i-1},q_i,b_0) for the isolated mixed-seam hole of the parent R511 proposal (this turn exists in the genuine three-hole SC range except the already one-hole aligned cells; if i=0 the parent packet is not three-hole). R3 supplies the forced tight reverses (c,b,a) and (d,c,b).

(1) The unique Hamilton P4 on F that retains the oriented Q-boundary dimer (c,d)=(q_{i+1},q_{i+2}) as its suffix is P_R=(b,a,c,d)=(c_1,c_0,q_{i+1},q_{i+2}). It is tight if and only if (c_1,c_0,q_{i+1}) and (c_0,q_{i+1},q_{i+2}) are tight.

(2) If P_R is tight, the spanning proposal
U=(q_0,...,q_i,b_0,...,b_r),\nV_R=(c_1,c_0,q_{i+1},...,q_m),
with empty pieces omitted, has complete uncertified-turn set {h} when i>=1, or empty mixed hole together with the two P_R turns when the parent already listed no h. In the genuine three-hole range 1<=i<=m-2 this is a literal one-hole proposal, so h is bad and reverse(h)=(b_0,q_i,q_{i-1}) is tight. The Q-suffix after q_{i+2} is certified by Q.

(3) If (c_1,c_0,q_{i+1}) is bad, then (q_{i+1},c_0,c_1) is tight. If (c_0,q_{i+1},q_{i+2}) is bad, then (q_{i+2},q_{i+1},c_0) is tight.

This is the exact SC dual of accepted R550: R550 preserves the Q-prefix dimer in CS, while this result preserves the Q-suffix dimer in SC. It does not rewrite C408.

## Hypotheses

H is finite Strong Level-(1) with pc(H)>2. The full accepted R513 both-bad SC packet is retained with s=1 and 1<=i<=m-2. Tight/bad are complementary by R3.

## Scope

Order-free coordinate-preserving refinement of the accepted R513 SC residue restricted to a dimer pure C-rail. Independent of C429/R550, which treats the CS orientation.

## Applicability

In an R513 both-bad SC cell with s=1, test the two P_R turns (c_1,c_0,q_{i+1}) and (c_0,q_{i+1},q_{i+2}). If both are tight, replace the R513 reverse-four-segment proposal by U sqcup V_R and keep only hole h. If either is bad, retain the corresponding R3 reverse. If s>=2, this theorem does not apply.

## Persistence

Retain the full R513 SC packet, cut index i, dimer pure rail K, both bad natural seam holes, the two P_R turn statuses, the sole-hole proposal when certified, and the displayed reverses when a P_R turn is bad.

## Exclusions / nonclaims

Does not replace or narrow R513. Does not treat s>=2 or the CS side (see R550). Does not assert that P_R is always tight. Does not claim an alternative deletion cover or lexicographic decrease.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** R568 is the SC-dual narrow seam implementation lemma now encapsulated by canonical five-cell parent R865.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Sound SC dimer-pure-C dual refinement of R550/R513 with exact one-hole branch.

## Proof

Work in the retained R513 both-bad SC packet with s=1. Then a=c_0, b=c_1, c=q_{i+1}, d=q_{i+2}, F={c_0,c_1,q_{i+1},q_{i+2}}, the turns (c_0,c_1,q_{i+1}) and (c_1,q_{i+1},q_{i+2}) are bad, and R3 gives (q_{i+1},c_1,c_0) and (q_{i+2},q_{i+1},c_1) tight. The parent mixed hole h=(q_{i-1},q_i,b_0) is present for 1<=i<=m-2.

(1) Any Hamilton P4 on F with suffix (q_{i+1},q_{i+2}) has the form (x,y,q_{i+1},q_{i+2}) with {x,y}={c_0,c_1}. The choice (c_0,c_1,q_{i+1},q_{i+2}) begins with the bad seam hole. The remaining choice is P_R=(c_1,c_0,q_{i+1},q_{i+2}), tight exactly when (c_1,c_0,q_{i+1}) and (c_0,q_{i+1},q_{i+2}) are tight.

(2) Assume P_R is tight. Form V_R by traversing (c_1,c_0) and then Q from q_{i+1} through q_m. The first two triples of V_R are the P_R turns. Every later triple on V_R is a Q-turn. The rail U is the unchanged R511 mixed rail (Q[0,i] followed by B), whose only mixed attachment in this range is h. There is no omitted C-vertex because s=1. Hence the complete uncertified-turn set is {h}. A one-hole spanning proposal cannot have its unique hole tight, so h is bad and reverse(h) is tight.

(3) Each bad P_R turn has its R3 reverse as displayed. No vertex of T is moved.

# R57 — Equality coalescence and root rotation

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement

For three Hamiltonian physical classes in an exact two-cover, if one selected transition is forced across each of two named cuts, the transition count is one plus nonnegative excess. On the equality face there is exactly one transition; it joins the two named classes and witnesses both cut requirements. The two class paths coalesce into one current component and the third class is the other component.

## Scope
In an order-ten exact return, equality therefore turns the surviving old five-path trimer and the old physical marker into a new global-longest five-path, while the old fixed trimer remains the other rail. The marker-cut transition and the R15/R16 return crossing are the same unique selected state, not two independent contacts.

The new five-plus-three root legitimately reopens the full split-free root package with the deleted old dimer as its new marker.

- **Lifecycle note:** Order-ten equality-coalescence/root-rotation stepping stone with no live consumers. Its transition-count/equality role is historically useful but not independently needed on the active surface.

# R571 — Two-class common-deletion absorber pressure

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement

Let H be a finite tight-path system with p=pc(H). Let D be a proper vertex set and write W=V(H)\\D=S disjoint-union C with S and C nonempty. Let T be a literal k-path cover of H-D, and let t be the number of selected adjacent states of T with one endpoint in S and the other in C. Write b_S (resp. b_C) for the number of maximal contiguous S-blocks (resp. C-blocks) of T. Then b_S+b_C=k+t.

If H[D union S] admits an a_S-path cover, then pc(H[C])>=p-a_S. If H[D union C] admits an a_C-path cover, then pc(H[S])>=p-a_C. Since b_S>=pc(H[S]) and b_C>=pc(H[C]), one has t>=2p-a_S-a_C-k whenever both covers exist.

In particular, if both D union S and D union C are Hamiltonian, then t>=2p-2-k. Thus in a smallest two-cover counterexample (p=3) every exact two-cover of such a residue has at least two S|C transitions: there is no tau=1 exact two-cover of H-D when both complementary D-augmented sides are Hamiltonian.

## Hypotheses

H is any finite tight-path system. No Strong Level-(1) hypothesis is used. Path-cover number pc is the ordinary minimum number of vertex-disjoint tight paths covering the vertex set.

## Scope

Order-free two-class special case of absorber/transition pressure. It does not treat r>=3 class partitions and does not manufacture Hamilton orders of an existing absorber.

## Applicability

Given a deletion D and a bipartition of H-D, compute a_S and a_C from whatever path covers of D union S and D union C are already certified. If both sides are Hamiltonian, discard every tau=1 exact two-cover of H-D.

## Persistence

Retain D,S,C,T,k,t and the two absorber covers. The inequality is graph-intrinsic. No currentness is claimed for T beyond the supplied cover.

## Exclusions / nonclaims

Does not force either side to be Hamiltonian. Does not produce a second Hamilton order of a single absorber. Does not treat three-or-more class partitions. Does not consume a selected crossing by capture or currentization. Does not depend on pending R566-R570.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** superseded
- **Lifecycle note:** The two-class absorber-pressure inequality is the r=2 specialization of accepted multi-absorber transition-pressure theorem C444/R567. Preserve the historical proof but use the stronger multi-class parent canonically.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Correct two-class absorber-pressure inequality; mathematically valid but canonically dominated by the stronger accepted R567 multi-class theorem.

## Proof

Let T be a k-path cover of W=S sqcup C. On each rail of T, every selected S|C adjacency ends one monochromatic block and starts another. A rail with t_i such adjacencies therefore contributes t_i+1 monochromatic blocks. Summing over rails gives b_S+b_C=k+t.

Let Q_S be an a_S-path cover of H[D union S] and let R_C be a pc(H[C])-path cover of H[C]. The two families are vertex-disjoint on W and together with D they cover V(H). Hence p=pc(H)<=a_S+pc(H[C]), so pc(H[C])>=p-a_S. The symmetric argument with an a_C-path cover of H[D union C] yields pc(H[S])>=p-a_C.

The S-blocks of T form a path cover of H[S], so b_S>=pc(H[S]). Likewise b_C>=pc(H[C]). Therefore k+t=b_S+b_C>=pc(H[S])+pc(H[C])>=(p-a_C)+(p-a_S), which is the stated inequality.

If both D union S and D union C are Hamiltonian then a_S=a_C=1, so t>=2p-2-k. For p=3 and k=2 this is t>=2. In particular no exact two-cover of H-D can have a unique S|C transition.

# R574 — Minimum two-bad R24 cell peels to a two-witness middle and closes through order ten

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Assume the unique exactly-two-bad transitive R24 seam cell of R555/R556, with Q=(q_0,...,q_m), m>=3. Then S=(q_1,q_0,b,z,q_m,q_{m-1}) is a tight P6. Its complement is exactly M={a,c} union V(Q[2,m-2]). Moreover the R536 left and right inward-propagation clauses apply to the complementary middle-gate edge {a,c}: q_3q_2a and q_3q_2c are tight whenever m>=3, and aq_{m-2}q_{m-3} and cq_{m-2}q_{m-3} are tight whenever m>=3. Consequently the exactly-two-bad cell is impossible for m<=5. For m=3 the complement M is the dimer {a,c}; for m=4 it is a three-set and hence has a tight Hamilton P3 by R3; for m=5 the two inward stars meet and (a,q_3,q_2,c) is a tight Hamilton P4 on M. In each case S together with that Hamilton path on M is a spanning two-cover of H. Thus any surviving exactly-two-bad order-three rail residue must have m>=6 (equivalently |V(H)|=m+5>=11).

## Hypotheses
Full accepted R543 hard frame plus the unique exactly-two-bad seam hypotheses of R555/R556; R536 inward propagation; R3.

## Scope
R24 restoration, minimum seam residue. This isolates exactly where the order-ten closure stops and the genuinely longer inward-propagation problem begins.

## Applicability
Use after R555/R556 when the six P-side seams have exactly two bad turns. For m<=5 it closes the residue immediately; for m>=6 retain the shell P6 and the two inward witness stars as the next coordinates.

## Persistence
Retain the shell P6, its complementary middle support M, and both inward-star pairs on a,c. In the surviving m>=6 branch these are simultaneous graph-intrinsic certificates.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not close the m>=6 middle. Does not assert the middle support is Hamiltonian for longer Q. Does not use the unrelated exact-2+2 n=8 problem.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Historical order-ten peel branch; order-ten closure is already solved and this route is not part of the modern R594/core spine.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Exact-two-bad shell P6 and inward stars close m<=5, reproducing the order-ten boundary noncircularly.

## Proof
By R556, at q_0 the M_S edge bz is fully outgoing, so q_0bz is tight; at q_m the same M_S edge bz is fully incoming, so bzq_m is tight. The standing R543 endpoint reverse stars give q_1q_0b and zq_mq_{m-1} tight. Hence S=(q_1,q_0,b,z,q_m,q_{m-1}) is a tight P6. Its support uses exactly b,z and the two Q endpoints with their immediate interior neighbors, so its complementary vertex set is M={a,c} union V(Q[2,m-2]).

At the left endpoint, the fully outgoing M_S gate is bz and its complementary M_S edge is ac. The R536 inward-propagation clause therefore gives q_3q_2a and q_3q_2c tight. At the right endpoint, the fully incoming M_S gate is again bz and the complementary edge is ac, so the exact right dual of R536 gives aq_{m-2}q_{m-3} and cq_{m-2}q_{m-3} tight.

Now close the short cases. If m=3, M={a,c}, which is a tight path of order two vacuously. If m=4, M={a,c,q_2}; by R3, for any ordering of these three vertices exactly one of it and its complete reverse is tight, so the three-set has a Hamilton tight P3. If m=5, M={a,c,q_2,q_3}. The left inward star gives q_3q_2c tight and the right inward star, since q_{m-2}=q_3 and q_{m-3}=q_2, gives aq_3q_2 tight. Thus (a,q_3,q_2,c) is a tight Hamilton P4 on M. In all three cases this Hamilton path on M is disjoint from S and together the two supports partition V(H), contradicting pc(H)>2. Therefore a surviving exactly-two-bad cell must have m>=6, equivalently |V(H)|=4+(m+1)=m+5>=11.

# R576 — Four-root transitive seam synchronization and the 2/4/5/5 law

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Retain a transitive order-three R24 frame with one fixed transitive matching-height four-cell X and tight path Q, and note that for every x in X the same Q together with any tight Hamilton trimer on X-{x} is an exact two-cover of H-x. Normalize each of the four deletion roots so its trimer edges are M_R>M_S>M_L and form its three left P-side seams and three right P-side seams as in R543. Then the sum of the numbers of bad left seams over the four roots is at least 8, and the corresponding sum of bad right seams is at least 8. Hence the four six-seam badness counts have total at least 16. Moreover at most one of the four roots can have exactly two bad seams. If one root has exactly two, then the other three roots have badness counts exactly 4,5,5 (in some order), so the multiset is {2,4,5,5}.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample; X is one transitive matching-height no-P4 four-cell; Q is the common tight complementary rail; each X+q_0 and X+q_m endpoint cell is P5-free with the common endpoint reverse stars. Uses R3/R4 for exact re-rooting and accepted R534,R546,R549 endpoint gate structure.

## Scope
R24 restoration. Simultaneous synchronization of the four one-vertex deletion roots carried by one transitive four-cell.

## Applicability
Use before spending any one root collision packet into payment. It guarantees that a minimum two-bad root, if present, comes with three simultaneous higher-badness sibling roots on the same X,Q frame.

## Persistence
Retain the physical matching-height cell X, the common Q, the four deleted-vertex labels, the three perfect-matchings viewed also as the three pair partitions of the four root labels, and every bad seam as graph-intrinsic turn data.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert any high-badness root alone closes H. Does not identify a spanning two-cover. Does not use R24 or any small-deletion theorem beyond R4 minimality.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** R576 is a frame-specific synchronization implementation step whose durable consequence is spine R596.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Four simultaneous deletion roots obey the claimed seam-count synchronization; the exact-two-bad case forces the 2/4/5/5 multiset.

## Proof
For every deleted vertex x in X, the three-set X-{x} supports a tight trimer by R3, so together with Q it is a literal two-path cover of H-x. It is exact: if H-x were Hamiltonian, that Hamilton path together with the singleton (x) would be a spanning two-cover of H, contrary to pc(H)>2 from R4. Thus all four normalized deletion roots are legitimate simultaneously on the same physical X,Q frame.\n\nLEFT END. Fix one of the two physical M_L edges e={u,v}. In each of the two deletion roots whose trimer contains e, the two bottom seams are precisely uvq_0 and vuq_0, merely listed in opposite order. Let b_e be the number of these two turns that are bad. R546 says no M_L edge is fully incoming to q_0, so b_e>=1 for each of the two M_L edges. R549 says some M_L edge is fully outgoing from q_0. For that edge q_0uv and q_0vu are tight, so R3 makes vuq_0 and uvq_0 both bad; hence b_e=2 for at least one M_L edge. Since each bad orientation of e is counted in both roots containing e, the four roots contain 2(b_{e_1}+b_{e_2})>=6 bad bottom-seam occurrences.\n\nNow inspect the middle seams. For a physical M_S edge f, the two deletion roots whose trimers contain f use exactly the two orientations of f into q_0 as their middle seams. R534 says exactly one M_S edge is fully outgoing from q_0 and the complementary M_S edge is fully incoming. On the outgoing edge both orientations f->q_0 are bad by R3, while on the incoming edge both are tight. Hence among the four middle-seam occurrences exactly two are bad. Therefore the total number of bad left seams over all four roots is at least 6+2=8.\n\nRIGHT END. The same count is dual with M_R. For each physical M_R edge e let c_e be the number of bad orientations q_muv,q_mvu. R546 says no M_R edge is fully outgoing from q_m, so c_e>=1 for both top edges. R549 says some M_R edge is fully incoming to q_m, whose two outgoing reverses are therefore both bad, so c_e=2 for at least one edge. Each orientation is counted in both roots containing that edge, giving at least 6 bad top-seam occurrences. The four right middle seams are the two outgoing orientations q_muv,q_mvu on each M_S edge; R534 makes one M_S edge fully incoming and the other fully outgoing, so exactly two of these four middle seams are bad. Thus the right total is at least 8, and the total six-seam badness over all four roots is at least 16.\n\nIt remains to sharpen the equality-two case. The two physical edges in each perfect matching induce a partition of the four deleted-vertex roots into two pairs: a root lies in the pair for edge e exactly when its trimer contains e. The three matchings M_L,M_S,M_R give the three distinct pair partitions of a four-element set. A root has total badness two only if it has exactly one bad left seam and exactly one bad right seam. Thus its M_L edge must be the edge with exactly one bad incoming orientation, its left M_S middle seam must lie on the fully-incoming (good) M_S edge, its M_R edge must be the top edge with exactly one bad outgoing orientation, and its right M_S middle seam must lie on the fully-outgoing (good) M_S edge. In particular the left-good and right-good M_S edge must be the same physical edge, since the two M_S root-pairs are disjoint. Such a root therefore lies simultaneously in one prescribed pair from each of the M_L,M_S,M_R pair partitions. Any two distinct root labels lie together in exactly one of these three pair partitions, so the intersection of one prescribed pair from all three partitions has size at most one. Hence at most one root has total badness two.\n\nFinally suppose such a root r exists. Its M_L pair is the unique one-bad extreme pair and the opposite M_L pair is fully bad; similarly for M_R. Its M_S pair is the good-middle pair at both ends and the opposite M_S pair contributes a bad middle seam at both ends. The other three root labels each share exactly one of the three selected pairs M_L,M_S,M_R with r. The root sharing only the selected M_L pair has left count 1+1=2 and right count 2+1=3, hence total 5. The root sharing only selected M_R is symmetric and also has total 5. The root sharing only selected M_S has left count 2+0=2 and right count 2+0=2, hence total 4. Thus the four-root multiset is exactly {2,4,5,5}.

# R586 — Longest-path terminal-dimer puncture is a canonical tau>=1 Hamiltonian-absorber frame

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Let H be a smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample and let K=(k_0,...,k_m), m>=2, be a proper globally longest tight path, with exterior E=V(H)\V(K). Fix the left terminal dimer D={k_0,k_1}, and write S=V(K)\D={k_2,...,k_m} and C=E. Assume S is nonempty, i.e. m>=2. Then X=H[D union S]=H[V(K)] is Hamiltonian via K.

By R5, pc(H-D)=2. By R21 and R508, every exact two-cover T of H-D selects at least one S|C transition: the surviving carrier K-D is a nonempty absorbable block. Thus every such T has tau>=1.

If T is a tau=1 exact two-cover of H-D, the R560 unique-transition normal form and the R570 rigidity alternative apply: D union C = {k_0,k_1} union E is non-Hamiltonian, and outside an R566/R435 output there is at most one Hamilton path of X ending (CS) or starting (SC) at the unique S-endpoint x of the selected crossing. Moreover R197 tail-signs the reverse start dimer (k_1,k_0) by every vertex of E, and head-signs the reverse end dimer (k_m,k_{m-1}) by every vertex of E. By R585 the absorber X is R561-free.

The right terminal dimer D'={k_{m-1},k_m} yields the exact dual frame. Thus every globally longest path supplies two canonical common-deletion Hamiltonian-absorber frames in which tau=1 is the remaining low-transition target and reversed-dimer extension is forbidden.

## Hypotheses
H is a smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample; K is a proper globally longest tight path of order at least three; D is a terminal physical dimer of K.

## Scope
Order-free smallest-counterexample parent. No R24 rail, transitive four-cell, or eight-vertex hypothesis.

## Applicability
Use as the concrete longest-path instance of the R570 tau=1 cell requested by current guidance. Subsequent work should attack this frame by a second Hamilton order of V(K) at x, or by forcing the opposite absorber {k_0,k_1} union E to be Hamiltonian (which R570 says would raise tau to at least 2).

## Persistence
Retains the globally longest path K, the chosen terminal dimer D, the partition (S,C), and any chosen exact two-cover T of H-D together with its unique crossing when tau=1.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert that a tau=1 cover exists. Does not select which S-vertex is the crossing endpoint. Does not itself produce a second Hamilton order or close the cell. Does not apply R561 to X.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Old globally-longest terminal-dimer tau>=1 frame has no live consumers, is not fully reconstructible as recorded, and is strategically superseded by modern deep-crossing/core interfaces R803/R804/R808/R810. Preserve historically.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Valid longest-path terminal-dimer puncture frame after replacing circular R5 with R24-free Pair-Deletion Rigidity R429.

## Proof
Let K=(k_0,...,k_m), m>=2, be globally longest and D={k_0,k_1}. Then S={k_2,...,k_m} is nonempty and C=E is nonempty because K is proper. The path K is a tight Hamilton path of X=D union S. Pair-Deletion Rigidity R429 gives pc(H-D)=2, so an exact two-cover T of H-D exists, with both rails nontrivial. The path K-D=(k_2,...,k_m) spans S, hence Q=K is a tight path on D union S. R508 therefore forces every exact two-cover of H-D to select a state with one end in S and the other in C. Equivalently R21 applied to the puncture of K at D says every exact two-cover of H-D crosses from the nonempty surviving carrier to the exterior, at least pc(K-D)=1 time. Thus tau(T)>=1. Now suppose tau(T)=1. R560 supplies the unique-transition normal form: one mixed rail carries all of S together with one C-block, and the other rail is a pure C-path; in particular b_C(T)=2. R570 applies to the Hamiltonian absorber X and this T: H[D union C] is non-Hamiltonian, and outside an R566 two-witness collision or an R435 reverse-order output there is at most one Hamilton path of X in the crossing-compatible boundary role at the unique S-endpoint x. R197 applied to K says that every e in E tail-signs (k_1,k_0) and every e in E head-signs (k_m,k_{m-1}). These certificates live on the terminal dimers of K, not necessarily on the selected crossing of T. R585 applied to K says X admits no one-vertex Hamilton extension into E and therefore carries no R561 reversed Hamilton dimer. The R578/R581 branch is closed in this frame. The right-end dimer {k_{m-1},k_m} is the exact dual.

# R587 — Three-vertex tau=1 wrap branches that force an R566 collision

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Let H be a finite Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament with pc(H)>2. Let D be proper, W=V(H)\D=S disjoint-union C with S,C nonempty, and suppose X=H[D union S] has exactly three vertices and is Hamiltonian. Let T be a literal exact two-cover of H-D with exactly one selected S|C transition, and write x for the unique S-endpoint of that transition. Let Q=(q_0,q_1,q_2) be a tight Hamilton path of X, and classify Q by the wrap tetrachotomy R579.

(CS) Suppose the unique transition is x y with y in C. If x=q_2 and the branch is SW2 or DF, then both Q=(q_0,q_1,q_2) and (q_1,q_0,q_2) are tight Hamilton paths of X ending at x with distinct penultimates q_1,q_0; R566 gives a same-oriented two-tail collision on (y,x). If x=q_1 and the branch is SW1, then rot1=(q_2,q_0,q_1) and the R3 reverse of beta, (q_0,q_2,q_1), are tight Hamilton paths ending at x with distinct penultimates q_0,q_2; R566 again gives a two-tail collision.

Thus the explicitly eliminated CS branch/role pairs are exactly (x=q_2, SW2), (x=q_2, DF), and (x=q_1, SW1). Outside an already-recorded R566/R435 output, R570 then says every surviving CS cell has ending-family size at most one. Equivalently the surviving labelled pairs are: DW with any x; SW1 with x in {q_0,q_2}; SW2 with x in {q_0,q_1}; and DF with x in {q_0,q_1}. No additional elimination is claimed for x=q_0 from this fixed Q.

(SC) The exact head/tail dual holds: whenever the corresponding displayed wrap certificates give two Hamilton starts at x with distinct successors, R566 produces a two-head collision on (x,y).

## Hypotheses
Strong Level-(1); pc(H)>2; |X|=3; X Hamiltonian; T exact two-cover of H-D with tau=1. Uses R579 wrap tetrachotomy, R566, R3.

## Scope
Order-free in |H|. The only size restriction is that the absorber D union S has three vertices. No R24, transitive four-cell, or global-longest hypothesis.

## Applicability
Use when a tau=1 cell has a three-vertex absorber. For a fixed Hamilton order Q, eliminate only the explicit branch/role pairs certified above; do not infer the formerly claimed extra endpoint eliminations at x=q_0 without another Hamilton order.

## Persistence
Retains D,S,C, the 3-vertex absorber, the chosen Q and its R579 branch, the crossing endpoints x,y, and the two explicit Hamilton paths that collide when the listed pairs occur.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not eliminate the surviving labelled branch/role pairs. Does not claim exact Hamilton-path uniqueness, only R570 at-most-one outside explicit interaction outputs. Does not derive any extra x=q_0 elimination by informal symmetry or by reversing Q unless that reversed order is separately certified tight. Does not treat |X|>=4.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Narrow three-vertex tau=1 wrap-role enumeration with no live consumers. Preserve historically; generic/current absorber and seam interfaces are preferred.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Accepted after narrowing the three-vertex wrap/role enumeration; no unjustified x=q0 symmetry remains.

## Proof
Since |X|=3 every tight triple on X is a Hamilton path of X. Let Q=(q_0,q_1,q_2). The R579 wrap seams are alpha=(q_2,q_0,q_1) and beta=(q_1,q_2,q_0). R3 fixes the three reverse orders: reverse(Q)=(q_2,q_1,q_0) is bad, reverse(alpha)=(q_1,q_0,q_2) is tight exactly when alpha is bad, and reverse(beta)=(q_0,q_2,q_1) is tight exactly when beta is bad. In CS, if x=q_2 then Q ends at x with penultimate q_1, while reverse(alpha) ends at x with penultimate q_0 exactly in SW2 and DF; these branches therefore give two endings and R566 yields a two-tail collision. If x=q_1, then alpha ends at x when alpha is tight and reverse(beta) ends at x when beta is bad; both occur exactly in SW1, again giving a two-tail collision. If x=q_0, the only displayed order ending at x is beta when beta is tight; reverse(Q) is always bad, so this fixed Q supplies no second ending at q_0 in any branch. Therefore the explicitly eliminated CS pairs are exactly (q_2,SW2),(q_2,DF),(q_1,SW1). The remaining labelled pairs are DW with any x; SW1 with x in {q_0,q_2}; SW2 with x in {q_0,q_1}; DF with x in {q_0,q_1}. Outside an already-recorded R566/R435 output, R570 gives ending-family size at most one in each surviving CS cell. The SC statement is the exact head/tail dual, using starts instead of endings and the head half of R566. No reversal of Q is assumed tight unless separately certified.

# R588 — Four-complement gap pressure compiles to local capture/payment or a reverse P4 ear

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Let H be a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample and let Q=(q_0,...,q_m), m>=2, be a vertex-simple tight path whose complement X=V(H)\\V(Q) has exactly four vertices. Then at every gap i between q_i and q_{i+1}, the accepted R583 obstruction array compiles to one of two physically typed outputs: (CP) a two-witness reverse-terminal-dimer packet on a local three-vertex subpath of Q, hence the accepted R542 short-carrier theorem forces a certificate-retaining capture/payment continuation; or (EAR) there are distinct x,y in X such that the carrier state q_i q_{i+1} is spanned by a literal reverse P4 ear, namely one of (q_{i+1},x,q_i,y) and (q_{i+1},y,q_i,x) is tight by R584. More explicitly, for an internal gap 1<=i<=m-2, the R583 left packet (x,q_i,q_{i-1}),(y,q_i,q_{i-1}) is exactly a two-witness packet on the reverse terminal dimer (q_i,q_{i-1}) of the tight trimer (q_{i-1},q_i,q_{i+1}); the right packet (q_{i+2},q_{i+1},x),(q_{i+2},q_{i+1},y) is exactly such a packet on (q_{i+2},q_{i+1}) for the tight trimer (q_i,q_{i+1},q_{i+2}). R542 consumes either packet. If neither occurs, R583 supplies two reverse-middle blockers and R584 gives (EAR). At i=0, the only terminal packet is on (q_2,q_1), the reverse terminal dimer of (q_0,q_1,q_2); absent it R583 supplies at least three reverse-middle blockers, any two of which give (EAR). The right endpoint is dual. Consequently an order-three singleton-deletion R24 frame with long rail Q has a gap-by-gap capture-or-ear structure all along Q; generic unspent R38 collision is not a terminal output of this compilation.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample; Q is tight with exactly four exterior vertices; |Q|>=3. Accepted R583, R584, R542.

## Scope
R24-relevant but order-unbounded along Q. The underlying four-complement obstruction R583 is order-free; smallest-counterexample structure enters only when terminal packets are consumed through R542.

## Applicability
Apply to a putative R24 counterexample H-z=P sqcup Q with |P|=3, where X=V(P) union {z}. Every gap of Q now has a physical continuation: capture/payment through a named local Q trimer, or a reverse P4 ear using two of the four exterior vertices. This replaces anonymous gap collisions by consumer-ready outputs and leaves the ear orientation as the only unspent local species.

## Persistence
In CP retain the gap index, local Q trimer, exact reverse terminal dimer, two exterior witness identities, and the R542 capture/payment ancestry. In EAR retain the gap index, carrier state, two exterior vertices, and literal P4 order. All input Q and X coordinates remain graph-intrinsic.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
R542 payment need not close H; it may end at a singleton signed-support descendant. A reverse P4 ear is not itself a spanning two-cover, and its orientation is generally opposite the endpoint role needed by R509/R566. The theorem does not assert simultaneous descendants for different gaps and does not prove R24 by itself.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Gap-by-gap compilation terminating in local capture/payment or reverse-P4-ear currency has no live consumers; modern R583/R833/R846/R875 physical packet interfaces are preferred.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Correct compilation of R583 gap trichotomy: terminal two-witness packets are exactly R542-ready, otherwise R584 gives a labelled reverse P4 ear.

## Proof
Fix a gap i. For 1<=i<=m-2, R583 gives one of three alternatives. In its left alternative there are distinct x,y in X with (x,q_i,q_{i-1}) and (y,q_i,q_{i-1}) tight. Since (q_{i-1},q_i,q_{i+1}) is a tight trimer inherited from Q, (q_i,q_{i-1}) is exactly its left reverse boundary dimer in the notation of R542. The witnesses x,y lie outside that trimer, so R542 applies and forces its capture/payment continuation. In the right alternative, use the tight trimer (q_i,q_{i+1},q_{i+2}); its right reverse boundary dimer is (q_{i+2},q_{i+1}), carrying the two R583 witnesses, so R542 again applies. In the third R583 alternative, two distinct reverse-middle turns (q_{i+1},x,q_i),(q_{i+1},y,q_i) are tight; accepted R584 gives the displayed P4 ear. At i=0, R583 has only the right terminal packet and the reverse-middle alternative. The right packet is on (q_2,q_1), the reverse terminal dimer of (q_0,q_1,q_2), hence R542-ready; if absent, at least three reverse-middle turns occur and any two invoke R584. The right endpoint is symmetric. These cases exhaust every gap.

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement

In a rotated root, the old exterior marker is a signed terminal dimer with a named adjacent witness. View the original root as an exact deletion frame for that marker. For an internal original dimer, the original root has two selected parent-cut crossings with distinct carrier-side endpoints, so at most one meets the sign witness. # R591 — The unique two-bad R24 cell forces a cross-end anchor trimer

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Retain the exact-two-bad transitive R24 cell of accepted R556 with Q=(q_0,...,q_m), m>=2, X={a,b,c,z}, and matching labels M_R={ab,cz}>M_S={ac,bz}>M_L={bc,az}. Put L=q_0 and R=q_m. Then the cross-end trimer (L,b,R)=(q_0,b,q_m) is tight. Indeed R556 supplies the extreme left gate Laz tight, and provisional R589 supplies cRb and bLa tight. If RbL were tight, the six-vertex order (c,R,b,L,a,z) would be a tight Hamilton P6 on X union {L,R}. Its complementary path Q^o=(q_1,...,q_{m-1}) is nonempty and tight, giving a spanning two-cover of H, contradiction. Therefore RbL is bad, and R3 forces its exact reversal LbR tight. Thus the signed anchor b singled out by the unique two-bad seam pattern is not merely common to the two endpoint collision packets: it lies in a graph-intrinsic tight trimer joining the two physical ends of Q.

## Hypotheses
The accepted exact-two-bad R24 frame R556; m>=2; provisional R589 cross-end reverse fan; R3.

## Scope
Specialized R24 restoration lemma for the unique minimum two-bad seam cell. The P6 obstruction is order-independent in the length of the interior rail.

## Applicability
Use in the surviving m>=6 branch of R574/R576. The long rail endpoints q_0,q_m now have a literal common bridge through the distinguished seam anchor b. This is a new cross-end coordinate unavailable in the earlier endpoint-local gate packet and is a candidate input for wrap/recompletion or common-deletion absorber constructions.

## Persistence
Retain X,Q,L,R, the distinguished anchor b, the exact one-hole P6 candidate (c,R,b,L,a,z), its bad hole RbL, and the forced tight cross-end trimer LbR.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert the cross-end trimer itself is a spanning component of a minimum cover, does not make Q wrap, and does not prove the complementary middle Hamiltonian. The conclusion depends on the exact-two-bad gate packet, not on an arbitrary transitive four-cell.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Historical cross-end trimer specialization of the exact-two-bad seam cell; no current external consumer.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Correct exact-two-bad cross-end anchor trimer derived from R556+R589 by a one-hole P6 obstruction.

## Proof
Write L=q_0,R=q_m. Accepted R556 gives Laz tight. Provisional R589 gives cRb and bLa tight. Consider K=(c,R,b,L,a,z). Its four consecutive turns are cRb, RbL, bLa, Laz. If the only uncertified turn RbL were tight, K would be a tight Hamilton P6 on X union {L,R}. Since m>=2, Q^o=(q_1,...,q_{m-1}) is a nonempty tight path, disjoint from K, and K sqcup Q^o spans H, contradicting pc(H)>2. Hence RbL is bad. Boundary antisymmetry R3 gives LbR tight.

# R599 — The exact-two R24 cell yields a four-cross-state weave on one pair deletion

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Assume the unique exactly-two-bad root of R555/R556 in the transitive R24 frame, labelled by X={a,b,c,z}, M_R={ab,cz}>M_S={ac,bz}>M_L={bc,az}, and Q=(q_0,...,q_m). Then the two side-maximal sibling roots of R596/R598 are x_L=c and x_R=a, and the exact enlarged covers are
H-c = (q_1,q_0,b,z,a) sqcup Q[2,m],
H-a = Q[0,m-2] sqcup (c,z,b,q_m,q_{m-1}).
Deleting the opposite endpoint a from the first enlarged P5 and c from the second produces two literal exact covers of the same pair deletion W=H-{a,c}:
T_L=(q_1,q_0,b,z) sqcup Q[2,m],
T_R=Q[0,m-2] sqcup (z,b,q_m,q_{m-1}).
These covers form a four-cross-state weave. T_L selects q_0 b across the two T_R components and selects q_{m-2}q_{m-1} across them; T_R selects b q_m across the two T_L components and selects q_1q_2 across them. Hence R176 applies at four named physical states on one common shadow W, producing four graph-intrinsic balanced-pair birth certificates with the pair-deletion coordinates {a,c}, central X-state bz, and both two-step Q cuts retained.

## Hypotheses
Unique exactly-two-bad transitive R24 root of accepted R555/R556; m>=6 by accepted R574; pending high-side enlargement results R596/R598; Pair-Deletion Rigidity R429; cross-state upgrade R176.

## Scope
Noncircular R24 restoration. Consumes the left/right enlarged roots in the equality-two branch into two explicit covers of one common pair deletion.

## Applicability
The common-shadow weave is a concrete interaction target for certificate payment or a future component-drop theorem; it is stronger than two unrelated one-sided enlarged roots.

## Persistence
All four selected cross states, the exact two cover orders, deleted physical pair {a,c}, shared vertices b,z, and Q interval cuts coexist in the original graph.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
R176 births are graph-intrinsic and need not be simultaneously current paid descendants. The four cross states do not by themselves yield a spanning two-cover under presently accepted consumers. This theorem does not treat frames with no exactly-two-bad root or the case x_L=x_R.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Historical four-cross-state weave of the exact-two-bad seam cell; modern five-cell/core interfaces supersede it strategically.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** The side-maximal roots are identified correctly by K4 root-pair intersections; deleting the exposed endpoint from the two enlarged singleton-deletion covers gives two exact covers of H-{a,c}, and all four named cross states genuinely cross the opposite component partition.

## Proof
Let r=z be the exactly-two-bad root. By R555 its bad seams are cbq_0 and q_mba, while R556 says that at q_0 the M_L edge az and M_S edge bz are fully outgoing, and at q_m the M_R edge cz and M_S edge bz are fully incoming.

In the construction of R596, x_L is the intersection of the root-pair whose trimer contains the fully-outgoing M_L edge az and the root-pair whose trimer contains the fully-outgoing M_S edge bz. The first pair is {b,c} and the second is {a,c}; their intersection is c. Thus x_L=c. Normalizing X-{c} gives local (a',b',c')=(b,a,z): a'b'=ab is M_R, a'c'=bz is M_S, and b'c'=az is M_L. R598 therefore reads
H-c=(q_1,q_0,b,z,a) sqcup Q[2,m].
Dually, x_R is the intersection of the root-pairs containing the fully-incoming M_R edge cz and fully-incoming M_S edge bz. These pairs are {a,b} and {a,c}, meeting in a. Normalizing X-{a} gives (a',b',c')=(z,c,b), and R598 reads
H-a=Q[0,m-2] sqcup (c,z,b,q_m,q_{m-1}).

In the first cover, a is the terminal vertex of the displayed P5, so deleting a leaves the tight P4 (q_1,q_0,b,z), disjoint from the tight suffix Q[2,m], and these supports partition W=H-{a,c}. In the second cover, c is the initial vertex of the displayed P5, so deleting c leaves (z,b,q_m,q_{m-1}), disjoint from Q[0,m-2], again covering W. By R429 pc(W)=2, hence both displayed two-covers are exact.

Now inspect their selected states. In T_L, q_0b is a selected state of (q_1,q_0,b,z); relative to T_R, q_0 lies in Q[0,m-2] and b lies in (z,b,q_m,q_{m-1}), so it crosses T_R-components. Also q_{m-2}q_{m-1} is selected in Q[2,m]; relative to T_R, q_{m-2} is in its Q-prefix and q_{m-1} in its right endcap, so this is a second crossing. Conversely, bq_m is selected in the right endcap of T_R and crosses the left endcap/suffix components of T_L; q_1q_2 is selected in the Q-prefix of T_R and likewise crosses those two T_L components. R574 gives m>=6 in the surviving exact-two cell, so all four displayed states and component intervals are present without endpoint degeneracy. Applying R176 to W with either cover as reference and each named crossing gives the four asserted balanced-pair birth certificates. The applications share the same proper shadow W and spare vertices a,c, while preserving their individual selected-state provenance.

# R600 — Minimum R24 cell has dual short-carrier-payable spoke collisions

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Retain the unique exactly-two-bad transitive R24 cell of R556, with X={a,b,c,z}, M_R={ab,cz}>M_S={ac,bz}>M_L={bc,az}, L=q_0 and R=q_m. Then the two hinge spokes {a,z} and {z,c} already carry tested-order-safe two-witness packets that are directly consumable by R542, without using the later source-replay contacts. On the left, R556 gives Laz tight and the matching-height cell gives caz tight. Thus the tested dimer (a,z) is head-signed by the two distinct witnesses L and c. The tight trimer K_L=(b,z,a) has (a,z) as its reverse terminal dimer, and both witnesses L,c lie outside K_L. Hence R542 applies to (a,z), with complementary carrier singleton b. Dually, R556 gives zcR tight and X gives zca tight, so the tested dimer (z,c) is tail-signed by the distinct witnesses R and a. The tight trimer K_R=(c,z,b) has (z,c) as a reverse boundary dimer, both witnesses R,a lie outside K_R, and R542 applies again, with the same complementary carrier singleton b. The two payable spoke dimers have opposite polarity and intersect exactly in hinge z, so R547 also cuts them to the ancestry-bearing floor on physical singletons (a),(c). Thus the minimum cell contains a dual R542 payment packet whose two short carriers share the same complementary singleton b, the middle of the original turn (a,b,c).

## Hypotheses
The accepted exact-two-bad R24 frame R556; smallest-counterexample hypotheses needed by R542; accepted R547.

## Scope
Specialized minimum R24 cell; tested-order-safe and independent of source-replay contacts or simultaneous paid descendants.

## Applicability
Use before any alternating-hinge replay analysis. It removes the earlier obstruction that the second-generation az and zc collisions had an internal witness: choose the intrinsic X-witness c on az and a on zc instead, making both packets directly R542-payable.

## Persistence
Retain the two physical spoke dimers (a,z),(z,c), their tested orientations and polarities, witnesses {L,c} and {R,a}, the short carriers (b,z,a),(c,z,b), common complementary singleton b, and the hinge-cut floor ancestry.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert that the two R542 paid descendants are simultaneously current, does not itself close the both-singleton floor, and does not identify the selected crossing in an arbitrary later representative.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Historical short-carrier payment branch; generic payment/capture currency is no longer scarce.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Both spoke dimers have the asserted same-polarity two-witness packets on valid reverse boundary dimers of tight short carriers, so R542 applies twice; the opposite-polarity supports meet only at z, making R547 yield the {a,c} floor.

## Proof
Put L=q_0 and R=q_m. Since az is fully outgoing at L by R556, Laz is tight. In the matching-height four-cell, caz is tight because M(ca)=M_S>M(az)=M_L. Hence Laz and caz are two head certificates on the same tested dimer (a,z), with witnesses L and c. Also (b,z,a) is tight because M(bz)=M_S>M(za)=M_L. Its reverse terminal dimer is exactly (a,z), and L,c are both outside {b,z,a}. Therefore all hypotheses of R542 hold and the az packet forces capture/payment with complementary carrier remainder {b}. On the right, R556 gives zcR tight because cz is fully incoming at R. The intrinsic turn zca is tight since M(zc)=M_R>M(ca)=M_S. Thus zcR and zca are two tail certificates on the same tested dimer (z,c), with witnesses R and a. The carrier (c,z,b) is tight because M(cz)=M_R>M(zb)=M_S; (z,c) is one of its reverse boundary dimers, and R,a are exterior to that carrier. R542 applies again, with complementary remainder {b}. The az packet is head-signed and the zc packet tail-signed, and their supports meet only at z. R547 therefore yields the ancestry-bearing opposite-sign singleton floor on a and c. No source-replay turn baz or zcb is used.

# R603 — Minimum R24 cell has a rigid four-incidence matrix and two explicit cross-end pair births

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Retain the surviving unique exactly-two-bad transitive R24 cell, write L=q_0,R=q_m, and assume m>=6. Then H-{a,c} has the two literal exact covers S_1 sqcup Q^o_2 and S_2 sqcup Q^o_2, where S_1=(q_1,L,b,z,R,q_{m-1}), S_2=(q_1,L,z,b,R,q_{m-1}), and Q^o_2=(q_2,...,q_{m-2}). The four selected incidences of b in these two covers force one rigid signed-dimer matrix: the tested dimer (b,a) is tail-signed by both L and z, while the tested dimer (c,b) is head-signed by both z and R. Hence both reverse terminal dimers of the original trimer J=(a,b,c) are directly R542-payable. Moreover the common-witness z incarnations admit explicit actualizations against the original long rail Q: pair-deleting {a,b} and using marker Q turns the tail-signed dimer (b,a) by z into the head-signed dimer (L,z) by q_1; pair-deleting {b,c} and using marker Q turns the head-signed dimer (c,b) by z into the tail-signed dimer (z,R) by q_{m-1}. Thus the cell contains two graph-intrinsic balanced-pair births Pi_A=((L,z)_head,(b,a)_tail) and Pi_C=((c,b)_head,(z,R)_tail), with cross-overlaps Pi_A.head cap Pi_C.tail={z} and Pi_A.tail cap Pi_C.head={b}, while the like-polarity cross supports are disjoint.

## Hypotheses
Accepted minimum-cell data R555/R556, endpoint stars from the R543 frame, safe Pair-Deletion Rigidity R429, actualization R526, short-carrier payment R542, and R3; m>=6 so Q^o_2 is nonempty.

## Scope
Specialized R24 minimum cell. Fully R5-free. The two pair births are graph-intrinsic historical certificates; no simultaneous paid descendant is asserted.

## Applicability
Use as the explicit nonanonymous input to R436/R441 or fixed-turn consumers. It also upgrades both reverse terminal dimers of abc to two-witness R542 packets.

## Persistence
Retain S_1,S_2,Q^o_2; the four b-incidences L->b->z and z->b->R; the witness sets {L,z} on (b,a) and {z,R} on (c,b); the pair-deletion covers (c,z) sqcup Q and (z,a) sqcup Q; the two marker tests zLq_1 and q_{m-1}Rz; and the exact births Pi_A,Pi_C.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert Pi_A and Pi_C are simultaneously current in one cover, does not claim their later paid floors coexist, and does not itself close R24.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Historical incidence-matrix/pair-birth branch with no current external consumer.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Fresh-session audit: statement matches P682. The repaired provenance is load-bearing and now complete: R543 supplies the endpoint/P5-free frame, R589 the cross-end turns used in the two P5 exclusions, and R557 the literal pair-deletion covers used for R526 actualization. No overclaim beyond historical pair births found.

## Proof
Let L=q_0,R=q_m. R556 and the endpoint stars give two tight P6s S_1=(q_1,L,b,z,R,q_{m-1}) and S_2=(q_1,L,z,b,R,q_{m-1}); their common complement Q^o_2=(q_2,...,q_{m-2}) is tight and nonempty for m>=6. Hence each is a literal two-cover of H-{a,c}, and R429 makes it exact. The two undecided fixed-turn incidence tests are forced locally. If Lab were tight, then (z,L,a,b,c) would be a P5 in X+L because zLa is tight (already forced in the aligned endpoint packet) and abc is tight; contradiction. Thus Lab is bad and baL is tight. Dually, if bcR were tight then (a,b,c,R,z) would be a P5 in X+R because abc and cRz are tight; hence bcR is bad and Rcb is tight. Now apply the elementary R434 incidence extraction directly, or simply read the signs. In S_1 the predecessor L->b together with baL makes (b,a) tail-signed by L, while the successor b->z together with zcb makes (c,b) head-signed by z. In S_2, z->b together with baz makes (b,a) tail-signed by z, while b->R together with Rcb makes (c,b) head-signed by R. Both witnesses in each packet lie outside J=(a,b,c), so R542 applies to both reverse terminal dimers. For explicit births use the common witness z. Pair-delete {a,b}; R557 already supplies the literal exact cover (c,z) sqcup Q. The marker Q is disjoint from (b,a) and z. Since q_1Lz is an endpoint-star turn, its reverse test zLq_1 is bad. The tail-signed branch of R526 therefore actualizes Q to the short head-signed support (L,z) with witness q_1. This gives Pi_A=((L,z)_head,(b,a)_tail). Pair-delete {b,c}; R557 supplies (z,a) sqcup Q. Since zRq_{m-1} is tight, the head-signed R526 marker test q_{m-1}Rz is bad, so the actualized opposite support is the tail-signed dimer (z,R) with witness q_{m-1}. This gives Pi_C=((c,b)_head,(z,R)_tail). The stated intersections are immediate.

# R604 — Cross-end rotated return has no quiet internal-middle replay

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Retain the surviving exact-two-bad R24 cell, write L=q_0 and R=q_m, and let J_*=(L,b,R) be the tight cross-end trimer from R591. The long rail supplies graph-intrinsic signed terminal dimers T_L=(q_1,L), tail-signed by witness b, and H_R=(R,q_{m-1}), head-signed by witness b. Let H-{L,R}=U sqcup V be any exact two-cover in which b is internal on one selected rail, with predecessor r and successor s. Then either H has a spanning two-cover, or at least one of the following explicit non-replay anchor contacts occurs: (L) rLb is bad, so R3 gives bLr tight; the proper dimer (b,L) meets the old tail-signed support T_L at its signed anchor L and is physically different from T_L, so R436 yields strict growth, a vertex-simple tight cycle, or a reverse-contact/reversal cell at the retained L-anchor. (R) bRs is bad, so R3 gives sRb tight; the proper dimer (R,b) meets the old head-signed support H_R at its signed anchor R and is physically different from H_R, so R436 yields the corresponding explicit nonquiet output at R. Indeed if neither seam is bad, replacing the selected singleton occurrence b in its rail by the tight segment L,b,R produces a spanning two-cover. Therefore every internal-b exact return of the rotated outer pair {L,R} is zero-quiet and consumes the original long-rail endpoint ancestry; the old b<->z source-replay mechanism cannot survive this rotated checkpoint.

## Hypotheses
Surviving exact-two-bad R24 cell with m>=6; endpoint stars q_1 L x and x R q_{m-1}; accepted cross-end trimer R591; exact pair-deletion cover supplied by R429; R3 and R436.

## Scope
Specialized R24 replay-breaker. Fully R5-free and representative-safe: the exact H-{L,R} cover is arbitrary and only its selected local neighbors of b are used.

## Applicability
Use after rotating to the cross-end outer pair {L,R}. If b is internal in any exact pair-deletion return, there is no protected quiet episode to budget: closure or an immediate physical anchor-contact certificate is forced.

## Persistence
Retain Q, J_*=LbR, old terminal signed supports (q_1,L) and (R,q_{m-1}) with common witness b, the exact H-{L,R} cover, b's selected neighbors r,s, the failed seam, its R3 mate dimer (b,L) or (R,b), and the R436 contact certificate.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not consume the case in which b is an endpoint in the chosen H-{L,R} cover. Does not claim an R436 growth/cycle/reversal output alone closes H. Does not require the old Q terminal dimers to be selected in the new pair-deletion cover.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Historical rotated-return replay branch below the unique two-bad seam route.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Internal-middle insertion of L,b,R has only the two attachment seams; failure of either reverses to a physically new dimer through the corresponding historical endpoint anchor, so R436 applies exactly as claimed.

## Proof
The endpoint stars give q_1Lb and bRq_{m-1} tight. Hence the dimer T_L=(q_1,L) is tail-signed by b with signed anchor L, while H_R=(R,q_{m-1}) is head-signed by b with signed anchor R. By R429 choose any exact H-{L,R}=U sqcup V and suppose b is internal on one rail with selected predecessor r and successor s. Since J_*=(L,b,R) is tight, replacing the occurrence b by the three-vertex segment L,b,R changes only the two attachment turns at the old neighbors: rLb on the left and bRs on the right. If both are tight, the modified rail together with the untouched other rail is a spanning two-cover of H, contradiction. Thus at least one attachment turn is bad. If rLb is bad, R3 gives bLr tight. Then Q_L=(b,L) is a proper tight dimer meeting T_L exactly in L, which is the signed anchor of T_L. Its support differs from T_L because b is in X while q_1 lies on Q. Apply R436 to the older tail-signed support T_L and later proper path Q_L. The exact-replay singleton exception is irrelevant because both are dimers, so R436 gives strict full-T_L growth, strict Q_L growth, a vertex-simple tight cycle, or a three-vertex reverse-contact/reversal cell. This is an explicit nonquiet L-anchor output. If bRs is bad, R3 gives sRb tight. Then Q_R=(R,b) is a proper dimer meeting H_R exactly in its signed anchor R and physically differing from H_R, so the head-side dual of R436 gives the corresponding nonquiet R-anchor output. Hence every internal-b return closes or consumes one of the original long-rail endpoint anchors.
