# R605 — Cross-end rotated endpoint return localizes to anchor contact, terminal collision, or exact state reversal

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Retain the surviving exact-two-bad R24 cell with L=q_0, R=q_m, m>=6, and tight cross-end trimer J_*=(L,b,R). Let H-{L,R}=U sqcup V be any exact two-cover in which b is an endpoint of one rail. If b is the head and that rail begins (b,u,v,...) (with v omitted when the rail has order two), then either H has a spanning two-cover, or: (A) a proper tight dimer through the old R-anchor is produced whose physical support differs from {R,q_{m-1}}, so R436 gives an explicit non-replay anchor-contact/growth/cycle/reversal output; or (C_R) u=q_{m-1}, v exists, and v q_{m-1} R is tight. In the latter case, comparing with the old Q-turn q_{m-2} q_{m-1} R, either v!=q_{m-2} and R523 gives a same-head two-witness collision on the identical tested dimer (q_{m-1},R), or v=q_{m-2} and the exact cover literally begins with the reversed old Q-state q_{m-1} q_{m-2}. The tail-end case is dual: unless a new non-replay L-anchor contact occurs, the rail ends (...,q_2,q_1,b), and either the predecessor differs from q_2 giving a same-tail two-witness collision on (L,q_1), or the cover literally selects the reversed old state q_2 q_1. Thus every endpoint-b return of H-{L,R} is role-localized at one terminal end of Q; no anonymous endpoint mate residue remains.

## Hypotheses
Surviving exact-two-bad R24 cell, m>=6; endpoint stars; J_*=LbR from R591; safe exact pair-deletion R429; R3,R436,R523.

## Scope
Specialized R24 endpoint-return normal form. Fully R5-free. Handles both order-two and longer endpoint rails.

## Applicability
Combine with the internal replay-breaker R604. Every exact H-{L,R} cover then yields closure or one of three concrete long-rail-end outputs: new anchor contact, tested-order terminal collision, or exact reversal of the old adjacent Q-state.

## Persistence
Retain the exact H-{L,R} cover, endpoint role of b, its first two or last two rail neighbors, the one/two-hole insertion candidate, the failed hole and R3 mate, and in the exceptional aligned case the old Q terminal turn and collision/reversed-state certificate.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not itself consume the exact old-state reversal branch and does not claim a terminal R523 collision alone closes H.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Historical rotated-endpoint contact/collision branch; contact production is non-scarce.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Endpoint insertion analysis is complete for order-two and longer rails. The only support-equality exception is u=q_{m-1} (or the left dual), where the endpoint star fixes the near seam and the far seam yields either a distinct-witness R523 collision or literal reversal of the old adjacent Q-state.

## Proof
Assume b is the head of its rail. Write P=(b,u) if |P|=2 and P=(b,u,v,...) otherwise. Replace b by the tight segment L,b,R. If |P|=2 the only new turn is bRu; if |P|>=3 the only new turns are bRu and Ruv. If all present turns are tight, the modified rail plus the untouched second rail spans H, contradiction. Hence some present hole is bad. If bRu is bad, R3 gives uRb tight. The dimer (R,b) is a proper path containing the signed anchor R of the old head-signed long-rail terminal support H_R=(R,q_{m-1}) (witness b); its support is different, so R436 gives the claimed non-replay R-anchor output. Suppose instead Ruv is bad. R3 gives vuR tight, so the proper dimer (R,u) meets H_R at R. If u!=q_{m-1}, the physical support differs from H_R and R436 again gives a non-replay output. Thus the only remaining case is u=q_{m-1}. But then bRu=bRq_{m-1} is tight by the endpoint star, so the second hole must indeed be the bad one and R3 yields v q_{m-1} R tight. The old Q-turn q_{m-2} q_{m-1} R is tight. If v!=q_{m-2}, these are same-head certificates on the identical tested oriented dimer (q_{m-1},R) with distinct witnesses, so R523 gives the stated collision. If v=q_{m-2}, P literally begins (b,q_{m-1},q_{m-2}), so it selects the exact reversal q_{m-1}q_{m-2} of the old Q-state q_{m-2}q_{m-1}. The order-two aligned case u=q_{m-1} cannot survive because its sole hole bRq_{m-1} is tight and would close. The tail case is exact dual. Write P=(...,v,u,b), try (...,v,u,L,b,R), and test vuL and uLb. A bad uLb gives bLu and hence a new L-anchor dimer unless u=q_1; a bad vuL gives Luv and hence a new L-anchor dimer unless u=q_1. When u=q_1, q_1Lb is tight by the endpoint star, so only vuL can be bad; its reverse Lq_1v is tight. Compare with the old Q-turn Lq_1q_2. If v!=q_2, these are same-tail certificates on tested dimer (L,q_1); if v=q_2, the cover literally ends with the reversed old state q_2q_1. This proves the normal form.

In case (3), the right terminal collision on tested dimer (q_{m-1},R), with witnesses q_{m-2} and v, is R542-ready using the tight short carrier (b,R,q_{m-1}); the left collision on (L,q_1), with witnesses q_2 and v, is R542-ready using the tight carrier (q_1,L,b). Surviving exact-two-bad R24 cell; accepted/internal proposed return lemmas R604,R605; endpoint stars; R542.

Its only additional step, consuming each same-polarity terminal collision through the appropriate reverse boundary dimer of a tight trimer via R542, is valid; exact adjacent-state reversal remains the sole unconsumed local residue as stated.

## Proof
If b is internal in the exact H-{L,R} cover, the direct argument of R604 gives closure or a non-replay R436 contact. Suppose b is an endpoint. The direct R605 endpoint insertion argument gives closure, a non-replay anchor contact, a same-polarity two-witness collision on (q_{m-1},R) or (L,q_1), or literal reversal of q_{m-2}q_{m-1} or q_1q_2. # R607 — Minimum R24 cell forces the short-trimer cross-end bridge pattern

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Retain the exact-two-bad transitive R24 cell of R556 with X={a,b,c,z}, L=q_0, R=q_m and m>=2. Then, in addition to the accepted R589 gate/cross-fan turns, the following eight turns are forced: aLc, zcL, baL, Rcb, Raz, aRc, RcL, RaL. Together with R591, the three vertices of the original short trimer therefore have the rigid cross-end middle pattern RaL, LbR, RcL. Equivalently a and c point from R to L while b points from L to R; the z-middle bridge is the only L/R middle orientation not determined here.

## Hypotheses
Accepted exact-two-bad R24 frame R556; X+L and X+R are P5-free; X union {L,R} is P6-free, since a Hamilton P6 there together with the nonempty Q^o=(q_1,...,q_{m-1}) would be a spanning two-cover; accepted R589 and R591; boundary antisymmetry R3.

## Scope
Specialized R24 six-cell normal form. The proof is finite and explicit, uses no computation, no R5/four-deletion exactness, and no cyclic-K4 argument.

## Applicability
Use in the surviving m>=6 minimum cell. Besides the short-trimer bridge RaL,LbR,RcL, the auxiliary turns baL,Rcb,Raz,aRc,aLc,zcL are retained for explicit same-frame actualizations and wrap analysis.

## Persistence
Retain X,Q,L,R, the eight displayed forced turns, the eight explicit forbidden Hamilton candidates in the proof, and the R591 bridge LbR.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not determine the z-middle bridge; does not itself give a Hamilton P6 or spanning two-cover; does not infer any paid descendant currentness.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Historical short-trimer cross-end bridge branch below the unique two-bad seam cell.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Fresh-session audit: the eight forced turns are supported by explicit one-hole P5/P6 obstructions. The potentially ambiguous Rab incidence is indeed the accepted R556 seam q_mab with q_m=R. R589/R591 and R3 supply the remaining displayed turns; no z-middle orientation or closure is overclaimed.

## Proof
All turns below except the displayed hole are already certified by R556/R589 and the matching-height cell X. Because X+L and X+R are P5-free, each listed P5 candidate must fail at its unique uncertified turn. (1) (b,c,L,a,z): bcL and Laz are tight, so cLa is bad and aLc is tight. (2) (b,L,c,z,a): bLc and cza are tight, so Lcz is bad and zcL is tight. (3) (z,L,a,b,c): zLa and abc are tight, so Lab is bad and baL is tight. (4) (a,b,c,R,z): abc and cRz are tight, so bcR is bad and Rcb is tight. (5) (c,z,a,R,b): cza and aRb are tight, so zaR is bad and Raz is tight. (6) (c,R,a,b,z): Rab and abz are tight, so cRa is bad and aRc is tight. Now X union {L,R} is P6-free: otherwise its Hamilton P6 together with Q^o=(q_1,...,q_{m-1}) two-covers H. Candidate (b,a,L,c,R,z) has baL,aLc,cRz tight, so LcR is bad and RcL is tight. Candidate (z,L,a,R,c,b) has zLa,aRc,Rcb tight, so LaR is bad and RaL is tight. Finally R591 supplies LbR. This proves the claimed backbone with no computation.

# R608 — Minimum R24 cell bidirectionally saturates both terminal edges of the short trimer

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
In the exact-two-bad transitive R24 cell, let J=(a,b,c), L=q_0, R=q_m. Both tested orientations of physical edge {a,b} are tail-signed with two exterior witnesses, and both tested orientations of {b,c} are head-signed with two exterior witnesses: (a,b) is tail-signed by z and R via abz,abR; (b,a) is tail-signed by z and L via baz,baL; (b,c) is head-signed by z and L via zbc,Lbc; (c,b) is head-signed by z and R via zcb,Rcb. Thus each physical terminal edge is bidirectionally saturated in one polarity and the two orientations share the common witness z. Moreover all four oriented packets are directly R542-payable. For {a,b}, use the tight carriers (b,a,c) and (a,b,c), so the complementary carrier singleton is c; for {b,c}, use (a,c,b) and (a,b,c), so the complementary carrier singleton is a. In each case the displayed two witnesses lie outside the chosen trimer carrier.

## Hypotheses
Exact-two-bad R24 cell R555/R556; the explicit backbone R607; matching-height turns of X; R542.

## Scope
Specialized minimum R24 cell. Tested-order-safe. No R5, R168, R169, R224, source-replay contact, or simultaneous paid-descendant hypothesis.

## Applicability
Use before any alternating-hinge analysis. The short trimer J has four directly payable reverse-boundary incarnations, two on each terminal physical edge, with common witness z and endpoint witnesses L/R.

## Persistence
Retain all four tested oriented dimers, their polarities and two named witnesses, the four chosen short carriers, complementary singleton a or c, and each independent R542 payment ancestry.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert the four R542 descendants coexist or that bidirectional saturation alone closes H. Does not use R407 as a closure theorem.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Historical terminal-edge saturation branch below the exact-two-bad seam route.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** The four signed terminal-dimer packets follow from R555/R556, matching-height X turns, and accepted R607. Each displayed tested orientation is a reverse boundary dimer of the stated tight trimer carrier with two distinct exterior witnesses, so R542 applies independently as claimed.

## Proof
The minimum seam cbL is bad, hence Lbc is tight; the minimum seam Rba is bad, hence abR is tight. The matching-height cell gives abz,baz,zbc,zcb tight. R607 gives baL and Rcb. Therefore (a,b) has tail witnesses z,R; (b,a) has tail witnesses z,L; (b,c) has head witnesses z,L; and (c,b) has head witnesses z,R, always on the identical tested orientation displayed. For R542, (a,b) is a reverse boundary dimer of the tight carrier (b,a,c), and (b,a) is a reverse boundary dimer of (a,b,c); both carriers have complementary singleton c and the witnesses are outside the carrier. Dually (b,c) is a reverse boundary dimer of (a,c,b) and (c,b) of (a,b,c), both with complementary singleton a and both witnesses outside. Hence R542 applies independently to all four packets. The common witness z also shows that each physical terminal edge is saturated in both tested orientations with the same polarity.

# R609 — Minimum R24 cell forces failure of at least one long-rail wrap seam

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Retain the exact-two-bad transitive R24 cell with Q=(L=q_0,q_1,...,q_{m-1},R=q_m), m>=2. Put alpha=(R,L,q_1) and beta=(q_{m-1},R,L), the two wrap seams of Q. Then at least one of alpha,beta is bad. Hence Q is never in the double-wrap branch of R579. More precisely, at least one of the following three Hamilton P5 absorbers is tight: K_a=(c,z,b,R,L) on {L,R} union (X-{a}); K_b=(c,R,L,a,z) on {L,R} union (X-{b}); K_c=(R,L,b,z,a) on {L,R} union (X-{c}). If K_a is tight, R540 forces alpha bad. If K_b or K_c is tight, R540 forces beta bad.

## Hypotheses
Exact-two-bad R24 frame R556; m>=2; X union {L,R} is P6-free; for each x in {a,b,c}, H-(X-{x})=Q sqcup (x) is an exact two-cover (otherwise a Hamilton residual together with a tight trimer on X-{x} two-covers H); R540 and R3.

## Scope
Specialized minimum R24 wrap lemma. No computation, no R5/four-deletion exactness, no R168/R169/R224.

## Applicability
Use before the R579 wrap tetrachotomy. It removes the double-wrap branch and leaves only SW1, SW2, or DF.

## Persistence
Retain whichever explicit K_a,K_b,K_c is tight, its omitted singleton, the associated R540 one-hole spanning proposal, and the exact bad wrap seam/mate.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not determine which wrap seam fails and does not rule out either single-wrap branch or the double-fail branch.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Historical long-rail wrap-seam branch below the exact-two-bad seam route.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Three-absorber argument is correct; R540 is applied at a terminal occurrence of L or initial occurrence of R with a single wrap-seam hole.

## Proof
The matching-height cell gives czb and bza tight, while R556 gives zbR,Lbz,Rca,caL,Laz tight. Thus K_a=(c,z,b,R,L) is tight exactly when bRL is tight, and K_c=(R,L,b,z,a) is tight exactly when RLb is tight. Suppose both K_a and K_c fail. Then bRL and RLb are bad, so R3 gives LRb and bLR tight. The six-set X union {L,R} is P6-free. In the candidate (b,L,R,c,a,z), the turns bLR,Rca,caz are tight; therefore LRc is bad and cRL is tight. In the candidate (z,c,a,L,R,b), the turns zca,caL,LRb are tight; therefore aLR is bad and RLa is tight. Hence K_b=(c,R,L,a,z) is tight, using cRL,RLa,Laz. So at least one of K_a,K_b,K_c is tight. For each omitted x, H-(X-{x})=Q sqcup (x) is an exact two-cover. Apply R540 to the corresponding K. In K_a, L is in terminal position 4 with predecessor R, so the one-hole left endpoint cut has unique hole alpha=(R,L,q_1); alpha is bad. In K_b and K_c, R is in position 1 or 0 with successor L, so the one-hole right endpoint cut has unique hole beta=(q_{m-1},R,L); beta is bad. Therefore at least one wrap seam fails, excluding double wrap.

# R61 — Quiet-return historical-seam alignment

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement

Retain one internal-route return representative with:

## Scope
- a current selected parent crossing;
- a current turn across the old marker cut;
- historical capture of the crossing's old-five-path-side endpoint;
- a graph-intrinsic returned terminal dimer; and
- the old historical terminal seam of the five-path.

Outside the accepted same-support sign outputs, the following normal form is exhaustive.

#### Near return

If the selected crossing uses the historical global endpoint adjacent to the old seam, current internality of that endpoint would create two distinct sign certificates on the same physical crossing support and enter the accepted sign basins. Hence the endpoint is current terminal in the quiet residue. The crossing is then the unique blocker of the historical terminal seam. A one-for-one, zero-debt exchange replaces it by that seam and makes the literal historical splice turn current.

#### Far return

If the crossing uses the opposite global endpoint, the exact support normal form forces one specific cross-gap chord. Exactly one chord endpoint is current terminal. A forced physical chain through the opposite global endpoint and the crossing's unique parent state identifies the blockers of two historical seams. Two one-for-one, zero-debt exchanges restore both seams while preserving the selected captured parent crossing.

This normal form is independent of the equality-versus-positive-excess split. An optional final terminal-boundary exchange may be made in a separate descendant.

The new information is exact blocker and exchange provenance and, in the far face, coexistence of both restored historical seam turns with the same selected captured crossing. Bare currentization of the full old five-path was already available from prescribed-path completion.

In SW1 (alpha=RLq_1 tight, beta=q_{m-1}RL bad), both LRx and RLx are tight for every x in X, so both (L,R) and (R,L) are tail-signed by every x. In SW2 (alpha bad, beta tight), both xLR and xRL are tight for every x in X, so both wrap orientations are head-signed by every x. Consequently, in either single-wrap branch, for every prescribed t in X each of the two tested wrap orientations is directly R542-payable using a tight trimer on {L,R,t} and any two witnesses from X-{t}; thus the same deleted physical pair {L,R} supports an eight-channel short-carrier payment fan indexed by t in X and the two wrap orientations.

## Hypotheses
Exact-two-bad frame R556; Q is globally longest; accepted R579; wrap-failure lemma R609; explicit backbone R607; m>=3 so the six-set P6 obstruction and endpoint stars are available; R542.

## Scope
R24-specific wrap amplifier. Strong-safe, tested-order-safe, no R5/R168/R169/R224 and no computation.

## Applicability
After R609, replace the three remaining wrap branches by: DF gives the literal reverse P4 across the two ends, while either single-wrap gives universal bidirectional same-polarity saturation of the wrap dimer and hence R542 capture/payment through every chosen short-cell singleton.

## Persistence
DF: retain q_1LRq_{m-1}. SW: retain the successful cyclic rotation of Q, its new endpoint role, all eight families LRx/RLx or xLR/xRL, the chosen t-carrier and two witnesses for each R542 packet, and the common physical deletion pair {L,R}.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert the eight paid descendants coexist; universal saturation is graph-intrinsic but each R542 continuation is alternative. Does not by itself close the DF reverse P4 or the single-wrap payment fan.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Historical wrap-amplification branch below the exact-two-bad seam route.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Single-wrap rotation remains globally longest; endpoint extension plus explicit P6 obstructions force bidirectional wrap saturation, and R542 carriers/witnesses are valid.

## Proof
Let alpha=RLq_1 and beta=q_{m-1}RL. R609 excludes double wrap. In DF, R579 gives q_1LR and LRq_{m-1} tight, hence the P4 (q_1,L,R,q_{m-1}). Now assume SW1: alpha is tight and beta bad, so rot1=(R,L,q_1,...,q_{m-1}) is a tight Hamilton order of supp(Q). Since Q is globally longest, rot1 is globally longest. For every x in X, xRL is therefore bad, else x could be prepended; R3 gives LRx tight for all x. We force RLx for all x using P6-freeness of X union {L,R}. First, in (z,c,a,L,R,b), zca,caL,LRb are tight, so aLR is bad and RLa tight. Second, in (b,L,R,c,a,z), LRc,Rca,caz are tight, so bLR is bad and RLb tight. Third, in (a,b,c,L,R,z), abc,bcL,LRz are tight, so cLR is bad and RLc tight. Finally, in (z,L,R,a,b,c), LRa,Rab,abc are tight, so zLR is bad and RLz tight. Hence both LRx and RLx are tight for every x: both wrap orientations are tail-signed by all X. In SW2, rot2=(q_1,...,q_{m-1},R,L) is globally longest. Appending x is impossible, so RLx is bad and xLR tight for every x. Reflect again. Candidate (z,c,a,L,R,b) with zca,caL,aLR tight forces LRb bad and bRL tight. Candidate (b,L,R,c,a,z) with bLR,Rca,caz tight forces LRc bad and cRL tight. Candidate (a,b,c,L,R,z) with abc,bcL,cLR tight forces LRz bad and zRL tight. Candidate (b,c,L,R,a,z) has bcL,cLR,Raz tight (Raz is R607), so LRa is bad and aRL tight. Thus xLR and xRL are tight for every x: both wrap orientations are head-signed by all X. For the payment fan, fix t in X. In SW1, (R,L,t) and (L,R,t) are tight carriers; (L,R) and (R,L) are their respective reverse left-boundary dimers and have at least three exterior tail witnesses X-{t}. In SW2, (t,R,L) and (t,L,R) are tight carriers; the two wrap orientations are the respective reverse right-boundary dimers and have at least three exterior head witnesses. Choose any two of those witnesses and invoke R542. This works independently for each t and each tested wrap orientation.

# R611 — Exact adjacent-state reversal at the rotated return forces short-carrier payment

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Retain the surviving exact-two-bad R24 cell with m>=6. In the right endpoint reversal residue of R605, an exact H-{L,R} cover has one rail beginning (b,q_{m-1},q_{m-2},...). Then R542 necessarily applies to one of the two orientations of the physical dimer {q_{m-1},q_{m-2}}. Put r_1=q_{m-1}, r_2=q_{m-2}, r_3=q_{m-3}. The current rail certifies b r_1 r_2 tight, while Q certifies r_3 r_2 r_1 tight. For each x in {a,c}, R3 chooses exactly one of x r_2 r_1 and r_1 r_2 x. If x r_2 r_1 is tight for at least one x, then it and r_3 r_2 r_1 give a same-head two-witness packet on tested dimer (r_2,r_1), which is a reverse boundary dimer of the tight carrier (b,r_1,r_2); the witnesses x,r_3 lie outside that carrier, so R542 applies. If neither x r_2 r_1 is tight, then r_1 r_2 a and r_1 r_2 c are both tight, giving a same-tail two-witness packet on tested dimer (r_1,r_2), which is a reverse boundary dimer of the tight carrier (r_3,r_2,r_1); witnesses a,c lie outside it, so R542 applies. The left reversal residue, where a rail ends (...,q_2,q_1,b), is the exact dual. Consequently the exact-state-reversal branch in the rotated endpoint normal form is always payable and is not a terminal R24 obstruction.

## Hypotheses
Surviving exact-two-bad R24 cell, m>=6; exact reversal residue from the explicit endpoint insertion analysis; R3 and R542.

## Scope
Specialized R24 reversal consumer. Fully R5-free and tested-order explicit.

## Applicability
Use after R605. It removes the last unconsumed local branch of any exact H-{L,R} return.

## Persistence
Retain the current reversed-state rail turn, the old adjacent Q turn, which of a,c supplies the matching orientation (or both opposite orientation certificates), the tested dimer orientation, the short carrier, and the two R542 witnesses.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert the paid descendant closes H; it only converts exact reversed-state return into the accepted R542 payment lineage.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Route-local adjacent-state reversal -> short-carrier payment leaf. Payment is non-scarce and this claim has no live consumers.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Exact adjacent-state reversal yields one of two R542-ready orientations by a complete R3 dichotomy; carrier and witness disjointness checks are correct.

## Proof
Right side. Let r_1=q_{m-1},r_2=q_{m-2},r_3=q_{m-3}. The endpoint-reversal cover selects b r_1 r_2, so K_+=(b,r_1,r_2) is tight. The old Q turn K_-=(r_3,r_2,r_1) is tight. For x=a,c, boundary antisymmetry on the reversal pair x r_2 r_1 / r_1 r_2 x gives exactly one tight turn. If x r_2 r_1 is tight for some x, then x r_2 r_1 and r_3 r_2 r_1 are both head certificates on the identical tested dimer D=(r_2,r_1), with distinct witnesses x,r_3. The dimer D is the reverse terminal dimer (c,b) of K_+=(b,r_1,r_2), and both witnesses are outside K_+, so R542 applies. Otherwise x r_2 r_1 is bad for both x=a,c, hence R3 makes r_1 r_2 a and r_1 r_2 c tight. These are two tail certificates on D'=(r_1,r_2) with witnesses a,c. The dimer D' is the reverse initial dimer (b,a) of K_-=(r_3,r_2,r_1), and a,c lie outside K_-, so R542 applies. The left side is obtained by reversing the notation: current turn q_2 q_1 b and old Q turn q_1 q_2 q_3 play the roles of K_+,K_-, and the same a,c dichotomy pays either (q_1,q_2) or (q_2,q_1).

# R612 — Opposite boundary carriers with three spare vertices force short-carrier payment

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Let H be a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample. Let A,B,p,q be vertices with tight trimers K_+=(p,A,B) or (A,B,p), so {A,B} occurs as one boundary state in orientation A->B, and K_-=(q,B,A) or (B,A,q), so the same physical boundary occurs in orientation B->A. Suppose there are three distinct vertices x_1,x_2,x_3 outside V(K_+) union V(K_-). Then one of the two tested orientations (A,B) or (B,A) carries a same-polarity two-witness packet whose witnesses lie outside the opposite carrier, and hence R542 forces a certificate-retaining capture/payment continuation. More explicitly, for each x_i, R3 makes exactly one of x_i A B and B A x_i tight. If two indices choose x_iAB, the tested dimer (A,B) is head-signed by those two witnesses and is the reverse boundary dimer of K_-. If two choose BAx_i, the tested dimer (B,A) is tail-signed by those two witnesses and is the reverse boundary dimer of K_+. By pigeonhole one case occurs, so R542 applies. The exact head/tail/reflected variants are included by orienting the two carriers so their displayed common boundary states are A,B and B,A.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample; two tight trimers carry opposite orientations of one common physical boundary dimer; at least three distinct spare vertices lie outside both trimer supports; R3 and R542.

## Scope
Order-free Strong Level-(1) payment parent. No R24, global-longestness, deletion-root synchronization, R5, R168, R169, or computation.

## Applicability
Whenever a path comparison produces an exact reversal of a boundary state of a retained tight trimer, do not stop at a generic reversal/contact output: with three spare vertices the reversed state itself forces an R542 payment packet.

## Persistence
Retain the two opposite boundary carriers, the physical boundary dimer, the three spare vertices, the two witnesses selected by pigeonhole, the tested dimer orientation and polarity, and the R542 carrier/payment ancestry.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert which orientation wins the pigeonhole and does not assert the R542 paid descendant closes H.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Order-free three-spare theorem terminates only in R542 payment, a non-scarce currency with no live consumers. Preserve historically.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Three-spare pigeonhole theorem is correct and order-free; in either orientation the winning dimer is the reverse boundary dimer of the opposite carrier.

## Proof
For i=1,2,3, boundary antisymmetry on the distinct triple {x_i,A,B} says exactly one of x_iAB and BAx_i is tight. If x_iAB is tight for at least two indices i,j, then the identical tested oriented dimer D=(A,B) is head-signed by the two distinct witnesses x_i,x_j. Because K_- contains the boundary state B,A, D=(A,B) is exactly the reverse boundary dimer of K_-. Both witnesses are outside K_- by hypothesis, so R542 applies. Otherwise at most one x_iAB is tight, hence BAx_i is tight for at least two indices. Then D'=(B,A) is tail-signed by two distinct spare witnesses. Since K_+ contains the boundary state A,B, D' is exactly its reverse boundary dimer, and the witnesses lie outside K_+; R542 applies again. This exhausts the two pigeonhole classes.

- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Historical high-side seed/prefix bookkeeping with no live consumers; modern R594/R619/R621 spine carries the durable frame structure.

R4 forbids each completed two-cover and R3 supplies the stated reverse. This limits only the strategic reach of R613: its standalone SL1 data-insufficiency model remains true, but its displayed left packet is not induced-realizable in the full R24 smallest-counterexample frame.

# R616 — Left high-side R24 seed synchronizes two enlarged roots and a double terminal witness rectangle

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Retain the synchronized transitive R24 frame and the accepted left high-side normalization of R596/R598. Write L=q_0, u=q_1, v=q_2, w=q_3, x_L=z, with M_R={ab,cz}>M_S={ac,bz}>M_L={bc,az}, and seed A_z=(u,L,a,c,b). Then the same physical frame contains a second enlarged deletion cover H-b=(u,L,c,a,z) sqcup Q[2,m], while H-z=(u,L,a,c,b) sqcup Q[2,m] is the accepted R598 cover. Moreover the same witness pair {b,z} tail-signs both tested oriented dimers (L,u) and (w,v): the four turns (L,u,b),(L,u,z),(w,v,b),(w,v,z) are tight. Thus the first left interior cell carries two simultaneous enlarged roots sharing the literal suffix Q[2,m] and a 2-by-2 graph-intrinsic witness rectangle on the two reverse boundary dimers (q_0,q_1) and (q_3,q_2).

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in the accepted R594 synchronized transitive order-three frame; use the R596 left high-side root normalized by x_L=z, outgoing M_L edge bc and outgoing M_S edge ac, with Q=(q_0,...,q_m), m>=4. Accepted R536,R598 and R3,R4.

## Scope
Noncircular R24 restoration. First-interior fixed-frame synchronization; no use of R24, R5, R169, or order-ten closure.

## Applicability
Use after the left high-side seed. It replaces the one-root/one-collision view of the first zipper cell by a fixed physical two-root object. A cover-valued consumer may compare the two exact deletion covers or consume the common witness rectangle without losing the q_0,...,q_3 coordinates to anonymous payment descendants.

## Persistence
Retain the physical labels L,u,v,w,a,b,c,z; both exact deletion covers with their common suffix Q[2,m]; and all four displayed witness turns. These are simultaneous graph-intrinsic facts in the original H.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not produce an L(2,r) advanced cover, does not assert the two deletion covers are current in one common deletion frame, does not by itself close H, and does not claim a generic signed-payment descendant preserves these coordinates.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** R616 is an implementation-level high-side seed now used only inside canonical accepted shape-C consumer R856.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Second enlarged root, exactness, inward-star witnesses, and the two P6 obstruction arguments are correct.

## Proof
Put L=q_0,u=q_1,v=q_2,w=q_3 and x_L=z. R596 normalizes the left high-side cell so the fully outgoing M_S edge is ac and its complementary M_S edge is bz. Accepted R536 first gives the two q_0-starting Hamilton P4s (L,a,c,b) and (L,c,a,z). Prepending u using the common endpoint reverse star uLx gives the tight P5s A_z=(u,L,a,c,b) and A_b=(u,L,c,a,z). A_z sqcup Q[2,m] is exactly R598. The supports of A_b and Q[2,m] partition H-b, so they form a literal two-cover of H-b. It is exact: if H-b were Hamiltonian, that Hamilton path together with singleton b would two-cover H, contradicting R4. This proves the second enlarged root. The inward-star clause of accepted R536, applied to the complementary M_S edge bz, gives (w,v,b) and (w,v,z) tight. It remains to prove the matching pair at (L,u). Suppose (b,u,L) were tight. Then (b,u,L,c,a,z) is a tight P6: besides the assumed first turn, its turns are uLc from the endpoint reverse star, Lca from full outgoing polarity of ac, and caz from the transitive matching-height rule M(ca)=M_S>M(az)=M_L. Together with the untouched tight suffix Q[2,m] this is a spanning two-cover of H, contradiction. Hence buL is bad and R3 gives Lub tight. Similarly, if zuL were tight then (z,u,L,a,c,b) would be a tight P6, using uLa, Lac, and acb; together with Q[2,m] it would two-cover H. Therefore zuL is bad and R3 gives Luz tight. Thus b and z simultaneously tail-sign both (L,u) and (w,v), as claimed.

# R618 — Right-root coincidence with the synchronized left pair yields a four-cross-state singleton-deletion weave

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Retain the synchronized transitive R24 frame, the pending synchronized left-root pair {b,z} of R616, and the accepted right high-side root x_R of R596/R598. Suppose x_R is one of {b,z}; write r=x_R. Then the same singleton deletion W=H-r carries two literal exact two-covers with opposite-end absorption: T_L=A_L sqcup Q[2,m], where A_L=(q_1,q_0,ell_1,ell_2,ell_3) is the R616 left enlarged P5 on {q_0,q_1} union (X-{r}), and T_R=Q[0,m-2] sqcup A_R, where A_R=(rho_1,rho_2,rho_3,q_m,q_{m-1}) is the R598 right enlarged P5 on (X-{r}) union {q_{m-1},q_m}. These two covers form a literal four-cross-state weave on W. Relative to T_R, T_L selects q_0 ell_1 and q_{m-2}q_{m-1} across the two T_R components. Relative to T_L, T_R selects q_1q_2 and rho_3 q_m across the two T_L components. Since W is proper, R176 applies independently to all four selected cross states, producing four graph-intrinsic balanced opposite-sign pair birth certificates while retaining the same deleted root r and both physical Q cuts. Consequently the nonlocal side-coupling dichotomy is sharp: either x_R lies in the left synchronized pair {b,z}, in which case this singleton-deletion four-weave exists, or x_R lies in the complementary pair {a,c}.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in the accepted R594 frame; m>=4; accepted R596/R598 supplies the right high-side enlarged cover; pending R616 supplies enlarged left covers for both roots b,z; x_R is one of b,z; accepted R176.

## Scope
Noncircular R24 restoration. First explicit nonlocal consumer of the synchronized left-root pair; no payment descendant or role-state assumption.

## Applicability
After R617 rules out purely left-local closure, test whether the right high-side root coincides with b or z. In the coincidence branch use the four-cross-state singleton-deletion weave as the retained nonlocal interaction object. The only root-location branch not covered is x_R in {a,c}.

## Persistence
Retain r, both exact W=H-r covers T_L,T_R, the left and right absorbed endpoint pairs, the four selected cross states q_0 ell_1, q_{m-2}q_{m-1}, q_1q_2, rho_3 q_m, and the four R176 birth certificates with their common singleton-deletion coordinate r.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert the four balanced-pair births are distinct or simultaneously current, does not itself pay them, and does not close H. Does not apply when x_R is in {a,c}.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Historical right-root coincidence weave with no live consumers; root synchronization is now canonicalized by R619/R621.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Conditional left/right same-root enlarged covers yield the four stated cross states on one proper singleton-deletion residue; each R176 application is valid.

## Proof
Because r is one of the two synchronized left roots, R616 gives the exact left cover T_L=A_L sqcup Q[2,m] of W=H-r, with A_L containing q_1,q_0 followed by all three vertices of X-{r}. Because r=x_R, R598 gives the exact right cover T_R=Q[0,m-2] sqcup A_R of the same W, with A_R containing all three vertices of X-{r} followed by q_m,q_{m-1}. In T_R, q_0 belongs to the Q-prefix component while ell_1 belongs to A_R, so the selected T_L state q_0 ell_1 is a cross state. Also q_{m-2} lies in the Q-prefix component and q_{m-1} lies in A_R, so the selected T_L state q_{m-2}q_{m-1} is a second cross state. Dually, in T_L, q_1 lies in A_L while q_2 lies in Q[2,m], so the selected T_R state q_1q_2 crosses T_L; and rho_3 lies in A_L while q_m lies in Q[2,m], so rho_3 q_m crosses T_L. W is proper with spare vertex r, hence R176 applies to each cross state. The final dichotomy is just X={a,b,c,z} partitioned as {b,z} union {a,c}.

# R623 — Every crossed R24 root is a preserved singleton coordinate for arbitrary target floors

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Retain the crossed phase and the sixteen root-labelled singleton-deletion cross states of R621. Fix a deleted root r in {a,b,c,z} and any one of the four R621 cross states belonging to H-r. The R176 birth generated from that cross state can be chosen with one signed support literally the singleton (r), and its opposite signed support of order at most two. Consequently there is a finite chosen ancestry-retaining continuation yielding either a spanning two-cover of H or a both-singleton balanced-pair floor whose one singleton is still exactly (r). Moreover, for every prescribed vertex x distinct from r, there is a further chosen continuation yielding either a spanning two-cover or an ancestry-bearing both-singleton floor with supports exactly {r},{x}, with r preserved throughout the nonclosing payment and steering. Thus in the crossed R24 phase each of the four deletion roots is a universal preserved floor coordinate, already at singleton-deletion level; the four cross states for a fixed root provide alternative birth ancestries for the same root-pinned capability.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in the crossed phase of pending R621; Q=(q_0,...,q_m), m>=4. Fix one R621 cross state in the proper residue W=H-r. Use the fully reconstructible accepted proof of R176, accepted R428, and accepted R432.

## Scope
Noncircular R24 restoration. Crossed phase. Strengthens the strategic content of R621 by exploiting the fact that its R176 spare vertex is uniquely the deleted root.

## Applicability
Use before generic pair payment or R620. When a downstream argument wants a floor containing a specific crossed-phase root r and any chosen second coordinate x, start from any R621 cross state for H-r, preserve r through the short payment, then steer only the opposite singleton to x. This keeps the deletion root physically pinned while retaining the original deep/shallow weave ancestry.

## Persistence
Retain r as the literal singleton signed support from the R176 birth; the selected R621 cross state and compared exact covers; the common R176 witness and local opposite support; all R428 refund certificates; the original deep/shallow Q-cut ancestry; and, during target steering, the fixed singleton r and the replacement certificate installing x.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not claim target floors for different x coexist. Does not claim the four cross-state ancestries for one root can be paid simultaneously. Does not preserve the original R621 exact covers as current through payment. Does not close an arbitrary root-pinned floor. Does not invalidate the R620 staircase route.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Universal preserved-floor-coordinate steering is old floor/payment architecture with no live consumers; current provenance rules avoid treating steerable singleton floors as closure progress.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Preferred proof P540 of accepted R176 indeed permits arbitrary spare d outside W; for W=H-r this forces d=r, producing singleton r with opposite support of order at most two. R428 preserves r and R432 installs any second target.

## Proof
Fix a root r and one R621 selected cross state xy in the residue W=H-r. In the fully reconstructible proof P540 of accepted R176, the spare vertex d may be chosen arbitrarily from V(H)-W. Here V(H)-W={r}, so d=r is forced. Let R_x be the component, in the crossed source cover, containing the selected cross endpoint x.

If R_x is nontrivial, P540 chooses a literal old neighbor p of x in R_x and, by R3, produces either a head-signed oriented dimer on {x,p} with common witness y or the tail-signed reversed dimer on the same two vertices with witness y. The automatic two-vertex path through d=r and y gives the opposite singleton sign on (r). Hence the R176 balanced pair has support profile 2+1 and one support is literally (r). If R_x is a singleton component, P540 instead uses the selected state xy itself to sign singleton (x), while the same automatic path through r and y gives the opposite singleton sign on (r). Hence the birth is already a both-singleton floor {r,x}. These are the only cases.

In the 2+1 case apply accepted R428 with p=r as the fixed singleton coordinate and the signed dimer as the opposite nontrivial support. Along its chosen nonclosing continuation, R428 preserves singleton (r) unchanged and strictly pays the opposite support until it is singleton. Thus either H acquires a spanning two-cover or an ancestry-bearing floor {r,v} is reached for some v, with the entire R621/R176 birth ancestry retained. In the 1+1 case take v=x and no payment is needed.

Now fix any prescribed vertex x_0 distinct from r. Apply accepted R432 to the active floor with target pair {r,x_0}. The proof of R432 requires only one replacement macro when the current floor already shares one target coordinate; choose the shared coordinate to be r. Therefore r is retained while the other singleton is replaced by x_0. The continuation either closes H or reaches exactly the floor {r,x_0}, with the incoming ancestry ledger retained. This proves both the root-pinned floor and arbitrary-target claims.

# R630 — Crossed endpoint P8 forces a pure-Q two-end collision alternative

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Retain the crossed R24 frame of accepted R621 with X={a,b,c,z}, Q=(q_0,...,q_m), m>=4, and write L=q_0, u=q_1, R=q_m, s=q_{m-1}. Then the two-end skip clause

(u,s,R) tight OR (L,u,s) tight

is physically certified by a literal spanning two-cover proposal. Consequently at least one of two explicit same-support same-polarity R38 interactions occurs: either the oriented right terminal dimer (s,R) is head-signed by the two distinct witnesses u and q_{m-2}, or the oriented left terminal dimer (L,u) is tail-signed by the two distinct witnesses s and q_2. Thus the crossed frame cannot keep both ends locally insulated: a single eight-vertex endpoint proposal forces a graph-intrinsic two-witness collision at one physical Q end, with the alternative itself coupling the opposite end.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in the accepted crossed frame of R621. Use the matching-height orientation on X, the crossed right middle-gate polarity from R621, the endpoint reverse stars from accepted R594, the tightness of Q, boundary antisymmetry R3, and accepted same-support sign interaction R38.

## Scope
Noncircular R24 restoration. Crossed phase only. Order-free for m>=4. Fixed-frame endpoint proposal; no payment descendant, R623 steering, mixed-root pair deletion, or order-ten closure is used.

## Applicability
Use as a preferred two-ended front door in the crossed phase. The output is not an anonymous historical contact: it is a tested-order R38 collision on one of the two physical terminal Q dimers, and the extra witness comes from the opposite end of Q. Downstream consumers should exploit that nonlocal witness identity rather than respending the collision as a generic same-support event.

## Persistence
Retain the literal endpoint path P_E=(a,b,z,R,s,u,L,c), the untouched complementary interval Q[2,m-2], the complete two-hole set {(R,s,u),(s,u,L)}, the mate clause {(u,s,R),(L,u,s)}, and in the two branches respectively the tested oriented dimer (s,R) with witnesses u,q_{m-2} or (L,u) with witnesses s,q_2.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert which collision branch occurs, that the two branches coexist, or that an R38 collision alone closes H. Does not claim the new opposite-end witness creates a new support rather than a new certificate on an already signed support. Does not use or imply pending R627-R629.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Valid two-ended endpoint proposal, but its terminal output is only a same-support R38 collision and its sole live consumer was retired capture machinery. Preserve the exact mate clause historically; current crossed work uses R621/R723 and physical core/seam interfaces.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Checked the eight-vertex endpoint proposal literally. Exactly the two stated turns are uncertified; antisymmetry yields usR or Lus, and Q supplies a distinct second witness on the same tested terminal dimer in either branch. Dependencies are R24-free.

## Proof
Consider the ordered eight-vertex path
P_E=(a,b,z,R,s,u,L,c).
Its consecutive turns are
(a,b,z), (b,z,R), (z,R,s), (R,s,u), (s,u,L), (u,L,c).
The first is tight by the matching-height rule M_R(ab)>M_S(bz). The second is tight because in the crossed phase the M_S edge {b,z} is fully incoming to R. The third and sixth are endpoint reverse-star turns supplied by R594: (z,R,s) and (u,L,c). Hence the only uncertified turns of P_E are h_R=(R,s,u) and h_L=(s,u,L).

The support of P_E is exactly X union {L,u,s,R}. Since m>=4, the complementary interval Q[2,m-2]=(q_2,...,q_{m-2}) is nonempty and tight. Thus if both h_R and h_L were tight, P_E sqcup Q[2,m-2] would be a literal spanning two-cover of H, impossible in the hypothetical counterexample. Therefore at least one of h_R,h_L is bad. Boundary antisymmetry R3 converts this into the physical mate clause
bar(h_R)=(u,s,R) tight OR bar(h_L)=(L,u,s) tight.
The literal proposal P_E sqcup Q[2,m-2] is the complete two-hole certificate.

If (u,s,R) is tight, the oriented physical dimer (s,R) is head-signed by witness u. Because Q itself is tight, its terminal turn (q_{m-2},s,R) is also tight, so the same tested oriented dimer (s,R) is head-signed by q_{m-2}. These witnesses are distinct because u=q_1 and m-2>=2. Accepted R38 therefore gives the same-support same-polarity two-witness interaction on (s,R), retaining both witness identities and tested order.

If instead (L,u,s) is tight, the oriented dimer (L,u) is tail-signed by witness s. The initial Q turn (L,u,q_2) is tight, so (L,u) is also tail-signed by q_2. Since s=q_{m-1} and m-1>=3, s!=q_2. R38 gives the corresponding same-support same-polarity interaction on (L,u).

Thus every crossed frame has one of these two explicit terminal collision packets, and the new witness in each packet is drawn from the opposite end of Q. This proves the statement.

# R633 — Crossed endpoint collision box forces dual terminal payment or full extreme-edge saturation

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Retain the crossed R24 frame of accepted R621 with X={a,b,c,z}, Q=(q_0,...,q_m), m>=4, L=q_0, u=q_1, R=q_m, s=q_{m-1}. Define C_L to mean a tested-order same-tail R38 collision on the physical dimer (L,u), with one witness q_2 and another witness in X. Define C_R dually as a same-head R38 collision on (s,R), with one witness q_{m-2} and another witness in X. Define four extreme-X collision packets:
C_ba: (b,a) tail-signed by distinct witnesses L,c;
C_bc: (b,c) head-signed by R,a;
C_za: (z,a) head-signed by R,c;
C_zc: (z,c) tail-signed by L,a.

Then at least one of the following two structural outputs holds:
(A) both terminal packets C_L and C_R occur. In this case the disjoint oppositely signed terminal dimers (L,u) and (s,R) form a direct mass-four balanced pair, so accepted R39 yields either a spanning two-cover or an ancestry-bearing mass-two floor retaining the two terminal collision ancestries;
(B) all four extreme-X packets C_ba,C_bc,C_za,C_zc occur. In this case R547 applied at hinge b to the opposite-polarity dimers (b,a),(b,c) gives an ancestry-bearing floor on physical pair {a,c}, while R547 applied at hinge z to (z,a),(z,c) gives a second ancestry-bearing floor on the same physical pair {a,c} with the singleton polarities reversed. The two floor ancestries are distinct and both are retained; by R444 their bare opposite singleton labels are not themselves declared a contradiction.

The dichotomy is forced by eight literal two-hole spanning proposals on the fixed endpoint set X union {L,u,s,R}. Thus the crossed frame cannot avoid both a genuinely two-ended terminal balanced-pair channel and complete collision saturation of the four extreme matching edges of X.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in the accepted crossed R621 frame. Use the matching-height rule on X, crossed gate polarities and endpoint stars retained by R621/R594, Q tightness, boundary antisymmetry R3, same-support interaction R38, direct balanced-pair descent R39, hinged opposite-sign collapse R547, and bare-floor fence R444.

## Scope
Noncircular R24 restoration. Crossed phase. Order-free for m>=4. Fixed physical endpoint-box theorem using only accepted mathematics; independent of pending R627-R632 and of the mixed-root staircase R620.

## Applicability
Preferred structural consumer of the crossed endpoint geometry. In branch (A), keep both physical terminal Q dimers and their cross-frame witness identities through the R39 ancestry ledger. In branch (B), keep both hinge-derived {a,c} floors separately; each is already aligned to a natural matching-height tight turn and carries nontrivial collision ancestry. Do not collapse the two opposite singleton labelings by bare sign logic.

## Persistence
Retain the eight endpoint P8 proposals and exact two-hole sets, the eight physical mate clauses, whichever R38 collision packets they force, and in branch (A) the disjoint terminal-dimer direct pair plus R39 descent ancestry. In branch (B) retain all four extreme-X collision packets, both hinge cuts b,z, and the two separately derived {a,c} floors with their ancestor dimers and witnesses.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert branches (A),(B) are exclusive. Does not assert an R38 collision, a mass-two floor, or reversed singleton polarities alone close H. Does not claim both R39 and R547 descendants are simultaneously current. Does not use any pending result from the present Builder batch.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** R633 is a route-specific endpoint-collision box; its durable descendants remain accepted and reconstructible from history.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** All eight endpoint P8 proposals were checked turn-by-turn. Their stated two-hole sets are complete, the R3 clauses decorate to the six named R38 packets with correct tested orientations and distinct witnesses, and the Boolean implication gives either both terminal packets or all four extreme-X packets. R39/R547/R444 consumers are correctly applied and dependencies are R24-free.

## Proof
All proposals below use the same untouched complementary tight interval Q[2,m-2], which is nonempty because m>=4. Hence an eight-vertex endpoint path on E=X union {L,u,s,R} with exactly two uncertified turns gives a literal spanning two-cover proposal with exactly those two holes.

First build four right-terminal clauses.
(1) P=(u,L,a,b,z,R,s,c). Its only holes are (L,a,b),(R,s,c), so R3 gives (b,a,L) OR (c,s,R).
(2) P=(u,L,a,c,b,R,s,z). Its holes are (c,b,R),(R,s,z), giving (R,b,c) OR (z,s,R).
(3) P=(u,L,c,a,z,R,s,b). Its holes are (a,z,R),(R,s,b), giving (R,z,a) OR (b,s,R).
(4) P=(u,L,c,z,b,R,s,a). Its holes are (L,c,z),(R,s,a), giving (z,c,L) OR (a,s,R).
Every other turn in these paths is one of: an endpoint star uLx or xRs, a crossed gate turn Lac/Lca/bzR/zbR, or a matching-height X turn abz/acb/caz/czb, respectively, so the displayed hole sets are complete.

Now build four left-terminal clauses.
(5) P=(a,u,L,c,z,b,R,s). Holes (a,u,L),(L,c,z), giving (L,u,a) OR (z,c,L).
(6) P=(b,u,L,c,a,z,R,s). Holes (b,u,L),(a,z,R), giving (L,u,b) OR (R,z,a).
(7) P=(c,u,L,a,b,z,R,s). Holes (c,u,L),(L,a,b), giving (L,u,c) OR (b,a,L).
(8) P=(z,u,L,a,c,b,R,s). Holes (z,u,L),(c,b,R), giving (L,u,z) OR (R,b,c).
Again all remaining turns are accepted endpoint-star, gate, or matching-height turns.

Decorate every literal by R38. The Q turns (L,u,q_2) and (q_{m-2},s,R) are tight. Thus any tight literal (L,u,x), x in X, makes (L,u) tail-signed by distinct witnesses x,q_2 and gives C_L; any tight (x,s,R) gives C_R using witnesses x,q_{m-2}. For the X literals, matching-height gives (b,a,c),(a,b,c),(c,z,a),(z,c,a) tight. Therefore (b,a,L) gives C_ba with witnesses L,c; (R,b,c) gives C_bc with R,a; (R,z,a) gives C_za with R,c; and (z,c,L) gives C_zc with L,a.

Consequently clauses (1)-(4) imply, respectively,
C_ba OR C_R,
C_bc OR C_R,
C_za OR C_R,
C_zc OR C_R,
while clauses (5)-(8) imply
C_L OR C_zc,
C_L OR C_za,
C_L OR C_ba,
C_L OR C_bc.
If both C_L and C_R hold, branch (A) follows. The tested dimer (L,u) is tail-signed and (s,R) is head-signed; their supports are disjoint for m>=4. By accepted R39 they form a direct mass-four balanced pair, with the stated closure-or-floor continuation.

If branch (A) fails, at least one of C_L,C_R is absent. If C_R is absent, the first four implications force all C_ba,C_bc,C_za,C_zc. If C_L is absent, the last four force the same four packets. Hence branch (B) holds.

In branch (B), C_bc is head polarity on (b,c) and C_ba tail polarity on (b,a); the two supports meet exactly at b. R547 cuts the hinge and produces opposite-signed singletons on c and a, hence an ancestry-bearing floor on {a,c}. Likewise C_za is head polarity on (z,a) and C_zc tail polarity on (z,c); cutting hinge z by R547 gives the same physical singleton pair {a,c} with the two polarities reversed. The original collision witnesses and hinge cuts remain ancestry. R444 forbids treating the bare reversed singleton labels themselves as a contradiction, so the durable output is the pair of distinct ancestry-bearing floors. This proves the theorem.

# R644 — Pure-Q two-end branch forces two same-frame cross-end captures in X

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Retain accepted R630. In the branch (L,u,s) tight, fix any exact two-cover T of H-{L,u}; by R429 both rails are nontrivial. Then at least two distinct vertices x in X are capture-capable in this same T using s as the exact sign witness of S=(L,u). For each x, use the endpoint-star carrier K_x=(u,L,x). Every T-adjacency incident with x is a selected crossing from C={x}=V(K_x)-V(S) to E=V(H)-V(K_x). Call x blocked when every such adjacency contains s. Because x lies on a nontrivial T-rail it has at least one rail neighbor. If x is internal it has two distinct neighbors, so at least one incident crossing avoids the single vertex s; hence a blocked x must be a rail endpoint whose unique neighbor is s. Since s has degree at most two in the two-path forest T, at most two vertices of X are blocked. Thus at least two distinct x are nonblocked, and R527 captures each such x using a selected crossing avoiding s. Dually, in the branch (u,s,R) tight, every exact T of H-{s,R} contains at least two X vertices capture-capable with witness u through S=(s,R) and carriers K_x=(x,R,s). The source crossings coexist in T; capture descendants are alternative historical continuations.

H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in the accepted crossed R621 frame; accepted R630, R429, R527, R594.

Noncircular R24 restoration. Crossed phase, m>=4. Uses R429 rather than R5/R168.

## Applicability
After R630, spend the opposite-end Q witness in any fixed exact deletion cover of the winning terminal dimer; at least two X vertices have source crossings avoiding that witness and are individually capturable.

## Persistence
Retain the R630 branch literal, tested terminal dimer and far-end witness, the fixed exact pair-deletion cover T, each nonblocked x and chosen selected crossing avoiding the witness, endpoint-star carrier K_x, marker orientation, captured x, and R527 certificate.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert the two capture descendants coexist, that every x is capturable with the far-end witness, or that capture closes H.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Same-frame cross-end capture production has no live consumers and capture is saturated currency under current guidance.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Valid same-frame blocked-endpoint count using R429 and R527.

## Proof
Assume first the R630 branch (L,u,s) tight. Then S=(L,u) is tail-signed by exact witness s. Fix any exact two-cover T of H-{L,u}; R429 supplies exactness and says both rails are nontrivial. For x in X, R594 gives K_x=(u,L,x) tight. Relative to signed support S inside K_x, the surviving carrier set in H-V(S) is C={x}; hence every T-adjacency incident with x is a selected C|E crossing in the sense of R527. Because the T-rail containing x is nontrivial, x has at least one rail neighbor. Call x blocked if every incident selected crossing contains s. If x is internal on its rail, it has two distinct neighbors, and at most one can equal s, so one incident crossing avoids s. Thus any blocked x is a rail endpoint and its unique neighbor is s. In the two-path forest T, vertex s has degree at most two, so it can be adjacent to at most two vertices of X. Therefore at most two of the four X vertices are blocked, and at least two distinct x are nonblocked. For each nonblocked x choose an incident selected crossing xy avoiding s. It is disjoint from S and avoids the exact sign witness. Apply R527 with carrier K_x, signed support S, witness s, cover T, and marker xy, orienting the marker to designate x as captured. This gives the claimed same-frame historical capture certificate for x. The source crossings for all such x coexist in T; their actualization descendants are separate choices. In the dual R630 branch (u,s,R) tight, S=(s,R) is head-signed by witness u. R429 fixes any exact non-singleton-rail cover T of H-{s,R}; R594 gives carriers K_x=(x,R,s). The identical blocked-endpoint argument with witness u shows at most two X vertices blocked, so at least two have an incident crossing avoiding u and are captured by R527. No R5 or R168 is used.

# R65 — Fresh-far payment contact / transparent-birth architecture

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement

The fresh far-return frame can issue a new same-frame capture certificate using the current selected crossing. The source star at the captured anchor is therefore the literal star in that fresh frame rather than transported historical currentness.

## Scope
The accepted payment architecture distinguishes:
- pre-birth payment/capture contact;
- post-birth protected-lineage first contact.

Star equality at birth is local information. It does not by itself prove designated-lineage membership or continuation licensing.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Historical fresh-far payment architecture fence; modern provenance warnings supersede its navigation role.
- **Curation note:** Durable provenance/currentness barrier separating fresh-frame information, pre-birth contact, and protected post-birth lineage contact.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Legacy migration verification: inherited independently accepted status from checksum-verified A7C2 continuity compression.

## Proof
Take the fresh far-return frame in the sense of R65: its relevant support-deletion representative is current and contains the selected crossing that is to be used for capture. Accepted reconstructible R527 applies locally to exactly such a frame. In its capture/refund branch, a selected crossing xy avoiding an admissible witness is used as the actualizing two-vertex marker in that same exact deletion cover. One may orient the marker so either physical endpoint is the captured signed anchor. R527 therefore produces a new same-frame historical capture certificate retaining the original selected physical crossing, chosen witness, marker orientation, captured endpoint, and terminal actualization test. No transported currentness is needed.

Consequently the source star at the captured anchor is the literal star certified in this fresh frame: one arm is the actual selected crossing used by R527 and any second source incidence used downstream must be certified in the relevant current/historical carrier, rather than imported merely because an older representative had a star at the same physical vertex. Accepted R528 makes this fence explicit: capture ancestry is attached to the physical event (captured vertex, crossing), while old selected orientation, old carrier/component identity, residual rails, endpoint roles, and unrelated incident supports do not transport automatically.

Finally the timing distinction in R65 is exactly the R42 interface. The same-frame capture/payment event is pre-protection birth data. Only after choosing an actual capture descendant and a designated quiet continuation does R42 start protected-lineage first-contact control. Thus equality of a local star at capture birth does not itself certify designated-lineage membership or license later quiet continuation. This proves the fresh-far transparent-birth architecture using current explicit interfaces.

# R653 — Cross-end three-to-two component drop makes both deleted endpoints universal preserved floor coordinates

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Retain the accepted transitive order-three R24 frame with V(H)=X disjoint union V(Q), X={a,b,c,z}, Q=(q_0,...,q_m), m>=4, and put L=q_0, R=q_m. Then each of the two deleted endpoints L and R is independently a universal preserved coordinate for ancestry-bearing mass-two floors, using only the fixed cross-end pair-deletion residue. More precisely, let W=H-{L,R}. The three disjoint tight paths Q^o=Q[1,m-1], D_1=(a,c), D_2=(b,z) form a literal three-cover of W. Let T be any exact two-cover of W. Since T has fewer components, the proof of R159 supplies a selected T-state xy crossing two components of this three-cover. Apply the fully reconstructed R176 proof to that same crossing. Because V(H)-W={L,R}, the arbitrary spare vertex d may be chosen as L or, in a separate alternative birth, as R. For either choice e in {L,R}, R176 produces a balanced opposite-sign pair with one signed support literally the singleton (e) and the opposite support of order at most two. Hence, unless H is already two-covered, accepted fixed-singleton descent R428 preserves (e) and reaches an ancestry-bearing both-singleton floor. From that floor, for every prescribed vertex x!=e, accepted R432 preserves e while replacing only the other singleton, yielding either a spanning two-cover or a floor exactly {e,x}. Thus L and R are separately universal floor coordinates. The L-pinned and R-pinned births may use the same physical selected cross state in T but are alternative historical continuations, not simultaneous active pairs.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in the accepted transitive order-three R24 frame; Q=(q_0,...,q_m), m>=4. Use accepted pair-deletion exactness/rigidity R429 to supply T, accepted component-drop theorem R159 and its R176 proof, accepted R428, and accepted R432.

## Scope
Noncircular R24 restoration. Order-free in the transitive order-three frame and independent of crossed/aligned middle-gate polarity. No R612, R542, R620, R623, endpoint collision packet, or pending result is used.

## Applicability
Whenever the four-vertex complement X and long rail Q are retained, delete both Q endpoints. Compare any exact H-{L,R} two-cover with Q[1,m-1] plus the two physical M_S dimers (a,c),(b,z). Choose spare L or R in the R176 birth, preserve it through R428, and steer the other floor coordinate by R432.

## Persistence
Retain the cross-end deletion residue W; reference three-cover Q[1,m-1],(a,c),(b,z); exact two-cover T; selected cross state xy; chosen spare e=L or R; the R176 birth with literal singleton e and opposite support; R428 refund ledger preserving e; and R432 target-steering ledger.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert the L-pinned and R-pinned pair births coexist as active representatives. Does not prescribe which two reference components are crossed or the other R176 support. Does not by itself close the resulting floor. Does not use middle-gate polarity and therefore is not specific to the crossed phase.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** R653 is a specialized endpoint-coordinate theorem superseded in purpose by the order-free universal preserved-coordinate theorem R654.
- **Curation note:** Cross-end pair-deletion specialization of the global universal-coordinate theorem, retained for its explicit common-residue/cross-state provenance.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Correct noncircular endpoint-preservation theorem. R429 gives the pair-deletion cover; a 3-to-2 component comparison supplies a cross-state; P540/R176 with spare L or R makes that endpoint a literal singleton support, then R428 preserves it to floor and R432 steers the partner. No R24-dependent input.

## Proof
Put W=H-{L,R}. Since m>=4, Q^o=Q[1,m-1] is a nonempty tight path. The physical dimers D_1=(a,c) and D_2=(b,z) are tight paths vacuously. Their supports are pairwise disjoint and together cover W, so R_0=Q^o sqcup D_1 sqcup D_2 is a literal three-component cover of W. Accepted Pair-Deletion Rigidity R429 supplies an exact two-cover T=T_1 sqcup T_2 of W.\n\nApply the component-drop argument of accepted R159 to R_0 and T. Because T has two components while R_0 has three, some selected adjacent state xy of T joins two distinct R_0 components: otherwise every T-component would lie wholly inside one R_0 component, forcing at least three T-components. Retain such xy.\n\nNow use the fully reconstructed R176 proof directly. Its spare vertex d may be chosen arbitrarily in V(H)-W. Here V(H)-W={L,R}. Fix e=L first and choose d=L. If the R_0-component containing x is nontrivial, R176 chooses an old neighbor p of x and uses R3 with witness y to sign a dimer on {x,p}; the automatic tight dimer through d=L and y gives the opposite singleton sign on (L). If that R_0-component is a singleton, R176 signs singleton (x) directly from xy and the same automatic L-y path gives the opposite singleton (L). Thus in all cases the birth has one signed support literally (L), while the other support has order one or two.\n\nIf the other support is already singleton, we are at an ancestry-bearing floor containing L. If it is a dimer, apply accepted R428 with L as the fixed singleton coordinate. Every nonclosing step preserves (L) and strictly pays the opposite support until both supports are singleton. Therefore closure occurs or a floor {L,v} is reached. For any prescribed target x!=L, accepted R432 may then be run with L as the already-shared target coordinate; its one-coordinate replacement macro preserves L and yields closure or the exact floor {L,x}.\n\nRepeat the identical construction from the same mathematical base residue and cross state xy but choose the R176 spare d=R. This gives an alternative birth with literal singleton (R), followed by R428 and R432 to closure or {R,x} for arbitrary x!=R. No simultaneous-currentness of the two births is asserted. This proves universal preservation for both endpoints.

# R655 — Dual terminal collision branch makes both Q endpoints universal preserved floor coordinates

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Retain the accepted crossed R24 frame of R621 and branch (A) of accepted R633. Thus the terminal physical dimer S_L=(L,u) is tail-signed and S_R=(s,R) is head-signed, with L=q_0,u=q_1,s=q_{m-1},R=q_m and m>=4. Then, without generic pair payment, the same fixed Q geometry yields an ancestry-bearing both-singleton floor exactly {L,R}: cut the contiguous middle interval Q[1,m-1]=(u,...,s) through the two historical signed dimers. Signed-Interval Rebirth leaves the tail-signed singleton (L) from S_L and the head-signed singleton (R) from S_R, retaining the R633 terminal-collision witnesses and the named Q cut. Consequently each Q endpoint is a universal preserved floor coordinate in this branch. For every prescribed x distinct from L there is a finite chosen ancestry-retaining continuation yielding either a spanning two-cover or the exact floor {L,x}, with L preserved during the final one-coordinate steering step; dually, for every x distinct from R there is closure or the exact floor {R,x}, with R preserved.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in the accepted crossed R621 frame; branch (A) of accepted R633 holds; accepted Signed-Interval Rebirth R425 and Complete Floor Pair Steering R432 are available.

## Scope
Noncircular R24 restoration. Crossed phase, conditional on accepted R633 branch (A). The direct endpoint-floor step is purely fixed-frame and uses only R425; the universal-target addendum uses R432, whose dependency closure is R175/R3/R4/R429/R433 and does not use R24, R5, R168, R169, R224, or R533.

## Applicability
When R633 lands in the dual-terminal branch, replace the anonymous R39 paid-floor conclusion by the literal endpoint floor {L,R}. Downstream consumers may then retain either physical Q endpoint while steering the other floor coordinate to any prescribed target.

## Persistence
Retain the two R633 tested terminal dimers with their original collision witness identities, the common carrier Q, the explicit cut interval Q[1,m-1], the R425 rebirth certificates leaving singleton L and singleton R, and any subsequent one-coordinate R432 replacement certificate. Alternative target steerings are separate descendants.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert R633 branch (A) always occurs. Does not make the branch-(B) hinge floors simultaneous with the endpoint floor. Does not by itself close H or claim target floors for different x coexist. Does not use generic R39 payment, R5, R168, R169, R224, R533, or R620.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** R655 is a specialized terminal-coordinate theorem superseded in purpose by the order-free universal preserved-coordinate theorem R654.
- **Curation note:** Branch-specific endpoint-coordinate construction retained only for its R633 terminal-collision/common-cut provenance; coordinate universality itself is covered globally by C518.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Correct. In R633(A), R425 applied to the common physical cut Q[1,m-1] rebirths (L,u) tail-sign as singleton L and (s,R) head-sign as singleton R, giving a literal opposite-sign floor {L,R}; R432 then preserves either endpoint while steering the other. Fully R24-free.

## Proof
Assume branch (A) of accepted R633. By definition, the fixed tested terminal dimer S_L=(L,u) carries tail polarity, while S_R=(s,R) carries head polarity. Their supports are disjoint because m>=4, and both occur as the two terminal dimers of the same retained tight rail Q=(L,u,q_2,...,q_{m-2},s,R). Keep all original R633 witness data.

Let C=Q[1,m-1]=(u,q_2,...,q_{m-2},s). This is a contiguous tight interval of Q. It meets S_L exactly in u and S_R exactly in s. Apply accepted Signed-Interval Rebirth / Tight-Path Cut Memory R425 separately to the two historical signed supports with the vertices met by C deleted. For the tail-signed path S_L=(L,u), the last surviving interval is the singleton (L); since u is the deleted right cut-neighbor, R425 certifies (L) with the same tail polarity, now with the physical cut boundary u available as the rebirth witness. For the head-signed path S_R=(s,R), the first surviving interval is the singleton (R); since s is the deleted left cut-neighbor, R425 certifies (R) with the same head polarity, with cut boundary s as the rebirth witness. Thus the two surviving singleton supports are disjoint and have opposite polarities. They form an ancestry-bearing mass-two balanced-pair floor exactly {L,R}. No generic pair-payment excursion is required: the floor is obtained directly from the one fixed Q interval cut, while the original R633 collision witnesses remain historical ancestry.

Now fix any x distinct from L. If x=R the displayed floor already has target {L,R}. Otherwise apply accepted R432 to the active floor S={L,R} with target T={L,x}. Since S and T share the coordinate L, use the one-replacement case in the proof of R432: retain L as the common singleton and replace only R by x. The chosen continuation yields either a spanning two-cover or the exact floor {L,x}, with L preserved through that replacement. This proves universal preserved-coordinate capability for L. The argument for R is the exact dual, applying R432 to target {R,x} and preserving R. Hence both Q endpoints are universal preserved floor coordinates throughout branch (A).

# R656 — Extreme-edge saturation compiles to a four-fiber short-carrier capture fan

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Retain branch (B) of accepted R633 in the crossed R621 frame. Then all four extreme collision packets are directly consumable by accepted R542, in four named sibling pair-deletion fibers. Specifically: (i) C_ba makes S=(b,a) a two-witness tail-signed reverse boundary dimer of the tight carrier K=(a,b,z), with witnesses L,c and complementary carrier singleton z; hence every exact two-cover of H-{a,b} contains an R508 z-to-exterior crossing, one of the two witnesses L,c avoids that crossing, and R542 gives capture/payment or a spanning two-cover. (ii) C_bc makes S=(b,c) a two-witness head-signed reverse boundary dimer of K=(z,c,b), with witnesses R,a and complementary singleton z, yielding the analogous packet in H-{b,c}. (iii) C_za makes S=(z,a) a two-witness head-signed reverse boundary dimer of K=(b,a,z), with witnesses R,c and complementary singleton b, yielding the packet in H-{z,a}. (iv) C_zc makes S=(z,c) a two-witness tail-signed reverse boundary dimer of K=(c,z,b), with witnesses L,a and complementary singleton b, yielding the packet in H-{z,c}. Thus the saturated branch is not merely two opposite hinge floors on {a,c}: it contains two z-centered sibling capture fibers across the b-hinge and two b-centered sibling capture fibers across the z-hinge, all with exact physical carrier and witness ancestry.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in the accepted crossed R621 frame and branch (B) of accepted R633 holds. Use accepted R542 and the matching-height X turns already retained by R621/R633.

## Scope
Noncircular R24 restoration. Crossed phase, branch (B) of accepted R633. Uses only accepted R633 and R542; the R542 dependency closure is R508/R527/R526/R427/R3 and does not use R24, R5, R168, R169, R224, or R533.

## Applicability
Use instead of collapsing branch (B) immediately to the bare {a,c} hinge floors. Compare the two z-centered sibling fibers H-{a,b} and H-{b,c}, or dually the two b-centered fibers H-{z,a} and H-{z,c}, so that the physical location of the forced R508 crossing and the original collision witnesses can be consumed across fibers.

## Persistence
Retain for each of the four packets: the R633 tested oriented collision dimer and both witness identities; the exact tight carrier K; the complementary singleton z or b; the corresponding pair-deletion fiber; the R508 selected singleton-to-exterior crossing; the witness selected to avoid that crossing; and all R527/R526/R427 capture-payment ancestry. Alternative fibers and descendants need not be simultaneously current.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert that the four R542 descendants coexist, that any one capture/payment output closes H, or that sibling crossings align automatically. Does not identify a common exact cover across different deletion fibers. Does not use the bare reversed singleton labels as progress.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Four-fiber short-carrier capture-fan leaf with no consumers; capture production is saturated.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** All four extreme R633(B) collision packets are correctly matched to explicit tight trimers whose reverse boundary dimer has the stated orientation and whose two witnesses lie outside the carrier. R542 applies in each named pair-deletion fiber.

## Proof
Assume branch (B) of accepted R633, so all four collision packets C_ba,C_bc,C_za,C_zc hold with the stated tested orientations, polarities, and two distinct witnesses. We verify the four R542 instances.

For C_ba, the tested dimer S=(b,a) is tail-signed by witnesses L and c. The matching-height rule on X gives the tight trimer K=(a,b,z), because M(ab)=M_R>M(bz)=M_S. Thus S=(b,a) is the reverse initial boundary dimer of K. Both witnesses L,c lie outside K. Accepted R542 applies. With D={a,b}, its R508 step uses the complementary carrier block {z} and therefore forces, in every exact two-cover of H-D, a selected state crossing {z} to V(H)\V(K). Such a two-vertex crossing cannot contain both distinct witnesses L,c, so one witness avoids it and the R527/R526 capture/payment branch applies unless H already has a spanning two-cover.

For C_bc, S=(b,c) is head-signed by witnesses R and a. The trimer K=(z,c,b) is tight since M(zc)=M_R>M(cb)=M_L. Here S=(b,c) is the reverse terminal boundary dimer of K, and R,a are outside K. R542 therefore applies in D={b,c}, with complementary singleton z and an R508 crossing from {z} to the exterior of K; one of R,a avoids the crossing.

For C_za, S=(z,a) is head-signed by witnesses R,c. The trimer K=(b,a,z) is tight since M(ba)=M_R>M(az)=M_L. S=(z,a) is its reverse terminal boundary dimer, R,c lie outside K, and R542 applies in D={z,a} with complementary singleton b.

For C_zc, S=(z,c) is tail-signed by witnesses L,a. The trimer K=(c,z,b) is tight since M(cz)=M_R>M(zb)=M_S. S=(z,c) is its reverse initial boundary dimer, L,a lie outside K, and R542 applies in D={z,c} with complementary singleton b.

These are four literal R542-ready packets. The first two share the same complementary singleton z while changing the second deleted endpoint across the common hinge b; the last two share complementary singleton b across the common hinge z. This is precisely the claimed four-fiber capture fan.
