# R657 — Sibling extreme-edge capture fibers force dual root-anchor interactions

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Retain branch (B) of accepted R633. Then there are two explicit source-localized R436 anchor interactions, one at z and one at b, obtained before generic pair payment. At z, use the C_ba and C_bc short-carrier packets. In an exact H-{a,b} two-cover, R508 forces a selected crossing incident with the complementary singleton z; choose one of the C_ba witnesses L,c avoiding that crossing and use R527/R526 with marker endpoint z designated as the new signed anchor. Since C_ba is tail polarity, this gives a nontrivial head-signed dimer anchored at z. Independently, in H-{b,c}, the C_bc packet and witnesses R,a give by the same construction a nontrivial tail-signed dimer anchored at z. These two graph-intrinsic sibling-fiber supports both contain the historical anchor z and are nontrivial, so R436 applied to either one as the older signed support and the other as the later tight path has no stationary-singleton exception and yields strict tight-path growth, a vertex-simple tight cycle, or a three-vertex reverse contact/reversal at z. Dually, C_za in H-{z,a} yields a tail-signed dimer anchored at b and C_zc in H-{z,c} yields a head-signed dimer anchored at b, forcing the analogous R436 event at b. Thus the saturated branch has two physically localized, non-replay root-anchor interactions tied to different sibling pair-deletion fibers.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in branch (B) of accepted R633. Use accepted R508, R527/R526 and R436; equivalently the four R542-ready packets established directly from R633.

## Scope
Noncircular R24 restoration. Crossed phase, branch (B) of R633. Uses accepted R633,R508,R527,R526,R436 and R3/R427 only through the cited accepted interfaces; no R24, R5, R168, R169, R224, R533, or mixed-root staircase is used.

## Applicability
Use as the preferred consumer of R633 branch (B): do not collapse the four extreme packets to anonymous {a,c} floors first. Actualize the common complementary root in each sibling pair and compare the two resulting nontrivial signed dimers directly by R436. The outputs retain which pair-deletion fiber and which extreme collision packet produced each side.

## Persistence
At z retain the C_ba collision support/witness pair, exact H-{a,b} cover and R508 crossing, chosen avoiding witness, R526 z-anchored head dimer; and separately the C_bc data from H-{b,c} and its z-anchored tail dimer. Retain the R436 physical growth/cycle/reversal certificate comparing the two. Dually retain the corresponding C_za/C_zc data and b-anchored event. The two fiber constructions are graph-intrinsic historical certificates and need not be current in one cover.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert that either R436 event is itself a spanning two-cover or contradiction. Does not assert the two z-anchored dimers or two b-anchored dimers are vertex-disjoint. Does not use R547 on them. Does not claim the z- and b-events occur in one current representative. The gain is source-localized non-replay anchor interaction, not immediate closure.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** R657 is an old capture-fiber producer; corrected durable consumer R783 remains active toolkit.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Correct sibling-fiber consumer. R527/R526 can designate the common complementary singleton z (dually b) as signed anchor, producing nontrivial opposite-polarity dimers from distinct fibers; R436 applies directly to the two proper paths meeting at that anchor and gives nonstationary growth/cycle/reversal output.

## Proof
Assume branch (B) of R633. We give the z argument; the b argument is dual.

The packet C_ba says S_1=(b,a) is tail-signed by two distinct witnesses L,c. As checked directly from the matching-height frame, K_1=(a,b,z) is tight and S_1 is its reverse initial boundary dimer, with complementary carrier singleton z. Pair-delete D_1={a,b}. Accepted R508 applied to K_1 says every exact two-cover T_1 of H-D_1 selects a state on physical support {z,y_1} crossing the singleton {z} to the exterior of K_1. Since L,c are distinct, at least one of them, call it w_1, is not y_1 and hence avoids the selected crossing. Use accepted R527 with this witness and the two-vertex marker {z,y_1}; choose the marker order so that z is the actualization endpoint. Because S_1 is tail-signed, the exact tail/head dual of R526 produces a head-signed opposite support P_z with signed head anchor z. The marker has order two. In the good-test branch P_z is that marker dimer; in the bad-test branch P_z is the two-vertex support consisting of z and the chosen sign witness. Hence in either branch P_z is a nontrivial graph-intrinsic tight dimer anchored at z.

Now C_bc says S_2=(b,c) is head-signed by witnesses R,a. The tight carrier K_2=(z,c,b) has S_2 as its reverse terminal boundary dimer and complementary singleton z. Pair-delete D_2={b,c}. R508 forces a selected crossing {z,y_2}. Choose w_2 in {R,a} avoiding y_2 and apply R527/R526 with z designated as the marker endpoint. Since S_2 is head-signed, the opposite support T_z is tail-signed, nontrivial, and has signed tail anchor exactly z. Thus P_z and T_z are two graph-intrinsic nontrivial tight dimers from sibling deletion fibers, both containing z, with the complete C_ba and C_bc source ancestries retained.

Apply accepted R436 to the signed support P_z and the proper tight path T_z. The latter contains the signed anchor z of P_z. The only stationary exception in R436 is exact replay of the same singleton support with no new certificate data. Here both paths have order two, and moreover T_z comes from the distinct sibling deletion fiber and opposite source collision packet. Therefore the at-anchor branch is nonstationary and R436 yields strict growth of one of the tight paths, a vertex-simple tight cycle, or a three-vertex reverse contact/reversal at z.

For b, C_za gives the head-signed dimer (z,a) with witnesses R,c and tight carrier K_3=(b,a,z); R508/R527/R526 in H-{z,a}, designating complementary singleton b, yields a nontrivial tail-signed dimer anchored at b. C_zc gives tail-signed (z,c) with witnesses L,a and tight carrier K_4=(c,z,b); the same construction in H-{z,c} yields a nontrivial head-signed dimer anchored at b. R436 on these two sibling-fiber supports gives the stated nonstationary event at b. This proves the corollary.

# R661 — Inward Q anchors force non-replay shallow-puncture events at both ends of the crossed frame

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Retain the crossed R621 frame with m>=6. There are two alternative ancestry-retaining continuations, one from each end of Q, each yielding either a spanning two-cover or a genuinely nonstationary R436 event at a named inward Q vertex. On the left, D_L=(q_3,q_2) is tail-signed by b. If m=6, the opposite-polarity inward dimer D_R=(q_4,q_3) meets D_L only at q_3, so R547 yields a floor containing singleton q_2 and its old tail-sign witness b is retained by the underlying R425 hinge cut. If m>=7, D_L and D_R are disjoint opposite-polarity dimers. Use R425 on D_L with q_3 deleted: singleton q_2 remains tail-signed by b while D_R is untouched, hence the resulting singleton/dimer pair is still balanced; R428 preserves q_2 while paying D_R to singleton width. Thus in every m>=6 case there is closure or an ancestry-bearing floor containing q_2 with the historical sign certificate witnessed by b. Use R432 to steer the other coordinate to b. In W=H-{q_2,b}, puncturing q_2 from the R621 shallow cover H-b=Q[0,m-1] sqcup (R,c,a,z) gives the literal three-cover Q[0,1] sqcup Q[3,m-1] sqcup (R,c,a,z). Any exact two-cover of W crosses two source components. Apply R176 to such a crossing with spare d=q_2. Besides the singleton support q_2, the P540 construction contains the automatic nontrivial sign-extension dimer through q_2 and its selected witness y in W. Since b is deleted, y!=b. Apply R436 to the retained old signed singleton q_2 and this later proper dimer through q_2; the stationary singleton exception is impossible because the later path has order two, so strict growth/cycle/reverse-contact occurs at q_2. The right dual uses D_R=(q_{m-2},q_{m-3}) head-signed by a, preserves q_{m-2} by R547 when m=6 or by R425+R428 when m>=7, steers to {q_{m-2},a}, punctures the shallow H-a cover, and feeds the automatic second-birth extension dimer into R436.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in the accepted crossed R621 frame; m>=6. Use accepted R536 inward signs, R547/R425, R39 only to recognize the disjoint direct pair for m>=7, fixed-singleton descent R428, floor steering R432, Pair-Deletion Rigidity R429, R176 with arbitrary spare, and R436.

## Scope
Noncircular R24 restoration, crossed phase, conditional m>=6. Repairs R659 by removing R224 and by using a genuine later nontrivial extension dimer at R436.

## Applicability
Use after the crossed frame is fixed when an inward Q coordinate should be converted into a non-replay event. The left lineage targets q_2 via the shallow H-b puncture; the right lineage targets q_{m-2} via H-a.

## Persistence
Retain the inward signed dimer and old witness, the R425/R547 cut that creates the preserved singleton, R428 and R432 ancestry, the shallow puncture three-cover, selected cross state, second R176 birth with its automatic extension dimer through the same anchor, and the R436 contact certificate.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not claim either R436 event closes H or that left/right continuations coexist. Does not use R224, R533, R5, R168, or R169. The later R436 input is the actual nontrivial extension dimer from R176, not a repeated singleton label.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Dual shallow-puncture R436-event leaf with no consumers; generic nonreplay growth/event currency is not current progress.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Valid noncircular inward-anchor construction. Accepted R176 proof P540 explicitly supplies the later proper extension dimer through the spare anchor required by R436.

## Proof
Write L=q_0,u=q_1,R=q_m,s=q_{m-1}. Accepted R536 in the crossed R621 frame gives q_3 q_2 b tight, so D_L=(q_3,q_2) is tail-signed by b. Dually a q_{m-2} q_{m-3} is tight, so D_R=(q_{m-2},q_{m-3}) is head-signed by a.

LEFT PRESERVED ANCHOR. If m=6, D_L=(q_3,q_2) and D_R=(q_4,q_3) meet only at q_3 with opposite polarities. R547 gives the singleton floor {q_2,q_4}; in its R425 hinge cut, q_2 is the old tail endpoint of D_L, hence its old witness b remains a graph-intrinsic tail-sign certificate. If m>=7, D_L and D_R are disjoint opposite-polarity signed dimers, hence form a direct balanced pair (R39). Apply R425 to D_L with deletion set {q_3}. The surviving last interval is singleton (q_2), and because q_2 is the old tail endpoint its witness remains b. D_R is disjoint from q_3 and is untouched, so (q_2) together with D_R is still a balanced opposite-sign pair. Apply R428 with singleton q_2 fixed. Unless H is already two-covered, this reaches a both-singleton floor containing q_2. Thus in every m>=6 case we have an ancestry-bearing floor containing q_2 and the historical tail-sign certificate q_2 witnessed by b. Apply R432 with target {q_2,b}; along the nonclosing one-coordinate replacement q_2 is preserved and the full incoming ancestry ledger, including the old q_2-b sign certificate, remains historical.

Put W=H-{q_2,b}. The accepted R621 shallow cover H-b=Q[0,m-1] sqcup (R,c,a,z), punctured at internal q_2, gives three nonempty tight paths A=Q[0,1], B=Q[3,m-1], C=(R,c,a,z) covering W. By R429 choose an exact two-cover T of W. Since T has two components and A,B,C are three nonempty source components, some selected state xy of T joins two different source components. Apply the fully reconstructed R176 proof to this crossing with spare d=q_2. In P540 the spare d receives a singleton sign using one selected endpoint y as witness, through the automatic ordered two-vertex path joining d and y. Denote that actual tight extension dimer by E_new; it has support {q_2,y}, contains the anchor q_2, and is nontrivial. Since y lies in W while b is deleted, y!=b. The old historical signed support is singleton (q_2) with witness b. Apply R436 to that old singleton support and the later proper tight path E_new. Because E_new has order two, the exact-singleton stationary replay exception is impossible. Hence R436 gives strict path growth, a vertex-simple tight cycle, or a reverse-contact/reversal cell at q_2.

RIGHT DUAL. If m=6, R547 leaves q_4=q_{m-2} from D_R and its old head witness a survives the hinge cut. If m>=7, apply R425 to D_R deleting q_{m-3}; singleton q_{m-2} remains head-signed by a while D_L is untouched, and R428 preserves q_{m-2} to a both-singleton floor. R432 steers the other coordinate to a. In W_R=H-{q_{m-2},a}, puncturing q_{m-2} from the shallow cover H-a=(c,z,b,L) sqcup Q[1,m] gives the three nonempty tight paths (c,z,b,L), Q[1,m-3], and Q[m-1,m]. Any R429 exact two-cover crosses two source components. Apply R176 with spare d=q_{m-2}; its automatic sign-extension dimer E_new^R has support {q_{m-2},y} with y in W_R and hence y!=a. R436 applied to the retained old singleton q_{m-2} and this nontrivial later dimer gives the dual non-replay event. This proves R661 without R224 or any R24-circular dependency.

# R676 — Every internal X block carries a same-frame collision-P4 two-sided packet

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Retain the accepted crossed beyond-ten sigma_G(T)=0 five-cell frame and let one X-dimer cell be an internal degree-two block on an oriented exact-cover rail T, with predecessor Q endpoint y^- and successor Q endpoint y^+. If the block is G_3={a,c}, orient it in T as S=(a,c) or S=(c,a). In the first orientation choose the fixed R649 head witness w=b; in the second choose w=z. Then (w,S) is tight. Because the predecessor transition gives (y^-,S) tight, R38 gives a same-tested-order same-head collision on S with witnesses w,y^-. Because the successor transition gives (S,y^+) tight, the four-vertex order (w,S,y^+) is itself a tight Hamilton P4. Thus the same internal G_3 block carries simultaneously a predecessor collision and a successor labelled P4, both retaining one fixed complementary-X witness w. Dually, if the internal block is G_4={b,z}, orient S=(b,z) and take w=a, or S=(z,b) and take w=c. R649 gives the fixed tail sign (S,w). The predecessor transition (y^-,S) concatenates directly to the Hamilton P4 (y^-,S,w), while the successor transition (S,y^+) gives an R38 same-tail collision with witnesses y^+,w. Hence every degree-two X block in the c_X=2 Internal-X shape and in every c_X=3 minimum shape carries a literal two-sided collision/P4 packet in one common exact cover; the P4 uses three X vertices and the Q endpoint on the opposite side of the block, while the collision uses the other adjacent Q endpoint.

## Hypotheses
H is in the accepted crossed R621/R665 sigma=0 minimum frame. One X cell is a degree-two contiguous T-block. Use accepted R649 and R38; P4 tightness is direct concatenation of the fixed source sign with the opposite-side T transition.

## Scope
Noncircular R24 restoration. Sigma=0 minimum five-cell geometry. No payment, R176, R436, R5, R168, R169, R224, R533, or generic R358.

## Applicability
Use in every Internal-X structural regime from accepted R670. Keep both adjacent Q endpoints and the common complementary-X witness. Do not spend either edge separately before testing splices that use the collision and P4 together.

## Persistence
Retain T and rail orientation, internal X block S, predecessor and successor Q endpoints y^-,y^+, the fixed complementary-X witness w, the R38 collision certificate on one side, and the explicit ordered Hamilton P4 on the other.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert the collision or P4 alone closes H. Does not apply to degree-one X blocks. Does not assert descendant payment representatives preserve the same T rail; the theorem is a same-frame graph-intrinsic packet.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Internal-X collision/P4 packet leaf with no consumers; current five-cell compression uses source-sink and exact-cover parents rather than packet manufacture.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** PASS. For an internal X block, the predecessor and successor T-transitions coexist in one exact cover. On one side the fixed R649 witness and Q endpoint give the R38 collision; on the other the two consecutive tight triples concatenate directly to the claimed labelled Hamilton P4. The dual G3/G4 orientation cases are correct.

## Proof
Let S be the oriented internal X-dimer block and y^- S, S y^+ the two literal adjacent T transitions. First take G_3={a,c}. If S=(a,c), accepted R649 gives the fixed head-sign turn (b,a,c); put w=b. If S=(c,a), R649 gives (z,c,a); put w=z. Thus in either case (w,S) is tight with w in the complementary X-dimer. The predecessor triple (y^-,S) is tight because it is consecutive in T and y^- lies in a Q cell. Since y^- differs from w, R38 gives a same-tested-order same-head collision on S with witnesses w and y^-. The successor triple (S,y^+) is also consecutive in T. Therefore the four-vertex sequence (w,S,y^+) has its two consecutive triples (w,S) and (S,y^+) tight and is a Hamilton P4. For G_4={b,z}, if S=(b,z) take the fixed R649 tail witness w=a, while if S=(z,b) take w=c. Then (S,w) is tight. The predecessor triple (y^-,S) concatenates with (S,w) to the Hamilton P4 (y^-,S,w). The successor triple (S,y^+) is a second tail-sign certificate on the same tested S, distinct from w, so R38 gives the same-tail collision. All certificates occur in the same fixed T and retain both adjacent Q endpoints. This proves R676.

# R683 — Inward middle-gate witness forces protected endpoint first contact or a cross-end trimer

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Retain the hypotheses of pending R682: S is one oriented crossed middle-gate X dimer, v is an exterior sign witness on S, and L=q_0,R=q_m. Then there is a chosen continuation with one of two source-localized outcomes. (FC) A protected first-contact event is exposed at one physical endpoint e in {L,R}, retaining S, v, the R649 endpoint carrier K_e, the actual selected carrier/exterior crossing through e, and the capture ancestry. (XET) One exact H-V(S) two-cover contains the tight cross-end trimer (L,v,R) or (R,v,L).

Indeed, take the R682 dichotomy. In its CAP branch, the endpoint e is captured through an actual selected crossing D={e,y} of the retained historical R649 carrier K_e, and K_e is a tight trimer containing a genuine historical carrier adjacency E={e,x} for some x in V(S). Before anonymous dimer payment, choose the actual R527 capture descendant and designate a quiet protected continuation. Accepted R312 applies verbatim to the packet (K_e,D,e,E): either an earlier event touching e is already exposed or the lawful old-carrier mirror reentry is itself first contact at e. Thus CAP sharpens to FC without relying on generic R436 growth or on the later singleton-width payment. The XET branch is unchanged.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in accepted crossed R621/R649; pending R682 applies to oriented middle-gate dimer S with exterior sign witness v. Accepted R312.

## Scope
Noncircular R24 consumer. Sharpens the capture arm of R682 to protected endpoint contact using the genuine R649 short carrier. No generic R436 and no need to spend the R526 singleton-payment branch.

## Applicability
Use after an anchor-exchange output adds q_2 or q_{m-2} as a same-polarity witness on a crossed middle-gate X dimer. Run R682. If it gives CAP, immediately apply R312 on the same R649 endpoint carrier rather than recording generic payment. The only alternative is the source-coupled cross-end trimer.

## Persistence
In FC retain S,v,e,K_e, the actual selected crossing D={e,y}, the R527 capture certificate, one genuine old carrier adjacency E at e, the designated R42 protected continuation, and the first-contact/mirror-reentry certificate. In XET retain the exact H-S cover and literal trimer order.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert first contact closes H. Does not consume the cross-end trimer. Does not assert both endpoint first-contact lineages coexist. Depends on pending R682 and therefore is itself pending until R682 is independently accepted.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Middle-gate witness -> protected contact/cross-end-trimer leaf with no consumers; route-specific contact production is noncanonical.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** PASS. In R682 CAP, the captured endpoint e lies on the retained historical R649 trimer carrier K_e and has a genuine carrier adjacency there. This is precisely the accepted R312 packet, so choosing the actual capture descendant and protected continuation gives earlier contact or first contact at e without generic growth.

## Proof
Apply pending R682. If XET occurs there is nothing to prove. Suppose CAP occurs at endpoint e. By the proof of R682, S is the signed dimer with witness v, K_e is the accepted R649 tight trimer on V(S) union {e}, and the chosen exact H-V(S) cover T selects a physical carrier/exterior crossing D={e,y} with y outside K_e and y!=v. Accepted R527 is applied to this exact crossing and oriented so that e is the captured signed anchor. Hence we have an actual historical capture certificate of e through D on the retained historical carrier K_e.

Because K_e is a trimer and e is its complementary carrier singleton, e is an endpoint of K_e and has a genuine historical carrier adjacency E={e,x} to the neighboring vertex x in V(S). Thus all hypotheses of accepted R312 are satisfied with A=K_e, crossing D, captured anchor e, and old adjacency E. Choose the actual R527 capture descendant and designate the quiet continuation required by R42, exactly as permitted in R312. Then R312 says either some earlier operation has already touched the protected anchor e, in which case that earlier contact is exposed, or the lawful R155 mirror reentry on the same retained carrier and old adjacency is itself first contact at e. In either case the outcome is a protected first-contact event at e retaining the original capture ancestry. No R526 payment or R436 growth is required. This proves FC.

# R687 — Crossed middle-gate dimers carry three carriers, so no single exterior witness escapes capture

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Retain the accepted crossed R621 frame with X={a,b,c,z}, endpoints L=q_0 and R=q_m, and let S be any one of the four oriented middle-gate M_S dimers (a,c),(c,a),(b,z),(z,b). Accepted R649 supplies for each such S not two but three tight trimer carriers whose supports exceed V(S) by a single vertex:

S=(a,c): carriers (z,c,a),(L,c,a),(R,c,a), complementary singletons z,L,R;
S=(c,a): carriers (b,a,c),(L,a,c),(R,a,c), complementary singletons b,L,R;
S=(b,z): carriers (z,b,c),(z,b,L),(z,b,R), complementary singletons c,L,R;
S=(z,b): carriers (b,z,a),(b,z,L),(b,z,R), complementary singletons a,L,R.

Write x_S for the X-vertex complementary singleton, so x_S is z,b,c,a respectively. In every case x_S lies in X and x_S,L,R are three distinct vertices.

Let v be any vertex outside X union {L,R} which is an exact sign witness on the tested orientation of S with the polarity appropriate to the displayed tight turn. Then the carrier-witness saturation theorem R686 applies with k=3 and |W|=1, so capture is unconditional: every exact two-cover T of H-V(S) contains a selected crossing at one of x_S,L,R that avoids v, accepted R527 captures that complementary singleton with v retained as the exact witness, and since S is a dimer accepted R526 yields either a spanning two-cover or a certificate-retaining singleton-width descendant.

The outcome refines into two cases, both of which now carry a capture.

(CAP-E) If some endpoint crossing avoids v, the capture may be taken at the physical endpoint L or R by orienting the marker accordingly. This is exactly the CAP output of pending R682.

(CAP-X) If neither endpoint crossing avoids v, then T contains the selected states {L,v} and {R,v}, so v is internal on its rail with neighbours L and R and T contains the cross-end tight trimer (L,v,R) or (R,v,L). This is the XET output of pending R682. But both rail adjacencies at v are then used, and x_S is distinct from L and R, so the third forced crossing at x_S cannot meet v. It therefore avoids v, and an x_S-anchored capture with the same witness v holds in the same cover T alongside the trimer.

Consequently the R682 dichotomy is not a choice between capture and a capture-free nonlocal alternative. Capture with the inward witness v is unconditional in the crossed frame, and the cross-end trimer, when it occurs, is additional structure that coexists with an X-anchored capture rather than replacing it. The present statement subsumes pending R682, whose two conclusions are CAP-E together with the trimer half of CAP-X, and it does so from the same accepted inputs R621,R649,R508,R527,R526 without depending on the review outcome of R682.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in the accepted crossed R621 frame with X={a,b,c,z}, Q=(q_0,...,q_m), L=q_0, R=q_m. S is one of the four oriented middle-gate M_S dimers. v lies outside X union {L,R} and is an exact same-polarity sign witness on the tested orientation of S. Pair-deletion exactness supplies an exact two-cover of H-V(S). Uses accepted R621, R649, R508, R527, R526 and the parent theorem R686.

## Scope
Noncircular R24 consumer. Crossed frame, one oriented middle-gate dimer, one exterior witness. No R5,R168,R169,R224,R533, generic R358, or R436. Does not use pending R675, R677-R682 or the five-cell residue classification.

## Applicability
Use in place of pending R682 whenever an anchor-exchange clause supplies q_2 or q_{m-2} as a single new same-polarity witness on an oriented G_3 or G_4 dimer. Do not treat the cross-end trimer as an uncaptured alternative: harvest the capture first, then treat the trimer as extra nonlocal geometry. The captured anchor is a physical Q endpoint in CAP-E and the X-vertex x_S in CAP-X.

## Persistence
Retain S with tested orientation and polarity, the witness v, the chosen exact H-V(S) cover T, all three R649 carriers with complementary singletons x_S,L,R, the three forced crossings, the avoiding crossing actually used, the captured vertex, R527/R526 capture-payment ancestry, and in CAP-X the literal rail order (L,v,R) or (R,v,L).

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert that captures at different complementary singletons coexist as paid descendants. Does not assert that an x_S-anchored capture has the same downstream value as an endpoint-anchored one; only that a capture exists. Does not apply when the additional witness lies in X union {L,R}. Does not by itself consume the cross-end trimer or close H. Does not assert any paid descendant remains current in T.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Three-carrier capture leaf with no consumers; quantitative/generic carrier saturation is preserved in canonical parent machinery.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** PASS. Accepted R649 genuinely supplies three distinct one-vertex carriers x_S,L,R for each oriented middle-gate dimer, and v outside X union {L,R} misses all three complementary singletons. Applying accepted R686 with k=3 makes capture unconditional. If both endpoint crossings meet v they are v's two rail adjacencies, so the x_S crossing must avoid v and yields the claimed coexisting X-anchored capture. The result is noncircular relative to R682.

## Proof
Step 1 (three carriers). Accepted R649 lists twelve R542-ready packets grouped by the four oriented M_S dimers, three per dimer, and certifies for each entry that K is a tight trimer and that S is exactly a reverse boundary dimer of K. Reading off supports only: for S=(a,c) the listed carriers are (z,c,a),(L,c,a),(R,c,a) with supports {a,c,z},{a,c,L},{a,c,R}; for S=(c,a) they are (b,a,c),(L,a,c),(R,a,c) with supports {a,c,b},{a,c,L},{a,c,R}; for S=(b,z) they are (z,b,c),(z,b,L),(z,b,R) with supports {b,z,c},{b,z,L},{b,z,R}; for S=(z,b) they are (b,z,a),(b,z,L),(b,z,R) with supports {b,z,a},{b,z,L},{b,z,R}. In every group each support equals V(S) union {one vertex}, and the three extra vertices are x_S,L,R with x_S the X-vertex z,b,c,a respectively. Since x_S lies in X and L,R are the two distinct physical endpoints of Q, the three complementary singletons are pairwise distinct. Hence S carries k=3 retained vertex-simple tight carriers with distinct complementary singletons.

Step 2 (the witness misses every complementary singleton). By hypothesis v lies outside X union {L,R}. Since x_S is in X, v is distinct from x_S, L and R. Also v is not in V(S), which is contained in X. Hence W={v} is disjoint from V(S) union {x_S,L,R}, and every hypothesis of R686 holds with k=3 and |W|=1.

Step 3 (unconditional capture). Clause (ii) of R686 applies: at least one of the three forced crossings avoids v. Applying accepted R527 with that carrier, the signed support S, the exact witness v, the cover T, and the avoiding crossing gives the capture/refund branch, with the corresponding complementary singleton designated as the captured signed anchor. Since S has order two and H is a hypothetical smallest counterexample, R527 invokes the aligned dimer payment of accepted R526, yielding either a spanning two-cover or a certificate-retaining descendant with singleton support.

Step 4 (case CAP-E). Suppose some endpoint crossing {e,y_e} with e in {L,R} has y_e not equal to v. Then Step 3 applies with that carrier and e may be designated as the captured signed anchor by orienting the marker accordingly. This coincides with the CAP output of pending R682.

Step 5 (case CAP-X). Otherwise both endpoint crossings meet v, so their physical supports are {L,v} and {R,v}. These are two distinct selected states of T incident with v. The vertex v lies in H-V(S) and therefore occupies exactly one position on exactly one rail, so these two states are its two rail adjacencies and v is internal on that rail with consecutive order (L,v,R) or (R,v,L). Since a T rail is a tight path, this segment is a graph-intrinsic tight trimer; this is the XET conclusion of pending R682. Now consider the third forced crossing {x_S,y_x} supplied by Step 1 and R508. If y_x were equal to v, then {x_S,v} would be a third rail adjacency at v, contradicting the previous sentence because x_S is distinct from L and R. Hence y_x is not v, the crossing at x_S avoids v, and Step 3 applies with the carrier whose complementary singleton is x_S. This gives a capture anchored at x_S in the same cover T, with v retained as the exact witness, coexisting with the literal trimer order.

Step 6 (conclusion). Steps 4 and 5 exhaust the cases, so capture is unconditional and the cross-end trimer never occurs without an accompanying X-anchored capture in the same frame. The conclusions of pending R682 are Step 4 together with the trimer half of Step 5, so the present statement subsumes R682. All inputs used are accepted: R621 for the frame, R649 for the three carriers, R508 inside R686 for the forced crossings, R527 for capture, R526 for payment, and R686 for the counting.

# R688 — The R682 cross-end alternative is witness-exclusive: a second admissible witness forces endpoint capture

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Retain the setting of pending R682: the accepted crossed R621/R649 frame with X={a,b,c,z}, endpoints L=q_0 and R=q_m, an oriented middle-gate dimer S among (a,c),(c,a),(b,z),(z,b), its two R649 short carriers K_L with V(K_L)=V(S) union {L} and K_R with V(K_R)=V(S) union {R}, and an admissible witness, meaning a vertex outside X union {L,R} that is a sign witness on the tested orientation with the polarity R682 requires. Let T be any exact two-cover of H-V(S).

(1) Exclusivity. The XET branch holds for at most one vertex. Since V(S) is deleted from H-V(S), every selected state of T incident with an endpoint e in {L,R} automatically has its other endpoint outside K_e = V(S) union {e}. Hence the R682 CAP condition for a witness v fails exactly when every selected state of T at L and every selected state of T at R has other endpoint v. So XET(v) says precisely: the only selected states at L and at R are to v. In particular XET(v) and XET(v_prime) cannot both hold for v != v_prime in the same T.

(2) Two-witness capture. Let v_1 != v_2 both be admissible R682 witnesses on the same deleted pair V(S), each for some orientation of that pair. Both orientations of a middle-gate dimer delete the same two vertices, so the two R682 dichotomies quantify over the same set of exact covers T. Then every exact two-cover T of H-V(S) lies in the CAP branch for at least one of v_1,v_2. Indeed, if T were XET for v_1, then T selects the state {L,v_1}, whose other endpoint v_1 lies outside K_L and differs from v_2; that is exactly the CAP condition for v_2 at e=L, and symmetrically {R,v_1} gives CAP for v_2 at e=R. Consequently the R527 capture and R526 payment continuation supplied by R682 apply unconditionally, retaining a named physical endpoint, a named inward witness, the tested dimer, and an actual selected crossing as source ancestry.

(3) Sharp form. The cross-end alternative is therefore not an independent geometry that must be separately consumed; it is a uniqueness condition on T. With pending R684 it is equivalent to deg_T(L)=deg_T(R)=1 with common neighbour v and T=(L,v,R) sqcup P. Any second admissible decoration of the same deleted pair, of either orientation and either polarity, refutes it. The economical way to close the XET branch is therefore to multiply witnesses on a fixed deleted pair rather than to build a consumer for the cross-end trimer.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in the accepted crossed R621 frame. Use pending R682 with its accepted inputs R649,R508,R527,R526. Both witnesses lie outside X union {L,R} and satisfy the R682 polarity hypothesis for some orientation of the same deleted middle-gate pair. Pending R684 is used only for the equivalent restatement in part (3).

## Scope
Noncircular R24 consumer sharpening. Single-cover argument about one deleted middle-gate pair; no new geometry. Depends on pending R682. No R5,R168,R169,R224,R533, generic R358, or R436.

## Applicability
Whenever a frame supplies two distinct exterior witnesses on the same deleted middle-gate pair, stop analysing XET and take the capture. Conversely, when only one witness is available, XET is the exact obstruction, and the cheapest repair is to produce a second witness on that same deleted pair rather than to consume the cross-end trimer.

## Persistence
Retain the deleted pair V(S), both orientations used, both admissible witnesses v_1,v_2, the exact cover T, the physical endpoint e realizing CAP, the actual selected crossing {e,v_j}, and the R527/R526 continuation ancestry.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert that a second admissible witness exists in any particular frame; that must be supplied separately. Does not assert that a captured or paid descendant closes H, that CAP events at L and at R coexist as paid representatives, or that both witnesses can be spent simultaneously. Inherits the R682 exclusion of witnesses lying in X union {L,R}. Depends on pending R682 and cannot be canonized before it.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Witness-exclusive endpoint-capture leaf with no consumers; capture production is non-scarce.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** PASS. Once S is deleted, every T-adjacency at L or R is automatically exterior to the corresponding R649 endpoint carrier. Thus R682-XET(v) is exactly the condition that every such adjacency uses v; R508 guarantees at least one at each endpoint, making the witness unique. For two admissible witnesses on the same deleted pair, an XET certificate for one is itself an avoiding endpoint crossing for the other orientation/support, so CAP follows. R684 lawfully supplies the exact-rail normal form.

## Proof
Write W=H-V(S) and let T be an exact two-cover of W.

Step 1. Normalize the CAP condition. R682 CAP for witness v asks for an endpoint e in {L,R} and a selected state {e,y} of T with y outside K_e=V(S) union {e} and y != v. Because V(S) has been deleted from W, no vertex of V(S) occurs in T at all, so any selected state {e,y} of T automatically has y outside K_e. The CAP condition for v is therefore equivalent to: some selected state of T at L or at R has other endpoint different from v.

Step 2. Exclusivity. R682 defines XET as the failure of CAP. By Step 1, XET(v) holds if and only if every selected state of T at L and every selected state at R has other endpoint exactly v. This determines v from T whenever any selected state at L or R exists, and R682 guarantees at least one such state at each of L and R by applying R508 to the two R649 carriers K_L and K_R in the same cover T. Hence XET(v) and XET(v_prime) with v != v_prime are incompatible in one T, which is claim (1).

Step 3. Two-witness capture. Let v_1 != v_2 be admissible witnesses on the same deleted pair V(S), for orientations S_1 and S_2 of that pair. Since V(S_1)=V(S_2)=V(S), both R682 dichotomies are statements about the same exact covers T of W. Fix T. If CAP holds for v_1 we are done. Otherwise XET(v_1) holds, so by Step 2 T selects {L,v_1} and {R,v_1}. The state {L,v_1} has other endpoint v_1, which lies outside K_L by Step 1 and satisfies v_1 != v_2. By Step 1 again this is exactly the CAP condition for v_2 at e=L. Hence CAP holds for v_2, proving (2). The R527 orientation and R526 payment continuation are then those already supplied by R682 for the witness whose CAP branch was realized, with the actual selected crossing {L,v_1} as the retained source crossing.

Step 4. Sharp form. Step 2 says XET(v) forces every selected state at L and at R to go to v, so L and R have T-degree one with common neighbour v; pending R684 records the resulting normal form T=(L,v,R) sqcup P. Thus XET is a uniqueness condition on T rather than an independent configuration, and is destroyed by any second admissible witness on the same deleted pair. This is (3).

The argument uses only the statement of R682, the fact that the two orientations of a middle-gate dimer delete the same pair, and elementary bookkeeping; it introduces no new geometry, no payment theory, and no order bound.

# R690 — The XET cross-end rail self-generates a two-witness endpoint packet

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Retain the accepted crossed R621/R649 frame with X={a,b,c,z}, physical endpoints L=q_0 and R=q_m, and let S be one oriented crossed middle-gate dimer among (a,c),(c,a),(b,z),(z,b). Let v lie outside X union {L,R}, and suppose the R684 XET normal form holds in an exact two-cover of H-V(S): one entire rail is K=(L,v,R) or K=(R,v,L), and the other rail P is Hamiltonian on the complementary vertex set. Then K itself is an R542-ready short carrier at one physical endpoint. More precisely: if V(S)={a,c} and K=(L,v,R), the reverse terminal dimer (R,v) is head-signed by both a and c; if K=(R,v,L), the reverse terminal dimer (L,v) is head-signed by both a and c. If V(S)={b,z} and K=(L,v,R), the reverse initial dimer (v,L) is tail-signed by both b and z; if K=(R,v,L), the reverse initial dimer (v,R) is tail-signed by both b and z. Hence accepted R542 applies to K in every XET case, with complementary singleton equal to the opposite physical endpoint. It yields an actual endpoint capture/refund packet. Since that endpoint has the genuine old carrier adjacency {e,v} inside K, accepted R312 gives a protected endpoint-contact continuation: either an earlier event touching e is already exposed, or the lawful old-carrier mirror reentry using {e,v} is itself first contact at e. In the inward-anchor applications v in {q_2,q_{m-2}} with m>=6, the retained carrier adjacency {e,v} is a strict Q-skipping chord rather than an original consecutive Q edge.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in the accepted crossed R621 frame. R684 supplies the exact XET deletion-cover normal form for an oriented middle-gate dimer S and exterior witness v. Use accepted R3, R621/R649 crossed gates, R542, and R312.

## Scope
Noncircular R24 consumer of the R684 XET branch. Converts the exact cross-end deletion rail into a new two-witness short-carrier endpoint packet and protected endpoint-contact probe. No R5,R168,R169,R224,R533,generic R358, or generic R436.

## Applicability
Whenever R682/R684 produces XET, do not treat L-v-R as merely extra trimer geometry. Read its orientation, use the crossed gates on the original deleted middle-gate pair to force the indicated two witness turns on the endpoint-v boundary dimer, invoke R542 on the cross-end rail itself, and then R312 through its genuine endpoint-v carrier adjacency. For v=q_2 or q_{m-2}, retain explicitly that endpoint-v is a Q-skipping chord.

## Persistence
Retain the deleted pair V(S), exact XET cover, oriented entire cross-end rail K, complementary Hamilton rail P, the two crossed-gate witness turns forced on the endpoint-v boundary dimer, the resulting R542 carrier packet, the actual selected capture crossing, captured physical endpoint e, and the old carrier adjacency {e,v} used for R312. In inward-anchor applications retain v=q_2 or q_{m-2} and its nonconsecutive Q relation to e.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not consume the CAP-E branch when XET does not occur. Does not assert the R312 earlier-contact alternative itself uses the endpoint-v chord; the chord is consumed explicitly in the mirror-reentry/first-contact alternative. Does not assert first contact alone closes H. Does not apply to a witness v lying in X union {L,R}. Does not address Reverse-Ear or sigma>0 branches.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Accepted XET endpoint-packet conversion is mathematically sound but has no downstream consumers and terminates only in generic R542/R312 protected-contact currency. Retain R684 XET geometry and generic capture/contact parents; archive this route-specific conversion.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** PASS. The four XET orientations are exhaustive. In each, badness of either required endpoint-v witness turn reverses by R3 and concatenates with the entire cross-end rail from R684 and the corresponding accepted crossed-gate turn from R621/R649 to form a tight P5 on V(S) union {L,v,R}; together with the complementary Hamilton rail this would be a forbidden spanning two-cover. Hence the indicated reverse boundary dimer has two distinct same-polarity witnesses outside K, exactly satisfying R542. Its complementary singleton is the stated physical endpoint e, and the retained trimer gives the genuine adjacency {e,v} required by R312. For v=q_2 or q_{m-2}, m>=6, {e,v} is nonconsecutive on Q. Scope and exclusions accurately delimit the conclusion.

## Proof
Let the R684 XET cover be T=K sqcup P, where P is Hamiltonian on V(H)\(V(S) union {L,v,R}). Because H is a hypothetical counterexample, there is no tight Hamilton P5 on the five-set V(S) union {L,v,R}: such a P5 together with P would be a spanning two-cover. We now use this single observation in four literal cases.

Case 1: V(S)={a,c} and K=(L,v,R). Accepted R649 contains the crossed-gate turns (R,a,c) and (R,c,a). If (a,R,v) were bad, R3 would make (v,R,a) tight, and then (L,v,R,a,c) would be a tight P5, using the turns (L,v,R), (v,R,a), (R,a,c), contradiction. Thus (a,R,v) is tight. Likewise, if (c,R,v) were bad, then (v,R,c) would be tight and (L,v,R,c,a) would be a tight P5 because (R,c,a) is tight. Hence both a and c head-sign the tested dimer (R,v). Since (R,v) is the reverse terminal boundary dimer of the tight trimer K=(L,v,R), K is an R542 short carrier with complementary singleton L.

Case 2: V(S)={a,c} and K=(R,v,L). Use the crossed-gate turns (L,a,c) and (L,c,a). Badness of (a,L,v) would force (v,L,a), making (R,v,L,a,c) a tight P5; badness of (c,L,v) would force (v,L,c), making (R,v,L,c,a) a tight P5. Therefore (L,v) is head-signed by both a,c. It is the reverse terminal boundary dimer of K, so R542 applies with complementary singleton R.

Case 3: V(S)={b,z} and K=(L,v,R). Accepted R649 contains (z,b,L) and (b,z,L). If (v,L,b) were bad, R3 would make (b,L,v) tight, and (z,b,L,v,R) would be a tight P5 using (z,b,L), (b,L,v), (L,v,R). Thus (v,L,b) is tight. If (v,L,z) were bad, R3 would make (z,L,v) tight, and (b,z,L,v,R) would be a tight P5 using (b,z,L). Hence the tested dimer (v,L) is tail-signed by both b,z. It is the reverse initial boundary dimer of K, so R542 applies with complementary singleton R.

Case 4: V(S)={b,z} and K=(R,v,L). Use the crossed-gate turns (z,b,R) and (b,z,R). Badness of (v,R,b) would force (b,R,v), giving the tight P5 (z,b,R,v,L); badness of (v,R,z) would force (z,R,v), giving the tight P5 (b,z,R,v,L). Thus (v,R) is tail-signed by both b,z, and R542 applies to K with complementary singleton L.

In every case R542 therefore yields, from an exact cover after deleting the displayed boundary dimer of K, an actual capture/refund packet at the complementary physical endpoint e. The tight trimer K is the retained historical carrier and e has genuine carrier adjacency {e,v}. Accepted R312 applies to this exact historical capture packet and old adjacency: along a chosen protected continuation, either an earlier event touching e has already appeared or the lawful mirror reentry through {e,v} is itself first contact at e. Finally, if v=q_2 or q_{m-2} and m>=6, then e is q_0 or q_m and {e,v} is not a consecutive edge of the original path Q. This records the desired strict Q-skipping carrier coordinate in the first-contact branch.

Then v itself has a valid historical capture certificate through a literal old-Q selected state in an exact H-V(S) two-cover. If v=q_{m-2}, choose the dual exact return containing Q[0,m-2] or Q[0,m-1]; D={q_{m-3},q_{m-2}} is selected and is a carrier/exterior crossing for K. R649 supplies a same-polarity endpoint witness outside K that avoids D (take R for v=q_2 and L for v=q_{m-2}). Hence accepted R527 applies and, by orienting the marker appropriately, designates v itself as the captured signed anchor. Since v has the genuine historical carrier adjacency to its neighboring S-vertex inside K, accepted R312 yields a chosen protected continuation on which either an earlier event touching v is exposed or the lawful old-carrier mirror reentry through that X-Q adjacency is itself first contact at v. Thus every same-polarity middle-gate R542 branch created by an inward anchor exchange already forces a protected contact at the strict interior Q coordinate q_2 or q_{m-2}; it need not be spent as anonymous X-dimer payment.

H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in the accepted crossed R621 frame; m>=6. S is one tested orientation of G_3={a,c} or G_4={b,z}. Noncircular R24 consumer of same-polarity X-dimer anchor-exchange branches in the accepted sigma=0 A-F portfolio. It creates strict physical Q-interior capture/contact without R5,R168,R169,R224,R533,generic R358,R436, or generic pair payment.

Does not consume opposite-polarity anchor-exchange branches, which are labelled Hamilton P4s. Does not consume same-polarity packets whose new witness is not q_2 or q_{m-2}. - **Lifecycle:** retired

Write d=q_{m-2} and r=q_{m-3}. We treat four source combinations; tested orientation inside each middle gate is arbitrary and is carried literally by the input trimer.

LEFT ANCHOR v=q_2, S=G_4={b,z}. R621 gives the deep exact singleton-deletion covers H-b=(q_1,L,c,a,z) sqcup Q[2,m] and H-z=(q_1,L,a,c,b) sqcup Q[2,m]. Either is a literal two-cover of H-{b,z}; it is exact, because if H-{b,z} were Hamiltonian then its Hamilton path together with the tight dimer on {b,z} would two-cover H. Choose either return. The input same-polarity G_4 branch is a tail certificate, so in its exact tested order K=(S,q_2) is a tight trimer on V(S) union {q_2}. LEFT ANCHOR v=q_2, S=G_3={a,c}. Use the R621 shallow covers H-c=(a,b,z,L) sqcup Q[1,m] and H-a=(c,z,b,L) sqcup Q[1,m]. RIGHT ANCHOR v=d=q_{m-2}, S=G_3={a,c}. Use the R621 deep covers H-a=Q[0,d] sqcup (c,z,b,R,q_{m-1}) and H-c=Q[0,d] sqcup (a,b,z,R,q_{m-1}). The same-polarity G_3 input is a head trimer K=(d,S). The long rail contains selected D={r,d}. Take L as the fixed same-head R649 witness; L lies outside K and avoids D. The Q rail contains D={r,d}. Take L as the fixed same-tail R649 witness. R527 captures d and R312 gives the protected contact alternative through the genuine d-S carrier adjacency.

All four cases use a selected old-Q state already present in a literal exact deletion return, but the captured anchor is the strict inward vertex q_2 or q_{m-2}, and the historical carrier adjacency used by R312 joins that inward Q vertex to the middle-gate X dimer. # R699 — The two crossed middle-gate deletions force mate geometry or an explicit opposite-sign X-anchored pair

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Retain the accepted crossed R621/R649 frame with X={a,b,c,z} and physical Q endpoints L=q_0,R=q_m. Choose arbitrarily one exact two-cover T_ac of H-{a,c} and one exact two-cover T_bz of H-{b,z}. Then at least one of the following holds. (MATE) In T_ac or T_bz, one of the two X-complementary R649 packets lies in the R696 END branch, and therefore supplies a literal spanning two-path proposal with one or two holes, together with the corresponding forced reverse turn or physical two-hole mate clause. (PAIR) Otherwise there exist e in {b,z} and f in {a,c} such that an R649 packet on {a,c} has an R696 FREE crossing {e,x} in T_ac avoiding both L,R, while an R649 packet on {b,z} has an R696 FREE crossing {f,y} in T_bz avoiding both L,R. Use L as the exact witness on the head-signed {a,c}-side packet and R as the exact witness on the tail-signed {b,z}-side packet. Same-frame R527/R526 actualization gives a graph-intrinsic tail-signed dimer P_e containing e and a graph-intrinsic head-signed dimer P_f containing f. More precisely V(P_e) is either {e,x} or {e,L}, and V(P_f) is either {f,y} or {f,R}. These two opposite-polarity supports cannot meet in both vertices and cannot contain each other's X anchor. They are therefore either disjoint or meet in exactly one hinge. In the disjoint case accepted R39 gives a direct mass-four balanced pair and, in the hypothetical-smallest-counterexample setting, a finite continuation to a spanning two-cover or an ancestry-bearing mass-two floor. In the hinged case accepted R547 collapses them directly to the two-singleton floor on {e,f}. Thus the pair of physical crossed middle-gate deletions cannot have only anonymous R542 payment residue: before payment it exposes either a concrete mate proposal or an explicit opposite-sign dimer pair rooted at one X vertex from each complementary middle gate.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in the accepted crossed R621/R649 frame. T_ac and T_bz are arbitrary exact two-covers of H-{a,c} and H-{b,z}. Use pending R698, accepted R527/R526 actualization, accepted R39, and accepted R547.

## Scope
Noncircular crossed-frame synthesis of the two physical middle-gate deletion covers. No five-cell classification, Reverse Ear, R5, R168, R169, R224, R533, generic R358, R436, or R450 is used. The result is source-local: its pair branch retains the two exact deletion covers, the two selected crossings, the chosen opposite endpoint witnesses L and R, and the two X anchors e,f.

## Applicability
Take any exact cover after deleting {a,c} and any exact cover after deleting {b,z}. Run the paired-orientation R698 test in each. If an END branch appears, keep its one/two-hole proposal. If neither deletion has END, choose the guaranteed FREE packet on each side, actualize the {a,c}-side with witness L and the {b,z}-side with witness R, and obtain opposite-signed X-anchored dimers that are automatically disjoint or singly hinged.

## Persistence
Durable cross-gate consumer of R696/R698. It converts two independent R649 source packets into physical mate geometry or an explicit opposite-polarity pair without using the fenced generic endpoint-rooted compilation.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert that the disjoint R39 floor preserves both X anchors as current singleton coordinates; only ancestry is retained there. Does not assert which e or f is selected. Does not assert the two exact deletion covers are the same cover. Does not use or require Chalkboard strategy.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Route-local middle-gate deletion -> mate or opposite-sign pair leaf with no consumers; bare pair currency is non-scarce and stronger physical fixed-cover parents now exist.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** PASS as a structural theorem. In the no-END branch, the two FREE actualizations have opposite polarity. The ac-side support is {e,x} or {e,L}, the bz-side support {f,y} or {f,R}; deletion identities give x!=f and y!=e, FREE gives x,y outside {L,R}, so the supports are disjoint except possibly a single marker-marker hinge x=y. R39 or R547 then applies exactly. Strategically, the resulting floor is not by itself credited as R24 progress.

## Proof
Fix arbitrary exact covers T_ac of H-{a,c} and T_bz of H-{b,z}. Pending R698, which couples the two R649 orientations on a common deletion cover, says that T_ac has a non-sandwich X-complementary packet at some e in {b,z}, and T_bz has a non-sandwich X-complementary packet at some f in {a,c}; each such packet is END or FREE. If either is END, R696 supplies exactly the MATE conclusion, so assume both are FREE. Let D_e={e,x} be the FREE selected state in T_ac. By definition x is outside the R649 carrier and x notin {L,R}; because T_ac omits a,c and f belongs to {a,c}, also x!=f. Accepted R649 proves that whichever tested orientation of {a,c} produced e is head-signed by both L and R. Apply R527 to S_e with exact witness L and selected crossing D_e, orienting the marker to designate e. The R527 proof invokes R526. Since the marker has order two and the source is head-signed, the resulting opposite support is a tail-signed dimer P_e: if the terminal marker test is tight it is the marker dimer on {e,x}, while if the test is bad it is the short support on {e,L}. Thus V(P_e) is {e,x} or {e,L}. Similarly let D_f={f,y} be the FREE selected state in T_bz. Here y avoids L,R, and because T_bz omits b,z while e belongs to {b,z}, y!=e. R649 proves that whichever tested orientation of {b,z} produced f is tail-signed by both L and R. Apply R527 with exact witness R, capturing f. The head/tail-dual R526 actualization yields a head-signed dimer P_f whose support is either {f,y} or {f,R}. Hence P_e and P_f have opposite polarity and distinct anchors e!=f. The second vertex of P_e is x or L, neither equal to f. The second vertex of P_f is y or R, neither equal to e. Moreover x,y avoid L,R and L!=R. Therefore the only possible intersection between V(P_e) and V(P_f) is the equality x=y in the marker-marker outcome; otherwise the supports are disjoint. If disjoint, their total support size is four and R39 gives a direct balanced pair, with the accepted smallest-counterexample continuation to closure or an ancestry-bearing mass-two floor. If x=y and both actualizations use their marker supports, the dimers meet in exactly the single hinge x and R547 yields opposite-sign singleton supports on the nonhinge vertices e and f, i.e. the floor {e,f}. This proves PAIR and the theorem.

Write the signed support witness as alpha and the marker rail as R=(r_0,...,r_s), s>=1, in the polarity convention of the old R70 frame. Accepted reconstructible R526 gives the complete actualization test. At the relevant marker end, test the terminal turn against alpha. If the test is bad, boundary antisymmetry supplies the reverse terminal turn and R526 actualizes the short opposite support exactly as (alpha,r_s) in the head-signed convention; the head/tail dual gives the corresponding initial-end formula. Let {e,q_i} be the selected inward state from R702. First D={a,c}. R649 fixes head polarity on either tested orientation of D, with both L and R as valid same-polarity witnesses for the X-complementary packet containing e. The state {e,q_i} avoids L. By the explicit head-signed R526 actualization used inside R527, either the terminal test (e,q_i,L) is tight, or it is bad and boundary antisymmetry gives (L,q_i,e) tight. # R715 — The two first-inward Q vertices Hamilton-couple through every X-root

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Retain the accepted R594 synchronized transitive frame with transitive P4-free four-cell X and Q=(q_0,...,q_m), m>=4. Put u=q_1 and s=q_{m-1}. Then for every x in X the five-set E_x={u,s} union (X\{x}) supports a tight Hamilton P5. Indeed the six-set E=X union {u,s} has six five-subsets. The two five-subsets E\{s}=X union {u} and E\{u}=X union {s} are non-Hamiltonian: a P5 on X union {u} together with the disjoint tight suffix Q[2,m] would two-cover H, and a P5 on X union {s} together with Q[0,m-2] would do the same. Accepted R195 says every six-set has at least four Hamilton five-subsets. Since two of the six are known non-Hamiltonian, all four remaining five-subsets must be Hamiltonian. Those four are exactly E_x for x in X. Thus every X-root admits a graph-intrinsic Hamilton P5 coupling the first inward vertices from the two ends of Q.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in accepted R594; Q=(q_0,...,q_m), m>=4; accepted R195.

## Scope
Noncircular R24 nonlocal bridge theorem. Uses both ends simultaneously and no crossed-middle-gate classification. No R5,R168,R169,R224,R533,capture,payment,generic R358,or R436.

## Applicability
Use whenever a one-sided route is fenced by R613/R626. The five-sets {q_1,q_{m-1}} union (X-{x}) carry opposite-end Hamilton P5s for every root x. Bare support Hamiltonicity is not closure; preserve an actual Hamilton order and especially endpoint roles of q_1,q_{m-1}. Combine with R582 or source-specific substitution rather than treating this as anonymous path-growth currency.

## Persistence
Retain the six-set X union {q_1,q_{m-1}}, the two certified non-Hamiltonian five-subsets X+q_1 and X+q_{m-1}, and for each x in X at least one Hamilton P5 order on {q_1,q_{m-1}} union (X-{x}). Orders need not coexist in one chosen representation but their support Hamiltonicity is graph-intrinsic.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not prescribe Hamilton orders, endpoint positions of q_1 or q_{m-1}, or simultaneous compatibility of the four P5 orders. Does not itself yield a spanning two-cover or a current exact-cover cut. Does not assert the four P5s are distinct as ordered paths.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** R715 gives bare two-ended Hamilton-P5 support with no endpoint-order consumer. R829 fences support/path abundance as progress; preserve historically.
- **Curation note:** Two-ended support theorem: every X-root couples q1 and q_{m-1} in a Hamilton P5 support; retain endpoint roles and do not confuse support abundance with closure.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Elegant two-ended support theorem: R195 plus the two forbidden one-sided five-sets forces all four {q1,q_{m-1}} plus three-X five-sets Hamiltonian. Retain as support geometry only; R829 forbids treating path abundance as closure.

## Proof
Put u=q_1 and s=q_{m-1}. If X+u had a Hamilton P5 P, then P and Q[2,m] would be vertex-disjoint tight paths whose supports partition V(H), contradicting pc(H)>2. Thus X+u is non-Hamiltonian. Dually X+s is non-Hamiltonian because a P5 there together with Q[0,m-2] would two-cover H. Now apply accepted R195 to the six-set X union {u,s}. At least four of its six five-subsets are Hamiltonian. Two specific five-subsets, X+u and X+s, are not. Therefore the other four must all be Hamiltonian. They are exactly {u,s} union (X-{x}) for x in X.

# R720 — Crossed middle-gate END clauses are selected-state reversals or labelled P4s

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Retain the accepted crossed R621/R649 frame with X={a,b,c,z}, endpoints L=q_0,R=q_m, and let D be either crossed middle-gate pair {a,c} or {b,z}. Fix one of the two R649 X-complementary packets on D, with tested reverse-boundary dimer S, tight trimer carrier K, complementary singleton e in X\D, and fixed same-polarity endpoint witnesses {L,R}. Let T be any exact two-cover of H-D and suppose accepted R696 is in its END branch at e, so e has T-degree one. Then the END output already has one of two source-localized forms: (REV) T contains a selected directed state pq whose reverse qp is a graph-intrinsic tight state occurring in the forced END reverse trimer; equivalently the END certificate contains a literal reversal of a current T-state. (P4) The END certificate supplies an opposite-polarity sign on the same tested oriented dimer S, and combining it with either fixed R649 endpoint witness distinct from the new witness via accepted R523 gives a labelled tight Hamilton P4. Hence a crossed middle-gate END branch never needs to be retained as an anonymous one/two-hole mate clause: it compiles immediately to selected-state reversal geometry or a labelled P4.

More explicitly, for D={a,c}, the complementary singleton is the initial vertex of K and S is one of (a,c),(c,a), fixed head-signed by L,R. In the aligned one-hole END orientation, the unique forced reverse contains the reverse of the selected e-exterior state, giving REV. In the nonaligned two-hole orientation, the exact R511 specialization has reversals (k_1,c_s,c_{s-1}) when the pure exterior rail has a predecessor and (k_2,k_1,c_s), where S=(k_2,k_1). The first reverses the selected pure-rail state (c_{s-1},c_s), giving REV; the second is a tail certificate on the same tested S, opposite the fixed head polarity, so R523 gives P4 after choosing L or R distinct from c_s.

Dually, for D={b,z}, the complementary singleton is the terminal vertex of K and S is one of (b,z),(z,b), fixed tail-signed by L,R. The aligned one-hole END orientation again forces the reverse of the unique selected e-exterior state. In the nonaligned two-hole orientation, the reverse-dual R511 holes give either the reverse of a selected boundary state of the pure exterior rail or a head certificate (c_0,S) on the same tested S. The latter is opposite the fixed tail polarity and therefore gives a labelled P4 by R523. These cases exhaust END.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in the accepted crossed R621/R649 frame. D is {a,c} or {b,z}; T is an exact two-cover of H-D; one X-complementary R649 packet is in the accepted R696 END branch. Use the exact trimer endpoint specialization of accepted R511 and accepted same-support sign interaction R523.

## Scope
Noncircular crossed-frame consumer of the accepted R696 END branch. No five-cell classification, R5,R168,R169,R224,R533,generic R358, capture/payment descent, R436, or R450. The outputs are physical current-state reversal geometry or a graph-intrinsic labelled P4.

## Applicability
Whenever R696 returns END on a crossed middle-gate R649 packet, do not preserve the generic mate clause as terminal currency. Read the exact one/two-hole R511 specialization. The one-hole case and one branch of the two-hole case literally reverse a selected T-state. The other two-hole branch is opposite polarity on the same tested middle-gate dimer and therefore yields a labelled P4 by R523 using the opposite endpoint witness.

## Persistence
Retain D,T,S,K,e, the literal END rail orientation and exact R511 proposal/hole set. In REV retain the selected T-state pq and the exact tight reverse state qp inside its forced reverse trimer. In P4 retain the exact opposite-polarity certificate on S, the chosen distinct endpoint witness from {L,R}, and the resulting ordered Hamilton P4 from R523.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not claim a selected-state reversal or labelled P4 alone closes H. Does not consume unrelated Reverse-Ear geometry or sigma>0 fragmentation. Does not compare certificates tested on opposite orientations of the same physical dimer; all R523 uses retain the exact R649 tested order.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** superseded
- **Lifecycle note:** Crossed middle-gate END consumer is subsumed by the stronger order-free two-witness short-carrier END theorem C633/R785.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** PASS. END is fully consumed into a reversal of an actual selected T-state or an opposite-polarity same-tested-dimer P4. Tested order and witness distinctness are preserved; no forbidden R24 dependencies are used.

## Proof
Fix the packet. First take D={a,c}. By R649 the two X-complementary carriers have the form K=(e,k_1,k_2) with e in {b,z}, and the tested reverse terminal dimer S=(k_2,k_1) is head-signed by both L and R. In END, e has degree one in T. If e is the terminal vertex of its mixed T-rail, the aligned endpoint case of R511/R509 has one hole; the forced reverse trimer contains the reversed physical state e c_s of the selected state c_s e. This is REV. Otherwise e begins the mixed rail. Write the other pure exterior rail C'=(c_0,...,c_s). The exact m=2,i=0 R511 formula gives the complete hole set {(c_{s-1},c_s,k_1) if s>=1} union {(c_s,k_1,k_2)}. At least one hole is bad. If the first is bad, R3 gives (k_1,c_s,c_{s-1}) tight, whose terminal state c_s c_{s-1} reverses the selected T-state c_{s-1} c_s: REV. If the second is bad, R3 gives (k_2,k_1,c_s) tight. Since S=(k_2,k_1), this is a tail certificate on the exact tested S. R649 supplies head certificates (L,k_2,k_1) and (R,k_2,k_1). The witness c_s lies outside K and can equal at most one of L,R, so choose h in {L,R} distinct from c_s. R523 on tested S with head witness h and tail witness c_s gives the literal P4 (h,k_2,k_1,c_s).

Now take D={b,z}. The two X-complementary carriers have the dual form K=(k_0,k_1,e), with tested reverse initial dimer S=(k_1,k_0) tail-signed by both L,R. If e begins its mixed rail, the aligned endpoint case has one hole and its forced reverse contains the reverse of the selected e-exterior state, giving REV. Otherwise e terminates the mixed rail. The exact CS,j=m reverse-dual of R511 has complete holes whose reversals are: one selected-boundary-state reversal on the pure exterior rail, or a turn (c_0,k_1,k_0)=(c_0,S). The first gives REV. The second is a head certificate on the exact tested S, opposite its fixed tail polarity. Choose h in {L,R} distinct from c_0; R523 applied to the head witness c_0 and tail witness h gives the labelled P4 (c_0,k_1,k_0,h). Thus every END case is REV or P4.

# R722 — A cross-end trimer amplifies to a labelled P4 or dual protected endpoint contacts

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Retain the accepted synchronized R594 frame with Q=(q_0,...,q_m), m>=4, write L=q_0,R=q_m, and let x be any vertex of X for which the graph-intrinsic cross-end trimer K=(R,x,L) is tight. Choose any two distinct probes y_1,y_2 in X\{x}. Then at least one of the following holds. (P4) For some i in {1,2}, the four-set {R,x,L,y_i} supports a labelled tight Hamilton P4. (DUAL-FC) Both physical endpoints are independently capture/contact-capable through the same cross-end carrier K. More precisely, D_L=(x,R) is tail-signed by both y_1,y_2 and D_R=(L,x) is head-signed by both y_1,y_2. In any exact two-cover of H-{x,R}, accepted R508 applied to K forces a selected crossing from complementary singleton L to the exterior; one of y_1,y_2 avoids that crossing, so accepted R527 may orient the crossing to capture L. Since K retains the genuine old carrier adjacency {L,x}, accepted R312 gives a protected first-contact continuation at L. Dually, in any exact two-cover of H-{L,x}, R508 forces a crossing from complementary singleton R; one probe avoids it, R527 captures R, and R312 through old carrier adjacency {R,x} gives protected first contact at R. The two source signed-dimer packets coexist graph-intrinsically; the later L- and R-contact continuations are separate choices.

Hence a cross-end trimer (R,x,L), including the CROSS output of pending R717, has a direct nonstationary consumer: labelled P4 or dual endpoint first-contact geometry. Generic Reverse-Ear replay is unnecessary.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in accepted R594; K=(R,x,L) is tight with x in X; y_1,y_2 are distinct vertices of X-{x}. Use accepted R700, R429, R508, R527, and R312.

## Scope
Noncircular direct consumer of a cross-end trimer. No crossed-middle-gate classification, R5,R168,R169,R224,R533,generic R358,generic R436, generic payment descent, or Reverse Ear is used. The theorem is upstream of pending R717 and applies to any graph-intrinsic tight K=(R,x,L).

## Applicability
Whenever a route produces (q_m,x,q_0), do not feed it only to R435. Probe K with two X vertices via accepted R700. A P4 branch is explicit. In the joint no-P4 branch, use the two reverse boundary dimers of K as two-witness packets; capture the complementary physical endpoint in the corresponding pair-deletion cover and immediately run R312 through the genuine cross-end carrier chord to x.

## Persistence
Retain K, x, chosen probes y_1,y_2, both R700 four-cell tests, and in DUAL-FC the exact tested dimers (x,R) and (L,x) with both witness identities. For each endpoint contact retain its pair-deletion cover, actual selected complementary-singleton crossing, chosen avoiding probe, R527 marker orientation/capture certificate, old K-adjacency {L,x} or {R,x}, and R312 protected-contact lineage. The two later continuations need not coexist.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert either protected first contact closes H or that the two endpoint continuations coexist. Does not claim the P4 branch is spanning. Does not use the stationary R435 seam output of pending R719. Does not assert existence of a cross-end trimer; it is a conditional consumer.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** R722 is a route-specific cross-end trimer/contact amplifier whose durable descendant is accepted toolkit R859.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** PASS. Direct noncircular consumer of any cross-end trimer: labelled P4 or independent protected first-contact probes at both physical Q endpoints. Generic Reverse Ear is unnecessary.

## Proof
Fix distinct y_1,y_2 in X-{x}. Apply accepted R700 to the tight trimer K=(a,b,c)=(R,x,L) with probes y_1,y_2. If either probe yields the R700 P4 branch, outcome P4 holds. Otherwise the DUAL-CP branch of R700 gives both reverse contacts for i=1,2: (x,R,y_i) and (y_i,L,x). Thus the tested reverse initial dimer D_L=(x,R) is tail-signed by y_1,y_2, while the tested reverse terminal dimer D_R=(L,x) is head-signed by y_1,y_2. These four turns are simultaneous graph-intrinsic facts.

For the left endpoint L, delete D_L={x,R}. Accepted R429 gives an exact two-cover T_L of H-{x,R}. In K the complementary carrier singleton is L, so accepted R508 applied with absorbable singleton {L} forces a selected carrier/exterior state C_L={L,z_L}. This two-vertex crossing contains at most one of the distinct probes y_1,y_2, so choose y_i avoiding C_L. The tested dimer D_L has the exact tail certificate (x,R,y_i). Accepted R527 therefore applies in the same deletion frame; choose the marker orientation designating L as the captured signed anchor. This gives a valid historical capture of L through C_L. The original carrier K is retained and contains the genuine adjacency E_L={x,L}. Hence the exact hypotheses of accepted R312 hold with A=K, crossing C_L, captured anchor L, and old adjacency E_L. Along a chosen protected continuation R312 exposes either earlier contact at L or lawful mirror reentry which is itself first contact at L.

For R, delete D_R={L,x}. R429 gives an exact two-cover T_R. The complementary singleton of the same carrier K is R; R508 forces a selected crossing C_R={R,z_R}. Choose one of y_1,y_2 avoiding C_R. Since D_R=(L,x) is head-signed by both probes, R527 captures R by orienting C_R accordingly. The retained carrier adjacency E_R={R,x} then feeds R312 and yields protected first contact at R. The source packets coexist because they are fixed signed facts of K and the probe tests; only the chosen pair-deletion representatives and later capture continuations are alternative. This proves DUAL-FC.

## Statement
Retain the accepted crossed R621 frame and pending R723, with X={a,b,c,z}, Q=(q_0,...,q_m), m>=4, L=q_0, u=q_1, v=q_2, d=q_{m-2}, s=q_{m-1}, R=q_m. Then the two sides admit exact one-hole first-step zipper dichotomies. LEFT: at least one of the following holds: (L-ADV) H-c has the literal exact two-cover (v,u,a,b,z,L) sqcup Q[3,m], or H-a has the literal exact two-cover (v,u,c,z,b,L) sqcup Q[3,m]; (L-SAT) both turns (b,a,u) and (z,c,u) are tight. In L-SAT the two top-matching reverse dimers are new two-witness R542-ready packets: (b,a) is tail-signed by distinct witnesses u,z and is a reverse boundary dimer of K=(a,b,c), while (z,c) is tail-signed by u,b and is a reverse boundary dimer of K=(c,z,a). RIGHT dually: at least one of (R-ADV) H-z=(R,a,c,b,s,d) sqcup Q[0,m-3] or H-b=(R,c,a,z,s,d) sqcup Q[0,m-3] is a literal exact two-cover; or (R-SAT) both (s,b,c) and (s,z,a) are tight. In R-SAT the two low-matching dimers are new two-witness R542-ready packets: (b,c) is head-signed by s,z with carrier K=(a,c,b), and (z,a) is head-signed by s,b with carrier K=(c,a,z). Thus failure of a cover-valued first inward root switch on a side forces an explicit new matching family of short-carrier packets rather than witness-only reminting.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in accepted crossed R621; pending R723 supplies (v,u,x) and (x,s,d) for every x in X. Use matching-height X turns, crossed gate turns from R621, boundary antisymmetry R3, and accepted R542 only for the packet typing.

## Scope
Noncircular first-step crossed zipper consumer. The advanced outputs are literal singleton-deletion exact covers moving the long-rail cut from q_2 to q_3 on the left or from q_{m-2} to q_{m-3} on the right. The saturation outputs live on the previously unused outer matchings M_R and M_L. No R5,R168,R169,R224,R533,five-cell classification,generic payment,R436,or computation is used.

## Applicability
Use after R723. On the left test only uab and ucz; on the right test only cbs and azs. A good test yields an advanced root cover immediately. If both tests on one side are bad, retain their exact reversals as the displayed R542-ready outer-matching packets.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** First-step zipper/root-switch production route is historical. Preserve durable descendants R736 fence and R819 order-ten self-renormalization, but do not expose the zipper root as a current interface.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** PASS. This is a genuine noncircular first-step zipper dichotomy: exact inward root switch or new outer-matching saturation on both sides. No prohibited R24-closing dependency is used.

## Proof
LEFT. Pending R723 gives (v,u,a) and (v,u,c) tight. The matching-height four-cell gives (a,b,z) and (c,z,b) tight, while the crossed left gate gives (b,z,L) and (z,b,L) tight. Hence P_c=(v,u,a,b,z,L) has every consecutive turn certified except h_c=(u,a,b): its turns are (v,u,a), h_c, (a,b,z), (b,z,L). If h_c is tight, P_c is a tight Hamilton P6 on {v,u,L} union (X-{c}); together with the untouched tight suffix Q[3,m] it is a literal two-cover of H-c, necessarily exact because a Hamilton H-c would two-cover H with singleton c. If h_c is bad, R3 gives (b,a,u) tight. The X turn (b,a,z) is also tight because M(ab)=M_R>M(az)=M_L. Thus tested dimer (b,a) is tail-signed by the distinct outside witnesses u,z. The tight trimer K=(a,b,c) has (b,a) as its reverse initial boundary dimer, and u,z lie outside K, so R542 applies. Similarly P_a=(v,u,c,z,b,L) has sole uncertified seam h_a=(u,c,z), because (v,u,c), (c,z,b), and (z,b,L) are tight. If h_a is tight it gives H-a=P_a sqcup Q[3,m]. If bad, R3 gives (z,c,u). Matching height gives (z,c,b) tight. The tight carrier K=(c,z,a) has reverse initial dimer (z,c), with witnesses u,b outside K, so this is the second L-SAT R542 packet. Therefore if neither L-ADV cover occurs, both L-SAT packets occur. RIGHT. R723 gives (b,s,d) and (z,s,d) tight. Crossed right gates give (R,a,c) and (R,c,a); matching height gives (a,c,b) and (c,a,z). Thus P_z=(R,a,c,b,s,d) has only h_z=(c,b,s) uncertified. If h_z is tight, P_z with Q[0,m-3] is an exact two-cover of H-z. If bad, R3 gives (s,b,c). Matching height gives (z,b,c), so (b,c) is head-signed by s,z; carrier K=(a,c,b) has reverse terminal dimer (b,c), and s,z lie outside K. Likewise P_b=(R,c,a,z,s,d) has sole seam h_b=(a,z,s). Tight h_b gives the advanced H-b cover. If bad, R3 gives (s,z,a); matching height gives (b,z,a), and carrier K=(c,a,z) has reverse terminal dimer (z,a), with outside head witnesses s,b. Hence failure of both right advanced covers gives exactly R-SAT. All displayed paths and witnesses are literal, and the only use of R542 is to identify the resulting two-witness packet type.
