# R726 — Every X-root in the synchronized transitive frame lies in a cross-end Hamilton P4

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Retain the accepted synchronized transitive R594 frame with X a matching-height P4-free four-cell and Q=(q_0,...,q_m), m>=4, endpoints L=q_0,R=q_m. Fix any x in X. Let r,s,l be its unique M_R-, M_S-, and M_L-neighbors in X. Then at least one of the two labelled four-sets {L,R,x,r} and {L,R,x,s} supports a tight Hamilton P4. In particular every x in X belongs to a Hamilton P4 that also contains both physical endpoints L and R. This conclusion holds before choosing the aligned/crossed middle-gate phase and uses no deletion-cover classification beyond the standing R594 endpoint P5-free cells.

Proof. By R3 exactly one of the complete-reversal pair (R,x,L),(L,x,R) is tight. CASE A: K=(R,x,L) is tight. Apply R518 to K with probes r and s. If either four-set is Hamiltonian, done. Assume both are P4-free. The r-probe gives (x,R,r) and (r,L,x). Matching height gives (s,l,r),(r,l,x),(l,s,x),(s,x,l). P5-freeness of X+L applied to (s,l,r,L,x) forces (L,r,l); then applied to (s,L,r,l,x) forces (r,L,s). P5-freeness of X+R applied to (l,s,x,R,r) forces (R,x,s). P4-freeness of {R,x,L,s} applied to (R,x,s,L) forces (L,s,x). Hence (r,L,s,x,l) is a forbidden Hamilton P5 of X+L.

CASE B: K=(L,x,R) is tight. Again probe by r and s and assume both four-sets P4-free. The r-probe no-P4 branch gives (x,L,r) and (r,R,x). Matching height gives the same four X turns. P5-freeness of X+R applied to (s,l,r,R,x) forces (R,r,l); then to (s,R,r,l,x) forces (r,R,s). P5-freeness of X+L applied to (l,s,x,L,r) forces (L,x,s). P4-freeness of {L,x,R,s} applied to (L,x,s,R) forces (R,s,x). Hence (r,R,s,x,l) is a forbidden Hamilton P5 of X+R. Thus one of the r- or s-probe four-sets is Hamiltonian in either orientation case.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in accepted R594. X is the transitive matching-height P4-free four-cell; L=q_0,R=q_m. Use accepted boundary antisymmetry R3 and four-cell amplifier R518. R594 supplies P5-freeness of X+L and X+R.

## Scope
Noncircular R24 structural theorem upstream of aligned/crossed classification. No R5,R168,R169,R224,R533,R358,payment,capture,R436,Reverse Ear,five-cell classification,or computation. It subsumes the orientation-specific pending R724 statement and renders the CROSS/no-CROSS split of pending R717 unnecessary for producing cross-end P4 support.

## Applicability
At the R594 synchronized transitive frame, immediately record for every x in X a Hamilton cross-end P4 support containing L,R,x and one of its M_R/M_S neighbors. Downstream work should preserve the root x and winning neighbor identity and seek a source-specific puncture/recompletion consumer of this cross-end P4 rather than entering middle-gate casework merely to obtain nonlocal endpoint geometry.

## Persistence
For each x retain its matching-neighbor labels r,s,l, the R3-selected cross-end trimer orientation, the two R518 probe tests, and the identity of the winning Hamilton four-set.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not specify the Hamilton order of the winning P4. Does not assert the four cross-end P4s for different roots have compatible/current orders in one representative. Does not by itself give a spanning two-cover. Does not say which of r or s wins for a fixed root.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** R726 gives cross-end Hamilton-P4 support but no live exact-cover consumer. R829 fences bare path-support abundance as progress; preserve historically.
- **Curation note:** Orientation-free cross-end parent: every X-root in the R594 frame lies in a Hamilton P4 containing both physical endpoints L,R.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Strong orientation-free parent: for every X-root in the R594 frame, whichever cross-end trimer orientation R3 selects, the matching-height/P5-free two-probe argument forces a Hamilton cross-end P4 support through L,R and that root. This subsumes the orientation-specific R724 statement.

## Proof
The matching-height identities used in both cases are (s,l,r), (r,l,x), (l,s,x), and (s,x,l), because the edge-height pairs are respectively M_R>M_S, M_S>M_L, M_R>M_S, and M_S>M_L.

Case A, (R,x,L) tight. Suppose both {R,x,L,r} and {R,x,L,s} are P4-free. R518 on probe r gives (x,R,r),(r,L,x). Candidate (s,l,r,L,x) in the P5-free cell X+L has first and last turns tight, so (l,r,L) is bad and R3 gives (L,r,l). Candidate (s,L,r,l,x) then has its last two turns tight, so (s,L,r) is bad and R3 gives (r,L,s). Candidate (l,s,x,R,r) in X+R has first and last turns tight, so (s,x,R) is bad and R3 gives (R,x,s). In the P4-free s-cell, candidate (R,x,s,L) now has first turn tight, hence (x,s,L) is bad and R3 gives (L,s,x). Finally (r,L,s,x,l) has turns (r,L,s),(L,s,x),(s,x,l) tight, contradicting P5-freeness of X+L.

Case B, (L,x,R) tight. Suppose both probe four-sets are P4-free. R518 on probe r gives (x,L,r),(r,R,x). Candidate (s,l,r,R,x) in X+R forces (R,r,l). Candidate (s,R,r,l,x) then forces (r,R,s). Candidate (l,s,x,L,r) in X+L forces (L,x,s). The P4-free s-cell candidate (L,x,s,R) forces (R,s,x). Finally (r,R,s,x,l) is a Hamilton P5 of X+R, contradiction.

R3 guarantees that exactly one of the two case orientations holds for each fixed x, completing the proof.

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement

- **Review note:** PASS. The saturation-to-P4 conclusion is correct. Before each R516 invocation, the written proof omits an explicit verification of the second same-polarity terminal sign, but it follows immediately from the assumed P4-free branch plus R3 and the displayed matching-height core: if that terminal sign were absent, its exact reversal concatenates with a known core turn to form a Hamilton P4. With that check supplied, the R516 signature is uniquely 11 on the left and 01 on the right, forcing exact reverse turns on {a,c,q1} or {a,c,q_{m-1}} and contradiction by R3.

## Proof
Write u=q_1 and s=q_{m-1}. LEFT. If L-ADV of R725 fails, L-SAT gives (b,a,u) and (z,c,u) tight. Suppose for contradiction that F_1={a,b,c,u} and F_2={c,z,a,u} are both Hamilton-P4-free. In the notation (A,B,C,y)=(a,b,c,u) of accepted R516, these are ABC, ACB, BAC, so among the four no-P4 signatures only signature 11 is compatible. The explicit signature-11 list in R516 contains C y A, hence (c,u,a) is tight. On F_2 use core trimer (c,z,a). The matching-height restriction to {c,z,a} likewise has (c,z,a),(c,a,z),(z,c,a) tight, again the ABC,ACB,BAC core and hence again signature 11 in coordinates (A,B,C,y)=(c,z,a,u). Signature 11 now contains C y A=(a,u,c). Thus both (c,u,a) and its exact reversal (a,u,c) would be tight, contradicting R3. Therefore F_1 or F_2 has a Hamilton P4. RIGHT. **Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Retain the crossed phase of accepted R619 in the normalization X={a,b,c,z}, left-enlarged roots {b,z}, right-enlarged roots {a,c}, and put L=q_0,u=q_1,R=q_m,s=q_{m-1}. Consider D={a,b} and W=H-D. Puncturing the left enlarged cover of H-b at a gives the literal three-cover S_L=(u,L,c) sqcup (z) sqcup Q[2,m] of W. Puncturing the right enlarged cover of H-a at b gives S_R=Q[0,m-2] sqcup (c,z) sqcup (R,s). Their common refinement is G_0={z}, G_1={c}, G_2={L,u}, G_3=Q[2,m-2], G_4={s,R}. Accepted pair-deletion rigidity R429 gives pc(W)=2, so choose any exact two-cover T of W. The R7 deficit identity on this five-cell partition gives t_G(T)>=3. The only distinct cell pairs lying in one component of either source three-cover are the four consecutive staircase pairs G_0G_1,G_1G_2,G_2G_3,G_3G_4. Therefore any selected T-state joining nonconsecutive cells crosses both S_L and S_R and accepted R176 gives a balanced opposite-sign pair birth retaining both source labels. If no such jump occurs, every intercell transition lies on a staircase adjacency. In the extremal case t_G(T)=3 each G_i is one contiguous T-block and the two T-rails are exactly two disjoint interval subpaths of the five-cell staircase, omitting one of its four adjacencies. Thus the full R620 staircase conclusion is available noncircularly with R429 replacing the old R5 existence step.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in the accepted crossed R619 phase, Q=(q_0,...,q_m), m>=4. Use accepted R619 source covers, accepted R429 pair-deletion rigidity, R7 deficit identity, and accepted R176. No R5,R168,R169,R224,R533 or generic R358 is used.

## Scope
Noncircular R24 restoration. Representative mixed pair D={a,b} in the crossed root-pair phase. This revision repairs the original R620 proof by replacing its unnecessary R5 call with accepted R429, whose dependency closure is R3/R4 only.

## Applicability
Use after the crossed phase whenever the outer matching pair {a,b} is the relevant mixed deletion. First inspect an exact H-{a,b} two-cover for a nonconsecutive staircase jump. Only the four t_G=3 interval-cut residues remain locally quiet. Unlike the previous revision, this route is admissible for independent R24 reconstruction.

## Persistence
Retain D={a,b}, both source three-covers S_L,S_R, ordered cells G_0,...,G_4, the exact pair-deletion cover T, every intercell transition and its source-cross labels, and in t_G=3 the unique omitted staircase adjacency.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not discharge the four interval-cut residues. Does not claim an R176 birth closes H. Does not assert the four outer matching deletions are literally identical without relabelling. The improvement is dependency repair, not a new closure of the staircase.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Historical mixed-root five-cell staircase with no live consumers; current five-cell interface is R862/R865/R866/R867/R870.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** PASS. R429 validly replaces the old R5 existence step. The punctured R619 covers refine to the stated five cells; exactly the four consecutive staircase pairs share a component in at least one source cover, so every nonconsecutive T-transition crosses both and is R176-eligible. R7 gives t_G=3+sigma. In the quiet t_G=3 case sigma=0 makes every Hamilton cell one contiguous T-block, and a two-component path forest on the five-cell path with three consecutive-only transitions is exactly the staircase with one adjacency omitted.

## Proof
The two punctured source three-covers and their common five-cell refinement are exactly as in accepted R620 and follow solely from accepted R619. The only circular ingredient in the preferred R620 proof was the sentence choosing an exact two-cover T of W via R5. Replace that sentence by accepted R429: for the physical pair {a,b}, pc(H-{a,b})=2, so an exact two-cover T exists and both rails are nontrivial. Now apply R7 to the five cells G_0,...,G_4, each of which has path-cover number one, obtaining t_G(T)=5-2+sigma=3+sigma>=3. Reading S_L and S_R in cell coordinates gives component pairs G_1G_2 and G_3G_4 for S_L together with singleton G_0, and G_2G_3 and G_0G_1 for S_R together with singleton G_4. Hence exactly the four consecutive staircase pairs share a source component; any nonconsecutive selected transition crosses both source decompositions and R176 applies. If all transitions are consecutive and t_G=3, then sigma=0, so each cell occurs as one contiguous block. Contracting cells yields a two-component path forest on the five-vertex staircase with three edges and no jump, necessarily two disjoint intervals omitting exactly one staircase adjacency. This proves the same conclusion as R620 with dependency set R429,R7,R176,R619 and no R5.

# R730 — First-step root advances are same-root state reversals with next-boundary shields

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Retain the accepted crossed R621 frame and accepted R723,R725. Put u=q_1, v=q_2, w=q_3 and d=q_{m-2}, s=q_{m-1}, rho=q_{m-3}. Every ADV output of R725 carries more than an anonymous deeper-cut cover.

LEFT. If L-ADV occurs with deleted root r in {a,c}, then the accepted R723 shallow cover of H-r contains Q[1,m] and hence selects the directed state (u,v), while the R725 advanced cover contains the short rail beginning (v,u,...) and hence selects the literal reverse state (v,u). Moreover both root turns (v,u,r) and (u,v,r) are tight, and the next inward reverse-boundary turn (q_4,w,r) is tight. Here (v,u,r) is the universal R723 star. If (r,v,u) were tight, r could be prepended to the advanced short rail, producing a spanning two-cover of H; hence R3 gives (u,v,r). Likewise if (r,w,q_4) were tight, r could be prepended to the advanced long rail Q[3,m], again two-covering H; hence R3 gives (q_4,w,r).

RIGHT. If R-ADV occurs with deleted root r in {b,z}, then the R723 shallow cover selects (d,s) on Q[0,m-1], while the R725 advanced short rail ending (...,s,d) selects its literal reverse (s,d). Moreover both (r,s,d) and (r,d,s) are tight, and the next inward reverse-boundary turn (r,rho,q_{m-4}) is tight. The first is the universal R723 star. If (s,d,r) were tight, r could be appended to the advanced short rail; if (q_{m-4},rho,r) were tight, r could be appended to Q[0,m-3]. Either would two-cover H, so R3 gives the displayed reversals.

Thus every first-step root advance is simultaneously (i) a same-deletion-root reversal of a selected physical Q state and (ii) a source-localized shield on the next deeper Q boundary. The ADV branch may therefore be carried in the same selected-state-reversal currency as accepted R720 while retaining a concrete seed for a second zipper step.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in the accepted crossed R621 frame; m>=4. Use accepted R3, R723 and R725.

## Scope
Noncircular crossed-frame refinement of the accepted R725 ADV branch. No R5,R168,R169,R224,R533,R358,payment,capture,R436,Reverse Ear,or computation.

## Applicability
Whenever R725 returns L-ADV or R-ADV, retain both exact covers of the same singleton deletion and the opposite selected orders of the physical first-inward dimer. Also retain the deleted root as a witness on both state orders and on the newly exposed next-inward reverse boundary. Downstream consumers should treat ADV as a source-labelled reversal plus a second-step zipper seed, not merely as cut movement.

## Persistence
Retain the deleted root r, the R723 shallow cover, the R725 advanced cover, the two oppositely directed selected states, the two root turns on those state orders, and the next-inward reverse-boundary turn with its failed insertion certificate.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert that a selected-state reversal alone closes H. Does not assert a second advanced cover or universal four-witness star at the next boundary. Does not consume the P4 alternative of pending R727. The left and right ADV outputs are independent alternatives and need not coexist.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Historical same-root state-reversal zipper branch.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** PASS. The shallow and advanced covers of the same singleton deletion literally select opposite orders of the first-inward Q dimer. Reinserting the deleted root at the advanced short rail or advanced long rail would give a spanning two-cover, so R3 forces the displayed same-root reverse-orientation turn and next-boundary shield. The m=4 endpoint cases remain valid because the residual Q rail is a dimer and prepending/appending the root creates the required three-vertex path.

## Proof
For L-ADV, R725 gives either H-c=(v,u,a,b,z,L) sqcup Q[3,m] or H-a=(v,u,c,z,b,L) sqcup Q[3,m]. For the same root r, R723 gives H-r=A_r^L sqcup Q[1,m]. Therefore Q[1,m] selects (u,v), while the advanced short rail selects (v,u). R723 already gives (v,u,r). If (r,v,u) were tight, prepend r to the advanced short rail; together with Q[3,m] this is a two-path cover of H, contrary to pc(H)=3. By R3, (u,v,r) is tight. Since m>=4, Q[3,m] begins (w,q_4). If (r,w,q_4) were tight, prepend r to this rail and retain the advanced short rail, again obtaining a two-cover of H. Hence R3 gives (q_4,w,r).

For R-ADV, R725 gives either H-z=(R,a,c,b,s,d) sqcup Q[0,m-3] or H-b=(R,c,a,z,s,d) sqcup Q[0,m-3]. For the same r, R723 gives H-r=Q[0,m-1] sqcup A_r^R. Thus the shallow Q rail selects (d,s), while the advanced short rail selects (s,d), and R723 gives (r,s,d). If (s,d,r) were tight, append r to the advanced short rail and retain Q[0,m-3], two-covering H; hence (r,d,s) is tight by R3. Finally Q[0,m-3] ends (q_{m-4},rho). If (q_{m-4},rho,r) were tight, append r and retain the advanced short rail, again two-covering H. R3 gives (r,rho,q_{m-4}). These arguments also cover m=4, where the relevant residual Q rail has order two.

# R731 — A first-step root advance creates a bidirectional same-root two-seam weave

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Retain accepted R723 and R725 in the crossed R621 frame. Every ADV output supplies two distinct selected cross states between the same shallow/advanced exact-cover pair of one singleton deletion, one in each comparison direction.

LEFT. Let r=c or a be an L-ADV winner. Write x=a when r=c and x=c when r=a. The shallow cover is T_0=A_r^L sqcup Q[1,m], with x in A_r^L and u=q_1,v=q_2,w=q_3 consecutive on Q[1,m]. The advanced cover is T_1=(v,u,x,...) sqcup Q[3,m]. Then T_1 selects the X-Q state (u,x), whose endpoints lie in the two distinct T_0 components, while T_0 selects the physical Q state (v,w), whose endpoints lie in the two distinct T_1 components. Accepted R176, with spare vertex r, therefore gives two graph-intrinsic balanced opposite-sign pair births Pi_L^out from (u,x) and Pi_L^in from (v,w), both retaining the same deleted root and the same ordered pair of exact-cover histories.

RIGHT. Let r=z or b be an R-ADV winner. Write x=b when r=z and x=z when r=b, and rho=q_{m-3}, d=q_{m-2}, s=q_{m-1}. The shallow cover is T_0=Q[0,m-1] sqcup A_r^R, with x in A_r^R and rho,d,s consecutive on Q[0,m-1]. The advanced cover is T_1=(R,...,x,s,d) sqcup Q[0,m-3]. Then T_1 selects the X-Q state (x,s), crossing the two T_0 components, while T_0 selects the Q state (rho,d), crossing the two T_1 components. R176 gives two graph-intrinsic balanced opposite-sign pair births Pi_R^out and Pi_R^in with the same common source ledger.

Thus ADV is a bidirectional two-seam weave: an outer X-Q recombination state and a deeper Q-Q recombination state are simultaneously certified by opposite comparisons of the same two exact covers. The two births coexist as graph-intrinsic certificates, although their later paid representatives are alternative choices.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in the accepted crossed R621 frame. Use accepted R176,R723,R725 and one literal ADV output.

## Scope
Noncircular source-localized refinement of the accepted R725 ADV branch. No R5,R168,R169,R224,R533,R358,payment,capture,R436,Reverse Ear,five-cell classification,or computation.

## Applicability
After any R725 ADV winner, retain the shallow and advanced covers as an ordered cover pair and record both cross states before choosing a downstream lineage. The next useful consumer should compare or merge the two R176 ancestries; applying generic payment to only one discards the new information.

## Persistence
Retain the deleted root, both literal exact covers, both selected cross states with their comparison directions, both R176 birth certificates, and the distinction between the outer X-Q seam and deeper Q-Q seam.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert that the two balanced-pair supports are disjoint, hinged, equal, opposite to one another, or simultaneously current after payment. Does not itself close H or force a second root advance. Does not authorize combining selected states from different representatives as one current cover.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Historical bidirectional same-root zipper weave branch.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** PASS. In every ADV branch the advanced X-Q state crosses the shallow cover partition, while the shallow next-Q state crosses the advanced cover partition. R176 applies independently in the two comparison directions with the deleted root as spare, yielding two source-distinct pair births with a common exact-cover ledger. No simultaneous-currentness beyond the source covers is claimed.

## Proof
Consider L-ADV. For r=c the shallow and advanced covers are (a,b,z,L) sqcup (u,v,w,...,R) and (v,u,a,b,z,L) sqcup (w,...,R). The advanced state (u,a) crosses the shallow partition, and the shallow state (v,w) crosses the advanced partition. For r=a replace a by c in the first cross state; the same component check is literal. Since W=H-r is proper and r is spare, R176 applies to each cross state. Both resulting pairs retain r and the two displayed cover histories.

For R-ADV with r=z, the shallow and advanced covers are (L,...,rho,d,s) sqcup (R,a,c,b) and (R,a,c,b,s,d) sqcup (L,...,rho). The advanced state (b,s) crosses the shallow partition, while the shallow state (rho,d) crosses the advanced partition. For r=b replace b by z in the first cross state. Apply R176 twice with spare root r. This proves the stated two-seam weave and its source localization.

# R732 — Exterior endpoint test for a tight P4 gives a P5 or a direct terminal-dimer pair

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Let H be a Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament, let K=(k_0,k_1,k_2,k_3) be a vertex-simple tight P4, and let y be a vertex outside V(K). Then exactly the following extension test is available. If (y,k_0,k_1) is tight, then (y,k_0,k_1,k_2,k_3) is a tight P5. If (k_2,k_3,y) is tight, then (k_0,k_1,k_2,k_3,y) is a tight P5. If both endpoint attachments are bad, boundary antisymmetry forces (k_1,k_0,y) and (y,k_3,k_2) tight. Hence the reversed initial dimer D_L=(k_1,k_0) is tail-signed by witness y and the reversed terminal dimer D_R=(k_3,k_2) is head-signed by the same witness y. Their physical supports are disjoint, so they form a graph-intrinsic balanced opposite-sign pair of total support mass four. Thus a tight P4 can fail both one-vertex endpoint extensions only by exposing an explicit opposite-polarity pair on its two terminal physical dimers. In a hypothetical smallest counterexample, accepted R514 may additionally descend this mass-four pair to a spanning two-cover or an ancestry-bearing mass-two floor.

## Hypotheses
Strong Level-(1); K is a vertex-simple tight P4; y is outside V(K). Smallest-counterexample minimality is needed only for the optional R514 descent sentence.

## Scope
Order-free P4 consumer. No R24 frame, deletion exactness, capture, payment, longest-path extremality, or cover comparison is used for the local P5-or-pair conclusion.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Generic P4 endpoint test ends in P5 or a bare opposite-sign dimer pair; neither is current closure currency and the theorem has no live consumers. Preserve historically.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Verified.

## Proof
The two positive attachment statements are immediate concatenations with the two certified turns of K. Assume both attachments are bad. By R3, badness of (y,k_0,k_1) gives its exact reversal (k_1,k_0,y) tight, so the tested dimer (k_1,k_0) is tail-signed by witness y. Badness of (k_2,k_3,y) gives its exact reversal (y,k_3,k_2) tight, so the tested dimer (k_3,k_2) is head-signed by y. The physical supports {k_0,k_1} and {k_2,k_3} are disjoint because K is vertex-simple. They therefore form a direct balanced opposite-sign pair; in the smallest-counterexample specialization their total support size is four, so R514 gives the optional descent.

# R733 — Every R727 P4 residue births an inward-coordinate signed-dimer pair before payment

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Retain the accepted crossed R621 frame and accepted R723,R727. Then every P4 branch of R727 has a source-localized balanced-pair consumer that retains the first inward Q coordinate on a nontrivial signed dimer. LEFT: write u=q_1,v=q_2. If R727 returns a tight Hamilton P4 K on {a,b,c,u}, put r=z; if it returns one on {c,z,a,u}, put r=b. Then H contains a graph-intrinsic balanced opposite-sign pair one of whose signed supports is a dimer containing u. More precisely, apply R732 to K with exterior vertex L=q_0. If neither endpoint attachment of L to K is tight, R732 gives the direct pair on the two reversed terminal dimers of K; exactly one of those two dimers contains u. If an endpoint attachment is tight, it produces a tight P5 J on {L,u} union (X-{r}), so J sqcup Q[2,m] is a literal exact two-cover of H-r. Compare this with the accepted R723 shallow cover A_r^L sqcup Q[1,m]. In J, the vertex u has a selected adjacency to a vertex of A_r^L, hence that state crosses the two components of the shallow cover. Apply the reconstructed R176 proof with the shallow cover as R, the P5 cover as T, spare vertex r, and crossed endpoint x=u. Since u is the endpoint of the old long rail Q[1,m] with old neighbor v, the resulting pair may be chosen with one signed support exactly a tested orientation of the physical dimer {u,v}, while the opposite signed support is the singleton (r). RIGHT is exact dual. Write d=q_{m-2},s=q_{m-1}. If the R727 P4 is on {a,c,b,s}, put r=z; if on {c,a,z,s}, put r=b. Testing exterior vertex R=q_m by R732 either gives a direct terminal-dimer pair with one dimer containing s, or gives a tight P5 J on {R,s} union (X-{r}). In the latter case Q[0,m-2] sqcup J is an exact cover of H-r; comparing it with the R723 right shallow cover Q[0,m-1] sqcup A_r^R and applying the endpoint-symmetric reconstruction of R176 at crossed endpoint s gives a balanced pair with one signed support a tested orientation of {d,s} and opposite singleton (r). Thus a labelled P4 in R727 is not terminal and need not be converted into an advanced P6: before any generic payment it already yields an inward-coordinate dimer pair tied either to the literal old first-inward Q edge or to one terminal dimer of the actual P4.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in the accepted crossed R621 frame; accepted R723 and R727 hold; use accepted R732 and the fully reconstructed R176 cross-state proof.

## Scope
Noncircular consumer of the P4 branch of the first-step zipper dichotomy. It retains q_1 or q_{m-1} on a nontrivial signed support before payment. No five-cell classification, R5,R168,R169,R224,R533,generic R358,R436, or floor steering is used.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired

- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Verified.

## Proof
Consider the left side; the right side is the exact reversal. Let K be the R727 P4 and let r be the unique X vertex omitted from its support, so r=z for support {a,b,c,u} and r=b for {c,z,a,u}. Test L against the two ends of an actual tight ordering K=(k_0,k_1,k_2,k_3). If both attachments fail, R732 gives the pair ((k_1,k_0),(k_3,k_2)) with common witness L and opposite polarities. The two terminal dimers partition V(K), so exactly one contains u. Otherwise one attachment succeeds and gives a tight P5 J on {L,u} union (X-{r}). The untouched Q[2,m] is disjoint and tight, hence J sqcup Q[2,m] is a literal exact two-cover T of H-r. R723 supplies the shallow exact cover R=A_r^L sqcup Q[1,m], where A_r^L has support {L} union (X-{r}). Since J contains the unique vertex u outside A_r^L and all other J vertices lie in A_r^L, at least one selected J-state uy or yu is incident with u and crosses the two components of R. Apply the reconstructed R176 proof to this physical cross state using spare d=r and choose x=u as the crossed endpoint lying in the R-component Q[1,m]. That component is nontrivial and u has old neighbor v=q_2. Boundary antisymmetry on {v,u,y} yields one signed tested orientation of the physical dimer {u,v} with witness y; the automatic singleton sign at r with the same witness gives the opposite polarity. Hence a balanced pair is born with nontrivial support {u,v} and opposite singleton {r}. On the right, a successful R-attachment gives J sqcup Q[0,m-2] and the old shallow cover Q[0,m-1] sqcup A_r^R. A selected J-state incident with s crosses the old components; use x=s and its old Q-neighbor d=q_{m-2} in the same R176 proof to obtain a signed dimer on {d,s} and opposite singleton r. # R734 — Every first-step root advance self-mints a reversed-state R696 packet

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Retain the accepted crossed R621 frame and accepted R723,R725. Every ADV output of R725 canonically creates a two-witness short-carrier packet on the reverse of the first-inward Q state, so accepted R696 applies immediately without generic payment.

LEFT. Suppose L-ADV occurs with deleted root r in {a,c}. Write x=a when r=c and x=c when r=a, and u=q_1,v=q_2,w=q_3. The advanced short rail begins with the tight trimer K_L=(v,u,x). Its reverse initial boundary dimer is S_L=(u,v). The original Q turn (u,v,w) makes w a tail witness on S_L. If (r,v,u) were tight, r could be prepended to the advanced short rail and, together with Q[3,m], would two-cover H. Hence boundary antisymmetry gives (u,v,r), so r is a second tail witness on the same tested orientation S_L. The witnesses r,w are distinct and lie outside K_L. Therefore S_L,K_L,{r,w} satisfy accepted R696.

RIGHT. Suppose R-ADV occurs with deleted root r in {b,z}. Write x=b when r=z and x=z when r=b, and rho=q_{m-3},d=q_{m-2},s=q_{m-1}. The advanced short rail ends with the tight trimer K_R=(x,s,d). Its reverse terminal boundary dimer is S_R=(d,s). The original Q turn (rho,d,s) makes rho a head witness on S_R. If (s,d,r) were tight, r could be appended to the advanced short rail and, together with Q[0,m-3], would two-cover H. Thus R3 gives (r,d,s), making r a second head witness on S_R. Again the witnesses are distinct and outside K_R, so R696 applies.

Consequently, in either ADV branch and in every exact two-cover of H-V(S_L) or H-V(S_R), the complementary singleton x has exactly one of the accepted R696 forms: (END) a literal one/two-hole spanning proposal plus same-frame capture; (FREE) one selected crossing usable with either named witness; or (SANDWICH) the literal witness trimer (r,x,w) or its reverse on the left, and (r,x,rho) or its reverse on the right. Hence a first-step root advance is not a terminal cover currency: it compiles directly to source-localized mate/capture/trimer geometry on the physically reversed rail state.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in the accepted crossed R621 frame; m>=4. Use accepted R3,R723,R725,R696.

## Scope
Noncircular crossed-frame consumer of the accepted R725 ADV branch. No R5,R168,R169,R224,R533,R358,generic payment,R436,Reverse Ear,five-cell classification,or computation.

## Applicability
Whenever R725 returns ADV, retain the first trimer of the advanced left short rail or the last trimer of the advanced right short rail. Test the reversed physical Q dimer with the deleted root and the adjacent original-Q vertex as its two witnesses, then apply R696. Do not preserve ADV merely as an abstract cut movement or spend it through generic R542 payment.

## Persistence
Retain the deletion root r, advanced exact cover, carrier K_L or K_R, tested reversed Q dimer, both named witnesses with exact turns, the failed root-reinsertion certificate, and the resulting exact R696 END/FREE/SANDWICH source cover.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert which R696 branch occurs or that any one branch alone closes H. Does not assert the R696 capture descendants coexist. Does not consume the separate labelled-P4 alternative of pending R727. The left and right constructions are dual alternatives and need not coexist.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Historical self-minted R696 zipper packet branch; route-specific packet production is noncanonical.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Verified.

## Proof
In L-ADV, the advanced exact cover is (v,u,x,...) sqcup Q[3,m], where x=a for deleted root c and x=c for deleted root a. Hence K_L=(v,u,x) is tight and S_L=(u,v) is its reverse initial boundary dimer. Since Q is tight, (u,v,w) is tight. If (r,v,u) were tight, (r,v,u,x,...) together with Q[3,m] would be a spanning two-cover of H, impossible. R3 therefore gives (u,v,r). Thus w and r are distinct tail witnesses on S_L outside K_L. Apply R696.

In R-ADV, the cover is (R,...,x,s,d) sqcup Q[0,m-3], where x=b for root z and x=z for root b. Thus K_R=(x,s,d) is tight and S_R=(d,s) is its reverse terminal boundary dimer. The Q turn (rho,d,s) is tight. If (s,d,r) were tight, appending r to the short rail would yield a spanning two-cover together with Q[0,m-3]; hence R3 gives (r,d,s). Therefore rho and r are distinct head witnesses on S_R outside K_R. Apply R696. Substituting the named witnesses into R696 gives the stated END/FREE/SANDWICH alternatives.

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Retain the accepted crossed R621 frame and accepted R723, with u=q_1,v=q_2,d=q_{m-2},s=q_{m-1}. Fix any x in X. Then the left first-inward reverse dimer D_L=(v,u) is tail-signed by x and the right first-inward reverse dimer D_R=(s,d) is head-signed by the same witness x. If m>=5 their physical supports are disjoint, so (D_R,D_L) is a direct graph-intrinsic balanced opposite-sign pair of total support mass four. In a hypothetical smallest counterexample, accepted R514 therefore gives a finite certificate-retaining continuation to a spanning two-cover or an ancestry-bearing mass-two floor. If m=4, the two supports meet exactly in the hinge q_2=d=v, so accepted R547 instead collapses them directly to the opposite-sign singleton pair {q_1},{q_3}. Thus for every m>=4 the crossed frame already contains a source-localized opposite-sign interaction joining the two first-inward Q boundaries. Moreover the construction is four-witness saturated: the same fixed physical dimer pair has a valid common-witness certificate for every x in X, and all four such source certificates coexist graph-intrinsically.

## Hypotheses
H is in the accepted crossed R621/R723 frame with m>=4. Smallest-counterexample minimality is needed only for the optional R514 descent when m>=5.

## Scope
Noncircular two-ended synthesis of R723. No R725/R727 zipper, R533 order gate, five-cell classification, capture, generic payment construction, or Reverse Ear is used. The conclusion is stronger than an anonymous pair birth because it retains the two literal first-inward Q dimers and any chosen common X witness.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Common-witness opposite-sign pair leaf with no consumers; bare pair production is not scarce progress.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Verified.

## Proof
R723 states that (v,u,x) is tight and (x,s,d) is tight for every x in X. Hence tested D_L=(v,u) is tail-signed by x and tested D_R=(s,d) is head-signed by x. Their supports are {q_1,q_2} and {q_{m-2},q_{m-1}}. For m>=5 these sets are disjoint, so they form a direct opposite-sign mass-four pair and R514 gives the optional smallest-counterexample descent. For m=4, q_{m-2}=q_2 while q_{m-1}=q_3, so the supports meet in exactly the hinge q_2; R547 deletes the hinge and leaves opposite-sign singletons q_1 and q_3. Since x was arbitrary in X, the identical physical support pair carries four alternative common-witness certificates.

# R744 — Universal first-inward carriers force two same-frame X-anchor capture/contact portals per side

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
LEFT. Fix any exact two-cover T_L of H-{u,v}, supplied by R429. Regard S_L=(u,v) as a tail-signed dimer with exact witness w=q_3, since Q gives (u,v,w) tight. For every x in X, accepted R723 gives the tight trimer K_x=(v,u,x), whose reverse initial boundary dimer is exactly S_L and whose complementary carrier singleton is x. Applying R508 to each K_x in the same T_L forces a selected state C_x={x,y_x} with y_x outside K_x. Call x blocked if the chosen crossing has y_x=w. Since T_L is a two-path forest, w has selected degree at most two, so at most two distinct x in X are blocked. Hence at least two distinct vertices x in X have witness-avoiding selected carrier/exterior crossings C_x. For each such x, R527 with S_L,w,K_x,C_x may orient the marker so that x itself is captured. The genuine historical carrier edge {u,x} in K_x then lets R312 expose a protected earlier-contact-or-first-contact event at x. Thus one fixed exact H-{u,v} cover contains source crossings making at least two distinct X anchors individually capture/contact-capable through literal first-inward X-Q carrier edges. RIGHT dually, fix any exact T_R of H-{d,s}. Regard S_R=(d,s) as head-signed by rho=q_{m-3} via the old Q turn (rho,d,s). For every x in X, R723 gives K_x=(x,s,d), whose reverse terminal dimer is S_R and complementary singleton x. R508 forces one selected crossing from each x in the same T_R; at most two can use rho as exterior endpoint, so at least two distinct x are capture-capable with witness rho. Capture x by R527 and apply R312 through the genuine carrier edge {x,s}.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in the accepted crossed R621 frame. Use accepted R723,R429,R508,R527,R312. Put L=q_0,u=q_1,v=q_2,w=q_3 and rho=q_{m-3},d=q_{m-2},s=q_{m-1},R=q_m.

## Scope
Noncircular direct consumer of the accepted R723 universal first-inward stars. It exploits four carrier singletons against one old-Q witness in one fixed pair-deletion cover. No R5,R168,R169,R224,R533,R358,generic payment,R436,five-cell classification,or R725/R727 zipper is used.

## Applicability
Use immediately after R723, before generic pair descent or first-step zipper classification. Choose one exact deletion cover of the first-inward Q dimer. Retain all four R508 source crossings; at least two avoid the unique adjacent Q witness and hence give alternative X-anchor protected-contact lineages. The useful provenance is the literal new carrier edge u-x or x-s joining X to the first inward Q vertex.

## Persistence
For each side retain the tested Q dimer and polarity, old-Q witness w or rho, the single exact pair-deletion cover, all four root-labelled R723 carriers, the four forced selected crossings, and at least two witness-avoiding X anchors with their capture and carrier-edge ancestry.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert the two capture descendants coexist after actualization, that the same X vertices are capturable on both sides, or that protected first contact closes H. Does not assert every X vertex is capturable in the fixed cover. Does not spend the resulting captures through generic payment.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** R744 is a protected-contact portal producer with no live consumer. Current guidance treats protected contact production as saturated currency.
- **Curation note:** Crossed first-inward k=4 specialization of the generic carrier-fan count, retained because downstream results use the named left/right deletion covers and portal coordinates.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** PASS. In one fixed exact H-{u,v} cover, R508 applies separately to all four R723 carriers and yields four distinct X-incident selected crossings. Only crossings through the unique old-Q witness w block same-frame R527 capture; path degree at w is at most two, so at least two distinct X anchors remain witness-avoiding. R527 lawfully designates the X endpoint as captured, and R312 uses the genuine historical carrier edge {u,x}; the right side is exact dual. The statement correctly fences coexistence/currentness. R429 is a retired but accepted exact dependency; live R4 independently supplies the exact pair-deletion cover existence, so this is provenance cleanup rather than a mathematical defect.

## Proof
LEFT. By R429 choose an exact two-cover T_L of H-{u,v}. Since Q is tight, (u,v,w) is tight, so S_L=(u,v) is tail-signed by witness w. For each x in X, accepted R723 gives (v,u,x) tight. Hence K_x=(v,u,x) is a tight trimer with reverse initial boundary dimer S_L and complementary singleton x. Apply accepted R508 to D={u,v}, absorbable singleton {x}, recompletion carrier K_x, and the same T_L. Obtain a selected T_L-state C_x={x,y_x} with y_x outside V(K_x). Do this for all four x. If y_x is not w, then witness w avoids C_x, so accepted R527 applies and, by its endpoint-choice clause, the marker may be oriented to designate x itself as the captured anchor. If y_x=w, call x blocked. Distinct blocked x give distinct selected edges xw incident with w. Since the selected-state graph of T_L is a union of two paths, deg_T_L(w)<=2. Therefore at most two x are blocked, leaving at least two distinct capture-capable X vertices. For each such x, K_x contains the genuine historical adjacency {u,x}; accepted R312 applied to the capture through C_x and this carrier edge gives either an earlier protected event touching x or lawful mirror reentry whose first contact is at x. RIGHT. Choose exact T_R of H-{d,s}. The old Q turn (rho,d,s) makes S_R=(d,s) head-signed by rho. R508 in the common T_R gives C_x={x,y_x}; at most two have y_x=rho because deg_T_R(rho)<=2. Every other crossing avoids the witness, so R527 captures x and R312 uses the genuine K_x edge {x,s}. # R746 — Two-sided first-inward portals share an X anchor or split along one matching layer

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Retain the accepted crossed R621/R723 frame and the fixed left/right exact pair-deletion covers and source crossings of pending R744. Let A_L be the set of vertices x in X for which the fixed cover T_L of H-{u,v} contains an R744 witness-avoiding carrier/exterior crossing, so x is capture/contact-capable through the genuine carrier edge {u,x}. Let A_R be defined dually in the fixed cover T_R of H-{d,s}, with portal edge {x,s}. Then |A_L|>=2 and |A_R|>=2, and exactly one of the following structural alternatives holds.

(COMMON) A_L intersect A_R is nonempty. Hence some named x in X has both a left protected-contact portal through {u,x} and a right protected-contact portal through {x,s}, with the two R744 source covers, selected crossings, avoiding witnesses q_3 and q_{m-3}, and capture ancestries retained. The later left and right continuations are separate choices.

(MATCHING-SPLIT) A_L intersect A_R is empty. Then necessarily |A_L|=|A_R|=2 and A_R=X\A_L. Consequently the unordered bipartition {A_L,A_R} is exactly one of the three perfect-matching layers of the transitive four-cell: M_R={{a,b},{c,z}}, M_S={{a,c},{b,z}}, or M_L={{a,z},{b,c}}. Which complementary edge is left-capable and which is right-capable remains part of the certificate.

Thus failure of a common two-ended X anchor is not an unstructured residue: all left/right capture portals separate along one named matching layer of X.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in the accepted crossed R621/R723 frame. Use the fixed-cover portal sets supplied by pending R744 and the accepted matching-height labeling of X.

## Scope
Noncircular two-ended compression of the pending R744 direct-capture route. Pure four-element set pigeonhole after R744; no payment,R436,Reverse Ear,five-cell classification,R5,R168,R169,R224,R533,R358,or computation.

## Applicability
After constructing both R744 fixed-cover portal sets, test their intersection before following any capture. In COMMON retain the same X anchor and both source ledgers. In MATCHING-SPLIT retain the exact matching layer and left/right assignment; downstream work should use the corresponding crossed/outer gate geometry rather than treating the four portals independently.

## Persistence
Retain T_L,T_R, the full good-anchor sets A_L,A_R, for every retained anchor its selected crossing and avoiding Q witness, and in MATCHING-SPLIT the named matching layer and side assignment.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert left and right capture descendants coexist, that the common anchor closes H, or that a matching-split branch is impossible. The sets are relative to the fixed exact covers and selected R508 crossings used in R744. Does not identify which matching layer occurs.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** R746 is a route-specific portal-set compression with no live consumers; protected-contact production is no longer a frontier.
- **Curation note:** Two-sided portal-set compression: common X anchor or complementary matching-layer split. Retained as a bounded structural interface rather than contact production.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Pure four-set pigeonhole is exact: two portal sets of size at least two either meet or are complementary two-sets, hence one of the three matching layers.

## Proof
By R744, at most two of the four left carrier singletons can be blocked by q_3 in T_L, so |A_L|>=2; dually |A_R|>=2. If A_L intersect A_R is nonempty, any x in the intersection carries the two displayed source-localized portals, proving COMMON. Otherwise the two subsets are disjoint. Since X has four vertices and both subsets have size at least two, each has size exactly two and their union is X. Every complementary pair partition of {a,b,c,z} is uniquely one of {ab|cz}, {ac|bz}, or {az|bc}, which are exactly the matching layers M_R,M_S,M_L in the accepted frame. This proves MATCHING-SPLIT.

# R749 — A tight cross-end turn (L,x,R) forces a non-Hamiltonian deep residue and renormalizes q_2 or q_{m-2} into a four-cell

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Retain the accepted synchronized transitive R594 frame: H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample, X is a no-P4 transitive matching-height four-cell with top matching M_R, Q=(q_0,...,q_m) with m>=4, L=q_0, u=q_1, s=q_{m-1}, R=q_m, and for every x in X the endpoint reverse stars (u,L,x) and (x,R,s) are tight.

Fix e in X for which the cross-end trimer (L,e,R) is tight. Let gamma be the M_R-partner of e and let {alpha,beta} be the other M_R edge, so X-{e}={alpha,beta,gamma}, and (alpha,beta,gamma),(beta,alpha,gamma) are tight by the R537 classification.

(1) RESIDUE. J=(u,L,e,R,s) is a tight P5. Hence the residue W=(X-{e}) union Q[2,m-2] is nonempty, has an exact two-cover, and has NO tight Hamilton path.

(2) LEFT SEAM (m>=5). Either (q_3,q_2,gamma) is tight, so gamma is an X tail witness on the deep reverse dimer (q_3,q_2); or both (q_2,gamma,alpha) and (q_2,gamma,beta) are tight. In the second case (q_2,gamma) is a two-witness star with witnesses alpha,beta, so accepted R537 gives either a tight Hamilton P4 on {q_2} union (X-{e}), a labelled P4 joining three X vertices to the deep coordinate q_2, or else {q_2} union (X-{e}) is itself a transitive matching-height no-P4 four-cell with top matching {{q_2,gamma},{alpha,beta}}.

(3) RIGHT SEAM (m>=5). For each ordered pair (x,y) with {x,y}={alpha,beta}: either (x,q_{m-2},q_{m-3}) is tight, so x is an X head witness on the deep dimer (q_{m-2},q_{m-3}); or (y,x,q_{m-2}) is tight. In the second case the ordered dimer (y,x) carries the two distinct witnesses gamma and q_{m-2}, so R537 gives either a tight Hamilton P4 on (X-{e}) union {q_{m-2}}, or that four-set is a transitive matching-height no-P4 four-cell with top matching {{alpha,beta},{gamma,q_{m-2}}}.

(4) m=4. Then W={alpha,beta,gamma,q_2} and (1) says W has no tight Hamilton P4. Hence (q_2,gamma,alpha),(q_2,gamma,beta),(alpha,beta,q_2),(beta,alpha,q_2) are all tight, and R537 applies with its no-P4 hypothesis literally verified: {q_2} union (X-{e}) is a transitive matching-height no-P4 four-cell with top matching {{q_2,gamma},{alpha,beta}}. At m=4 there is no witness escape.

Every output is a graph-intrinsic tightness fact about one fixed frame, so the left and right conclusions coexist. No cover selection, capture, payment, witness actualization, R436 event, or Reverse Ear is spent.

REMARK (unconditional cross-end coverage). By accepted R3 exactly one of (L,x,R) and (R,x,L) is tight for each x in X. Accepted R722 consumes the orientation (R,x,L). Together with this theorem, every vertex of X therefore has a direct cross-end consumer with no further hypothesis: either R722 labelled P4 / dual protected endpoint contacts, or the present deep-residue renormalization.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample in the accepted R594 synchronized transitive frame, m>=4. Uses only accepted R3 (boundary antisymmetry), R4 (minimality, pc(H)=3), R537 (four-cell classification), R594, and for the remark accepted R722.

## Scope
Noncircular direct consumer of the cross-end orientation (L,x,R), complementary to accepted R722. Pure residue non-Hamiltonicity plus seam antisymmetry plus four-cell renormalization. No R5,R168,R169,R224,R533, generic R358, generic payment, R436, Reverse Ear, five-cell classification, or computation.

## Applicability
Whenever a route exposes a tight (q_0,x,q_m) turn, including the cross-end SANDWICH output of pending R748, do not stop at the P5. Delete the P5 and use non-Hamiltonicity of the deep residue to block both concatenations of the two M_R-derived X trimers with Q[2,m-2]. This moves attention from the endpoint box to the deep coordinates q_2 and q_{m-2}, and in the non-witness branch renormalizes one of them into a four-cell together with three X vertices.

## Persistence
Retain e, the M_R-partner gamma, the other M_R edge {alpha,beta}, the tight P5 J, the residue W and its non-Hamiltonicity, and for each seam which branch occurred. In a four-cell branch retain the new top matching and the four-set identity. All facts are graph-intrinsic and coexist.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert that any branch closes H. Does not assert existence of an e with (L,e,R) tight; it is a conditional consumer, made unconditional over X only in combination with R3 and accepted R722. Does not determine the matching order of the new four-cell, nor which of the two seam branches occurs. Does not assert that Q[2,m-2] is contiguous in any exact two-cover of W. Does not use the third tight trimer of X-{e}, so it does not depend on the relative height of M_S and M_L.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** R749 is the source-frame renormalization step beneath accepted toolkit R859; preserve it as proof ancestry rather than a default-search theorem.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** PASS. The endpoint reverse stars plus (L,e,R) form the claimed P5 J. R4 makes the proper residue W two-coverable and pc(H)=3 forbids a Hamilton path in W. For m>=5, each M_R-derived X trimer concatenated to the deep Q interval has exactly two possible new seam turns; non-Hamiltonicity forces at least one seam bad, and R3 reverses it to the stated deep witness or two-witness-star alternative. R537 then gives precisely P4-or-transitive-four-cell renormalization. The right-hand argument is the exact dual. For m=4 the residue itself is the four-set, so no-P4 is literal and both concatenation directions force the four turns needed by R537. All outputs are graph-intrinsic and coexist. The R722 remark correctly makes the two cross-end orientations exhaustive by R3.

## Proof
Write X-{e}={alpha,beta,gamma}, where gamma is the M_R-partner of e and {alpha,beta} is the other M_R edge. By the R537 classification of a transitive matching-height four-cell, for each M_R edge {x,y} and each w outside it both (x,y,w) and (y,x,w) are tight. Applying this to {alpha,beta} with w=gamma gives the two tight trimers T_1=(beta,alpha,gamma) and T_2=(alpha,beta,gamma). Only these two trimers are used, so no assumption about the relative height of the two cross matchings is needed.

(1) The consecutive triples of J=(u,L,e,R,s) are (u,L,e), tight by the R594 endpoint reverse star; (L,e,R), tight by hypothesis; and (e,R,s), tight by the other R594 endpoint star. So J is a tight P5. Since |X-{e}|=3, W is a nonempty proper induced subsystem, so pc(W)<=2 by R4 and W has an exact two-cover. If W had a tight Hamilton path P, then J and P would be vertex-disjoint tight paths covering V(H), giving a spanning two-cover and contradicting pc(H)=3 (R4). Hence W has no tight Hamilton path.

(2) Let m>=5. For i=1,2 write T_i=(p_0,p_1,p_2). The sequence (p_0,p_1,p_2,q_2,q_3,...,q_{m-2}) enumerates V(W), and its consecutive triples are (p_0,p_1,p_2), (p_1,p_2,q_2), (p_2,q_2,q_3), and triples internal to Q. The first is tight by the R537 classification and the last kind are tight because Q is a tight path. By (1) the sequence is not a tight path, so (p_1,p_2,q_2) or (p_2,q_2,q_3) is bad, and boundary antisymmetry R3 makes (q_2,p_2,p_1) or (q_3,q_2,p_2) tight. Both T_1 and T_2 have p_2=gamma, with p_1=alpha and p_1=beta respectively. Hence if (q_3,q_2,gamma) is not tight, then (q_2,gamma,alpha) and (q_2,gamma,beta) are both tight. R537 with A=q_2, B=gamma, c=alpha, d=beta then gives either a tight Hamilton P4 on Z={q_2,alpha,beta,gamma} or the transitive matching-height no-P4 cell structure on Z with top matching {{q_2,gamma},{alpha,beta}}.

(3) Dually, for m>=5 the sequence (q_2,...,q_{m-2},p_0,p_1,p_2) enumerates V(W) with consecutive triples internal to Q together with (q_{m-3},q_{m-2},p_0), (q_{m-2},p_0,p_1) and (p_0,p_1,p_2). By (1) it is not tight, so one of the two seam triples is bad and R3 gives (p_0,q_{m-2},q_{m-3}) or (p_1,p_0,q_{m-2}) tight. Taking T_1 gives the ordered pair (x,y)=(beta,alpha) and T_2 gives (x,y)=(alpha,beta), which is the stated alternative. In the second alternative (y,x,q_{m-2}) is tight, and (y,x,gamma) is tight by the R537 classification, so the ordered dimer (y,x) has the two distinct witnesses gamma and q_{m-2}, both outside {x,y}; note q_{m-2} is outside X. R537 with A=y, B=x, c=gamma, d=q_{m-2} gives either a tight Hamilton P4 on {alpha,beta,gamma,q_{m-2}} or the cell structure with top matching {{alpha,beta},{gamma,q_{m-2}}}.

(4) For m=4 we have Q[2,m-2]=(q_2) and W={alpha,beta,gamma,q_2}, so a tight Hamilton path of W is exactly a tight Hamilton P4 on this four-set, and by (1) there is none. For i=1,2 with T_i=(p_0,p_1,p_2), the sequences (p_0,p_1,p_2,q_2) and (q_2,p_0,p_1,p_2) are therefore not tight; since (p_0,p_1,p_2) is tight, R3 gives (q_2,p_2,p_1) tight and (p_1,p_0,q_2) tight. Ranging over i=1,2 yields (q_2,gamma,alpha), (q_2,gamma,beta), (alpha,beta,q_2), (beta,alpha,q_2) all tight. R537 now applies to Z={q_2,alpha,beta,gamma} with A=q_2,B=gamma,c=alpha,d=beta, and its no-P4 hypothesis is literally verified by (1); hence Z is a transitive matching-height no-P4 four-cell with top matching {{q_2,gamma},{alpha,beta}}.

All conclusions are statements about which ordered triples of H are tight, together with the non-Hamiltonicity of one fixed induced subsystem. Nothing is selected, captured, paid, or actualized, so the left and right outputs hold simultaneously.

REMARK. By R3 exactly one of (L,x,R) and (R,x,L) is tight for each x in X, and accepted R722 is a direct consumer of the orientation (R,x,L). Hence every vertex of X has a cross-end consumer unconditionally.

# R752 — One-witness carrier fans expose all but two complementary singletons to protected contact

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Let H be a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample. Let S be a fixed tested signed physical dimer with exact sign witness w, and let T be one exact two-cover of H-V(S). Let K_1,...,K_k, k>=3, be retained tight trimers such that S is the same reverse boundary dimer of every K_i and V(K_i)=V(S) union {c_i}, where c_1,...,c_k are pairwise distinct and w lies outside V(S) union {c_1,...,c_k}. Then one fixed cover T makes at least k-2 distinct complementary singletons c_i individually capture/contact-capable with the same witness w. More precisely, accepted R508 applied to each carrier K_i in the same T forces a selected state C_i={c_i,y_i} with y_i outside V(K_i). At most two indices can have y_i=w, because those blocked states are distinct selected edges incident with w and the selected-state graph of T is a union of two paths, so deg_T(w)<=2. Hence for at least k-2 indices, C_i avoids w. For each such i, accepted R527 may use that exact state and witness w and orient the marker so that c_i itself is the captured anchor. Since K_i is a trimer with S as a reverse boundary dimer, c_i has a genuine historical carrier adjacency to one endpoint of S inside K_i. Accepted R312 therefore converts the capture into an earlier-contact-or-first-contact protected lineage at c_i using that genuine old-carrier edge. All forced source crossings C_i coexist in the single exact cover T; the later capture/contact descendants are alternative historical continuations. In particular k=3 guarantees one protected-contact-capable complementary singleton and k=4 guarantees at least two.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample. S is a fixed tested signed dimer with exact witness w. T is an exact two-cover of H-V(S). K_i are retained tight trimers sharing S as the same reverse boundary dimer, with pairwise distinct complementary singletons c_i, and w is disjoint from S and every c_i. Uses accepted R508, R527, and R312.

## Scope
Order-free parent theorem for same-frame carrier counting and protected contact. No crossed frame, endpoint normalization, R5, R168, R169, R224, R533, generic R358, payment, R436, Reverse Ear, or computation.

## Applicability
Use whenever several one-vertex trimer carriers share one tested signed dimer inside one exact support-deletion cover. Count the carrier singletons before designing per-carrier arguments: a single witness can block at most two of them. For four carriers, retain at least two simultaneous witness-avoiding source crossings and feed each alternative capture through its genuine trimer edge to R312. This is the parent counting mechanism behind first-inward four-carrier portals and applies equally to terminal-dimer witness packets.

## Persistence
Retain S with tested orientation and witness w, the one fixed exact cover T, all carrier trimers K_i and complementary singletons c_i, all R508-selected source crossings C_i, the set of blocked indices y_i=w, and at least k-2 witness-avoiding indices. For any chosen unblocked index retain marker orientation, capture of c_i, its genuine K_i carrier adjacency, and the R312 protected-contact lineage. Source crossings coexist in T; descendants are alternative.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert that different capture or protected-contact descendants coexist after actualization. Does not assert the forced exterior endpoints y_i are distinct, that the witness-avoiding crossing for a given c_i is unique, or that protected first contact closes H. Does not assert the selected state remains current after capture. Gives no positive count when k<3. Does not itself produce the exact deletion cover or the signed witness.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** R752 is a quantitative one-witness contact-production specialization with no live consumers; generic saturation parent R686 remains available.
- **Curation note:** Quantitative parent for one-witness carrier fans: in one fixed two-path cover a single witness blocks at most two complementary singleton carriers.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** PASS. This is not redundant with accepted R686: R686(ii) guarantees existence of a capture for singleton witness and k>=3, whereas R752 quantifies the localization in one fixed cover, showing at most two carrier singletons can be blocked by the chosen witness and hence at least k-2 distinct c_i are individually capture-capable; R312 then lawfully compiles each chosen capture through its genuine old trimer adjacency to protected contact. Coexistence is claimed only for the source crossings, not descendants.

## Proof
For each i, put D=V(S) and S_i={c_i}. Because K_i is a tight trimer spanning exactly D union S_i and T is an exact two-cover of H-D, accepted R508 applies with absorbable block S_i and recompletion path K_i. It yields a selected T-state C_i={c_i,y_i} with y_i outside V(K_i). Call i blocked when y_i=w. Since the c_i are pairwise distinct, distinct blocked indices give distinct selected edges {c_i,w} incident with w. The selected-state graph of an exact two-path cover is a disjoint union of two paths, so every vertex has selected degree at most two. Therefore at most two indices are blocked. Hence at least k-2 indices satisfy y_i!=w. For such an index, c_i!=w by hypothesis and y_i!=w, so the exact witness w avoids C_i. Accepted R527 applies to the retained signed support S, witness w, carrier K_i, exact cover T, and selected carrier/exterior crossing C_i. By its marker-orientation clause we designate c_i itself as the captured signed anchor. Because S is a reverse boundary dimer of the trimer K_i, the complementary singleton c_i is an endpoint of K_i and has a genuine carrier adjacency E_i to one endpoint of S. The physical crossing C_i crosses the retained historical carrier K_i at c_i, so accepted R312 applies with historical carrier A=K_i, crossing C_i, captured anchor c_i, and old adjacency E_i. It gives a protected continuation on which either an earlier event touching c_i is exposed or the lawful old-carrier mirror reentry is itself first contact at c_i. The R508 crossings for all i were selected in the same original T, so those source states coexist. R527/R312 descendants are chosen separately and no coexistence after actualization is claimed. This proves the count and the k=3,4 specializations.

# R768 — Two probes of one trimer force a P4 or a dual-packet Hamilton P5

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Let H be a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample, let K=(a,b,c) be any vertex-simple tight trimer, and let y,z be two distinct vertices outside V(K). Then at least one of the following holds. (P4) One of the four-sets V(K) union {y} or V(K) union {z} supports a tight Hamilton P4. (P5+DUAL) Neither four-set supports a Hamilton P4; then the five-set V(K) union {y,z} supports a graph-intrinsic tight Hamilton P5, and simultaneously both reverse boundary dimers of K are two-witness short-carrier packets with the same witness pair {y,z}: D_L=(b,a) is tail-signed by both y and z, while D_R=(c,b) is head-signed by both y and z. Hence each boundary packet is independently eligible for the accepted R696 geometric END/FREE/SANDWICH refinement, but the Hamilton P5 should be retained before any such packet is spent. The P5 and both packet ledgers coexist graph-intrinsically; later capture/payment descendants from the two packets are alternative continuations.

## Hypotheses
H is a hypothetical smallest Strong Level-(1) counterexample; K=(a,b,c) is a vertex-simple tight trimer; y,z are distinct and lie outside V(K). Use accepted R700 and accepted R522.

## Scope
Order-free parent compression of two-probe trimer geometry. No crossed frame, five-cell classification, R5,R168,R169,R224,R533,generic R358,R436,R312,Reverse Ear,or computation. It strengthens the geometric reading of accepted R700 by exposing the accepted R522 Hamilton P5 in the joint no-P4 branch.

## Applicability
Use whenever a tight trimer is probed by two distinguished outside vertices. Do not treat the R700 DUAL-CP branch as merely two payment packets: before spending either packet, retain the Hamilton P5 on the trimer plus both probes. In the inward-anchor frame, a BAD R176 trimer K lies in H-{q_2,q_{m-2}}, so probes q_2,q_{m-2} give either an inward-anchor P4 or a tight P5 containing K and both inward anchors, with both reverse-boundary packets still available.

## Persistence
Retain K, probes y,z, the two four-cell probe outcomes, and in the joint no-P4 branch the exact R522 Hamilton P5 order/certificate together with both R700 reverse-boundary tested dimers, both witness identities, polarities, carrier K, and complementary singleton identities. Later R696/R527/payment descendants need not coexist.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert the P5 is spanning or current in a particular path cover. Does not claim the P5 alone closes H or moves a selected cut. Does not assert END/FREE/SANDWICH outcomes for the two boundary packets coexist in one cover, since they use separate support-deletion covers. Does not claim later packet descendants coexist. Does not supersede R700 or R522; it is their source-preserving composition.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** R768 terminates in generic P4/P5 manufacture and has no live consumers; R829 fences path manufacture as closure progress.
- **Curation note:** Order-free two-probe trimer amplifier: P4 or a Hamilton P5 carrying the simultaneous dual reverse-boundary packet.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Sound source-preserving composition of accepted R700 and R522. If either probe gives a P4, stop; otherwise both four-sets are no-P4, so R700 supplies the two common-witness reverse-boundary packets and R522 simultaneously supplies a Hamilton P5 on the same five vertices.

## Proof
Fix K=(a,b,c) and distinct outside probes y,z. Apply accepted R700. If one of its two R518 probe tests yields a Hamilton P4 on V(K) union {y} or V(K) union {z}, this is the P4 outcome. Otherwise both tests are in their no-P4 branches. R700 then gives its DUAL-CP conclusion: D_L=(b,a) is tail-signed by both y,z and D_R=(c,b) is head-signed by both y,z, with K as the common trimer carrier. Because neither four-set K union {y} nor K union {z} has a Hamilton P4, accepted R522 applies directly to the same tight trimer K and the two probes y,z and yields a literal graph-intrinsic tight Hamilton P5 on V(K) union {y,z}. The R522 construction does not alter the graph-intrinsic R700 sign certificates, so the P5 and both dual packet ledgers are simultaneously retained. This proves the stated P4-or-(P5+DUAL) alternative.

# R77 — Protection-birth eligibility predicate collapse

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement

The canonical protection theorem requires an actual capture descendant plus a designated quiet continuation. It does not require a separate abstract “eligibility” predicate.

## Scope
The strict-paid Type-E frame `S` is already an actual descendant of the fresh capture/payment ancestry and may be chosen as protection birth when a designated continuation is fixed.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** Historical protection-birth eligibility collapse; no live use remains.
- **Curation note:** Durable correction: protection requires an actual capture descendant plus designated continuation, not an abstract eligibility label.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Legacy migration verification: inherited independently accepted status from checksum-verified A7C2 continuity compression.

## Proof
Accepted reconstructible R42 states its protection hypothesis exactly: choose one actual capture descendant and one designated quiet continuation. From that point the captured physical anchor remains protected until the named target role is reached or the first later genuine event touching it is exposed. No additional abstract eligibility predicate appears among the hypotheses or is used in the proof.

Therefore any strict-paid Type-E frame, or any other frame, that is already an actual descendant of the relevant capture/payment ancestry may be chosen as the protection birth as soon as one designated continuation is fixed and the R42 retained-anchor datum is present. Conversely, merely satisfying some abstract label without an actual capture descendant would not meet R42. Thus the old separate eligibility predicate is logically redundant: protection birth is exactly the concrete R42 data of actual descendant plus chosen continuation. This is the R77 collapse statement.

# R770 — Internal-block puncture forces one-step path extension or a reverse endpoint contact

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Let H be a finite Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament with pc(H)>2, and let J=(j_0,j_1,...,j_r) be a proper vertex-simple tight path with r>=2 and nonempty exterior E=V(H)\\V(J). Put D={j_1,...,j_{r-1}} and S={j_0,j_r}. Suppose T is a literal exact two-cover of H-D. Since J is a tight path on exactly D union S, accepted R508 forces T to select a physical state with one endpoint in S and the other in E. Let h in E be the exterior endpoint. If the touched endpoint is j_0, boundary antisymmetry on {h,j_0,j_1} gives exactly one of (h,j_0,j_1) and (j_1,j_0,h) tight. In the first case (h,j_0,j_1,...,j_r) is a literal tight path extending J by one vertex at its head; in the second case (j_1,j_0,h) is a reverse head-contact trimer. If the touched endpoint is j_r, boundary antisymmetry on {j_{r-1},j_r,h} gives exactly one of (j_{r-1},j_r,h) and (h,j_r,j_{r-1}) tight. In the first case (j_0,...,j_r,h) extends J by one vertex at its tail; in the second case (h,j_r,j_{r-1}) is the dual reverse tail-contact trimer. Thus every supplied exact internal-block-deletion two-cover of a proper tight path yields either a one-vertex extension of that path or a named reverse endpoint contact. In a hypothetical smallest counterexample, D itself is a proper graph-intrinsic tight path (a singleton when r=2, otherwise the contiguous internal subpath), so accepted R4 supplies such an exact two-cover and the extension-or-reversal alternative is unconditional for every proper tight path.

## Hypotheses
Finite Strong Level-(1) boundary tournament H with pc(H)>2; J=(j_0,...,j_r) is a proper tight path with r>=2 and nonempty exterior; T is a supplied exact two-cover of H-{j_1,...,j_{r-1}}. For the unconditional smallest-counterexample corollary, use accepted R4.

## Scope
Order-free and path-length-free recompletion parent theorem. The local implication uses only R508 and R3 once the internal-block deletion cover is supplied. Minimality is used only through R4 to supply that cover. No longest-path assumption, R5,R168,R169,R224,R533,generic R358,R436,R312,Reverse Ear,or computation.

## Applicability
Use on any proper role-labelled tight path before invoking path-length-specific puncture lemmas. Repeated use gives a finite growth-or-reverse-contact process: successful branches strictly enlarge the physical path by one vertex; failure branches expose a graph-intrinsic reverse contact at a terminal physical dimer. R769 is the P5/internal-trimer specialization and should be read through this parent.

## Persistence
Retain J, its internal block D, endpoint pair S, exact cover T, selected endpoint-to-exterior crossing, touched endpoint, exterior vertex h, and resulting extended path or reverse endpoint-contact trimer. Selectedness is T-relative; the tight extension/contact is graph-intrinsic.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert which endpoint is touched, that both endpoints have crossings in one cover, that extension can continue indefinitely without a reverse-contact branch, or that a reverse endpoint contact alone closes H. Does not imply all exterior vertices reverse-contact a non-longest path; compare R199 for the globally longest universal shield.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** R770 is the old generic grow-until-reversal process. R829 makes path-length growth strategically noncanonical, and no live consumer remains.
- **Curation note:** Use the general internal-block puncture compiler rather than path-length-specific puncture lemmas unless a specialization carries genuinely additional structure.
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** Sound general parent. R508 applied to the internal-block deletion forces an endpoint-to-exterior selected state; one R3 test gives either one-vertex extension or the exact reverse endpoint contact. In a smallest counterexample R4 supplies the deletion two-cover because the internal block is itself a proper tight path.

## Proof
Let D={j_1,...,j_{r-1}}, S={j_0,j_r}, and E=V(H)\\V(J). Because r>=2, D is nonempty; because J is proper, E is nonempty. The path J is vertex-simple and tight and has vertex set exactly D union S. Hence accepted R508 applies to every exact two-cover T of H-D and forces a selected state crossing S|E. Let h be its E-endpoint. If the S-endpoint is j_0, apply R3 to {h,j_0,j_1}. Exactly one of (h,j_0,j_1) and (j_1,j_0,h) is tight. The former concatenates with all old turns of J to give the one-vertex head extension (h,j_0,j_1,...,j_r); the latter is the named reverse head contact. If the S-endpoint is j_r, apply R3 to {j_{r-1},j_r,h}. Exactly one of (j_{r-1},j_r,h) and (h,j_r,j_{r-1}) is tight. The former yields the one-vertex tail extension (j_0,...,j_r,h); the latter is the reverse tail contact. These cases exhaust the R508 crossing. In a hypothetical smallest counterexample, D is itself a proper graph-intrinsic tight path: for r=2 it is the singleton (j_1), and for r>=3 it is the contiguous tight subpath (j_1,...,j_{r-1}). Accepted R4 therefore gives an exact two-cover of H-D, making the alternative unconditional.

# R775 — The universal first-inward stars force a depth-two P5 or a cross-depth P4 on every X-pair

**Record status:** `USABLE/LEGACY`

## Statement
Retain the accepted crossed R621/R723 frame with X={a,b,c,z}, Q=(q_0,...,q_m), m>=4, and write u=q_1, v=q_2, d=q_{m-2}, s=q_{m-1}. Accepted R723 gives, for every x in X, the two tight first-inward trimers (v,u,x) and (x,s,d). Then exactly one of the following two regimes holds. (P5) For some x in X the middle turn (u,x,s) is tight. Then the three consecutive turns (v,u,x), (u,x,s), (x,s,d) certify the explicit tight Hamilton P5 J_x=(v,u,x,s,d) on {q_2,q_1,x,q_{m-1},q_{m-2}}. (CROSS-P4) For every x in X the reverse middle turn (s,x,u) is tight. In this regime, for every two distinct x,y in X, boundary antisymmetry on the triple {x,u,y} makes exactly one of (x,u,y) and (y,u,x) tight. If (x,u,y) is tight, then (s,x,u,y) is a tight P4; if (y,u,x) is tight, then (s,y,u,x) is a tight P4. Hence in the no-P5 regime every unordered X-pair supports a role-labelled cross-depth P4 containing both first-inward hinges q_{m-1} and q_1. Thus the universal first-inward stars cannot remain as four unrelated one-sided trimers: they assemble either into a depth-two two-ended P5 through one X vertex or into a complete pair-indexed family of cross-depth P4s through q_{m-1},q_1.

## Hypotheses
H lies in the accepted crossed R621/R723 frame; m>=4; X has four vertices disjoint from Q. Uses accepted R723 and boundary antisymmetry R3.

## Scope
Pure accepted-input first-inward geometry. No minimality beyond the standing frame, no deletion cover, R5,R168,R169,R224,R533,R350,generic R358,R508,R527,R542,R312,R436,floor steering,Reverse Ear,five-cell classification,or computation.

## Applicability
Use before any capture/contact or pair-deletion recompletion. The P5 branch is an explicit two-ended depth-two path containing q_2 and q_{m-2}. In the complementary regime, choose an X-pair with a useful matching-layer role and retain the corresponding cross-depth P4. This route is independent of pending R772/R774, though those results retain compatible first-inward hinge ancestry.

## Persistence
In P5 retain x and the exact three turns (v,u,x),(u,x,s),(x,s,d). In CROSS-P4 retain the universal reverse turns (s,x,u) for all x and, for each chosen pair {x,y}, the exact R3 winner at middle u and the resulting labelled P4 order. All outputs are graph-intrinsic.

## Exclusions / nonclaims
Does not assert the P5 or P4 is spanning, current in a cover, or alone closes H. Does not assert the CROSS-P4 regime is impossible. Does not use the matching-height order of X beyond the availability of distinct vertices; a downstream consumer may choose a pair according to M_R,M_S,M_L. Does not claim a physical cut has moved yet.

## Record notes
- **Lifecycle:** retired
- **Lifecycle note:** R775 is valid frame-specific P4/P5 abundance but has no live or pending consumers; R829 fences treating such path manufacture as closure progress. Preserve historically. 
- **Review status:** accepted
- **Review note:** PASS. For each x, R3 on {q_1,x,q_{m-1}} gives exactly one forward or reverse middle turn. Any forward turn concatenates with the two accepted R723 first-inward stars to the stated vertex-simple P5. If no forward turn exists, all reverse middle turns hold. For any distinct x,y, R3 on {x,q_1,y} selects exactly one order, which concatenates with the corresponding reverse middle turn to the stated cross-depth P4. The dichotomy is exhaustive and mutually exclusive and uses only accepted R3,R723.

## Proof
For every x in X, accepted R723 gives (v,u,x) and (x,s,d) tight. Apply R3 to the triple {u,x,s}. Exactly one of (u,x,s) and (s,x,u) is tight. If the first occurs for some x, the vertex-simple order (v,u,x,s,d) has consecutive tight turns (v,u,x), (u,x,s), (x,s,d), proving P5. Suppose no x has (u,x,s) tight. Then (s,x,u) is tight for every x in X. Fix distinct x,y. Apply R3 to {x,u,y}; exactly one of (x,u,y),(y,u,x) is tight. In the first case, (s,x,u) and (x,u,y) certify P4 (s,x,u,y). In the second, (s,y,u) and (y,u,x) certify P4 (s,y,u,x). Since x,y were arbitrary, every unordered X-pair has such a cross-depth P4. This proves the dichotomy.
