# R846 WEAVE has forced ancestral crossings and a boundary-complete restoration ledger

**Workspace:** D17
**State:** established
**Key:** `directed-triangle-r846-weave-restoration`

**Summary:** In an R846 WEAVE, the double-DIRECT double-blocked trapped bridge is now a finite exact transition system. Third-label holonomy first gives either a same-five-support selected reversal with strict R548 transport toward R561, or one selected-dimer continuation fan. The DIRECT siblings trim to a common visible complement forest, and R508 forces current complement crossings out of c and the surviving U/V pieces. A c-boundary P5 plus R548 moves the actual c-rail monotonically to a matching boundary; the forced one-hole splice failure reverses the current c-x state, and one further turn gives R561 on Y+{x} or complete one-sided boundary inaccessibility. Crucially, that locked c-boundary now has two explicit lifts to the pair-deletion residue H-{u,v}: a forward lift preserving the current c-x orientation and a reverse lift using the triangle P4. Each has at most two new seams. Simultaneous success gives two exact representatives with the SAME enlarged active support and IDENTICAL Hamilton complement B selecting {c,x} oppositely, exactly currentizing the fixed-complement reversal input. One-sided success is a strict codimension-four to codimension-two representative transition. Only simultaneous failure of both complete lift windows remains, with all physical seams and predecessor/successor ancestry retained. No generic payment is used. The short boundary-currentization residue sharpens further: if the current complement rail J has only three vertices, its enlarged active support is Y plus two exterior vertices and is Hamiltonian by R887/R902, so an exact H-{u,v} representative exists even when both named lift windows fail. Hence the genuinely double-blocked two-window residue requires |J|>=4. Opposite R548 rotations of the current c-rail sharpen the simultaneous-wrap-failure branch: |J|=2 gives the opposite dimer order for free; for |J|=3 a failed opposite rotation is itself a spanning reverse trimer; and for |J|=4 double wrap failure gives a reverse P4 spanning all of J. For complement rails of order at most four, double-wrap failure gives a genuine same-support/common-complement c-x reversal, while a successful wrap is only a reversible exact representative change until separately consumed. In the simultaneous-wrap-failure branch, any long state not already reversed has |J|>=5, a nonempty middle M, and a reverse-boundary P4 K with TWO explicit original-J crossing edges between K and M. These named crossings, not anonymous R159 currency, are the next interface. In the smallest |J|=5 survivor, deterministic first-bad cuts of the forward and reverse blocked lifts give two literal three-covers of H-{u,v} with common B. Their common active refinement has 3 or 4 blocks and always contains {c,x} as one block. Any exact pair-deletion two-cover therefore has at least 2 or 3 coarse selected transitions. If it does not mix B with the active support, one obtains an exact B-retaining codimension-two representative. If it has no edge leaving {c,x}, then {c,x} is an entire dimer rail and free reversal plus R561 restores one deleted vertex, giving a codimension-one exact representative. Hence the remaining bounded hard cell has, in one actual pair-deletion cover, both a B-to-active support-transfer edge and a current edge leaving {c,x}, plus at least one further coarse transition. This is kept as a physical portal, not paid through R176. Paired cyclic-tail lifts sharpen the long lock further: if either succeeds, H-{u,v} gains an exact representative with literal B; if both fail, exhaustive triangle order control propagates the one-sided Hamilton-boundary obstruction from the current c-x edge to the preceding selected J-edge d-x. This is a physical one-edge lock movement, not generic packet currency, and is stated only as one-step propagation rather than an automatic iteration. In F1G1, choosing an exact H-{u,v} representative with minimum coarse transition count t across A={a,b}, P={j0,j1,m}, Q={c,x}, B completely consumes the equality case t=2. Equality makes all four blocks contiguous. A 3+1 shape isolating A gives codim-1 by free dimer reversal plus R561; isolating the trimer P gives codim-1 or closure by probing P+u and P+v and using R522 if both are P4-free. The three 2+2 pairings are exact block-transfer exits: B+A | J preserves the current x-c rail; B+P | (a,b,c,x) currentizes reverse c-x; B+Q | (A+P) moves the c-x block into the B-side and solves the missing A-P support. Thus only strict excess transition t>=3 remains, forcing physical fragmentation of A,P,Q,or B in a transition-minimal representative.

### 1. Setup inside the current R846 WEAVE branch
Retain Section 7 of `directed-triangle-two-rail-absorption`. Fix one reverse triangle dimer

  D=(p,q)=(y_{i+1},y_i),

and let y=y_{i+2} be the third triangle vertex. Thus the three cyclic Hamilton orders of Y are

  (q,p,y),   (p,y,q),   (y,q,p).

In the all-role-trapped branch accepted R846 gives, among its alternatives, an exact WEAVE cover T of H-D. Its two starts are exactly a_0,b_0, its two ends exactly a_p,b_q, and y is internal on one T rail. Orient that rail as

  S=(s,...,u,y,v,...,t),

and the other rail as C=(s',...,t'). Put

  U=(s,...,u),   V=(v,...,t).

Deleting y gives the literal three-cover

  R=U|V|C

of W=H-Y, while ancestral A|B is an exact two-cover of the same W.

### 2. The WEAVE endpoint pairing forces named ancestral crossings
The generic component-count argument already shows that some selected adjacency of A|B crosses two R-components. The endpoint pairing identifies more.

**Parallel pairing.** Suppose the WEAVE rails join a_0 to a_p and b_0 to b_q. If y lies on the a_0-to-a_p rail, then a_0 is in U and a_p is in V. Since A=(a_0,...,a_p) is connected, reading A from a_0 to a_p gives a first selected adjacency whose endpoints lie in distinct R-components. Thus A contains a physically named R-crossing. If y lies on the b_0-to-b_q rail, the dual statement holds for B. No claim is made that the other ancestral rail has no crossing.

**Crossed pairing.** Suppose the WEAVE rails join a_0 to b_q and b_0 to a_p, and y lies on the first one; the other cases are exact duals. Then a_0 is in U, b_q is in V, and b_0,a_p are both in C. Hence A starts in U and ends in C, so A contains a selected R-crossing. Likewise B starts in C and ends in V, so B contains a selected R-crossing. Therefore a crossed WEAVE forces two ancestral crossing lineages simultaneously, one selected edge of A and one selected edge of B.

For each retained crossing xy, accepted R176 may be reconstructed with R as the larger cover and A|B as the smaller cover. Its proof retains xy and an actual old R-neighbor of one crossing endpoint when that R-component is nontrivial. This provenance is retained; the balanced-pair descendant is not the progress claim here.

### 3. Boundary-complete restoration ledger
The previous version of this section claimed that replacing the internal vertex y by a cyclic Hamilton order of Y created only two new turns. That is true only when u and v are respectively the source and terminal of the whole S-rail. In general a 3-uniform tight path also sees one turn farther out on each side. We record the complete ledger.

If u has a predecessor on S, call it r. If v has a successor on S, call it w. Thus, when they exist, the retained T turns

  (r,u,y),   (y,v,w)

are tight. Replace y by the three cyclic Hamilton orders of Y. The genuinely new turns are:

  row 0, order (p,y,q):
    (r,u,p) if r exists,
    (u,p,y),
    (y,q,v),
    (q,v,w) if w exists;

  row 1, order (q,p,y):
    (r,u,q) if r exists,
    (u,q,p),
    (p,y,v),
    while (y,v,w) is inherited if w exists;

  row 2, order (y,q,p):
    (r,u,y) is inherited if r exists,
    (u,y,q),
    (q,p,v),
    (p,v,w) if w exists.                                  (WR.1)

The internal Y-turn in each row is tight by the directed-triangle order. If every genuinely new turn of one row were tight, that row would replace y by all of Y in S while leaving the other WEAVE rail C untouched, giving a literal spanning two-cover of H. Hence every row of (WR.1) contains a bad genuinely new turn.

Call the four possible one-step-farther turns

  L_p=(r,u,p),  L_q=(r,u,q)          when r exists,
  R_p=(p,v,w),  R_q=(q,v,w)          when w exists             (WR.2)

the OUTER restoration seams.

If an outer seam is bad, R3 gives an exact triangle-labelled reversal of an ACTUAL selected T-state:

  L_p bad => (p,u,r) tight,
  L_q bad => (q,u,r) tight,
  R_p bad => (w,v,p) tight,
  R_q bad => (w,v,q) tight.                                (WR.3)

Thus an outer failure is not anonymous payment. It reverses the selected T-state r-u or v-w inside a displayed tight trimer, with the omitted triangle vertex p or q as the retained witness.

Assume now that every relevant outer seam in (WR.2) is tight. Then the only uncertified turns in the three spanning restoration proposals are exactly the six central turns

  row 0: (u,p,y) and (y,q,v),
  row 1: (u,q,p) and (p,y,v),
  row 2: (u,y,q) and (q,p,v).                              (WR.4)

Consequently every row of (WR.4) contains a bad turn. This is the genuine 3-by-2 central restoration matrix, but it is valid only after the outer-clean test above.

The outer-clean branch carries additional physical signs. If r exists, then

  (r,u,p), (r,u,q), (r,u,y)

are all tight, the last being inherited from T. Hence the actual selected dimer (r,u) is tail-signed by all three vertices of Y. If w exists, then

  (p,v,w), (q,v,w), (y,v,w)

are all tight, so the actual selected dimer (v,w) is head-signed by all three vertices of Y. Thus every depth-two side of an outer-clean WEAVE already carries a uniform three-witness packet on a CURRENT selected T-boundary state.

Boundary cases are literal. If u is the source of its T-rail, there are no left outer seams. If v is the terminal, there are no right outer seams. If S=(u,y,v) is the whole rail, both outer families are absent and (WR.4) is exactly the complete restoration ledger.

### 4. Correct hard WEAVE interface
The crossed pairing remains the strongest ancestry cell: one actual selected R-crossing on each ancestral rail A and B. The parallel pairing retains a forced crossing on the ancestral rail whose endpoints are separated by y. In either pairing the SAME exact WEAVE T now has the following proof-correct dichotomy before generic R159/R176 payment:

1. **OUTER-REVERSAL.** Some outer restoration seam fails, producing one of the exact current-cover reversals (WR.3) of the selected T-state adjacent to the y-slot. Retain the physical selected edge, its orientation in T, the omitted Y-witness, the full WEAVE cover, and the ancestral crossing ledger.

2. **OUTER-CLEAN.** Every relevant outer seam is tight. Then the central matrix (WR.4) is genuinely complete, and every depth-two side adjacent to y is uniformly signed by all three Y vertices on its actual selected T-dimer. Retain those selected dimers, all three witnesses, all six central seam truth values, the complete T order, and the ancestral crossings.

No spanning two-cover, R561 support, or strict representative descent is asserted merely from this dichotomy. The intended next consumer must couple the ancestral crossing with the current selected-state reversal in OUTER-REVERSAL, or with the uniform selected-boundary signs plus complete central matrix in OUTER-CLEAN. Generic R159/R176 payment remains downstream of this reconstruction data.


### 5. OUTER-CLEAN accessibility collapses to singleton transport, a trapped reverse bridge, or two uniform states
Index the directed triangle cyclically as

  z_0=p,  z_1=y,  z_2=q,

so pi_i=(z_i,z_{i+1},z_{i+2}) is tight for every i modulo 3. In the OUTER-CLEAN branch define

  L_i = 1 iff (u,z_i,z_{i+1}) is tight,
  R_i = 1 iff (z_{i+1},z_{i+2},v) is tight.              (WR.5)

These are exactly the left and right role-accessibility bits of the complete central matrix (WR.4). Counterexamplehood gives

  L_i R_i = 0 for every i,                                (WR.6)

because L_i=R_i=1 would replace y by the whole cyclic order pi_i and restore H in the two WEAVE rails.

The useful comparison is the cross-index pair (L_i,R_{i-1}).

#### 5.1 Good-good cross-index pair gives an actual singleton-deletion representative
Suppose

  L_i=R_{i-1}=1.                                          (WR.7)

Since R_{i-1}=1 is exactly (z_i,z_{i+1},v) tight, replace the local T segment

  ... r,u,y,v,w ...

by

  ... r,u,z_i,z_{i+1},v,w ... .                           (WR.8)

Every required turn is certified. The two central turns are (WR.7); if r exists then (r,u,z_i) is either inherited when z_i=y or one of the OUTER-CLEAN left seams, and if w exists then (z_{i+1},v,w) is either inherited when z_{i+1}=y or one of the OUTER-CLEAN right seams. Boundary cases require no absent turn. Hence the modified S-rail is tight.

Its vertex set is exactly the old T-rail vertex set with the single internal label y replaced by the two labels z_i,z_{i+1}. Therefore, together with the untouched WEAVE rail C, it is a literal spanning two-cover

  T_i^+ of H-z_{i+2}.                                     (WR.9)

It is exact: H-z_{i+2} cannot be Hamiltonian, since a Hamilton path there together with singleton {z_{i+2}} would two-cover H. Thus (WR.7) is not merely a seam success. It is an ACTUAL neighboring-fiber representative transition.

Two of the three switches currentize directly back to the original pair-deletion WEAVE. If {z_i,z_{i+1}} contains y and one deleted label d in {p,q}, puncturing d from T_i^+ gives a literal three-cover of H-{p,q}. If the local order is u-d-y-v, the original T selected state u-y crosses the two split pieces; if the local order is u-y-d-v, the original selected state y-v does so. Thus the singleton switch carries an exact named component-crossing state of the ORIGINAL WEAVE upon return to its pair-deletion fiber. The third switch, with {z_i,z_{i+1}}={p,q}, is a genuine rotation to the H-y singleton fiber.

#### 5.2 Bad-bad cross-index pair is an exactly trapped reverse bridge
Suppose instead

  L_i=R_{i-1}=0.                                          (WR.10)

R3 reverses the two failed turns to

  (z_{i+1},z_i,u),   (v,z_{i+1},z_i) tight,

so

  K_i=(v,z_{i+1},z_i,u)                                   (WR.11)

is a literal tight reverse bridge across the physical u|v slot. OUTER-CLEAN makes this bridge exactly two-ended trapped. If r exists, (r,u,z_i) is tight, so its complete reverse (z_i,u,r), the unique turn needed to append the old left continuation after K_i, is bad. If w exists, (z_{i+1},v,w) is tight, so (w,v,z_{i+1}), the unique turn needed to prepend the old right continuation before K_i, is bad. Thus (WR.11) records a physical reversal of the local u-to-v role whose two natural reattachments are both explicitly blocked by the SAME outer-clean data.

#### 5.3 No switch and no reverse bridge forces a uniform extreme
Assume no i satisfies (WR.7) and no i satisfies (WR.10). Then each cross-index pair has opposite truth values, so

  R_{i-1}=1-L_i for every i.                              (WR.12)

Equivalently R_j=1-L_{j+1}. Combine this with (WR.6). If some L_j=1, then R_j=0, hence L_{j+1}=1 by (WR.12); cycling forces all three L_i=1 and all three R_i=0. If no L_j=1, all L_i=0 and (WR.12) forces all R_i=1. Therefore the complete OUTER-CLEAN accessibility state has the exact trichotomy

  SINGLETON-SWITCH: some L_i=R_{i-1}=1, producing (WR.9);
  REVERSE-BRIDGE: some L_i=R_{i-1}=0, producing the trapped (WR.11);
  UNIFORM: L=Z_3,R=empty or L=empty,R=Z_3.                (WR.13)

In particular every nonuniform accessibility pattern contains an actual neighboring-fiber transition or a named two-ended blocked reversal. There is no residual raw six-bit matrix.

### 6. The two uniform extremes are maximal one-sided boundary fans, not local R561
In the uniform state L=Z_3,R=empty, all three paths

  (u,z_i,z_{i+1},z_{i+2})

are tight, while R3 turns every failed R_i into

  (v,z_{i+2},z_{i+1}) tight.                              (WR.14)

Thus u has all three role-correct cyclic accesses and v head-signs all three reverse Y-dimers. If r exists, OUTER-CLEAN prepends r to every left access, giving three Hamilton P5s on {r,u} union Y beginning with the ACTUAL selected state (r,u). At the same time no Hamilton path on this five-support can end with the reverse state (u,r): its penultimate vertex would be some z in Y and would require (z,u,r), but OUTER-CLEAN has (r,u,z) tight and hence (z,u,r) bad by R3. So the local five-support is maximally one-sided at (r,u); chasing R561 on that same boundary dimer is provably blocked.

Dually, in L=empty,R=Z_3, v has all three role-correct cyclic exits and u tail-signs all three reverse Y-dimers. If w exists there are three Hamilton P5s on Y union {v,w} ending with the ACTUAL selected state (v,w), while no Hamilton path on that support can begin with (w,v), because every required (w,v,z) is the reverse of the OUTER-CLEAN tight turn (z,v,w).

Therefore the remaining transition-free OUTER-CLEAN states are two explicit one-sided boundary fans. Any further progress must use the retained ancestral A/B crossing(s), another deletion fiber, or a larger support; the selected adjacent five-support itself cannot supply the missing R561 reverse boundary state.

### 7. OUTER-CLEAN synchronizes all three pair-deletion fibers over one fixed punctured base
There is a still simpler transition test that uses only the OUTER-CLEAN seams. For each z in Y test

  M_z=(u,z,v).                                             (WR.15)

Exactly one of M_z and its complete reverse (v,z,u) is tight by R3.

If M_z is tight, replace the current local segment u-y-v by u-z-v and leave every other vertex order unchanged. If r exists, the required turn (r,u,z) is either inherited for z=y or is OUTER-CLEAN; if w exists, (z,v,w) is likewise inherited or OUTER-CLEAN. Hence

is a literal two-cover of

It is exact. If H-(Y-{z}) were Hamiltonian, the two deleted vertices form a vacuous tight dimer path, so H would have a spanning two-cover. Puncturing z from T_z recovers exactly the SAME three-cover

  R=U|V|C of H-Y                                          (WR.18)

for every successful z. Thus every successful direct test produces a sibling exact pair-deletion representative over one fixed component base, with the same untouched rail C, the same U and V orders, the same four WEAVE endpoints, and the same ancestral A/B crossing ledger. The original WEAVE T is precisely the z=y member of this family.

If M_z is bad, R3 gives instead the literal reverse trimer

  (v,z,u) tight.                                          (WR.19)

Therefore the complete OUTER-CLEAN pair-fiber interface is a three-bit DIRECT/REVERSE star on the identical physical slot u|v:

This is stronger than treating the three reverse-Y-dimer R846 applications independently. If two vertices a,b in Y lie in the DIRECT branch, then (u,a,v) and (u,b,v) are both tight. R3 on {a,u,b} chooses exactly one of (a,u,b),(b,u,a), so one of

  (a,u,b,v),  (b,u,a,v)                                  (WR.21)

is a literal tight P4. If two vertices a,b lie in the REVERSE branch, then (v,a,u),(v,b,u) are tight; the same R3 test gives one of

  (v,a,u,b),  (v,b,u,a)                                  (WR.22)

as a literal tight P4. Thus multiplicity on either side of the DIRECT/REVERSE star already has a labelled four-vertex realization, while every DIRECT representative continues to puncture to the same R.

The remaining high-value consumer is now concrete: compare sibling DIRECT lifts, or a DIRECT lift against a REVERSE-slot trimer, while retaining the fixed ancestral crossing(s) of A|B across R. A transition that changes the first ancestral crossing location, reverses one selected slot boundary on a common support, or lowers deletion codimension is legitimate progress; exporting the star as generic signed-pair currency is not.

### 8. Every DIRECT sibling has a real outer boundary; a one-sided sibling is a rigid tau=1 absorber cell
Fix a DIRECT label z, so T_z=(U,z,V)|C is the exact sibling cover from (WR.16). Put

  D_z=Y-{z},
  S_z={u,z,v},
  C_z=V(H)-(D_z union S_z).                               (WR.23)

The five-set D_z union S_z=Y union {u,v} is Hamiltonian by the directed-triangle five-Hamiltonicity. Apply accepted R508 with deletion D_z, absorbable block S_z, and exact cover T_z. Every exact T_z must select an S_z|C_z state.

In the displayed sibling cover the only possible such selected states are physical slot-boundary states: r-u when r exists, and v-w when w exists. The vertex z has only u,v as T_z-neighbors, and the untouched rail C contains no S_z vertex. Therefore

  at least one of r or w exists.                           (WR.24)

In particular the lifted rail can never be exactly the three-vertex path (u,z,v). This removes the both-boundaries-absent case from WR.1-WR.4.

If exactly one outer side exists, T_z has exactly one S_z|C_z transition, so accepted R570 applies. It gives

  H-{u,z,v} is non-Hamiltonian.                            (WR.25)

Moreover the unique boundary role is rigid outside the explicit R570 collision/R435 outputs. The proof-aware R573 form sharpens this against OUTER-CLEAN.

- LEFT-ONLY: r exists and w does not. The unique transition is r-u from C_z into S_z. If a Hamilton path of X=Y union {u,v} starts (u,h), R573 forces (h,u,r) tight. For h in Y this contradicts OUTER-CLEAN, which has (r,u,h) tight and therefore (h,u,r) bad. Hence any Hamilton path of X starting at u, if one exists at all, must start with the single possible non-Y successor v. Outside the R570 interaction outputs there is at most one such Hamilton path.

- RIGHT-ONLY: w exists and r does not. The unique transition is v-w from S_z into C_z. If a Hamilton path of X ends (h,v), R573 forces (w,v,h) tight. For h in Y this contradicts OUTER-CLEAN tightness of (h,v,w). Hence any Hamilton path of X ending at v, if one exists, must have the single possible non-Y predecessor u. Again, outside the R570 interaction outputs there is at most one such Hamilton path.

Thus every DIRECT sibling is either TWO-SIDED at the physical slot, or is a genuine tau=1 absorber cell whose only possible exterior boundary accessibility on X is through the oriented dimer u-v. Five-Hamiltonicity alone does not guarantee that this u/v endpoint family is nonempty, so no endpoint-accessibility conclusion is added.

### 9. One-sided DIRECT siblings have zero role-correct absorber-boundary access
Retain a DIRECT label z and the five-vertex Hamilton absorber support

  X=Y union {u,v}.

Section 8 showed, using accepted R573 against the OUTER-CLEAN seams, that in a LEFT-ONLY sibling every Hamilton path of X starting at u would have to begin with the ordered dimer (u,v). The all-role-trapped ancestry eliminates even this last possibility. In LEFT-ONLY the successor w does not exist, so v is the terminal t of the original WEAVE rail S. Hence v is one of the ancestral terminals a_p,b_q. If a Hamilton path of X began

  (u,v,...),

then deleting its first vertex u would leave a Hamilton P4 on Y union {v} STARTING at v. But Section 6 of the parent directed-triangle normal form defines the terminal role trap precisely by absence of such a role-correct P4. Therefore

  LEFT-ONLY DIRECT => no Hamilton path of X starts at u.       (WR.26)

The dual is exact. In RIGHT-ONLY the predecessor r does not exist, so u is the source s of the original WEAVE rail and therefore u is one of a_0,b_0. Section 8 says any Hamilton path of X ending at v would have to end with (u,v). Deleting v would leave a Hamilton P4 on Y union {u} ENDING at u, forbidden by the ancestral source role trap. Thus

  RIGHT-ONLY DIRECT => no Hamilton path of X ends at v.        (WR.27)

This sharpens the generic R570 zero-or-one boundary statement to literal ZERO in the inherited role-correct boundary direction. It does not claim that X is non-Hamiltonian: five-Hamiltonicity still guarantees Hamilton paths on X, but none may use the forbidden ancestral boundary role.

### 10. A DIRECT label gates every trapped reverse bridge into R561 or an exact named blocker
Return to a trapped reverse bridge from (WR.11). Write

  a=z_i,  b=z_{i+1},

Thus K is Hamilton on the four-support {u,v,a,b} and ends with the ordered dimer (a,u), while it begins with (v,b).

  (u,a,v) tight.                                              (WR.29)

Test the single turn

is Hamilton on the SAME four-support as K. It begins with (u,a), while K ends with the reverse state (a,u). Accepted R561 therefore applies literally to this four-support. If gamma is bad, R3 retains the exact blocker

Dually, suppose b is DIRECT, so (u,b,v) is tight. Test

If delta is tight, then

is Hamilton on the same four-support, ending with (b,v), while K begins with the reverse state (v,b). Again R561 applies literally. If delta is bad, R3 gives the exact blocker

These select the physical edge {u,b} in opposite directions. Hence the double-blocked two-DIRECT bridge carries a genuine FULL-SUPPORT selected-edge reversal on the four-set. ### 11. The double-DIRECT double-blocked bridge has a third-label complement descent
Retain the hard cell at the end of Section 10. Write cyclically

  a=z_i,  b=z_{i+1},  c=z_{i+2}.

Thus the trapped bridge is (v,b,a,u), both a and b are DIRECT, and both one-turn R561 gates block. In particular

  (u,a,v), (u,b,v), (b,v,a), (b,u,a)

are tight, and Section 10 gives the two Hamilton P4 orders

  U^o=U-u,   V^o=V-v.

on W=H-X, with empty U^o or V^o terms omitted. Thus the visible complement is independent of whether the a- or b-sibling is used.

Accepted R4 applied to either Hamilton P4 in (WR.37) gives pc(W)=2 exactly. Fix any actual exact complement cover

  J | B                                                   (WR.39)

of W, naming J as the rail containing c. Three source-specific R508 obligations are present before any component-drop payment. is a literal tight path on X union U^o: its only junction beyond inherited turns is the OUTER-CLEAN turn (r,u,b). Hence every exact complement cover crosses U^o. Dually, whenever V^o is nonempty,

is tight, using the OUTER-CLEAN turn (a,v,w), so every exact complement cover crosses V^o. Therefore the complement portal is not an arbitrary component-count edge: the same exact representative has forced selected transitions out of {c}, U^o when present, and V^o when present.

has every turn certified except

  B_c bad => (u,b,v,a,c) tight.                            (WR.45)

For (WR.44), use c as a desired TERMINAL of its current complement rail J. If c is not terminal, apply the R548 head rotation of J, which moves c one position toward the terminal boundary. Every successful rotation is an ACTUAL exact two-cover of the same W and decreases the nonnegative terminal distance of c by exactly one. If a required wrap turn fails, stop with the exact R548 reverse-wrap shield attached to that current J representative. The dimer case is covered by R548: reversing the two-vertex rail moves c to the opposite boundary for free. Thus, absent a wrap shield, finitely many exact representative transitions reach

Now append b,u,a,v to J. By (WR.44), (WR.32), and DIRECTness of a, the only new turn is

If it were tight, the enlarged J together with the untouched complement rail B would two-cover H. Therefore (WR.47) is bad, and R3 gives

Together with the cyclic triangle turn (a,b,c), this yields the literal endpoint-labelled P4

  (a,b,c,x).                                               (WR.49)

The current complement boundary state is x->c in J, while (WR.49) realizes the same physical pair in the reverse local order c->x; retain J, B, x, its old predecessor window, and the full R548 rotation ancestry.

Dually, for (WR.45) use c as a desired SOURCE. Repeated successful R548 tail rotations strictly decrease its source distance, while a failed rotation gives the exact named wrap shield. Absent such a shield one reaches

Prepending u,b,v,a to J has only the new turn (a,c,x). Tightness would close H with B, so it is bad and R3 gives (x,c,a). Since (c,a,b) is a cyclic triangle turn,

  (x,c,a,b)                                                (WR.51)

is a literal endpoint-labelled P4. Again its local c-x order reverses the ACTUAL selected boundary state c->x of the current complement rail.

Consequently the double-DIRECT double-blocked trapped bridge has a well-founded exact-complement consumer before generic payment: choose either available c-boundary P5 from (WR.44)-(WR.45), rotate the CURRENT c-rail toward the matching boundary, and obtain either a strict exact representative transition at every successful step, an exact R548 wrap shield, or a boundary-anchored triangle P4 reversing the actual current c-neighbor state. The terminal P4 is not by itself a fixed-complement selected reversal, because its support differs from J. Its value is the retained physical c-x reversal together with the exact complement representative and rotation ancestry; the next splice must use that current support rather than export (WR.49)/(WR.51) as anonymous P4 currency.


### 12. The boundary-anchored complement reversal has a one-turn R561 gate
The terminal P4s (WR.49) and (WR.51) are not merely generic four-vertex outputs. Their missing opposite boundary role is decided by one turn on the SAME physical c-x support.

First suppose the complement descent ends at

  J=(...,x,c)

and hence (WR.49) gives

a Hamilton P4 on Y union {x} ending with (c,x). Test

If G_T is tight, then

is Hamilton on the SAME support and begins with the reverse ordered dimer (x,c). Accepted R561 therefore applies literally to Y union {x}. This is genuine full-support R561, with the physical boundary state inherited from the actual complement rail J.

If G_T is bad, R3 gives

  (a,c,x) tight.                                           (WR.55)

The preceding one-hole absorption failure already gave (b,c,x) tight in (WR.48), so both a and b now certify the same reverse local orientation c->x of the actual selected J-boundary support {c,x}. More strongly, NO Hamilton P4 on Y union {x} begins with (x,c). The only two possible continuations after x,c use the remaining labels a,b. The order (x,c,a,b) is blocked by G_T, while (x,c,b,a) contains the directed-triangle reverse turn (c,b,a), which is bad because (a,b,c) is tight. Thus the failure branch is an exact one-sided boundary lock, not merely absence of the displayed R561 witness.

The source case is dual. If the descent ends at

  J=(c,x,...)

then (WR.51) gives

which begins with the reverse of the selected J state c->x. Test

  G_S=(b,c,x).                                             (WR.57)

If G_S is tight, the cyclic triangle turn (a,b,c) gives

  P_end=(a,b,c,x),                                         (WR.58)

so accepted R561 again applies on Y union {x}. If G_S is bad, R3 gives (x,c,b) tight; together with the already retained (x,c,a) from (WR.51), the reverse local orientation x->c has two named Y witnesses. Moreover no Hamilton P4 on Y union {x} ends with (c,x): the order (a,b,c,x) is blocked by G_S, while the only other ordering (b,a,c,x) contains the bad reverse triangle turn (b,a,c), since (c,a,b) is tight.

Therefore every wrap-shield-free double-DIRECT complement descent terminates at

  OR an exact one-sided Hamilton-boundary lock on the reverse of the CURRENT selected c-x support, carrying both remaining Y labels as named same-orientation witnesses.             (WR.59)

The locked branch should be consumed with the retained complement rail J and its predecessor/successor window. It must not be spent as an anonymous same-polarity packet: the useful information is that J selects one c-x direction while the opposite direction is graph-intrinsically realized but cannot occur as the corresponding Hamilton boundary of Y union {x}.


### 13. Before entering the complement, the third-label holonomy gives a five-support reversal or one selected-dimer continuation fan

### 14. A locked c-boundary has two explicit lifts to H-{u,v}; simultaneous success currentizes the common complement
Retain a wrap-shield-free terminal of Section 12 in the one-sided-lock branch, together with its exact complement cover J|B of

  W=H-{u,v,a,b}.

The active objective is now to restore a,b while leaving u,v deleted. This raises the current representative from codimension four to the pair-deletion residue H-{u,v}. The locked triangle P4 supplies one lift, while the literal J order supplies an opposite-orientation lift.

#### 14.1 Terminal c-boundary
Suppose

  J=(j_0,...,j_{r-1}=x,j_r=c),   r>=1,                    (WR.68)

so J selects x->c, while Section 12 retains the reverse-boundary Hamilton P4

  (a,b,c,x).                                               (WR.69)

There are two complete reconstruction words on the SAME enlarged support V(J) union {a,b}.

**Forward lift, preserving x->c.** Put

  F_T=(a,b,j_0,j_1,...,j_r).                              (WR.70)

Every old J turn is inherited. Its complete new-turn window is exactly

  f_1=(a,b,j_0),
  f_2=(b,j_0,j_1).                                        (WR.71)

The second turn exists because J is non-singleton, forced already by R508. If both are tight, F_T|B is a literal two-cover of H-{u,v}; it is exact, because a Hamilton path on H-{u,v} together with the vacuous dimer {u,v} would two-cover H. The selected boundary state x->c survives unchanged.

**Reverse lift, selecting c->x.** Remove the terminal pair x,c from the displayed J order and append the locked P4 (WR.69). If r=1 this is simply

  R_T=(a,b,c,x),                                          (WR.72a)

with no new junction turn. If r=2,

  R_T=(j_0,a,b,c,x),                                      (WR.72b)

has the single new turn (j_0,a,b). If r>=3, put

  R_T=(j_0,...,j_{r-2},a,b,c,x),                          (WR.72c)

whose complete new-turn window is

  g_1=(j_{r-3},j_{r-2},a),
  g_2=(j_{r-2},a,b).                                      (WR.73)

All later turns are the cyclic triangle turn (a,b,c) and the retained lock turn (b,c,x). Thus whenever its existing window is tight, R_T|B is another exact two-cover of H-{u,v}, on the IDENTICAL support partition as F_T|B and with the SAME literal Hamilton complement B, but selecting the physical state c->x opposite to F_T.

Consequently:
- if both F_T and R_T succeed, the pair-deletion fiber H-{u,v} contains two exact representatives with identical active support and literal complement B that select {c,x} oppositely. This is precisely the full currentization hypothesis required by the fixed-complement selected-reversal consumer; no support or complement identification remains implicit.
- if exactly one succeeds, it is already an ACTUAL neighboring-fiber representative transition from W to H-{u,v}, reducing deletion codimension from four to two while retaining B and the physical c-x ancestry.
- if neither succeeds, each of the two displayed COMPLETE seam windows contains a bad turn.   J=(j_0=c,j_1=x,...,j_r),   r>=1,                        (WR.74)

so J selects c->x and the retained reverse-boundary P4 is

with complete new-turn window

with the single new turn (a,b,j_2). If r>=3,

#### 14.3 The five-vertex short support eliminates r=2 double blocking
There is one further automatic short-support collapse. Suppose r=2 in either the terminal or source construction. Then the enlarged active support of the two lift tests has exactly five vertices and is

where Y={a,b,c} is the retained directed comparison triangle and j is the unique remaining J-vertex outside {x,c}. By accepted R887, the directed comparison triangle makes the induced five-vertex boundary tournament on Z_5 nonintegrable. Accepted R902 says every nonintegrable five-vertex boundary tournament is Hamiltonian. Hence Z_5 has some literal Hamilton P5, independently of which displayed forward/reverse seams fail. Together with the untouched Hamilton complement B this gives an exact two-cover of H-{u,v}. Thus r=2 always yields a genuine codimension-four to codimension-two representative transition, although the resulting Hamilton order need not preserve the named c-x boundary orientation.

Thus the one-sided c-x lock is not a terminal local packet. It feeds a finite SAME-SUPPORT LIFT TEST on H-{u,v}. Its progress metric is explicit: simultaneous success gives genuine fixed-complement selected reversal, one-sided success lowers deletion codimension, the five-vertex short support lowers deletion codimension even when both named windows block, and only simultaneous failure of two at-most-two-hole windows with |J|>=4 remains. The latter keeps every physical endpoint and seam needed for the next reconstruction.

### 16. In the smallest |J|=5 simultaneous-wrap-failure cell, paired first-bad cuts force a current c-x portal or a lower-codimension representative
Retain the terminal simultaneous-wrap-failure normalization of Section 15 in its smallest long case

  J=(j_0,j_1,m,x,c),                                      (WR.89)

so the middle M is the singleton {m}. The inherited J turns are

For the actual cell F_iG_j, intersect the two active two-block partitions in (WR.93). After deleting empty intersections the common active refinement is:

  F1G1: {a,b} | {j_0,j_1,m} | {c,x};

Thus the locked physical pair {c,x} is one whole refinement block in every cell. Including B, the refinement has four nonempty cells in F1G1 and five in the other three cells.

Now fix ANY exact two-cover T=T_1|T_2 of H-{u,v}; existence and exactness follow from smallest-counterexample minimality, since a Hamilton H-{u,v} together with the deleted dimer would two-cover H. Split the two T-rails at every selected edge joining distinct cells of the appropriate refinement (WR.94) together with B. If t is the number of such intercell selected edges, the split forest has exactly 2+t nonempty path fragments. Every refinement cell contains at least one fragment, so

  t>=2 in F1G1,
  t>=3 in F1G2, F2G1, F2G2.                               (WR.95)

This is only the first component-count step of R159, kept at the physical selected-edge level; no R176/payment descendant is taken.

Two immediate consumers sharpen (WR.95).

**B-quiet representative.** If T has no selected B-to-active edge, then no T-rail can contain vertices from both B and the seven-vertex active support. Since T has exactly two nonempty rails and both supports are nonempty, one rail spans all of B and the other spans all seven active vertices. Replacing the B-rail order by the retained literal Hamilton order B gives an exact H-{u,v} representative

  P_Z | B                                                  (WR.96)

with P_Z Hamiltonian on {a,b,c,j_0,j_1,m,x}. This is a genuine codimension-four to codimension-two currentization retaining the literal complement B. No claim is made about the c-x orientation selected by P_Z.

**No c-x exit.** Suppose instead that T has no selected edge with exactly one endpoint in {c,x}. Then any T-component meeting {c,x} is contained wholly in that two-vertex set. Because vertices outside {c,x} remain to be covered and T has only two rails, c and x cannot be two separate singleton rails. Hence one entire T-rail is exactly the dimer {c,x}. Reversing that dimer is free, so the same exact pair-deletion fiber has both orientations on the identical support with the identical other Hamilton rail. Accepted R561 on the dimer support then Hamilton-extends {c,x} by u (or v); retaining the other rail gives a literal exact singleton-deletion two-cover of H-v (respectively H-u). If these are the same physical edge, the lower bound (WR.95) still forces at least one additional intercell selected transition (at least two additional transitions in the three four-block active cells). Thus the genuinely hard |J|=5 residue is not merely 'both lift windows fail': it already carries a pair-deletion current portal with literal support transfer at B, a current departure from {c,x}, and at least one further coarse transition, all inside one exact T.

The refinement argument above uses the singleton middle only through the exact |J|=5 first-bad covers (WR.93)-(WR.94); no long-M generalization is asserted.

Retain the terminal long-portal state of Sections 15-16. Write

  J=(j_0,...,d,x,c),   d=j_{r-2},                         (WR.99)

  L_b=(j_0,...,d,x,b,c,a).                                (WR.101)

The complete new-turn windows are respectively

  A_1=(d,x,a),   A_2=(x,a,b),
  B_1=(d,x,b),   B_2=(x,b,c).                             (WR.102)

Every other turn is inherited from J or is one of the cyclic Y-turns. Hence if either window is fully tight, the corresponding word together with the untouched literal rail B is an exact two-cover of H-{u,v}. This is a genuine codimension-four to codimension-two representative lift.

Assume both cyclic-tail rows fail. Then there is NO Hamilton path on Y union {d,x} beginning with the actual current state (d,x):

  no Hamilton P5 on Y+{d,x} starts (d,x).                 (WR.103)

Indeed, after the forced initial d,x there are only six orders of a,b,c. The suffix a,b,c is exactly L_a and is blocked by failure of its complete window. The suffix b,c,a is exactly L_b and is likewise blocked. The suffix a,c,b contains the bad reverse triangle turn (a,c,b), the suffix b,a,c contains the bad reverse triangle turn (b,a,c), and the suffix c,b,a contains the bad reverse triangle turn (c,b,a). The remaining cyclic suffix c,a,b contains the already established bad lock turn (x,c,a) from (WR.100). These six cases are exhaustive.

Thus simultaneous failure has moved the role obstruction by one PHYSICAL selected J-edge: the previous lock forbade the relevant Hamilton boundary through x->c on Y+{x}; the new lock forbids Hamilton boundary access beginning with d->x on Y+{d,x}. The literal complement B, the full J order, and both blocked two-turn windows remain retained. This is not an anonymous two-witness packet.

The first seams record additional orientation data. If A_1 and B_1 are both bad, R3 gives

  (a,x,d), (b,x,d) tight,                                 (WR.104)

so a,b are two named head witnesses on the reverse tested dimer (x,d). If A_1 and B_1 are both tight, failure of both rows forces A_2,B_2 bad, while A_1,B_1 make a,b two named tail witnesses on the CURRENT tested dimer (d,x). Mixed cells retain one current-direction continuation and one exact reverse witness. None of these refinements is paid through R523/R542 here; (WR.103) is the stronger common conclusion.

The source-lock case is the exact boundary dual, and its words may be written without ambiguity. For

  J=(c,x,d,j_3,...),                                      (WR.105)

retain the source one-sided lock that no Hamilton P4 on Y+{x} ends with (c,x). Test

  L'_a=(c,a,b,x,d,j_3,...),
  L'_b=(b,c,a,x,d,j_3,...).                               (WR.106)

Their only new turns are respectively (a,b,x),(b,x,d) and (c,a,x),(a,x,d). If either row succeeds, it again gives an exact H-{u,v} representative with literal B. If both fail, the same six-order check gives

  no Hamilton P5 on Y+{x,d} ends with (x,d).              (WR.107)

The two cyclic suffixes are the failed rows; the three noncyclic Y orders contain a bad reverse-triangle turn; and the remaining cyclic order a,b,c,x,d is blocked by the inherited source-lock turn (b,c,x).

This is a one-step propagation theorem, not yet an automatically iterable descent. The new obstruction lives on the five-support Y+{d,x}; another inward step requires a new pair of complete reconstruction words. Its value is exactly Director v40's requested strict physical movement of the boundary-role obstruction while the current J edge and literal complement B remain visible.


### 18. The minimum-transition F1G1 bypass collapses to codimension one or three exact block transfers
Specialize Section 16 to the first-first cell F1G1. Write

  A={a,b},
  P={j_0,j_1,m},
  Q={c,x}.                                                  (WR.108)

The literal source orders are the dimer A, the trimer P=(j_0,j_1,m), and the dimer Q. More structure is retained: the original complement rail

  J=(j_0,j_1,m,x,c)

Hamiltonizes P union Q, while the locked triangle path

  L=(a,b,c,x)

Hamiltonizes A union Q with the opposite Q orientation. The two first-bad seams are exactly the two missing A-to-P exterior joins. Thus this cell is a three-block Hamilton triangle A,P,Q with B as the only remaining bypass.

Among all exact two-covers T of H-{u,v}, choose one minimizing the number t of selected transitions between the four coarse cells

  A | P | Q | B.                                           (WR.109)

Section 16 gives t>=2. Suppose first that t=2. Splitting T at the two coarse transitions produces exactly four path fragments, one for each nonempty cell. Hence every coarse cell occurs as ONE contiguous T-block. The induced two-rail cover of the four block labels has exactly two edges.

The hard hypotheses from Section 16 exclude B as a one-block rail, because that is the B-quiet lift (WR.96), and exclude Q as a one-block rail, because that is the c-x dimer improvement (WR.97). Therefore a 3+1 coarse shape can isolate only A or P.

**A isolated.** Then one T-rail is exactly the dimer A. Reverse its orientation freely. Accepted R561 on the two dimer orders says that u (or v) Hamilton-extends A. Keeping the other T-rail therefore gives an exact singleton-deletion two-cover of H-v (respectively H-u). This is strict codimension-two to codimension-one progress.                          (WR.110)

**P isolated.** Then one T-rail is exactly the tight trimer P=(j_0,j_1,m). Test the two four-sets P+u and P+v. If either has a Hamilton P4, replace P by that P4 and keep the other T-rail, obtaining an exact singleton-deletion two-cover. If neither four-set has a P4, accepted R522/P537 applied to the same trimer P with fourth vertices u,v gives a Hamilton P5 on P+{u,v}; together with the untouched other T-rail this would be a spanning two-cover of H. Hence in a counterexample the isolated-trimer branch necessarily makes a codimension-one transition. This is the only step here that uses the |J|=5 singleton-middle fact essentially: P is a trimer.                         (WR.111)

It remains to consider a 2+2 coarse shape. There are exactly three support pairings:

  (B union A) | (P union Q),
  (B union P) | (A union Q),
  (B union Q) | (A union P).                               (WR.112)

Each is already an ACTUAL exact pair-deletion representative because it is the support partition of T. The first two can be normalized without any seam test: in the first pairing replace the P union Q rail order by the retained literal J; in the second replace the A union Q rail order by the retained literal L=(a,b,c,x). Thus they become respectively

  H[B union A] | J,                                        (WR.113)
  H[B union P] | (a,b,c,x),                                (WR.114)

where H[S] denotes the actual Hamilton T-rail on the displayed support S. The first transfers the restored block A into the complement side while preserving the literal current J and x->c boundary. The second transfers P into the complement side and currentizes the reverse c->x boundary on the literal locked path.

In the third pairing, the B union Q rail contains Q={c,x} as one contiguous dimer block and has exactly one coarse attachment to B, while the other rail Hamiltonizes the formerly missing support A union P. Thus this representative moves the entire Q block into the B-side and simultaneously supplies a one-edge current extension of the c-x block into B. Retain the orientation of Q selected by T, the exact B-neighbor at that attachment, and the Hamilton A union P order.                         (WR.115)

No scalar descent is claimed from the three transfers (WR.113)-(WR.115); they are finite exits from the F1G1 paired-blocked state and must be consumed in their new support locations rather than renamed as K improvement.

Therefore the ONLY F1G1 state not already leaving the cell at minimum coarse transition count is

  t>=3.                                                     (WR.116)

Equivalently, after choosing T to minimize t, the split forest has at least five fragments on only four coarse cells, so at least one of A,P,Q,B is physically fragmented in T. This is a strict excess-transition obstruction e=t-2>=1. The next F1G1 consumer should use which small block fragments: fragmentation of A or Q separates a physical dimer; fragmentation of P splits the singleton-middle trimer; fragmentation of B gives multiple literal support-transfer contacts. The present section does not classify those HIGH cells further.

# The quiet endpoint-only F1G1 transfer has a two-step support descent

**Workspace:** D17
**State:** established
**Key:** `directed-triangle-f1g1-endpoint-mu-transfer`

**Summary:** In the endpoint-only pair-deletion cell obtained after puncturing the restored labels a,b back to literal old rails J|B, the terminal c-x lock prevents either restored label from being appended after c. Let mu count restored labels on the B-side. Then mu=2 or 1 admits an explicit one-turn transfer lowering mu by one; failure gives an exact ancestral/current boundary reversal. At mu=1, R573 compresses the blocker to a two-witness current-boundary fan or a start-rigid trimer state. Thus mu is a genuine bounded support coordinate; the role-rigid terminal remains unconsumed.

### 1. Exact endpoint-only cell and support coordinate
Retain the terminal c-x one-sided-lock ancestry from `directed-triangle-r846-weave-restoration` SV11804. In particular J is the literal old current rail ending (...,x,c), B is the literal old complement rail, and the two restored triangle labels are A={a,b}. The lock gives

  (a,c,x), (b,c,x) tight,

hence by R3 both (x,c,a) and (x,c,b) are bad. Work only in the quiet endpoint-only pair-deletion class: T is an exact two-cover of H-{u,v}, deleting a,b from T leaves exactly the literal old orders J|B, and the restored labels occur only in endpoint blocks of those two rails. Since neither label can be appended after terminal c, every restored label lying on the J-side is a source prepend.

Define

  mu(T)= number of vertices of {a,b} lying on the rail containing literal B.

Then mu is in {0,1,2}; mu=0 already preserves literal B and is the desired exit from this endpoint-only cell.

### 2. mu=2 lowers to mu=1 or gives an ancestral J shield
Assume mu=2. Choose an outermost restored endpoint label z on the B-rail so that deleting z leaves a Hamilton path on B together with the other restored label. Such z exists whether a,b occupy opposite B ends or one two-label endpoint block. Test the single source-prepend turn

  theta=(z,j0,j1),

where J=(j0,j1,...,x,c). If theta is tight, replace z on the B-side by the rail (z,J), leaving the post-deletion B-side rail literally unchanged. This is an exact H-{u,v} cover with mu=1. If theta is bad, R3 gives

  (j1,j0,z) tight,

an exact reversal of the ancestral selected source dimer j0->j1 with the actually transferred label z retained as witness. If a,b occupy opposite B ends then either is outer-removable; a mu-minimal choice forces both corresponding tests to fail and gives two named witnesses on that same reverse J boundary.

### 3. mu=1 lowers to mu=0 or gives a current-boundary shield
Assume mu=1. Write the J-side rail as (w,J), where w is one restored label, and let z be the unique restored label on an endpoint of the B-side rail. Deleting z leaves literal B. The candidate

  (z,w,J) | B

introduces exactly one new turn, (z,w,j0), because (w,j0,j1) is inherited from T. If this turn is tight, the candidate is an exact H-{u,v} cover with mu=0. If it is bad, R3 gives

  (j0,w,z) tight.

The current T boundary is w->j0, so this is an exact reversal on the same physical boundary pair with the other restored triangle label z retained as witness.

Thus every successful transfer strictly lowers the integer coordinate 2->1->0. No reversible rotation is counted as progress.

### 4. R573 compresses the mu=1 terminal
At a mu=1 failure set D={u,v}, S={w}, and let C be the remaining vertices of H-D-S. The exact target cover has the unique S|C transition w->j0, and X=D union S={u,v,w} is Hamiltonian. If X has a Hamilton path ending (p,w), accepted R573/P648 applied to the actual transition gives

  (j0,w,p) tight.

Together with (j0,w,z), this is a two-witness same-orientation fan on the same current reversed boundary dimer j0->w. If no Hamilton path of X ends at w, then the two possible orders (u,v,w) and (v,u,w) are both bad; R3 gives both

  (w,v,u), (w,u,v) tight.

Thus w is a literal START-RIGID three-vertex absorber state.

### 5. Exact scope
This section proves only the bounded endpoint-only support transfer. Its terminal outputs are: literal-B mu=0 representative; ancestral j0j1 reverse shield; current wj0 two-witness fan; or start-rigid {u,v,w}. The fan and start-rigid state are retained unconsumed. No R523/R542 payment and no spanning closure is asserted from them.

# The F1G1 fragmented-A floor reduces to one no-A|B split-rail topology

**Workspace:** D17
**State:** established
**Key:** `directed-triangle-f1g1-fragmented-a-floor`

**Summary:** For a transition-minimal F1G1 exact pair-deletion representative with A={a,b} fragmented and t=3, P,Q,B are whole blocks. The 1+4 rail shape is consumed; if both A-singletons lie on one rail, A-Q-A contradicts t-minimality, A-B-A enters the exact mu-transfer unit outside R435 order activity, and A-P-A forces a two-ended R548 wrap-shield pair. If A lies on both rails, any actual A|B boundary gives a one-seam current-boundary reversal, while the no-A|B case has only two support types; one collapses to t=2 via the locked A+Q path, leaving only (A-P)|(A-Q-B). This is a conditional reduction, not closure.

### 1. Fragmentation identity and the t=3 floor
Retain the F1G1 first-bad cell of SV11804 with coarse blocks

  A={a,b}, P={j0,j1,m}, Q={c,x}, B,

literal J=(j0,j1,m,x,c) on P union Q and locked L=(a,b,c,x) on A union Q. For an exact H-{u,v} cover T let b_X(T) be the number of maximal coarse X-blocks along its two rails. If t(T) is the number of selected edges joining distinct coarse cells, splitting the two rails at all such transitions gives

  t=b_A+b_P+b_Q+b_B-2.

Assume T is transition-minimal in F1G1, A is fragmented, and t=3. Then b_A=2 and necessarily

  b_P=b_Q=b_B=1.

Thus there are exactly five coarse blocks A,A,P,Q,B.

### 2. The 1+4 rail shape is consumed
A 1+4 coarse split isolates one whole block. An isolated A is a singleton target rail; the other rail is Hamiltonian, while the singleton together with deleted u,v forms a tight trimer in some order, giving a spanning two-cover of H. Isolated B is the B-quiet codimension-two currentization already proved in SV11804. Isolated Q is the {c,x} dimer-to-codimension-one branch there. If P is isolated, test P+u and P+v. A Hamilton P4 gives codimension-one reconstruction; if both are P4-free, accepted R522/P537 Hamiltonizes P+{u,v}, closing H with the other rail. Hence every genuinely hard t=3 fragmented-A representative has a 2+3 coarse split.

### 3. Both A-singletons on one rail
Then the three-block rail is A-X-A for X in {P,Q,B}.

If X=Q, its support is A union Q. Replacing that entire rail by the retained locked Hamilton path L=(a,b,c,x) changes A-Q-A to one A-Q transition while leaving the other rail unchanged, giving t=2, contrary to transition minimality.

If X=B, the other rail has support P union Q and may be normalized to literal J. If the current Hamilton order on the whole B-block differs from the literal ancestral B order, retain the explicit R435 order activity. Outside R435, the A-B-A rail together with literal J is exactly the mu=2 endpoint-only cell of `directed-triangle-f1g1-endpoint-mu-transfer`; apply that bounded consumer and retain its terminal output.

If X=P, consider the two cyclic rotations of the actual A-P-A rail that move one endpoint A-label across the rail and make the two A-labels contiguous. Either successful R548 wrap would reduce the number of A-blocks by one and hence produce t=2, contradicting transition minimality. Therefore both relevant wrap turns fail. R3 yields a two-ended named wrap-shield pair on the actual P-block endpoints and the two A labels. This pair is retained; no generic packet payment is taken.

### 4. A-singletons on different rails: conditional A|B currentization
Now each target rail contains one A-singleton. Suppose one of them, h, is actually adjacent to the whole B-block, and let e be the other A-label. If the current boundary is h|B with B beginning b0, replace the P union Q support by literal J and move e next to h on the B-side. The existing h|B turn certifies the second junction, so the sole new seam is

  kappa=(e,h,b0).

If kappa were tight the resulting exact cover would have t=2. Therefore kappa is bad and R3 gives

  (b0,h,e) tight,

an exact reversal of the current selected h->b0 boundary with e as witness. Dually, for B|h with B ending bL, the sole seam (bL,h,e) is bad and R3 gives (e,h,bL). If |B|=1, either orientation of this trimer Hamiltonizes A union B and together with literal J gives the forbidden t=2 exit. Thus any surviving conditional A|B shield has |B|>=2.

### 5. The no-A|B split has one unresolved topology
Assume instead that no A-singleton is adjacent to B. Up to reversing rails and exchanging a,b, there are only two coarse support types:

  (A-P) | (A-Q-B),
  (A-Q) | (A-P-B).

Indeed in a 2+3 split the two blocks adjacent to the two A-singletons must be P and Q, leaving B as the far block of the three-block rail.

The second type cannot survive transition minimality. Its A-Q rail has support exactly A union Q, so replace it by L=(a,b,c,x); leave the existing contiguous P-B rail untouched. The result has exactly the two coarse transitions A-Q and P-B, hence t=2.

Therefore the only no-A|B t=3 fragmented-A topology not consumed above is

  (A-P) | (A-Q-B),

up to the stated symmetries. This section does not claim to consume that final topology. In particular R933 is not invoked merely from the deleted pair {u,v}; its endpoint-controlled Hamilton-path hypothesis is not supplied by the retained four-support paths.

### 6. Exact scope
At the minimum fragmented-A floor t=3, every branch leaves by codimension improvement/closure, the exact mu consumer, a named two-ended wrap shield, a current A|B reversal, or the single no-A|B support type (A-P)|(A-Q-B). For t>=4 at least one of P,Q,B fragments in addition to A, but no further taxonomy is asserted here.

# FILE: A7C3/WORKSPACE/D17/112-directed-triangle-f1g1-two-ended-b-transposition.md

<!-- BEGIN FILE: A7C3/WORKSPACE/D17/112-directed-triangle-f1g1-two-ended-b-transposition.md -->

# The two-ended fragmented-B transfer has a paired endpoint-transposition gate

**Workspace:** D17
**State:** established
**Key:** `directed-triangle-f1g1-two-ended-b-transposition`

**Summary:** In the Director-v42 F1G1 t=3 cell where B is the unique fragmented coarse block and both exact target rails are mixed, each rail has its active support at one end and therefore has an active endpoint dimer. A rail of order three already gives codimension one or closure by R522 with probes u,v. Otherwise swapping the two endpoint vertices has exactly two new turns. Full success gives two exact same-support covers with the identical other rail and an oppositely selected endpoint dimer, so the fixed-complement selected-reversal consumer applies. Double failure gives genuine R561 on the four-vertex terminal window by reversing the next-inward selected edge; mixed failure gives a complete one-sided Hamilton-boundary lock on that same current edge. Applying the gate to both rails simultaneously yields two retained inward boundary certificates whenever neither rail produces the desired selected reversal. No ancestral interval/order assumption on the two B fragments is used.


### 1. Exact v42 two-ended B-transfer setup
Retain the F1G1 |J|=5 laboratory of exact parent SV11804. Put

  G=H-{u,v},
  A={a,b},  P={j0,j1,m},  Q={c,x},

with retained literal paths

  J=(j0,j1,m,x,c),   L=(a,b,c,x).

Assume the Director-v42 first fragmented-B equality cell: T=T_1|T_2 is an exact two-cover of G with total coarse transition count t=3; B is the unique fragmented coarse cell; A,P,Q are each whole contiguous T-blocks; and B has exactly two B|active transitions, one on each target rail. Cutting those two physical transitions gives nonempty B-blocks B_1,B_2 and nonempty active blocks Z_1,Z_2, with

  V(Z_1) disjoint-union V(Z_2)=A union P union Q.

There is only one active-active coarse transition in T, so the three whole active coarse cells distribute 1+2 between Z_1,Z_2. Equivalently, up to swapping rails, their supports are

  A | (P union Q),
  P | (A union Q),
  Q | (A union P).

No order statement about B_1,B_2 inside the ancestral literal B is made or used. What matters below is only their ACTUAL T-orders and the two physical B|active attachments. Each target rail consists of one B_i block and one Z_i block, in one of the two actual orders B_i Z_i or Z_i B_i. In particular the active block is an endpoint block of its rail and has at least two vertices.

### 2. A three-vertex mixed rail already lowers deletion codimension or closes
Suppose one target rail R has order three. It is a literal tight trimer and the other target rail S is Hamilton on the remaining vertices of G. Probe the trimer R by the two deleted vertices u,v.

If R+u has a Hamilton P4, replace R by that P4 and retain S; this is a literal two-cover of H-v. The dual applies with v. If neither R+u nor R+v has a Hamilton P4, accepted R522/P537 applied to the common tight trimer R and probes u,v gives a Hamilton P5 on V(R)+{u,v}; together with S this is a spanning two-cover of H, contradiction.

Hence every surviving two-ended B-transfer target has both T-rails of order at least four.

### 3. Terminal active endpoint: one two-turn transposition gate
Take one target rail whose active block is terminal, and write its actual last four vertices as

  ... , r,s,h,e,                                           (BT.1)

where h,e are the last two vertices of the active block Z_i. Thus (r,s,h) and (s,h,e) are inherited T-turns and the physical endpoint state h->e is selected in T. Test only the adjacent endpoint transposition

  ... , r,s,e,h.                                           (BT.2)

Its COMPLETE new-turn window is

  alpha=(r,s,e),    beta=(s,e,h).                          (BT.3)

No earlier turn changes.

**SUCCESS.** If alpha,beta are both tight, replacing the rail by (BT.2) gives another exact cover T* of the SAME residue G with the SAME unordered rail supports and the IDENTICAL untouched other Hamilton rail. The endpoint support {h,e} is selected h->e in T and e->h in T*. Thus this is a literal fixed-complement selected reversal on the whole target-rail support, not a graph-intrinsic local reversal detached from the cover. Apply `fixed-complement-selected-reversal-normal-form` SV7559 immediately. Its R548 transport keeps the support, complement, and physical reversed dimer fixed while decreasing its declared boundary distance; if it reaches R561 on the whole rail support, u (or v) Hamilton-extends that rail and the untouched other rail gives an exact singleton-deletion two-cover. If transport blocks first, retain the exact named wrap shield supplied by that consumer.

**DOUBLE FAILURE.** If alpha and beta are both bad, R3 gives

  (e,s,r),    (h,e,s) tight.                               (BT.4)

Hence

  K=(h,e,s,r)                                               (BT.5)

is a Hamilton P4 on the same four-support as the inherited

  P=(r,s,h,e).                                              (BT.6)

P begins with r->s and K ends with s->r, so accepted R561 applies literally on {r,s,h,e}, with the next-inward CURRENT T-edge {r,s} as its boundary-reversed dimer. If the whole rail has order four, this R561 support is the whole rail and immediately absorbs u (or v), giving a codimension-one exact cover with the other target rail unchanged. For a longer rail no such whole-rail extension is asserted; retain the prefix and the local R561 support exactly.

**MIXED FAILURE.** Suppose exactly one of alpha,beta is tight. Then there is NO Hamilton P4 on {r,s,h,e} ending with the reverse boundary state (s,r). There are only two orders of h,e before s,r. The order

  (h,e,s,r)

requires precisely reverse(beta) and reverse(alpha); in the mixed branch exactly one of those two turns is bad. The other order

  (e,h,s,r)

starts with (e,h,s), which is the complete reverse of the inherited tight turn (s,h,e), hence is bad. Thus

  no Hamilton P4 on {r,s,h,e} ends (s,r).                  (BT.7)

So the mixed gate is not an anonymous failed swap: it currentizes a complete one-sided Hamilton-boundary lock on the next-inward selected T-edge r->s.

### 4. Source active endpoint: exact dual
If the active block is the source of its target rail, write the first four actual vertices as

  e,h,s,r,...                                               (BT.8)

with endpoint state e->h selected. Swap only the first two vertices:

  h,e,s,r,...                                               (BT.9)

The complete new window is

  alpha*=(h,e,s),    beta*=(e,s,r).                        (BT.10)

If both pass, this is again an exact same-support/common-complement selected reversal and SV7559 applies. If both fail, their reversals give

  (s,e,h),   (r,s,e)

and hence the Hamilton P4 (r,s,e,h), which begins r->s while the inherited (e,h,s,r) ends s->r; R561 applies on the same four-support. If exactly one passes, the two possible orders beginning with the reverse state r->s are blocked exactly as in Section 3, so

  no Hamilton P4 on {r,s,h,e} begins (r,s).                (BT.11)

Again the output is a one-sided lock on an ACTUAL selected T-edge, not generic sign currency.

### 5. Both physical B attachments survive the reduction
Apply Sections 2-4 independently to the two actual target rails of the v42 cell. The endpoint pair chosen on each rail lies inside its active endpoint block, so the test never assumes that B_i is an interval of ancestral B and never reorders B_i. The other whole target rail is literally unchanged in every SUCCESS branch. Therefore a successful gate on EITHER side already supplies the exact same-support/common-complement reversal required by the named fixed-complement consumer while the second physical B|active attachment remains present in the unchanged complement rail.

If neither side succeeds and no order-three rail exists, the SAME exact target cover T simultaneously retains two inward current-edge certificates, one on each rail. Each certificate is one of:

  (DF) a genuine R561 four-support on the next-inward selected edge, with the complete two-bad-turn ancestry (BT.3) or (BT.10); or
  (MX) a complete one-sided four-support Hamilton-boundary lock on that selected edge, with exactly which transposition seam passed and which failed retained.

Thus the three 1+2 active-support distributions do not require separate B-order taxonomies at this stage. The unresolved two-ended transfer has been reduced to a paired current-boundary state on the two actual rails. This is not declared closure: in particular a local DF support inside a longer rail is not silently promoted to a whole-rail R561 witness, and an MX lock is not spent through R523/R542.

### 6. A locked A-Q specialization eliminates one mixed orientation
One useful source-specific sharpening is available when the two-active-cell side is A union Q. Suppose, in the terminal form (BT.1), the endpoint dimer {h,e} is A and the immediately preceding current dimer {r,s} is Q. In the mixed branch (BT.7), if the current Q order were x->c then the forbidden reverse boundary would be c->x. But the retained literal path

  L=(a,b,c,x)

is a Hamilton P4 on A union Q ending c->x. Hence this mixed orientation is impossible. Therefore a surviving terminal mixed gate with endpoint A and inward Q must carry the current Q orientation c->x.

Dually, in the source form (BT.8), if the endpoint dimer is Q and the immediately inward dimer is A, a current A order b->a would make the forbidden reverse source boundary a->b, contradicted by L, which begins a->b. Hence a surviving source mixed gate in that placement must carry A in the current orientation a->b.

These are orientation restrictions inside the paired boundary state, not a claim that the remaining mixed cases close.

### Scope
This section consumes no generic component-drop/payment output. Its purpose is to use the exact two-ended B-transfer representative itself. A short mixed rail lowers codimension or closes; a successful endpoint transposition gives a legal whole-cover fixed-complement selected reversal with its named consumer applied; and otherwise both rails simultaneously expose exact inward current-boundary geometry. Higher B-contact cells, t>=4, the other F/G cells, long-middle M, and the separate mu=1 start-rigid terminal are outside scope.

<!-- BEGIN FILE: A7C3/WORKSPACE/D17/113-directed-triangle-f1g1-p-aq-bidirectional-merge.md -->

# The P | (A union Q) fragmented-B split has a bidirectional active-merge blocker

**Workspace:** D17
**State:** established
**Key:** `directed-triangle-f1g1-p-aq-bidirectional-merge`

**Summary:** In the v42 t=3 fragmented-B support split P | (A union Q), write the current whole active blocks as a tight trimer P_T=(p0,p1,p2) and a Hamilton four-path Z_T=(z0,z1,z2,z3). Either concatenation P_T Z_T or Z_T P_T, if its complete two-turn junction window passes, Hamiltonizes all seven active labels and with the retained literal B gives the desired exact H-{u,v} representative. Thus an unresolved cell blocks both directions, yielding one exact reversed free-boundary witness from each two-turn window. Because |P|=3, the P-side endpoint-transposition certificate of SV14216 is simultaneously pinned to the physical B|P attachment. Outside explicit same-support R435 order activity, P_T is the literal (j0,j1,m) and Z_T is the literal L=(a,b,c,x); then the P_T Z_T window is already blocked at its first seam by the ancestral F1G1 G1 failure (j1,m,a), so only the opposite L P window {(c,x,j0),(x,j0,j1)} is new. Its first-bad alternatives retain either the dual-Q common-source fork (j0,c,x),(j0,x,c), or the two-continuation fork (j1,j0,c),(j1,j0,x) together with (c,x,j0). This is a structured two-ended blocker, not closure or generic packet payment.

### 1. Exact v42 support split
Retain the exact F1G1 t=3 fragmented-B cell of SV14216 and specialize to the active support distribution

  P | (A union Q),

where P={j0,j1,m}, A={a,b}, Q={c,x}. Let the two whole active blocks in the actual exact target cover T of G=H-{u,v} have their ACTUAL tight orders

  P_T=(p0,p1,p2),
  Z_T=(z0,z1,z2,z3),

with V(P_T)=P and V(Z_T)=A union Q. The two B-fragments and both physical B|active attachments remain exactly as in T; no statement about their ancestral B-order is made.

Because the P-side active block has exactly three vertices, the inward certificate of the endpoint-transposition gate in SV14216 is pinned to the physical B|P attachment. If P_T is terminal on its mixed rail, the SV14216 window (...,r,s,h,e) has s,h,e equal to the three P vertices and r equal to the touched B endpoint, so r->s is the actual B->P transition. If P_T is source, the dual first-four window has its inward state s->r equal to the actual P->B transition. Hence every non-success P-side gate already returns DF or MX geometry on one of the two v42 physical B contacts.

### 2. Both active concatenations are complete two-turn tests
Test the two Hamilton concatenations of the ACTUAL active block orders.

First,

  M_PZ=(p0,p1,p2,z0,z1,z2,z3).

Its complete new-turn window is exactly

  lambda_1=(p1,p2,z0),
  lambda_2=(p2,z0,z1).

Every other turn is inherited from P_T or Z_T. If both lambda turns are tight, M_PZ is a Hamilton path on all seven active labels. Together with the retained literal Hamilton path B on the disjoint complement this gives

  M_PZ | B

as an exact two-cover of H-{u,v}. This is precisely the desired literal-B codimension-two currentization, so an unresolved cell must block the window. Under deterministic FIRST-BAD normalization:

  PZ1: lambda_1 bad, hence (z0,p2,p1) tight;
  PZ2: lambda_1 tight and lambda_2 bad, hence (z1,z0,p2) tight.

Thus the failed P->Z merge retains either a named witness on the reverse terminal dimer of P_T or a named witness on the reverse source dimer of Z_T.

Second,

  M_ZP=(z0,z1,z2,z3,p0,p1,p2).

Its complete new-turn window is

  rho_1=(z2,z3,p0),
  rho_2=(z3,p0,p1).

Again, full success gives M_ZP|B, the desired literal-B exact pair-deletion representative. Hence the unresolved cell blocks this window as well. FIRST-BAD gives

  ZP1: rho_1 bad, hence (p0,z3,z2) tight;
  ZP2: rho_1 tight and rho_2 bad, hence (p1,p0,z3) tight.

Therefore the SAME exact fragmented-B target carries, in addition to its two physical B attachments and the P-side contact certificate from Section 1, a blocker from EACH direction of active merging. These are free-boundary blockers on the actual active block orders. No R523/R542 payment is taken.

### 3. R435-quiet current orders reduce the new work to one two-turn window
Compare P_T with the retained literal trimer

  P=(j0,j1,m)

and compare Z_T with the retained locked Hamilton path

  L=(a,b,c,x).

Both comparisons are on identical supports. By accepted R435/P448, outside explicit same-support order activity the current contact order is increasing relative to the reference order. Since every vertex of each support is a contact, the quiet case forces literal equality

  P_T=(j0,j1,m),
  Z_T=(a,b,c,x).

This is only a normalization of the R435-quiet subcell; the R435-active alternatives remain structured outputs and are not called progress by themselves.

In this quiet subcell the P->Z merge is

  (j0,j1,m,a,b,c,x),

whose first junction turn is exactly

  (j1,m,a).

But F1G1 means the ancestral G1 first seam (j1,m,a) is bad. Hence the P->Z active merge is already blocked with the retained reverse turn

  (a,m,j1) tight.

The only genuinely new active-merge test is therefore the opposite concatenation

  (a,b,c,x,j0,j1,m),

with complete window

  h_1=(c,x,j0),
  h_2=(x,j0,j1).

At least one is bad. FIRST-BAD gives exactly two subcells.

### 4. The two quiet first-bad outputs retain the old wrap ancestry
The simultaneous-wrap-failure parent SV11804 already retains

  (j0,c,x),
  (j1,j0,c)

tight.

If h_1 is bad, R3 gives

  (j0,x,c) tight.

Thus on the three-support {j0,c,x} both terminal Q orientations are realized from the common source j0:

  (j0,c,x),  (j0,x,c).

Neither corresponding reverse boundary can start a Hamilton trimer on this same support: (x,c,j0) is the complete reverse of the already-tight (j0,c,x), while (c,x,j0)=h_1 is bad. Retain this as the dual-Q common-source boundary lock; it is stronger data than one anonymous reversed seam.

If h_1 is tight and h_2 is bad, R3 gives

  (j1,j0,x) tight.

Together with the old wrap turn (j1,j0,c), the reverse ancestral source dimer j1->j0 has TWO named tight continuations c and x, while h_1=(c,x,j0) is also tight. Retain this two-continuation fork with the actual Q orientation and the old reverse-boundary P4 ancestry. No claim is made that this same-polarity fork is itself R561 or closure.

### 5. Scope
This section only treats the v42 support split P | (A union Q). It proves a legal simultaneous two-direction active-merge test and identifies the exact failure geometry. It does not consume the resulting DF/MX plus merge-blocker state, does not assume any order on B1,B2, and does not extend to the other two 1+2 support distributions or to t>=4. Its useful output is that the P-side physical B contact and both free active merge directions are now simultaneously currentized, with the F1G1 G1 blocker reused in the quiet literal-order subcell rather than respent as generic sign currency.
